chapters.title: Don't Die Early
chapters.intro:
This section covers three things: deaths from accidents and injuries such as traffic crashes, fires, and poisoning; a few vaccines and screening tests with the strongest evidence; and bodily warning signs that warrant getting checked. The numbers in the benefits column come from randomized trials, studies that followed large groups of people for many years, or official statistics. The costs are the author's rough estimates based on market prices, intended only for comparison with one another. Do not cite them.

The entries in this section are grouped by topic below, with entry numbers in parentheses.

**On the road**: Wear a seat belt (Entry 1), wear a helmet (Entry 2), do not speed or drive after drinking (Entry 9), and use child safety seats (Entry 10).

**Fire, gas, and electricity at home**: Install smoke alarms (Entry 3), replace gas hoses when their service life expires (Entry 4), do not bring electric bicycles into building corridors (Entry 6), keep fire extinguishers and a first-aid kit ready (Entry 26), fit the guard before using an angle grinder (Entry 42), and ventilate, test, and put protective measures and attendant monitoring in place before entering a septic tank (Entry 46).

**Accidents involving children, older adults, and the outdoors**: Install window opening restrictors (Entry 11), keep children near water in sight at all times (Entry 12), practice balance exercises after age 60 (Entry 13), do not eat wild mushrooms (Entry 5), do not pick up metal objects of unknown origin (Entry 36), measure ice thickness before going onto natural ice outdoors (Entry 41), and finish rehydrated wood ear mushrooms in the same meal (Entry 48).

**Vaccines**: Get the five-marker hepatitis B panel (Entry 14), tetanus (Entry 15), HPV vaccine (Entry 16), influenza vaccine (Entry 20), shingles vaccine (Entry 21), and pneumococcal vaccine (Entry 22).

**Screening and diagnostic checks**: Measure blood pressure (Entry 7), test fasting blood glucose (Entry 8), breast cancer screening (Entry 17), cervical cancer screening (Entry 18), colorectal cancer screening (Entry 19), testing for Helicobacter pylori (Entry 23), low-dose chest CT (Entry 24), bone density testing (Entry 39), osteoporosis medication (Entry 40), taking anticoagulants after a diagnosis of atrial fibrillation (Entry 44), a one-time hepatitis C antibody test (Entry 45), and gastroscopy screening (Entry 47).

**Bodily warning signs and sexual health**: Blood in urine visible to the naked eye (Entry 27), checking cardiovascular health first when erectile problems occur (Entry 28), improving erectile function by losing weight and quitting smoking (Entry 29), condoms and not sharing needles (Entry 30), HIV testing (Entry 31), and pre-exposure prophylaxis medication (Entry 38).

**Mental health crises**: Call China's 12356 hotline if you have suicidal thoughts (Entry 25), tell someone first if you have suicidal thoughts (Entry 32), continuing to gamble even after borrowing money to do so (Entry 37), the costs of surviving pesticide ingestion or coal gas inhalation (Entry 33), the costs after a fall from height (Entry 34), the costs of losing a kidney (Entry 35), and directly asking someone around you whether they have thought about suicide (Entry 43).

entries.title: Wear a seat belt, in both the front and back seats
entries.cost: Free. Takes an extra 2 seconds each time you get into a vehicle.
entries.summary: Wearing a seat belt in the front seat of a passenger car reduces the chance of being killed in a crash by more than 40%. In the front seat of a light truck, the reduction is 60%. Among people killed inside vehicles in the United States in 2022 whose seat belt use was known, half were not wearing one.
entries.benefit: The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) estimates that wearing a seat belt reduces the risk of fatal injury for front-seat occupants of passenger cars by 45%. For front-seat occupants of light trucks, the reduction is 60%. Among people killed in passenger vehicles (small motor vehicles that carry people) in the United States in 2022 whose seat belt use was known, 50% were unbelted. The World Health Organization (WHO) states that seat belts reduce the risk of death among vehicle occupants by up to 50%. WHO estimates that 248,099 people died in road traffic crashes in China in 2021, equivalent to 17.4 deaths per 100,000 people. The National Bureau of Statistics yearbook records 62218 road traffic deaths in 2021
entries.sources: NHTSA (2024). Occupant Protection in Passenger Vehicles: 2022 Data (DOT HS 813 573): “Among killed passenger vehicle occupants with known restraint use, 48 percent of those in the front row and 60 percent of those in the second row were unrestrained.” <https://crashstats.nhtsa.dot.gov/Api/Public/ViewPublication/813573> ; WHO (2025). Road traffic injuries fact sheet. <https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/road-traffic-injuries> ; WHO GHO RS_196/RS_198 (China, 2021). <https://ghoapi.azureedge.net/api/RS_196?$filter=SpatialDim%20eq%20%27CHN%27> ; National Bureau of Statistics of China (2022). China Statistical Yearbook 2022, Table 24-5, Road Traffic Accidents (2021): 62218 deaths. <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/ndsj/2022/html/C24-05.jpg>
entries.notes: Wear a seat belt in the back seat too. In the same report, 60% of those killed in the second row whose seat belt use was known were unbelted. The figures of 45% and 60% are estimates calculated by the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) using crash databases (citing Kahane 2015). They are not from randomized trials. WHO's death toll for China is a modeled estimate, about 4 times the 62218 deaths in the statistical yearbook. The two sets of statistics differ in scope; only WHO's definition is used here.

entries.title: Wear a helmet and fasten it when riding a motorcycle or electric bicycle
entries.cost: A helmet costs 100 to 300 yuan. Putting it on takes 5 seconds each time.
entries.summary: Wearing a helmet with the strap fastened reduces a motorcyclist's chance of dying in a crash by about 40%. Head injuries are reduced by about 70%. The strap must be snug; a helmet sitting loosely on your head does not count as wearing one.
entries.benefit: Cochrane pooled the results of multiple studies. Wearing a helmet reduced motorcyclists' risk of death by 42%. The original estimate was OR 0.58, with a 95% confidence interval (95% CI) of 0.50 to 0.68. Head injuries were reduced by 69% (OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.25 to 0.38)
entries.sources: Liu BC et al. (2008). Helmets for preventing injury in motorcycle riders. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD004333.pub3>
entries.notes: Fasten the helmet strap; hanging a helmet on the handlebars does not count as wearing it. The figures above come from motorcycles. There is no direct research on electric bicycles; the findings are extrapolated because head injuries occur in the same way after a collision. For helmets when skiing, snowboarding, or cycling, see Section 22, Entry 12 (Wear a helmet when skiing or mountain biking). For the minimum age for children to ride on public roads, see Section 30, Entry 20 (Riding an electric bicycle on public roads under age 16).

entries.title: Install smoke alarms; if you burn coal indoors or use gas for heating in winter, also install a carbon monoxide alarm
entries.cost: A smoke alarm costs 30 to 100 yuan. A carbon monoxide alarm costs 50 to 150 yuan. After installation, replace the batteries once a year.
entries.summary: A working smoke alarm can reduce the chance of dying in a residential fire by about 60%. In 40% of fatal residential fires in the United States, people were asleep when the fire started. If you burn coal or use gas indoors in winter, add a carbon monoxide alarm. In China, 11,500 people died from carbon monoxide poisoning in 2018; during the three winter months, about 70% of the deaths occurred at home.
entries.benefit: A study in North Carolina, United States, examined a group of residential fires, retrospectively comparing households where fatalities occurred with those where they did not. Having a working smoke alarm at home reduced the risk of death by about 60%. The original estimate was OR 0.39, with a 95% confidence interval (95% CI) of 0.18 to 0.83. Among fatal fires in occupied residential buildings in the United States from 2018 to 2020, 24% of homes had no smoke alarms, and in 41% people were asleep when the fire started. China reported 11,523 deaths from carbon monoxide poisoning in 2018. Of these deaths, 72.59% in December, 67.42% in January, and 66.48% in February occurred at home
entries.sources: Marshall SW et al. (1998). Fatal residential fires: who dies and who survives? JAMA. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.279.20.1633> ; USFA (2022). Fatal Fires in Residential Buildings (2018-2020), Topical Fire Report Series 22(2). <https://www.usfa.fema.gov/downloads/pdf/statistics/v22i2.pdf> ; You J et al. (2020). Number of Deaths due to Carbon Monoxide Poisoning by Month and by Place of Death — China, 2018. China CDC Weekly. <https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2020.008>
entries.notes: Reason for the B rating: For smoke alarms, there is only one study, which retrospectively compared households where fatalities occurred with those where they did not; it was not a randomized trial. There are no studies showing that carbon monoxide alarms themselves reduce mortality. The benefit here is inferred from the concentration of poisoning deaths in winter and at home.

entries.title: Replace gas hoses and stoves when their service life expires, do not alter gas piping yourself, and feel free to refuse doorstep sales pitches from gas companies
entries.cost: A compliant gas hose costs a few dozen yuan. Replace the stove every few years. When replacing it, take a moment to check whether its service life has expired.
entries.summary: Replacing hoses and stoves when their service life expires is a user's obligation explicitly stated in China's Regulations on the Administration of Urban Gas. Altering piping or removing gas meters yourself is expressly prohibited by the regulations. The same regulations also state that gas companies cannot require you to buy products or services they specify. You can simply refuse doorstep sales pitches claiming that you “must replace” something.
entries.benefit: The regulations make it a user's obligation to “promptly replace gas-burning appliances, connecting pipes, and other items that the state has expressly ordered to be phased out or whose service life has expired”: if your stove or hose reaches the end of its service life or has been phased out by the state, you must replace it. The regulations also prohibit “unauthorized installation, modification, or removal of indoor gas facilities and gas metering devices,” which includes altering piping and removing gas meters yourself. They also expressly state that gas operators must not require users to purchase products they specify or accept services they provide
entries.sources: State Council of China (2010). Regulations on the Administration of Urban Gas (State Council Order No. 583), Article 27: “Gas users shall comply with rules for the safe use of gas, use compliant gas-burning appliances and gas cylinders, and promptly replace gas-burning appliances, connecting pipes, and other items that the state has expressly ordered to be phased out or whose service life has expired”; prohibited acts under Article 28 include “(1) Unauthorized operation of public gas valves,” “(2) Using gas pipes as load-bearing supports or grounding conductors,” and “(4) Unauthorized installation, modification, or removal of indoor gas facilities and gas metering devices”; Article 20 prohibits gas operators from “(6) Requiring gas users to purchase products they specify or accept services they provide”; under Article 29, users may complain about charges and services to gas administration departments and other relevant authorities, and “the relevant departments shall handle the complaint within 15 working days of receiving it.” <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2010/content_1758214.htm>; Shenzhen Municipal Housing and Construction Bureau (2024). Tips for Safe Gas Use (II): “Immediately close the main gas valve in your home,” “Quickly open doors and windows to ventilate,” “Do not switch household lights, range hoods, or other electrical appliances on or off,” and “People should evacuate quickly, move to a safe place, and promptly call the gas company's emergency reporting number.” <https://zjj.sz.gov.cn/zcjzts/content/post_11882410.html>; Zhangjiagang Municipal Emergency Management Bureau (2024). Knowledge for Safe Gas Use: “Do not hastily turn on an exhaust fan to ventilate” and “Only call for help after moving away from the scene.” <https://www.zjg.gov.cn/zjgszwz/yjaqzs/202411/72b4fad7399c48378302460c6ce2d55b.shtml>; State Administration for Market Regulation of China (2023). Product Quality and Safety Risk Advisory for Gas Appliances (republished by the Ezhou Municipal Urban Construction Commission): “Users are encouraged to install and use protective devices such as smart gas meters, gas leak safety protection devices, self-closing valves, standalone smoke fire detectors, and combustible gas detectors and alarms.” <https://cjw.ezhou.gov.cn/zxzx/gzdt/202308/t20230821_569108.html>
entries.notes: The wording of the regulations can be checked word for word, but it only establishes your obligation to replace pipes when their service life expires; it does not establish how many accidents replacement prevents. No official statistics were found on how much replacing pipes according to their service life reduces gas accidents, so this receives only a C rating. If someone making a home safety inspection asks you to buy a self-closing valve or alarm they specify, you can refuse and can also file a complaint, because Article 20, item 6 of the regulations prohibits gas companies from making such demands. Self-closing valves and alarms themselves are encouraged by China's State Administration for Market Regulation; if you choose to install them, select compliant products yourself. If you smell gas, first close the main gas valve; for bottled gas, close the cylinder valve. Then open doors and windows to ventilate; do not turn on an exhaust fan. Do not switch lights, range hoods, or any other electrical appliances on or off, and do not touch a lighter. Then evacuate and call the gas company's emergency reporting number only after leaving the scene. Carbon monoxide poisoning is a separate matter; see Section 13.

entries.title: Do not pick, buy, or eat wild mushrooms; no “folk identification method” is valid
entries.cost: Free. The difficult part is giving up a seasonal wild delicacy.
entries.summary: In 2025 alone, the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention investigated 828 mushroom poisoning incidents, involving 2165 people and 13 deaths. That year, 34 additional mushroom species were identified that had not previously been recorded as causing poisoning. Testing for poison with a silver needle, assuming mushrooms eaten by insects are safe, and believing only brightly colored mushrooms are poisonous—none of these claims is valid.
entries.benefit: In 2025, the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention investigated 828 mushroom poisoning incidents involving 2165 people and 13 deaths. The case fatality rate was 0.6%, meaning that 0.6% of those poisoned died. From 2019 to 2024, there were 276 to 676 incidents annually, with case fatality rates ranging from 0.87% to 2.86%. In 2025 alone, 138 poisonous mushroom species were identified, including 34 recorded for the first time in China as causing poisoning. The Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention's public education material refutes folk identification methods one by one. Only brightly colored mushrooms are poisonous: false; toxicity has nothing to do with color. Mushrooms eaten by insects or infested with maggots are safe: false; many highly poisonous mushrooms are also eaten by insects when mature. Poisonous mushrooms change color when cooked with silverware or garlic: false; mushroom toxins do not contain sulfur, whereas sulfur is what turns a silver needle black. Deep-frying at high temperatures removes toxins: also unreliable. Its conclusion is that “there is currently no simple, easy, quick, and effective way to identify whether a mushroom is poisonous.” The Beijing Municipal Administration for Market Regulation's 2026 advisory says that if you feel unwell after accidental ingestion, “seek medical attention immediately; do not attempt to treat it yourself.” Keep any remaining mushrooms and food scraps to help doctors identify the poison
entries.sources: Mushroom Poisoning Outbreaks — China, 2025. China CDC Weekly (2026): “In 2025, China CDC investigated 828 mushroom poisoning incidents across 27 provincial-level administrative divisions (PLADs), affecting 2,165 individuals and causing 13 deaths - a case fatality rate of 0.6%, the lowest of the past six years. In total, 138 poisonous mushroom species were identified, including 34 newly recorded in poisoning incidents in China.” “From 2019 to 2024, the annual number of incidents ranged from 276 to 676, and the case fatality rate ranged from 0.87% to 2.86%.” <https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2026.120>; the same journal’s 2024 annual report <https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2025.106>; Yin Yu and Li Haijiao, Institute of Occupational Health, Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention (2019). Preventing and Controlling Mushroom Poisoning: A Long Road Ahead: “Method 4: Mushrooms eaten by insects or containing maggots are nonpoisonous. Wrong!” “Method 6: Poisonous mushrooms change color when cooked with silverware, scallions, garlic, or rice. Wrong!” “Therefore, there is currently no simple, convenient, fast, and effective way to determine whether a mushroom is poisonous.” <https://www.chinacdc.cn/jkkp/zyjk/zdzs/201908/t20190802_301109.html>; Beijing Center for Disease Prevention and Control (2023). Stay Away from Poisonous Mushrooms; Don’t Be a ‘Mushroom Daredevil’: “Folk methods of identifying poisonous mushrooms—such as judging by color and shape, growing environment, whether silverware detects poison, secretions, or the presence of maggots or insects—are all unreliable.” <https://www.bjcdc.org/cdcmodule/jkfw/yyyspjk/jkyf/swzdyf/2023/35518.shtml>; Beijing Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (2026). Risk Advisory on Preventing Poisoning from Accidentally Eating Wild Mushrooms: “Seek medical attention immediately. Do not treat it yourself, lest you delay diagnosis and treatment. Properly preserve samples such as leftover wild mushrooms and food scraps.” <https://scjgj.beijing.gov.cn/zwxx/scjgdt/202606/t20260625_4715961.html>
entries.notes: If you suspect you ate the wrong mushroom, go to a hospital immediately; do not try to treat it at home. Bring any leftover mushrooms, food scraps, or photos you took. There are several types of poisonous mushroom poisoning, and identifying the mushroom helps doctors give the right treatment. New species are recorded as poisonous to humans every year, so the assumption that “locals can reliably identify them” does not hold up. Claims that you can test for poison with a silver needle or by cooking mushrooms with garlic, that mushrooms eaten by insects are safe, or that only brightly colored mushrooms are poisonous are all false. Wood ear mushrooms and snow fungus soaked for too long, and wet rice noodles kept too long, pose a different kind of poisoning risk; see Item 48 (Soaked Wood Ear Mushrooms).

entries.title: Don’t bring an electric bicycle into the hallway or elevator, or charge it at home
entries.cost: Costs nothing. The hard part is parking at the shared charging point downstairs every time and walking a few dozen extra meters.
entries.summary: Parking or charging an electric bicycle in the lobby, corridor, or stairwell of a high-rise residential building is expressly prohibited by regulations issued by China’s Ministry of Emergency Management. Those who refuse to correct the violation face fines of 500 to 1,000 yuan as individuals, or 2,000 to 10,000 yuan if engaged in business. The fine is the smaller concern: a fire there would burn in your only escape route.
entries.benefit: Regulations issued by China’s Ministry of Emergency Management expressly prohibit “parking electric bicycles or charging them in the public lobbies, evacuation corridors, stairwells, or emergency exits of high-rise civil buildings.” You may neither park nor charge one in any of those places. If the violation is not corrected, individuals and entities not engaged in business face fines of 500 to 1,000 yuan; those engaged in business face fines of 2,000 to 10,000 yuan. These regulations do not cover elevators or the inside of homes. In a response to a deputy to China’s National People’s Congress, the Ministry of Emergency Management said it had made improper indoor parking or charging of electric bicycles and batteries a priority in its campaign to address major fire safety risks. Its public warning concerned the dangers of “bringing bicycles into buildings, running charging cables out of homes, and modifying bicycles or batteries yourself.” Elevators are governed by local regulations: since May 1, 2025, Beijing has prohibited bringing electric bicycles or rechargeable batteries into elevator cars. Individuals who refuse to correct a violation face fines of 500 to 1,000 yuan
entries.sources: China’s Ministry of Emergency Management (2021). Regulations on Fire Safety Management of High-Rise Civil Buildings (Ministry of Emergency Management Order No. 5, Articles 37 and 47). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-08/01/content_5628815.htm>; China’s Ministry of Emergency Management (2023). Letter in Response to Proposal No. 00969 at the Fifth Session of the 13th National Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference: “In 2021, 18,000 electric bicycle fires were reported nationwide, causing 65 deaths, 222 injuries, and direct property losses of 221 million yuan. Of these, 3,782 occurred inside buildings, causing 60 deaths and 175 injuries.” <https://www.mem.gov.cn/gk/jytabljggk/zxwytadfzy/2022zx/202301/t20230119_440918.shtml>; China’s Ministry of Emergency Management (2025). January 15, 2025 Press Conference: “The number of fires per million electric bicycles fell from 5.6 in 2023 to 3; the number of fires fell 42.2% year on year, and casualties fell by more than 90%.” <https://www.mem.gov.cn/xw/xwfbh/2025n01y15xwfbh_6337/>; China’s Ministry of Emergency Management (2024). Response to Suggestion No. 7187 at the First Session of the 14th National People’s Congress: “Improper indoor parking or charging of electric bicycles (storage batteries), failure to establish fire compartments as required, and other issues were made priorities of the 2023 special inspection and rectification campaign for major fire safety risks.” “Publicized and warned the public about the fire risks and dangers of ‘bringing bicycles into buildings, running charging cables out of homes, and modifying bicycles or batteries yourself.’” <https://www.mem.gov.cn/gk/jytabljggk/rddbjydfzy/2023_5984/202401/t20240130_476731.shtml>; Beijing Fire and Rescue, republished by the People’s Government of Dongcheng District, Beijing (2025). Beijing Fire Safety Regulations: Individuals Can Be Fined Up to 1,000 Yuan for Bringing Electric Bicycles or Batteries into Elevators: “Bringing electric bicycles or rechargeable batteries into elevator cars is prohibited. Units that violate this rule and refuse to correct the violation may be fined 2,000 to 10,000 yuan, and individuals may be fined 500 to 1,000 yuan.” <https://www.bjdch.gov.cn/ztzl/aqsczbgjsnxd/zdgz/202504/t20250410_4061604.html>
entries.notes: Don’t buy a modified battery, use an off-brand charger, or leave it charging unattended overnight. Once a lithium battery catches fire, the flames can spread across it within tens of seconds while it releases highly toxic smoke. If a bicycle parked in the hallway catches fire, it burns in your only escape route. According to figures published by China’s Ministry of Emergency Management, there were 18,000 electric bicycle fires nationwide in 2021, killing 65 people. Of those, 3,782 fires occurred inside buildings and killed 60 people; almost all the deaths were indoors. After the 2024 rectification campaign, the number of fires fell 42.2% from the previous year, and casualties fell by more than 90%. Fires per million bicycles fell from 5.6 to 3. That press conference did not provide an absolute total for the full year.

entries.title: Measure your blood pressure; if it’s high, take medication to bring it to the target level
entries.cost: A digital blood pressure monitor costs 100 to 200 yuan. One measurement takes 1 minute. Most blood pressure medications cost a few to a few dozen yuan per month. The hard part is continuing to take them even when you have no symptoms.
entries.summary: For every 10 mmHg reduction in systolic blood pressure, the risk of a major cardiovascular event falls by about 20%, and the risk of stroke falls by 27%. The risk of heart failure falls by 28%, and the risk of death by 13%. Among people aged 35 to 75 in China, 44.7% have high blood pressure, but only 7.2% have it under control.
entries.benefit: A combined analysis of 123 trials involving more than 610,000 people found that each 10 mmHg reduction in systolic blood pressure was associated with about a 20% lower risk of major cardiovascular events. The reported value was RR 0.80, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.77 to 0.83. Systolic pressure is the higher of the two blood pressure numbers. The risk of stroke was about 27% lower (RR 0.73), and the risk of heart failure about 28% lower (RR 0.72). All-cause mortality fell by 13% (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.84 to 0.91). A screening study of 1.7 million people aged 35 to 75 in China found that 44.7% had high blood pressure. Among those people, 44.7% knew they had it, 30.1% were receiving treatment, and only 7.2% had it under control
entries.sources: Ettehad D et al. (2016). Blood pressure lowering for prevention of cardiovascular disease and death: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Lancet. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(15)01225-8> ; Lu J et al. (2017). Prevalence, awareness, treatment, and control of hypertension in China (China PEACE Million Persons Project). Lancet. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(17)32478-9>
entries.notes: First, get your blood pressure measured. Fewer than 1 in 10 people with high blood pressure in China have it under control, so this one measurement is among the best-value actions in this book. There is still debate about what counts as reaching the target—130 or 140—but there is no dispute about finding out whether you have high blood pressure and bringing it down.

entries.title: If you’re overweight after age 35, get a fasting blood glucose test; if it’s normal, test again every three years
entries.cost: A fasting blood glucose test costs a little over 10 yuan. An HbA1c test costs a few dozen yuan. All it takes is one blood draw at a hospital.
entries.summary: For a few dozen yuan and one tube of blood, you can detect prediabetes before you have any symptoms at all. The official US screening recommendation is for people aged 35 to 70 who are overweight or obese to be tested. If the result is normal, test again every three years. The US threshold for overweight is a body mass index of 25, lowered to 23 for Asian Americans; under the Chinese standard, a BMI of 24 counts as overweight.
entries.benefit: The US Preventive Services Task Force is the US body that issues official screening recommendations. Its current recommendation is to screen adults aged 35 to 70 who are overweight or obese for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes, even if they have no symptoms at all. Overweight means a body mass index of ≥25, and obesity means ≥30. For Asian Americans, it recommends lowering the threshold to a BMI of ≥23 because their diabetes risk is higher at the same BMI. Under the Chinese industry standard, a BMI from 24.0 to less than 28.0 is overweight, and ≥28.0 is obese. This recommendation has a grade of B. It also states: “Screening every 3 years is a reasonable approach for adults with normal blood glucose”
entries.sources: US Preventive Services Task Force (2021). Screening for Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes. <https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/screening-for-prediabetes-and-type-2-diabetes>: “at a lower BMI (≥23) if the patient is Asian American”; General Office of China’s National Health Commission (2024). Explanation of Core Knowledge for Residents on Weight Management (2024 Edition): “According to the industry standard Determination of Adult Weight (WS/T 428-2013) … 24.0≤BMI＜28.0 is overweight, and BMI≥28.0 is obese.” <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202407/P020240703481519509521.pdf>; Wang L et al. (2021). Prevalence and Treatment of Diabetes in China, 2013-2018. JAMA: “In 2018, among adults with diabetes, 36.7% (95% CI, 34.7%-38.6%) reported being aware of their condition” “These rates did not change significantly from 2013.” <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2021.22208>
entries.notes: Finding out you have prediabetes does not automatically mean you need medication. Eating less, moving more, and losing some weight can lower the risk of developing diabetes by 30% to 60%. In a 2018 nationwide survey, only 36.7% of Chinese adults with diabetes knew they had it, with no significant improvement compared with 2013. For more on that risk reduction, what to change after a diagnosis, and how soon to retest, see Section 2, Item 45 (If You’re Diagnosed with Prediabetes).

entries.title: When driving, don’t speed, drink and drive, or look at your phone; pull over and rest when you’re sleepy
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Driving a little slower adds a few minutes to a trip. The hard part is drinking less at social meals and resisting the urge to look when a message arrives. On long drives, stop and rest for at least 20 minutes every 4 hours.
entries.summary: For every 1% increase in average vehicle speed, the risk of a fatal crash rises by about 4%. There is no safe threshold at which “a little alcohol is fine” for driving. Handling a phone while driving raises the odds of a crash to 3.6 times those of attentive driving; dialing raises them to 12.2 times. When drowsiness is visible to others, the odds of a crash are about 3.4 times as high.
entries.benefit: According to the World Health Organization (WHO), every 1% increase in average vehicle speed raises the risk of a fatal crash by 4%. The risk from drink-driving starts rising even at very low blood alcohol concentrations. WHO also says drivers who use a mobile phone are about 4 times as likely to be involved in a crash as those who do not, and hands-free phones are not much safer. A US study installed cameras in the vehicles of more than 3,500 drivers and recorded 905 crashes that injured people or damaged vehicles. The comparison was with driving footage in which the driver was alert, attentive, and had not been drinking. Taken together, different ways of handling a phone raised the odds of a crash to 3.6 times as high (OR 3.6). The odds were 12.2 times as high when dialing, 6.1 times when typing a message, 4.8 times when reaching for a phone, 2.7 times when scrolling on a phone, and 2.2 times when talking on a handheld phone. Visibly drowsy driving in the footage was associated with 3.4 times the odds (OR 3.4)
entries.sources: WHO (2025). Road traffic injuries fact sheet: “Drivers using mobile phones are approximately 4 times more likely to be involved in a crash than drivers not using a mobile phone.” “Hands-free phones are not much safer than hand-held phone sets.” <https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/road-traffic-injuries> ; Dingus TA et al. (2016). Driver crash risk factors and prevalence evaluation using naturalistic driving data. PNAS 113(10):2636-2641. <https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1513271113> ; Road Traffic Safety Law of the People’s Republic of China (amended 2021), Article 22, paragraph 2: “A person whose excessive fatigue affects safe driving must not drive a motor vehicle”; Article 90: “A warning or a fine of 20 to 200 yuan shall be imposed.” <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817ab231eb017abd617ef70519> ; Regulations for the Implementation of the Road Traffic Safety Law of the People’s Republic of China (revised 2017), Article 62: A person driving a motor vehicle must not engage in “(3) making or answering calls on a handheld phone, watching television, or other behavior that interferes with safe driving” or “(7) driving a motor vehicle continuously for more than 4 hours without stopping to rest, or stopping to rest for less than 20 minutes.” <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f3cbb3c016f40f566c10e23> ; China’s Ministry of Public Security (2021). Measures for the Administration of Points for Road Traffic Safety Violations (Ministry of Public Security Order No. 163), Article 11: Violations carrying 3 points each include “(6) making or answering calls on a handheld phone, or other behavior that interferes with safe driving, while driving a motor vehicle” and “(14) driving a goods vehicle continuously for more than 4 hours without stopping to rest, or stopping to rest for less than 20 minutes”; Article 9: Violations carrying 9 points each include “(7) driving a medium-sized or larger passenger vehicle or a vehicle transporting hazardous goods continuously for more than 4 hours without stopping to rest, or stopping to rest for less than 20 minutes.” <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2022/content_5679697.htm>
entries.notes: The 1% and 4% figures linking speed and death were calculated from an accident model, not a randomized trial. For drunk driving, the WHO gave only the direction of the effect, not a number. This section has not checked the original literature on how much risk rises with each amount of alcohol consumed. The multipliers for phone use and drowsiness refer to crashes that injure people or damage vehicles, not deaths. The comparison group was selected to represent the most ideal driving conditions, so these multipliers are somewhat higher than they would be if compared with ordinary driving. Chinese regulations cover holding a phone while making a call: the penalty is a fine of 20 to 200 yuan and 3 points on the driver’s license. Using a hands-free device is legal, but the WHO says it is not much safer. Driving continuously for more than 4 hours without taking a break of at least 20 minutes is also illegal in China. Truck drivers receive 3 points; drivers of medium-sized or larger passenger vehicles and vehicles carrying hazardous materials receive 9 points. If you feel drowsy, pull into a service area, park, and rest for a while. Cold medicines and antihistamines containing chlorpheniramine or diphenhydramine can also make you drowsy; see Section 34, Item 12 (chlorpheniramine). If you often feel drowsy while driving and snore loudly, see Section 3, Item 27 (sleep apnea).

entries.title: Use a child safety seat for children under 4 when riding in a car; do not hold them in your arms
entries.cost: One seat costs 300 to 2,000 yuan and can be used for several years. Allow an extra minute each time you get in the car to secure the child.
entries.summary: For infants under one year old riding in a car, a safety seat lowers the probability of a fatal injury in a crash by about 70%. For children aged 1 to 4, it lowers the probability by about half. Holding a child in your arms does not have this effect.
entries.benefit: The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) estimates that safety seats reduce the risk of fatal injury for infants under one year old in passenger cars by 71%. For children aged 1 to 4, the reduction is 54%. The World Health Organization (WHO) reports a 71% reduction in infant deaths
entries.sources: NHTSA (2024). Occupant Protection in Passenger Vehicles: 2022 Data (DOT HS 813 573). <https://crashstats.nhtsa.dot.gov/Api/Public/ViewPublication/813573> ; WHO (2025). Road traffic injuries fact sheet. <https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/road-traffic-injuries>
entries.notes: Secure the seat according to its instructions; installing it incorrectly is effectively the same as not installing it. For children under one year old, install it rear-facing so the child faces the back of the car. The figures above are U.S. government estimates based on crash data.

entries.title: If you have children at home, fit window opening restrictors on windows and balconies; insect screens are not a safety barrier
entries.cost: A set of window opening restrictors or a child safety lock costs a few dozen yuan. Installation takes ten minutes.
entries.summary: A set of restrictors costs a few dozen yuan. New York City installed window guards free of charge for high-risk households and explained their use during home visits; reported child falls in one borough fell by half over three years. New York City later passed a law requiring landlords to install guards in homes where children aged 10 or younger live. Insect screens are not a safety barrier.
entries.benefit: Starting in 1972, New York City ran a program called “Children Can’t Fly,” providing free window guards in high-risk neighborhoods and explaining them during home visits. Reported falls in the Bronx declined by 50% from 1973 to 1975. New York City subsequently amended its Health Code to require landlords to install window guards in apartments where children aged 10 or younger live
entries.sources: Spiegel CN, Lindaman FC (1977). Children can't fly: a program to prevent childhood morbidity and mortality from window falls. American Journal of Public Health: “Significant reduction in falls resulted, particularly in the Bronx, where reported falls declined 50 percent from 1973 to 1975”; the 1976 amendment to the New York City Health Code was “to require that landlords provide window guards in apartments where children ten years old and younger reside”. <https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.67.12.1143>; (2021). Unintentional Window Falls in Children and Adolescents. Academic Pediatrics: 38,840 emergency department visits recorded in the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System from January 2007 to August 2017; “The majority of falls occurred in children under the age of 6 and were related to falls from a second story or below”. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.acap.2020.07.008>
entries.notes: Do not put beds, sofas, boxes, or other things children can climb on next to windows or balcony edges. Insect screens only keep mosquitoes out; they can come loose with a push, so do not treat them as guards. This is not only for people living on high floors: in the U.S. data, most falls occurred from the second floor or lower. For children who fall down stairs while in a wheeled baby walker, see Section 20, Item 15 (do not buy a wheeled baby walker).

entries.title: Keep children in sight near water; wear a life jacket when boating or swimming in open water
entries.cost: A life jacket costs 50 to 200 yuan. You also need to devote your attention to watching the child.
entries.summary: Among people who fall overboard, those wearing a life jacket have about half the risk of drowning to death as those without one. Drowning remains the leading cause of death among children aged 1 to 14 in China. The drowning death rate in rural areas is about twice that in cities.
entries.benefit: A study using U.S. Coast Guard data compared matched pairs of people with similar circumstances. Among people who fell overboard from recreational boats, those wearing a life jacket had about half the risk of drowning to death. The adjusted relative risk was RR 0.51, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.35 to 0.74. In China, the drowning death rate among people under 20 fell from 6.60 per 100,000 in 2013 to 3.28 per 100,000 in 2021. The rural rate was about twice the urban rate. In 2021, it was 3.84 per 100,000 in rural areas and 2.01 per 100,000 in urban areas. Drowning remains the leading cause of death among children aged 1 to 14. In 2021, the drowning death rate for children aged 1 to 14 was 3.23 per 100,000, which was 0.99 per 100,000 higher than the rate for road traffic injuries, the second-leading cause. Among injury deaths of people aged 0 to 19 in 2021, drowning accounted for 31.1% and road traffic for 27.9%. The drowning death rate was highest among those aged 15 to 19, at 3.95 per 100,000; among males in that age group it was 5.99 per 100,000
entries.sources: Cummings P et al. (2011). Association between wearing a personal floatation device and death by drowning among recreational boaters. Injury Prevention. <https://doi.org/10.1136/ip.2010.028688> ; Li Z et al. (2023). Unintentional Drowning Mortality Among Individuals Under Age 20 — China, 2013–2021. China CDC Weekly: “in China, it is deemed the primary cause of death for children between the ages of 1 and 14. According to 2021 data, the rate of unintentional drowning in this age group is 3.23 per 100,000, surpassing road traffic injuries, the second leading cause of fatalities, by 0.99 per 100,000.” “rural areas exhibited roughly double the mortality rate found in urban areas”. <https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2023.198> ; Zhou J et al. (2024). Injury Mortality of Children and Adolescents Aged 0–19 Years — China, 2010–2021. China CDC Weekly: “drowning and road traffic crashes were the top two causes of child injury deaths, explaing 31.1% and 27.9% of total injury deaths”. <https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2024.057>
entries.notes: The A grade applies only to the life jacket part. Keeping children in sight is a matter of general consensus; considered on its own, it has only a C grade. There are no randomized trials, and there will not be any in the future. In China, drowning deaths are concentrated in rural areas and among males aged 15 to 19. For playing on ice in winter, see Item 41 (measure the thickness of natural ice before stepping onto it).

entries.title: If you are over 60, train your balance and leg strength, and make your bathroom and stairs safer
entries.cost: Practice tai chi or balance exercises 2 to 3 times a week for 30 minutes each time. Bathroom non-slip mats, grab bars, and night-lights cost from a few dozen to a few hundred yuan. The hard part is keeping up the exercise over the long term.
entries.summary: Practicing balance exercises such as tai chi two or three times a week reduces the number of falls among older people by about 23% and the number of people who fall by 15%. Having someone assess and modify the home reduces the number of falls by about 20%. Falls are the leading cause of injury-related death among people aged 65 and older in China, and more than half happen in their own homes.
entries.benefit: Cochrane pooled 108 trials involving 23,407 people. Exercise reduced the number of falls among older people by 23%. The fall rate ratio was RaR 0.77, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.71 to 0.83. The number of people who fell declined by 15% (RR 0.85). Having someone conduct a home safety assessment and make modifications reduced the fall rate by about 20% (RR 0.81, 95% CI 0.68 to 0.97). Tai chi lowered the risk of falling by about 29% (RR 0.71). In China, falls are the leading cause of injury-related death among people aged 65 and older. Of falls among older people recorded in 2018 surveillance, 55.97% occurred at home
entries.sources: Sherrington C et al. (2019). Exercise for preventing falls in older people living in the community. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD012424.pub2> ; Gillespie LD et al. (2012). Interventions for preventing falls in older people living in the community. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD007146.pub3> ; Lu Z et al. (2021). Characteristics of Falls Among Older People — China, 2018. China CDC Weekly. <https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2021.013>
entries.notes: This item applies to people over 60 who live in their own homes, rather than in nursing homes. The studies above counted falls, not deaths. The path from a fall to a hip fracture and then death can be short for an older person. Poor vision also increases falls; if cataracts make it hard to see where you are going, see Section 17, Item 9 (cataract surgery). For older people pulled over while walking a dog, see Section 17, Item 10 (older people walking dogs). For whether your bones can withstand a fall, see Item 39 of this section (bone density testing).

entries.title: Get the five-marker hepatitis B blood test, and use it with your vaccination record to decide whether you need vaccination
entries.cost: One test costs a few dozen yuan. For adults who need vaccination, the three hepatitis B vaccine doses cost about 100 to 300 yuan in total; check the price at your local vaccination clinic. They are usually given at months 0, 1, and 6.
entries.summary: In the Qidong study, vaccination against hepatitis B at birth was associated with an 84% lower probability of later developing liver cancer. That reduction cannot be applied directly to adults, and a low antibody level alone is not a reason to get all three doses again. People with normal immune function who completed the full course and once had protective antibody levels usually do not need a booster. If you do not know whether you were vaccinated, take your test results to a vaccination clinic for an assessment.
entries.benefit: The Qidong trial randomized groups, not individuals, and followed them for 30 years. Hepatitis B vaccination of newborns reduced primary liver cancer by 84%. The 95% confidence interval was 23% to 97%. The rate of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) positivity fell by 72% (95% CI 68% to 75%); this rate is the proportion of people found to carry the virus. In the control group, 67.8% received catch-up vaccination at ages 10 to 14. The efficacy of catch-up vaccination against HBsAg positivity in early adulthood was only 21% (95% CI 10% to 30%), much weaker than vaccination at birth. In China’s overall population, the proportion testing positive for HBsAg fell by 52% from 1992 to 2014; among children under 5, it fell by 97%. These figures cannot be applied directly to adult catch-up vaccination. People with normal immune function who completed the full course and once developed protective antibody levels retain immune memory after their antibody levels decline and usually do not need a booster. Immune memory means the body can rapidly mobilize its defenses when it encounters the virus again. Whether catch-up vaccination is needed should be determined from the vaccination record and tests for surface antigen, surface antibody, and core antibody. If your vaccination history is unclear, go to a vaccination clinic for an assessment.
entries.sources: Qu C et al. (2014). Efficacy of neonatal HBV vaccination on liver cancer and other liver diseases over 30-year follow-up of the Qidong hepatitis B intervention study. PLoS Medicine: “The estimated efficacy of catch-up vaccination on HBsAg seroprevalence in early adulthood was 21% (95% CI 10%-30%), substantially weaker than that of the neonatal vaccination (72%, 95% CI 68%-75%).” <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pmed.1001774> ; Cui F et al. (2017). Prevention of Chronic Hepatitis B after 3 Decades of Escalating Vaccination Policy, China. Emerging Infectious Diseases. <https://doi.org/10.3201/eid2305.161477>; Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention. Hepatitis B (vaccine-based prevention; frequently asked questions, Question 4). <https://www.chinacdc.cn/jkyj/mygh02/ymkyfjb/yxgy/>; CDC. Pink Book, Chapter 10: Hepatitis B (Immunogenicity and Vaccine Efficacy; Serologic Testing of Vaccine Recipients). <https://www.cdc.gov/pinkbook/hcp/table-of-contents/chapter-10-hepatitis-b.html>; CDC (2023). Screening and Testing for Hepatitis B Virus Infection: CDC Recommendations — United States, 2023 (Table 1; Persons Who Are Fully Vaccinated Against HBV Infection). <https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/72/rr/rr7201a1.htm>
entries.notes: Adults who have never been vaccinated, did not finish the series, or have an unclear vaccination history should bring their vaccination records and lab test results to a vaccination clinic. If the doctor confirms that you are still susceptible to infection, get vaccinated according to the schedule or catch up on missing doses. You cannot conclude that the original vaccination failed based solely on a single negative antibody test years later. Average people who have completed the full course do not need to repeatedly test antibodies just to decide whether to get a booster. Those who test negative for protective antibodies within the prescribed timeframe after completing the full course should have a doctor arrange catch-up vaccination and retesting. Populations such as those on dialysis, immunocompromised individuals, and those with occupational exposure to blood also require separate evaluation. Testing positive for core antibodies may indicate a past infection; it cannot simply be treated as never having been infected and requiring revaccination. The vaccine cannot treat an existing infection. Those who test positive for surface antigen HBsAg should go to a hepatology department for evaluation; see Section 16, Item 11 (Those testing positive for hepatitis B surface antigen should have a liver ultrasound every six months).

entries.title: If punctured by an iron nail or wood splinter, or if a wound is contaminated with dirt, get it treated on the same day and ask whether a tetanus shot is needed
entries.cost: Registration plus wound treatment costs several tens of yuan. If the doctor says a shot is needed, the vaccine or immunoglobulin costs several tens to several hundreds of yuan.
entries.summary: In the United States, once tetanus develops, about 1 in every 10 people dies. Deep wounds and wounds contaminated with dirt carry the highest risk. If the wound is dirty and it has been a full 5 years since the last shot, get 1 booster dose. Getting it treated on the same day costs no more than several tens of yuan; don't delay.
entries.benefit: Among tetanus cases in the United States, about 1 in every 10 cases is fatal. Deep wounds and wounds contaminated by dirt carry higher risks. China's 2024 clinical practice guidelines classify wounds into two tiers. Clean wounds treated within 6 hours that are not contaminated with soil, feces, or animal saliva are considered low-risk. Wounds treated only after more than 6 hours, contaminated with these substances, or puncture wounds, avulsions, crush injuries, burns/scalds, frostbite, or wounds with retained foreign bodies are considered high-risk. Those who have received 3 or more doses, with the last dose less than 5 years ago, need no shots at all. For 5 to 10 years, high-risk wounds receive 1 booster dose. At 10 years or more, get 1 booster dose regardless of tier. Those who have not completed all 3 doses or do not remember clearly must complete the full vaccine course. High-risk wounds also require simultaneous administration of passive immunizing agents (injections that deliver antibodies directly, such as immunoglobulin or antitoxin).
entries.sources: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Tetanus: “Tetanus bacteria can get into someone's body through broken skin, usually through injuries.” “Tetanus can lead to death (1 in 10 cases in the United States are fatal).” “People who didn't complete the primary series or who aren't up to date with their 10-year tetanus booster shots are also at increased risk.” “Vaccination also helps prevent tetanus in people with wounds, depending on their tetanus vaccination history.” <https://www.cdc.gov/tetanus/about/index.html>; General Office of the National Health Commission (2024). Notice on Issuing the Guidelines for Diagnosis and Treatment of Non-Neonatal Tetanus (2024 Edition) (Guo Wei Ban Yi Ji Han [2024] No. 381, risk classification on appendix page 16, Table 4 on page 20). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202410/content_6982262.htm>; Appendix PDF (scanned copy). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202410/P020241023483425528555.pdf>
entries.notes: Once you arrive at the hospital, let the doctor make the judgment; do not make decisions on your own, and do not skip asking just because it seems troublesome. Not all wounds require a shot. The doctor will assess which tier the wound belongs to, then ask when you last received a shot, and then decide. “A shot in childhood is effective for a lifetime” is incorrect. If the wound is dirty, a booster is needed once it has been a full 5 years since the last shot. Therefore, before going, think about which year you received your last tetanus shot.

entries.title: For women, getting the HPV vaccine as early as possible is best
entries.cost: Domestic bivalent is about 300-plus yuan per dose, and imported nine-valent is about 1,300 yuan per dose. A total of 2 to 3 doses are administered. Each trip takes half a day.
entries.summary: Sweden tracked 1.67 million women. Among those who received the HPV vaccine before age 17, the probability of subsequently developing invasive cervical cancer was only about one-eighth of that in unvaccinated women. For those vaccinated between ages 17 and 30, it was also only about half. Therefore, the earlier you get it, the more worthwhile it is.
entries.benefit: Sweden tracked 1.67 million women for statistical analysis: the incidence rate of invasive cervical cancer among vaccinated individuals was lower than among the unvaccinated. For those vaccinated before age 17, it was about 88% lower (IRR 0.12, 95% CI 0.00 to 0.34; in parentheses are the original value and its confidence interval). For those vaccinated at ages 17 to 30, it was about 53% lower (IRR 0.47, 95% CI 0.27 to 0.75). The World Health Organization designates girls aged 9 to 14 who are not yet sexually active as the priority vaccination target.
entries.sources: Lei J et al. (2020). HPV Vaccination and the Risk of Invasive Cervical Cancer. New England Journal of Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1917338>; WHO. Cervical cancer fact sheet: “HPV vaccination is a priority for all girls aged 9–14 years, before they become sexually active.” <https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/cervical-cancer>
entries.notes: The World Health Organization prioritizes vaccination for girls aged 9 to 14 who are not yet sexually active. Vaccinating at ages 17 to 30 still yields a drop of over 50%. That Swedish study only followed participants up to age 30; it provides no figures on how much the risk decreases if vaccinated after age 30. Even after vaccination, cervical cancer screening is still required; vaccination cannot replace screening; see Item 18 (Cervical cancer screening for women over age 30).

entries.title: Women should undergo breast cancer screening starting at age 40, with mammography every two years
entries.cost: Mammography costs two to three hundred yuan each time. Many regions offer free screening programs. It takes half a day every two years.
entries.summary: Women aged 40 to 74 getting a mammogram every two years is explicitly recommended in official US screening guidelines. For those aged 75 and older, as well as supplementary ultrasound and MRI for dense breasts, official conclusions state that evidence is still insufficient. When physical exam packages charge extra for these, you can skip them.
entries.benefit: The US Preventive Services Task Force is the official US agency providing screening recommendations. Its current recommendation is: “recommends biennial screening mammography for women aged 40 to 74 years.” Breast X-ray imaging is what is commonly referred to as mammography. This recommendation has a grade of B. For women aged 75 and older, as well as supplementary ultrasound and MRI for dense breasts, it determined that “current evidence is insufficient.” China's 2021 breast cancer screening guidelines recommend that women at average risk start screening at age 45, once every 1 to 2 years. High-risk women start at age 40, once a year.
entries.sources: US Preventive Services Task Force (2024). Breast Cancer: Screening. <https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/breast-cancer-screening>; He Jie, Chen Wanqing, Li Ni, et al. (2021). Guideline for breast cancer screening and early diagnosis and treatment in China (2021, Beijing). Chinese Journal of Oncology, 43(4), 357-382: “Recommendation 8.1: For the average-risk population, it is recommended to start breast cancer screening from age 45” “Recommendation 8.2: For the high-risk population, it is recommended to start breast cancer screening from age 40” “Recommendation 9.1: For the average-risk population, it is recommended to undergo breast cancer screening once every 1 to 2 years”. <https://doi.org/10.3760/cma.j.cn112152-20210119-00061>
entries.notes: The age to start screening varies across countries; China's 2021 guideline starts at age 45 for average risk. Those whose parents, children, or biological siblings have had breast cancer, as well as those carrying BRCA mutations, belong to high-risk categories and must consult a doctor individually to establish a plan; this item does not apply.

entries.title: Women aged 30 and older should undergo cervical cancer screening, prioritizing HPV testing
entries.cost: HPV testing costs 100 to 300 yuan per time. For those with negative results, once every 5 years is sufficient. Sampling takes a few minutes.
entries.summary: In that rural India trial, women who received just a single HPV test had about half the probability of dying from cervical cancer. The probability of being diagnosed with advanced cervical cancer was also about 50% lower. At one to two hundred yuan per test, screen once every 5 years according to US recommendations.
entries.benefit: That rural India trial was cluster-randomized rather than individually randomized. The subjects were women aged 30 to 59. With just a single round of HPV testing screening, the risk of dying from cervical cancer was about 48% lower. The original value was HR 0.52, confidence interval 95% CI 0.33 to 0.83. The risk of being diagnosed with advanced cervical cancer was about 53% lower (HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.32 to 0.69). For screening intervals, refer to the US Preventive Services Task Force 2018 recommendations: for women aged 30 to 65 undergoing high-risk HPV testing alone, screen once every 5 years.
entries.sources: Sankaranarayanan R et al. (2009). HPV screening for cervical cancer in rural India. New England Journal of Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa0808516>; US Preventive Services Task Force (2018). Cervical Cancer: Screening: “For women aged 30 to 65 years, the USPSTF recommends screening every 3 years with cervical cytology alone, every 5 years with high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) testing alone, or every 5 years with hrHPV testing in combination with cytology (cotesting).” <https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/cervical-cancer-screening>
entries.notes: People who have received the HPV vaccine still need screening, because the vaccine does not cover all virus types. What makes this study rare is that it is a randomized screening trial that directly took mortality as the endpoint, and only conducted one round of screening.

entries.title: Undergo colorectal cancer screening starting at age 45 to 50, using fecal immunochemical testing for fecal occult blood or colonoscopy
entries.cost: Fecal testing costs several tens of yuan, done once every 1 to 2 years. Colonoscopy costs several hundreds to over a thousand yuan; if the result is negative, once every 10 years is sufficient. Set aside one day for bowel prep before a colonoscopy.
entries.summary: Getting a fecal occult blood test costing several tens of yuan every one to two years is associated with an approximately 16% lower probability of dying from colorectal cancer, and 25% lower for those who completed at least one round. For people invited to undergo a colonoscopy, the probability of developing colorectal cancer over the next ten years dropped from 1.20% to 0.98%.
entries.benefit: Cochrane pooled multiple studies together. For people undergoing fecal occult blood screening, the risk of dying from colorectal cancer was about 16% lower. Original value RR 0.84, confidence interval 95% CI 0.78 to 0.90. For those who participated in at least one round, it was about 25% lower (RR 0.75). Looking again at the NordICC randomized trial: among people invited to undergo colonoscopy, colorectal cancer incidence over 10 years fell from 1.20% to 0.98%. Original value RR 0.82, confidence interval 95% CI 0.70 to 0.93.
entries.sources: Hewitson P et al. (2007). Screening for colorectal cancer using the faecal occult blood test, Hemoccult. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD001216.pub2> ; Bretthauer M et al. (2022). Effect of Colonoscopy Screening on Risks of Colorectal Cancer and Related Death. New England Journal of Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2208375>
entries.notes: Controversy. NordICC was calculated based on people who were “invited to undergo colonoscopy.” Colorectal cancer mortality was 0.28% versus 0.31% (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.64 to 1.16), a difference that remains within the margin of error. This indicates that the mortality benefit of colonoscopy was previously overestimated. The evidence for fecal testing regarding mortality is actually more robust. Guidelines in various countries set the starting age between 45 and 50. Those with a family history of this disease should start earlier. For those who already have colon cancer and have completed surgery and chemotherapy, see Section 16, Item 14 regarding exercise (After surgery and chemotherapy for colon cancer).

entries.title: People with cardiovascular disease and older adults should receive an annual influenza vaccine
entries.cost: One shot costs 50 to 150 yuan. Get it once every autumn.
entries.summary: In the trial of influenza vaccination after myocardial infarction, the proportion of deaths within one year dropped from 4.9% to 2.9%. People with cardiovascular disease and older adults should get a booster shot every autumn, costing 50 to 150 yuan.
entries.benefit: A trial conducted after myocardial infarction randomized 2,571 people. Neither doctors nor patients knew which shot was administered. Among those who received the influenza vaccine, all-cause mortality over 12 months was 2.9%. Among those receiving placebo, it was 4.9%. Original value HR 0.59, confidence interval 95% CI 0.39 to 0.89. Placebo is a control injection containing no active ingredients. The HR for cardiovascular death was 0.59. Another study pooled multiple studies together. Major cardiovascular events occurred in 3.6% of those receiving the influenza vaccine versus 5.4% in controls. Original value RR 0.66, confidence interval 95% CI 0.53 to 0.83. Cardiovascular death RR 0.74 (95% CI 0.42 to 1.30; this difference remains within the margin of error and cannot be considered statistically significant).
entries.sources: Fröbert O et al. (2021). Influenza Vaccination After Myocardial Infarction: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Multicenter Trial. Circulation. <https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.121.057042> ; Behrouzi B et al. (2022). Association of Influenza Vaccination With Cardiovascular Risk: A Meta-analysis. JAMA Network Open. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2022.8873>; Demicheli V et al. (2018). Vaccines for preventing influenza in the elderly. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD004876.pub4> (The Cochrane review mentioned in the notes)
entries.notes: Controversy. Grade A applies only to people with cardiovascular disease. For otherwise healthy older adults, the Cochrane review could only draw one conclusion: one-season influenza incidence fell from 6% to 2.4%. It rated the certainty of this evidence as “low,” and the evidence regarding mortality as “very low.” The source of the review is that 2018 paper by Demicheli V et al. For pregnant women, see Section 27, Item 18 (Inactivated influenza vaccine during pregnancy); for COPD patients, see Section 16, Item 12 (Inhalers for COPD).

entries.title: Get the shingles vaccine after age 50
entries.cost: The recombinant shingles vaccine requires two doses, totaling about 3,000 to 4,000 yuan. This amount is paid entirely out-of-pocket.
entries.summary: In phase III clinical trials, this vaccine prevented 97% of shingles cases, with similar results across all age groups. The downside is that the two doses cost three to four thousand yuan entirely out-of-pocket. What this money buys back is a 97% reduction in incidence.
entries.benefit: A phase 3 trial spanning 18 countries included 15,400 people. Participants were randomly divided into two groups: one received the vaccine and the other a control injection. They were followed for an average of 3.2 years. Shingles occurred in 6 people in the vaccine group and 210 in the placebo group. That works out to 0.3 versus 9.1 cases per 1,000 person-years; 1,000 person-years means the number of cases observed among 1,000 people over one year. The paper states: “Overall vaccine efficacy against herpes zoster was 97.2% (95% CI 93.7–99.0, P<0.001).” Efficacy across the age groups ranged from 96.6% to 97.9%. During the 7 days after injection, reactions at the injection site and throughout the body were more common in the vaccine group. Grade 3 symptoms (the most severe category) were reported by 17.0% of the vaccine group and 3.2% of the placebo group. Rates of serious adverse events and death were similar in the two groups.
entries.sources: Lal H, Cunningham AL, Godeaux O, et al. (2015). Efficacy of an adjuvanted herpes zoster subunit vaccine in older adults. New England Journal of Medicine, 372(22), 2087-2096：「There were solicited or unsolicited reports of grade 3 symptoms in 17.0% of vaccine recipients and 3.2% of placebo recipients. The proportions of participants who had serious adverse events or potential immune-mediated diseases or who died were similar in the two groups.」<https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1501184>
entries.notes: Its value for money is not particularly good because it is expensive. Shingles itself is rarely fatal; the real trouble is postherpetic neuralgia, which can cause pain for months to years. During the week after vaccination, reactions at the injection site and throughout the body were more common than after a placebo injection. The most severe category (grade 3 symptoms) was reported by 17.0% versus 3.2%; serious adverse events were similar in the two groups.

entries.title: Get a pneumococcal vaccine if you are over 65
entries.cost: Several hundred yuan. It is free for older adults in some areas.
entries.summary: In a trial of 84,500 older adults, the 13-valent pneumococcal vaccine prevented about 46% of pneumonia caused by the types covered by the vaccine. It prevented 75% of the most dangerous invasive infections. But it showed no effect against “pneumonia from all causes,” so do not expect it to prevent every kind of pneumonia.
entries.benefit: In the Netherlands, 84,500 people over 65 were randomly divided into two groups for comparison. The trial used the 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine. Its efficacy against pneumonia caused by vaccine-covered types was 45.6%. The confidence interval was 95.2% CI 21.8–62.5. “Vaccine-covered types” means the bacterial types this vaccine protects against. Its efficacy against invasive pneumococcal disease was 75.0% (95% CI 41.4–90.8); this is the most dangerous category of infection. It had no effect against pneumonia from all causes combined.
entries.sources: Bonten MJ, Huijts SM, Bolkenbaas M, et al. (2015). Polysaccharide conjugate vaccine against pneumococcal pneumonia in adults. New England Journal of Medicine, 372(12), 1114-1125. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1408544>
entries.notes: It protects only against the types covered by the vaccine; getting vaccinated does not mean you cannot get pneumonia. Older adults in China commonly receive the 23-valent polysaccharide vaccine, which is different from the 13-valent conjugate vaccine used in this trial. The efficacy figures above cannot be applied directly to it.

entries.title: Test for Helicobacter pylori and eradicate it if you test positive
entries.cost: A carbon-13 or carbon-14 breath test costs 100 to 200 yuan. Eradication requires taking four medicines together; a two-week course costs 200 to 500 yuan. The hard part is taking every dose on schedule for the full two weeks.
entries.summary: In a trial in Linqu, Shandong, that followed people for 22 years, those who had Helicobacter pylori eradicated were about half as likely to develop stomach cancer later. They were about 40% less likely to die from stomach cancer. A test costs 100 to 200 yuan, and eradication requires two weeks of medication.
entries.benefit: The randomized trial in Linqu, Shandong, followed participants for 22 years. People who received treatment to eradicate Helicobacter pylori had about half the risk of developing stomach cancer. The original figure was OR 0.48, with a 95% CI of 0.32 to 0.71. Their risk of dying from stomach cancer was about 38% lower (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.39 to 0.99).
entries.sources: Li WQ et al. (2019). Effects of Helicobacter pylori treatment and vitamin and garlic supplementation on gastric cancer incidence and mortality: follow-up of a randomized intervention trial. BMJ. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.l5016>
entries.notes: Reinfection is still possible after eradication, so have everyone in the household tested and treated together. The participants in this trial lived in an area with a high incidence of stomach cancer. People living in areas with a low incidence will gain much less benefit in practice. Eradication does not replace gastroscopy; if you are over 45 and at high risk, see item 47 (get screened with gastroscopy).

entries.title: If you are a heavy smoker, get a low-dose chest CT once a year
entries.cost: Each scan costs 200 to 400 yuan and takes 10 minutes. Also account for the follow-up examinations after a false alarm and the anxiety during that period.
entries.summary: For heavy smokers who meet the criteria, having a low-dose CT once a year lowers the chance of dying from lung cancer by 20% compared with having chest X-rays alone. The overall chance of dying is 6.7% lower. The costs include follow-up examinations after a suspicious result and the anxiety during that time.
entries.benefit: The US NLST randomized trial enrolled 53,454 people, all aged 55 to 74, with a smoking history of at least 30 pack-years, who had quit no more than 15 years earlier. A pack-year is a measure of smoking: smoking one pack a day for one year equals one pack-year. The results were as follows. Compared with people who received only chest X-rays, those who received low-dose CT had a 20.0% relative reduction in lung cancer deaths. The 95% CI was 6.8 to 26.7. Overall mortality fell by 6.7% in relative terms, with a 95% CI of 1.2 to 13.6. Each person was screened for three consecutive years. Across the three rounds, 24.2% of low-dose CT results were suspicious. Of those suspicious results, 96.4% were false alarms (false positives).
entries.sources: National Lung Screening Trial Research Team (2011). Reduced Lung-Cancer Mortality with Low-Dose Computed Tomographic Screening. New England Journal of Medicine：「The rate of positive screening tests was 24.2% with low-dose CT and 6.9% with radiography over all three rounds. A total of 96.4% of the positive screening results in the low-dose CT group and 94.5% in the radiography group were false positive results.」<https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1102873>
entries.notes: This item applies only to smokers at high risk. In the same trial, 24.2% of results from the three rounds of low-dose CT were suspicious, and 96.4% of those were false alarms (false positives). People who did not smoke were not included in this trial, so it cannot tell us whether screening benefits them.

entries.title: If you are depressed or have suicidal thoughts, call China’s 12356 hotline; do not keep sleeping pills or pesticides at home
entries.cost: Free. Make one phone call. Also lock up medications and keep pesticides out of the home.
entries.summary: The evidence for keeping potentially lethal things out of reach has continued to grow stronger. After access to painkillers was restricted, related suicides fell by 43%; after barriers were installed at places where people often jumped, they fell by 86%. So do not keep sleeping pills or pesticides at home. When you feel you might take your own life, first call 12356. The number works throughout China and is available for at least 18 hours each day.
entries.benefit: A systematic review of research from nearly 10 years found that evidence for restricting access to lethal means has continued to grow stronger. After access to painkillers was controlled, suicides involving painkillers fell by 43%. After barriers were added at places where people often jumped, suicides there fell by 86% (79% to 91%; the range in parentheses is the confidence interval for that figure). Cognitive programs in schools reduced suicide attempts by about 55% (OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.24 to 0.85). Medication for depression and psychological therapy are important parts of suicide prevention. In China, from May 1, 2025, dialing 12356 anywhere in the country connects callers to a mental health assistance hotline, available for no less than 18 hours each day.
entries.sources: Zalsman G et al. (2016). Suicide prevention strategies revisited: 10-year systematic review. Lancet Psychiatry. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S2215-0366(16)30030-X> ; National Health Commission of China (2024). Notice on the use of “12356” as the nationally unified telephone number for mental health assistance hotlines (National Health Commission Medical Administration Letter〔2024〕No. 259). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202412/content_6994470.htm>
entries.notes: Why this receives a B: most of the evidence on restricting access to lethal means comes from ecological studies, which compare figures before and after policies were introduced. There is no evidence that the hotline itself reduces mortality. Suicidal impulses often last only a few minutes to a few hours; moving lethal things farther away is itself an intervention. For data on this time scale and long-term outcomes after a suicide attempt, see item 32 in this section (tell someone close to you as soon as suicidal thoughts arise). For what may happen after someone is rescued, see item 33 in this section.

entries.title: Equip your home with a fire extinguisher, fire blanket, escape respirator and first-aid kit, and check them once a year
entries.cost: A fire extinguisher, a fire blanket, one respirator per person and a first-aid kit cost several hundred yuan altogether. Buy them once, then spend ten minutes checking them each year.
entries.summary: A fire extinguisher, fire blanket, escape respirator and first-aid kit all appear on the Ministry of Emergency Management of China’s 11-item household emergency supplies list. A set costs several hundred yuan and only needs to be bought once. In studies where people received home visits offering household safety guidance, the rate of injuries was about one-quarter lower.
entries.benefit: The Ministry of Emergency Management of China’s National Basic Recommended List of Household Emergency Supplies contains 11 items. Among them, “fire extinguishers and fire blankets” are for “putting out fires in their early stages”; the list also states that “a fire blanket can be draped over the body for escape.” “Respirator” means a “fire-filtering self-rescue respirator, for use when escaping a fire.” “Medicines for external use” means “hemostatic powder, hemostatic dressings, gauze bandages and similar items, for treating wounds.” Cochrane pooled 98 studies involving 2,605,044 people. Household safety interventions reduced the injury rate to an IRR of 0.89. The 95% CI was 0.78 to 1.01. Among interventions delivered through home visits, the injury rate was about 25% lower (IRR 0.75, 95% CI 0.62 to 0.91).
entries.sources: Ministry of Emergency Management of China (2020). National Basic Recommended List of Household Emergency Supplies. <https://www.mem.gov.cn/kp/shaq/202011/t20201129_372149.shtml> ; Kendrick D et al. (2012). Home safety education and provision of safety equipment for injury prevention. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD005014.pub3> ; Wusheng County Market Supervision Administration (2025). Consumer advice on portable fire extinguishers, fire doors (windows), and point-type heat (smoke) fire detectors. <https://www.wusheng.gov.cn/gasylbzj/c109568/zzzq/content/content_1988424970198126592.html> ; Guizhou Provincial Fire and Rescue Corps (2025). Fire blankets for every home: a complete guide to their functions and use (reposted from Beijing Fire and Rescue). <https://gz.119.gov.cn/xfkp/xfcs/202503/t20250313_87157898.html> ; NVWA (2014). Blusdekens oktober 2014 (inspection report by the Netherlands Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority; the original page is no longer online, and the link is to a web archive from October 20, 2021). <https://web.archive.org/web/20211020154732/https://www.nvwa.nl/binaries/nvwa/documenten/consument/consumentenartikelen/non-food/overige-non-food/blusdekens-oktober-2014/Factsheet+Blusdekens+Oktober+2014.pdf>
entries.notes: Contested. In the same Cochrane review, the category of interventions that did not provide equipment had an injury rate about 20% lower. The original figure was IRR 0.78, with a 95% CI of 0.66 to 0.92. The group given equipment did not do better. Most of the reduction in injuries came from education during home visits and changes to the home, so the benefit of the equipment is rated “moderate,” not “large.” When buying a fire extinguisher, look for the CCC mark; on a stored-pressure extinguisher, the gauge needle should be in the green zone. Most fire blankets are made of fiberglass. Hold only the two pull straps; do not touch the blanket’s surface with bare hands. Using a fire blanket to cover a burning pan of oil is also disputed: in 2014, a Dutch regulator tested 22 brands, and none reliably put out the fire when used as an ordinary person would use it. If a pan of oil catches fire, turn off the heat first and put a lid on the pan. For smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms, see item 3 in this section. For how to use a tourniquet, see section 13, item 12. For how to choose each item, where to keep it and how often to replace it, see [docs/Household Emergency Equipment Checklist.md](../docs/家庭应急装备清单.md).

entries.title: If you see blood in your urine, get it checked even if it does not hurt and even if your urine looks clear the next day
entries.cost: A routine urine test costs a few dozen yuan, and a urinary tract ultrasound costs 100 to 200 yuan. If the doctor thinks it is needed, a cystoscopy costs around 1,000 yuan more.
entries.summary: In British outpatient records, about 2.8% of people over 60 who had visible blood in their urine were eventually diagnosed with bladder cancer. For those aged 40 to 59, the figure was about 1.2%. Those figures are not high, but they are high enough that you must get checked. Even if it happened only once, involved very little blood and did not hurt, get it checked.
