entries.benefit: A British study used electronic records from community general practices (primary care), comparing 4,915 bladder cancer cases with 21,718 controls. Among people with visible blood in their urine, the proportions eventually found to have bladder cancer were as follows. For people over 60, it was 2.8%, with a 95% CI of 2.5 to 3.1. For people aged 40 to 59, it was 1.2%, with a confidence interval of 0.6 to 2.3. The technical name for this proportion is positive predictive value. Blood in the urine that is visible only under a microscope also matters. The odds ratio was 20, with a 95% CI of 12 to 33. For people over 60, the proportion was 1.6%, with a confidence interval of 1.2 to 2.1. The UK National Health Service (NHS) says blood in the urine can be a sign of cancer and must be checked. Even if you have no other symptoms, it is the first time it has happened or there is very little blood, make an appointment with a doctor promptly.
entries.sources: Price SJ, Shephard EA, Stapley SA, Barraclough K, Hamilton WT (2014). Non-visible versus visible haematuria and bladder cancer risk: a study of electronic records in primary care. British Journal of General Practice, 64(626), e584-e589. <https://doi.org/10.3399/bjgp14X681409>；NHS. Blood in urine：「Blood in your pee must be checked out because it can be a sign of cancer.」「But do not self-diagnose.」「It may not be blood in your pee if: you've recently eaten beetroot … you're taking a new medicine … it's happening during your period」. <https://www.nhs.uk/symptoms/blood-in-urine/>；NHS. Symptoms of bladder cancer：「You have blood in your pee, even if: you do not have any other symptoms; it's the first time it's happened; there's only a small amount of blood; you're not sure if it's blood」. <https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/bladder-cancer/symptoms/>
entries.notes: Lack of pain is no reason to ignore it. The UK National Health Service (NHS) says to make an appointment with a doctor promptly if there is blood in your urine, even if you have no other symptoms, it is the first time, there is very little or you are unsure whether it is blood. Pain when urinating, frequent urination and fever may indicate a urinary tract infection. Waves of severe pain from the side of the lower back to the groin, along with an inability to sit still, may indicate a stone. But the NHS also says not to draw your own conclusion: let a doctor assess it. Redness seen during menstruation, after eating beetroot or after starting a new medicine may not be blood in the urine. If you are taking anticoagulants, do not assume on your own that the medication caused it. That is the author’s advice; the studies above did not calculate results separately for these people. The benefit is rated “small” because there are detection rates but no effect size for “how much earlier testing reduces deaths.”

entries.title: If you have trouble with erections, get your cardiovascular health checked first; do not treat it as merely “a problem in the bedroom”
entries.cost: A doctor’s appointment costs a few dozen yuan. A blood pressure measurement and blood tests for glucose and lipids cost 100 to 200 yuan. It takes one trip to the hospital and a few days’ wait for the results.
entries.summary: Men with erectile dysfunction are about 40% more likely than other men to develop cardiovascular disease later and about 60% more likely to have a heart attack. The difference is greater at younger ages. So get your blood pressure, blood glucose and blood lipids checked first; do not just buy medication on your own to mask the problem.
entries.benefit: A meta-analysis pooled 14 follow-up studies involving 92,757 men, with an average follow-up of 6.1 years. Compared with men without erectile dysfunction, men with the condition had the following subsequent risks. Overall cardiovascular events were about 44% higher (RR 1.44, 95% CI 1.27 to 1.63; this is the confidence interval). Heart attacks were about 62% higher (RR 1.62, 1.34 to 1.96). Cerebrovascular events were about 39% higher (RR 1.39, 1.23 to 1.57). Death from any cause was about 25% higher (RR 1.25, 1.12 to 1.39). There was no clear difference in cardiovascular deaths (RR 1.19, 0.97 to 1.46). The younger the men, the higher the risk ratio. The ratio was higher among men whose underlying cardiovascular risk was moderate than among those at either high or low risk. Studies that identified erectile dysfunction using questionnaires calculated a ratio of 1.61 (1.38 to 1.86). Studies that asked a single question calculated 1.27 (1.18 to 1.37).
entries.sources: Vlachopoulos CV, Terentes-Printzios DG, Ioakeimidis NK, Aznaouridis KA, Stefanadis CI (2013). Prediction of cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality with erectile dysfunction: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies. Circulation: Cardiovascular Quality and Outcomes, 6(1), 99-109. <https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCOUTCOMES.112.966903>; DailyMed (the US National Library of Medicine’s drug labeling database). VIAGRA (sildenafil citrate) tablet, CONTRAINDICATIONS. <https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/lookup.cfm?setid=d905dc8d-917f-4ea3-a4ee-a1ecf6967d4e>; NHS. Erectile dysfunction (impotence): “Most men occasionally fail to get or keep an erection. This is usually caused by stress, tiredness or drinking too much alcohol, and it's nothing to worry about.” “See a GP or go to a sexual health clinic if: erection problems keep happening”. <https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/erection-problems-erectile-dysfunction/>
entries.notes: These 14 studies all followed groups of people and observed the outcomes; they were not randomized trials. So “40% higher” is an association, not evidence of causation. The UK National Health Service (NHS) says most men occasionally cannot get an erection, often because they are tired, stressed, or have drunk too much, and there is no need to worry. See a doctor if it keeps happening. The checks are the same ones discussed in items 7 and 8 of this section: measure blood pressure and check fasting blood glucose, along with blood lipids, smoking status, and waist circumference. Do not buy “male enhancement” supplements online. Legitimate medications of this kind are prescription drugs. Their prescribing information lists nitrates as a contraindication: people taking medicines such as nitroglycerin must not take them, because combining them can cause a sudden drop in blood pressure. For ways to improve erectile function, see item 29 of this section (losing weight and quitting smoking can improve it). The benefit is rated “medium,” not “large”: 44% is the difference in risk between two groups, not a measure of “how much one checkup reduces deaths.” It is not rated “small,” either: the signal in item 27 of this section (blood in the urine visible to the naked eye) comes with only a detection rate. There are established treatments for the high blood pressure, diabetes, and abnormal blood lipids found through these checks.

entries.title: Lose weight, quit smoking, and control blood pressure and blood glucose; erectile function can improve too
entries.cost: It costs nothing and may even save money. The hard part is sticking with it long term: managing what you eat, getting active, and quitting smoking.
entries.summary: Managing cardiovascular risk factors can improve erectile function itself. On a questionnaire, scores rise by an average of 2 to 3 points. The questionnaire has a maximum score of 25, and a score above 22 is considered normal.
entries.benefit: A meta-analysis combined 6 randomized controlled trials involving 740 men. The interventions were lifestyle changes or medication to control cardiovascular risk factors, with follow-up lasting at least 6 weeks. The result: scores on an erectile function questionnaire (IIEF-5) improved by an average of 2.66 points (95% CI 1.86 to 3.47, the confidence interval). After excluding the 2 trials that used statins (143 people), the remaining 4 trials relying solely on lifestyle changes (597 people) still showed an improvement of 2.40 points (1.19 to 3.61). The IIEF-5 is a five-question questionnaire with a total score ranging from 5 to 25. The original paper divides scores into five categories: 22 to 25 means no dysfunction, while 5 to 7 means severe dysfunction
entries.sources: Gupta BP, Murad MH, Clifton MM, Prokop L, Nehra A, Kopecky SL (2011). The effect of lifestyle modification and cardiovascular risk factor reduction on erectile dysfunction: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Archives of Internal Medicine, 171(20), 1797-1803. <https://doi.org/10.1001/archinternmed.2011.440>; Rosen RC, Cappelleri JC, Smith MD, Lipsky J, Peña BM (1999). Development and evaluation of an abridged, 5-item version of the International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF-5) as a diagnostic tool for erectile dysfunction. International Journal of Impotence Research, 11(6), 319-326. <https://doi.org/10.1038/sj.ijir.3900472>; China Food and Drug Administration (2016). CFDA: Beware of the illegal addition of “sildenafil” to some products: “Driven by profit, criminals have mixed sildenafil, the main ingredient of ‘Viagra,’ into corn flour to produce large quantities of illegal products claiming to enhance sexual performance”; “China has never approved the registration of any health food that ‘improves male sexual function’”; “Using sildenafil without a doctor’s guidance poses a serious threat to users’ health and lives.” <http://app.www.gov.cn/govdata/gov/201605/16/380625/article.html>
entries.notes: The interventions in these 6 trials differed: some combined weight loss and exercise, while others used medication to control blood pressure and blood lipids. There were only 740 people in total. So the direction of the effect is clear, but the size of the improvement varies from person to person. The benefit is rated “small” because the only endpoint is a questionnaire score; there is no figure for “how many fewer people later developed a disease.” These same actions have hard endpoints elsewhere. For quitting smoking, see section 2, item 1 (quit smoking; the earlier, the better). For weight loss, see section 2, item 32 (keep BMI between 20 and 25). For blood pressure, see item 7 of this section (measure your blood pressure and take medication if it is high). Medication itself is not off limits, provided it is prescribed by a doctor. In 2016, the former China Food and Drug Administration warned that China had never approved a health food that could “improve male sexual function.” Criminals have mixed sildenafil, an ingredient in this type of medication, into illegal products claiming to enhance sexual performance. Taking it without a doctor’s guidance can endanger health and life. For how to assess supplements sold online, see section 28, item 4 (do not buy weight-loss drugs that promise rapid results).

entries.title: Use a condom from start to finish every time you have sex, and do not share needles or other injection equipment
entries.cost: One condom costs one or two yuan. The hard part is not the money; it is using one every time and putting it on from the start.
entries.summary: Wearing a condom from start to finish every time reduces the risk of HIV transmission between heterosexual partners by roughly 70% or more. Using one “most of the time” makes little difference compared with not using one. Condoms also protect against other sexually transmitted infections, but they cannot prevent transmission of syphilis or herpes from areas the condom does not cover.
entries.benefit: One analysis combined 25 studies involving 10,676 heterosexual couples. In each couple, one partner had HIV and the other did not, a situation called serodiscordance. Compared with people who never used condoms, those who used them every time had about a 71% lower risk of HIV transmission. The original value was RR 0.29, with a 95% CI of 0.20 to 0.43. Compared with people who used condoms inconsistently, their risk was about 77% lower (RR 0.23, 95% CI 0.13 to 0.40). The authors concluded that, although condoms are not perfect, “consistent use can reduce HIV transmission by more than 70%.” The World Health Organization says using condoms correctly and consistently is one of the most effective ways to prevent sexually transmitted infections, including HIV. But condoms cannot protect against ulcers in areas they do not cover, such as those caused by syphilis or genital herpes
entries.sources: Giannou FK, Tsiara CG, Nikolopoulos GK, et al. (2016). Condom effectiveness in reducing heterosexual HIV transmission: a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies on HIV serodiscordant couples. Expert Review of Pharmacoeconomics & Outcomes Research, 16(4), 489-499. <https://doi.org/10.1586/14737167.2016.1102635>; Fonner VA et al. (2016). Effectiveness and safety of oral HIV preexposure prophylaxis for all populations. AIDS. <https://doi.org/10.1097/QAD.0000000000001145> (pre-exposure prophylaxis, PrEP); WHO (2025). Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) fact sheet: “When used correctly and consistently, condoms offer one of the most effective methods of protection against STIs, including HIV. Although highly effective, condoms do not offer protection for STIs that cause extra-genital ulcers (i.e., syphilis or genital herpes).” <https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/sexually-transmitted-infections-(stis>)
entries.notes: The difference between “inconsistent use” and “no use” is small. A condom needs to be used every time, from start to finish, to be effective. Sharing needles or other injection equipment is another, separate, efficient route of transmission unrelated to sex; injecting drugs, tattooing, and piercing all count. People at high risk can also use pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), which means taking medication in advance to prevent infection. In an analysis combining 18 studies, in trials where more than 70% of participants took their medication on schedule, people taking PrEP had about a 70% lower risk of HIV infection than those taking a placebo. The original risk ratio was 0.30, with a 95% CI of 0.21 to 0.45. Trials with fewer people taking the medication on schedule showed no protective effect. PrEP is a prescription medication. Ask an infectious diseases department or a disease control center; do not buy it online yourself. For what to do after a possible exposure, see section 13

entries.title: Get an HIV test after a high-risk exposure; testing at designated disease control centers in China is free and the results are confidential
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Make a trip to a disease control center or designated medical institution and give a blood sample. The hard part is taking the step of asking for the test.
entries.summary: An HIV test at a designated disease control center in China costs nothing. Without your consent, no organization or individual may disclose your name, address, workplace, or medical history. A positive result is not a death sentence: people who keep taking medication until the virus is undetectable do not transmit it to their sexual partners. In the study, there was not a single transmission between partners in that situation.
entries.benefit: Article 23 of China’s Regulations on AIDS Prevention and Treatment states that the health authorities of local people’s governments at or above the county level designate certain medical and health institutions. These institutions “shall provide free counseling and preliminary screening tests to people who voluntarily seek AIDS counseling and testing.” The point of testing early is not merely psychological reassurance: current antiretroviral treatment can suppress the virus to undetectable levels. The World Health Organization’s position is that “people living with HIV who are receiving antiretroviral treatment and have an undetectable viral load do not transmit HIV to their sexual partners.” The PARTNER study followed 782 male same-sex couples in which one partner had HIV and the other did not, a situation called serodiscordance. Follow-up totaled 1,593 couple-years (the years of follow-up for each couple added together). During that period, there were 76,088 instances of condomless sex and 15 new infections. After comparing the viruses’ genes through phylogenetic analysis, the researchers found that none of the 15 infections came from the partner: transmission between partners was zero. Article 39 of China’s Regulations on AIDS Prevention and Treatment provides: “Without the consent of the person concerned or their guardian, no organization or individual may disclose the name, address, workplace, likeness, medical history, or any other information that could reveal the specific identity of a person infected with HIV, a person with AIDS, or a member of their family.”
entries.sources: State Council of China (2006). Regulations on AIDS Prevention and Treatment (Articles 3, 23, 38, and 39). <https://wjw.beijing.gov.cn/zwgk_20040/zcwj2022/flfg/202304/t20230408_2992986.html> (reposted by the Beijing Municipal Health Commission); Rodger AJ, Cambiano V, Bruun T, et al. (2019). Risk of HIV transmission through condomless sex in serodifferent gay couples with the HIV-positive partner taking suppressive antiretroviral therapy (PARTNER): final results of a multicentre, prospective, observational study. The Lancet, 393(10189), 2428-2438. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(19>)30418-0; Guangdong Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention. Explainer on the HIV testing window period. <https://web.archive.org/web/20260915151957/https://cdcp.gd.gov.cn/jkjy/kpydjwjxz/content/post_3441820.html> (source for the window-period figures; the original page has been taken down, and the link points to a web archive dated 2026-09-15)
entries.notes: The window period determines when a test result is meaningful. According to the Guangdong Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention, nucleic acid tests can detect infection after about 1 week, fourth-generation combined antigen-antibody tests after about 2 weeks, and third-generation antibody tests after about 3 weeks. Testing is recommended at least 2 weeks after exposure, with a repeat test 2 to 4 weeks later. More than 99.99% of infections can be ruled out 3 months after the last high-risk exposure. A positive self-test result is not a confirmed diagnosis; it must be checked at a disease control center or a legitimate institution. Article 3 of the Regulations states that no organization or individual may discriminate against people with HIV or their families, and that their rights concerning marriage, employment, medical care, school admission, and other matters are protected by Chinese law. Article 38 also requires people with HIV to “promptly inform those with whom they have sexual relations of their infection or illness.” For screening for three diseases during pregnancy and prevention of mother-to-child transmission, see section 27

entries.title: As soon as suicidal thoughts arise, tell someone close to you and let them help you through the next several dozen minutes
entries.cost: It costs nothing. The hard part is speaking up at the time and accepting that you cannot be alone for the next few hours.
entries.summary: In one interview study, nearly half of the people who had attempted suicide said no more than 10 minutes passed between their first suicidal thought and the attempt. Three-quarters had contact with someone close to them during that time. Among people who had been to hospital after self-harm, about 2% had died by suicide after 1 year and about 7% after more than 9 years; the vast majority did not subsequently die by suicide.
entries.benefit: Eighty-two people who had attempted suicide were interviewed within 3 days of admission to hospital: 47.6% (39 people) said no more than 10 minutes passed between the first suicidal thought in that episode and the act itself. Those for whom the process took longer had significantly higher scores for suicidal intent. Scores on an impulsivity scale were unrelated to how long the process took. Some 76.8% (63 people) said they had some contact with a partner, family member, or friend during that time. The authors concluded that the window for intervention is usually very short, leaving professionals limited opportunity to intervene at that stage. They therefore argued for teaching ordinary people how to recognize warning signs and intervene. Another systematic review brought together 90 follow-up studies. Among people who sought medical care after self-harm, the median proportion who harmed themselves again without dying within 1 year was 16%. The proportion who died by suicide within 1 year was 2%. Among those followed for more than 9 years, about 7% died by suicide
entries.sources: Deisenhammer EA, Ing CM, Strauss R, Kemmler G, Hinterhuber H, Weiss EM (2009). The duration of the suicidal process: how much time is left for intervention between consideration and accomplishment of a suicide attempt? Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, 70(1), 19-24. <https://doi.org/10.4088/JCP.07m03904>；Owens D, Horrocks J, House A (2002). Fatal and non-fatal repetition of self-harm: systematic review. British Journal of Psychiatry, 181, 193-199. <https://doi.org/10.1192/bjp.181.3.193>
entries.notes: Why the evidence is rated B: Deisenhammer’s study included only 82 people at one hospital and relied on their recollections afterward. Owens’s review reports the median proportion across 90 studies that used different methods; it does not combine them into a single estimate. The same review also states explicitly that the risk of suicide among people who have self-harmed remains hundreds of times that of the general population. So “the vast majority did not subsequently die by suicide” describes this group as a whole. It cannot be taken as a guarantee for any one person, and needed medical care is still needed. For moving lethal means out of reach and China’s 12356 hotline, see item 25 of this section. For several first steps to take when you feel low, see section 3, item 18. For lasting effects after someone is saved, see item 33 of this section. If you suspect someone close to you has these thoughts, you can ask directly; see item 43 of this section (ask someone close to you directly if their emotional state seems wrong). For what you can do when someone close to you expresses these thoughts, see section 8, item 15

entries.title: Do not assume that being “saved” is a safety net: after pesticide ingestion or carbon monoxide poisoning, emergency care may save a life but may not save the lungs or brain
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Just know this in advance.
entries.summary: Paraquat has no effective antidote, and more than 40% of one group of patients in Bangladesh did not survive. It causes lung inflammation and gradual scarring; the kidneys and liver are injured too. Among people rescued after carbon monoxide poisoning who received only ordinary oxygen, nearly half had impaired brain function six weeks later. Even among those who received hyperbaric oxygen, one-quarter still did.
entries.benefit: A systematic review on paraquat poisoning: The case fatality rate is extremely high, because it is inherently highly toxic and lacks effective treatment. It is actively transported into lung tissue against a concentration gradient—scientifically termed active uptake against a concentration gradient—resulting in pneumonitis and pulmonary fibrosis. It also causes renal injury and hepatic injury simultaneously. The review explicitly states: Gastric lavage should not be performed. Hemodialysis and hemoperfusion are unlikely to change the clinical course. The evidence for the efficacy of corticosteroids and immunosuppressants is very weak. The review also noted a sentence: "The mortality rate in all centres was high despite widespread variations in treatment." Ten tertiary hospitals in Bangladesh admitted 1,420 cases from 2013 to 2024, of which 257 analyzable cases had a case fatality rate of 43.2%. Common manifestations were lower limb edema caused by acute renal failure at 71.2%, vomiting at 65.8%, and abdominal pain at 58.0%. The trial on acute carbon monoxide poisoning was a double-blind randomized controlled trial, with 76 people in each of the two groups. Neither the doctors nor the patients knew which group they were assigned to. At six weeks, among those with cognitive sequelae, there were 19/76 (25.0%) in the hyperbaric oxygen group. In the normobaric oxygen group, it was 35/76 (46.1%), P=0.007. After adjusting for other factors, OR was 0.45 (95% CI 0.22 to 0.92; the parentheses contain the confidence interval of this number). Another study observed 73 consecutive cases: 30% had cognitive sequelae, and 12% developed white matter hyperintensities. China revoked the registration and production licenses for paraquat aqueous solutions starting July 1, 2014, and halted production. Starting July 1, 2016, the sale and use of aqueous solutions were halted domestically. Starting September 26, 2020, the sale and use of soluble gel formulations were prohibited within the country. Official documents state that "causing suicides from ingesting paraquat to occur from time to time" was the direct reason for strengthening regulation.
entries.sources: Gawarammana IB, Buckley NA (2011). Medical management of paraquat ingestion. British Journal of Clinical Pharmacology, 72(5), 745-757. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-2125.2011.04026.x>; Chowdhury FR et al. (2026). Clinical and Laboratory Profile of Paraquat Poisoning: A Toxicological Crisis in Bangladesh. American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene, 115, 176-182. <https://doi.org/10.4269/ajtmh.25-0719>; Weaver LK, Hopkins RO, Chan KJ, et al. (2002). Hyperbaric oxygen for acute carbon monoxide poisoning. New England Journal of Medicine, 347(14), 1057-1067. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa013121>; Parkinson RB, Hopkins RO, Cleavinger HB, et al. (2002). White matter hyperintensities and neuropsychological outcome following carbon monoxide poisoning. Neurology, 58(10), 1525-1532. <https://doi.org/10.1212/wnl.58.10.1525>; General Office of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs (2018). Circular on Earnestly Strengthening the Supervision and Administration of Paraquat (Nong Ban Nong [2018] No. 17). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2018-12/31/content_5442594.htm>
entries.notes: Reason for giving a B rating: The subjects of these studies were poisoned patients, not exclusively a suicide attempt population; the carbon monoxide trial also included accidental poisonings. Therefore, the sequelae proportions above cannot be directly equated with the "probability of outcomes for suicide attempters." Only one thing can be confirmed: no method can guarantee that it leaves no sequelae. For on-site management of carbon monoxide, see Section 13, Item 19. If pesticides or medications are ingested by mistake, do not induce vomiting first, and bring the bottle to the hospital; see Section 13, Item 20. For not hoarding pesticides and sleeping pills at home, see Item 25 of this section. This book does not compare the lethality rates of different methods, nor does it describe any specific methods.

entries.title: Don't Gamble on Falling from a Height Thinking You'll "Just Lie Down for a Few Days and Recover": Most People Admitted to the Trauma ICU Survive, but the Cost is Measured in Years
entries.cost: Costs no money. It is just about seeing this ledger clearly beforehand.
entries.summary: In a hospital in Xinjiang, among people who fell from a height and were admitted to the trauma ICU, only 5.5% died, but injuries were severe and treatment was prolonged. Nearly half sustained simultaneous injuries to three or more body regions, more than one-third were placed on a ventilator, and the longest ICU stay was 132 days. For half of the people, the fall height did not exceed 3 meters. Among those severely injured, fewer than 60% were later able to return to work.
entries.benefit: A trauma ICU (Intensive Care Unit) in southern Xinjiang compiled statistics. From April 2020 to July 2024, a total of 289 cases of falls from a height were admitted here. The average age of this cohort was 40.3 years. The median fall height was 3 meters; 26.6% fell from over 5 meters, and 11.4% fell from over 10 meters. The median Injury Severity Score (ISS) was 24; the higher this score, the more severe the injury, with 63.3% of patients having an ISS greater than 20. 47.1% had injuries involving 3 or more anatomical sites, and 18.3% involved 4 or more. 36% required mechanical ventilation, with a median ventilation duration of 103.5 hours. The median length of ICU stay was 8 days, ranging from a minimum of 1 day to a maximum of 132 days. In-hospital or 30-day mortality was 5.5% (16/289). A trauma center in Germany admitted 84 polytrauma patients with ISS ≥ 25; polytrauma refers to simultaneous injuries to multiple anatomical regions. The proportion returning to work during the follow-up period was 58%. Age, duration of ICU treatment, and self-rated health were predictive factors. In 2024, the nationwide average inpatient expenditure per hospitalization (average cost spent per hospital admission) in China was 9,870.0 yuan, a decrease of 4.3% compared to the previous year at current prices. In the same year, total national health expenditure was 9,089.55 billion yuan, of which personal out-of-pocket health expenditure was 2,500.75 billion yuan, accounting for 27.5%.
entries.sources: Chen Y, Li W, Wang X, Zhong Q, Abudurexiti A, Qiu Q, Li J, Luo J (2025). Clinical features and prognostic predictors for patients admitted to trauma intensive care unit due to fall from height in South Xinjiang. International Journal of Emergency Medicine, 18, 142. <https://doi.org/10.1186/s12245-025-00959-4>; Simmel S, Wurm S, Drisch S, Woltmann A, Coenen M (2020). Prädiktion der Rückkehr zur Arbeit nach Polytrauma bei Patienten mit einem ISS von mindestens 25. Die Rehabilitation, 59(2), 95-103. <https://doi.org/10.1055/a-0977-6853>; National Health Commission (2025). Interpretation of the 2024 Statistical Bulletin on the Development of Health and Wellness in China. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202512/content_7050025.htm>
entries.notes: Reason for giving a B rating: The fall cohort was compiled from old medical records retrieved by a single hospital, without separating accidental falls from intentional self-harm. The return-to-work cohort had only 84 people, and was in Germany. Neither cohort can be directly taken as "what happens to a person after jumping from a building." The average expenditure per hospitalization is an average calculated across all hospitalizations nationwide, not the cost of fall injuries; citing it is only to provide a verifiable lower baseline. The original paper only provided the height distribution for this cohort, so the correspondence between height and outcome is not written here. For pressure ulcers, which should be monitored most closely during prolonged bed rest, see Section 17, Item 8. For deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, see Section 13, Item 11 (one leg suddenly swells up). For what to do when thoughts arise, see Item 32 of this section. For the consequences of poisoning, see Item 33 of this section (don't treat "being saved" as a safety net). Below is the author's own experience: Falling from the fourth floor, beforehand assuming "it would heal in a dozen days or so." In reality, one year of hospitalization, surgeries in four places, plates fitted, unable to turn over or sit up independently for half a year, and the family went into debt borrowing money for it.

entries.title: Don't Trade Away a Kidney for Money Thinking "Missing One is No Big Deal": The Remaining One Has to Work for Two, and 86% of Kidney Sellers Report Deteriorated Health Afterward
entries.cost: Costs no money. It is just about seeing this ledger clearly beforehand.
entries.summary: Among regular living kidney donors in the US who underwent multi-layer screening prior to donation, the rate progressing to uremia after 15 years was 31 per 10,000. Among equally healthy people who did not donate, it was 4 per 10,000. In a cohort of people in India who sold kidneys, 6 years later 86% reported deteriorated health, and three-quarters remained in debt.
entries.benefit: A US study compared 96,217 living kidney donors with 20,024 matched healthy non-donors. The latter came from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES III). Looking then at the estimated risk of progressing to uremia 15 years post-donation: among donors it was 30.8 per 10,000, with a confidence interval of 95% CI 24.3–38.5. Among healthy non-donors it was 3.9 per 10,000, with a confidence interval of 95% CI 0.8–8.9, P<0.001. The medical term for uremia is end-stage renal disease (ESRD); once reaching this stage, one must rely on dialysis or transplantation to survive. The estimated lifetime risk of developing ESRD: 90 per 10,000 for donors, 326 per 10,000 for the unscreened general population, and 14 per 10,000 for healthy non-donors. Norway also conducted a comparison. On one side were 1,901 kidney donors with a median follow-up of 15.1 years. On the other side were 32,621 eligible donor controls with a median follow-up of 24.9 years. All-cause mortality was about 30% higher in kidney donors (HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.11–1.52). Cardiovascular mortality was about 40% higher (HR 1.40, 1.03–1.91). Progression to ESRD was roughly tenfold higher (HR 11.38, 4.37–29.6). The overall incidence of ESRD in this cohort of donors was 302 cases per million. Another US study followed 3,698 kidney donors, of whom 11 developed ESRD, equivalent to 180 cases per million person-years of observation, compared to 268 cases in the contemporary general population. Of this cohort, 255 people returned for follow-up testing an average of 12.2 ± 9.2 years post-donation. Among them, 85.5% had a glomerular filtration rate (GFR) ≥ 60 ml/min/1.73 m² (60 is the clinical lower limit of normal). 32.1% had hypertension. 12.7% had proteinuria (protein leaking into the urine). A survey in Chennai, India examined 305 kidney sellers, surveyed an average of 6 years after selling: 96% sold to pay off debts, receiving an average of $1,070. After nephrectomy, average family income decreased by one-third (P<0.001), the number of people living below the poverty line increased, and three-quarters remained in debt at the time of the survey. 86% reported worse health compared to before nephrectomy, and 79% would not recommend selling a kidney to others.
entries.sources: Muzaale AD, Massie AB, Wang MC, Montgomery RA, McBride MA, Wainright JL, Segev DL (2014). Risk of end-stage renal disease following live kidney donation. JAMA, 311(6), 579-586. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2013.285141>；Mjøen G, Hallan S, Hartmann A, et al. (2014). Long-term risks for kidney donors. Kidney International, 86(1), 162-167. <https://doi.org/10.1038/ki.2013.460>；Ibrahim HN, Foley R, Tan L, et al. (2009). Long-term consequences of kidney donation. New England Journal of Medicine, 360(5), 459-469. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa0804883>；Goyal M, Mehta RL, Schneiderman LJ, Sehgal AR (2002). Economic and health consequences of selling a kidney in India. JAMA, 288(13), 1589-1593. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.288.13.1589>
entries.notes: Controversy: The study by Ibrahim et al. used the general public as the comparison group. Its conclusion was that survival and the risk of developing uremia (ESRD) among kidney donors were comparable to those of the general public. Once Muzaale and Mjøen changed the comparison group to people who were "equally healthy and equally qualified to donate kidneys," the risk was noticeably higher. The discrepancy lies in whom they are compared against, not in the donors themselves. All three studies agree that the absolute risk is small (30.8 per 10,000 over 15 years, i.e., 30.8 out of 10,000 people). So the key point is not that "donating a kidney is extremely dangerous"; what needs to be looked at are two other things. The remaining kidney does indeed pay a price, as the proportions of hypertension and proteinuria demonstrate. These figures all originate from cohorts who were screened preoperatively, had follow-up care postoperatively, and could return to the hospital if complications arose. Black-market kidney selling has none of these three safeguards, and the follow-up survey from India presents an entirely different outcome. The original studies only provided figures for self-reported deteriorated health, proteinuria, hypertension, and ESRD incidence, with no figures such as "how many people became bedridden," which will not be supplemented here. For relative-only restrictions, fines, and criminal liabilities in legal donation, see Section 9, Item 22 (do not sell your own organs). For those who already require dialysis, for direct inter-provincial settlement and long-term medications, see Section 16, Items 1 and 2 (take medications fully as prescribed; cross-provincial record-filing for outpatient chronic and special diseases).

entries.title: Do Not Pick Up, Disassemble, or Sell Metal Parts of Unknown Origin; Stay Far Away from Anything Bearing the Trefoil Warning Symbol
entries.cost: Costs no money. If you see unfamiliar metal cylinders, lead pots, or components dismantled from equipment, detour around them; do not pick them up, do not take them apart, and do not put them in your pocket.
entries.summary: Radiation is invisible to the naked eye, and radioactive sources are solids sealed inside small metal casings, so "looking fine" cannot serve as a judgment. The probability of an ordinary person encountering one is extremely low, with fewer than 1 incident per 10,000 radioactive sources per year. However, once encountered, the consequences are severe: in Brazil in 1987, individuals dismantled a radiotherapy machine from an abandoned clinic, ultimately resulting in 4 deaths.
entries.benefit: Science popularization by the National Nuclear Safety Administration states that radioactive sources are solid radioactive materials permanently sealed in containers or tightly encapsulated. Industrial level gauges, flaw detectors, and hospital gamma knives all use this type. Category III radioactive sources, in the absence of shielding, can cause permanent injury within hours of contact and can be fatal within days to weeks. X-rays are invisible to the naked eye, and gamma rays are electromagnetic waves just like them. Protection against external exposure relies on three things: reducing time, increasing distance, and adding shielding. Gamma rays have strong penetrating power, requiring thick concrete walls or lead to block them. As of 2025, there are approximately 178,000 radioactive sources in use and 355,000 radiation-emitting devices (units/sets) nationwide across China. The annual incidence rate of radiation accidents involving radioactive sources has remained stable at below 1 per 10,000 sources. The classification is as follows: The loss, theft, or loss of control of Category I or Category II radioactive sources constitutes a major radiation accident. Category III constitutes a relatively large radiation accident. The loss or theft of Category IV or Category V sources, or incidents resulting in personnel receiving radiation doses exceeding the annual dose limit, constitute general radiation accidents. Official case: In June 2020, the ironmaking plant of Ningxia Iron and Steel Group was carrying out gamma-ray flaw detection work on a blast furnace piping renovation project. A Category II iridium-192 radioactive source exposed three workers to radiation. Chen suffered Grade III acute radiation cutaneous injury to the left hand. Liu suffered Grade IV injury to the left thumb and index finger, and Grade III to the middle, ring, and little fingers. Fan suffered Grade I–II injury to the left hand. The radiation doses received by all three individuals severely exceeded the dose limits stipulated by national standards; the two responsible entities had their radiation safety licenses revoked and were fined 70,000 yuan. International case: In Goiânia, Brazil, in 1987, a teletherapy unit in an abandoned clinic was dismantled. A 50.8 TBq cesium-137 radioactive source inside was extracted, and the sealed capsule containing the source was also breached. Approximately 112,000 people were monitored. Among them, 249 individuals suffered internal or external contamination. Of these 249 individuals, 129 had moderate to severe contamination, and 50 required close medical surveillance. Ultimately, 4 people died (nationwide / international).
entries.sources: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (2025). 2024 Report on the State of China's Ecology and Environment. <https://www.mee.gov.cn/ywgz/sthjjcgl/hjzljcypj/202506/t20250605_1120773.shtml>; National Nuclear Safety Administration (2026). Results of China's Nuclear and Radiation Safety Regulation in 2025. <https://nnsa.mee.gov.cn/tpxw/202601/t20260107_1140062.html>; Ministry of Ecology and Environment (2021). Notice on the Handling of a Radiation Accident Caused by Illegal and Noncompliant Gamma-Ray Radiography Operations. <https://www.mee.gov.cn/xxgk2018/xxgk/xxgk06/202101/t20210121_818216.html>; State Council (2019). Regulations on the Safety and Protection of Radioisotopes and Radiation-Emitting Devices (2019 revision, Articles 34, 42, and 68). <https://www.mee.gov.cn/ywgz/fgbz/xzfg/201909/t20190918_734315.shtml>; Ministry of Environmental Protection (2009). Notice on Establishing a System for Graded Handling and Reporting of Radiation Accidents Involving Radioisotopes and Radiation-Emitting Devices (radiation accident classification standards). <https://www.mee.gov.cn/gkml/zj/wj/200910/t20091022_172414.htm>; National Nuclear Safety Administration. [Applications of Nuclear Technology] What Is a Radioactive Source?: “A radioactive source is radioactive material, other than material within the nuclear fuel cycle of research reactors and power reactors, that is permanently sealed in a container or tightly encapsulated and is solid”; “sealed sources are used in devices such as level gauges and gamma radiography machines”; a Category III radioactive source “can cause permanent injury after a person is exposed to it without protection for several hours, and can cause death after exposure for several days to several weeks.” <https://nnsa.mee.gov.cn/ztzl/haqshmhsh/hyfsaqkp/kptw/202406/t20240624_1076670.html>; National Nuclear Safety Administration (reposting material from the Shandong Environmental Nuclear and Radiation Division). Popular Science on Nuclear and Radiation: “cesium-137 used in industrial level gauges, iridium-192 used in radiography machines, and cobalt-60 used in hospital gamma knives, among others.” <https://nnsa.mee.gov.cn/ztzl/haqshmhsh/hyfsaqkp/kptw/202406/t20240624_1076991.html>; National Nuclear Safety Administration. Remarkable Nuclear Technology (16)—Radiation Protection and Management: “There are generally three basic ways to protect against external exposure: limiting time, increasing distance, and using shielding.” <https://nnsa.mee.gov.cn/ztzl/haqshmhsh/hyfsaqkp/kptw/202406/t20240624_1076933.html>; National Nuclear Safety Administration. [Radiation Protection] What Types of Radiation Are There?: “Gamma rays, like X-rays, are electromagnetic waves”; “They have relatively strong penetrating power and require thick material for shielding; thick concrete walls or lead and other materials are commonly used for protection.” <https://nnsa.mee.gov.cn/ztzl/haqshmhsh/hyfsaqkp/kptw/202406/t20240624_1076595.html>; National Nuclear Safety Administration. Nuclear Knowledge in Everyday Life—X-Ray Security Scanners: “X-rays, also called Röntgen rays, are a type of radiation invisible to the naked eye.” <https://nnsa.mee.gov.cn/ztzl/haqshmhsh/hyfsaqkp/kptw/202406/t20240624_1076874.html>; Hunan Provincial Geological Institute (2023). Radiation-Emitting Devices in Nuclear Technology Applications (excerpted from the Study Guide to Comprehensive Nuclear Safety Knowledge): “The core component of an X-ray machine is the X-ray tube”; “delayed radiation remains after an accelerator is shut down”; “after an accelerator is shut down, the effects of induced radioactivity must be considered when entering the accelerator hall or target hall.” <http://hnsdzy.hunan.gov.cn/dzy/c101626/c101627/c101633/202304/t20230411_29311495.html>; International Atomic Energy Agency (1988). The Radiological Accident in Goiânia. IAEA, Vienna. <https://www-pub.iaea.org/MTCD/Publications/PDF/Pub815_web.pdf>; Wang Furu, Wang Jin, Yu Ningle, et al. (2019). Medical Follow-Up of an Exposed Person After the Nanjing “5.7” Lost Radioactive Source Accident. Chinese Journal of Radiological Medicine and Protection, 39(11), 859–863. <https://doi.org/10.3760/cma.j.issn.0254-5098.2019.11.011>; China Environment News (2014-05-15). The 48 Hours After a Radioactive Source Went Missing (Xu Xiaotie, Shao Yi, Chu Fangqiao, Tang Jingru). <http://nnsa.mee.gov.cn/ztzl/haqshmhsh/hjbzl/202406/P020240624472937009953.pdf> (archived webpage <https://web.archive.org/web/20261005044102/http://nnsa.mee.gov.cn/ztzl/haqshmhsh/hjbzl/202406/P020240624472937009953.pdf>)
entries.notes: If you really encounter one: move away, remember its location, do not move it, and call China's 110 emergency police number. The regulations require reporting it to the ecology and environment authority, the public security authority, and the health authority. The only protective steps an ordinary person can take are to stay farther away and spend less time nearby; a pocket or plastic bag will not block gamma rays. X-ray machines and CT scanners produce radiation when their X-ray tubes are powered; they do not themselves contain radioactive sources. This follows from how radiation-emitting devices work. Accelerators are different: after shutdown, induced radioactivity remains in structural materials and the air inside the facility. The real danger is the sealed radioactive source inside equipment; gamma knives, gamma radiography machines, and level gauges all contain sources. In the Goiânia accident, someone opened a machine and took out the source. So do not count on being able to recognize a radioactive source: do not dismantle, sell, or take home any equipment part of unknown origin. In China, people have also picked up radioactive sources without knowing what they were. In May 2014, a factory in the Nanjing Chemical Industry Park lost an iridium-192 radioactive source during radiography work. A warehouse administrator found it during an inspection and put it in his work-clothes pocket. He was later diagnosed with mild acute radiation sickness and an acute radiation-induced skin injury on his right leg. He spent a year in hospital and still needed two crutches to walk several years later. Two other workers said they had seen it; one thought it was a necklace on his way to work, picked it up to look at it, then threw it away. The company that lost the source was Tianjin Hongdi Engineering Inspection Development Co., Ltd. No official accident report was found for this incident. The finder’s injuries are described in a follow-up paper published by doctors at the Jiangsu Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention; the account of picking up the source and throwing it away appears only in reporting by China Environment News. People working in scrap recycling, dismantling, hardware, and construction are more likely to encounter such a source; this is an inference from the Goiânia and Nanjing accidents. If you see a cordoned-off area marked with the radiation trefoil at a construction site, go around it. This entry concerns radioactive sources that are out of control. A nuclear power plant leak is a different kind of accident and is not covered here. The main beneficiaries are you and family members who are at the scene with you.

entries.title: If you keep gambling even after borrowing money and your mood stays low, call China’s 12356 mental health assistance hotline first, then put your bank cards and payment passwords in a family member’s care
entries.cost: No cost. Make one phone call. Put your bank cards, payment passwords, and lending apps in a family member’s care. The hard part is first admitting that you cannot control your gambling.
entries.summary: Among people in Sweden who saw a specialist for gambling problems, deaths by suicide were 15 times as high as among their peers, and deaths from all causes were 1.8 times as high. Depression was the signal that predicted who would die by suicide. So if you keep gambling even after borrowing money and your mood stays low, call China’s 12356 mental health assistance hotline first.
entries.benefit: A Swedish nationwide register study identified 2,099 people diagnosed with gambling disorder by specialist services between 2005 and 2016. Gambling disorder means being unable to control gambling to the point that it affects your life. Compared with Swedes of the same age, these people aged 20 to 74 had 1.8 times the all-cause mortality and 15 times the suicide mortality (both figures are standardized mortality ratios, or SMRs). During follow-up, 67 people died, including 21 who died by suicide. Depression predicted death by suicide. The authors published a correction in 2023: suicide mortality was 12.1 times as high for men and 16.1 times as high for women. Since May 1, 2025, people throughout China have been able to reach a mental health assistance hotline by dialing 12356. It operates for at least 18 hours each day (Sweden / nationwide in China).
entries.sources: Karlsson A, Håkansson A. (2018). Gambling disorder, increased mortality, suicidality, and associated comorbidity: A longitudinal nationwide register study. Journal of Behavioral Addictions, 7(4), 1091–1099. <https://doi.org/10.1556/2006.7.2018.112>; Karlsson A, Håkansson A. (2023). Corrigendum to: Gambling disorder, increased mortality, suicidality, and associated comorbidity. Journal of Behavioral Addictions, 12(1), 302. <https://doi.org/10.1556/2006.2023.10000>; National Health Commission (2024). Notice on the Use of “12356” as the Nationwide Unified Telephone Number for Mental Health Assistance Hotlines (National Health Medical Administration Letter [2024] No. 259). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202412/content_6994470.htm>
entries.notes: The evidence is rated B because there is only one study, and it included only people who had seen a specialist. Their conditions tended to be more severe, so the 15-fold figure cannot be applied to everyone who plays cards. Having a family member manage your money is a practice based on experience, without direct research evidence; rated separately, it is Grade C. For the legal limits on gambling, see Section 9, Item 13 (do not take a cut of the stakes or gamble online). For whether you should repay a family member’s gambling debt, see Section 8, Item 44 (gambling debts are not joint marital debts). For what to do after thoughts of suicide arise, see Item 32 of this section (tell someone close to you first). You are the main beneficiary; family members who notice the warning signs can also help the person follow this advice.

entries.title: Men who have sex with men and engage in high-risk sexual activity should ask a designated HIV/AIDS hospital about pre-exposure prophylaxis; taking it on schedule can reduce infections by about 70%
entries.cost: This is a prescription medication and, in most places, you pay for it yourself. Prices range from several hundred to several thousand yuan. Before it is prescribed, you need HIV, kidney function, and hepatitis B tests. After that, you need a checkup every 3 months. The difficult part is taking it on time every day.
entries.summary: When someone who does not yet have HIV takes an antiretroviral medication in advance, it is called pre-exposure prophylaxis. For people who take it on schedule, the risk of infection can fall by about 70%. For people who take it inconsistently, it has virtually no effect. It is a prescription medication: a hospital must check your health before prescribing it, and you need regular follow-up checks afterward.
entries.benefit: The medication is a combination tablet containing emtricitabine and tenofovir. The iPrEx trial assigned 2,499 men who have sex with men and transgender women to take either the medication or a placebo every day. The medication group had 44% fewer infections (95% CI 15–63). Protection was much stronger among people who had measurable medication in their blood. The UK PROUD trial included 544 men who have sex with men. The group that started the medication immediately had 86% fewer infections than the group that delayed starting for a year (90% CI 64–96, a 90% confidence range). In France’s IPERGAY trial, taking the medication as needed before and after sex reduced infections by 86% (95% CI 40–98). A meta-analysis used by the World Health Organization combined the trials. Overall, the RR was 0.49 (0.33–0.73, about 51% lower). In trials where medication adherence exceeded 70%, the RR was 0.30 (0.21–0.45, about 70% lower). Where adherence was below 40%, the RR was 0.95, meaning virtually no effect. China’s National Medical Products Administration approved this medication for pre-exposure prophylaxis in August 2020. Adults and adolescents weighing at least 35 kilograms can use it (multiple countries / China).

China’s Plan for Containing and Preventing HIV/AIDS (2024–2030). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202412/content_6992033.htm>
entries.notes: Trial participants were mainly men who have sex with men, so they are the group for whom asking about it is most relevant. Other people who engage in high-risk sexual activity can also ask a doctor whether it is appropriate for them. Before it is prescribed, you must first confirm that you do not have HIV; if someone who already has HIV takes it, the virus can develop drug resistance. A self-test result is not sufficient evidence. People with hepatitis B may have a hepatitis flare when they stop taking it, so they need to be tested before it is prescribed. The World Health Organization recommends taking it as needed only for men who have sex with men, and this approach is suitable for those who have sex less than twice a week on average. The regimen is 2 tablets 2 to 24 hours before sex, then 1 tablet at 24 hours and 1 tablet at 48 hours afterward. Women and people with hepatitis B must take it every day. In the trial of the as-needed regimen, gastrointestinal and kidney-related adverse effects were more common in the medication group than in the placebo group, so follow-up checks cannot be skipped. China began piloting it among men who have sex with men in 2019; the 2024 plan calls for its “standardized implementation.” No nationwide policy providing it free of charge was found. Visit the infectious diseases department or sexually transmitted infections and HIV/AIDS clinic of a local designated HIV/AIDS hospital to get a prescription; first call your local Center for Disease Control and Prevention to ask which hospital can prescribe it. It does not prevent sexually transmitted infections such as syphilis or gonorrhea, so you still need to use condoms; see Item 30 of this section (use a condom throughout sex). If high-risk activity has already occurred, see Section 13, Item 38 for what to do afterward (obtain post-exposure prophylaxis within 72 hours). You are the main beneficiary, and it also protects your partner.

entries.title: Women aged 65 and over should have a dual-energy X-ray bone density scan once; postmenopausal women with osteoporosis risk factors need not wait until 65
entries.cost: Go to a hospital for a dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry bone density scan (DXA for short) of your lumbar spine and hip. You lie down, and it takes just a few minutes. If paying yourself, it generally costs one or two hundred yuan; prices vary by location. The heel ultrasound test in some health checkups, which involves placing one foot on a device, is only an initial screening test and cannot confirm a diagnosis.
entries.summary: Women aged 65 and over, and postmenopausal women with osteoporosis risk factors, should have their bone density checked once. Assessing risk first, then giving medication to those at high risk, can reduce hip fractures by about 17%. In absolute terms, that is about 5 fewer hip fractures per 1,000 people screened. No change in all-cause mortality was observed.
entries.benefit: The US Preventive Services Task Force’s 2025 recommendation is to screen women aged 65 and over for osteoporosis (Grade B recommendation). It also recommends screening postmenopausal women under 65 who are found to be at high risk of fracture through a risk assessment (Grade B). The evidence for men was insufficient, so it made no recommendation for them. The evidence review prepared for this recommendation combined 3 randomized trials involving 42,009 older European women. Screening involved assessing fracture risk first, checking bone density in those at high risk, and giving medication to those found to be at high risk. The screening group had about 17% fewer hip fractures. The original figure was RR 0.83, with a 95% CI of 0.73 to 0.93. In absolute numbers, screening prevented 5 hip fractures per 1,000 people screened. One of the studies, the UK SCOOP trial, enrolled 12,483 women aged 70 to 85. Its screening group had about 28% fewer hip fractures (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.59 to 0.89), with no detectable difference in mortality. The Chinese Medical Association’s 2017 clinical guideline recommends bone density testing for women over 65 and men over 70. It also recommends testing people below those ages who have one or more osteoporosis risk factors. In a nationwide survey conducted in 2017–2018, osteoporosis prevalence among people over 40 was 20.6% for women and 5.0% for men (China).

(2021). Prevalence of Osteoporosis and Fracture in China: The China Osteoporosis Prevalence Study. JAMA Network Open. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2021.21106>
entries.notes: Caveats: SCOOP’s prespecified primary outcome was all osteoporotic fractures. The screening group did not have a clear reduction in these fractures (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.85 to 1.03); only hip fractures were reduced. All three trials assessed risk first and then measured bone mineral density. None separately compared bone mineral density testing alone. The evidence review also estimated that 11.8% to 24.1% of people identified by screening were overdiagnosed, meaning they would never have had a fracture because of osteoporosis during their lifetime. As for whether men should be screened, the US says the evidence is insufficient, while Chinese guidelines set the age at over 70; follow your doctor’s advice. This item concerns whether your bones can withstand a fall. To reduce falls, see Item 13 (balance and leg strength); do both. For what to do after osteoporosis is detected, see Item 40 (take medication if osteoporosis is detected). The main beneficiaries are you and your parents.

entries.title: If you are diagnosed with osteoporosis, or have broken a bone after a minor fall, ask a doctor to prescribe osteoporosis medication and keep taking it; do not substitute calcium supplements
entries.cost: You need a prescription and will need to keep taking the medication for several years. Common options include an oral medication taken once a week and an intravenous medication given once a year. When you first start treatment, have your bone mineral density checked every year; once it is stable, have it checked every 1 to 2 years. The hard part is continuing treatment even when you feel fine.
entries.summary: For postmenopausal women already diagnosed with osteoporosis or who have had a fracture, alendronate can cut hip fractures by about half. Symptomatic spinal fractures fall by more than half. Among older people who start a once-yearly intravenous medication after hip-fracture surgery, about 35% fewer have another fracture over two years. Calcium supplements alone cannot replace these medications.
entries.benefit: A fragility fracture is a fracture caused by minor trauma or occurring during everyday activities. The Chinese Medical Association’s 2017 guidelines identify three groups for medication. The first is people who have had a fragility fracture of the spine or hip. The second is people with a bone mineral density T-score of -2.5 or lower, whether or not they have had a fracture. The third is people with low bone mass who have also had a fragility fracture of the wrist, upper arm, or pelvis, or whose calculated fracture risk is high. The guidelines also state that “there is currently insufficient evidence that calcium supplementation alone can replace treatment with other osteoporosis medications.” Cochrane updated its review of alendronate in 2025. Among postmenopausal women who already had osteoporosis or a fracture, hip fractures were about 51% less frequent in the treatment group. The original estimate was RR 0.49, with a 95% CI of 0.25 to 0.96. Symptomatic spinal fractures were about 55% less frequent (RR 0.45, 95% CI 0.28 to 0.73). The HORIZON trial enrolled 2,127 people who had undergone surgery for a hip fracture; their average age was 74.5. They began once-yearly intravenous zoledronic acid within 90 days after surgery, and the median follow-up was 1.9 years. New fractures fell from 13.9% to 8.6%, a reduction of about 35%. Deaths fell from 13.3% to 9.6%, a reduction of about 28%. The guidelines state that about 20% of people die from various complications within one year of a hip fracture. In a nationwide survey conducted in 2017–2018, only 1.4% of women diagnosed with osteoporosis or who had had a fracture were taking medication, and only 0.3% of men were (China).

(2021). Prevalence of Osteoporosis and Fracture in China: The China Osteoporosis Prevalence Study. JAMA Network Open. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2021.21106>
entries.notes: Caveats: A meta-analysis pooling 38 trials found no clear reduction in all-cause mortality from these medications (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.91 to 1.05). Zoledronic acid alone also showed no statistically significant effect (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.68 to 1.13). The authors concluded that these medications should be used only to reduce fractures. The certainty of the Cochrane estimates was also rated low to moderate. For women who have not had a fracture and whose fracture risk is lower, alendronate showed no clear effect on hip fractures (RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.43 to 1.32). Trials lasting a few years cannot fully capture rare side effects such as osteonecrosis of the jaw and atypical femoral fractures. Keep your follow-up appointments, and do not start extra medication or stop treatment on your own. Injections suit some people, while oral medication suits others; your doctor should decide which to use. For how to detect osteoporosis, see Item 39 (bone mineral density testing). Menopausal hormone therapy can also reduce fractures, but it is generally considered only when other medications are unsuitable. For hormone therapy for hot flashes and night sweats, see Section 2, Item 43 (seek an assessment for hormone therapy for hot flashes around menopause). The main beneficiaries are you and your parents.

entries.title: Before stepping onto ice in the wild, drill a hole and measure its thickness; stay off if it is under 15 cm, and avoid river ice and the edges of ice-fishing holes
entries.cost: The easiest option is to go to an officially managed ice rink, which costs no extra money. If you insist on going onto ice in the wild, bring an ice drill or ice chisel to make a hole and measure its thickness. Also buy a pair of ice-rescue picks—two pointed spikes with handles—and hang them in front of your chest. Together, these cost from a few dozen to one or two hundred yuan. Measuring again after each stretch of walking takes extra time.
entries.summary: Chinese official guidance says ice must be 15 cm thick before adults can skate on it. The minimum in US and Canadian guidance is 10 cm, and that applies only to newly formed clear ice. White ice is only half as strong, so it needs to be twice as thick. On the same sheet of ice, it might be a foot thick in one spot and only an inch or two thick a few steps away. Measure as you go.
entries.benefit: Public guidance from the China Meteorological Administration says adults can skate when the ice reaches 15 cm thick. Outdoor ice rinks must also have 15 cm of ice before they can open. The Beijing Municipal Water Authority says an officially managed natural ice rink may open only when the ice is 15 cm thick and, for the following week, temperatures stay between -8°C and 1°C with no strong winds. Ice in the wild often has holes cut by people fishing, and it is difficult for the ice to freeze solid again after a hole is made. The Minnesota Department of Natural Resources’ guidelines apply only to newly formed clear ice: stay off ice thinner than 4 inches (about 10 cm); at 4 inches, walking and ice fishing are permitted. White ice formed when snow melts and refreezes is only about half as strong as clear ice, so the required thickness should be doubled. On the same body of water, ice may be a foot thick in one spot and only an inch or two thick a few feet away. Ice over flowing water is usually dangerous, especially near streams, bridges, and culverts. Ice near the shore may also be thinner than ice farther out. The US National Weather Service likewise gives 4 inches as the minimum for walking, ice fishing, and skating. The Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety relays advice from the Canadian Red Cross: 15 cm for several people skating or walking together, and 20 cm for a skating gathering with many people. These are safety guidelines; no research has calculated how many deaths following them prevents (China nationwide / US and Canada).
entries.sources: China Meteorological Administration (2019). Want to take a brisk walk on ice? How thick must the ice be to be safe? <https://www.cma.gov.cn/kppd/kppdqxyr/kppdtyqx/201901/t20190124_513302.html>; Beijing Municipal Water Authority (2024). Beijing’s officially managed river and lake ice rinks have not yet met the standards for opening; do not risk skating on “wild ice”: “After the Start of Spring, as temperatures warm, ice becomes thinner day by day. In some places it melts and water seeps through, and it could break at any time, so you must not go onto the ice after the Start of Spring.” “If the lower part of the ice looks like fine vertical icicles, take particular care, because these upright ice crystals show that the ice has become brittle.” <https://swj.beijing.gov.cn/swdt/ztzl/fnsbaqztxc/fnszlxx/202412/t20241226_3973959.html>; Minnesota Department of Natural Resources. General ice thickness guidelines. <https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/safety/ice/thickness.html>; Minnesota Department of Natural Resources. Ice safety. <https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/safety/ice/index.html>; Minnesota Department of Natural Resources. Steps for surviving immersion. <https://www.dnr.state.mn.us/safety/ice/survival.html>; National Weather Service. Winter Weather Safety: Ice and Frost. <https://www.weather.gov/safety/winter-ice-frost>; Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety. Working on or near Ice Covered Water - Basic Information. <https://www.ccohs.ca/oshanswers/hsprograms/work_ice.html>
entries.notes: All the official guidelines say no ice is 100% safe. Adequate measured thickness is only a minimum threshold, not a guarantee. The Beijing Municipal Water Authority says that after the Start of Spring, temperatures warm and ice becomes thinner day by day; some places melt and water seeps through, so you must not go onto the ice after the Start of Spring. If the lower half of the ice looks like fine vertical icicles, the ice has become brittle and is dangerous even if it looks thick. If you do fall through, do not take off your clothes: air trapped in thick clothing can help you float. Turn toward the direction you came from, where the ice is strongest. Rest your arms on the ice, drive the ice picks into it, kick backward, and drag yourself out. Once out, do not stand up. Lie flat and roll away from the hole, then get warm as soon as possible; go to a hospital if you are severely chilled. If you see someone fall through the ice, do not run over to pull them out. See Section 13, Item 25 (do not enter the water yourself when you see someone drowning). First call for help and dial China’s emergency number 110, then extend a pole or throw a rope. The main beneficiaries are you and the children you take to play on the ice.

entries.title: Fit the guard and wear safety goggles plus a face shield before using an angle grinder; hold it firmly with both hands, and do not fit a woodworking saw blade to cut wood
entries.cost: A pair of safety goggles plus a face shield costs a few dozen yuan. Check the guard and disc before each use, and unplug the grinder before changing the disc; this takes another minute or two. The hard part is keeping the guard on and using both hands even when it feels like a nuisance.
entries.summary: An angle grinder spins extremely fast. If its disc shatters, fragments can fly out and injure someone; fitting a woodworking saw blade can also cause sudden kickback. In two accidents in China, both grinders had saw blades fitted and no guards. One person severed an artery in the thigh, and the other cut an artery in the neck; neither survived. A guard, safety goggles plus a face shield, and a firm two-handed grip cost very little.
entries.benefit: The Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety and safety authorities in Queensland, Australia, list the following practices: Inspect the guard and disc before turning on the machine; do not use discs that have cracks, chips, or deformation. The maximum rotational speed marked on the disc must not be lower than the speed marked on the machine, and both the diameter and the arbor hole must match the machine. Disconnect power before changing discs. Secure the workpiece to be ground or cut beforehand. Wear safety glasses or goggles, supplemented with a full-face shield over them. Hold both handles firmly with both hands, maintaining stable footing. Cutting discs must not be used for grinding, which makes the disc much more prone to shattering. Do not put the machine down until the disc has come to a complete stop. Direct sparks and debris toward areas free of people, and keep combustible materials away from the surrounding area. A Queensland safety alert noted that the designed peripheral speed of a cutting disc is approximately 70 meters per second. Fitting a large 356 mm disc onto a 230 mm machine raises the peripheral speed to at least 120 meters per second, making the disc prone to shattering. In February 2016, a local worker using a 230 mm angle grinder was struck in the chest by flying fragments and died from internal injuries. There are two domestic accident investigation reports from China. In 2019, a worker in Harbin replaced a cutting disc with a toothed saw blade and proceeded to cut wooden planks without installing a safety guard. The saw blade snagged his trousers, severed his femoral artery, and he died from blood loss. In 2024, a worker in Futian, Shenzhen, used an angle grinder fitted with a woodworking saw blade—without installing either the guard or the auxiliary handle—to cut a wooden door frame. The machine kicked back, severing his carotid artery and killing him. The national standard cited in the report states: "Do not attach a saw chain, woodcarving blade or toothed saw blade." In emergency department injury surveillance in South Korea from 2011 to 2018, there were 8,697 visits for injuries caused by high-rotation cutting tools, among which 4,603 visits involved grinder-type tools. Hand injuries accounted for 46.4%, and head injuries accounted for 23.0%. Compared with other similar tools, grinders were associated with roughly twice the odds of sustaining severe injuries (OR 2.07, 95% CI 1.88–2.29). A hospital in Mianyang, Sichuan, admitted 36 inpatients with angle grinder eye injuries over a two-year period. In 10 patients, the best-corrected visual acuity with glasses remained below 0.05 after surgery. Among 742 cases of acute hand and forearm trauma at a hospital in Turkey over one year, angle grinders accounted for 82 cases. Except for 8 cases, none occurred during work, and 44% were retired individuals. Among 15 angle grinder injury patients at a trauma center in Japan from 2017 to 2018, 9 involved misuse such as attaching saw blades to cut wood. Among them, 2 patients suffered complete finger amputations, and 1 suffered a partial amputation (Canada, Australia / China / South Korea, Turkey, Japan).
