entries.notes: Rated C because these practices derive from safety agency guidelines and accident investigations; no studies have quantified how many injuries are averted by adhering to them. Injury data only illustrate injury severity, and all are case series from single hospitals or single countries. The magnitude of benefit is rated as Moderate based on judgment: consequences can include death, blindness, and finger amputation, but they fall solely on the person operating the angle grinder. The instruction manual for the machine in Harbin explicitly stated not to install toothed saw blades and that guards must be fitted. The worker had a handsaw right at hand; cutting wood should have been done with woodworking tools like that. Loose clothing, dangling jewelry, and long hair must all be tied back and secured, as they can be dragged in. Grinding generates substantial dust and noise; for specific requirements on masks and earplugs, see Section 19, Item 10 (Employers Must Provide Protective Equipment). If a major blood vessel is actually lacerated, immediately apply firm, unrelenting direct pressure to the wound; see Section 13, Item 12 (Direct Firm Hand Pressure for Massive Bleeding). The beneficiary is primarily yourself, while also protecting family members standing nearby to assist. For how to preserve an amputated finger if one is severed, see Section 13, Item 47 (Severed Fingers and Toes).

entries.title: Directly ask someone around you who seems emotionally distressed, "Have you thought about suicide?"; asking will not increase their desire to do so
entries.cost: Zero financial cost. Asking takes one sentence, plus spending some time listening to them. The difficulty lies in bringing it up, as many fear that asking will inadvertently trigger or implant the thought.
entries.summary: The fear that mentioning suicide will trigger suicidal thoughts is not supported by research. Adding suicide questions to questionnaires for secondary school students did not make respondents feel more distressed, nor did suicidal ideation increase. Adolescents with pre-existing depressive symptoms actually felt less distressed after being asked, and adolescents with prior suicide attempts showed a decrease in suicidal ideation.
entries.benefit: A total of 2,342 students across 6 high schools in New York State were randomly assigned by classroom into two groups. One group's questionnaire contained questions about suicide, while the other group's did not. Immediately after completing the questionnaire and 2 days later, there were no differences in distress levels between the two groups (P = .66 and P = .41; a P-value greater than 0.05 indicates no detectable difference). Two days later, reporting having had suicidal thoughts occurred in 4.7% of the asked group versus 3.9% of the unasked group, showing no detectable difference (P = .49). Students with pre-existing depressive symptoms actually experienced less distress after being asked (P = .01). Students with a history of prior suicide attempts actually experienced a decrease in suicidal ideation after being asked (P = .02). A 2022 meta-analysis evaluated 17 studies and pooled data from 8 studies comparing "asked" versus "not asked." After asking, there was no significant increase in immediate or subsequent suicidal ideation, suicidal behavior, non-suicidal self-injury, or psychological distress. The strongest evidence came from 8 randomized controlled trials with low or unclear risk of bias. Another literature review from 2014 likewise noted that not a single study found a significant increase in suicidal ideation following inquiry.
entries.sources: Gould MS, Marrocco FA, Kleinman M, Thomas JG, Mostkoff K, Cote J, Davies M (2005). Evaluating iatrogenic risk of youth suicide screening programs: a randomized controlled trial. JAMA, 293(13), 1635-1643. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.293.13.1635>；Polihronis C, Cloutier P, Kaur J, Skinner R, Cappelli M (2022). What's the harm in asking? A systematic review and meta-analysis on the risks of asking about suicide-related behaviors and self-harm with quality appraisal. Archives of Suicide Research, 26(2), 325-347. <https://doi.org/10.1080/13811118.2020.1793857>；Dazzi T, Gribble R, Wessely S, Fear NT (2014). Does asking about suicide and related behaviours induce suicidal ideation? What is the evidence? Psychological Medicine, 44(16), 3361-3363. <https://doi.org/10.1017/S0033291714001299>
entries.notes: Reasons for rating B: These studies only demonstrate that asking causes no harm; no study has calculated how many suicide deaths are prevented by asking. The magnitude of benefit is rated as Small, also because mortality figures are lacking, leaving only the surrogate endpoint of "ideation did not increase." The mode of questioning in the research consisted mostly of questionnaires and research interviews rather than in-person questions from family and friends; extrapolating to face-to-face inquiries is an inference. If asking reveals that they have indeed considered it, do not walk away: accompany them in dialing 12356, and move medications and pesticides far out of reach; see Item 25 of this section (Dial 12356 When Experiencing Suicidal Ideation). If they state an intention to harm others as well, or have already prepared the means, close relatives can directly escort them to medical care or call 110. For procedures, see Section 8, Item 15 (Close Relatives May Directly Escort for Medical Evaluation). From the emergence of the thought to taking action, nearly half take no more than 10 minutes; see Item 32 of this section (Tell Someone Nearby as Soon as a Suicidal Thought Arises). The primary beneficiaries are spouses and direct relatives, though the question can just as well be asked of friends and colleagues.

entries.title: Get an ECG if you experience palpitations or an irregular heartbeat; if atrial fibrillation is detected, have a physician assess anticoagulant therapy to prevent stroke, and do not substitute aspirin for it
entries.cost: A single ECG costs several tens of yuan. Warfarin is very inexpensive, but requires regular blood tests to adjust the dosage. Novel anticoagulants do not require frequent blood tests and are more expensive. The challenge lies in having to take them daily even in the absence of symptoms, and notifying doctors that you are taking anticoagulants before tooth extractions or surgical operations.
entries.summary: Atrial fibrillation is chaotic heartbeat irregularity; blood stasis in the heart easily forms clots, which cause a stroke when flushed into the brain. Taking anticoagulants as evaluated by a physician reduces stroke by roughly 60% and mortality by roughly 30%. Drugs like aspirin only reduce it by about 20% and cannot serve as a substitute. In surveys from 2014 to 2016, only 6% of high-risk atrial fibrillation patients in China were taking anticoagulants.
entries.benefit: During atrial fibrillation, the atria quiver chaotically, causing blood to pool in the atria and readily form blood clots. When a clot travels into cerebral vessels, it causes a stroke. The most common symptoms are palpitations, fatigue upon exertion, and chest discomfort, though approximately 25% of individuals report having no symptoms at all. A definitive diagnosis can be made with a single-lead ECG recording of 30 seconds or longer, or a standard 12-lead ECG of 10 seconds or longer. A 2007 meta-analysis pooled 29 randomized trials comprising 28,044 individuals. Compared with no treatment, dose-adjusted warfarin reduced stroke by approximately 60% (a 64% reduction, confidence interval 49% to 74%). Antiplatelet drugs like aspirin reduced it by only about 20% (a 22% reduction, confidence interval 6% to 35%). In direct comparisons between the two drug classes, warfarin reduced risk by a further 39% compared with antiplatelet agents. The absolute annual increase in major extracranial bleeding did not exceed 0.3%. A Cochrane review restricted to 2,313 individuals without a prior stroke found that warfarin lowered mortality by roughly 30% (OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.50 to 0.94). Four large trials totaling 71,683 individuals compared novel oral anticoagulants with warfarin. The new drugs further reduced stroke and systemic embolism by 19% (RR 0.81) and mortality by 10% (RR 0.90). Intracranial hemorrhage was reduced by 52% (RR 0.48), but gastrointestinal bleeding was increased by 25% (RR 1.25). Aspirin cannot replace anticoagulants. Among 5,599 individuals unsuitable for warfarin, apixaban reduced stroke and systemic embolism by 55% compared with aspirin (HR 0.45). Major bleeding was 1.4% versus 1.2% per year, showing no detectable difference (HR 1.13, confidence interval 0.74 to 1.75). Another trial enrolled only 973 individuals aged 75 and older. For the composite outcome of fatal or disabling stroke, intracranial hemorrhage, and arterial embolism, warfarin reduced risk by 52% compared with aspirin (RR 0.48). Extracranial bleeding was 1.4% versus 1.6% per year. China's 2023 atrial fibrillation guidelines use the CHA2DS2-VASc-60 score. Heart failure, hypertension, diabetes, vascular disease, age 60 to 64, and female sex each count as 1 point; age 65 and older and prior stroke each count as 2 points. Oral anticoagulants are recommended for men with a score of 2 or higher and women with a score of 3 or higher. For men with 1 point and women with 2 points, they may be considered after weighing bleeding risks and patient preferences. The guidelines do not recommend antiplatelet drugs for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation. The US 2023 guidelines explicitly state that whether to prescribe anticoagulants depends on stroke risk, not on whether atrial fibrillation is paroxysmal or persistent. They also specify that bleeding risk scores should not be used in isolation to withhold anticoagulation, but rather to identify modifiable bleeding risk factors. In a 2014 to 2016 survey in China among individuals aged 45 and older, atrial fibrillation had a prevalence of 1.8%, representing approximately 7.9 million people. Among those aware of their atrial fibrillation, awareness was 78.3% in urban areas but only 35.3% in rural areas. Only 6.0% of individuals with high-risk atrial fibrillation were taking anticoagulants. In a 2020 to 2021 nationwide survey, 43.8% of identified atrial fibrillation cases were newly detected during the survey. Among those previously diagnosed, 32.1% were using anticoagulants, and in rural areas, the figure was only 19.8%.

entries.notes: The debate is about screening; there is no debate about taking anticoagulants once atrial fibrillation has been found. There is insufficient evidence on whether people without symptoms should specifically be screened for atrial fibrillation. The US Preventive Services Task Force concluded in 2022 that the evidence was insufficient to judge the benefits and harms. In Sweden, people aged 75 to 76 were invited to undergo two weeks of ECG monitoring. About 7 years later, the combined outcome of death, stroke, and bleeding was only 4% lower, just enough to reach statistical significance. In Denmark, people aged 70 to 90 had small devices implanted to record their heart rhythm over the long term. Atrial fibrillation was detected in 31.8% versus 12.2%, but there was no discernible reduction in strokes. China's 2023 guidelines say that, when people over 65 see a doctor, checking their pulse or doing an ECG can be considered. So people with symptoms should get checked, and those over 65 can ask the doctor to check their pulse during a visit; there is no need to buy a device specifically for screening. Once you are taking an anticoagulant, do not add painkillers such as ibuprofen on your own; see Section 34, Item 3 (ask a doctor before taking ibuprofen if you take an anticoagulant). You need to take the medicine long term; do not stop because you feel fine. See Section 16, Item 1 (take medication for the full duration prescribed). High blood pressure also counts toward the risk score; see Item 7 of this section (measure your blood pressure). People with atrial fibrillation do not all need to give up coffee; see Section 2, Item 26 (drink three to four cups of coffee a day). If your mouth suddenly droops or one side becomes weak, call China's 120 emergency number immediately, whether or not you have taken your medication; see Section 13, Item 3 (sudden drooping of the mouth and weakness in one arm). The main beneficiaries are you and the older members of your family.

entries.title: Adults should get a hepatitis C antibody test once; if positive, get a nucleic acid test, and if the infection is confirmed, take oral medication for 8 to 12 weeks—most people can be cured
entries.cost: A hepatitis C antibody test requires one tube of blood and generally costs a few dozen yuan out of pocket; prices vary by location. If the antibody test is positive, another blood sample is taken for a nucleic acid test to see whether the virus is still present. If the infection is confirmed, go to a local designated hepatitis C hospital for a prescription. Most regimens involve taking one tablet a day for 8 to 12 weeks, with the medication cost reimbursed through China's medical insurance. The hard part is remembering to get tested when you have no symptoms.
entries.summary: A hepatitis C infection can cause no symptoms for decades. One antibody test, followed by a nucleic acid test if the result is positive, will tell you whether you have it. If the infection is confirmed, 8 to 12 weeks of oral medication clears the virus in more than 95% of people. Among people who clear the virus, the subsequent risk of death is about 60% lower and the risk of liver cancer about 70% lower. These medicines were added to China's medical insurance coverage in 2019, and their prices fell by more than 85% on average.
entries.benefit: Hepatitis C spreads through blood, and there is no vaccine. The World Health Organization says chronic hepatitis C often causes no symptoms for decades; by the time symptoms appear, the liver may already be badly damaged. A positive antibody test only shows that you have been infected before. A nucleic acid test is needed to find out whether the virus is still present. About 30% of people clear the virus on their own within 6 months of infection, without treatment. The World Health Organization says oral direct-acting antivirals taken for 8 to 12 weeks can cure almost all patients. An evidence review prepared for the US Preventive Services Task Force combined 49 treatment studies and found cure rates above 95% for every genotype. Cure means the virus is undetectable in the blood 12 weeks after treatment ends. Serious adverse events occurred in 1.9%, and 0.4% stopped treatment because of side effects. The same review pooled observational follow-up studies, which did not have randomized comparison groups. Compared with people who were not cured, those who were cured had about 60% lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.28–0.56, 13 studies) and about 71% lower liver cancer risk (HR 0.29, 95% CI 0.23–0.38, 20 studies). A French study followed 9,895 patients with chronic hepatitis C for a median of 33.4 months. After accounting for age, degree of liver fibrosis, alcohol consumption, and other factors, people who took the medication had about 52% lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.33–0.70) and about 34% lower liver cancer risk (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.46–0.93). Among US veterans, 15,059 patients with hepatitis C and advanced liver disease took these medicines. Over an average follow-up of about 1.6 years, 2.6 of every 100 cured patients died per year of follow-up, compared with 12.3 of every 100 who were not cured. After accounting for other factors, the risk of death was about 74% lower (HR 0.26, 95% CI 0.22–0.31). In 2020, the US Preventive Services Task Force recommended testing all adults aged 18 to 79 (Grade B recommendation). For most people, one test in a lifetime is enough. China's 2022 prevention and treatment guidelines recommend antibody screening for all adults, regular testing for those with ongoing high-risk exposure, and nucleic acid testing for everyone whose antibody test is positive. In a 2006 nationwide survey, the antibody-positive rate among people aged 1 to 59 was 0.43%. A pooled analysis of multiple studies found rates of 0.60% in the general population, 48.67% among people who use drugs, and 6.59% among people receiving hemodialysis. China's National Healthcare Security Administration says that before price negotiations, a course of hepatitis C medication mostly cost more than 50,000 yuan. The three hepatitis C medicines added to China's medical insurance coverage through negotiations in 2019 fell in price by more than 85% on average (United States, France / China).

entries.notes: Dispute: The 2017 Cochrane review considered only randomized trials. Most of the 138 trials it found were short term, so they could not establish whether these drugs reduce deaths or liver disease. It considered “cure” to mean only that the virus was undetectable in the blood; randomized trials had not yet confirmed a link between that outcome and fewer deaths. All the figures above for deaths and liver cancer come from observational follow-up records. No study has directly compared screening with no screening, either. The national program identifies people who should be tested, including those preparing for surgery, blood transfusion, endoscopy, or dialysis, and those whose liver function tests are abnormal for an unknown reason. It also includes people who have injected drugs, sold plasma, had multiple sexual partners, or had sex with other men. People with HIV and the spouses and sexual partners of people with hepatitis C should also be tested. The program also proposes encouraging people over 40 to get tested. The guidelines state that most current patients had a blood transfusion or sold plasma before 1993. Tattooing, ear piercing, and sharing razors or toothbrushes can also spread the virus. Hugging and sharing dishes, chopsticks, or drinking glasses generally do not. Antibody tests remain positive after a cure; a nucleic acid test is needed to determine whether reinfection has occurred. Reinfection is possible after a cure, and people who continue to share needles or other injection equipment should have a nucleic acid test at least once a year. Those diagnosed during pregnancy should be treated after giving birth and stopping breastfeeding, and should use contraception during treatment. People who already have cirrhosis still need regular liver cancer screening after a cure. For avoiding shared injection equipment, see item 30 of this section (do not share injection equipment with others). Hepatitis B requires a different set of tests; see item 14 of this section (check the five hepatitis B markers). For HIV, see item 31 of this section (get tested for HIV once). The guidelines state that hepatitis C combined with excessive drinking can lead to liver failure; for drinking, see section 2, item 19 (drink less or do not drink). You are the main beneficiary, and this also protects your spouse and sexual partners.

entries.title: Before entering a confined space such as a septic tank, manhole, sewage tank, vegetable cellar, basement, or fermentation tank, ventilate it, confirm that gas tests meet safety requirements, and put protective measures and a safety attendant in place; do not enter if the conditions are inadequate. If someone collapses inside, do not follow them in; call China's emergency numbers 119 and 120
entries.cost: Ventilation, testing, protective equipment, and a safety attendant all cost money for equipment and personnel, as well as time. For household tank cleaning, give priority to a trained team with the right equipment; ask local providers about the cost. If the conditions are inadequate, do not go down yourself. The hard part is resisting the urge to jump in when someone collapses inside.
entries.summary: Places such as septic tanks, manholes, and vegetable cellars can accumulate toxic gases or become oxygen deficient. A person can collapse within seconds. Before entering, ventilate the space, confirm that gas tests meet safety requirements, put protective measures in place, and have someone outside watch throughout. Do not enter if any one of these is missing. Opening the cover and waiting a while does not establish that it is safe inside. If you see someone collapse, do not follow them in; call China's emergency numbers 119 and 120.
entries.benefit: A “confined space” means a fully or partly enclosed place not intended for people to occupy for long periods, such as a septic tank, manhole, sewage tank, cellar, or vessel. China's Ministry of Emergency Management analyzed relatively serious confined-space accidents at industrial and commercial enterprises since 2013. Poisoning and asphyxiation accounted for 96.8% of accidents and 96.9% of deaths. The main harmful gases were hydrogen sulfide, carbon monoxide, nitrogen, and carbon dioxide. Accidents involving inadequate protection and reckless rescue attempts accounted for 87.4% of accidents and 86.8% of deaths. The Ministry's 2020 safety guidance manual says that reckless rescue attempts increased casualties in nearly 80% of accidents. More than 50% of those who died in confined spaces were rescuers. In 2018, the Office of the State Council Work Safety Committee reported eight accidents. In each, only one person was initially in danger; after reckless rescue attempts, three to four people died in each accident. In 2019, three people cleaning a sewage tank at a paper mill in Dongguan inhaled hydrogen sulfide and passed out. Six people went into the tank one after another to rescue them, and seven people died in the end. In 2020, a worker fell into a materials tank in the fermentation workshop of a noodle products factory in Jiaozuo. Others attempted a reckless rescue, and six people died in total. The US National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health investigated 70 fatal confined-space accidents from 1983 to 1993, in which 109 people died. Of those, 39 (36%) had entered to rescue someone. Only four of those 39 were professional responders, such as police officers or firefighters. Its 1986 warning said that about 60% of those who died were people trying to rescue someone. The manual says hydrogen sulfide smells like rotten eggs, but at high concentrations the nose can no longer detect it. At concentrations above 1,000 milligrams per cubic meter, it can kill within seconds. At high carbon dioxide concentrations, a person can lose consciousness and collapse within seconds. The manual says that if conditions at the scene do not allow people to carry out a rescue themselves, they should promptly call China's emergency numbers 119 and 120, and that “forced rescue attempts must never be allowed.” Pulling someone out from outside is possible only if the trapped person is wearing a full-body harness connected to a safety rope outside. Order No. 13 of China's Ministry of Emergency Management requires industrial and commercial enterprises to “ventilate first, then test, then begin work.” Enterprises must provide testing, ventilation, protective, and rescue equipment suited to the risks, with a safety attendant present throughout. Ventilation and testing must also continue during the work, and no one may enter if conditions fail to meet safety requirements. Safety attendants must stop reckless rescue attempts made without proper safety measures. The Anshun Municipal Health Commission warns that vegetables stored in a cellar that has been sealed for a long time consume oxygen and release carbon dioxide. Before going down into the cellar, open the vents and ventilate it thoroughly. This ventilation advice does not replace gas testing, protective measures, or a safety attendant (China / United States).

entries.notes: The evidence is rated C because these are accident statistics and safety regulations; no study has calculated how many deaths following them would prevent. The scale of benefit is rated medium based on a judgment: the consequence is death, often several deaths in one incident, but the risk applies only to people who need to enter such places. At home, the situations most likely to arise are cleaning your own septic tank or biogas digester, or going down into a vegetable cellar or basement to get vegetables. Do not rely on smell to judge whether it is safe; the absence of a rotten-egg smell does not mean hydrogen sulfide is absent. If you are told to go down a manhole or into a tank at work and there is no ventilation, testing, safety attendant, or harness, you can refuse. For the basis for refusing, see section 19, item 10 (you can refuse work without protective measures). If someone collapses inside, first call out for help and call China's emergency numbers 119 and 120. What you can do from outside is open the cover and blow air in. Once the person has been pulled out, move them to fresh air; if they are not breathing normally, give chest compressions. See section 13, item 1 (someone has collapsed and is not breathing normally). The response is the same whether the person who collapsed is a coworker, neighbor, or stranger, for the same reason given in section 13, item 25 (do not enter the water yourself when you see someone drowning). For carbon monoxide from burning coal indoors, see item 3 of this section (carbon monoxide alarm). You are the main beneficiary, because you may be the one tempted to go in to rescue someone; family members working alongside you also benefit.

entries.title: If you are over 45 and live in an area with high rates of stomach or esophageal cancer, have a family history, or test positive for Helicobacter pylori, get screened by upper endoscopy
entries.cost: A standard upper endoscopy costs several hundred yuan; a sedated upper endoscopy costs several hundred yuan more. Prices vary by location. You need to go on an empty stomach, and the appointment and related time take up half a day. If you choose a sedated upper endoscopy, someone must accompany you. The uncomfortable part is the few minutes when the tube passes through your throat.
entries.summary: Among people over 45 at high risk of stomach or esophageal cancer, those who have had an upper endoscopy are about half as likely to die from these cancers. But people who voluntarily get screened may already take better care of their health, so this figure is likely too large. Using the strictest comparison, esophageal cancer deaths were only about 20% lower, and the result was within the margin of error. Guidelines do not recommend screening for people outside the high-risk group.
entries.benefit: China's National Health Commission defined high-risk groups as follows in its 2024 programs. A person must first be at least 45 years old and then meet any one of the following conditions. First, they live in a county with a high incidence of stomach or esophageal cancer. For stomach cancer, this means an age-standardized incidence rate above 20 cases per 100,000 people; for esophageal cancer, above 15 cases per 100,000. Second, a parent, child, or sibling has had the cancer in question. Third, they test positive for Helicobacter pylori; this condition applies only to stomach cancer. Fourth, they smoke, drink heavily, eat a high-salt diet, or often eat pickled foods; for esophageal cancer, often consuming very hot foods or drinks is also included. Fifth, they have had conditions such as atrophic gastritis, a stomach ulcer, stomach polyps, Barrett's esophagus, or reflux esophagitis. Screening is generally for ages 45 to 74. Upper endoscopy is preferred and, in principle, is done once every five years. The 2022 national guidelines explicitly recommend against stomach cancer screening for people outside the high-risk group. A study in six high-incidence areas of China followed about 637,500 people aged 40 to 69. Compared with people who were not invited for screening, those who had one upper endoscopy had about a 57% lower risk of dying from upper gastrointestinal cancer. The original estimate was RR 0.43, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.40 to 0.47. The incidence of upper gastrointestinal cancer was about 23% lower (RR 0.77). Only 33.53% of those invited actually had the procedure. Counting everyone who was invited, deaths were about 31% lower (RR 0.69, 95% CI 0.66 to 0.72). Another study was conducted in villages with high rates of esophageal cancer. It did not use random assignment and followed people for 10 years. Cumulative deaths from esophageal squamous cell carcinoma were 3.35% in the screening group and 5.05% in the control group. In South Korea's national screening program, people who had an upper endoscopy were about 47% less likely to die from stomach cancer. The original estimate was OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.51 to 0.56. No difference was apparent for people who had a barium study (OR 0.98). The more upper endoscopies people had, the lower their risk. Pooling 10 Asian studies, stomach cancer deaths were about 40% lower among people who had an upper endoscopy. The original estimate was RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.49 to 0.73. There was no apparent change in the number of people developing stomach cancer. A village-randomized trial in northern China enrolled 33,800 people aged 45 to 69 and followed them for nine years. Among people assigned to the screening group, esophageal cancer deaths were about 18% lower (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.53 to 1.26), a result still within the margin of error. Incidence was about 19% lower (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.60 to 1.09), also not statistically significant. A 2023 meta-analysis adjusted for the bias that people who voluntarily get screened may already be healthier. Among people who actually had an upper endoscopy, stomach cancer deaths were about 48% lower (RR 0.52, confidence interval 0.39 to 0.79). Across the entire screening program, the estimate was only RR 0.94 (confidence interval 0.71 to 1.28), with no discernible effect (China / South Korea / Asia).

entries.notes: Controversies. Most evidence showing gastroscopy reduces mortality compares people who voluntarily underwent screening with those who did not. People who voluntarily go for checkups are inherently more health-conscious, which inflates the apparent benefits. A 2023 meta-analysis assessed the risk of bias in these studies as moderate to serious. In the cluster-randomized trial by village for esophageal cancer, the difference in mortality after 9 years remained within the margin of error. The harms listed in the 2022 guidelines include overdiagnosis, false positives, and missed diagnoses, as well as bleeding, perforation, cardiopulmonary events, aspiration pneumonia, and infection. Overdiagnosis refers to detecting cancer that would never cause symptoms or problems in a person's lifetime. For those who cannot tolerate standard gastroscopy, the protocol specifies that it can be performed under anesthesia or sedation. People aged 45 and older who test positive for Helicobacter pylori are considered at high risk for gastric cancer by default. For eradication, see Item 23 (Test for Helicobacter pylori and eradicate if positive); however, eradication cannot replace gastroscopy—both are required. The protocol does not recommend barium meals, standalone pepsinogen testing, tumor markers, or PET scans for screening. For tumor marker panels, see Section 6, Item 7 (Whole-body PET-CT and tumor marker panels). For those diagnosed with atrophic gastritis, intestinal metaplasia, or intraepithelial neoplasia, follow-up examinations should be more frequent, as directed by a doctor. To find out whether your county of residence is considered a high-risk area, you can consult the local center for disease control and prevention or county hospital. If you are already experiencing difficulty swallowing, hematemesis (vomiting blood), or melena (black stools), you need medical treatment, not screening; see Section 34, Item 6 (Go directly to the hospital for difficulty swallowing, hematemesis, or melena). For those who like drinking very hot tea, see Section 2, Item 30 (Let hot drinks cool a bit before drinking). The beneficiaries are primarily yourself, and also include your parents.

entries.title: Consume soaked wood ear and snow fungus within the same meal without leaving them overnight; eat fresh wet rice noodles like hefen and changfen on the day of purchase; do not make fermented cornflour products at home
entries.cost: Costs no money. Only soak as much wood ear or snow fungus as you will eat, and discard any leftovers. Only buy the amount of wet rice noodles you can finish on the same day. The difficulty lies in being reluctant to throw away extra soaked mushrooms, and in some households' habit of making homemade suantangzi (fermented sour corn noodles).
entries.summary: Wood ear and snow fungus soaked for too long, wet rice noodles kept for too long, and cornflour fermented at home can produce a toxin called bongkrekic acid. It cannot be eliminated by boiling, and there is no antidote. In China over an eleven-year period, approximately 30% of people who fell ill from this poisoning died.
entries.benefit: In the national foodborne disease outbreak surveillance, a total of 19 bongkrekic acid poisoning outbreaks were reported from 2010 to 2020. These involved 146 illnesses, 43 deaths, and a case-fatality rate of 29.5% (meaning 29.5% of people who fell ill died). Broken down by food item: 9 outbreaks from homemade fermented cornflour products, with 33 deaths; 5 outbreaks from wet rice noodles, with 7 deaths; 3 outbreaks from wood ear mushrooms, with 5 illnesses and 3 deaths. In 2020, 143 deaths from food poisoning were reported nationwide, with bongkrekic acid accounting for 12 deaths. Those ranked ahead of it were poisonous mushrooms (80 deaths) and methanol (14 deaths). A risk alert from the Beijing Municipal Administration for Market Regulation states: Bongkrekic acid cannot be destroyed by 100°C boiling or pressure cooker steaming, and there is currently no specific antidote. Since 2018, Guangdong has required wet rice noodles to be sealed in small packages with clearly marked expiration dates. Comparing before and after, the average annual number of cases in the province dropped from 6.25 to 0.5.
entries.sources: Zhang H 等 (2023). Epidemiology of foodborne bongkrekic acid poisoning outbreaks in China, 2010 to 2020. PLoS One 18(1):e0279957:「From 2010–2020, a total of 19 BA poisoning outbreaks were reported to the China National Foodborne Disease Outbreak Surveillance System. These outbreaks involved 146 illnesses, 139 hospitalizations, and 43 deaths, with a case-fatality rate of 29.5%.」<https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0279957> ; Li H 等 (2021). Characteristics of Settings and Etiologic Agents of Foodborne Disease Outbreaks — China, 2020. China CDC Weekly 3(42):889-893. <https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2021.219> ; Yuan Y 等 (2020). A Foodborne Bongkrekic Acid Poisoning Incident — Heilongjiang Province, 2020. China CDC Weekly 2(51):975-978:「In October 2020, 9 persons in Jidong County, Heilongjiang Province died after consuming a homemade fermented corn flour product — sour soup — with a case fatality rate of 100%.」<https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2020.264> ; Liu Z 等 (2026). Controlling the Storage Time Is an Effective Measure to Reduce the Risk of Bongkrekic Acid Poisoning Caused by Wet Rice Noodles. Foodborne Pathog Dis 23(7):468-472 (online first 2025-05-12):「The annual average number of BKA poisoning cases in Guangdong Province dropped from 6.25 before implementing the code to 0.5 after implementing the code.」<https://doi.org/10.1089/fpd.2024.0131> ; Beijing Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (2023). Risk Alert on Food Poisoning Caused by Bongkrekic Acid: \"Bongkrekic acid is heat-stable and cannot be destroyed even after boiling at 100°C or pressure cooking.\" \"Currently, there is no specific antidote for bongkrekic acid.\" \"Snow fungus, wood ear, and their processed products soaked overnight must not be consumed.\" \"Mushrooms that have lost their shape, are sticky, have lost elasticity, or have an off-odor must not be consumed.\" \"Induce vomiting as soon as possible to discharge stomach contents and reduce toxin absorption; seek timely treatment at a hospital.\" <https://scjgj.beijing.gov.cn/hdjl/xfts/202309/t20230904_3248296.html> ; Hunan Provincial Administration for Market Regulation (2025). [Food Safety Science Communication] Deadly Bongkrekic Acid Warning: \"Soak snow fungus in cold water (room temperature) for 3–4 hours, and soak wood ear in cold water for 1–2 hours, changing water 1–2 times during the process to remove microorganisms; the maximum soaking time must not exceed 8 hours for either.\" \"If snow fungus or wood ear feels sticky to the touch after soaking, has poor elasticity, a sour/foul odor, or if the soaking water is cloudy, it indicates spoilage and should be discarded immediately.\" \"When poisoning occurs, induce vomiting immediately to reduce toxin absorption; preserve as much of the suspected causative food as possible, and seek medical attention promptly.\" \"Anyone who consumed the same food, whether symptomatic or not, should be sent to the hospital for examination.\" <https://amr.hunan.gov.cn/amr/xxx/xtdtx/202506/t20250630_33725786.html> ; Guizhou Provincial Administration for Market Regulation (2023). Food Safety Alert on Guarding Against Bongkrekic Acid Poisoning: \"When purchasing snow fungus, wood ear, and related food products, choose regular channels; do not soak overnight, and process and consume in a timely manner.\" <https://amr.guizhou.gov.cn/zfxxgk/fdzdgknr/tzgg_5626971/tzgg_5626972/202307/t20230728_81318622.html>
entries.notes: In October 2020, members of several families in Jidong County, Jixi City, Heilongjiang Province ate homemade suantangzi (fermented sour corn noodles) for breakfast. All 9 people who ate it died. Soaking wood ear in cold water for one to two hours is sufficient; soaking time guidelines vary across regions, with Hunan specifying no longer than 8 hours at most. If the mushroom pieces are sticky, lack elasticity, have a sour or foul odor, or if the soaking water turns cloudy, discard the entire bowl. If vomiting, dizziness, or general weakness occurs after eating, induce vomiting immediately and bring the leftover food to the hospital. Those who ate the meal together must also be checked, even if they have no symptoms. For wild mushrooms, see Item 5 (Do not eat wild mushrooms).

chapters.title: Don't Die a Slow Death
chapters.intro:
This section includes only two categories of chronic risks: those with a major impact on all-cause mortality, and those supported by solid evidence. Several items are labeled \"Randomized Trial,\" meaning people were randomly divided into two groups for comparison; these results are the most reliable. All remaining figures come from observational studies that merely tracked and recorded data without grouping. Risk ratios calculated in such studies, such as HR and RR, are confounded by two types of interference: these people were different to begin with, and some only adopted the behavior after falling ill. Therefore, these figures indicate only the direction and approximate magnitude of the effect; they do not imply that doing the same will guarantee a reduction of that exact size.

The items in this section are divided into the following blocks by theme, with item numbers in parentheses.

**Tobacco, Alcohol, and Betel Nut**: Quit smoking as early as possible (Item 1), do not smoke at home or in the car (Item 2), get medication before quitting smoking (Item 3), set a quit date (Item 4), visit a smoking cessation clinic or call 12320 (Item 5), consider e-cigarettes only if unable to quit (Item 6), do not chew betel nut (Item 8), drink less or not at all (Item 19), do not quit cold turkey on your own if your hands shake upon stopping (Item 20), count your weekly alcohol consumption accurately (Item 21).

**Things to Eat and Drink Less Of**: Do not drink sugar-sweetened beverages (Item 7), eat less processed meat (Item 18), eat less ultra-processed food (Item 28), do not drink boiling-hot tea or soup (Item 30), throw away the whole package if it gets moldy (Item 46), do not eat raw fish or shrimp made from freshwater species (Item 47).

**Things to Substitute or Eat More Of**: Switch to low-sodium salt (Item 9), eat a small handful of nuts every day (Item 22), replace red meat with fish and poultry (Item 23), replace refined white rice and flour with whole grains (Item 24), drink tea more than three times a week (Item 25), drink three to four cups of coffee every day (Item 26), eat enough to reach 5 servings of fruits and vegetables (Item 27), eat chili peppers more than four times a week (Item 33), drink one or two servings of milk daily (Item 34), no need to give up eggs (Item 35).

**Exercise and Body Weight**: Walk 7,000–8,000 steps a day (Item 11), play racquet sports (Item 14), accumulate fragmented bouts of vigorous physical activity (Item 15), do strength training every week (Item 16), do not sit continuously for too long (Item 17), keep BMI between 20 and 25 (Item 32), count daily dog walking toward your walking volume (Item 44), get screened for prediabetes (Item 45).

**Sleep and Night Shifts**: Sleep around 7 hours each night (Item 13), keep naps within half an hour (Item 37), catch up on sleep the next day after staying up late (Item 38), transfer away from night-shift positions as early as possible (Item 39).

**Kitchen Cooking Oil and Smoke**: Do not burn coal or firewood for cooking or heating (Item 29), do not buy unpackaged custom-pressed peanut oil (Item 40), replace lard and butter with vegetable oil (Item 41), turn on the range hood when stir-frying (Item 42).

**Dental Care, Medication, and Other Habits**: Brush thoroughly and clean between teeth (Item 10), take medication regularly as prescribed by your doctor (Item 12), go outside and get some sunshine during the day (Item 31), take baths if conditions permit (Item 36), get evaluated for hormone therapy for perimenopausal hot flashes (Item 43).

entries.title: Quit smoking, the earlier the better
entries.cost: Costs no money; in fact, it saves money. A pack of cigarettes a day costs around 20–30 CNY; quitting saves this money. The difficulty lies in enduring the withdrawal phase, which typically lasts several weeks to several months.
entries.summary: In US studies, people who smoke live on average more than ten years less than those who do not. Quitting before age 40 eliminates about 90% of the excess mortality risk associated with continued smoking. The earlier you quit, the more years you regain. Continuing to smoke after a fracture increases the odds of nonunion by approximately 2.3 times compared to not smoking, so do not smoke before the bone has properly healed.
entries.benefit: A US cohort study that tracked a group of people (observational, non-randomized) found that current smokers have a life expectancy more than 10 years shorter than never-smokers. Quitting before age 40 eliminates approximately 90% of the excess mortality risk caused by continuing to smoke. Quitting at ages 25–34 gains about 10 years of life, at ages 35–44 about 9 years, and at ages 45–54 about 6 years (reported as life-years in the original text). Similar research in China showed: in the 2010s, the mortality risk for urban male smokers was 1.65 times that of non-smokers (RR 1.65), and for rural males it was 1.22 times. After voluntarily quitting smoking for a full 10 years, the excess risk associated with smoking nearly disappeared. The same applies after fractures. Pooling 19 observational, non-randomized studies, the odds of fracture nonunion (the bone failing to heal) in smokers were approximately 2.3 times those in non-smokers (OR 2.32, 95% CI 1.76–3.06, adjusted for other factors). The risk was also elevated in tibial fractures and open fractures. In a Swedish randomized controlled trial, among 50 patients who participated in a 6-week smoking cessation program following emergency fracture surgery, 20% developed at least one postoperative complication, compared to 38% among the 55 patients who did not participate. For scheduled surgeries, smoking cessation can be initiated 4 to 8 weeks before surgery, with weekly counseling and nicotine replacement therapy. Doing so lowers postoperative complications by about 58% (RR 0.42, 95% CI 0.27–0.65, 2 trials, 210 participants).
entries.sources: Jha P 等 (2013). 21st-century hazards of smoking and benefits of cessation in the United States. NEJM. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMsa1211128> ; Chen Z 等 (2015). Contrasting male and female trends in tobacco-attributed mortality in China: evidence from successive nationwide prospective cohort studies. Lancet. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(15)00340-2> ; Oberg M 等 (2011). Worldwide burden of disease from exposure to second-hand smoke: a retrospective analysis of data from 192 countries. Lancet. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(10)61388-8> (the two figures for secondhand smoke); Scolaro JA 等 (2014). Cigarette smoking increases complications following fracture: a systematic review. J Bone Joint Surg Am. <https://doi.org/10.2106/JBJS.M.00081> ; Nåsell H 等 (2010). Effect of smoking cessation intervention on results of acute fracture surgery: a randomized controlled trial. J Bone Joint Surg Am. <https://doi.org/10.2106/JBJS.I.00627> ; Thomsen T 等 (2014). Interventions for preoperative smoking cessation. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD002294.pub4> (the figures for fractures and surgery)
entries.notes: Inhaling other people's smoke also kills: in 2004, approximately 603,000 deaths worldwide were attributable to secondhand smoke, accounting for about 1% of total global deaths that year. Even if you do not smoke yourself, stay away from other people's smoke, and especially keep children from inhaling it. For how to quit, specific methods are detailed in the following four items: Item 3 (Smoking cessation medications), Item 4 (Set a quit date), Item 5 (Visit a smoking cessation clinic), Item 6 (E-cigarettes). The figure on fracture nonunion comes from observational, non-randomized studies; smokers may also differ from non-smokers in other aspects that cannot be entirely adjusted for. The smoking cessation trial after fracture surgery included only 105 participants. When the authors recalculated using an odds ratio, the difference was no longer statistically significant (OR 2.51, 95% CI 0.96–6.9).

entries.title: Do not smoke at home or in the car, and do not let guests smoke inside the home
entries.cost: Costs no money and takes no time. The difficulty lies in speaking up to ask family members and guests not to smoke at home.
entries.summary: In 2004, approximately 600,000 people worldwide died from inhaling other people's smoke, nearly 30% of whom were children. People exposed to secondhand smoke have around a 30% higher risk of hypertension, heart disease, and stroke. Secondhand smoke inhaled at home is more harmful than that inhaled outdoors.
entries.benefit: In 2004, 603,000 people worldwide died from secondhand smoke, about 1.0% of all deaths worldwide; 28% of those who died were children. Pooling 57 studies, people exposed to secondhand smoke had about 1.28 times the odds of developing hypertension as those who were not exposed (odds ratio). The odds ratios were 1.39 for heart disease, 1.50 for myocardial infarction, and 1.36 for stroke. The risk from secondhand smoke exposure at home was higher than the risk from exposure outside the home.
entries.sources: Öberg M, Jaakkola MS, Woodward A, Peruga A, Prüss-Ustün A (2011). Worldwide burden of disease from exposure to second-hand smoke: a retrospective analysis of data from 192 countries. Lancet: “603,000 deaths were attributable to second-hand smoke in 2004, which was about 1·0% of worldwide mortality. 47% of deaths from second-hand smoke occurred in women, 28% in children, and 26% in men”; “61% of DALYs were in children”. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(10)61388-8>; (2026). The Associations Between Secondhand Smoke Exposure and Various Cardiovascular Diseases: A Meta-Analysis. Nicotine & Tobacco Research: 57 studies; “hypertension (OR: 1.28, 95% CI: 1.15 to 1.40), heart disease (OR: 1.39, 95% CI: 1.28 to 1.50), myocardial infarction (OR: 1.50, 95% CI: 1.17 to 1.84), stroke (OR: 1.36, 95% CI: 1.18 to 1.54)”; “Home exposure has a higher risk of CVD than non-home exposure”. <https://doi.org/10.1093/ntr/ntaf111>
entries.notes: Start with the home, because people spend a long time there, and pooled results from multiple studies show that secondhand smoke exposure at home is more harmful than exposure outside the home. Children bear 61% of the health burden caused by secondhand smoke. For quitting smoking yourself, see item 1 of this section.

entries.title: Don’t rely on willpower alone to quit smoking; get medication first: varenicline can more than double your chance of success
entries.cost: Nicotine patches and gum are available over the counter at pharmacies. An 8- to 12-week course costs from several hundred yuan to more than 1,000 yuan. Varenicline and bupropion require a prescription from a smoking cessation clinic or respiratory medicine department. This cost is roughly offset by the cigarettes you do not buy over the same period.
entries.summary: The proportion of people who successfully quit with varenicline is more than twice that with a placebo. With nicotine replacement products such as patches and gum, it is about 50% higher than with no medication. Using patches and gum together raises it by more than another 20%.
entries.benefit: Pooling 41 randomized trials involving 17,395 people, the smoking cessation success rate in the varenicline group was 2.32 times that in the placebo group (RR 2.32, 95% CI 2.15–2.51; this is the confidence interval; high-certainty evidence). Varenicline also performed better than bupropion (RR 1.36, about 36% higher) and a single nicotine replacement product (RR 1.25, about 25% higher). For nicotine replacement products versus no medication, 133 trials involving 64,640 people found a success rate about 55% higher (RR 1.55, 95% CI 1.49–1.61). Adding a fast-acting form (gum or lozenges) to a patch raised the success rate by about 27% compared with using just one form (RR 1.27, 95% CI 1.17–1.37; 16 trials, 12,169 people; high-certainty evidence). Side effects: compared with placebo, the proportion of people taking varenicline who experienced nausea was about 2.6 times as high (RR 2.61); insomnia was about 37% more common (RR 1.37), and vivid dreams were also more common. The review says nausea is the most common side effect; most cases are mild to moderate and generally subside gradually. The instructions for one nicotine patch sold in the United States specify a three-step dose reduction: use a 21 mg patch for 6 weeks, then a 14 mg patch for 2 weeks, then a 7 mg patch for 2 weeks, and then stop.
entries.sources: Livingstone-Banks J, Fanshawe TR, Thomas KH, et al. (2023). Nicotine receptor partial agonists for smoking cessation. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 5, CD006103. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD006103.pub8>; Hartmann-Boyce J, Chepkin SC, Ye W, Bullen C, Lancaster T (2018). Nicotine replacement therapy versus control for smoking cessation. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 5, CD000146. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD000146.pub5>; Theodoulou A, Chepkin SC, Ye W, et al. (2023). Different doses, durations and modes of delivery of nicotine replacement therapy for smoking cessation. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 6, CD013308. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD013308.pub2>; Shanghai Municipal Health Commission (2021). Choose the Right Medication to Make Quitting Smoking a Little Easier: “There are mainly three types of smoking cessation medication available on the market: nicotine replacement therapy medications, bupropion, and varenicline”; “Nicotine replacement therapy medications are over-the-counter (OTC) drugs and can be bought at a pharmacy counter; bupropion and varenicline are prescription drugs and can only be obtained after visiting a hospital smoking cessation clinic or respiratory medicine department, with a doctor’s prescription dispensed by a pharmacist”. <https://wsjkw.sh.gov.cn/jtyx/20211119/df50681e01ba49f896d54f771d8176ae.html>; Haleon (2025). NICODERM CQ (nicotine) patch, extended release. DailyMed prescribing information: “use according to the following 10-week schedule: STEP 1 … 21 mg patch/day … Weeks 1-6 … 14 mg … Weeks 7-8 … 7 mg … Weeks 9-10”. <https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=93b2d1b9-83c1-40b5-b6af-90c38c8d6cef> (for the sentence about reducing the patch dose)
entries.notes: The smoking cessation medications sold in China fall into the three categories above, and only nicotine replacement products are available over the counter. Common reactions to varenicline are nausea, vivid dreams, and poor sleep. Tell your doctor if you have a history of psychiatric illness; this is the author’s recommendation. A course of nicotine replacement therapy generally lasts 8 to 12 weeks. Reduce the patch dose step by step according to the instructions or your doctor’s advice before stopping. Medication addresses the discomfort of withdrawal during those first few weeks, but it does not address situations that make you want to smoke. So use it together with item 4 of this section (set a quit date) and item 5 (visit a smoking cessation clinic).

entries.title: Set a quit date and stop smoking all at once on that day; don’t taper off first
entries.cost: Free. Just choose a day on the calendar and tell your family and coworkers in advance.
entries.summary: Many people plan to smoke a few fewer cigarettes each day and gradually cut down to zero. But by the sixth month, 22% of those who set a date and stopped all at once had not smoked again, compared with only 15.5% of those who cut down gradually. So set a date and stop all at once when it arrives.
entries.benefit: In the United Kingdom, 697 smokers were randomly divided into two groups. One group stopped smoking all at once on their quit date; the other reduced their smoking by 75% over the two weeks before their quit date. Both groups received behavioral support from nurses and used nicotine replacement products before and after the quit date. At week 4, 49.0% of the group that stopped all at once (95% CI 43.8–54.2; this is the confidence interval) had not relapsed, compared with 39.2% of the gradual-reduction group (34.0–44.4), for a relative risk of 0.80 (0.66–0.93). By month 6, the figures were 22.0% (18.0–26.6) for the group that stopped all at once and 15.5% (12.0–19.7) for the gradual-reduction group, for a relative risk of 0.71 (0.46–0.91). At week 4, people who had already preferred to cut down gradually also had a lower success rate than those who preferred to stop all at once (38.3% versus 52.2%).
entries.sources: Lindson-Hawley N, Banting M, West R, Michie S, Shinkins B, Aveyard P (2016). Gradual Versus Abrupt Smoking Cessation: A Randomized, Controlled Noninferiority Trial. Annals of Internal Medicine, 164(9), 585–592. <https://doi.org/10.7326/M14-2805>; Theodoulou A, Chepkin SC, Ye W, et al. (2023). Different doses, durations and modes of delivery of nicotine replacement therapy for smoking cessation. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 6, CD013308 (the section on starting nicotine replacement products in advance). <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD013308.pub2>
entries.notes: There is debate. An earlier Cochrane review specifically comparing these two approaches concluded that they were about equally effective (RR 0.94, 95% CI 0.79–1.13; 10 trials, 3,760 people), but that review was withdrawn in 2019 and is no longer updated. So the best evidence currently available is the randomized trial above, which favors stopping all at once. Both groups in that trial also started using nicotine replacement products before their quit date. That practice has evidence of its own: starting in advance raised the success rate by about 25% compared with starting on the quit date (RR 1.25, 95% CI 1.08–1.44; 9 trials, 4,395 people; moderate-certainty evidence). So a reasonable schedule is to set a date, start using a patch two weeks beforehand, and stop smoking all at once on that date.

entries.title: Visit a smoking cessation clinic, or call China’s 12320 health consultation hotline to ask about local smoking cessation services
entries.cost: One clinic registration costs from a few yuan to a few dozen yuan. Behavioral support generally consists of 4 to 8 sessions lasting half an hour to an hour each, usually totaling no more than 5 hours. Calling the hotline is free.
entries.summary: Medication and having someone check in with you regularly are two separate forms of help; they work better together. The proportion who successfully quit among people taking medication and receiving follow-up from a dedicated person is nearly twice that among people given only brief advice. Telephone support counts too: multiple proactive follow-up calls from a smoking cessation hotline raise the success rate by about 25% to nearly 40%.
entries.benefit: Pooling 52 trials involving 19,488 people, the smoking cessation success rate with medication plus behavioral support was 1.83 times that with usual care or brief advice (RR 1.83, 95% CI 1.68–1.98; this is the confidence interval; high-quality evidence). In the 43 trials that recruited participants in healthcare settings, it was 1.97 times as high (1.79–2.18). Looking at telephone counseling separately: among people who had called a smoking cessation hotline themselves, those who received multiple proactive follow-up calls had a success rate about 38% higher than those who only received materials or had a single conversation (RR 1.38, 95% CI 1.19–1.61; 14 trials, 32,484 people). Among people who had not called a hotline themselves and were offered telephone counseling by the researchers, the rate was about 25% higher (RR 1.25, 95% CI 1.15–1.35; 65 trials, 41,233 people). Both findings are based on moderate-certainty evidence.
entries.sources: Stead LF, Koilpillai P, Fanshawe TR, Lancaster T (2016). Combined pharmacotherapy and behavioural interventions for smoking cessation. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 3, CD008286. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD008286.pub3>; Matkin W, Ordóñez-Mena JM, Hartmann-Boyce J (2019). Telephone counselling for smoking cessation. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 5, CD002850. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD002850.pub4>; Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention (2021). “China Smoking Cessation Platform” WeChat Mini Program Officially Launched: “Under the guidance of the Tobacco Control Action Working Group of the Healthy China Initiative, the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention and the World Health Organization Representative Office in China jointly created the ‘China Smoking Cessation Platform’ WeChat mini program, an authoritative Chinese repository of smoking cessation resources. Its main content includes detailed information on smoking cessation hotlines and clinics, as well as online smoking cessation service resources”; the footer of the same website lists “Health consultation telephone number: 12320”. <https://www.chinacdc.cn/jkyj/yckz/gzdt/202203/t20220310_296389.html>
entries.notes: How to find services in China: search WeChat for the “China Smoking Cessation Platform” mini program, which lists smoking cessation hotlines and clinics around the country; you can also call China’s 12320 health consultation hotline to ask whether there is a local smoking cessation clinic. Most of the trials above were conducted outside China, and the level of service provided by smoking cessation clinics varies greatly by location, so treat the figures as an indication of the general direction. For medication to use alongside the support, see item 3 of this section (smoking cessation medications).

entries.title: Consider e-cigarettes only if you still cannot quit; if you have never smoked, stay away from them
entries.cost: A device and cartridges cost from a few dozen to several hundred yuan per month. In China, only tobacco-flavored products may be purchased, and only from stores with a tobacco monopoly retail license.
entries.summary: Switching from cigarettes to nicotine-containing e-cigarettes results in about 60% more people quitting than using nicotine replacement products; the evidence for this is highly reliable. But there is still insufficient safety data on long-term use, so do not assume they are harmless. These trials all compared people who wanted to quit smoking; if you have never smoked, stay away from e-cigarettes.
entries.benefit: A continuously updated review included 80 randomized trials involving 29,861 people. Compared with nicotine replacement therapy, nicotine-containing e-cigarettes raised the smoking cessation success rate by about 61% (RR 1.61, 95% CI 1.23–2.12; this is the confidence interval; high-certainty evidence, 11 trials, 4,114 people). In absolute terms, about 4 more people per 100 successfully quit (1 to 7 more people). The proportions experiencing serious adverse events were roughly the same in the two groups (risk difference 0.01, 95% CI −0.01 to 0.02; moderate-certainty evidence). Compared with behavioral support alone or no support, the success rate was about 75% higher (RR 1.75, 95% CI 1.39–2.20; low-certainty evidence).
entries.sources: Lindson N, Livingstone-Banks J, Butler AR, et al. (2026). Electronic cigarettes for smoking cessation. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 8, CD010216. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD010216.pub11>; State Tobacco Monopoly Administration (2022). Measures for the Administration of Electronic Cigarettes (State Tobacco Monopoly Administration Announcement No. 1 of 2022, effective May 1, 2022), Article 18: Anyone engaging in the retail sale of electronic cigarettes must apply to the tobacco monopoly administrative authority for a tobacco monopoly retail license. Article 22: “The sale of electronic cigarette products to minors is prohibited.” Article 23, paragraph 2: “No individual, legal person, or other organization may sell electronic cigarette products, aerosolized substances, or nicotine for electronic cigarettes through information networks other than the electronic cigarette trading management platform specified in these Measures.” Article 26: “The sale of flavored electronic cigarettes other than tobacco-flavored ones, and electronic cigarettes to which users can add aerosolized substances themselves, is prohibited.” <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2022/content_5697988.htm>; World Health Organization (2023-12-14). Urgent action needed to protect children and prevent the uptake of e-cigarettes: “E-cigarettes as consumer products are not shown to be effective for quitting tobacco use at the population level”; “it is not recommended that governments permit sale of e-cigarettes as consumer products in pursuit of a cessation objective”; “Whilst long-term health effects are not fully understood”. <https://www.who.int/news/item/14-12-2023-urgent-action-needed-to-protect-children-and-prevent-the-uptake-of-e-cigarettes>; Department of Health and Social Care (2023-04-11). Smokers urged to swap cigarettes for vapes in world first scheme: “almost 1 in 5 of all smokers in England will be provided with a vape starter kit alongside behavioural support”. <https://www.gov.uk/government/news/smokers-urged-to-swap-cigarettes-for-vapes-in-world-first-scheme>; Supreme People’s Procuratorate of China (2021). Suzhou’s Wujiang District, Jiangsu: Prosecutors reveal a new type of drug disguised as a trendy product: “These ‘get-high’ electronic cigarettes contain synthetic cannabinoids, a class of substances placed under control in its entirety by the state.” <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/zdgz/202110/t20211011_531831.shtml>
entries.notes: Controversy. In 2023, the World Health Organization said there was no evidence that selling electronic cigarettes as ordinary consumer products helps people quit smoking at the population level. It does not recommend that governments allow their sale for smoking cessation; if they are used for that purpose, they should be regulated as medicines. It also said their long-term health effects are not fully understood and expressed concern that children and young people might start using them. England took the opposite approach starting in 2023, giving about one million smokers vape starter kits along with smoking cessation support. China has not banned all electronic cigarette sales, but regulates them strictly under the Measures for the Administration of Electronic Cigarettes. Only tobacco-flavored products may be sold; fruit-flavored products and those to which users can add e-liquid themselves may not be sold. They can be bought only in physical stores holding tobacco monopoly retail licenses. Apart from sales through the nationally designated electronic cigarette trading management platform, selling them on other websites, online stores, or social media apps is illegal. They may not be sold to minors either. So fruit-flavored electronic cigarettes that are still available come through illegal channels and fall outside regulatory oversight. That is how ‘get-high electronic cigarettes’ adulterated with synthetic cannabinoids have circulated; see Section 22, Item 4 (do not accept a vape cartridge offered by someone else). The products tested in the review were regulated nicotine-containing products; e-liquids of unknown origin were not included. As for which to try first, start with Item 3 of this section (smoking cessation medication): the evidence for it is stronger, and it is cheaper.

entries.title: Stop drinking sugary beverages; switching to sugar-free ones does not solve the problem
entries.cost: It costs nothing and takes no time. Switching to plain water or unsweetened tea also saves money. The hard part is breaking the habit of drinking sweet beverages, including sugar-free ones.
entries.summary: In US studies, people who drank more than two servings of sweetened beverages a day were about 20% more likely to die during the study period than people who almost never drank them. Those who drank one to two servings a day were more than 10% more likely to die. Switching to sugar-free drinks showed no benefit either: people who drank more than two glasses of artificially sweetened beverages a day were instead about 25% more likely to die.
entries.benefit: Two large US studies followed groups of people. Both were observational, with no assignment to groups, and covered about 118,000 people and 36,000 deaths. People who drank more than 2 servings a day had about a 21% higher risk of death than those who drank less than 1 serving a month (HR 1.21). For those who drank 1–2 servings a day, the risk was about 14% higher (HR 1.14). The European EPIC follow-up study was also observational, with no assignment to groups, and covered 450,000 people in 10 countries. Comparing people who drank more than 2 glasses a day with those who drank less than 1 glass a month, the risk was about 8% higher for sugar-sweetened soft drinks (HR 1.08, 95% CI 1.01–1.16), about 26% higher for artificially sweetened beverages (the sugar-free versions; HR 1.26, 1.16–1.35), and about 17% higher for all soft drinks combined (HR 1.17, 1.11–1.22).
entries.sources: Malik VS et al. (2019). Long-Term Consumption of Sugar-Sweetened and Artificially Sweetened Beverages and Risk of Mortality in US Adults. Circulation. <https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.118.037401>; Mullee A, Romaguera D, Pearson-Stuttard J, et al. (2019). Association Between Soft Drink Consumption and Mortality in 10 European Countries. JAMA Internal Medicine, 179(11), 1479-1490. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamainternmed.2019.2478>
entries.notes: The controversy concerns sugar-free drinks. The association for artificially sweetened beverages was even stronger than for sugary ones. This is quite possibly reverse causation: people who were already overweight or had diabetes may have switched to sugar-free versions. So do not conclude from this that artificial sweeteners are more toxic. But it does show, at a minimum, that there is no evidence to support the claim that ‘switching to sugar-free means there is nothing to worry about.’ Switching to plain water or unsweetened tea is the safest bet. Also, these studies only followed and recorded people; they did not assign them to groups in a trial. People who drink more sweetened beverages may already have less healthy lifestyles, so the figures may be too high.

entries.title: Do not chew betel nut
entries.cost: It costs nothing and takes no time, and saves the money you would spend on betel nut. The hard part is giving up the habit of chewing it.
entries.summary: People who chew betel nut are about 20% more likely to die during the same period than those who do not. Their risks of diabetes and metabolic syndrome are about 50% higher. The risks of oral and esophageal cancer are additional.
entries.benefit: A combined analysis of 17 Asian studies covered 388,000 people. The risk of death among people who chewed betel nut was about 21% higher than among those who did not (relative risk 1.21, P=0.02). The death analysis included 179,600 of those people. The risk of developing diabetes was about 47% higher (1.47), and the risk of developing metabolic syndrome was about 51% higher (1.51). Betel nut itself is also a known risk factor for oral and esophageal cancer. Oral cancer: a combined analysis of 50 studies found that, in the Indian subcontinent, chewing betel nut without tobacco was associated with about 2.56 times the risk of oral and oropharyngeal cancer compared with not chewing it (95% CI 2.00–3.28). With tobacco added, the risk was about 7.74 times as high (5.38–11.13). In Taiwan, chewing betel nut without tobacco was associated with about 10.98 times the risk (4.86–24.84). In India and Taiwan, the more people chewed each day and the more years they had chewed, the higher their risk. Esophageal cancer: a combined analysis of 12 Asian studies found that people who chewed betel nut had about 3.05 times the risk of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma compared with those who did not (2.41–3.87). For people who both chewed betel nut and smoked, the risk was about 6.79 times as high (4.71–9.79). After quitting: a combined analysis of 13 studies found that people who had stopped chewing betel nut with tobacco had about a 34% lower risk of head and neck cancer than those still chewing it (RR 0.66, 0.54–0.81). Those who had stopped chewing it without tobacco had about a 27% lower risk (RR 0.73, 0.56–0.95). Those who had quit for more than 20 years had about a 63% lower risk (RR 0.37, 0.22–0.61).
entries.sources: Yamada T, Hara K, Kadowaki T (2013). Chewing betel quid and the risk of metabolic disease, cardiovascular disease, and all-cause mortality: a meta-analysis. PLoS One, 8(8), e70679. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0070679>；Guha N, Warnakulasuriya S, Vlaanderen J, Straif K (2014). Betel quid chewing and the risk of oral and oropharyngeal cancers: a meta-analysis with implications for cancer control. International Journal of Cancer, 135(6), 1433-1443. <https://doi.org/10.1002/ijc.28643>；Akhtar S (2013). Areca nut chewing and esophageal squamous-cell carcinoma risk in Asians: a meta-analysis of case-control studies. Cancer Causes & Control, 24(2), 257-265. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10552-012-0113-9>；Shah K, Boffetta P, Seyyedsalehi MS (2025). Reversal of head and neck cancer risk after the cessation of use of smokeless tobacco and betel quid use: meta-analysis. Cancer Epidemiology, Biomarkers & Prevention, 34(5), 619-626. <https://doi.org/10.1158/1055-9965.EPI-24-1502>
entries.notes: The more years people chew and the more they chew each day, the higher their risk of oral cancer. After quitting, the risk falls over time. In studies from India, betel nut with tobacco was more dangerous than betel nut without it. Most betel nut chewed in Taiwan does not contain tobacco, yet the risk is still very high.

entries.title: Replace the salt at home with low-sodium salt (potassium salt)
entries.cost: A bag costs a few yuan more than ordinary salt. Simply switch when buying salt; it takes no extra time. The taste is almost unchanged.
entries.summary: Among people in rural China who had had a stroke or were over 60 and had high blood pressure, those whose households switched to low-sodium salt were about 12% less likely to die and about 14% less likely to have a stroke over nearly five years.
entries.benefit: A randomized trial in rural China included 20,995 people, all of whom had had a stroke or were over 60 and had high blood pressure. They were followed for 4.74 years. Compared with the group using ordinary salt, the group using low-sodium salt had about a 12% lower risk of death (RR 0.88), about a 14% lower risk of stroke (RR 0.86), and about a 13% lower risk of major cardiovascular events (RR 0.87). There was no statistically detectable difference between the groups in events involving excessively high blood potassium.
entries.sources: Neal B et al. (2021). Effect of Salt Substitution on Cardiovascular Events and Death. NEJM. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2105675>; O'Donnell M et al. (2014). Urinary sodium and potassium excretion, mortality, and cardiovascular events. NEJM. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1311889> (the contrasting PURE study)
entries.notes: Controversy. The PURE study only followed and recorded people over a long period; it did not assign them to groups. It reported that people who excreted less than 3 g of sodium a day had about a 27% higher risk of death or a cardiovascular event. Those who excreted more than 7 g a day had about a 15% higher risk. According to its results, too little and too much are both undesirable, and the middle range is best. But in the randomized trial in rural China cited here, low-sodium salt replaced only part of the sodium; it would not push sodium that low. Also note that the trial participants were older people at high risk. The benefit of switching salt for healthy young people would be much smaller. People with impaired kidney function, or who are taking potassium-sparing medications, should ask a doctor before switching salt.

entries.title: Brush your teeth thoroughly, clean between them once a day, and see a dentist if you have missing teeth
entries.cost: Dental floss or interdental brushes cost a few dozen yuan a year, and a professional dental cleaning costs one or two hundred yuan each time. Allow an extra two or three minutes a day. The hard part is making cleaning between your teeth a daily habit. If you cannot clean your teeth thoroughly with a manual toothbrush, you can switch to an electric one. It costs a few hundred yuan, and the brush head needs regular replacement.
entries.summary: In a Japanese study, people who used dental floss or interdental brushes were about 10% less likely to die during the same period. Older people who had lost all their teeth were about 90% more likely to die; those with fewer than 20 teeth remaining were about twice as likely. Electric toothbrushes remove 10–20% more plaque than manual brushing and reduce gum inflammation somewhat, but it is still unclear how much that difference matters.
entries.benefit: A Japanese study followed 9,676 people for 6 years. People who used tools to clean between their teeth had about an 11% lower risk of death (hazard ratio 0.89). Those who used tongue-cleaning tools had about a 23% lower risk (0.77). Separately, a combined analysis of multiple studies looked at older adults living in the community. Those with no teeth had about 1.87 times the odds of death (odds ratio, 95% CI 1.35–2.59; this is the confidence interval). Those with fewer than 20 teeth had about 2.04 times the odds (1.67–2.49). Electric versus manual toothbrushes: a combined analysis of 51 randomized trials found about 11% less plaque with electric brushes after 1 to 3 months of use and about 21% less after more than 3 months. Gingivitis was about 6% and 11% less severe, respectively. The review authors said it was unclear how important these differences were for health.
entries.sources: Wang K, Matsuyama Y, Kiuchi S, et al. (2026). Routine oral health practices and all-cause mortality. Journal of Dentistry. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jdent.2026.106789>；Ko MJ, Seo S, So JS, et al. (2026). Deteriorated oral health and function as risk factors for physical disability and mortality in community-dwelling older adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis. European Geriatric Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s41999-025-01319-4>；Yaacob M, Worthington HV, Deacon SA, et al. (2014). Powered versus manual toothbrushing for oral health. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD002281.pub3>；Deacon SA, Glenny AM, Deery C, et al. (2010). Different powered toothbrushes for plaque control and gingival health. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD004971.pub2>
entries.notes: Controversy. These studies only followed and recorded people. People with poor dental health often have poorer overall health and financial circumstances too. It is unclear whether poor teeth harm the body or poor health harms the teeth. But the cost of this action is very low, and gum disease and missing teeth themselves affect eating. Among electric toothbrushes, round heads that rotate back and forth have been tested most often (27 trials); compared with manual brushes, they clearly reduced plaque and gingivitis in both the short and long term. No study has tested whether replacing missing teeth reduces deaths. The recommendation to replace them is the author’s judgment, based on how missing teeth affect eating. An independent review did not reach a conclusion about which type of electric toothbrush is better because there were too few trials. For the cost of a dental implant and which dental services China’s medical insurance covers, see Section 24, Item 12 (ask for the all-inclusive price before getting a dental implant).

entries.title: Walk 7,000–8,000 steps a day, or accumulate 150–300 minutes of brisk walking a week
entries.cost: It costs nothing. By step count, walk 60–90 minutes a day; you can fit that into commuting and grocery shopping. By exercise time, allow 20–45 minutes a day. The hard part is keeping it up over the long term.
entries.summary: People who walk around 7,800 steps a day are about 45% less likely to die during the same period than people who walk only 3,500 steps. Measured by time, brisk walking for 150–300 minutes a week is likewise associated with about a 30% lower risk than no exercise. Beyond a certain amount, the risk stops falling; for people over 60, 6,000–8,000 steps are enough. Meeting either target is sufficient.
entries.benefit: A combined analysis of 15 studies that followed groups of people was observational, with no assignment to groups. The 15 studies included 47,471 people and 3,013 deaths. People were divided into four groups by daily step count. The median for the lowest group was 3,553 steps/day; the medians for the other three groups were 5,801, 7,842, and 10,901 steps/day. Compared with the lowest group, their risks of death were about 40%, 45%, and 53% lower, respectively (HR 0.60, 0.55, 0.47). For people over 60, benefits tended to level off after 6,000–8,000 steps.
