entries.notes: The five stimulus control rules in the cost column are taken from the American Academy of Sleep Medicine's 2021 guideline. Sleep restriction involves first compressing your time in bed down to the duration you actually spend asleep, and then gradually adding time back based on sleep efficiency. The guideline notes that it increases daytime sleepiness; people who drive or operate machinery should use it with caution. Those with manic tendencies, uncontrolled epilepsy, or severe pre-existing daytime sleepiness should also use it with caution, ideally with follow-up from a physician. Relying solely on general sleep hygiene education—such as routines, diet, and environment—is ineffective on its own and is not recommended by the guideline. Sleeping poorly for a few nights does not count as insomnia disorder. In such cases, first establish a fixed wake-up time; see item 2 in this section (fixed wake-up time). Then see item 4 (no caffeine after 2:00 PM) and item 8 (no illuminated screens for one hour before bed). For those with loud snoring, gasping during sleep, or severe daytime sleepiness, clinical guidelines require ruling out sleep apnea first. For diagnostic testing methods, see item 27 in this section (sleep apnea). For low mood combined with poor sleep, see item 18 in this section (first steps when experiencing low mood). Sleeping pills are prescription medications; that meta-analysis only examined short-term use in adults aged 60 and older. Benefit rated Moderate: the combined reduction in time to fall asleep and time spent awake during the night is about 45 minutes per night, amounting to hours per week. Total sleep duration barely changed. The paper analyzing 20 trials excluded individuals with insomnia who had comorbid conditions. In China, which hospital department to visit is based on author experience (Grade C) and varies across hospitals; inquire whether this therapy is offered before registering for an appointment. The beneficiary is primarily yourself. Do not expect melatonin to cure chronic insomnia; see Section 6, item 34 (relying on melatonin to cure chronic insomnia).

entries.title: If you snore loudly, have witnessed breathing pauses during sleep, or are sleepy enough during the day to doze off while driving, go to a hospital for sleep monitoring to check for sleep apnea; use a PAP machine at night for moderate to severe cases
entries.cost: Start by visiting a hospital's sleep clinic, respiratory medicine department, or otolaryngology (ENT) department. A definitive diagnosis requires an overnight sleep study (polysomnography), conducted either by sleeping at the hospital or borrowing equipment to wear while sleeping at home. For those who need a PAP machine, the device generally must be purchased out of pocket, which is a considerable expense. The difficulty lies in adherence: you must wear the mask to sleep every night. In the first few weeks, it feels unfamiliar and uncomfortable, and many people take it off after just a few hours.
entries.summary: Sleep apnea occurs when breathing repeatedly stops or becomes shallow during sleep, causing nighttime awakenings and daytime drowsiness. Using a PAP machine significantly reduces daytime sleepiness and cuts car accidents by about 70%. However, trials have not found that it prevents heart disease or reduces mortality; the primary purpose of wearing it is to stay alert during the day.
entries.benefit: The American Academy of Sleep Medicine's 2017 diagnostic guideline outlines who is more likely to have moderate to severe sleep apnea: experiencing excessive daytime sleepiness on most days, plus at least two of the following three criteria: 1) frequent loud snoring; 2) witnessed breathing cessations, gasping, or choking awakenings during sleep; and 3) diagnosed hypertension. The guideline requires using sleep monitoring for a definitive diagnosis rather than questionnaires alone. An apnea-hypopnea index of 5 or more events per hour accompanied by symptoms meets the diagnostic threshold; 15 or more events per hour qualifies regardless of symptoms. The American Academy of Sleep Medicine's 2019 systematic review pooled 38 randomized controlled trials. Compared with no treatment, individuals using a PAP machine saw their self-rated sleepiness score drop by 2.4 points (95% CI 1.9–2.8). This score is based on the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (out of a maximum of 24 points; higher scores indicate greater sleepiness). Looking only at people who were not sleepy to begin with, 5 trials showed a 1.0-point drop, which the authors considered clinically insignificant. The same systematic review pooled 10 pre-and-post treatment studies: following PAP therapy, the motor vehicle crash rate was 0.3 times the pre-treatment rate (RR 0.3, 0.2–0.4), a reduction of about 70%. Another 2010 meta-analysis combining 9 similar studies yielded an RR of 0.278 (0.22–0.35). It also noted that a single night of use produced a marked reduction in daytime sleepiness, and simulated driving performance improved within 2 to 7 days. A 2009 analysis by the same group of authors estimated that untreated patients have roughly 1.21 to 4.89 times the crash risk of others. Regarding cardiac outcomes and lifespan: The SAVE trial enrolled 2,717 patients aged 45 to 75 with moderate-to-severe OSA and established coronary artery disease or prior stroke, following them for an average of 3.7 years post-randomization. Cardiovascular events occurred in 17.0% of the PAP group and 15.4% of the non-PAP group, showing no significant difference between the two groups (HR 1.10, 0.91–1.32). Those in the PAP group wore the device for an average of only 3.3 hours per night; snoring, daytime sleepiness, quality of life, and mood all improved. A 2017 meta-analysis combining 10 randomized trials and 7,266 individuals likewise found no difference in overall mortality (RR 1.13, 0.99–1.29). A 2019 estimation calculated that approximately 176 million people aged 30 to 69 in China have this condition, accounting for 23.6%, of whom about 65.52 million have moderate-to-severe disease (8.8%), representing the highest absolute number of cases in the world.

entries.notes: Controversies: Whether PAP machines prevent heart disease and extend lifespan has not been demonstrated in randomized trials. Participants in SAVE were mostly not particularly sleepy and had low device adherence; however, the 2017 meta-analysis stratified by hours of use and still found no difference. The crash statistics come from pre-and-post treatment comparisons rather than randomized allocation, meaning participants may simply have become more cautious after receiving treatment. China's case numbers are extrapolated solely from a 2005 study of 3,648 participants, and this estimation was funded by a PAP device manufacturer. The US Preventive Services Task Force stated in 2022 that screening asymptomatic individuals has unclear balances of benefits and harms. Therefore, those who do not snore and do not experience daytime sleepiness do not need to seek diagnostic testing specifically. Benefit rated Moderate is an interpretive judgment: a 2.4-point drop on the sleepiness scale did not quantify how many additional hours of daytime alertness are gained each day. Which hospital department to register with is based on author experience (Grade C) and varies across hospitals. If you feel drowsy while driving, pull over first; see Section 1, item 9 (pull over and rest as soon as you feel sleepy). For prolonged daytime sleep, see Section 2, item 37 (investigate the cause if naps exceed one hour). For chronic insomnia, see item 26 in this section (chronic insomnia). The beneficiaries are primarily yourself, alongside passengers sharing your vehicle and other road users.

chapters.title: Don't Waste Time
chapters.intro: This section accounts solely for time. It examines how many hours can be reclaimed per day, per week, or per year, or how much the proportion of tasks completed on schedule can be increased. Time is not converted into lifespan here, nor is it converted into money. Where money is involved, only calculation methods are provided, not conclusions. The evidence for most items in this section comes from single studies or aggregate statistics from time-use surveys, so the evidence grades are primarily B and C.

entries.title: Reframe "planning to do something" into "what to do, at what time, in what place, and upon encountering what"
entries.cost: Free of cost. Spend 1 to 2 minutes on each task writing an "if... then..." statement. For example: "When I sit down at my desk at 8:00 AM on Tuesday, I will write the introduction first."
entries.summary: Reframe "I want to do this task" into "When I sit down at my desk at 8:00 AM on Tuesday, I will write the introduction first." Aggregating across 94 tests, people who formulate plans this way achieve their goals at a markedly higher rate, representing a medium-to-large effect size. It alters only how a single sentence is framed, costing no money and requiring minimal effort.
entries.benefit: Aggregating across 94 independent tests, individuals who pre-formulate their intentions into "if... then..." statements have higher rates of goal attainment. In psychology, this framing is termed implementation intentions. The effect size is d = 0.65, qualifying as medium-to-large. It works across three distinct phases: getting started, holding firm when interrupted, and disengaging from endeavors doomed to fail.
entries.sources: Gollwitzer, P. M., & Sheeran, P. (2006). Implementation intentions and goal achievement: A meta-analysis of effects and processes. Advances in Experimental Social Psychology, 38, 69–119. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0065-2601(06)38002-1>
entries.notes: This approach works only for things you genuinely want to do. If you do not want the goal itself, writing more sentences will not help. Also, most participants in these studies were students, and most of the habits studied concerned health. The approach may not work as well in a work setting.

entries.title: Write down your stopping conditions before you start
entries.cost: Costs nothing. When you start, spend five minutes writing down: “If I have not reached a specified target by a specified date, I will stop.” The hard part is honoring that commitment when the day comes. Stopping in front of others can feel embarrassing.
entries.summary: Before you start, write one sentence: If I have not reached a specified target by a specified date, I will stop. Taken together, multiple studies show that writing such a rule can help people withdraw from efforts that are bound to fail. The time saved is all the time you would otherwise have kept putting into them.
entries.benefit: Taken together, studies of implementation intentions show that a prearranged “if…then…” rule can also help people withdraw from efforts that are bound to fail. The original wording is “disengagement from failing courses of action.” The time saved is the time you would otherwise have continued to put in.
entries.sources: Gollwitzer, P. M., & Sheeran, P. (2006). Implementation intentions and goal achievement: A meta-analysis of effects and processes. Advances in Experimental Social Psychology, 38, 69–119. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0065-2601(06)38002-1>
entries.notes: Set your stopping conditions when you first start, while you are still thinking calmly. Setting them afterward can be distorted by what you have already invested. When deciding, consider only future investment and future returns; see item 3. Also, “willingness to withdraw” is just one finding within a synthesis of multiple studies. No one has separately calculated how much time it saves.

entries.title: When deciding whether to continue, consider only future investment and future returns, not how much you have already invested
entries.cost: Costs nothing. The hard part is accepting that the time you have already put in is gone and cannot be recovered.
entries.summary: Money and time already invested make people more inclined to keep going. Taken together, 98 sets of data show that this tendency consistently occurs. So, when deciding whether to continue, count only how much more you will have to put in and how much you can still get back. Leave out what you have already spent.
entries.benefit: Money, effort, and time already invested make people more inclined to continue. In psychology, this is called the sunk cost effect. An analysis combining 98 sets of data confirmed that this tendency consistently occurs. Avoiding it means you will not keep putting in time just because you “do not want it to go to waste.”
entries.sources: Arkes, H. R., & Blumer, C. (1985). The psychology of sunk cost. Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes, 35, 124–140. <https://doi.org/10.1016/0749-5978(85)90049-4>；Roth, S., Robbert, T., & Straus, L. (2015). On the sunk-cost effect in economic decision-making: A meta-analytic review. Business Research, 8(1), 99–138. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40685-014-0014-8>
entries.notes: Arkes and Blumer’s theater experiment worked like this. A theater at Ohio University sold season tickets and randomly assigned buyers one of three prices: the full price of US$15, a US$2 discount, or a US$7 discount. During the first half of the season, the full price group attended an average of 4.11 performances; the other two groups attended 3.32 and 3.29. In the second half, there was no clear difference among the three groups. Roth and colleagues found that this effect fades over time and affects older people less.

entries.title: Estimate a task’s duration from the actual time similar past tasks took, rather than working forward from your plan
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Before estimating, spend a few minutes checking how long a similar task actually took last time.
entries.summary: Students estimated that they would finish their papers in 33.9 days, but actually took 55.5 days. Only 29.7% finished within the time they had estimated. Another group was asked to recall how long a similar task had taken before making an estimate; the proportion finishing on time rose from 29.3% to 60.0%.
entries.benefit: Students expected to finish their papers in 33.9 days but actually took 55.5 days. Only 29.7% finished within their own estimated time. Researchers asked another group to connect their past experiences to the task at hand before estimating. In this group, the proportion finishing on time rose to 60.0%, from 29.3% in the control group. The optimism that led to underestimating the time needed no longer appeared in this group.
entries.sources: Buehler, R., Griffin, D., & Ross, M. (1994). Exploring the "planning fallacy": Why people underestimate their task completion times. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 67(3), 366–381. <https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.67.3.366>；Flyvbjerg, B. (2006). From Nobel Prize to project management: Getting risks right. Project Management Journal, 37(3), 5–15. <https://doi.org/10.1177/875697280603700302>；Halkjelsvik, T., & Jørgensen, M. (2012). From origami to software development: A review of studies on judgment-based predictions of performance time. Psychological Bulletin, 138(2), 238–271. <https://doi.org/10.1037/a0025996>
entries.notes: Buehler’s study included only Canadian university students. It was a single study with small groups: 37 people and about 40 people per group. Estimating from historical data on similar projects is called reference class forecasting; for details on its use in engineering, see Flyvbjerg. After synthesizing multiple studies, Halkjelsvik noted that underestimation is more common than overestimation, but the size of the difference varies greatly with the task and research method.

entries.title: Send an agenda before a meeting; do not hold meetings without one; stand if you can
entries.cost: Costs nothing. The organizer spends 5 to 10 minutes writing an agenda before the meeting. Standing meetings require participants’ cooperation.
entries.summary: When an agenda is sent beforehand, participants are more likely to feel that the meeting is useful. In an experiment, seated meetings lasted 34% longer than standing meetings, with no difference in the quality of the decisions made.
entries.benefit: Two surveys included 958 and 292 people, respectively. Their results showed that participants were more likely to feel a meeting was effective when an agenda had been sent beforehand, and the association was statistically supported. In another experiment, 55 groups met while seated and 56 groups met while standing. Seated meetings lasted 34% longer. The quality of the decisions did not differ between the two formats.
entries.sources: Leach, D. J., Rogelberg, S. G., Warr, P. B., & Burnfield, J. L. (2009). Perceived meeting effectiveness: The role of design characteristics. Journal of Business and Psychology, 24(1), 65–76. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10869-009-9092-6>；Bluedorn, A. C., Turban, D. B., & Love, M. S. (1999). The effects of stand-up and sit-down meeting formats on meeting outcomes. Journal of Applied Psychology, 84(2). <https://doi.org/10.1037/0021-9010.84.2.277>
entries.notes: The standing meeting experiment involved five person groups doing a task in a laboratory. Its findings cannot simply be applied to long or large meetings. Leach measured participants’ own perceptions of a meeting’s effectiveness, not how much work was actually accomplished.

entries.title: Reduce the number of meetings; use asynchronous written communication when it can resolve the issue
entries.cost: Costs nothing. It requires cooperation from coworkers and supervisors. The hard part is that writing something clearly takes more effort than saying a sentence aloud.
entries.summary: The more meetings people have in a day, the more tired they feel and the greater they perceive their workload to be. Cancel one meeting, and you save its entire length, minute for minute.
entries.benefit: Two surveys examined employees working more than 35 hours a week, with 676 and 304 participants, respectively. The effect of time spent in meetings on work attitudes and well-being is not fixed; it depends on two things: the quality of the meetings and how much the job depends on other people. Another study had people keep diaries for a week. It found that more meetings on a given day were associated with greater fatigue and a higher perceived workload. The time saved equals the length of the meetings you eliminate.
entries.sources: Rogelberg, S. G., Leach, D. J., Warr, P. B., & Burnfield, J. L. (2006). "Not another meeting!" Are meeting time demands related to employee well-being? Journal of Applied Psychology, 91(1). <https://doi.org/10.1037/0021-9010.91.1.83>；Luong, A., & Rogelberg, S. G. (2005). Meetings and more meetings: The relationship between meeting load and the daily well-being of employees. Group Dynamics: Theory, Research, and Practice, 9(1). <https://doi.org/10.1037/1089-2699.9.1.58>
entries.notes: Debate: Rogelberg 2006 found that the relationship between the number of meetings and well-being is not uniformly negative. For jobs that depend heavily on other people, more meetings may even be beneficial. Also, no study has directly compared “switching to asynchronous written communication” with holding meetings. That recommendation is the author’s own inference.

entries.title: Break large tasks into subtasks before estimating the time and getting started
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Breaking down the task itself takes 5 to 15 minutes.
entries.summary: When estimating how long a task will take, people do not automatically break it down and count each part. Listing the subtasks first leads to less underestimation. Once the task is broken down, each small step can be started right away, which also makes procrastination less likely.
entries.benefit: When estimating a task’s duration, people do not on their own divide a task with several components into separate parts. For example, writing a literature review, writing the discussion, and organizing references are separate tasks. Listing the subtasks before estimating helps reduce the tendency to underestimate the time needed, known as the planning fallacy. After the task is broken down, each small step becomes an action you can start immediately, and procrastination decreases too. Among the strongest predictors of procrastination in the research are aversion to the task and postponement of the task itself.
entries.sources: Kruger, J., & Evans, M. (2004). If you don't want to be late, enumerate: Unpacking reduces the planning fallacy. Journal of Experimental Social Psychology, 40(5), 586–598. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jesp.2003.11.001>；Steel, P. (2007). The nature of procrastination: A meta-analytic and theoretical review of quintessential self-regulatory failure. Psychological Bulletin, 133(1). <https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.133.1.65>
entries.notes: How far should you break it down? Aim for subtasks that can each be completed in one sitting; breaking them down too finely also takes time. Also, for the study by Kruger and Evans, only the direction of the finding was verified from the abstract; the specific percentages were not checked against the full original text.

entries.title: Set your own date for tasks without an external deadline
entries.cost: Costs nothing. The hard part is honoring the date once you set it. If you disregard it when the day comes, it is as though you never set it.
entries.summary: When someone else set a deadline, 80.6% of students finished before it. Only 38.7% finished within the time they themselves had predicted. Completion times closely followed the deadline and had little to do with their own estimates. So, for tasks without a deadline, set one yourself and honor it.
entries.benefit: Among students with an external deadline, 80.6% finished before it. Only 38.7% finished within the time they themselves had predicted. Completion times closely followed the deadline, with a correlation coefficient of r = 0.82; the closer this number is to 1, the tighter the relationship. The relationship with students’ own predictions was very weak.
entries.sources: Buehler, R., Griffin, D., & Ross, M. (1994). Exploring the "planning fallacy": Why people underestimate their task completion times. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 67(3), 366–381. <https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.67.3.366>
entries.notes: Tell someone else the date you set, and it becomes more like an externally set deadline. The research verified that deadlines set by others work. Deadlines you set for yourself, such as timeboxing or using a Pomodoro timer, have not been directly tested here; the recommendation is extrapolated from that finding.

entries.title: Treat procrastination as avoidance of discomfort, rather than a lack of effort
entries.cost: Costs nothing. All you change is where you look first: ask what about the task feels unpleasant, then work out what to do.
entries.summary: How unpleasant a task feels, whether you think you can do it, how easily immediate distractions draw you away, and how strong your self-control is have the strongest relationships with procrastination. Personality traits such as neuroticism and sensation seeking have only very weak associations with it. So you can start by making the task less unpleasant and the first step smaller, instead of just scolding yourself and forcing yourself through it.
entries.benefit: A meta-analysis combining 691 correlation coefficients found several strong, consistent relationships with procrastination: task aversiveness, how far away the deadline is, self-efficacy (believing you can do it), impulsiveness, and conscientiousness and its components of self-control, distractibility, organization, and achievement motivation. Neuroticism, rebelliousness, and sensation seeking had only very weak associations with procrastination. The author used temporal motivation theory to explain this pattern: a task’s appeal in the present falls rapidly as its reward moves further into the future.
entries.sources: Steel P (2007). The nature of procrastination: a meta-analytic and theoretical review of quintessential self-regulatory failure. Psychological Bulletin, 133(1), 65–94. <https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.133.1.65>
entries.notes: The magnitude of the benefit is rated “medium” because these studies indicate a direction but do not measure how many hours can be saved. For specific actions, see item 1 of this section (write down “what time, where, and what to do when something happens”), item 7 (break large tasks into subtasks), and item 8 (set a date for tasks without an external deadline). These are syntheses of correlational studies, so they cannot show what causes what.

entries.title: Put what you need within reach and move what you want to avoid farther away; do not count on resisting it in the moment
entries.cost: Costs nothing and takes a few minutes each time. Put your phone in another room, and lay out your book and computer on the desk.
entries.summary: When something is farther away, people take less of it. Placing the same snacks farther away clearly reduces how much people eat, a medium sized effect. Offering fewer options also clearly reduces the number of people who take them. These methods do not require you to resist temptation in the moment and take only minutes to set up.
entries.benefit: A Cochrane review included 24 randomized trials. Moving food farther away reduced the amount eaten, with a standardized mean difference of −0.60 (95% CI −0.84 to −0.36, the plausible range; 12 studies, 1,098 people; low certainty evidence), a medium sized effect. Reducing the number of available options produced a larger decrease in selection of that food, with a standardized mean difference of −1.13 (95% CI −1.90 to −0.37; 3 studies, 154 people; low certainty evidence). Regression analysis showed that the farther away the food was and the more limited the options were, the stronger the effect.
entries.sources: Hollands GJ, Carter P, Anwer S, et al. (2019). Altering the availability or proximity of food, alcohol, and tobacco products to change their selection and consumption. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 9, CD012573. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD012573.pub3>
entries.notes: Reason for the B rating: all 24 studies included in the review concerned food; none concerned alcohol or cigarettes. Fourteen were conducted in laboratories, and all came from high income countries. Applying “move it farther away and you will use it less” to phones and games is therefore an extrapolation without direct trials. One specific action, putting a phone out of sight, has been tested directly; see section 3, item 1 (turn off unnecessary notifications and keep your phone out of sight while working).

entries.title: Put money at stake to help yourself follow through, but first ask whether you are willing to stake it
entries.cost: A deposit scheme requires you to put up some of your own money first, which you forfeit if you do not follow through. The deposit in the trial was US$150.
entries.summary: To push yourself to follow through, you can either collect a reward if you succeed or pay a deposit in advance and get it back with an additional reward if you succeed. Among people willing to join either scheme, 13 percentage points more succeeded with a deposit. But only 13.7% were willing to pay a deposit, versus 90% willing to accept a reward, so deposits help only those willing to stake their money.
entries.benefit: A randomized trial in the United States involving 2,538 people assigned employees and their friends and family to four incentive schemes or usual care. The reward scheme (about US$800 for success) had an acceptance rate of 90.0%; the deposit scheme (pay US$150 up front, with an additional US$650 reward) had an acceptance rate of 13.7%. Six month continuous smoking abstinence rates ranged from 9.4% to 16.0% across the four incentive schemes, versus 6.0% with usual care. The rate was 15.7% for the reward scheme and 10.2% for the deposit scheme. But among the 13.7% of people willing to join either scheme, the six month abstinence rate was 13.2 percentage points higher with the deposit scheme than with the reward scheme (95% CI 3.1 to 22.8, the plausible range).
entries.sources: Halpern SD, French B, Small DS, et al. (2015). Randomized trial of four financial-incentive programs for smoking cessation. New England Journal of Medicine, 372(22), 2108–2117. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1414293>
entries.notes: This trial studied smoking cessation. Applying its findings to writing a paper or exercising is an extrapolation, so the magnitude of the benefit is rated “medium.” When choosing a scheme, first consider whether you would actually use it, rather than which is more effective. A method that most people refuse to accept is of no use to those people, however strong its effect. So first choose a method you are willing to accept; staking a smaller amount is still better than staking nothing. For how to quit smoking itself, see section 2, item 3 (smoking cessation medication).

entries.title: Measure new habits in months, not “21 days”
entries.cost: Costs nothing. You need to repeat the same action every day in the same setting for several months.
entries.summary: There is no basis for the claim that “a habit forms in 21 days.” In one 12 week study, the time it took for an action to become something people did without thinking ranged from 18 days at the fast end to 254 days at the slow end. It is normal if it still does not feel easy after two or three weeks. Missing a day along the way does not reset your progress to zero.
entries.benefit: Ninety-six volunteers each chose an action involving eating, drinking, or activity, performed it daily in a fixed setting (for example, “after breakfast”) for 12 weeks, and rated how automatic it felt each day. Data from 82 people were sufficient for analysis, and the model was successfully fitted for 62. The time needed to reach 95% of each person’s maximum level of automaticity ranged from 18 to 254 days. The study also found that missing one opportunity to perform the action had no substantial effect on habit formation.
entries.sources: Lally P, van Jaarsveld CHM, Potts HWW, Wardle J (2010). How are habits formed: Modelling habit formation in the real world. European Journal of Social Psychology, 40(6), 998–1009. <https://doi.org/10.1002/ejsp.674>
entries.notes: There is only this one study, involving 96 people, and all the actions were simple (such as eating a serving of fruit after a meal). No one has measured how long more complex activities take to become habits, such as running three times a week or writing every day. So, if it still feels hard after two weeks, that is not evidence of failure. To make repetition actually happen, tie the action to a fixed setting; see item 1 of this section (write down “what time, where, and what to do when something happens”).

entries.title: If procrastination is already affecting your life, use self-help materials backed by a randomized trial; you do not necessarily need a therapist
entries.cost: A self-help book costs a few dozen yuan; some materials are free. You need to put in about ten weeks, reading one section and doing one exercise each week.
entries.summary: Procrastination severe enough to cause distress can improve. Practicing with cognitive behavioral self-help materials for ten weeks worked clearly better than doing nothing, both with guidance and entirely on one’s own. There was no detectable difference between guided and unguided self-help, so working through the materials on your own can also be effective.
entries.benefit: One hundred and fifty people were randomly assigned to three groups: therapist guided self-help, unguided self-help, and a waitlist control. After ten weeks, the between-group effect size on the Pure Procrastination Scale was d = 0.70 for the guided group (95% CI 0.29–1.10, the plausible range) and d = 0.50 for the unguided group (0.10–0.90). On the Irrational Procrastination Scale, the corresponding figures were 0.81 (0.40–1.22) and 0.69 (0.29–1.09). The proportions achieving clinically significant improvement were 31.3% to 40.0% for the guided group and 24.0% to 36.0% for the unguided group. The two groups did not differ significantly on any outcome.
entries.sources: Rozental A, Forsell E, Svensson A, Andersson G, Carlbring P (2015). Internet-based cognitive-behavior therapy for procrastination: A randomized controlled trial. Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology, 83(4), 808–824. <https://doi.org/10.1037/ccp0000023>
entries.notes: Participants were Swedish adults, and the materials were in Swedish. The same set is not readily available in Chinese, so the magnitude of the benefit is rated “medium.” The materials contained familiar elements: behavioral activation, behavioral experiments, stimulus control, and explanations of motivation and working methods. For stimulus control, see item 10 of this section (move what you want to avoid farther away). If procrastination is accompanied by a marked low mood or anxiety, start with section 3, item 18 (get moving, get sunlight, sleep on schedule, talk to someone, and call 12356, China’s mental health support hotline).

entries.title: Use your own hourly pay to decide which household chores to outsource
entries.cost: You have to pay for outsourcing; the amount depends on the service you buy. You also need to spend some time once to calculate your hourly pay.
entries.summary: People in China spend an average of 1 hour and 17 minutes a day on housework. Among those who actually did housework that day, the average was 1 hour and 59 minutes. People who spend money to buy time have higher life satisfaction. Spending the same amount on buying time rather than things also makes people happier in the moment.
entries.benefit: Residents of China spend an average of 1 hour and 17 minutes a day on housework. Among only those who did housework, the average is 1 hour and 59 minutes. These figures come from a 2024 survey covering 38,500 households and 107,000 people. Another study sampled 6,271 people in four countries and found that people who spent money to buy time had higher life satisfaction. The researchers also conducted an experiment in everyday life: spending the same amount on buying time produced greater happiness in the moment than buying material goods.
entries.sources: Whillans, A. V., Dunn, E. W., Smeets, P., Bekkers, R., & Norton, M. I. (2017). Buying time promotes happiness. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. <https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1706541114>; National Bureau of Statistics of China (2024). Bulletin of the Third National Time Use Survey (No. 2). <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202410/t20241031_1957216.html>
entries.notes: First, calculate your hourly pay: monthly after-tax income ÷ actual hours worked in a month. Then check what it would cost to outsource the chore. If the price per unit of outsourcing is lower than your hourly pay and you will actually use the time saved to earn money or rest, outsource it. Everyone’s hourly pay and outsourcing prices differ, so you need to do the calculation for yourself. Also, Whillans measured how happy people felt after spending money to buy time, not how many hours they saved.

entries.title: Set a firm limit on short videos and aimless scrolling
entries.cost: Costs nothing. The steps take only a few minutes: turn off notifications, delete the app, or set a daily time limit for it. The hard part is controlling the urge to open it.
entries.summary: In 2024, people in China spent an average of 5 hours and 37 minutes a day online; among those who actually went online that day, the figure was 6 hours and 3 minutes. Calculated the same way, the average in 2018 was only 2 hours and 42 minutes. This is the largest figure in this section. Cut one hour a day, and you gain 365 hours a year.
entries.benefit: Chinese residents spend an average of 5 hours and 37 minutes online each day. Counting only people who actually went online that day, the average is 6 hours and 3 minutes. People who used the internet that day account for 92.9%. These figures are from 2024. In 2018, the figure calculated the same way was only 2 hours and 42 minutes. This is the largest figure in this section. Cutting one hour of that time each day frees up 365 hours a year. Separately, according to the China Internet Network Information Center, as of June 2025, internet users spent an average of 30.6 hours online each week, 1.9 hours more than six months earlier. Short-video services had 1.068 billion users, accounting for 95.1% of internet users.
entries.sources: National Bureau of Statistics of China (2024). Bulletin on the Third National Time Use Survey (No. 2). <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202410/t20241031_1957216.html>; National Bureau of Statistics of China (2019). Bulletin on the 2018 National Time Use Survey. <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202302/t20230203_1900224.html>; China Internet Network Information Center (2025). The 56th Statistical Report on China's Internet Development. <https://www.cnnic.net.cn/NMediaFile/2025/0730/MAIN1753846666507QEK67ZS9DH.pdf>
entries.notes: Time online includes work, study, and socializing; it is not all wasted. This is rated C because no study has calculated how much time people get back after setting limits or what they use that time for. The available evidence consists only of aggregate statistics. For the category of scrolling to see how other people are doing, a randomized trial measured both how much time people got back and how their mood changed; see Section 3, Item 20.

entries.title: Stop watching television and scrolling through news; check the information you need at set times
entries.cost: It costs nothing. The hard part is breaking the habit of opening them without thinking, and you may miss some immediate updates.
entries.summary: People aged 15 and over in the United States watch 2.6 hours of television a day, taking up half of all their leisure time. In 2018, people in China watched an average of 1 hour and 40 minutes a day; those aged 75 to 84 watched 3 hours and 16 minutes. If you switch to checking the information you need at set times, this is where the time savings can come from.
entries.benefit: People aged 15 and over in the United States watch 2.6 hours of television a day. Their total leisure time is 5.2 hours, so television takes up half of it. These are 2025 figures. Chinese residents watch an average of 1 hour and 40 minutes of television a day, while people aged 75 to 84 watch 3 hours and 16 minutes. These are 2018 figures.
entries.sources: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (2026). American Time Use Survey — 2025 Results. <https://www.bls.gov/news.release/atus.nr0.htm>; National Bureau of Statistics of China (2019). Bulletin on the 2018 National Time Use Survey. <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202302/t20230203_1900224.html>
entries.notes: Only aggregate statistics are available. No study has calculated what people do with the time saved after watching less television and news. Checking information in batches is the author's own practice.

entries.title: Spend time once to learn keyboard shortcuts and automation for the software you use regularly
entries.cost: It costs nothing. You need to invest anywhere from a few hours to several dozen hours learning. The hard part is that, when you first start, you will be slower than you are with a mouse.
entries.summary: Most people accustomed to using Word still click toolbar icons. In an experiment comparing groups, keyboard shortcuts were faster than both menus and icons. Learning them is a one-time cost; after that, you recoup the time with every operation, every day. The longer you do the same kind of work, the more you gain back.
entries.benefit: A study of 251 experienced Word users found that most rarely used the faster keyboard shortcuts and still relied mainly on clicking icons in the toolbar. An experiment comparing groups confirmed that, of the three methods—menus, icons, and keyboard shortcuts—shortcuts were fastest. The time saved accumulates little by little with the number of operations you perform each day. People who do the same kind of work for a long time benefit most.
entries.sources: Lane, D. M., Napier, H. A., Peres, S. C., & Sándor, A. (2005). Hidden costs of graphical user interfaces: Failure to make the transition from menus and icon toolbars to keyboard shortcuts. International Journal of Human-Computer Interaction. <https://doi.org/10.1207/s15327590ijhc1802_1>
entries.notes: Learn only the operations you use more than ten times a day; learning too many is another form of waste. Also, that efficiency experiment had only six participants, and its abstract did not state how many seconds were saved per operation.

entries.title: Prioritize commute time when choosing where to live, and shorten your one-way commute
entries.cost: The cost is high. You may have to pay higher rent or move to a smaller home. Moving itself also takes time.
entries.summary: In German longitudinal data, people with longer commutes felt worse about their lives. This loss was not made up for by wages or housing. Cutting 30 minutes from each one-way commute saves 5 hours a week.
entries.benefit: Chinese residents spend an average of 50 minutes a day traveling. Counting only people who traveled that day, the figure is 1 hour and 2 minutes. These are 2024 figures. German data tracking the same people over a long period show that people with longer commutes consistently have lower subjective well-being (how good they feel their lives are). This loss was not compensated for by income or housing. A review bringing together multiple studies also confirmed that the longer the commute, the less satisfied people are with it, regardless of the mode of transport. Cutting 30 minutes from each one-way commute saves about 5 hours a week.
entries.sources: Stutzer, A., & Frey, B. S. (2008). Stress that doesn't pay: The commuting paradox. Scandinavian Journal of Economics, 110(2), 339–366. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-9442.2008.00542.x>; Chatterjee, K., et al. (2020). Commuting and wellbeing: A critical overview of the literature with implications for policy and future research. Transport Reviews, 40(1), 5–34. <https://doi.org/10.1080/01441647.2019.1649317>; National Bureau of Statistics of China (2024). Bulletin on the Third National Time Use Survey (No. 2). <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202410/t20241031_1957216.html>
entries.notes: Dispute: After reviewing multiple studies, Chatterjee and colleagues pointed out that no consistent relationship is yet apparent between commute length and overall life satisfaction. They believe people can generally offset the loss from a long commute with a better job or home. Also note that the travel statistics cover all trips, not just commuting. If you can travel to and from work outside peak hours, the same journey can take less time.

chapters.title: Don't waste money
chapters.intro:
This section counts money only: how much you can save, how much annual returns differ, and how much you can expect to get back on average over the long term from a sum of money. These amounts are not converted into lifespan or time. Items involving investment only explain how to do the calculations and use only verified historical data. None of them constitutes investment advice.

The items in this section are grouped by topic below. Item numbers are in parentheses.

**Everyday expenses**: Turn off automatic renewals (Item 1), recalculate mobile phone and broadband plans (Item 4), decline extended warranties for electronics (Item 11), choose medicines selected through centralized procurement (Item 12), drink boiled tap water (Item 14), pay per gym visit (Item 21), set a cooling-off period for large purchases (Item 23), and do not stock up because of a crossed-out price (Item 24).

**Impulse spending and children's spending**: Do not buy lottery tickets (Item 5), do not tip livestreamers (Item 8), seek a refund when a child makes in-app purchases or tips a livestreamer (Item 9), anyone who asks a child to tell them a verification code is a scammer (Item 10), count trendy bracelets and collectible toys by the money spent on them (Item 33), accept only a CMA report for jewelry and gemstones (Item 34), and randomized sales such as blind boxes and card draws (Item 35).

**Online shopping and asserting your rights**: Sign a written contract for advance payments (Item 22), check platform rules when shopping online (Item 29), problems with goods bought in a livestream (Item 30), claim ten times the purchase price for unsafe food (Item 31), check inspection results and certification before buying big-ticket items (Item 32), buy prepackaged food if you want to see an ingredient list (Item 36), and being taken into a shop on a group tour (Item 50).

**Taxes, housing provident fund, and medical insurance**: Annual personal income tax reconciliation (Item 2), withdraw from the housing provident fund for renting or renovating too (Item 3), link family members for shared use of medical insurance funds (Item 13), personal pension accounts (Item 20), and pay into employee pension insurance at the lowest contribution tier if you pay it yourself (Item 46).

**Saving, borrowing, and investing**: Walk away as soon as you see promises of high returns (Item 6), convert borrowing costs to an annual interest rate first (Item 7), do not trade stocks frequently (Item 15), do not borrow to invest (Item 16), use broad-market index funds as core holdings (Item 17), choose funds with low fees (Item 18), do not put all your money in one place (Item 19), save an emergency fund first (Item 27), compare the options before paying off a mortgage early (Item 28), sell losing stocks according to a rule (Item 37), buy U.S. stocks through QDII or Stock Connect with Hong Kong (Item 38), do not buy virtual currencies (Item 45), and verify financial products recommended by bank employees before buying (Item 51).

**Insurance**: Prioritize pure protection insurance (Item 25), buy enough third-party liability insurance (Item 26), insure only against losses you cannot absorb (Item 39), buy term life insurance for income earners first (Item 40), cancel insurance during the cooling-off period (Item 41), distinguish deposits from insurance at a bank counter (Item 42), do not use an agent to cancel insurance (Item 43), and name a specific person as the beneficiary (Item 44).

**Buying a car**: Inspect the car on the spot when taking delivery (Item 47), state in writing that a used car has not been in an accident (Item 48), and do not pay a financial service fee at a 4S dealership (Item 49).

entries.title: Turn off all automatic renewals and renew manually when each subscription expires
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Go through the automatic payment lists in Alipay, WeChat, Apple, and Android; this takes 10 to 20 minutes once. Each time you renew afterward, you will have to make one extra tap yourself.
entries.summary: The savings come from subscriptions you stopped using long ago but are still paying for each month. Going through the automatic payment lists in Alipay, WeChat, Apple, and Android takes less than 20 minutes. Under Chinese rules, merchants must clearly remind you before charging you, and they must provide a way to cancel at any time that is easy to find and use.
entries.benefit: The money you save is the total cost of subscriptions you no longer use but are still paying for. It differs from person to person; there is no single figure. Chinese regulators require merchants to clearly remind you before renewal and provide a simple option to cancel at any time, at no additional cost (China; effective since 2021).
entries.sources: State Administration for Market Regulation of China (2021, amended in 2025). Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Online Transactions (Order No. 37 of the State Administration for Market Regulation, Article 18). <https://www.samr.gov.cn/zw/zfxxgk/fdzdgknr/fgs/art/2025/art_4b47c79b8d994a42bba4835997688faa.html>
entries.notes: For services you really do use often, an annual subscription is generally cheaper than paying monthly, so keeping automatic renewal may be better value. Turn off the subscriptions you forgot about long ago that are still charging you. For how operators selling website memberships should give reminders, see Section 26, Item 13 (selling automatically renewing memberships).

entries.title: Reconcile your personal income tax once a year from March to June, and claim the special additional deductions you are entitled to
entries.cost: It costs nothing. You can do it in the Chinese Personal Income Tax app in just over ten minutes.
entries.summary: These people can usually get a refund by filing: those who worked only a few months of the year, changed jobs during the year, or did not claim deductions for children's education, a mortgage, rent, or supporting elderly relatives. You can do it on your phone in just over ten minutes. If your annual comprehensive income is under CNY 120,000, or the additional tax you owe is under CNY 400, you may choose not to file.
entries.benefit: Reconcile four kinds of income together: wages and salaries, remuneration for personal services, author's remuneration, and royalties. Tax you overpaid is refunded; tax you underpaid must be paid. You may choose not to file in either of two situations: your annual comprehensive income does not exceed CNY 120,000, or the additional tax you owe does not exceed CNY 400. These two rules were set in a 2023 announcement by China's State Taxation Administration and remain in force through December 31, 2027. Conversely, the following people can usually get a refund by filing: those who had income for only a few months of the year, changed jobs during the year, or failed to claim deductions for children's education, a mortgage, rent, supporting elderly relatives, and similar expenses.
entries.sources: State Taxation Administration of China (2025). Measures for the Administration of Annual Reconciliation of Individual Income Tax on Comprehensive Income (Article 6) and their interpretation. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202502/content_7006465.htm>; Ministry of Finance of China and State Taxation Administration of China (2023). Announcement on Continuing the Implementation of Policies Concerning the Annual Reconciliation of Individual Income Tax on Comprehensive Income. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202308/content_6900594.htm>
entries.notes: People who owe additional tax must also file; failing to do so is illegal. There are seven special additional deductions: children's education, continuing education, medical expenses for serious illnesses, home loan interest, housing rent, supporting elderly relatives, and care for children under age three. You can choose either the mortgage deduction or the rent deduction, but you cannot claim both.

entries.title: The housing provident fund is not just for buying a home: you can withdraw funds for rent, renovations, and property management fees under the new Chinese regulations effective September 20, 2026
entries.cost: It costs nothing. You only need to complete the withdrawal procedure once.
entries.summary: You do not have to be buying a home to access your housing provident fund. The new Chinese regulations list nine circumstances in which withdrawals are allowed, including paying rent, renovating a home you live in, and paying property management fees. After you apply, the housing provident fund center must tell you within 3 days whether the withdrawal is approved.
entries.benefit: The amended Chinese regulations list nine circumstances in which withdrawals are allowed. They include paying rent, renovating a home you live in, and paying property management fees for a home you live in. The housing provident fund management center must decide whether to approve or refuse a withdrawal within 3 days of accepting your application.
entries.sources: State Council of China (2026). Decision of the State Council on Amending the Regulations on the Administration of the Housing Provident Fund (State Council Order No. 844, adopted at the State Council's 93rd executive meeting on July 31, 2026; “effective from September 20, 2026”): Amended Article 24 states, “An employee may withdraw the balance held in the employee's housing provident fund account under any of the following circumstances: (1) paying rent; (2) purchasing, constructing, rebuilding, or carrying out major repairs to a home occupied by the employee; (3) repaying principal and interest on a home purchase loan; (4) renovating a home occupied by the employee; (5) paying property management fees for a home occupied by the employee; (6) retiring from work or retiring on reaching retirement age; (7) completely losing the ability to work and terminating the employment relationship with the employing organization; (8) settling abroad; or (9) other housing consumption circumstances approved by the State Council.” Article 25 states, “The housing provident fund management center shall decide whether to approve or refuse a withdrawal within 3 days of accepting the application”; Article 18 states that contribution rates “must each be no less than 5% of the employee's average monthly wage in the preceding year.” <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2026/issue_12946/202608/content_7079363.html>
entries.notes: The money in the account consists of part of your own wages plus the part contributed by your employer. If you leave it there, it earns interest at only a very low rate. The Chinese regulations also state that if an employee dies or is declared dead, their heirs and legatees may withdraw the account balance. Local housing provident fund management centers determine what documents are required and the exact procedures. Check your local center's service guide before you go. The housing provident fund can also be used for a home purchase loan at a lower interest rate than a commercial loan; see Section 15, Item 16 (use a housing provident fund loan first). For property management companies that use water or power shutoffs to demand property management fees, see Section 15, Item 17 (property management companies shutting off water and power).

entries.title: Reassess your mobile phone and broadband plans once a year; switch to a lower tier if you do not need what you are paying for, and complain if the operator refuses to switch you
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Checking a bill takes just over ten minutes. The hard part is standing firm if customer service refuses to move you to a lower tier.
entries.summary: The old plan you are on is often tens of yuan more expensive than plans currently on sale. Tens of yuan a month add up to hundreds of yuan wasted in a year. Under Chinese rules, an operator cannot refuse to let you transfer your number to another operator without a valid reason, delay the transfer, or create a separate set of rates specifically for people transferring their numbers. If it blocks you, file a complaint.
entries.benefit: Rules issued by China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology state that operators must not “refuse, obstruct, or delay providing number portability services to users without a valid reason.” They must also not “use technical means such as interception or restrictions to affect the quality of communication services for users transferring their numbers.” Nor may they “set special tariff plans and marketing plans for users transferring their numbers.” Old plans are often tens of yuan more expensive than plans currently on sale. If you never switch, you waste hundreds of yuan each year.
entries.sources: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology of China (2019). Regulations on the Administration of Number Portability Services (MIIT Information and Communications Administration [2019] No. 242). <http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2019-11/13/content_5451483.htm>
entries.notes: First, use the operator's app to check how much mobile data and calling time you actually used over the past six months, then choose a plan based on that usage. If customer service says, “You have to go to a store to move to a lower tier” or “You cannot change plans during the contract period,” ask for the rule in writing. If they cannot provide it, call China's 12300 service to complain.

entries.title: Do not buy lottery tickets
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Not buying them saves money.
entries.summary: Under Chinese rules, at least 50% of sales revenue from lotto and number-based lottery tickets must be allocated to prizes; for Double Color Ball, the share is 51%. For every CNY 1 you spend, you can expect to get back only CNY 0.51 on average over the long term, a consistent loss of 49%. Lottery sales across China totaled CNY 623.486 billion in 2024, of which CNY 161.031 billion went directly to public welfare funds and was not included in prizes.
entries.benefit: China's Ministry of Finance sets minimum shares of sales revenue allocated to prizes: 50% for lotto and number-based lotteries, 65% for instant lotteries, and 73% for prediction-based lotteries. Double Color Ball allocates 51% of sales revenue to prizes: for every CNY 100 in tickets sold, only CNY 51 goes toward prizes. For you, that means that for every CNY 1 you spend, you can expect to get back only CNY 0.51 on average over the long term, losing 49%. Lottery sales across China totaled CNY 623.486 billion in 2024; CNY 161.031 billion of that went into public welfare funds and did not return to ticket buyers (China, 2024).
entries.sources: Ministry of Finance of China (2015). Notice on Regulating and Strengthening the Administration of the Proportions of Lottery Funds (Finance Comprehensive [2015] No. 94). <http://m.mof.gov.cn/czxw/201511/t20151113_1560814.htm>; Ministry of Finance of China (2025). Ministry of Finance Announcement No. 8 of 2025 (collection and distribution of lottery public welfare funds in 2024). <http://zhs.mof.gov.cn/zhengcefabu/202508/t20250828_3970977.htm>; China Welfare Lottery Double Color Ball Game Rules (Article 14). <https://mzj.nc.gov.cn/ncsmzj/flcp/202111/5dccc1a5da89434e94a62f8ea0e5887e.shtml>
entries.notes: Over the long term, you will lose money on average. That is built into the rules and has nothing to do with luck. You can still buy a ticket, but treat it only as a CNY 2 entertainment expense each time, never as an investment.

entries.title: Walk away immediately when seeing "high yield", "capital preservation", or "guaranteed profit"
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Just pause when hearing these words.
entries.summary: The former chairman of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission stated in 2018: if yields exceed 6%, raise a question mark; if they exceed 8%, it is very dangerous; above 10%, be prepared to lose all principal. Legitimate wealth management is no longer permitted to promise capital preservation or guaranteed returns. Losses incurred from participating in illegal fund-raising are borne by yourself according to regulations; no one will bail you out if trouble arises.
entries.benefit: The former chairman of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission made a statement at the 2018 Lujiazui Forum. His exact words were: "If yields exceed 6%, raise a question mark; if they exceed 8%, it is very dangerous; above 10%, be prepared to lose all principal." New asset management regulations require financial institutions "shall not promise capital preservation or guaranteed yields," and also mandate that "when redemption difficulties arise, financial institutions shall not advance funds in any form for redemption." Therefore, legitimate wealth management no longer offers any concept of capital preservation. Losses from participating in illegal fund-raising "shall be borne by fund-raising participants themselves"; no one will compensate you after an incident occurs (China, 2018, 2021)
entries.sources: Guo Shuqing (2018). Preventing and Defusing Financial Risks, Striving to Cross Major Hurdles (Speech at the 10th Lujiazui Forum, Official Website of the National Financial Regulatory Administration): "In the process of cracking down on illegal fund-raising, strive through various means to make the public realize that high returns mean high risks; if yields exceed 6%, raise a question mark; if they exceed 8%, it is very dangerous; above 10%, be prepared to lose all principal." <https://www.nfra.gov.cn/cn/view/pages/ItemDetail.html?docId=182418>; reposted by Tianjin Municipal Local Financial Regulatory Bureau. <https://jrgz.tj.gov.cn/ztlm/ztzl/jrjfwphjr/202006/t20200625_2744709.html>; People's Bank of China et al. (2018). Guiding Opinions on Regulating the Asset Management Business of Financial Institutions (Yinfa [2018] No. 106, Articles 2 and 6). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2018/content_5323101.htm>; State Council (2021). Regulations on the Prevention and Handling of Illegal Fund-raising (State Council Decree No. 737, Article 25). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2021/content_5588815.htm>
entries.notes: The three lines of 6%, 8%, and 10% were drawn empirically by regulators, not as statutory clauses. The original remarks were made while discussing crackdowns on illegal fund-raising, targeting wealth management products and investment companies promising high returns. This does not constitute investment advice. If doing business on your own and needing to borrow money or recruit equity partners, see Section 12, Item 26 (Pooling money with others to do business) for the red lines.

entries.title: Do not use credit card minimum payments, and do not use installment plans or consumer loans for consumption; if borrowing is unavoidable, convert interest into an annualized percentage rate before comparing
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Requires setting aside enough cash before the statement date to pay in full. The hard part is resisting using installments to dilute large expenses. When borrowing is unavoidable, spend a few minutes clarifying the annualized interest rate of each loan.
entries.summary: The minimum payment is a loan with interest calculated daily, which converts to approximately 18% per year under the pre-2020 upper ceiling; once used, the grace period becomes invalid. Installments advertised as "monthly fee of 0.6%" equate to roughly 13.8% annually, not 7.2%. This is because the principal is repaid monthly, yet the fee is continuously assessed on the initial amount. To determine which loan is more expensive, look only at the annualized interest rate, never daily interest or monthly fee rates.
entries.benefit: Credit card overdraft interest rates had caps and floors prior to 2020: the cap was "a daily interest rate of 0.05%", and the floor was 0.7 times the cap. 0.05% per day converts to 18.25% per year, which is simple interest: calculated at 18.25% per year without rolling interest back into principal. Starting in 2021, pricing shifted to autonomous negotiation between card-issuing institutions and cardholders. Once the minimum payment is used, interest is calculated daily on the full amount of the unpaid principal, and the interest-free grace period is voided simultaneously. The central bank has mandated that card issuers display annualized interest rates (interest rates converted to a full annual basis) in a prominent manner, and "must not display only daily interest rates or daily repayment amounts." Starting in 2021, all lending institutions must prominently disclose the annualized interest rate when advertising and signing contracts. Daily and monthly rates may be displayed together, but cannot be more conspicuous than the annualized rate. The annualized interest rate must include interest and all fees directly related to the loan. For installment repayments of principal, calculate the actual funds used based on the remaining principal after each installment repayment. The People's Bank of China provided an example calculation: borrowing 100,000 yuan, repaid over 12 months, paying 0.5% of the original principal each month as an installment fee. At the time of borrowing, an additional 1,000 yuan service fee is charged. Calculated as simple interest, the annualized rate is approximately 12.80%. Calculated as compound interest (Internal Rate of Return / IRR method), the annualized rate is approximately 13.58%. Looking merely at the fee rate, one might assume only 0.5% × 12 + 1% = 7% is spent in a year. In reality, it is roughly double that figure, because the principal decreases every month while the installment fee continues to be charged against the original 100,000 yuan. Following the same calculation, a credit card split into 12 installments with a 0.6% fee per installment and no other fees nominally appears as 7.2% per year. Under compound interest, the annualized rate is approximately 13.8%, which is around 1.9 times the nominal figure. From 6 to 36 installments, it consistently falls between 1.8 and 2 times. If the lender is an individual or ordinary company, it falls under private lending. If the agreed interest rate exceeds 4 times the one-year LPR at the time the contract was signed, the courts will not uphold the excess portion. On August 20, 2026, the one-year LPR was 3.0%, making 4 times that rate 12%. For interest deducted from the loan upfront, the court calculates the principal based on the amount actually received. This ceiling does not apply to licensed financial institutions such as banks and consumer finance companies. Nor does it apply to seven categories of local financial organizations, including microfinance companies, pawnshops, and financial leasing companies. Therefore, you cannot apply the 12% cap to their loans; you must inspect the annualized interest rate written on the contract (China, 2020, 2021)
entries.sources: People's Bank of China (2020). Notice on Promoting the Market-Oriented Reform of Credit Card Overdraft Interest Rates (Yinfa [2020] No. 327). <https://xining.pbc.gov.cn/zhengwugongkai/4081330/4406346/4693549/4159909/index.html>; People's Bank of China (2021). Announcement of the People's Bank of China [2021] No. 3 (Articles 1, 3, 4; Annex "Examples of Calculating Annualized Loan Interest Rates Using the Internal Rate of Return Method", Example 3). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-03/31/content_5597156.htm>; Supreme People's Court (Second Amendment 2020). Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases (Articles 1, 25, 26). <http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/94b6623974526df7d2430a3c73f050.html> (Gazette of the Supreme People's Court); Supreme People's Court (2020). Official Reply on the Scope of Application of the New Judicial Interpretation on Private Lending (Fashi [2020] No. 27). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/285171.html>; National Interbank Funding Center Authorized by the People's Bank of China (2026). Announcement of Loan Prime Rate (LPR) on August 20, 2026. <https://www.chinamoney.com.cn/chinese/rdgz/20260820/3399885.html>
entries.notes: 18.25% is calculated directly by multiplying "0.05% × 365", without factoring in compounding interest. If actually compounded monthly, it would be even higher. A few banks offer discounts; the annualized interest rate explicitly stated on your own statement shall prevail. When cash flow is genuinely tight, prioritize borrowing through legitimate channels with lower interest rates rather than carrying a balance on minimum payments to let interest compound. When comparing two loans, ask the counterparties to provide the annualized interest rate calculated by compound interest. If they provide simple interest, regulations require it to be clearly marked as "simple interest"; simple interest will be somewhat lower than compound interest. The 13.8% and the 1.8 to 2 times figures are calculated by this book according to the People's Bank of China's methodology, and the calculations are documented in the verification records. In private lending, stay away from usury; see also Section 7, Item 15 (Do not borrow via usury). For extra fees charged by dealerships when arranging car loans, see Section 5, Item 49 (Financial service fees at 4S dealerships). If you are already unable to repay, see Section 7, Item 23 (Already unable to repay credit cards and online loans).

entries.title: Do not tip live streamers, do not top up games, and do not make impulse purchases
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Spend a few minutes doing three things: disable password-free payment, set per-transaction and daily limits, and unlink payment methods stored on platforms. The hard part is holding yourself back from making that tap in the moment.
entries.summary: Domestic gamers spend an average of roughly 480 yuan per person per year on games, and once spent, it is basically impossible to recover. The law only permits refunds for money spent by minors without parental consent; there is no such provision for adults. The most effortless method is preemptive defense: turn off password-free payment, set per-transaction and daily limits, and unlink payment methods.
entries.benefit: This is a substantial expense. In 2024, the actual sales revenue of the domestic gaming market was 325.783 billion yuan, with 674 million users, averaging approximately 480 yuan per person (calculated by dividing the former two figures). Money spent is practically unrecoverable. There is only one exception: when tipping or top-ups are made by a person with limited capacity for civil conduct (referring here to minors) without the consent of their guardian, "the People's Court shall uphold" the guardian's request for a refund. For adults' own tips and top-ups, no such regulation exists. Furthermore, minors are originally only permitted to play online games on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays, and statutory holidays. The allowable playtime is strictly from 20:00 to 21:00 each day, for 1 hour only (China, 2020, 2021)
entries.sources: National Press and Publication Administration (2024). China's Gaming Market Revenue Exceeded 325.7 Billion Yuan This Year Reaching a New Record (Game Publishing Committee of the China Audio-Video and Digital Publishing Association, "2024 China Game Industry Report"). <https://www.nppa.gov.cn/xxfb/ywdt/202412/t20241216_877445.html>; Supreme People's Court (2020). Guiding Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Lawful and Proper Trial of Civil Cases Involving the COVID-19 Pandemic (II) (Fafa [2020] No. 17, Item 9). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/230181.html>; National Press and Publication Administration (2021). Notice on Further Strict Management to Effectively Prevent Minors from Becoming Addicted to Online Games (Guoxin Chufa [2021] No. 14). <https://www.nppa.gov.cn/xxfb/tzgs/202108/t20210830_666285.html>
entries.notes: Rated Level B because no one has directly measured "how much money not tipping can save"; only industry-wide aggregate figures exist. Turning off password-free payment and setting limits are empirical practices, rated Level C when considered individually. The original texts of Articles 19 and 145 of the Civil Code are already quoted verbatim in Item 9 (Children topping up and tipping on mobile phones). This does not constitute investment advice. If your spouse makes large tips behind your back using communal funds, see Section 10, Item 22 (Tipping live streamers).

entries.title: When children top up or tip via mobile phones, large expenditures by those aged eight and above can be claimed for refund if not ratified by parents
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Requires spending time gathering evidence and negotiating with platforms; platforms usually refuse first, then refund. If negotiations fail, suing is the only option, which takes several months to start, with legal fees paid out of pocket. Therefore, preparing all materials first and going through the platform and 12315 is more cost-effective. The hard part is when the child refuses to speak, requiring patience to question them thoroughly.
entries.summary: When money spent by a child aged eight or older is disproportionate to their age and intelligence, it is valid only with parental consent or retroactive ratification. If parents neither consent nor ratify the expenditure, the transaction is invalid, and a refund can be demanded. Children under eight years old are inherently incapable of spending money independently. If parents remain silent without stating a position, it is legally deemed a refusal to ratify.
entries.benefit: A minor aged eight or older is a person with limited capacity for civil conduct, meaning they can only independently perform acts commensurate with their age and intelligence. Civil juridical acts disproportionate to their age and intelligence are valid only upon consent or ratification by their statutory agent: parents must nod in advance, or ratify afterward. Children under eight years old are persons without capacity for civil conduct and cannot make decisions on their own; their affairs are handled on their behalf by their statutory agents. Where statutory agents make no statement, it is deemed a refusal to ratify: if parents remain silent the entire time, it is treated as not ratifying the transaction
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code. Full text reposted by Supreme People's Procuratorate. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml> Article 19: "A minor aged eight or older is a person with limited capacity for civil conduct, and the performance of civil juridical acts by such minor shall be represented by their statutory agent or conducted with the consent or ratification of their statutory agent; however, such minor may independently perform civil juridical acts that purely yield benefits or civil juridical acts commensurate with their age and intelligence." Article 20: "A minor under the age of eight is a person without capacity for civil conduct, and civil juridical acts shall be performed on their behalf by their statutory agent." Article 145: "A civil juridical act performed by a person with limited capacity for civil conduct that purely yields benefits or is commensurate with their age, intelligence, and mental health status is valid; other civil juridical acts performed by such person are valid upon consent or ratification by their statutory agent." "Where the statutory agent fails to make a statement, it shall be deemed a refusal to ratify."
entries.notes: The key lies in the burden of proof: you must produce evidence demonstrating that the person operating the phone was the child, not you. Useful materials include: top-up times concentrated during school hours or parents' working hours, device usage logs, the child's chat records and gaming history, and statements by the child. There is no unified monetary threshold for "commensurate with age and intelligence"; a gaming skin costing tens of yuan and a tip amounting to tens of thousands of yuan are not the same thing. Preemptive prevention is more effortless: set password-free spending limits for payment methods, enable youth mode, and do not tell the child payment passwords. For situations involving your own impulsive tipping or top-ups, see the item in this section on "Do not tip live streamers, do not top up games, and do not make impulse purchases".

entries.title: Teach children to remember one rule: anyone online who asks you to take a parent's phone to operate it or report verification codes is a scammer
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Walk through the six categories below with the child, and make an agreement: "If you get scammed, tell me first; I won't scold you." At the same time, set password-free limits on payments, activate youth mode, and keep payment passwords secret from the child. The hard part is holding your temper if an actual scam happens.
entries.summary: The routines of these six scam categories differ, but the final step involves the identical action: instructing the child to take the parent's phone to transfer money. Therefore, teaching one sentence is sufficient: whoever asks you to touch your parents' phone or report verification codes is a scammer. Add one more sentence: "If you get scammed, tell me first; I won't scold you."
entries.benefit: The Quanzhou Anti-Fraud Center, in collaboration with the Quanzhou Municipal Education Bureau, dissected six types of scams specifically targeting juveniles. Their routines vary, but the final step is the identical action: getting the child to transfer money using a parent's phone. Type 1: low-price private transactions of gaming accounts and equipment. Xiao Wang transferred 260 yuan privately; the other party claimed "transfers by minors violate regulations, and the account must be frozen." He clicked a "verification link" using his father's phone, and over 30,000 yuan was transferred out of the account. The original text warned that scammers will request parents' bank cards, passwords, and SMS verification codes, which "must never be provided." Type 2: "lifting anti-addiction controls." The other party threatened "if you don't transfer money to cancel it, your parents will go to jail." The child transferred 7,000 yuan using the mother's phone. The original text stated that anti-addiction systems are officially configured, and "there are simply no 'private unlocking' channels." Type 3: tip refunds. Scammers impersonated "official customer service," claiming minor tips could be refunded, requiring "using a parent's Alipay to send gifts to designated live stream rooms to process the refund"; 73,000 yuan was tipped out of the mother's account, and the person was blacklisted. The original text stated "if someone adds you and asks you to 'send gifts to get refunds', it is 100% a scam." Type 4: impersonating classmates or teachers. Scammers hacked accounts and sent voice messages naming individuals to borrow money. During back-to-school seasons, they infiltrated class groups impersonating teachers to post "pay 500 yuan for miscellaneous school fees," with profile pictures and nicknames matching real teachers, while planting shills in the group saying "already paid." Type 5: celebrity fan clubs. Scammers pulled children into "celebrity fan groups to collect 888 yuan red packets." They first had the child transfer 48.88 yuan for "verification." Then they intimidated them by saying "minor participation is a violation, the platform will freeze 80,000 yuan, and parents will go to jail." A total of 16,000 yuan was defrauded. The original text noted "real police officers and lawyers will never contact minors online to investigate, let alone ask for a parent's phone to operate." Type 6: using low-priced goods on second-hand platforms to lure people off-platform for private transfers. The same material also listed three red lines that children themselves should never cross. First, do not lend, sell, or rent bank cards and phone SIM cards; if cards are used to launder illicit funds, it may constitute the crime of aiding information network criminal activities. Having a criminal record will affect graduate school and civil service examinations. Second, part-time jobs involving "mobile communication relay hubs" (shoujikou) are illegal crimes. Third, for overseas "high-paying recruitment," individuals may be placed under physical control as soon as they arrive abroad (Nationwide, October 2025)
entries.sources: Quanzhou Anti-Fraud Center (2025). The First Lesson of the School Year | Anti-fraud is a Required Course for Teenagers; These 6 Major Traps Must Be Avoided! <http://gat.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/fjjffpzxrx/spjq/202510/t20251028_7026836.htm> (Reposted by Fujian Provincial Public Security Department)
