entries.notes: Rated Level B because official sources provide breakdowns of scam scripts and individual cases without incident rates or statistical figures on prevention efficacy. This must be distinguished from Item 9 (Children topping up and tipping on mobile phones): money spent by children on top-ups and tips of their own accord can be claimed for refund under the Civil Code. Money defrauded by scammers does not fall under that provision and can only be addressed by calling the police to stop payment pursuant to Section 8, Item 2. Whether it can be recovered depends on whether the funds remain in the account. The core script scammers use to intimidate children is "you violated the rules, your parents will go to jail." Explaining to children in advance that this sentence itself is the hallmark of a scam is more effective than probing after the fact. The promise "tell me first if you are scammed, and I won't scold you" must be genuinely honored. The original text warned in the tip-refund category: "Do not hide it after being scammed; inform parents and report to the police immediately to reduce losses." The phrase "anyone online" in the title is the author's summary synthesized from these six scam categories for easy memorization by children; no such literal phrase appears in the source text. For the adult version of acquaintance impersonation and AI face-swapping, see Section 8, Items 3 and 4 (Hard anti-fraud rules, Hang up first when transfers are involved). Adults are the same: never handle verification codes or facial recognition on behalf of anyone; see Section 8, Item 45 (Reading out verification codes).

entries.title: Reject extended warranties on electronic products
entries.cost: Costs nothing. The tradeoff is having to pay out of pocket if repairs are needed after the warranty expires, though the probability of this happening is low.
entries.summary: Extended warranties typically sell for 10% to 50% of the original product price, and sellers' profit margins on them are more than ten times higher than on regular merchandise—this price difference is the extra money you pay. For major components like washing machine motors and refrigerator compressors, national regulations already mandate a 3-year warranty. If encountering a very cheap extended warranty, divide the extended warranty price by the cost of a single repair; the resulting quotient represents the minimum probability of breaking down at least once during those years required to break even.
entries.benefit: Extended warranties are typically priced at 10% to 50% of the product’s original price. An industry estimate cited in the study puts the average gross margin on extended warranties at 50% to 60%: for every 100 yuan in sales, 50 to 60 yuan is gross profit. That is about 18 times the gross margin on ordinary products. In 2003, extended warranties accounted for only 3% to 4% of Best Buy’s revenue but contributed more than 50% of its profit (United States, retail data from the 2000s). If you encounter an extended warranty priced well below that range, you can work it out yourself: warranty price ÷ cost of one repair = the probability of a breakdown needed to break even. It is worth buying only if you estimate that the chance of at least one breakdown during the warranty period exceeds that figure. For example, if an extended warranty costs 25 yuan and one repair would cost 300 yuan, the chance of at least one breakdown would have to exceed about 8% to break even. The 300 yuan here is only an example, not a statistic. Before calculating, subtract the coverage already required by the state. The state-mandated three-guarantees period starts on the date the invoice is issued: the whole washing machine or refrigerator is covered for 1 year, and major components for 3 years. For washing machines, the major components are the motor, timer, program controller, and capacitor; for refrigerators, they include the compressor and thermostat. For the period when an extended warranty overlaps with the three guarantees, you are paying for something you already have (China nationwide, since 1995).
entries.sources: Chen T, Kalra A, Sun B (2009). Why Do Consumers Buy Extended Service Contracts? Journal of Consumer Research 36(4):611-623. <https://doi.org/10.1086/605298>; State Economic and Trade Commission et al. (1995). Provisions on Liability for the Repair, Replacement, and Return of Certain Goods (State Economic and Trade Commission [1995] No. 458; Article 8: the three-guarantees validity period is calculated from the date the invoice is issued; appendix, Catalogue of Certain Goods Subject to the Three Guarantees [First Batch]: whole washing machines and household refrigerators, 1 year; major components, 3 years). Administrative normative document of the State Administration for Market Regulation. <https://www.samr.gov.cn/zw/zfxxgk/zc/xzgfxwj/art/2019/art_f943e66de125437d92df701e1654c47c.html>
entries.notes: The gross-margin figure is an industry estimate from another source (Business Week 2004) cited by the paper, not a figure the researchers measured themselves. The calculation above applies to ordinary people who can afford to pay for one repair themselves. Someone who depends on a device for a living and has no backup needs to calculate differently. Screen-breakage insurance for phones and similar products also needs a separate calculation: first estimate how often you drop your phone, then see whether the premium is worth it. If an extended warranty is very cheap, buying it will not cost you more than a few dozen yuan even if it proves unnecessary. Before buying, check when coverage starts: if it starts on the purchase date, the first few years overlap with the three guarantees. Also check whether the seller, the brand, or a third-party company provides the coverage, and whether home-visit and replacement-part fees are charged separately. Check the manual and warranty card too; the brand’s own promised warranty period may be longer than the three-guarantees period.

entries.title: Prioritize generic drugs that have passed the consistency evaluation and drugs selected through centralized procurement
entries.cost: Costs nothing. When a doctor prescribes a drug or you buy one, ask one more question: “Is there a centrally procured drug available under its generic name?”
entries.summary: Prices fell by an average of 53% in the second batch of centrally procured drugs, with the largest reduction reaching 93%. By April 2026, 11 batches had been completed, covering 490 drugs. When getting a prescription or buying medicine, ask, “Is there a centrally procured drug available under its generic name?” You can get the same active ingredient and spend substantially less.
entries.benefit: In the second batch of China’s nationally organized centralized drug procurement, prices fell by an average of 53%, with the largest reduction reaching 93%. As of April 2026, 11 batches had been conducted, covering 490 drugs. A total of 1,695 drugs had passed, or were deemed to have passed, the consistency evaluation. That is about 2/3 of commonly used chemical medicines in clinical practice (China, official data from 2020 to 2026).
entries.sources: National Healthcare Security Administration (2020). Answers to Reporters’ Questions on the Second Batch of Nationally Organized Centralized Drug Procurement and Use. <https://www.nhsa.gov.cn/art/2020/1/17/art_38_2264.html>; National Healthcare Security Administration (2026). State Council Routine Policy Briefing: Improving the Mechanism for Drug Price Formation Across the Full Life Cycle and All Channels. <http://www.nhsa.gov.cn/art/2026/4/15/art_14_20221.html>; General Office of the State Council (2016). Opinions on Conducting Consistency Evaluations of the Quality and Efficacy of Generic Drugs (General Office of the State Council [2016] No. 8). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2016-03/05/content_5049364.htm>; China Food and Drug Administration (2016). Notice on the Release of Three Technical Guidelines, Including the Selection and Determination of Reference Preparations for Ordinary Oral Solid Dosage Forms (2016 No. 61), Appendices 1 and 3; republished by the Hainan Provincial Medical Products Administration. <https://amr.hainan.gov.cn/himpa/ztzl/fzy/201607/t20160720_1591587.html>; National Healthcare Security Administration (2024). Strict Quality Oversight of Centrally Procured Drugs: “Full Coverage” of Both Company Inspections and Product Sampling. <https://www.nhsa.gov.cn/art/2024/12/30/art_52_15287.html>; National Healthcare Security Administration (2025). Officials from the Healthcare Security and Drug Regulatory Departments Answer Questions from a People’s Daily Health Client Reporter on Issues Concerning Centrally Procured Drugs. <https://www.nhsa.gov.cn/art/2025/2/9/art_14_15647.html>
entries.notes: Controversy: people often say, “The consistency evaluation compares only ingredients, not effectiveness.” That is half right. To pass the evaluation, healthy people take the drug, and blood samples are used to measure the concentration curve after it enters the bloodstream. That curve is then compared with the original brand-name drug’s curve; a result within 80% to 125% passes. Requirements are stricter for drugs where a small difference in dose can cause harm. Excipients are the fillers and coatings other than the active ingredient, and they may differ from those in the original drug. Regulations require only that the active ingredient, dosage form, way of taking the drug, and therapeutic effect be the same. So the evaluation really is not a matter of “having patients take it for a while and seeing whether they get better.” A separate set of studies addresses its effects in patients. The National Healthcare Security Administration has organized hospitals to conduct real-world studies. By December 2024, these covered 63 centrally procured drugs, nearly 100 top-tier Grade A hospitals, and more than 300,000 patients. The results found no difference from the original brand-name drugs. For example, with metformin, 83.4% of the generic group met the glycated hemoglobin target, compared with 78.9% of the original-drug group. The fasting blood glucose target showed the reverse: 83.8% of the generic group met it, compared with 87.6% of the original-drug group. Each group did better on one measure. In January 2025, some doctors publicly said that centrally procured drugs “don’t lower blood pressure, anesthetics don’t put people to sleep, and laxatives don’t work.” Healthcare security and drug regulators investigated seven hospitals in Shanghai and concluded that these claims mostly came from secondhand accounts and personal impressions. The laxative singled out had not yet begun to be used in hospitals at the time. They also acknowledged in the same investigation that problem drugs had indeed been found in sampling. Among more than 1,600 selected products in the first nine batches, nine were disqualified because of quality risks. Of those nine, six were imported drugs (including three original brand-name drugs) and three were domestically produced. There are two practical things you can do. First, if you want to keep using the original brand-name drug, you can usually still get it prescribed. Centralized procurement accounts for only 60% to 80% of hospitals’ purchasing volume; hospitals decide what to purchase for the rest. Original drugs have not been banned, but you will pay more out of pocket. Second, after changing medication for a chronic condition, do not judge by how you feel. As described in Section 16, Item 3 (record every measurement in the same notebook), keep track of blood pressure, blood glucose, and glycated hemoglobin. If the results really worsen, see your doctor and ask the doctor to report a suspected adverse drug reaction. Do not stop taking the drug on your own.

entries.title: Set up family sharing once in your Chinese medical insurance app so funds in your employee medical insurance personal account can pay for your spouse’s, parents’, and children’s medical care and medicines
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Set up family sharing once in the medical insurance app for the place where you are insured, or at the agency that administers your coverage.
entries.summary: Set up family sharing once, and the money in your employee medical insurance personal account can be used for your spouse’s, parents’, and children’s medical care and medicines. Without it, only you can use that money, and it will keep sitting in the account.
entries.benefit: Money in your personal account can pay the portion of medical costs that you, your spouse, your parents, or your children must pay yourselves when receiving care at designated medical institutions. It can also pay your out-of-pocket portion when buying medicines, medical devices, and medical consumables at designated retail pharmacies. The policy document also proposes exploring the use of personal accounts to pay family members’ individual contributions to the Chinese basic medical insurance scheme for urban and rural residents.
entries.sources: General Office of the State Council (2021). Guiding Opinions on Establishing and Improving the Outpatient Mutual-Aid Coverage Mechanism under Employee Basic Medical Insurance (General Office of the State Council [2021] No. 14), Item (5): “Personal accounts are mainly used to pay policy-covered out-of-pocket expenses incurred by insured persons at designated medical institutions or designated retail pharmacies. They may be used to pay the medical expenses borne by insured persons themselves and their spouses, parents, and children when receiving care at designated medical institutions, as well as the expenses they bear when purchasing medicines, medical devices, and medical consumables at designated retail pharmacies. The use of personal accounts to pay individual contributions for spouses, parents, and children to participate in basic medical insurance for urban and rural residents, among other purposes, shall be explored. Personal accounts must not be used for public-health expenses, sports and fitness, wellness and health-maintenance spending, or other expenditures outside the scope of basic medical insurance coverage.” <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-04/22/content_5601280.htm>
entries.notes: Many people have several thousand yuan sitting in their personal accounts while elderly family members pay for medicines out of pocket. Once set up, family sharing remains valid long term. In most places it is called “family sharing” and can be arranged in the local Chinese medical insurance app. Note the corresponding hard limit: personal accounts cannot be used for fitness, wellness, or health-maintenance purchases. Using one to buy health supplements at a pharmacy as a way to cash out the funds is medical insurance fraud.

entries.title: Drink boiled tap water instead of regularly ordering large water-dispenser bottles or buying bottled water year-round
entries.cost: Buy a kettle. Boiling water takes a little time each time, plus a small amount of gas or electricity.
entries.summary: At 20 yuan per large bottle for a water dispenser, the water costs about 1 yuan per liter, more than 200 times the price of Beijing tap water. If a family drinks one bottle a week, it will spend just over 1,000 yuan a year; the same amount of tap water costs less than 5 yuan. Tap water is subject to a mandatory Chinese national standard. Ordinarily, you can boil it and drink it.
entries.benefit: Beijing’s first-tier residential water rate is 5 yuan per cubic meter, or 0.005 yuan per liter. A large bottle for a household water dispenser holds 18.9 liters. At 20 yuan a bottle, that is about 1.06 yuan per liter, or about 210 times the price of tap water. If a family drinks one bottle a week, 52 bottles a year come to about 983 liters. The bottled water costs about 1,040 yuan, while the same amount of tap water costs about 4.9 yuan. At an assumed price of 1 yuan for a 500-milliliter small bottle, bottled water costs 2 yuan per liter, 400 times the price of tap water. Drinking water is governed by the mandatory Chinese national standard GB 5749-2022. The standard was issued on March 15, 2022, and took effect on April 1, 2023. The responsible authority is China’s National Disease Control and Prevention Administration (China, 2015 water price and 2022 standard).
entries.sources: Beijing Municipal Commission of Development and Reform. Residential Water Price Table. <https://fgw.beijing.gov.cn/bmcx/djcx/jzldj/202003/t20200331_1752796.htm>; State Administration for Market Regulation, National Public Service Platform for Standards Information. GB 5749-2022 Standards for Drinking Water Quality. <https://openstd.samr.gov.cn/bzgk/std/newGbInfo?hcno=99E9C17E3547A3C0CE2FD1FFD9F2F7BE>; Hangzhou Joint Investigation Team (2025). Report on the Investigation into Abnormal Water Supply in Certain Residential Communities in Hangzhou’s Yuhang District (July 23, 2025), republished by Xinhua Net <http://www.news.cn/20250723/1be62dac3b0b4461a643791ff552e93d/c.html>; People’s Government of Yuhang District, Hangzhou. Yuhang District Source-Water Quality Monitoring Data for April/May/June 2025 (released by Hangzhou Yuhang Water Affairs Holding Group; testing conducted by Hangzhou Jiashu Environmental Monitoring Co., Ltd.; Attachment PDF, Table 1, Item 24, “fecal coliforms”) <https://www.yuhang.gov.cn/art/2025/5/8/art_1229204072_59140140.html>, <https://www.yuhang.gov.cn/art/2025/6/5/art_1229204072_59142885.html>, <https://www.yuhang.gov.cn/art/2025/7/3/art_1229204072_59146464.html>; Cybersecurity Bureau of the Ministry of Public Security (2025). Shao Mouhao Criminally Detained for Fabricating a False “Police Incident Report” and Spreading the “Fecal Water” Rumor <http://www.news.cn/politics/20250722/3178b3bd189c4eb4b293982e92aab438/c.html>; Chongqing Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (2022). Consumer Notice on Large-Bottle Drinking Water (October 25, 2022) <https://scjgj.cq.gov.cn/bkzs/spbk/202210/t20221025_11222964.html>
entries.notes: The point of controversy is that compliance testing checks water as it leaves the treatment plant and at the ends of the pipe network. When something goes wrong with the water source or distribution network, standards can briefly fail to be met. On July 16, 2025, the raw water entering Hangzhou’s Renhe Water Plant had an unusual smell, and tap water in some residential communities in Renhe and Liangzhu smelled bad. The official conclusion was that algae decomposed under oxygen-poor conditions, producing thioether compounds. After the water source was changed, neither total coliforms nor Escherichia coli were detected in water leaving the plant, and all tested parameters met the drinking-water standard GB 5749-2022. Afterward, seven officials were held accountable, all July water charges were waived, and filter cartridges were replaced for free. But fecal coliform counts at the same water source had already been rising for several consecutive months before the incident. At the Yongsheng intake on the Tiaoxi River, the count was 10 per liter in April, 7,300 per liter in May, and 16,000 per liter in June. The limit for Class III surface water under standard GB 3838 is 10,000 per liter. In the same month, the counts at Siling Reservoir, at 28,000 per liter, and Mantoushan Reservoir, at 24,000 per liter, also exceeded the limit. What follows is the author’s advice; the official report did not say this: boiling kills microorganisms, but it cannot remove substances that cause odors or chemicals dissolved in the water. If you notice an unusual smell or the water turns yellow or cloudy, stop drinking it and report the problem to the water supplier and China’s 12345 government service hotline. Switch temporarily to bottled water; do not expect a few extra minutes of boiling to fix it. But this was an isolated local incident, for which compensation was also provided locally, and it still does not justify buying bottled water year-round. The online claim that “a sewage pipe was connected incorrectly” came from a forged police incident report; the person who posted it has been criminally detained (see Section 9). The prices of 20 yuan for a large water-dispenser bottle and 1 yuan for a 500-milliliter bottle are assumptions for the calculation. Recalculate using actual prices in your city. Large-bottle water is not necessarily cleaner either: Chongqing’s market regulator warns that the longer it is stored after opening, the greater the risk of microbial contamination; water dispensers should be cleaned at least once every 2 to 3 months. If the secondary water-supply facilities in an older residential complex fail to meet standards, you can add a filter or buy drinking water in that situation. Water prices vary by location; the Beijing figure is only meant to show the order of magnitude.

entries.title: Avoid frequent stock trading, especially when prices are soaring or plunging
entries.cost: Costs nothing. The hard part is resisting the urge to trade whenever you see news, or to put in more money when everyone else seems to be making money.
entries.summary: The American households that traded most frequently in the 1990s earned only 11.4% a year, while the overall market returned 17.9% over the same period. Trading costs were the main reason for the gap. During China’s 2014–2015 boom and crash, the 85% of households with the smallest accounts traded too often. They earned 250 billion yuan less than they would have by simply holding their stocks, about 30% of their initial investment.
entries.benefit: This study examined 66,465 household accounts at a US discount brokerage from 1991 to 1996. The most frequent traders earned an annualized return of 11.4%, meaning an average of 11.4% a year. The overall market returned 17.9% over the same period, while the average household earned 16.4%. The average household’s annual turnover rate was 75%: over a year, it replaced three-quarters of the stocks it held. There was little difference in gross returns (money earned before trading fees) between the frequent traders and the less frequent traders. The gap therefore came mainly from the transaction costs paid when buying and selling (United States, 1991 to 1996). The Chinese data: the study used daily account data from the Shanghai Stock Exchange, covering all approximately 40 million accounts. The sample period was the 18 months from July 2014 to December 2015. During those 18 months, the Shanghai Composite Index first rose by more than 150%. It peaked at 5,166.35 points on June 12, 2015, then fell by 40% by the end of December. Household accounts were divided into four groups by the market value of their stock holdings at the start of the period. The smallest-account group comprised 85% of all household accounts, while the largest-account group comprised 0.5%. The two groups had roughly the same combined stock market value at the start: 880 billion yuan and 808 billion yuan, respectively. The result was that the smallest 85% lost 250 billion yuan through active trading, while the largest 0.5% gained 254 billion yuan. “Lost” here means relative to holding the same stocks throughout the same market period without doing anything. Each amount was approximately 30% of its group’s initial stock market value: 28% for the former and 31% for the latter. For comparison, the market was relatively calm during the two and a half years before June 2014. In any 18-month period within that time, the corresponding difference was only 1% to 3% of initial market value. During the boom and crash, household accounts turned over their stock holdings about once every three weeks on average, nearly 18 times a year (Shanghai, China, 2014 to 2015; comparison period 2012 to 2014).
entries.sources: Barber BM, Odean T (2000). Trading Is Hazardous to Your Wealth: The Common Stock Investment Performance of Individual Investors. The Journal of Finance 55(2):773-806. <https://doi.org/10.1111/0022-1082.00226>; An L, Lou D, Shi D (2022). Wealth redistribution in bubbles and crashes. Journal of Monetary Economics 126:134-153. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmoneco.2022.01.001>; Publicly available working-paper draft by the same authors (October 2021; the Chinese figures were checked word for word against it). <https://personal.lse.ac.uk/loud/AnLouShi.pdf>
entries.notes: The U.S. data are from the 1990s, and the commission and stamp duty structure for A-shares is different, but the principle that “the more you trade, the lower your take-home return” is the same. This is not advice against buying stocks, and the Chinese study does not say that either. It calculates that, during the same market period, the more actively households with small accounts traded, the more money flowed to the parties on the other side of their trades. The people who made that money were not institutions but the individuals with the largest accounts: during this period, about 90% of trading volume on the Shanghai Stock Exchange came from retail accounts; Table 1 of the paper puts the figure at 87% of daily trading volume. The widely circulated claim that “90% of retail investors lose money” has no verifiable official statistic behind it, so this entry does not use that figure. Turnover rates offer a comparison: in this market cycle, Chinese household accounts turned over nearly 18 times a year, while the U.S. households turned over only three-quarters of their holdings in a year. In quieter years, this gap in China was only 1% to 3%, so the most important time to resist the urge to trade is when the market is hottest. This is not investment advice.

entries.title: Do not borrow to invest, use leverage, or buy what you do not understand
entries.cost: It costs nothing. The hard part is resisting the thought, when the market is doing well, that you could “borrow a little to earn a little more.”
entries.summary: If you borrow to buy stocks and the value falls below the required threshold, you will be forced to sell if you cannot put up more money. A loss on paper becomes a real loss on the spot, with no chance to “wait for it to recover.” Under Chinese regulatory rules, people who have traded securities for less than six months or whose average daily assets over the most recent 20 trading days are below 500,000 yuan cannot open a margin financing account. That threshold itself shows that this is not meant for ordinary people.
entries.benefit: Leverage means borrowing money to buy, and it magnifies losses. After you buy with margin financing, the market value of your collateral may fall below the maintenance collateral ratio set by the securities firm. That ratio governs the assets you have pledged to the firm. If the value falls below the threshold and you cannot restore it by adding collateral, your position will be forcibly liquidated: the securities firm will sell the holdings for you. A loss on paper becomes a real loss on the spot, with no chance to “wait for it to recover.” Chinese regulatory rules say that customers who “have engaged in securities trading for less than six months, lack the ability to bear risk, or have had average daily securities assets below 500,000 yuan over the most recent 20 trading days” may not open a credit account. That threshold itself shows that this is not a tool for ordinary people (China, 2015).
entries.sources: China Securities Regulatory Commission (2015). Measures for the Administration of Securities Firms’ Margin Financing and Securities Lending Business (CSRC Order No. 117, Article 12). <https://www.csrc.gov.cn/csrc/c106256/c1654005/content.shtml>; Shanghai Stock Exchange. Explanation of the Rules for the Implementation of Margin Financing and Securities Lending Transactions on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (investor education material). <https://www.sse.com.cn/services/tradingservice/margin/edu/c/10074042/files/a1f1c4833302451fb9130dbb94116c56.pdf>
entries.notes: The advice “do not buy what you do not understand” has no direct support in the literature; it is a matter of consensus and, considered on its own, receives a C rating. Using a consumer loan or a cash advance from a credit card to invest is also a form of leverage. For their interest rates, see item 7 of this section (Do not use the minimum payment on a credit card). This is not investment advice.

entries.title: Use broad-market index funds instead of actively managed funds for the long-term core of your portfolio (the money you plan to leave invested)
entries.cost: It costs nothing. The trade-off is giving up the possibility of “picking a star fund manager.” The hard part is bearing the decline when the index falls instead of pulling out midway.
entries.summary: Taken together, the stocks bought by U.S. actively managed funds already look a lot like the whole market. But the extra management fees they charge come directly out of the returns you receive. When fund performance is repeatedly recalculated as a matter of luck for comparison, very few funds earn enough extra to cover their own fees.
entries.benefit: The combined portfolio of U.S. actively managed equity funds is close to the market portfolio: taken together, these funds hold stocks in proportions much like those of the whole market. But the higher costs of active management translate directly into lower net returns for investors (what they receive after fees). The study used bootstrap simulations, repeatedly reshuffling performance at random to see what luck alone could achieve. It found that very few funds generate enough excess return to cover their costs: the amount a fund earns above the market is not enough to pay the fee it charges (United States, published in 2010). S&P Dow Jones Indices compiles statistics each year: in 2024, 65% of actively managed U.S. large-cap equity funds underperformed the S&P 500. Across the 24 years it has tracked, an average of 64% underperformed each year. Over the 15 years ending in 2024, there was no category in which a majority of active funds outperformed.
entries.sources: Fama EF, French KR (2010). Luck versus Skill in the Cross-Section of Mutual Fund Returns. The Journal of Finance 65(5):1915-1947. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1540-6261.2010.01598.x>; S&P Dow Jones Indices (2025). SPIVA U.S. Scorecard Year-End 2024. <https://www.spglobal.com/spdji/en/spiva/article/spiva-us/> (the official website blocks automated retrieval; figures checked against an archive dated 2025-05-12: <https://web.archive.org/web/20250512071051/https://www.spglobal.com/spdji/en/spiva/article/spiva-us/>); S&P Dow Jones Indices (2025). SPIVA Asia Ex-Japan Scorecard Mid-Year 2025 (Report 1a; underperformance rates for China Large-Cap versus the S&P China A 300: 60.5% over 1 year, 69.6% over 3 years, and 50.8% over 5 years). <https://web.archive.org/web/20251103165922/https://www.spglobal.com/spdji/en/documents/spiva/spiva-asia-ex-japan-mid-year-2025.pdf> (the official website blocks automated retrieval; checked against an archive); Harvey CR, Liu Y (2022). Luck versus Skill in the Cross Section of Mutual Fund Returns: Reexamining the Evidence. The Journal of Finance, 77(3). <https://doi.org/10.1111/jofi.13123> (a source presenting a challenge to the conclusion)
entries.notes: Dispute: another paper reexamined this conclusion. It argued that the Fama–French method of repeatedly resampling the data did not draw enough samples. Under that paper’s method, even when a fund clearly earns more, the result could be judged “indistinguishable from luck.” So the conclusion that “almost no funds have skill” may be too strong. The Chinese figures are not as one-sided as the U.S. figures. According to S&P Dow Jones Indices’ statistics through June 2025, the proportion of actively managed A-share large-cap funds that underperformed the S&P China A 300 Index was 60.5% over 1 year, 69.6% over 3 years, and 50.8% over 5 years. These statistics cover only up to 5 years; they provide no longer-term figures. So it is not yet settled that actively managed funds in China underperform index funds over the long term, although index funds’ lower fees remain a fact. This is not investment advice.

entries.title: Among similar funds, prefer those with lower fees
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Before buying, take another look at the combined amount of these three charges: “management fee + custodian fee + sales service fee.”
entries.summary: For each additional percentage point in the annual fee rate, the amount you end up with is about 18% lower after 20 years and about 26% lower after 30 years. Choosing a lower-fee fund within the same category means losing less to fees.
entries.benefit: A difference in fees gradually eats into your money through compounding: the small amount deducted each year adds up year after year. If the annual fee rate is 1 percentage point higher, the ending value after 20 years is about 18.2% lower (1 − 0.99^20 ≈ 0.182), and after 30 years it is about 26% lower. Ending value means the money left in the account at that point. Since 2023, China has pursued reform of public fund fees, lowering the fee caps for actively managed equity funds (funds that mainly buy stocks selected by a fund manager). From July 7, 2023, the management fee rate for newly registered funds of this type may not exceed 1.2%, and the custodian fee rate may not exceed 0.2%. A total of 136 fund companies also reduced these two fees on their existing products to below those caps.
entries.sources: China Securities Regulatory Commission (2023). Head of a relevant CSRC department answers reporters’ questions on public fund fee reform. <http://www.csrc.gov.cn/csrc/c100028/c7418692/content.shtml>; Xiamen Office of the China Securities Regulatory Commission (2024). “Newly registered actively managed equity funds are uniformly subject to caps of ‘no more than 1.2% for the management fee rate and no more than 0.2% for the custodian fee rate.’” <http://www.csrc.gov.cn/xiamen/c105636/c7511608/content.shtml>; Fama EF, French KR (2010). See item 17 (broad-market index funds). <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1540-6261.2010.01598.x>
entries.notes: This calculation is simply the result of applying the formula; it assumes the two funds earn the same amount before fees. In practice, you must also account for subscription fees, redemption fees, and sales service fees on Class C shares. This is not investment advice.

entries.title: Do not stake all your money on one stock, one platform, or one home
entries.cost: It costs nothing. The hard part is accepting that you will not happen to bet on the single most profitable choice.
entries.summary: As long as several assets do not rise and fall in perfect lockstep, spreading your money among them leaves the average return you can expect unchanged while reducing the swings in your account. Conversely, if you stake all your money on one stock, one platform, or one home, trouble with that one holding puts all your money in trouble.
entries.benefit: As long as several assets do not rise and fall in perfect lockstep, spreading your money among them leaves expected return (what you can earn on average) unchanged while reducing volatility (the ups and downs in your account). This is a basic conclusion of portfolio selection proposed by Markowitz in 1952 and has remained in use for decades. Conversely, if you stake all your money on one stock or one platform, its variance is the variance of your entire portfolio: your money rises and falls by exactly as much as it does. If something goes wrong, you have no hedge and no other assets to make up the loss.
entries.sources: Markowitz, H. (1952). Portfolio Selection. The Journal of Finance, 7(1), 77–91. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1540-6261.1952.tb01525.x>
entries.notes: This receives a B rating because the classic paper is a purely mathematical derivation and does not calculate an actual figure for “how much less you might lose through diversification.” Diversification can reduce the ups and downs in your account, but it cannot guarantee that you will not lose money. Buying a broad-market index fund (see item 17 of this section) is itself an easy way to diversify. This is not investment advice.

entries.title: Calculate the tax savings and check withdrawal conditions before opening a personal pension account; if you pay no individual income tax or your tax rate is only 3%, do not contribute solely for the tax deduction
entries.cost: Opening an account costs nothing, but you cannot withdraw the money you contribute whenever you want. Besides reaching the age for claiming a basic pension, you can also withdraw if you meet specified conditions involving medical expenses, unemployment, or minimum living assistance; see the notes for the exact thresholds. If you do not qualify, you may still have to wait many years.
entries.summary: If you contribute the full 12,000 yuan and the entire deduction falls within one tax bracket, the net tax savings are 840, 2,040, and 3,240 yuan in the 10%, 20%, and 30% brackets, respectively. These figures already subtract the 3% tax paid on withdrawal; recalculate if the deduction crosses brackets. People in the 3% bracket pay back on withdrawal the tax they saved, so at best they break even. Do not put money you may need at any time into the account: early withdrawals are limited to specified circumstances such as medical expenses, unemployment, and minimum living assistance.
entries.benefit: You can deduct the amount you contribute, up to 12,000 yuan each year, from comprehensive income or business income based on the amount actually paid. Investment returns within the account are temporarily exempt from individual income tax. When withdrawn, the money is not included in comprehensive income and is taxed separately at 3%. To calculate the tax saved in the contribution year, subtract the full-year tax after the deduction from the full-year tax before it. The deduction may move some income into a lower tax bracket, so you cannot always multiply the contribution by your current marginal tax rate. The marginal tax rate is the rate applied to each additional yuan earned. For example, suppose all other deductions have been taken, and annual taxable comprehensive income before the contribution is 40,000 yuan, with tax payable of 1,480 yuan. After contributing and deducting 12,000 yuan, taxable income becomes 28,000 yuan and tax payable is 840 yuan, so tax paid that year falls by 640 yuan. Ignoring investment returns and the time value of money, withdrawing that 12,000 yuan of principal later incurs 360 yuan in tax, leaving a net tax difference of 280 yuan. Only if you contribute the full 12,000 yuan and the entire deduction falls within a single tax bracket can you calculate that year’s tax savings using that bracket’s rate. Again counting only principal and ignoring investment returns and the time value of money, the net tax differences for the 10%, 20%, and 30% brackets are 840, 2,040, and 3,240 yuan, respectively. These are differences in tax amounts arising at different times; they cannot be treated as investment returns, much less divided by the number of years to produce an annualized return. Someone who originally pays no individual income tax receives no current tax saving but still pays 3% on withdrawal. Someone originally subject only to the 3% bracket saves no more than 3% of the contribution in current tax. If annual comprehensive income, after all deductions, does not exceed 36,000 yuan, it falls in this bracket. Counting only principal and ignoring the time value of money, that tax saving does not exceed the tax later due when the principal is withdrawn, so the tax deduction alone cannot establish that contributing is worthwhile. Having individual income tax withheld from your monthly wages does not mean your full-year income falls in the 10% bracket. The annual contribution limit is calculated by calendar year, and unused allowance cannot be carried forward. China’s personal pension system took effect nationwide on December 15, 2024. From September 1, 2025, early withdrawal is also permitted for those who meet specified conditions involving medical expenses, receipt of unemployment benefits, or minimum living assistance. You cannot withdraw at will before meeting a withdrawal condition, so the account is unsuitable for emergency funds you may need at any time (nationwide, China).
entries.sources: Ministry of Finance and State Taxation Administration of China (2024). Announcement on Implementing Preferential Individual Income Tax Policies for Personal Pensions Nationwide (Ministry of Finance and State Taxation Administration Announcement No. 21 of 2024, December 12, 2024). <https://fgk.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfgk/c102416/c5237110/content.html>; Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security of China and four other departments (2022). Measures for the Implementation of Personal Pensions (Articles 7, 8, 9, 12, and 13). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-11/05/content_5724783.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress of China (2018). Individual Income Tax Law of the People’s Republic of China (seventh amendment of 2018, Individual Income Tax Rate Schedule 1). <http://www.npc.gov.cn/zgrdw/npc/xinwen/2018-09/05/content_2060671.htm>; Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security of China and four other departments (2025). Notice on Matters Concerning the Withdrawal of Personal Pensions (Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security Document [2025] No. 39, items 1, 2, 3, and 7). <https://fgk.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfgk/c100013/c5242402/content.html>
entries.notes: There are currently six withdrawal conditions: reaching the age for claiming a basic pension, becoming completely unable to work, settling abroad or outside mainland China, and the following three. For medical expenses, the relevant period is the 12 months before the application. Eligible expenses are the applicant’s, spouse’s, or minor children’s out-of-pocket costs for items covered by the medical insurance catalog after insurance reimbursement. The cumulative amount must exceed the province’s per capita disposable income for residents in the previous year. For unemployment, the question is whether unemployment insurance benefits were received for a total of at least 12 months in the 2 years before the application. For minimum living assistance, the applicant must currently be receiving urban or rural minimum living assistance payments. If you meet any one condition, you can apply for verification through the bank where you opened the account, China’s National Social Insurance Public Service Platform, or other channels. If the money has already been used to buy a product, you must also follow that product’s rules. Do not put emergency funds into the account (see item 27 on emergency funds). Whether contributing is worthwhile also depends on how long you can leave the money invested, the product’s returns, fees, and risks; you cannot decide from the tax saving alone. You must choose products in which to invest the money in the account, and some products can lose value. For choosing products, see items 17 and 18 of this section (broad-market index funds and preferring lower fees). Proof of the deduction is issued by the Personal Pension Information Management Service Platform. For wages, salaries, and other income subject to the cumulative withholding method, the deduction may be taken during withholding in the current year or in the following year’s annual tax reconciliation. For other income, the deduction is taken during the following year’s reconciliation as required (see item 2 on annual tax reconciliation).

entries.title: Pay for the gym by the visit or for a short term unless you have a stable attendance record of more than a year
entries.cost: If you pay by the visit, each visit costs a little more than the per-visit cost implied by an annual membership. You need to estimate honestly how many times you will actually go each month.
entries.summary: In the three years of U.S. data, members who chose contracts costing more than $70 a month went an average of only 4.3 times a month, equivalent to more than $17 per visit. Yet a 10-visit pass cost only $10 per visit. These members paid an average of $600 extra over the course of their memberships. Unless you already have a record of going regularly for more than a year, paying by the visit or buying a short-term pass is better value.
entries.benefit: This study examined three years of data on 7,752 members of three U.S. fitness clubs. Members who chose contracts costing more than $70 a month went an average of only 4.3 times a month, equivalent to more than $17 per visit. A 10-visit pass, by comparison, cost only $10 per visit. These members paid an average of $600 extra over the course of their memberships. In addition, the proportion of monthly-paying members who had still not canceled after more than a year was 17% higher than the proportion of annual-paying members (United States, three years of panel data).
entries.sources: DellaVigna S, Malmendier U (2006). Paying Not to Go to the Gym. American Economic Review 96(3):694-719. <https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.96.3.694>
entries.notes: This is only one study, and it uses U.S. data. But the underlying principle is widespread: people overestimate their future self-control. If you already have a record of going more than twice a week for a full year, an annual membership really is cheaper.

entries.title: Get a written contract when you prepay; a business facing serious risks must stop taking prepayments, and you have the right to recover your unused balance before it shuts down and disappears
entries.cost: It costs nothing. The hard part is insisting on a written contract on the spot instead of accepting “top up your balance first and we’ll sort it out later.”
entries.summary: When a business takes your prepayment, it must sign a written contract with you that explains how refunds work. If the business develops serious operating problems, it must stop taking prepayments; it must also tell you in advance if it is going to close or relocate. You can then require it to continue providing the service or refund the unused balance. A business that violates these rules can be fined.
entries.benefit: The Chinese regulations require a business that takes prepayments to enter into a written contract that specifies how refunds will be made. If the business faces major operating risks, it must stop collecting prepayments. If it decides to close or relocate, it must inform consumers in advance. Consumers have the right to require the business to continue fulfilling the contract or to refund the unused balance. Violations may be punished by a fine of 1 to 10 times the unlawful gains; if there are no unlawful gains, the fine may be up to 500,000 yuan.
entries.sources: State Council (2024). Regulations on the Implementation of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests (State Council Decree No. 778, effective July 1, 2024). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202403/content_6940159.htm> Article 22: "Where a business operator provides commodities or services by collecting advance payments, it shall enter into a written contract with the consumer specifying matters such as the specific content of the commodities or services, prices or fees, methods of refunding advance payments, and liability for breach of contract." "Where a business operator fails to provide commodities or services as agreed, it shall perform the agreement or refund the advance payment as requested by the consumer." "Where a business operator encounters major business risks that may affect its normal provision of commodities or services in accordance with contract stipulations or transaction practices, it shall stop collecting advance payments. Where a business operator decides to suspend business or relocate service premises, it shall notify consumers in advance... Consumers... have the right to request the business operator to continue performing its obligation to provide commodities or services, or request a refund of the unused advance payment balance."; Article 50, Paragraph 2: "Where a business operator violates the provisions of Article 22 of these Regulations, the relevant administrative department shall order it to make corrections, and may, depending on the circumstances, issue a warning, confiscate illegal income, and/or impose a fine of not less than 1 time but not more than 10 times the illegal income; where there is no illegal income, impose a fine of not more than 500,000 yuan"
entries.notes: The regulation provides legal grounds for post-incident litigation; it cannot prevent issues beforehand. If a merchant really runs away, the money is most likely no longer in the account. Therefore, first follow the entry "Pay per visit or for short cycles at gyms" in this section to top up less; if something really happens, then rely on this regulation to defend your rights. Article 27 of the same regulation also specifies that when merchants collect deposits, they must agree in advance on the method, procedure, and timeframe for refunds, and must not set unreasonable conditions on refunds.

entries.title: Set a 24-hour cooling-off period for large non-essential purchases; make good use of the 7-day unconditional return policy for online shopping
entries.cost: Costs nothing. The thing you want will be received one day later. Return shipping costs usually have to be paid by yourself. The hard part is refraining from placing the order on the day.
entries.summary: What you save on are the things you no longer want the next day. For online purchases, you can return them without giving a reason within seven days starting from the date you receive the goods. Several categories cannot be returned: customized to your specifications, fresh and perishable goods, unsealed digital products, and newspapers or periodicals.
entries.benefit: What is saved is the portion of impulse buys that "you no longer want the next day." As for what proportion this accounts for, no uniform figure can be given. For commodities purchased online, they can be returned without reason within seven days starting from the date of receipt. Four categories are excluded: customized goods, fresh and perishable goods, unsealed digital products, and newspapers/periodicals (China, effective since 2017)
entries.sources: State Administration for Market Regulation (2020 revision). Interim Measures for Seven-Day Unconditional Returns of Online Purchased Commodities (SAMR Decree No. 31). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-11/03/content_5557118.htm>
entries.notes: The "cooling-off period" itself is an empirical practice without direct literature support. What the cooling-off period fails to intercept can still fall back on the institutional mechanism of the 7-day unconditional return policy. Before returning, confirm two things first: whether the commodity is on the non-returnable list, and whether the packaging is still intact.

entries.title: Do not stockpile goods for "crossed-out prices" and major promotions
entries.cost: Costs nothing. The price is that you will also pass up some genuine discounts. You have to remember the everyday prices of the few items you frequently buy. The hard part is refraining from stockpiling on the day of the major promotion.
entries.summary: When people judge whether an item is expensive, they get anchored by the very first number they see, and subsequent adjustments are usually insufficient. Therefore, "original price 999, current price 499" makes you systematically overestimate how cheap it is. According to regulations, the benchmark that must be used for a discount is merely the lowest transaction price in that shop during the seven days prior to the promotion. That crossed-out price was not necessarily ever actually sold at.
entries.benefit: Human judgment gets anchored by the first number seen, and subsequent adjustments are usually insufficient. Thus, "original price 999, current price 499" systematically inflates your estimate of "how much cheaper it is." Regulatory rules require that the benchmark for a price reduction shall be the lowest transaction price in the same shop within the seven days preceding the promotion. What discount is offered must take the lowest price actually sold by this shop in the seven days before the promotion as the reference. That crossed-out price was not necessarily ever actually sold at (China, effective since 2020)
entries.sources: Tversky A, Kahneman D (1974). Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases. Science 185(4157):1124-1131. <https://doi.org/10.1126/science.185.4157.1124>; State Administration for Market Regulation (2020). Interim Provisions on Regulating Promotional Activities (SAMR Decree No. 32, Article 21). <https://www.samr.gov.cn/zw/zfxxgk/fdzdgknr/fgs/art/2023/art_cae53a080be2401e8f91c6d6291539f8.html>
entries.notes: The anchoring effect is a conclusion reached in the laboratory; no one has calculated how much money is actually lost by stockpiling goods. Stockpiling also involves several costs you would not record on the ledger: items expiring, taking up space, and "since there is plenty at home, let's use more." Only stockpile items that meet all three conditions: long shelf life, definitely will be used up, and the unit price is genuinely lower than previous prices.

entries.title: Prioritize pure-protection (consumption-type) insurance, and treat "refunds" and "dividends" as non-guaranteed components
entries.cost: Pure-protection insurance does not return money upon maturity, which might psychologically feel like "this money was spent in vain." Saving money has to be arranged by yourself. The hard part is accepting that this money will not be recovered.
entries.summary: The dividend and refund portions of money are not guaranteed to you by the insurance company. The product manual must state in bold type that "future policy dividends are non-guaranteed benefits." The extra premiums you pay for refunds are equivalent to handing money over to the insurance company to save on your behalf, with unguaranteed returns and poor liquidity when you want to withdraw it.
entries.benefit: Regulatory rules require that the product disclosure manuals for participating (dividend-paying) products must state in bold typeface: "Future policy dividends are non-guaranteed benefits, and their dividend distribution is uncertain." The dividend illustration is the dividend calculation table shown to you by the insurance company, and its upper limit for interest spread is 4.5% minus the product's pricing interest rate. The pricing interest rate is the locked-in rate of return specified in the contract. The extra premiums paid for refund-type and participating-type policies are equivalent to savings entrusted to the insurance company's management. Their returns are not guaranteed, and liquidity is poor, making withdrawals not easy (China, effective since 2023)
entries.sources: China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (2022). Rules on Information Disclosure of Personal Insurance Products with Terms Exceeding One Year (CBIRC Regulations 〔2022〕 No. 24). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2023-01/04/content_5735014.htm>
entries.notes: Controversy: For people who cannot save money at all, refund-type insurance forces regular payments, and this function has practical value. The advice above targets ordinary people who can manage their own finances. Exactly how much better "buying pure-protection insurance and investing the saved premiums yourself" is compared to "buying refund-type insurance" depends on the specific product; there are no systematic data that can be cited in this section. Does not constitute investment advice.

entries.title: Buy sufficient third-party liability insurance: Compulsory traffic insurance limits are nationally uniform and low; excesses come out of your own pocket
entries.cost: Commercial third-party liability insurance costs several hundred to over a thousand yuan a year. The higher the coverage amount purchased, the cheaper the premium amortized per unit of coverage becomes.
entries.summary: When you are at fault, compulsory traffic insurance pays out a maximum across three items: 180,000 yuan for death and disability, 18,000 yuan for medical expenses, and 2,000 yuan for property losses. The three items are calculated separately and cannot be diverted to cover one another. Compensation for injuring someone may exceed these limits, and the excess amount must come out of your own family's pocket, so commercial third-party liability insurance must be bought in sufficient amounts.
entries.benefit: Compulsory traffic insurance implements uniform liability limits nationwide. Limits are divided into four separately calculated items: death and disability, medical expenses, property loss, and compensation when you bear no fault. Following the 2020 comprehensive auto insurance reform, the current total liability limit is 200,000 yuan. Within these 200,000 yuan: 180,000 yuan for death and disability, 18,000 yuan for medical expenses, and 2,000 yuan (0.2万元) for property loss. When you are not at fault: 18,000 yuan for death and disability, 1,800 yuan for medical expenses, and 100 yuan for property loss. Any portion exceeding the limits is borne by the tortfeasor personally; the party that hit someone must pay out of pocket. For those who fail to purchase compulsory traffic insurance, the vehicle will be impounded, and a fine equal to 2 times the required premium payable under the statutory minimum liability limits will be imposed
entries.sources: State Council (2006, 2012 revision). Regulations on Compulsory Traffic Accident Liability Insurance for Motor Vehicles (State Council Decree No. 462, amended by Decree No. 618), Article 23: "Compulsory traffic accident liability insurance for motor vehicles shall implement uniform liability limits nationwide. Liability limits are divided into compensation limits for death and disability, compensation limits for medical expenses, compensation limits for property losses, and compensation limits when the insured bears no liability in a road traffic accident." "Liability limits shall be formulated by the insurance regulatory body in conjunction with the public security department, health department, and agricultural department of the State Council." Article 21 indemnification within limits; Article 39 for failure to insure, "the traffic management department of the public security organ shall impound the motor vehicle... and impose a fine equal to 2 times the insurance premium payable for insuring under the minimum liability limits in accordance with regulations." <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2012/content_2131962.htm>; China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (2020). Guiding Opinions on the Implementation of Comprehensive Auto Insurance Reform (CBIRC Development 〔2020〕 No. 41, IV(4): "Raise the total liability limit of compulsory traffic insurance from 122,000 yuan to 200,000 yuan, among which the compensation limit for death and disability is increased from 110,000 yuan to 180,000 yuan, the compensation limit for medical expenses is increased from 10,000 yuan to 18,000 yuan, and the compensation limit for property losses remains unchanged at 2,000 yuan [0.2万元]"). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2020/content_5567758.htm> (Gazette of the State Council)
entries.notes: The limits are determined by financial regulatory authorities and are subject to adjustment. This set of figures represents the prevailing values following the comprehensive auto insurance reform in September 2020; you can verify them again before purchasing insurance. The key is its structure: compulsory traffic insurance pays out separately by category; if an item's limit is not exhausted, the remaining allowance cannot be diverted to cover another item. Total compensation for injuring someone can vastly exceed it, and no insurance will cover the exceeding difference on your behalf. Regarding exactly how much third-party liability coverage to purchase, this book does not provide a specific figure. However, it is one of the few places in this book where "spending a few hundred extra yuan protects against a very low-probability event that, if it actually happens, can crush an entire family."

entries.title: Save up an emergency fund of 3 to 6 months of living expenses first, and keep it where it can be withdrawn at any time
entries.cost: Costs nothing. The price is that this money must forgo higher yields and can only be kept in demand deposits, money market funds, or readily accessible deposits. The hard part is refraining from touching it while accumulating it.
entries.summary: Keep 3 to 6 months of living expenses in a place where it can be withdrawn at any time. That way, in the event of unemployment or illness, you won't need to borrow high-interest money such as credit card minimum repayments, nor will you have to sell off your investments at a loss. Money deposited in banks is covered by deposit insurance, compensating up to 500,000 yuan per depositor at the same bank.
entries.benefit: With an emergency fund, you won't need to borrow money or sell off investments at a loss when unemployed or ill. For annualized interest rates on consumer loans and credit card minimum repayments, see Item 7 of this section (Do not use credit card minimum repayment). Money deposited in banks is protected by deposit insurance, with a maximum compensation of 500,000 yuan per depositor at the same bank (China, 2015)
entries.sources: State Council (2015). Deposit Insurance Regulations (State Council Decree No. 660, Article 5). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/content/2015-03/31/content_9562.htm>; People's Bank of China, National Financial Regulatory Administration, China Securities Regulatory Commission (2025). Measures for the Customer Due Diligence and Custody of Client Identity Data and Transaction Records by Financial Institutions (Decree 〔2025〕 No. 11, Articles 7, 28, and 52, effective January 1, 2026). <https://www.pbc.gov.cn/tiaofasi/144941/144957/5916164/index.html>; Office of the Financial Commission of the CPC Shanghai Municipal Committee (2025-12-01). Three departments including the central bank issue new regulations; cash withdrawals at banks will no longer face "one-size-fits-all" questioning: "The document removed 'individuals depositing or withdrawing cash exceeding 50,000 yuan must register the source of funds'". <https://jrj.sh.gov.cn/ZXYW178/20251201/1da352ee5150414b8db1ce248f4e37c6.html>
entries.notes: "3 to 6 months" is a universally accepted empirical rule of thumb, but no original official or academic source has been found, so it is rated Grade C. The amount should be calculated based on your own monthly fixed expenditures, not on your income. In the new anti-money laundering measures effective January 1, 2026, the clause "individuals depositing or withdrawing cash exceeding 50,000 yuan must register the source of funds" no longer exists. The new measures require banks to understand the source and intended use of funds only when money laundering risks are relatively high, rather than asking everyone in a blanket manner. Even if a bank needs to restrict transactions, basic and necessary financial services such as healthcare and social security must be safeguarded. Paying medical bills can be done directly via bank transfer or card swipe without needing to withdraw cash first. Does not constitute investment advice.

entries.title: Run a comparative calculation before prepaying your mortgage; do not rely on intuition
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Spend half an hour running the numbers. You need to honestly estimate the stable, after-tax rate of return you can achieve.
entries.summary: Prepaying a mortgage is equivalent to locking in a guaranteed return equal to your mortgage interest rate. Therefore, ask only one thing: Is the stable after-tax return you can achieve over the long term higher than your mortgage rate? If it is higher, do not rush to prepay; if it is not higher or uncertain, then prepay. With equal monthly installments (level payments), interest accounts for a large portion in the early years; the earlier you prepay, the more interest you save. The "prepayment calculator" in banking apps can calculate the exact figures directly.
entries.benefit: Here is the calculation method. First, let the annual mortgage interest rate be r, based on your contract. On August 20, 2026, the LPR for terms over 5 years was 3.5%; actual execution rates add or subtract basis points relative to the LPR. Next, let g be the annualized after-tax yield of your alternative investment: the percentage this money could earn on average per year if invested elsewhere. The definite return rate of prepayment is r; with every prepayment made, it is equivalent to steadily earning r. If g is stably greater than r, keeping the money invested is more cost-effective. If g is less than r, or if g is completely uncertain, prepaying is equivalent to locking in a risk-free return of r. In the first few years of equal monthly installments (level payments), interest accounts for a substantial share of what you pay in, so the earlier you prepay, the more interest you save. This can be viewed directly with specific numbers using the "prepayment trial calculation" feature in banking apps (China, 2026 interest rates)
entries.sources: National Interbank Funding Center authorized by the People's Bank of China (2026). Loan Prime Rate (LPR) Announcement on August 20, 2026. <https://www.chinamoney.com.cn/chinese/rdgz/20260820/3399885.html>
entries.notes: Only the calculation method is provided here, not a definitive conclusion. Situations where investment returns stably exceed the mortgage rate are in the minority. But regardless of which side you choose, you must retain sufficient emergency cash first. In addition, pay attention to whether the contract contains prepayment penalty clauses. Before prepaying, you can first negotiate with the bank for a rate cut; see Section 15, Item 15 (Negotiate interest rate reductions). Does not constitute investment advice.

entries.title: Base online purchases on platform rules and legal provisions, not on live streamers or "positive reviews"
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Check after-sales terms and earnest money (deposit) rules one extra time before placing an order. After receiving the goods, retain the orders, live stream playback screenshots, and chat histories properly. The hard part is not getting swept along by the streamer's atmosphere.
entries.summary: If a merchant defrauds you, compensation is three times the price paid, or a minimum of 500 yuan if the triple amount is less than 500 yuan. If a platform knows a seller is infringing rights but fails to intervene, it bears joint and several liability. Earnest money can be collected up to a maximum of 20% of the contract amount; if you default, the deposit is forfeited, and if the seller defaults, they must refund double the deposit to you. Fabricating orders or fake reviews in live streaming rooms incurs legal liability; big-data price discrimination against existing customers is expressly prohibited.
entries.benefit: Where a business operator commits fraudulent acts, compensation is three times the purchase price, or 500 yuan if the calculated amount is less than 500 yuan. Where a platform knows or should have known that a seller infringes rights but fails to take necessary measures, it shall bear joint and several liability, and you can demand this compensation directly from the platform. Live streaming rooms and streamers must not fabricate traffic figures such as transactions, follows, views, or likes, nor may they publish false information; those causing damage shall bear civil liability. Organizing false transactions and fake reviews to assist others with promotional hype carries a fine of up to 1 million yuan; where circumstances are serious, a fine of 1 million to 2 million yuan may be imposed, and business licenses may be revoked. Earnest money (dingjin) must not exceed 20% of the contract's subject matter value. If you fail to perform the contract, the deposit will not be refunded; if the seller fails to perform, double the deposit must be returned to you. Automated decision-making using personal information must not apply unreasonable differential treatment in transaction prices or other terms, which is colloquially known as big-data price discrimination (nationwide)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2013 amendment). Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests (Articles 44 and 55). <https://www.samr.gov.cn/zfjcj/tzgg/art/2023/art_615af9ed6bcd4974bf853dd2e02bc663.html> (reposted by the State Administration for Market Regulation); Cyberspace Administration of China and seven other departments (2021). Administrative Measures on Online Live Streaming Marketing (Trial) (Articles 18 and 28). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-04/23/content_5601682.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2025 revision). Anti-Unfair Competition Law (Articles 9 and 25). <https://www.ssf.gov.cn/portal/rootfiles/2025/09/01/1758444945285569-1758444945303119.pdf> (reposted by the National Council for Social Security Fund); National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 586 and 587). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/233181.html>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2021). Personal Information Protection Law (Article 24). <https://www.stats.gov.cn/gk/tjfg/xgfxfg/202503/t20250310_1958923.html> (reposted by the National Bureau of Statistics); Shandong Provincial Market Supervision Administration (2025). Six Typical Cases of Online Unfair Competition. <https://www.samr.gov.cn/jjj/fbzdjz/art/2025/art_cbaed1c006584baeb6823a6b01325ba4.html>
entries.notes: Regarding "which platform offers the best value for money and where you are least likely to buy substandard products," there are no official comparative data available to cite, so this book does not provide platform rankings. What can be checked are only overall spot check results (see Item 32, Check national spot-check bulletins). After the 2025 revision of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, false advertising was moved from the former Article 8 to Article 9. Penalties were moved from Article 20 to Article 25. The new law came into effect on October 15, 2025. Do not cite the old article numbers when preparing written materials. Among that batch of cases in Shandong, a company organized "brushers" to conduct 75 false transactions with a principal amount exceeding 680,000 yuan and was investigated and penalized; the fine amount was not specified in the bulletin. For 7-day unconditional returns, see Item 23 of this section (Make good use of the 7-day unconditional return policy for online shopping).

entries.title: When issues arise with items bought in live streaming rooms, first request the seller's and promoter's information from the platform; the platform is obligated to provide it
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Simply submit a request to the platform.
entries.summary: When problems occur with purchases from live streaming rooms, the most common deadlock is not knowing whom to sue. At this point, you can directly demand that the platform provide information regarding the live streaming room operator and the live marketing personnel, as well as relevant business activity records. The platform must provide them.
entries.benefit: When consumer disputes arise, operators of live streaming marketing platforms shall, in accordance with the consumer's request, provide relevant information regarding the live streaming room operator and live marketing personnel, as well as relevant business activity records. The most common difficulty in live stream rights defense is not knowing whom to sue; once you obtain this information, you will know whom to sue
entries.sources: State Council of China (2024). Regulations on the Implementation of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests (State Council Order No. 778, effective July 1, 2024). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202403/content_6940159.htm>: “Where a business operator provides goods or services through online livestreaming or other means, it shall fulfill its obligations concerning the protection of consumer rights and interests in accordance with the law. An operator of a livestream marketing platform shall establish and improve a consumer rights protection system and define a mechanism for resolving consumer disputes. When a consumer dispute arises, the operator of the livestream marketing platform shall, at the consumer’s request, provide necessary information, including information about the livestream room operator and livestream marketing personnel, and records of the relevant business activities.” “Where livestream content published by a livestream room operator or livestream marketing personnel constitutes a commercial advertisement, they shall fulfill the obligations of an advertisement publisher, advertisement operator, or advertising endorser in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Advertising Law of the People’s Republic of China.”
entries.notes: Before placing an order, save a screen recording of the livestream and the host’s promises. If something goes wrong, first ask the platform for information about the seller and the person promoting the product, then decide whether to file a complaint or sue. The same regulations also provide for three things. First, merchants may not expand on their own the range of goods ineligible for a seven-day return without giving a reason. Second, they may not make “ineligible for returns without giving a reason” the default option. Third, they may not refuse your return unless you have confirmed that condition.

entries.title: If you buy unsafe food, you can claim ten times the price in addition to a refund; if the additional compensation is less than 1,000 yuan, it is set at 1,000 yuan
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Keep the food, packaging, and receipt; do not throw them away or wash them, and take photos on the spot. Start with the merchant or platform. If you cannot reach an agreement, call China’s 12315 consumer complaints hotline. If you end up suing, it will take months. The hard part is resisting the urge to throw the item away first.
entries.summary: If you buy expired or spoiled food, the food itself, its packaging, and the receipt are your evidence. Do not rush to throw them away. You can claim compensation equal to ten times the price or three times your loss; if the additional compensation is less than 1,000 yuan, it is set at 1,000 yuan. You choose whether to approach the seller or the producer. Whichever one you approach must pay first and cannot pass you off to the other.
entries.benefit: If you suffer harm from food that does not meet food safety standards, you can demand compensation for your loss from the business operator or from the producer. The party receiving your compensation claim bears primary responsibility: it must pay first and may not shirk responsibility. In other words, whichever party you approach must pay you first and cannot pass you off to the other party. In addition to compensation for your loss, you can demand additional compensation equal to ten times the price or three times the loss, and “where the amount of additional compensation is less than 1,000 yuan, it shall be 1,000 yuan.” There is one exception: “except where defects in the food’s labels or instructions do not affect food safety and would not mislead consumers.” A judicial interpretation sets out several further rules. First, three conditions must all be met. The buyer bought the food for personal or family consumption. The food does not meet food safety standards. And there is no evidence proving that the buyer knew this at the time of purchase. If those conditions are met, “punitive compensation equal to ten times the price shall be calculated on the basis of the price actually paid.” Second, if someone buys food knowing that it does not meet the standards and then claims compensation, the people’s court will uphold the claim only “within the scope of reasonable needs for daily consumption.” For repeated purchases and repeated lawsuits, the total quantity bought across the purchases is assessed within that same scope. Third, courts will not uphold punitive compensation for several types of defects, provided they would not cause consumers to misunderstand the food’s safety. These defects are nonstandard font sizes, typos, extra characters, or missing characters; nonstandard ways of stating net content and specifications; and the absence of storage conditions on foods that have no special storage requirements (throughout China).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress of China (third amendment, 2025). Food Safety Law (Article 148). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=7b5a76d0461745a08d3f964916b87ef3> (National Database of Laws and Regulations of China; effective December 1, 2025); Supreme People’s Court of China (2024). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Punitive Compensation for Food and Drugs (Judicial Interpretation [2024] No. 9, Articles 1, 6, 7, 8, 12, 13, 14, 15, and 16; effective August 22, 2024). <http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/bf531a70471f10d377788f28d3d8f8.html> (Gazette of the Supreme People’s Court of China)
entries.notes: The order in which you gather evidence matters more than the amount of money. First, take photos and videos showing the packaging, production date, foreign object, and purchase record, then contact the merchant or platform. Do not throw the item away or wash it before communicating with them. China’s 12315 service mediates; it does not issue rulings. If the merchant firmly denies responsibility, the only remaining route is to sue. For how small claims litigation works, see Section 8, Item 22 (being scammed in online shopping or secondhand transactions). Also note: whether a foreign object such as a hair or insect found in food means it “does not meet food safety standards” usually has to be determined by the market regulation authorities or through testing. It is not up to you to decide. So the claim that “finding one hair in your food guarantees you 1,000 yuan” is false. Fraud involving ordinary goods is compensated at three times the price, or 500 yuan if that amount is less than 500 yuan. See Item 29 of this section (know the platform rules and legal provisions for online shopping). If you make food to sell, separate rules govern which permits you need, what to put on the label, and why you cannot claim that it treats illness. For details, see Section 12, Items 8 through 11 (food permits, labels, the limits on efficacy claims, and the threshold for criminal liability). Conversely, there are clear limits on turning compensation claims into a business. First, maliciously creating the appearance that a merchant has illegally produced or sold goods, then using complaints or lawsuits to threaten the merchant and demand compensation, may constitute extortion. Courts must transfer the leads and materials to the police. Second, if you sue using a fabricated appearance of wrongdoing, the court will dismiss your claim. If it constitutes a sham lawsuit, you may be fined or detained according to the seriousness of the circumstances. The merchant may also sue you for infringement of reputation. The beneficiaries of this item are you and your family.
