entries.title: Before buying a major item, check national inspection notices, 3C certification, and the energy efficiency label
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Spend a few minutes checking the official websites of China’s State Administration for Market Regulation and Certification and Accreditation Administration.
entries.summary: In 2024, China’s national inspections sampled 25,250 batches of products, and 14.3% failed to meet standards. The e-commerce channel fared worse: 7,297 batches were sampled, and 23.5% failed; the figure for physical stores was 15.1%. Before buying a major item, spend a few minutes checking inspection notices, then check whether its 3C certificate is genuine. If an energy efficiency label is required, it must be present.
entries.benefit: In 2024, China’s national supervisory inspections sampled 25,250 batches of products, with a failure rate of 14.3%. Of these, 7,297 batches were sampled through the e-commerce channel, with a failure rate of 23.5%, up 1.8 percentage points from the previous year. Physical stores accounted for 8,055 sampled batches, with a failure rate of 15.1%. You can check the authenticity of a compulsory product certification (3C) certificate in the “Certification Results” section of the official website of China’s Certification and Accreditation Administration. Energy efficiency labels are mandatory for products in the applicable catalogue. The label must show the energy efficiency grade, energy efficiency indicators, and energy efficiency information code. Forging or misusing an energy efficiency label, or failing to display one when required, is punishable under China’s Energy Conservation Law (throughout China).
entries.sources: State Administration for Market Regulation of China (2025). Notice on the Results of National Supervisory Inspections of Product Quality in 2024. <https://www.samr.gov.cn/zw/zfxxgk/fdzdgknr/zljds/art/2025/art_02676c16ac634fd9a48ec6ea10eb000d.html>; Certification and Accreditation Administration of China. “Certification Results” search entry on its official website. <https://www.cnca.gov.cn/>; National Development and Reform Commission of China and General Administration of Quality Supervision, Inspection and Quarantine of China (2016). Measures for the Administration of Energy Efficiency Labels (Order No. 35, Articles 3, 7, and 27). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2021-11/30/content_5713245.htm>
entries.notes: In an inspection, regulators select some goods for testing. The results are not the compliance rate for the whole market, and you cannot use them to rank platforms. There is no research on how much checking reduces your chance of buying substandard products, so this is rated B. The Certification and Accreditation Administration’s search platform at cx.cnca.cn could not be opened when this section was verified; use the entry point on the cnca.gov.cn homepage. The figures in inspection notices are updated every year, so check the latest notice when you use them.

entries.title: Treat beaded bracelets, jade, luxury watches, and collectible toys as money spent, not money saved
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Just do not count “it may appreciate later” among your reasons for buying. The hard part is resisting the urge to increase your budget for something said to “hold its value.”
entries.summary: The prices of these items already include consumption tax, with value-added tax calculated separately. Watches priced at 10,000 yuan or more each are taxed at 20%; gold, silver, and platinum jewelry and diamonds at 5%; and other jewelry and gemstones at 10%. You do not get that tax back when you resell the item. If you really like it, buy it as a purchase for your own enjoyment, not as an investment.
entries.benefit: First, consider the purchase. The rates in the Consumption Tax Taxable Items and Rates Schedule are as follows: “luxury watches,” 20%; under “precious jewelry and gemstones,” gold and silver jewelry, platinum jewelry, diamonds, and diamond jewelry, 5%; other precious jewelry and gemstones, 10%. “Luxury watches” means “all types of watches with a selling price, excluding value-added tax, of 10,000 yuan or more per watch.” Next, consider turning the item into cash. The basis here is China’s Measures for the Administration of Pawnshops. Article 36: the pawn term may not exceed six months. Article 37 concerns the interest rate on the pawn loan, meaning the interest on the money the pawnshop lends you. This interest is calculated using the statutory six-month lending rate published by the People’s Bank of China and the pawn term. Interest may not be deducted in advance from the money paid to you. Article 38: the monthly comprehensive fee rate for pawning movable property as collateral, such as a watch or jade, may not exceed 42‰ of the pawn loan. The separate comprehensive fee charged each month may not exceed 4.2% of the amount borrowed. The rate is 27‰ for a real estate mortgage and 24‰ for a pledge of property rights. Article 40: if you neither redeem nor renew the pawn within five days after the term expires, it becomes an unredeemed pawn and the item no longer waits for you to redeem it. Article 43: an unredeemed item valued at more than 30,000 yuan may be entrusted for auction. Auction expenses and the principal and interest of the pawn loan are deducted from the auction proceeds first. Any remainder is returned to the customer; any shortfall may still be recovered from the customer (throughout China). Article 11 of the Interim Regulations on Consumption Tax provides only that taxable consumer goods for export are exempt; it contains no provision for refunding consumption tax when an individual resells something they bought.
entries.sources: State Council of China (2008). Interim Regulations of the People’s Republic of China on Consumption Tax (State Council Order No. 539, including the attached Consumption Tax Taxable Items and Rates Schedule). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-11/14/content_1795.htm>; Ministry of Finance of China and State Administration of Taxation of China (2006). Notice on Adjusting and Improving Consumption Tax Policies (Finance and Taxation [2006] No. 33). <http://www.mof.gov.cn/zhengwuxinxi/zhengcefabu/2006zcfb/200805/t20080524_34758.htm>; Ministry of Commerce of China and Ministry of Public Security of China (2005). Measures for the Administration of Pawnshops (2005 Order No. 8, Articles 36, 37, 38, 40, and 43). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2005/content_93074.htm>
entries.notes: If you pawn an item, do the math carefully: the cap on the monthly comprehensive fee is 42‰ of the loan amount, which comes to roughly half the loan amount over a year. Interest on the loan is extra. That “half over a year” is a rough figure obtained by multiplying the monthly fee rate directly by 12 to show the order of magnitude; it is not an exact annual interest rate. The tax rates and fee rates are figures explicitly stated in the rules. The conclusion that “you cannot recover that tax when you resell the item” is inferred from the absence of a refund provision in the regulations. There are no official statistics this book can cite on whether these items appreciate over the long term, so it makes no predictions and offers no judgment on any category. The point is only to stop you from treating consumption as an investment. If you like something and enjoy wearing it, there is no problem buying it for your own enjoyment. Increasing your budget because it will “hold its value” or “sell for more later” is where you risk losing money. Gold also has two sides: investment gold bars bought and sold by weight are different from jewelry sold by the piece. Jewelry prices include design and workmanship costs, which are usually not counted when it is bought back. Listing prices on secondhand platforms are not sale prices; do not treat them as market prices.

entries.title: For jewelry and gemstones, accept only a test report bearing the CMA mark, and check the institution on the issuing authority’s official website
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Check the issuing institution’s qualifications once before placing an order; it takes only a few minutes.
entries.summary: Certificates can be forged, so check the institution that issued the certificate. A testing institution must be accredited to issue reports to the public, and its report must bear the CMA mark. The issuing authority publishes a list of institutions on its official website, so you can check whether the institution is on it. In a case investigated by Chinese authorities, a “national testing certificate” accompanying the goods had been made through someone the seller contacted.
entries.benefit: First, the rules, from China’s Measures for the Administration of the Accreditation of Inspection and Testing Institutions. Article 2: accreditation is an evaluation and authorization of inspection and testing institutions that “issue data and results with evidentiary effect to the public”: the institution is reviewed before being authorized to issue certificates. Article 15: the accreditation mark consists of two parts, the CMA design and the accreditation certificate number. Article 21: when an institution issues data or results with evidentiary effect to the public, it must place the accreditation mark on the inspection and testing report. Article 22: the accreditation authority must publish information about accredited institutions on its official website and indicate the status of their certificates. Article 34: issuing data or results with evidentiary effect to the public without obtaining accreditation in accordance with the law incurs a fine of 30,000 yuan. Article 37: forging, altering, or misusing an accreditation certificate or mark incurs a fine of up to 30,000 yuan. Next, official cases from the “Crack Down on Counterfeits and Clear Their Sources” examples involving traditional crafts markets, published by China’s State Administration for Market Regulation on June 4, 2026. First, a livestream room in Donghai, Jiangsu, claimed it was selling “natural, untreated by acid, unenhanced Grade A jadeite from Myanmar.” The livestream room also displayed a “national testing certificate.” Testing found dyed quartzite jade, treated jadeite, glass, and plastic instead. The person involved had contacted someone to make that certificate. Second, in another case in the same county, authorities seized 469 products suspected of being counterfeit natural crystal; tests showed that 210 were natural crystal and 259 were synthetic crystal. Third, a shop in Zhenping, Henan, made its own display board for livestreaming. It read “GIA CMA Zhongyu Jewelry and Gemstone Appraisal Center Certified Partner.” The shop had also bought 181 certificate-of-conformity labels bearing the name “National Jewelry and Gemstone Quality Supervision and Inspection Center” online. These labels were sold together with bracelets (throughout China).
entries.sources: General Administration of Quality Supervision, Inspection and Quarantine of China (issued 2015, amended 2021). Measures for the Administration of the Accreditation of Inspection and Testing Institutions (Articles 2, 15, 21, 22, 34, and 37). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2021-04/22/content_5723677.htm>; State Administration for Market Regulation of China (2026). State Administration for Market Regulation Publishes a Group of Typical “Crack Down on Counterfeits and Clear Their Sources” Cases in Traditional Crafts Markets. <https://www.samr.gov.cn/xw/zj/art/2026/art_1529399cfe874b8780c4496eb0158020.html>; Standardization Administration of China. GB/T 16552—2017, Jewelry and Gemstones—Nomenclature (current standard, implemented May 1, 2018). <https://openstd.samr.gov.cn/bzgk/gb/newGbInfo?hcno=18FFB042811998A0309E05CF452B2438>
entries.notes: China has a national standard for naming jewelry and gemstones. A test finding may be written as “quartzite jade (dyed)” or “jadeite (treated),” with a qualification in parentheses. Those words in parentheses account for the price difference. “Grade A,” “from an old pit,” and “unenhanced” are seller’s claims, not appraisal findings. The livestream room selling dyed quartzite jade used exactly this language. Other tactics appeared in the same group of cases: faking a mining site, arranging for people to pose as “miners” on a livestream, using paid commenters to create excitement in the livestream room, and inventing stories about an “urgent need for money” or a “seriously ill family member.” Some sellers also claimed products could “prevent and treat rheumatism, boost immunity, improve sleep quality, and clear blood vessels”; these claims were investigated as false advertising. For general checks before buying a major item, see Item 32 of this section (check inspection notices and 3C certification). For whom to approach when something goes wrong in a livestream room, see Items 29 and 30 (know platform rules for online shopping; ask the platform for information when a problem arises in a livestream room).

entries.title: Treat blind boxes, card draws, and other randomized sales as money you will not get back
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Set a firm budget before buying. The hard part is stopping even when you do not draw the one you want.
entries.summary: Merchants must prominently display the rules of the draw, the probabilities, and the number of limited-edition items. They may not manipulate results behind the scenes or include empty boxes. The document only encourages merchants to offer a guaranteed outcome and set limits on spending and the number of draws. For blind boxes bought online, if the merchant has clearly explained the terms and you have confirmed them, you cannot return the box within seven days without giving a reason after opening it.
entries.benefit: The basis is China’s Guidelines for Regulating Blind Box Business Practices (Trial). Article 9 lists key information that must be prominently disclosed so consumers know it before buying: product name, type, style, rules of the draw, product distribution, number of limited-edition products released, probability of drawing each product, and range of product values. The same article also prohibits three practices. First, a business operator may not indirectly induce purchases by manipulating the draw result through the backend, arbitrarily changing the probabilities, or similar means. Second, it may not refuse or deliberately delay delivery of a blind box by offering cash conversion, repurchase, or an exchange purchase. Third, it may not include empty boxes. Article 11 merely “encourages” business operators to establish a guaranteed-outcome mechanism and guide rational spending by setting limits on the time spent drawing, the amount spent, and the number of draws. Article 17 covers blind box products sold online. Where the business operator has fully informed and alerted the consumer, and the consumer has confirmed this for that individual purchase, the seven-day right to return without giving a reason may be inapplicable after the blind box is opened. The business operator may not replace the consumer’s confirmation with a box checked by default. Article 21: a business operator may not conduct gambling activities, or activities that amount to gambling, in the name of blind boxes. Article 23: blind boxes may not be sold to children under eight; sales to minors aged eight or older require confirmation, in accordance with the law, that the relevant guardian has consented (throughout China).
entries.sources: State Administration for Market Regulation of China (2023). Guidelines for Regulating Blind Box Business Practices (Trial) (State Administration for Market Regulation Enforcement Notice [2023] No. 39, Articles 9, 11, 17, 21, and 23). <https://www.samr.gov.cn/zw/zfxxgk/fdzdgknr/zfjcs/art/2023/art_e2facd76a7fb4e90b03912cffb5e7d53.html>
entries.notes: This document is guidance on what businesses should do; it is not itself a basis for penalties. If something goes wrong, the matter is handled under China’s Product Quality Law, Anti-Unfair Competition Law, and Consumer Rights and Interests Protection Law. There are three specific grounds on which you can file a complaint: the probabilities were not disclosed, the disclosed probabilities did not match the actual ones, or you bought an empty box. Before complaining, screen-record the rules shown on the page and the unboxing process. There is a condition for excluding opened products from the seven-day no-reason return policy: the seller must have fully informed you, you must have confirmed this for that individual purchase, and the seller cannot use a preselected checkbox to confirm on your behalf. Separate rules apply to sales to minors: sellers must not sell to children under eight, and for those aged eight or older, they must first confirm that a guardian has consented. For refunds when a child uses a phone to top up an account or send tips, see Item 9 of this section (Children using phones to top up accounts and send tips). For a 24-hour cooling-off period for large nonessential purchases, see Item 23 (Set a cooling-off period for large nonessential purchases). For the cycle of “the excitement fades as soon as you have it, so you keep buying,” see Section 6, Item 23 (Don’t expect buying things to improve your mood).

entries.title: If you care what has been added to food, buy the prepackaged version: Chinese law does not require an ingredients list at bulk-food counters
entries.cost: Costs nothing. The prepackaged version of the same food is usually a little more expensive than the bulk version. Checking the ingredients list takes a few seconds.
entries.summary: Chinese law requires an ingredients list only on prepackaged food, not on food sold in bulk. Bulk-food counters need only display the name, production date, shelf life, and producer. So “no additives listed” does not mean “no additives added”; it means only that the law does not require them to be listed. If you care, buy the prepackaged version, which has the ingredients list and names of additives printed on it.
entries.benefit: Article 67 of China’s Food Safety Law requires labels on prepackaged food. The label must state nine categories of information. The second is “ingredients or an ingredients list,” and the seventh is “the generic names, as specified in national standards, of the food additives used.” Article 68 requires much less for food sold in bulk. It says: when selling food in bulk, food businesses must mark its container or outer packaging with “the food’s name, production date or production batch number, shelf life, and the name, address, contact details, and other information of the producer and business operator.” This article mentions neither an ingredients list nor additives. The difference is especially clear with frozen aquatic products. GB 2760—2024 permits phosphoric acid and phosphates to be used in frozen aquatic products as moisture-retaining agents, commonly called water-retention agents. The maximum permitted amount is 5.0 g/kg, calculated as phosphate radicals. Use within that limit is legal. The problems are excessive use and adding ice to increase weight. After CCTV’s 2025 March 15 Gala exposed shrimp products with “unlawful, excessive addition of water-retention agents (compound phosphates) and added ice to increase weight,” market regulators required companies to “clearly state on product labels the water-retention agent ingredients (such as phosphates), net content (excluding the weight of the ice glaze), and ingredients list” (China nationwide; the Food Safety Law was amended for the third time in 2025 and took effect on December 1, 2025).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (third amendment in 2025). Food Safety Law of the People’s Republic of China (Articles 67 and 68; promulgated September 12, 2025; effective December 1, 2025). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=7b5a76d0461745a08d3f964916b87ef3>; National Health Commission and State Administration for Market Regulation (2024). National Food Safety Standard: Standard for the Use of Food Additives (GB 2760—2024, Appendix A, Table A.1, food category 09.02.01, frozen aquatic products, under “phosphoric acid and phosphates”; A.3 provides that food additives listed in Table A.1 must be used within the specified scope and maximum amounts). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202403/content_7001729.htm>; Lu’an Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (2025). Advisory and Warning Letter to Relevant Businesses Producing Aquatic Products or Using Water-Retention Agents (March 24, 2025). <https://scjgj.luan.gov.cn/zwzx/tzgg/5414606.html>
entries.notes: “Not listed” does not mean “not added”; it means only that the law does not require it to be listed. If you want to know the ingredients, buy the prepackaged version. For frozen peeled shrimp, frozen fish pieces, and similar products, the net content on the prepackaged product excludes the ice glaze. Calculate the unit price from that weight to get the real price. Bulk products are priced according to the displayed price, but may shrink substantially after thawing. Water-retention agents are legal within the limit and are not a safety problem; do not treat them as poison. Excessive additions and adding ice to increase weight are a money issue: you have paid the price of seafood for water. Conversely, a bulk-food counter may fail to display even the four required categories of information. If any of the name, production date, shelf life, or producer and business operator’s name, address, and phone number is missing, it violates Article 68. You can choose not to buy it, or call China’s 12315 consumer complaint hotline. For how to label prepackaged food if you run a shop yourself, see Section 12, Item 9 (Prepackaged food labels). The beneficiaries of this item are you and your family, placing it in the top two tiers.

entries.title: Sell losing stocks according to rules you set in advance; don’t count on buying more as the price falls to lower your average cost and recover your losses
entries.cost: Costs nothing. The hard part is admitting that this investment has already lost money and then selling it.
entries.summary: People often sell their winners and stubbornly hold their losers. In seven years of records from 10,000 US accounts, a stock that had risen was over 50% more likely to be sold than one that had fallen. The same investors were also more inclined to buy more of their losing stocks. Yet, over the following year, the losing stocks they kept underperformed the winning stocks they sold by an average of 3.4 percentage points.
entries.benefit: This study examined all transactions from 1987 to 1993 in 10,000 accounts at a US discount brokerage. The proportion of gains realized (PGR) was 0.148. The proportion of losses realized (PLR) was 0.098. The difference was 0.050, with a t-statistic above 35. On any given day, a stock that had risen was over 50% more likely to be sold than one that had fallen. The same accounts were also more inclined to buy more of their losing stocks. The proportion of losing stocks bought again was 0.135, versus 0.094 for winning stocks, with a t-statistic of 19. The study also tested the idea that “the ones you keep will recover.” It found the opposite: over the following year, the winning stocks sold had an average excess return 3.4 percentage points higher than the losing stocks kept. Excess return means the portion of the return above that of the market index. The authors also calculated an example using average values. For an equal US$1,000 sale of stock, selling the losing stock rather than the winning stock produced a return about 4.4% higher over the following year. That 4.4% included tax savings from claiming a deduction sooner by selling the losing stock. The tax deduction was calculated under the US tax system (United States, 1987–1993).
entries.sources: Odean T (1998). Are Investors Reluctant to Realize Their Losses? The Journal of Finance 53(5):1775-1798. <https://doi.org/10.1111/0022-1082.00072>
entries.notes: This item addresses “whether to sell”; Item 15 (Don’t trade stocks frequently) addresses “don’t keep taking action.” The two do not conflict. In the author’s experience, setting rules in advance and following them actually means trading less often; the study did not measure this. Buying more as the price falls does lower your average cost: mathematically, buying more at a lower price makes the average cost lower. The mistake is treating it as a way to recover your losses. Its actual effect is to increase the amount of money you have staked on that one stock; see Item 19 (Don’t put all your money in one stock). The tax deduction portion was calculated under the US tax system and cannot simply be applied in China; the rest of the findings still hold. These are US account data from the 1980s and 1990s; trading costs and taxes in China’s A-share market differ. This is not investment advice.

entries.title: If you want to buy overseas assets such as US stocks, use QDII funds or Stock Connect; don’t open an account with an overseas broker or use your annual foreign-exchange purchase allowance to buy them
entries.cost: Costs nothing. You can buy QDII funds in your own bank or brokerage app in a few minutes. The trade-off is a smaller selection than an overseas broker offers.
entries.summary: From May 2026, overseas brokers such as Tiger, Futu, and Longbridge are no longer allowed to open accounts for people in mainland China. For accounts already open, investors can only sell and transfer their money out during the two-year period; they cannot buy more. The annual foreign-exchange purchase allowance cannot be used to buy overseas stocks either. Violators lose access to that allowance for the current year and the following two years. If you want to buy overseas assets, use QDII funds or Stock Connect.
entries.benefit: On May 22, 2026, eight Chinese agencies—the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, Ministry of Public Security, People’s Bank of China, State Administration for Market Regulation, National Financial Regulatory Administration, Cyberspace Administration of China, and State Administration of Foreign Exchange—issued the Implementation Plan for the Comprehensive Rectification of Illegal Cross-Border Securities, Futures, and Fund Business Activities. Its overall requirement is to “completely eliminate illegal cross-border business activities by overseas securities, futures, and fund institutions after two years of concentrated rectification.” Overseas institutions may not market or solicit customers within mainland China or “provide related transaction services such as account opening, processing trading instructions, and fund transfers.” For people with existing accounts, the plan says to “prohibit overseas institutions from illegally providing existing investors in mainland China with services such as buy transactions and transfers of funds in; allow only one-way sell transactions and transfers of funds out.” After the two-year period, mainland Chinese websites, trading software, and supporting servers are to be “completely shut down.” On the same day, the CSRC announced plans to confiscate all illegal proceeds of the relevant domestic and overseas entities associated with Tiger, Futu, and Longbridge and impose severe penalties in accordance with the law. An accompanying response to reporters says authorities will “guide mainland Chinese investors to invest overseas through lawful channels such as Stock Connect, Qualified Domestic Institutional Investors (QDII), and Cross-Boundary Wealth Management Connect.” On foreign-exchange purchases, the State Administration of Foreign Exchange’s Personal Application for Foreign Exchange Purchase states that foreign exchange purchased by individuals “must not be used for capital-account items that have not yet been opened, such as buying property overseas, securities investment, buying life insurance, and buying investment-linked insurance with returns or dividends.” Violators are placed on a “watch list” and “will not have access to the individual simplified allowance in the current year and the following two consecutive years.” They may also face administrative penalties and referral for an anti-money-laundering investigation, and the information will be included in their personal credit records (China nationwide, from May 2026).
entries.sources: China Securities Regulatory Commission (2026-05-22). The China Securities Regulatory Commission and Seven Other Agencies Jointly Issue the Implementation Plan for the Comprehensive Rectification of Illegal Cross-Border Securities, Futures, and Fund Business Activities. <https://www.csrc.gov.cn/csrc/c100028/c7634324/content.shtml>; China Securities Regulatory Commission (2026-05-22). Relevant Officials of the China Securities Regulatory Commission Answer Reporters’ Questions About the Implementation Plan for the Comprehensive Rectification of Illegal Cross-Border Securities, Futures, and Fund Business Activities. <https://www.csrc.gov.cn/csrc/c100028/c7634328/content.shtml>; China Securities Regulatory Commission (2026-05-22). The CSRC Takes Serious Action Against Tiger and Other Institutions in Cases of Illegal Cross-Border Business. <https://www.csrc.gov.cn/csrc/c100028/c7634330/content.shtml>; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (2021). Personal Application for Foreign Exchange Purchase (Appendix 1). <https://www.safe.gov.cn/safe/file/file/20210402/30fab7a9646f417ca9d2f67ff4c1e5f0.pdf>
entries.notes: These documents regulate overseas institutions; they do not specify penalties for investors themselves. If you already have an account with an overseas broker, you can sell and transfer the money back within the two-year period. Each of the three lawful channels has its own eligibility requirements; ask your bank or broker about them first. The fact that US stocks rose substantially in the past does not mean they will do so in the future. For QDII purchases, also follow the approach in Item 17 (Broad-market index funds) and Item 19 (Don’t put all your money in one stock, one platform, or one home). Choose a broad-market index instead of staking everything on a single market. Overseas cash withdrawals have a separate allowance; see Section 21, Item 6 (Overseas cash withdrawals). This is not investment advice.

entries.title: Buy insurance only for losses you could not bear yourself; use an emergency fund for losses you could bear
entries.cost: Costs nothing. List the major losses your household might face and identify which ones your savings could not cover. This takes half an hour once.
entries.summary: The premiums you pay will not all come back as claims payments; some pay the insurer’s expenses and profits. Insurance is therefore worth buying for losses that rarely happen but that your household could not afford if they did, such as a serious illness, injuring someone while driving, or the death of a family breadwinner. Cover smaller losses your savings could bear with an emergency fund.
entries.benefit: Only part of the premiums an insurance company collects is paid out as claims. The rest pays sales and operating expenses and the company’s profits. Chinese regulators require companies selling individual short-term health insurance to publish their “combined loss ratio” on their websites every six months. It is roughly the proportion of premiums paid out in claims; you can check a company’s website to see how much it pays out. So, for a given loss, buying insurance costs you a little money on average over the long run. In return, it spreads a large expense that could overwhelm your household into a small annual payment. The smaller the loss and the more readily you can pay it yourself, the less worthwhile that exchange becomes. By this standard, several types already discussed in this book are worth buying. For annual medical insurance, see Section 7, Item 20 (Annual medical insurance). If you own a car, see Item 26 of this section (Third-party liability insurance). If you travel abroad, see Section 21, Item 4 (Medical care overseas). If someone in your household depends on your income, see Item 40 of this section (Term life insurance) (China nationwide, from 2021).
entries.sources: General Office of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (2021). Notice on Issues Concerning the Regulation of Short-Term Health Insurance Business (CBIRC General Office Document [2021] No. 7; combined loss ratios are disclosed every six months on company websites). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-01/12/content_5579193.htm>
entries.notes: This is rated C because there are no official figures for calculating which types of insurance are financially worthwhile to buy; what is offered here is a way to make the trade-off. For products such as cracked-screen insurance and flight-delay insurance, where the loss is a few hundred yuan and you can afford it yourself, this standard suggests you can skip them. Critical illness insurance compensates for income lost during the years you cannot work because of illness; people with enough savings to cover one or two years out of work can consider skipping it. Basic medical insurance is social insurance and is not assessed by this method; you still need to pay for it. See Section 7, Item 9 (Resident medical insurance). For what should cover small losses, see Item 27 of this section (Emergency fund). The beneficiaries of this item are you and your family.

entries.title: If someone in your household depends on your income, buy term life insurance for the breadwinner first, before buying it for a child
entries.cost: A few hundred to a few thousand yuan a year, depending on age, the coverage amount, and the number of years covered (the author’s rough estimate; no official figures). Before applying, you must disclose your health status truthfully. This takes half an hour once.
entries.summary: Term life insurance covers a fixed number of years. If the insured person dies during that period, the household receives a sum of money. It is intended for family members who depend on your income, such as when the mortgage has not been paid off or your children are still young. If no one depends on you financially, you do not need it. Children do not earn an income, and Chinese law limits how much death insurance taken out for a child can pay.
entries.benefit: Chinese regulators define life insurance as personal insurance with a person’s lifespan as the insured subject. It includes term life insurance, whole life insurance, endowment insurance, and other types. Term life insurance pays benefits if the insured person dies, and its coverage period is a fixed number of years. Whole life insurance covers the person for life. Accidental injury insurance pays only when an accident causes death or disability; it does not pay when someone dies of illness and cannot replace life insurance. A contract that pays benefits upon death requires the insured person’s consent and agreement to the coverage amount; otherwise, the contract is invalid. Parents taking out death insurance for their minor children are exempt from that requirement, but the total benefits payable on a child’s death must not exceed the limit set by the regulator. Life insurance coverage is usually in the hundreds of thousands of yuan, so the benefit is rated large. There is no official formula for how much coverage to buy. The author’s method is to add the outstanding mortgage, the cost of raising the children until adulthood, and several years of household expenses (China nationwide; amended in 2015).
entries.sources: China Insurance Regulatory Commission (2011). Measures for the Administration of Insurance Clauses and Premium Rates of Personal Insurance Companies (CIRC Order No. 3 of 2011, Articles 8 and 12). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2012/content_2163594.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (amended 2015). Articles 33 and 34 of the Insurance Law of the People’s Republic of China. <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7c4060811>
entries.notes: This is rated C because official sources provide only definitions and limits. “Insure adults first” is inferred from the question, “Whose lost income would leave the household unable to get by?” If something happens to a child, the household does not lose an income. If a breadwinner dies, the mortgage and the children’s expenses remain. When money is limited, buy term life insurance and annual medical insurance for the breadwinner first, then medical insurance for the children. For how to assess truthful disclosure and guaranteed renewal, see Section 7, Item 20 (Annual medical insurance). The beneficiaries of this item fall in tier ②: your spouse and children.

entries.title: If you regret signing up for personal insurance lasting more than a year, cancel during the cooling-off period for a nearly full refund of your premiums
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Call the insurance company’s customer service line or visit a service counter; it takes a little over ten minutes. The hard part is settling down to read the contract within 15 days after signing it.
entries.summary: Personal insurance lasting more than a year has a cooling-off period. If bought through a bank, it lasts 15 days after you receive the policy; cancelling during that period incurs at most a 10-yuan processing fee. If you cancel after the cooling-off period, you can recover only the refundable amount stated in the policy, often less than you paid. When the insurer calls to ask whether you understand the policy, do not say you do if you do not.
entries.benefit: For personal insurance with a coverage period exceeding one year, Chinese regulators require the contract to state when the cooling-off period begins and how many days it lasts. It must also state the policyholder’s rights during that period. The cooling-off period for long-term health insurance must be at least 15 days. Insurance bought through a bank with a coverage period exceeding one year must provide a 15-calendar-day cooling-off period in the contract. It starts on the day you receive the policy and acknowledge receipt in writing. The cover of this type of policy must display this notice: “Within 15 days of receiving the insurance contract, you have the right to cancel for a full refund (less a processing fee of no more than 10 yuan). You will incur a loss if you cancel after 15 days.” After the cooling-off period, you can still terminate the contract at any time. Within 30 days, the insurer must refund the policy’s cash value (the refundable portion of the policy) as specified in the contract. A risk notice from financial regulators says that, when long-term personal insurance is cancelled after the cooling-off period, its cash value is often lower than the total premiums paid. For new personal insurance policies lasting more than a year, the insurer must make a follow-up call during the cooling-off period. The call must confirm whether you understand the losses from cancellation and your rights during the cooling-off period (China nationwide, from 2010 and 2019).
entries.sources: General Office of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (2019). Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Insurance Agency Business of Commercial Banks (Yin Bao Jian Ban Fa [2019] No. 179, Articles 36, 67, and 68). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2019-12/03/content_5457853.htm>; China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (2019). Measures for the Administration of Health Insurance (CBIRC Decree 2019 No. 3, Article 15). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2019-12/04/content_5458542.htm>; China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (2022). Information Disclosure Rules for Personal Insurance Products of More than One Year (Yin Bao Jian Gui [2022] No. 24, requiring product specification sheets to explicitly state the starting time, number of days, and rights of the cooling-off period). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2023-01/04/content_5735014.htm>; China Insurance Regulatory Commission (2010). Basic Service Regulations for Personal Insurance Business (CIRC Decree 2010 No. 4, Article 15). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2010/content_1702219.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2015 Amendment). Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 15 and 47. <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7c4060811>; Ningxia Financial Regulatory Bureau (2026-06-16). Risk Warning on Preventing Illegal Surrender Agency. <https://www.nfra.gov.cn/branch/ningxia/view/pages/common/ItemDetail.html?docId=1261442&itemId=2188>
entries.notes: The cooling-off period is a rule set for personal insurance of more than one year. For one-year medical insurance and accident insurance, regulations do not require it; whether it exists depends on the policy terms. For policies not bought at a bank, the number of days is subject to what is written in the contract—upon receiving the policy, immediately turn to the "Cooling-off Period" clause. Participating and savings-type insurance involve larger sums of money, making the cooling-off period most valuable to utilize; see Item 25 of this section (Pure protection type). The benefit is rated "Medium" because what can be saved is the difference between the paid premium and the cash value, commonly ranging from hundreds to thousands of yuan, with no official statistics available. The beneficiary of this item is yourself.

entries.title: Before signing at the bank counter, check clearly whether what is in your hands is a deposit or insurance
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Spend an extra two minutes reading the cover of the contract before signing.
entries.summary: Banks are permitted to sell insurance as agents, but they are forbidden from describing it as a deposit. The cover of an insurance contract must print "Insurance Contract" and the name of the insurance company in large type, and the words "deposit" or "savings" must not appear. If an insurance company is on the cover, this money is not a deposit, and surrendering the policy after the cooling-off period will incur a loss. Those over 65 purchasing at a bank may in principle only be sold products with guaranteed returns.
entries.benefit: Regulations explicitly state that banks must not bundle or confuse the sale of insurance with savings deposits, mutual funds, or bank wealth management products. They must not make simplistic analogies between insurance returns and deposit returns, nor describe non-guaranteed returns as guaranteed. Insurance policy documents and promotional materials are not permitted to use the bank's name or logo, and words such as "deposit," "savings," or "jointly launched with the bank" must not appear. The cover of an insurance policy must print "Insurance Contract" in a font size of no less than size 72, and the insurance company's name in a font size of no less than size 2. For three categories of people buying insurance, in principle only products with guaranteed policy benefits may be sold: applicants over 65 years of age; applicants purchasing regular-pay products who are over 60 years of age; and those whose declared annual income is lower than the local per capita disposable income of residents. Insurance policies for these three categories of people must also be transferred to the insurance company for manual underwriting and must not be automatically issued at bank outlets. Personnel from insurance companies are not allowed to sell insurance inside bank outlets. Insurance of more than one year sold by banks has a 15-day cooling-off period; surrendering after the cooling-off period incurs a loss (Nationwide, effective October 2019)
entries.sources: General Office of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (2019). Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Insurance Agency Business of Commercial Banks (Yin Bao Jian Ban Fa [2019] No. 179, Articles 30, 31, 32, 36, 42, and 49). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2019-12/03/content_5457853.htm>
entries.notes: Rated Tier B because the regulations are written very clearly, but there are no official figures on "how much money misled individuals have lost." Elderly family members are most likely to encounter this when depositing money at a bank; help them check the cover when accompanying them. If a contract has already been signed, surrender it within 15 days according to Item 41 of this section (Cooling-off period). If an employee recommends a wealth management product, verify it in the bank's own app or official website before buying; see Item 51 of this section (Flying slips privately sold by employees). If you feel you were misled and want to know how to file a complaint, see Item 43 of this section (Surrender agency). The beneficiaries of this item are yourself and elderly family members.

entries.title: If you want to surrender an insurance policy, handle it directly with the insurance company yourself instead of using "surrender agents"; if you feel misled, call 12378 to complain
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Calling the insurance company's customer service or visiting the counter yourself involves running around once or twice more compared to handing it over to an intermediary.
entries.summary: Claims online touting "full premium refunds upon surrender" are classified as false information by regulators. These surrender agents take 30% to 50% of the refunded money and will collect your bank card, SIM card, and home address. Once surrendered, coverage is gone as well. If you feel misled, first contact the insurance company's customer service; if negotiations fail, call 12378—the entire process is free.
entries.benefit: In February 2026, the National Financial Regulatory Administration, the Cyberspace Administration of China, the Ministry of Public Security, the People's Bank of China, and the China Securities Regulatory Commission jointly issued a risk warning. It stated that claims such as "full premium refund upon surrender" constitute false information and run counter to laws and regulations such as the Insurance Law. Those operating "rights-defense agencies" charge exorbitant service fees, and if you wish to withdraw halfway through, you may face litigation for "breach of contract." They will also collect your SIM card, bank card, insurance policies, home address, and your children's schools. If this information is resold, you may encounter telecom fraud and unauthorized card charges. The June 2026 warning from the Ningxia Financial Regulatory Bureau detailed this even further: such intermediaries agree to collect an agency fee of 30% to 50% of the surrender payout upon success, and demand exorbitant liquidated damages if the client pulls out midway. They instruct people to fabricate grounds for complaints such as sales misrepresentation or forged signatures. Those who comply may violate the Public Security Administration Punishment Law, and serious cases may constitute joint offenses involving false accusation and frame-up or extortion. Insurance liability terminates immediately upon policy surrender. When purchasing similar insurance in the future, premiums may rise or coverage may be refused due to older age or newly diagnosed health conditions. If genuinely misled, first file a complaint and negotiate through the insurance company's official customer service; if unresolved, call the 12378 Banking and Insurance Consumer Rights Protection Hotline—the whole process is free. If you are merely temporarily unable to afford premiums, you can first ask the insurance company whether services like reduced paid-up insurance or policy loans are available. Reduced paid-up insurance means making no further premium payments in the future, with the sum insured proportionally lowered (Nationwide, 2026)
entries.sources: National Financial Regulatory Administration, Cyberspace Administration of China, Ministry of Public Security, People's Bank of China, China Securities Regulatory Commission (2026-02-06). Risk Warning on Guarding Against the Traps of Illegal "Rights-Defense Agency" Short Videos and Live Streams (Reprinted on the official website of the Cyberspace Administration of China). <https://www.cac.gov.cn/2026-02/06/c_1772110875635198.htm>; Ningxia Financial Regulatory Bureau (2026-06-16). Risk Warning on Preventing Illegal Surrender Agency. <https://www.nfra.gov.cn/branch/ningxia/view/pages/common/ItemDetail.html?docId=1261442&itemId=2188>; Hunan Financial Regulatory Bureau (2025-07-23). Risk Warning on Preventing the Illegal "Surrender Agency" Black and Gray Industry. <https://www.nfra.gov.cn/branch/hunan/view/pages/common/ItemDetail.html?docId=1218753&itemId=1480>
entries.notes: The Hunan Financial Regulatory Bureau reported a case in 2025: a woman was persuaded by a "friend" to use a surrender agent, paid a "consulting fee," and in the end only received a surrender payout based on cash value. Three months after surrendering the policy, she was diagnosed with breast cancer, and that critical illness insurance was already gone. You must calculate whether to surrender for yourself: if the coverage is still needed and you cannot afford it, first ask about reduced paid-up insurance. To surrender during the cooling-off period yourself, see Item 41 of this section (Cooling-off period). Intermediaries for "interest suspension and account hanging" and "anti-debt collection" for credit cards and online loans follow the same routine; see Section 7, Item 23 (Already unable to repay credit cards or online loans). The beneficiary of this item is yourself.

entries.title: Name specific individuals as beneficiaries on the insurance policy, and remember to claim the payout if an accident occurs: claims must be asserted within 5 years for life insurance and 2 years for other insurance
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Fill it in once when applying for insurance; future changes of beneficiary require written notice to the insurance company.
entries.summary: If no beneficiary is designated, or if the beneficiary predeceases the insured, the insurance proceeds are treated as an estate and must first be used to repay debts owed by the deceased. If the beneficiary is designated as "wife So-and-So" and a divorce occurs later, it is treated as having no designated beneficiary at the time of the event. Family members must know that this policy exists: claims must be asserted within 5 years of knowing an event occurred for life insurance, and within 2 years for other insurance.
entries.benefit: The Insurance Law stipulates that beneficiaries are designated by the insured or the policyholder. If designated by the policyholder, consent from the insured is required. In three situations, insurance proceeds are treated as the estate of the insured and distributed under succession rules: First, no beneficiary is designated, or the designation is unclear. Second, the beneficiary dies before the insured and there is no other beneficiary. Third, the beneficiary forfeits or renounces the beneficiary right in accordance with the law and there is no other beneficiary. If the beneficiary and the insured die in the same event and the order of deaths cannot be determined, the beneficiary is presumed to have died first. Money treated as an estate must first satisfy taxes and debts owed by the deceased, with only the remainder being distributed. The Supreme People's Court interpretation explicitly provides: if a beneficiary is designated by "name plus status relationship" and the status relationship changes by the time the event occurs, it is deemed that no beneficiary was designated. A change of beneficiary that has not been notified to the insurance company is ineffective against the insurance company. The limitation period for claiming payouts is 5 years for life insurance and 2 years for other insurance, both calculated from the date when the claimant knew or should have known of the occurrence of the insurance accident. Life insurance coverage amounts are usually in the hundreds of thousands of yuan, hence the benefit is rated "Large" (Nationwide, 2015 Amendment, effective 2021)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2015 Amendment). Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 26, 39, 41, and 42. <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7c4060811>; Supreme People's Court (2020 Amendment). Interpretation (III) on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the "Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China", Article 9, Paragraph 2, Item 3, and Article 10. <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808181799df4000179ac03d7f21115>; National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code of the People's Republic of China, Article 1159. <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5c500bf>
entries.notes: Once the statute of limitations expires, the insurance company can refuse to pay out, and it is very difficult to recover the money via litigation. Therefore, family members must at least know which companies you have purchased insurance from. Update the beneficiary designation following a divorce, remarriage, or the birth of a child. For retrieving money from various places one by one after someone passes away, see Section 25, Item 9 (Retrieving one by one). Using death to clear debts does not work; see Section 29, Item 13 (Debt repayment). The beneficiaries of this item fall into Tier ②, being your spouse and children.

entries.title: Do not spend money buying virtual currencies like Bitcoin or Tether, and do not follow others when invited to invest: transactions are not protected by law, and losses cannot be recovered even through litigation
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Do not buy coins, and do not join crypto groups that claim "order-following" or "guaranteed profits." The cost is missing out on profits when coin prices surge.
entries.summary: Domestically, virtual currencies are not recognized as money; individuals' coin-purchasing transactions can be judged invalid, and losses are borne by oneself. Someone paid about 448,000 yuan to buy Tether from others, and when the platform later prevented withdrawals, their lawsuit demanding the money back was dismissed by the court. Being stolen by others is a different matter: someone who stole coins was sentenced to 7 years in prison for the crime of theft.
entries.benefit: In February 2026, eight government departments including the People's Bank of China issued Circular Yin Fa [2026] No. 42. The circular clearly states that virtual currencies such as Bitcoin, Ether, and Tether "do not possess legal tender status, and should not and cannot be circulated and used as currency in the market." Exchanging RMB for crypto, crypto-to-crypto exchanges, and token financing all constitute illegal financial activities and are "strictly prohibited without exception." Overseas institutions are also forbidden from providing such services to residents within the border. On the personal investment front, the original wording of the circular is: "Where any entity or individual invests in virtual currencies, real-world asset tokens, and related financial products, violating public order and good morals, the relevant civil juristic acts shall be invalid, and any losses arising therefrom shall be borne by themselves." The 2021 Circular Yin Fa [2021] No. 237 was repealed simultaneously, with this sentence retained in the new circular. Court case: From February 2018 to July 2019, a Mr. Tang paid about 448,000 yuan (exact value: 448,000 yuan) to two individuals claiming to be platform merchants to purchase Tether. Later, the platform prevented withdrawals and could not be logged into. He filed a lawsuit to recover the money. The court held that exchanging RMB for virtual currency was an invalid investment act, and the loss must be borne by himself. The court dismissed the lawsuit, and the second instance upheld the ruling (Yixing, Jiangsu, published March 2025). Being stolen from is a different matter: virtual coins worth more than 4 million yuan in someone's account were stolen by a "hacker"; one of the thieves was sentenced to 7 years' imprisonment for the crime of theft and fined 20,000 yuan (Zhengzhou, Henan)
entries.sources: People's Bank of China, National Development and Reform Commission, Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, Ministry of Public Security, State Administration for Market Regulation, National Financial Regulatory Administration, China Securities Regulatory Commission, State Administration of Foreign Exchange (2026). Circular on Further Preventing and Disposing of Risks Related to Virtual Currencies (Yin Fa [2026] No. 42, Articles 1 and 19). <https://www.csrc.gov.cn/csrc/c100028/c7614318/content.shtml> (Published by China Securities Regulatory Commission); Yixing People's Court (2025). Suffering Losses from Virtual Currency Investment: Risk and Liability Are Self-Borne. <https://yx.wxfy.gov.cn/article/detail/2025/09/id/8970543.shtml>; [Good Procuratorial Stories of the New Era] Stealing Virtual Currency Leads to Conviction for Theft (2024). <https://www.yw.gov.cn/art/2024/2/2/art_1229143073_59471301.html> (Reprinted by Yiwu Municipal People's Government Website); People's Court Daily (2024). Criminal Law Characterization of Illegally Stealing Virtual Currency. <http://www.sdcourt.gov.cn/jningzcfy/386500/386502/31441533/index.html> (Reprinted by Zoucheng People's Court Website); Federal Bureau of Investigation (2022). Scammers Target and Exploit Owners of Cryptocurrencies in Liquidity Mining Scam (Alert Number I-072122-PSA). <https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2022/PSA220721>
entries.notes: "Losses are borne by oneself" applies to financial disputes between you and coin sellers or signal callers; courts will not help you recover invested funds, so do not count on filing a lawsuit after the fact. Being stolen from or scammed out of funds constitutes a criminal case, which should still be reported to the police. Those who already hold coins must also guard against theft via QR code scanning. In Lianshui, Jiangsu, someone scanned a code during an in-person meeting, and approximately 57,000 Tether coins were transferred out of their wallet. These coins were worth approximately 394,000 yuan (exact value: 393,665.461434 yuan); an article published in the People's Court Daily argued that this should be prosecuted as theft. The US Federal Bureau of Investigation warned in 2022 of a similar tactic: a prompt requesting a series of permissions pops up in your wallet; once you click agree, the counterparty can transfer out your coins without limit. The prevention methods it provided are: do not connect your wallet to uncertain websites, and periodically use third-party authorization query tools to inspect which websites your wallet has granted token transfer permissions to. Using your own bank card to collect funds, purchase coins, or transfer coins on behalf of others is a different matter and can lead to a criminal conviction; see Section 9, Item 5 ("Part-time jobs" requiring you to use your own card to collect funds). For how to recognize "wealth management" promising high returns, see Item 6 (Walk away immediately upon seeing "high return", "capital preservation", or "guaranteed profit"). For legal channels to buy overseas assets, see Item 38 (Buying US stocks through QDII funds or Hong Kong Stock Connect). This does not constitute investment advice.

entries.title: For people without an employer paying employee pension insurance on their own, paying at the lowest tier and first accumulating the required years is most cost-effective; do not treat it as an instant windfall upon paying, as even at the lowest tier it takes about 10 years of collecting benefits to break even
entries.cost: Funds are paid entirely out of pocket at 20% of the contribution base; even at the lowest tier, it costs several hundred to over a thousand yuan per month. Contributions must be paid on time for at least 15 years, and starting in 2030 this minimum duration will rise year by year toward 20 years. Before completing contributions and retiring, this money cannot be withdrawn.
entries.summary: For individuals without an employer paying employee pension insurance on their own, contributing at the lowest tier and completing the required years is most cost-effective. The bulk of the collected pension is indexed to the local average wage in the year of retirement. Converted at the wage levels of that time, paying at the lowest tier for 15 years and beginning to collect at age 60 takes about 10 years to break even; the portion contributed toward higher tiers takes about 17 years to break even. It is worth paying, but it is not an instant windfall.
entries.benefit: A 2005 State Council decision sets out how to contribute and how to receive a pension. People without an employer who pay their own contributions (formally called flexible workers) contribute 20% of their contribution base, of which 8% is credited to their individual account. Since 2019, they have been able to choose their contribution base, within a range of 60% to 300% of the average wage of employed people at urban employers across all sectors in their province. The pension after retirement has two parts. The first is the basic pension. Add the local average monthly wage of employed workers in the previous year to your own average contribution wage, divide by 2, and you receive 1% of that amount for each full year of contributions. The second is the individual account pension: the money in the account divided by the number of months used to calculate payments. That number is 139 for retirement at age 60 and 170 for retirement at age 55. The later you retire, the smaller the number of months. The following examples are calculated from the formulas, not official figures. Suppose the local average monthly wage in your retirement year is 8,000 yuan, and both average wages used in the calculation are treated as that same amount. All amounts below are expressed at the wage level in the retirement year, and interest credited to the individual account is assumed to keep pace exactly with wage growth. At the lowest contribution level, 60%, the contribution base is 4,800 yuan and the monthly contribution is 960 yuan. Over 15 years, you contribute about 173,000 yuan (172,800 yuan exactly). From age 60, you receive about 1,457 yuan a month: 960 yuan as the basic pension and about 497 yuan from the individual account. That is about 17,500 yuan a year (approximately 17,487 yuan exactly). It takes about 9.9 years of payments to recoup your contributions, meaning until around age 70. At the 100% level, you contribute about 288,000 yuan over 15 years (288,000 yuan exactly) and receive about 2,029 yuan a month. The extra contributions of about 115,000 yuan compared with the lowest level (115,200 yuan exactly) bring only about 572 yuan more per month; it takes about 16.8 years of payments to recoup that extra amount. This is because half of the basic pension calculation uses the local average wage, regardless of how much you contributed, benefiting those who contribute less. At the lowest level, each additional year of contributions still takes about 9.9 years to recoup, making it better value than moving to a higher level. At that level, the basic pension makes up most of the money you receive. This payback period does not depend on local wage levels. Where wages are higher, contributions and payments rise in the same proportion, leaving the payback period unchanged. Contributions made in earlier years have smaller nominal amounts, but the pension paid at retirement is based on the average wage at that time. So if you compare only the nominal amounts paid in and received, you recoup your contributions sooner than 9.9 years. The law requires at least 15 years of cumulative contributions at retirement to receive monthly payments. If you have contributed for less than that, you can continue until you meet the requirement. From January 1, 2030, this minimum will rise by 6 months each year, gradually reaching 20 years. If a person dies, the money remaining in their individual account can be inherited. The state will raise pensions when appropriate in light of growth in average employee wages and increases in prices. If the pension insurance fund does not have enough to make payments, the government provides a subsidy (nationwide).
entries.sources: State Council (2005). Decision on Improving the Basic Pension Insurance System for Enterprise Employees (State Council Document [2005] No. 38, Articles 3 and 6, and the annex “Table of Months Used to Calculate Individual Account Pension Payments”). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_7376.htm>; General Office of the State Council (2019). Comprehensive Plan for Reducing Social Insurance Contribution Rates (General Office of the State Council Document [2019] No. 13, Parts 1 and 3). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2019-04/04/content_5379629.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2024). Decision on Implementing a Gradual Delay of the Statutory Retirement Age (Article 2 of the annex, “State Council Measures on Gradually Delaying the Statutory Retirement Age”). <https://www.gov.cn/yaowen/liebiao/202409/content_6974294.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2010, amended 2018). Social Insurance Law (Articles 10, 12, 13, 14, 16, 17, and 18). <https://www.gov.cn/guoqing/2021-10/29/content_5647616.htm>
entries.notes: The examples are only meant to show the approximate scale. What you can actually receive depends on the local average wage, your contribution level, the interest credited to your individual account, and the year you retire. Pensions are adjusted upward after retirement; that is not included here, so the actual payback period will be somewhat shorter. After a delayed retirement, fewer months are used to calculate payments, so the monthly individual account payment is higher. If you work for an employer, the employer contributes 16% and you contribute 8%. Without an employer, no one pays that 16% for you: you pay the entire 20% yourself. If someone dies before receiving enough payments to recoup their contributions, the balance in the individual account can be inherited, and surviving family members can also receive a funeral subsidy and a bereavement benefit. If you cannot afford the minimum monthly contribution, you can first join the urban and rural residents' pension insurance scheme; see Section 31, Item 11 (working without joining an employer means flexible employment). For whether you can receive a social insurance subsidy, see Section 7, Item 12 (recognition as a person facing employment difficulties). For interrupted contributions and back payments, see Section 7, Item 18 (interrupted social insurance contributions). For transferring your pension insurance relationship after moving to another city, see Section 19, Item 19 (transferring pension and medical insurance relationships to the new place of enrollment).

entries.title: When collecting a new car, inspect it on the spot and keep the invoice and three-guarantees certificate; if a major defect appears in the first 7 days or first 60 days, you may be able to demand a replacement or a refund
entries.cost: No monetary cost. Spend half an hour when collecting the car checking the exterior and interior with the salesperson and verifying the documents supplied with the car. Keep the invoice and three-guarantees certificate. Get a repair order every time you take the car in for repairs. If you need a replacement or refund, you will have to make several trips to the dealership; if you cannot reach an agreement, you will also have to file a complaint or sue.
entries.summary: If a major component such as the engine or transmission needs replacing because of a defect within the first 7 days after you receive a new car, you can demand a replacement car or a refund. Within the first 60 days or 3,000 kilometers, brake or steering failure, a cracked body, a fuel leak, or a battery fire can also entitle you to a replacement or refund. If the same defect remains after repeated repairs during the three-guarantees validity period, you can also obtain a replacement or refund, but you must pay compensation for the car's use based on the distance driven.
entries.benefit: These rules are called the three guarantees for household motor vehicles. They cover passenger vehicles such as sedans and SUVs, as well as pickup trucks, bought for personal use; vehicles used commercially are excluded. The three-guarantees validity period is at least 2 years or 50,000 kilometers, whichever comes first. The free-repair period is at least 3 years or 60,000 kilometers, whichever comes first. The periods start on the invoice date, or on the delivery date if it differs from the invoice date. During the free-repair period, quality problems must be repaired free of charge, with no labor or materials charges. Within the first 7 days, if a quality problem means that the engine, transmission, traction battery, drive motor, or a major component of any of them needs replacing, you may use the invoice and three-guarantees certificate to choose a replacement car or a refund. Within the first 60 days or 3,000 kilometers, you may also choose a replacement or refund if a quality problem causes steering failure, brake failure, a cracked body, a fuel leak, or a traction battery fire. Four other situations qualify for a replacement or refund during the three-guarantees validity period. First, a serious safety fault remains after 2 repairs, or a new serious safety fault occurs. Second, the engine or one of the other three major components has been replaced twice because of a quality problem, but the car still cannot be used normally. Third, the same major part has been replaced twice, but the car still cannot be used normally. Fourth, repairs have taken more than 30 days in total, or the same quality problem has been repaired more than 4 times. For a replacement or refund under these four conditions, you must pay compensation for use, calculated as car price × distance driven ÷ 1,000 × n. The manufacturer states n on the three-guarantees certificate; it cannot exceed 0.5%. If a single repair takes more than 5 days, the dealership must provide a loan car or cover transportation costs starting on day 6. When replacing or refunding the car, the dealership must also reimburse the vehicle registration fee, the cost of added accessories or decoration after depreciation, and any service fees it charged you. After receiving a replacement or refund request, the dealership must respond within 10 working days and give reasons if it refuses. It cannot refuse its three-guarantees obligations because you did not have the car serviced there. Intentional delay or refusal to honor the three guarantees without good reason is punishable under Article 56 of the Consumer Rights and Interests Protection Law (nationwide; effective January 1, 2022).
entries.sources: State Administration for Market Regulation (2021). Provisions on the Responsibility to Repair, Replace, or Refund Household Motor Vehicle Products (Administration Order No. 43, Articles 13, 18–24, 26–28, 30, 32, 38, and 40; effective January 1, 2022). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-07/27/content_5627788.htm>
entries.notes: Repair orders are the evidence of how many days the car has spent in repair and how many times it has been repaired. Make sure each order clearly records the fault and the times the car entered and left the dealership. You can calculate compensation for use yourself: for a 200,000-yuan car driven 10,000 kilometers, with n at the maximum 0.5%, you would pay about 10,000 yuan. If the dealership refuses, first call China's 12315 consumer complaint hotline. The market regulation department provides mediation. If mediation fails, your only option is to sue. Under the ordinary first-instance procedure, the case is supposed to be concluded within 6 months, although that period can be extended. You pay your own lawyer's fees; the other party does not pay them even if you win. If the car is sold to someone else during the free-repair period, the three-guarantees certificate goes with it and the three-guarantees obligations remain unchanged. Ask the seller for it when buying a used car. If a dealer conceals a used car's history of an accident or flood damage, see Item 48 of this section (concealed accident or flood damage in a used car). The beneficiary category is you and your family.

entries.title: Before buying a used car from a dealer, check its insurance claims and repair records and put “not an accident-damaged or flood-damaged car” in the contract; if the dealer concealed damage, you can seek a refund plus compensation of three times the car price
entries.cost: You will have to pay a third-party organization to inspect the car; prices vary by area. Before buying, spend an hour or two checking its insurance claims and repair records. When signing the contract, take the extra time to put the promises about the car's condition in writing. If you have been deceived, you will have to sue; the case may take two or three years from start to finish.
entries.summary: If you buy a used car from a dealer who deliberately conceals its true condition, such as accident or flood damage, you can return the car and also seek compensation of three times its price. But you can get the triple-price compensation only if you prove the dealer deliberately concealed the information. If the dealer says it did not know and the court accepts that, you get only the purchase price back plus interest. The triple-price compensation does not apply to purchases from private individuals.
entries.benefit: A used-car seller must give the buyer truthful information about the vehicle's use, repairs, accidents, inspections, whether it is mortgaged, whether taxes and fees have been paid, and its scrappage deadline. If the seller's concealment and fraud make it impossible to transfer ownership, the seller must accept the car back unconditionally and refund the purchase price. Article 55 of the Consumer Rights and Interests Protection Law says that if a business commits fraud when supplying goods, it must pay additional compensation at the consumer's request. The amount is three times the purchase price, or 500 yuan if that calculation is less than 500 yuan. This provision applies only to businesses, not purchases from private car owners. There is a case from Rizhao, Shandong. In May 2023, a person surnamed Sun bought a car from a used-car dealership for a total of 53,000 yuan. The dealership promised it had not been in a major accident. In October that year, an inspection company found that it was a car with major accident damage. Records showed it had been in an accident that January and classified as a total loss. The court of first instance rescinded the contract and ordered the dealership to refund 53,000 yuan and pay another 159,000 yuan, three times the car price. In April 2025, the Rizhao Intermediate People's Court upheld the judgment on appeal. The parties had not signed a written contract; Sun still won using a receipt stamped by the dealership. There is also a case with the opposite outcome. In January 2018, a person surnamed Wang in Henan paid 240,000 yuan for a car under a contract promising no accident or flood damage. Wang later discovered that the car had been in an accident before delivery and that repairs had cost 5,100 yuan. Both the original trial and the retrial ordered a refund plus triple-price compensation. The Zhengzhou Intermediate People's Court changed the judgment on appeal, and a further retrial upheld the appeal judgment. The reason was that the accident and repairs had already occurred when the dealer bought the car, and there was no evidence that the dealer knew about them and deliberately concealed them. The case was therefore treated only as a breach of contract: the contract was terminated and the 240,000-yuan purchase price plus interest refunded, with no triple-price compensation. That court noted that buyers can check a used car's insurance claims through various channels and can also hire an independent professional to inspect it (nationwide).
entries.sources: Ministry of Commerce, Ministry of Public Security, State Administration for Industry and Commerce, and State Taxation Administration (2005). Measures for the Administration of Used-Car Transactions (Order [2005] No. 2, originally Article 17; Ministry of Commerce Order No. 3 of 2017 deleted Articles 9–11 and renumbered the remaining articles accordingly, making it Article 14 now). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2006/content_327851.htm>; Ministry of Commerce (2017). Decision on Repealing and Amending Certain Regulations (Ministry of Commerce Order No. 3 of 2017). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2017/content_5244878.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (amended 2013). Consumer Rights and Interests Protection Law (Article 55). <https://www.samr.gov.cn/zfjcj/tzgg/art/2023/art_615af9ed6bcd4974bf853dd2e02bc663.html>; National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 148 and 152). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; Shandong Legal Daily (2025). Used-Car Dealership Sued for Concealing a Car's Accident History; Court Orders Rescission of Contract, Refund, and Triple-Price Compensation. <http://www.sdcourt.gov.cn/rzzy/404983/404968/41465920/index.html> (reposted on the Rizhao Intermediate People's Court's official website); Claim for “Refund Plus Triple-Price Compensation” on the Grounds That the Buyer Was Not Told a Used Car Had Been in an Accident (2021). <https://www.mawei.gov.cn/xjwz/zwgk/ztzl/pfzl/yasf/202108/t20210802_4153847.htm> (reposted in the “Explaining the Law Through Cases” section of the Fuzhou Mawei District People's Government website; original place of publication not stated)
entries.notes: Triple-price compensation applies only when the seller is a business, such as a car dealer or used-car dealership. If you buy from a private car owner and are deceived, you can only ask a court to rescind the contract and return your money under the Civil Code. You must seek rescission within 1 year of learning of the deception, and no later than 5 years after the transaction. Even if the contract says something like “sold as is,” put promises such as “not an accident-damaged, flood-damaged, or fire-damaged car” in writing so you have something to compare against later. Both cases took around two years from purchase to judgment, and you pay your own lawyer's fees. Checking records and getting an inspection before a lawsuit is therefore the best value. If a new car is still within its free-repair period, its three-guarantees certificate goes with the car; see Item 47 of this section (the three guarantees for new cars). For comparing car loans, see Item 7 of this section (convert borrowing costs to an annualized interest rate first). The beneficiary category is you and your family.

entries.title: When buying a car from a 4S dealership, do not pay a “financial services fee”; you do not have to arrange insurance, financing, or registration through the dealership either
entries.cost: No monetary cost. Before signing the contract, spend a few minutes asking what each charge is for, and have the dealership put it in the contract or issue an invoice. Arranging insurance and registration yourself means making one extra trip.
