entries.notes: There are several reasons for the B rating. The life tables are World Health Organization model estimates, not figures published by China’s National Bureau of Statistics. “Save 26% less” is a model result, not a figure obtained by following real people. The finding about estimating one’s lifespan comes from just one study, and there are no comparable data on Chinese populations to cite. “Most people need to save for old age” is the author’s inference from the probabilities of living to sixty and eighty, not a study’s conclusion. The benefit magnitude is rated medium, using the same standard as Item 23 of this section (do not expect buying things to improve your mood). The money saved might amount to tens of thousands of yuan, but there is no figure showing what that money would buy in return, so the benefit is not rated large. The same study also found that older people, conversely, overestimate how long they will live and spend their savings too slowly. This item is therefore aimed mainly at young and middle-aged people. It does not argue against spending money on things and experiences you enjoy; the only rationale it seeks to stop is “I’m going to die anyway.” If an accident or serious illness does happen, what helps is an emergency fund and insurance. See Section 5, Item 27 (emergency fund) and Section 5, Item 39 (buy insurance against losses you cannot bear). If someone in your household depends on your income, see Section 5, Item 40 (term life insurance). If you make purchases when you feel low, see Item 23 of this section (buying things to improve your mood). The beneficiary is you.

entries.title: Do not have arthroscopic debridement or part of the meniscus removed just because a middle-aged or older person’s knee has gradually started to hurt (osteoarthritis or a degenerative meniscal tear); start with weight loss and thigh muscle exercises
entries.cost: You avoid the cost of surgery and the 2 to 6 weeks of recovery afterward. What you need to do is exercise your thigh and buttock muscles several times a week over the long term, preferably after asking a rehabilitation doctor or physical therapist to teach you a routine. If you are overweight, you also need to eat less, move more, and lose weight. The difficulty is that exercise and weight loss both take time to work, while surgery sounds like a one-time solution.
entries.summary: For middle-aged and older people with knee pain from degeneration, arthroscopic debridement or removal of part of the meniscus works no better than sham surgery. Sham surgery involves only a few cuts in the skin, yet afterward people’s pain and walking ability are about the same as after real surgery. Any benefit lasts only a few months at most, and surgery can also cause blood clots in the leg. Consistent leg exercises can reduce knee pain, and losing weight can reduce it further for people who are overweight.
entries.benefit: First, consider osteoarthritis. A 2002 trial divided 180 people with knee osteoarthritis into three groups: arthroscopic debridement, arthroscopic lavage, and sham surgery. Sham surgery involved only a few cuts in the skin; the arthroscope was not inserted. Neither the patients nor the assessors knew who had received which procedure. At every follow-up over two years, neither real procedure produced better pain or function outcomes than sham surgery. Knee pain was scored from 0 to 100, with higher scores meaning more pain. At one year, the sham-surgery group scored 48.9, the lavage group 54.8, and the debridement group 51.7. Another trial in 2008 enrolled 178 people with moderate to severe knee osteoarthritis. One group had arthroscopic debridement plus physical therapy and medication. The other received only physical therapy and medication. The total symptom score ran from 0 to 2,400, with higher scores meaning worse symptoms. After two years, the groups scored 874 versus 897, a difference of 23 points (95% CI −208 to 161, the plausible range), with no difference between them. Next, consider the meniscus. A 2013 Finnish trial enrolled 146 people aged 35 to 65. All had symptoms of a degenerative medial meniscal tear and did not have osteoarthritis. One group had a partial meniscectomy; the other had sham surgery. At 12 months, none of the three main scores differed between the groups. For example, knee pain after exercise, scored from 0 to 10, fell by 3.1 and 3.3 points, respectively. A 2015 meta-analysis pooled 9 trials. People who had surgery had 3 to 5 points less pain at 3 to 6 months (on a 0-to-100 scale). By 1 to 2 years there was no difference, and function had not improved either. Now consider the harms. Symptomatic deep-vein thrombosis in the leg occurred about 4.13 times per 1,000 operations (1.78–9.60). Other harms included pulmonary embolism, infection, and death. On this basis, an international expert panel convened by the British Medical Journal (BMJ) in 2017 strongly recommended against arthroscopy for almost everyone with a degenerative knee condition. The panel specified that recovery after surgery takes 2 to 6 weeks. Finally, consider what to do instead. A 2016 Norwegian trial enrolled 140 middle-aged people with degenerative meniscal tears. One group completed 12 weeks of supervised exercise; the other had a partial meniscectomy. After two years, their knee scores differed by only 0.9 points (−4.3 to 6.1), with no difference between the groups. At three months, the exercise group had stronger thigh muscles. The 2015 edition of a Cochrane systematic review pooled 44 trials involving 3,537 people. Exercise reduced knee pain by the equivalent of 12 points (on a 0-to-100 scale; plausible range 10 to 15 points), with high-quality evidence. Two to six months after people stopped exercising, pain was still 6 points lower. A 2013 US trial enrolled 454 people aged 55 or older who were overweight or obese and had knee osteoarthritis. Those who combined diet and exercise lost an average of 10.6 kilograms (11.4% of their body weight). At 18 months, their pain score (on a 0-to-20 scale) was 3.6, compared with 4.7 for those who only exercised. Surgery seems worthwhile because “cleaning out the worn and torn parts” sounds like it addresses the cause directly, and many people really do feel better afterward

entries.notes: There is disagreement. China’s 2018 guidelines for diagnosing and treating osteoarthritis take a different position. They say arthroscopic debridement works better for knee osteoarthritis accompanied by “mechanical symptoms,” such as loose bone fragments inside the joint or a displaced meniscal tear. They also say that long-term outcomes are comparable to conservative treatment and that benefits may be limited when the joint space has narrowed substantially. The website hosting the original text of the new 2021 guidelines requires manual verification, so the text could not be checked word for word and was not cited. The BMJ expert panel’s position is that mechanical symptoms such as occasional catching or clicking also fall within its recommendation against arthroscopy; a knee that is truly locked and cannot be straightened may be an exception. The panel’s recommendation also does not cover two groups: people whose knees swell rapidly after major trauma (usually because of bleeding inside the joint), and young people with sports injuries. These situations call for an in-person assessment by an orthopedist. Arthroscopy is not knee replacement. The panel says joint replacement should be reserved for people with severe disease for whom conservative treatment has failed. For what painkillers you can take when it hurts, see Section 34, Item 3 (ask a doctor before taking painkillers such as ibuprofen). Do not count on glucosamine for relief; see Item 5 of this section (glucosamine and chondroitin). For exercises, see Section 2, Item 16 (strength training); for weight loss, see Section 2, Item 32 (lose weight if you are overweight). The medium benefit rating is a judgment: no officially published figure was found for the cost of these operations in China. The main benefits are saving the cost of surgery and the weeks of recovery afterward, while avoiding rare harms such as blood clots. The beneficiaries are you and the older people in your family.

entries.title: Do not expect melatonin to cure chronic insomnia: on average, it helps people fall asleep only about 7 minutes sooner. Start with cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia
entries.cost: It costs nothing and saves the money you would spend buying melatonin over the long term. The difficulty is that melatonin is readily available, and taking a pill is much easier than going to a hospital for several weeks of treatment.
entries.summary: On average, people who sleep poorly fall asleep only about 7 minutes sooner and sleep about 8 minutes longer with melatonin than with a placebo. The American Academy of Sleep Medicine does not recommend it for chronic insomnia. In China, it is sold as a health food, with a label stating, “This product cannot replace medication.” It can, however, reduce jet lag when you fly across more than 5 time zones.
entries.benefit: First, consider the size of the effect. A 2013 meta-analysis pooled 19 trials involving 1,683 people. Each trial randomly assigned participants to groups and compared melatonin with a placebo. None of the participants’ sleep disturbances was caused by another illness, and 14 of the trials studied insomnia. People taking melatonin fell asleep an average of 7.06 minutes sooner (95% CI 4.37–9.75, the plausible range). Their total sleep time increased by 8.25 minutes (1.74–14.75). The improvement in sleep quality was also small (SMD 0.22, 0.12–0.32). The authors themselves stated that the reduction in time to fall asleep was smaller than with other sleeping pills. Next, consider the guidelines. In 2017, the American Academy of Sleep Medicine issued guidelines on medication for chronic insomnia. It suggested that doctors not use melatonin to treat difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep; the recommendation was rated “weak.” It was based on 3 trials, all of which used 2 milligrams of prolonged-release melatonin and enrolled only participants over age 55. The quality of the evidence was rated “very low.” Sleep quality was the only outcome that could be pooled (SMD 0.21, −0.36 to 0.77), and the result did not reach clinical significance. In China, the stated health function of health foods containing melatonin is “helps improve sleep.” Their precautions state “This product cannot replace medication,” and the groups for whom they are unsuitable are children and adolescents, pregnant women, and breastfeeding women. A 2026 public education article from the Beijing Municipal Administration for Market Regulation also said that melatonin is “by no means a ‘miracle drug.’” Jet lag is a separate matter. A Cochrane systematic review included 10 trials, 9 of which reported the same finding: taking melatonin before local bedtime after flying across more than 5 time zones can reduce jet lag. Daily doses of 0.5 to 5 milligrams work about equally well. It seems worthwhile because it is a hormone the body naturally produces, which sounds gentle, and it requires no prescription

entries.notes: Controversy: The authors of that meta-analysis believe that melatonin's side effects are relatively small, and its efficacy does not diminish with prolonged use. Therefore, it may have a place in insomnia treatment. Science communication from the Beijing Municipal Administration for Market Regulation states that it is suitable for relieving difficulty falling asleep in middle-aged and older adults caused by insufficient melatonin secretion. However, in the three trials from the American Academy of Sleep Medicine, the participants happened to all be over 55 years old, yet the conclusion was still that the effect was insufficient. There are benefits, but they are simply too small to be considered a cure. For long-term insomnia, first undergo cognitive behavioral therapy; see Section 3, Item 26 (Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia). For snoring, nighttime gasping/suffocation, or severe daytime sleepiness, first check for sleep apnea; see Section 3, Item 27 (Sleep Monitoring for Sleep Apnea). The label also states that those driving or operating machinery should not take it before or while working. Giving melatonin to children is not considered in this entry; domestic product labels clearly state that it is not suitable for children and adolescents. The rating of small benefit is based on judgment: no official figures were found regarding how much money melatonin costs per year. The beneficiary is yourself.

entries.title: Do not request IV infusions for colds or ordinary fevers, nor get seasonal IV infusions to "flush out the blood vessels" or "unblock blood vessels"
entries.cost: Costs no money; in fact, it saves the cost of an IV drip and the several hours spent sitting in a clinic. The difficulty lies in many people believing that an IV bag makes you recover faster, and some older adults have even formed a habit of getting seasonal IV infusions, feeling that a doctor who refuses to prescribe one hasn't examined them thoroughly.
entries.summary: Common colds and viral sore throats are listed by Guangdong provincial health authorities as diseases that, in principle, do not require intravenous infusions. Experts at a National Health Commission press conference clarified that seasonal IV infusions cannot wash away plaques inside blood vessels and may even increase the burden on the heart and kidneys. Of the adverse drug reactions reported nationwide, more than half involve parenteral administration, with intravenous injection accounting for 90% of those.
entries.benefit: No studies have specifically compared getting an IV infusion versus not getting one during a cold, so this item must rely on official documents and surveillance data. First, looking at colds: In 2017, the Health and Family Planning Commission of Guangdong Province issued a document requiring primary healthcare institutions to reduce unnecessary intravenous infusions. The document clearly stated that medication should follow the principle advocated by the World Health Organization: "oral when possible rather than by injection; intramuscular injection when possible rather than intravenous." Intravenous infusion is only to be used under three circumstances: first, difficulty swallowing; second, severe absorption impairment, such as vomiting or severe diarrhea; third, when the condition is critical and rapidly progressing, requiring the drug to reach a high concentration in the body very quickly. The document attached a list of common and frequent diseases that in principle do not require IV infusion in outpatient and emergency departments. The first item under internal medicine is "upper respiratory tract infections: common cold, viral pharyngolaryngitis." Next, looking at "flushing the blood vessels": The National Health Commission held a press conference on August 6, 2025. At the conference, a chief physician from Dongfang Hospital of Beijing University of Chinese Medicine dispelled this rumor. The exact words were: "Getting an IV infusion at the change of seasons to clear blood vessels and prevent cerebral infarction is an erroneous claim." Infusions cannot "flush away" or "unblock" atherosclerotic plaques. Blindly receiving IV infusions may increase the burden on the heart or kidneys, potentially even triggering heart failure. Finally, looking at risks: The Annual Report on National Adverse Drug Reaction Monitoring (2024) compiled statistics by route of administration. Among reported adverse reactions, parenteral administration accounted for 57.2%, and oral administration accounted for 33.1%. Among parenteral administration, intravenous injection accounted for 91.0%. This is the composition of reported cases, not the probability of an incident occurring per infusion. It seems cost-effective because the IV bag is visible and finishes while lying down, giving people the impression that the medicine acts faster and more thoroughly.
entries.sources: Office of the Health and Family Planning Commission of Guangdong Province (2017). Notice on Strengthening the Management of Intravenous Infusions in Primary Healthcare Institutions (Yue Wei Ban Han [2017] No. 332) and its annex "Common and Frequent Diseases That in Principle Do Not Require Infusion Therapy in Outpatient and Emergency Departments," reprinted on the Conghua District People's Government of Guangzhou Municipality website. <https://www.conghua.gov.cn/attachment/7/7361/7361750/7215543.pdf>; National Health Commission (2025). Annual Report on National Adverse Drug Reaction Monitoring (2024). <https://www.cdr-adr.org.cn/center_news/202504/t20250407_51076.html>
entries.notes: Rated Level C because there are only official documents and expert clarifications, with no clinical trials calculating how many incidents are avoided by not getting IV infusions. Those who genuinely need an IV infusion should receive it as usual—such as for severe dehydration, vomiting to the point of being unable to keep down medication, or critical condition—following the doctor's instructions. Asking a doctor for antibiotics for a cold is equally useless; see Section 34, Item 7 (No Antibiotics for Colds). For diarrhea, drink oral rehydration salts first; see Section 34, Item 8 (Oral Rehydration Salts). What genuinely works for preventing stroke is keeping blood pressure and blood lipids under control and taking medication long-term according to medical advice; see Section 1, Item 7 (Measuring Blood Pressure) and Section 2, Item 12 (Regular Blood Lipid Tests). The list of conditions not requiring IV infusions is determined by each province individually; Guangdong's list is from 2017, and whether it has been updated since has not been found. The rating of small benefit is based on judgment: what is saved is the cost of one IV infusion and a few hours, while adverse reactions cannot be calculated as a per-infusion probability. The beneficiaries are yourself and the older adults in your family.

chapters.title: How to Survive When You Have No Money
chapters.intro:
What is calculated in this section is money and safety nets. How much money can be received, how much can be exempted, what services can be obtained, and what conditions must be met are all detailed within, without being converted into lifespan. Policies change every year and vary from place to place, so monetary amounts and eligibility thresholds are subject to what is published in your locality for the current year.

Entries in this section are divided into the following categories by topic, with item numbers in parentheses.

**Lost Your Job**: Claiming unemployment insurance benefits online (Item 1), identification of persons with employment difficulties (Item 12), claiming vocational training subsidies (Item 13).

**Owed Wages**: Complain to labor inspection first (Item 2), apply for legal aid (Item 3), distinguish who your actual employer is when wages are owed (Item 22).

**Emergency Relief and Basic Safety Nets**: Go to a relief station (Item 4), apply for temporary assistance (Item 6), apply for minimum subsistence guarantee (Dibao) (Item 7), the two subsidies for persons with disabilities (Item 8), replace a lost resident identity card immediately (Item 11), having genuinely nowhere to sleep (Item 21), unable to repay credit cards or online loans (Item 23).

**Medical Insurance and Social Insurance**: Do not let basic medical insurance for urban and rural residents lapse (Item 9), use medical insurance and medical assistance first for serious illnesses (Item 10), do not panic if social insurance payments are interrupted (Item 18), obtain a medical insurance or critical illness insurance policy (Item 20).

**Finding Work and Starting Over**: Public employment services and gig/casual labor markets (Item 5), use systematic methods for job hunting (Item 14), do not pay security deposits or surrender personal identification (Item 15), there are pathways to start over even after imprisonment or bankruptcy (Item 19).

**Housing and Food**: Queuing for public rental housing (Item 16), reducing housing and food expenses to the bare minimum (Item 17).

entries.title: If you become unemployed, apply for unemployment insurance benefits online first
entries.cost: Costs no money. You can submit the application using a mobile phone through any of three portals: the "掌上 12333" (Handheld 12333) app, the electronic social security card Mini Program in WeChat or Alipay, or the National Social Insurance Public Service Platform. Having a social security card or a resident identity card in hand is sufficient to complete the process; in most areas, there is no need to visit in person. The prerequisite is completing unemployment registration beforehand.
entries.summary: If both your employer and yourself have paid contributions for at least 1 full year, and the resignation was not initiated by you voluntarily, you can receive payments after completing unemployment registration and being willing to seek employment. With 1 to less than 5 years of payments, you can receive benefits for up to 12 months; for 5 to less than 10 years, up to 18 months; for 10 years or more, up to 24 months. During the period of receiving benefits, your urban employee basic medical insurance will be paid for by the unemployment insurance fund on your behalf.
entries.benefit: Three conditions must be met simultaneously: First, the employer and you personally must have paid unemployment insurance contributions for a cumulative total of at least 1 year. Second, the resignation was not initiated by you voluntarily (termed in law as "interruption of employment not due to one's own will"). Third, unemployment registration has been completed, and there is a willingness to seek employment. How long you can receive benefits is calculated based on contribution years: for a cumulative total of at least 1 year but less than 5 years, benefits can be received for up to 12 months; for at least 5 years but less than 10 years, up to 18 months; for 10 years or more, up to 24 months. The monthly amount paid is set by provincial-level governments and varies across provinces. The amount is lower than the local minimum wage but higher than the urban minimum subsistence guarantee (Dibao). The national target is to gradually raise it to 90% of the minimum wage standard. During the period of receiving unemployment insurance benefits, you continue to participate in urban employee basic medical insurance and enjoy basic medical insurance benefits. The required basic medical insurance contributions are paid out of the unemployment insurance fund, and you do not pay them individually (Nationwide, regulations effective since 1999).

Notice on Further Adjusting Unemployment Insurance Benefit Standards: "To implement the requirements of the 'Guiding Opinions of the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and the Ministry of Finance on Adjusting Unemployment Insurance Benefit Standards' (Ren She Bu Fa [2017] No. 71) to 'gradually raise unemployment insurance benefit standards to 90% of the minimum wage standard'". <https://rst.ln.gov.cn/rst/zfxx/zc/ywfl/shbx/2024092014161280895/index.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2010). entries.notes: Voluntary resignation does not count as "not due to one's own will," making you ineligible to collect. Therefore, do not sign "voluntary resignation for personal reasons" when departing; see Section 19, Item 7. Unemployment insurance benefits are calculated starting from the day you complete unemployment registration; register late, and you receive them late. The very first thing to do after leaving is to go register. Registration requires the termination certificate issued by your employer; see Section 19, Item 17 (Termination Certificate). On whether non-compete agreements must be observed and what to do if the company does not provide compensation, see Section 11, Item 12 (Signed a Non-compete Agreement). Urban employee medical insurance during the collection period is paid on your behalf by the unemployment insurance fund. Amounts vary substantially across provinces, subject to what is announced in the jurisdiction where your insurance was paid. The "90% of the minimum wage" originates from the 2017 guiding opinions of the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and the Ministry of Finance (Ren She Bu Fa [2017] No. 71), which stated verbatim: "gradually raise unemployment insurance benefit standards to 90% of the minimum wage standard." This is a goal, not an indication that 90% is currently paid everywhere. The original text page on the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security's official website could not be opened on this machine; this sentence was verified against the citation in the document from the Department of Human Resources and Social Security of Liaoning Province.

entries.title: When owed wages, complain to labor inspection first, then apply for labor arbitration; neither route charges fees, and most cases reach an outcome within a few months
entries.cost: Costs no money; neither complaints nor arbitration charge fees. You need to prepare labor contracts, pay stubs, attendance records, bank transfer records, and chat records, making 1 to 3 trips to the human resources and social security bureau or the arbitration commission. Applying for arbitration has a 1-year time limit (legally known as the statute of limitations for arbitration). If you are still working at this employer while wages are being withheld, you are not subject to this 1-year limit. If you have already resigned, you must file within 1 year starting from the date of resignation. The difficulty lies in making repeated trips and locating evidence piece by piece, during which it is easy to become discouraged.
entries.summary: First, call 12333 or go to the labor inspection division of the human resources and social security bureau to file a complaint; investigation must conclude within 60 working days after filing. Once substantiated, the company can be ordered to pay within a specified deadline; failing to pay by the deadline incurs an additional compensation of 50% to 100%. If that still fails, apply for labor arbitration, which concludes within 45 days. However, "concluding a case" does not equal "funds in your account": if the company has no assets or the boss has fled, you may still fail to recover money even after winning.
entries.benefit: The first step is filing a complaint: Dial 12333, or go to the labor inspection division of the local human resources and social security bureau to complain. The law stipulates that investigations must conclude within 60 working days after a case is accepted, which may be extended by another 30 working days for complex cases. Once substantiated, the company can be ordered to pay off the amount within a time limit. If it still fails to pay after the deadline, an additional compensation of 50% to 100% of the payable amount must be paid. In 2024, labor inspection agencies nationwide investigated and handled 137,000 cases, recovering 8.65 billion yuan in wages for 654,000 workers. If you have an IOU or payroll sheet in hand and the wage arrears facts are clear, you can also apply directly to a primary people's court for a payment order. A payment order is an order to pay issued by the court to the company, which is issued within 15 days after court acceptance. The second step is applying for arbitration: The law stipulates that a case must be concluded within 45 days after acceptance, which can be extended by 15 days. Those seeking unpaid wages can apply for preliminary execution: executing a portion first without waiting for the entire case trial to finish. If the owed amount does not exceed 12 times the local monthly minimum wage, it falls under final arbitration: once the arbitration ruling is made, it is final, and the company cannot file a lawsuit. In 2024, 4.257 million cases were handled nationwide, with 4.156 million cases concluded. The concluded case amount was 93.47 billion yuan. The mediation success rate was 79.6%, the arbitration case conclusion rate was 98.2%, and the arbitration termination rate was 73.7%. Some people say this process drags on for "half a year to a year"; this refers to the portion of cases that proceed to court after arbitration. That portion involves 6 months for the first instance (3 months for summary procedures), plus another 3 months for the second instance. In 2024, courts concluded 88,000 cases involving claims for labor remuneration, recovering 28.54 billion yuan, and 998 individuals were sentenced for the crime of refusing to pay labor remuneration (Nationwide).
entries.sources: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2025). Statistical Bulletin on the Development of Human Resources and Social Security Undertakings in 2024. <https://www.mohrss.gov.cn/SYrlzyhshbzb/zwgk/szrs/tjgb/202506/W020250616518526345602.pdf>; Supreme People's Court (2025). Amendment (VIII) to the Criminal Law, Article 41, namely Article 276-1 of the Criminal Law. <http://www.npc.gov.cn/cwhhdbdh/c6626/c14002/c14003/201905/t20190523_390477.html>; Supreme People's Court (2013). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Criminal Cases Involving Refusal to Pay Labor Remuneration (Fa Shi [2013] No. 3, Article 3). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/5041.html>; State Council (2019). Regulations on Guaranteeing Wage Payment for Migrant Workers (State Council Decree No. 724, Articles 10, 26, 30, 31, 32, and 41). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2020/content_5469641.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2021). Legal Aid Law (Articles 31 and 42). <https://www.beijing.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengcefagui/qtwj/202504/t20250402_4053713.html>
entries.notes: Complaints and arbitration can help, but distinguish between a case being closed and money reaching your account. The 98.2% case closure rate only means the procedures were completed. If the company has no assets or the boss has disappeared, you may still get no money even if you win. The Supreme People's Court publishes only the total amount recovered through enforcement (2.3 trillion yuan in 2024) and says that the “enforcement completion rate remains high.” There are no official data on how much of the wages owed in these cases ultimately reached the people owed them. The bulletin does not define “arbitration finalization rate”; this entry takes it to mean that the case did not go on to court after the arbitration award. Unpaid wages can qualify for a criminal investigation once they reach certain thresholds. One threshold is wages owed to one person for more than three months, with the amount exceeding a threshold set between 5,000 and 20,000 yuan. Another is wages owed to more than 10 people, totaling more than a threshold set between 30,000 and 100,000 yuan. In either situation, if the employer still does not pay after being ordered to do so, the case meets the threshold for a criminal investigation. Each province's high court and provincial procuratorate set and publish the specific thresholds for that province within these ranges. Check your province's thresholds before filing a complaint, and raise them in person when you complain. Migrant construction workers have additional protections: dedicated wage accounts and rules requiring the general contractor to pay outstanding wages first. Approaching the general contractor is more effective than approaching the labor subcontractor. Both of these routes depend on there being an employer. Unlicensed workshops and shops still count; you can file a complaint and seek arbitration. If you do private work for a household or individual, such as working as a nanny, it does not count as an employment relationship: you need to go to court. See Item 22 (first establish who hired you). The financial hardship requirement is waived when migrant workers in cities apply for legal aid to recover unpaid wages. The original text of the Labor Contract Law and the Civil Procedure Law is quoted from reposted pages of the State Taxation Administration and the Guizhou Provincial Administration for Market Regulation (both on gov.cn), because the pages on the National People's Congress of China website could not be opened. The Eighth Amendment to the Criminal Law could not be fetched from the National People's Congress of China website, so it was opened and checked using curl instead.

entries.title: If you cannot afford to go to court, apply for legal aid: cases involving unpaid wages, maintenance payments, and work injuries are already covered
entries.cost: Free. Legal aid does not charge the person receiving it anything.
entries.summary: You can apply for free legal aid to recover unpaid wages, claim maintenance payments, seek social insurance or minimum living allowance benefits, or claim for losses suffered while acting courageously for a just cause. Call China's 12348 public legal services hotline or visit a local legal aid center. You no longer need to return to your place of household registration for proof of financial hardship; you only need to give a truthful account of your circumstances. A lawyer must be appointed for defendants who may be sentenced to death and for defendants who are blind, deaf, unable to speak, or minors.
entries.benefit: A State Council regulation specifies six categories of civil matters covered by legal aid. Its wording is: “Requests for state compensation in accordance with the law; requests for social insurance benefits or minimum living allowance benefits; requests for pensions or relief funds; requests for maintenance, child support, or other support payments; requests for payment of labor remuneration; and claims to civil rights and interests arising from acts of courage for a just cause.” In plain terms: seeking state compensation, social insurance or minimum living allowance benefits, pensions or relief funds, maintenance or child support, unpaid wages, or compensation for losses suffered while acting courageously for a just cause. In criminal cases, lawyers must be appointed for defendants who may be sentenced to death and for defendants who are blind, deaf, unable to speak, or minors, regardless of their financial circumstances.
entries.sources: State Council (2003). Regulations on Legal Aid (State Council Order No. 385, Articles 10, 11, and 12). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_6944.htm>; relevant official of the Ministry of Justice (2021). Answers to reporters' questions on implementing the Legal Aid Law. <http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2021-12/29/content_5665114.htm>
entries.notes: The Legal Aid Law took effect on January 1, 2022, with one change. Previously, you had to “submit proof of financial hardship.” Now you only need to give a truthful account of your financial circumstances; you no longer need to return to your place of household registration for a certificate. Apply through a local legal aid center or public legal services center, or call China's 12348 public legal services hotline.

entries.title: When you have nowhere to turn, go to a relief station for food, lodging, and a ticket home
entries.cost: Free. You can go to a local relief management station yourself, or tell a police officer or civil affairs department and ask them to take you there. When you arrive, you must truthfully register your name and the belongings you have with you. The hard part is telling someone that you have no money and nowhere to go.
entries.summary: A relief station provides food and lodging, takes you to a hospital if you are ill, helps you contact your family, and gives you a travel ticket if you cannot afford to get home. A stay generally lasts no more than 10 days. You come and leave voluntarily; this is not detention, and the station does not give out cash. Tickets are issued for travel to your place of household registration or your place of residence, so decide where you need to return before you go.
entries.benefit: Relief stations provide food and accommodation that meet hygiene requirements. If you suddenly become seriously ill while at the station, you will be taken to a hospital for treatment. Staff will also help you contact relatives and your employer or other organization. If you cannot afford a ticket to your place of household registration or residence, the station will provide a travel voucher: a bus, train, or boat ticket. Your place of household registration is your registered hometown; your place of residence is where you currently live on a regular basis. Relief generally lasts no more than 10 days. It can be extended while you wait for family to pick you up, treatment, or placement. When police or other administrative officials encounter people who are homeless and begging in the course of their duties, they should tell them that they can seek help. They must guide and escort people with disabilities, minors, older people, and people with limited mobility to a relief station (nationwide, since 2003).
entries.sources: State Council (2003). Measures for the Administration of Relief for Homeless and Begging Persons with No Means of Support in Cities (State Council Order No. 381, Articles 5, 6, and 7). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2003/content_62246.htm>; Ministry of Civil Affairs (2003). Implementing Rules for the Measures for the Administration of Relief for Homeless and Begging Persons with No Means of Support in Cities (Ministry of Civil Affairs Order No. 24, Articles 11 and 12). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2003/content_62510.htm>
entries.notes: You seek help voluntarily and leave voluntarily; this is not detention. The station provides basic food and lodging, not cash. Travel vouchers are issued for your place of household registration or residence, so decide where you need to go before seeking help. For arrangements at night and in winter, see Item 21 (when you really have nowhere to sleep).

entries.title: Start your job search with free public employment services and casual work markets, rather than fee-charging agencies
entries.cost: Free. Register with a public employment service agency at county level or above, such as an employment service center or human resources market. You can also register at a local casual work market. If you do not know the address, call China's 12333 human resources and social security hotline.
entries.summary: Government-run employment service centers and human resources markets charge nothing for job referrals, career guidance, policy advice, or employment and unemployment registration. The law expressly prohibits them from making money from these services. Registration and posting information at casual work markets are also free. Register as unemployed while you are there: you will need that registration to receive unemployment insurance benefits or be recognized as a person having difficulty finding employment.
entries.benefit: The law requires all of the following to be free: advice on employment policies; information about vacancies and labor demand; career guidance and job referrals; employment and unemployment registration; and employment assistance for people having difficulty finding work. These agencies may not engage in commercial activities or profit from these services. Registration and publication of job-seeking and recruitment information for casual work are also provided free to the public and have been included in public employment information services. Additional assistance must be provided to casual workers who have spent a long time waiting for work (that is, who have not been able to get jobs for a long time), those from low-income households, and others facing difficulties (nationwide).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007, amended 2015). Employment Promotion Law (Article 35). <https://www.gov.cn/guoqing/2021-10/29/content_5647636.htm>; Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and four other departments (2022). Opinions on Strengthening the Development of Casual Work Markets and Improving Job-Seeking and Recruitment Services (Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security Document [2022] No. 38). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-07/09/content_5700177.htm>
entries.notes: Unemployment registration is a prerequisite for receiving unemployment insurance benefits and being recognized as a person having difficulty finding employment, so take care of it while you are there. If you do casual work paid by the day, check your pay on the spot and keep the other party's contact details and a record of the work you did.

entries.title: Apply for temporary assistance first when a sudden crisis strikes
entries.cost: Free. Apply to the township government or subdistrict office where the crisis occurred, and explain what happened to your household: for example, a fire, a traffic accident, a family member's sudden serious illness, or a sudden increase in essential day-to-day expenses. For sudden, urgent hardship, the “small-amount, rapid relief” process involves no check of your household finances and no public notice, and is generally completed within 3 days. A sudden rise in medical or education expenses requires public notice before approval. Prepare the documents on the local checklist; this usually takes 1 to 2 visits.
entries.summary: If a sudden crisis such as a fire, traffic accident, or family member's sudden serious illness temporarily makes it impossible to cover basic living costs, you can apply for temporary assistance from the township government or subdistrict office where it happened. You do not have to be receiving the minimum living allowance. Such urgent cases are generally processed within 3 days, with the highest assistance amount capped at one month's local minimum living allowance standard. In other cases, the highest amount is capped at six months of that standard.
entries.benefit: Two types of households can receive temporary assistance. The first is a household that, because of an accident or a family member's sudden serious illness, temporarily cannot cover even basic expenses such as food, accommodation, and medical care. The second is a household receiving the minimum living allowance whose essential expenses suddenly increase beyond what it can afford. Local governments at county level or above decide and publish which circumstances qualify and how much is paid (nationwide system since 2014; amounts set locally). The Social Assistance Law, effective July 1, 2026, describes eligible people as those whose “basic living conditions are temporarily in serious difficulty due to sudden, urgent, disastrous, or similar hardship,” and provides for cash assistance or supplies. Apply for temporary assistance to the township government or subdistrict office “where the urgent hardship occurred.” If the situation is urgent and the amount is small, assistance must be given first and the formalities completed afterward. A document issued by the Ministry of Civil Affairs and the Ministry of Finance in late 2025 sets out how assistance is provided. Sudden crises, accidental injuries, and serious illnesses use the “small-amount, rapid relief” process: household finances are no longer checked, no public notice is required, processing generally takes no more than 3 days, and the highest assistance amount does not exceed one month's local minimum living allowance standard. Households just above the minimum living allowance threshold and households facing hardship because of unavoidable expenses that fall into difficulty after a sudden rise in costs such as medical care or education receive assistance after public notice, in principle through “one approval, payments in stages.” For temporary assistance outside the small-amount, rapid relief process, the highest amount does not exceed six times the local monthly minimum living allowance standard (nationwide, from 2026; specific standards set locally).
entries.sources: State Council (2014, revised 2019). Interim Measures for Social Assistance (State Council Order No. 649, Articles 47, 48, and 49). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2019/content_5468952.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2026). Social Assistance Law (effective July 1, 2026, Articles 29, 37 paragraph 2, and 50; Article 29: “For people whose basic living conditions are temporarily in serious difficulty due to sudden, urgent, disastrous, or similar hardship, the social assistance administration department shall provide temporary assistance by issuing assistance payments, distributing supplies, or other means.” Article 37 paragraph 2: “An application for temporary assistance shall be made by the person concerned or a family member living with them to the township people's government or subdistrict office where the urgent hardship occurred.” Article 50: “Where an application for temporary assistance concerns an urgent situation, a small assistance amount, and an immediate need for assistance, assistance shall be provided first.”). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=016c39ca7739492cab1fe3aef22941c7>; Ministry of Civil Affairs and Ministry of Finance (2025). Opinions on Further Strengthening and Improving the Temporary Assistance System (Ministry of Civil Affairs Document [2025] No. 68, Part II, Items 1, 2, and 5: “The processing time for ‘small-amount, rapid relief’ generally does not exceed 3 days”; “The highest assistance amount does not exceed one month's local minimum living allowance standard”; “In principle, the method of ‘one approval, payments in stages’ shall be used”; “The highest assistance amount does not exceed six times the local monthly minimum living allowance standard”). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202601/content_7056503.htm>
entries.notes: You do not have to be receiving the minimum living allowance already. Specific amounts vary greatly by locality; use the figures published locally for the current year. The Interim Measures for Social Assistance were not expressly repealed when the Social Assistance Law took effect, and the National Database of Laws and Regulations still marked them as valid as of October 2026. Where the two differ, follow the law.

entries.title: Apply for the minimum living allowance if your income is below the local threshold; if it is slightly above the threshold or medical and education costs are high, apply for medical, education, housing, or employment assistance
entries.cost: Free. A family member living in the same household submits a written application to the township government or subdistrict office at the place of household registration. If applying yourself is inconvenient, you can authorize a village committee or residents' committee to apply on your behalf. You must agree to a check of household income and assets. It usually takes 2 to 3 visits; bring your identity card, household registration booklet, and proof of income and assets. The difficult part is disclosing your household finances for inspection and waiting for the public notice period. If you do not qualify for the minimum living allowance, apply for medical, housing, or employment assistance through the township government or subdistrict office at your place of household registration. Apply for education assistance through the school your child attends.
entries.summary: You can apply if your household's income per person is below the local minimum living allowance threshold and its assets also meet the rules. At the end of 2024, the nationwide average monthly minimum living allowance standard was 798.1 yuan per person in urban areas and 593.9 yuan in rural areas. Payments can cover the difference or be set at fixed amounts by tier. If your income is a little above the threshold, or medical and education costs are too high, you may still be able to apply for medical, education, and housing assistance even if you do not qualify for the minimum living allowance.
entries.benefit: If your household's total income divided by the number of household members is below the local minimum living allowance standard, and your household's assets are within the permitted limits, you can receive the allowance. At the end of 2024, the nationwide average standard was 798.1 yuan per person per month in urban areas and 593.9 yuan per person per month in rural areas. The allowance covered 6.250 million people in urban areas and 33.615 million in rural areas. Under the difference-based method, the monthly allowance equals the local standard minus household income per person. For example, if the local standard is 798.1 yuan and each person in your household has a monthly income of 500 yuan, each person receives 298.1 yuan a month, not 798.1 yuan. The Social Assistance Law, effective from July 2026, also permits fixed amounts by tier: the allowance “may be paid according to the actual difference between household income per person and the local minimum living allowance standard, or at fixed amounts by tier.” The standard is set by taking the previous year's local consumer spending per person, multiplying it by a specified ratio, and adjusting it periodically. Put simply, it is calculated by applying a discount factor to what the average local resident spent in the previous year (nationwide averages; figures vary by locality). There are two further categories for people who do not qualify for the allowance. The first is households just above the minimum living allowance threshold: their assets meet the rules and their income per person is below 1.5 times the local minimum living allowance standard (under a 2023 national document). The Social Assistance Law, effective from July 2026, instead provides for provinces to set this category's threshold at a specified percentage above the minimum living allowance standard. The second is households facing hardship because of unavoidable expenses. Their income per person must be below the previous year's local disposable income per person, and their assets must meet the rules. Essential costs such as medical care and education must also exceed a locally specified share of total household income. Both categories can receive medical, education, and housing assistance. Education assistance includes fee reductions or exemptions, grants and living allowances, and student loans. In urban areas, housing assistance takes the form of priority access to public rental housing or rental subsidies. Unemployed people who are able to work in either category can also receive employment assistance. People with severe disabilities or serious illnesses in households just above the minimum living allowance threshold can be included individually in the minimum living allowance program and receive monthly payments (nationwide, since 2023; percentages and eligibility rules set locally).
entries.sources: State Council (2014, revised 2019). Interim Measures for Social Assistance (State Council Order No. 649, Articles 9, 10, and 11; Article 12: “The civil affairs department of the county-level people's government shall pay a monthly minimum living allowance equal to the difference between the income per person of family members living together and the local minimum living allowance standard”). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2019/content_5468952.htm>; National Bureau of Statistics (2025). Social programs develop favorably and people's well-being continues to improve—statistical report on society and livelihoods since the start of the 14th Five-Year Plan. <https://www.gov.cn/lianbo/bumen/202509/content_7042627.htm>; Ministry of Civil Affairs and three other departments (2024). Guiding Opinions on Further Improving the Determination and Adjustment of Minimum Living Allowance Standards (Ministry of Civil Affairs Document [2024] No. 16). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202403/content_7007237.htm>; General Office of the State Council (2023). Notice Forwarding the Opinions of the Ministry of Civil Affairs and Other Bodies on Strengthening Dynamic Monitoring of Low-Income Populations and Providing Social Assistance by Level and Category (General Office of the State Council Document [2023] No. 39, Part II: “Households that do not meet the conditions for the minimum living allowance but have income per person below 1.5 times the local minimum living allowance standard and whose assets comply with relevant local rules shall be recognized as households just above the minimum living allowance threshold”; Part IV: “People with particular difficulties, such as patients with serious illnesses and people with severe disabilities, in households just above the minimum living allowance threshold may be included individually in the minimum living allowance program”). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202310/content_6911066.htm>; General Office of the Ministry of Civil Affairs (2024). Notice on Strengthening the Identification and Dynamic Monitoring of Low-Income Populations (General Office of the Ministry of Civil Affairs Letter [2024] No. 31). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202405/content_6948767.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2026). Social Assistance Law (effective July 1, 2026, Articles 18, 19, 21, 22, 24 through 27, 37, and 38; Article 18 paragraph 2: “The minimum living allowance may be paid according to the actual difference between household income per person and the local minimum living allowance standard, or at fixed amounts by tier.” Article 21 paragraph 3: “The standard for households just above the minimum living allowance threshold shall be set at a specified percentage above the local minimum living allowance standard or the minimum living allowance guideline standard”). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=016c39ca7739492cab1fe3aef22941c7>
entries.notes: The minimum living allowance is a last-resort safety net; apply at your place of household registration. Your application may be refused if your household's home, car, or savings exceed local limits, or if your children are able to support you. Approval brings other benefits: assistance with paying for resident medical insurance (see Item 9 on resident medical insurance), access to medical assistance for treatment (see Item 10 on medical assistance), and no financial hardship check when applying for legal aid (see Item 3 on legal aid).

entries.title: If you have a disability certificate, apply for the two disability allowances
entries.cost: Free. Bring your disability certificate and submit a single application at your subdistrict or township office.
entries.summary: People with disabilities in households receiving the minimum living allowance can receive a living allowance. If your disability is classified as Grade I or II and you need long-term care, you can receive a care allowance. You can receive both. Each province sets its own amounts, which vary greatly; ask your subdistrict office for the details. Bring your second-generation disability certificate and apply once at your subdistrict or township office.
entries.benefit: The State Council established two allowances. The first is the living allowance for people with disabilities in financial difficulty. The document says it covers “people with disabilities in households receiving the minimum living allowance; where conditions permit, localities may gradually expand coverage to low-income people with disabilities and other people with disabilities in financial difficulty.” In other words, people with disabilities in households receiving the minimum living allowance are covered first, and localities with sufficient resources may expand coverage. The second is the care allowance for people with severe disabilities. The document says it covers “people with severe disabilities whose disability is classified as Grade I or II and who need long-term care.” The two allowances can be received together.
entries.sources: State Council (2015). Opinions on Fully Establishing a Living Allowance for People with Disabilities in Financial Difficulty and a Care Allowance for People with Severe Disabilities (State Council Document [2015] No. 52). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2015-09/25/content_10181.htm>
entries.notes: Standards are set by provincial governments and vary greatly by locality. Applicants must bring a second-generation disability certificate. If you cannot apply in person, you can authorize a family member to do it for you.

entries.title: Keep paying for residents’ health insurance, starting at 400 yuan a year; households in difficulty may get a reduction or exemption
entries.cost: The part you pay yourself is at least 400 yuan per person per year. This is the national standard for 2024 and 2025; localities may set a higher amount. Pay during the designated annual enrollment and payment period. People in extreme hardship receive full assistance, so the government pays the entire amount. Minimum-living-allowance recipients receive a fixed subsidy, with the government paying a set portion.
entries.summary: Individuals pay at least 400 yuan a year, and in 2025 the government adds a per-person subsidy of at least 700 yuan. People in extreme hardship receive full assistance; minimum-living-allowance recipients receive a fixed subsidy. A lapse in payments has a cost: if you enroll outside the designated period or have not paid continuously, there is a three-month period after payment during which medical expenses are not reimbursed. In principle, each additional year without coverage adds another month.
entries.benefit: In addition to the part you pay yourself, the government provides a per-person subsidy. It was at least 670 yuan in 2024. In 2025 it increased by 30 yuan from the previous year to at least 700 yuan, while the individual contribution remained at least 400 yuan (Medical Insurance Document [2025] No. 22, as reported in provincial documents). The 2026 Government Work Report says the subsidy will increase by another 24 yuan. For minimum-living-allowance recipients and people in extreme hardship, eligible medical expenses remaining after health insurance reimbursement can receive a further reimbursement of at least 70% through medical assistance. The cost of a lapse in payments is a waiting period. If you enroll outside the designated payment period or have not paid continuously, there is a fixed three-month waiting period for benefits after payment. Medical expenses incurred during that period are not reimbursed. In principle, each additional year without coverage adds one more month (nationwide from 2025).
entries.sources: National Healthcare Security Administration (2024). Policy interpretation of the Notice on Work Related to Basic Medical Coverage for Urban and Rural Residents in 2024 (Medical Insurance Document [2024] No. 19). <https://www.nhsa.gov.cn/art/2024/8/26/art_105_13634.html>; Hebei Provincial Healthcare Security Administration et al. (2025). Notice on Work Related to Basic Medical Coverage for Urban and Rural Residents in 2025 (Hebei Medical Insurance Document [2025] No. 6, a local document). <https://www.renqiu.gov.cn/renqiu/ybjbmwj/202510/6d90754638a248cba655e94ea518a3bb.shtml>; Anhui Provincial Healthcare Security Administration et al. (2025). Notice on Work Related to Basic Medical Coverage for Urban and Rural Residents in 2025 (reposted by the Huaibei Municipal Healthcare Security Administration): “In accordance with the requirements of the Notice on Work Related to Basic Medical Coverage for Urban and Rural Residents in 2025 (Medical Insurance Document [2025] No. 22) issued by the National Healthcare Security Administration, the Ministry of Finance, and the State Taxation Administration”; “The per-person government subsidy standard for residents’ health insurance has increased by 30 yuan from the previous year, reaching at least 700 yuan per person per year.” <https://ybj.huaibei.gov.cn/zcwj/zcwj/58004084.html>; General Office of the State Council (2021). Opinions on Improving the Medical Insurance and Assistance System for Serious and Major Diseases (General Office of the State Council Document [2021] No. 42). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2021/content_5659514.htm>; General Office of the State Council (2024). Guiding Opinions on Improving the Long-Term Mechanism for Enrollment in Basic Medical Insurance (General Office of the State Council Document [2024] No. 38). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/content/202408/content_6965741.htm>; National Healthcare Security Administration (2026). These Health Insurance Measures Mentioned in the 2026 Government Work Report. <https://www.nhsa.gov.cn/art/2026/3/5/art_14_19809.html>
entries.notes: The National Healthcare Security Administration’s 2025 notice (Medical Insurance Document [2025] No. 22) has not been publicly posted on either the administration’s official website or the Chinese government website. The 700-yuan and 400-yuan figures match in documents from both Hebei and Anhui provinces; the Anhui document explicitly says they are based on that notice. While you are receiving unemployment insurance benefits, unemployment insurance pays for your employee health insurance, so you do not need to enroll twice.

entries.title: If you become seriously ill, use health insurance, catastrophic illness insurance, medical assistance, and out-of-area registration first; avoid online loans
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Follow the steps in order. First, before being hospitalized in another province, register through the “National Out-of-Area Medical Treatment Registration” mini-program in the “National Healthcare Security Administration” WeChat official account. Second, settle the bill directly when you leave the hospital. Third, if the amount you must pay after reimbursement is still too high, apply for medical assistance through your township government or subdistrict office. Fourth, if you are still employed, take sick leave under the statutory medical treatment period, during which you are off work because of illness and cannot be dismissed; if the condition is work-related, use work injury insurance. Fifth, if you cannot pay your credit card bill, contact the bank to negotiate installment payments. Sixth, if the money is still insufficient, raise funds through an individual assistance platform designated by the Ministry of Civil Affairs. The main documents needed are a diagnosis certificate, an itemized expense list, and a settlement statement. Expect two to four visits. The hard part is making repeated trips to handle procedures while you are ill.
entries.summary: Follow the steps in order: before hospitalization in another province, register through the “National Healthcare Security Administration” WeChat official account, then settle the bill directly when discharged without paying the full amount upfront. If you still cannot afford your share after reimbursement, apply for medical assistance through the township or subdistrict office. Employed people have a statutory medical treatment period of 3 to 24 months based on their years of service, during which the company cannot dismiss them. Avoid online loans and high-interest private loans.
entries.benefit: China collectively calls basic health insurance, catastrophic illness insurance, and medical assistance its “three-tier system,” with each layer providing another level of support. Minimum-living-allowance recipients and people in extreme hardship receive assistance covering at least 70% of eligible medical expenses. Patients with serious illnesses who were not previously poor but have become poor because of medical costs may also apply for further assistance. If you register before hospitalization in another province, you can settle the bill directly upon discharge instead of paying the full amount upfront and then seeking reimbursement where you are insured. If you stop working because of illness, the statutory medical treatment period lasts 3 to 24 months, depending on your years of service. During that period, the company may not terminate your employment contract, and sick pay may not be less than 80% of the local minimum wage. Employees with work-related injuries have a period of leave with pay while recovering and not working. During that period, their original wages and benefits continue to be paid monthly by their employer; it generally lasts no more than 12 months. If your credit card debt exceeds your ability to repay but you are willing to repay it, you can negotiate a personalized installment plan with the bank that reschedules the debt for up to five years. Once an agreement is signed, the bank must stop debt collection. Online individual assistance platforms that raise funds on someone’s behalf must be designated by the civil affairs department of the State Council. The platforms must verify whether the request for help is genuine. Donations may be paid only to the person seeking help or to an account that person provides (nationwide).
entries.sources: General Office of the State Council (2021). Opinions on Improving the Medical Insurance and Assistance System for Serious and Major Diseases (General Office of the State Council Document [2021] No. 42). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2021/content_5659514.htm>; National Healthcare Security Administration (2025). How Can Medical Expenses Incurred in Another Province Be Reimbursed Directly? <https://www.nhsa.gov.cn/art/2025/3/16/art_14_16010.html>; Ministry of Labour (1994). Provisions on the Medical Treatment Period for Enterprise Employees Who Are Ill or Injured for Non-Work-Related Reasons (Ministry of Labour Document [1994] No. 479, Articles 2 and 3). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2022-08/31/content_5711269.htm>; Ministry of Labour (1995). Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Labour Law (Ministry of Labour Document [1995] No. 309, Article 59). <http://hrss.jl.gov.cn/ldgx/ldyggl/201608/t20160824_2401358.html> (reposted by the Jilin Provincial Department of Human Resources and Social Security); State Council (revised 2010). Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance (State Council Order No. 586, Articles 30 and 33). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1778064.htm>; China Banking Regulatory Commission (2011). Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Credit Card Business of Commercial Banks (China Banking Regulatory Commission Order No. 2 of 2011, Article 70). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1893974.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (2023). Decision on Amending the Charity Law (Article 124). <https://www.gov.cn/yaowen/liebiao/202312/content_6923390.htm>; Ministry of Civil Affairs and four other departments (2024). Measures for the Administration of Online Individual Assistance Platforms (Order No. 75, Articles 3, 11, 13, and 17). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2024/issue_11646/202410/content_6980857.html>
entries.notes: The share of costs covered by medical assistance and the annual reimbursement cap are set by the place where you are insured. The statutory medical treatment period has six tiers, based on your total years of work and your years with your current employer. After that period ends, the company may be able to terminate your contract legally, so check which tier applies to you in advance. People receiving emergency treatment or resuscitation are also on the list of those who need to register for out-of-area care. The healthcare administration’s page does not say whether emergency cases are registered automatically or whether registration can be completed afterward; call the place where you are insured to ask. Avoid online loans and high-interest private loans. Courts protect interest only up to four times the one-year loan prime rate (LPR); see Item 15 on avoiding high-interest loans. The portion above that threshold is not protected, but you still have to repay the principal. You will not have the energy to fight such a lawsuit from a hospital bed. Urgent, serious injury or illness is different: call China’s 120 emergency number even if you have no money. Hospitals may not refuse, evade, or delay treatment. The emergency treatment costs for that stage are paid by the Disease Emergency Assistance Fund; see Section 24, Item 8 (“Emergency patients must be treated first, too”). The original page for Ministry of Labour Document [1995] No. 309 cannot be opened on the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security website; its content is taken from a provincial human resources and social security department’s repost. For how to negotiate installments with your bank when you cannot pay your credit card bill, see Item 23 (“When you can no longer repay credit cards or online loans”).

entries.title: Replace a lost ID card immediately; if you need one urgently, get a temporary ID card first
entries.cost: You must pay the card production fee. This is a statutory charge; the amount is set nationally, so check the locally posted rate. Apply at the police station where your permanent household registration is located. It takes one visit.
entries.summary: For a replacement, the card must be issued within 60 days of the day you submit the form. If you need an ID urgently, apply for a temporary ID card at the same time. It is issued within three days and is valid for three months. Without an ID card, you cannot find work, obtain accommodation, open an account, or collect subsidies. It is a prerequisite for all these procedures.
entries.benefit: The public security authority must issue the card within 60 days from the day you submit the Resident Identity Card Application Registration Form. If you urgently need identification while a first-time application, renewal, or replacement is being processed, you can apply for a temporary resident identity card. The public security authority must issue it within three days of receiving the application. It is valid for three months (nationwide).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (2003). Resident Identity Card Law (Presidential Order No. 4, Articles 12 and 20). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2003/content_62254.htm>; Ministry of Public Security (2005). Measures for the Administration of Temporary Resident Identity Cards (Ministry of Public Security Order No. 78, Articles 2, 7, 9, 12, and 17). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2021-12/25/content_5712922.htm>
entries.notes: Without an ID card, you cannot find work, obtain accommodation, open an account, or collect subsidies; it is a prerequisite for all these procedures. The Resident Identity Card Law was amended in 2011. The text cited here was published in 2003; the currently effective provisions govern. Whether you can apply outside the place of your household registration depends on local public security announcements.

entries.title: After registering as unemployed, seek recognition as a person facing employment difficulties to obtain social insurance subsidies or a public-service job
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Apply for recognition at a public employment service agency in your subdistrict or community. Eligibility varies by locality. Common categories include older people, people unemployed long term, members of minimum-living-allowance households, people with disabilities, and members of households where no one is employed. You must register as unemployed before applying. The hard parts are checking each eligibility requirement and paying social insurance contributions upfront.
entries.summary: Once recognized, you can receive a subsidy for social insurance contributions you pay yourself, in principle no more than two-thirds of what you actually pay, for up to three years. If an employer hires you or you are placed in a public-service job, the employer’s share of social insurance contributions can also be subsidized. Subsidies for public-service jobs are based on the local minimum wage. These jobs pay little but include social insurance and can help you through a transition. Social insurance subsidies are often paid as reimbursements, so you must pay upfront.
entries.benefit: Once recognized, people without an employer who pay their own social insurance contributions (called flexible employment) can receive a social insurance subsidy. In principle, the subsidy is no more than two-thirds of what you actually pay and can be received for up to three years. If an employer hires you or you are placed in a public-service job, the employer receives subsidies based on the pension, medical, and unemployment insurance contributions it actually pays. Public-service jobs are positions created with government funding, and their subsidies are based on the local minimum wage. Government-created public-service jobs give priority to people facing employment difficulties. There is also a one-time job-seeking subsidy for university graduates. It covers graduates from minimum-living-allowance households, households where no one is employed, and households of people in extreme hardship. Graduates with disabilities and those who have received national student loans also qualify. The subsidy is paid in the academic year of graduation (national framework; localities set eligibility criteria and amounts).
entries.sources: Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (revised 2023). Measures for the Administration of Employment Subsidy Funds (Finance and Social Security Document [2017] No. 164, revised and issued in December 2023). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202401/content_6926462.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (2007, amended 2015). Employment Promotion Law (Articles 52 and 53). <https://www.gov.cn/guoqing/2021-10/29/content_5647636.htm>
entries.notes: Public-service jobs do not pay much, but they include social insurance and can help during a transition. Social insurance subsidies are often paid as reimbursements, so you must pay upfront. Ask China’s 12333 service line or your subdistrict office about the specific eligibility requirements.

entries.title: While unemployed, claim vocational training, employment internship, and social insurance subsidies; do not pay for training yourself
entries.cost: It costs nothing. The training itself takes considerable time. The hard part is attending the entire course and earning a certificate before you can receive the subsidy.
entries.summary: If you complete training and obtain a qualifying certificate, you can receive a vocational training subsidy, up to three times per person. University graduates who have not found work within two years of graduation and unemployed young people aged 16 to 24 can take part in employment internships and receive a basic living allowance during the internship. First check the “Vocational Training Subsidy Catalogue” on your local human resources and social security bureau’s official website; do not pay to enroll in a course yourself.
entries.benefit: Regulations from the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security list a range of employment subsidy fund programs: money the government specifically sets aside to subsidize employment. People who complete training and obtain a qualifying certificate receive a vocational training subsidy, up to three times per person. People facing employment difficulties who pay their own social insurance contributions (flexible employment) can receive a subsidy for up to three years; if they are less than five years from the statutory retirement age, it can be extended until retirement. University graduates who pay their own social insurance contributions can receive a subsidy for up to two years; for those hired by an enterprise, the subsidy lasts up to one year. University graduates who have not found work within two years of graduation, as well as unemployed young people aged 16 to 24, can take part in employment internships and receive a basic living allowance during the internship.
entries.sources: Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2023). Measures for the Administration of Employment Subsidy Funds (Articles 5, 7, and 10). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202401/content_6926462.htm>
entries.notes: Each province sets the specific list of subsidized training and the subsidy amounts. First check the “Vocational Training Subsidy Catalogue” on your local human resources and social security bureau’s official website. University graduates in their graduation year from minimum-living-allowance households or households where no one is employed, as well as those with outstanding student loans or disabilities, have a separate one-time job-seeking and entrepreneurship subsidy.

entries.title: Do more than submit résumés: use a systematic job search—learn skills, set goals, and ask others for help
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Set aside one to two hours a day for several weeks. You can skip paid courses and use free career guidance from public employment service agencies instead. The hard parts are keeping at it every day when no one is supervising you and taking the initiative to ask others for help.
entries.summary: People who took part in job-search coaching had 2.67 times the odds of finding work compared with those who did not. The useful elements are learning specific job-search skills, explaining yourself clearly, setting clear goals, taking initiative, and asking others for help.
entries.benefit: A combined analysis of 47 controlled studies of job-search coaching found the following. The studies used experimental or quasi-experimental designs and compared separate groups. The group that received coaching had 2.67 times the odds of finding work compared with the group that did not (OR 2.67, an odds ratio). Several components of the coaching were effective. First, teaching job-search skills. Second, improving self-presentation (explaining yourself clearly). Third, increasing self-efficacy (believing you can do it). Fourth, encouraging initiative. Fifth, setting goals. Sixth, seeking social support (asking others for help). Coaching that both taught skills and increased motivation had the greatest effect.
entries.sources: Liu S, Huang JL, Wang M (2014). Effectiveness of job search interventions: a meta-analytic review. Psychological Bulletin 140(4): 1009–1041. <https://doi.org/10.1037/a0035923>
entries.notes: Most of these studies were conducted in Europe and North America and used structured group courses. Applying their findings in China means extrapolating results from elsewhere; they were not measured domestically. In practice, seeking social support means asking people you know to introduce you to employers or refer you internally. Do not be embarrassed to ask.

entries.title: Do not pay deposits, surrender documents, sign up for “training loans,” join pyramid schemes, or take high-interest loans
entries.cost: It costs nothing. If you hear “pay first, then start work,” “complete training first, then we’ll arrange a job,” or “recruit more people,” refuse on the spot. Keep chat records and proof of transfers. The hard part is that the more urgently you need money, the more tempting it is to take a chance, and saying “no” on the spot is not easy.
entries.summary: Employers may not withhold your ID card, demand a deposit, or collect money under another name. If an employment agency fails to find you a job, it must refund its fee. Training loans that require you to pay for training before starting work, and pyramid schemes that pay you for recruiting people, are scams identified by Chinese authorities. Courts will not uphold the portion of loan interest exceeding four times the one-year loan prime rate (LPR), but you still have to repay the principal.
