entries.benefit: A company may not withhold your ID card or other documents, require you to find a guarantor, or demand money or property under another name. If it violates these rules, it will be ordered to return what it took and fined 500 to 2,000 yuan per person. Employment agencies likewise may not withhold documents or collect deposits. If they fail to find you a job, they must refund the agency fee. Using a job posting to induce you to pay a training fee or take out a loan first is a “recruitment-to-training” or “training loan” scam specifically flagged by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and four other departments. Schemes that pay commissions for recruiting people and require payment to join are pyramid schemes; participants can be fined up to 2,000 yuan. For private loans, courts will not uphold the portion of interest exceeding four times the one-year loan prime rate (LPR) in effect when the contract was signed. This new rule replaced the old method that divided rates into three bands using 24% and 36% thresholds (nationwide, from August 2020).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (2007). Labour Contract Law (Presidential Order No. 65, Articles 9 and 84). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm>; Ministry of Labour and Social Security (2007). Provisions on Employment Services and Employment Management (Ministry of Labour and Social Security Order No. 28, Articles 14, 55, and 58). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2022-11/28/content_5711307.htm>; Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and four other departments (2026). Risk Alert: Beware of “Recruitment-to-Training” and “Training Loan” Schemes. <https://chinajob.mohrss.gov.cn/h5/c/2026-05-18/543038.shtml>; State Council (2005). Regulations on the Prohibition of Pyramid Selling (State Council Order No. 444, Articles 2, 7, and 24). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2005/content_80604.htm>; Supreme People’s Court (2020). Decision on Amending the Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases (Judicial Interpretation [2020] No. 6, Article 26). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/249031.html>; Supreme People’s Court (2020). Judicial Protection Cap on Private Lending Interest Rates Adjusted to “Four Times the One-Year LPR.” <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/249051.html>
entries.notes: Four times the LPR is the upper limit of interest that courts are willing to protect; it does not mean "if you borrowed it, you don't have to repay it"—the principal must still be repaid. This judicial interpretation was amended once more in December 2020; article numbers changed, so refer to the currently effective text. For how to convert processing fees of installment plans and online loans into annualized interest rates, see Section 5, Item 7 (Converting Interest into Annualized Rates). The more urgently you need money, the more likely you are to be targeted by these schemes. First go through the legitimate channels mentioned earlier in this section: unemployment insurance benefits, labor inspection complaints, legal aid, relief stations, and temporary assistance.

entries.title: Housing difficulties: Join the queue for public rental housing first
entries.cost: Application is free of charge. Submit materials to the municipal or county housing security department, and provide written consent authorizing them to verify the circumstances you reported. If the materials are incomplete, they will inform you all at once of what needs to be supplemented. The period of waiting in line for housing is called the waiting period (queue period), which generally does not exceed 5 years.
entries.summary: Three criteria must be met simultaneously: owning no housing locally, or housing space is below standard; income and assets are below standard; and for migrant workers, having been stably employed locally for the prescribed number of years. The waiting period is published locally. This is a distant water that cannot quench immediate thirst, but queueing costs nothing; applying earlier gets you placed sooner.
entries.benefit: You can apply if you meet all three criteria. First, having no housing locally, or housing space is below the prescribed standard. Second, income and assets are below prescribed standards. Third, for migrant workers, having maintained stable employment locally for the prescribed number of years. Specific conditions are determined and published by housing security departments of direct-administered municipalities, cities, and counties. People registered on the waiting list are called waiting targets (eligible applicants on the waiting list); the housing security department shall arrange housing units for them within the waiting period (national framework, eligibility thresholds and rents determined locally, since 2012).
entries.sources: Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development (2012). Measures for the Administration of Public Rental Housing (Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development Decree No. 11, Articles 7, 8, 10). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2012/content_2226147.htm>
entries.notes: This is distant water that cannot quench immediate thirst, but queueing costs nothing; applying earlier gets you placed sooner. Various localities also have other types such as government-subsidized rental housing (affordable rental housing), with different rules; check the website of the local housing and urban-rural development department.

entries.title: Paring housing and food costs to the minimum: Shared monthly rentals instead of daily rentals; home cooking and subsidized senior dining halls instead of takeout
entries.cost: Finding a place takes 1 to 3 days. The deposit is usually 1 month's rent (author's rough estimate). Cooking for yourself takes 30 to 60 minutes per day. The difficult part lies in cooking by hand every day and resisting the urge to order takeout.
entries.summary: In national per capita consumption in 2025, food accounted for 29.3% and housing accounted for 21.7%; combined, the two accounted for more than half, so cutting these two items is the most effective. According to the author's experience, daily rentals and hourly rooms converted to a monthly basis are more expensive than shared rentals; cooking for yourself is cheaper than ordering takeout. When job hunting, ask clearly whether room and board are included; positions that include them essentially wipe out these two major expense categories.
entries.benefit: In 2025, the national resident average per capita expenditure was 29,476 yuan (referred to as per capita consumption expenditure). Among this, food, tobacco, and alcohol accounted for 8,631 yuan, or 29.3%. Housing accounted for 6,397 yuan, or 21.7%. Combined, the two exceeded half, so compressing these two items is most effective. Elderly meal assistance services are rolled out to all seniors, taking forms such as senior canteens, senior dining tables, and meal assistance service points; seniors in financial distress receive additional differentiated subsidies. As a reference: as of January 1, 2026, the lowest first-tier monthly minimum wage among all provinces was Qinghai at 2,080 yuan, and the highest was Shanghai at 2,740 yuan (Nationwide, 2025 to 2026).
entries.sources: National Bureau of Statistics (2026). Income and Consumption Expenditure of Residents in 2025. <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfbhjd/202601/t20260119_1962321.html>; Ministry of Civil Affairs and ten other departments (2023). Action Plan on Actively Developing Elderly Meal Assistance Services (Min Fa [2023] No. 58). <https://www.gov.cn/govweb/zhengce/zhengceku/202310/content_6911233.htm>; Department of Human Resources and Social Security of Sichuan Province (2026). National Provincial, Autonomous Regional, and Directly Administered Municipal Minimum Wage Standards (as of January 1, 2026, reposting the table from the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security official website). <https://rst.sc.gov.cn/rst/ylbxjwjgzxx/2026/7/10/89a8ef06cc264d29b282d7c62f362a6b.shtml>
entries.notes: Daily rental rooms and hourly rooms calculated monthly are much more expensive than shared rentals; this is an empirical judgment without official figures. Whether elderly meal assistance sites are open to non-seniors and what they charge varies by locality. When looking for a job, ask clearly whether room and board are included; positions that include room and board can directly wipe out these two major expense items. The original page of the table from the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security could not be opened; figures are taken from the reposted page of the Sichuan Provincial Department of Human Resources and Social Security.

entries.title: Don't panic if social security contributions are interrupted: Pension is calculated cumulatively; medical insurance is supplemented according to rules
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Resident pension and resident medical insurance can be paid individually on an annual basis. If employee social insurance is interrupted, there is no need to spend money finding an agency for fake payroll affiliation ("guakao") just to "keep it unbroken."
entries.summary: Pensions are calculated based on cumulative years, not consecutive years; gaps do not reset the count to zero, and reaching statutory retirement age with an accumulated 15 years allows you to receive monthly payments. Those who have paid employee medical insurance for sufficient years do not need to pay anymore after retirement; the required years differ across localities. Contribution gaps affect two things: after resuming payments for resident medical insurance, medical expenses are not reimbursed for a certain period; furthermore, local home purchasing, household registration (hukou), and points-based residence systems often require consecutive contribution payments.
entries.benefit: Basic pension insurance is calculated on cumulative contribution years; interruptions in between do not wipe the slate clean. Upon reaching statutory retirement age, accumulating a full 15 years entitles one to receive monthly pension payments. If insufficient, one may continue contributing until reaching 15 years. When changing work locations (formally termed "cross-pooling regions"), the pension relationship transfers with the individual, and contribution years continue to accumulate upward. When cumulative contributions for employee medical insurance reach the nationally prescribed years, no further payments are required after retirement. The penalty for interrupting resident medical insurance is a waiting period: after payments resume, medical treatments are not reimbursed for a period of time (for resident medical insurance, see Item 9) (Nationwide).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2010, amended 2018). Social Insurance Law (Articles 16, 19, 27). <https://www.gov.cn/guoqing/2021-10/29/content_5647616.htm>; General Office of the State Council (2024). Guiding Opinions on Improving the Long-Term Mechanism for Basic Medical Insurance Participation (Guo Ban Fa [2024] No. 38). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/content/202408/content_6965741.htm>
entries.notes: Regarding the number of years after which employee medical insurance contributions are no longer required in retirement, the law states "nationally prescribed years," but figures implemented locally differ, and often differ between men and women. Call 12393 or consult the healthcare security bureau at your place of coverage. Contribution interruptions mainly affect local qualifications requiring consecutive payments for a certain number of months, such as buying a house, obtaining household registration (hukou), and points systems; these rules are set locally, so check local regulations. Spending money on agencies for "affiliation" (guakao) contribution proxies may result in lost money and carries legal risks; it is not recommended. For how to transfer pension and medical insurance relations when changing cities for work and avoiding cashing out/terminating insurance, see Section 19, Item 19 (Transferring Pension and Medical Insurance Relations to a New Place of Insured Coverage). The 15-year threshold will increase by 6 months every year starting in 2030, gradually reaching 20 years; for calculating the financial math of self-paying, see Section 5, Item 46 (Paying Employee Pension Insurance on Your Own).

entries.title: Served time, went bankrupt, or ended up on the dishonest judgment debtors list: The law provides paths for starting over; complete the formalities first
entries.cost: No processing fees are charged. Released prisoners report to the justice office or subdistrict office at their place of household registration or residence to apply for resettlement, assistance, and education (government resettlement and support). Those on the list of dishonest judgment debtors should pay off what is owed and then apply to the executing court to have their names removed. Individuals who have maintained social insurance in Shenzhen for a full 3 years can apply for personal bankruptcy. Every step requires preparing materials, undergoing interviews, and undergoing a 1-to-3-year observation/supervision period. The hard part is having to explain past events to people over and over again and enduring the observation period.
entries.summary: Persons released after serving their sentences must not be discriminated against in employment, schooling, or social security; those experiencing hardship in daily living receive government assistance in resettlement. For those under 18 at the time of crime and sentenced to 5 years or less, records are sealed, and they need not report them when enlisting or job hunting. The duration on the dishonest list is 2 years; once debts are cleared, the court shall delete the name within 3 working days. Criminal records of adults are not sealed; they must be truthfully reported when enlisting in the military or seeking employment.
entries.benefit: Persons released after serving their sentences enjoy equal rights with other citizens in accordance with the law and shall not be discriminated against in employment, schooling, and social security entitlements. For those experiencing living difficulties, the government of the place of household registration or residence shall assist with resettlement and provide relief and support in accordance with the law (Prison Law revised in 2026, effective November 1). A 2010 central document requires strengthening vocational training for them, including eligible individuals in the minimum subsistence guarantee (subsistence allowance / dibao), and establishing transitional resettlement bases. For those under 18 at the time of the crime and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of 5 years or less, criminal records are sealed and need not be reported when enlisting or job hunting; where the individual applies for a certificate of no criminal record, it shall be issued within 3 working days. The term of inclusion on the dishonest judgment debtor list is 2 years. Once debts are paid in full, or circumstances such as reaching a settlement with the opposing party occur, the court shall delete the name within 3 working days. The Personal Bankruptcy Regulations of the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone is currently the only personal bankruptcy regulation; after bankruptcy is declared and a 3-year observation period is completed, unpaid debts can be discharged. When an enterprise legal person cannot pay off debts due and owes more than it owns (termed insolvent / liabilities exceeding assets), it can apply for reorganization, settlement, or bankruptcy liquidation. After bankruptcy procedures are concluded, the enterprise proceeds to handle cancellation of registration. However, guarantors and other jointly liable debtors of the enterprise "shall continue to bear the liability for discharge in accordance with the law" for the unliquidated portion. Bosses who personally signed guarantees for the company must still repay the debts themselves. Criminal records of adults are not sealed: Article 100 of the Criminal Law stipulates that anyone who has received criminal punishment according to law must truthfully report having received criminal punishment when enlisting or seeking employment, and may not conceal it (Nationwide; personal bankruptcy only in Shenzhen).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2026). Prison Law (2026 Revision, Articles 59, 60, 62). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202604/t20260430_726746.shtml>; General Office of the CPC Central Committee and General Office of the State Council (2010). Notice Forwarding the "Opinions of the Central Committee for Comprehensive Management of Social Public Security on Further Strengthening Resettlement, Assistance, and Education Work for Persons Released upon Completion of Sentences and Persons Discharged from Reeducation Through Labor" (Zhong Ban Fa [2010] No. 5). <http://www.hnziyang.gov.cn/jc_zy/63/84/content_19460.html> (reposted by the Government of Ziyang District, Yiyang City); Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). Criminal Procedure Law (2018 Amendment, Article 286). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/201810/t20181027_396818.shtml>; Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of Justice (2022). Implementation Measures on the Sealing of Juvenile Criminal Records (Articles 9, 15). <https://gat.hunan.gov.cn/gat/jwgk/zfxxgk/xxgkml/zcfgjjd/zcfg/202205/t20220531_24795836.html> (reposted by the Public Security Department of Hunan Province); Supreme People's Court (amended 2017). Several Provisions on Publishing Information on the List of Dishonest Persons Subject to Execution (Articles 2, 10). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/37182.html>; Standing Committee of Shenzhen Municipal People's Congress (2020). Personal Bankruptcy Regulations of Shenzhen Special Economic Zone (Articles 2, 23, 95, 97, 103). <https://sf.sz.gov.cn/xxgk/xxgkml/zcfg/content/post_8586018.html>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2006). Enterprise Bankruptcy Law (Presidential Decree No. 54, Articles 2, 7, 120, 121, 124; Article 124: "The guarantors and other jointly liable debtors of a bankrupt party shall, after the conclusion of bankruptcy proceedings, continue to bear the liability for discharge in accordance with the law for claims that were not satisfied pursuant to bankruptcy liquidation procedures."). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2006/content_413952.htm>; National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Article 100, Paragraph 1: "Anyone who has undergone criminal punishment in accordance with the law shall, at the time of enlisting in the armed forces or taking employment, truthfully report to the unit concerned that he has undergone criminal punishment, and shall not conceal it." This page is the original 1997 text). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2011). Amendment (VIII) to the Criminal Law (Article 19: "A paragraph is added to Article 100 of the Criminal Law as the second paragraph: 'A person who was under the age of 18 at the time of committing a crime and was sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years shall be exempt from the reporting obligation specified in the preceding paragraph.'"). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf68be604a1>
entries.notes: Adult criminal records are not sealed. Article 100 of the Criminal Law requires that one must truthfully report having received criminal penalties when enlisting or seeking employment. Occupations such as civil servants, judges, lawyers, teachers, and political vetting have separate statutory restrictions; the aforementioned prohibition of discrimination does not alter this. The text of the Prison Law in force before November 1, 2026 corresponds to Articles 37 and 38; article numbers are subject to the effective text. An original page for Zhong Ban Fa [2010] No. 5 was not found on the Central Government website; it is taken from a district government repost. During the personal bankruptcy observation period, one cannot fly first class, engage in high consumption, or purchase real estate. Eight categories of debts, including compensation arising from intentional infringement upon another's personal rights, are not discharged. Debt exemptions obtained through fraudulent means may also be revoked.

entries.title: Before serious illness, supplement basic medical insurance with a one-year medical insurance or critical illness insurance policy, looking clearly for the four characters for "guaranteed renewal"
entries.cost: Young people buying a one-year expense-compensation medical insurance pay several hundred yuan per year. Expense-compensation refers to the kind that reimburses based on the money you actually spend. Critical illness insurance starts at several thousand yuan per year (author's rough estimate, no official figures). Before buying insurance, you must truthfully disclose your health status, taking a one-off 30 minutes.
entries.summary: This type of insurance supplements the out-of-pocket portion remaining after medical insurance reimbursements, as well as income loss from work stoppage. Before buying, look specifically for the four characters "guaranteed renewal": policies without these four words might be discontinued or face price hikes next year. Health conditions must be truthfully disclosed; concealing them may result in claim denials. Pay your basic medical insurance first before considering this item.
entries.benefit: Officials divide such products into two types. Medical insurance reimburses based on the medical expenses you actually incur. Illness insurance pays out a direct sum of money according to the agreed amount as soon as illnesses specified in the contract are diagnosed. Both supplement the portion you must pay yourself after medical insurance reimbursements, as well as losses from stopping work. Health insurance with an insurance period of one year or less and without guaranteed renewal written in its clauses falls under short-term health insurance. Only those exceeding one year, or with guaranteed renewal written in, are long-term health insurance. "Guaranteed renewal" means: when renewing upon expiration, the company must continue coverage according to the original terms and agreed rates. Insurance companies may not induce the same individual to repeatedly purchase expense-compensation medical insurance with identical or similar coverage functions. If you buy two policies, the same outlay can only be reimbursed once. Disease definitions for critical illness insurance follow unified industry standards, covering 28 severe diseases and 3 mild diseases. Malignant tumors, acute myocardial infarction, and sequelae of stroke are core diseases (Nationwide, since 2019 and 2020).
entries.sources: China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (2019). Measures for the Administration of Health Insurance (CBIRC Decree 2019 No. 3, Articles 2, 4, 41). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2019-12/04/content_5458542.htm>; Insurance Association of China, Chinese Medical Doctor Association (2020). Q&A on the Specifications for the Use of Disease Definitions in Critical Illness Insurance (2020 Revision). <https://www.iachina.cn/art/2020/11/5/art_8616_104705.html>; China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (2020). Notice Concerning Matters Related to the Use of the "China Life Insurance Industry Critical Illness Experience Incidence Table (2020)" (Yin Bao Jian Fa [2020] No. 51). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-11/06/content_5557791.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (amended 2015). Article 16 of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China (Truthful Disclosure and Non-Rescission after Two Years from Contract Formation). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7c4060811>
entries.notes: Rated Level B because the authorities only provided definitions and rules, without figures on "how much can be saved by purchasing." "Million-yuan medical insurance" (Million Medical Insurance) is a marketing name; regulatory-wise it counts as short-term health insurance. If "guaranteed renewal" is not written into the policy terms, it may be withdrawn from sale or face price increases next year; before purchasing, look for these four characters in the terms first. For two medical insurance policies that reimburse based on actual spending, the same expense cannot be reimbursed twice, so do not stack purchases. If you already have an illness when purchasing insurance and fail to disclose it truthfully, claims will be denied when trouble arises. Truthful disclosure has a two-year limit: once two years have elapsed from contract formation, the insurance company can no longer rescind the contract on grounds of failure to truthfully disclose, and must pay out if an event occurs. If intentional non-disclosure is discovered within two years, events occurring prior to contract rescission will not be compensated, and premiums will not be refunded. For which losses are worth covering with insurance, see Section 5, Item 39 (Losses You Cannot Shoulder). Pay your resident medical insurance (Item 9) first before considering this item. The disease definition standards were released by industry associations under the guidance of the CBIRC, and are not government documents.

entries.title: When truly without a place to sleep, 24-hour business venues can only serve as an emergency for one night; prioritize relief stations
entries.cost: Waiting areas in airports and railway stations generally cost nothing. Fast-food restaurants and internet cafes require spending a little money on consumption. Sleep is restless, and belongings carry the risk of theft. The hard part is not daring to truly fall asleep all night.
entries.summary: Airport and train station waiting areas can get you through a night, having restrooms and power outlets, but there are no official data saying this is safe. Relief stations have personnel on duty 24 hours a day; nighttime arrivals will also receive assistance first. In winter, some areas also open temporary cold-shelter sites. For those unwilling to enter a station, patrol personnel will also provide food and cold-weather clothing.
entries.benefit: You can get through a night in 24-hour commercial premises; they have toilets and can charge devices. As to whether it is safe there, there are no official figures. On the relief station side, the Ministry of Civil Affairs requires the assistance hotline to remain open around the clock, implementing 24-hour duty shifts. When persons in difficulty come to seek help, assistance is provided first in accordance with policies. Those whose employment has fallen through, who have been stolen from or robbed, or who have suddenly lost their source of livelihood can obtain emergency transitional basic living security. Where conditions permit, places such as community service centers are opened as temporary shelter sites. In winter, persons in difficulty are also guided toward relief stations or temporary cold-shelter venues. For those unwilling to enter a relief station, patrol personnel will give food, clothing, and warming supplies, and leave behind contact methods for seeking help. At night, during temperature drops, and in rain, snow, and freezing weather, patrols are intensified. Stations, docks, underpasses, bridges, culverts, and construction sites are key patrol areas (Nationwide, civil affairs departments have carried out annual winter special relief campaigns since 2013).
entries.sources: Author's experience (24-hour business venues section); General Office of the Ministry of Civil Affairs (2022). Notice on Solidly Conducting the "Delivering Warmth in Chilly Winter" Special Relief Action (Parts 2, 3, 4, 5; Part 3: "Ensure the assistance hotline remains open around the clock, respond promptly to clues of calls for help, and implement relief first according to policy regulations for persons in difficulty who come to seek assistance"). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-12/11/content_5731351.htm>; Ministry of Civil Affairs, Central Political and Legal Affairs Commission, Ministry of Public Security, and 11 other departments (2020). Notice on Conducting a Special Action to Greatly Enhance the Quality of Relief and Management Services for Homeless and Begging Persons in Distress (Min Fa [2020] No. 14, Part 2, Item 3: "Continue to solidly perform special relief work under extreme weather conditions, such as 'Delivering Warmth in Chilly Winter' and 'Delivering Coolness in Summer'"). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-03/24/content_5494916.htm>; Ministry of Civil Affairs (2003). Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the Measures for Assisting and Managing Vagrants and Beggars without Assured Living Sources in Urban Areas (Ministry of Civil Affairs Decree No. 24, Articles 2, 3, 5). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2003/content_62510.htm>
entries.notes: The safety risks are real. Keep your belongings close, do not accept drinks or food from strangers, and avoid secluded corners. Do not sleep outdoors at night under bridges, by rivers, or at construction sites. Sleeping outdoors in extreme weather can be fatal. For what food and lodging Chinese assistance stations provide and whether they issue travel tickets, see Item 4 (Go to an assistance station when you have nowhere else to turn). Assistance stations only admit people who cannot secure food and lodging themselves and have no relatives or friends to rely on. When entering a station, you must describe your circumstances truthfully; those who refuse to do so will not receive assistance. The Ministry of Civil Affairs requirements mentioned above come from a notice issued in the winter of 2022. Local authorities issue separate arrangements each year; follow the local ones. Some places clear people out in the middle of the night. Do not get into a confrontation with security staff.

entries.title: If you are owed wages, first find out who hired you: report an unlicensed workshop or labor subcontractor to labor inspection all the same; go to court only for private work done for a household or individual
entries.cost: It costs nothing. First establish three things: whether the other party runs a shop, factory, or other business; whether the work was subcontracted from a company or construction site; and whether you worked in someone's home. You can check whether the other party has a business license in China's National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System.
entries.summary: If an unlicensed workshop or shop owes you wages, you can still complain to labor inspection and apply for labor arbitration; the owner can also be held personally liable. If a labor subcontractor owes you money for work subcontracted from a construction site, the general contractor or project owner must pay. Only private work for a household or individual, such as working as a nanny, falls outside labor disputes and must be pursued in court.
entries.benefit: Article 2 of China's Labor Contract Law defines employing entities as organizations such as enterprises, individual economic organizations, and private non-enterprise entities; an individual person does not count. The Supreme People's Court's judicial interpretation on labor disputes lists several kinds of disputes that are not labor disputes. The first is a dispute between a household or individual and a domestic worker. The second is a dispute between an individual craftsperson and a helper or apprentice. The third is a dispute between a rural household operating under a contract and a person it employs. These must be brought before a court as ordinary civil disputes, subject to a three-year limitation period. An employing entity without a business license is not among these exceptions. Article 93 of the Labor Contract Law covers entities without lawful business qualifications. If you have already done the work, the entity or its investors must pay your wages, economic compensation, and damages. An investor is someone who put up the money to establish the entity. Article 29 of that interpretation covers three kinds of entities: those that never obtained a business license, those whose licenses have been revoked, and those that continue operating after their registered business term has expired. If you have a dispute with such an entity, name the entity or its investors as parties. Article 33 of China's Regulations on Labor Security Supervision provides that the human resources and social security authorities still conduct labor security inspections where an entity without a business license, or whose license has been revoked, employs people. If an individual contractor hires workers unlawfully and causes them harm, the organization that awarded the contract and the individual contractor are jointly and severally liable for compensation (Article 94 of the Labor Contract Law). A project owner or general construction contractor sometimes awards or subcontracts work to an individual or an entity without lawful business qualifications. If migrant workers are consequently owed wages, the project owner or general construction contractor must settle the arrears (Article 36 of the Regulations on Ensuring the Payment of Wages to Migrant Workers) (nationwide).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (amended 2012). Labor Contract Law (Articles 2, 93, and 94). <https://fgk.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfgk/c100009/c5193025/content.html> (republished in the State Taxation Administration's policy and regulations database); Supreme People's Court (2020). Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Labor Dispute Cases (I) (Judicial Interpretation〔2020〕No. 26, Articles 2 and 29). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/282121.html>; State Council (2004). Regulations on Labor Security Supervision (State Council Order No. 423, Article 33). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2004/content_63042.htm>; State Council (2019). Regulations on Ensuring the Payment of Wages to Migrant Workers (State Council Order No. 724, Article 36). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2020/content_5469641.htm>; National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 188). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; State Council (2006). Measures for the Payment of Litigation Costs (State Council Order No. 481, Articles 6 and 29). <https://www.gov.cn/ziliao/flfg/2006-12/29/content_483682.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (amended 2023). Civil Procedure Law (Articles 152 and 225). <https://amr.guizhou.gov.cn/zwgk/xxgkml/jcxxgk/zcfg/fl/202401/t20240129_83645867.html> (republished by the Guizhou Provincial Administration for Market Regulation)
entries.notes: Decide in this order. First, check whether the work was passed down from a company or construction site. If so, approach the company that awarded the contract or the general contractor. For the dedicated wage account at construction sites and advance payment by the general contractor, see Item 2 (Complain to labor inspection first if you are owed wages). Next, check whether the other party is doing business: for a shop, factory, or workshop, use labor inspection and arbitration whether or not it has a license, and name the owner personally as a party to the arbitration. Only for the remaining cases of private work for a household or individual should you go to court. In court, you must file the case and present evidence yourself. Under the rules, an ordinary first-instance proceeding must be concluded within six months, though the period can be extended. You must pay your own lawyer's fees; they are not among the litigation costs a court orders the losing party to bear. If you cannot afford a lawyer, you can apply for legal aid; see Item 3 (Legal aid). If you have an IOU, you can first apply for a payment order; see Item 2 (Payment order). For a small amount, use small-claims proceedings; see Section 8, Item 22 (Fraud in secondhand transactions and small-claims proceedings). The limitation period is three years; see Section 8, Item 19 (There are deadlines for asserting your rights). No route guarantees that the money will reach you. If the other party has no assets, you may win and still collect nothing.

entries.title: If you can no longer repay your credit card or online loans, call the bank or platform's customer service yourself to ask for a tailored installment plan or an extension. Do not borrow anew to repay old debts or pay intermediaries offering “suspended interest and deferred repayment,” “credit record repair,” or “anti-collection” services
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Call the official customer service number printed on the back of the card or published in the app, and explain that you cannot repay now but are willing to repay. Have proof of your income, unemployment, or illness ready. You will often need to call several times. If you reach an agreement, make monthly payments under the new plan. Until the debt is paid off, you cannot get another credit card. The hard part is answering the bank's calls yourself and explaining your difficulties over and over.
entries.summary: If you cannot repay your credit card but are willing to do so, you can ask the bank to negotiate a tailored installment plan lasting up to five years. Once an agreement is signed, the bank must stop collection efforts. But the bank can refuse, and any overdue payment already recorded will still remain on your credit report. Regulators have specifically warned against fee-charging intermediaries that offer to arrange “suspended interest and deferred repayment” or “wipe clean” your credit record. Do not use them.
entries.benefit: There are express rules for credit cards. If the debt exceeds your ability to repay but you remain willing to repay, the bank “may” negotiate with you on an equal footing and sign a tailored installment repayment agreement. The agreement may last no more than five years. It must specify how much you owe, how much is due each installment, and whether annual fees and interest will be charged during repayment. Once both sides sign, the bank and the collection agency it has engaged must stop collection efforts. This restriction does not apply if you fail to pay under the agreement. If the agreement is oral, the bank must keep an audio recording at least until the debt is paid off. Debt already placed on an installment plan cannot be placed on another one; a tailored installment plan is the sole exception (2022 regulatory notice). When the People's Bank of China repealed the old bank card rules in 2025, it specified that these provisions would continue to govern credit cards. There is no uniform rule for online loans equivalent to tailored installment plans. Whether you can obtain an extension or pay in installments depends on the contract and the lending institution. If the lender is a consumer finance company, regulations prohibit it from using violence, threats, intimidation, or harassment to collect debts. Neither banks nor consumer finance companies may pursue collection from people unconnected with the debt. As for fee-charging intermediaries, China's National Financial Regulatory Administration and four other departments jointly issued a risk alert in 2026. The alert says that claims such as “loans/credit cards do not need to be repaid,” “debt negotiation,” “debt replacement,” and “wiping clean credit records” are false information. These “agent rights-protection” services charge high service fees; if you try to withdraw partway through, you may even be accused of breaching the contract. They collect your bank card and mobile phone card details, home address, and children's school information. If you follow their instructions to submit false materials, deliberately evade debts, or use complaints to exert pressure, serious cases may involve unlawful or criminal conduct. In 2022, the Beijing office of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission also singled out advertisements for “suspended interest and deferred repayment,” “stopping collection,” and “a complete interest waiver.” It said that if you listen to these people, delay repayment, and stop contacting the bank, an adverse overdue payment record is very likely to be left on your credit report. In 2022, China's National Development and Reform Commission launched a targeted campaign against “credit record repair.” Its notice said that these people confuse credit-report disputes with credit restoration and commit fraud under labels such as “credit record repair,” “wiping clean records,” and “deleting entries.” Adverse information in a credit report is retained for five years from the day the adverse conduct or event ends, and is deleted when those five years expire. During the retention period, you can add an explanatory statement to the record, which the credit reporting agency must record (nationwide).
entries.sources: China Banking Regulatory Commission (2011). Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Credit Card Business of Commercial Banks (China Banking Regulatory Commission Order No. 2 of 2011, Articles 68 and 70). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1893974.htm>; China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission and People's Bank of China (2022). Notice on Further Promoting the Standardized and Healthy Development of Credit Card Business (CBIRC Regulation〔2022〕No. 13, Articles 19 and 30). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-07/07/content_5699827.htm>; People's Bank of China and National Financial Regulatory Administration (2025). Decision on Repealing the Measures for the Administration of Bank Card Business (Order〔2025〕No. 6). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2025/issue_12206/202508/content_7035429.html>; National Financial Regulatory Administration (2024). Measures for the Administration of Consumer Finance Companies (Order No. 4 of 2024, Articles 53 and 56). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2024/issue_11346/202405/content_6951507.html>; National Financial Regulatory Administration, Cyberspace Administration of China, Ministry of Public Security, People's Bank of China, and China Securities Regulatory Commission (2026-02-06). Risk Alert on Illegal “Agent Rights-Protection” Traps in Short Videos and Live Streams (republished on the official website of the Cyberspace Administration of China). <https://www.cac.gov.cn/2026-02/06/c_1772110875635198.htm>; Beijing Office of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (2022-10-25). Notice on Conducting a Targeted Campaign Against “Credit Record Repair.” <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-04/01/content_5682847.htm>; State Council (2013). Regulations on the Administration of the Credit Reporting Industry (State Council Order No. 631, Article 16). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2013-01/29/content_2303.htm>; Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate (amended 2018). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Obstructing Credit Card Administration (Judicial Interpretation〔2018〕No. 19, Articles 6 and 8). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/132701.html>; Ningxia Office of the National Financial Regulatory Administration (2026-06-16). Risk Alert on Preventing Illegal Agents from Handling Insurance Surrenders (12378 hotline). <https://www.nfra.gov.cn/branch/ningxia/view/pages/common/ItemDetail.html?docId=1261442&itemId=2188>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (amended 2023). Civil Procedure Law (Articles 152 and 164). <https://amr.guizhou.gov.cn/zwgk/xxgkml/jcxxgk/zcfg/fl/202401/t20240129_83645867.html> (republished by the Guizhou Provincial Administration for Market Regulation); State Council (2006). Measures for the Payment of Litigation Costs (State Council Order No. 481, Articles 6 and 29). <https://www.gov.cn/ziliao/flfg/2006-12/29/content_483682.htm>
entries.notes: The rule on tailored installment plans says a bank “may” negotiate; it does not have to agree, and the bank has the right to refuse. If you cannot reach an agreement, the bank can sue you in court for repayment. Under the rules, an ordinary first-instance proceeding must be concluded within six months, though the period can be extended; the period for a simplified proceeding is three months. You must pay for your own lawyer. That expense is not among the litigation costs a court orders the losing party to bear. If a judgment is entered and you still cannot pay, the case proceeds to enforcement; see Section 8, Item 20 (If you are sued or subject to enforcement). If you are placed on the list of judgment defaulters, see Section 8, Item 21 (Being placed on the judgment defaulters list). Simply being unable to repay is not a crime. The judicial interpretation issued by China's two highest judicial bodies states that failure to repay on time alone is insufficient to establish an intent to take the money for yourself. If, after running up a credit card overdraft, you flee, change your contact details to evade collection, or transfer assets, the overdraft may be deemed malicious. A malicious overdraft can be prosecuted as credit card fraud; an unpaid principal balance of 50,000 yuan or more counts as a relatively large amount. So answer the bank's calls, and tell the bank if your phone number or address changes. Borrowing anew to repay old debts only causes interest to snowball. Before comparing loans, look at the annualized interest rate; see Section 5, Item 7 (Convert interest to an annualized rate). For high-interest private loans, see Item 15 (Do not take out usurious loans). If collectors call your family or coworkers, or insult or threaten you, complain to the lender first. If a bank does not resolve the issue, call China's 12378 banking and insurance consumer complaint hotline; it is free. If your physical safety is threatened, call China's 110 emergency police number directly. If your credit report contains an error, see Section 8, Item 9 (Check your credit report for free) for how to check it and raise a dispute without charge. If you cannot repay because of a serious illness, also see Item 10 (For serious illness, first use medical insurance and medical assistance). Seeking an “insurance surrender agent” is the same kind of scheme; see Section 5, Item 43 (Do not use an insurance surrender agent). You yourself are the main beneficiary.

chapters.title: Do not ruin your own life: legal and financial safety
chapters.intro:
This section weighs money and personal freedom; it does not convert them into years of life. It covers three things: what liability the law imposes on you, how much compensation you can avoid paying by following the guidance, and what procedural rights you have when something happens. All article numbers have been checked against the official texts.

The items in this section are grouped by topic below. The numbers in parentheses are item numbers.

**Preventing fraud**: If you discover you have been defrauded, request a stop-payment order immediately (Item 2); hard rules against fraud (Item 3); seeing a face in a video does not count as verification (Item 4); do not lend anyone your bank card or mobile phone card (Item 8); check your credit report for free (Item 9); fraud in online shopping and secondhand transactions (Item 22); ask the price before an in-home repair (Item 27); do not carry things for strangers (Item 29); helping with a face scan can make you part of an AB loan scheme (Item 45).

**Signing, borrowing, and debt**: Read the entire document before signing (Item 17); write clear terms in an IOU when lending money (Item 18); there are deadlines for asserting your rights (Item 19); report your assets truthfully if you are subject to enforcement (Item 20); being placed on the judgment defaulters list (Item 21); do not become a company's nominal legal representative (Item 28); a family member has incurred gambling debts (Item 44).

**Conflict and resentment**: Call the police first when a conflict starts (Item 10); you may fight back against an attack you cannot escape (Item 11); do not seek revenge after a grievance (Item 12); do not harm people who have nothing to do with it (Item 13); when thoughts of taking someone down with you arise (Item 14); when someone close to you says that no one should get to live well (Item 15); buying someone insurance before harming them is a dead end (Item 38).

**Dating and marriage**: Think carefully before handing over a large gift (Item 23); transfer betrothal gifts through a bank (Item 24); put premarital property arrangements in writing (Item 25); verify marital status before marrying (Item 26); if you experience domestic violence, call the police first (Item 43).

**Reporting to the police, being accused, and gathering evidence**: If summoned, get a lawyer first (Item 5); when something happens, come forward and explain it yourself (Item 6); when someone reports you using fabricated facts (Item 33); insufficient evidence should result in an acquittal (Item 34); apply for state compensation (Item 35); ask for a case acceptance receipt when reporting to the police (Item 39); do not give money to those handling your case (Item 40); record a conversation that may turn hostile (Item 41); photograph the whole scene first (Item 42).

**Online speech and online abuse**: Do not insult people or spread rumors online (Item 16); turn on protective settings first if you are subjected to online abuse (Item 37).

**Sex and coercion**: Do not have sex with someone who is not fully conscious (Item 31); if someone demands money over an explicit video chat, call the police directly (Item 32); if you are a victim seeking compensation, do not meet the other party alone (Item 36).

**Driving, dogs, and preventing theft**: Do not flee after a traffic accident (Item 1); do not drive after drinking (Item 7); keep your dog on a leash (Item 30); fit proper locks to doors and windows (Item 46).

entries.title: After a traffic accident, stop, help anyone injured, and call the police. Do not flee
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Stop, turn on your hazard lights, help anyone injured, and call the police. Waiting for the traffic police will cost you at most an hour or two. If it is a minor accident, no one is injured, and neither party disputes the facts, take photos first. Then record the other party's name, phone number, license plate number, driver's license number, insurance certificate number, and the parts of the vehicles that were hit. After both parties sign, you can leave the scene and negotiate a settlement yourselves.
entries.summary: If you flee, you are presumed fully responsible for the accident. Your driver's license will be revoked, and if the flight constitutes a crime, you can never get another one. There is a more immediate cost: commercial vehicle damage insurance and third-party liability insurance do not cover hit-and-run accidents at all. You could have to pay hundreds of thousands of yuan in compensation yourself. Staying at the scene to help anyone injured and call the police costs you at most an hour or two.
entries.benefit: The party who flees must bear full responsibility for the accident. Your liability may be reduced somewhat only if you can prove that the other party was also at fault. Fleeing also results in revocation of your driver's license. If the flight constitutes a crime, you can never apply for a driver's license again. If the accident constitutes the crime of causing a traffic accident, fleeing carries a sentence of three to seven years. If a person dies because you fled, the sentence is more than seven years. Insurance will not cover it either: under commercial vehicle insurance, vehicle damage coverage and third-party liability coverage uniformly exclude “fleeing after causing a traffic accident” and “deliberately damaging or falsifying the scene or destroying evidence.” You will have to pay compensation of potentially hundreds of thousands of yuan entirely yourself (nationwide).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2021). Road Traffic Safety Law (revised 2021, Articles 70 and 101). <https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/205308/index.html> (republished by the Beijing Traffic Management Bureau of the Public Security Bureau); State Council (2017). Regulations for the Implementation of the Road Traffic Safety Law (State Council Order No. 405, revised 2017, Articles 86 and 92). <http://xzfg.moj.gov.cn/front/law/detail?LawID=75>; National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Article 133). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml>; Insurance Association of China (2020). Model Clauses for Commercial Motor Vehicle Insurance (2020 edition) (Articles 9 and 22). <https://www.iachina.cn/art/2020/9/4/art_24_104621.html>; Ministry of Public Security (2024). Provisions on the Application for and Use of Motor Vehicle Driving Licenses (amended by Ministry of Public Security Order No. 172, effective January 1, 2025; Article 15, item 3: a person who “flees after causing a traffic accident and whose flight constitutes a crime” may not apply for a motor vehicle driving license). <https://ga.tj.gov.cn/zwgk/zcwj/jg3/202501/t20250103_6824050.html> (republished by the Tianjin Municipal Public Security Bureau)
entries.notes: If someone is injured, help them first, then call the police. If you must move anything at the scene to help someone, first mark where the vehicle and people originally were. “I didn’t feel anything after the collision, so I drove away” may still be treated as fleeing the scene afterward. If you are unsure, call the police. The insurance provision cited is a model clause, a standard template used by the insurance industry. What your insurance will actually cover depends on the policy you hold.

entries.title: If you discover you have been scammed, immediately call China’s 110 or 96110 and ask for a stop-payment order; do not investigate on your own first
entries.cost: Free. Make one call and clearly state when you transferred the money, how much you transferred, and the recipient’s account number. Keep screenshots of the transfer and your chat records.
entries.summary: The short period just after the money is transferred matters most. Police can order an emergency stop-payment and quickly freeze the funds, and banks must cooperate. Once the money has been moved and dispersed, the chance of recovering it falls sharply. So call China’s 110 or 96110 first; do not investigate or ask around on your own first. If 96110 calls you, it is the police trying to warn you. Answer the call.
entries.benefit: China’s public security authorities have the power to make immediate inquiries about funds involved in a case, order an emergency stop-payment, and freeze the funds quickly. Banks and payment institutions must cooperate. Frozen money is returned to victims according to the prescribed procedure. Once the money has been moved and dispersed, the probability of recovering it drops substantially, so the sooner payment is stopped, the more effective it is. 96110 is China’s unified nationwide anti-fraud warning hotline. If it calls, the police are trying to warn you; be sure to answer (nationwide in China, since December 2022).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress of China (2022). Anti-Telecom and Online Fraud Law (Articles 20 and 34). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202209/t20220902_575631.shtml>; Fujian Provincial Public Security Department (2023). If 96110 Calls, Be Sure to Answer. <http://gat.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/fjjffpzxrx/spjq/202303/t20230306_6126156.htm> (provincial public security authority webpage)
entries.notes: Anyone claiming to represent China’s public security authorities, procuratorates, or courts who asks you to transfer money to a “safe account” is running a scam. The law says only to “establish a stop-payment and freezing system,” meaning that banks must hold the money. How much can be recovered depends on whether the money is still in the account when you report the scam. The information about the “National Anti-Fraud Center” app and 96110 comes from a Fujian Provincial Public Security Department page; the original page on the Ministry of Public Security’s website could not be opened.

entries.title: Remember the firm anti-fraud rules: do not readily trust incoming calls, disclose information, or click links, and verify carefully before transferring money. The seven most common types of scams all follow this pattern
entries.cost: Free. Memorize the “three don’ts and one do,” read through the seven types below, install the “National Anti-Fraud Center” app, and always answer calls from China’s 96110. If someone asks you to transfer money, share your screen, download an unfamiliar app, click a link, or give them a verification code, hang up first, then call an official number to check. The hard part is that the other person often creates a sense of urgency; you need to resist that pressure and hang up first.
entries.summary: If someone asks you to transfer money, share your screen, download an unfamiliar app, click a link, or give them a verification code, hang up first, then call back using an official number to check. Task-based rebate scams, fake online investments and wealth management, online loan scams, impersonation of customer service, impersonation of China’s public security authorities, procuratorates, or courts, romance scams known as “pig butchering,” and sexually enticing task-based scams all seek to get you to transfer money first. Recognizing them beforehand costs far less than trying to recover your money afterward.
entries.benefit: Chinese law requires the government and relevant departments to explain the methods used in different kinds of telecom and online fraud to the public. Public security authorities, together with financial, telecommunications, and cyberspace authorities, must establish a system of warnings and interventions and promptly warn people who may be about to be scammed. 96110 is the unified nationwide hotline for those warnings and interventions; answer if it calls. In a June 2026 briefing, China’s Ministry of Public Security reported that the 10 most prevalent types of scam accounted for 85% of all telecom and online fraud cases. Task-based rebate scams occurred most often, accounting for 25%. Fake online investments and wealth management caused the greatest losses, accounting for about 40% of all losses. The identifying features set out by type by the Fujian Provincial Public Security Department are as follows. Task-based rebate scams: “Someone inviting you to make money together is probably trying to make money off you”; if you cannot finish the assigned tasks, they will not return your principal. Fake investments and wealth management: paid promoters in a group display their returns; the scammers first give you a small rebate, then get you to invest more, and demand that you “pay tax” to withdraw funds. Online loans: “A loan does not require a deposit or fabricated bank transaction history. If you encounter such a demand, it is certainly fake.” Impersonation of customer service: scammers say you have signed up for a membership that will incur automatic charges or affect your credit record, then pressure you to transfer money to cancel it. These scammers often ask you to download an app called something like “XX Meeting” and then turn on screen sharing. Once you share your screen, “everything on your phone, including message pop-ups, SMS verification codes, and password entry, can be seen clearly.” The Shanghai Anti-Fraud Center warns: “Any mention of a ‘meeting ID,’ ‘screen sharing,’ or ‘remote control’ is a scam.” Impersonation of China’s public security authorities, procuratorates, or courts: “Public security authorities, procuratorates, and courts have no such thing as a ‘safe account.’ Anyone claiming to represent them who handles a case or takes a statement by phone, QQ, WeChat, or the internet is a scammer.” Abroad, scammers also impersonate Chinese embassies and consulates, claiming that you are suspected of money laundering, have important documents to collect, or have a passport or visa problem. They then transfer the call to a supposed “public security” authority in China. The Chinese Embassy in the United States specifically warns international students: “Anyone claiming to work for an embassy or consulate abroad, a telecommunications operator, customs, or another such organization who says you are suspected of a related violation or crime and proactively transfers your call to a public security authority is a scammer!” “Pig butchering” romance scams: “Do not readily trust a ‘romantic partner’ you have never met and have seen only in photos or videos”; they never video call or meet in person but frequently have an urgent need for money. Sexually enticing task-based scams: before agreeing to meet, they tell you to “complete tasks,” and the amount you pay keeps growing. Recognizing a scam beforehand costs far less than trying to stop payment afterward. How much a stop-payment order can recover depends on whether the money is still in the account when you report the scam. For how to stop payment, see Item 2 (call China’s 110 or 96110 and request a stop-payment order) (nationwide in China, since December 2022).

Among them, task-based rebate scams are the most prevalent, accounting for 25% of all such cases; fake online investment and wealth management scams cause the greatest losses, accounting for about 40% of all losses from such cases.” <https://www.mps.gov.cn/n2254536/n2254544/n2254552/n10491781/index.html>; Fujian Provincial Public Security Department (2023). If 96110 Calls, Be Sure to Answer. <http://gat.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/fjjffpzxrx/spjq/202303/t20230306_6126156.htm> (provincial public security authority webpage, including the reminder “Do not readily trust incoming calls, disclose information, or click links; verify carefully before transferring money,” and a warning to “beware of scam calls from numbers beginning with 192”); Fujian Provincial Public Security Department (2023 to 2024).
