First Letter of the School Year (III) (January 28, 2025). <https://us.china-embassy.gov.cn/chn/lsfw/lsxz/lstx/202503/t20250305_11568435.htm>; “pig butchering” romance scams <http://gat.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/fjjffpzxrx/spjq/202308/t20230818_6232030.htm>; sexually enticing task-based scams <http://gat.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/fjjffpzxrx/spjq/202403/t20240307_6410612.htm>
entries.notes: People claiming to represent China’s public security authorities, procuratorates, or courts, customer service, a leader, or a platform’s risk control team who ask you to “cooperate with an investigation,” “cancel a membership,” “complete tasks for rebates,” or act on “inside investment information” are following the same playbook. Real loans do not require a deposit, and China’s public security authorities, procuratorates, and courts have no “safe accounts.” Remembering those two points can block a large share of these scams. The evidence rating is B because this reminder is an official public awareness message, with no figures showing how much remembering it reduces the risk of being scammed. The reminder and breakdown of the seven types come from provincial public security department pages. China’s Ministry of Public Security reported 10 prevalent types of scam in 2026. The other types are impersonation of e-commerce or logistics customer service, loan and credit record scams, fake online gaming transactions, online dating scams, impersonation of leaders or acquaintances, and airline ticket refund or change scams. They follow the same pattern: ultimately, they ask you to transfer money. If you are abroad and receive a call from someone claiming to represent a Chinese embassy or consulate or a public security authority in China, saying you are involved in a case, have documents to collect, or have a passport problem, hang up first in every case. International students are a key target of this type of scam. An acquaintance who approaches you in person and asks you to “help with a face scan” for a loan may leave you with a debt without asking you to transfer money; see Item 45 (helping with a face scan). For scams involving outsourced operation of an online store that you may encounter while doing business, see Section 12, Item 24 (outsourced operation of an online store).

entries.title: Seeing a face on video or hearing a voice on the phone does not verify someone’s identity. If a money transfer is involved, hang up first and call back using an old number saved in your contacts
entries.cost: Free. Make one more call and wait a few more minutes. Avoid posting videos showing your face clearly or long voice recordings on public accounts. The hard part is that the other person often pressures you to act immediately; resist transferring money on the spot.
entries.summary: Seeing a face or hearing a voice does not verify someone’s identity. Whenever a money transfer is involved, hang up first, then call back using an old number saved in your own contacts, or ask someone you both know. If the other person says “the signal is bad” or “I’m in a meeting” and refuses a face-to-face video call, treat it as a scam.
entries.benefit: The Cybersecurity Bureau of China’s Ministry of Public Security gives three methods. The first is to check an action: ask the person to turn their head in one continuous motion, or cover their face completely with their palm and then quickly move it away. The original text says, “Current AI technology is prone to stuttering, blurring, or distortion when simulating these complex facial occlusions and changes in light and shadow.” The second is to listen for details in the voice: “AI-generated speech sometimes lacks natural pauses for breath or emotional variation, or has a slightly mechanical quality or unusual background noise.” The third is to verify through multiple channels. The original text calls this “the most essential step”: “After hanging up, directly call a phone number the other person regularly uses and that you know well (do not call back the suspicious incoming number), or check indirectly with a third person you both know.” The reminder is: “Do not readily trust video or voice; check actions and verify further.” Under Chinese law, using face or voice replacement for fraud has long been prohibited. Platforms providing face generation, face replacement, synthetic human voice, or voice imitation services must apply a conspicuous label. No organization or individual may maliciously remove, alter, forge, or conceal that label. But platforms follow the rules and scammers will not add a label, so “I didn’t see an AI label” is not evidence that the person is real. The Criminal Investigation Bureau of China’s Ministry of Public Security published a case involving a gang of 14 people. Investigators found more than 50,000 synthetic moving-face videos and personal information on more than 500,000 citizens. Police also seized 60 cloud servers (nationwide in China; labeling obligation effective September 1, 2025).
entries.sources: Cybersecurity Bureau of the Ministry of Public Security of China (2025). Seeing ≠ Believing: Beware of New AI Scams! <http://gat.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/fjjffpzxrx/spjq/202509/t20250922_7013008.htm> (reposted by the Fujian Provincial Public Security Department); Cyberspace Administration of China, Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, and Ministry of Public Security (2022). Provisions on the Administration of Deep Synthesis Internet Information Services (Articles 6, 16, and 17; effective January 10, 2023). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-12/12/content_5731431.htm>; Cyberspace Administration of China, Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, Ministry of Public Security, and National Radio and Television Administration (2025). Measures for Labeling AI-Generated Synthetic Content (Article 10; effective September 1, 2025). <https://www.cac.gov.cn/2025-03/14/c_1743654684782215.htm>; Criminal Investigation Bureau of the Ministry of Public Security of China and CCTV News (2026). Police Uncover More Than 50,000 Synthetic Moving-Face Videos: Who Is “Copying” Your Face? <http://gat.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/fjjffpzxrx/spjq/202603/t20260330_7117146.htm> (reposted by the Fujian Provincial Public Security Department)
entries.notes: To call back, use an old number saved in your own contacts. Do not call back the number shown on caller ID or use a new number sent by the other person in a chat. If the person refuses a face-to-face video call or a requested action, claiming “the signal is bad” or “I’m in a meeting,” treat it as a scam. Checking actions is only an aid; AI keeps improving. The only reliable method is the third one: checking through another channel. If you have already transferred money, see Item 2 of this section (immediately call China’s 110 and request a stop-payment order). To prevent your face and voice from being collected, see Section 14. The evidence rating is B because the official sources provide detection methods and cases, but no figures showing “how much the scam rate falls after people verify identity this way.” The Ministry of Public Security’s official website (mps.gov.cn) again returned site-wide 521 errors and could not be opened. The original articles by its Cybersecurity Bureau and Criminal Investigation Bureau were obtained from pages reposted by the Fujian Provincial Public Security Department.

entries.title: If you are accused of a crime or summoned for questioning, consult a lawyer first; do not settle privately or delete records
entries.cost: Lawyers’ fees start at several thousand yuan. If you have financial difficulties, you can apply to a Chinese legal aid agency for a lawyer at no charge. When questioned, answer only questions relevant to the case and leave the rest to your lawyer. The hard part is staying calm at the time instead of rushing to explain yourself.
entries.summary: You can consult a lawyer from the first time you are called in for questioning. If your lawyer requests a meeting with you, the detention center must arrange it within 48 hours at the latest, and the conversation will not be monitored. You can decline to answer questions unrelated to the case.
entries.benefit: From your first interrogation, or from the time compulsory measures are imposed on you (restricting your personal freedom), you have the right to appoint a lawyer. While the case is still being investigated by Chinese public security authorities, only a lawyer may act as your defender; you cannot appoint someone who is not a lawyer. If the lawyer requests a meeting, the detention center must arrange it within 48 hours at the latest, and the meeting must not be monitored. No one may be forced to prove their own guilt. You have the right to refuse to answer questions unrelated to the case. A single summons or compelled appearance may last no more than 12 hours, or 24 hours for an especially serious and complex case. A summons is a notice to come in for questioning; a compelled appearance means being forcibly brought in for questioning. Authorities may not use repeated consecutive summonses to hold someone in custody in effect. Anyone who fabricates facts to falsely accuse another person with the aim of having them prosecuted for a crime faces a sentence of up to 3 years, or 3 to 10 years if the act causes serious consequences. If a case is dropped after you have been detained or arrested, or no prosecution is brought, or you are acquitted, you may apply for state compensation. Compensation for each day is calculated using the national average daily wage of employees in the preceding year (nationwide in China).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress of China (2018). Criminal Procedure Law (2018 amendment, Articles 34, 35, 39, 52, 119, and 120). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/201810/t20181027_396818.shtml>; National People’s Congress of China (1997). Criminal Law (Article 243). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress of China (2012). State Compensation Law (2012 amendment, Articles 17 and 33). <https://www.stats.gov.cn/gk/tjfg/xgfxfg/202503/t20250306_1958899.html> (reposted by the National Bureau of Statistics of China)
entries.notes: Do not approach the other person privately or contact their family. Any “private settlement” might be interpreted as an admission. Chat records, call logs, and travel records are material you can use to establish your innocence; deleting them also deletes your own evidence. Misremembering something, or making a report that later proves unfounded, does not constitute the crime of false accusation. This item applies to anyone accused of a crime, regardless of gender. For three expanded discussions, see Items 33 (pursuing the person who fabricated the facts), 34 (acquittal when evidence is insufficient, and petitions and retrials), and 35 (state compensation calculated by the day after detention) of this section.

entries.title: If something happens, come forward and explain it: voluntary surrender can reduce a sentence by up to 40%, and a less serious crime can mean a larger reduction or even no punishment; “waiting out the prosecution time limit” will not work
entries.cost: Free. Go to a Chinese public security authority and turn yourself in, or stay where you are and call the police, then give a truthful account of what happened. The hard part is resisting the thought, “Wait and see; maybe no one will investigate.”
entries.summary: Voluntary surrender can reduce the sentence by up to 40%; in a less serious case, punishment may be waived entirely. If you give a truthful account only after the authorities come to you, the reduction is generally at most 20%. Running away or refusing to admit what happened brings neither benefit. Hoping to hide for a few years until the case passes the prosecution time limit does not work either: once an investigation has been formally opened, the time you spend evading it is not counted toward the prosecution time limit.
entries.benefit: Article 67 of China’s Criminal Law: A person who voluntarily turns themselves in after committing a crime and truthfully confesses their offense has surrendered. A person who surrenders may receive a lighter or reduced punishment; for a less serious crime, punishment may be waived. A person who does not turn themselves in but truthfully confesses their offense may receive a lighter punishment; if the truthful confession prevents especially serious consequences, punishment may be reduced. The sentencing guidelines of China’s Supreme People’s Court and Supreme People’s Procuratorate set out specific ranges. The baseline sentence is the sentence first calculated from the circumstances of the case; all the percentages below are reductions from that baseline. Voluntary surrender may reduce the baseline sentence by up to 40%. For a less serious crime, it may reduce it by more than 40%, or punishment may be waived according to law. Among truthful confessions without surrender, truthfully confessing one’s offense reduces the baseline sentence by up to 20%. Truthfully confessing a more serious offense of the same kind that the judicial authorities have not yet discovered reduces it by 10% to 30%. A truthful confession that prevents especially serious consequences reduces it by 30% to 50%. Pleading guilty and accepting punishment reduces it by up to 30%. Where voluntary surrender, a substantial truthful confession, return of illicit gains or restitution, compensation and the victim’s forgiveness, or other such circumstances are present together, the reduction is up to 60%; for a less serious crime, it may exceed 60%, or punishment may be waived according to law. Article 87 of the Criminal Law sets four prosecution time limits according to the maximum statutory sentence: 5, 10, 15, or 20 years. But Article 88 expressly provides an exception. Once a procuratorate, public security authority, or state security authority has opened an investigation, or a court has accepted a case, someone who evades investigation or trial is not protected by the prosecution time limit (nationwide in China; sentencing ranges effective since July 1, 2021).
entries.sources: National People’s Congress of China. Criminal Law of the People’s Republic of China (consolidated text incorporating the Eleventh Amendment to the Criminal Law), Articles 67, 87, and 88. <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808181796a636a0179822a19640c92>; Supreme People’s Court and Supreme People’s Procuratorate of China (2021). Guiding Opinions on Sentencing for Common Crimes (Trial) (Fa Fa [2021] No. 21, effective July 1, 2021), Part III, items (6), (7), and (14). Full text reposted by the Zhangye Municipal People’s Procuratorate, Gansu Province. <http://www.zhangye.jcy.gov.cn/info/1039/2086.htm>; Supreme People’s Court of China (2010). Opinions on Several Specific Issues Concerning the Handling of Voluntary Surrender and Meritorious Service (Fa Fa [2010] No. 60), Part I. Gazette of the Supreme People’s Court. <http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/f3089058d37e11cd16d801530934ae.html>
entries.notes: The beneficiary of this entry is yourself. Voluntary surrender (zishou) is only a mitigating circumstance; guilt will still be established, and how much the sentence is reduced is decided by the court. Sentencing opinions require that the scope of leniency for serious violent crimes and drug crimes be strictly controlled. Traffic accidents have a separate set of algorithms. Remaining at the scene, rescuing victims, and reporting to the public security organ count as voluntary surrender to the authorities, but since these are already statutory obligations in the first place, the scope of leniency must be strictly controlled. Surrendering to the authorities after fleeing still counts as voluntary surrender, but the heavier tier of statutory penalties must be taken as the benchmark before deciding whether to reduce the sentence and by how much. For what to do at an accident scene, see Section 8, Item 1 (In a traffic accident: first stop, rescue victims, and call the police). Retaining a lawyer first does not conflict with making a truthful confession, see Section 8, Item 5 (If accused, hire a lawyer first). What a lawyer helps you verify is whether the written interrogation record is accurate, not concocting a story for you.

entries.title: If you have drunk alcohol, do not touch the steering wheel—including electric bicycles and "just moving the car a bit"—and do not lend a vehicle to someone who has been drinking or lacks a driver's license
entries.cost: A designated driver or a taxi costs a few tens of yuan. Agree in advance before the gathering on who will not drink today. The difficulty lies in pushing back when being pressured to drink at social gatherings.
entries.summary: Driving under the influence of alcohol results in a 6-month license suspension and a fine of 1,000 to 2,000 yuan; reoffending brings administrative detention plus license revocation. Drunk driving (DUI) leads directly to license revocation, a 5-year ban on retaking the test, and criminal liability under the crime of dangerous driving. If an accident occurs after drinking, commercial auto insurance will never pay out. If you lend your car to someone knowing they have been drinking or lack a driver's license, you must also pay a share of the compensation if an accident happens.
entries.benefit: Driving after drinking alcohol results in a temporary suspension of the driver's license for 6 months and a fine of 1,000 to 2,000 yuan. For repeat offenders, administrative detention of up to 10 days and license revocation apply. Drunk driving (intoxicated driving) directly revokes the driver's license, bars retaking the driving test for 5 years, and pursues criminal liability under the crime of dangerous driving, resulting in a sentence of criminal detention and a fine; criminal detention means short-term incarceration. Penalties are even heavier for commercial vehicles: driving a commercial vehicle after drinking results in 15 days of administrative detention, a 5,000 yuan fine, and a 5-year driving ban. Drunk driving a commercial vehicle brings a 10-year driving ban, and you can never drive a commercial vehicle again for life. Causing a major accident while driving after drinking or while intoxicated, where a crime is constituted, leads to a lifetime driving ban. Commercial motor vehicle insurance strictly refuses payouts for driving after drinking or drug use. Short-distance drunk driving such as moving a car or parking into a spot within residential communities or parking lots may be exempt from criminal processing. However, the driver's license is still revoked, and fines and detention apply as driving after drinking. For riding electric bicycles, the State Council's implementation regulations also specify that one "must not ride while intoxicated"; violators face a warning or a fine of 5 to 50 yuan. Lending a vehicle to someone without a license, or whose license has been revoked or temporarily suspended, carries a fine of 200 to 2,000 yuan, and your own driver's license can also be revoked simultaneously. If an accident occurs after lending a car, the driver is liable in principle. However, if you knew or should have known that they had consumed alcohol or had no license and still gave them the car, the court will determine that you were at fault and hold you liable for part of the compensation according to your fault. In a case published by the Supreme People's Court in May 2026, a car owner knew that a tablemate had consumed alcohol and still handed the vehicle over to them to drive. The car owner was sentenced to jointly compensate alongside the driver within the scope of 40% (National)

entries.notes: Drunk driving is a criminal offense that leaves a criminal record, affecting one's political screening/vetting and eligibility for certain professional qualifications. "Drinking" (driving after drinking) and "intoxicated driving" are demarcated by blood alcohol concentration (BAC), with specific thresholds prescribed by national standards. This section did not independently verify this numeric value; do not rely on intuition to estimate which bracket you fall into. The Road Traffic Safety Law does not list a separate administrative fine for handing over a car to someone who has been drinking alcohol. Article 99 only penalizes handing over a vehicle to someone who lacks a driver's license, or whose license is revoked or suspended. In the 2023 drunk driving opinions from the two supreme judicial bodies and two ministries, there are also no specific provisions targeting the person providing the vehicle. The consequences in this area primarily fall under civil compensation.

entries.title: Do not lend your bank cards, SIM cards, or payment accounts to anyone; "running points" (money laundering transactions) is not a part-time job
entries.cost: Costs no money. When someone says, "Borrow your card to run a transaction, I'll give you a few hundred yuan," just refuse.
entries.summary: Renting, lending, or selling bank cards, SIM cards, or payment accounts to others is illegal in itself. Fines range from 1 to 10 times the illegal proceeds; if there are no illegal proceeds or they are under 20,000 yuan, the maximum fine is 200,000 yuan, and serious circumstances warrant detention of up to 15 days. If you assist in receiving or transferring money knowing that others are using it for crimes, serious circumstances constitute the crime of aiding information network criminal activities, punishable by up to 3 years of imprisonment.
entries.benefit: Renting, lending, buying, or selling telephone SIM cards, bank accounts, payment accounts, or internet accounts is illegal in itself. Illegal proceeds will be confiscated, accompanied by a fine of 1 to 10 times the illegal proceeds. Where there are no illegal proceeds or the illegal proceeds are less than 20,000 yuan, a fine of up to 200,000 yuan will be imposed. If the circumstances are serious, administrative detention of up to 15 days applies. You may also be recorded in credit records, have account functions restricted, and have non-counter business suspended (meaning you can only conduct transactions at bank counters). If you knowingly provide assistance such as payment and settlement to someone who uses the internet to commit crimes, serious circumstances constitute a crime. The charge is the crime of aiding information network criminal activities (abbreviated as bangxin zui), punishable by fixed-term imprisonment of up to 3 years and a concurrent fine (National)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2022). Anti-Telecom and Online Fraud Law (Articles 31, 44). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202209/t20220902_575631.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2015). Criminal Law Amendment (IX) (Article 29, namely Article 287-2 of the Criminal Law). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180205_364562.shtml>
entries.notes: Saying "I didn't know what they were going to use the card for" will not protect you. Investigators deduce whether you knowingly acted based on external circumstances: having received kickbacks or benefits, or handling transactions with manifestly abnormal cash flows, can both be counted as you having known. If your card is used by others to receive stolen funds, even if you are ultimately not deemed criminally liable, your accounts will be frozen and you will personally face disciplinary punishments. Helping others do facial recognition verification or reading verification codes to bypass real-name verification carries the same penalty rules as this item; see Item 45 (Helping do a facial scan).

entries.title: Check your personal credit report for free twice a year to see if there are loans or cards not opened by yourself
entries.cost: Costs no money. Querying online can be completed in ten minutes.
entries.summary: You can check your personal credit report online for free twice a year, taking just ten minutes. Check via the People's Bank of China Credit Reference Center official website or mobile banking apps; do not use third-party "credit check" apps. Negative credit records are retained for 5 years from the date the underlying event terminates, after which they must be deleted. If you have an objection, you can raise it, and they must reply to you in writing within 20 days.
entries.benefit: Administrative regulations stipulate that "personal information subjects have the right to obtain their own credit reports free of charge twice a year," allowing you to check your credit twice a year for free. The retention period for negative information is "5 years from the date the negative conduct or event terminates; if exceeding 5 years, it shall be deleted." If you have objections to the report, you may submit them. The credit reporting agency or the entity providing the information must provide you with a written reply within 20 days from the date of receiving the objection
entries.sources: State Council (2013). Regulation on the Administration of Credit Reference Industry (State Council Decree No. 631, Articles 16, 17, 25). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2013-01/29/content_2303.htm>
entries.notes: When identity cards are misused by others to take out online microloans or apply for credit cards, the individual often only discovers it when their home mortgage loan application gets rejected, by which point it has already dragged on for years. The access portal for checking is the official website of the Credit Reference Center of the People's Bank of China, or mobile banking apps. Do not use third-party "credit check" apps; those types of apps are themselves collecting your information. You should check especially after helping an acquaintance "do a facial scan or serve as a witness"; see Item 45 (Helping do a facial scan). For cases where defaults have already occurred and someone charges money claiming they can "whitewash your credit report," see Section 7, Item 23 (Credit cards and online loans already impossible to repay). Debit cards and phone SIM cards registered in your name cannot be seen in your credit report and must be queried separately; see Section 14, Item 11 (How many phone cards in your name).

entries.title: When a conflict arises, call the police first and do not use physical force; the party striking first easily makes the other party's counterattack count as justifiable self-defense
entries.cost: Costs no money. Retreat to a crowded area to call the police, ensuring the other party's actions are captured on surveillance cameras. The difficulty lies in holding back from talking back or pushing and shoving.
entries.summary: Hitting someone leads to 5 to 10 days of administrative detention and a fine of 500 to 1,000 yuan. Gang attacks, assaulting elderly people, pregnant women, children, or disabled persons, or beating others repeatedly brings 10 to 15 days of detention and a fine of 1,000 to 2,000 yuan. Inflicting minor injuries constitutes a criminal case, punishable by up to 3 years of imprisonment; serious injuries bring 3 to 10 years. Two people fighting each other does not count as justifiable self-defense, so step back first and call the police.
entries.benefit: Assaulting another person or intentionally injuring them warrants detention of 5 to 10 days and a concurrent fine of 500 to 1,000 yuan. Assaulting in a group, assaulting the elderly, pregnant women, children, or persons with disabilities, or assaulting others multiple times or assaulting multiple persons at once carries heavier penalties: detention of 10 to 15 days and a concurrent fine of 1,000 to 2,000 yuan. Engaging in gang brawls is handled as picking quarrels and provoking trouble (xunxin zishi), carrying up to 15 days of detention and a 2,000 yuan fine; picking quarrels and provoking trouble refers to making unprovoked trouble and inciting disturbances. Intentionally injuring another person's body to the point of constituting a crime is punishable by up to 3 years of imprisonment; causing serious injury to someone is punishable by 3 to 10 years. Two persons fighting each other is legally termed mutual brawling and does not qualify as justifiable self-defense. However, if the other party strikes first and uses clearly excessive means, or if you have made diligent efforts to evade and the other party continues to attack, your counterattack will generally be recognized as defense. Only when retaliation goes too far does it constitute excessive defense, which must simultaneously meet two criteria: clearly exceeding the necessary limits, and causing major damage. Even if it truly exceeds the limits, punishment shall still be mitigated or exempted (National, Public Security Administration Punishments Law effective from January 1, 2026)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2025). Public Security Administration Punishments Law (2025 Revision, Articles 30, 51). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml>; National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Articles 20, 234). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml>; Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security (2020). Guiding Opinions on Lawfully Applying the System of Justifiable Self-Defense (Fa Fa [2020] No. 31, Articles 6, 9, 11, 14). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/251611.html>
entries.notes: After the 2025 revision of the Public Security Administration Punishments Law, all article numbers changed. Assaulting another person changed from Article 43 of the old law to Article 51; materials referencing the old article numbers are already outdated. How "minor injuries" are assessed in "inflicting minor injuries leads to criminal sentencing" is determined by forensic appraisal standards, which this section did not verify. If the other party has already fallen to the ground, or has already fled, the unlawful infringement is deemed to have ceased; if you then chase after them and strike, it will not count as defense. Carrying knives, collapsible batons, or stun guns on your person for self-defense will result in penalties if inspected; see Section 9, Item 26 (Don't buy collapsible batons or stun guns for self-defense).

entries.title: You can strike back against unavoidable unlawful infringement, but only hit the person who is actively acting, and stop as soon as they stop
entries.cost: Attorney fees start from several thousand yuan; those facing financial hardship can apply for legal aid. The cost lies mainly in the aftermath: a case is often initially opened as intentional injury, requiring cooperation with investigations or even being detained for over ten days first. The hard part is staying calm and not panicking during this period.
entries.summary: When someone is actively committing an unlawful infringement against you or others, taking action to stop them and injuring them carries no criminal liability as long as it is not clearly excessive. If the other party is committing ongoing physical violence, murder, robbery, rape, kidnapping, injuring or killing them does not count as excessive defense. But you can only hit the person actively acting, and stop when they stop. Even if the final determination sides with you, a case may still be opened against you and you may be detained for several days first.
entries.benefit: The Criminal Law defines what counts as justifiable self-defense. When the interests of the state, the public interest, or the personal, property, or other rights of oneself or others are suffering an ongoing unlawful infringement, taking action to stop it and injuring the ongoing infringer constitutes justifiable self-defense, incurring no criminal responsibility. The same article also states: "Where justifiable self-defense clearly exceeds the necessary limits and causes major damage, criminal liability shall be borne, but punishment shall be mitigated or exempted." There is an additional paragraph: "Where defensive action is taken against ongoing physical violence, murder, robbery, rape, kidnapping, or other violent crimes that seriously endanger personal safety, resulting in the injury or death of the unlawful infringer, it does not constitute excessive defense and incurs no criminal liability." The guiding opinions from the two supreme judicial bodies and one ministry elaborate on these boundaries in more detail. To establish excessive defense, both "clearly exceeding necessary limits" and "causing major damage" must be simultaneously satisfied; neither can be missing. "Causing major damage" refers to causing serious injury or death to the unlawful infringer; causing minor injuries or lighter wounds does not count. The infringement is only considered over when the unlawful infringer has truly lost the capacity to inflict harm or has genuinely abandoned the infringement. Defense must be directed at the unlawful infringer themselves. If the other party's infringement is manifestly minor and you can see that, yet you directly stop it using methods sufficient to cause serious injury or death, it will not be recognized as an act of defense. Official cases illustrate procedural costs. Guiding Case of the Supreme People's Procuratorate No. 47 (Yu Haiming case): On the night of August 27, 2018, public security organs opened an investigation as an "intentional injury case." On September 1, the Kunshan Public Security Bureau determined it was justifiable self-defense pursuant to Article 20, Paragraph 3 of the Criminal Law and dismissed the case. Guiding Case No. 45 (Chen case): A student surrounded and beaten by 9 people fought back with a knife, causing serious injury to 3 people. Public security opened an investigation on suspicion of intentional injury and placed him in criminal detention. The procuratorial organ determined it was justifiable self-defense and did not approve the arrest, whereupon the public security released him. If public security deems an arrest necessary after detention, it shall submit it to the procuratorate for examination and approval within 3 days (reporting to the procuratorate for approval of arrest). Under special circumstances, this may be extended by 1 to 4 days. For major suspects who wander around committing crimes, commit crimes repeatedly, or commit crimes in gangs, it may be extended to 30 days. The procuratorate then makes a decision within 7 days (National)
entries.sources: National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Article 20). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml>; Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security (2020). Guiding Opinions on Lawfully Applying the System of Justifiable Self-Defense (Fa Fa [2020] No. 31, Articles 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 13, 14, 19). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/251611.html>; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2018). Twelfth Batch of Guiding Cases (Guiding Case No. 45 Chen's Justifiable Self-Defense Case, Guiding Case No. 47 Yu Haiming's Justifiable Self-Defense Case). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/jczdal/201812/t20181219_402920.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). Criminal Procedure Law (2018 Amendment, Article 91). Full text reposted by Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region People's Procuratorate <https://www.nx.jcy.gov.cn/zwsy/qwfb/202011/t20201119_608817.html>
entries.notes: The default action remains stepping back and calling the police as stated in Item 10 (When a conflict arises, call the police first and do not use physical force). Two people fighting each other does not count as defense, nor does continuing to pursue and hit the other party after they have fallen to the ground or fled. Only consider fighting back at the exact moment there is no retreat left; this is not encouraging counterattacks. After the incident, there are three things to do: First, do not leave the scene after calling the police. Second, act quickly to preserve surveillance video and witnesses; the guiding opinions require public security to retrieve on-site video and audio recordings and question witnesses at the earliest opportunity. Third, hire a lawyer before being formally interrogated by the police, see Item 5 (If accused, hire a lawyer first). If the case is ultimately dismissed, not prosecuted, or ends in acquittal, you can apply for state compensation on a per-diem basis for the days you were detained; see Item 35 (State compensation after detention). Striking out in defense of others is likewise permitted by law. However, stepping empty-handed into a fight between strangers carries risks that must be weighed separately; see Section 13, Item 37 (Coming across a group brawl). The beneficiaries of this entry are primarily oneself and family members.

entries.title: If you hold a grudge against someone—unpaid wages, wrongful termination, or being scammed out of money—pursue complaints, arbitration, and lawsuits; do not seek them out to settle scores
entries.cost: Costs no money; neither complaints nor arbitration charge fees. Requires making one or two trips and waiting several months. The difficulty lies in holding back from using physical violence during these months.
entries.summary: Taking the statutory route, the worst outcome is not getting the money back. Seeking retaliation, you still won't get the money back, and killing someone carries up to the death penalty. Xu Jiajin, failing to receive his graduation diploma and dissatisfied with his internship remuneration, used a knife causing 8 deaths and 17 injuries, and has already been executed. Pursuing unpaid wages via complaints and arbitration recovered 8.65 billion yuan for 654,000 people nationwide in 2024.
entries.benefit: The statutory route has official numbers. In 2024, labor inspection nationwide investigated and handled 137,000 cases, recovering 8.65 billion yuan in wages for 654,000 people. Furthermore, 998 people were criminally sentenced for the crime of refusing to pay labor remuneration. For how to file a complaint with labor inspection and how to apply for labor arbitration regarding unpaid wages, see Section 7, Item 2. The price tag for the retaliation path is written in Article 232 of the Criminal Law: "Whoever intentionally commits homicide shall be sentenced to death, life imprisonment, or fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 10 years; if the circumstances are relatively minor, they shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 3 years but not more than 10 years." Official case: Xu Jiajin failed his exams, did not receive his graduation certificate, and was dissatisfied with his internship compensation. On November 16, 2024, he returned to Wuxi Vocational Institute of Arts and Technology carrying a knife and committed violent attacks, causing 8 deaths and 17 injuries. In the first instance, he was sentenced to death and deprived of political rights for life for the crime of intentional homicide, which was approved and executed by the Supreme People's Court on January 20, 2025. What he was dissatisfied with were the school and that payment, but the victims were fellow students, and he still did not get a single cent of that compensation (National)
entries.sources: National People's Congress of China (1997). Criminal Law (Article 232). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml>; Xinhua News Agency (2024). Knife attack at a campus in Yixing, Jiangsu, leaves 8 dead and 17 injured. <http://www.news.cn/20241117/65a18fddb453469ebe91c78eda669893/c.html> (reproduces the Yixing police statement, including the casualty figures and the original wording about the motive); Supreme People's Procuratorate of China (2025). Xu Jiajin, convicted in the Wuxi campus knife attack, executed. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/zdgz/202501/t20250120_680197.shtml>; Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security of China (2025). 2024 Statistical Bulletin on the Development of Human Resources and Social Security. <https://www.mohrss.gov.cn/SYrlzyhshbzb/zwgk/szrs/tjgb/202506/W020250616518526345602.pdf>; Supreme People's Court of China (2025). Work Report of the Supreme People's Court ("Fan Weiqiu, who drove into pedestrians, Xu Jiajin, who carried out a campus knife attack, and others were sentenced to death"). <https://www.gov.cn/yaowen/liebiao/202503/content_7013680.htm>
entries.notes: Interns who are still in school generally are not considered to have established an employment relationship with the organization. If you cannot collect your internship pay, you can only ask your school to help resolve it or sue in court; labor arbitration is not available. If you are owed money for private work done for a household or an individual, you likewise need to go to court; see Section 7, Item 22 (first identify who hired you). For how to file a complaint or seek arbitration over unpaid wages, see Section 7, Item 2. For the limits on debt collection, see Section 9, Item 15 (do not detain or confine someone to collect a debt). If you take the legal route, the worst outcome is that you do not recover the money: closing a case does not mean the money has reached your account. If you take revenge, you still will not recover the money, and killing someone can carry a death sentence.

entries.title: However angry you are, do not attack people who have nothing to do with it: driving into a crowd or attacking people in a public place is prosecuted as endangering public safety by dangerous means, with a minimum sentence of three years; if someone dies, the sentence starts at ten years and can be as severe as death
entries.cost: It costs nothing. The hard part is suppressing the thought while you are angry.
entries.summary: Driving into a crowd or attacking people in a public place is prosecuted as endangering public safety by dangerous means. Even if no one is injured, the sentence starts at three years. If someone dies, the sentence is at least ten years, life imprisonment, or death. Unhappy with the division of property in his divorce, Fan Weiqiu drove into a crowd exercising at the Zhuhai Sports Center, killing 35 people and injuring 43. He has been executed.
entries.benefit: Article 114 of China's Criminal Law states: "Anyone who endangers public safety by setting a fire, breaching a dike, causing an explosion, releasing poisonous or radioactive substances, infectious disease pathogens, or other dangerous substances, or by other dangerous means, without yet causing serious consequences, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of three to ten years." Even if no one is injured, the sentence starts at three years. Under Article 115, causing serious injury or death, or major losses to public or private property, carries a sentence of at least ten years' imprisonment, life imprisonment, or death. An official case: after his marriage broke down and his life went badly, Fan Weiqiu was also unhappy with the outcome of his divorce property division and "resolved to vent his personal resentment by driving into a crowd." On the evening of November 11, 2024, he drove into people exercising at the Zhuhai Sports Center. The attack killed 35 people and injured 43. At first instance, he was sentenced to death for endangering public safety by dangerous means and deprived of political rights for life. The sentence was carried out on January 20, 2025, after approval by the Supreme People's Court of China. What angered him was the result of his divorce property division; the people he hit were runners he did not know (China nationwide).
entries.sources: National People's Congress of China (1997). Criminal Law (Articles 114 and 115). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml>; Xinhua News Agency (2024). Vehicle attack in Zhuhai, Guangdong, kills 35 and injures 43. <http://www.news.cn/20241112/29c6af4f6ee4455b92832f3c2b13a93a/c.html> (reproduces a statement from the Zhuhai Municipal Public Security Bureau); Supreme People's Procuratorate of China (2024). First-instance verdict in Fan Weiqiu's case of endangering public safety by dangerous means: death sentence and deprivation of political rights for life. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/zdgz/202412/t20241227_677757.shtml>; Supreme People's Procuratorate of China (2025). Fan Weiqiu, convicted in the Zhuhai vehicle attack, executed. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/zdgz/202501/t20250120_680196.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress of China (2025). Public Security Administration Punishments Law (2025 revision, Articles 29 and 50). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml>
entries.notes: "I don't want to live anyway" does not earn a reduction in sentence. The Supreme People's Court of China's 2025 work report states its approach to such cases: "Those whose heinous crimes challenge the bottom lines of law and morality must be punished firmly, severely, and swiftly in accordance with the law." Even making threats is already illegal. Threatening to set a fire, cause an explosion, or poison people, thereby disrupting public order, carries 5 to 10 days' detention and may also carry a fine of up to 1,000 yuan. Writing a threatening letter or using another method to threaten someone's personal safety is also illegal. That carries up to 5 days' detention or a fine of up to 1,000 yuan. These provisions are under China's Public Security Administration Punishments Law, effective January 1, 2026. If your thoughts have reached this point, see Item 14 (treat thoughts such as "take someone down with me" as an emergency).

entries.title: Treat thoughts such as "take someone down with me" or "we'll die together" as an emergency: leave the scene, hand your car keys and knife to someone else, and call China's 12356 hotline
entries.cost: It costs nothing. The hard parts are admitting that something is wrong with you right now and putting the objects in someone else's hands.
entries.summary: The window between having thoughts like these and acting on them can be very short. Of 82 people who had attempted suicide, 47.6% said no more than 10 minutes passed between their first thought and acting on it. So the task is not to "think it through" but first to put some distance between yourself and the steering wheel, knife, gas valve, and rope, and get through those ten minutes. Then call China's 12356 hotline.
entries.benefit: The window between thoughts like these and action is very short. Researchers interviewed 82 people who had attempted suicide within three days of their admission to hospital. Of these, 47.6% said no more than 10 minutes passed from the first thought to the attempt. A 10-year systematic review (which brought together and examined studies from a ten-year period) found that the evidence for restricting access to lethal means was continuing to strengthen. After controls on analgesics, suicides associated with them fell by 43%. After barriers were installed at jumping hotspots, suicides fell by 86% (79% to 91%). Putting some distance between yourself and the steering wheel, knife, gas valve, and rope is about getting through those ten minutes. 12356 is China's unified national mental health support hotline, answered for at least 18 hours a day (China nationwide, from May 1, 2025).
entries.sources: Deisenhammer EA et al. (2009). The duration of the suicidal process: how much time is left for intervention between consideration and accomplishment of a suicide attempt? Journal of Clinical Psychiatry. <https://doi.org/10.4088/JCP.07m03904>; Zalsman G et al. (2016). Suicide prevention strategies revisited: 10-year systematic review. Lancet Psychiatry. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S2215-0366(16)30030-X>; National Health Commission of China (2024). Notice on the Use of "12356" as the Nationwide Unified Mental Health Support Hotline Number (National Health Commission Medical Administration Letter [2024] No. 259). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202412/content_6994470.htm>
entries.notes: The reason for the B rating is that both pieces of evidence come from research on suicide; there is no direct research applying them to "urges to hurt others." The Deisenhammer study also involved only 82 people at one hospital. When you are not in a fit state, do not drive or work a shift in which you are responsible for other people's safety; hand over your duties first. If you want to hurt yourself, see Section 1, Item 25 (call China's 12356 hotline when you have suicidal thoughts). For what to do first when you feel low, see Section 3, Item 18.

entries.title: If someone close to you says "No one gets to have a good life" or "I'll take the children with me," do not dismiss it as something said in anger: close relatives can take them directly for an assessment, and Chinese police must respond when an incident is reported
entries.cost: Registration and examination fees range from tens to hundreds of yuan. Accompanying them to the hospital takes half a day to a full day. The hard part is persuading them to go with you.
entries.summary: If a family member says "No one gets to have a good life" or "I'll take the children with me," a close relative can take them to a hospital, which may not refuse to assess them. If they are diagnosed with a severe mental disorder and have already acted violently or pose an imminent danger, hospitalization does not require their consent. If you cannot tell whether they are just speaking in anger, call China's 12356 hotline for advice first, or call China's police emergency number, 110, to have officers come to the scene. Keeping it secret for them is not helping them.
entries.benefit: The second paragraph of Article 28 of China's Mental Health Law states: "Where a person suspected of having a mental disorder has engaged in conduct that harms themselves or endangers the safety of others, or is at risk of harming themselves or endangering the safety of others, their close relatives, their employer, and the local public security authority shall immediately take measures to stop them and send them to a medical institution for a mental disorder diagnosis." The same article also provides: "A medical institution may not refuse to diagnose a person suspected of having a mental disorder who has been sent to it for diagnosis." Article 29 requires the hospital to keep such a person at the hospital, promptly assign a licensed psychiatrist to make a diagnosis, and issue a conclusion in a timely manner. Article 30 provides that hospitalization is voluntary in principle. There is an exception: the diagnosis concludes that the person has a severe mental disorder and "has already engaged in conduct endangering the safety of others, or poses a risk of endangering the safety of others." Such a person shall receive inpatient treatment without their consent as a prerequisite. A threat to hurt someone can itself be reported directly to China's police emergency number, 110. Writing a threatening letter or using another method to threaten someone's personal safety carries up to 5 days' detention or a fine of up to 1,000 yuan. Threatening to set a fire, cause an explosion, or release dangerous substances, thereby disrupting public order, carries 5 to 10 days' detention and may also carry a fine of up to 1,000 yuan (China nationwide, under the Public Security Administration Punishments Law effective January 1, 2026).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress of China (2025). Public Security Administration Punishments Law (2025 revision, Articles 29 and 50). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress of China (2012, amended in 2018). Mental Health Law (Articles 28, 29, 30, and 35). <https://www.gov.cn/guoqing/2021-10/29/content_5647635.htm>; French Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety (BEA) (2016). Final Report BEA2015-0125.en: Accident on 24 March 2015 at Prads-Haute-Bléone to the Airbus A320-211 registered D-AIPX operated by Germanwings. <https://bea.aero/uploads/tx_elydbrapports/BEA2015-0125.en-LR.pdf>
entries.notes: For the purposes of counting beneficiaries, this item counts spouses, parents, and children who live with the person. "No one gets to have a good life" usually includes you, and the law gives the right to take someone for an assessment specifically to close relatives. Outsiders cannot take that step; they can only call the police. Taking someone for an assessment is only for genuine signs of danger. Words said in anger during an argument do not count, and you cannot use this process to confine a family member in a hospital because they will not do as you say. The same law also states that if a further diagnosis or an assessment finds that the person does not have a severe mental disorder, the hospital may not keep them as an inpatient (Article 35). If you cannot tell, call China's 12356 hotline for advice first, or call China's police emergency number, 110, to have officers come to the scene. If you are unsure whether they want to die by suicide, you can ask directly. Asking will not make them want to do it more; see Section 1, Item 43 (ask someone close to you who seems emotionally unwell directly). The investigation of Germanwings Flight 9525 concluded that the authorities and the employer could not take any action to stop the copilot from flying that day because "neither he nor anyone else—doctors, colleagues, or family members—had informed them." All 150 people aboard died: 2 pilots, 4 cabin crew members, and 144 passengers.

entries.title: Do not insult people online, make up rumors, or share unverified claims; if you are targeted by online abuse, preserve evidence before reporting it to the police
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Think for another ten seconds before posting. If you are attacked, take screenshots and screen recordings, save links and account IDs, complain to the platform first, then report it to the police. The hard part is resisting the urge to insult them back.
entries.summary: Publicly insulting someone or fabricating defamatory claims carries up to 5 days' detention or a fine of up to 1,000 yuan; more serious cases carry 5 to 10 days' detention. If the circumstances are serious, it constitutes the crime of insult or defamation, punishable by up to 3 years' imprisonment. Conversely, if you are targeted by online abuse, cases of insult and defamation generally require you to bring the case to court yourself, so you need to take screenshots, make screen recordings, and save links yourself.
entries.benefit: Publicly insulting someone, or fabricating facts to defame them, carries up to 5 days' detention or a fine of up to 1,000 yuan. More serious cases carry 5 to 10 days' detention. Repeatedly sending insulting or threatening messages, harassing, pestering, or stalking someone, or secretly photographing and spreading another person's private information, is subject to the same penalties. Deliberately spreading rumors and thereby disrupting public order carries 5 to 10 days' detention. In serious circumstances, conduct constitutes the crime of insult or defamation, punishable by up to 3 years' imprisonment. If you are defamed online and have difficulty obtaining evidence, you can ask the court to request assistance from the police (China nationwide, under the Public Security Administration Punishments Law effective January 1, 2026).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress of China (2025). Public Security Administration Punishments Law (2025 revision, Articles 29 and 50). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml>; National People's Congress of China (1997). Criminal Law (Article 246). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress of China (2015). Criminal Law Amendment (IX) (Article 16, adding the third paragraph to Article 246 of the Criminal Law). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180205_364562.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress of China (2015). Criminal Law Amendment (IX) (new third paragraph of Article 246). Full text republished by China's National Public Complaints and Proposals Administration <https://www.gjxfj.gov.cn/gjxfj/fgwj/flfg/webinfo/2017/03/1601761496614423.htm>; Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate of China (2013). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Defamation and Other Offenses Committed Using Information Networks (Judicial Interpretation [2013] No. 21, Article 1). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/zdgz/201309/t20130910_62417.shtml>
entries.notes: The crimes of insult and defamation are, in principle, "handled only upon complaint," meaning you have to bring the case to court yourself. The police generally do not open a case on their own, and you have to gather the evidence yourself. There are two exceptions. First, cases that "seriously harm social order and national interests" can be handled directly by the police (second paragraph of Article 246 of the Criminal Law). Second, if you are defamed online and genuinely have difficulty obtaining evidence yourself, the court can ask the police to assist with the investigation (third paragraph of the same article, added by Criminal Law Amendment IX). You can still be held responsible for reposting. The 2013 interpretation on online defamation by China's Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate states that knowingly posting online something fabricated that damages another person's reputation, where the circumstances are egregious, is treated as "fabricating facts to defame another person." For what to do after being targeted by online abuse, see Item 37 of this section (preserve evidence first, then choose a course of action). The article number for insult and defamation changed from Article 42 of the old law to Article 50 of the new law.

entries.title: Read the whole document before signing; do not sign for someone else or sign blank paper
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Spend a few more minutes reading any contract, IOU, guarantee, or employment document from start to finish. Ask about anything you do not understand on the spot, then photograph it for your records. The hard part is taking your time to read it all in front of the other person.
entries.summary: Once you sign, it counts; a fingerprint has the same effect as a signature. "I didn't read it carefully" or "I thought it was something else" is hard to establish in court. So spend a few more minutes reading from start to finish, ask about anything you do not understand on the spot, and photograph it for your records. Do not sign for anyone else or sign blank paper, and clearly state the intended use on any photocopy of your identity card.
entries.benefit: A contract lawfully formed is protected by law and binds both parties who sign it. Once you sign, you must fully perform your obligations as agreed. Article 490 of China's Civil Code states that when a contract is made in writing, it is formed when both parties "sign it, affix their seals, or put their fingerprints on it." Fingerprints, signatures, and seals are three equally valid methods; a contract is formed when fingerprints are used, too. "I didn't read it carefully" or "I thought it was something else" is hard to establish in court. If you do not sign, you will not take on debts and responsibilities that are not yours (China nationwide).
entries.sources: National People's Congress of China (2020). Civil Code (Articles 465, 490, and 509). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>
entries.notes: "Do not sign for someone else, do not sign blank paper, and state the intended use on photocopies of your identity card" are practical rules of thumb; there is no separate official document for them. They serve the same purpose: preventing your signature from being incorporated into a legally valid contract that you then have no choice but to acknowledge. Courts generally also treat an electronic signature or facial recognition confirmation as something you signed yourself. If an acquaintance asks you to help obtain a loan by scanning your face or signing, see Item 45 (helping someone with a quick face scan).

entries.title: Write a complete IOU when lending money; before guaranteeing someone else's debt, decide whether you are willing to repay it for them
entries.cost: It costs nothing. On one sheet of paper, clearly state the lender, borrower, amount, interest rate, term, and repayment method, and have both parties sign it. Transfer the money electronically to leave a record; do not hand over cash.
entries.summary: An IOU should contain everything: lender, borrower, amount, interest rate, term, repayment method, and both parties' signatures. Transfer the money electronically; do not hand over cash. A complete record makes it easier to sue. When guaranteeing someone else's debt, check whether the document says "joint and several." With an ordinary guarantee, the creditor must first try to recover the money from the borrower through enforcement before turning to you; with a joint and several guarantee, the creditor can demand payment directly from you.
entries.benefit: A loan contract should be in writing and generally include the type of loan, currency, purpose, amount, interest rate, term, and repayment method. A complete record makes it easier to sue. If the guarantee contract does not specify the type of guarantee, or specifies it unclearly, it is treated as an ordinary guarantee. As an ordinary guarantor, you can wait. The creditor must first sue or seek arbitration, then apply for compulsory enforcement against the borrower's property. Only if the debt remains unpaid after enforcement do you have to repay it for the borrower. Conversely, signing a "joint and several liability guarantee" removes that protection: the creditor can demand payment directly from you (China nationwide).
entries.sources: National People's Congress of China (2020). Civil Code (Articles 668, 681, 686, and 687). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>
entries.notes: For money you lend, courts will not protect the portion of interest exceeding four times the LPR; see Section 7. Writing the borrower’s ID number on the IOU and labeling the money a “loan” are practical rules of thumb. Whether the guarantee document contains the words “joint and several” determines whether creditors must seek payment from the borrower first or can demand payment from you alongside the borrower. Read it carefully before signing. If you were told you would be a guarantor but the document you actually signed was a loan agreement, see Item 45 (you are the borrower, not the guarantor).

entries.title: There are deadlines for enforcing your rights: 3 years for civil claims and 1 year for labor arbitration. Once the deadline passes, the other side need only say, “The limitation period has expired”
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Don’t just remind yourself to ask for repayment: use WeChat, text messages, email, or registered mail to leave a record of your demand.
entries.summary: The limitation period for civil claims is 3 years, starting when you know your rights have been infringed. After it expires, the court will not raise the issue on its own, but the other side need only say in court, “The limitation period has expired.” The debt still exists; you just cannot recover it through the claim. Before the 3 years are up, a demand for repayment that leaves a record can restart the 3-year period. Labor disputes follow a separate rule: the limitation period for arbitration is 1 year.
entries.benefit: China’s Civil Code provides that “the limitation period for requesting a people’s court to protect civil rights is three years.” The period begins “from the date on which the rights holder knows or ought to know that their rights have been infringed and who the obligor is”: the day you know you have suffered a loss and know whom to pursue. The maximum is 20 years from the date the right was infringed. Once the period expires, “the obligor may raise a defense of nonperformance.” The court will not check the limitation period on its own, but the other side can invoke it in court. The debt still exists; you just cannot recover it through the claim. Four events interrupt the limitation period, causing the 3 years to start again. First, you demand performance from the person who owes you. Second, the other side agrees to perform. Third, you file a lawsuit or apply for arbitration. Fourth, another circumstance has the same effect as one of these. The interruption must occur before the 3 years expire; making a demand afterward does not restart the period. If repayment is agreed in installments, the period begins when the final installment falls due. Four categories of claims are not subject to a limitation period. First, demands to stop an infringement, remove an obstruction, or eliminate a danger. Second, demands for the return of your own real property or registered movable property. Third, child support, support for elderly parents, and maintenance. Fourth, other circumstances provided by law. Labor disputes follow a separate rule: the limitation period for arbitration is 1 year from the date you know or ought to know that your rights have been infringed. But “where a dispute over unpaid labor remuneration arises during the existence of an employment relationship, an employee’s application for arbitration is not subject to the arbitration limitation period provided in the first paragraph of this article; however, where the employment relationship has ended, the application shall be made within one year from the date it ended” (nationwide in China).
entries.sources: National People’s Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 188, 189, 192, 193, 195, 196, and 197). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (2007). Labor Dispute Mediation and Arbitration Law (Article 27). <https://rsj.ankang.gov.cn/Content-2150407.html> (reposted by the Ankang Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau)
entries.notes: This may be the cheapest thing you can do in the entire book. Before the 3 years expire, a recorded demand for repayment can restart the 3-year period. Doing nothing could needlessly cost you the ability to win a lawsuit. Agreeing in advance that “I won’t invoke the limitation period” has no effect; neither does an agreement between the parties to lengthen or shorten the 3 years. Conversely, if the other side still agrees to repay after the deadline, they cannot then invoke the limitation period to refuse payment. If they have already repaid voluntarily, they cannot demand the money back. For IOUs and guarantees, see Item 18 (IOUs and guarantees). For the enforcement stage, see Item 20 (if you are sued and subject to enforcement, report your assets truthfully). Overtime pay and pay for unused annual leave follow the labor arbitration rules; see Section 19, Items 1 and 2. Localities calculate the limitation period for double wages owed when no contract was signed differently; see Section 19, Item 20 (double wages).

entries.title: If you are sued and subject to enforcement, report your assets truthfully and repay what you can. Do not transfer your home or money to relatives, friends, or a company
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Report your assets as the court requires: what you have now and what you had during the year before you received the enforcement notice. Repay what you can first. If you cannot repay in full, discuss a settlement and installment payments with the enforcement applicant, the party seeking repayment.
entries.summary: Giving a home away or making a sham transfer to a company, or transferring money to relatives or friends, so that a judgment cannot be enforced constitutes the crime of refusing to enforce a judgment or ruling. The penalty is up to 3 years’ imprisonment, or 3 to 7 years in especially serious circumstances. Relatives or friends who knowingly help hide money or transfer title are treated as accomplices, and the assets can still be recovered. If you refuse to report your assets or make a false report, you can be fined up to 100,000 yuan as an individual and detained for up to 15 days.
entries.benefit: Transferring assets can itself constitute the offense. The Standing Committee of China’s National People’s Congress has issued an interpretation of Article 313 of the Criminal Law. It expressly lists “where the person subject to enforcement hides, transfers, or intentionally damages property, or transfers property without compensation or at a clearly unreasonable low price, making a judgment or ruling impossible to enforce” as “having the ability to comply with enforcement but refusing to do so, in serious circumstances.” Hiding or transferring money, deliberately destroying your own belongings, giving them away, or selling them cheaply so that the judgment cannot be enforced all count. A 2024 interpretation by the two highest judicial authorities (the Supreme People’s Court and the Supreme People’s Procuratorate) added ten further circumstances. These include disposing of your property interests through a sham settlement or sham transfer. They also include buying someone else’s property at a clearly unreasonable high price or guaranteeing someone else’s debt. Each deliberately drains assets that could be used to repay your debt. The penalty for refusing to enforce a judgment or ruling is up to 3 years’ imprisonment. In especially serious circumstances, it is 3 to 7 years’ imprisonment plus a fine. Especially serious circumstances include using sham litigation, arbitration, or notarization to obstruct enforcement; gathering a crowd to storm an enforcement site; surrounding, detaining, or assaulting enforcement personnel; or causing the enforcement applicant to die by suicide or harm themselves because of the refusal to comply. An outsider who is not a party to the case but knows the circumstances and colludes with the person subject to enforcement to help hide money or transfer title is treated as an accomplice to the offense. Property disposed of unlawfully must be recovered according to law, or restitution ordered. A transfer made after the defendant receives notice to respond to the lawsuit but before the judgment takes effect also counts. In civil proceedings, a creditor can ask the court to revoke a transfer made as a gift or at a clearly unreasonable low price. If you refuse to report your assets or report them falsely, the court can impose a fine of up to 100,000 yuan on an individual. It can also impose detention for up to 15 days (nationwide in China; the interpretation by the two highest judicial authorities took effect in December 2024).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (2002). Interpretation of Article 313 of the Criminal Law of the People’s Republic of China. <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2002/content_61738.htm>; Supreme People’s Court and Supreme People’s Procuratorate (2024). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Refusal to Enforce Judgments or Rulings (Judicial Interpretation [2024] No. 13, Articles 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 11, and 12). Published on the Supreme People’s Court’s website; full text checked against a repost by Guangdong Province’s Guangzhou Prison. <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/447931.html>, <http://gzjy.gd.gov.cn/zxxx/content/post_4608108.html>; Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (2015). Criminal Law Amendment (IX) (Article 39, amending Article 313 of the Criminal Law). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180205_364562.shtml>; National People’s Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 538, 539, and 540). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (amended 2023). Civil Procedure Law (Articles 114, 118, and 252). Reposted by the Guizhou Provincial Market Regulation Bureau: <https://amr.guizhou.gov.cn/zwgk/xxgkml/jcxxgk/zcfg/fl/202401/t20240129_83645867.html>
entries.notes: The online suggestion to “put your home in a company’s name as employee housing and transfer all your money to relatives” is no loophole: gifts and sham transfers are exactly what the judicial interpretation names. Relatives, friends, and companies that help you do this are treated as accomplices, and recoverable assets can still be recovered. Conversely, genuinely having no money does not constitute this offense. To decide whether you have the money but refuse to repay, necessary living expenses for you and the family members you support must first be deducted. If you repay part or all of the money before the procuratorate brings charges, and the circumstances are minor, it may decide not to prosecute. Repayment before the first-instance judgment can result in a lighter penalty or even an exemption from punishment. For what to do after being placed on a list or having your spending restricted, see Item 21 (spending restrictions or inclusion on the list of untrustworthy judgment debtors). For how to recover after fulfilling your obligations, see Section 7, Item 19 (how to start over after being on the untrustworthy judgment debtors list).

entries.title: If your spending is restricted or you are put on the untrustworthy judgment debtors list, find out which provision was used and apply to correct an erroneous inclusion
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Ask the court handling enforcement which ground was used to include you. Prepare proof that you have repaid or complied with the judgment (proof of performance), or prepare guarantee documents. For spending necessary for daily life or business, you must apply separately each time. The hard part is making repeated trips and applications yourself.
entries.summary: First find out whether you are subject to spending restrictions or have been put on the untrustworthy judgment debtors list; these are two separate measures. There are only six grounds for inclusion on the list. The listing period is 2 years, and those who have fully performed their obligations must be removed within 3 working days. Spending restrictions prohibit nine categories of spending, including any seat on a G-prefixed high-speed train. You can apply separately for spending necessary for daily life or business.
entries.benefit: There are only six grounds for inclusion on the untrustworthy judgment debtors list. First, having the ability to perform an obligation but refusing to do so. Second, obstructing or resisting enforcement through forged evidence, violence, or threats. Third, evading enforcement through sham litigation, sham arbitration, or hiding or transferring assets. Fourth, violating the asset reporting system. Fifth, violating a spending restriction order. Sixth, refusing without good reason to perform an enforcement settlement agreement. A person must not be included under the first ground (having the ability to perform but refusing) if they have provided a sufficient and effective guarantee, or if the property seized, detained, or frozen is enough to repay the debt. A minor who is subject to enforcement must not be included. The listing period is 2 years. It can be extended by 1 to 3 years if the person obstructs or resists enforcement through violence or threats in serious circumstances, or commits multiple acts of dishonesty. The court must remove a person within 3 working days in seven circumstances, including when the obligation has been fully performed, a settlement agreement has been fully performed, or the court has ruled to terminate enforcement. A person who actively fulfills their obligations or voluntarily corrects the dishonest conduct can also be removed early. An individual subject to spending restrictions cannot make purchases in nine high-spending categories or make purchases unnecessary for daily life and work. First, taking a plane, a soft-sleeper train berth, or a second-class or higher cabin on a ship. Second, high spending at star-rated or higher inns and hotels, nightclubs, or golf courses. Third, buying real property or building, extending, or luxuriously renovating a home. Fourth, renting a luxury office building, hotel, or apartment for office use. Fifth, buying a vehicle unnecessary for business operations. Sixth, tourism or vacations. Seventh, sending children to expensive private schools. Eighth, paying high premiums for insurance-based financial products. Ninth, taking any seat on a G-prefixed high-speed train, or a first-class or higher seat on another high-speed train. If one of these is necessary for daily life or business operations, you must apply to the court and obtain approval first. The court can lift the spending restrictions if you provide a genuinely effective guarantee or the enforcement applicant agrees (nationwide in China).
entries.sources: Supreme People’s Court (amended 2017). Several Provisions on Publishing Information on the List of Untrustworthy Persons Subject to Enforcement (Articles 1, 2, 3, 4, and 10). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/37182.html>; Supreme People’s Court (amended 2015). Several Provisions on Restricting High Spending and Related Spending by Persons Subject to Enforcement (Judicial Interpretation [2015] No. 17, Articles 3, 8, and 9): “(9) Taking any seat on a G-prefixed high-speed train, a first-class or higher seat on another high-speed train, or engaging in other spending unnecessary for daily life and work.” <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/15046.html>
entries.notes: A spending restriction means a restriction on high spending. These provisions were issued in 2010 and amended in 2015 by Judicial Interpretation [2015] No. 17. The title changed to Several Provisions on Restricting High Spending and Related Spending by Persons Subject to Enforcement; this item follows the current amended text. Three changes in 2015 matter here. It added the ninth category, covering every seat on a G-prefixed high-speed train. It removed the qualification “paid for with their own property”; the old text said a person “must not engage in the following acts involving payment of expenses with their property.” It also provided that when an organization is subject to spending restrictions, its actual controller is restricted too, but can apply to the court handling enforcement for private spending paid for with personal funds. The untrustworthy judgment debtors list and spending restrictions are separate measures; you may be subject to only one. For how to start over after removal from the list, see Section 7, Item 19 (how to start over after being on the untrustworthy judgment debtors list). The current text does not say whether a spouse or children are restricted in spending money they earned themselves. If this comes up, ask the court handling enforcement.

entries.title: If you are scammed while shopping online or buying secondhand, complain to the platform first, then report it to the police, then decide whether suing is worth it
entries.cost: Complaining to the platform and reporting to the police cost nothing. If you sue over 10,000 yuan or less, the case acceptance fee is 50 yuan; it is halved for simplified procedure, mediation, or withdrawal of the suit. Filing, hearings, and enforcement each take at least half a day to a day. Filing online can save you a trip. Keep your order details, chat records, transfer records, and shipping documents. The hard part is not giving up amid the back-and-forth.
entries.summary: Contact the platform first. Platforms have deposits and penalty rules, so they can act fastest.
