Then report it to the police: depending on the province, fraud involving 3,000 to 10,000 yuan or more meets the criminal fraud threshold; cases below it are handled under public security penalties. If you sue, you can bring an online shopping dispute before the court where you received the goods. Small claims use a procedure that concludes within 2 months, and you can file online.
entries.benefit: Fraud involving 3,000 to 10,000 yuan or more constitutes the “relatively large amount” threshold for the crime of fraud; each province sets its local threshold within that range. The penalty at this level is up to 3 years’ imprisonment, plus a fine or a fine alone. Below the criminal threshold, public security penalties apply: detention for 5 to 10 days or a fine of up to 2,000 yuan. In more serious circumstances, the penalty is detention for 10 to 15 days and a possible fine of up to 3,000 yuan. In civil proceedings, you can sue over an online shopping contract dispute in the court where you received the goods; you need not travel to the seller’s location. Small claims procedure applies if the amount in dispute is no more than 50% of the previous year’s average annual wage of employed persons in your province. A small claims case has a final judgment at first instance (it takes effect when given and cannot be appealed). It must be concluded within 2 months of filing; the simplified procedure takes 3 months. Civil proceedings can be conducted online and have the same legal effect as offline proceedings (nationwide in China; the Civil Procedure Law took effect in January 2024, and the Public Security Administration Punishments Law in January 2026).
entries.sources: Supreme People’s Court and Supreme People’s Procuratorate (2011). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in Handling Criminal Fraud Cases (Judicial Interpretation [2011] No. 7, Article 1). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/sfjs/201802/t20180201_363736.shtml>; National People’s Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Article 266). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (2025). Public Security Administration Punishments Law (2025 revision, Article 58). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (amended 2023). Civil Procedure Law (Articles 16, 164, 165, and 168). <https://fgw.sh.gov.cn/ys-syjf-zc-2.4.1-h5/20240408/073febdb2b04464390546232d4089f51.html> (reposted by the Shanghai Municipal Development and Reform Commission); Supreme People’s Court (amended 2022). Interpretation on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law (Article 20). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/353651.html>; State Council (2006). Measures for the Payment of Litigation Costs (State Council Order No. 481, Articles 13, 15, and 16). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_6929.htm>
entries.notes: You can work out whether suing is worth it this way: multiply your after-tax hourly earnings by the time it will take, then add the court’s case acceptance fee. Allow half a day to a day each for filing, a hearing, and possibly applying for enforcement. Compare the result with the amount you hope to recover, then discount that amount to estimate whether you could actually collect if you win. Decide whether to sue based on those figures. After the 2025 revision of the Public Security Administration Punishments Law, all the article numbers changed: theft and fraud moved from Article 49 of the old law to Article 58. After the 2023 amendment to the Civil Procedure Law, small claims procedure is in Article 165. Do not copy outdated sources for either. “Complain to the platform first” is practical advice: platforms have deposits and penalty rules and can act fastest. The procuratorate’s webpage for Judicial Interpretation [2011] No. 7 does not show its document number; that number still needs to be checked against the original page from the Supreme People’s Court.

entries.title: Think carefully before giving a large gift during a relationship or marriage; once delivered, it generally cannot be recovered
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Before making a large transfer, ask yourself: is this a loan or a gift? If it is a loan, write an IOU and put “loan” in the transfer note. The hard part is saying this out loud.
entries.summary: Once you hand over the money, you generally cannot get it back. You can freely revoke a gift only before ownership passes to the recipient. After the transfer is completed, it can be revoked only in three circumstances: the recipient seriously infringes your rights or those of your close relatives, fails to support you when obligated to do so, or fails to fulfill an agreed obligation. So before making a large transfer, decide whether it is a loan or a gift.
entries.benefit: You can revoke a gift before ownership passes to the recipient; the law calls this point the transfer of property rights. Once the money transfer or transfer of title is complete, only three grounds for revocation remain. First, the recipient seriously infringes your rights or those of your close relatives. Second, the recipient fails to support you despite having an obligation to do so. Third, the recipient fails to fulfill an obligation agreed in the gift contract. Gifts and gift money of modest value given on commemorative occasions such as holidays or birthdays are not betrothal gifts. Ordinary spending intended to express or deepen affection is not a betrothal gift either. Neither category is returned as a betrothal gift after a breakup (nationwide in China).
entries.sources: National People’s Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 658 and 663). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; Supreme People’s Court (2024). Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Hearing Disputes Involving Betrothal Gifts (Judicial Interpretation [2024] No. 1, Article 3). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/423442.html>
entries.notes: “Special amounts such as 520 and 1314 are usually treated as gifts” is a common statement in legal practice, but this section did not find an official original text from the Supreme People’s Court, so it does not present that statement as a conclusion. If a gift has been notarized at a notary office, you cannot simply change your mind and revoke it. Whether a transfer counts as a loan or a gift ultimately depends on the evidence. A message saying “I’ll lend you this money for now” is far more useful than arguing about it afterward.

entries.title: Transfer betrothal gifts through a bank account with a note stating their purpose, and keep your chat records; money demanded under the pretext of marriage can be recovered
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Pay betrothal gifts, the three gold items, and the gift money given when changing how you address your future in-laws by transfer, and state the purpose clearly in the transfer note. Keep a record of verbal agreements in chat messages, or have family members present to confirm them.
entries.summary: Demanding property under the pretext of marriage is prohibited by law, and courts support its return. You can request the return of betrothal gifts if the marriage was never registered, if it was registered but the couple genuinely never lived together, or if giving the gifts before marriage caused financial hardship for the giver. Gifts generally are not returned when the marriage was registered and the couple lived together. So transfer betrothal gifts, the three gold items, and the gift money given when changing how you address your future in-laws with a note stating their purpose. Whoever pays should keep the evidence, whether man or woman.
entries.benefit: The law prohibits the extortion of property by taking advantage of marriage. If one party extorts property by taking advantage of marriage under the guise of betrothal gifts (caili), and the other party demands its return, the court will support it. There are three situations where a return can be demanded: first, marriage registration was not completed; second, marriage registration was completed, but the parties never actually lived together; third, the betrothal gifts were given before marriage, and giving them resulted in financial hardship for the paying party. If registration has been completed and the parties have lived together, return is generally not granted. However, if the period of living together was short and the amount of the betrothal gifts was excessively high, the court will determine a return proportion. The proportion depends on how the money was actually spent, whether there was a dowry, whether there was pregnancy/childbearing, and whether either party was at fault. If the parties did not register marriage but have already cohabited, it is handled proportionally in the same manner (Nationwide, effective February 2024)
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 1042). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; Supreme People's Court (2024). Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes Involving Betrothal Gifts (Fa Shi [2024] No. 1, Articles 2, 5, 6). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/423442.html>; Supreme People's Court (2020). Interpretation on the Application of the Marriage and Family Section of the Civil Code (I) (Fa Shi [2020] No. 22, Article 5). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/282071.html>
entries.notes: Whether betrothal gifts count as an "excessively high amount" depends on the per capita disposable income of the payer's locality and their family's circumstances; there is no nationwide uniform figure. How much should be returned is determined by judges on a case-by-case basis. The rules are the same for the paying party and the receiving party: whoever gives money should preserve evidence. Holding a wedding banquet without registering the marriage is not legally recognized as a married couple; see Section 10, Item 21 (Even after holding a wedding banquet, you must register the marriage).

entries.title: Don't fear premarital property: write out clearly beforehand about adding names to house deeds and parental contributions
entries.cost: Writing a written property agreement yourself costs no money; notarization incurs a separate fee. When parents provide money, ask them to write a one-sentence written explanation. The whole matter takes a few hours as a one-time cost. The hard part is opening your mouth to talk about money with family members.
entries.summary: Premarital property is your personal property; it will not turn into community property just because of years of marriage. Spouses can agree in writing that premarital and postmarital properties remain separate. Keep one thing in mind: an agreement to add the other's name to a house deed can still be revoked before the change of registration; once registered, it belongs to the other party. A party who hides, transfers, squanders property, or fabricates debts during divorce may receive a smaller share or no share at all.
entries.benefit: Premarital property is personal property; it will not turn into community property just because of years of marriage. Spouses can agree in writing that: premarital property and postmarital income belong to each separately, belong jointly, or are partly joint; this agreement is binding on both parties. House purchase funds contributed by parents before marriage are deemed gifts to their own child, unless explicitly stated as given to both persons. Contributions by parents after marriage are handled according to agreements; absent an agreement, they are handled under the principle of community property. An agreement made before or during marriage to gift one party's real property to the other party, or to make it jointly owned by both, can be revoked before the change of registration. After registration, it belongs to the other party. A party who conceals, transfers, sells off, or squanders community property, or fabricates debts during divorce, may receive a smaller share or no share at all (Nationwide)
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 1063, 1065, 1092). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; Supreme People's Court (2020). Interpretation on the Application of the Marriage and Family Section of the Civil Code (I) (Fa Shi [2020] No. 22, Articles 29, 31, 32). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/282071.html>
entries.notes: A property agreement is equally valid for both men and women. If you want to use it against debts your spouse owes to third parties, the prerequisite is that the creditor knows you have this agreement. If they do not know, it cannot govern them. An agreement is valid even without notarization; notarization merely saves disputes over signatures and dates in the future. For how to clearly write whether parental contributions toward house purchases are loans or gifts, see Section 10, Item 11 (Parental contributions toward house purchases).

entries.title: Verify the other party's marital status before marriage; swindling money under the guise of marriage will be prosecuted as the crime of fraud
entries.cost: Costs no money. Take a look at the marital status on the other party's ID card and household register (hukou booklet) before registration. For large property transactions, keep transfer records and chat logs.
entries.summary: A bigamous marriage is invalid. Anyone who enters into a marriage while having a spouse, or marries someone knowing they have a spouse, faces up to 2 years of imprisonment. Swindling money under the guise of marriage will be prosecuted as fraud; an especially huge amount is sentenced to 10 years or more or life imprisonment. Take a look at the marital status on the other party's ID card and household register before registration.
entries.benefit: A bigamous marriage is invalid. Anyone who commits bigamy while having a spouse, or who knowingly marries someone who already has a spouse, faces a sentence of up to 2 years. Defrauding public or private property involving a relatively large amount is sentenced to up to 3 years and a fine. For a huge amount, 3 to 10 years. For an especially huge amount, 10 years or more or life imprisonment, plus a fine or confiscation of property (Nationwide)
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 1051). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Articles 258, 266). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml>
entries.notes: "Marriage fraud" itself is not a statutory crime name. Whether it can be handled as the crime of fraud depends on whether the person intended from the very beginning to take the money for themselves and fabricated lies to get the money, and it also requires public security organs to file a case and investigate. As to whether it reaches a "relatively large amount," the monetary thresholds are determined by judicial interpretations and can be adjusted locally; they were not verified in this section. Victims of marriage fraud include both men and women; there are cases of defrauded betrothal gifts as well as defrauded dowries.

entries.title: For on-site repairs, vehicle inspections, and renovations: ask the price before they start, and watch alongside throughout the entire process
entries.cost: Costs no money. Before work begins, ask clearly about fee standards and which parts are to be replaced, take photos of the quotation, or have the other party send text. After repair, ask for repair vouchers and invoices, and keep the old parts. Also stand next to them watching for one or two hours. The hard part is keeping an eye on it throughout the whole process without walking away.
entries.summary: Home appliance repair must clearly display fee standards, provide vouchers and invoices, and must not falsely report faults or replace good parts without justification; serious violations face fines of up to 30,000 yuan. All operators must mark prices clearly and must not add charges beyond marked prices. Therefore, before starting work, ask clearly about prices and parts to replace; after repair, demand vouchers and invoices, and keep old parts. If overcharged, call 12315 first.
entries.benefit: Home appliance repair operators must clearly display charging standards, quality specifications, warranty periods, and complaint phone numbers for service items and spare parts. They must provide consumers with repair service vouchers and fee invoices, and truthfully fill in repair items and details. They must not falsely list, exaggerate, or forge repair items, must not falsely report faulty components, and must not intentionally replace properly functioning components. For serious violations, a fine of up to 30,000 yuan shall be imposed. All business operators must mark prices clearly, must not add surcharges beyond the marked price, and must not collect any unmarked fees. Luring consumers with low prices while settling at high prices, as well as false discounts, constitute price fraud. Operators must prominently mark service items, contents, prices, and billing methods, and must not make false or misleading publicity (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Ministry of Commerce (2012). Administrative Measures on the Home Appliance Repair and Service Industry (Ministry of Commerce Order No. 7 of 2012, Articles 5, 7, 9, 14). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2012/content_2231695.htm>; State Administration for Market Regulation (2022). Provisions on Clearly Marked Prices and Prohibition of Price Fraud (SAMR Order No. 56, Articles 5, 8, 19). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2022/content_5699926.htm>; State Council (2024). Regulations on the Implementation of the Law on Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests (State Council Order No. 778, Articles 9, 10). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202403/content_6940159.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2013 Amendment). Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests (Articles 8, 10): "Consumers have the right to demand business operators provide... information such as the contents, specifications, and fees of services depending on the circumstances of the commodities or services" "have the right to reject compulsory transactions by business operators". <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7670606ef> (National Database of Laws and Regulations)
entries.notes: If overcharged, call 12315 first; penalties are issued by commerce and market supervision departments, without requiring you to file a lawsuit yourself. Rated Grade B because although the rules are official, there are no exact figures on "how much money watching alongside can save," which relies mainly on experience. Asking prices, keeping vouchers, and retaining old parts should be done equally for anyone, without judging people by appearances. That appliance measure only governs home appliance repairs; vehicle inspections and renovations refer to the clearly marked prices provisions and implementation regulations. The Law on Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests, which sits at a higher legal level than these provisions, also specifies two of your rights. Article 8 states that you have the right to require operators to explain service contents, specifications, and fees. Article 10 states that you have the right to refuse compulsory transactions.

entries.title: Don't be a "nominal legal representative"; don't lend your ID card to others to register a company
entries.cost: Costs no money. If someone asks you to "just put down your name without managing anything," simply refuse.
entries.summary: The law presumes that the legal representative is the person managing affairs; "I was only a nominal figurehead and knew nothing" is not grounds for exemption from liability. If the legal representative causes damage to others in performing duties, the company compensates first; after compensating, it can seek recovery from you if you are at fault. For those who are already nominal representatives, Company Law allows you to resign, and the company must determine a new legal representative within 30 days.
entries.benefit: The legal representative is assumed by a director or manager who actually executes company affairs; the law presumes that you are the person managing affairs. If the legal representative causes damage to others in the performance of duties, the company compensates first. After compensating, it can look back and seek recovery from the at-fault legal representative (recovering this money). Directors and senior executives owe duties of loyalty and diligence to the company (being loyal to the company and handling affairs conscientiously). If they cause damage to others in performing duties and have intentional misconduct or gross negligence themselves, they must also pay out of their own pocket. "Being unaware" is not legally recognized grounds for liability exemption. Article 10 of the Company Law explicitly states: "Where the legal representative resigns, the company shall determine a new legal representative within thirty days from the date of resignation of the legal representative." (Nationwide, effective July 2024)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2023). Company Law (2023 Revision, Articles 10, 11, 180, 191). <https://www.gov.cn/yaowen/liebiao/202312/content_6923395.htm>
entries.notes: The original text of the Company Law only specifies where liability falls. A more common consequence of acting as a nominal figurehead is: when the company faces court enforcement, the legal representative is also subjected to restrictions on high consumption, and tax and administrative penalties may also implicate you. These consequences stem from other laws and enforcement regulations; the original texts were not verified in this section, hence the Grade B rating. For those who have already lent their name, Company Law allows you to resign, and the company must determine a new legal representative within 30 days. For having your name borrowed to take out loans, see Item 45 (Helping scan your face).

entries.title: Do not carry items for strangers when entering/exiting borders, and do not receive parcels of unknown origin on someone's behalf
entries.cost: Costs no money. Simply refuse.
entries.summary: Advice from the Department of Consular Affairs of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to outbound citizens is: do not carry luggage or items for others, especially contraband, or things you do not know about. All countries ban drug imports; the luggage is in your hands, and you are the one who must answer questions and declare at customs. The same applies to domestic package pickups on others' behalf, especially those requiring you to advance money and get refunded later.
entries.benefit: The advice given by the Department of Consular Affairs of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to outbound citizens is "please be sure to avoid carrying luggage and items for others, especially contraband items or items you do not know about". The same paragraph states, "All countries ban the entry of drugs, protected animal and plant products, etc.", requiring you to "truthfully declare restricted items and cash amounts as required", and also "truthfully answer inquiries from customs, immigration, and other personnel". For items carried for others, you cannot clearly state what is inside, making it impossible to truthfully declare. The same applies domestically. A 2025 risk alert from the Hubei Provincial Postal Administration stated that major forms of fraud using courier services include "high-value item collection on behalf of others", and clearly noted that "all cases demanding advance payment of funds under the pretext of express delivery 'brushing' or 'doing tasks' are fraud"
entries.sources: Department of Consular Affairs, Ministry of Foreign Affairs (2026). What Advice Is Available for Chinese Citizens Preparing to Go Abroad? (China Consular Services Website, July 13, 2026). <https://cs.mfa.gov.cn/zggmcgx/lsbhyxz/cjwd_149483/202607/t20260713_11981016.html>; Hubei Provincial Postal Administration (2025). Risk Alert on Preventing Fraud Conducted Through Postal and Courier Channels (March 25, 2025). <https://hb.spb.gov.cn/hubsyzglj/c100057/c100058/202503/17998076d1f74959b1d4378ddb9d3564.shtml>
entries.notes: Official prompt pages from the General Administration of Customs and the Ministry of Public Security regarding this matter could not be opened; the entry/exit portion only cites the page from the Department of Consular Affairs of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Furthermore, the original text gives only principles rather than statutory articles, hence rated Grade B. You must likewise be careful about bringing medicine abroad for others; see Section 21, Item 12 (Bringing medicine abroad).

entries.title: Dogs must be kept on a leash: an incident without a leash incurs strict liability (you compensate regardless of fault), paying in full. Dogs must also receive rabies vaccines on schedule and undergo dog registration
entries.cost: A leash costs a few tens of yuan. Vaccinating the dog against rabies and handling registration also cost money, with fees varying by locality. The hard part is remembering to leash every time you go out and remembering to take the dog for shots when due.
entries.summary: If a dog injures someone, you must in principle compensate regardless of whether you are at fault, and compensation can only be reduced or waived if you prove the other party acted intentionally or with gross negligence. For an unleashed dog, only "the other party's intentional misconduct" remains as grounds for mitigation; for relatively serious circumstances, detention may also be imposed. Failing to vaccinate a dog against rabies as required will lead to an order to rectify and potentially fines. If a prohibited vicious dog injures someone, there are no grounds for liability exemption.
entries.benefit: If a domestic animal injures someone, the keeper or manager must compensate, legally termed assuming tort liability. Only if it can be proven that the injured person intentionally provoked the animal or had gross negligence can liability be exempted or mitigated. However, if management regulations are violated and safety measures were not taken, such as failing to leash a dog when required, only "intentional misconduct by the infringed party" remains as grounds for mitigation. If a prohibited vicious dog injures someone, there are no grounds whatsoever for liability exemption. Article 89 of the Law on Public Security Administration Punishments provides that anyone who fails to take safety measures for an animal, resulting in injury to others, shall be fined up to 1,000 yuan. If circumstances are relatively serious, detention of 5 to 10 days shall be imposed. Article 30 of the Animal Epidemic Prevention Law requires that dog keepers must regularly vaccinate dogs against rabies according to regulations. Then, take the immunization certificate issued by an animal diagnosis and treatment institution (such as a pet hospital) to apply for dog registration with the local registry. When taking a dog outdoors, dog tags must be worn and leashes used as required to prevent dogs from injuring people and spreading epidemics. Article 92 of the same law provides that where dogs are not vaccinated against rabies in accordance with regulations, agricultural and rural departments shall order rectification within a time limit. A fine of up to 1,000 yuan may be imposed. If not rectified upon expiration, a fine of 1,000 to 5,000 yuan shall be imposed, and an animal diagnosis and treatment institution, harmless disposal site, etc., will be commissioned to handle it on your behalf, with the required expenses borne by you
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code. Full text republished by Supreme People's Procuratorate. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml> Article 1245: "Where a domesticated animal causes damage to another person, the animal keeper or manager shall bear tort liability; however, if it can be proven that the damage was caused by the intentional act or gross negligence of the infringed person, liability may not be assumed or may be mitigated." Article 1246: "Where, in violation of management regulations, no safety measures are taken for an animal and damage is caused to another person, the animal keeper or manager shall bear tort liability; however, if it can be proven that the damage was caused by the intentional act of the infringed person, liability may be mitigated." Article 1247: "Where dangerous animals such as vicious dogs prohibited from being kept cause damage to another person, the animal keeper or manager shall bear tort liability." Article 1249: If an abandoned or escaped animal causes damage during such period, liability shall be borne by the original keeper or manager; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2025). Law on Public Security Administration Punishments (2025 Revision, effective 2026-01-01). National Database of Laws and Regulations. <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff80818197af9ccc0197b159c38a0408> Article 89, Paragraph 3: "Whoever fails to take safety measures for an animal, resulting in injury to another person, shall be fined up to one thousand yuan; where the circumstances are relatively serious, detention of not less than five days but not more than ten days shall be imposed."; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2021). Animal Epidemic Prevention Law (2021 Revision, effective 2021-05-01). National Database of Laws and Regulations. <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080817703add2017737395a973e31> Article 30, Paragraph 1: "Entities and individuals raising dogs shall regularly vaccinate them against rabies in accordance with regulations, and apply for registration with the local dog registration authority with immunization certificates issued by animal diagnosis and treatment institutions." Paragraph 2: "When taking dogs outdoors, dog tags shall be worn as required and measures such as leashing shall be adopted to prevent dogs from injuring people and spreading epidemic diseases." Paragraph 5: "Specific measures for epidemic prevention management in raising dogs shall be formulated by provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government." Article 92: "The competent department of agriculture and rural affairs of a local people's government at or above the county level shall order rectification within a prescribed time limit and may impose a fine of not more than 1,000 yuan; if it fails to rectify within the time limit, a fine of not less than 1,000 yuan but not more than 5,000 yuan shall be imposed, and the competent department of agriculture and rural affairs of a local people's government at or above the county level shall entrust an animal diagnosis and treatment institution, harmless disposal site, etc. to handle it on its behalf, and the necessary expenses shall be borne by the violator", applicable circumstance item (3): "Failing to regularly vaccinate raised dogs against rabies in accordance with regulations"
entries.notes: Compensation for dog bites includes medical expenses, lost wages, rabies vaccines, and immunoglobulin. Walking away and leaving it unattended does not relieve liability: if an animal injures someone during abandonment or escape, it still falls on the original keeper. The Animal Epidemic Prevention Law leaves the specific measures for dog epidemic prevention to each province, autonomous region, and municipality directly under the Central Government. Where to register, how much to charge, and how often shots are required depend on local dog management regulations. For what to do after being bitten, see Section 13, Item 13 (Being bitten or scratched by dogs or cats).

entries.title: Do not engage in sexual intercourse if the other party is drunk to the point of being unconscious, asleep, or possibly under 14 years old
entries.cost: Costs no money. The cost is stopping things in that moment. The hard part is halting on the spot.
entries.summary: If the other party is drunk to the point of being unconscious or asleep, they cannot give effective consent. Having sexual intercourse at this time legally counts as rape, with a basic sentence of 3 to 10 years. The reliable practice is to not engage in sexual relations, and when the drinking gathering ends, hand the person over to their own friends or family. For age determination, see Section 9, Item 18 (Under 14 years of age).
entries.benefit: Article 236 of the Criminal Law: Whoever rapes a woman by violence, coercion, or other means shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years and not more than ten years. "Other means" is not limited to physical force; when the other party is unconscious or asleep and cannot give effective consent, it falls under these four words. Where the rape of a woman involves heinous circumstances, multiple women raped, and other scenarios, the sentence shall be fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years, life imprisonment, or death. The same article also provides that whoever engages in sexual intercourse with a young girl under fourteen years of age shall be deemed to have committed rape and be given a heavier punishment. For how a young girl is determined, see Section 9, Item 18 (Under 14 years of age). A legal popularization article by the People's Procuratorate of Xicheng District, Beijing, stated that "sexually assaulting a woman after intoxicating or drugging her likewise constitutes the crime of rape". The key lies in "whether it violates the victim's true inner willingness"; whether the victim resisted at the time "is not the key". Article 237 of the Criminal Law governs forcible indecency: Whoever forcibly commits indecency against another person by violence, coercion, or other methods shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years or criminal detention (Nationwide)
entries.sources: National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Article 236). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml>; National People's Congress (amended in 2020). Criminal Law (Article 237). <https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index.html> (reposted as a consolidated text by the Beijing Municipal Public Security Traffic Management Bureau); People's Procuratorate of Xicheng District, Beijing (2018). Why They No Longer Remain Silent……. <https://www.bjjc.gov.cn/c/xicheng/xjjsl/320654084.jhtml>
entries.notes: The rating is B because the statutory provision says only the four Chinese characters meaning “other means.” “Getting someone drunk also counts as rape” comes from a procuratorate article explaining the law; it is not a judicial interpretation. The statutory provision on rape mentions only women. When a man is subjected to this kind of assault, it is prosecuted as the crime of forcible indecency, so you must not touch someone in this way regardless of whether they are male or female. If you are the victim, see Section 13, Item 42 (after a sexual assault) for what to do first. If you drink until you black out, you face both the risk of being accused and the risk of being blackmailed. For blackmail, see Item 32 of this section (if someone uses something against you to demand money, report it to the police).

entries.title: If someone demands money after sex or a nude chat by threatening to report you to the police, send photos, or tell your employer, pay nothing, delete no records, and report it directly to the police
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Take screenshots of the other person's account, chat records, and payment QR code, and bring your phone to a police station. The hard part is resisting the urge to “pay first to make it go away.”
entries.summary: Using threats such as “I'll report you to the police” or “I'll send the photos to your employer” to demand money is extortion. Pay nothing, delete no records, and report it to the police immediately. If the person actually sends out the photos, they also violate your right to privacy. Extortion involving 2,000 to 5,000 yuan or more carries a sentence of up to 3 years; 30,000 to 100,000 yuan or more carries 3 to 10 years.
entries.benefit: Article 274 of the Criminal Law: Anyone who extorts public or private property, where the amount is relatively large or the extortion is repeated, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of up to three years, short-term detention, or public surveillance, and shall also or solely be fined. Short-term detention means being held for a short period; public surveillance does not involve confinement but restricts freedom; “also or solely be fined” means an additional fine or a fine alone. Where the amount is huge or there are other serious circumstances, the sentence is fixed-term imprisonment of three to ten years plus a fine. Where the amount is especially huge or there are other especially serious circumstances, the sentence is fixed-term imprisonment of more than ten years plus a fine. The Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate also issued an interpretation: Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Extortion (Judicial Interpretation [2013] No. 10, effective April 27, 2013). Article 1 of this interpretation sets three monetary tiers. Extortion of public or private property worth 2,000 to 5,000 yuan or more is deemed a “relatively large amount.” An amount of 30,000 to 100,000 yuan or more is deemed a “huge amount.” An amount of 300,000 to 500,000 yuan or more is deemed an “especially huge amount.” Article 3: Extortion committed three or more times within two years shall be deemed “repeated extortion” (nationwide). Article 1032 of the Civil Code: No organization or individual may infringe another person's right to privacy by prying, intruding, disclosing, publicizing, or other means. Article 1033 prohibits disturbing the peace of a person's private life through telephone calls, text messages, instant messaging tools, and other means. So if the other person actually sends out the photos, they further violate your right to privacy; it is not your fault. The Fujian Provincial Public Security Department's advice concerning similar cases says, verbatim: “Be sure to preserve the evidence, call 110 promptly, and do not continue transferring money.”
entries.sources: National People's Congress (amended in 2020). Criminal Law (Article 274). <https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index.html> (reposted as a consolidated text by the Beijing Municipal Public Security Traffic Management Bureau); Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate (2013). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Extortion (Judicial Interpretation [2013] No. 10). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/5310.html>; National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 1032 and 1033). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 1195): “The rights holder has the right to notify the network service provider to take necessary measures such as deletion, blocking, and disabling links. The notice shall include preliminary evidence of the infringement and the rights holder's true identity information”; “If the provider fails to take necessary measures promptly, it shall bear joint and several liability with the network user for the increased portion of the harm.” <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5c500bf> (National Database of Laws and Regulations); Fujian Provincial Public Security Department (2024). Because of One “Hookup” Message, I Ended Up 230,000 Yuan in Debt. <http://gat.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/fjjffpzxrx/spjq/202403/t20240307_6410612.htm>; Shenzhen Municipal Public Security Bureau (2022). How Does a “Nude Chat” Scam Succeed Step by Step? <https://ga.sz.gov.cn/JMHD/YWZSK/XJGL_ZS/content/post_9577428.html>; Beijing Anti-Fraud (2023). Preventing Nude Chat Extortion (reposted by the Fujian Provincial Public Security Department). <https://gat.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/fjjffpzxrx/dxal/202302/t20230210_6107918.htm>; Procuratorate Daily (2018). Convicted Twice but Unrepentant: Threatening Online Acquaintances by Exposing Their Private Information (reposted on the website of the People's Procuratorate of Gulou District, Xuzhou). <https://xzgl.jsjc.gov.cn/jianwu/baxiang/201804/t20180409_420934.shtml>; Procuratorate Daily (2022). Man Threatens to Publish Nude Photos to Force 10 Women to Have Sex with Him; Big-Data Screening Flags a “Police Report”! (website of the Supreme People's Procuratorate). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/202212/t20221212_595435.shtml>
entries.notes: Each province sets its own thresholds for the three monetary tiers within the ranges provided by the judicial interpretation. An amount of 2,000 to 5,000 yuan or more counts as a “relatively large amount.” An amount of 30,000 to 100,000 yuan or more counts as a “huge amount.” An amount of 300,000 to 500,000 yuan or more counts as an “especially huge amount.” The exact threshold where you live depends on the local standard. Extortion three or more times within two years also counts as “repeated extortion,” even if the amount each time is small. Do not delete chat records or photos yourself, close your account, or simply block the person. That would also delete your own evidence; see Item 5 of this section (if summoned, get a lawyer first and do not delete records). If you are actually placed under investigation, these records are also material you can use in your own defense. Do not try to “negotiate installment payments,” either. Shenzhen police have described how nude chat extortion works. The scammer induces you to install a supposed nude chat app that is actually a Trojan horse that extracts your contacts. The scammer then records the entire interaction and demands money by threatening to send the video to all your contacts. Beijing police say that once you agree to pay to “settle it privately,” the scammer will keep demanding money without end. Demanding money by threatening to “tell your family you like people of the same sex” is the same kind of extortion. In Yancheng, Jiangsu, someone arranged to meet people through a same-sex social app and then used this tactic to obtain 14,500 yuan. After a victim reported him, he was prosecuted. He had previously been convicted twice for using the same method. Using nude photos to force someone to have sex is prosecuted as rape. In Xiangshan, Zhejiang, someone deceived multiple women on a social platform into sending nude photos, then threatened to publish them. Investigators identified 10 victims. One of them reported the threat to the police as soon as she received it. She had never met the person, but the procuratorate still treated the case as attempted rape. The perpetrator was ultimately prosecuted for rape and forcible indecency. So do not send nude photos to someone you met online. Conversely, if you are the victim and seek compensation from the person who infringed your rights, a high amount does not by itself make your claim extortion. For how to claim compensation, see Item 36 of this section (seeking compensation when you are the victim). If the photos really are posted online, you can notify the platform to remove them. Article 1195 of the Civil Code provides that you have the right to notify the platform to delete or block the content or disable the links. Your notice must include preliminary evidence of the infringement and your true identity information. If the platform fails to act promptly after receiving the notice, it and the poster are jointly liable for the increased portion of the harm.

entries.title: If someone reports you using fabricated facts, you can seek to have them held accountable: conduct warranting a public security penalty can bring detention, rising to 5 days or more for more serious circumstances; conduct amounting to a crime can bring a sentence of up to 3 years
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Report it to a Chinese public security authority and explain that the other person fabricated the allegations. The hard part is producing evidence that they made them up deliberately.
entries.summary: Fabricating facts to falsely accuse someone in order to have them held accountable is itself unlawful. It is punishable by detention for up to 5 days or a fine of up to 1,000 yuan; in more serious circumstances, detention is 5 to 10 days. If it rises to the level of a crime, it is the crime of false accusation and framing, punishable by up to 3 years. But misremembering or reporting the wrong person does not count. To have the other person held accountable, you must prove they intended to frame you.
entries.benefit: Article 50 of the Public Security Administration Punishments Law (revised June 27, 2025; effective January 1, 2026) addresses false accusations. Fabricating facts to falsely accuse and frame another person, in an attempt to have that person criminally prosecuted or subjected to a public security administration penalty, is punishable. The penalty is detention for up to five days or a fine of up to 1,000 yuan. In more serious circumstances, it is detention for five to ten days, possibly accompanied by a fine of up to 1,000 yuan. Article 243 of the Criminal Law addresses the crime of false accusation and framing. Fabricating facts to falsely accuse and frame another person with the intent of having that person criminally prosecuted, where the circumstances are serious, is punishable by fixed-term imprisonment of up to three years, short-term detention, or public surveillance. If serious consequences result, the sentence is fixed-term imprisonment of three to ten years. State personnel who commit the offense described in the preceding paragraph are punished more severely; this means a sentence toward the heavier end of the same sentencing range. Where the accusation was mistaken or a report proved inaccurate, rather than being a deliberate attempt to frame someone, the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs do not apply. Misremembering or making a mistaken accusation is not prosecuted under those two paragraphs (nationwide).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2025). Public Security Administration Punishments Law (2025 revision, Article 50). <https://gaj.beijing.gov.cn/wsgs/2024zcwj/zcfg/202506/t20250630_4134266.html> (full text reposted by the Beijing Municipal Public Security Bureau); National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Article 243). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml>
entries.notes: To have the other person held accountable, proving only “I didn't do it” is not enough. You also have to prove that they “fabricated facts” and “intended to frame” you. The latter is much harder to prove, so an attempt to hold them accountable may fail. There are no publicly available nationwide statistics on the filing and handling of false accusation cases that this book could find, so it gives neither an incidence rate nor a gender breakdown. For evidence and remedies after you are accused, see Items 34 and 35 of this section (acquittal when evidence is insufficient, and state compensation).

entries.title: Insufficient evidence should result in acquittal, and confessions extracted by coercion should be excluded; even after conviction, you can petition and seek a retrial
entries.cost: The procedures themselves cost nothing, but petitions and retrials take a great deal of time. You will usually need a lawyer, with legal fees starting at several thousand yuan. If you have financial difficulties, you can apply for legal aid; see Item 5 of this section (get a lawyer first if accused). The hard part is not giving up through round after round of waiting.
entries.summary: The threshold for conviction is set out in the Criminal Procedure Law: the evidence on which the case is decided must be verified as true through statutory procedures, and the evidence in the case as a whole must rule out reasonable doubt. If that standard cannot be met, the defendant should be acquitted. Confessions obtained through torture and testimony obtained through violence or threats must be excluded; they cannot be used as the basis for a judgment. After a judgment takes legal effect, you, your legal representative, and your close relatives can still file a petition.
entries.benefit: Article 55 of the Criminal Procedure Law: For evidence to be reliable and sufficient, these conditions must be met—the evidence used to decide the case has all been verified as true through statutory procedures, and, considering the evidence in the case as a whole, reasonable doubt about the facts found has been ruled out. Ruling out reasonable doubt means looking at all the evidence together: there must not remain another plausible account of the facts. Article 56: Statements by criminal suspects or defendants collected through illegal methods such as torture to extract confessions, and witness testimony and victim statements collected through illegal methods such as violence or threats, shall be excluded. If evidence that must be excluded is discovered during investigation, review for prosecution, or trial, it shall be excluded in accordance with the law and must not be used as a basis for a recommendation to prosecute, a decision to prosecute, or a judgment. Article 200(3): Where the evidence is insufficient to find the defendant guilty, the court shall deliver a judgment of not guilty on the grounds that the evidence is insufficient and the alleged crime has not been established. Article 252 provides a way to petition. Parties, their legal representatives, and their close relatives may file a petition with a people's court or a people's procuratorate against a judgment or ruling that has already taken legal effect. But filing a petition does not suspend enforcement of the judgment or ruling. Article 253 lists the circumstances in which a people's court shall retry a case (nationwide).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). Criminal Procedure Law (2018 amendment, Articles 55, 56, 200, 252, and 253). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/201810/t20181027_396818.shtml>
entries.notes: These are minimum safeguards written into the system; they do not guarantee an outcome. This book has no verifiable official data on the acquittal rate in Chinese criminal cases or the rate at which judgments are changed after petitions, so it gives no percentages and does not assess individual cases. There are three things you can do. First, retain a lawyer after the first interrogation; see Item 5 of this section (get a lawyer first if accused). Second, read the interrogation record word for word before signing it. Third, do not admit to something you did not do just to “get out sooner.” Pleading guilty and accepting punishment can only lead to leniency; it does not remove liability. Where the statutory conditions are met, the court shall retry the case.

entries.title: If you were detained and the case was then dropped, you were not prosecuted, or you were acquitted, apply for state compensation calculated by the day
entries.cost: It costs nothing. Submit a compensation application to the authority that originally ordered the detention or arrest, brought the prosecution, or issued the judgment.
entries.summary: If you were detained or arrested and the case was later dropped, you were not prosecuted, or you were acquitted, you can apply for state compensation. Time spent in custody is compensated by the day, at 495.94 yuan per day from May 18, 2026. If the consequences were serious, additional compensation for mental distress is payable. There is no compensation if you committed an offense but were not prosecuted only because the circumstances were minor; there is also none if the prosecution period had expired, you were below the age of criminal responsibility, or you gave a false statement yourself.
entries.benefit: Article 17 of the State Compensation Law lists several circumstances in which a victim has the right to compensation. The first concerns detention: a citizen was detained in violation of the Criminal Procedure Law, or was lawfully detained but held beyond the statutory time limit, and the authorities subsequently decided to drop the case or not to prosecute, or a judgment of acquittal ended the pursuit of criminal liability. The second concerns arrest: after a citizen was arrested, the authorities decided to drop the case or not to prosecute, or a judgment of acquittal ended the pursuit of criminal liability. The third concerns retrial: a case was retried under the trial supervision procedure, the judgment was changed to an acquittal, and the punishment imposed by the original judgment had already been carried out. The trial supervision procedure is the procedure for reopening a judgment that has already taken effect. Article 33: Compensation for infringing a citizen's personal freedom is calculated for each day according to the national average daily wage of employees in the preceding year. Article 35: Where mental harm is caused, the authority shall, within the scope of the impact of the infringement, eliminate its effects on the victim, restore the victim's reputation, and offer an apology; where serious consequences are caused, it shall pay an appropriate sum for mental distress. Article 19 lists six circumstances in which the state does not pay compensation. First, you deliberately gave a false statement or fabricated other evidence of your guilt and were detained or sentenced as a result. Second, someone who bears no criminal responsibility under Articles 17 or 18 of the Criminal Law was detained. Examples include someone below the age of criminal responsibility, or a person with a mental illness who caused harm when unable to recognize or control their actions. Third, someone who is not to be held criminally liable under the Criminal Procedure Law was detained. This includes circumstances that were clearly minor and caused little harm and are therefore not considered a crime, cases past the limitation period for prosecution, and cases in which the suspect died. It also includes minor criminal conduct for which the procuratorate decides not to prosecute, commonly called relative non-prosecution (also called discretionary non-prosecution). It likewise includes non-prosecution after a minor completes the probation period for conditional non-prosecution, and non-prosecution following a settlement with the victim. Fourth, personal conduct by case-handling personnel unrelated to the exercise of their official powers. Fifth, harm caused by your own deliberate conduct, such as injuring or mutilating yourself. Sixth, other circumstances specified by law. Article 7 of the Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate's 2015 judicial interpretation on criminal compensation confirms again that the state does not compensate people who bear no criminal responsibility or who receive relative non-prosecution for time in custody. But if, after prosecution, a court wrongly sentences someone to short-term detention, fixed-term imprisonment, or life imprisonment and the sentence has been carried out, compensation is still due for the period of continued confinement after the judgment was rendered. Article 8 of the interpretation: If a case-handling authority refuses compensation on the grounds that “you gave a false statement yourself” or “you injured or mutilated yourself,” that authority bears the burden of proof. The Supreme People's Procuratorate issued a notice in May 2026. On May 15, 2026, the National Bureau of Statistics published the figures for 2025. The national average annual wage of employees in urban non-private-sector organizations was about 129,000 yuan (129,441 yuan). The average daily wage calculated from that figure is 495.94 yuan. When procuratorates at all levels make state compensation decisions from May 18, 2026, they use that figure. Compensation for infringing a citizen's personal freedom is 495.94 yuan per day. The previous rate was 475.52 yuan per day and had been used since May 2025 (nationwide).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (amended in 2012). State Compensation Law (Articles 17, 19, 33, and 35). <https://www.stats.gov.cn/gk/tjfg/xgfxfg/202503/t20250306_1958899.html> (reposted by the National Bureau of Statistics); Supreme People's Procuratorate (2026). Supreme People's Procuratorate Announces Latest Compensation Rate for Infringement of Citizens' Personal Freedom. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbh/202605/t20260519_727675.shtml>; Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate (2015). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Compensation Cases (Judicial Interpretation [2015] No. 24, Articles 7 and 8). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/16409.html>; National People's Congress (2018). Criminal Procedure Law (2018 amendment, Articles 16, 177, 181, 284, and 290). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/201810/t20181027_396818.shtml>. Article 19 of the State Compensation Law and that interpretation cite the article numbers in the 2012 Criminal Procedure Law (Article 15, Article 173(2), Article 273(2), and Article 279); after the 2018 amendment, these correspond respectively to Article 16, Article 177(2), Article 284(2), and Article 290.
entries.notes: This daily rate is updated each May when the National Bureau of Statistics of China publishes the previous year’s average annual wage for employees of urban non-private entities. Check the rate for the year in question; do not simply use the figure in this entry. When you receive a decision not to prosecute, first check the grounds it gives. If it says “no criminal facts” or “insufficient evidence,” you can apply for compensation. If it says “the circumstances of the crime are minor,” or the limitation period for prosecution has expired, you generally cannot receive compensation for the days you were detained. If you disagree with a decision of discretionary non-prosecution, you can appeal to the procuratorate within 7 days of receiving it. The case-handling authority determines compensation for mental distress according to the consequences; there is no uniform formula. The authority that originally decided to detain you—public security, the procuratorate, or the court—is the one that must pay. Apply to it first. If you disagree with how it handles your application, pursue the matter through the procedures in China’s State Compensation Law. For an example of the calculation, see the decision in Guo Li’s case in Item 36 of this section (claiming compensation when you are the victim). Guo Li was detained for 1,826 days. Compensation was calculated using the rate for the year the decision was made, not the year he was detained. The rate used was the 2016 national average daily wage for employees, 258.89 yuan. Compensation for restriction of personal freedom was about 473,000 yuan (472,733.14 yuan). He also received about 165,000 yuan (165,450 yuan) for mental distress. He had sought 88.88 million yuan in compensation for ten years of mental distress; the amount beyond what was awarded was denied. You should also know what cannot be compensated. That decision found that the following were outside the scope of state compensation: lost income, compensation for physical health, property losses, lawyer’s fees, and a subsidy for living expenses in the detention center.

entries.title: If you are the victim seeking compensation, use China’s 12315 service, file a lawsuit, or work through a lawyer; do not go alone to a meeting arranged by the other side, and do not tie “pay me” to “I won’t expose this” in one statement
entries.cost: No cost. Use China’s 12315 service, file a lawsuit in court, or have a lawyer make the claim. Record the entire conversation if you meet to negotiate. The hard part is resisting the urge to negotiate with the other side alone.
entries.summary: If you are the victim, you have a legal basis for claiming compensation from the party that infringed your rights. A “high demand” does not automatically turn the claim into extortion. But the cost can be enormous: Guo Li was first sentenced to five years in prison for extortion and was acquitted only after a retrial. So use channels that leave a record. Do not go alone to a place chosen by the other side to negotiate, and do not state “pay me” and “then I won’t expose this” as a single condition.
entries.benefit: Official case: In 2008, after the relevant Chinese authorities announced that certain batches of “Scient” brand milk powder contained melamine, the examination of Guo Li’s daughter found “several punctate strong echoes visible within the central collecting systems of both kidneys.” Guo repeatedly sought compensation from the seller and Scient, and publicized the matter through the media. In June 2009, the two sides reached an agreement under which Scient paid 400,000 yuan in compensation. Guo provided a written statement saying he would not pursue the matter further and was giving up his compensation claim. The company later reported him to the police, and the Chao’an County People’s Court sentenced him to five years’ imprisonment for extortion. The Guangdong Provincial People’s Procuratorate recommended a retrial. Its recommendation said that “the existing evidence is insufficient to establish that Guo Li subjectively intended unlawful possession.” As the child’s legal guardian, Guo “had the right to seek compensation from the milk powder manufacturer, and his claim had a legal basis.” The recommendation also stated that “consumers have the right to expose and criticize, through mass media, conduct that harms their lawful rights and interests.” On April 7, 2017, the Guangdong Provincial High People’s Court acquitted Guo on retrial. Its reason was that “the original trial’s finding that Guo Li, with the intent of unlawful possession, used threats and coercion to forcibly obtain property was based on unclear facts and insufficient evidence; the nature of Guo Li’s conduct did not go beyond a civil dispute.” Guo was detained for 1,826 days, from July 23, 2009, to July 22, 2014 (Guangdong; verdict changed on retrial in 2017).
entries.sources: Guangdong Provincial People’s Procuratorate (2017). Retrial recommendation by the Guangdong Provincial Procuratorate leads to Guo Li’s acquittal. <http://www.gd.jcy.gov.cn/jcyw2/201704/t20170411_1975029.shtml> (official website of the Guangdong Provincial People’s Procuratorate); Compensation Committee of the Guangdong Provincial High People’s Court (2018). State compensation case in which Guo Li applied for compensation from the Chaozhou Intermediate People’s Court of Guangdong Province on the basis of his acquittal on retrial ((2018) Yue Wei Pei No. 11). <https://www.gdcourts.gov.cn/caipanwenshuxuandeng/caipanwenshuxuandeng/content/post_1045709.html>
entries.notes: The evidence rating is B because this is only one case, not a rate that can be generalized. It shows two things at once: claiming compensation is itself lawful, and the police may still open a case and investigate you. The lowest-risk route is to leave the claim to a lawyer or file a lawsuit directly with the court, without contacting the other side alone. Be especially careful if the other side invites you to “meet in person to resolve it” in its own locality; reports to the police and case filings usually occur where the other side is located. Once you sign a settlement agreement, follow it. Making a separate, large compensation demand afterward is especially likely to be interpreted as “coercion.” For what to do after a case is filed against you, see Items 5, 34, and 35 of this section (get a lawyer first; insufficient evidence should result in acquittal; state compensation). If the other side uses something it has on you to demand money, see Item 32 of this section (the other side demands money by threatening to call the police or release photos).

entries.title: Targeted by online abuse: turn on protections and preserve evidence first, then choose among the platform, a court injunction, and reporting it to the police
entries.cost: No cost. Spend a dozen or so minutes right away setting up protections and preserving evidence. If you reach the point of applying for an injunction or bringing a private prosecution, you will need to go to court and may also need a lawyer. The hard part is preserving evidence while being abused instead of trading insults.
entries.summary: Do three things right away: turn on the platform’s protective settings, save the content using its quick evidence-preservation feature, and report it through the quick-reporting entry point. You can then apply to a court for an injunction ordering the person to stop. You can also bring a case in court yourself; if gathering evidence is difficult, you can ask the public security authorities for assistance. If there are serious consequences such as suicide and an egregious social impact, the procuratorate may prosecute the case instead.
entries.benefit: Article 15 of Fa Fa [2023] No. 14 concerns injunctions. The rights holder has evidence showing that the actor is committing or is about to commit an unlawful act infringing the rights holder’s personality rights. Unless the act is stopped promptly, the rights holder’s lawful rights and interests will suffer irreparable harm. If the rights holder applies under Article 997 of China’s Civil Code, the people’s court may issue a personality-rights infringement injunction in accordance with the law. Such an injunction is a court order telling the other side to stop first. Article 11 of the same guidance concerns evidence collection. In a private prosecution, “if the victim genuinely has difficulty providing evidence, the victim may request assistance from the public security authorities.” The public security authorities should promptly identify the actor and collect evidence concerning how the material spread and its impact. Online service providers should provide necessary technical support. “If evidence collected with the assistance of the public security authorities meets the conditions for accepting a private prosecution, the people’s court shall decide to file the case.” If evidence cannot be collected, the public security authorities should explain this in writing. A private prosecution is a case the victim must bring to court personally. Article 12 of the guidance lists five circumstances that should be deemed to “seriously endanger social order” under Article 246, paragraph 2, of China’s Criminal Law. First, causing serious consequences such as mental disorder or suicide for the victim or a close relative, with an egregious social impact. Second, arbitrarily targeting members of the general public, with information spreading widely and prompting many vulgar, malicious comments, and with an egregious social impact. Third, insulting or defaming multiple people or repeatedly disseminating the material, with an egregious social impact. Fourth, organizing or directing people to disseminate large amounts of material across multiple platforms, with an egregious social impact. Fifth, other circumstances. Article 4 of the guidance says that organizing “human flesh searches,” unlawfully collecting citizens’ personal information, and publishing it to an unspecified large number of people is punishable as the crime of infringing citizens’ personal information if the circumstances are serious. Article 23 of China’s Regulations on the Governance of Online Violence Information requires platforms to provide these protective options: blocking unfamiliar or specified users; limiting who can see information you post; prohibiting reposts or comments; and accepting private messages only from friends or refusing all private messages. Article 25 requires a quick evidence-preservation feature. Article 26 requires a prominent quick complaint and reporting entry point. Article 15 requires platforms that discover suspected unlawful or criminal conduct to report it promptly to the public security authorities.
entries.sources: Supreme People’s Court, Supreme People’s Procuratorate, and Ministry of Public Security of China (2023). Guiding Opinions on Punishing Online Violence and Related Unlawful and Criminal Acts in Accordance with the Law (Fa Fa [2023] No. 14, Articles 4, 11, 12, and 15). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/412992.html>; National People’s Congress of China (2020). Civil Code (Article 997). Full text reproduced by the Supreme People’s Procuratorate <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; Cyberspace Administration of China, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of Culture and Tourism, and National Radio and Television Administration (2024). Regulations on the Governance of Online Violence Information (Articles 15, 23, 25, and 26; effective August 1, 2024). State Council Gazette <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2024/issue_11526/202408/content_6969181.html>
entries.notes: The order is based on speed and cost: the platform is fastest and cheapest, so preserve evidence and report the abuse there first. Court is slowest and most expensive; decide afterward whether to bring a case. You bear the procedural costs of all three routes yourself. You must apply to the court yourself for an injunction. For a private prosecution, you must file the case in court yourself and provide the evidence yourself. For the procuratorate to take over and bring a public prosecution, the case must fall into one of the five circumstances listed in Article 12 of Fa Fa [2023] No. 14. Otherwise, you can only bring the case yourself. There are two things not to do. First, do not trade insults: insulting them back could make you the person penalized under Item 16 of this section (do not insult people or spread rumors online). Second, do not delete content in your own account; it is evidence. If you cannot cope, call China’s 12356 hotline; see Section 1, Item 25. For asking a platform to delete your personal information, see Section 14, Item 8. If you helped a stranger but were filmed and the footage was posted online, see [Should you stop when something happens to a stranger?](../docs/遇到陌生人出事该不该停.md).

entries.title: The law blocks “buy someone life insurance, then harm them” from the outset: you get none of the money, and intentional homicide and insurance fraud are punished together
entries.cost: No cost.
entries.summary: A contract for insurance payable upon the death of an adult family member is invalid if you buy it without that person’s knowledge. If the policyholder intentionally causes the insured person’s death, the insurer does not pay; someone who intentionally kills a person they would inherit from also loses inheritance rights. China’s Criminal Law specifically lists this kind of insurance fraud and requires it to be punished together with intentional homicide, for which the maximum penalty is death. You get none of the money.
entries.benefit: Article 34 of China’s Insurance Law: a contract under which insurance benefits are payable upon death is invalid unless the insured person consents and approves the insured amount. The insured person is the person covered by the policy. This restriction does not apply when parents insure their minor children. Article 39: when the policyholder designates a beneficiary, the insured person’s consent is required. The policyholder is the person who pays for the insurance; the beneficiary is the person who receives the money after the insured event. Article 43 concerns intentional harm. If the policyholder intentionally causes the insured person’s death, disability, or illness, the insurer is not liable to pay insurance benefits. If the policyholder has paid at least two years’ worth of premiums in full, the cash value is refunded to other persons entitled to it. If a beneficiary intentionally causes the insured person’s death, disability, or illness, or attempts to kill the insured person, that beneficiary loses the right to the benefits. Article 27, paragraph 2: if the policyholder or insured person intentionally causes an insured event, the insurer has the right to terminate the contract and is not liable to compensate or pay benefits; except as provided in Article 43, it does not refund the premiums. Article 1125 of China’s Civil Code: a person who intentionally kills someone they would inherit from loses the right to inherit. Article 198, paragraph 1, item 5, of China’s Criminal Law lists “a policyholder or beneficiary intentionally causing the death, disability, or illness of the insured person to obtain insurance benefits by fraud” as insurance fraud. If the amount is relatively large, the penalty is up to 5 years’ imprisonment and a fine of 10,000 to 100,000 yuan. If the amount is huge, the penalty is 5 to 10 years. If it is especially huge, the penalty is more than 10 years. Paragraph 2: if such conduct also constitutes another crime, it is punished under the rules for combined punishment of multiple crimes. Combined punishment means determining the sentence for several crimes together. Article 232: intentional homicide is punishable by death, life imprisonment, or at least ten years’ imprisonment. The example is the case of Zhang, whose given name includes the character Song, in Xuancheng, Anhui. In the early hours of July 18, 2016, he drove into a pond, and his wife drowned. Less than half a month before the incident, he had taken out four policies on his wife, each worth 1 million yuan. He was arrested on July 25. The court punished him for intentional homicide and insurance fraud together, sentencing him to death with a reprieve and fining him 50,000 yuan.
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress of China (amended 2015). Insurance Law of the People’s Republic of China, Articles 27, 34, 39, and 43. <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7c4060811>; National People’s Congress of China (2020). Civil Code of the People’s Republic of China, Article 1125. <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5c500bf>; Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress of China. Criminal Law of the People’s Republic of China (consolidated text as amended by Criminal Law Amendment XI), Articles 198 and 232. <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808181796a636a0179822a19640c92>; Legal Daily, reproduced by the Anhui Provincial People’s Procuratorate (2020-01-13). Wife-killing insurance fraud uncovers another case within the case (a typical case of supervision of false civil litigation by the Anhui Provincial People’s Procuratorate). <http://www.ah.jcy.gov.cn/jczt/jjslhyqkjc/mtjj/202001/t20200113_2758841.shtml>
entries.notes: The beneficiary of this entry is you: what it helps you avoid is a death sentence or life imprisonment. The death and the judgment in the example come from the original text of a typical case published by the procuratorial authorities; the main text includes no details beyond the investigative methods described there. Insurance fraud that does not involve a death, such as staging an accident or exaggerating a loss, is also a crime. People who help by giving testimony are implicated too; see Section 9, Item 21 (staging accidents or exaggerating losses to obtain insurance payouts). Buying insurance for family members is itself normal. The thought to guard against is “buy insurance, then harm them.” Treat an impulse to hurt a family member as an emergency; see Items 14 and 15 of this section (when you have the thought yourself; when someone close to you says something threatening).

entries.title: Ask for a case acceptance receipt when you report a crime; if the police do not open an investigation, ask for written notice: you can seek reconsideration within 7 days and then review within another 7 days, and the procuratorate can order the public security authorities to open a case
entries.cost: No cost. Ask one more question on the spot and get the case acceptance receipt. Then follow up on progress according to the deadlines above. The hard part is speaking up to ask, again and again.
entries.summary: When you report a crime to the police, get a case acceptance receipt on the spot; it proves you made the report. If the public security authorities decide not to open a case, they should give you a written notice of refusal to file a case. If you disagree, you can apply for reconsideration within 7 days and, if you still disagree, apply for review within a further 7 days. You can also ask the procuratorate to supervise the public security authorities’ decision to open a case.
entries.benefit: Article 171 of China’s Provisions on the Procedures for Handling Criminal Cases by Public Security Authorities (as amended by Ministry of Public Security Order No. 159) governs case acceptance receipts. It says: “When public security authorities accept a case, they shall prepare a case acceptance registration form and a case acceptance receipt, and give the receipt to the person who brought in the suspect, the person who reported the case, the complainant, or the informant.” Article 174: “The public security authorities shall promptly examine accepted cases or criminal leads they discover.” Article 178 governs whether a case is filed. If, after examining an accepted case, the authorities believe that a crime has occurred, criminal responsibility needs to be pursued, and the case falls within their jurisdiction, they must file it. Filing requires the approval of the head of a public security authority at county level or above. If they decide not to file a case, they must also give you a document: “For a case with a complainant, if the public security authorities decide not to file the case, they shall prepare a notice of refusal to file a case and deliver it to the complainant within three days.” Article 179 governs what to do if you disagree. It says: “If a complainant disagrees with a decision not to file a case, the complainant may, within seven days of receiving the notice of refusal to file a case, apply for reconsideration to the public security authority that made the decision; the public security authority shall make a decision within thirty days of receiving the application for reconsideration.” It continues: “If the complainant disagrees with the reconsideration decision not to file a case, the complainant may, within seven days of receiving the reconsideration decision, apply for review to the public security authority at the next higher level; that authority shall make a decision within thirty days of receiving the application for review. If the higher-level public security authority revokes the decision not to file a case, the lower-level public security authority shall implement that decision.” The time limits for reconsideration and review may be extended for major or complex cases, but the extension “must not exceed thirty days, and the applicant must be notified in writing.” Article 112 of China’s Criminal Procedure Law: a case should be filed if a crime is believed to have occurred and criminal responsibility needs to be pursued; if no case is filed, the authorities must “notify the complainant of the reasons for not filing.
