If the complainant disagrees, the complainant may apply for reconsideration.” Article 113: “If a victim believes that the public security authorities have failed to file and investigate a case that should be filed and investigated, and raises the matter with a people’s procuratorate, the people’s procuratorate shall require the public security authorities to explain their reasons for not filing. If the people’s procuratorate finds those reasons untenable, it shall notify the public security authorities to file the case, and the public security authorities shall do so upon receiving the notice.” Article 61 of China’s Provisions on the Procedures for Handling Administrative Cases by Public Security Authorities imposes the same requirement. For a case within the unit’s jurisdiction, it “shall immediately investigate and handle the case, prepare a case acceptance registration form and a case acceptance receipt, and give the receipt to the person who reported the case, the complainant, the informant, or the person who brought in the suspect.” The time limit for handling a public security administration case “shall not exceed 30 days from the date of acceptance; for a major or complex case, it may be extended by 30 days with the approval of the public security authority at the next higher level.” Time spent on expert examinations does not count toward the case-handling period. Article 9 of China’s Regulations on Supervision of Public Security Authorities governs complaints about police officers. It says: “For public complaints about ongoing unlawful conduct or disciplinary violations by public security authorities or their people’s police officers, supervisory bodies shall promptly dispatch officers, handle the matter on site in accordance with the rules, and promptly inform the complainant of the outcome” (nationwide in China).
entries.sources: National People’s Congress of China (2018). Criminal Procedure Law (amended 2018, Articles 112 and 113). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f135f46016f1d1b81b01351>; Ministry of Public Security of China (2020). Decision on Amending the Provisions on the Procedures for Handling Criminal Cases by Public Security Authorities (Ministry of Public Security Order No. 159) and the full amended text. <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2020/content_5549884.htm>; Ministry of Public Security of China (2013/amended 2019). Provisions on the Procedures for Handling Administrative Cases by Public Security Authorities (Ministry of Public Security Order No. 125, amended by Order No. 149). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2013/content_2321117.htm>, <http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2018-12/31/content_5428593.htm>; State Council of China (2011). Regulations on Supervision of Public Security Authorities (State Council Order No. 603, Article 9). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2011-09/08/content_6138.htm>
entries.notes: The beneficiary is yourself. Reporting an incident to the police does not guarantee that it will be handled immediately, but whether it is handled and how long it takes are governed by express statutory standards and deadlines, rather than depending on the mood of the officer taking the report that day. Keep three actions in mind in sequence: ① Obtain an case acceptance receipt (受案回执) on the spot, and record the case number and the accepting unit. ② If the deadline expires without an outcome, follow up on the progress according to the time limit mentioned above, asking "which procedural stage is the case currently at?" rather than "why aren't you looking after me?". ③ If you receive a notice of decision not to file a criminal case (不予立案通知书), first examine the grounds; request reconsideration within 7 days, and then seek a review within another 7 days. At the same time, you may petition the people's procuratorate for filing supervision (立案监督); these three paths do not conflict. Public security administrative cases refer to matters such as fights and petty theft. The statutory period for handling an administrative case is calculated from the date of acceptance, not exceeding 30 days. For major or complex cases, an extension of an additional 30 days may be granted upon approval by the public security organ at the next higher level. The time spent on forensic/expert evaluations is not included. If the reception attitude is poor, lodge a complaint through the supervisory inspection (督察) channel, while continuing to pursue the case itself through the case-filing procedures. Incidents such as picking up lost items or neighborhood disputes are not criminal cases in the first place. Public security organs will handle them as administrative cases or via mediation, or even merely record them on file; do not construe this as "a report is ignored". For the stop-payment process after being defrauded, see Item 2 of this section (Call 110 immediately to request a stop-payment). For experiencing cyberbullying, see Item 37 of this section (When facing cyberbullying, secure evidence first before choosing a course of action).

entries.title: Do not give cash or cards to case investigators and law enforcement personnel: Bribers themselves are sentenced, and bribing supervisory, law enforcement, or judicial personnel warrants even heavier penalties
entries.cost: Free. It is simply about not doing it.
entries.summary: "Spending a bit of money to settle a matter" constitutes an independent crime under the Criminal Law, and those who give money are also sentenced. The penalty for bribing is fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 3 years; where the circumstances are serious, 3 to 10 years; and where the circumstances are especially serious, not less than 10 years or life imprisonment. Offering bribes to supervisory, administrative law enforcement, or judicial personnel explicitly falls into the tier warranting heavier punishment. Giving money under extortion without obtaining illegitimate gains does not constitute bribery.
entries.benefit: Article 389 of the Criminal Law defines the crime of bribing: "Whoever, for the purpose of obtaining illegitimate gains, gives property to state functionaries commits the crime of offering bribes." The same article also provides: "Whoever, in economic activities, violates state provisions by giving property to state functionaries where the amount is relatively large, or violates state provisions by giving state functionaries rebates or service charges under any guise, shall be penalized for the crime of offering bribes." It also reserves an exception: "Whoever gives property to state functionaries due to extortion, without obtaining illegitimate gains, does not commit the crime of offering bribes." Sentencing is set forth in Article 390 of the Criminal Law (amended by Criminal Law Amendment (XII), effective March 1, 2024). The original text provides: "Whoever commits the crime of offering bribes shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years or criminal detention, and shall also be fined; if the circumstances are serious for seeking illegitimate gains through bribery, or if major losses are caused to national interests, the sentence shall be fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than ten years, and a fine; if the circumstances are especially serious, or if exceptionally grave losses are caused to national interests, the sentence shall be fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years or life imprisonment, and a fine or confiscation of property." There are seven statutory circumstances warranting heavier punishment: "(1) Offering bribes on multiple occasions or to multiple persons; (2) Offering bribes by state functionaries; (3) Offering bribes in national key engineering projects or major projects; (4) Offering bribes to seek promotion or adjustment in duties or ranks; (5) Offering bribes to supervisory, administrative law enforcement, or judicial personnel; (6) Offering bribes in fields such as ecological environment, finance and taxation, workplace safety, food and drugs, disaster prevention and relief, social security, education, and healthcare to carry out illegal and criminal activities; (7) Using illegal gains to offer bribes." The concluding paragraph reserves an avenue for leniency upon voluntary confession: "Any briber who voluntarily confesses their bribery acts prior to prosecution may be given a mitigated punishment or have their punishment reduced. Among them, those whose offenses are relatively minor, who play a critical role in breakthroughs in investigations or in solving major cases, or who perform major meritorious services, may receive a mitigated punishment or be exempted from punishment" (National).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China (Consolidated Text Amended by Criminal Law Amendment (XI)), Article 389. <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808181796a636a0179822a19640c92>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2023). Criminal Law Amendment (XII) of the People's Republic of China (Item 5, amending Article 390 of the Criminal Law; effective March 1, 2024). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081818c3ce31f018cb6a6bc412f55>
entries.notes: The beneficiary is yourself. Do not expect to escape punishment with a bribe. The other party has colleagues, logbooks, surveillance, and supervisory bodies. What you hand over serves as evidence against him when he is investigated, as well as evidence of your own crime; moreover, this category of bribery is explicitly classified under the harsher punishment tier. If you actually encounter the other party extorting perks, follow the channels described in Item 39 (Demand a case acceptance receipt on the spot when reporting to police). Retain the acceptance receipt and documents, and report the matter to supervisory inspection organs or discipline inspection and supervision organs. The exemption condition provided by Paragraph 3 of Article 389 of the Criminal Law is "being extorted and not obtaining illegitimate gains." Once you use this opportunity to obtain something you were not entitled to obtain, this condition no longer holds. Red packets (kickbacks) in hospitals follow a different set of rules; see Section 24, Item 11.

entries.title: For phone calls and face-to-face meetings that may turn sour, turn on recording directly: You do not need to obtain the other party's consent in advance for conversations you participate in
entries.cost: Free. Just turn on call recording on your phone or use a recording app. Record from start to finish, and preserve the original file after recording without editing or overwriting.
entries.summary: In matters of borrowing money, outstanding debts, compensation, refunds, and labor disputes, reaching an understanding over the phone without preserving a record can lead to conflicting stories from both sides months later. You may record conversations in which you personally participate; failing to notify the other party beforehand will not, solely on that ground, render it inadmissible as evidence. What is impermissible is wiretapping, intruding upon others' privacy, breaking into someone's home to make surreptitious recordings, or coercing the other party to speak.
entries.benefit: Article 66 of the Civil Procedure Law lists audio-visual materials and electronic data as evidence. Article 106 of the Supreme People's Court's Judicial Interpretation of the Civil Procedure Law excludes evidence obtained through only three methods. These three are: severely infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of others, violating mandatory statutory provisions, or seriously violating public order and good morals. "Failing to notify the other party in advance" does not fall within these three. Article 15 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Evidence: To use audio and video recordings as evidence, the original medium in which they are stored must be submitted, such as the original mobile phone. Article 90: Audio-visual materials and electronic data with questionable points cannot be used alone to establish facts. A judge's article republished on the official website of the Supreme People's Court also notes: Recordings must be lawfully obtained, truthful in content, unedited, and relevant to the case (National).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (Amended 2023, effective January 1, 2024). Civil Procedure Law (Article 66). Full text republished by Shanghai Municipal Development and Reform Commission <https://fgw.sh.gov.cn/ys-syjf-zc-2.4.1-h5/20240408/073febdb2b04464390546232d4089f51.html>; Supreme People's Court (Second Amendment 2022). Interpretation on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Article 106). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/353651.html>; Supreme People's Court (Amended 2019). Some Provisions on Evidence in Civil Procedures (Articles 14, 15, 90). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/212721.html>; Liu Danni (2023). Law in the Movie "Lost in the Stars" (People's Court Daily, republished on the official website of the Supreme People's Court). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/406032.html>
entries.notes: The beneficiaries are yourself and your family. In the recording, try to ensure that the people, events, monetary amounts, and time correspond accurately. Rather than merely asking "When will you give it to me?", you can naturally ask, "When do you plan to repay the 50,000 yuan borrowed from me last year?". Submit the recordings to the court, arbitration commission, or police; do not post them online. Publicly disclosing others' statements may trigger privacy and defamation disputes; see Item 16 of this section (Do not scold people or fabricate rumors online). Having a recording does not guarantee winning; the court must evaluate whether it is authentic and relevant in conjunction with other evidence. The recording only resolves whether an assertion can be proved; whether to actually file a lawsuit and how long it will take must be calculated separately. For materials that should be saved before resigning, see Section 19, Item 8 (Save pay stubs and attendance records before resigning). All the legal bases above are civil procedure rules; separate regulations govern the use of evidence in criminal and administrative cases.

entries.title: When an incident occurs on site: First capture a panoramic view, then capture the relative positions, and finally capture damage and injuries; do not delete original photos and videos
entries.cost: Free. Use a mobile phone to record continuously for several tens of seconds to several minutes. First ensure your own safety, without delaying rescuing persons or incident handling.
entries.summary: If you only take close-ups of a single scratch on a vehicle or an item on the ground, days later nobody will know where it originally was. First capture a wide panoramic video encompassing intersections, house numbers, vehicles, people, and the surroundings; then capture mutual relative positions; finally shoot details. If an item or vehicle must be moved, photograph it beforehand if possible. Retain the original photos and videos on your phone; do not merely keep a copy that has passed through chat apps.
entries.benefit: Article 66 of the Civil Procedure Law lists physical evidence, audio-visual materials, and electronic data as evidence. Article 14 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Evidence lists images, audio, and video as electronic data. Article 15 requires the submission of originals of electronic data; using video recordings as evidence requires submitting the original storage medium. Photographs and video recordings preserve the scene state that would otherwise quickly alter, allowing cross-verification with police records, maintenance records, medical records, and witness accounts. The sequence of "panoramic view, relative positions, details" is an empirical practice; it is not stipulated by law (National).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (Amended 2023, effective January 1, 2024). Civil Procedure Law (Article 66). Full text republished by Shanghai Municipal Development and Reform Commission <https://fgw.sh.gov.cn/ys-syjf-zc-2.4.1-h5/20240408/073febdb2b04464390546232d4089f51.html>; Supreme People's Court (Amended 2019). Some Provisions on Evidence in Civil Procedures (Articles 14, 15). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/212721.html>
entries.notes: The beneficiaries are yourself and your family. Rated C because the shooting sequence is merely empirical experience; legal statutes only govern that photos and video recordings can serve as evidence and require originals to be submitted. If someone is injured, or there is fire, gas leaks, or other hazards, prioritize rescuing persons and moving out of danger first; do not delay for the sake of taking pictures. For actions to take at a traffic accident scene, see Item 1 of this section (In a traffic accident: Stop, rescue, and report to police first).

entries.title: When facing domestic violence: Call the police first to preserve a police response record, then petition the court for a personal safety protection order; no prior divorce required, and no fee charged
entries.cost: Free. Applying for a personal safety protection order requires no litigation fees and no security/guarantee. What it costs is time spent reporting to the police, having injuries examined, and drafting the application. The hardest part is broaching the subject with family members.
entries.summary: According to multi-country data, over one-third of murdered women are killed by their intimate partners, often as the culmination of chronic domestic violence. Among battered women, those who have been strangled face more than 7 times the risk of being murdered compared to those who have not. Therefore, if beaten, call the police immediately, and then apply to the court for a protection order. The court must generally give an answer within 72 hours.
entries.benefit: First, the risks. Pooling data from 66 countries (systematic review): in female homicide cases, 38.6% were committed by intimate partners, compared to 6.3% for men. The authors noted that such homicides are often the final step in an escalating history of abuse. Another study compared 506 homicides and attempted homicides with 427 women who experienced physical abuse without such outcomes: those previously strangled by their partner faced 6.70 times the odds of attempted homicide compared to those not strangled (OR 6.70, 95% CI 3.91–11.49), and 7.48 times the odds of homicide (OR 7.48, 95% CI 4.53–12.35). Next, the law. Victims and close relatives can report to the police. Public security organs must respond in a timely manner, stop domestic violence, investigate and collect evidence, and assist with medical care and injury verification. Where the circumstances are relatively minor, the public security organ may issue an admonition letter (告诫书) to the perpetrator. Persons suffering domestic violence or facing realistic dangers of domestic violence may apply to the court for a personal safety protection order. The court must make a ruling within 72 hours of acceptance, or within 24 hours in emergency situations. Protection orders can prohibit the perpetrator from committing domestic violence; prohibit harassing, stalking, or contacting you and your close relatives; and order the perpetrator to move out of your residence. A protection order is valid for up to 6 months and can be extended upon application before expiration. The application is not conditioned upon divorce. The court may issue it as long as it determines there is a "relatively high likelihood" of domestic violence. If the other party violates the protection order, the court may impose a fine of up to 1,000 yuan or administrative detention of up to 15 days. Where a crime is constituted, the matter is handled under the crime of refusing to execute a judgment or ruling. Regular insults, threats, stalking, harassment, as well as freezing and starvation, also constitute domestic violence.
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2015). Anti-Domestic Violence Law (Articles 2, 13, 15, 16, 19, 23, 28, 29, 30, 34). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7f9d60889>; Supreme People's Court (2022). Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Personal Safety Protection Order Cases (Fa Shi [2022] No. 17, Articles 1, 3, 6, 10, 12). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/366021.html>; Supreme People's Court (2016). Reply on Relevant Procedural Issues Concerning Personal Safety Protection Order Cases (Fa Shi [2016] No. 15, Items 1, 2). Full text republished by Pingyuan County People's Court <http://qdzy.sdcourt.gov.cn/dzpyfy/393141/393283/1461545/index.html>; Stöckl H et al. (2013). The global prevalence of intimate partner homicide: a systematic review. Lancet. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(13)61030-2>; Glass N et al. (2008). Non-fatal strangulation is an important risk factor for homicide of women. Journal of Emergency Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jemermed.2007.02.065>
entries.notes: The beneficiaries are primarily yourself and your family. Homicide proportions are derived from foreign data; China has no publicly available statistics under the identical definition. Gather evidence: police response records, admonition letters, injury assessment results, medical records, written guarantees written by the other party, chat logs, and audio recordings can all be used. For audio recordings, see Item 41 of this section (Audio recording). Protection orders do not require hiring a lawyer, and decisions are generally made within several days. Filing for divorce or seeking compensation constitutes a separate lawsuit; ordinary first-instance civil procedures are stipulated to conclude within 6 months and may be extended, with attorney fees borne by oneself. Domestic violence victims can seek legal aid, and courts may defer, reduce, or waive court costs. A protection order does not equate to guaranteed personal safety; call 110 first if facing immediate danger. Where victims are coerced or intimidated and unable to apply personally, close relatives, public security organs, women's federations, neighborhood committees, or village committees may apply on their behalf. If the victim is a friend or colleague, you can accompany them to report to the police and visit the hospital. If you witness a stranger being beaten in their home, calling 110 is sufficient. Do not step in to intervene physically yourself; the rationale is in Section 13, Item 37 (Coming across a group brawl). For how to structure child custody and visitation during divorce, see Section 10, Item 23 (Child support and visitation).

entries.title: When a family member incurs debts from gambling, do not rush to pay on their behalf: Gambling debts are not protected by law, and money borrowed for gambling does not count as joint spousal debt
entries.cost: Free. The difficulty lies in withholding money when creditors come knocking and family members plead in tears. If the creditor actually files a lawsuit, you must respond to the suit.
entries.summary: Debts incurred at the gambling table are not protected by courts. Where creditors lend money knowing full well that it is borrowed for gambling, the court also does not protect the sum. Money borrowed by one spouse for gambling cannot be deemed a joint debt to be repaid by both. Without judicial trial, courts cannot require the non-borrowing spouse to bear liability on their behalf.
entries.benefit: The 2017 Notice of the Supreme People's Court set out four points. Debts incurred by one party in illegal and criminal activities such as gambling or drug use shall not be granted legal protection. Where creditors knew or should have known that the borrowed funds were to be used for gambling or drug abuse and still lent the money, legal protection shall not be granted. Where one party borrows money in their own name to engage in illegal and criminal activities and requests that it be treated as joint spousal debt, the court shall not support it. Without undergoing trial proceedings, the non-borrowing party cannot be required to bear civil liability (National, effective 2017).
entries.sources: Supreme People's Court (2017). Notice on Properly Adjudicating Cases Involving Spousal Debts in Accordance with the Law (Fa [2017] No. 48, Articles 2, 4). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/36982.html>
entries.notes: Rated B because this is an internal court notice without quantitative figures, and whether creditors had knowledge depends on evidence. This notice was issued under the Marriage Law at the time. For how joint spousal debt is determined after the implementation of the Civil Code, see Section 10, Item 12 (Large debts borrowed by a spouse). For loans where the creditor was unaware that the funds were used for gambling, repayment is still required, but only by the borrowing party personally. Proving that the funds were used for gambling requires bank transaction records, gambling platform records, or public security disposition records, which should be preserved routinely. If a creditor actually sues, standard first-instance procedures are stipulated to conclude within 6 months and can be extended; summary procedures take 3 months. Each party covers their own attorney fees, which are not borne by the losing party. If creditors come to block or detain people at your door, see Section 9, Item 15 (Collecting debts without detaining people), and call the police directly. If the person themselves is in despair to the point of being suicidal from gambling, see Section 1, Item 37 (When gambling leads to borrowing to gamble, call 12356 first). The beneficiaries are primarily spouses and direct relatives.

entries.title: When an acquaintance asks you to "help do a facial scan and serve as a witness" to process a loan, or asks you to read out a verification code, do not agree: This is called an AB loan—the borrower is you, not a guarantor
entries.cost: Free. The difficulty lies in refusing relatives and friends to their faces. Even if the other party says "it's just being a witness" or "you won't have to bear responsibility", refuse just the same. Do not hand your mobile phone, ID card, or bank cards over to brokers, and do not perform facial scans or sign documents according to a broker's arrangements. Verification codes are for your own use only; do not read them out even if asked by acquaintances.
entries.summary: The so-called "helping do a facial scan and serving as a witness" is actually borrowing money from the bank in your name. The borrower is you, not a guarantor; after the money is transferred to the acquaintance, the bank will still pursue you for repayment. Even though the broker deceived you, as long as the bank had no knowledge, you cannot revoke this loan contract. A letter of commitment written to you by an acquaintance stating "I will repay it" has no binding effect on the bank.
entries.benefit: A 2022 risk alert from the Fujian Regulatory Bureau of the National Financial Regulatory Administration described this scheme. Customer A did not qualify for a loan. The intermediary said A needed a guarantor and told A to find B, who had good qualifications. But when arranging the loan, the intermediary used B’s identity information to apply, and A received the money. The alert said that “B was the borrower in substance” and that B “did not know they were the borrower rather than a guarantor until the bank sought repayment.” A 2024 alert from the Shandong Regulatory Bureau said intermediaries would promise B that they “would bear no responsibility.” The intermediary would also coach B in advance on how to answer the bank’s questions before the loan was approved. In fact, B would apply as the borrower. In 2024, the Shanghai Putuo District Court published a case in which a salesperson used B’s phone to download a bank app and applied for a loan directly in B’s name. The money entered B’s account, B transferred it to A, and A paid more than 80,000 yuan in fees. Eight members of the intermediary group were sentenced to between 10 months and 4 years for contract fraud. The intermediary’s conviction does not transfer the loan to someone else. Article 149 of the Civil Code says that when a third party commits fraud, the deceived party can request cancellation only if the other party “knew or should have known” about it. The other party here is the bank; if the bank did not know, the contract cannot be cancelled on that basis. Where cancellation is possible, the request must be made to a court within 1 year of learning of the fraud (Article 152). Borrowers must repay by the agreed deadline (Article 675). A contract binds only the people who entered into it (Article 465). Transferring the debt to someone else requires the bank’s consent (Article 551). So a written promise from A does not bind the bank. B can only sue A to recover the money. Courts also uphold the contract when someone completes facial recognition for another person without reading it. In a case concluded in 2025 by the Shizhong District Court in Neijiang, Jiang borrowed from a small-loan company but could not obtain the loan alone. Without Zhang’s knowledge, Zhang’s son gave Jiang her identity information so that she could be a co-borrower. The loan process required Zhang herself to complete facial recognition. She did, but did not read the contract. The court said she “should have foreseen the importance and legal consequences of facial recognition” and ordered her and Jiang to repay the remaining principal of more than 60,000 yuan together. The Electronic Signature Law states that “a reliable electronic signature has the same legal effect as a handwritten signature or seal.” The Anti-Telecommunications and Online Fraud Law provides that no one “may assist with real-name verification”; violations are punishable by a fine and, in serious cases, detention. An ordinary first-instance civil procedure is, by law, to be concluded within 6 months, though the period can be extended. Lawyers’ fees are not among statutory litigation costs and must be paid by the person hiring the lawyer (China nationwide).

Measures for the Payment of Litigation Costs (State Council Order No. 481, Article 6). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_6929.htm>; Sichuan Chang’an Network (operated by the Political and Legal Affairs Commission of the CPC Sichuan Provincial Committee; source: Sichuan Legal Daily) (2025). One Facial-Recognition Scan Left Her Liable for a Loan of Tens of Thousands of Yuan; Court: The Party Should Have Foreseen the Importance and Legal Consequences of Facial Recognition (September 23, 2025). <https://www.sichuanpeace.gov.cn/azsf/20250923/2992615.html>; Xinzhou Intermediate People’s Court, Shanxi Province (reposting People’s Court Daily) (2021).
