entries.notes: You are the beneficiary. Fire prevention zones and periods are designated and announced by local governments at or above the county level. They vary by place, so check local announcements before going up a mountain. The Ministry of Emergency Management states that forest fires are frequent and particularly common during the Qingming Festival. The fines apply only within fire prevention zones during fire prevention periods. The crime of negligently causing a fire does not depend on either: if you accidentally start a fire that meets the threshold for opening a case, it applies. In both cases, the defendants received suspended sentences only after turning themselves in or actively fighting the fire and replanting. Forest restoration costs are separate and can be much higher than fines. When reporting a fire, clearly state the county, township, village, and mountain, how large the fire is, and your phone number. You can also call China's 119 emergency number; the Xie Moujun case records that he voluntarily called the fire and rescue emergency number after the fire started. The fine amounts cited in many online articles come from two 2008 fire prevention regulations that were repealed in 2026. If the fire grows large, do not try to fight it yourself. Seek shelter in an open area without vegetation, an area that has already burned, or beside a stream; do not run with the wind.

entries.title: When taking civil service, graduate school, driving licence, or professional qualification exams, do not take an exam for someone else, have someone take it for you, buy or sell answers, or help organize cheating
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Do not believe claims about “guaranteed-pass classes,” “VIP channels,” or groups selling answers. Do not bring phones, earphones, or other devices that can send or receive information into the exam room. If you do not pass, prepare again for the next sitting. The hard part comes when you miss the passing score by just a few points and someone offers to guarantee that you will pass for a price.
entries.summary: Having someone else take an exam for you or taking one for someone else are both crimes. You may be sentenced to criminal detention and fined; anyone who becomes a civil servant through exam impersonation is dismissed from public office. Organizing cheating or selling answers is punishable by up to seven years. Driving licence exams count too: a driving school owner was sentenced for organizing students to cheat. If the conduct does not amount to a crime, the exam result is invalidated, and you may also be barred from exams or from retaking the exam for one year.
entries.benefit: Article 284-1 of China’s Criminal Law covers four types of conduct, provided the exam is a “national examination prescribed by law.” Organizing cheating is punishable by up to 3 years’ imprisonment or criminal detention, together with or instead of a fine. In serious circumstances, the sentence is 3 to 7 years. Providing cheating equipment or other assistance to an organizer carries a penalty in the same range. Selling or supplying answers for the purpose of cheating also carries a penalty in the same range. Taking an exam for someone else, or having someone else take it for you, is the crime of taking an exam by proxy, punishable by criminal detention or public surveillance, together with or instead of a fine. The 2019 judicial interpretation by China’s Supreme People’s Court and Supreme People’s Procuratorate specifies which exams count. The national college entrance examination, postgraduate entrance examination, self-study higher education examinations, and adult college entrance examination count, as do central and local civil service examinations. Qualification examinations for legal professionals, teachers, certified public accountants, physicians, and construction engineers also count. In 2024, the Supreme People’s Court stated explicitly that driving licence examinations belong to this category too. Organizing cheating in the national college entrance examination, postgraduate entrance examination, or civil service examination automatically counts as “serious circumstances.” So does organizing cheating involving 30 or more instances of examinee participation, or obtaining at least 300,000 yuan in illegal proceeds. If someone is caught before an exam begins but has already obtained its questions and answers, the crime still counts as completed. Answers sold need not be complete or entirely correct for a conviction. A person who takes an exam by proxy may receive a suspended sentence if the circumstances are relatively minor, or may not be prosecuted if they are minor. According to Supreme People’s Court statistics, 11,146 people were sentenced for these three crimes between November 2015 and April 2024. Conduct that does not amount to a crime is handled under the rules for the relevant exam. In China’s national education examinations, using a device to receive answers or having someone else take the exam invalidates the result and can also lead to a ban on taking exams for 1 to 3 years. In civil service examinations, taking an exam by proxy or participating in organized cheating leads to disqualification, an entry in the person’s integrity record, and a long-term record of the violation. Anyone already employed is dismissed or expelled if the violation is discovered. Cheating in a driving licence examination leads to disqualification, invalidation of subjects already passed, a fine of up to 2,000 yuan, and a one-year ban on reapplying for a driving licence. Someone who takes a driving licence examination for another person has their own driving licence revoked and cannot reapply for 3 years. Official case one: a group led by a person surnamed Zhang, with the given name Jie, used composite photographs and fake identity cards to have stand-ins take civil service and other national examinations for candidates 89 times. The three ringleaders received sentences ranging from 5 years to 5 years and 6 months. Eighteen candidates who hired stand-ins were sentenced for taking an exam by proxy to 2 to 4 months’ criminal detention and fined 30,000 to 100,000 yuan. People who became civil servants through proxy exam taking were dismissed from public office. Official case two: from 2017 to 2023, the owner of a driving school organized students to cheat in driving licence examinations. The methods included altering examination system data, having instructors take exams by proxy, and giving students earpieces for remote prompts. The owner was sentenced to 6 years and 6 months, including for bribery; the other 23 people received sentences ranging from 6 months to 1 year and 10 months (nationwide).

entries.notes: You yourself are the beneficiary. Simply looking at someone else’s answers yourself or wearing an earpiece to receive answers is not listed as a crime in the statutory provision; it is handled under the exam rules above. But passing purchased answers on to classmates becomes the unlawful provision of exam questions and answers. In a case involving leaked questions for the Level II Construction Engineer examination, candidates resold answers through successive intermediaries, and someone posted them in a QQ group with more than 1,700 members. If a student takes an exam by proxy or has someone else take one for them, the examination body will notify the school, which may expel the student. Employer recruitment exams and school final exams are not “national examinations,” but using eavesdropping or covert photography devices, or creating a group to distribute cheating information, may still be punished as other crimes. In official case one, the person who made fake identity cards for the stand-ins was sentenced to 3 years for forging identity documents. For identity documents, see Item 16 of this section (Do not lend your identity card to anyone). For paying an intermediary to obtain a professional title assessment on your behalf, see Item 22 of Section 23 (Do not hire an intermediary to obtain a professional title assessment on your behalf).

chapters.title: Are Dating and Marriage Worth It?
chapters.intro:
This section breaks “Is marriage worth it?” into separate calculations for money, time, health, legal risk, and relationship quality. Each calculation uses only figures with traceable sources: official statistics or meta-analyses (which pool data from multiple studies and analyze them again). This section makes no moral judgment and does not draw a conclusion for you. The health calculations use mortality risk; the time calculations use minutes per day; and the legal calculations use the wording of statutory provisions. These three approaches are not converted into one another. For the method of breaking down the calculations, a fill-in checklist, and common misconceptions, see [docs/Is Marriage Worth It.md](../docs/结婚划不划算.md).

The items in this section are grouped by topic below, with item numbers in parentheses.

**Meeting people and dating**: Meet more people (Item 1), stop after the other person rejects you (Item 2), judge interest by behavior (Item 3), take turns answering questions that gradually get more personal (Item 5), and long-distance relationships are no worse than local ones (Item 6).

**Relationship quality**: Consider how you feel in the relationship (Item 4), argue about the issue rather than attacking the person (Item 17), and attend couples therapy together (Item 20).

**The calculations behind whether marriage is worth it**: Start with marriage registration data (Item 7), discount health benefits based on observational data (Item 8), calculate the time cost using unpaid labor (Item 9), calculate the cost of leaving (Item 15), keep a separate account of marriage for the sake of older family members (Item 16), and specify child support and visitation clearly when divorcing (Item 23).

**Marriage registration and premarital health checks**: An identity card is all you need to register a marriage (Item 13), get a premarital health check (Item 14), and obtain a marriage certificate even if you have held a wedding banquet (Item 21).

**Money and debt**: Start with the legal default rules for finances (Item 10), specify whether parents’ money for a home is a loan or a gift (Item 11), consider a large debt incurred by one spouse (Item 12), and consider a spouse using shared money to tip a livestreamer or transfer money to someone outside the marriage (Item 22).

**Same-sex partners and sexual orientation**: Same-sex partners should arrange a voluntary guardianship agreement and wills (Item 18), and do not marry by concealing your sexual orientation (Item 19).

entries.title: Meet more people instead of fixating on one: you cannot predict whether two people will be compatible before they meet
entries.cost: No money. Spend your time meeting more people instead of repeatedly thinking about the same person. The hard part is resisting the urge to fixate.
entries.summary: In two speed-dating studies, participants completed more than 100 questionnaire items about partner preferences before meeting. The questionnaires could predict who tended to like others in general and who tended to be popular in general, but not whether two particular people would have chemistry. You can only learn whether you are compatible after meeting. So meeting more people is a better use of your time than betting everything on one person.
entries.benefit: In two speed-dating studies, participants completed more than 100 self-report measures related to partner choice (questionnaires in which people rated themselves) before meeting. The researchers used a random forest model (an algorithm for finding patterns) to make predictions. The questionnaires could predict “how readily a person tends to like others overall,” explaining 4%–18% of the variance. Variance means differences between people; the questionnaires explained only a small part of those differences. They could also predict “how popular a person tends to be overall,” explaining 7%–27%. But they could not predict “whether these two particular people would have chemistry”: no combination of traits and preferences measured before the meeting could do so. The same researchers had earlier conducted another speed-dating experiment. Before meeting, participants reported their ideal-partner preferences, such as whether they valued looks or financial prospects more. Those preferences did not predict their interest in any particular person at the event.
entries.sources: Joel S, Eastwick PW, Finkel EJ (2017). Is romantic desire predictable? Machine learning applied to initial romantic attraction. Psychological Science, 28(10), 1478-1489. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797617714580>；Eastwick PW, Finkel EJ (2008). Sex differences in mate preferences revisited: do people know what they initially desire in a romantic partner? Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 94(2), 245-264. <https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.94.2.245>
entries.notes: The two studies show only that compatibility “cannot be calculated before meeting”; they do not say that “no amount of effort helps.” You can only find out whether you are compatible after meeting, so it is worth spending time getting to know more people and actually meeting each one, rather than putting all your hopes on one person. All the study participants were university students in Europe and North America. China’s dating and marriage environment is different, so discount the findings when applying them to yourself.

entries.title: Stop after the other person clearly rejects you: continued harassment violates China’s public security law; it is not “sincerity”
entries.cost: No money or time. The hard part is holding back: stop sending messages and stop waiting for the person.
entries.summary: If the other person has clearly said no and you repeatedly message them or wait for them, interfering with their normal life, that has been a violation of China’s public security law since January 2026. The penalty can be up to 5 days’ detention or a fine of up to 1,000 yuan. In more serious circumstances, the penalty is 5 to 10 days’ detention. The public security authorities may also order you not to contact the person; violating that order brings another 5 to 10 days’ detention.
entries.benefit: China’s Public Security Administration Punishments Law, effective January 1, 2026, lists harassment and stalking as a separate offence. The provision covers “repeatedly sending obscene, insulting, threatening, or similar messages, or using methods such as harassment, persistent pestering, or stalking to interfere with another person’s normal life.” This conduct is punishable by up to five days’ detention or a fine of up to 1,000 yuan. In more serious circumstances, the penalty is five to ten days’ detention and may include a fine of up to 1,000 yuan. This provision adds another measure: with approval from the head of a public security organ, the offender may be ordered not to contact the person harmed for a specified period. Violating the no-contact order brings a further five to ten days’ detention.
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (revised 2025). Public Security Administration Punishments Law (Article 50, paragraph 1, item 5 and paragraph 2; Article 136). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml> (reposted by the Supreme People’s Procuratorate)
entries.notes: No research supports the idea that “pursuing someone relentlessly will win them over,” but detention and no-contact orders are written explicitly into law. Records of these violations must be sealed and may not be provided or disclosed to ordinary organizations or individuals, although relevant organizations may access them under national rules. The law looks at whether you repeatedly harassed, pestered, or stalked the person and interfered with their normal life, not at what you intended. Continuing after the other person has clearly rejected you is the situation most likely to be considered interference; that last sentence is the author’s judgment.

entries.title: To judge whether someone is interested, look at behavior rather than “signals”: who initiates, who makes plans, and who follows up
entries.cost: No money and not much time. The hard part is changing your habits: stop analyzing the other person’s expressions and tone, and start recording what actually happens.
entries.summary: When strangers of different sexes talk for about ten minutes and then judge each other, they are fairly accurate at identifying “the other person was not flirting,” but have much more trouble recognizing “the other person was flirting.” So do not draw conclusions from expressions and tone in a single conversation alone. People who feel more attracted to someone are more likely to initiate messages and arrange meetings afterward, although that association is weak.
entries.benefit: Two studies measured how accurately people recognize flirting. The first had 52 pairs of strangers of different sexes talk for 10 to 12 minutes. Afterward, each person reported whether they had been flirting and whether they thought the other person had been flirting. The result was that “interactions without flirting were judged more accurately, while interactions with flirting were judged less accurately.” The second study asked 261 observers to judge 26 one-minute videos and reached the same conclusion. People can identify “the other person was not flirting” fairly reliably but have difficulty identifying “the other person was flirting.” A third study examined behavior. It combined three speed-dating events involving 559 people and more than 6,600 dates, then followed the participants. The more someone’s attraction to a particular person stood out during the meeting, the more likely they were to message and ask that person out afterward. The average correlation coefficient for these associations was about 0.15 (a weak association). This shows that interest is expressed in behaviors such as initiating contact and arranging meetings. But the study did not compare whether behavior or facial expressions and tone were more accurate indicators.
entries.sources: Hall JA, Xing C, Brooks S (2015). Accurately detecting flirting: error management theory, the traditional sexual script, and flirting base rate. Communication Research, 42(7), 939-958. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0093650214534972>; Perilloux C, Kurzban R (2015). Do men overperceive women's sexual interest? Psychological Science, 26(1), 70-77. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797614555727> (the side raising the dispute); Baxter A, Maxwell JA, Bales KL, Finkel EJ, Impett EA, Eastwick PW (2022). Initial impressions of compatibility and mate value predict later dating and romantic interest. PNAS, 119(45), e2206925119. <https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2206925119>
entries.notes: There is a dispute. Other research argues that men do not overestimate women’s sexual intentions; instead, women underreport their own intentions on questionnaires. There is still no conclusion about who judges more accurately. Neither of the first two studies measured behavioral cues. The third shows that attraction is expressed through messaging and arranging meetings. But no study has directly compared whether “behavior is a more accurate guide than expressions and tone”; that is the author’s inference. The author suggests looking at whether the other person initiates contact, makes plans for the next meeting, and follows up even when you do not take the lead.

entries.title: To judge whether a relationship is good, focus mainly on how you feel in it, rather than your partner’s credentials
entries.cost: No money and not much time. The hard part is changing your perspective: put away the partner checklist and pay attention to how you get along.
entries.summary: The strongest indicators of relationship quality are your own feelings, not your partner’s credentials. Examples include whether you feel your partner is committed, whether you feel appreciated, and how often you argue. Your own reports are two to four times as useful for prediction as your partner’s reports. But questionnaires can barely predict whether the relationship will improve or worsen later.
entries.benefit: A machine-learning analysis of 43 longitudinal datasets of couples from 29 laboratories—longitudinal means recording the same couples over time—found that the strongest predictors of relationship quality all came from a person’s feelings about the relationship: perceived partner commitment, appreciation, sexual satisfaction, perceived partner satisfaction, and conflict. Among factors concerning the individual, the strongest were life satisfaction, negative emotions, depression, avoidant attachment, and anxious attachment. At the start of the studies, the relationship factors could explain at most 45% of the variance. Variance here means differences in relationship quality between couples; 45% is the portion of those differences these factors could account for. By the end of the studies, they explained at most 18%. What is more, the predictive power of “factors you reported yourself” was two to four times that of “factors your partner reported.” Adding individual differences and the partner’s reports to a person’s own reported feelings about the relationship provided no additional predictive power. Whether a relationship improved or worsened during the study could barely be predicted from any combination of self-reported measures; the original wording is “largely unpredictable from any combination of self-report variables.”
entries.sources: Joel S, Eastwick PW, Allison CJ, et al. (2020). Machine learning uncovers the most robust self-report predictors of relationship quality across 43 longitudinal couples studies. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 117(32), 19061-19071. <https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1917036117>
entries.notes: To judge whether your current relationship is good, asking how you feel is more accurate than checking your partner against a list of credentials. But do not expect to predict what the relationship will be like later. For the calculation linking relationship quality and physical health, see Item 17 of this section (Treat relationship quality as part of your health calculation).

entries.title: To grow closer, take turns answering a set of questions that gradually get more personal; do not rely on scripted lines
entries.cost: No money. It takes 45 minutes.
entries.summary: Two strangers who took turns answering 36 questions that gradually became more personal felt closer after 45 minutes than people who spent the same amount of time making small talk. What mattered was taking turns speaking honestly and gradually going deeper, not scripted lines. This shows only that they felt closer at the time; it does not mean a long-term relationship will develop.
entries.benefit: Researchers paired people who did not know each other and had them take turns answering three sets of increasingly personal questions, 36 in total. The questions ranged from “Who would you most like to invite to dinner?” to “When was the last time you cried in front of someone else?” After 45 minutes, their sense of closeness was significantly greater than that of a control group that made small talk for the same length of time. It was also greater than the average rating the university students in the study gave their closest real-life relationships.
entries.sources: Aron A, Melinat E, Aron EN, Vallone RD, Bator RJ (1997). The experimental generation of interpersonal closeness: a procedure and some preliminary findings. Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin, 23(4), 363-377. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0146167297234003>
entries.notes: Only one experiment has been conducted. Its participants were university students, and it measured closeness only over a short period; it did not test whether a long-term relationship could develop. The closeness in the experiment came from two people taking turns and gradually sharing deeper truths about themselves. It did not depend on scripted lines, tactics, or one-sided performance. So a useful approach in conversation is, “I’ll share something real and ask a question that goes just as deep,” with both people taking turns.

entries.title: Long-distance relationships are no worse than local ones; the real hurdle is the first three months after moving together
entries.cost: There are travel costs and time spent on the round trip. You see each other less often than couples who live in the same city. The hard part is coping with not seeing each other over the long term.
entries.summary: Long-distance relationships were actually more stable while the partners lived apart. Researchers think this is because it is easy to imagine your partner as better than they really are: the less often you meet, the more idealized they become. The real hurdle comes after moving together. In the tracking data, about half of the long-distance couples reached the point of living in the same city; the other half ended their relationships while still apart. Of those who reunited, one-third broke up within 3 months.
entries.benefit: Two studies reached consistent conclusions. Long-distance relationships are actually more stable during the period of separation than geographically close relationships. The reason is that in long-distance relationships, the degree of idealizing the partner—thinking they are better than they actually are—is significantly higher; the studies measured idealization distortion, romantic love, relationship reminiscence, and perceived agreement. Moreover, the less they see each other, the more idealized the thinking becomes. However, this stability holds only while the two parties remain separated; once they become geographically close, long-distance couples are more prone to breaking up. The study tracking the transition from long-distance to geographically close gave the following proportion: about half of long-distance couples made it to the step of moving in together, while the other half ended during the separation. Among the half that reunited, one-third broke up within 3 months after reuniting. Changes after reunion reported by participants included: loss of autonomous space, learning more about both the good and the bad of the partner, difficulties in scheduling time, and increased conflict and jealousy. The longer the interval between meetings during the separation and the stronger the idealization, the less stable the relationship was after reuniting
entries.sources: Stafford L, Merolla AJ, Castle JD (2006). When long-distance dating partners become geographically close. Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, 23(6), 901-919. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0265407506070472>; Stafford L, Merolla AJ (2007). Idealization, reunions, and stability in long-distance dating relationships. Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, 24(1), 37-54. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0265407507072578>; Dargie E et al. (2015). Journal of Sex & Marital Therapy, 41(2), 181-202. <https://doi.org/10.1080/0092623X.2013.864367> (the long-distance study in the notes)
entries.notes: The subjects were dating relationships among American college students, not including marriages, and from an earlier period, so do not directly apply the absolute proportions. Another study surveyed 717 individuals in long-distance relationships and 425 individuals in geographically close relationships. Differences in relationship quality between the two types were very small; whether a relationship is good mainly depends on the respective circumstances of the two individuals and the relationship itself, not distance. Therefore, when deciding whether to do long-distance, do not use "long-distance always ends in breakup" as a reason. What needs advance preparation are the few months after reuniting, when autonomous space decreases, mutual knowledge increases, and conflicts and jealousy also increase

entries.title: Look at registration data before listening to elders: What are the statistical criteria for marriage and divorce rates
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Read through the marriage registration section in the Ministry of Civil Affairs' annual statistical bulletin, which takes a few minutes.
entries.summary: In 2024, 6.106 million couples registered for marriage nationwide, down 20% from the previous year, and 3.513 million couples divorced. Claims online that the divorce rate exceeds half divide these two numbers to get about 57.5%. But those divorcing and those marrying are not the same group of people, so this cannot be interpreted as half of marriages ending in divorce. The marriage rate of 4.3‰ and divorce rate of 2.5‰ in the bulletin are calculated by dividing by the national population.
entries.benefit: In 2024, 6.106 million couples nationwide legally registered for marriage, a 20.5% decrease compared to the previous year, with a crude marriage rate of 4.3‰. In the same year, 3.513 million couples legally handled divorce procedures, among which 2.622 million couples registered for divorce with civil affairs departments, and 891,000 couples divorced via court judgment and mediation. The crude divorce rate was 2.5‰. The bulletin notes that the marriage (divorce) rate = number of couples married (divorced) in the current year / average total population in the current year × 1000‰. This is a "crude rate," where the denominator is the entire population, not the married population
entries.sources: Ministry of Civil Affairs (2025). Statistical Bulletin on the Development of Civil Affairs in 2024 (Section V(II)1 Marriage Registration Services, Note 5), web and PDF versions. <https://www.mca.gov.cn/n1288/n1294/n1554/c1662004999980006190/content.html>, <https://www.mca.gov.cn/gdnps/n2445/n2451/n2458/n2681/c1662004999980006189/attr/400985.pdf>
entries.notes: The common online claim of a "divorce rate over 50%" divides the number of couples divorced in a given year by the number of couples married in that year: 351.3 / 610.6 ≈ 57.5%. This is called the "divorce-to-marriage ratio." The two numbers being divided do not represent the same group of people, nor does this indicator exist in the bulletin, so it cannot be read as "half of marriages will end in divorce." To calculate the "probability that a given marriage will ultimately end in divorce," one would need to track the same cohort of married individuals continuously over time; such official data was not found for this section

entries.title: Factor in the health benefits of marriage, but discount them according to observational data
entries.cost: Costs no money and no time. Just remember one point: these numbers indicate that mortality is lower among married individuals, which is two things co-occurring; it cannot be determined whether marriage is what makes you live longer.
entries.summary: Among older adults, married individuals have about a 12% lower probability of dying during the same period compared to unmarried individuals, and those who have never married have about a 24% higher probability compared to married individuals. But this is merely two things co-occurring; it cannot be determined whether marriage plays a causal role. These numbers basically come from Europe and the United States and can only serve as an order-of-magnitude reference for China.
entries.benefit: A meta-analysis targeting older adults pooled and recalculated multiple studies, comprising 53 comparison groups and over 250,000 people. All pooled studies were cohort studies that merely tracked and recorded outcomes without randomized group controls. For married relative to unmarried individuals, all-cause mortality had an RR of 0.88, 95% CI 0.85–0.91 (RR is relative risk, CI is confidence interval), meaning about a 12% lower probability of dying during the same period. In the same study, widowed was 1.11, divorced or separated was 1.16, and unmarried was 1.11—higher by approximately 11%, 16%, and 11%, respectively. No difference between sexes. The most conservative estimate was RR 0.94, only about 6% lower. Another meta-analysis compared unmarried (never married) relative to married individuals using 95 publications and over 500 million people. The result was HR 1.24 (1.19–1.30), meaning about a 24% higher probability of dying during the same period. Moreover, the older the age, the smaller the gap. There was also a meta-analysis broken down by sex, covering 21 studies and over 7.89 million people: regardless of sex, being unmarried co-occurred with total mortality, cancer mortality, and cardiovascular mortality. The gaps in cardiovascular mortality and total mortality were larger for men. Relative to unmarried women, unmarried men had 31% higher stroke mortality and 9% higher all-cause mortality
entries.sources: Manzoli L, et al. (2007). Marital status and mortality in the elderly: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Soc Sci Med 64:77–94. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.socscimed.2006.08.031>；Roelfs DJ, et al. (2011). The rising relative risk of mortality for singles: meta-analysis and meta-regression. Am J Epidemiol 174(4):379–389. <https://doi.org/10.1093/aje/kwr111>；Wang Y, et al. (2020). Sex differences in the association between marital status and the risk of cardiovascular, cancer, and all-cause mortality: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 7,881,040 individuals. Glob Health Res Policy 5:4. <https://doi.org/10.1186/s41256-020-00133-8>
entries.notes: The controversy lies in the possibility that married individuals might have been selected in the first place—for example, inherently healthier individuals may find it easier to get married. This was inferred by the authors based on study designs; none of the three meta-analyses calculated how much of the effect selection accounted for. All three meta-analyses used observational data from existing populations, merely tracking and recording without randomized group controls. The authors themselves also noted the presence of publication bias or methodological limitations. Roelfs also found that the more rigorously a study was conducted, the smaller the calculated gap. These figures are predominantly based on European and American populations and can only serve as an order-of-magnitude reference for China

entries.title: Calculate the time ledger based on "unpaid labor"; clarify division of labor before getting the marriage certificate
entries.cost: Costs no money. Spend one to two hours before marriage establishing a clear division of labor for unpaid tasks like housework, caring for the elderly and young, and whose job takes a back seat, and then execute according to that division. The difficulty lies in laying things out openly and not putting it off without discussing it.
entries.summary: The National Time Use Survey tabulated unpaid tasks such as housework and accompanying/caring for family members. Among those who did them on the survey day, men averaged 1 hour and 52 minutes daily, while women averaged 3 hours and 29 minutes. The survey was not grouped by marital status, so there is no official figure for "how much more housework is added after marriage"; this gender gap can only serve as an upper-bound reference. The division of labor can be negotiated into a different form before registering the marriage.
entries.benefit: The 2024 National Time Use Survey. Unpaid labor refers to unpaid activities such as housework and accompanying/caring for family members. Among individuals who performed such activities on the survey day, the daily average spent was 2 hours and 45 minutes, of which men spent 1 hour and 52 minutes and women spent 3 hours and 29 minutes. The proportion of people who performed such activities in a day was 67.5% for men and 83.9% for women. The daily average for resident household chores was 1 hour and 17 minutes; counting only those who performed them, it was 1 hour and 59 minutes, 28 minutes less than in 2018. Accompanying and caring for family members averaged 30 minutes daily; counting only those who performed it, it was 1 hour and 46 minutes. The 2018 figures were: household chores 45 minutes for men and 2 hours 6 minutes for women; accompanying and caring for children 17 minutes for men and 53 minutes for women
entries.sources: National Bureau of Statistics (2024). Bulletin of the Third National Time Use Survey (No. 2, No. 3). <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202410/t20241031_1957216.html>, <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202410/t20241031_1957215.html>; National Bureau of Statistics (2019). Bulletin of the 2018 National Time Use Survey. <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202302/t20230203_1900224.html>
entries.notes: Both surveys were grouped only by gender, urban/rural area, and age, not by marital status. Therefore, there is no official figure for "how much more housework increases after marriage," and the gender gap can only be used as an upper-bound reference. These figures are national averages; the division of labor between the two of you can completely be negotiated into a different form

entries.title: Look at the statutory default rules for marriage finances first, then decide whether to make a written agreement
entries.cost: Costs no money. Read through the articles addressing property in the Marriage and Family Part of the Civil Code. If needed, the two parties can sign a written property agreement; the law only requires it to be in writing, with no notarization required. The difficulty lies in talking openly about money matters in advance.
entries.summary: If no written agreement is signed, the law defaults to wages, bonuses, earnings from business and investment, and inherited or gifted property acquired during the marriage belonging jointly to both parties. Pre-marital property, or property specified in a will or gift contract as belonging solely to one party, is separate personal property. The two parties can agree in writing on separate ownership, which is binding once signed. A party who contributes more through child-rearing or caring for elderly relatives may claim compensation upon divorce.
entries.benefit: The default rules when no separate agreement is made are: wages, bonuses, labor remuneration, earnings from production, business, and investments, intellectual property yields, and inherited or gifted property acquired during the marriage are jointly owned by the spouses (Article 1062). Pre-marital property, personal injury compensation, property explicitly specified in a will or gift contract as belonging to only one party, and dedicated daily personal effects of one party are separate personal property (Article 1063). Both parties may agree in writing that pre-marital and post-marital property shall be separately owned, jointly owned, or partially separately owned and partially jointly owned. This agreement is legally binding on both parties (Article 1065). A party who bears more obligations due to child-rearing, caring for elderly relatives, or assisting the other party in work has the right to request compensation upon divorce (Article 1088)
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (effective January 1, 2021, Articles 1062, 1063, 1065, 1088). National Database of Laws and Regulations <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?title=%E4%B8%AD%E5%8D%8E%E4%BA%BA%E6%B0%91%E5%85%B1%E5%92%8C%E5%9B%BD%E6%B0%91%E6%B3%95%E5%85%B8&id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5c500bf>; for full statutory text, see Gazette of the Supreme People's Court reprint <http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/7f184078694d811fb3314f6af9accf.html>
entries.notes: There are no official statistics on bride price (caili), weddings, or marital homes, so this entry provides no figures. The amount of compensation under Article 1088 is first negotiated by the two parties themselves; if negotiations fail, it is determined by the court, with no fixed formula. A written property agreement is useful for both sides: it serves the higher-earning spouse, and it also serves the spouse who performs more unpaid work such as housework and caretaking

entries.title: When parents provide funds to purchase a home, write clearly at the time of transfer whether it is a loan or a gift
entries.cost: Costs no money. On the day the funds are contributed, write a one-page statement specifying whether this money is a gift to someone or a loan to someone, with signatures from both the contributing parents and the adult child. If it is designated as a loan, have both spouses sign, and write the exact same phrasing in the transfer memo.
entries.summary: If parents contribute money to buy a home before marriage, it defaults to a gift to their own child only. Money contributed after marriage without an agreement is treated as community property of the spouses. Starting February 2025, if one party's parents provide the full funding during marriage without specifying it is only for their own child, the court may award the home to the child of the funding party upon divorce, and then determine whether and how much to compensate the other party. If it is to be counted as a loan, write it down clearly on the day of transfer with both parties signing.
entries.benefit: Where parents contribute funds toward the purchase of a home for both parties prior to marriage, it is deemed a gift solely to their own child, unless the parents explicitly express that it is a gift to both parties. Where funds are contributed after marriage, any agreement governs. If there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, it is handled under the principles of marital community property. Effective February 1, 2025, there is an additional rule: where one party's parents contribute the full funding during the marriage and the gift contract does not explicitly state that it is a gift solely to their own child, upon property division during divorce, the court may award the home to the child of the funding party. After such an award, the court will synthesize several factors to determine whether to compensate the other party and how much to compensate. These factors are: circumstances of cohabitation and raising shared children, fault in the divorce, magnitude of contribution to the family, and the market value of the home at the time of divorce. Where one party's parents provide partial funding, or both parties' parents contribute funds, the home shall be awarded to one party based on the funding sources and proportions, with reasonable compensation (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Supreme People's Court (2020). Interpretation (I) on the Application of the Marriage and Family Part of the Civil Code (Fa Shi [2020] No. 22, Article 29). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/282071.html>; Supreme People's Court (2025). Interpretation (II) on the Application of the Marriage and Family Part of the Civil Code (Fa Shi [2025] No. 1, Article 8). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/452771.html>; National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 1062, Paragraph 1, Item 4). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>
entries.notes: Writing it clearly serves both sides. Parents who put up the money no longer need to rely on retroactively fabricating an IOU at the time of divorce to protect their capital contribution. After Interpretation (II) takes effect, who contributed the money is itself a basis for dividing the house, rather than looking solely at whose name is on the property deed. The party receiving the funds also does not have to wait until divorce to find out what this money counts as. If handling it as a loan, handle it genuinely as a loan: both parties agree it is a loan, specify repayment terms, state it clearly in the bank transfer memo, and leave repayment records when necessary. If any element is missing, it will have to be explained in court

entries.title: Large debts borrowed by one spouse without your signature or subsequent ratification do not automatically become your debt
entries.cost: Costs no money. Do not sign as a "co-borrower" or "guarantor" on your spouse's promissory notes or guarantee agreements. Also do not write statements like "we will pay this money back" in chat messages, as this may be deemed a subsequent ratification of the debt. The difficulty lies in holding back from responding when pressed by creditors.
entries.summary: Debts borrowed by a spouse behind your back, as long as they significantly exceed the family's daily household expenses and you have not signed or subsequently ratified them, do not automatically become your debt. The creditor must independently prove that this money was used for joint family living or joint business operations. However, for money used to purchase a home, if it indeed became the house where you live together or jointly own, the other party can often prove this point.
entries.benefit: Debts borrowed under the following circumstances constitute joint marital debts. First, debts jointly signed by both spouses. Second, debts subsequently ratified by one spouse—meaning recognizing the debt after the fact, such that both acknowledge the obligation. Third, debts borrowed by one spouse during the marriage in their individual name for daily family household needs. Debts borrowed by one spouse in their individual name that significantly exceed daily family household expenses do not constitute joint marital debts. The exception is if the creditor (the party seeking repayment) can prove that the money was used for the couple's joint living or joint production and operations, or was an obligation acknowledged by both parties. Funds borrowed to purchase a home significantly exceed daily family household needs; the burden of proof rests on the party asserting the claim, and the creditor must produce the evidence themselves. However, if this money indeed turned into a home jointly inhabited or jointly owned by the spouses, creditors are often able to prove the element of "used for joint marital living." Therefore, what is truly effective is the step in Item 11 (writing clearly whether parental funding is a loan or a gift at the time of contribution) (Nationwide, effective 2021)
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 1064). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; Supreme People's Court (Second Amendment 2020). Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases (Articles 15, 16). <http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/94b6623974526df7d2430a3c73f050.html> (Gazette of the Supreme People's Court)
entries.notes: When dividing property upon divorce, if the other party's parents suddenly produce a loan agreement signed only by the spouse, it must be examined in two steps. Step one is to see whether this loan actually occurred in reality. If you state that the money was never delivered at all and can present a coherent justification, the court will evaluate several matters together: the loan amount, how the funds were delivered, the financial capacities of both parties, regular transaction habits, whether there were corresponding changes in property, and what witnesses say. If the opposing party can only produce bank transfer slips, they are still required to prove that the lending relationship was formed. Step two, after the loan is established to have occurred, is to evaluate whether it constitutes a joint debt. For general rules on promissory notes and guarantee agreements, see Section 8, Item 18

entries.title: Marriage registration requires only an ID card plus a signed statement, no household register needed, no fees, certificate issued on the spot
entries.cost: Costs no money. Both individuals must appear in person. Completion usually takes a few dozen minutes.
entries.summary: Starting May 2025, marriage registration requires only two things: one's own resident ID card, plus a signed statement. The statement certifies that the person has no spouse and has no direct lineal blood relationship or collateral blood relationship within three generations with the other party. There is no need to bring a household register (hukou), nor is there a need to return to the location of either party's registered household. Registration charges not a single cent, and certificates are issued on the spot for those meeting the criteria.
entries.benefit: The new Regulations on Marriage Registration, effective May 10, 2025, revised the materials required for marriage registration by mainland residents. The statutory text states that only two items need to be submitted: "(1) One's resident ID card; (2) A signed statement confirming that one has no spouse and has no direct lineal blood relationship or collateral blood relationship within three generations with the other party." The household register (hukou) is no longer a mandatory document. The registration authority is "the civil affairs department of the county-level people's government, or the township (town) people's government determined by the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government in accordance with the principle of facilitating the public." The restriction in the old regulations requiring registration "at the place of permanent household registration of one of the parties" has been abolished. The regulations also specify: "Marriage registration authorities shall not collect fees for handling marriage registrations." The regulations also specify: "For parties who meet the conditions for marriage, registration shall be granted on the spot and a marriage certificate shall be issued." For circumstances where registration will not be granted, the regulations list four items: "(1) Not having reached the statutory marriageable age; (2) Not being completely voluntary on the part of both the man and the woman; (3) One or both parties already having a spouse; (4) Being direct lineal blood relatives or collateral blood relatives within three generations"
entries.sources: State Council (2025). Regulations on Marriage Registration (State Council Decree No. 804, Articles 2, 6, 8, 9, 10). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202504/content_7017752.htm>
entries.notes: There are only four situations where registration authorities will refuse to handle registration: not reaching the statutory marriageable age, not being completely voluntary by both parties, one or both parties already having a spouse, and the two being direct lineal blood relatives or collateral blood relatives within three generations. The only potential charges are peripheral services like photography and photocopying. Registration itself does not charge a single cent; if you encounter a "document fee" or "expedited fee," directly refuse and file a complaint. For the 30-day cooling-off period in divorce registration, see Item 15 of this section (Exit Costs). For the consequences of holding a wedding without registering the marriage, see Item 21 of this section (Even If You Host a Banquet, Go Get the Marriage Certificate)

entries.title: Undergo a premarital medical examination before marriage; if you have a major illness, you must truthfully disclose it to your partner before registration
entries.cost: Most regions offer free or discounted examinations for eligible age groups. Paying out of pocket costs only a few hundred yuan. It takes half a day.
entries.summary: If you have a major illness and do not truthfully disclose it to your partner before registration, the other party can petition the court to revoke the marriage. This must be filed within one year from the date they become aware of it. The premarital examination itself has not been a prerequisite for obtaining a marriage certificate since 2003, and going is voluntary. The cost depends on local policy; it takes half a day.
entries.benefit: The legal consequences of concealment are clear. The new Regulations on Marriage Registration stipulate that 'where one party suffers from a major illness, they shall truthfully inform the other party before marriage registration; where they fail to do so truthfully, the other party may, in accordance with the provisions of Article 1053 of the Civil Code, petition a people's court to revoke the marriage.' The state treats premarital medical examinations as the primary line of defense in the prevention and control of birth defects. The current target is that 'the premarital medical examination rate and the target population coverage rate of preconception eugenic health examinations shall be maintained at above 70% and 80%, respectively.' The document also requires 'promoting the nearby co-location of premarital medical examination institutions and marriage registration venues for the convenience of the public.' The document also promotes ''one-stop' services for marriage registration, premarital medical examinations, and reproductive guidance.' The Civil Code stipulates that where one party suffers from a major illness, they shall truthfully inform the other party before marriage registration; if they fail to do so truthfully, the other party may petition a people's court to revoke the marriage. A petition to revoke a marriage shall be submitted within one year from the date the party knows or should have known of the cause for revocation. A premarital medical examination is not a prerequisite for obtaining a marriage certificate. When responding to a CPPCC proposal in 2022, the Tai'an Municipal Health Commission stated: 'While the 2003 Regulations on Marriage Registration abolished 'mandatory premarital examinations', it clearly required that marriage registration authorities shall not impose additional obligations when processing marriage registrations.' The premarital medical examination certificate is also not listed among the marriage registration materials in Article 8 of the current regulations.
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 1053). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; State Council (2025). Regulations on Marriage Registration (State Council Decree No. 804, Articles 8 and 12). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202504/content_7017752.htm>; General Office of the National Health Commission (2023). Action Plan for Improving Birth Defect Prevention and Control Capabilities (2023–2027) (Guo Wei Ban Fu You Fa [2023] No. 9). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202308/content_6900320.htm>; National Health Commission and Four Other Departments (2020). Circular on Strengthening Premarital Healthcare Work (Guo Wei Fu You Han [2020] No. 205): 'Actively advocate for regions to implement free premarital checkups based on local conditions.' <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-05/22/content_5513902.htm>; Tai'an Municipal Health Commission (2022). Reply to 'Suggestions on the Management of Premarital Medical Examinations' (Proposal No. 188 of the First Session of the 14th Municipal CPPCC). <http://www.taian.gov.cn/art/2022/7/8/art_176934_24592.html>
entries.notes: A premarital medical examination has not been a mandatory preliminary step for obtaining a certificate since 2003, and going is voluntary. However, the clause stating that 'failing to truthfully disclose a major illness' indeed grants the other party the right to petition the court to revoke the marriage, which must be raised within one year from the date of discovery. There is no nationwide unified regulation mandating free premarital examinations. The 2020 circular from the National Health Commission and four other departments merely stated: 'Actively advocate for regions to implement free premarital checkups based on local conditions.' Therefore, whether it is free and which items are examined are decided locally by each region; inquire at local maternal and child healthcare institutions or the one-stop service windows of marriage registration offices.

entries.title: Calculate exit costs: divorce by agreement has a 30-day cooling-off period, and divorce by litigation has statutory conditions
entries.cost: Costs no money. Spend a little time before marriage reading through this: in case you want to exit, how long will it take, and what procedures must be followed. The hard part is thinking about breaking up before even getting married.
entries.summary: Divorce by agreement is not settled simply after signing. Within 30 days after submitting the application, either party can withdraw it. After the period expires, both parties must personally go to collect the divorce certificate within 30 days; failing to go is treated as a withdrawal. If the other party does not agree, the only option is to file a lawsuit. The court will conduct mediation first; in circumstances such as domestic violence, bigamy, or living apart for a full two years, a divorce shall be granted if mediation fails.
entries.benefit: A divorce by agreement requires signing a written divorce agreement and applying in person at the marriage registration authority (Article 1076). Within 30 days from the date the registration authority receives the application, either party may withdraw it. Within 30 days after the expiration of this period, both parties must apply in person for a divorce certificate; failure to apply is deemed a withdrawal (Article 1077). When one party disagrees, the litigation route is taken, and the court shall conduct mediation first. Under circumstances such as bigamy or cohabitation with another person, domestic violence or maltreatment and abandonment, repeated gambling or drug abuse despite education, or living apart due to emotional discord for a full two years, a divorce shall be granted if mediation is ineffective. If a divorce is denied by judgment and the parties live apart for another full year, a subsequent lawsuit for divorce shall be granted (Article 1079). In 2024, there were 3.513 million divorces nationwide, of which 891,000 couples went through court judgments or mediation.
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (Articles 1076, 1077, and 1079). <http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/7f184078694d811fb3314f6af9accf.html>; Ministry of Civil Affairs (2020). Circular on Implementing the Relevant Provisions on Marriage Registration in the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (Min Fa [2020] No. 116). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-12/04/content_5567010.htm>; Ministry of Civil Affairs (2025). Statistical Bulletin on the Development of Civil Affairs in 2024. Citation same as Item 7 (What are the statistical scopes of the marriage rate and divorce rate?).
entries.notes: The cooling-off period applies only to divorce by agreement. There is no cooling-off period for divorce by litigation, but the cycle is longer. Court costs and attorney fees vary across regions, so no figures are listed in this entry. High exit costs do not mean you should not get married, but you should know this before marriage. For those with children, see Item 23 of this section (Child support and visitation) for how to draft child support and visitation terms.

entries.title: Keep a separate ledger for 'marrying for the elders,' and do not mix it with your own ledger
entries.cost: Costs no money. Write in two columns on paper. One column is which benefits in this marriage are your own, which can be calculated from the earlier items in this section. The other column is which benefits belong to the elders: peace of mind, face, and an end to marriage-nagging. The hard part is keeping the elders' column separate and not merging it into your own.
entries.summary: The elders' share of the benefits—namely peace of mind, face, and no more nagging—is real. But it will not automatically turn into your health gains or relationship quality. Meanwhile, the three ledgers of time, money, and exit costs are borne entirely by you. By writing out two columns on paper to clearly separate which benefits belong to yourself and which belong to the elders, you can see at a glance whether this deal is worth it.
entries.benefit: The elders' benefits are real. But they do not automatically convert into your health gains (Item 8) or relationship quality (Item 4: whether a relationship is good depends on your own feelings). Meanwhile, the time ledger (Item 9), the financial ledger (Items 10 to 12), and the exit costs (Item 15) are borne entirely by the party concerned. After keeping separate ledgers, you will be able to see for yourself whether the cost-effectiveness of 'quest-completing marriage' is high or low.
entries.sources: Author's experience, methodological recommendation; for data, see the preceding items in this section.
entries.notes: The elders' column can also be counted as carrying heavy weight; how you weigh it is up to you to decide. For the fill-in-the-blank checklist, see [docs/Is Marriage Worth It.md](../docs/结婚划不划算.md).

entries.title: Treat relationship quality as a health ledger: focus on the issue rather than the person during arguments, without name-calling or sarcasm
entries.cost: Costs no money. When arguing, stick strictly to the matter at hand, without insulting, being sarcastic, or bringing up past grievances. The hard part is holding your tongue in the heat of anger.
entries.summary: Spouses with good relationships have better physical health and lower mortality risks. This correlation is modest, roughly comparable to the correlation between diet and health. In one experiment, for couples who consistently exhibited hostility during arguments, the healing rate of small experimentally induced wounds was only 60% of that of calm couples.
entries.benefit: Pooling 126 studies covering over 72,000 individuals (meta-analysis): the higher the marital quality, the better the physical health, with correlation coefficients r ranging from .07 to .21. A correlation coefficient of 0 means completely unrelated, and 1 means perfect synchrony. Among them, the correlation with lower mortality risk is r = .11. Smaller cardiovascular reactivity during arguments is r = -.13. The authors noted that these effects are all small, roughly comparable to the associations between dietary health habits and health. In another crossover experiment, 42 healthy married couples were each admitted to the hospital twice, for 24 hours each time. One visit involved a mutually supportive conversation, while the other involved discussing a matter of disagreement. Following the argument, blister wounds created in the experiment healed more slowly. Couples who exhibited greater hostility during both visits had a wound healing rate that was only 60% of that of couples with low hostility. On the morning following the argument, inflammatory markers in their blood (IL-6, tumor necrosis factor) also rose significantly more.
entries.sources: Robles TF, Slatcher RB, Trombello JM, McGinn MM (2014). Marital quality and health: a meta-analytic review. Psychological Bulletin. <https://doi.org/10.1037/a0031859>; Kiecolt-Glaser JK et al. (2005). Hostile marital interactions, proinflammatory cytokine production, and wound healing. Archives of General Psychiatry. <https://doi.org/10.1001/archpsyc.62.12.1377>
entries.notes: Reason for assigning grade B: Most aggregated studies are merely observational follow-ups without controlled grouping. Therefore, it is impossible to distinguish whether poor relationships make people sick, or poor health makes relationships worse. In some studies, the association remained even after controlling for age and income. The original Robles paper also stated that some results exhibit publication bias. Studies explicitly comparing men and women found virtually no sex differences. This section found no meta-analysis directly comparing mortality rates between 'low-quality marriages' and 'staying unmarried.' Thus, the claim that 'a bad marriage is more harmful to health than staying unmarried' can only be considered an inference. The wound experiment included only 42 couples. 'Focusing on the issue rather than the person, without insulting or sarcasm' is a practice inferred by the author from the 'hostile behaviors' in the experiment; no study has directly compared it. If arguments are fierce and unmanageable, go to couples therapy together; see Item 20 of this section (Couples therapy). If arguing escalates to physical violence, or chronic insults and threats, it is no longer a communication issue—it is domestic violence; see Section 8, Item 43 (Experiencing domestic violence). If considering whether to leave, see Item 15 of this section (Exit costs) for exit costs.

entries.title: Same-sex couples should execute powers of attorney, agreed guardianship, and wills while both are lucid: legally, you are not close relatives, and without these you have no signing rights or inheritance rights
entries.cost: Agreed guardianship and wills are executed at a notary office; notarization fees vary across regions, starting from a few hundred yuan. A handwritten will costs nothing. The process takes one or two half-days in total. The hard part is for both individuals to sit down and discuss illness and death.
entries.summary: Under the law, close relatives include spouses, parents, children, and siblings; a partner does not count. Without executing documents in advance, when one party falls critically ill, the other cannot make decisions on their behalf. When one party passes away, the other inherits not a single cent of the estate. The three documents govern distinct stages: power of attorney while lucid, agreed guardianship after losing decision-making capacity, and a will after death.
entries.benefit: Article 1045 of the Civil Code lists close relatives as spouses, parents, children, siblings, paternal grandparents, maternal grandparents, grandsons, granddaughters, and maternal grandchildren. Under Article 1127, statutory heirs are first spouses, children, and parents, followed by siblings, paternal grandparents, and maternal grandparents. A partner appears in neither category. Article 1219 governs surgical procedures, special examinations, and special treatments: where explanation cannot or should not be given to the patient, medical personnel must explain to the patient's 'close relatives' and obtain their consent. There are three avenues to remedy this. First, Article 33 permits an adult to agree in advance in writing with 'other individuals willing to serve as guardians' on a guardian. After the person loses or partially loses capacity for civil conduct, this designated person serves as guardian, and the guardian acts as their statutory agent. Second, Article 165 stipulates that a written power of attorney shall state the agent's name, delegated matters, scope of authority, and duration, and be signed or sealed by the principal. The agency terminates upon the principal's death or loss of capacity for civil conduct. Third, Article 1133 permits the making of a will to bequeath personal property to individuals outside the scope of statutory heirs. An article by the Yichang Municipal Bureau of Justice published on the website of the Department of Justice of Hubei Province explicitly stated that same-sex couples can notarize an agreed guardianship agreement, appointing each other as their future guardian (Nationwide).
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 23, 33, 165, 173, 1045, 1124, 1127, 1133–1140, 1142, and 1219). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5c500bf> (National Laws and Regulations Database); Yichang Municipal Bureau of Justice (2021). Agreed Guardianship Notarization: The Notarial Path to the Rainbow. 'Practice Collection' column on the website of the Department of Justice of Hubei Province. <https://sft.hubei.gov.cn/fbjd/sjhc/202101/t20210108_3208602.shtml>
entries.notes: The partner's legal status when receiving an estate is that of a 'testamentary donee/legatee,' not an heir. Upon learning of the legacy, they must explicitly express acceptance within 60 days; failure to do so is deemed a waiver. Neither the partner nor any person with an interest in the matter can serve as a will witness. If multiple wills have been executed, the last one prevails; see Section 17, Item 2 (Later wills supersede earlier wills). As to whether an agreed guardian can directly sign a surgical consent form, hospital practices vary, so inquire in advance at your regularly visited hospitals. If family members refuse to recognize these documents, a lawsuit must be filed: first-instance ordinary proceedings are required by regulation to conclude within 6 months, which can be extended, with attorney fees paid out of pocket. Therefore, try to execute the documents at a notary office whenever possible. For jointly purchased housing and jointly saved money, draft a separate written agreement reflecting actual financial contributions. For how to execute agreed guardianship, see Section 17, Item 1 (Designating a future guardian in writing). The beneficiaries are yourself and your partner.

entries.title: Do not get married by concealing your sexual orientation, and do not treat a marriage of convenience as a convenient shortcut: legally it is a genuine marriage, and the only way to exit is through divorce
entries.cost: Costs no money. The hard part is withstanding family pressure to marry, which may have to be endured for many years.
entries.summary: Marrying while concealing sexual orientation is legally neither void nor revocable; the only way to exit is divorce. A marriage of convenience is also a genuine marriage: money earned after marriage is considered joint marital property, and debts signed jointly or borrowed for ordinary household daily expenses belong to both parties. Upon divorce, the deceived party can demand a larger share of property and compensation for mental anguish, but whether courts will uphold this remains unsettled.
entries.benefit: Article 1051 of the Civil Code stipulates that a marriage is void only under three circumstances: bigamy, prohibited kinship, or failure to reach statutory marriage age. Articles 1052 and 1053 stipulate that a marriage is revocable only under two circumstances: marriage under coercion, or premarital concealment of a major illness. Article 17 of Interpretation (I) on the Marriage and Family Part stipulates that if a petition to declare a marriage void is based on reasons other than these three, the court shall render a judgment dismissing it. Therefore, the only way to exit is divorce. A marriage of convenience, once registered, is a lawful marriage. Article 1062 stipulates that wages, bonuses, and remuneration for labor services earned after marriage are joint marital property. Article 1064 stipulates that debts incurred under joint signature by both spouses, or incurred by one spouse for the family's daily household life, are joint marital debts. Divorce damages are governed by Article 1091. Circumstances where damages can be sought are limited to bigamy, cohabitation with another person, domestic violence, maltreatment or abandonment of family members, and 'other major faults.' Article 2 of Interpretation (I) defines 'cohabitation with another person' as cohabitation with 'an opposite-sex individual outside marriage.' Thus, same-sex relationships can only be contested under 'other major faults.' Damages include compensation for emotional distress; the deceived party must raise this concurrently when filing for divorce, and it will not be granted if divorce is denied. Since the implementation of the Civil Code, no publicly available court judgments of this type have been found. Under the prior legal regime, an article published on the Jiangsu High People's Court website in 2013 discussed a case in which a wife sued for divorce because her husband concealed his homosexuality. The article outlined two viewpoints. One held that homosexuality was not among the statutory faults at the time, and neither a larger property division nor emotional distress compensation should be supported. The author favored the other viewpoint: treating the deceived party as the 'faultless party,' favoring her in property division, and awarding compensation for mental distress (Nationwide).
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 1051–1054, 1062, 1064, 1079, 1087, and 1091). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5c500bf> (National Laws and Regulations Database); Supreme People's Court (2020). Interpretation (I) on the Application of the Marriage and Family Part of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (Fa Shi [2020] No. 22, Articles 2, 17, and 86–90). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff80808177e75f880178006736f21aaf>; Zhu Laikuan and Wang Hongjuan (2013). Can damages be claimed in a divorce caused by homosexuality? Jiangsu Courts Network. <http://www.jsfy.gov.cn/article/26621.html>
entries.notes: Regarding receiving a larger share of property and emotional distress damages, there is only one analytical article, which does not state how the case was ultimately decided; thus, whether they can be obtained depends on the specific court. The Civil Code added the category of 'other major faults' compared to the previous law, opening a viable avenue for the deceived party to contest. The legal statutes themselves are Grade A. If each party in a marriage of convenience has their own same-sex partner, relationships between those partners are not protected by marriage law, and property must be separately and clearly specified in writing; see Item 18 of this section (Same-sex couples executing agreed guardianship and wills). Divorcing from a marriage of convenience likewise requires undergoing the 30-day cooling-off period or litigation; see Item 15 of this section (Divorce by agreement has a 30-day cooling-off period). If a waiver of compensation is specified in a divorce agreement, a subsequent lawsuit will not be upheld. The beneficiary is first the spouse who would otherwise be deceived, and second yourself: once the concealment is discovered, divorce, property division, and child custody will all descend upon you at once.

entries.title: When a relationship is stuck in recurring arguments and cold wars, go to couples therapy together: waiting passively almost never makes it get better on its own
entries.cost: Costs money. Charged per session, varying across regions and hospitals, so no numbers are listed in this entry. In research studies, sessions are typically attended once a week; in one trial, it lasted about 8 months from start to finish. The hard part is that both people must attend and persist through to completion.
entries.summary: Stuck couples who complete couples therapy together become significantly more satisfied with the relationship, with approximately 70% showing improvement. Couples merely waiting on a waitlist show virtually no change. However, effects fade over time: by year 5 of follow-up, about half remain noticeably improved, while about a quarter have separated or divorced.
entries.benefit: A 2020 meta-analysis aggregated 58 studies and 2,092 couples. Following couple therapy, the pre-to-post change in relationship satisfaction was g = 1.12 (credible interval 0.92–1.31), which the authors characterized as a large effect. g is an effect size; see the README glossary. For couples assigned to waitlists, over the same period g = 0.12 (−0.04 to 0.29), showing no significant improvement. Couples with worse relationships at the start actually improved more. A 2012 review noted that couple therapy resulted in improvement for 70% of treated couples. Another randomized trial recruited 134 couples with chronic, severe marital discord and administered approximately 8 months of two forms of behavioral couple therapy. Upon completion, satisfaction changes were d = 0.90 and 0.71. By year 5, 50.0% and 45.9% of couples in the two approaches, respectively, still maintained significant improvement. The authors termed this significant improvement \"clinically meaningful improvement.\" At the same time, 25.7% and 27.9% were already separated or divorced.
entries.sources: Roddy MK, Walsh LM, Rothman K, Hatch SG, Doss BD (2020). Meta-analysis of couple therapy: effects across outcomes, designs, timeframes, and other moderators. Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology, 88(7), 583-596. <https://doi.org/10.1037/ccp0000514>; Lebow JL, Chambers AL, Christensen A, Johnson SM (2012). Research on the treatment of couple distress. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 38(1), 145-168. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1752-0606.2011.00249.x>; Christensen A, Atkins DC, Baucom B, Yi J (2010). Marital status and satisfaction five years following a randomized clinical trial comparing traditional versus integrative behavioral couple therapy. Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology, 78(2), 225-235. <https://doi.org/10.1037/a0018132>; Rathgeber M, Bürkner PC, Schiller EM, Holling H (2019). The efficacy of emotionally focused couples therapy and behavioral couples therapy: a meta-analysis. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 45(3), 447-463. <https://doi.org/10.1111/jmft.12336> (disputing party); Shadish WR, Baldwin SA (2003). Meta-analysis of MFT interventions. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 29(4), 547-570. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1752-0606.2003.tb01694.x> (disputing party); Karakurt G, Whiting K, van Esch C, Bolen SD, Calabrese JR (2016). Couples therapy for intimate partner violence: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 42(4), 567-583. <https://doi.org/10.1111/jmft.12178>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018 amendment). Mental Health Law (Articles 23, 51). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7448a066d> (National Laws and Regulations Database)
entries.notes: The controversy lies in how long the effects last. In another meta-analysis that included only randomized trials, g = 0.60 upon completion and 0.44 after six months. By 12 months, data remained only for behavioral couple therapy, with g = 0.06, showing almost no retention. Another review summarizing 20 meta-analyses stated that clinically meaningful effects appeared in 40% to 50% of individuals. \"70% improvement\" and \"40% to 50% clinically meaningful improvement\" use different standards, so do not mix and compare them. The 5-year trial lacked an untreated control group, making it unclear whether divorces increased or decreased. The 2020 meta-analysis aggregated exclusively heterosexual couples and found no domestic randomized trials, so its applicability to oneself requires a discount. Where to go domestically in China: The Mental Health Law stipulates that psychotherapy must be conducted in medical institutions, and psychological counseling personnel may not conduct psychotherapy. You can visit the psychiatric or psychological departments of hospitals to inquire whether couple therapy is available. If seeking organizations outside hospitals, first clarify their credentials and what training they have received. In cases involving domestic violence, do not attend together right away. The 2016 meta-analysis clearly stated that its conclusions apply only to mild-to-moderate situations where both parties engage in physical conflict during disputes. Violence characterized by controlling the other party or causing severe harm is not included. The profession also worries about retaliation at home after discussions. If you are beaten, first consult Section 8, Item 43 (Experienced domestic violence). For how to speak during arguments, see Item 17 of this section (Focus on the issue, not the person during arguments); to think through whether to leave, see Item 15 of this section (Exit costs). The beneficiaries are yourself and your spouse.
