entries.title: Even if you held a wedding and hosted a banquet, you still need to obtain a marriage certificate: Those without registration are not legally spouses, and you have no spousal inheritance rights if the other party passes away
entries.cost: Costs no money. The two of you go to the marriage registration office together; it takes several dozen minutes.
entries.summary: For those who only held a wedding without registering after February 1994, you are not spouses in the eyes of the law, but merely cohabiting. If the other party passes away, you cannot inherit their estate in the capacity of a spouse. When wishing to separate, the court also will not handle it as a divorce. Retroactively registering solves this, and its validity can be applied retroactively.
entries.benefit: The Civil Code stipulates that \"a marital relationship is established upon completion of marriage registration. Those who have not registered marriage shall complete registration retroactively.\" The Supreme People's Court's judicial interpretation divides those who have not registered but live together in the name of husband and wife into two categories. Those who already met the conditions for marriage before February 1, 1994, are treated as de facto marriages. For those after this date, the court \"shall inform them to complete marriage registration retroactively.\" For those who do not complete registration retroactively, they are treated as cohabitation relationships. When one party passes away and the other party seeks to inherit in the capacity of a spouse, it is also handled according to this principle. A spouse is a first-order heir, so the unregistered party cannot be included. Regarding the cohabitation relationship itself, the court will not accept requests to \"terminate\" it, but will only accept disputes over property division and child custody. After completing registration retroactively, the validity of the marriage \"is calculated from the time both parties met the substantive requirements for marriage stipulated by the Civil Code.\" Children are unaffected. \"Children\" under the Inheritance Part of the Civil Code explicitly include children born out of wedlock, who are first-order heirs equally alongside children born in wedlock.
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 1049, 1127, 1131). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; Supreme People's Court (2020). Interpretation (I) on the Application of the Marriage and Family Part of the Civil Code (Fa Shi [2020] No. 22, Articles 3, 6, 7, 8). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/282071.html>
entries.notes: If you have not registered when the other party passes away, you are not an heir, but it does not mean you can get nothing. The Civil Code stipulates that for those who \"provided comparatively more maintenance\" to the deceased, \"an appropriate share of the estate may be distributed.\" This requires you to present evidence to fight for it yourself; if negotiations fail, you will have to litigate. According to regulations, ordinary first-instance proceedings are completed within 6 months and can be extended; attorney fees are paid by yourself, and how much is distributed is determined by the judge. Therefore, while both people are present, go complete the registration retroactively first. Retroactive registration is the same as the initial registration: both parties must appear in person; for materials, see Item 13 of this section (Obtaining a marriage certificate requires only an ID card). Betrothal gifts (caili) can be requested to be returned when no registration was made; see Section 8, Item 24 (Transfer betrothal gifts by bank transfer). The beneficiaries are yourself and your spouse.

entries.title: A spouse behind your back uses large amounts of marital community funds to tip livestreamers or transfer money to someone outside the marriage: You can request division of community property without divorcing, and money transferred to someone outside the marriage can be recovered by suing
entries.cost: Requires litigation. Attorney fees are paid by yourself; they are not included in the litigation costs borne by the losing party. According to regulations, ordinary first-instance proceedings are completed within 6 months and can be extended; summary proceedings take 3 months. You also need to dig up bank transaction statements and tipping records item by item yourself.
entries.summary: If a spouse uses community funds to give large tips to livestreamers without discussing it with you, you can petition the court to divide community property without divorcing. During a divorce, the other party can also be awarded a smaller share or nothing. For money transferred to someone outside the marriage, you can sue the recipient to return it, and they must return it even if they claim they have already spent it. However, all of this requires litigation, attorney fees are paid by yourself, and first-instance proceedings take several months.
entries.benefit: The Civil Code stipulates that spouses have \"equal rights of disposition\" over community property. Where one party conceals, transfers, sells off, damages, or squanders community property during the marriage, the other party may request the court to divide community property without needing to divorce first. When dividing property upon divorce, the party who engaged in such conduct may be awarded a smaller share or nothing. If discovered only after divorce, a lawsuit may be filed again to request re-division. Interpretation (II), effective from February 1, 2025, specifies two scenarios. Article 6 governs tipping. Where one party, without the other party's consent, uses community property to tip on livestreaming platforms in amounts that significantly exceed the family's general consumption level, it constitutes \"squandering.\" If the other party requests division during the marriage, or that the tipping party receive a smaller share or nothing upon divorce, the court shall support it. Article 7 governs transfers to persons outside the marriage. Where one party gifts community property to another person for purposes such as bigamy, cohabitation with another person, or other violations of the duty of fidelity, and the other party claims that this gift is invalid, the court shall support it. After it is invalidated, the recipient of the funds must return them. At the same time, this may also serve as grounds to request division during marriage, or that the other party receive a smaller share or nothing upon divorce. In typical cases released simultaneously by the Supreme People's Court, one party transferred 730,000 yuan over more than 4 years during marriage to an individual with whom they had an improper relationship, and the other party transferred back 170,000 yuan. The court ordered the recipient to return the 560,000 yuan actually received; the court did not support the recipient's defense that \"part of the funds had already been spent\" (Nationwide).
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 157, 1043, 1062, 1066, 1092). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; Supreme People's Court (2025). Interpretation (II) on the Application of the Marriage and Family Part of the Civil Code (Fa Shi [2025] No. 1, Articles 6, 7). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/452771.html>; Supreme People's Court (2025). Typical Cases Involving Marriage and Family Disputes (Case 4: Cui v. Ye and Gao on a Gift Contract Dispute). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/452761.html>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2023 amendment). Civil Procedure Law (Articles 152, 164). <https://amr.guizhou.gov.cn/zwgk/xxgkml/jcxxgk/zcfg/fl/202401/t20240129_83645867.html>; State Council (2006). Measures on the Payment of Litigation Costs (State Council Decree No. 481, Articles 6, 29). <https://www.gov.cn/ziliao/flfg/2006-12/29/content_483682.htm>
entries.notes: The clause on tipping has a threshold: without your consent, the amount significantly exceeds the family's general consumption level, and it severely impairs community property. Occasional small tips do not meet this standard. The remedies provided by Interpretation (II) for tipping are property division and receiving a reduced share; it does not state that money can be recovered from the livestreamer or the platform. For the clause on transfers to persons outside the marriage, what is recovered is the money actually received by the recipient; portions transferred back to the spouse must be deducted. You must prepare the evidence yourself: transaction statements from banks and payment apps, tipping records, and chat logs that demonstrate the relationship between the two parties. For procedures on property division and divorce, see Item 15 of this section (Exit costs). For what money counts as community property, see Item 10 of this section (First check statutory default rules for money and accounts). For a spouse borrowing money outside the marriage, see Item 12 of this section (Large debts borrowed by one spouse). For tipping less yourself, see Section 5, Item 8 (Do not tip livestreamers). The beneficiary is yourself. Conversely, if you are the person outside the marriage receiving the money, the funds received must be returned, even if they have already been spent.

entries.title: When couples with minor children divorce, write with whom the child will live, monthly child support amount, and visitation methods and schedules into the divorce agreement: The more specific it is written, the fewer subsequent lawsuits after divorce
entries.cost: Written into the agreement during an uncontested divorce by mutual agreement, it costs no money. The difficulty lies in the two parties having to sit down and negotiate the details, such as which day of the month to pay, which account to pay into, which weekend to pick up the child, and how to split winter and summer vacations. If negotiations fail, litigation is required. The acceptance fee for divorce cases is 50 to 300 yuan per case. Attorney fees are paid by yourself; they are not included in the litigation costs borne by the losing party. According to regulations, ordinary first-instance proceedings are completed within 6 months and can be extended; summary proceedings take 3 months. Raising disputes over child support or visitation again after divorce requires filing a separate lawsuit.
entries.summary: With whom the child lives, how much is paid each month, and when you can see the child can be negotiated and written into the agreement by the two parties. If negotiations fail, the court decides; for those with a fixed income, child support is generally 20% to 30% of the paying party's monthly income. If the other party does not pay the agreed-upon money, you can file a lawsuit to recover it. If the other party blocks you from seeing the child, the court can fine or detain them, but will not forcibly bring the child to see you.
entries.benefit: The Civil Code stipulates that the amount and duration of child support payments, as well as the methods and schedules for visitation, are first agreed upon by both parties; if agreement cannot be reached, the court decides. For children under two years of age, custody is in principle awarded to the mother. For children who have reached two years of age, decisions are made according to the \"principle of what is most beneficial to the minor child.\" If the child has reached eight years of age, the child's own wishes shall be respected. Starting from February 2025, where one party exhibits domestic violence, gambling or drug abuse, infidelity/cohabitation, or snatching/concealing the child, the court prioritizes awarding custody to the other party. The child support amount depends on the child's actual needs, the parents' financial ability, and the local living standards. For those with a fixed income, it is generally paid at 20% to 30% of monthly gross income. For those supporting two or more children, the proportion may be raised, but generally does not exceed 50% of monthly gross income. For those without a fixed income, this proportion is referenced based on total annual income or the average income of the same industry. For example, with a monthly income of 8,000 yuan, based on this proportion it is 1,600 to 2,400 yuan per month (calculated independently). Child support is generally paid until the child reaches 18 years of age. Once an amount is set by agreement or judgment, the child may still request reasonable expenses exceeding the original amount when necessary, such as when illness or educational expenses exceed estimates. An agreement stipulating that one party does not pay child support is also valid. However, if the living standards of the party raising the child drop significantly, or if the child's necessary expenses increase significantly, the child may still request the other party to pay. For child support not paid according to the agreement after divorce, a lawsuit can be filed to recover the arrears. After a court judgment or mediation statement takes effect, if the other party fails to perform, an application for compulsory enforcement may be filed. Against persons who refuse to assist with visitation, the court may impose detention or fines, but \"may not enforce compulsory execution on the child's person or the act of visitation\" (Nationwide).
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 1084–1086). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; Supreme People's Court (2020). Interpretation (I) on the Application of the Marriage and Family Part of the Civil Code (Fa Shi [2020] No. 22, Articles 44–53, 55, 58, 61, 65–68). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/282071.html>; Supreme People's Court (2025). Interpretation (II) on the Application of the Marriage and Family Part of the Civil Code (Fa Shi [2025] No. 1, Articles 12, 14, 16, 17). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/452771.html>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2023 amendment). Civil Procedure Law (Articles 114, 152, 164, 247). <https://amr.guizhou.gov.cn/zwgk/xxgkml/jcxxgk/zcfg/fl/202401/t20240129_83645867.html>; State Council (2006). Measures on the Payment of Litigation Costs (State Council Decree No. 481, Articles 6, 13, 29). <https://www.gov.cn/ziliao/flfg/2006-12/29/content_483682.htm>
entries.notes: The 20% to 30% range is a reference line for court rulings, not a statutory lower limit for agreements; the two parties can negotiate other figures. When drafting the agreement, specify the payment date, account, and through what date payments continue; specify visitation down to the day of the week, pick-up and drop-off times, and how holidays are divided, so that there is proof afterward. If one parent or relatives snatch or conceal the child, an application can be made to the court for a personal safety protection order; see Section 8, Item 43 (Personal safety protection orders). For divorce procedures and the cooling-off period, see Item 15 of this section (Exit costs). The beneficiary is first the child, and second yourself.

chapters.title: Red lines programmers and tech workers easily cross
chapters.intro:
The yardstick for this section is personal liberty and money; what it buys you in return is "not getting locked up" and "not having to pay damages." People who write code and work in tech often treat the matters below as "just technical issues." Yet they correspond to specific criminal offenses under the criminal law, or specific sums of money to be paid in civil liability. Each item provides the figures specified in statutory provisions, as well as cases published on the official websites of the Supreme People's Procuratorate and the Supreme People's Court. The Criminal Law is cited from the consolidated text "Amended in Accordance with Criminal Law Amendment (XI)" reprinted by the Beijing Municipal Public Security Bureau Traffic Management Bureau. Item 1 is a general entry explaining how to evaluate risks before taking action, and what to do first if trouble arises.

The entries in this section are divided into the following blocks by theme, with item numbers indicated in parentheses.

**Before Taking Action**: Ask first before taking action whether they would report it to the police (Item 1).

**Cheats, Scripts, and Cracks**: Game cheats and helper tools (Item 2), scripts for ticket snagging, order brushing, and exploiting promotions (Item 3), scrapers crawling only public pages that require no login (Item 4), tools that automatically skip or block ads in other apps (Item 18), cracking patches and keygens (Item 20).

**Touching Other People's Systems**: Not running your own programs on other people's computers (Item 8), not testing others' systems without written authorization (Item 9), reporting vulnerabilities according to regulations (Item 10), DDoS traffic attacks (Item 21).

**Taking Freelance Orders and Side Gigs**: Development orders for gambling, fraud, and pornography apps (Item 5), circumvention tools and VPN accounts (Item 11), AI relay endpoints (Item 19).

**Resignation and Ownership**: Handing over all account permissions upon departure (Item 6), not taking source code upon departure (Item 7), having signed non-compete agreements (Item 12), code written with company resources belonging to the company (Item 13), GPL and other open-source code (Item 14).

**Launching Products**: Collecting only personal information necessary for business (Item 15), obtaining ICP filing before going live (Item 16), generative AI security assessments and algorithm filing (Item 17).

entries.title: Before taking action, ask first: Will the vendor, platform, or company report it to the police? Seek a criminal defense attorney immediately after being investigated
entries.cost: Costs 0 yuan. Before acting, replace the question "Can this be done technically?" with another: "Will the vendor, platform, or company report it to the police?" The hard part is resisting the thought that "nobody cares about such a minor thing," because case-handling organs have the legal authority to retrieve server logs, payment records, and group chat histories
entries.summary: Before acting, ask first: Will the vendor, platform, or company report it to the police? Case-handling organs have the authority to retrieve server logs, payment records, and group chat histories. If you are placed under criminal detention, a decision on whether to formally arrest you must be made within up to 37 days. You are entitled to retain a lawyer from your first interrogation; the lawyer can submit opinions to the procuratorate against approving arrest, and can also apply for release on bail pending trial.
entries.benefit: Any entity or individual that discovers criminal facts has the right to report them to the police. If the case-handling organ considers that criminal facts exist, it shall file a case. Courts, procuratorates, and public security organs "have the right to collect and obtain evidence from relevant units and individuals," and relevant units and individuals must provide it truthfully. After a person is criminally detained, the public security organ must submit a request for arrest approval (applying to the procuratorate for formal arrest) within 3 days. Under special circumstances, this may be extended by 1 to 4 days. In circumstances such as committing crimes from place to place (continuous offenses across regions), it may be extended up to 30 days. The procuratorate then takes 7 days to decide. Added together, the decision on whether to arrest is made within at most 37 days. When reviewing an arrest approval, "if the defense attorney makes a request, the procuratorate shall hear the defense attorney's opinions." The attorney also has the right to apply for a change of compulsory measures, such as changing detention to release on bail pending trial, and the case-handling organ must reply within 3 days. From the first interrogation onwards, or from the date compulsory measures (such as detention or arrest) are adopted, you may retain an attorney. During the stage where the case is still under investigation by public security organs, only attorneys may be retained. When an attorney requests a meeting, the detention center must arrange it within 48 hours at the latest. Where an offender may be sentenced to public surveillance, criminal detention, or other penalties lighter than imprisonment, or where an offender may only be sentenced to supplementary punishments without a principal penalty, release on bail pending trial may be granted. Release on bail pending trial means paying a cash deposit or providing a guarantor, and waiting at home while the case proceeds. The maximum duration of release on bail pending trial is 12 months (National)
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2018). Criminal Procedure Law (Amended 2018, Articles 34, 39, 54, 67, 79, 88, 91, 97, 110, 112). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/201810/t20181027_396818.shtml>
entries.notes: These 37 days count the time from initial detention until the procuratorate decides whether or not to approve arrest; it is not the ceiling for total detention. After arrest is approved, the detention period during investigation begins, which continues counting downward. What a lawyer can do within these 37 days is visit the client in person, submit an opinion to the procuratorate that "arrest should not be approved," and apply for release on bail pending trial. In the author's view, if you wait until after public prosecution is instituted to find a lawyer, the checkpoint of arrest approval has already passed. All remaining entries in this section address the exact same issue: whether the counterparty has grounds to report the matter to the police.

entries.title: Do not build or sell game cheats and helpers, including AI helpers that "only read the screen and do not touch memory," nor sell modified versions that add features to software like WeChat
entries.cost: Costs 0 yuan. The price is giving up income from such outsourced gigs and "utility tools." The hard part is that this money comes quickly, and it is not immediately obvious who would pursue legal liability
entries.summary: Selling cheats to 20 person-times or earning 5,000 yuan is enough to warrant a sentence of up to 3 years; especially serious circumstances warrant 3 to 7 years. Someone developed wallhack and aimbot cheats, sold over 80,000 yuan in 3 months, and was sentenced to 1 year of imprisonment suspended for 1 year, plus a 5,000 yuan fine. Someone took server-side programs to run private servers and collected over 20 million yuan in top-ups, receiving a top sentence of 4 years and fines up to 10 million yuan.
entries.benefit: Providing programs and tools specifically used for intruding into or illegally controlling computer information systems is punishable by fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 3 years if circumstances are serious, and concurrently or solely with a fine. Concurrent imposition means both prison time and a fine, whereas sole imposition means only a fine. Where circumstances are especially serious, the penalty is 3 to 7 years of fixed-term imprisonment and a fine. The threshold for "serious circumstances" is providing tools to 20 person-times or more, or illegal gains of 5,000 yuan or more. Illegal gains refer to the money made through the act. Intentionally circumventing or undermining technical protection measures established by rights holders may also constitute the crime of copyright infringement, punishable by not more than 3 years of fixed-term imprisonment, or 3 to 10 years if circumstances are serious. Official cases: Wang and others manufactured and sold cheats that achieved wallhack and aimbot functionality by reading and modifying game memory. In 3 months, they sold over 80,000 yuan with profits exceeding 30,000 yuan. They were sentenced to 1 year of imprisonment suspended for 1 year, with a fine of 5,000 yuan. A 1-year suspension means receiving a 1-year sentence without being locked up initially; if no further offenses are committed during that year, there is no need to serve prison time. Xiang and others sold "TZ" series cheats with sales exceeding 200,000 yuan; Xiang was sentenced to 3 years of imprisonment suspended for 3 years, and fined 20,000 yuan. Liu and others obtained game server-side programs, modified parameters to run private servers, and collected over 20 million yuan in top-ups. Sentences ranged from 4 years to 2 years and 6 months, with fines from 10 million to 1.3 million yuan. This applies beyond games as well. A Shanghai company developed ROM flashing packages that gave WeChat on mobile phones dozens of extra features such as auto-forwarding, auto-liking, and bulk messaging. These phones were marketed and sold as "marketing phones" totaling 2,381 units. In 2019, the Shanghai Xuhui District Court convicted the company of copyright infringement, imposing a fine of 500,000 yuan on the company, and sentenced the person in charge to 1 year and 6 months of imprisonment suspended for 1 year and 6 months (National)
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Criminal Law (Amended in Accordance with Criminal Law Amendment (XI), Article 285, Paragraph 3; Article 217, Item 6). <https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index.html>; Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate (2011). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases Endangering Computer Information System Security (Article 3). <https://ga.sz.gov.cn/ZWGK/ZCFG/ZCJD/content/post_1304363.html> (Reprinted by Shenzhen Municipal Public Security Bureau); Supreme People's Procuratorate (2026). Shanghai Jing'an: Severely Punishing the Black and Gray Industry of Producing and Selling Game Cheats to Jointly Safeguard a Clean Cyberspace. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/zdgz/202608/t20260825_735480.shtml>; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2021). Typical Cases of Intellectual Property Protection by Procuratorial Organs in 2020 (Case 5). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/xwfbh/wsfbt/202104/t20210425_516525.shtml>; National Copyright Administration (2020). Release of the Top 10 Typical Copyright Cases in Shanghai for 2019 (Released by Shanghai Municipal Copyright Administration, Case 8: Copyright Infringement Case of Shanghai Yugong Network Technology Co., Ltd. and Others). <https://www.ncac.gov.cn/xxfb/ywxx/202004/t20200430_47269.html>
entries.notes: Published cheat judgments all involve reading and writing game memory or bypassing anti-cheat mechanisms. For helper tools that "only capture screens and simulate keystrokes," no official court precedents have been found yet. However, the ticket-snagging case in Item 3 demonstrates that not touching memory and merely sending requests can equally be convicted as the crime of illegally obtaining data. Ultimately, whether an act constitutes a crime and which specific offense applies is determined by case-handling organs based on the evidence and materials submitted when vendors report to the police, not by what the author says. Selling to 20 person-times meets the threshold for "serious circumstances," which is a very low volume.

entries.title: Do not write or sell scripts for ticket snagging, flash sales, order brushing, or promotion exploiting, even if it is merely "automating button clicks"
entries.cost: Costs 0 yuan and takes no time
entries.summary: Even without modifying memory or cracking systems, simply sending requests faster than a human can still lead to criminal conviction; earning 5,000 yuan or causing 10,000 yuan in losses to the other party is sufficient. Someone used purchased 12306 accounts to snag over 200 tickets on behalf of others and earned over 20,000 yuan; they were sentenced to 1 year and 6 months of imprisonment suspended for 1 year and 6 months, and fined 5,000 yuan. A person selling ticket-snagging software in an online store was ordered to pay 20,000 yuan in compensation for unfair competition.
entries.benefit: Intruding into computer information systems or obtaining data stored therein by other technical means is punishable by fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 3 years, and concurrently or solely with a fine, where circumstances are serious; where circumstances are especially serious, the penalty is 3 to 7 years. The threshold for "serious circumstances" is illegal gains of 5,000 yuan or more, or causing losses of 10,000 yuan or more. Official cases: An individual used cheating software to import purchased 12306 accounts in bulk, submitting ticket purchase requests intensively via multithreading. He snagged more than 200 train tickets on behalf of others and reaped over 20,000 yuan in profit. The court convicted him of the crime of illegally obtaining computer information system data, sentencing him to 1 year and 6 months of imprisonment suspended for 1 year and 6 months, with a fine of 5,000 yuan. Zheng sold ticket-snagging software targeting a ticketing app in an online store; he was found to have engaged in unfair competition and ordered to pay 20,000 yuan in damages (National)
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Criminal Law (Amended in Accordance with Criminal Law Amendment (XI), Article 285, Paragraph 2). <https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index.html>; Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate (2011). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases Endangering Computer Information System Security (Article 1). <https://ga.sz.gov.cn/ZWGK/ZCFG/ZCJD/content/post_1304363.html>; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2026). Shanghai Jing'an: Investigation and Prosecution of a Case of Using Cheating Software to Snag Train Tickets in Bulk for Profit. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/dfjcdt/202607/t20260707_731426.shtml>; Supreme People's Court (2025). Typical Intellectual Property Cases of the People's Courts in 2024 (Case 7, Unfair Competition Case Involving Ticket-Snagging Software). <https://enipc.court.gov.cn/zh-cn/news/view-4205.html>
entries.notes: The script in the ticket-snagging case did not modify memory or crack any systems; it was simply "faster than humans," yet it was still convicted under Article 285 of the Criminal Law. Charging money to snag tickets on behalf of others and selling scripts both count as seeking illegal profits. For the scenario of using it just once for personal use, no official cases were found.

entries.title: Web scrapers should only crawl public pages requiring no login, without bypassing anti-scraping defenses or touching personal information, and crawled data must not be sold
entries.cost: Costs 0 yuan. A scraper is a program that automatically browses web pages and extracts data from them. Before scraping, check the robots file and API authorization terms; robots is the file a website places in its root directory specifying which pages are disallowed from scraping. Do not scrape data that requires logging in, tokens (temporary access credentials), or cracking signatures to obtain. The hard part is that obtaining this data is technically effortless, so refraining relies entirely on self-discipline
entries.summary: Bypassing defenses such as login, tokens, and signatures to obtain data is punishable by up to 3 years of imprisonment under serious circumstances, and 3 to 7 years under especially serious circumstances. Scraping personal information brings even greater trouble. 50 entries regarding whereabouts, communication contents, credit reports, or property constitute serious circumstances. 500 entries of accommodation, health, or transaction data, 5,000 entries of other types, or making 5,000 yuan in profit, are treated the same.
entries.benefit: Obtaining data from systems by circumventing protections carries the same sentencing scale as Item 3 (scripts for ticket snagging, flash sales, and order brushing): imprisonment of not more than 3 years, or 3 to 7 years. Illegally obtaining, selling, or providing citizens' personal information constitutes "serious circumstances" if it meets any of the following criteria: 50 or more entries of whereabouts tracking, communication contents, credit information, or property information; 500 or more entries of accommodation, communication records, health, or transaction information; 5,000 or more entries of other personal information; or illegal gains of 5,000 yuan or more. Serious circumstances warrant fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 3 years, and concurrently or solely a fine; especially serious circumstances warrant 3 to 7 years. Official cases: Software developer Li disguised a feature that stole mobile phone albums as an "Attractiveness Test" app, acquiring 1,751 facial photos. He also resold social engineering database records and was sentenced to 3 years of imprisonment suspended for 3 years. A social engineering database is a database that aggregates personal information leaked from various sources. A network technology company used crawlers to scrape store and order data from a food delivery platform, causing losses of over 40,000 yuan, and was prosecuted for the crime of illegally obtaining computer information system data (National)
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Criminal Law (Amended in Accordance with Criminal Law Amendment (XI), Article 285, Paragraph 2; Article 253-1). <https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index.html>; Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate (2017). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Infringing Citizens' Personal Information (Articles 3, 4, 5). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbt/201705/t20170509_190088.shtml>; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2022). Typical Cases of Procuratorial Organs Punishing Crimes Infringing Citizens' Personal Information in Accordance with Law (Case 2). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/xwfbh/wsfbt/202212/t20221207_594915.shtml>; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2025). Procuratorial Organs Punishing Crimes Endangering Enterprise Data Security in Accordance with Law to Serve and Guarantee Enterprise Innovation and Development (Case 1). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbh/202501/t20250124_680670.shtml>
entries.notes: The 2017 judicial interpretation provides that "providing legally collected information to others without the subject's consent" also counts as "providing." Exporting a company's user table to external partners likewise falls under this provision. 5,000 entries is merely the volume of a single small database table.

entries.title: Do not accept development orders for gambling, fraud, or pornography apps; do not set up payment gateways or unban accounts for "clients"
entries.cost: Costs 0 yuan. The price is giving up these outsourced gigs with high quotations and vague requirements. The hard part is that the money offered by the counterparty is often significantly higher than normal orders
entries.summary: Accepting development orders while knowingly aware that it is a gambling app will be handled as being an accomplice to establishing a casino. The crime of establishing a casino carries a sentence of up to 5 years, or 5 to 10 years for serious offenses—far heavier than simply providing assistance, which is capped at 3 years. In an esports betting app case, 28 people were sentenced to 1 year to 3 years and 6 months for establishing a casino. A person who unbanned QQ accounts for a fraud gang was sentenced to 1 year and 6 months, and fined 20,000 yuan.
entries.benefit: Knowingly providing technical support, payment settlement, or other assistance to others using the internet to commit crimes is punishable by fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 3 years, and concurrently or solely with a fine, where circumstances are serious. Where the act concurrently constitutes other crimes, punishment is imposed under the heavier charge. Establishing a casino carries a sentence of not more than 5 years and a fine; where circumstances are serious, the sentence is 5 to 10 years. Official cases: The Zhang Sheng Group developed gambling games and engaged in "turnkey white-label exports" (baowang waixiao), collecting site-building and reporting fees, involving nearly 7 billion yuan. Zhang Sheng was sentenced to 9 years and 9 months, and fined 50 million yuan. Seventy-nine people responsible for outsourced R&D, including Wang Qiang, received sentences ranging from 6 months to 9 years and 9 months. Chen Dong and others developed and operated an esports betting app with a tech team writing code in Hainan; 28 individuals were sentenced to prison terms ranging from 1 year to 3 years and 6 months for the crime of establishing a casino, alongside fines. Zhang ran a studio unbanning suspended QQ accounts for fraud syndicates and was sentenced to 1 year and 6 months, plus a 20,000 yuan fine (National)
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Criminal Law (Amended in Accordance with Criminal Law Amendment (XI), Article 287-2; Article 303, Paragraph 2). <https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index.html>; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2023). Setting Up Gambling Websites and Selling Them, Involving Nearly 7 Billion Yuan. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/zdgz/202307/t20230711_621248.shtml>; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2022). Minhang District, Shanghai: Handling a New Type of Online Casino Establishment Case. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/zdgz/202208/t20220805_569952.shtml>; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2025). Typical Cases of Punishing the Crime of Aiding Information Network Criminal Activities and Related Crimes in Accordance with Law (Case 1). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbt/202507/t20250728_702377.shtml>
entries.notes: "Knowing" does not require the counterparty to state the intended purpose out loud. Quotations significantly above market price, functionalities consisting of top-ups, cash withdrawals, and odds calculations, and clients refusing to explain their purpose will all be used during case handling to infer that you were clearly aware. Technical personnel developing gambling apps are treated as accomplices to the crime of establishing a casino, rather than under the tier capped at 3 years for aiding information network criminal activities (abbreviated as bangxin zui in Chinese).

entries.title: Hand over all account permissions upon departure; do not drop databases, leave backdoors, or change passwords to lock systems, even if the company owes you money
entries.cost: Costs 0 yuan. If the company owes you wages, recover them through labor arbitration instead of taking matters into your own hands (for labor arbitration, see Section 7). The hard part is resisting the impulse to touch the systems in the heat of anger
entries.summary: Having accounts and passwords issued by the company does not mean you can still use them after leaving. Illegally controlling systems carries up to 3 years of imprisonment under serious circumstances. Deleting data so that systems cannot function carries up to 5 years where consequences are serious, and 5 years or more where consequences are especially serious. A dismissed engineer used his original administrator account to delete data and logs, causing over 120,000 yuan in losses; he was sentenced to 3 years of imprisonment suspended for 5 years, and fined 30,000 yuan.
entries.benefit: Illegally controlling a computer information system, if the circumstances are serious, is sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 3 years, and concurrently or independently sentenced to a fine; if the circumstances are especially serious, the sentence is 3 to 7 years. Deleting or modifying system functions or data, causing the system to fail to operate normally, if the consequences are serious, is sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 5 years; if the consequences are especially serious, the sentence is not less than 5 years. Official cases: After senior IT engineer Lü [Surname] was dismissed, he logged into the company's shared server using the original administrator account. He changed passwords and deleted data and logs, causing losses of over 120,000 yuan. He was sentenced to 3 years of imprisonment suspended for 5 years, and fined 30,000 yuan. Software company employee Bai [Surname] intentionally added erroneous code while writing an upgrade program, causing customer systems to be unable to log in, resulting in losses of over 40,000 yuan. He was prosecuted for the crime of destroying computer information systems (Nationwide)
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Criminal Law (amended in accordance with Criminal Law Amendment (XI), Article 285, Paragraph 2; Article 286). <https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index.html>; Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate (2011). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases Involving Hazards to Computer Information System Security (Articles 1, 11). <https://ga.sz.gov.cn/ZWGK/ZCFG/ZCJD/content/post_1304363.html> (reprinted by Shenzhen Public Security Bureau); Supreme People's Procuratorate (2024). Typical Cases of Procuratorial Organs "Severely Punishing Cybercrime in Accordance with Law and Assisting in the Comprehensive Governance of Cyberspace" (Case 6). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbh/202402/t20240223_644505.shtml>; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2025). Procuratorial Organs Severely Punishing Crimes Infringing on Enterprise Data Security in Accordance with the Law to Serve and Safeguard Enterprise Innovation and Development (Case 7). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbh/202501/t20250124_680670.shtml>
entries.notes: Accounts and passwords provided by a company do not mean you can still use them after leaving your job. Logging in with an account beyond the scope of authorization, according to the stance in Procuratorial Guiding Case No. 36, is considered intrusion; see Item 9 (Do not test others' systems without written authorization). In the Lü [Surname] case, after logging in, he modified the administrator password and deleted data. The procuratorate found that the system did not shut down as a result, so he was not prosecuted for the crime of destroying computer information systems, but instead for the crime of illegally controlling computer information systems. Losses are calculated together with necessary expenses incurred to restore the data. According to the 2011 interpretation by the SPC and SPP, causing losses of 10,000 yuan or more qualifies as "serious circumstances", and reaching 50,000 yuan is considered especially serious. The losses in the Lü [Surname] case exceeded 120,000 yuan, which was recognized as especially serious circumstances.

entries.title: Do not take source code, customer lists, or technical documentation when departing; do not upload them to personal cloud drives; do not reuse them at your next employer
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Completely delete company materials from personal computers and cloud drives before departing. The difficulty lies in the fact that some files were written line by line by yourself, making it hard to part with them
entries.summary: The copyright of code written on the job generally belongs to the company, and customer lists may also qualify as trade secrets; taking them away amounts to taking company property. A departed employee who brought security inspection system source code to a new company was personally sentenced to 5 years and fined 500,000 yuan, and the new company was fined 4 million yuan. Someone who exploited system vulnerabilities to download over 33,000 design files was sentenced to 1 year and 10 months. The company can also independently seek civil damages from you.
entries.benefit: Breaching confidentiality obligations to disclose trade secrets or use them for oneself, if the circumstances are serious, is sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 3 years, and concurrently or independently sentenced to a fine; if the circumstances are especially serious, the sentence is 3 to 10 years and a fine. The Anti-Unfair Competition Law also classifies two acts as infringement: obtaining trade secrets via "electronic intrusion" (intruding into systems via technical means); and instigating or aiding others in breaching confidentiality obligations. Official cases: Sun [Surname]ming and other departed employees took security inspection system source code and core algorithms and used them in the new company's products. Sun [Surname]ming was sentenced to 5 years and fined 500,000 yuan, and the new company was fined 4 million yuan. Tian [Surname] exploited system vulnerabilities to download more than 33,000 design files, and was sentenced to 1 year and 10 months and fined 100,000 yuan. Engineer Yang [Surname] stored App module source code on personal computers and in the cloud, and developed similar Apps after jumping ship; he was prosecuted for the crime of infringing upon trade secrets (Nationwide)
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Criminal Law (amended in accordance with Criminal Law Amendment (XI), Article 219). <https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index.html>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2025). Anti-Unfair Competition Law (2025 Revision, Article 10). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699862.shtml>; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2025). Typical Cases of Intellectual Property Protection by Procuratorial Organs (Case 7). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbh/202504/t20250423_693691.shtml>; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2020). Typical Cases of Intellectual Property Protection by Procuratorial Organs for 2019 (Case 16). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbh/202004/t20200425_459623.shtml>; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2025). Procuratorial Organs Severely Punishing Crimes Infringing on Enterprise Data Security in Accordance with the Law to Serve and Safeguard Enterprise Innovation and Development (Case 5). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbh/202501/t20250124_680670.shtml>
entries.notes: The copyright of "code written by oneself" generally also belongs to the company; on this point, see Item 13 (Code written using company resources belongs to the company). Taking it away amounts to taking company property. Customer lists constitute business operation information and may also constitute trade secrets. Beyond criminal sentencing, the company can also initiate separate civil claims for damages.

entries.title: Do not run your own programs on others' computers, servers, or cameras; do not use company machines for mining
entries.cost: Costs nothing and takes no time
entries.summary: Controlling others' computers, servers, or cameras without permission: reaching 20 units results in a sentence of not more than 3 years; if especially serious, 3 to 7 years. If it does not reach the threshold of a crime, it also entails detention of not more than 5 days, and possible fines of 50,000 to 500,000 yuan. Persons who have received criminal punishment for this are subject to a lifetime ban from key positions in cybersecurity management and network operation.
entries.benefit: Exercising illegal control over computer information systems, if the circumstances are serious, is sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 3 years, and concurrently or independently sentenced to a fine; if the circumstances are especially serious, the sentence is 3 to 7 years. Illegally controlling 20 or more units constitutes "serious circumstances". If it does not yet reach the threshold of a crime, public security organs shall confiscate illegal gains, impose detention of not more than 5 days, and may impose a fine of 50,000 to 500,000 yuan. If the circumstances are relatively serious, detention of 5 to 15 days is imposed, and a fine of 100,000 to 1,000,000 yuan may be imposed. Those who have received public security administrative penalties may not hold key positions in cybersecurity management and network operations for 5 years, and those who have received criminal punishments are banned for life. Official cases: Li [Surname] purchased IP addresses of network cameras and used software to control 105 cameras to pry into privacy; he was sentenced to 3 years of imprisonment suspended for 5 years, and fined 20,000 yuan. Wu [Surname] and others implanted trojans into mobile phone motherboards, controlling more than 3.3 million mobile phones to return verification codes; they were sentenced to between 2 years and 4 years and 6 months (Nationwide)
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Criminal Law (amended in accordance with Criminal Law Amendment (XI), Article 285, Paragraph 2). <https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index.html>; Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate (2011). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases Involving Hazards to Computer Information System Security (Article 1). <https://ga.sz.gov.cn/ZWGK/ZCFG/ZCJD/content/post_1304363.html>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2025). Cybersecurity Law (amended in 2025, effective January 1, 2026, Articles 29, 66; 2016 text Articles 27, 63; the lifetime career ban is in Paragraph 3 of the amended Article 66). <https://www.cac.gov.cn/2025-12/29/c_1768735112911946.htm>; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2022). Binzhou Development Zone, Shandong: Handling an Illegal Control of Computer Information Systems Case. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/dfjcdt/202205/t20220518_557113.shtml>; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2021). Typical Cases of Fully Exercising Procuratorial Functions to Advance Cyberspace Governance (Case 6). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/xwfbh/wsfbh/202101/t20210125_507452.shtml>
entries.notes: For mining using company servers, no published cases from the SPP or SPC were found; this item is written according to the legal provision on "controlling others' systems without permission." "Lifetime ban from engaging in key positions" is an additional consequence attached by the Cybersecurity Law on top of fines and criminal sentencing, which is heavier than a fine for technical professionals.

entries.title: Do not test others' systems without written authorization; "good intentions" and "reporting after the fact" are not statutory grounds for exculpation
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Before participating in vendor SRCs or crowdsourced testing, first obtain documents explicitly stating the scope of authorization, target lists, and testable time windows. An SRC is a Security Response Center organized by vendors themselves specifically to receive externally reported vulnerabilities. Stop once it is verified that the vulnerability indeed exists. The difficulty lies in giving up that impulse to "try it out in passing"
entries.summary: Statutory convictions look at whether there was authorization and how much was obtained; they make no mention of your original intention. Obtaining 500 sets of ordinary account passwords, or earning 5,000 yuan, or causing 10,000 yuan in losses to the other party is enough to warrant a sentence of not more than 3 years. To prove a vulnerability, exporting a user table in passing often exceeds 500 sets in a single action. Having an account and password in hand but using them beyond the authorized scope also constitutes intrusion.
entries.benefit: Systems of ordinary companies and individuals belong to computer information systems outside the fields of state affairs, national defense construction, and cutting-edge science and technology. Intruding into such systems, or using other technical means to obtain data stored, processed, or transmitted therein: if the circumstances are serious, one is sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 3 years or criminal detention, and concurrently or independently sentenced to a fine. If the circumstances are especially serious, the sentence is 3 to 7 years and a fine. "Serious circumstances" have several criteria: obtaining 10 or more sets of identity authentication information (such as accounts and passwords) for online financial services like payment settlement, securities trading, and futures trading; obtaining 500 or more sets of other identity authentication information; illegally controlling 20 or more computer information systems; illegal gains of 5,000 yuan or more, or causing economic losses of 10,000 yuan or more. Reaching 5 times or more the figures above constitutes "especially serious circumstances". Official cases: Procuratorial Guiding Case No. 36 established a statement: "Using accounts and passwords to log into a computer information system beyond the scope of authorization constitutes the act of intruding into a computer information system." This means that having the account and password originally in hand, but using them outside the scope of authorization, is in itself an act of intrusion. In that case, three individuals used accounts, passwords, and tokens acquired through work to log into internal company systems remotely. They downloaded data outside their work scope and sold it online, generating illegal gains of 37,000 yuan. The three were sentenced to 4 years, 3 years and 9 months, and 4 years respectively, and each was fined 40,000 yuan (Nationwide)
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Criminal Law (amended in accordance with Criminal Law Amendment (XI), Article 285, Paragraphs 1, 2). <https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index.html>; Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate (2011). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases Involving Hazards to Computer Information System Security (Article 1). <https://ga.sz.gov.cn/ZWGK/ZCFG/ZCJD/content/post_1304363.html> (reprinted by Shenzhen Public Security Bureau); Supreme People's Procuratorate (2017). Ninth Batch of Guiding Cases (Procuratorial Guiding Case No. 36, Wei Menglong, Gong Xu, and Xue Dongdong's Case of Illegally Obtaining Computer Information System Data). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/jczdal/201710/t20171017_202593.shtml>; CNR News (2016-06-29). White Hat Arrested After Publishing Vulnerability; Jiayuan Denies "Phishing" Him Into a Trap (Reporter Zhao Ke, Intern Reporter Liu Xiangxi). <https://m.cnr.cn/news/yctt/20160629/t20160629_522531823.html> (Web Archive <https://web.archive.org/web/20261005043859/https://m.cnr.cn/news/yctt/20160629/t20160629_522531823.html>)
entries.notes: That guiding case, Procuratorial Guiding Case No. 36, was itself a case of profiting from selling data. Citing it is solely for the sentence "logging in beyond the scope of authorization also counts as intrusion," not to imply that good-faith testing will receive an equally severe sentence. Neither Article 285 of the Criminal Law nor the 2011 interpretation writes good intentions or reporting after the fact as reasons not to constitute a crime. Based on this, the author infers: what your original intention was and whether you reported it after the fact cannot cancel out the criminal charge; they can only affect the severity of sentencing or whether to prosecute. A vendor first expressing thanks and subsequently reporting the incident to police are not contradictory; saying thank you does not equate to authorization. In 2016, a security researcher colloquially known as a "white hat" submitted a vulnerability of the Century Jiayuan website to a third-party vulnerability platform. Later, Century Jiayuan reported it to the police, and he was arrested. Century Jiayuan told reporters that the police report was because data had been taken away by someone, and at the time they did not know the person taking the data was the one who submitted the vulnerability. This case only had media reports, without a verdict or official bulletin, and there is no official statement on the ultimate outcome. No verbatim verifiable cases of good-faith testing were found on the official websites of the SPC and SPP either, so this item is graded solely according to legal provisions and penalty standards. If you want to do it, go through vendors' public SRCs or assessments with written entrustment, putting the scope, targets, and time windows into the documents. Use minimal evidence to prove the existence of a vulnerability; do not extract data in bulk. The tier that does not reach the threshold of a crime also incurs public security administrative penalties as well as career bans, with fine amounts and durations identical to Item 8 (Do not run your own programs on others' machines). How to handle vulnerabilities after discovery: see Item 10 (Submit vulnerabilities according to regulations).

entries.title: Submit vulnerabilities according to regulations; do not disclose details, release exploit tools, or hand them over to overseas entities before patching
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Report vulnerabilities to the product provider or to official platforms. Before the vendor fixes them, do not publish details or verification code
entries.summary: Individuals are also governed by the Provisions on the Administration of Network Product Security Vulnerabilities. Before the vendor provides a remediation method, you cannot disclose the vulnerability, nor disclose details of vulnerabilities in systems currently in use. You cannot release programs or tools dedicated to exploiting vulnerabilities; when disclosing, you must simultaneously clarify how to fix them. Undisclosed vulnerabilities must not be provided to overseas organizations and individuals other than the vendor.
entries.benefit: These Provisions govern three categories of targets: domestic network product providers, network operators, and organizations or individuals engaged in activities such as vulnerability discovery, collection, and publication. No organization or individual may use vulnerabilities to engage in activities endangering cybersecurity, nor illegally collect, sell, or publish vulnerability information. Publishing vulnerability information to the public must adhere to five rules. First, it must not be published before the product provider offers remediation measures. Second, details regarding the existence of vulnerabilities in networks, information systems, and equipment currently in use by network operators must not be published. Third, hazards and risks must not be deliberately exaggerated, and vulnerability information must not be used to conduct malicious hype or fraud. Fourth, programs and tools specifically used to exploit vulnerabilities to conduct activities endangering cybersecurity must not be published or provided. Fifth, remediation or preventive measures should be released simultaneously when publishing. In addition, undisclosed vulnerability information must not be provided to overseas organizations or individuals other than the product provider. The Provisions encourage reporting vulnerabilities to four official platforms: First, the Cybersecurity Threat and Vulnerability Information Sharing Platform of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. Second, the Vulnerability Platform of the National Network and Information Security Information Notification Center. Third, the Vulnerability Platform of the National Computer Network Emergency Response Technical Team/Coordination Center of China. Fourth, the Vulnerability Database of the China Information Security Evaluation Center. Those who violate the provisions by collecting or publishing vulnerability information shall be handled according to law by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and the Ministry of Public Security in accordance with their respective duties. Where the circumstances constitute situations stipulated in the Cybersecurity Law, punishment shall be imposed in accordance with that law. Publishing network security information such as system vulnerabilities to the public shall comply with relevant state regulations. For violations, the relevant competent departments shall order rectification, issue warnings, and may impose fines of not less than 10,000 yuan and not more than 100,000 yuan. For refusal to rectify or serious circumstances, fines of not less than 100,000 yuan and not more than 1,000,000 yuan shall be imposed. They may also order the suspension of relevant businesses, suspension of operations for rectification, or closure of websites or applications. Relevant business permits may also be revoked or business licenses revoked. Directly responsible persons in charge and other directly responsible personnel shall be fined not less than 10,000 yuan and not more than 100,000 yuan (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, Cyberspace Administration of China, Ministry of Public Security (2021). Provisions on the Administration of Network Product Security Vulnerabilities (MIIT Lian Wang An [2021] No. 66, Articles 2, 4, 9, 10, 14, effective September 1, 2021). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2021/content_5641351.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2025). Cybersecurity Law (amended in 2025, effective January 1, 2026, Articles 28, 65; 2016 text Articles 26, 62; Article 14 of the Provisions cites the article numbers from the 2016 text). <https://www.cac.gov.cn/2025-12/29/c_1768735112911946.htm>
entries.notes: The Provisions explicitly include individuals among the regulated subjects; "I am just an amateur hobbyist" is not an exception. Submitting domestic system vulnerabilities to overseas bug bounty platforms falls squarely under the rule that "undisclosed vulnerabilities must not be provided overseas." Whether one is qualified to test is addressed in Item 9 (Do not test others' systems without written authorization); this must be viewed separately from how to handle vulnerabilities once obtained. Legally discovered vulnerabilities may also be penalized due to non-compliant publication methods; vulnerabilities discovered through unauthorized testing are problematic at both ends—testing and publication. The Provisions do not specifically differentiate the scenario where "the vendor has been notified, but does not fix it." The author's recommendation is to keep a record of the consultation and reporting process, while simultaneously reporting to the four official platforms mentioned above.

entries.title: Do not sell circumvention tools or VPN accounts; do not set up such nodes for others
entries.cost: Costs nothing and takes no time
entries.summary: Setting up outbound lines on one's own, or using international channels other than national public channels: public security organs may order cessation of networking, issue a warning, impose a fine of not more than 15,000 yuan, and confiscate illegal gains. For those running businesses based on this, case-handling organs can handle it under the crime of illegal business operations; serious circumstances warrant a sentence of not more than 5 years. This item addresses selling and setting up nodes. For personal use, penalties are capped at a warning plus a fine.
entries.benefit: Direct international networking must use international entrance/exit channels provided by the national public telecommunications network. No entity or individual may establish or use other channels on their own: neither setting up outbound lines themselves nor using channels set up by others. For violations, public security organs shall order cessation of networking, give warnings, and may concurrently impose fines of not more than 15,000 yuan and confiscate illegal gains. For those running businesses based on this, case-handling organs may handle it as the crime of illegal business operations. Serious circumstances warrant a sentence of not more than 5 years, and a concurrent or independent fine of 1 to 5 times the illegal gains. Especially serious circumstances warrant a sentence of not less than 5 years (Nationwide)
entries.sources: State Council (1997). Interim Provisions on the Administration of International Interconnection of Computer Information Networks (Articles 6, 14). <https://nyncw.cq.gov.cn/wsdw/zz/zhfb/wlyxxaq/202406/t20240619_13306645.html> (reprinted by Chongqing Municipal Commission of Agriculture and Rural Affairs); National People's Congress (2020). Criminal Law (amended in accordance with Criminal Law Amendment (XI), Article 225, Item 4). <https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index.html>
entries.notes: At the time of writing this section, no published judgments involving circumvention were found on the official websites of the SPC and SPP, and local handling varies considerably, so it is graded B. For personal self-use, the maximum penalty is the warning plus fine stipulated in Article 14 of the Interim Provisions.

entries.title: Signed a non-compete agreement: if the company fails to pay monthly compensation after departure, issue a written demand; if unpaid for 3 full months, you can terminate it; positions with no access to trade secrets can request confirmation that the clause is ineffective
entries.cost: Costs no money. When leaving, properly retain the original copy of the non-compete agreement, as well as evidence that the company failed to make monthly payments
entries.summary: A non-compete restriction means you are not allowed to work for industry competitors for a period after departure, up to a maximum of 2 years, and the company must pay monthly compensation. If no amount is agreed upon, it is paid at 30% of your average wage over the 12 months prior to departure, not lower than the local minimum wage. If unpaid for 3 months due to the company's reasons, you can request termination. Starting in 2025, for positions with no access to trade secrets, you can request confirmation that the clause is ineffective.
entries.benefit: Non-compete restrictions can only bind senior executives, senior technical personnel, and other persons with confidentiality obligations. The maximum term is 2 years. The company must provide monthly economic compensation during this period. If no compensation amount is agreed upon, it is paid at 30% of the average wage over the 12 months prior to departure, and not lower than the local minimum wage. If unpaid for 3 months due to the company's own reasons, the employee can request to terminate this non-compete restriction. If the company proactively terminates it, it must pay an additional 3 months of compensation. Starting in 2025, employees whose positions had no knowledge of or access to trade secrets can request confirmation that the clause is ineffective. If the agreed scope exceeds the secrets they actually knew, the exceeding portion is invalid. Official case: A pharmaceutical company sued its Chief Technology Officer, Zheng, claiming 7.1 million yuan in liquidated damages. The court found that the new employer's products were not substitutable with the original company's, that the non-compete scope should be limited to the secrets he actually knew, and dismissed all claims (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2012). Labor Contract Law (2012 Amendment, Articles 23, 24). <https://yjglj.fushun.gov.cn/008/20260622/d846d3c2-df3d-4c4c-af16-898ede43e1ee.html> (reprinted by Fushun Municipal Emergency Management Bureau); Supreme People's Court (2020). Interpretation (I) on the Application of Law to the Trial of Labor Dispute Cases (Articles 36 to 40). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/282121.html>; Supreme People's Court (2025). Interpretation (II) on the Application of Law to the Trial of Labor Dispute Cases (Fa Shi [2025] No. 12, Articles 13 to 15). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/472691.html>; Supreme People's Court (2025). Typical Cases of Labor Disputes (Case 4). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/472681.html>
entries.notes: The legal provisions only look at whether it has been unpaid for 3 full months due to the company's reasons; a written demand is the author's recommended method for preserving evidence. Conversely, if the agreement is valid and the company has paid monthly, but you still go to work for a competing product, you must pay liquidated damages as agreed. After paying, you may also be required to observe the remainder of the non-compete period. If the company agrees with senior executives, senior technical personnel, and other persons with confidentiality obligations that they may not engage in competing activities during their employment, it also counts even if the company does not pay extra money. Except for non-compete restrictions and service terms for special training, the company cannot stipulate that you pay liquidated damages; see Section 19, Item 22 (Demanded to pay liquidated damages upon departure).

entries.title: Code written during working hours or using company resources belongs to the company; build your own open-source projects using your own time and equipment, without mixing company code
entries.cost: Costs no money. Read the intellectual property clauses in your employment contract clearly when onboarding. The difficulty lies in personal projects and company work often being mixed on one computer; they must be separated
entries.summary: For software written mainly relying on company equipment, internal networks, or business data and for which the company bears responsibility, copyright belongs to the company, and you only retain the right of authorship; the same applies if stipulated in a contract. If written after hours, as long as company computers or business data were used, it may likewise be counted as the company's. For inventions made primarily using company resources, patents also belong to the company.
entries.benefit: Works created to complete the work tasks of an entity are works for hire (things made while working on the job). Under general circumstances, copyright belongs to the author, the entity has the right of priority use within its business scope, and the author may not license a third party to use it in the same manner within 2 years. But there are two categories of exceptions. One category includes engineering designs, software, and other works created mainly utilizing the entity's material and technical conditions and for which the entity bears responsibility. The other category includes works stipulated by contract to belong to the entity. For these two categories, the author only retains the right of authorship. An entity's material and technical conditions refer to things like company equipment, internal networks, and business data. Inventions and creations completed in execution of the entity's tasks, or mainly utilizing the entity's material and technical conditions, are service inventions. The right to apply for a patent and the patent rights obtained both belong to the entity (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2020). Copyright Law (2020 Amendment, Article 18). <http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202011/t20201119_308796.html>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2020). Patent Law (2020 Amendment, Article 6). <http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202011/t20201119_308800.html>
entries.notes: Software is directly written into the category of "copyright belongs to the entity"; programmers almost never fall into the tier of "copyright belongs to the author, entity enjoys priority use within two years." Even if "written after hours," as long as company computers, internal networks, or company business data were used, it can equally be considered created mainly relying on the entity's equipment and materials. If you want to keep personal projects clean, use your own machine, don't touch company repositories, and don't overlap with company business.

entries.title: When building products with open-source code such as GPL, open-source them as required by the license or change the license; do not act as if "no one cares"
entries.cost: Costs no money. Before using other people's open-source code, take a look at its license (the conditions of use specified by the author). The GPL family requires products using it to also open-source their code, which conflicts with closed-source commercial sales; if there is a conflict, switch to another. The difficulty lies in giving up a library you are already accustomed to using
entries.summary: For copyright infringement, compensation is paid according to the other party's losses or the profits you earned; for intentional and serious circumstances, compensation can be awarded at 1 to 5 times. A company hired a competitor's former employee to create substantially similar software, arguing that the other party's software used GPLv2 and was supposed to be open-source. The Supreme People's Court held that whether the other party open-sourced or not did not affect its copyright, and still ordered cessation of infringement and compensation of 500,000 yuan.
entries.benefit: For copyright infringement, compensation is paid based on the actual losses of the rights holder, or based on the profits earned by the infringer. If neither can be calculated clearly, it is determined with reference to how much normally needs to be paid to purchase this authorization. In cases of intentional infringement with serious circumstances, compensation of 1 to 5 times can be awarded. Where public interest is harmed, illegal gains may additionally be confiscated and fines imposed. Official case: (2021) Zui Gao Fa Zhi Min Zhong No. 51. The defendant hired former employees of the plaintiff and developed gateway software substantially similar to the plaintiff's software. The defendant argued that the plaintiff's software was based on GPLv2 and was originally supposed to be open-source. The Supreme People's Court determined that "whether the developer itself violated the GPLv2 agreement and whether it enjoys software copyright are two separate issues," ordering cessation of infringement and compensation of 500,000 yuan (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2020). Copyright Law (2020 Amendment, Articles 53, 54). <http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202011/t20201119_308796.html>; Intellectual Property Tribunal of the Supreme People's Court (2022). Case of Copyright Infringement Involving "Open-Source Software" ((2021) Zui Gao Fa Zhi Min Zhong No. 51). <https://ipc.court.gov.cn/zh-cn/news/view-3042.html>
entries.notes: This case illustrates that "the other party used GPL code" cannot serve as an excuse for copying it. Conversely, GPL authors suing commercial parties who fail to open-source have already obtained legally effective judgments domestically; because the original text was not found on the Supreme People's Court official website, it is not cited in this section. Rated Level B because compliance with open-source licenses can only be governed by contracts and general provisions in copyright law, with no single dedicated statutory provision.

entries.title: When making an App, collect only personal information strictly necessary for business, obtain guardian consent for users under 14, and write a clear privacy policy
entries.cost: Costs no money. Before launch, cross-check the App's requested permissions list against the privacy policy, dropping unnecessary permissions whenever possible. The difficulty lies in product managers always wanting to retain extra data that "might be useful later"
entries.summary: Collect only information strictly necessary for business; for those under 14 years old, guardian consent is required. Violators are first ordered to correct, and the App may be suspended. Refusing to correct brings a fine of up to 1 million yuan, and responsible persons are fined 10,000 to 100,000 yuan. Serious cases bring fines of up to 50 million yuan or up to 5% of the previous year's annual turnover, with responsible persons fined 100,000 to 1 million yuan.
entries.benefit: Processing personal information shall have a clear and reasonable purpose, be directly related to that purpose, and adopt methods that have the least impact on personal rights and interests. Processing personal information requires obtaining individual consent, or complying with statutory circumstances. For individuals under 14 years of age, consent from parents or guardians must be obtained. Violators shall be ordered to correct, issued a warning, and have illegal gains confiscated by regulatory authorities, and services of the unlawful App shall be ordered suspended or terminated. Those refusing to correct shall be fined up to 1 million yuan, and directly responsible persons in charge and other directly responsible personnel shall be fined 10,000 to 100,000 yuan. Where circumstances are serious, a fine of up to 50 million yuan, or up to 5% of the previous year's annual turnover, shall be imposed. Responsible personnel shall be fined 100,000 to 1 million yuan. Such persons may also be barred from serving as directors, supervisors, or senior executives of relevant enterprises for a certain period. Where selling or providing personal information constitutes a crime, see Item 4 (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2021). Personal Information Protection Law (Articles 6, 13, 31, 66). <http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202108/t20210820_313088.html>
entries.notes: The statutory provision does not specify which positions "other directly responsible personnel" refers to. The author deduces that people who write code and design products may also be included; this book found no cases that could be verified verbatim. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology periodically issues notices on the takedown of non-compliant Apps; because this section did not verify which specific notice it was, it is not cited.

entries.title: Complete ICP filing before websites or Apps go live, and retain logs for more than 6 months according to Multi-Level Protection Scheme requirements
entries.cost: Filing is free, done through the cloud vendor's process, which in the author's experience takes several days to a few weeks. Multi-Level Protection Scheme (MLPS) assessments are charged according to level. MLPS, abbreviated as Dengbao, is a set of security management actions required by the state for websites and systems, classified according to system importance
entries.summary: Filing does not cost money; domestic servers without filing that refuse to correct will be shut down. Those claiming non-commercial filing but actually charging fees will be fined 3 to 5 times the illegal gains, or 100,000 to 1 million yuan. Logs must be kept for a full 6 months; refusing to correct or causing consequences brings a fine of 10,000 to 100,000 yuan.
entries.benefit: Commercial internet information services practice licensing, while non-commercial services practice filing. Without obtaining a license or filing, one shall not engage in such activities. For unfiled entities, telecommunications regulatory authorities shall order correction; those refusing to correct shall be ordered to close the website. Unlicensed commercial operations shall have illegal gains confiscated and be fined 3 to 5 times the illegal gains, or fined 100,000 to 1 million yuan. Failing to display the filing number on the website home page incurs a fine of 5,000 to 50,000 yuan. Network operators must establish security management systems, prevent attacks, retain network logs for no less than 6 months, and classify, back up, and encrypt data in accordance with the Multi-Level Protection Scheme (Dengbao). Failure to perform these duties brings an order to correct and a warning.
