Those refusing to correct or causing consequences shall be fined 10,000 to 100,000 yuan, with supervisory personnel fined 5,000 to 50,000 yuan (Nationwide)
entries.sources: State Council (2011). Measures for the Administration of Internet Information Services (2011 Revision, Articles 4, 19, 22). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1860864.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2025). Cybersecurity Law (2025 Amendment, effective January 1, 2026, Articles 23, 61; Articles 21, 59 in the 2016 text). <https://www.cac.gov.cn/2025-12/29/c_1768735112911946.htm>
entries.notes: If domestic servers are not filed, access providers are not allowed to provide access to you. For how to file, fines for not displaying the filing number, and how to check whether a service provider has qualifications, see Section 26, Item 4 (Filing is required if the server is located domestically). The real pitfalls are two situations: filing as personal non-commercial while actually charging fees, or changing domain names or entities without modifying the filing. The author's view is that retaining logs for 6 months is both an obligation and self-protection; when an incident occurs, it can be used to show that you were not the perpetrator. Apps and mini-programs must also be filed before launching, using procedures found in the same item.

entries.title: Conduct security assessments and algorithm filings according to regulations before providing generative AI services to the public, and add labels to generated content
entries.cost: Costs no money, but requires going through the cyberspace administration department's process, which takes some time to complete. As long as the developed tools do not provide services to the domestic public, these measures do not apply
entries.summary: Generative AI services facing the public that can influence public opinion or mobilize people must undergo security assessments and algorithm filings before launch, and must complete alteration or deregistration procedures if modified or discontinued. Generated images and videos must have labels added. Small tools for self-use and not open to the public do not need to worry about this. Violations are punished according to laws such as the Cybersecurity Law.
entries.benefit: Providing generative artificial intelligence services with public opinion attributes or social mobilization capacity shall undergo security assessments in accordance with national regulations. Algorithm filing, as well as subsequent alteration and deregistration procedures, must also be completed pursuant to algorithm recommendation management provisions. Public opinion attributes or social mobilization capacity refers to the ability to influence public views or organize and mobilize people. Providers shall add identifiers to generated content such as images and videos. The measures explicitly state that where enterprises, scientific research institutions, etc. research, develop, and apply generative artificial intelligence technology, "if they do not provide generative artificial intelligence services to the domestic public, the provisions of these measures shall not apply." Those violating the measures "shall be penalized in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations such as the Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China, the Data Security Law of the People's Republic of China, the Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, and the Law of the People's Republic of China on Progress of Science and Technology." The measures took effect on August 15, 2023 (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Cyberspace Administration of China and six other departments (2023). Interim Measures for the Administration of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (Articles 2, 12, 17, 21). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891752.htm>
entries.notes: These measures themselves do not specify fine amounts. Violations require referring back to penalties in the Cybersecurity Law, Data Security Law, and Personal Information Protection Law, hence rated Level B. Civil cases where AI-generated content infringed others' copyright or likeness rights were not verified with original texts on the Supreme People's Court official website and are not cited. For relay stations that resell overseas large-model APIs at low prices, see Item 19 of this section (AI relay stations).

entries.title: Do not build or distribute tools that automatically skip or block ads in other Apps; even free tools can be ruled unfair competition
entries.cost: Costs no money. The price is giving up a very popular small utility. The difficulty lies in feeling that you didn't make any money and merely clicked "skip" on behalf of the user
entries.summary: Building software that skips or blocks ads in other Apps on behalf of users can result in being sued by the other party for unfair competition. Not charging money can still count; business operators governed by law include individuals providing services. A browser that blocked Mango TV's pre-roll ads by default paid 800,000 yuan in compensation. An App enabling users to directly skip Mango TV's splash screen ads paid 80,000 yuan in damages.
entries.benefit: The law stipulates that business operators shall not use technical means to obstruct or disrupt the normal operation of network products or services legally provided by other business operators. Business operators here refer to natural persons, legal persons, and unincorporated organizations providing goods or services. If damage is caused to the other party, compensation is paid based on the other party's actual losses, or based on the benefits you obtained as a result, plus reasonable expenses incurred by the other party to stop the infringement. Market regulation departments can also impose fines of 100,000 to 1 million yuan, and 1 million to 5 million yuan in serious circumstances. Official cases: Built-in features of 720 Browser blocked pre-roll and pause ads on Mango TV's website by default. The first instance dismissed Mango TV's lawsuit. The Guangzhou Intellectual Property Court reversed on appeal, finding it constituted unfair competition and ordering compensation of 800,000 yuan for economic losses and reasonable expenses. In 2021, the Supreme People's Court listed it as a typical case. The "Lan Jingling" App allowed users to directly skip Mango TV's splash screen ads. The first instance ordered it to cease and pay 80,000 yuan in economic losses and 10,000 yuan in reasonable expenses. In April 2024, the Beijing Intellectual Property Court affirmed on appeal. The appellate court held that it actually blocked the splash screen ads, rather than merely clicking "skip" on the user's behalf (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2025 Revision). Anti-Unfair Competition Law (Articles 2, 13, 22, 29). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808181971552b40197b1016efc5437>; Supreme People's Court (2021). Typical Cases of Anti-Monopoly and Anti-Unfair Competition by People's Courts (Case 5: "720 Browser" Unfair Competition Dispute, (2018) Yue 73 Min Zhong No. 1022). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/324491.html>; Beijing Political and Legal Affairs Network (2024-04-18). "Mango TV" Sues "Lan Jingling" for Unfair Competition, Winning in Second Instance (Source: Jingfa Wangshi). <https://www.bj148.org/sa1/ajbb/202404/t20240418_1664299.html>; Caijing Client (2023-09-10). App blocks splash screen ads; Tencent sends lawyer's letter demanding takedown—is it reasonable? (Caijing E-law, Fan Rui). <https://www.mycaijing.com/article/detail/500930?source_id=40> (Web Archive <https://web.archive.org/web/20261005041658/https://www.mycaijing.com/article/detail/500930?source_id=40>)
entries.notes: The two judgments used provisions prior to revision. Following the 2025 revision, this article was moved to Article 13, and data, algorithms, and platform rules were added. The appellate court stated that what was adjudicated was blocking; users clicking "skip" themselves is unaffected. In August 2023, the free ad-skipping tool "Li Tiaotiao" on Android received a lawyer's letter from Tencent. The lawyer's letter stated that it blocked Tencent Browser's ads, constituting unfair competition, and demanded its removal within 48 hours. The developer said it was non-profit and charitable; reports stated it only accepted sporadic tips. Nevertheless, it announced an indefinite suspension of updates, and several similar software programs also stopped. This incident only had media reports, with no lawsuit and no judgment. When individual developers receive a lawyer's letter, they either stop or spend their own money hiring a lawyer to respond to the lawsuit. Ordinary procedures in first instance are required by regulation to conclude within 6 months, which can be extended; attorney fees are generally paid by yourself. For writing a script purely for your own personal use, no cases of enforcement were found. For paying compensation for selling ticket-snatching software under unfair competition, see Item 3 of this section (Ticket-snatching and flash-sale scripts). The beneficiary is yourself.

entries.title: Do not set up "AI relay stations" to resell overseas large-model APIs at low prices: stationmasters in Shanghai have already been criminally detained
entries.cost: Costs no money. The price is giving up a side business with low barriers to entry and seemingly attractive cash flow. If you genuinely want to do model aggregation, take the legitimate path: obtain operating licenses and connect officially authorized models, which will cost significant money and time
entries.summary: AI relay stations are websites that resell overseas large-model API access at low prices. A webmaster in Shanghai stated that he was placed in criminal detention for 37 days as a result, is currently on bail pending trial, will definitely be sentenced, and has already paid restitution and surrendered illicit gains. The Ministry of State Security has also issued a risk warning stating that some relay stations lack operational qualifications, and some unlawfully transmit user data overseas without authorization.
entries.benefit: In June 2026, the Ministry of State Security issued a risk warning. The warning stated that AI relay stations act as an intermediary proxy layer between users and the official services of model developers. Some relay stations lack operational qualifications. Certain stations transmit data input by users to overseas servers without obtaining the compliance qualifications for cross-border data transfer or undergoing statutory security assessment procedures. Some even allow users to bypass restrictions on network access, official authorization, and cross-border transmission. In June 2026, China Newsweek reported on a relevant case. In May 2026, a relay station webmaster in Shanghai posted a shutdown notice in a technical community. He stated that because he had illicitly obtained large-model API interfaces, he was criminally detained by the Shanghai police for 37 days and was currently released on bail pending trial. He said he 「will definitely be sentenced in the future」, had already paid restitution and surrendered illicit gains, and still had to pay a fine. The report stated that such relay stations batch-register or purchase subscription accounts of overseas large models, set up servers abroad as jump hosts, and then resell access to domestic users at low prices (Nationwide / Shanghai).
entries.sources: Ministry of State Security (2026). "AI Relay Stations", Guard Against the Risks. <https://www.szzg.gov.cn/2026/xwzx/szkx/202606/t20260608_5331487.htm> (Digital China Summit official website reprint from the Ministry of State Security WeChat official account); China Newsweek (2026-06-22). AI Relay Stations Face a Rectification "Storm" (Reporter: Meng Qian). <https://www.chinanews.com/cj/2026/06-22/10644787.shtml> (Web archive <https://web.archive.org/web/20261005042903/https://www.chinanews.com/cj/2026/06-22/10644787.shtml>).
entries.notes: This case relies solely on media reports and the personal account of the party involved; there is no court judgment or police bulletin, and there is no official statement on what specific criminal charge was applied. The specific charges and prison sentences circulating online originate from articles by lawyers and are not cited in this book. Therefore, one cannot say that 「operating a relay station is definitely a crime」, but only that individuals have already been placed in criminal detention for doing so. To legally aggregate models, charging fees requires obtaining an operating license; see Section 26, Item 2 (Paid Websites Require Licenses). Providing generative AI services to the public requires filing and registration; see Item 17 of this section (Generative AI Security Assessments). Transferring user data overseas is subject to statutory conditions; see Section 26, Item 10 (Cross-Border Transfer of User Information). Users of relay stations face other risks; see Section 14, Item 10 (AI Relay Stations). The beneficiary is yourself.

entries.title: Do not write, sell, or disseminate software cracking patches, keygens, or cracked versions; once commercial sales reach the threshold, sentences are handed down for the crime of copyright infringement
entries.cost: Zero monetary cost. The trade-off is giving up quick-money side hustles like selling cracked versions, registration keys, or cracked hardware dongles. Also, do not post cracking patches to forums or cloud storage drives. The difficulty lies in the fact that cracking feels like purely technical work rather than stealing.
entries.summary: Verifications like registration key checks and hardware dongles are technical protection measures of software; bypassing them without permission constitutes infringement, and compensation must be paid even if no money was charged. Cracking or selling cracking tools for profit triggers criminal sentencing once illicit gains reach 30,000 yuan or sales reach 50,000 yuan, with a maximum sentence of 10 years. In one case, individuals manufactured and sold cracked dongles bundled with pirated software; three co-defendants received prison sentences ranging from 1 year to 3 years and 2 months.
entries.benefit: First, civil liability. Copyright law permits rights holders to apply technical measures to their works. Technical measures refer to effective technologies, devices, or components used to prevent or restrict unauthorized exploitation of works. Without the permission of the rights holder, no one may intentionally circumvent or break technical measures. Nor may anyone manufacture, import, or provide relevant devices or components to the public for the purpose of circumventing technical measures, or intentionally provide technical services to assist others in circumventing them. Computer software constitutes a copyrightable work; engaging in any of these acts constitutes an infringement, requiring cessation of infringement and compensation for losses. The amount of compensation is calculated based on the actual losses suffered by the rights holder or the profits gained by the infringer. Where damages are difficult to ascertain, they are assessed with reference to standard licensing fees. In cases of intentional infringement with serious circumstances, punitive damages of 1 to 5 times may be awarded. Where public interest is simultaneously harmed, the copyright administration authorities may also confiscate illegal income. Where the illegal business turnover exceeds 50,000 yuan, a fine of 1 to 5 times the turnover may be imposed; where turnover is below 50,000 yuan or cannot be determined, a fine of up to 250,000 yuan may be imposed. Next, criminal liability. Criminal Law Amendment (XI) incorporated 「intentionally circumventing or breaking technical measures」 into the crime of copyright infringement, provided it is done for the purpose of making a profit. Where the illegal gains reach 30,000 yuan or more, or the illegal business turnover reaches 50,000 yuan or more, the penalty is fixed-term imprisonment of up to 3 years, concurrently or separately with a fine. When reaching 10 times these amounts, the penalty is 3 to 10 years of imprisonment concurrently with a fine. Anyone who, knowing that others are committing the crime of copyright infringement, provides them with devices, components, or technical services primarily used to circumvent or break technical measures shall also be held criminally liable under this crime once the thresholds are met. Official Case 1: From March 2019 to July 2022, Liu XX, in order to make money, personally produced 「hardware dongles」 capable of circumventing software technical measures. He also duplicated pirated software and sold it bundled with the dongles. His illegal business turnover exceeded 1.06 million yuan. The Shanghai No. 3 Intermediate People's Court determined that his circumstances were especially serious and sentenced him for the crime of copyright infringement. The Supreme People's Procuratorate noted that this was the nation's first copyright infringement case of the 「intentional circumvention or destruction of technical measures」 type following the implementation of Criminal Law Amendment (XI). In April 2023, the Shanghai court sentenced three defendants in this series of cases to prison terms ranging from 1 year to 3 years and 2 months, some with reprieves, and fines ranging from 700,000 to 80,000 yuan. Official Case 2: Medical equipment repairman Liu XX spent 80,000 yuan in a QQ group to buy 50 sets of cracked hardware dongles, then resold them online for several thousand yuan each. Plugging them in bypassed medical equipment identity authentication and accessed maintenance software. The Putuo District People's Court of Shanghai sentenced him to 1 year and 2 months' imprisonment, suspended with a reprieve, and a fine of 80,000 yuan. Official Case 3: Starting in May 2021, Li XX and others in Xuzhou hired people to develop cracking programs for gaming consoles and manufactured cracking devices for sale. The illegal business turnover exceeded 39 million yuan. In November 2024, 10 people were sentenced to prison terms between 2 years and 6 months and 3 years and 6 months, some with reprieves, and fines ranging from 11 million to 1.5 million yuan (Nationwide).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2020). Criminal Law Amendment (XI) (Item 20, amending Article 217, Item 6 of the Criminal Law). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/202012/t20201227_503682.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2020). Copyright Law (2020 Amendment, Articles 3, 49, 50, 53, 54). <http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202011/t20201119_308796.html>; Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate (2025). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Intellectual Property Infringement (Fa Shi [2025] No. 5, Article 13). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbt/202504/t20250424_693977.shtml>; Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate (2025). Typical Cases of Criminal Protection of Intellectual Property Rights (Case 6: Copyright Infringement Case of Liu XX and Liu XX). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbt/202504/t20250424_693978.shtml>; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2024). Supreme People's Procuratorate: Guiding the Handling of the Nation's First Copyright Infringement Case of the "Intentional Circumvention or Destruction of Technical Measures Type". <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/2024zgjtzwlft/202402/t20240228_645416.shtml>; Procuratorial Daily (2023-04-18). Selling Pirated Dongles to Unlock Medical Equipment Security Systems (Reprinted by the official website of the Supreme People's Procuratorate). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/zdgz/202304/t20230418_611586.shtml>; National Copyright Administration (2025). Top Ten Cases of Combating Infringement and Piracy Nationwide in 2024 (Case 6: Case of Li XX and Others in Xuzhou, Jiangsu Sabotaging Technical Measures to Infringe Copyright). <https://www.ncac.gov.cn/xxfb/ywxx/202508/t20250801_925366.html>.
entries.notes: The beneficiary is yourself. The Copyright Law leaves a few exceptions: technical measures may be circumvented to test the security performance of computer systems and networks, or to conduct encryption research and software reverse engineering research. However, the same article specifies that the technologies, devices, or components used for circumvention must not be provided to others. Thus, doing research for yourself is permissible, but distributing or selling them is not. Distributing cracking patches for free does not meet the criteria for the crime of copyright infringement, because this offense requires a for-profit purpose. However, civil infringement still stands; software companies can issue lawyer letters and sue you for compensation. Under regular procedure, first-instance civil lawsuits are statutory required to be concluded within 6 months, which can be extended, and attorney fees are generally borne by yourself. Uploading entire cracked software suites online for public download constitutes unauthorized dissemination of works; for criminal thresholds, see Section 9, Item 24 (Sharing Cloud Drive Resources). For game cheats bypassing anti-cheat mechanisms, see Item 2 of this section (Game Cheats and Assistive Tools).

entries.title: Do not help others launch DDoS traffic attacks, do not sell or rent out "stress testing" traffic platforms, and do not launch attacks on the opponent's server when losing in online games
entries.cost: Zero monetary cost. DDoS refers to controlling large numbers of machines to flood targets with simultaneous requests, clogging servers until they become unusable. The trade-off is passing up businesses that charge per-attack fees or sell traffic packages, as well as holding back temporary anger. When conflicts arise in gaming or business, pursue reports, complaints, or police interventions instead of paying someone to attack targets yourself.
entries.summary: Using DDoS to bring down others' websites, servers, or games constitutes the crime of sabotaging computer information systems. Severe consequences result in fixed-term imprisonment of up to 5 years; especially serious consequences result in 5 years or more. Paying and ordering platforms to carry out attacks also constitutes a joint crime. Individuals who operated DDoS websites collecting membership fees to take attack orders have been sentenced to prison terms ranging from 10 months to 5 years and 6 months.
entries.benefit: Interfering with the functions of a computer information system, causing the system to fail to operate normally, where the consequences are serious, is punishable by fixed-term imprisonment of up to 5 years or criminal detention. Where the consequences are especially serious, the punishment is 5 years or more. Courts regard DDoS as the "interference" described here. Several criteria define "serious consequences": one is causing the primary software or hardware of 10 or more computer information systems to fail to operate normally; another is obtaining illegal gains of 5,000 yuan or more, or causing economic losses of 10,000 yuan or more; yet another is causing a system that provides services to more than 10,000 users to fail to operate normally for an aggregate duration of 1 hour or more. Reaching 5 times these numbers of machines or amounts of money counts as especially serious consequences. Knowingly providing programs or tools for sabotage to someone committing such destruction is penalized as a joint crime. The threshold is illegal gains of 5,000 yuan or more, or providing them to 10 or more person-times. The same applies to providing assistance such as server hosting or technical support with illegal gains of 5,000 yuan or more. Providing programs or tools specifically designed for intruding into or illegally controlling computer information systems to 20 person-times or more, or with illegal gains of 5,000 yuan or more, is punishable by up to 3 years' imprisonment, concurrently or separately with a fine. Where the act does not constitute a crime, interfering with computer information system functions or providing such tools, causing harm, results in administrative detention of up to 5 days; relatively serious circumstances result in detention of 5 to 15 days. Official Case 1 (SPP Guiding Case No. 69): In early 2017, Yao Xiaojie and others were hired to establish the "Dark Night Group" abroad. They purchased massive server resources and manipulated trojans to launch DDoS attacks. On three occasions, they attacked the IPs of three gaming companies hosted on the cloud servers of an internet company, causing login failures and frequent user disconnections. The victim company spent over 40,000 yuan on emergency repairs. In June 2018, the Nanshan District Court of Shenzhen sentenced 11 defendants to terms between 1 and 2 years for the crime of sabotaging computer information systems. Official Case 2: In March 2017, Tang XX and Wang XX built a DDoS website capable of membership top-ups and attack task submissions. They accepted orders to launch traffic attacks against over 80 target IPs. The Haimen District Court of Nantong sentenced Tang XX and others to terms ranging from 10 months to 5 years and 6 months for the crime of sabotaging computer information systems. Zhang XX, who placed orders on this website to suppress a competitor, submitted over 100 attack tasks against 11 IPs or domain names belonging to the competitor's company. The court held that the orderer and the website operators constituted a joint crime; the orderer was the instigating party and was deemed a principal offender. Official Case 3: Wang XX established a DDoS platform, explicitly selling attacks categorized under "Bronze", "Silver", "Gold", and "Diamond" packages. He was prosecuted by the Haidian District People's Procuratorate of Beijing for the crime of illegal use of information networks; in 2020, he was sentenced at first instance to 1 year's imprisonment and a fine of 50,000 yuan (Nationwide).
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Criminal Law (Amended in accordance with Criminal Law Amendment (XI), Articles 285(3), 286, 287-1). <https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index.html>; Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate (2011). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Endangering Computer Information System Security (Fa Shi [2011] No. 19, Articles 2, 3, 4, 9, 11). <https://ga.sz.gov.cn/ZWGK/ZCFG/ZCJD/content/post_1304363.html> (Shenzhen Public Security Bureau reprint); Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2025). Public Security Administration Punishments Law (2025 Revision, Article 33). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml>; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2020). Eighteenth Batch of Guiding Cases (SPP Guiding Case No. 69, Case of Yao Xiaojie and 10 Others Sabotaging Computer Information Systems). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/jczdal/202004/t20200408_458415.shtml>; Higher People's Court of Jiangsu Province (2020-09-24). Jiangsu Courts Issue Typical Cases of Crimes Endangering Cybersecurity (Case 2: Case of Tang XX and Others Committing the Crime of Sabotaging Computer Information Systems). <https://www.jsfy.gov.cn/article/91613.html>; People's Court Daily (2025-02-08). Conviction and Sentencing of Cyberattack Acts Committed via DDoS Websites (Analysis of Reference Case 2024-18-1-254-001 in the People's Court Case Database, Shandong Courts Website reprint). <http://www.sdcourt.gov.cn/dyzy/372897/372899/33201805/index.html>; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2020). Haidian District, Beijing: Suspect Sentenced in DDoS Attack Platform Case. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/zdgz/202009/t20200901_478510.shtml>.
entries.notes: The beneficiary is yourself. Such platforms operate under the banner of "stress testing". It is only considered a legitimate stress test if the system being tested is your own, or if the counterparty has provided you with written authorization to test their system. Attacking another's server follows the exact same principle as Item 9 (Do Not Test Others' Systems Without Written Authorization). Local practices regarding the specific charges applied to platform operators accepting orders are not uniform across different regions. In the Haimen case, the charge was sabotaging computer information systems, with a maximum sentence of 5 years and 6 months; in the Haidian case, the charge was illegal use of information networks, resulting in a 1-year sentence. The commentary in the People's Court Daily noted that judicial practices for such cases have not been entirely consistent, but the designated database case categorized it as the crime of sabotaging computer information systems. In SPP Guiding Case No. 69, the attacked internet company reported the crime to the police. The public security authority sent the electronic data provided by the company to the Guangdong Branch of the National Computer Network Emergency Response Technical Team/Coordination Center of China (CNCERT) for analysis, uncovering 14 controlling servers. Chat logs and bank transaction records substantiated the purchase of control permissions over those servers. For selling trojans that control others' computers, see Item 8 of this section (Do Not Run Your Own Programs on Others' Machines).

chapters.title: Entrepreneurship and Doing Business: Do Not Lose the Family Fortune
chapters.intro:
This section accounts solely for monetary costs and legal liabilities, without converting them into lifespan. When opening a shop or running a company, which missteps will wipe out your own savings, your family's assets, and your spouse's money all together? What does the law prescribe, and can risks be separated in advance? Recommendations based purely on practical experience without supporting literature are marked Grade C.

The entries in this section are grouped into the following thematic clusters, with entry numbers in parentheses.

**Do Not Stake the Family Fortune Before Opening**: Launch a venture only with money you can afford to lose (Item 1), do not sign personal guarantees for corporate loans (Item 2), choose the right legal entity before opening (Item 3), do not serve as a nominal shareholder (Item 4), check franchise filings before joining (Item 5), ask clear questions before paying someone to operate your online store (Item 24), raise venture funds only from relatives, friends, and employees (Item 26), put partnership store agreements in writing (Item 28).

**Registration and Licenses**: Determine your business name and scope of operations before registering (Item 6), do not open for business before licenses are granted (Item 7), verify whether the leased premises permit your intended store type before signing the lease (Item 27).

**Food Business**: Determine your classification tier before entering the food industry (Item 8), labeling prepackaged food (Item 9), regular food must not claim medicinal efficacy (Item 10), criminal thresholds for food safety (Item 11).

**Tax Filings, Annual Reports, and Invoices**: File tax returns truthfully and on schedule even with zero income (Item 12), issue invoices only based on genuine transactions (Item 13), anyone claiming to be from the tax bureau demanding immediate payments is a scammer (Item 14), submit the prior year's annual report online during the first half of each year (Item 25).

**Contracts and Employment**: Record payments as a forfeited earnest deposit (dìngjīn 定金) rather than an advance reservation deposit (dìngjīn 订金) (Item 15), sign employment contracts within the first month of hiring (Item 16), pay wages strictly in accordance with contracts and the law (Item 17), perform work strictly according to operating procedures while on the job (Item 22).

**Products and Procurement**: Sell before manufacturing (Item 18), pass production samples through mass-production checklists first (Item 19), retain receipts and upstream vendor records when sourcing goods (Item 20), create graphic designs yourself or purchase proper licenses (Item 21).

**Exit**: Exit according to statutory procedures when facing losses (Item 23).

entries.title: Start a business only with money you can afford to lose; do not touch family savings, and do not borrow money to launch
entries.cost: Zero monetary cost. Before taking action, set a fixed ceiling for yourself: losing every penny of this sum must not impair your mortgage payments, child rearing, or medical care. Do not invest a cent beyond this number. Money from family members and borrowed funds must not be counted toward this sum. The hard part is resisting the urge to pump in additional capital when the business appears to be picking up.
entries.summary: Debts owed by an individually-owned business (gětǐhù) must be repaid using assets in your own name. Where it is unclear whether operations were run by the household, debts are satisfied using all family property. Starting a limited company is not entirely safe either: when the company cannot service its debts, creditors can demand that you accelerate and pay up front the subscribed capital contributions that you pledged but have not yet matured. Therefore, determine your investment budget strictly by the criterion of 「being able to repay mortgages and afford medical care even if every penny is wiped out」.
entries.benefit: Losing money does not just mean the money is gone. For debts owed by an individually owned business (individual industrial and commercial household), if the business was run by you alone, it must be repaid using money and property under your personal name (borne by personal property). If it was run by the entire family together, or if it is unclear who ran it, it must be repaid using the whole family's money and property (borne by family property). Debts signed by both spouses count as joint debts to be repaid by both individuals together. If one party gave approval after the fact, it also counts. For money borrowed by one party in their own name, as long as the creditor can prove that this money was used in a business operated jointly by the couple, it is still repaid by both individuals together. There is also a rule on the company side: the money a shareholder initially promised to contribute in registered capital is called subscribed capital contribution. When a company cannot pay its debts that are due, for the portion whose payment deadline has not yet arrived, creditors can demand that the shareholder pay it up ahead of schedule (National).
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 56, 1064). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2023). Company Law (2023 Revision, Articles 47, 54). <https://www.gov.cn/yaowen/liebiao/202312/content_6923395.htm>
entries.notes: “Afford to lose” means: even if this sum of money is completely lost, you will not have to sell your house or borrow money from relatives to plug the hole. Regarding official statistics on how many enterprises can survive and how many years they survive on average, verifiable original sources were not found on the official websites of the National Bureau of Statistics or the State Administration for Market Regulation this time. Therefore, no figures are written in the main text; only legal consequences are described, and it is rated Grade B.

entries.title: Do not sign personal guarantees for company loans, and even more so, spouses should not sign along
entries.cost: Costs nothing. When a bank, supplier, or landlord asks you to sign a “shareholder personal joint and several guarantee” or a “spouse signature,” pause first. Signing that page is equivalent to personally surrendering the protection of “company debts do not look to individuals” (surrendering limited liability). If you can avoid signing, do not sign. If you absolutely must sign, sign only a “general guarantee,” and write clearly the maximum amount of money you are guaranteeing. The difficult part is that the other party often says “if you don't sign, we won't disburse the loan”; you must stand firm against it.
entries.summary: If what you sign is a “joint and several liability guarantee,” when the company cannot repay the money, creditors can bypass the company and come directly to you. Only by writing “general guarantee” do they have to sue the company first; only after selling off company property and seeing how much is still short will it be your turn. If a spouse signs along, both people's family assets are dragged in together, and the “limited” of a limited liability company will no longer count for you personally.
entries.benefit: That sentence on the guarantee letter means “if the person who owes money does not repay, it will be repaid by you.” If it is written as a “joint and several liability guarantee,” the creditor does not have to go looking for the company and can come straight to your door to demand payment from you. If it is written as a “general guarantee,” the creditor must first sue the company or go to arbitration, and then petition the court to forcibly sell the company's property to pay off the debt. Only after selling it off and seeing how much is still lacking does it become your turn to make up the difference. Debts signed by both husband and wife count as joint debts to be repaid by both individuals together. If one party nodded their approval after the fact, it counts as well. Once the spouse signs, both people's family assets are dragged in together (National, starting 2021).
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 681, 687, 688, 1064). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>
entries.notes: The author's experience is that when banks extend loans to small and micro enterprises, they frequently require shareholders to personally sign joint and several guarantees; this book found no official statistics. Loans can still be taken out; just make sure to understand clearly what is being signed away on that page before signing. The guaranteed amount should be kept strictly within the “afford to lose” figure from Section 1 (only start a business with money you can afford to lose). For general rules on IOUs and guarantee letters, see Section 8, Item 18.

entries.title: Choose the right entity before opening: sole proprietorships and partners are liable all the way to the end; only limited liability companies are truly “limited”
entries.cost: Registration is handled on the local government affairs service website, taking a few hours in one go. After opening a limited liability company, bookkeeping and tax filing are required every month, which is a long-term expense: doing it yourself takes time, while hiring an agency for bookkeeping costs money, with prices varying by region.
entries.summary: Individually owned businesses and general partners repay as much as they owe, whereas shareholders of limited liability companies only compensate up to the amount they promised to contribute during registration. However, however much you promised, you must genuinely produce that much within 5 years: entering 1 million yuan means you might end up owing 1 million yuan. If company accounts and personal household accounts are mixed together, or if the company is used to evade debts, “limited” will also become invalid. If you are the sole shareholder, you must also provide accounting records yourself to prove there is no commingling.
entries.benefit: Debts owed by an individually owned business must be repaid using personal money and property, or repaid using the whole family's money and property. Partners in a general partnership enterprise bear unlimited joint and several liability for the debts of the partnership enterprise. This means repaying whatever is owed, and it is not finished until it is fully repaid. Creditors can also single out just one of the partners and demand that they repay the entire amount. Limited partnerships are different: the limited partners in them are only liable up to the amount of money they promised to contribute (limited to their subscribed capital contributions). Shareholders of a limited liability company are likewise only liable up to the amount of money they promised to contribute (limited to their subscribed capital contribution amount). However, “limited” will become invalid under three circumstances. First, the promised money must genuinely be fully paid up within 5 years from the establishment of the company; when the company cannot repay due debts, creditors can demand advance payment. Second, money that has already been invested and subsequently withdrawn (unauthorized withdrawal of capital contribution) must be returned. Third, when the company is used as a shell to evade debts and severely harms the interests of creditors, in which case you must personally repay the company's debts along with it (bear joint and several liability). Companies with only one shareholder are even stricter: that shareholder must personally prove that the company's money and their own money are kept separate. If they cannot prove it, they must personally repay the company's debts along with it. Courts mainly examine whether the money and the books are separated. Shareholders using company money casually without keeping records, or failing to separate company accounts from personal accounts, are both considered commingling (National, starting July 2024).
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 56). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2006). Partnership Enterprise Law (2006 Revision, Article 2). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2006/content_413955.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2023). Company Law (2023 Revision, Articles 4, 23, 47, 53, 54; Article 23, Paragraph 3: “In a company with only one shareholder, where the shareholder cannot prove that the company's property is independent of the shareholder's own property, they shall bear joint and several liability for the company's debts.”). <https://www.gov.cn/yaowen/liebiao/202312/content_6923395.htm>; Supreme People's Court (2019). Minutes of the National Courts' Civil and Commercial Trial Work Conference (Point 10 “Commingling of Personalities”): “The most primary manifestation is whether the property of the company and the property of the shareholder are commingled and indistinguishable” “The account books of the company and the account books of the shareholder are not separated, rendering the property of the company and the property of the shareholder indistinguishable”. <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/199691.html>
entries.notes: Use company accounts and personal accounts separately, do not receive customer payments into personal cards, do not use company money to pay for family household expenses, and retain complete accounting records. Do not enter an inflated large figure for registered capital just for appearances.

entries.title: Do not act as a nominal shareholder, and do not hold equity on behalf of others
entries.cost: Costs nothing. When someone comes saying “borrow your ID card to list as a shareholder” or “let's put the shares under your name for now,” turn them down across the board.
entries.summary: Once your name is recorded on the register, you are a shareholder in the eyes of the law. The money promised at registration must be paid up on schedule; failing to pay not only requires making up the payment but also compensating the company for losses. If other shareholders did not genuinely pay in their money when the company was founded, you will also repay whatever is missing along with them. The business is run by someone else, but the debt is recorded under your name.
entries.benefit: A shareholder recorded in the register is a shareholder in the legal sense. You must pay in the promised money without missing a single cent within the period specified in the company's articles of association (fully pay the subscribed capital contribution). For those who fail to pay on schedule, in addition to making up the payment, they must also compensate the company for losses. If any shareholder failed to genuinely pay in their money when the company was established, the other shareholders at the time of establishment will repay along with them within this shortfall (bear joint and several liability). When the company cannot repay debts that are due, creditors can demand that the money whose deadline has not yet arrived be paid in advance. The person who actually runs the business is not on the registration, but the debt is recorded under your name (National, starting July 2024).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2023). Company Law (2023 Revision, Articles 47, 49, 50, 54). <https://www.gov.cn/yaowen/liebiao/202312/content_6923395.htm>; Supreme People's Court (2020 Amendment). Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (III) (Fa Shi [2011] No. 3, amended twice by Fa Shi [2014] No. 2 in 2014 and Fa Shi [2020] No. 18 in 2020, Articles 24, 25): “If there are no invalidating circumstances provided by law, the people's court shall determine that the contract is valid” “Where the actual contributor requests the company to change the shareholder without the consent of more than half of the company's other shareholders... the people's court shall not support it” “Where the nominal shareholder's disposal of equity causes losses to the actual contributor, and the actual contributor requests the nominal shareholder to bear compensation liability, the people's court shall support it”. <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808181799def980179ac07a9ca117c> (National Laws and Regulations Database); Supreme People's Court (2025). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (Draft for Comments), Article 90. <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/477881.html>
entries.notes: Between the nominal shareholder acting on another's behalf and the actual person funding the investment, an equity entrustment agreement counts as valid provided there are no invalidating circumstances. However, if the actual funder wishes to switch their name onto the registry, it requires the consent of more than half of the other shareholders. If the nominal person sells or pledges the equity, the court handles it by reference to bona fide acquisition under the Civil Code. If the buyer was unaware, the price was reasonable, and registration has already been handled, the funder cannot recover the equity and can only seek compensation from the nominal person. In September 2025, the Supreme People's Court already issued a draft for comments on a new interpretation; after the new interpretation is finalized and takes effect, this entire set of provisions will be repealed. As of September 2026, the 2020 amended version remains in effect, and this item is based on it. For the risks of acting as a nominal legal representative, see Section 8, Item 28.

entries.title: Check Ministry of Commerce filing before franchising, obtain written disclosure, and write a “cooling-off period” into the contract
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Go to the Ministry of Commerce's “Commercial Franchise Information Management System” website to check whether the brand owner has filed a record. Then require the other party to provide you with written materials detailing everything that should be disclosed before signing, together with the text of the contract. This can be completed in a few hours.
entries.summary: According to regulations, the brand owner itself must first open 2 directly operated stores, operate them for a full 1 year, and file a record with the commercial administration department within 15 days after signing the contract. Before signing, it must provide you with written materials covering 12 items, including franchise fees, how security deposits are refunded, and whether existing stores are profitable. If you cannot find the filing, they refuse to provide materials, or they demand payment before letting you see the contract, walk away immediately.
entries.benefit: Regulations require the brand owner (referred to in the regulations as the franchisor) to have at least 2 directly operated stores opened and operated by itself, and to have operated them for more than 1 full year. Starting from the day the first franchise contract is signed, it must file a record with the competent commercial department within 15 days. Those failing to file will be fined 10,000 to 50,000 yuan. Those failing to file after the deadline has passed will be fined 50,000 to 100,000 yuan and publicly announced. Before signing the contract, it must provide you with written materials on the matters that should be disclosed, totaling 12 items. These include what types of franchise fees are charged and how much each is, under what circumstances security deposits are refunded, how many franchise stores currently exist, and how business is performing. They also include summaries of audit reports audited in the past 2 years, as well as lawsuits and arbitrations engaged in over the past 5 years. The contract must also explicitly stipulate that the franchisee may unilaterally withdraw as they wish (unilateral rescission) within a certain period after signing. If the brand owner conceals information or provides false information, the franchisee may rescind the contract (National, starting May 2007).
entries.sources: State Council (2007). Regulations on the Administration of Commercial Franchises (State Council Decree No. 485, Articles 7, 8, 12, 22, 23, 25). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_4179.htm>; Ministry of Commerce (2012). Administrative Measures on the Information Disclosure of Commercial Franchises (Ministry of Commerce Decree 2012 No. 2, Articles 5, 9). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2012/content_2177025.htm>; Ministry of Commerce. Commercial Franchise Information Management System. <https://txjy.syggs.mofcom.gov.cn/>
entries.notes: If you cannot find a record of filing, they refuse to provide disclosure documents, or they demand payment first before letting you see the contract, walk away directly. The “cooling-off period” refers to those few days after signing the contract during which you can still unilaterally withdraw on your own terms. The number of days is determined by the contract; the regulations only specify “a certain period,” so demand that the exact number of days be written into the contract when signing. Regarding the “average sales volume, gross profit, and net profit of existing franchise stores” disclosed by the brand owner, press for where the numbers came from; the measures require the brand owner to explain the sources. For arrangements not called franchising that only charge service fees for “proxy operation” or “store-opening training,” see Item 24 (Proxy Operation and Store-Opening Training).

entries.title: Finalize name, business premises, business scope, and registered capital before registering; once materials are complete, the license can be collected on the spot
entries.cost: The registration step itself costs nothing. Registration fees for enterprises and individually owned businesses have been suspended since January 1, 2015. Handle it yourself on the local government affairs service website or go to the government affairs service hall, taking a few hours in one go. Carving official seals, hiring an agency for bookkeeping, and renting a registered address (address hosting) are market purchases of services, not government-collected fees.
entries.summary: Registration itself costs nothing; registration fees were suspended back in 2015, and if someone charges money, it is not a registration fee. There are only five items of materials to submit: application form, identity or qualification certificates, business premises documents, articles of association or partnership agreement, plus anything else specifically named by regulations. When materials are complete, the license is issued on the spot; if it cannot be issued on the spot, it is completed within 3 working days, with an additional 3 working days for complex cases.
entries.benefit: The regulations strictly define the materials to be submitted into five items: “(1) Application form”; “(2) Applicant qualification documents and natural person identity certificates”; “(3) Relevant documents concerning domicile or primary business premises”; “(4) Articles of association of a company, non-corporate enterprise legal person, or specialized farmers' cooperative (federation), or partnership agreement of a partnership enterprise”; “(5) Other materials required to be submitted by laws, administrative regulations, and the State Council market supervision and administration department.” Translated into plain English: an application form, a document proving who you are or that you are qualified to do this, plus a document proving that the storefront or office space is allocated for your use, along with the company's articles of association or partnership agreement. Anything else specifically requested by regulations must also be submitted. Companies must also submit appointment documents and identity certificates for the legal representative, directors, supervisors, and senior executives. Individually owned businesses do not need to submit articles of association. Names are “independently declared by the applicant in accordance with the law”—named by yourself and declared by yourself. Registered capital “implements a subscribed registration system”—first write down how much you promise to contribute, with no need to pull it out on the spot. The business scope is selected from the classification published by the registration authority. Where materials are complete and in the correct format, they are “confirmed and registered on the spot.” For matters that cannot be completed on the spot, they are completed “within 3 working days,” with an additional 3 working days granted for complex situations. “The date of issuance of the business license shall be the date of establishment of the market entity”: the date printed on the license is the day the company or store is established (National, starting March 2022).
entries.sources: State Council (2021). Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (State Council Decree No. 746, Articles 10, 13, 14, 16, 19, 21). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2021/content_5636139.htm>; State Administration for Market Regulation (2022). Implementing Rules for the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (SAMR Decree No. 52, Articles 12, 25, 26). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-03/02/content_5676403.htm>; Ministry of Finance, National Development and Reform Commission (2014). Notice on Cancelling, Suspending, and Exempting a Batch of Administrative and Institutional Fees (Cai Shui [2014] No. 101, Annex 1). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2014-12/23/content_5023513.htm>; General Office of the State Council (2018). Opinions on Further Compressing the Time Required to Start an Enterprise (Guo Ban Fa [2018] No. 32, Part II, Item 3). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2018-05/17/content_5291643.htm>
entries.notes: Registration itself is free of charge. If someone charges money, they are charging for market services such as agency handling or seal carving. The price of seal carving is determined by the market. The 2018 document from the General Office of the State Council clearly states that “applicants shall independently choose seal manufacturing entities” and “it is strictly prohibited to designate seal manufacturing entities to produce official seals,” so if someone says “you must go to a designated place to carve seals,” you do not have to accept it. How much registered capital you fill in does not affect your facade; it only determines your upper limit of liability, and it must be fully paid within 5 years; see Section 3 of this chapter (Choose the right entity before opening). If the business scope includes licensed items, you cannot open for business before the permit is issued; see Section 7 of this chapter (Trades requiring permits).

entries.title: For trades requiring permits, do not open for business before the permit is issued
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Check clearly before opening whether the business you want to do requires a permit. Running catering or selling food requires obtaining a food business permit. If you only sell prepackaged foods made by others, no permit is required, and it has been changed to record-filing instead. Open for business only after the permit is issued.
entries.summary: Opening for business without a permit will be investigated and penalized by the department in charge of that permit according to its regulations. For those operating without even a business license and without specialized penalty rules, they will be ordered to cease business, have their earned money confiscated, and be fined up to 10,000 yuan. Selling state-monopolized or restricted goods, or engaging in securities, futures, insurance, or payment and settlement services under serious circumstances constitutes the crime of illegal business operation, with the lowest sentencing tier being up to 5 years.
entries.benefit: Opening doors for business without obtaining a permit will be investigated and handled by the department designated by laws and regulations. Operating without a business license where the law does not specify penalties will result in an order to cease, confiscation of the earned money (illegal gains), and a fine of up to 10,000 yuan. There is also an even heavier tier: trading in goods that are monopolized, specialized, or restricted by laws and regulations without permission; or engaging in securities, futures, insurance, or fund payment and settlement businesses without approval. In these two circumstances, serious cases constitute the crime of illegal business operations. The sentence is fixed-term imprisonment of up to 5 years or criminal detention (short-term confinement), along with a fine of 1 to 5 times the earned money. Cases with especially serious circumstances are sentenced to 5 years or more (National).
entries.sources: State Council (2017). Measures for Investigating and Dealing with Unlicensed and Unpermitted Operations (State Council Decree No. 684, Articles 5, 6, 13). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2017-08/23/content_5219861.htm>; State Administration for Market Regulation (2023). Administrative Measures for Food Operation Licensing and Record-Filing (SAMR Decree No. 78, Article 4). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2023/issue_10606/202307/content_6894763.html>; National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Article 225). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml>
entries.notes: Licensing conditions for financial, medical, and tutoring/training categories each have specialized laws; this item only verified general investigation rules and Criminal Law provisions. Milk tea shops and snack stalls fall under catering services and must obtain a food business permit. Renovating first before obtaining a permit and holding a soft opening before the permit is issued are common pitfalls. For how the food industry is categorized into tiers and whether selling fresh meat and vegetables requires a permit, see Item 8 (When doing food business, first check which tier you fall into).

entries.title: When doing food business, first check which tier you fall into: production and catering require permits, selling only prepackaged foods is changed to record-filing, and selling fresh meat and vegetables requires no permit
entries.cost: The license itself is free of charge. However, the site and facilities must meet standards, and the on-site inspection plus license processing will take several weeks. Meat sellers must also retain quarantine certificates and meat quality inspection certificates for every batch.
entries.summary: Making goods yourself to sell—such as snack shops, braised foods, baking, and homemade pickles—all requires obtaining a permit or license; small workshops and food vendors are handled according to provincial rules. If you only sell prepackaged foods that meet the standard definition, you do not need to obtain a food operation license, but you must file a record. Selling raw, fresh meat, vegetables, and the like does not require a license. If you are required to obtain a permit or license but fail to do so, a fine of 50,000 to 100,000 yuan will be imposed even if the value of the goods is less than 10,000 yuan.
entries.benefit: Food Safety Law: To engage in the food business, you must obtain a license first. Producing food yourself, selling food, and providing catering services all require obtaining a license in accordance with the law. "However, those who sell edible agricultural products and those who only sell prepackaged foods are not required to obtain a license. Those who only sell prepackaged foods shall report to the food safety supervision and administration department of the local people's government at or above the county level in the place where they are located for filing." Edible agricultural products refer to unprocessed items such as raw, fresh meat and vegetables. Whether something is prepackaged food must be judged according to the applicable standards; you cannot simply look at whether someone else made it or whether it has packaging. For the specific definition, see Item 9 (Labels for Prepackaged Foods). "Specific administrative measures for small food production and processing workshops, food vendors, and the like shall be formulated by provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government"; rules for these two categories are set by each province itself. For those who engage in food business operations without obtaining a license, all illegal income earned, food, as well as tools, equipment, and raw materials shall be confiscated. If the total monetary value of this batch of goods calculated at the selling price (the value of the goods) is less than 10,000 yuan, a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan shall be imposed concurrently. If the value of the goods is 10,000 yuan or more, a fine of not less than 10 times but not more than 20 times the value of the goods shall be imposed. Regulation on the Administration of Pig Slaughtering: Pigs may only be slaughtered at state-designated slaughtering plants, subject to centralized official quarantine. "Except for individuals slaughtering pigs for personal consumption in rural areas which are not subject to designated slaughtering, no unit or individual may engage in pig slaughtering activities without designation." "Pig products operated by units and individuals engaged in pig product sales and meat food production and processing, as well as catering service operators and collective dining units, must be pig products from pig designated slaughtering plants (facilities) that have passed quarantine and meat quality inspection." Therefore, the pork you sell and use must come from designated slaughtering plants, and must pass both quarantine and meat quality inspection. For those who privately slaughter pigs outside designated slaughtering plants, operations will be ordered closed down, and the pigs, slaughtering tools, equipment, and illegal income earned shall be confiscated together. The fine amounts fall into the same tier as operating a food business without a license above. Animal Epidemic Prevention Law: Animal products sold and transported must carry quarantine certificates and quarantine marks along with the goods. For those failing to carry them, correction shall be ordered, and a concurrent fine of up to the value of equivalent qualified goods shall be imposed. Judicial interpretations govern punitive damages—that is, the additional compensation amount on top of a refund. If the food produced or sold by small workshops and food vendors does not conform to food safety standards and the buyer claims ten times compensation, the court shall support it (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (3rd Amendment 2025). Food Safety Law (Articles 35, 36, 122). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=7b5a76d0461745a08d3f964916b87ef3>; State Council (2021). Regulation on the Administration of Pig Slaughtering (State Council Decree No. 742, Articles 2, 23, 31). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-07/22/content_5626534.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2021 Revision). Animal Epidemic Prevention Law (Articles 51, 100). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080817703add2017737395a973e31>; Supreme People's Court (2024). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Food and Drug Punitive Damages Dispute Cases (Fa Shi [2024] No. 9, Article 4). <http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/bf531a70471f10d377788f28d3d8f8.html>
entries.notes: The thresholds for small workshops, small catering establishments, and food vendors are set by each province; specific numbers are not written in this item. Go to the official website of the market supervision bureau in your province, search for "Regulations on the Administration of Food Small Workshops, Small Catering Establishments, and Food Vendors," and check the local version. Selling homemade food online does not mean you need one less license just because it is "online"; what requires licensing still requires licensing. On how to handle business entities and licenses, see Item 6 (Determine Name, Premises, and Business Scope Before Registration). On whether other trades require licenses, see Item 7 (Trades That Require Licenses). On how much compensation a buyer can claim, see Section 5, Item 31 (Tenfold Compensation for Food).

entries.title: Check Labels First When Selling Prepackaged Foods: Complete Labeling of Production Date, Shelf Life, and Ingredient List in Accordance with Regulations
entries.cost: Printing labels costs a few cents to a few tens of cents per sheet. Accurately filling in the date and ingredients for each batch will take some time.
entries.summary: Whether an item counts as prepackaged food depends on whether it is prepackaged in a predetermined quantity with a uniformly indicated weight or volume, not merely on whether it has a bag. Goods that are weighed and bagged only when purchased, foods prepared and sold on-site, and catering takeout cannot be treated as prepackaged foods simply because of a bag or takeout box. If prepackaged foods fail to label what should be labeled, a fine of 5,000 to 50,000 yuan applies for goods valued at less than 10,000 yuan. Bulk food must also be labeled with information such as name and date.
entries.benefit: As of October 2026, the current GB 7718-2011 requires prepackaged foods to be packaged in predetermined quantities or prepared in packaging materials and containers. The packaging must have a uniform weight or volume indication. Items weighed and bagged only when a customer purchases them cannot be judged as prepackaged foods simply because they are bagged. Foods prepared and sold on-site are not covered by these general labeling rules, nor can catering takeout be treated as such merely by virtue of having a food container. The Food Safety Law requires packaging of prepackaged food to bear labels. For food sold directly to consumers, except where standards expressly permit omission, the label must state the name, specifications, net content, production date, ingredients or ingredient list, producer's name, address, contact information, and shelf life. In addition, product standard codes, storage conditions, generic names of food additives used in the national standard, and production license numbers must be indicated. Matters required by laws, regulations, or food safety standards to be indicated shall also be indicated. When selling bulk food, containers and outer packaging must also state the name, production date or production batch number, and shelf life. The name, address, contact information, etc., of the food producer or operator must also be stated. If prepackaged foods produced or sold lack labels, or if labels and instructions do not conform to the provisions of this law, the illegal income and food shall be confiscated together. If the total monetary value of this batch of goods calculated at the selling price (the value of the goods) is less than 10,000 yuan, a fine of not less than 5,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan shall be imposed concurrently. If the value of the goods is 10,000 yuan or more, a fine of not less than 5 times but not more than 10 times the value of the goods shall be imposed. Where the circumstances are serious, operations shall be ordered suspended or closed down until the license is revoked. Where labels or instructions merely have minor defects (blemishes) that neither affect food safety nor mislead consumers, correction shall be ordered first. Only upon refusal to correct will a fine of not more than 2,000 yuan be imposed. The new version of the "General Rules for the Labeling of Prepackaged Foods" numbered GB 7718-2025 was released on March 16, 2025. It takes effect on March 16, 2027, with a two-year transition period in between. The new version includes foods that are prepackaged and then sold by weight or piece within its scope, but catering foods and foods prepared and sold on-site are still not applicable. The new version requires setting up an independent area on the packaging to display both the production date and the shelf life expiration date at the same time. The dates must use high-contrast, easily visible fonts and colors, and be arranged in year-month-day order (Nationwide)
