Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Food and Drug Punitive Damages Dispute Cases (Fa Shi [2024] No. 9, Articles 6, 8). <http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/bf531a70471f10d377788f28d3d8f8.html> (Tiers of labeling defects vs. omission of mandatory labeling items); Beijing Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (2026). Can't Find the Production Date? Food Labels Are Getting a "Facelift"! Must-See Key Points of the New Regulations. <https://scjgj.beijing.gov.cn/zwxx/scjgdt/202605/t20260507_4639154.html> (Effective date, transition period, and new requirements for date display)
entries.notes: Labeling defects are divided into two categories, and both the fine amounts and compensation amounts follow this distinction. One category is minor defects, such as typos or non-standard font sizes, which neither affect food safety nor mislead people. For these, the market supervision department will only order you to correct them; only upon refusal to correct will a fine of not more than 2,000 yuan be imposed, and buyers cannot obtain ten times compensation. The other category is failure to label what must be labeled by law, such as omitting the production date or shelf life that cannot be omitted. The judicial interpretation explicitly states that this does not count as a minor defect. Fines are calculated based on the value of goods: if less than 10,000 yuan, a fine of 5,000 to 50,000 yuan; if 10,000 yuan or more, a fine of 5 to 10 times the value of goods. Furthermore, the buyer can additionally claim ten times the price of the food from you, with amounts less than 1,000 yuan counted as 1,000 yuan (see Section 5, Item 31, Tenfold Compensation for Food). Current standards contain provisions on omitted items for certain foods and very small packages, which must be verified against the product. GB 7718-2025 has not yet officially taken effect; you cannot take the expanded scope of the new version as the current definition. The specific format is subject to the original text of the applicable standard.

entries.title: Ordinary Food Is Not Allowed to Claim Disease Treatment: Labels, Instructions, Advertisements, and Livestream Pitches All Count
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Review promotional slogans, product detail pages, and livestreaming pitches. The difficult part is refraining from saying phrases like "lowers the three highs" or "cures constipation."
entries.summary: In labels, instructions, and advertisements for ordinary food, claims of disease prevention or treatment are prohibited. Except for the three categories of medical, drug, and medical device advertisements, no other advertisements are allowed to claim disease treatment or use terms that sound like medicines. The fine is 1 to 3 times the advertising expenses; where advertising expenses cannot be calculated, the fine is 100,000 to 200,000 yuan. In serious cases, the business license can also be revoked.
entries.benefit: Food Safety Law: "The labels and instructions of food and food additives shall not contain false content, and shall not involve disease prevention or treatment functions. Producers and business operators shall be responsible for the contents of the labels and instructions provided by them." "The content of food advertisements shall be true and lawful, shall not contain false content, and shall not involve disease prevention or treatment functions. Food producers and business operators shall be responsible for the truthfulness and legality of the contents of food advertisements." This means packaging, instructions, and advertisements may not claim disease prevention or treatment functions, and sellers themselves bear responsibility for whatever is written. Those who boast about food in advertisements to deceive consumers shall be punished according to the Advertising Law. The Advertising Law also contains a prohibition. "Except for advertisements for medical treatment, drugs, and medical devices, any other advertisements are prohibited from involving disease treatment functions, and may not use medical terminology or terminology that easily confuses the promoted goods with drugs or medical devices." Except for the three categories of medical, drug, and medical device advertisements, other advertisements are uniformly forbidden to claim disease treatment or use words sounding like drugs or medical devices. For violations of this provision, the advertisement shall be ordered stopped. Furthermore, the party that released the advertisement (the advertiser) shall be ordered to make a public clarification within the corresponding scope of dissemination to eliminate the adverse effects. A fine of not less than 1 time but not more than 3 times the advertising expenses shall also be imposed. Where advertising expenses cannot be calculated, or where the reported figure is noticeably low, a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan shall be imposed. Where the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 3 times but not more than 5 times the advertising expenses shall be imposed, or a fine of not less than 200,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan. The business license can also be revoked, putting an end to the business directly (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (3rd Amendment 2025). Food Safety Law (Articles 71, 73, 125, 140). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=7b5a76d0461745a08d3f964916b87ef3>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2021 Amendment). Advertising Law (Articles 17, 58). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817ab231eb017abd6bd860052d>
entries.notes: "Health-care functions" are likewise not something ordinary food can claim. The health-care functions that health food can claim may only come from catalogs designated by the state, and products must go through registration or filing; ordinary food does not undergo this process. On how buyers identify this kind of phrasing, see Section 6, Item 10 (Do Not Spend Large Sums Buying Health Supplements to Condition Your Body). Beyond packaging and advertisements, product detail pages, livestreaming pitches, and WeChat Moments copy all count as advertising content; once published, they leave a record.

entries.title: The Food Industry Has a Criminal Line: Selling Meat from Animals That Died of Disease or Selling Substandard Goods Suffices for Crime; Adding Toxic or Harmful Substances Ignores Amounts, with Sentencing Starting Below Five Years
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Follow the procedures in Item 8 (When Making Food, First See Which Tier You Fall Into): retain quarantine certificates and purchase vouchers, and include in the ingredient list only substances with verifiable approval numbers.
entries.summary: The preceding items fine money; this item arrests people. Selling diseased dead meat, meat failing inspection, or goods severely exceeding limits for pesticide residues, veterinary drug residues, or heavy metals carries a sentence of up to 3 years. As long as it is "sufficient to" cause serious food poisoning, the crime is constituted without requiring anyone to actually fall sick. Adulterating food with toxic or harmful non-food raw materials starts at fixed-term imprisonment of up to 5 years, regardless of how much money you made selling it.
entries.benefit: Article 143 of the Criminal Law governs this tier. If the food you produce or sell fails to meet food safety standards, as long as it is "sufficient to cause a serious food poisoning accident or other serious foodborne disease," a crime is established. The sentence is fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 3 years or criminal detention (short-term custody), along with a concurrent fine. If serious harm is caused to human health, or if there are other serious circumstances, the sentence is fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 3 years but not more than 7 years, along with a fine. If the consequences are especially serious, the sentence is fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 7 years or life imprisonment, with a concurrent fine or confiscation of all property under the offender's name. Article 144 governs adulteration. Whoever mixes toxic or harmful non-food raw materials into the food produced or sold, or knowingly sells food mixed with such materials, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 5 years, along with a fine. If serious harm is caused to human health, or if there are other serious circumstances, the sentence is fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 5 years but not more than 10 years, along with a fine. If death is caused, or there are other especially serious circumstances, punishment shall be imposed in accordance with Article 141 (not less than 10 years, life imprisonment, or the death penalty). The Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate issued an interpretation (the Interpretation of the SPC and SPP). It specifies which circumstances qualify as "sufficient to cause a serious food poisoning accident or other serious foodborne disease." The first is "containing pathogenic microorganisms, pesticide residues, veterinary drug residues, biotoxins, heavy metals, or other contaminants that seriously exceed standard limits." The second is "being meat and meat products of livestock, poultry, beasts, and aquatic animals that died of disease, died of unknown causes, or failed inspection and quarantine." The third is "being explicitly prohibited by the state from production and sale for special needs such as disease prevention and control." The fourth is "foods for special medical purpose or staple and supplementary foods exclusively for infants and young children whose nutritional components seriously fail to meet food safety standards." Using additives in excessive amounts or in incorrect categories, to the extent that it leads to the consequences mentioned above, is likewise convicted under Article 143. What counts as "toxic and harmful non-food raw materials" is not up to you to decide. One category comprises substances prohibited by laws and regulations from being added to food. Another category comprises substances on lists announced by relevant State Council departments, such as banned pesticides and drugs prohibited from use in food animals. Another scenario also counts as "other serious circumstances" under Article 144: producing or selling an amount of 100,000 yuan or more but less than 200,000 yuan, where the location is primary and secondary school campuses, preschool and childcare institutions, eldercare institutions, and their surroundings, and the sales targets are minors or elderly people. Operating slaughter and sales by privately setting up pig slaughterhouses outside designated slaughtering plants, where the circumstances are serious, is penalized as the crime of illegal business operations. Reaching 100,000 yuan or more, or earning 50,000 yuan or more, counts as "serious circumstances" (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2020 Amendment). Criminal Law (Articles 141, 143, 144). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808181796a636a0179822a19640c92> (National Database of Laws and Regulations); Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate (2021). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases Jeopardizing Food Safety (Fa Shi [2021] No. 24, Articles 1, 2, 5, 7, 9, 17, 18, effective January 1, 2022). <https://scjg.hebei.gov.cn/info/79117> (Hebei Provincial Administration for Market Regulation reprint of the full text), <https://sft.ln.gov.cn/sft/ywgz/zfflgw/xzys/2525860BD0F843EFA7A3B7FDC330614E/index.shtml> (Liaoning Provincial Department of Justice reprint of the full text, both verified word for word as identical)
entries.notes: The dividing line from the preceding three items is: whether food safety itself has been breached. Failing to obtain a permit, omitting labeling items, and exaggerating curative effects are punished with fines. Selling diseased dead meat, substandard goods, improperly adding additives, and mixing non-food raw materials lead into criminal proceedings. The most effortless line of defense remains the set of actions in Item 8 (When Making Food, First See Which Tier You Fall Into). Source meat only from designated slaughtering plants. Retain quarantine certificates and meat quality inspection certificates for each batch. Use only ingredients with verifiable approval numbers. So-called "cheap clearance meat" and "off-cuts of unknown origin" are the most frequent entry points for trouble in food criminal cases. The page of the original source in the Supreme People's Court Gazette returned a 502 error in this round, so two provincial official reprints were cited and verified against each other word for word.

entries.title: File Taxes Honestly and on Schedule Once You Obtain a License; File Even Without Income, and Only File a Zero Return If Qualified
entries.cost: Costs nothing. File by yourself monthly or quarterly in the electronic tax bureau; each time takes a few minutes. Hiring an outsourced bookkeeper is a separate market expense. If you hire staff, you must also complete social security registration within 30 days from the date of establishment. The hard part is remembering to file on time even in months with no business.
entries.summary: Even if there is no tax to pay, tax declarations must be filed on schedule; fill in income, costs, and expenses truthfully, and do not fill in all zeros simply because there is no income. Failure to file will result in an order to correct within a prescribed time limit and may incur a fine of up to 2,000 yuan; in serious cases, a fine of 2,000 to 10,000 yuan. Failing to file for all tax categories for three consecutive months will cause the entity to become an abnormal taxpayer and have invoices suspended.
entries.benefit: "Where a taxpayer has no tax payable during a tax period, they shall still handle tax returns in accordance with regulations": Even if not a single cent of tax needs to be paid for the current period, forms still have to be filed as usual. The Law on the Administration of Tax Collection also requires truthful filing in accordance with regulations. Having no revenue, having no profit, and having no tax to pay are three different things. Even if there is no revenue, costs and expenses that have already been incurred, such as rent and wages, must still be truthfully filled in and reported in accordance with regulations. If there is tax-exempt income, it must also be entered into the corresponding field and cannot simply be treated as zero revenue. Whether a zero tax return can be filed requires checking conditions and form-filling requirements tax category by tax category. The corporate income tax filing guidelines from the Foshan Tax Authority give an example: A company only meets the conditions for one-click zero tax filing after financial statements have already been submitted and cumulative revenue, costs, and profits for the current period are all zero. At this point, items like employee headcount and total assets still need to be filled in; it is not a matter of entering zero for the entire form. For failing to file on schedule, "the tax authority shall order rectification within a prescribed time limit and may impose a fine of not more than 2,000 yuan; where the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 2,000 yuan but not more than 10,000 yuan may be imposed." If one fails to file and also underpays tax, the tax will be recovered, a daily late fee must be paid along with it, and a separate fine of "not less than 50 percent but not more than five times the amount of tax underpaid" will be imposed. The late fee is added at 0.05% per day. "Where no tax return has been filed for any tax category for three consecutive months, the tax collection and administration system will automatically designate it as an abnormal taxpayer and suspend the use of its invoice領用簿 (invoice requisition book) and invoices." If you file nothing for three consecutive months, the system will automatically classify you as an abnormal taxpayer, and you will neither be able to obtain nor issue invoices. The status is automatically lifted only after filing back returns and accepting penalties. An entity that employs staff "shall, within 30 days from the date of its establishment... apply for social insurance registration with the local social insurance administrative agency" (National)
entries.sources: State Council (2002). Announcement on Matters Concerning Tax Collection and Administration (State Taxation Administration Announcement [2019] No. 48, Article 3). <https://fgk.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfgk/c100012/c5195194/content.html> ; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). Individual Income Tax Law (2018 Amendment, Article 12). <https://fgk.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfgk/c100009/c5193028/content.html> ; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). Social Insurance Law (2018 Amendment, Article 57). <http://www.npc.gov.cn/zgrdw/npc/xinwen/2019-01/07/content_2070267.htm> ; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). Enterprise Income Tax Law (2018 Amendment, Article 54). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f135f46016f2106acd11784> (National Database of Laws and Regulations) ; State Administration for Market Regulation and five other departments (2025). Enterprise Deregistration Guide (2025 Revision) (Announcement [2025] No. 52). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202512/content_7053238.htm>
entries.notes: After the "multiple certificates into one" reform, there is no need to handle tax registration separately. Use the Unified Social Credit Code on your business license to log in to the electronic tax bureau, confirm the registration information, and declare which taxes you need to pay. Individually owned businesses (getihu) and sole proprietorships pay individual income tax on business operation income. First make a payment "within 15 days after the end of a month or quarter," and then "handle annual reconciliation and settlement before March 31 of the year following the receipt of income" (tallying the total accounts for the entire year, refunding overpayments or supplementing underpayments). Limited liability companies pay corporate income tax, prepaying monthly or quarterly. The full-year total account is settled "within five months from the date of the end of the year," with a deadline of May 31 of the following year. Even if you have not opened for business, you must still file, doing a zero filing only when eligible. If you fail to file for all tax categories for three consecutive months, you will become an abnormal taxpayer and invoice usage will be suspended. The 2025 Enterprise Deregistration Guide clearly stipulates that before handling tax deregistration, an abnormal taxpayer "must first lift the abnormal status and make supplementary tax filings." For how to proceed with deregistration, see Item 23 of this section (Exit according to procedure when losing money)

entries.title: Issue Invoices Only for Real Transactions, and Small-Scale Taxpayers Should Make Full Use of Tax Exemptions
entries.cost: Costs no money. Do not buy invoices, do not sell invoices, and do not "funnel money and issue invoices" for others. Issue invoices and file taxes based on actual business transactions.
entries.summary: Before the end of 2027, small-scale taxpayers with monthly sales under 100,000 yuan or quarterly sales under 300,000 yuan are exempt from value-added tax (VAT). Taxes originally levied at 3% are also reduced to 1% during the same period. Conversely, finding someone to issue invoices to use for tax deductions constitutes false issuance, carrying a starting sentence of up to 3 years in prison, plus a fine of 20,000 to 200,000 yuan.
entries.benefit: The category with small scale that pays tax under simplified methods is called small-scale taxpayers. The law states: "Where sales do not reach the threshold amount, value-added tax shall be exempted." This line is called the threshold amount (起征点). From January 1, 2026, to December 31, 2027, the threshold amount is 100,000 yuan on a monthly basis, and 300,000 yuan on a quarterly basis. Calculated on a per-transaction or daily basis, it is 1,000 yuan; if sales do not reach this line, no tax is due. During the same period, taxes originally payable at 3% are reduced to 1%, except for sales or leasing of real estate and transfers of land use rights. Conversely, issuing special VAT invoices or other invoices that can be used for tax deductions without genuine transactions constitutes false invoicing (虚开). It is punishable by fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 3 years or criminal detention, along with a fine of 20,000 to 200,000 yuan. Issuing for others, issuing for oneself, having others issue for oneself, or introducing others to issue all count. Where the tax amount involved is relatively large, the sentence is 3 to 10 years. Where the amount is huge, the sentence is 10 years or more or life imprisonment (National)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2024). Value-Added Tax Law (Effective January 1, 2026, Article 23). <https://fgk.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfgk/c100009/c5237365/content.html> ; Ministry of Finance, State Taxation Administration (2026). Announcement on Matters Concerning the Convergence of Value-Added Tax Preferential Policies After the Implementation of the Value-Added Tax Law (Ministry of Finance and State Taxation Administration Announcement [2026] No. 10, Articles 1, 2, 6). <https://fgk.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfgk/c102416/c5247434/content.html> ; National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Article 205). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml>
entries.notes: The Value-Added Tax Law comes into force on January 1, 2026. The original two small-scale taxpayer relief announcements, 2023 No. 19 and 2023 No. 1, are suspended or repealed accordingly. The monetary thresholds have not changed, but the legal basis has changed; this entry has been updated according to the new documents. The original page of the Criminal Law is the 1997 version, and Article 205 was later adjusted across sentencing tiers by amendments. Only those tiers verified and unmodified are written here. What is exempted is VAT; income tax is calculated separately. "Finding someone to issue invoices to deduct costs" is false invoicing, not tax planning.

entries.title: Anyone Claiming to Be from the Tax Bureau Calling or Messaging to Urge You to Pay Money or File Taxes into a Designated Account Is a Scammer; Handle Tax Matters Only via the Electronic Tax Bureau and 12366
entries.cost: Costs no money. When receiving calls, text messages, or friend requests claiming "tax spot check," "account abnormality," or "fines if you don't file taxes," hang up first and do not reply. Then call 12366 or call the landline of the competent tax authority to verify.
entries.summary: Tax authorities will not call to ask for your bank card passwords, payment passwords, or SMS verification codes, nor will they provide an account for you to transfer tax money to. Genuine on-site tax inspectors must show an inspection notice and an inspection certificate. If you receive this type of call, hang up first, then call 12366 to verify. If you have already transferred money, immediately call 110 or 96110 to stop payment.
entries.benefit: The original text of the State Taxation Administration's reminder: "Tax authorities will not solicit bank card passwords, payment passwords, account balances, or SMS verification codes related to bank card payments and receipts via WeChat Mini Programs, phone calls, text messages, or other methods." "Some lawbreakers pretend to be tax officials to contact taxpayers under the guise of providing 'assistance with tax filing,' 'agency services for tax incentives,' 'policy guidance,' etc." To verify, call the "12366 Tax and Fee Service Hotline or the landline of the competent tax authority." For genuine on-site tax audits (inspections), inspectors "must present an inspection notice and an inspection certificate." "Taxes can only be paid via the electronic tax bureau or at the tax service hall; tax authorities will not provide designated bank accounts." There is also a rule for intermediaries handling taxes for others. "Extorting taxpayers or withholding agents in the name of tax authorities and tax personnel" incurs fines depending on the severity of the circumstances. Using the banner of the tax bureau and tax officials to extort taxpayers and withholding units falls under this scenario. Impersonating personnel of state organs to practice deceit is subject to administrative detention of not less than 10 days but not more than 15 days, and may additionally be fined not more than 1,000 yuan. Where an act constitutes both the crime of fraud and the crime of swindling by impersonating state personnel, "conviction and punishment shall be determined in accordance with the provision that provides for a heavier penalty" (whichever clause punishes more severely governs sentencing) (National)
entries.sources: State Taxation Administration (2025). Tax Department Reminds Taxpayers—Enhance Awareness of Prevention and Be Alert to Internet-Related Tax Scams. <https://www.chinatax.gov.cn/chinatax/n810219/n810724/c5243181/content.html> ; Yangzhou Tax Service, State Taxation Administration (2023). Yangzhou Tax Scam Prevention Promotional Material. <https://jiangsu.chinatax.gov.cn/art/2023/8/28/art_23038_432322.html> ; State Taxation Administration (2025). Measures for the Administration of Tax-Related Professional Services (Trial) (State Taxation Administration Decree No. 58, Article 32, Item 7, and Article 33). <https://fgk.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfgk/c100011/c5239044/content.html> ; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2025). Public Security Administration Punishments Law (2025 Revision, Effective January 1, 2026, Article 62). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml> ; Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security (2016). Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases Such as Telecom and Network Fraud (Fa Fa [2016] No. 32). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/201612/t20161221_176278.shtml>
entries.notes: This kind of scam specifically targets newly registered sole proprietorships and small companies. The script is "the system shows that you haven't filed taxes, and if you don't handle it today you'll be fined," and then they direct you to their own public account or mini-program, charging hundreds of yuan a time. Yet that tax return was originally free and can be completed by yourself in a few minutes. Hiring an agency in the market for bookkeeping is not illegal, but it is not a government agency and will not push you in the name of the tax bureau. For those who have already paid money or transferred funds, immediately call 110 or 96110 to request payment stoppage according to Section 8, Item 2 (Stop payment when scammed). Impersonating market regulation departments, saying you missed filing your annual report and asking you to pay money for agency processing, is the exact same routine; see Item 25 of this section (Annual reports are free of charge)

entries.title: When Collecting Money Write "Dingjin" (定金, Earnest Money Deposit) Not "Dingjin" (订金, Booking Deposit), State Liquidated Damages Explicitly, and Vet Payment Terms Like Lending Money
entries.cost: Costs no money. Write the two characters "定金" (earnest money) into the contract, with the amount not exceeding 20% of the total contract value. Collect payment before shipping goods. Before agreeing to let the other party take goods first and pay later (granting payment terms/credit period), vet the other party thoroughly first.
entries.summary: Only writing the two characters "定金" triggers the double-reimbursement rule: if you breach the contract, you cannot get this money back; if the other party breaches, they must refund you double. The portion exceeding 20% of the contract value does not count. Written as "订金", the law provides no such rule. Granting payment credit is equivalent to lending your own money to the other party for free; if they collapse, it becomes bad debt.
entries.benefit: An earnest money deposit (定金) only counts once the money is actually delivered to the counterparty's hands (established upon actual delivery). If the party paying the earnest money breaches the contract, they cannot get this money back. If the party receiving the earnest money breaches the contract, they must refund the original amount plus pay an identical amount (double refund). The portion exceeding 20% of the total contract value (the subject matter value of the principal contract) is not treated as earnest money. Where agreed liquidated damages are outrageously higher or lower than actual losses, the court may adjust them downward or upward upon a party's request. Where both liquidated damages and earnest money are written into a contract, if a breach actually occurs, one can only choose to claim one of them, not both (National, since 2021)
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 585, 586, 587, 588). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>
entries.notes: "订金" (booking deposit) does not carry the deposit rules of "定金" under the Civil Code and is generally treated merely as an advance payment. This is the prevailing view in practice; this section has not verified judicial precedents. For paying subscription deposits when buying new commercial housing and subsequently failing to sign a formal contract, special rules apply separately; see Section 15, Item 11 (Subscription earnest money). Offering payment credit terms is essentially lending your money interest-free to the other party; if they go bust, it becomes bad debt. Before offering payment terms, check the other party's records on the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System to see if they have been sued.

entries.title: Sign a Written Contract Within the First Month of Employment, and Register for Social Insurance Within 30 Days
entries.cost: The company-funded portion of social insurance must be paid continuously, and the contribution rates vary across regions. Signing the contract itself costs no money; simply use the standard contract template from the local human resources and social security department.
entries.summary: If a person has worked for a full month without a written contract being signed, double wages must be paid each month starting from the second month, continuing up to one full year. Social insurance must be registered within 30 days of employment; if not handled and overdue without rectification, a fine of 1 to 3 times the payable social insurance contributions will be imposed. Legally, there is no such concept as "employee voluntarily waives social insurance."
entries.benefit: Where an employee has worked for a full month but less than one year without a written employment contract signed, double monthly wages must be paid. Social insurance registration must be handled for the employee within 30 days starting from their first day of work. For non-compliance, rectification is ordered first. For failure to comply within the prescribed time limit, a fine of 1 to 3 times the payable social insurance contributions is imposed, and the person directly in charge is separately fined 500 to 3,000 yuan. If social insurance is not paid on time or in full, a late surcharge of 0.05% per day is added starting from the date of default. If still unpaid beyond the deadline, an additional fine of 1 to 3 times the outstanding amount is imposed. The employer must declare on its own initiative and pay the full amount on time. Only statutory force majeure events such as natural disasters permit delayed payment or reductions. There is no concept of "employee voluntarily waives" (National)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Labor Contract Law (Articles 10, 82). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm> ; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2010). Social Insurance Law (2018 Amendment, Articles 58, 60, 84, 86). <https://www.mohrss.gov.cn/xxgk2020/fdzdgknr/zcfg/fl/202011/t20201102_394629.html>
entries.notes: Double wages are calculated from the second month all the way up to one full year; the longer the delay, the more expensive it becomes. For employees without signed contracts and unpaid social insurance, once a workplace injury occurs or arbitration is sought after departure, you will face supplementary contributions, fines, plus compensation payments. Combined, they are often far higher than the modest amount saved. For how employees claim double wages, see Section 19, Item 20 (Double wages).

entries.title: Pay Wages According to Contract and Law; Keep Salary Increases, Loans, and Bonuses in Writing
entries.cost: Costs no money. Specify wages clearly in the contract. Keep a signed piece of paper for every salary increase, bonus, advance, and loan without exception. Do not make verbal promises. Also, do not pay company wages out of your own pocket. The difficult part is sticking to this rule even when acquaintances ask.
entries.summary: Wages must be paid on time and in full according to the contract and the law. If in arrears, employees can directly request an order for payment from the court. If pay raises, bonuses, and advances are merely verbal, the party unable to produce evidence loses out when disputes arise. Lending personal money to an employee is not legally mandated to be in writing, but it is best to write an IOU (promissory note) specifying the amount, interest, and repayment date.
entries.benefit: Content that must be specified in a labor contract includes how wages are paid and how social insurance is contributed. Employers must pay wages timely and in full in accordance with the contract and state regulations. If payment is withheld or delayed, the employee may directly apply to the court for an order for payment (a collection document issued by a court). When a boss lends their own money to an employee, this constitutes a loan contract. The exact wording of the Civil Code is: "A loan contract shall be in written form, except where otherwise agreed upon between natural persons." An employer lending money personally to an employee is precisely a loan between two natural persons, so the law does not mandate a written form. Contract terms "generally include clauses on the loan category, currency, purpose, amount, interest rate, term, and repayment method." Drafting a loan note based on these items is the author's advice. Verbally promised bonuses lack black-and-white proof; when a real dispute breaks out, the party unable to produce evidence loses out (National)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Labor Contract Law (Articles 17, 30). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm> ; National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 469, 668). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>
entries.notes: It is not about refusing to help people; it is about following procedures even when helping. Once extra-institutional favors become customary, disputes will arise when you want to stop them. When personal loans and company accounts are mingled, if the company incurs losses, bad debts will fall squarely on you. The statutory provisions have been verified; the recommendations themselves are based on experience, hence Level C.

entries.title: Sell First, Make Later: Validate Customer Demand with Pre-sales and Small Orders Before Investing in Production
entries.cost: Dozens to hundreds of yuan to make a sample or a landing page. Then find dozens of real customers and get them to prepay or place small orders. This is a few weeks slower than starting production directly. The hard part is holding back from manufacturing the goods first.
entries.summary: An Italian study found that entrepreneurs who first formulated hypotheses and then validated them with market feedback performed better in business. They were also more likely to pivot in a timely manner, without dropping out earlier. Therefore, if no one is willing to prepay and no one is willing to place small orders, do not believe that "if you build it, buyers will naturally come."
entries.benefit: A randomized controlled trial tracked 116 Italian startup enterprises for about one year. A randomized controlled trial randomly divides people into two groups, provides training to only one group, and then compares the outcomes of the two groups. The result: entrepreneurs who received training and made decisions by "first proposing hypotheses, then rigorously testing them with market feedback" achieved better performance. They were also more likely to pivot to alternative solutions in a timely manner, without having a higher early abandonment rate. Projects that look promising but actually cannot succeed are called false positive projects by the authors. The authors' explanation is that this approach reduces the probability of continuing to throw money into such projects (Italy, published in 2020)
entries.sources: Camuffo A, Cordova A, Gambardella A, Spina C (2020). A Scientific Approach to Entrepreneurial Decision Making: Evidence from a Randomized Control Trial. Management Science 66(2):564-586. <https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2018.3249>
entries.notes: There is only this single study, the sample size is small, and it was conducted in Italy, so it is rated Level B. The title, source, and abstract have been checked against Crossref and Semantic Scholar; the exact effect numbers in the full text were not verified in this section. Put into practice: if no one is willing to prepay and no one is willing to place small orders, do not believe that "once it's made, someone will buy it."

entries.title: Once Samples Are Made, Review the Mass-Production Checklist Before Discussing Starting Operations
entries.cost: A few hundred yuan for a small-batch trial production run. Then spend several hours calculating yield rate clearly—that is, how many pieces out of 100 can be sold. Supplier minimum order quantities (MOQs) and payment terms, how much capital inventory will tie up, packaging and logistics, certifications and permits, and trademarks must also be tallied clearly item by item. The hard part is resisting the urge to skip this step and start production directly.
entries.summary: The difference between one sample and a thousand pieces lies in where your money is tied up. The yield rate determines the real cost; the minimum order quantity (MOQ) and payment terms dictate how much money you have to advance upfront; and inventory decides when that money can return. If a product falls within the catalogue for compulsory product certification, it cannot leave the factory or be sold without certification and without displaying the certification mark.
entries.benefit: The difference between one sample and a thousand pieces lies in where your money is tied up. The yield rate determines the real cost—the yield rate is what percentage of a produced batch passes inspection and can be sold. How much a supplier requires you to order at minimum per order (minimum order quantity, MOQ), and how long after shipping it takes before you receive payment (payment terms)—these two factors dictate how much money you have to advance upfront. Inventory decides when the money comes back. Products included in the catalogue for compulsory product certification must pass certification first, and must display the certification mark on the product, before they can leave the factory and be sold. Those who leave the factory and sell without authorization in the absence of certification shall be penalized according to the regulations on certification and accreditation. Operating in catering and selling food requires obtaining a food business license (nationwide).
entries.sources: General Administration of Quality Supervision, Inspection and Quarantine (AQSIQ) (2009). Regulations on Compulsory Product Certification (AQSIQ Decree No. 117, Articles 2 and 49). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2010/content_1533513.htm>; State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) (2023). Measures for the Administration of Food Business Licensing and Filing (SAMR Decree No. 78, Article 4). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2023/issue_10606/202307/content_6894763.html>
entries.notes: The checklist itself is an experiential method; the statutory provisions have been verified against original texts. Before going into production, first check whether there are similar registered trademarks in the trademark search system of the China National Intellectual Property Administration, and then apply for your own trademark. For the red lines regarding using others' trademarks and graphic designs, see entries 20 and 21 (keep receipts for inventory purchases; create your own designs or purchase licenses). The compulsory certification catalogue is subject to the latest version published by the State Administration for Market Regulation.

entries.title: Keep purchase receipts and upstream vendor info for every batch of goods, and do not buy when the purchase price is conspicuously lower than market price: when fake goods bought by employees for the company count as corporate crime, the boss is also the one sentenced
entries.cost: Costs no money. For every batch of goods, keep these items in good order: procurement contracts, invoices, payment records, and the upstream vendor's business license and authorization documents. Furthermore, establish an internal rule: whoever procures the goods must sign for them, and goods with prices conspicuously lower than market prices are strictly rejected. The hard part is passing up those low-priced goods that look very profitable.
entries.summary: Selling counterfeit goods: earning 30,000 yuan, or reaching sales of 50,000 yuan, is enough for a criminal sentence of up to 3 years. For goods that haven't been sold yet, it also counts if the value of the goods reaches three times the sales threshold. "I didn't know it was fake" is not up to you to declare: if the purchase price is conspicuously lower than the market price and you cannot provide a justifiable reason, it can be established that you had knowledge. Only by keeping procurement contracts, invoices, payment records, and upstream vendor information can you have the path to exemption from compensation.
entries.benefit: Selling goods knowing they are commodities bearing counterfeit registered trademarks crosses the threshold for criminal sentencing once the money earned (illegal gains) reaches 30,000 yuan. It is the same once the sales amount reaches 50,000 yuan. Sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 3 years, concurrently with a fine, or sentenced only to a fine. Reaching ten times this standard results in 3 to 10 years of imprisonment concurrently with a fine. Goods still stuck in the warehouse and not yet sold also count: if the value of the goods reaches more than three times the sales amount threshold, it likewise constitutes a crime. "Knowing" does not require you to admit it yourself. The 2025 judicial interpretation by the Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate lists five circumstances under which it can be directly determined that you had knowledge, unless you can produce evidence proving that you genuinely did not know: First, knowing that the registered trademark on the commodity has been altered, swapped, or covered. Second, forging or altering authorization documents from the trademark registrant, or knowing that such documents have been forged or altered. Third, having received criminal or administrative penalties for selling counterfeit goods, and then selling the same kind again. Fourth, without justifiable reasons, purchasing or selling goods at prices conspicuously lower than market prices. Fifth, after discovery by administrative law enforcement agencies or judicial organs, transferring or destroying evidence such as infringing goods and accounting vouchers, or providing false certification. Where a company commits this offense, "the unit shall be sentenced to a fine, and its directly responsible persons in charge and other directly responsible personnel" shall be punished under the same provision. That is, the company pays a fine, and the decision-making person in charge and the handlers are sentenced under the same provision. Therefore, when a company commits this violation, even if the goods were procured by an employee, the person who made the final decision will also be sentenced. Conversely, the Trademark Law leaves a way out: if at the time of sale you genuinely did not know that the goods infringed on another person's registered trademark, and "can prove that the commodity was legally acquired by oneself and explain the provider, one shall not bear liability for compensation." Whether one can be exempted from compensation depends entirely on having receipts and upstream vendor info; without keeping them, this provision cannot be used (nationwide, judicial interpretation effective from April 26, 2025).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2020). Criminal Law Amendment (XI) (Items 17 and 24, namely Articles 214 and 220 of the Criminal Law). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/202012/t20201227_503682.shtml>; Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate (2025). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Intellectual Property Infringement (Legal Interpretation [2025] No. 5, effective April 26, 2025). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbt/202504/t20250424_693977.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2019). Trademark Law (2019 Amendment, Articles 57 and 64; Articles 72 and 78 after the June 26, 2026 revision, effective January 1, 2027). <https://www.cnipa.gov.cn/art/2019/7/30/art_95_28179.html>, <https://www.cnipa.gov.cn/art/2026/6/26/art_95_206942.html>
entries.notes: Cosmetics, alcohol and beverages, maternal and infant products, digital electronics, and clothing are high-incidence categories for these cases. Their common feature is that the exact same model of goods has a huge price spread. Claims like "channel goods," "factory overruns," or "overseas duty-free" cannot substitute for receipts. Beyond criminal sentencing, there is another layer of administrative penalty: where infringement is established, infringing goods and tools are confiscated, and where the illegal business volume is 50,000 yuan or more, a concurrent fine of up to 5 times may be imposed. If you discover something is wrong only after having procured the goods, immediately cease sales, seal them up, and then contact the brand owner or the market supervision department. Do not continue selling, and especially do not destroy the goods and accounting records. Destroying evidence falls squarely into the fifth circumstance above for "presuming you knowingly sold counterfeit goods." For using others' graphic designs, see entry 21 (either make designs yourself or buy licenses). There is a specific setup targeted at this provision: someone visits you unsolicited, saying that a batch of pens or other small commodities is free for you, to be placed in the store for sale with profits split later. A few days later, someone comes to buy them, collects evidence on the spot, and then claims compensation for infringement. For free goods, all three conditions required for exemption from compensation are entirely missing: no procurement contract and payment records, inability to identify the genuine provider, and conspicuously abnormal pricing. Not a single condition of "legally acquired and explaining the provider" can be applied. Therefore, for unsolicited door-to-door deliveries with no receipts provided and only a WeChat ID left, strictly keep them off the shelves. If you genuinely want to do consignment sales, sign a written consignment contract, keep copies of the other party's ID card and business license, and stipulate in writing who owns the goods and who bears liability in case of infringement.

entries.title: Either make patterns on products, packaging, tags, and promotional images yourself or purchase licenses; changing a color or adding an icon does not count as "having modified it"
entries.cost: Licensing from legitimate stock photo libraries starts from several tens of yuan per image. Hiring someone for original design ranges from several hundred to several thousand yuan. For every single image used on a product, retain a copy of the licensing certificate and purchase record. The hard part is not using images casually searched online.
entries.summary: Changing a color, swapping the background color, or adding your own icon to another's image is still using another's work without permission. For the purpose of making money, reproducing another person's work of fine art: earning 30,000 yuan, generating 50,000 yuan in business, or printing 500 copies constitutes the crime of copyright infringement, punishable by up to 3 years of imprisonment. On the trademark side, being "similar enough to easily cause confusion" itself constitutes infringement.
entries.benefit: The Copyright Law juxtaposes "using a work by adaptation, translation, annotation, etc., without permission of the copyright owner" alongside direct reproduction as infringing acts. Therefore, changing colors, switching background colors, or adding one's own icon onto an original image remains the unauthorized use of another person's work. The threshold for criminal penalties is right here: for the purpose of making money, printing and selling (reproducing and distributing) works of fine art without permission from the work's copyright owner. Three numbers can trigger the crime: the money earned (illegal gains) reaches 30,000 yuan; or this business reaches 50,000 yuan (illegal business turnover); or the cumulative printed quantity reaches 500 copies (pieces). Reaching any single one of these figures constitutes the crime of copyright infringement, punishable by fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 3 years, concurrently with a fine, or only a fine. Reaching ten times the threshold is punishable by 3 to 10 years. Merely selling infringing copies printed by others, if earning 50,000 yuan or more, or selling 100,000 yuan or more, is punishable by not more than 5 years under the crime of selling infringing reproductions. The same applies to trademarks; the following two circumstances that are "likely to cause confusion" are themselves within the scope of infringement: one is using a trademark similar to a registered trademark on the same kind of goods; the other is using an identical or similar trademark on similar goods. "Similar" is an explicitly stated infringement circumstance in statutory law. Tweaking another's trademark before using it, as long as it is likely to cause confusion, still counts as infringement (nationwide, judicial interpretation effective from April 26, 2025).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2020). Copyright Law (2020 Amendment, Article 52, Item 6, and Article 53). <http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202011/t20201119_308796.html>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2020). Criminal Law Amendment (XI) (Items 20 and 21, namely Articles 217 and 218 of the Criminal Law). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/202012/t20201227_503682.shtml>; Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate (2025). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Intellectual Property Infringement (Legal Interpretation [2025] No. 5). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbt/202504/t20250424_693977.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2019). Trademark Law (2019 Amendment, Article 57, Item 2; Article 72, Item 2 after the 2026 revision). <https://www.cnipa.gov.cn/art/2019/7/30/art_95_28179.html>
entries.notes: There are three common pitfalls. First is taking cartoon figures and celebrity photos found on the web and printing them on clothes, mugs, and phone cases. Second is fonts: commercial fonts mostly require separate licensing; free preview does not equal free commercial use. Third is when design drafts made for clients sandwich in unlicensed assets, the liability still falls on the party selling the goods. To save trouble, use stock libraries with commercial licenses and save the license page. Or have the designer specify clearly in the contract where the materials came from, the scope of licensing, and that the designer will be responsible if any issues arise. Beyond criminal sentencing, there are also civil damages and administrative fines: where public interest is harmed, illegal gains can be confiscated, along with a fine of 1 to 5 times the illegal business turnover. For trademark search before production, see entry 19 (run samples through the mass production checklist first). Conversely, if your own images are used by others, defend your rights according to this same set of rules. For the criminal threshold regarding uploading others' manga, movies, and TV shows to the internet, running ads, and collecting membership fees, see section 9, entry 24 (translating manga, pirating movies and TV shows).

entries.title: Act according to operational protocols on the job; for kindness outside protocols, first think through who bears liability
entries.cost: Costs no money. Handle matters at work according to rules, doctor's orders, and standard processes. Do not make decisions for others beyond your scope of authority. Before wanting to help, first ask yourself: if something goes wrong, who is responsible? The hard part is resisting pleas on the spot to "make an exception."
entries.summary: Taking nurses as an example: the regulations specify that upon discovering a patient's condition is critical, one must immediately notify a physician; upon discovering a doctor's order violates regulations, one must raise it with the prescribing physician. Other positions are the same: first see clearly where your own protocol draws the line for "mandatory reporting." Furthermore, voluntarily stepping forward to provide emergency assistance without liability if the rescued person is injured.
entries.benefit: Taking nurses as an example, the job boundaries stipulated by laws and regulations are as follows: upon discovering a condition is critical, immediately notify a physician. In emergencies, in order to rescue a dying or critically ill patient, necessary emergency care may be implemented first. Upon discovering a doctor's order is illegal, non-compliant, or violates technical standards for diagnosis and treatment, one must raise it with the physician, and report to the department head when necessary. The Civil Code has a separate provision: if one voluntarily steps forward to render emergency aid and consequently causes injury to the rescued person, the aiding party does not pay compensation (bears no civil liability) (nationwide).
entries.sources: State Council (2008). Regulations on Nurses (State Council Decree No. 517, Article 17). <http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_6169.htm>; State Council (2020). Regulations on Nurses (2020 Revision, Article 17). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081777d07c50177b8ed29bf3950> (National Database of Laws and Regulations); National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 184). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>
entries.notes: Follow standard operating protocols within your post; emergency rescue is protected by law. For all other matters, first distinguish whose authority and whose responsibility it is, and do not let personal goodwill substitute for institutional decisions. The Regulations on Nurses was revised in 2020 via State Council Decree No. 726, altering only the articles regarding registration; Article 17 was left completely unchanged. Because the official original text of the clauses regarding practicing according to clinical diagnosis and treatment standards in the Law on Physicians could not be opened this time, it has not been cited.

entries.title: If running at a loss, exit following procedure: deregister via simplified procedure if eligible, file for bankruptcy if insolvent, and do not simply abandon it
entries.cost: Simplified deregistration can be handled on your own: post it publicly on the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System for 20 days. For those with debts not yet fully repaid, accounts must be settled first, collecting what should be collected and paying what should be paid; this step is called liquidation. Going through bankruptcy requires petitioning the court and takes several months. The hard part is not wanting to face it after losing money and endlessly stalling without taking action.
entries.summary: For those with no debts, no unpaid wages, taxes, or social security, all investors write a letter of commitment; if nobody raises objections during 20 days of public announcement, simplified deregistration can proceed. Individually owned businesses do not need a public announcement and are directly deregistered if there are no objections within 10 days. If a company cannot pay its debts, it can apply for bankruptcy. For businesses left abandoned, failing to file annual reports for 2 consecutive years and unreachable, business licenses are revoked, and the responsible legal representative cannot serve as a legal representative again within 3 years.
entries.benefit: Neither owing others nor others owing you, or all debts have already been settled in full. No wages owed, no social security owed, no taxes owed. All investors have provided a written commitment. Satisfying these conditions, posting publicly for 20 days without objections allows you to pursue simplified deregistration. Individually owned businesses do not require public notice; if relevant departments have no objections within 10 days, deregistration is processed directly. A company that cannot repay debts due and whose debts exceed its assets (insolvency) may apply to the court for reorganization, conciliation, or bankruptcy liquidation. Entities already dissolved but not liquidated whose debts exceed their assets: those responsible for liquidation shall apply for bankruptcy liquidation. The consequences of simply leaving things unattended are as follows: failure to publicly announce annual reports on schedule will result in being placed on the list of enterprises with abnormal operations. Failing to submit annual reports for 2 consecutive years, being listed on the abnormal operations list without rectification, and being unreachable at the registered address will result in revocation of the business license. When an enterprise's license is revoked, any legal representative who bears personal responsibility for this shall not serve as a company's legal representative, director, supervisor, or senior manager within 3 years. These 3 years are calculated starting from the date of license revocation. Those already listed on the abnormal operations list cannot even undergo simplified deregistration (nationwide).
entries.sources: State Council (2021). Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (State Council Decree No. 746, Articles 31, 32, and 33). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-08/24/content_5632964.htm>; State Administration for Market Regulation and Five Other Departments (2025). Enterprise Deregistration Guide (2025 Revision) (Announcement No. 52 of 2025). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202512/content_7053238.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2006). Enterprise Bankruptcy Law (Articles 2 and 7). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2006/content_413952.htm>; State Council (2024 Revision). Interim Regulations on Enterprise Information Publicity (Revised by State Council Decree No. 777, Article 18): "Where an enterprise has been placed on the list of enterprises with abnormal operations due to failure to submit annual reports in accordance with provisions for two consecutive years and has not rectified the situation, and cannot be contacted through its registered domicile or business premises, its business license shall be revoked by the market supervision and administration department at or above the county level." <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081819c46fcc5019cd18fc6e9557d> (National Database of Laws and Regulations); State Council (2024). Decision on Amending and Repealing Certain Administrative Regulations (State Council Decree No. 777). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2024/issue_11246/202403/content_6941844.html>; Regulations on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (Article 12, Item 4) and Company Law (2023 Revision, Article 178, Paragraph 1, Item 4): having served as the legal representative of an enterprise whose business license was revoked for violating the law and being personally liable, where less than 3 years have elapsed since the date of revocation of the business license, one shall not serve as a legal representative, director, supervisor, or senior management personnel. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-08/24/content_5632964.htm>; <https://www.gov.cn/yaowen/liebiao/202312/content_6923395.htm>
entries.notes: The Interim Regulations on Enterprise Information Publicity was revised in 2024 via State Council Decree No. 777, taking effect on May 1, with no subsequent changes. The old Article 17 provision "listed on the list of seriously illegal enterprises after abnormal operation reaches 3 years" has been deleted. The current list of enterprises with serious illegalities and dishonesty governs enterprises that commit serious fraud in their annual reports. Many descriptions online still follow the old version—do not copy them. For when to submit annual reports and how to make up for missed reports, see entry 25 of this section (submitting the previous year's annual report online from January 1 to June 30 each year). Personal bankruptcy systems (including for individual businesses) are currently piloted in only a few regions; original texts were not verified for this section, so they are not included.

entries.title: Before paying someone to manage your online store, taking store-opening training, or doing "zero-inventory" operations, first ask clearly whether more money will be required later and where sales volume comes from
entries.cost: Costs no money. Before handing over money, obtain three things: a written contract, the full official name of the other party's company, and refund conditions. Only pay money to the company named in the contract, never transferring to personal accounts. The hard part is holding back from paying on the spot when the other party displays screenshots of "students earning over 10,000 a month."
entries.summary: This type of scam first collects a fee, then repeatedly demands extra money using excuses like "package upgrades," advancing payments for goods, or unfreezing fees. Orders and revenue shown in the back end may be fabricated; when you want to withdraw cash, you cannot withdraw it. Relying on fake review-brushing to boost sales volume is itself illegal, and operational agencies that get caught will face penalties.
entries.benefit: The Higher People's Court of Guangdong Province once ruled on an e-commerce agency operations scam. Fifty-five individuals, including someone surnamed Jiang and someone surnamed Xu, opened multiple companies in Guangzhou, Nanning, and Hangzhou. The court determined that they "clearly knew they fundamentally lacked the capability and technical conditions for e-commerce agency operations." Nevertheless, under the pretext of managing Taobao online shops on behalf of others, they lured 7,711 victims into purchasing and upgrading "service packages." In total, they defrauded victims of over 52.994 million yuan. The two primary culprits were sentenced to 14 years and 13 years and 6 months of imprisonment, respectively, for fraud. The court stated that the scam was designed to be "seamlessly tightly knit" and that "multiple victims were deceived repeatedly." In 2025, the Jiangsu Provincial Public Security Department broke down the "no-inventory" cross-border e-commerce scam into four steps. Step 1: post messages on social media platforms advertising "zero foundation" and "no need to stockpile goods." Step 2: add you under the identity of "operations guidance" and have you download a designated platform. Step 3: soon after opening your shop, you get your first order. The other party asks you to advance the product cost price first, claiming that the buyer's payment is frozen in the platform and will be unfrozen upon delivery confirmation. Subsequently, the backend fabricates a large volume of orders, prompting you to continuously add money. Step 4: when you want to withdraw funds, they claim there is an "account anomaly" or "system maintenance," demanding that you pay additional unfreezing fees or handling fees. In the case study, Ms. Zhang successively advanced over 900,000 yuan, and 3 days later the website could no longer be opened. Look also at fake order brushing. An agency operator organized fake group purchases for merchants to boost rankings. The market regulation department fined it 100,000 yuan, the platform deducted its 50,000 yuan deposit, and the court supported the platform's deposit deduction. The Supreme People's Court listed it as a typical case in 2026, stating verbatim that "fabricated transactions, fake order brushing, and reputation manipulation are fundamentally acts explicitly prohibited by law." The State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) also publicized a case in 2025. A company selling "one-click shop transfer" and "one-click dropshipping" software that scraped product information from other platforms to list them for sale was fined 530,000 yuan. SAMR reminded business operators that they "must not carry out illegal acts such as 'stealing store content via搬家 (transfer)' and 'operating without inventory'." The way out lies in the Civil Code: if a contract was signed because you were deceived through fraudulent means by the counterparty, you can petition a people's court or arbitration institution to revoke it. It must be filed within 1 year from the date you knew of the fraud. After revocation, the money acquired by the counterparty because of it shall be returned (National).
entries.sources: Higher People's Court of Guangdong Province (2023). Typical Cases of Guangdong Courts Combating and Governing Telecom Network Fraud Crimes (Case 3: Fraud Case of a 55-Person Criminal Syndicate Involving Jiang, Xu, et al.). <https://www.gdcourts.gov.cn/gsxx/quanweifabu/anlihuicui/content/post_1388464.html>; Jiangsu Provincial Public Security Department (2025). Prevention Tips: No-Inventory Cross-Border E-commerce, Beware of Scams!. <https://gat.jiangsu.gov.cn/art/2025/2/13/art_89956_11491354.html>; Supreme People's Court (2026). Supreme People's Court Releases Typical Cases on Regulating Platform Operations in Accordance with Law and Protecting Consumers' Legitimate Rights and Interests (Case 3: Service Contract Dispute Case of a Certain Agency Operator v. a Certain Platform). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/507691.html>; State Administration for Market Regulation (2025). State Administration for Market Regulation Publicizes Five Typical Cases of Online Unfair Competition (Case 1). <https://www.samr.gov.cn/xw/zj/art/2025/art_0d043840ec9445a689496bcf30c94820.html>; National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 148, 152, 157). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>.
entries.notes: When you see "zero foundation," "no need to stockpile goods," "low investment, high return," and "guaranteed profitability," pause first. When someone asks you to advance payment for goods into their designated platform, also pause first. Before handing over money, go to the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System to check the counterparty's business license and penalty records. Clearly specify the service scope in the contract, as well as how money is refunded if goals are not met. Preserve chat records, contracts, and transfer screenshots properly. If you have already transferred money, immediately dial 110 or 96110 to request payment stoppage; see Section 8, Item 2 (Stop Payment After Being Scammed). If the counterparty actually performed work and the results were merely poor, it is mostly considered a contract dispute, which requires negotiation, complaints, or a lawsuit. Revoking a contract requires litigation; first-instance ordinary procedures are prescribed to conclude within 6 months, which can be extended, lawyer fees are borne by yourself, and by the time judgment is rendered, the counterparty might have long since run off. If someone collects money under the banner of franchising, first check records according to Item 5 (Check Ministry of Commerce Filings Before Franchising). The beneficiary is primarily yourself.

entries.title: Those opening a company or operating as an individual industrial and commercial household: submit the prior year's annual report online from January 1 to June 30 each year; report even with zero business; annual reporting is free of charge
entries.cost: Costs no money. Log in to the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System yourself to fill it out and submit it once a year. Individual industrial and commercial households can also submit on paper. Submitting the annual report to the market regulation department and filing taxes monthly or quarterly with the tax bureau are two different matters. Filing taxes is not equivalent to submitting the annual report. The difficult part is that it only occurs once a year, making it easy to forget.
entries.summary: Those who start a company or run an individual industrial and commercial household must submit the prior year's annual report online once during the first half of each year. Failure to report leads to placement on the list of enterprises with abnormal operations; you can apply for removal after filing retroactively. Annual reporting is free of charge; callers claiming you missed your filing and directing you to pay mini-programs or official accounts for proxy handling are scammers; check the publicity system yourself first. Primary culprits of such scams have been sentenced to over 10 years.
entries.benefit: A company must, "from January 1 to June 30 each year, submit its annual report for the preceding year to the market supervision and administration department through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and publicize it to the public." Those failing to report past the deadline will be included in the list of enterprises with abnormal operations, "and subjected to administrative penalties in accordance with the law." The list of enterprises with abnormal operations is displayed on the publicity system and can be checked by anyone. In contexts such as government procurement and engineering bidding, enterprises on the list will be restricted or banned from entry. Individual industrial and commercial households must likewise report the previous year's annual report from January 1 to June 30 each year, which can be reported online or submitted on paper. Individual industrial and commercial households that commenced operations in the current year report starting from the following year. Individual industrial and commercial households can choose for themselves whether or not to make the contents of their annual reports public, but failure to report will still result in inclusion on the list of abnormal operations. For those included on the list due to failure to submit annual reports, once the missing years are retroactively filed, they may apply to the market regulation department at the place of registration for removal. If a company fails to report for 2 consecutive years, is included on the list and still fails to rectify, and cannot be contacted at its registered address, its business license shall be revoked. Annual reports of enterprises must be publicized to the public. If an individual industrial and commercial household chooses not to publicize its report contents, the system will still publicize that it "has already submitted its annual report." Therefore, whether a report was submitted and whether you are on the list can be verified simply by checking the publicity system yourself. SAMR has warned of a type of scam: individuals "impersonating market regulation personnel" call to claim you missed the deadline to report and have already been put on the list of enterprises with abnormal operations. They then "guide you to search for so-called mini-programs or official accounts," asking you to entrust proxy handling and pay fees. SAMR's stance is that "annual reporting is free of charge." Submitting annual reports and applying for removal from the list of enterprises with abnormal operations "must be done through official channels such as the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System." Courts have already sentenced such cases as fraud. The Jingde County People's Court of Anhui adjudicated one case: a registration agency company had telephone operators "deliberately conceal their identity," leading individual industrial and commercial households to believe they were personnel from the market regulation department. The operators then guided victims to third-party mini-programs, charging a "manual declaration materials fee" of 98 to 398 yuan. They defrauded 10,099 individual industrial and commercial households nationwide of over 3.19 million yuan in total. Three principal offenders committed fraud and were sentenced to terms ranging from 10 years and 6 months to 10 years and 8 months. In a case adjudicated by the Nanhu District People's Court of Jiaxing, the mini-program actually stated in fine print that "submission is free." The court still convicted them of fraud on the grounds that the operators "deliberately concealed the actual fact that business operators could process it online, and fabricated lies about large fines." In this case, 9 people were sentenced to terms ranging from 8 months to 4 years (National).
entries.sources: State Council (2024 Revision). Interim Regulations on Enterprise Information Publicity (Revised by State Council Decree No. 777, Articles 8, 18, 19). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081819c46fcc5019cd18fc6e9557d> (National Laws and Regulations Database); State Administration for Market Regulation (2025). Decision on Amending Four Departmental Rules Including the Measures for Annual Reporting of Individual Industrial and Commercial Households (SAMR Decree No. 108, with re-promulgated Measures for Annual Reporting of Individual Industrial and Commercial Households Articles 3, 5, 8, 10, 13, 16, and Measures for the Administration of the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations Articles 6, 11). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2026/issue_12546/202602/content_7057451.html>; State Administration for Market Regulation (2023). @All Business Entities: These Are All Fake (reprinted in Department Trends of the State Council Web, originally published on SAMR's "Shishuo Xinyu" WeChat Official Account). <https://www.gov.cn/lianbo/bumen/202311/content_6917465.htm>; State Administration for Market Regulation (2024). SAMR Issues Reminder: Annual Reporting Is Free of Charge, Do Not Be Deceived (reprinted by Binzhou Municipal Administration for Market Regulation). <http://amr.binzhou.gov.cn/art/2024/12/16/art_164869_10306521.html>; People's Court of Jingde County, Anhui Province (2025). Case of Impersonating Market Regulation Personnel to Commit Fraud Against Individual Industrial and Commercial Households by Charging Annual Inspection Filing Fees (reprinted by Wuxi Municipal Administration for Market Regulation). <https://scjgj.wuxi.gov.cn/doc/2025/03/20/4524579.shtml>; People's Court of Nanhu District, Jiaxing Municipality (2024). Enterprise Annual Reports Require Fees? Do Not Fall into the "Annual Report Fraud" Trap. <http://nhcourt.gov.cn/art/2024/7/23/art_1217290_58718476.html>.
entries.notes: Upon receiving a call claiming you failed to submit your annual report, hang up first, log in to the publicity system yourself to check, or call the market regulation department at your place of registration to inquire. Do not click links in text messages, nor pay fees in mini-programs or official accounts provided by the other party. This is the exact same routine as scams impersonating the tax bureau; see Item 14 of this Section (Anyone Claiming to Be from the Tax Bureau Urging You to Pay Money for Tax Filings Is a Scammer). If you have already transferred money, dial 110 or 96110 immediately to request payment stoppage. The Measures for Annual Reporting of Individual Industrial and Commercial Households and the Measures for the Administration of the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations were revised twice in 2025. The current version took effect on December 25, 2025. Annual reporting and tax filings are managed separately; for how to file taxes, see Item 12 of this Section (Declare Truthfully and on Schedule); both must be done on time. After a company's license is revoked, the responsible legal representative cannot serve as a legal representative again within 3 years; see Item 23 of this Section (Exit According to Procedure If Losing Money). If you do not plan to continue operations, go deregister according to that item; do not procrastinate by neglecting annual reports. The beneficiary is primarily yourself.

entries.title: When pooling money to do business, talk in person only with relatives, friends, and employees; do not publicly recruit people to invest in Moments or chat groups, nor let relatives and friends pull in others on your behalf
entries.cost: Costs no money. When borrowing money or gathering people to take equity stakes, approach only relatives, friends, and employees whom you personally know, talking face-to-face one by one. Do not post on Moments, do not post in chat groups, do not print flyers, and do not hold promotional pitch meetings. If relatives or friends say "I'll help you ask around other people," stop them on the spot. The difficult part is that when short on money, "pulling in a few more people" seems like the fastest way to get funds.
entries.summary: Borrowing money or pooling share capital from relatives, friends, and employees is not illegal in itself. What is illegal is public promotion, taking money from strangers, and promising principal return with interest or investment returns. Collecting 1 million yuan, or taking money from 150 people, reaches the threshold for criminal sentencing, starting at under 3 years. If the money was used for legitimate business and fully returned prior to prosecution, criminal punishment may be waived.
entries.benefit: Article 176 of the Criminal Law governs "whoever illegally absorbs public deposits or absorbs public deposits in disguised form, disrupting financial order." The punishment is fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 3 years or criminal detention, and concurrently a fine, or a fine alone. If the amount is huge or there are other serious circumstances, the sentence is 3 to 10 years. If the amount is especially huge or there are other especially serious circumstances, the sentence is 10 years or more.
