Judicial interpretations by the Supreme People's Court specify that all four conditions must be met simultaneously: First, taking money without lawful approval from relevant departments, or using the guise of lawful business operations. Second, publicizing openly to society via networks, media, pitch conferences, flyers, mobile phone messages, and other avenues. Third, promising to repay principal with interest or provide returns within a certain period via money, physical goods, equity, etc. Fourth, collecting money from non-specific members of the general public. The same article continues: "Where funds are absorbed from specific targets among relatives, friends, or within one's own unit without open publicity to society, it does not constitute illegal absorption or disguised absorption of public deposits." However, an opinion by the Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, and Ministry of Public Security outlines two exceptions that still count as absorbing funds from the general public: First, when collecting money from relatives, friends, or employees, knowingly allowing them to collect money on your behalf from strangers while letting it happen unchecked. Second, hiring outsiders as employees for the purpose of collecting money, and subsequently taking money from them. There are three criminal threshold lines, reaching any one of which suffices: collecting 1 million yuan or more, collecting from 150 people or more, or causing direct losses of 500,000 yuan or more to others. Collecting 5 million yuan or more, collecting from 500 people or more, or causing losses of 2.5 million yuan or more to others enters the 3-to-10-year bracket. The amount is calculated in full based on total funds taken in. Where the funds were primarily used in normal production and business operations and all collected funds can be refunded prior to prosecution, criminal punishment may be waived. Where circumstances are significantly minor and harm is not serious, it will not be handled as a crime. If it does not reach the criminal threshold, there are still administrative penalties. The local leading department for handling illegal fundraising will impose a fine of 20% to 1 time the fundraised amount. Where an entity engages in fundraising, the legal representative and persons directly responsible shall be "given a warning and fined not less than 500,000 yuan but not more than 5 million yuan" (National, judicial interpretation effective March 1, 2022).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2020). Amendment (XI) to the Criminal Law (Item 12, namely Article 176 of the Criminal Law). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/202012/t20201227_503682.shtml>; Supreme People's Court (2022 Amendment). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Criminal Cases Involving Illegal Fundraising (Fa Shi [2022] No. 5 Amendment, Articles 1, 3, 4, 6). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/346901.html>; Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security (2014). Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Illegal Fundraising (Points 2, 3). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/201404/t20140401_70180.shtml>; State Council (2021). Regulations on the Prevention and Handling of Illegal Fundraising (State Council Decree No. 737, Articles 2, 19, 25, 30). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-02/10/content_5586632.htm>.
entries.notes: Once deemed illegal fundraising, relatives and friends who lent you money will also suffer losses. Article 25 of the Regulations stipulates that losses sustained from participating in illegal fundraising shall be borne by the fund providers themselves. Article 19 of the Regulations also explicitly calls out a common form in business: collecting money when selling goods, providing services, or investing in projects with promises of returns in cash, equity, or physical goods. Selling stored-value cards or membership cards in a store while promising rebates or profit-sharing and collecting from unfamiliar customers falls squarely into this provision. When short on money, the safer path is obtaining bank loans, or converting money into equity and writing it into a partnership agreement; see Item 28 (Partnership Agreements). For how fund providers can protect themselves, see Section 5, Item 6 ("High Yield", "Capital Preservation", "Guaranteed Profit"). For how elderly people can protect themselves, see Section 17, Item 5 (Stay Away from All "Pension Investment"). The beneficiaries are primarily yourself, followed by the relatives and friends who lend you money.

entries.title: Leasing a storefront to open a shop: check whether this premises can accommodate your shop before signing; converting residential premises into a shop requires unanimous consent of all owners in the same building; no new restaurants generating cooking fumes may be opened in residential buildings
entries.cost: Costs no money. Before signing a lease, paying a deposit, and renovating, spend a few hours clarifying three things. First, the designated use on the property ownership certificate: is it residential or commercial? Second, is this building purely residential, a commercial-residential building, or a standalone commercial store, and does anyone live upstairs? Third, for catering businesses, verify whether there is a dedicated exhaust flue, then go to the local market regulation department to ask whether a food operation permit can be issued. The difficult part is that when landlords or agents say "No problem, the previous tenant ran one," you still have to verify it yourself.
entries.summary: Converting a residential property into a shop requires unanimous consent from all other owners in the same building; one single objecting household makes it unacceptable. If neighbors sue you to restore the property to its original state and pay compensation, the court will support them. Neither residential buildings nor commercial-residential buildings without dedicated exhaust flues permit newly opened restaurants that generate cooking fumes; if discovered, you will first be ordered to rectify. Refusal to rectify results in store closure and fines of 10,000 to 100,000 yuan, and renovation costs and deposits might just be lost as a result.
entries.benefit: Civil Code Article 279: "Where an owner changes residential premises into commercial premises, in addition to abiding by laws, regulations, and management covenants, the owner shall obtain the unanimous consent of interested owners." The judicial interpretation of the Supreme People's Court elaborates in greater detail: all other owners in the same building count as "interested owners." Owners in other buildings of the same residential compound must prove that the value of their property or quality of life is affected to qualify. Where a conversion occurs without their unanimous consent, if they request cessation, restoration to original state, or compensation for losses, the people's court shall support it. Using the defense that "a majority of owners agreed" will not be supported by the court. The Ecological Environment Code takes effect on August 15, 2026, at which time the Law on the Prevention and Control of Atmospheric Pollution is simultaneously repealed. Article 250 of the Code prohibits newly building, altering, or expanding catering service projects that produce cooking fumes, peculiar odors, or waste gas in three types of locations: first, residential buildings; second, commercial-residential mixed-use buildings not equipped with dedicated exhaust flues; third, commercial floors in commercial-residential mixed-use buildings adjacent to residential floors. For violations, an order to rectify shall be issued first. For refusal to rectify, closure shall be ordered, along with a fine of 10,000 to 100,000 yuan. The Code also requires local governments to provide reminders regarding prohibitive catering site selection requirements during the registration process. When applying for a food operation permit, the venue must be commensurate with the variety and quantity of food operated, and maintain prescribed distances from toxic and hazardous premises and other pollution sources. Conversely, if the premises itself fails to comply with mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations regarding conditions of use, you may terminate the lease contract, provided that the inability to use was not caused by you (National).
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 279, 724). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; Supreme People's Court (2020 Revision). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Dispute Cases Involving Building Condominium Ownership (Articles 10, 11). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808181799df6140179b092ef2d2af9> (National Laws and Regulations Database); National People's Congress (2026). Ecological Environment Code (Articles 250, 1132, 1242, taking effect on August 15, 2026). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=96630961659b4d87a65b7b1c595097fa> (National Laws and Regulations Database); State Administration for Market Regulation (2023). Measures for the Administration of Food Operation Licensing and Filing (SAMR Decree No. 78, Article 12). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2023/issue_10606/202307/content_6894763.html>.
entries.notes: "The previous tenant operated one" does not prove you can; it could be that nobody ever sued them, or it was already operating before the Code took effect. Management covenants may also contain additional restrictions; ask the property management office for a copy to review before signing. If the property is not permitted for such use and you need to terminate the lease to recover deposits and renovation losses, you will have to litigate if the landlord refuses. First-instance ordinary procedure is prescribed to finish within 6 months, which can be extended, with lawyer fees paid out of pocket. Therefore, writing "the lease may be terminated and deposits refunded if permits cannot be obtained or closure is ordered" directly into the lease agreement saves far more trouble. For what licenses must be obtained, see Item 7 (Trades Requiring Licenses) and Item 8 (Check Which Tier You Fall into Before Handling Food). The beneficiary is primarily yourself.

entries.title: When several people partner up to open a shop, put capital contributions, profit distribution, who has the final say, who draws a salary, and exit mechanisms into a written agreement before opening
entries.cost: Costs nothing. The partners sit down to discuss things once or twice, clearly write down a dozen or so items, and each sign it. Standard partnership agreement templates can be found online, and you can fill them out item by item following the ten items listed in the Partnership Enterprise Law. What is difficult is that acquaintances often feel that "talking about money hurts feelings" and feel too embarrassed to bring it up.
entries.summary: If you do not write an agreement, the law sets the rules for you. Decisions require unanimous consent, profits are distributed according to the actual capital contributed by each person, and the person who minds the shop every day receives no salary by default. Where no partnership term is agreed upon, anyone can notify the others a reasonable time in advance and then withdraw. If you want to change any of these, it must be written into an agreement beforehand.
entries.benefit: Article 4 of the Partnership Enterprise Law explicitly states that a partnership agreement shall be concluded through consensus among all partners and in written form. Article 18 lists ten items that must be written into the agreement. Among them are the forms of capital contribution, amounts, and deadlines for payment; methods of profit distribution and loss sharing; and who executes partnership affairs. There are also admission and withdrawal of partners, dispute resolution, dissolution and liquidation, and liability for breach of contract. For those who do not establish a partnership enterprise but merely partner up to run a business, the partnership contract provisions of the Civil Code apply. For matters not specified in the contract, the Civil Code provides several default rules. Making decisions on partnership affairs requires unanimous consent of all partners, unless otherwise agreed in the partnership contract. A partner who executes partnership affairs cannot claim remuneration on that account, unless otherwise agreed in the partnership contract. Profits and losses are distributed according to the contract's terms. Where there is no agreement, it shall first be settled through negotiation. If negotiation fails, it is distributed in proportion to actual capital contributions paid in. If proportions cannot be determined, it is divided equally. Partners bear joint and several liability for partnership debts; anyone who repays more than their share may seek reimbursement from the others. Where no partnership term is agreed upon, it is deemed an open-ended partnership, and partners may terminate at any time provided they give reasonable advance notice to the others. Where a partnership enterprise has been established and no partnership term was agreed upon, a partner may withdraw from the partnership simply by giving 30 days' advance notice to the others. The agreement also cannot stipulate that all profits go only to some partners, or that only some partners bear all losses (National).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2006). Partnership Enterprise Law (2006 Revision, Articles 4, 18, 33, 46). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf63dce034d> (National Database of Laws and Regulations); National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 967, 970, 971, 972, 973, 976). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>
entries.notes: The most frequent quarrels are over how to split things between the one who contributes money and the one who contributes labor. If one puts in money without managing affairs, and the other puts in no money but minds the shop every day, under default rules the one minding the shop receives less in distribution and draws no salary. Therefore, the salary or equity share for contributing labor must be explicitly specified. The agreement only governs relations among partners. For external debts, general partners still bear unlimited liability to the end; see Item 3 (Choose the right business entity before opening). For red lines on bringing in more people to invest money, see Item 26 (Pooling money from others to do business). The statutory provisions have been verified against original texts; "writing an agreement reduces quarrels" is empirical knowledge without statistical data, hence rated Grade C. The beneficiaries are you and your partners.

chapters.title: Emergencies: What to Do First
chapters.intro:
This section covers what to do first, what to do next, and what not to do when something happens. Entries on first aid and the outdoors calculate specific causes of death and survival proportions. Entries on threats and scams calculate money and personal freedom. The two types of figures cannot be converted into one another. These entries are intended first and foremost for yourself, your spouse, and your immediate relatives. 79.2% of cardiac arrests occur at home; the people you are most likely to save are family members. Friends and coworkers come next. Helping strangers is not without benefit, but this tier carries the lowest benefit, and you might also be extortionately blamed or dragged into legal cases. Therefore, entries of this type place self-protection actions and exemption clauses right up front.

This section includes only actions that need to be taken within a few minutes. Recognizing scams or extortion over compromising material requires responses measured in days, which are not in this section. For the hard rules against fraud and the seven high-incidence scams, see Section 8, Item 3 (Hard rules against fraud). For extortion involving private photos or recorded video chats, see Section 8, Item 32 (When the other party uses compromising material to demand money). If money has already been transferred out, immediately call 110 or 96110 to request a stop-payment; see Section 8, Item 2 (Stop-payment).

Entries in this section are divided into the following blocks by topic, with item numbers in parentheses.

**CPR and Choking**: Someone collapses without normal breathing (Item 1), do not rush to help an elderly person up after a fall (Item 2), someone choking and unable to speak (Item 26), an infant choking and unable to cry out (Item 43), infant CPR (Item 44).

**Sudden Acute Illnesses**: Sudden facial drooping or weakness on one side (Item 3), dizziness and inability to stand steadily (Item 4), sudden loss of vision in one eye (Item 5), one eye feeling distended and painful (Item 6), crushing chest pain (Item 7), tearing severe pain (Item 8), the worst headache of your life (Item 9), an elderly person becoming sluggish after bumping their head (Item 10), sudden swelling in one leg (Item 11), anaphylactic shock (Item 15), someone convulsing and collapsing (Item 16), a diabetic person suddenly trembling (Item 17).

**Trauma and Burns**: Apply pressure to the wound first for heavy bleeding (Item 12), bitten by a dog or cat (Item 13), rinse with cool water after a burn (Item 14), do not pull out foreign objects embedded in the body (Item 40), do not move if a fracture is suspected (Item 41), severed finger (Item 47), an entire permanent tooth knocked out (Item 48).

**Poisoning, Fire, and Accidents**: Cut power first when someone suffers electric shock (Item 18), carbon monoxide alarm sounding (Item 19), accidental ingestion of cleaners, pesticides, or medications (Item 20), chemical splash onto the body (Item 21), dizziness without sweating in high temperatures (Item 22), giving light salt water to heatstroke victims (Item 23), crawl close to the floor during a fire (Item 24), seeing someone drowning (Item 25), check the building first during an earthquake (Item 30), a child swallowing a button battery or magnetic beads (Item 45), do not leave an intoxicated person to sleep alone (Item 46).

**Outdoors**: Stay in place when lost in uninhabited areas (Item 27), shivering and slurred speech indicate hypothermia (Item 28), do not cut or suck a snakebite (Item 29), encountering bears, wild boars, or feral dogs (Item 31), encountering thunderstorms in the wild (Item 32), ascend slowly onto plateaus (Item 33), bitten by a tick (Item 34), boil outdoor water before drinking (Item 35).

**Conflicts and After Rescuing Others**: Demands for money in desolate wilderness (Item 36), stumbling upon a group fight (Item 37), getting injured or spending money while rescuing others (Item 39).

**Sexual Assault and HIV Exposure**: Possible HIV exposure (Item 38), after experiencing sexual assault (Item 42).

entries.title: When someone collapses, is unresponsive, and not breathing normally, immediately press firmly on the chest, and have bystanders call 120 and locate an AED
entries.cost: Costs nothing. A CPR class by the Red Cross or a hospital takes half a day to a full day, and learning it once is enough to use for years. Even if you have never taken a class, you can do it: place your hands overlapping at the midpoint between the two nipples, press down firmly at a rate of about 2 times per second, and do not stop.
entries.summary: Cardiac arrests often happen at home; when someone provides timely chest compressions, the proportion surviving to hospital discharge is higher. If they are unresponsive and not breathing normally, start compressions; occasional agonal gasps do not count as normal breathing. Overlap your hands and press firmly on the chest, while simultaneously telling bystanders to call 120 and find an AED.
entries.benefit: Combined data from 79 studies covering 142,740 individuals (meta-analysis). Among people whose heart stopped outside a hospital (out-of-hospital cardiac arrest), only 7.6% survived to hospital discharge overall. Bystander CPR is associated with higher survival to hospital discharge. After stratifying by the baseline survival rates of individual studies, people who received bystander CPR had survival rates to discharge ranging from 3.9% to 16.1%. These two numbers come from different strata and cannot be taken as the change before and after compressions. In 53% of cases someone witnessed the onset nearby, but only 32% actually received bystander compressions. China's BASIC-OHCA registered 38,227 emergency-admitted cases. Among them, 30,282 cases (79.2%) of cardiac arrest occurred at home. In this group, the bystander compression rate was 20.3%, and 1.2% survived to discharge. The sequence is to start compressions first, then have a second person make the phone call and retrieve an AED. Once the machine is powered on, follow its voice prompts. Whether to perform compressions depends on whether there is normal breathing. The 2025 International Red Cross first aid guidelines state that in the first few minutes after cardiac arrest, a person may still gasp irregularly and with difficulty, or breathe heavily with noise. This does not count as normal breathing. If you are unsure whether it is normal, assume it is not. Abnormal breathing, including gasping, irregular breathing, and absence of breathing, requires immediate CPR.
entries.sources: Sasson C et al. (2010). Predictors of survival from out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Circulation: Cardiovascular Quality and Outcomes. <https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCOUTCOMES.109.889576> ; Zheng J et al. (2023). Incidence, process of care, and outcomes of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in China: a prospective study of the BASIC-OHCA registry. The Lancet Public Health. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S2468-2667(23)00173-1> ; International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (2025). International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2025, p. 154: "If the person is breathing abnormally (gasping, taking irregular breaths or not breathing), start CPR immediately"; p. 161: "In the first few minutes after cardiac arrest, a person may have agonal breathing (an irregular and laboured breathing pattern, or gasping noisily). This type of breathing is not normal. If there is any doubt about whether breathing is normal, assume it is not". <https://www.ifrc.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/IFRC%20International%20First%20Aid,%20Resuscitation%20and%20Education%20Guidelines%202025.pdf> ; National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 184). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>
entries.notes: For infants under 1 year old, the technique differs and requires rescue breaths; see Item 44 of this section (Infant CPR). Do not pinch the philtrum (Renzhong) first, do not look for family members first, do not record videos first. Also, do not hold back on pressing firmly out of fear of breaking ribs. Article 184 of the Civil Code explicitly stipulates: a person who voluntarily provides emergency rescue assistance shall not bear civil liability if the recipient of the assistance suffers harm.

entries.title: When an elderly person falls or someone collapses, squat down first to call them and call 120, and do not rush to pull them up; walking away in the stranger tier is also legal in China, but if you stop, do not physically lift or move them
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Squatting down to ask a question and making a call takes a few minutes. What is difficult is restraining the impulse to reach out and help them up. For strangers, there is an additional calculation: calling 120 leaves your phone number, which may result in a callback, or you might be questioned once. If you are truly targeted by the family, a lawsuit takes months at a minimum. Moreover, even if the court ultimately rules in your favor, you must pay your own attorney's fees.
entries.summary: This set of practices is primarily used for your own elderly family members and acquaintances. Squat down first to call them and check if there is normal breathing; if they are unresponsive and not breathing normally, follow Item 1 (Press firmly on the chest). Even if they have normal breathing, do not pull or lift them into an embrace; they might have fallen because of a prior stroke or syncope, and forcing them up will worsen it. Ask whether they remember how they fell; if they have back pain or signs resembling a fracture, do not move them under any circumstances, and call 120 on the spot.
entries.benefit: The Ministry of Health's Technical Guidelines for Fall Intervention in the Elderly explicitly state two sentences. One is "Falls are the leading cause of injury-related death among elderly people aged 65 and over in China". The other is "When finding an elderly person who has fallen, do not rush to help them up; handle the situation according to specific conditions". If they are unconscious, call emergency services immediately. If there is vomiting, turn the head to one side and clear the mouth and nose. If breathing and heartbeat have stopped, perform chest compressions immediately. "If movement is necessary, ensure stability and keep them supine as much as possible". If they are conscious, first ask whether they have memory of the fall process; "if they cannot recall it, it may be syncope or a cerebrovascular accident". If there is severe headache, or mouth drooping, slurred speech, or weakness in hands and feet, "immediately helping the elderly person up may worsen cerebral hemorrhage or cerebral ischemia, aggravating the condition". If there are signs of fracture, or back pain, or fecal/urinary incontinence, "if you lack relevant professional knowledge, do not move them casually". In all the above cases, emergency numbers should be called immediately. If the elderly person wants to stand up on their own, you may assist them to stand slowly, "rest in a sitting or lying position and observe, leaving only after confirming there is no harm". As for "fear of being extortionately blamed", the law provides as follows. Article 90 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China contains two sentences. The first sentence is "The parties shall provide evidence to prove the facts upon which their litigation claims are based...". The second sentence is "Before a judgment is rendered, where a party fails to provide evidence or the evidence is insufficient to prove their factual claims, the party bearing the burden of proof shall bear the adverse consequences". The original text of Article 1198 of the Civil Code is: "Where the operator or manager of business premises or public premises such as hotels, shopping malls, banks, stations, airports, stadiums, and entertainment venues, or the organizer of mass activities, fails to fulfill safety assurance obligations and causes harm to others, they shall bear tort liability." Article 184 of the Civil Code: "Where a person causes harm to the recipient of aid due to voluntarily undertaking emergency rescue actions, the rescuer shall not bear civil liability". The Supreme People's Court has published a typical case: A pharmacy operator performed CPR on a person in cardiac arrest and fractured the person's ribs. The recipient of aid was hospitalized for 18 days and demanded over 9,000 yuan in compensation. The court ruled that the rescuer bore no civil liability.
entries.sources: Ministry of Health (2011). Technical Guidelines for Fall Intervention in the Elderly ("Handling After Falls in the Elderly"). Full text PDF via Guangdong Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention <http://cdcp.gd.gov.cn/gcdcdfiles/editor/uploadfile/20111027094832117.pdf>, full text of on-site handling section reprinted by Guinan County People's Government <https://www.guinan.gov.cn/lnb/zc1__zwgk/zc/aztfl/qt/content_27609778> ; National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 183, 184). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml> ; Supreme People's Court (2023). Typical Cases of People's Courts Upholding Fairness and Efficiency and Practicing Socialist Core Values (Case 13, Qi v. Sun health right dispute case, Kangping County People's Court of Liaoning Province). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/408162.html> ; Supreme People's Court (Second Amendment 2022, Effective April 10, 2022). Interpretation on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Article 90). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/353651.html> ; Article 1198 of the Civil Code, full text reprinted by Supreme People's Procuratorate as above; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (Amended 2023, Effective January 1, 2024). Civil Procedure Law (Articles 152, 164). Full text reprinted by Shanghai Municipal Development and Reform Commission <https://fgw.sh.gov.cn/ys-syjf-zc-2.4.1-h5/20240408/073febdb2b04464390546232d4089f51.html> ; State Council (2006). Measures on the Payment of Litigation Costs (State Council Decree No. 481, Articles 6, 29). <https://www.gov.cn/ziliao/flfg/2006-12/29/content_483682.htm> ; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2025). Public Security Administration Punishments Law (2025 Revision, Effective January 1, 2026, Article 26, Item 1; Article 50, Item 5). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml> ; Federal Ministry of Justice of Germany. Strafgesetzbuch (StGB) § 323c Unterlassene Hilfeleistung; Behinderung von hilfeleistenden Personen. <https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/stgb/__323c.html>
entries.notes: Rated B because the guidelines only specify how to manage the situation, without providing figures on "how many fewer deaths occur if followed." Article 184 exempts harm caused during rescue efforts, provided that your actions are voluntary and the situation is an emergency. It does not cover scenarios like "taking it upon oneself to stuff someone into a private car to rush them to the hospital"; waiting for 120 is safer. Do not hang up after calling 120; follow the instructions of the dispatch operator. This set of judgments is primarily meant for one's own elderly relatives and acquaintances. If it is an unfamiliar stranger on the street, walking away is not illegal and is the least troublesome option: Chinese law does not mandate that you must render aid. Things may differ once abroad. In Germany, for example, encountering an accident or dangerous situation where you can help without putting yourself in major danger, yet failing to help, is itself a crime, punishable by up to 1 year in prison or a fine. When abroad, calculate according to local laws. The costs of stopping must be calculated layer by layer: time, leaving phone numbers, being confronted by family members, being sued in court, trouble brought to your workplace, being filmed and uploaded to the internet. For details, see [docs/遇到陌生人出事该不该停.md](../docs/遇到陌生人出事该不该停.md). If you truly decide to stop, the single rule you must follow is **do not move them with your hands**, for reasons that are medical, not legal: forcefully lifting or propping someone up may worsen cerebral hemorrhage or spinal cord injuries. There is one exception: if you operate or manage the premises, or if you organized the event, walking away may incur liability. The security duty imposed by Article 1198 of the Civil Code requires you to assume a portion of safety responsibility for individuals on the premises. For fall prevention itself, see Section 1, Item 13 (practicing balance and leg strength). For delayed symptoms after an elderly person bumps their head, see Item 10 of this section. For financial compensation after being injured while rescuing someone, see Item 39 of this section. For how to preserve evidence and report to the police when experiencing cyberbullying, see Section 8, Item 16.

entries.title: Sudden crooked mouth, weakness in one arm, slurred speech: call 120 immediately; do not wait, do not drive yourself
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Three actions, learned after watching once: have them smile, raise both arms flat, and say a complete sentence.
entries.summary: If a mouth becomes crooked, one arm feels weak, or speech becomes unclear, call 120 immediately. For a stroke, if medications can unblock the blood vessel, the earlier the treatment begins, the greater the chances of recovery. Even if more than 4.5 hours have elapsed or the onset time is unknown, do not give up on emergency care; let doctors examine and make the assessment. Record the time of onset, do not offer water or medication, and do not drive yourself.
entries.benefit: Combining individual patient data from 9 randomized trials of intravenous thrombolysis involving 6,756 patients with acute ischemic stroke (meta-analysis). Ischemic stroke is a stroke caused by a blocked blood vessel, and intravenous thrombolysis involves administering medication to clear the blocked vessel. This study assessed whether there was significant disability (modified Rankin Scale score 0–1) after 3 to 6 months. For thrombolysis with alteplase administered within 3 hours of onset, the odds ratio was 1.75, 95% CI 1.35–2.27 (credible interval). The actual proportions were 32.9% in the treated group versus 23.1% in the control group, a difference of 9.8 percentage points. An odds ratio is not a ratio of probabilities and cannot be interpreted as a 1.75-fold probability of recovery. When delayed to 3 to 4.5 hours, the odds ratio was 1.26 (1.05–1.51). Beyond 4.5 hours, it was 1.15 (0.95–1.40), where this study did not identify a statistically clear difference. This does not mean that treatment cannot be administered after 4.5 hours. The 2026 guidelines from the American Heart Association and American Stroke Association support extending the thrombolytic window for selected patients. Patients with an unknown onset time or onset between 4.5 and 9 hours may still be eligible for thrombolysis after screening with specialized imaging examinations. Whether medication can be administered must be evaluated by a physician; the earlier medical care is sought, the better. The 2017 pre-hospital emergency consensus by the Emergency Medicine Branch of the Chinese Stroke Association requires emergency personnel to transport suspected stroke patients "in the shortest possible time to the nearest certified stroke center, or a hospital capable of performing intravenous thrombolysis and/or endovascular treatment," and to "pre-notify the receiving hospital before the suspected stroke patient arrives." The consensus also specifies that acute stroke patients may suffer respiratory impairment due to factors such as "aspiration."
entries.sources: Emberson J, Lees KR, Lyden P, et al. (2014). Effect of treatment delay, age, and stroke severity on the effects of intravenous thrombolysis with alteplase for acute ischaemic stroke: a meta-analysis of individual patient data from randomised trials. Lancet, 384(9958), 1929-1935. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(14)60584-5>; Emergency Medicine Branch of Chinese Stroke Association (2017). Expert consensus on pre-hospital care of stroke. Chinese Journal of Emergency Medicine, 26(10), 1107-1114. <http://www.cem.org.cn/rhtml/20171002/index.htm>; Prabhakaran S et al. (2026). 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke. Stroke. <https://doi.org/10.1161/STR.0000000000000513>; American Heart Association (2026). Top Things to Know: 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With AIS, Point 3. <https://professional.heart.org/en/science-news/2026-guideline-for-the-early-management-of-patients-with-acute-ischemic-stroke/top-things-to-know>
entries.notes: Thrombolysis is more effective the earlier it is performed, but emergency care should not be abandoned simply because more than 4.5 hours have passed. Calling 120 rather than driving oneself is because, according to the pre-hospital emergency consensus, emergency personnel must transport the individual to a hospital capable of thrombolysis and notify the hospital in advance to prepare. Record the exact time symptoms began, as doctors need it to evaluate treatment eligibility. Do not administer water or medication, which the author deduced from the "aspiration" noted in the consensus: stroke patients may choke. Do not wait to "rest a bit and see."

entries.title: Sudden vertigo and unsteadiness, double vision, vision blacking out in one eye, or inability to touch your nose with your finger: also call 120 as a stroke
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Add two more actions beyond the three actions of "facial asymmetry, arm raise, speech" (Item 3, sudden crooked mouth, slurred speech). One is to have the person stand upright and close their eyes to see if they sway, then ask if they have double vision or missing areas in their field of view. The other is, when suspecting it yourself, extend your finger to touch your nose, and do it again with eyes closed.
entries.summary: Checking only the three criteria of "facial asymmetry, arm raise, speech" misses more than 10% of strokes, because some strokes initially present without a crooked mouth or paralyzed hand. Factoring in unsteadiness, double vision, or visual field deficits reduces missed cases to 4.4%. Sudden severe dizziness and inability to stand, seeing double, or failing to touch your nose with a finger warrants calling 120 just the same, and recording the time just the same.
entries.benefit: In 2014, the University of Kentucky Stroke Center reviewed medical records of 736 cases of acute ischemic stroke (strokes caused by blocked blood vessels). Among them, 14.1% of patients entirely lacked the three symptoms of facial asymmetry, arm weakness, and slurred speech (FAST) at onset. Incorporating "gait unsteadiness, leg weakness, visual symptoms" into the screening reduced the missed proportion from 14.1% to 4.4%. An examination of 465 emergency records of ischemic stroke across two American hospitals showed that 22% were initially missed. When vessels supplying the posterior part of the brain were blocked (posterior circulation stroke), 37% were initially missed, compared to only 16% for anterior circulation. The odds of being missed were approximately 1.99 times higher for individuals with dizziness than those without (odds ratio 1.99), and 4.02 times higher for those with nausea and vomiting. Stroke warning signs listed in the International Red Cross 2025 first aid guidelines also include "sudden trouble in seeing with one or both eyes" and "sudden trouble walking or experiencing dizziness, loss of balance or coordination."
entries.sources: Aroor S, Singh R, Goldstein LB (2017). BE-FAST (Balance, Eyes, Face, Arm, Speech, Time): Reducing the Proportion of Strokes Missed Using the FAST Mnemonic. Stroke, 48(2), 479-481. <https://doi.org/10.1161/STROKEAHA.116.015169>; Arch AE, Weisman DC, Coca S, et al. (2016). Missed Ischemic Stroke Diagnosis in the Emergency Department by Emergency Medicine and Neurology Services. Stroke, 47(3), 668-673: "Thirty-seven percent of posterior strokes were initially misdiagnosed compared with 16% of anterior strokes". <https://doi.org/10.1161/strokeaha.115.010613>; International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (2025). International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2025, pp. 366–367: "Sudden trouble in seeing with one or both eyes" "Sudden trouble walking or experiencing dizziness, loss of balance or coordination". <https://www.ifrc.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/IFRC%20International%20First%20Aid,%20Resuscitation%20and%20Education%20Guidelines%202025.pdf>
entries.notes: Blockage of blood vessels in the posterior brain (posterior circulation stroke) often causes neither a crooked mouth nor a paralyzed hand, presenting merely with dizziness, unsteady gait, and double vision, making it the most easily missed. Imprecise finger-to-nose testing and inability to stand steadily with eyes closed fall under what the Red Cross guidelines describe as "loss of balance or coordination." However, no single action can conversely rule out a stroke: if symptoms appear suddenly and do not resolve, call 120 and record the precise onset time. The Kentucky study only reviewed medical records from a single hospital, and the authors explicitly stated that further validation is needed.

entries.title: One eye suddenly going dark like a curtain being pulled down, even if resolving on its own in a few minutes: go to the emergency department that same day as a stroke
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Emergency evaluation and vascular examinations take up half a day to a full day.
entries.summary: One eye suddenly going dark like a pulled-down shade may indicate a blocked blood vessel in the ocular fundus; the longer the blockage lasts, the less retina can be salvaged. It is also a form of cerebral ischemia; even if it resolves on its own within a few minutes, you must still go. Switching minor strokes and transient cerebral ischemia to same-day evaluation and same-day treatment reduced recurrent strokes within 90 days from 10.3% to 2.1%. Go to an emergency department with a stroke center on the same day; do not wait until the next day.
entries.benefit: A 2021 American Heart Association scientific statement regarding central retinal artery occlusion (blockage of the primary blood vessel in the ocular fundus) explicitly stated: "acute central retinal artery occlusion is an emergency." Healthcare systems should identify and triage it as an emergency. The longer the duration of ischemia, the less retina can be salvaged. The Oxford EXPRESS study looked at two categories of patients: minor stroke, and cerebral ischemia with spontaneously resolving symptoms (medically termed transient ischemic attack). This cohort was subsequently switched to same-day assessment and same-day initiation of treatment. Following the change, the proportion of recurrent strokes within 90 days dropped from 10.3% (32/310) to 2.1% (6/281). The abstract of this scientific statement also noted that central retinal artery occlusion is a form of acute ischemic stroke and a harbinger of subsequent cerebrovascular and cardiovascular events. The UK National Health Service (NHS) lists "blurred vision or loss of sight in 1 or both eyes" as a stroke symptom, specifying that even if symptoms stop on their own after a short while, immediate medical attention is still required. Anyone who experienced stroke symptoms in the past 24 hours that have since resolved must likewise call emergency services.
entries.sources: Mac Grory B, Schrag M, Biousse V, et al. (2021). Management of Central Retinal Artery Occlusion: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association. Stroke, 52(6), e282-e294：「Central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO) is a form of acute ischemic stroke that causes severe visual loss and is a harbinger of further cerebrovascular and cardiovascular events」. <https://doi.org/10.1161/STR.0000000000000366> ；NHS. Symptoms of a stroke：「blurred vision or loss of sight in 1 or both eyes」「Symptoms of a stroke can sometimes stop after a short time, so you may think you're OK. Even if this happens, get medical help straight away」「you've had signs of a stroke within the last 24 hours even if they've now stopped」. <https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/stroke/symptoms/> ; Rothwell PM, Giles MF, Chandratheva A, et al. (2007). Effect of urgent treatment of transient ischaemic attack and minor stroke on early recurrent stroke (EXPRESS study): a prospective population-based sequential comparison. Lancet, 370(9596), 1432-1442. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(07)61448-2>
entries.notes: Rated B because EXPRESS was not a randomized controlled trial. It compared two time periods—before and after the change in practice—within the same population, and other conditions may have also changed between the two periods, making this component inseparable. Vision going black for a few minutes and then recovering on its own is easily brushed aside as "fatigue" or "low blood sugar." The NHS explicitly states that immediate medical attention is required even if symptoms resolve on their own; in the EXPRESS cohort without same-day treatment, 10.3% experienced another stroke within 90 days. Sudden vision loss in one eye, even if painless and without redness, must be taken seriously. Do not wait to register for an outpatient ophthalmology appointment the next day; go directly to an emergency department at a hospital with a stroke center.

entries.title: One eye feeling distended, painful, red, seeing rainbow halos around lights, accompanied by headache, nausea, and vomiting: visit an ophthalmic emergency department the same day
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Measuring intraocular pressure and examining the anterior chamber at an ophthalmic emergency department takes up half a day.
entries.summary: This may be an acute attack of glaucoma, where fluid in the eye fails to drain, intraocular pressure spikes, and damages the optic nerve connecting to the brain. The longer it is delayed, the greater the likelihood of permanent blindness. During the lockdown in Wuhan, patients waited an average of 241 hours before receiving treatment, with 21.87% suffering blindness. During the same period the following year without lockdown, the average delay was 121 hours, and blindness accounted for 7.84%.
entries.benefit: An ophthalmic hospital in Wuhan compared acute primary angle-closure glaucoma patients across two time periods. During the 76 days of the 2020 lockdown, there were 54 individuals (64 eyes), and during the same period in 2021, there were 46 individuals (51 eyes), with both groups sharing similar demographic characteristics. From the onset of symptoms to receiving treatment, the duration was 241.84 ± 211.95 hours in the lockdown group versus 121.53 ± 96.12 hours in the control group (P=0.001). Intraocular pressure upon presentation was 52.63 ± 12.45 mmHg versus 45.16 ± 9.79 mmHg (P=0.001). The proportion of blindness was 21.87% versus 7.84%. Detection of glaucomatous optic neuropathy occurred in 20/64 eyes (31.25%) versus 7/51 eyes (13.73%) (P=0.03). A hospital in South Korea reviewed 50 eyes that experienced a single attack and subsequently underwent lensectomy. One year later, 25 eyes (50%) were left with varying degrees of visual field defect. A longer interval from symptom onset to intraocular pressure reduction correlated with a higher likelihood of permanent deficits (P=0.005). Another prospective study had 43 individuals with shallow anterior chambers lie prone in a dark room for 1 hour. Intraocular pressure in both eyes rose significantly (P<0.01). The median increase was 3.60 mmHg in the dominant eye and 2.70 mmHg in the fellow eye (P<0.05). The NHS explicitly notes that glaucoma can sometimes develop suddenly, with symptoms including intense eye pain, redness, rainbow-colored rings around bright lights, blurred vision, nausea and vomiting, and headache; call emergency services or go to an emergency department if they arise suddenly. It typically occurs when fluid cannot drain from the eye, elevating eye pressure and damaging the optic nerve connecting the eye to the brain. Those at higher risk include people over age 50, those with parents or siblings with glaucoma, people of Asian descent, and individuals with myopia, hyperopia, or diabetes. Zhongshan Ophthalmic Center treated 243 angle-closure glaucoma patients aged 40 and younger between 2012 and 2019.
entries.sources: Zhou L, Wu S, Wang Y, Bao X, Peng T, Luo W, Ortega-Usobiaga J (2022). Clinical presentation of acute primary angle closure during the COVID-19 epidemic lockdown. Frontiers in Medicine, 9, 1078237. <https://doi.org/10.3389/fmed.2022.1078237> ; Sung MS, Kim HJ, Park SW (2023). Predictors of long-term visual field outcome after an episode of acute primary angle closure. Clinical & Experimental Ophthalmology, 51(4), 291-299. <https://doi.org/10.1111/ceo.14206> ; Wang J, Wang J, Ng TK, Huang C (2025). Asymmetric intraocular pressure changes in dominant and contralateral eyes: the dark room prone provocative test. Seminars in Ophthalmology, 40(4), 325-331. <https://doi.org/10.1080/08820538.2024.2443972> ; NHS. Glaucoma: "Sometimes glaucoma can develop suddenly and cause symptoms such as: intense eye pain, a red eye, tenderness around the eyes, seeing rainbow-coloured circles around bright lights, blurred vision, feeling sick (nausea) and being sick, a headache" "This happens when the fluid in your eye cannot drain as it should". <https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/glaucoma/> ; Lin SF, Xiao H, Chen LM, et al. (2022). [Clinical features of young inpatients with angle-closure glaucoma]. Chinese Journal of Ophthalmology, 58(1), 28-34. <https://doi.org/10.3760/cma.j.cn112142-20210301-00104>
entries.notes: There are two reasons for assigning a grade B. First, the two cohorts in Wuhan were compared by reviewing old medical records, and the lockdown itself brought about other differences that cannot be separated from the factor of "delay." Second, the South Korean cohort included only 50 eyes and was also retrospective. The trigger discussed does not refer to looking at screens. In that prospective study, individuals with shallow anterior chambers had an increase in intraocular pressure after lying prone in a dark room for 1 hour. For high-risk groups, refer to the items listed by the NHS: age over 50, a family history of the condition, and hyperopia (farsightedness). Young people can also get it; among that group of patients under 40 years old at Zhongshan Ophthalmic Center, more than 60% were caused by other eye diseases (secondary). During an attack, headache, nausea, and vomiting can occur; do not treat it merely as gastroenteritis or migraine—first check whether the eyes are red or painful, and whether rainbow halos appear around lights. Losing vision in a single eye without pain or redness is another matter; see item 5 (sudden blackout in one eye). For whether blue-light-blocking glasses are useful, see Section 6, Item 16 (blue-light-blocking glasses).

entries.title: If chest pain with pressure, tightness, or a squeezing sensation lasts for more than 15 minutes without relief, or if the pain is accompanied by cold sweats, nausea, or shortness of breath, call 120; do not tough it out on your own and do not drive yourself
entries.cost: Costs nothing.
entries.summary: If chest pain feels like pressure, tightness, or squeezing, and does not ease after more than 15 minutes, call 120. If the pain is severe, accompanied by cold sweats, or causes shortness of breath, you should call after just a few minutes of pain. Among those whose blood vessels were opened with a balloon within 55 minutes of hospital arrival, 30-day mortality was 2.8%. For those exceeding 55 minutes, it was 9.7%. Do not drive yourself to the hospital.
entries.benefit: A nationwide survey on acute coronary syndromes was conducted in Israel. The analyzed subjects were patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, a type of heart attack. The interval measured was from hospital arrival to opening the occluded blood vessel with a balloon (balloon angioplasty). When the interval was ≤55 minutes, 30-day mortality was 5/178 (2.8%). When the interval was >55 minutes, 30-day mortality was 15/155 (9.7%). The chest pain guidelines from the UK National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) list symptoms suggestive of acute coronary syndrome: pain in the chest, arms, back, or jaw lasting longer than 15 minutes; chest pain accompanied by nausea and vomiting, marked sweating, or breathlessness. The International Red Cross 2025 first aid guidelines state that if pain is severe, accompanied by shortness of breath, or if the face looks pale, ashen, and clammy, call emergency services immediately, "even if the pain has only lasted a couple of minutes." Heart attack pain can also radiate to the jaw, upper abdomen, and between the two shoulder blades. Symptoms in women, older adults, and people with diabetes may be less obvious.
entries.sources: Karkabi B, Meir G, Zafrir B, et al. (2021). Door-to-balloon time and mortality in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction. European Heart Journal - Quality of Care and Clinical Outcomes. <https://doi.org/10.1093/ehjqcco/qcaa037>; NICE (2010, updated 2016). Recent-onset chest pain of suspected cardiac origin: assessment and diagnosis (CG95), item 1.2.1.3: "pain in the chest and/or other areas (for example, the arms, back or jaw) lasting longer than 15 minutes" "chest pain associated with nausea and vomiting, marked sweating, breathlessness, or particularly a combination of these". <https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg95/chapter/Recommendations>; International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (2025). International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2025, pp. 357–358: "Access EMS even if the pain has only lasted a couple of minutes" "Symptoms may be more subtle or uncommon in some populations, such as people who are female, elderly or have diabetes". <https://www.ifrc.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/IFRC%20International%20First%20Aid,%20Resuscitation%20and%20Education%20Guidelines%202025.pdf>; NHS. Heart attack: "Do not drive yourself to A&E". <https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/heart-attack/symptoms/>
entries.notes: The Israeli study compared the delay that occurred after arriving at the hospital, not the interval from symptom onset to hospital arrival. But the principle is the same: the sooner the blood vessel is opened, the better. The pain may be felt in the upper abdomen, back, or jaw. Symptoms in women, the elderly, and diabetics may be less pronounced, presenting only as breathlessness or discomfort. The 15-minute threshold is what NICE provides for clinicians to differentiate cases; it is not meant for you to just sit and wait: if the pain is intense, accompanied by cold sweats, or causes shortness of breath, call within minutes. The NHS explicitly notes not to drive yourself to the emergency department.

entries.title: If there is sudden, tearing-like severe pain that travels all the way from the chest toward the back and down to the lower back, call 120 and clearly state that it feels "like tearing"
entries.cost: Costs nothing.
entries.summary: If severe tearing pain travels from the chest toward the back and down to the lower back, call 120 and state directly: "It feels like it is tearing, and the pain is moving downward." For type A dissection treated with medications alone without surgery, the in-hospital mortality rate is 58%. Its management is different from that of a heart attack; doctors will only test for it if they think of it first. If there is a large difference in blood pressure between both arms or if a pulse cannot be felt on one side, report that as well.
entries.benefit: The International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection (IRAD) enrolled 464 cases across 12 centers. Aortic dissection is the disease characterized by severe, tearing-like chest and back pain. Among the first symptoms reported by patients, the most common was the sudden onset of severe, sharp pain. However, manifestations vary widely, and typical signs like an absent pulse on one side appeared in only 15.1% of patients. Total in-hospital mortality was 27.4%. For type A dissection without surgery and treated with medication alone, mortality was 58%. The 2022 aortic disease guideline from the American Heart Association and the American College of Cardiology uses a scoring table to determine the probability of dissection. High-risk conditions include connective tissue disorders like Marfan syndrome, a family history of aortic disease, and known thoracic aortic aneurysms. High-risk pain characteristics include chest, back, or abdominal pain that is sudden in onset, excruciatingly severe, and ripping or tearing in quality. High-risk examination signs include an absent pulse on one side or a marked difference in systolic blood pressure between both arms. The guideline also specifies that uncontrolled hypertension is a known risk factor for aortic rupture and dissection.
entries.sources: Hagan PG, Nienaber CA, Isselbacher EM, et al. (2000). The International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection (IRAD): new insights into an old disease. JAMA, 283(7), 897-903. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.283.7.897>; Isselbacher EM, Preventza O, Hamilton Black J, et al. (2022). 2022 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Aortic Disease. Circulation, 146(24), e334-e482, Table 24 (ADD-RS): "Marfan syndrome or other connective tissue disease" "Family history of aortic disease" "Ripping or tearing in quality" "Pulse deficit or systolic blood pressure differential"; "Uncontrolled hypertension is a known risk factor for aortic rupture and dissection". <https://doi.org/10.1161/CIR.0000000000001106>
entries.notes: Upon arriving at the hospital, proactively state: "It feels tearing, and the pain is moving downward," so that doctors will suspect dissection and order a contrast-enhanced CT scan. For myocardial infarction, medications that prevent clotting—such as anticoagulants and thrombolytics—are commonly used. The author infers that using these drugs for a dissection could worsen bleeding, so doctors need to rule out dissection first. A substantial blood pressure discrepancy between both arms or an unpalpable pulse on one side serves as a clue. Those with poorly controlled blood pressure, Marfan syndrome, or a family history of aortic disease are at high risk. Likewise, do not drive yourself, and do not endure it until the next day.

entries.title: If a sudden "worst headache of your life" peaks within an hour, go to the emergency room immediately for a head CT scan
entries.cost: Visiting the emergency room itself does not cost much. Having a head CT scan in the emergency room costs several hundred yuan.
entries.summary: What matters is how fast it reaches peak intensity; of severe headaches that peak within an hour, about 6% are due to a ruptured blood vessel on the brain's surface. If you meet even one criterion—age 40 or older, neck pain or stiffness, or someone witnessed you pass out—go to the emergency room for a head CT. Onset during exertion, an instantaneous thunderclap onset, or an inability to bend the neck forward also count. Most people who get checked turn out to be fine, but if it is missed, rebleeding can occur.
entries.benefit: Ten emergency departments in Canada conducted a prospective cohort study of 2,131 cases of "severe headache peaking within one hour," with predefined criteria and follow-up tracking. Among them, 132 cases (6.2%) were subarachnoid hemorrhage (a ruptured blood vessel on the surface of the brain). The Ottawa SAH Rule has six criteria: age 40 and older, neck pain or stiffness, and witnessed loss of consciousness. The other three criteria are onset during exertion, a thunderclap headache (peaking instantly), and limited neck flexion on physical examination. Meeting any single criterion warrants evaluation. This rule identified all individuals with hemorrhage, with a sensitivity of 100%, 95% CI 97.2%–100.0% (credible interval). The trade-off is that among those without hemorrhage, only 15.3% were ruled out by it (specificity 15.3%).
entries.sources: Perry JJ, Stiell IG, Sivilotti MLA, et al. (2013). Clinical decision rules to rule out subarachnoid hemorrhage for acute headache. JAMA, 310(12), 1248-1255. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2013.278018>
entries.notes: What matters is not "how severe the pain is," but "how fast it reaches peak pain"; a headache that explodes within seconds to a minute is the true red flag, whereas a gradually worsening migraine is not. If accompanied by vomiting, neck stiffness, photophobia, or transient syncope, take it even more seriously. A specificity of only 15.3% means that the vast majority of people evaluated under this rule end up having nothing wrong. However, if missed, another hemorrhage could occur, making the scan well worth doing. Do not just take a painkiller to suppress it and go back to sleep.

entries.title: If an older adult develops an unsteady gait, sluggishness, lethargy, or weakness on one side 2–3 weeks to several months after bumping their head, get a head CT scan
entries.cost: A head CT scan costs 200–300 yuan.
entries.summary: After an older adult bumps their head, blood usually does not accumulate until the third week. The impact is often just a minor bump, and more than half of patients cannot recall having sustained an injury. After surgery for this condition, the recurrence rate can reach up to 33%, and the case fatality rate can reach up to 32%. If an elderly person suddenly becomes confused, walks unsteadily, feels constantly sleepy, or has weakness in one hand, trace back to ask whether they bumped their head in the past two to three months before taking them for a CT scan.
entries.benefit: The Chinese Neurosurgical Society of the Chinese Medical Association and other bodies published the "Chinese Expert Consensus on the Medical Treatment of Chronic Subdural Hematoma." Chronic subdural hematoma is a pool of blood that slowly accumulates between the brain meninges. In professional terms, it is a chronic space-occupying lesion formed by the accumulation of blood between the arachnoid mater and the dura mater. It "usually forms in the third week after head trauma" and is more common in elderly people. After surgical intervention, recurrence rates can reach up to 33%, and the case fatality rate can reach up to 32%. Among patients aged 90 and older, only 24% achieve a good overall recovery. Systematic review: globally, there are 3.39 to 39.1 new cases per 100,000 people annually, increasing with age, and it can triple in those aged 80 and older. The most common causes are trauma and falls, followed by chronic alcoholism, the use of medications that prevent blood from clotting (anticoagulants), and violent injury. Geriatric medicine review: clinical manifestations "typically include confusion, cognitive decline, gait disturbance, or somnolence, which may resemble other geriatric syndromes." This review also stated that the rising incidence is related to more people taking anticoagulants and antiplatelet drugs (such as aspirin and clopidogrel), and older adults being more prone to falls. Another literature review specified that there is a time lag between the injury and the onset of symptoms, and the trauma sustained is usually very mild, so it is often overlooked. More than 50% of patients deny having suffered an injury.
entries.sources: Zhang J et al. (2021). Expert consensus on drug treatment of chronic subdural hematoma. Chinese Neurosurgical Journal, 7(1), 47. <https://doi.org/10.1186/s41016-021-00263-z> ; Dziho A et al. (2025). Global prevalence and incidence of chronic subdural hematoma: A systematic review. Brain and Spine, 5, 105893. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bas.2025.105893> ; Mathon B, Shotar E (2026). Diagnostic and therapeutic management of chronic subdural hematoma in elderly patients. Gériatrie et Psychologie Neuropsychiatrie du Vieillissement, 24(1), 30-41. <https://doi.org/10.1684/pnv.2026.1274> ; Iliescu IA, Constantinescu AI (2015). Clinical evolutional aspects of chronic subdural haematomas - literature review. Journal of Medicine and Life, 8(Spec Issue), 26-33: "the brain injury, usually minor" "patients deny the existence of a trauma in over 50% of the cases". <https://europepmc.org/article/MED/26361507>
entries.notes: The impact is often just a minor bump, and more than half of older adults cannot recall having been injured. Therefore, if the family notices that "recently they've suddenly become confused, unsteady while walking, constantly sleepy, or weak in one hand," look back first to ask whether they have fallen or bumped their head in the past two or three months before going for a CT scan. Its presentation resembles other geriatric conditions; do not directly attribute it to "dementia" or "sequelae from the last stroke." Older adults taking aspirin, clopidogrel, warfarin, or direct oral anticoagulants face higher risks, as do those with chronic heavy alcohol consumption. For fall prevention, see Section 1, Item 13 (practicing balance and leg strength). If memory worsens year by year and was not caused by a head bump, see Section 17, Item 13 (memory clinics).

entries.title: If one leg suddenly swells, feels tight, or hurts to the touch, seek medical care as soon as possible; if accompanied by sudden shortness of breath or chest pain, call 120 immediately
entries.cost: A leg vascular ultrasound (lower extremity venous ultrasound) costs one to two hundred yuan.
entries.summary: If one leg suddenly swells, becomes visibly thicker than the other, and hurts to the touch, get a lower extremity venous ultrasound as soon as possible. If accompanied by sudden shortness of breath or chest pain, call 120 directly; among people diagnosed with pulmonary embolism, 17.4% die within 3 months. Traveling by car or plane for more than 4 hours approximately doubles the risk; get up and walk around at regular intervals. Those with high-risk factors for thrombosis should ask a doctor before departure whether to wear compression stockings.
entries.benefit: The International Cooperative Pulmonary Embolism Registry (ICOPER) enrolled 2,454 patients with confirmed acute pulmonary embolism across 52 hospitals in 7 countries. Pulmonary embolism occurs when blood clots block the pulmonary arteries. The all-cause mortality rate within 3 months in this cohort was 17.4% (426/2,454). The World Health Organization's WRIGHT Project: continuous travel of more than 4 hours "approximately doubles" the risk of blood clots forming in veins and traveling to the lungs (venous thromboembolism). However, the probability apportioned to an individual remains very low; prolonged sitting without movement for over 4 hours is "approximately 1 in 6,000." The UK National Health Service (NHS) recommends wearing loose clothing, drinking plenty of water, avoiding alcohol, and getting up to walk whenever possible during flights, train rides, or car trips of over 4 hours. A 2021 Cochrane review pooled 12 randomized controlled trials where passengers took flights lasting over 5 hours. Among those wearing graduated compression stockings, asymptomatic deep vein thrombosis detected only through screening was reduced by about 90%: OR 0.10, 95% CI 0.04 to 0.25 (confidence interval). Out of 2,637 people, 50 cases were detected: 3 among stocking wearers and 47 among non-wearers. None of these trials recorded any deaths, cases of pulmonary embolism, or symptomatic blood clots. Therefore, whether compression stockings can prevent these truly adverse outcomes cannot yet be calculated.
entries.sources: Goldhaber SZ, Visani L, De Rosa M (1999). Acute pulmonary embolism: clinical outcomes in the International Cooperative Pulmonary Embolism Registry (ICOPER). Lancet, 353(9162), 1386-1389. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(98)07534-5> ; WHO (2007). Study results released on travel and blood clots. <https://www.who.int/news/item/29-06-2007-study-results-released-on-travel-and-blood-clots> ; NHS. DVT (deep vein thrombosis)：「If you're travelling for 4 hours or more by plane, train or car」「wearing loose clothing」「drinking plenty of water」「avoiding alcohol」「walking around when possible」. <https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/deep-vein-thrombosis-dvt/> ; Clarke MJ, Broderick C, Hopewell S, Juszczak E, Eisinga A (2021). Compression stockings for preventing deep vein thrombosis in airline passengers. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 4, CD004002. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD004002.pub4>
entries.notes: When both legs swell together, it is mostly a problem of heart, liver, kidney, or venous function. One leg suddenly swelling and becoming visibly thicker than the other is the typical presentation of deep vein thrombosis. High-risk situations include long-distance car or plane travel, bed rest after surgery or fractures, plaster casts, the peri-pregnancy and postpartum period, malignancies, and taking oral contraceptives. When a blood clot detaches and blocks the pulmonary artery, it becomes a pulmonary embolism: sudden shortness of breath, chest pain worsening with deep inhalation, rapid heart rate, lightheadedness, and coughing up blood (hemoptysis). At this stage, call 120 directly. 17.4% is the mortality rate among diagnosed pulmonary embolism cases, not "swelling in the leg carries such a high risk"; do not frighten yourself with this figure. That WHO study did not evaluate methods of prevention. It only mentioned flexing the ankles up and down and exercising the calves while seated, avoiding tight clothing en route, and consulting a doctor before departure if you have concerns. The compression stocking trials did include high-risk passengers, but they only screened for asymptomatic small clots; therefore, those with high-risk factors should ask a doctor first before deciding whether to wear them.

entries.title: For massive hemorrhage, first press firmly on the wound with your hands; apply a tourniquet if direct pressure on a limb fails, and call 120 at the same time
entries.cost: A windlass tourniquet costs tens to over one hundred yuan; keep one in the car and in your first aid kit. Learning once to "fasten it above the wound, twist until bleeding stops, and record the time" takes a few minutes.
entries.summary: First press down firmly with your hands or clothing; if limb bleeding cannot be stopped by pressure, apply a tourniquet, then call 120, and do not loosen it once applied. Among battlefield casualties, 90% of those who had a tourniquet applied before shock survived, compared to only 10% of those who received one after shock set in; all 5 individuals who needed a tourniquet but did not receive one died. Fasten it above the wound, twist until bleeding stops, and note the time; do not substitute with shoelaces or ropes. For the neck and torso, only direct pressure can be used; never apply a tourniquet.
entries.benefit: Eleven Level 1 trauma centers in Texas, USA, admitted 1,026 cases of peripheral vascular injury over 6 years. Among them, 181 cases (17.6%) had a tourniquet applied before arrival at the hospital. Calculated directly without any adjustments, mortality was 3.9% in the tourniquet group and 5.2% in the non-tourniquet group. After evening out other factors (multivariate adjustment), tourniquet application remained independently associated with survival. The adjusted OR was 5.86, with a confidence interval of 95% CI 1.41 to 24.47. Among 232 casualties at a Baghdad combat support hospital: 90% of those who had a tourniquet applied before shock set in survived, compared to only 10% when applied after shock occurred. All 5 individuals who needed a tourniquet but did not receive one died, whereas 87% of those who received one survived. The sequence is: direct pressure using clothing or towels → apply a tourniquet for limb bleeding that cannot be controlled by pressure → call 120 → do not loosen.
entries.sources: Teixeira PGR et al. (2018). Civilian Prehospital Tourniquet Use Is Associated with Improved Survival in Patients with Peripheral Vascular Injury. Journal of the American College of Surgeons. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jamcollsurg.2018.01.047> ; Kragh JF et al. (2009). Survival with emergency tourniquet use to stop bleeding in major limb trauma. Annals of Surgery. <https://doi.org/10.1097/SLA.0b013e31818842ba> ; Emergency Physicians Branch of the Chinese Medical Doctor Association et al. (2020). Expert consensus on the emergency application of tourniquets. Chinese Journal of Emergency Medicine 29(6):773-779: "During prehospital first aid, once a tourniquet is applied, loosening it is not recommended unless alternative definitive hemostatic care is available" "The maximum duration of use should not exceed 2 h. However, if objective conditions prevent hospital care or no alternative hemostatic method is available, the tourniquet should not be released before formal rescue is obtained". <https://doi.org/10.3760/cma.j.issn.1671-0282.2020.06.006>, full text <http://www.cem.org.cn/rhtml/20200606/index.htm>
entries.notes: Do not use thin items such as ropes or shoelaces as tourniquets; they cannot compress the artery and will cut the skin. Once a tourniquet is applied, do not periodically loosen it to "bleed it out." Hemorrhage on the neck and torso can only be pressed, never wrapped with a tourniquet. In those battlefield data, the tourniquet itself did not lead to any amputations, and transient nerve palsy occurred in 4 cases. The expert consensus of Chinese emergency physicians is consistent: once applied in the prehospital setting, loosening is not recommended unless other methods can achieve definitive hemostasis. For upper arm bleeding, fasten on the middle-to-upper third of the upper arm; for thigh bleeding, fasten at the groin/base of the thigh. Do not apply over the forearm, lower leg, elbow, or knee. The consensus recommends striving not to exceed 2 hours in total before and after arriving at the hospital; however, if reaching a hospital is impossible and no other hemostatic methods exist, do not untie it before formal rescue arrives. Makeshift tourniquets made from belts, neckties, or sleeves are difficult to stop bleeding on their own and require a stick to twist tight.

entries.title: If bitten or scratched with broken skin by a dog or cat, first rinse alternately with soapy water and running water for 15 minutes, and get vaccinated on the same day
entries.cost: Rinsing costs nothing. A full course of rabies vaccine costs several hundred yuan. Category III exposures also require rabies passive immunization agents (direct injection of ready-made antibodies), costing several hundred to over a thousand yuan. The most costly thing is delay.
entries.summary: Once rabies develops, the case fatality rate is nearly 100%, so neither rinsing nor vaccination after a bite can be skipped. First rinse thoroughly, alternating with soapy water and clean running water for 15 minutes, and go for vaccination on the same day. Puncture bites or having broken skin licked count as Category III exposure, which requires adding passive immunization agents. Being "domesticated or vaccinated" does not change the management; the level is determined by the wound, not by the dog's origin.
entries.benefit: Original text from the 2023 specifications by the National Disease Control and Prevention Administration and the National Health Commission: "The case fatality rate of rabies is nearly 100%." The management is "thoroughly rinse all bite and scratch sites alternately with soapy water (or other weakly alkaline cleansers) and running clean water under a certain pressure for approximately 15 minutes." Minor nibbling of uncovered skin or scratches without bleeding constitutes Category II exposure and requires vaccination. Transdermal bites or broken skin licked constitute Category III exposure: "the wound should be managed, and rabies passive immunization agents should be administered alongside rabies vaccination." WHO: Globally, approximately 59,000 people die from rabies each year, with 99% transmitted by dogs.
entries.sources: General Office of the National Disease Control and Prevention Administration, General Office of the National Health Commission (2023). Notice on the Issuance of the Operational Specifications for Rabies Post-Exposure Prophylaxis and Management (2023 Edition). <https://www.ndcpa.gov.cn/jbkzzx/c100014/common/content/content_1706569159854649344.html> ; WHO. Rabies Fact Sheet. <https://www.who.int/zh/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/rabies>
entries.notes: Do not skip treatment just because the animal is "domesticated or vaccinated." The specifications evaluate the severity of the wound (exposure category), not the dog's origin. Do not bandage the wound yourself. The 10-day observation period can only determine whether to discontinue vaccination, not whether to initiate it. Bites from wild animals or bats are managed in the same manner. For dog owners, vaccinate your dog against rabies on schedule and leash it when going outdoors; see Section 8, Item 30 (dogs must be leashed).

entries.title: Immediately rinse a burn with cool running water for 20 minutes; do not apply toothpaste or soy sauce
entries.cost: Free of charge. Takes 20 minutes.
entries.summary: Children who received cool running water for a full 20 minutes within 3 hours of injury had a lower likelihood of subsequently requiring skin grafting. It must be cool water, not ice water; applying ice exacerbates tissue damage. If clothing adheres to the wound, do not pull it off forcefully; cover with a clean cloth after rinsing and go to the hospital. Do not apply toothpaste, soy sauce, sesame oil, or flour. If you only remember after some time has passed, supplementary rinsing within three hours is still beneficial.
entries.benefit: An Australian study followed 2,495 children with thermal burns. For children who rinsed with cool running water for 20 minutes within 3 hours after injury, the odds ratio for subsequent skin grafting was 0.6, 95% CI 0.4–0.8 (confidence interval). This indicates a lower likelihood of skin grafting, but cannot be directly translated into saying the probability of grafting is only 60%. Pooled results from 7 studies likewise found that "20 minutes of cool running water within three hours of injury significantly reduced the likelihood of requiring skin grafting and operative wound management." The International Red Cross 2025 First Aid Guidelines clearly state not to rinse with ice-cold water or apply ice, as this may aggravate the injury. The NHS clearly states that clothing and jewelry near the burn should be removed, but anything stuck to the wound should not be disturbed, nor should any creams, oils, or butter be applied to burns.
entries.sources: Griffin BR, Frear CC, Babl F, Oakley E, Kimble RM (2020). Cool Running Water First Aid Decreases Skin Grafting Requirements in Pediatric Burns: A Cohort Study of Two Thousand Four Hundred Ninety-five Children. Annals of Emergency Medicine, 75(1), 75-85. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.annemergmed.2019.06.028> ; Griffin B, Cabilan CJ, Ayoub B, et al. (2022). The effect of 20 minutes of cool running water first aid within three hours of thermal burn injury on patient outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Australasian Emergency Care, 25(4), 367-376. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.auec.2022.05.004> ; International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (2025). International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2025, page 289: "Do not use ice-cold water" "Do not apply ice, as this may aggravate the injury". <https://www.ifrc.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/IFRC%20International%20First%20Aid,%20Resuscitation%20and%20Education%20Guidelines%202025.pdf> ; NHS. Burns and scalds: "do not remove anything that is stuck to the affected area" "do not put any creams, oils or butter on burns or scalds". <https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/burns-and-scalds/treatment/>
entries.notes: Use cool water, not ice water; ice application aggravates injury. If clothing is stuck to the wound, do not tear it off forcefully; cover with a clean cloth after rinsing and go to the hospital. Do not apply toothpaste, soy sauce, sesame oil, or flour; the NHS clearly states that no creams or oils of any kind should be applied to burns.
