In areas with high human and animal activity, even seemingly clear surface water must be guarded against all enteric pathogens, including Cryptosporidium. In rarely visited backcountry waters, the main threats to protect against are Giardia and enteric bacteria.
entries.sources: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Yellow Book · Water Disinfection for Travelers: "All organisms that may cause illness from drinking water are killed within seconds at boiling temperature" "CDC recommends that travelers boil water for a full minute to account for user variability in identifying boiling points and to add a margin of safety" "Although the boiling point for water decreases with increasing elevation, at common travel elevations the temperature needed to achieve boiling is still well above the temperature required to inactivate enteric pathogens" "Many filters do not reliably remove viruses" "Cryptosporidium, is poorly inactivated by chlorine- or iodine-based disinfection at practical concentrations"; Table 1.8.3 lists the primary threats of "Clear surface water near human and animal activity" as "All enteric pathogens, including Cryptosporidium". <https://www.cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/preparing-international-travelers/water-disinfection-for-travelers.html>
entries.notes: The same page also notes that it is not strictly necessary to reach a boil: maintaining 60 °C for 30 minutes is equally effective, and boiling is simply a visible endpoint that requires no thermometer. If you cannot boil water, use a filter or chemical disinfection tablets; both have pathogens they fail to cover, so boil whenever possible. Stream water that appears clear can still harbor parasites; do not judge by appearance.

entries.title: If a stranger demands money from you in the wilderness, give them the money, do not fight back, memorize their features, and call the police once you get away
entries.cost: The cash on your person. The hard part is holding back your anger.
entries.summary: When confronted face-to-face and your personal safety is threatened, prioritize saving your life; do not risk fighting or giving chase over money. After the perpetrator leaves with the money, pursuing to recover property may still qualify as justifiable defense, but that depends on the on-scene circumstances and methods used. Once you escape, note physical features, accent, license plate, and direction of flight, and dial 110.
entries.benefit: Life is worth more than money; the other party is risking a severe felony for a few hundred yuan. Article 263 of the Criminal Law provides that whoever robs public or private property by violence, coercion, or other methods shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than ten years, and concurrently fined. In circumstances such as using a firearm, home invasion, or causing serious injury or death, the sentence is ten years or more up to the death penalty. Article 20 of the Criminal Law on justifiable defense protects actions taken to "halt an ongoing unlawful infringement." The 2020 Guiding Opinions from the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the Ministry of Public Security clearly state that although property has already been taken, if it can be recovered through pursuit and interception, the infringement may be deemed ongoing. Whether it qualifies as justifiable defense also depends on the immediate circumstances and the purpose of halting the infringement. Determining excessive defense requires satisfying both conditions: clearly exceeding necessary limits and causing significant harm. One cannot determine that defense has ended solely because the other party took the money and turned around. For your own safety, do not risk fighting or giving chase over money. Immediately after escaping, record physical appearance, accent, license plate, and direction of flight, and call 110.
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020 Amendment). Criminal Law (Articles 20 and 263). <https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index.html> (Consolidated text reprinted by Beijing Municipal Public Security Bureau Traffic Management Bureau); Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security (2020). Guiding Opinions on the Lawful Application of the Justifiable Defense System, points 6, 8, and 11. <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/251611.html>
entries.notes: The reason for Grade C rating is that there is no direct literature showing "giving money without confronting is safer"; legal statutes only illustrate the other party's legal risks and your legal boundaries. Whether an action qualifies as justifiable defense still requires verification and investigation, and you may face investigation or detention before such determination. For procedural costs, see Section 8, Item 11 (You may fight back against unavoidable infringement). Do not follow them to a remote place to "withdraw money." Do not give up your phone passcode. Do not get into their vehicle. Giving money first is limited to occasions where you are trapped face-to-face and personal safety is threatened; still report it to the police once you escape. When someone tries to extort money online using private photos or recorded naked video chats, it is the exact opposite—you must not give a single cent; see Section 8, Item 32 (When someone extorts money using leverage). Do not count on carrying expandable batons, stun guns, or daggers; merely carrying them out the door is itself punishable; see Section 9, Item 26 (Do not buy expandable batons or stun guns for self-defense).

entries.title: If you encounter a group brawl, back away and leave; do not step in to break it up, do not watch the spectacle, and do not pick up weapons off the ground; if you want to call the police, retreat to a safe distance and dial 110
entries.cost: Costs nothing. The hard part is resisting two urges: stepping in to pull people apart, and standing around watching the drama. After reporting to the police, you might be contacted for a follow-up statement, costing at most half a day.
entries.summary: The moment you lay hands on someone, breaking up a fight turns into participating in a brawl; what you should do is step back and leave. Active participants in affray face up to 3 years of imprisonment. For large groups, causing severe disruption of public order on roadways, or carrying weapons, the penalty is 3 to 10 years. If you wish to report it, back away to a safe distance and dial 110, clearly stating the location, number of people, whether they are holding knives or clubs, and whether anyone is lying motionless.
entries.benefit: Article 292 of the Criminal Law: "Whoever gathers a crowd to engage in affray shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years, criminal detention, or public surveillance for the ringleaders and other active participants." For those who repeatedly engage in affray, involve large numbers with broad negative social impact, severely disrupt social order in public places or main traffic thoroughfares, or carry weapons, "shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than ten years." "Where gathering a crowd to engage in affray causes serious injury or death," offenders are convicted and punished under the crimes of intentional injury or intentional homicide. The Public Security Administration Punishments Law also sets penalties. Assaulting others incurs 5 to 10 days of administrative detention and a fine of 500 to 1,000 yuan. Brawling in a gang is handled as picking quarrels and provoking trouble, punishable by up to 15 days of administrative detention and a fine of 2,000 yuan. Article 5 of the Guiding Opinions on the Lawful Application of the Justifiable Defense System: Unlawful infringement "includes not only unlawful infringement directed against oneself, but also unlawful infringement endangering the state, public interests, or directed against others." Article 9 of the Opinions states that if one party strikes first and uses clearly excessive means, the striking back by the other party shall generally be determined as an act of defense. The same applies where one party strikes first and continues the infringement even as the other party makes efforts to avoid conflict.
entries.sources: National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Articles 232, 234, 292, 305, and 310). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2025). Public Security Administration Punishments Law (2025 Revision, Articles 30 and 51). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml>; Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security (2020). Guiding Opinions on the Lawful Application of the Justifiable Defense System (Fa Fa [2020] No. 31, Articles 5 and 9). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/251611.html>; National People's Congress (2018). Criminal Procedure Law (2018 Revision, Articles 62, 110, 111, and 193). Full text reprinted by the People's Procuratorate of Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region <https://www.nx.jcy.gov.cn/zwsy/qwfb/202011/t20201119_608817.html>
entries.notes: It is rated B because the consequence half is backed by rigid statutory provisions, but the step of "stepping back and calling the police, not getting physically involved to break up a fight" has no official original text; it is deduced from statutory provisions and "how mutual assault is identified." Saying "I came to break up the fight" is not an amulet; the determination depends on whether you used physical force and whom you struck. If the other party is already on the ground or has fled, and you still chase after them to hit them, it is no longer considered self-defense. If you see someone surrounded and being beaten one-sidedly, legally you certainly can stop it. Legitimate defense protects not only oneself, but also others. However, going in bare-handed will mostly just add another injured casualty. Shouting for help, recording video from afar, and calling the police are far more effective. "Not putting your hands on anyone, not gathering to watch" only benefits you. The benefits of calling 110 mainly fall upon the person on the ground, belonging to the lowest tier of beneficiaries in this book; whether you are willing to spend this time is for you to weigh yourself. Before weighing it, there are several things you should know. The obligation to testify already exists in the first place: Article 62 of the Criminal Procedure Law clearly states that anyone who knows the circumstances of a case has an obligation to testify; not making this call will not make it disappear. If severe injury or loss of life occurs, police pulling surveillance footage will find the people present all the same, and standing around watching actually makes you the easiest to be registered. If the reporting person is unwilling to make their name public, the case-handling authorities "shall keep it confidential for him" (Article 111). Once you clearly explain the location, number of people, and whether weapons are involved, you can hang up; you do not have to stay on site. What leads to admonition or detention of up to ten days is when the court summons you to appear, and without producing legitimate reasons, you still refuse to testify (Article 193). Passersby very rarely reach this step. Not calling the police is not illegal in itself: the phrase "has the right as well as the duty" in Article 110 of the Criminal Procedure Law carries no penal provision. Nor are there crimes in the Criminal Law punishing ordinary people for failing to report known information; walking away is a lawful option. After walking away, there are only two red lines. First, helping hide someone afterward or providing false testimony to harbor them (Article 310 of the Criminal Law: fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 3 years; where the circumstances are serious, 3 to 10 years). Second, intentionally giving false testimony when called upon to testify (Article 305: fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 3 years; where the circumstances are serious, 3 to 7 years). Silence and speaking truthfully are both fine; fabricating statements is what gets you into trouble. For being caught in a conflict yourself, see Section 8, Item 10; for extortion by strangers, see Item 36 of this section; for money after getting injured while rescuing others, see Item 39 of this section.

entries.title: If potentially exposed to HIV, obtain PEP within 72 hours—the sooner, the better
entries.cost: Medication for a 28-day course costs over a thousand yuan, paid out of pocket in most areas. You must make a hospital trip that very night. The hard part is admitting on the spot that you might have been infected and heading out the door immediately.
entries.summary: If you suspect you may have been exposed to HIV, 72 hours is a hard line, and it is best to take the medication within 2 hours. The medication must be taken continuously for 28 days. Beyond 72 hours, this route is gone, so do not wait until the next day to decide.
entries.benefit: The Beijing Municipal People's Government's AIDS prevention science popularization column states: preventive medication after exposure is called post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP for short), and one should "take preventive medication within 2 hours whenever possible, preferably within 24 hours, and not exceeding 72 hours." One must also "take it continuously for 28 days." Beyond 72 hours, initiation is no longer recommended; this is a hard time limit. The Beijing article also clearly notes that "taking medication regularly every day yields better blocking efficacy than frequently missing doses." The technical guidelines of the National Center for AIDS/STD Control and Prevention of the Chinese CDC clearly state that missing doses or discontinuing medication on one's own will reduce preventive efficacy. The guidelines require follow-up for drug side effects in the 2nd week after starting medication, and HIV and HCV antibody testing at 30 days and 90 days after exposure. The Chongqing CDC released in 2024 that 29 clinics across 26 districts and counties in the municipality can prescribe pre- and post-exposure prophylaxis, among which 14 provide 24-hour services
entries.sources: Beijing Municipal People's Government. Cannot tell before from after? Six questions and answers to fully understand HIV pre-exposure/post-exposure prophylaxis. <https://www.beijing.gov.cn/fuwu/bmfw/jhsyfwzdzx/sjazbr/fakp/202311/t20231110_3299397.html>; National Center for AIDS/STD Control and Prevention, Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention (2020). Technical Guidelines for HIV Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (Trial): "Patients taking medication may discontinue due to intolerance to drug side effects, or miss doses due to other reasons. All of these will reduce the preventive effectiveness of the drug" "Physicians should conduct HIV and HCV antibody testing follow-up on medication recipients at 30 days and 90 days after exposure, respectively". <https://www.chinacdc.cn/jkyj/crb2/yl/azb/jswj_azb/202410/t20241027_302131.html>; Chongqing Center for Disease Control and Prevention (2024). Chongqing Guidelines for Standardized Process Construction of 24-Hour HIV Post-Exposure Prophylaxis Clinics Released, Multiple Hospitals Now Provide Round-the-Clock Service: "The number of institutions in Chongqing currently providing HIV pre-exposure and post-exposure prophylaxis drug services has increased to 29 clinics across 26 districts and counties" "Clinics able to provide 24-hour round-the-clock service have reached 14". <https://www.cqcdc.org/index.php?a=shows&catid=2270&id=3045>
entries.notes: Where to get it: HIV designated medical institutions designated by the local CDC, usually registering under infectious diseases (STD/AIDS clinics). Some cities have already established 24-hour clinics, such as Chongqing. Before going, call the local CDC to ask which facility has the medication in stock; do not waste time in the emergency department. Circumstances counted as "exposure" include unprotected sexual intercourse, condom breakage, needle sticks, and blood coming into contact with mucous membranes; whether to use medication is ultimately judged by the physician. Medication must be completed for the full 28 days; missing doses will reduce effectiveness. Afterward, undergo follow-up examinations at 30 days and 90 days post-exposure as instructed by the physician. PEP is only a remedy and cannot replace routine prevention. For daily prevention and testing, see Section 1, Items 30 and 31 (using condoms throughout, and getting tested if high-risk behavior occurred).

entries.title: If injured or out-of-pocket while rescuing someone, first pursue the tortfeasor and basic medical insurance, then apply for recognition of courageous deeds (Jianyi Yongwei)
entries.cost: Costs no money. Applying requires submitting materials, waiting for recognition, and making several trips, taking several weeks to several months.
entries.summary: If rescuing someone ends up taking a toll on you, you do not have to just accept bad luck. Those injured performing courageous deeds receive treatment first and are billed later; medical expenses are borne by the tortfeasor, and if the person has fled or cannot afford compensation, it is covered through basic medical insurance. If there is no tortfeasor, upon your request, the person you rescued must by law provide appropriate compensation. At the same time, apply for recognition of courageous deeds; if injured and eligible, work-related injury insurance benefits are implemented.
entries.benefit: Article 183 of the Civil Code: "Where a person suffers damage from protecting the civil rights and interests of another person, the tortfeasor shall bear civil liability, and the beneficiary may grant appropriate compensation. Where there is no tortfeasor, the tortfeasor has escaped, or the tortfeasor is unable to bear civil liability, and the victim requests compensation, the beneficiary shall give appropriate compensation." Guo Ban Fa [2012] No. 39 addresses what to do with personnel injured performing courageous deeds. Medical institutions must establish green channels, "adhering to the principle of 'treatment first, payment later'". The original text regarding medical expenses states: "For medical expenses incurred due to emergency treatment, where there is a tortfeasor or responsible person, they shall be borne by the tortfeasor or responsible person; where there is no tortfeasor or responsible person, or where the tortfeasor or responsible person has escaped or is unable to bear them, they shall be resolved through the basic medical security system in accordance with regulations." In cases of death, "where criteria for martyr assessment are met, they shall be assessed as martyrs in accordance with the law"; "where circumstances are deemed as work-related injury, they shall enjoy a lump-sum work-related death subsidy as well as a special survivor allowance equivalent to 40 months of their own wages." For disability, "where conditions for enjoying work-related injury insurance benefits are met, corresponding benefits shall be implemented pursuant to the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance; where conditions are not met, the civil affairs department shall assess the disability grade and implement corresponding benefits." In employment, they are "prioritized for inclusion in employment assistance with key support provided," and public-welfare positions "prioritize placement of eligible courageous deed personnel." In housing, they are "prioritized for inclusion in the housing security system, with priority allocation of rental or purchase of indemnificatory housing or issuance of housing rental subsidies"
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 183). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; General Office of the State Council forwarding Ministry of Civil Affairs and other departments (2012). Opinions on Strengthening the Protection of the Rights and Interests of Personnel Performing Courageous Deeds (Guo Ban Fa [2012] No. 39). <https://www.gov.cn/zwgk/2012-07/26/content_2191928.htm>
entries.notes: It is rated B because what benefits can be received is fixed by national documents. However, how much prize money is awarded and how the recognition process runs are decided by each province's own regulations on courageous deeds; figures vary by region and were not verified province by province in this round. Typically, applications are submitted to the public security organ or courageous deeds work organization (foundation) of the place where the incident occurred. Whether it can be recognized depends on evidence: retain police case receipts, on-site surveillance footage, names and phone numbers of eyewitnesses, and hospital medical records on the spot. If litigation is required, the civil rights and interests of courageous deeds fall within the scope of free legal aid in the first place. For national standards on lump-sum work-related death subsidies and how disability grades convert into money, see Section 19, Items 14 and 15. For how to apply for legal aid, see Section 7, Item 3.

entries.title: If a knife, rebar, or glass is impaled in the body, apply pressure around the foreign object to stop bleeding; do not pull it out
entries.cost: Costs no money. The hard part is resisting the instinct to "pull it out first" and watching over the person while waiting for the ambulance.
entries.summary: Pulling it out can cause massive hemorrhage and will also make it harder for doctors to gauge how deeply it injured. The method is: call 120, apply pressure around the foreign object using hands or dressings to stop bleeding, and stabilize the foreign object with padding so it does not wobble. If internal organs are exposed from an abdominal wound, do not stuff them back in; cover them with a clean, moist dressing. If a chest wound is bubbling, do not seal it airtight with plastic wrap; sealing it airtight may collapse the lung.
entries.benefit: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies 2025 International First Aid Guidelines: "First aiders should apply pressure around an object (e.g. knife) that is stuck in the body to control bleeding, stabilise the object, and not remove it." "Do not remove any impaled foreign object from an abdominal or chest wound, as doing so may cause major bleeding and make it harder to assess the severity of the injury." "An impaled foreign object should be stabilized; if the object pulsates with the heartbeat, let it pulsate and stabilize it loosely." "First aiders should not push exposed internal organs back into the body." Open chest wounds without active gushing bleeding "may be left uncovered and without a dressing, because sealing the wound could cause air to accumulate in the chest cavity, leading to partial or complete lung collapse (pneumothorax)." Emergency medical services should be called immediately for all penetrating chest and abdominal wounds
entries.sources: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (2025). International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2025, pp. 256–257, 267–268. <https://www.ifrc.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/IFRC%20International%20First%20Aid,%20Resuscitation%20and%20Education%20Guidelines%202025.pdf>
entries.notes: It is rated B because this is the accepted practice in clinical guidelines; there are no randomized trials, as one cannot divide wounded patients into "pull" and "do not pull" groups to experiment. Upon arriving at the hospital, go directly to the triage desk at the entrance of the emergency department that sorts cases by urgency, report a "penetrating injury," and do not line up at the registration window. Under Beijing's triage standards, severe bleeding and intense pain can be classified as Level 2, requiring admission to the resuscitation room (see Section 24, Item 7 (Emergency Triage Desk)). If truly punctured through, call 120; Beijing's protocol requires emergency medical doctors to notify the hospital in advance to prepare to receive Level 1 and 2 patients. For how to apply pressure and use a tourniquet for massive bleeding, see Item 12.

entries.title: If a fracture is suspected, stop moving that part; support it immobile, apply a cold pack for under 20 minutes, and do not snap it straight yourself
entries.cost: Costs no money. Find a rigid board, rolled-up magazine, or clothing as support. Apply cold objects through a layer of cloth.
entries.summary: Treat injured hands and feet as fractures first; being able to stand and move still does not rule it out. Keep the injured area immobile, support it with hands or brace it in place with a rigid board, and apply a cold compress for no more than 20 minutes at a time. Do not snap it straight yourself; if bone punctures the skin, stop bleeding first, and do not push it back. X-rays can miss fractures; if films are normal but the doctor still suspects a fracture or ligament injury, undergo reexamination or obtain an MRI as instructed by the doctor.
entries.benefit: The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies published the 2025 International First Aid Guidelines. It states that "any injury to the hands or feet should initially be treated as a suspected fracture." It also states that "an X-ray is the only accurate way to confirm a fracture. When unsure, treat it as a fracture." The purpose of immobilization is to "minimise movement and pain." Cold application "for a maximum of 20 consecutive minutes at a time can relieve pain; cooling longer than this may damage the skin." "When long bones such as the femur are injured, bleeding from the bone itself can be fatal." Call emergency medical services when pain or swelling is severe, signs of shock are present, a femur (thigh bone) fracture occurs, or the limb position is visibly abnormal. For angulated fractures, consider manipulating back into position (reduction) on site only if two conditions are met simultaneously: first, "in remote (or limited-resource) settings where the limb below the angulation is cold, pale, or the first aider cannot properly immobilize it for transport"; second, the rescuer is trained. Open fractures (broken bone puncturing the skin) require stopping bleeding and preventing infection first. However, a failure to detect it on initial X-ray does not mean there is no fracture. The UK National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) has a hip fracture guideline. It states: for suspected hip fractures with normal X-rays, "offer MRI". If MRI is unavailable within 24 hours, consider CT. NICE's fracture guideline states: for suspected scaphoid fractures of the wrist, "consider MRI as the first-line imaging modality following a thorough physical examination." The scaphoid is a small bone in the wrist. A Cochrane literature review stated: "initial plain radiographs cannot exclude a fracture." Among the studies it included, for patients with normal X-rays where clinicians still suspected a scaphoid fracture, the median proportion with an actual fracture was 20%. The American College of Radiology has appropriateness criteria for acute knee trauma. It states: when X-rays show no fracture but occult fracture or internal joint derangement is still suspected, MRI is "usually appropriate" as the next step. It also states that MRI is highly accurate for detecting occult fractures, meniscal tears, and ligament injuries
entries.sources: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (2025). International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2025, pp. 301–302. <https://www.ifrc.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/IFRC%20International%20First%20Aid,%20Resuscitation%20and%20Education%20Guidelines%202025.pdf>; National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (2011). Hip fracture: management. NICE guideline CG124, Section 1.1.1. <https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg124/chapter/Recommendations>; National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (2016). Fractures (non-complex): assessment and management. NICE guideline NG38, Section 1.2.3. <https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng38/chapter/Recommendations>; Mallee WH et al. (2015). Computed tomography versus magnetic resonance imaging versus bone scintigraphy for clinically suspected scaphoid fractures in patients with negative plain radiographs. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD010023.pub2>; Taljanovic MS et al., Expert Panel on Musculoskeletal Imaging (2019). ACR Appropriateness Criteria: Acute Trauma to the Knee, Variant 3. American College of Radiology. <https://acsearch.acr.org/docs/69419/Narrative/>
entries.notes: It is rated B because these are all accepted practices. Prehospital traction splinting for femur (thigh bone) fractures is supported by only one retrospective chart review study, with very low evidence certainty. The findings showed less blood transfusion volume within 24 hours and shorter hospital stays, while differences in mortality and complications were too small to be conclusive. As for reducing first (aligning the bone back to original position) versus immobilizing as found, no evidence was found at all. There are three common misconceptions. Being able to stand and walk does not mean there is no fracture. Use only cold compresses, not hot compresses, nor alternating hot and cold. Sprains do not "get better once loosened up through movement"; rest first. Do not smoke before bones have healed; see Section 2, Item 1 (Smoking Cessation). Do not count on heavily supplementing calcium or drinking bone broth to make bones heal faster; see Section 6, Item 30 (Aggressively Supplementing Calcium After a Fracture). For movement contraindications when a fracture is suspected after an elderly person falls, see Item 2. If a leg swells after casting or bed rest, be alert to thrombosis; see Item 11. For whether to undergo disability appraisal and apply for a disability certificate after treatment, see Section 24, Items 9 and 10.

entries.title: After sexual assault, go to a safe place first and call 110; before examination of injuries, do not shower, do not wash clothes, do not tidy the room, and go to a hospital within 72 hours
entries.cost: Calling the police costs no money. Emergency contraceptives are OTC drugs and can be bought at pharmacies. A course of PEP costs over a thousand yuan; whether to take it is judged by a doctor; see Item 38 of this section (Obtain PEP within 72 hours). The hard part is that it is very difficult to speak up at the time, and one strongly desires to take a shower right away.
entries.summary: Traces left on the body, clothing, and inside the room are the most critical evidence for identifying the perpetrator. Therefore, try not to shower before the examination of injuries, nor wash clothes or tidy the room, and call 110 as early as possible. Emergency contraceptives are available at pharmacies; the earlier taken, the more effective. Go to a hospital within 72 hours so a doctor can evaluate whether PEP is needed.
entries.benefit: A prosecutor from the Beijing People's Procuratorate stated: "Whether a minor or an adult, when encountering infringement or harm, one should immediately call 110 to report to the police." Timely reporting to the police and seeking medical attention "facilitates investigative authorities in promptly examining the scene, extracting physical evidence and traces, and securing evidence." The anti-sexual assault handbook from the People's Daily, reprinted by the Guizhou Provincial Department of Civil Affairs, states: "Once unfortunately subjected to sexual assault, the most crucial matter is preserving evidence." Evidence such as "body fluids, hair, exfoliated skin cells, communication records, and other evidence" must be retained; "after being assaulted, do not bathe, wash clothes, tidy up the room, or throw things away without authorization." In cases committed by acquaintances, retain call logs and communication records. If the other party subsequently threatens or attempts to bribe you, evidence must also be preserved. The Beijing Xicheng District People's Procuratorate wrote: "Try not to bathe before undergoing a physical examination." The World Health Organization states that emergency contraception can be used when "women are subjected to sexual assault without effective contraceptive protection." It is recommended to use it within 5 days, and the earlier it is used, the more effective it is. For emergency contraceptive pills containing levonorgestrel (a type of progestin), the pregnancy rate among women who used them was 1.2% to 2.1%. Levonorgestrel tablets sold in domestic pharmacies in China are over-the-counter drugs. According to the Wuhan Municipal Health Commission: within "72 hours after unprotected sexual intercourse, the earlier the medication is taken, the better the effect of preventing pregnancy." HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) should be initiated within 2 hours whenever possible, and at the latest no more than 72 hours (nationwide).

entries.notes: Given a B because these represent official case-handling experience and medication guidance, lacking specific figures on "how much higher the conviction rate becomes after following these procedures." The beneficiaries are primarily yourself and your family members. The 72-hour window for emergency contraceptive pills is the standard specified in domestic Chinese package inserts; the World Health Organization states that they remain useful within 5 days, but effectiveness declines the longer you wait, so do not delay. For those already pregnant, emergency contraceptive pills have no effect. When reporting to the police, state things truthfully, without concealing anything, and without exaggerating. If the other party contacts you afterward to settle privately, offers money, or threatens you, retain all records and do not delete them. Thinking it through before reporting to the police is also acceptable, but evidence fades and disappears over time. Regardless of whether you report to the police, you must go to a hospital within the effective time limits. For audio recording, see Section 8, Item 41 (Audio Recording). If the other party subsequently blackmails you using photographs or by threatening to report to the police, that is likewise a crime; see Section 8, Item 32 (The Other Party Extorting Money by Threatening Police Reports or Releasing Photos). If this happens to a friend, accompany them to report to the police and go to the hospital; do not first advise them to take a bath and rest. For how to educate children in daily life and how parents should respond when children speak up, see Section 30, Item 19 (Understanding Private Body Parts). For nightmares and flashbacks persisting past one month, see Section 29, Item 14 (Trauma-Focused Psychotherapy). For routine contraception after childbirth, see Section 27, Item 20 (Breastfeeding Does Not Equal Contraception).

entries.title: If an infant under 1 year old chokes and cannot cry out, perform 5 back slaps prone, flip over for 5 chest thrusts, alternating between the two; do not compress the abdomen
entries.cost: Costs no money. Watching the movements once or attending an infant first aid class takes a few minutes to half a day. The hard part is managing in the panic to first flip the child over and position them securely face down.
entries.summary: If the child can still cough or cry out, let them cough on their own while you monitor closely beside them. If they cannot cry out and their face turns purple, have someone call 120. Position the infant face down along your forearm and use the heel of your hand to deliver 5 firm slaps between the two shoulder blades; if the object does not come out, flip them over and deliver 5 rapid thrusts to the center of the chest. Alternate between the two; do not compress the abdomen. If the child becomes unresponsive, switch immediately to CPR.
entries.benefit: The American Heart Association and the American Academy of Pediatrics issued the 2025 Pediatric Basic Life Support Guidelines. The guidelines state: choking (such as foreign body airway obstruction) "is one of the leading causes of death in infants and children." The most common substance aspirated by infants is liquid. If the child is still coughing and still able to vocalize, it is mild; allow the child to cough on their own while monitoring closely to see if it worsens. If coughing is very weak, absent, unable to cry out, or the face turns purple, it is severe. For severe obstruction, call emergency medical services first, then "deliver cycles of 5 back slaps followed by 5 chest thrusts until the object is expelled or the infant becomes unresponsive." The guidelines do not recommend abdominal thrusts for infants because of the risk of injuring abdominal organs. For chest thrusts, using the heel of one hand is now recommended because it achieves deeper compressions than the original two-finger method. If the infant becomes unresponsive, immediately begin CPR, starting with chest compressions without checking for a pulse. Any visible foreign body before ventilations should be removed. The guidelines explicitly state "do not perform blind finger sweeps." The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies' 2025 International First Aid Guidelines adopt the same approach: first deliver up to 5 firm slaps between the shoulder blades; if ineffective, turn the infant over and deliver up to 5 chest thrusts; if still ineffective, call emergency services immediately. For chest compressions, it utilizes an encircling hands technique with two thumbs pressing. The Fujian Red Cross Emergency Care Training Center states that for infants under 1 year old, one should perform "5 back slaps + 5 chest thrusts." When delivering back slaps, place the infant prone along your forearm with the head lower than the torso.

entries.notes: Rated B because the evidence supporting this technique comes primarily from case reports, lacking exact numbers on "how many deaths can be averted by following this." The benefit is rated "Large" based on judgment: a completely blocked airway can cause cardiac arrest in a child within minutes. Beneficiaries are almost exclusively your own children. For children over 1 year old and adults, switch to abdominal thrusts; see Item 26 of this section (Choking: Back Slaps Plus Abdominal Thrusts). Different organizations describe the hand technique for chest thrusts differently. The American guidelines use the heel of one hand, the International Red Cross uses two thumbs, and older courses used two fingers. The 2025 American guidelines no longer recommend two fingers because they do not compress deeply enough. Keep small objects like coins and small toys out of children's reach. For what to do after a child becomes unresponsive, see Item 44 of this section (Infant CPR).

entries.title: If an infant under 1 year old is unresponsive with no normal breathing, put the phone on speaker, call 120, and perform infant CPR: 30 compressions to 2 breaths
entries.cost: Costs no money. Learning infant CPR requires practicing in a class once, taking half a day to a full day. The hard part is giving rescue breaths covering the child's mouth and nose, along with fearing to press hard enough.
entries.summary: If tapping the soles of the feet yields no response and there is no normal breathing, put the phone on speaker and dial 120 while keeping your hands working continuously. Encircle the chest with both hands and compress with two thumbs; if you cannot encircle, use the heel of one hand, pressing to a depth of approximately 4 cm at a rate of about 2 per second. For every 30 compressions, cover the child's mouth and nose with your mouth and deliver 2 breaths. Most cardiac arrests in infants stem from respiratory distress; performing CPR that includes rescue breathing results in higher survival rates.
entries.benefit: The American Heart Association and the American Academy of Pediatrics issued the 2025 Pediatric Basic Life Support Guidelines. The guidelines state: for cardiac arrest in infants and children, the primary etiology remains respiratory compromise. Among infants experiencing out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, only 6.6% survived to hospital discharge. When laypersons encounter an infant or child who is unresponsive, not breathing normally, and showing no signs of life, they "should immediately begin CPR" without checking for a pulse. Compression depth should be at least one-third the anteroposterior diameter of the chest, "approximately 1.5 inches (4 cm)" in infants. The rate is 100 to 120 compressions per minute. For a single rescuer, perform 30 compressions to 2 breaths. For two rescuers, perform 15 compressions to 2 breaths. In infants, compress using the heel of one hand or the two-thumb encircling hands technique. If you cannot encircle, use the heel of the hand. The two-finger compression technique has been removed because it fails to compress deeply enough. The guidelines also note that for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in infants and children, adding rescue breaths to compressions improves survival. A US registry evaluated 3,900 pediatric patients under age 18 with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, of whom 59.4% were infants. Among those receiving bystander CPR, the adjusted rate of survival to discharge was 13.2%, compared to 9.5% for those without CPR—an adjusted OR of 1.57 (approximately 57% higher odds of survival), 95% CI 1.25–1.96 (confidence interval). In infants, CPR with rescue breathing was associated with higher survival, and surviving children demonstrated better neurological recovery. Compressions-only CPR yielded outcomes similar to no bystander CPR. The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies also released its 2025 International First Aid Guidelines. It states: to check for responsiveness in an infant, gently pick up the child or flick the soles of their feet. If you are alone, place the call to emergency services yourself using speakerphone. If you do not have a phone available that allows you to call while performing compressions, perform 1 minute of CPR before going to call. A public science article from the Capital Institute of Pediatrics, reprinted by the Beijing Municipal Health Commission, states: "If only 1 person is present, perform 2 minutes of CPR first before calling the 120 ambulance." Compression depth is "4 cm for infants." For ventilations in infants under 1 year old, deliver "mouth-to-mouth-and-nose" breaths.

entries.notes: Rated B because survival statistics come from observational registry studies. Furthermore, the calculations are across all children, and the abstract did not provide separate figures specifically for infants. Benefit is rated "Large" based on calculations across all children: survival to discharge rose from 9.5% to 13.2%, a relative increase of approximately 40%. Beneficiaries are almost exclusively your own children. Compared with Item 1 of this section (Firm Chest Compressions), there are three differences: infants require rescue breaths, as compression-only CPR performs poorly in infants; compress the chest using two thumbs or one palm heel to a depth of about 4 cm, without interlocking two hands; if you are alone and cannot call while compressing, compress first before calling. How long to compress first varies across authorities: the single-rescuer protocol from the Capital Institute of Pediatrics and the American guidelines specifies 2 minutes, whereas the International Red Cross specifies 1 minute. Using a mobile phone on speakerphone eliminates this dilemma entirely. The European Resuscitation Council teaches delivering 5 initial rescue breaths before compressions, whereas the American guidelines teach compressions before rescue breaths; both are far superior to doing nothing. Domestic older Chinese training taught two-finger compressions, but the 2025 American guidelines have discarded this technique. For arrest caused by choking, check inside the mouth before ventilating and only extract visible foreign objects; see Item 43 of this section (Infant Choking).

entries.title: If a child swallows a button battery or swallows two or more strong magnetic beads, go immediately to an emergency department at a hospital with endoscopy capabilities; do not wait for them to pass spontaneously, and do not induce vomiting
entries.cost: Costs no money; emergency imaging and endoscopic foreign body removal fees are separate. In daily life, tighten screw-secured battery compartments on remote controls, digital scales, and car key fobs. Store spare batteries and magnetic beads well out of children's reach. The hard part is that most of the time no one witnesses the child swallowing them, and the child may initially show no symptoms whatsoever.
entries.summary: When a button battery lodges in the esophagus, it can burn through and cause severe injury in as little as 2 hours, even if the child initially appears completely fine. Two or more magnetic beads will attract each other across intestinal walls, potentially pinching and perforating the bowel. If ingestion is suspected, go immediately to a hospital for X-rays; do not induce vomiting, do not wait for them to pass in the stool, and do not wait for symptoms to develop before going.
entries.benefit: Data from the US National Poison Data System from 1985 to 2009 showed a 6.7-fold increase in the proportion of button battery ingestions resulting in severe injury or death. The most dangerous are 20 mm diameter lithium coin cells. For children under 4 years old and lithium cells 20 mm or larger in diameter, outcomes were markedly worse. When a battery lodges in the esophagus, it can cause severe injury leaving permanent sequelae in as little as 2 to 2.5 hours. In 92% of fatal cases and 56% of severe injury cases, no one witnessed the child swallowing the battery at the time. At least 54% of fatal cases and 27% of severe injury cases were initially misdiagnosed due to non-specific symptoms. Even after the battery is extracted, the tissue injury can continue to penetrate deeper. Esophageal perforation, tracheoesophageal or aortoesophageal fistulas, and massive hemorrhage have all occurred days later. In another analysis of 8,648 cases, among batteries ingested by children under 6 years old, 61.8% were obtained directly from electrical appliances or electronic devices. The management guideline from the National Capital Poison Center states: if battery ingestion is suspected, "do not induce vomiting." A battery lodged in the esophagus "can cause severe burns in as little as 2 hours"; "do not wait for symptoms to develop." Children under 12 require immediate X-ray imaging to locate the battery. Product injury surveillance by the Guangdong Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention showed nearly 100 injury cases related to accidental battery ingestion over the past five years, the majority involving button batteries. Children aged 0 to 6 accounted for 92.9% of those injured. Moderate or severe injuries accounted for 39.3%, and those requiring hospitalization accounted for 25.0%. Its recommendation is to "seek medical attention immediately; never induce vomiting or feed the child on your own." The same surveillance report notes that when Buckyballs (magnetic beads) are ingested, beads in adjacent bowel loops will "attract each other and pinch the intestinal wall, thereby causing bowel obstruction or bowel perforation"; if accidental ingestion is suspected, "the child should be taken to the hospital immediately for treatment." A 2025 literature review compiling 130 children who experienced enteroenteric fistulas after ingesting 2 or more magnets reported a median age of 3.3 years; 95.5% required surgical intervention, 19% developed postoperative complications, and 1 child died.

entries.notes: The rating is set to B because the figures come from poison hotlines and case registries, without control comparisons for "how many fewer deaths occur if followed." The benefit is rated as "large" based on judgment: a battery can cause severe burns within 2 hours in the esophagus, and fatal cases mostly occur when no one saw the ingestion and treatment was delayed by misdiagnosis. Those who benefit are almost entirely children in one's own household. Bring an identical battery model, the packaging, or the electronic appliance along; the doctor will rely on it to identify which type of battery it is. Regarding whether to feed honey on the way, domestic and foreign recommendations differ. The U.S. National Capital Poison Center recommends that for children aged 1 year or older, with ingestion occurring less than 12 hours ago, who are able to swallow, and when honey is readily at hand, it can be given: feed 10 mL every 10 minutes, up to 6 times. Its rationale comes from experiments on live pigs; a 2023 pooled review noted that human evidence remains very limited. The Guangdong CDC advises against feeding anything. Honey must absolutely not be given to infants under 1 year old. Honey can only slow down the burn rate and cannot replace removal; do not delay departing to seek out honey. When a battery and a magnet are ingested together, the U.S. National Capital Poison Center mandates that the battery must still be retrieved even if it has reached the stomach. The elderly can also ingest them: among 8,648 cases, 15.5% involved swallowing batteries mistaken for pills, mostly by elderly individuals. Across all cases, 36.3% involved hearing aid batteries. If someone is choking in the throat and cannot catch their breath, first handle it according to Item 26 of this section (back blows plus abdominal thrusts for choking) or Item 43 (infant choking). For accidental ingestion of cleaning agents or medications, see Item 20 of this section (accidental ingestion of cleaning agents).

entries.title: When someone is drunk, place them in a side-lying position and have someone stay with them constantly; do not leave them to sleep alone; call 120 if they cannot be awakened, breathe slowly or irregularly, have seizures, or feel cold to the touch
entries.cost: Free. Requires someone to stay watching for several hours, often the entire night. The difficulty is that you may have been drinking as well and want to go home to sleep, while everyone tends to assume that "they'll be fine after sleeping it off."
entries.summary: A person who is so drunk that they pass out can choke to death on their own vomit, or their breathing may gradually stop. Place them on their side, have someone stay with them constantly, and do not leave them to sleep alone in a room. If they cannot be awakened, their breathing slows or becomes irregular, they have seizures, or their skin turns cold or bluish, call 120 immediately. Do not force coffee down them, do not put them in a cold shower, and do not stick fingers down their throat to induce vomiting.
entries.benefit: The UK's National Health Service (NHS) lists the manifestations of alcohol poisoning as: confusion, slurred speech, inability to stand, vomiting, incontinence of urine or feces, pale or bluish skin, slow or irregular breathing, seizures, and inability to be awakened. If you suspect someone has alcohol poisoning, or if they have seizures, lose consciousness, or stop breathing, call the emergency number. What you should do is stay by their side, "because there's a risk they could choke on their own sick or stop breathing." If they are conscious, help them sit up. If they have passed out, place them in the side-lying recovery position and monitor whether their breathing is normal. If they are still awake, can swallow, and are not vomiting, they may take small sips of water. Keep them warm using a coat or blanket. There are five things not to do. Do not let them drink more alcohol. Do not give them food, as they could choke. Do not give them coffee or caffeinated drinks, which will exacerbate dehydration. Do not put them in a cold shower or cold bath, as they could get chilled, fall, or pass out in the water. Do not try to make them throw up. An article by emergency physicians published on the website of the Shaanxi Provincial Health Commission states that in intoxicated individuals, throat reflexes are weakened, making it easy to aspirate vomitus into the trachea during vomiting, with severe cases leading to "direct asphyxiation death." Emergency departments frequently receive intoxicated individuals who are already deceased, with large amounts of vomitus suctioned from the trachea. When the lethargic/stuporous stage is reached—with a pale complexion, purplish-blue lips, clammy and cold skin, falling body temperature, and shallow breathing—call 120 immediately. At this point, place them on their side, "do not induce vomiting or feed them food," cover them with a blanket for warmth, and turn them regularly. If their heartbeat and breathing stop, perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation immediately. Hospital public educational material reprinted by the Beijing Municipal Health Commission writes: "For intoxicated individuals, never allow them to sleep alone, lest the patient suffocate without anyone to provide rescue." A pharmacist article reprinted by the Fujian Provincial Medical Products Administration notes that intoxicated individuals "must strictly be kept in a side-lying position," and that hypothermia can trigger cardiac arrest. The U.S. CDC estimates that from 2010 to 2012, an annual average of 2,221 people aged 15 and older in the United States died of alcohol poisoning, equivalent to about 6 people per day.

entries.notes: The rating is set to B because these represent official public education materials and emergency clinical experience, without data on "how many fewer deaths occur if followed." The benefit is rated as "large" based on judgment: choking to death and respiratory arrest both occur when no one is watching; having someone stay with them allows timely discovery and timely calling of 120. Recommendations on inducing vomiting are inconsistent. Some domestic public educational sources say that individuals who can still walk and talk can have their pharynx stimulated to induce vomiting. Inducing vomiting must absolutely never be attempted in someone who cannot be awakened; this point is unanimous domestically and abroad. The NHS advises against inducing vomiting at any time. This set of practices applies first and foremost to family members, but more frequently one encounters friends and colleagues drinking together. Fellow drinkers also bear a legal duty of care. The Taixing Court in Jiangsu ruled on a case: two individuals, fully aware that a co-diner at their table was already drunk, failed to notify his family and did not escort him home; he fell into a river and drowned in the early morning hours. The two were held responsible for 7% and 3% of the liability respectively, paying a combined compensation of approximately 104,000 yuan (exact value 103,887 CNY). The Supreme People's Court Guiding Case No. 227 also clarifies that co-drinkers who fail to fulfill their duty of warning and care must share compensation according to their fault. Therefore, when the gathering ends, hand the person directly over to their family, or watch over them until they wake up. For an intoxicated stranger collapsed on the roadside, calling 120 is sufficient; do not manually move them, for reasons detailed in Item 2 of this section (do not rush to pull someone up). Intoxication readily causes hypothermia; for how to keep warm, see Item 28 of this section (hypothermia). For those taking cephalosporins or metronidazole who have also consumed alcohol, see Section 34, Item 11 (do not drink alcohol while taking cephalosporins or metronidazole). To prevent intoxicated individuals from taking hot baths or steam saunas, see Section 22, Item 11 (do not soak in hot springs after drinking alcohol).

entries.title: If a finger or toe is severed, first compress the wound to stop bleeding, wrap the severed part in moist gauze, place it into a sealed bag, put the bag in ice water, and go to a hospital with a hand surgery department
entries.cost: Free. Keep a pack of clean gauze and several sealable plastic bags ready at home. The difficulty is attending to the person first before the severed digit amidst the panic, while also resisting the urge to bury the severed digit directly in ice or submerge it directly in water.
entries.summary: First apply manual pressure directly on the wound to stop bleeding, and call 120. Wrap the severed part in moist, clean gauze, seal it in a bag, and then place the bag in ice water; do not let it directly touch ice, and do not soak it directly in water. Without cooling, a severed digit can only wait for about 4 to 6 hours. For reattached fingers, over 80% survive successfully.
entries.benefit: The U.S. National Library of Medicine's MedlinePlus first aid page states: apply direct manual pressure to the wound to stop bleeding, and elevate the injured area. A tourniquet may be applied for life-threatening bleeding. The severed part should be properly saved and accompany the person. If the cut surface is dirty, gently rinse it first. Wrap it in a clean, damp cloth, place it into a sealed plastic bag, and place the bag in ice water. Without placing it in a bag, do not put it directly into water or ice, and do not place it directly on ice. Dry ice must not be used, as it will freeze and injure the severed digit. If no cold water is available, keep it away from heat as much as possible. Cooling allows the severed digit to wait longer; without cooling, "about 4 to 6 hours is all" it can remain viable for reattachment. Do not assume the severed part is too small to be worth saving. Do not push severed parts or bones back in. The American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons' fingertip amputations page offers consistent instructions, adding that it is best to proceed to a hospital with hand specialists immediately on duty. Across 31 combined studies, 86.8% of severed digits survived after reattachment (1,976 successful digits, 300 failures). Among 1,087 people who underwent replantation, 82.9% returned to work. Another pooled analysis of 12 studies reported a survival rate of 85.3% for replanted digits. There is also a pooled analysis of 12 studies and 3,645 people: when ischemia time of the severed digit before surgery exceeded 8 hours, necrosis after reattachment was more likely to occur, with odds approximately 2.25 times those of under 8 hours: OR 2.25, 95% CI 1.43 to 3.54 (confidence interval).

(2026). Return-to-Work After Attempted Digit Replantation: A Systematic Review of 31 Studies. HAND. <https://doi.org/10.1177/15589447241279445>; Stone N et al. (2021). Comparing digital replantation versus revision amputation patient reported outcomes for traumatic digital amputations of the hand: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Microsurgery. <https://doi.org/10.1002/micr.30738>; Yu F et al. (2026). Risk factors associated with postoperative necrosis after digital replantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Frontiers in Surgery. <https://doi.org/10.3389/fsurg.2026.1795247>
entries.notes: The rating is set to B because the preservation methods come from consensus in guidelines and textbooks, while survival rates come from follow-up observational studies. No controlled trials comparing different preservation methods were found. The benefit is rated "Moderate" based on judgment: what is saved is a finger, not a life. Whether it can be replanted and whether it is worth replanting must be decided by a doctor based on the injury; crushed or torn-off fingers are much harder to replant than cleanly cut ones. MedlinePlus also reminds us that saving a life comes before saving a severed finger: stop the bleeding first before dealing with the finger. If bleeding cannot be controlled by pressure, see Item 12 of this section (Firmly press down on the wound with your hand first during major bleeding) for how to apply a tourniquet. Chopping vegetables at home, getting hands caught in door gaps, and using power tools can all sever fingers. For angle grinder protection, see Section 1, Item 42 (Install the protective guard before using an angle grinder). The beneficiaries are primarily yourself and your family members, especially those who frequently use power tools or perform manual labor.

entries.title: If a permanent tooth (a tooth that grows in after losing baby teeth) is completely knocked out, hold it by the crown, give it a quick rinse, put it back if possible, and if not, soak it in milk and see a dentist immediately; do not put baby teeth back
entries.cost: Free. Milk and saline solution can be found at home or in convenience stores; dental care costs are separate. The difficult parts are daring to insert the knocked-out tooth back into the dental socket yourself, and identifying on the spot whether the dislodged tooth is a baby tooth or a permanent tooth.
entries.summary: Hold the tooth by the crown and do not touch the root. If it is dirty, gently rinse it with milk or saline solution. Put it back into its original position if you can, and bite down on a clean cloth. If it cannot be put back, soak it in milk and see a dentist immediately; do not leave it dry wrapped in a tissue. For teeth replanted on the spot, about 20% later fuse between the root and bone, whereas for those left dry for over an hour, it exceeds 80%. Do not put baby teeth back.
entries.benefit: The UK National Health Service (NHS) dental trauma page states: hold the tooth by the crown—the white part protruding outside the gum—and do not touch the root. If the tooth is dirty, gently rinse it in milk, saline, or saliva. Try to put it back into its original socket in the gum. If it goes in, gently bite down on a clean piece of cloth to hold it in place, and see a dentist as soon as possible. If it cannot be put back, soak it in milk or saliva. Do not put baby teeth back, as this can damage the permanent tooth growing underneath. Even if a knocked-out tooth cannot be found, you should still book an emergency dental appointment. The steps on the International Association of Dental Traumatology's "Save Your Tooth" poster are the same: find the tooth, hold it by the crown, plug the sink, and rinse it with cold tap water. Then choose one of three options: put it back in place, soak it in a cup of milk or saline, or hold it between the cheek and gums. Finally, see a dentist immediately. A study from the dental trauma database at Copenhagen University Hospital in Denmark selected 145 permanent teeth that were replanted after being knocked out in 116 patients, following them for 7 months to 23 years. It examined the risk of the tooth root fusing with the alveolar bone (ankylosis), after which the root is gradually resorbed. The risk was 17.2% for those replanted on the spot, 55.3% for those soaked in saliva or saline before replantation, and 85.7% for those kept dry for over 1 hour. This hospital previously tracked a cohort of 400 teeth, which was re-analyzed in 2020. For children's teeth where the root had not fully developed, the risk of ankylosis was 33.9% with dry storage under 20 minutes, rising to 60.0% over 60 minutes. For teeth with fully developed roots, it rose from 59.4% to 86.4%. Both groups were estimates at 900 days after replantation. A 1995 study on these 400 teeth also found that soaking them in tap water for more than 20 minutes mostly led to root resorption. Over the follow-up period, 30% of these 400 teeth were eventually extracted.
entries.sources: NHS. Knocked-out tooth (reviewed 2025-02-06): "Hold the tooth by the white bit that sticks out of the gum (the crown) – do not touch the root", "If the tooth is dirty, rinse it gently in milk, saline or saliva", "Do not put a baby tooth back in as it could damage the tooth growing underneath", "If you cannot put the tooth back in, you can put it in either milk or saliva". <https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/knocked-out-tooth/>; International Association of Dental Traumatology. Save your tooth (poster). <https://iadt-dentaltrauma.org/guidelines-and-resources/save-a-tooth-poster/>; Gul A et al. (2024). Risk of ankylosis of avulsed teeth immediately replanted or stored under favorable storage conditions before replantation: A long-term clinical study. Dental Traumatology. <https://doi.org/10.1111/edt.12898>; Lauridsen E et al. (2020). Risk of ankylosis of 400 avulsed and replanted human teeth in relation to length of dry storage: A re-evaluation of a long-term clinical study. Dental Traumatology. <https://doi.org/10.1111/edt.12520>; Andreasen JO et al. (1995). Replantation of 400 avulsed permanent incisors. 1. Diagnosis of healing complications. Endodontics & Dental Traumatology. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1600-9657.1995.tb00461.x>; Andreasen JO et al. (1995). Replantation of 400 avulsed permanent incisors. 4. Factors related to periodontal ligament healing. Endodontics & Dental Traumatology. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1600-9657.1995.tb00464.x>
entries.notes: The rating is set to B because the figures come from observational follow-up studies at a single hospital without parallel controls. The benefit is rated "Moderate" based on judgment: what is saved is a tooth, not a life, and the endpoint measured is root ankylosis, not direct tooth loss. The researchers also noted that a portion of teeth kept dry for over an hour still did not develop ankylosis, so even if time has passed, do not throw the tooth away; bring it along for the dentist to evaluate. Tap water should only be used for a quick rinse; do not soak the tooth in water to transport it. Beneficiaries are primarily your own children, but it applies equally to adults who fall, play sports, or hit their mouths while cycling. The NHS notes that teeth that cannot be saved can initially be replaced with a removable denture, with a bridge or dental implant considered after healing. For how to inquire about dental implant costs, see Section 24, Item 12 (Ask for an all-inclusive price before getting dental implants).

chapters.title: Account and Information Security
chapters.intro: Scope: Money and personal information. When an account is logged into by someone else, what is lost first is money. The other party will also use your account to scam people in your contact list. Your identity is effectively taken away as well.

entries.title: Enable two-factor authentication for email, payment, and social accounts, prioritizing mobile push notification prompts over SMS verification codes
entries.cost: Free. Set it up once for each account; setup takes just two to three minutes.
entries.summary: Two-factor authentication means that when logging in, in addition to the password, an extra confirmation is required to verify your identity. Using on-device mobile push notification prompts where you tap to confirm blocks over 90% of phishing account takeovers; SMS verification codes are easier to be phished than push prompts. Relying on older methods such as answering "Where did you last log in?" or "What is your backup email?" blocked as few as 10% of phishing takeovers.
entries.benefit: Google analyzed 350,000 real account takeover attempts (also called account hijacking). One category relies on device-based verification, such as a mobile push prompt asking you to tap confirm, or inserting a security key. This category blocked "more than 94% of phishing-based hijacking attempts and 100% of automated hijacking attempts." Phishing refers to tricking you into entering passwords on fake websites; automated refers to machines testing leaked passwords in bulk. The other category relies on answering knowledge-based questions, such as asking where you last logged in or what your recovery email is. This category "only blocked as low as 10% of phishing hijacking attempts and 73% of automated hijacking attempts." Within device-based verification, SMS verification codes are weaker than mobile push prompts. Phishers correctly guessed or tricked users into providing 4% of SMS verification codes, compared to only 1% for push prompts. In targeted attacks directed at specific individuals, SMS blocked only 76%, whereas push prompts blocked 90%.
entries.sources: Doerfler P, Thomas K, Marincenko M, et al. (2019). Evaluating Login Challenges as a Defense Against Account Takeover. The World Wide Web Conference (WWW '19). <https://doi.org/10.1145/3308558.3313481>
entries.notes: The same study also found that this type of verification can sometimes lock out the legitimate user. 52% of legitimate users failed on their first login attempt, though ultimately 97% still managed to get in. Enable this feature for your email first, because most other accounts allow password recovery via email. Keep verification codes strictly to yourself; for what consequences you face by reading out codes or scanning your face on behalf of others, see Section 8, Item 45 (Reading out verification codes).

entries.title: Use a unique password for email, never reusing it on any other website
entries.cost: Free. Storing it in a password manager means you don't have to remember it yourself. The difficult part is breaking the old habit of using a single password everywhere.
entries.summary: Passwords stolen from other websites will be directly attempted by attackers to log into your email. Once your email is accessed by someone else, every account that can reset passwords via email is lost along with it. Therefore, use a unique password for your email and never use it anywhere else.
entries.benefit: Attempting to log in using usernames and passwords leaked from elsewhere one by one is called credential stuffing, and your email will be targeted this way as well. Once someone gains access to your email, all accounts using it for password recovery are compromised together. The recommendation from the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency is: use a different strong password for each account, at least 16 characters long, and store it in a password manager.
entries.sources: US CISA. Use Strong Passwords. <https://www.cisa.gov/secure-our-world/use-strong-passwords>
entries.notes: If you cannot remember them, use your browser's built-in password manager. It remembers passwords for each site on your behalf, which is far better than using the same password everywhere. Do not store passwords in WeChat Favorites or Notes.

entries.title: Set a lock screen passcode on your phone, and set a PIN for your SIM card
entries.cost: Free. You only need to set the lock screen passcode and the PIN once each.
entries.summary: A SIM card is that small card inside your phone, relied upon to receive SMS verification codes. If your phone is lost, the finder might remove this card, insert it into another phone to receive verification codes, and reset your accounts one by one. Setting a PIN on the card cuts off this avenue, as entering this code is required immediately upon powering up whenever the card is moved to another phone.
entries.benefit: When a phone is lost, the quickest path for the finder is to insert the SIM card into another phone to receive your SMS verification codes. With these codes, they can reset your accounts one after another. If a PIN is set on the SIM card, moving it to another phone requires entering the PIN upon powering on, leaving the finder unable to use it to receive verification codes. In October 2020, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) reported a real case. After a user's phone was stolen, they failed to promptly report the loss of the SIM card, giving criminals an opportunity. The criminals logged into a government services app using the "phone number plus verification code," obtaining the user's ID number and other information. They then changed the telecom customer service password. Even though the user later reported the loss of the SIM card, the criminals used social engineering scripts to deceive telecom customer service into unfreezing the card. Finally, exploiting "password recovery" vulnerabilities on online lending platforms, they reset payment passwords and stole funds via online loans. MIIT used this case to remind users to set a SIM card PIN promptly and report the loss of their phone immediately. As for the lock screen passcode, the US Federal Communications Commission recommends: set a strong password on your phone to restrict access by others. When a phone is lost or stolen, it prevents unauthorized usage charges and protects your personal data from theft.
entries.sources: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (2020). MIIT Alert! Strengthen Personal Information Protection Awareness. Reprinted by gov.cn from Gongxin Weibo, 2020-10-22. <https://app.www.gov.cn/govdata/gov/202010/22/464049/article.html>; US FCC. Protect Your Smart Device. <https://www.fcc.gov/consumers/guides/protect-your-mobile-device>
entries.notes: The PIN is configured in the phone's settings under the "SIM Card Lock" option. The default factory code is generally 1234 or 0000. If entered incorrectly three times in a row, it must be unlocked using the PUK code provided by your telecom carrier. Therefore, write this code down on paper after setting it up. Rated Level C because both sources are official alerts, alongside an individual case study, with no quantitative studies calculating how much financial loss setting a PIN actually prevents. For what to do first when losing your phone, see Item 4 (Steps to take in this order if you lose your phone).

entries.title: If you lose your phone, follow this order: report the SIM card lost, remotely lock the device, change passwords, report to the police, and freeze bank cards
entries.cost: Free. Completing the entire sequence takes about ten to fifteen minutes.
entries.summary: Sequence matters more than speed. First, reporting the SIM card lost cuts off the critical lifeline of verification codes. Next, remotely lock the phone, then change your email and payment passwords using a computer, followed by filing a police report to obtain an incident receipt, and finally freezing bank cards as needed. If your phone is not with you, you can borrow someone else's phone to call carrier customer service to report the loss.
entries.benefit: Order matters more than speed. Step 1: Report the SIM card lost, so others cannot receive your verification codes. Step 2: Remotely lock the phone and wipe its contents. Step 3: Change your email and payment passwords from a computer. Step 4: Report to the police and get an incident receipt. Finally, freeze bank cards as needed. The US Federal Communications Commission also advises: even if you think it is merely misplaced, lock it remotely. If it is stolen, report it to the police immediately with the model and IMEI number (the phone's identity number), and notify your carrier right away.
entries.sources: US FCC. Protect Your Smart Device. <https://www.fcc.gov/consumers/guides/protect-your-mobile-device>; the sequence of steps is based on author experience; for replacing an ID card, see Section 7; for fraudulent loans under your name, see the item on credit reports in Section 8
entries.notes: Note down the customer service numbers of the three major carriers in advance: China Mobile 10086, China Unicom 10010, China Telecom 10000. Also note the city where your phone number was registered, as customer service will ask. You can just as easily call customer service from someone else's phone to report the loss.

entries.title: If unauthorized charges appear on your card, report it lost and freeze it first, then report to the police, and then demand bank reimbursement: the burden of proving "it was swiped by you" rests on the bank
entries.cost: Free. As soon as you notice suspicious activity on the card, immediately report it lost or freeze it. Retain police records, loss-reporting records, and transaction notifications sent by the bank. If you still have the physical card on you, perform a small inquiry or deposit/withdrawal nearby to leave a record proving that the genuine card was in your possession when the incident occurred. The difficult part is resisting the urge to argue with customer service first—report the loss first.
entries.summary: If unauthorized charges appear on your card, you must first provide evidence such as police incident reports and loss-reporting records. If the bank claims the charge was made by you personally, the burden of proof is on the bank; if it cannot produce proof, it must reimburse you. The prerequisite is that you report the loss and freeze the card as soon as you discover it. If you delay reporting, any additional subsequent losses must be borne by yourself.
entries.benefit: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court divide the "burden of producing evidence." If you claim that transactions resulted from counterfeit card theft or online unauthorized charges, you must provide evidence first. Counterfeit card theft means someone duplicated your card and swiped it. The following can serve as proof: effective legal documents, records showing where the genuine card was located during the bank card transaction, and where the transaction took place. Also included are account transaction statements, transaction notifications, police records, loss-reporting records, and so on. **Conversely, if the card-issuing bank or non-bank payment institution (third-party payment) claims that the charge was made by the cardholder in person or with their authorization, the burden of proof rests on them.** If the bank fails to verify in a timely manner after you notify them, or fails to promptly provide and preserve transaction slips and surveillance videos, resulting in the unavailability of evidence, the adverse consequences of the missing evidence shall be borne by the bank. Once established: debit card (savings card) holders may demand that the card-issuing bank pay the principal and interest of the misappropriated deposit and compensate for losses. Credit card holders may demand a refund of deducted overdraft principal, interest, and liquidated damages, along with compensation for losses; if the bank conversely demands that you repay this overdraft amount, the court will not support it. You may also demand that the card-issuing bank promptly revoke corresponding adverse credit records (Nationwide, effective May 25, 2021).
entries.sources: Supreme People's Court (2021). Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Civil Dispute Cases Involving Bank Cards (Articles 4, 5, 7, 14, 15). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/304771.html>
entries.notes: There are two scenarios where you must bear liability yourself. First, if you failed to properly safeguard items like your bank card, password, or verification code and were at fault yourself (the original text reads "at fault for failing to fulfill the obligation of proper safekeeping"), you bear liability proportional to your fault. Therefore, do not share passwords with others, and do not forward verification codes to others (see Item 1, prioritizing mobile push prompts for two-factor authentication). Second, failing to report the loss in a timely manner, allowing losses to continue expanding; that additional portion must be borne by yourself. Therefore, the first step is always to report the loss and freeze the card, rather than calling customer service to argue first. Third-party payment institutions are also subject to these rules. If their promotional materials specify "advance compensation" and the commitment is specific and explicit, you can demand that they compensate you in advance accordingly.
