Opinions on Reforming and Improving Real Estate Credit Management to Accelerate the Construction of a New Model of Real Estate Development (Yin Fa [2026] No. 171, Article 24). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2026/issue_13026/202610/content_7082770.html>; People's Bank of China (2024). Responsible Official of the People's Bank of China Answers Press Questions on Improving the Commercial Personal Residential Mortgage Rate Pricing Mechanism (Introducing People's Bank of China Announcement [2024] No. 11). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202409/content_6977671.htm>
entries.notes: As to how large a deviation is required before negotiation is allowed, the regulatory document did not give a specific figure; it is governed by the announcements of your lending bank. This provision governs floating-rate residential mortgages issued by banks. If the bank does not agree to a rate cut and you have surplus funds on hand, you can compare calculations according to Section 5, Item 28 (Prepaying Your Mortgage Early). Loan replacement cannot involve borrowing more; the new loan cannot exceed the remaining principal of the old loan.

entries.title: If you need a loan to buy a first home, use a Housing Provident Fund loan first; if the quota is insufficient, add a commercial loan to form a combination loan—do not directly finance entirely with a commercial loan
entries.cost: Costs no money. Requires one or two extra trips to the Provident Fund Management Center or entrusted banks, and loan disbursement may be several days later than doing a commercial loan alone. The prerequisite is that you have already contributed to the Housing Provident Fund continuously for a certain period.
entries.summary: The provident fund loan interest rate for first-home purchases with terms over 5 years is 2.6%, and the interest rate for newly issued bank mortgages in June 2026 was approximately 3.1%. For a loan of 1 million CNY over 30 years, using exclusively a provident fund loan saves about 96,000 CNY in interest compared to using entirely a commercial loan. The amount you can borrow from the provident fund has a ceiling; any shortfall can be made up with a commercial loan, which is called a combination loan.
entries.benefit: The People's Bank of China issued a document on May 7, 2025, lowering housing provident fund loan interest rates, effective May 8. The first-home provident fund loan interest rate for terms over 5 years is 2.6%, and for terms of 5 years or less (inclusive of 5 years) it is 2.1%. For second homes, terms over 5 years are no less than 3.075%, and 5 years or less are no less than 2.525%. As of October 2026, this remains the most recent adjustment. Commercial mortgage rates are determined by adding or subtracting basis points relative to the LPR; LPR stands for Loan Prime Rate. On September 20, 2026, the 5-year-plus LPR was 3.5%. The People's Bank of China's China Monetary Policy Implementation Report for the second quarter of 2026 explicitly stated that in June, "the interest rate on newly issued personal housing loans was approximately 3.1%." Regarding how much can be saved, below is an example calculated using the equal monthly installment (principal and interest) formula. For a loan of 1 million CNY over 30 years, at a 2.6% interest rate the monthly payment is about 4,003 CNY, while at 3.1% it is about 4,270 CNY. That is about 267 CNY less per month, saving about 96,000 CNY in interest over 30 years. If your quota only covers a 600,000 CNY provident fund loan and the remaining 400,000 CNY goes through a commercial loan, it is still more cost-effective than an entirely commercial loan. That is about 160 CNY less per month, saving about 58,000 CNY in interest over 30 years. The provident fund interest rate floor for second homes is 3.075%, which is almost the same as the commercial loan rate of 3.1%, saving very little money.
entries.sources: People's Bank of China (2025). Notice on Lowering Personal Housing Provident Fund Loan Interest Rates (May 7, 2025). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202505/content_7022708.htm>; People's Bank of China (2025). Ibid. (original text on the People's Bank of China official website). <https://www.pbc.gov.cn/zhengwugongkai/4081330/4406346/4693549/2025120618351696797/index.html>; National Interbank Funding Center authorized by the People's Bank of China (2026). Loan Prime Rate (LPR), published on 2026-09-20: over 5-year tenor 3.50%. <https://www.chinamoney.com.cn/chinese/bklpr/>; People's Bank of China (2026). China Monetary Policy Implementation Report, Second Quarter 2026. <https://www.pbc.gov.cn/zhengcehuobisi/125207/125227/125957/2026nhbzczxbg/2026081218435062865/index.html>; State Council (2026). Regulations on the Administration of Housing Provident Funds (repromulgated after the third revision by State Council Decree No. 844, effective September 20, 2026; Article 9, Item (3) "determine the maximum loan amount of housing provident funds", Article 26 "Employees who contribute to the housing provident fund may apply to the housing provident fund management center for a housing provident fund loan when purchasing, building, renovating, or overhauling owner-occupied housing" "a decision approving or denying the loan shall be made within 10 days from the date of accepting the application", Article 27). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2026/issue_12946/202608/content_7079363.html>; Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, Ministry of Finance, People's Bank of China (2014). Notice on Developing Personal Housing Provident Fund Loan Operations (Jian Jin [2014] No. 148, reprinted by Beijing Housing Provident Fund Management Center). <https://gjj.beijing.gov.cn/web/zwgk61/_300587/_300688/375516/index.html>; Beijing Municipal Commission of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, Beijing Municipal Commission of Planning and Natural Resources, Beijing Housing Provident Fund Management Center (2026). Notice on Further Optimizing and Adjusting the City's Real Estate Policies (Jing Jian Fa [2026] No. 400, Part Three). <https://gjj.beijing.gov.cn/web/zwgk61/2024zcwj/436433464/436433467/744089355/index.html>; Guangzhou Housing Provident Fund Management Center (2026). Service Guide for Personal Housing Provident Fund Loans (Standard Provident Fund Loans), Parts 10 to 12. <https://gjj.gz.gov.cn/bsfw/qtfw/content/post_5748060.html>
entries.notes: There are four hurdles to using a provident fund loan. First, you must have contributed enough to the provident fund. The 2014 document issued by the three ministries/commissions including the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development states that you must make continuous, full contributions for more than 6 months before you can apply; contributions made in other localities can be combined in the calculation. Loan quotas and terms vary by locality, and the maximum quota is set by the local provident fund management committee. For instance, in Beijing, the maximum for a single contributor purchasing a first home is 1.2 million CNY, and one can borrow 200,000 CNY for each year of contributions. In Guangzhou, the maximum for a single person is 1 million CNY, with a loan term not exceeding 30 years, and the building age plus the loan term for a second-hand home must not exceed 50 years. For buyers of second-hand homes, the housing price is calculated based on whichever is lower between the online registered contract price and the appraised value; if the appraised value is low, the amount you can borrow is reduced. Finally, there are many procedural steps. The regulations require the provident fund center to issue a conclusion within 10 days of accepting the application, after which mortgage registration must be processed. That disbursement is slower than for commercial loans is the author's experience; if the seller is eager to receive payment, make sure to agree on using a provident fund loan before signing the contract. The down payment ratio for a combination loan must simultaneously satisfy the requirements of both the provident fund and commercial loan sides. Provident fund balances can also be withdrawn to repay loans; see Section 5, Item 3 (The Provident Fund Isn't Just for Buying a Home). Those who have already taken out entirely commercial loans can negotiate with the bank to lower the interest rate; see Item 15 of this section (Negotiating to Lower Interest Rates).

entries.title: If Living in a Residential Community and the Property Management Cuts Off Water, Electricity, Heating, or Gas to Force Payment of Property Fees, Complain to the Local Real Estate Administrative Authority; if You Owe Property Fees, the Property Management Can Only Demand Payment, Sue, or Apply for Arbitration
entries.cost: Costs no money. Making a phone call or writing a complaint takes a few dozen minutes. If the property management refuses to rectify and you want it to compensate for losses, you must file a lawsuit in court.
entries.summary: Property management cannot cut off water, electricity, heating, or gas to force you to pay property management fees; if you encounter this, complain to the local real estate administrative authority. If property management has provided services in accordance with the agreement, you cannot refuse to pay using "I never used them" as an excuse; if you default without paying, it can sue. You can refuse to pay portions that are unauthorized markups or duplicate charges, and if already paid, you can demand them back.
entries.benefit: Article 944 of the Civil Code conveys three layers of meaning. The first layer states verbatim: "Property service providers shall not demand payment of property service fees by means such as stopping the supply of electricity, water, heat, or fuel gas." The second layer: where the property service provider has rendered services pursuant to the agreement, property owners may not refuse to pay property fees on the grounds that they "have not accepted or do not need to accept" the services. The third layer: if a property owner fails to pay on time, the property service provider may urge payment within a reasonable period. If the deadline passes without payment, the property service provider may file a lawsuit or apply for arbitration. The Regulations on Property Management also state that if an owner fails to pay property service fees on time, the property owners' committee shall urge payment within a specified period. If the period expires without payment, the property service enterprise may file a lawsuit with the people's court. For complaints, go to the real estate administrative department of the local people's government at or above the county level; the regulations require them to handle property owners' complaints in a timely manner. The Supreme People's Court's judicial interpretation explicitly provides that if property management expands the scope of charges, raises charge standards, or imposes duplicate charges without authorization, you may raise this as a defense to refuse payment. For non-compliant fees that have already been paid, a refund can be demanded.
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 944; 654, 656). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; State Council (2018 3rd Revision). Regulations on Property Management (Articles 5, 44, 48, 64). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f3cbb3c016f40daebf30779>; Supreme People's Court (2020). Decision on Modifying 27 Civil Judicial Interpretations Including the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the 'Trade Union Law of the People's Republic of China' in Civil Trial Work" (Fa Shi [2020] No. 17, Item 14 modifies former Article 5 of the interpretation on property service disputes, adjusted in clause order to Article 2: "Where a property service provider violates the terms of the property service contract or the provisions of laws, regulations, and departmental rules by unauthorizedly expanding the scope of charges, raising charge standards, or imposing duplicate charges, and an owner raises a defense on the grounds of non-compliant charges, the people's court shall support it. Where an owner requests the property service provider to refund the non-compliant fees already collected, the people's court shall support it."). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/282621.html>
entries.notes: What the law prohibits is property management using the cut-off of water and electricity as a means of demanding property fees. If what is owed is the water, electricity, or gas bill itself, the situation is different. If, after demand by the electricity supplier, you still fail to pay within a reasonable period, electricity supply can be suspended in accordance with state-mandated procedures, with advance notification required. Water, gas, and heat supplies follow this rule by reference. The regulations also stipulate that entities supplying water, electricity, gas, heat, etc., must collect fees from final users. If property management's cut-off of water or electricity causes you losses and you want compensation, you must file a lawsuit in court. First-instance ordinary procedure is legally required to be concluded within 6 months, which can be extended; summary procedure takes 3 months; attorney fees are generally paid out of pocket. For tenants being forced to move out by landlords cutting off water and power, see Item 2 (Cutting Off Water and Electricity, Changing Locks). The benefit rating is moderate based on judgment: property management fees range from several hundred to several thousand CNY a year, and there are no standardized statistics on losses caused by heating or water shutoffs.

entries.title: When Taking Delivery of a New Home, Inspect It on the Spot and Record Issues in the Handover Document; for Leaks and Plumbing/Electrical Failures, Seek Repairs from the Developer Within the Warranty Period of the Residential Quality Warranty
entries.cost: Costs no money. Spend an extra two to three hours on the handover day checking walls, floors, doors, windows, plumbing, and electricity room by room, taking photos for records. Hiring someone to assist with the home inspection costs extra money.
entries.summary: The developer must provide you with a Residential Quality Warranty upon delivery. The statutory minimum warranty period for construction entities is 5 years for waterproof leaks in bathrooms, roofs, and exterior walls, and 2 years for electrical/plumbing conduits and interior fit-outs, both calculated from completion acceptance. The warranty period the developer gives you cannot be shorter than the remaining warranty period provided by the construction entity. If it refuses to repair or delays repairs during the warranty period, you may hire someone else to repair it, with the expenses borne by the developer.
entries.benefit: Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development regulations specify that when selling commercial residential properties, developers must provide buyers with the Residential Quality Warranty and the Residential User Manual. Developers bear quality warranty responsibilities for the properties sold, with the warranty period starting from the delivery date. The warranty period for commercial housing must not be less than the remaining duration of the quality warranty document provided by the construction entity to the developer. If quality defects falling within the warranty scope arise during the warranty period, the developer must repair them and compensate for resulting losses. The developer is not responsible for damage caused by force majeure or improper use. The minimum warranty period for construction entities is set by State Council regulations, starting from the day of completion acceptance and passing inspection. Waterproofing of roofs, and anti-leakage for bathrooms, rooms, and exterior walls with waterproofing requirements, is 5 years. Heating and cooling systems are 2 heating or cooling seasons. Electrical wiring/conduits, water supply and drainage pipelines, equipment installation, and fit-out works are 2 years. Foundation engineering and main structural engineering are the reasonable service lifespans specified in design documents. The Supreme People's Court's judicial interpretation stipulates that during the warranty period, the developer must undertake repair obligations. "Where the seller refuses to repair or drags out repairs within a reasonable period, the buyer may make repairs on their own or entrust others to do so. The repair costs and other losses caused during the repair period shall be borne by the seller." Where housing quality issues seriously affect normal living and use, you may terminate the contract and demand compensation. If the quality of the main structure is verified to indeed be non-compliant, you may also terminate the contract and demand compensation. Inspecting room by room on the delivery day, writing problems into the delivery record, and taking photos is the author's experience. Improper use is excluded from warranty coverage, so for issues already documented at delivery, it is difficult for the developer to argue that they were damaged by your renovations.
entries.sources: Ministry of Construction (2001). Measures for the Administration of Commercial Housing Sales (Ministry of Construction Decree No. 88, Articles 32, 33). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2002/content_70143.htm>; State Council (2019 Revision). Regulations on the Quality Management of Construction Projects (Article 40). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f3cbb3c016f410b40e11333>; Ministry of Construction (2000). Measures for the Quality Warranty of Housing Construction Projects (Ministry of Construction Decree No. 80, Articles 7, 8, 17). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2001/content_60677.htm>; Supreme People's Court (2020 Amendment). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Hearing Dispute Cases of Contracts for the Sale of Commercial Housing (Articles 9, 10). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/282621.html>
entries.notes: Warranty scope and duration must be agreed upon between the developer and you in the contract, with the contract and the Residential Quality Warranty prevailing. If stated to be longer than statutory requirements, follow the longer term. The sales administrative measures also mention provisions from the 1998 quality warranty system; the original minimum warranty periods stipulated therein could not be retrieved, so numbers are not listed here. If issues arise during the warranty period, notify the developer in writing first and retain a copy; this is the author's experience. If the developer neither repairs nor acknowledges it, file a lawsuit in court. First-instance ordinary procedure is legally required to be concluded within 6 months, which can be extended; summary procedure takes 3 months; attorney fees are generally paid out of pocket. For floor area discrepancies and advertising promises not matching reality, see Item 12 (Floor Area Discrepancies). For delayed delivery and delayed property title certificate processing, see Item 13 (Delayed Delivery). The benefit rating is moderate based on judgment: repair expenses vary greatly depending on the property and problem, with no standardized statistics.

chapters.title: How to Live After Developing a Chronic Disease
chapters.intro: Metric: All-cause mortality and money. After a chronic illness is diagnosed, there are often several decades left to live; this section calculates how to manage those decades.

entries.title: Take Medications Fully as Prescribed; Do Not Stop Just Because You Feel Better
entries.cost: Costs no money; instead, it saves money on treating future complications. Taking medication takes only a few minutes each day; the hard part is taking it without missing a single day.
entries.summary: People who take their medications fully as directed by doctors have about half the likelihood of dying during the same period compared to those who take medications intermittently. This figure must be discounted. People who take even placebos fully as prescribed also have lower mortality, indicating that part of the benefit stems from "people who can adhere to taking medication being more health-conscious to begin with."
entries.benefit: Synthesized across 21 studies and 46,847 people (meta-analysis): compared to people taking medication intermittently, those who fully adhered to medical advice had about a 44% lower likelihood of dying during the same period. The raw value was an odds ratio of 0.56, 95% CI 0.50–0.63 (confidence interval). Looking only at demonstrably efficacious treatments, it was about 45% lower (0.55, 0.49–0.62).
entries.sources: Simpson SH, Eurich DT, Majumdar SR, et al. (2006). A meta-analysis of the association between adherence to drug therapy and mortality. BMJ, 333(7557), 15. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.38875.675486.55>
entries.notes: Controversy. This is also one of the numbers in this book that most requires a discount. In the same pooled analysis, even people who fully adhered to placebos (dummy pills) had lower mortality (0.56, 0.43–0.74). This indicates that a substantial part of the benefit comes from "people who can adhere to taking medication being more health-conscious to begin with." The author refers to this confounding factor as the healthy adherer effect.

entries.title: Complete the Chronic and Special Outpatient Disease Recognition First, Then Complete Non-Local Care Filing; Direct Non-Local Settlement Can Then Be Handled for Hypertension, Diabetes, Chemoradiotherapy, Dialysis, and Anti-Rejection Therapy
entries.cost: Costs no money. File a non-local medical care registration on the medical insurance app before departure; it can be handled right on your mobile phone.
entries.summary: For five conditions—hypertension, diabetes, outpatient chemoradiotherapy for malignant tumors, uremia dialysis, and anti-rejection therapy after organ transplantation—outpatient visits in non-local jurisdictions can basically be settled directly by swiping medical insurance cards. You do not need to front the money yourself first and then return to the coverage-registration locality for reimbursement. However, you must first complete outpatient chronic and special disease recognition at your coverage-registration locality, and then complete non-local medical care filing. It only works if both steps are completed.
entries.benefit: Documents from the National Healthcare Security Administration state that this milestone has already been achieved. The verbatim phrasing is "basically achieving county-level availability of cross-provincial direct settlement for outpatient expenses of 5 chronic and special outpatient diseases, including hypertension, diabetes, outpatient chemoradiotherapy for malignant tumors, uremia dialysis, and anti-rejection therapy after organ transplantation." "County-level availability" means it can be handled at the county level. The document also adds 5 new conditions on top of these 5.
entries.sources: General Office of the National Healthcare Security Administration, General Office of the Ministry of Finance (2024). Notice on Prudent and Orderly Expansion of the Scope of Chronic and Special Outpatient Diseases Eligible for Cross-Provincial Direct Settlement (Yi Bao Ban Fa [2024] No. 19). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202409/content_6974467.htm>
entries.notes: The prerequisite is that both tasks must be completed: first obtain outpatient chronic and special disease recognition at the coverage-registration locality, and then complete non-local medical care filing. As for the progress in opening up the 5 newly added conditions, schedules vary across localities, subject to announcements by local medical insurance authorities. For situations where a hospital lacks the negotiated medication you need, see Section 24, Item 13 ("Dual-Channel" Designated Pharmacies).

entries.title: Do Follow-Up Reviews at the Intervals Given by the Doctor, and Record the Metrics of Each Visit in the Same Notebook
entries.cost: Each examination costs dozens to hundreds of CNY. Visiting the hospital plus waiting for results takes some time. The hard part is having to go every so often, making it easy to procrastinate again and again.
entries.summary: Chronic illnesses are about observing changes over a period of time, not values from a single measurement. Measuring blood pressure at home by yourself alone does not demonstrate a reduction in blood pressure as a result. Only when bringing readings to your doctor and having the doctor adjust medication accordingly does blood pressure decline more substantially. When switching hospitals, institutions generally should not make you repeat tests that bear mutual recognition marks.
entries.benefit: What needs to be monitored in chronic illnesses is how values change over a period of time; looking at a single instance is not enough. For hypertension, there is a pooled analysis that combined raw data from 7,138 individuals across 15 randomized trials. Compared to patients receiving usual care, people who self-monitored blood pressure at home had an average change in clinic systolic blood pressure of −3.2 mmHg after 12 months (95% CI −4.9 to −1.6, confidence interval). For self-monitoring alone without accompanying interventions, no effect was observed: −1.0 mmHg (−3.3 to 1.2, differences could be due to chance). With the greatest co-interventions/support, it decreased by 6.1 mmHg (3.2 to 9.0). Co-interventions refer to doctors, pharmacists, or patients themselves adjusting medications based on readings, combined with health education and lifestyle guidance. The author's conclusion is that self-measuring alone does not lower blood pressure; it is only useful when paired with adjusting medication based on readings. These figures are all blood pressure measurements and do not directly look at mortality. When switching hospitals, regulations issued by four departments including the National Health Commission stipulate: where existing examination and testing results provided by a patient meet mutual recognition conditions and satisfy clinical diagnostic and treatment needs, hospitals and physicians shall not repeat examinations and tests. Test reports eligible for mutual recognition bear the "HR" mark, such as "National HR" (全国HR).
entries.sources: Tucker KL, Sheppard JP, Stevens R, et al. (2017). Self-monitoring of blood pressure in hypertension: A systematic review and individual patient data meta-analysis. PLoS Medicine, 14(9), e1002389. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pmed.1002389>; National Health Commission, National Healthcare Security Administration, National Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Health Bureau of the Logistic Support Department of the Central Military Commission (2022). Notice on the Issuance of the Administrative Measures for the Mutual Recognition of Medical Institution Examination and Testing Results (Guo Wei Yi Fa [2022] No. 6), Articles 13, 17, and 19. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-02/19/content_5674575.htm>
entries.notes: Only rated Grade B because direct evidence is limited to a single condition, hypertension, and the endpoint only reached blood pressure, not mortality. Whether "recording metrics in a notebook" itself provides benefits—no studies looking at health outcomes were found. Record at least four things each time: date, metric value, medications being taken at the time, and medication doses. Taking photos of lab reports with a smartphone works too, but keep them all in one place, not scattered here and there. Mutual recognition has exceptions: when a patient's condition changes, results fluctuate rapidly, prior to surgery or blood transfusion, or during emergency resuscitation, hospitals may retest. For how to photocopy and retain medical records and imaging, see Section 24, Item 5 (Keep your own copy of medical records, test reports, and imaging).

entries.title: Don't discontinue standard treatments to try folk remedies or health supplements
entries.cost: Costs nothing, and even saves money spent on health supplements. Takes up no time. The difficulty lies in holding your ground when others repeatedly urge you to try them.
entries.summary: For cancers that were originally curable, people who used only alternative therapies and did not undergo standard treatment had 2.5 times the risk of death compared to those receiving standard treatment. People who used complementary therapies alongside treatment more frequently refused surgery, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy; that is where the excess deaths came from. Some herbal medicines can also weaken the effects of immunosuppressants and anticoagulants; consult your attending physician before taking them.
entries.benefit: Two studies in US cancer registry data looked at patients with non-metastatic, originally curable breast, prostate, lung, and colorectal cancers. The first study examined individuals who used alternative therapies alone, receiving none of surgery, radiotherapy, chemotherapy, or endocrine therapy. Compared to matched patients receiving standard treatment, their risk of death was 2.5 times as high (HR 2.50, 95% CI 1.88–3.27, about 1.5 times higher). For breast cancer it was 5.68 times (3.22–10.04), lung cancer 2.17 times (1.42–3.32), and colorectal cancer 4.57 times (1.66–12.61). The second study examined individuals who used complementary therapies alongside standard treatment. Their rates of refusing surgery were 7.0% versus 0.1%, refusing chemotherapy 34.1% versus 3.2%, refusing radiotherapy 53.0% versus 2.3%, and refusing endocrine therapy 33.7% versus 2.8%. The 5-year survival rate was 82.2% versus 86.6%, with a risk of death 2.08 times as high (HR 2.08, 1.50–2.90, about double). After accounting for treatment delays and refusals, complementary therapy itself showed no association with mortality (HR 1.39, 0.83–2.33). The authors concluded that the excess deaths stemmed from refusing standard treatment. China's State Administration for Market Regulation requires health food labels to state: "Health food is not medicine and cannot substitute for medicine to treat diseases." The US National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NCCIH) clearly states that St. John's wort (Hypericum perforatum) weakens the effects of multiple medications. These include cyclosporine, which prevents organ transplant rejection, and the anticoagulant warfarin.
entries.sources: Johnson SB, Park HS, Gross CP, Yu JB (2018). Use of Alternative Medicine for Cancer and Its Impact on Survival. Journal of the National Cancer Institute, 110(1), 121-124. <https://doi.org/10.1093/jnci/djx145>; Johnson SB, Park HS, Gross CP, Yu JB (2018). Complementary Medicine, Refusal of Conventional Cancer Therapy, and Survival Among Patients With Curable Cancers. JAMA Oncology, 4(10), 1375-1381. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamaoncol.2018.2487>; State Administration for Market Regulation (2019). Press Conference Held by the State Administration for Market Regulation on the "Guidelines for Warning Labels on Health Food" and the "Administrative Measures on Health Food Raw Material Catalogs and Health Function Catalogs". <https://www.samr.gov.cn/tssps/sjdt/tpxw/art/2023/art_4b658b824b1b4b0ba57c09a56cc93aad.html>; National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (2025). St. John's Wort. <https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/st-johns-wort>
entries.notes: Only rated Grade B. Both studies looked only at cancer, tracked from registry data without randomized controls; individuals who chose alternative therapies may have differed in other respects as well. For the calculations on stopping medications for chronic diseases such as hypertension and diabetes, see Item 1 (Take medications strictly as prescribed). If you want to try supplements, tell your attending physician first. On whether it is worth spending money on health supplements, see Section 6, Item 10 (Health supplements, herbal pastes, and tonics).

entries.title: For stable chronic diseases, community hospitals can prescribe up to 12 weeks of medication at a time
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Going to the community health service center and asking whether long-term prescriptions can be written is just a matter of asking one question.
entries.summary: Patients whose conditions are stable and whose medications have not changed can get up to 12 weeks of medications prescribed at once at community health service centers. This saves the half-day otherwise spent each month traveling to and queuing for appointments at major hospitals. Within the same medical insurance coverage locality, the reimbursement rate for inpatient stays at primary-level hospitals is in principle roughly ten percentage points higher than at the next tier up.
entries.benefit: Eliminates the need to travel back and forth each month to major hospitals and wait in line for prescription refills. Within the same medical insurance coverage locality (also called an overall pooling area), the reimbursement rate for inpatient care at primary-level hospitals is in principle about 10 percentage points higher than at the next tier up.
entries.sources: General Office of the State Council (2026). Several Measures on Accelerating the Construction of a Graded Healthcare Delivery System. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202604/content_7065031.htm>: "For eligible chronic disease patients, primary-level medical and health institutions may issue single long-term prescriptions for up to 12 weeks of medication."; same document: "In principle, the inpatient reimbursement rates among medical and health institutions within an overall pooling area shall maintain a tiered gap of around 10 percentage points", and requires higher-level hospitals to establish outpatient clinics at primary levels for common and chronic conditions such as hypertension, diabetes, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease; same document: "Tertiary hospitals shall focus on acute, critical, and complex diseases, strengthen referral, consultation, and inpatient services, gradually and appropriately reduce routine outpatient visits for common diseases and chronic diseases with clear diagnoses and stable conditions", "and extend general outpatient clinics run by specialist teams to primary-level medical and health institutions"
entries.notes: "Eligible" is determined by physicians, generally applying to patients with confirmed diagnoses and stable drug regimens. The medications remain identical; what is saved is the half-day monthly trip and the registration fee. If the primary-level institution lacks the specific medication you need, you can ask whether drug shortage registration and delivery services are available. The same document also requires tertiary hospitals to gradually scale back general outpatient clinics for such chronic conditions and extend specialist teams' general clinics down to the community level. Therefore, those who still treat major hospitals merely as prescription refill stations will find it increasingly difficult to book appointments in the future. If the community lacks your specific medication or you need a specialist to monitor regimen adjustments, you can obtain online follow-up consultations and prescription refills through the hospital where you were diagnosed; see Section 24, Item 14 (Online follow-up consultations at internet hospitals).

entries.title: Before signing up with a family doctor in the community, ask clearly what is covered by medical insurance and what is paid out-of-pocket
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Asking one extra question before signing takes just a minute.
entries.summary: Contracted basic service packages are covered by medical insurance according to regulations. Customized service packages must be paid entirely out-of-pocket. When someone pitches an "upgraded package," first ask clearly whether it is a basic or customized package, whether it has been filed with authorities, and how much it costs per year.
entries.benefit: Basic service packages are paid by medical insurance according to regulations. Customized service packages are paid entirely out-of-pocket; such packages must also be filed with county-level health authorities for the record.
entries.sources: General Office of the State Council (2026). Several Measures on Accelerating the Construction of a Graded Healthcare Delivery System. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202604/content_7065031.htm>: "Strengthen the linkage between primary outpatient payment policies and contracted services; basic service packages shall be included in medical insurance payments according to regulations; customized service packages shall be filed by contracted primary medical and health institutions with county-level health authorities according to procedures, with costs paid by individuals."
entries.notes: The value of contracting itself lies in having someone follow your condition over the long term, not in how many services are bundled into the package. When someone pitches an "upgraded package," first ask three questions: Is this a basic package or a customized package? Has it been filed with authorities? How much does it cost per year?

entries.title: Get a fundus exam upon a diabetes diagnosis, then follow the schedule set by your doctor; get a foot exam annually
entries.cost: A dilated fundus examination costs tens to several hundred yuan. Foot examinations are usually included in outpatient visits at no extra cost. The challenge lies in remembering to get examined even when neither eyes nor feet feel uncomfortable.
entries.summary: When diabetes damages the fundus or feet, there is virtually no sensation until vision is lost or ulceration begins. Detecting it early still leaves room for treatment. For type 2 diabetes, get a dilated fundus exam immediately upon diagnosis; for type 1, start screening 5 years after disease onset. If one or two exams show no abnormalities and blood glucose meets target levels, the interval can be relaxed to once every 1–2 years. Check feet annually.
entries.benefit: Diabetes damaging the fundus is called retinopathy; damaging the feet is called diabetic foot. Both produce virtually no sensation before problems emerge. Catching them early leaves room for treatment. Waiting until sight is lost or feet begin to ulcerate is too late.
entries.sources: American Diabetes Association (2026). Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, Chapter 12: Retinopathy, Neuropathy, and Foot Care. Diabetes Care: "People with type 2 diabetes should have an initial dilated and comprehensive eye examination by an ophthalmologist or optometrist at the time of the diabetes diagnosis." "Adults with type 1 diabetes should have an initial dilated and comprehensive eye examination by an ophthalmologist or optometrist 5 years after the onset of diabetes." "If there is no evidence of retinopathy from one or more annual eye exams and glycemic indicators are within the goal range, then screening every 1–2 years may be considered." "Perform a comprehensive foot evaluation at least annually to identify risk factors for ulcers and amputations." <https://doi.org/10.2337/dc26-S012>
entries.notes: Type 2 diabetes requires an examination right upon diagnosis, whereas type 1 screening begins 5 years after onset. The difference is that type 2 has often been quietly elevated for several years already. If one or two exams show no issues and blood glucose is at goal, the frequency can be relaxed to once every 1 to 2 years. Those with dulled sensation in their feet should inspect the soles of their feet themselves every day, using a mirror if necessary. Kidneys must also be checked annually; see Item 13 (Urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio).

entries.title: If you have had kidney stones, drink 2.5–3 liters of water daily and lower salt intake to under 6 grams
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Turn drinking water throughout the day into a habit. Drink even more on days with heavy sweating; the difficulty lies in remembering to do it every day.
entries.summary: Among people who develop calcium stones for the first time with no identifiable cause, about one-fourth will develop them again within five years if nothing is done. Among those who drink sufficient water daily, just over 10% recur within five years—a reduction of more than half. British guidelines recommend drinking 2.5 to 3 liters of water daily and keeping salt intake under 6 grams.
entries.benefit: A 5-year randomized controlled trial evaluated 199 patients who developed calcium stones for the first time without an identifiable cause (idiopathic calcium nephrolithiasis). One group drank at least 2 liters of water daily, while the other received no intervention. Over 5 years, recurrence occurred in 12/99 (12.1%) of the increased-water group versus 27/100 (27.0%) of the no-intervention group (P=0.008). A smaller P-value indicates that the difference between the two groups is less likely to be due to chance. Mean time to recurrence: 38.7±13.2 months versus 25.1±16.4 months (P=0.016). Baseline 24-hour urine volume among stone formers was significantly lower than among healthy controls: 1,057±238 mL versus 1,401±562 mL in men (P<0.0001), and 990±230 mL versus 1,239±440 mL in women (P<0.001). NICE guideline NG118, Section 1.8.1, recommends that adults drink 2.5 to 3 liters of water daily, and children and young people drink 1 to 2 liters depending on age. Add fresh lemon juice to water, avoid carbonated drinks, and keep daily salt intake under 6 grams for adults. Section 1.7.1 of the same NICE guideline advises considering stone analysis for adults who have had renal or ureteric stones. Section 1.8.3 recommends considering potassium citrate for recurrent stones that are predominantly calcium oxalate. NICE found insufficient evidence for 24-hour urine testing and made no recommendation. The European Association of Urology (EAU) guidelines on urolithiasis take a different approach: every stone patient should undergo reliable stone analysis. Recurrent stone formers are classified as high-risk and must collect two consecutive 24-hour urine samples for specialized metabolic evaluation. Its general preventive goal is drinking 2.5 to 3 liters of water daily to maintain a daily urine output of 2 to 2.5 liters.
entries.sources: Borghi L, Meschi T, Amato F, Briganti A, Novarini A, Giannini A (1996). Urinary volume, water and recurrences in idiopathic calcium nephrolithiasis: a 5-year randomized prospective study. The Journal of Urology, 155(3), 839-843. <https://doi.org/10.1016/s0022-5347(01)66321-3>; National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (2019). Renal and ureteric stones: assessment and management. NICE guideline NG118, Sections 1.7.1, 1.8.1, 1.8.3. <https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng118/chapter/Recommendations>; European Association of Urology (2026). EAU Guidelines on Urolithiasis, Chapter 4 Metabolic Evaluation and Recurrence Prevention (Sections 4.1, 4.1.2, Table 4.5). <https://uroweb.org/guidelines/urolithiasis/chapter/metabolic-evaluation-and-recurrence-prevention> (For the list of high-risk stone formers, see Table 3.3 in the same guideline: <https://uroweb.org/guidelines/urolithiasis/chapter/guidelines>)
entries.notes: Recurrences were reduced by about 55% at no financial cost; by this book's cost-effectiveness calculus, this is the most cost-effective recommendation in this section. What to monitor is 24-hour urine volume—the European guideline targets 2 to 2.5 liters daily, rather than just tracking fluid intake. People who sweat heavily or work in high-temperature environments need to drink even more. That trial was conducted on patients experiencing a first episode of idiopathic calcium stones. Stones have multiple compositions; uric acid stones, infection stones, and cystine stones each require distinct management strategies. Both British and European guidelines recommend having a stone analysis performed. For recurrent formers, European guidelines additionally require 24-hour urine testing before deciding whether to add pharmacological treatment, whereas British guidelines consider the evidence for this test insufficient. Do not quit calcium to prevent stones; see Section 6, Item 21. When an attack involves severe colicky flank or abdominal pain, go to the hospital; it cannot simply be flushed out by drinking more water. Painless hematuria requires different evaluations; see Section 1, Item 27.

entries.title: After a confirmed gout diagnosis, if tophi develop, imaging shows bone erosion, or flares occur 2 or more times per year, take long-term urate-lowering medication to keep serum urate below 360 µmol/L continuously
entries.cost: Allopurinol costs a few to several tens of yuan per month. In the beginning, serum urate is checked every few weeks to adjust the dose; once stable, it is checked every few months. For the first 3 to 6 months, a flare-prophylaxis medication must also be taken concurrently. The difficulty lies in continuing to take it consistently even when there is no pain.
entries.summary: Those who have developed tophi, bone erosions on imaging, or 2 or more flares per year should take long-term urate-lowering medication to suppress serum urate below 360 µmol/L. For those with infrequent flares, whether to start medication should be discussed with a doctor. Among patients whose dosages were adjusted by nurses according to lab results, 95% reached target levels after two years, compared to only 30% under usual care. Medication must not be stopped after reaching the target; dietary restrictions achieve only limited reductions.
entries.benefit: In a randomized two-arm controlled trial involving 517 adults who had experienced a flare within the past 12 months: one group received nurse-led care that clearly explained the nature of the disease to patients and adjusted uric acid to target according to indicators. The other group saw general practitioners as usual. At 2 years, the proportion with serum uric acid reduced to <360 µmol/L (6 mg/dL) was 95% versus 30%. The likelihood of reaching target was 3.18 times that of the usual-care group (RR 3.18, 95% CI 2.42–4.18; this interval represents the reliable range of the number), P<0.0001. Several secondary endpoints in the second year—flare frequency, tophi, and quality of life—were also all superior to usual care. For each additional year of life gained adjusted for quality of life (quality-adjusted life year), the cost was £5,066. The same trial also conducted a follow-up study, sending questionnaires to 438 individuals with an 82% response rate. Both groups self-reported the number of flares over the past 12 months. The median in the treat-to-target group was 0 flares (with the middle half of participants falling between 0–0 flares). In the usual-care group, it was 1 flare (0–3), P<0.001. This range in parentheses is called the interquartile range. The proportion still taking urate-lowering medication in the treat-to-target group was 1.19 times that of the usual-care group (adjusted RR 1.19, 1.09–1.30). The American College of Rheumatology 2020 Gout Guideline strongly recommends initiating urate-lowering therapy in three types of patients: those with subcutaneous tophi, those with gout-induced bone erosion visible on radiographic examination, and those with ≥2 flares per year. For those who have had more than one flare but fewer than 2 per year, the guideline conditionally recommends taking it; conditional recommendations are to be decided jointly by doctor and patient discussions. For those having a first flare, it is conditionally recommended not to start immediately. Exceptions are those who concurrently have stage 3 or higher chronic kidney disease, serum uric acid >9 mg/dL, or a history of urolithiasis; for these, it is conditionally recommended to take it. The practice is to continually monitor serum uric acid and adjust dosage according to results until reaching the target, with a goal of <6 mg/dL. Allopurinol is the preferred choice, also preferred for people with stage 3 or higher chronic kidney disease, with a starting dose of ≤100 mg/day. Concomitant anti-inflammatory prophylaxis is administered at initiation for at least 3 to 6 months. The same guideline also cited a cohort observation of cases: these patients discontinued medication after long-term good control, and after discontinuation their serum uric acid still remained <7 mg/dL. Among them, only 13% (27/211) had zero flares during the 5-year follow-up period. In terms of diet, for people who limit or abstain from alcohol, serum uric acid is 1.6 mg/dL lower than for non-limiters; one serving of beer increases serum uric acid by 0.16 mg/dL. The effects of healthy diets, the Mediterranean diet, and the DASH diet are even smaller. There is disagreement regarding which urate-lowering drug should be preferred. The American College of Rheumatology guideline strongly recommends allopurinol as the first choice on the grounds that when sufficient doses are used, it is effective, well-tolerated, safe, and inexpensive. It also conditionally recommends: for individuals taking febuxostat who have a history of cardiovascular disease or a new cardiovascular event, switch if an alternative drug is available. This recommendation is consistent with the boxed warning FDA added to febuxostat. One of the supporting pieces of evidence is the CARES trial, in which 6,190 gout patients with concomitant cardiovascular disease were randomized to febuxostat or allopurinol. The all-cause mortality risk in the febuxostat group was 1.22 times that of the allopurinol group (HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.01–1.47, about 22% higher). Cardiovascular mortality was 1.34 times (1.03–1.73, about 34% higher). The European FAST trial reached a different conclusion. Enrolling 6,128 patients over age 60 with cardiovascular risk factors, major cardiovascular events with febuxostat were not higher than with allopurinol (HR 0.85, 0.70–1.03). Deaths were 7.2% in the febuxostat group and 8.6% in the allopurinol group. For people taking uricosuric medications that promote renal excretion of uric acid, the American College of Rheumatology conditionally recommends against urinary alkalinization because there is no evidence demonstrating efficacy, with very low certainty of evidence. It simultaneously requires reminding these individuals to drink plenty of water. People with known kidney stones or stage 3 or higher chronic kidney disease should not use this class of drugs. The same guideline notes that the HLA-B\*5801 genotype is most common in individuals of Han Chinese, Korean, and Thai descent, accounting for 7.4%, compared with 3.8% in African Americans, and 0.7% each in White and Hispanic populations. When Asian and African Americans take allopurinol, their risk of developing allopurinol hypersensitivity syndrome is 3 times that of White individuals in both groups. The guideline conditionally recommends testing for HLA-B\*5801 before starting allopurinol in these two groups, with very low certainty of evidence

entries.notes: Controversy: National guidelines differ on which medication to use for lowering uric acid. The US guideline prefers allopurinol, recommending that people with cardiovascular disease switch away from febuxostat if possible, but the European FAST trial did not observe febuxostat to be more dangerous. Domestically in China, benzbromarone remains available; it is a uricosuric drug that promotes uric acid excretion. The Chinese Medical Association guidelines (2019 edition and 2024 update) provided separate recommendations regarding drug selection and urine alkalinization. As for whether taking benzbromarone requires adding sodium bicarbonate to alkalinize urine, the US guideline considers that there is no evidence; act according to the physician's judgment, but drinking plenty of water must not be skipped. **For Han Chinese individuals, it is worth testing for HLA-B\*5801 before using allopurinol**. It is an innate genotype governing immune responses, and the test result never changes throughout one's life. Carriers of this gene account for 7.4% among Han Chinese, Korean, and Thai populations, compared to only 0.7% in White and Hispanic populations. When Asian and African Americans use allopurinol, their risk of developing allopurinol hypersensitivity syndrome is 3 times that of White individuals; in severe cases, this condition causes widespread skin shedding and can be fatal. The American College of Rheumatology 2020 Gout Guideline suggests that these two populations may consider getting tested before taking the drug. **Starting urate-lowering therapy actually makes flares more likely to be triggered initially**, which is why the guidelines explicitly require co-administering a prophylactic anti-inflammatory drug for the first 3 to 6 months. "It hurt even more after taking the urate-lowering drug, so I stopped" is a common failure mode in this matter. What should be done when pain strikes is to add anti-inflammatory drugs according to medical advice, not to stop urate-lowering medication. Different organizations write target values differently: <6 mg/dL is approximately equivalent to 360 µmol/L; lab reports in China mostly use µmol/L. Having high uric acid detected on a routine checkup without ever having had a flare is a different matter; see Section 6, Item 19. For sugar-sweetened beverages and alcohol, see Section 2, Items 7 and 19 (Do not drink sugar-sweetened beverages; drink little or no alcohol). Eating large amounts of meat and seafood in a single sitting or drinking alcohol can trigger flares; see Item 10 (When having barbecue or dining out, avoid consuming large amounts of meat and seafood in one sitting)

entries.title: Those who have had gout: when having barbecue or dining out, avoid consuming large amounts of meat and seafood in one sitting, and drink less alcohol as well
entries.cost: Costs no money. Order fewer meat skewers and seafood dishes and drink less alcohol when having barbecue or dining out. The difficulty lies in self-control at the dinner table.
entries.summary: For people who have had gout, when purine intake over the preceding two days was highest, the likelihood of a flare was nearly 5 times that of when intake was lowest, even while on urate-lowering medication. Drinking two to four drinks of alcohol the day before raised the likelihood of a flare by about half, with beer, baijiu/liquor, and wine all counting.
entries.benefit: A study tracked 633 gout patients online for 1 year, comparing the two days before each person's flare with two flare-free days in the same individual (a case-crossover study). Purine is a dietary component that turns into uric acid in the body. Dividing total purine consumed over two days into five tiers from lowest to highest, compared with the lowest tier, the likelihoods of a flare in the subsequent four tiers were 1.17, 1.38, 2.21, and 4.76 times, respectively (OR, trend P<0.001). Counting animal-source purines alone, they were 1.42, 1.34, 1.77, and 2.41 times. Counting plant-source purines alone, they were 1.12, 0.99, 1.32, and 1.39 times. Examined separately by sex, alcohol consumption status, and use of diuretics, allopurinol, NSAID pain relievers, or colchicine, the results remained consistent throughout. Another study by the same team of researchers examined alcohol consumed in the 24 hours preceding a flare among 724 gout patients. Compared with no drinking, consuming >1 to 2 drinks was 1.36 times (95% CI 1.00–1.88, reliable range), and >2 to 4 drinks was 1.51 times (1.09–2.09). Wine, beer, and hard liquor were each independently associated with flares. For individuals who have not had gout, look to another follow-up study: 47,150 men in the United States were followed for 12 years with observational recording only and no group allocation. The highest one-fifth of meat consumers had about a 41% higher risk of developing gout than the lowest one-fifth (RR 1.41, 1.07–1.86). Seafood was about 51% higher (1.51, 1.17–1.95). In contrast, the highest dairy consumers had about a 44% lower risk (0.56, 0.42–0.74). Purine-rich vegetables and total protein showed no discernible association. Within the same cohort, each additional 12-ounce (about 355 mL) bottle of beer per day was associated with an approximately 49% higher risk (1.49, 1.32–1.70). One drink of hard liquor per day was associated with an approximately 15% higher risk (1.15, 1.04–1.28). Wine showed no statistically significant difference (1.04, 0.88–1.22)

entries.notes: Written primarily for people who have already experienced flares. For those who have never had gout, the impact of diet on uric acid is smaller than commonly thought. Among 16,760 White American adults without gout, dietary habits explained no more than 0.3% of the variance in serum uric acid, whereas common genetic variants explained 23.9%. Therefore, when someone around you develops gout after eating barbecue and drinking beer, diet is merely one trigger; constitution accounts for much more. The studies examined the ingested quantities of meat, seafood, and alcohol, regardless of whether grilled or not; cold seafood appetizers paired with beer count just the same. All three studies were observational tracking without group assignment, what was eaten at the time of flares was self-reported online by patients, and the subjects were all Americans; data on Chinese populations could not be found. That dairy figure is also merely observational tracking; there are no trials proving that drinking more milk prevents gout. Eating less cannot replace urate-lowering medication, as lowering it purely through dietary restriction is limited; see Item 9 (Take urate-lowering medication long term once diagnosed with gout). The accounting for processed meat and alcohol in terms of mortality rates can be found in Section 2, Item 18 (Eat less processed meat) and Section 2, Item 19 (Drink less or no alcohol)

entries.title: Those testing positive for hepatitis B surface antigen: undergo a liver ultrasound plus alpha-fetoprotein test every six months, decide whether to take antiviral medication based on physician assessment, and do not stop on your own once started
entries.cost: Visit a hepatology or infectious disease clinic every six months for blood draw and an ultrasound; costs vary across regions. For those requiring antiviral medication, the National Healthcare Security Administration stated that following volume-based centralized procurement, the annual cost of entecavir dropped to just over 100 yuan. The difficulty lies in continuing to get checked on schedule even when asymptomatic, and persisting with taking the medication continuously.
entries.summary: For individuals carrying hepatitis B virus, having an ultrasound and alpha-fetoprotein test every six months reduced liver cancer deaths by nearly 40% in a Shanghai trial. The more virus in the blood, the more cases of liver cancer developed down the line. When individuals with already severe liver fibrosis or cirrhosis took antiviral medication, liver cancer cases were reduced by about half. Most need to take the medication long term; stopping on one's own easily triggers viral rebound.
entries.benefit: In a randomized controlled trial in Shanghai involving 18,816 people aged 35 to 59, all were infected with hepatitis B virus or had a history of chronic hepatitis. The screening group was invited to undergo alpha-fetoprotein testing and ultrasound every 6 months, while the control group received no screening. Alpha-fetoprotein is an indicator checked via blood test, which frequently rises when liver cancer develops. There were 32 deaths from liver cancer in the screening group and 54 in the control group. Liver cancer mortality was 83.2 per 100,000 versus 131.5 per 100,000. The screening group was 0.63 times that of the control group (95% CI 0.41–0.98, confidence interval), approximately 37% lower. Among the liver cancers detected in the screening group, 46.5% underwent surgical resection, compared to only 7.5% in the control group. In a cohort follow-up study in Taiwan involving 3,653 people aged 30 to 65 who were surface antigen-positive, with an average follow-up of 11.4 years, data were only recorded without group allocation. The more virus in the blood at enrollment, the more liver cancer developed later. For viral loads below 300 copies per milliliter, there were 108 cases of liver cancer per 100,000 person-years. For those over 1 million copies per milliliter, there were 1,152 cases. Cumulative incidence rates of liver cancer were 1.3% and 14.9%, respectively. After adjusting for sex, age, smoking, alcohol consumption, transaminases, and cirrhosis, the pattern of more virus leading to more liver cancer still held true. In an Asian randomized controlled trial of 651 chronic hepatitis B patients with preexisting severe liver fibrosis or cirrhosis, one group took lamivudine and the other took placebo, for a median duration of 32.4 months. Liver cancer occurred in 3.9% versus 7.4%, with risk reduced by about half (HR 0.49, P=0.047). Disease progression was 7.8% versus 17.7% (HR 0.45, approximately 55% lower). The Chinese Medical Association's 2022 guidelines state that individuals with chronic hepatitis B virus infection should undergo abdominal ultrasound and alpha-fetoprotein testing every 6 months to screen for liver cancer. High-risk individuals should be tested at least every 3 to 6 months. For carriers who do not currently require medication, complete blood count, liver function, viral markers, alpha-fetoprotein, and ultrasound should be checked every 6 to 12 months. Once the criteria for medication are met, treatment should be started immediately. For those with detectable virus in the blood, antiviral treatment is recommended if over 30 years old, regardless of whether transaminases are elevated. The same applies to those with a family history of liver cirrhosis or liver cancer due to hepatitis B. The oral medications recommended by the guidelines belong to the entecavir and tenofovir class. The guidelines specify that most people require long-term medication, as the rate of viral rebound after stopping the medication is high.

After centralized procurement, the annual cost of entecavir dropped to a little over 100 yuan". <https://www.nhsa.gov.cn/art/2025/12/29/art_14_19172.html>
entries.notes: Controversy: Some do not accept the conclusions of that Shanghai trial. A 2003 Cochrane systematic review recalculated the data using its own algorithm and found that the difference in liver cancer mortality was not statistically significant (OR 0.81, 0.54–1.22). The 2012 updated version stated that the trial had a high risk of bias, the numbers reported across several publications were inconsistent, and no firm conclusions could be drawn. Therefore, "screening every 6 months" relies on this single controversial trial combined with national guidelines. Lamivudine is an older drug; in trials, 49% of patients developed drug-resistant mutations, and guidelines now recommend drugs such as entecavir instead. Whether to start or stop medication depends on viral load, transaminases, degree of liver fibrosis, and family history, and should be decided by a doctor. For those who are not yet infected, getting tested for hepatitis B serological markers ("two pairs and a half") and receiving vaccination, see Section 1, Item 14 (Hepatitis B serological testing). Hepatitis C is a different disease; see Section 1, Item 45 (Hepatitis C antibody). Alcohol harms the liver; see Section 2, Item 19 (Drink less or avoid alcohol). The beneficiary is primarily yourself.

entries.title: For those diagnosed with COPD, demonstrate your inhaler technique in person to your doctor or pharmacist during follow-up visits; for those hospitalized due to an acute exacerbation, undergo pulmonary rehabilitation after discharge
entries.cost: Having your inhaler technique checked costs nothing extra: bring your medication to follow-up visits and demonstrate how you use it in person, which takes a few minutes. Pulmonary rehabilitation involves supervised exercise training combined with instruction on medication use and self-management, requiring multiple sessions according to a prescribed protocol; costs vary by region. The difficulty lies in adhering to the training after discharge when your body is still weak.
entries.summary: Among people using inhalers, only about 30% have entirely correct technique, and some errors prevent medication from reaching the lungs. Patients who make critical errors have about twice the rate of hospitalization or emergency department visits due to exacerbations. Pulmonary rehabilitation after hospitalization for an acute exacerbation reduces the likelihood of readmission by more than half, and improves quality of life and walking capacity. Whether it reduces mortality has not yet been demonstrated.
entries.benefit: A national sampling survey in China conducted spirometry on 50,991 adults aged 20 and older. The prevalence of COPD was 8.6% (95% CI 7.5–9.9, confidence interval), corresponding to approximately 99.9 million people. Among those aged 40 and older, it was 13.7%. Among COPD patients, only 12.0% had previously undergone spirometry. An analysis pooling 144 studies examined 54,354 patients whose inhaler technique was directly observed in person by trained evaluators. Completely correct technique accounted for 31%, acceptable technique 41%, and poor technique 31%. Comparing the earlier 20 years to the later 20 years, there was no improvement. Among those using pressurized metered-dose inhalers, 45% failed to coordinate actuation with inhalation. Those who inhaled neither fast enough nor deeply enough accounted for 44%, and 46% failed to hold their breath after inhalation. A French observational study without group allocation observed 2,935 COPD patients using inhalers by physicians. More than half made errors in operation. Critical errors that prevent medication delivery ranged from 15.4% to 46.9% across various inhaler devices. The proportion of patients hospitalized or visiting the emergency room due to exacerbations in the past 3 months was 3.3% among patients without errors and 6.9% among those with critical errors (OR 1.86, 1.14–3.04). The executive summary of the GOLD 2023 report specifies that healthcare providers and patients must be taught how to properly use inhaler devices, and technique must be checked regularly during follow-up visits. It also recommends that COPD patients receive vaccines such as influenza and pneumococcal vaccines according to local guidelines. A 2016 Cochrane systematic review pooled 20 randomized controlled trials involving 1,477 individuals, comparing pulmonary rehabilitation after a COPD acute exacerbation against usual care without rehabilitation. Eight studies with 810 individuals evaluated readmission: those receiving rehabilitation had an approximately 56% lower likelihood of readmission (OR 0.44, 95% CI 0.21–0.91), with moderate-quality evidence. However, results varied substantially across studies. Six studies with 670 individuals evaluated mortality: OR 0.68 (0.28–1.67), where the difference may have been due to chance, with low-quality evidence. Improvements in quality of life exceeded the threshold perceptible to patients, with high-quality evidence. The 6-minute walking distance increased by an average of 62 meters (38–86 meters), with high-quality evidence.
entries.sources: Wang C, Xu J, Yang L, et al.; China Pulmonary Health Study Group (2018). (2017). Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbation and inhaler device handling: real-life assessment of 2935 patients. Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease 2023 Report: GOLD Executive Summary. Pulmonary rehabilitation following exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
