BMJ, 349, g4315. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.g4315> (opposing)
entries.notes: Controversy: Opinions vary on when pulmonary rehabilitation should begin. A randomized controlled trial in the UK started rehabilitation within 48 hours of hospital admission and found no reduction in readmissions at one year (HR 1.1). Mortality was actually higher (OR 1.74, 95% CI 1.05–2.88). The executive summary of the GOLD 2023 report states that the effectiveness of starting within the first 4 weeks after discharge remains unclear. Therefore, what should be done is to wait until your condition stabilizes after discharge and follow the doctor's schedule, rather than adding extra exercise on your own during the acute inpatient phase. The Cochrane review also noted that more recently included studies showed smaller effect sizes than earlier ones. Both inhaler studies were observational surveys without group allocation, and no trial has directly proven that "checking technique during follow-up visits" reduces hospitalizations. Specific technique varies by device; follow the package insert and physician demonstrations. For the influenza vaccine, see Section 1, Item 20 (Influenza vaccine); for the pneumococcal vaccine, see Section 1, Item 22 (Pneumococcal vaccine). If you are still smoking, quit smoking first; see Section 2, Item 3 (Do not rely solely on willpower to quit smoking; get medication first). The beneficiary is primarily yourself.

entries.title: Those with diabetes should have their urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio and serum creatinine tested once a year; those with hypertension should also be tested, to detect chronic kidney disease early
entries.cost: Collect a single urine sample to check the urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, and have blood drawn to test creatinine; have your doctor order both together during a follow-up visit. The challenge is remembering to get tested even when your kidneys have no uncomfortable symptoms.
entries.summary: Among Chinese adults with chronic kidney disease, only 10% know they have the condition. For diabetic patients, annual urine and blood tests can detect it earlier. For those found to have elevated urinary protein, starting medications such as dapagliflozin reduces the combined occurrence of kidney function deterioration, progression to dialysis, or death by about 40%, and reduces death by about 30%.
entries.benefit: In China's 2018–2019 national chronic disease surveillance, 176,874 adults underwent both blood and urine tests. Approximately 8.2% had chronic kidney disease, translating to about 82 million people. Among them, 73.3% were still in the early stages, stages 1 to 2. Only 10.0% were aware that they had the disease. Another survey examined 9,672 patients with type 2 diabetes across 45 hospitals nationwide, and 31% had chronic kidney disease. Among these 2,997 individuals, only 27% had previously been screened for kidney disease. The KDIGO 2024 clinical practice guideline for kidney disease states that individuals at risk should be tested simultaneously for urine albumin and glomerular filtration rate (how much blood the kidneys can filter per minute). The highest-priority groups for screening are patients with hypertension, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease. The American Diabetes Association 2026 standards state that patients with type 2 diabetes, regardless of treatment, should be screened at least annually for urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio and estimated glomerular filtration rate. The same applies to patients with type 1 diabetes with a disease duration of 5 years or more. For those with diabetes combined with hypertension and moderately elevated urine albumin (30 to 299 mg/g), ACE inhibitors or ARBs are recommended as antihypertensive medications. Once detected, medications are available. A randomized controlled trial enrolled 4,304 patients with chronic kidney disease, an estimated glomerular filtration rate between 25 and 75, and a urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio between 200 and 5,000. Over a median of 2.4 years, 9.2% of the group taking dapagliflozin experienced the following composite events: a decline in kidney function of more than half, progression to end-stage kidney disease, or death from renal or cardiovascular causes. In the placebo group, it was 14.5%. HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.51–0.72), approximately 39% lower. Deaths were 4.7% versus 6.8%, HR 0.69 (0.53–0.88), approximately 31% lower. The efficacy was similar regardless of the presence of diabetes.
entries.sources: Wang L, Xu X, Zhang M, et al. (2023). Prevalence of Chronic Kidney Disease in China: Results From the Sixth China Chronic Disease and Risk Factor Surveillance. JAMA Internal Medicine, 183(4), 298-310. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamainternmed.2022.6817>; Shi L, Xue Y, Yu X, et al. (2024). Prevalence and Risk Factors of Chronic Kidney Disease in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes in China: Cross-Sectional Study. JMIR Public Health and Surveillance, 10, e54429. <https://doi.org/10.2196/54429>; Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) CKD Work Group (2024). KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease. Kidney International, 105(4S), S117-S314, Practice Point 1.1.1.1, 1.1.1.2. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.kint.2023.10.018>; American Diabetes Association (2026). Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026 Chapter 11 Chronic Kidney Disease and Risk Management. Diabetes Care, 49(Suppl 1), S246-S260, Recommendations 11.1a, 11.6a. <https://doi.org/10.2337/dc26-S011>; Heerspink HJL, Stefánsson BV, Correa-Rotter R, et al. (2020). Dapagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease. New England Journal of Medicine, 383(15), 1436-1446. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2024816>
entries.notes: Rated only Grade B because whether "screening once a year" in itself can reduce deaths has not been directly compared in randomized trials. The mortality reduction figures come from people who were already screened, found to have elevated urinary protein, and then took medication. The magnitude of benefit was therefore judged to be moderate, rather than mechanically classified as large based on the drop in mortality. A single elevated test result does not constitute a confirmed diagnosis; KDIGO requires repeat testing for confirmation. For patients with hypertension, guidelines do not set a fixed interval for how often to test—follow your doctor's advice. What medication to take is decided by a doctor; do not purchase and take them on your own. For the fundus and foot exams required for diabetes, see Item 7 (undergoing a fundus exam). The beneficiary is primarily yourself.

entries.title: After colon cancer surgery and chemotherapy, participate in a supervised exercise program and stick with it for three full years
entries.cost: Exercises like walking cost nothing. Visiting a hospital's rehabilitation department or exercise prescription clinic for physical fitness assessment and an exercise prescription incurs registration fees and examination fees; hiring a personal trainer is extra. It requires spending several additional hours per week exercising, and maintaining it for three years. Those who exercise experience slightly more muscle and joint injuries.
entries.summary: After colon cancer surgery and chemotherapy, participants in a three-year supervised exercise program had about a 28% lower risk of recurrence, new primary cancer, or death, and about a 37% lower risk of death. At 8 years, approximately 90% of those who exercised were still alive, compared to about 83% of those who received only educational materials. Those who exercised had slightly more muscle and joint injuries.
entries.benefit: A randomized controlled trial conducted across 55 centers (CHALLENGE) enrolled 889 colon cancer patients. They had all completed surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy, had high-risk stage II or stage III disease, and had no metastases at enrollment. Enrollment occurred 2 to 6 months after completing chemotherapy, and participants engaged in less than 150 minutes of exercise per week prior to enrollment. 445 individuals participated in a three-year exercise program, and 444 received only health education materials. During the first 6 months of the exercise program, participants met with a physical activity consultant biweekly to discuss adherence and also completed one supervised session under the consultant's observation. In months 6 to 12, this was shifted to in-person or telephone sessions, after which only minimal support was maintained through Year 3. The goal was to increase exercise by 10 metabolic equivalent task (MET) hours per week (a unit measuring physical activity volume) above baseline; any moderate-to-vigorous physical activity counted, and the protocol anticipated that most people would choose walking. At one year, weekly recreational physical activity in the exercise group increased by 15.6 MET-hours, compared with 5.1 in the control group. With a median follow-up of 7.9 years, the risk of recurrence, a new primary cancer, or death was approximately 28% lower in the exercise group than in the control group, HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.55–0.94). At 5 years, the rate of survival without these events was 80.3% versus 73.9%. Mortality was approximately 37% lower, HR 0.63 (0.43–0.94). At 8 years, the survival rate was 90.3% versus 83.2%. Musculoskeletal adverse events were 18.5% versus 11.5%. A cost analysis from the same trial, calculated based on the Canadian public healthcare system, found that the exercise program initially cost 2,917 CAD per person; however, due to fewer recurrences, the 5-year total healthcare cost was actually 1,589 CAD lower per person.
entries.sources: Courneya KS, Vardy JL, O'Callaghan CJ, et al.; CHALLENGE Investigators (2025). Structured Exercise after Adjuvant Chemotherapy for Colon Cancer. New England Journal of Medicine, 393(1), 13-25. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2502760>; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00819208. Colon Health and Life-Long Exercise Change Trial (trial protocol and eligibility criteria). <https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT00819208>; Courneya KS, Vardy JL, O'Callaghan CJ, et al. (2016). Effects of a Structured Exercise Program on Physical Activity and Fitness in Colon Cancer Survivors: One Year Feasibility Results from the CHALLENGE Trial. Cancer Epidemiology, Biomarkers & Prevention, 25(6), 969-977. <https://doi.org/10.1158/1055-9965.EPI-15-1267>; Chan KKW, Chu RWK, Cheung MC, et al.; CHALLENGE Investigators (2026). Structured Exercise Program After Adjuvant Chemotherapy for Colon Cancer: A Cost-Utility Analysis of the CHALLENGE Trial. Journal of Clinical Oncology, 44(22), 2130-2139. <https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO-26-00765>
entries.notes: The trial enrolled only colon cancer patients, not rectal cancer patients, and only those who had complete surgical resection, completed chemotherapy, and had no metastases. Therefore, it cannot be directly extrapolated to other cancers or patients with advanced disease. The primary outcome was recurrence, a new primary cancer, or death. Overall mortality was a secondary outcome, which the authors described as "consistent with longer survival" rather than treating it as a definitive conclusion. There is no ready-made identical program domestically in China, but you can consult an oncology department or rehabilitation medicine department to have an exercise prescription written. Undergo a physical fitness assessment before starting; in the trial, every person completed exercise testing before enrollment. For how to calculate walking volume, see Section 2, Item 11 (walking 7,000–8,000 steps daily). For strength training, see Section 2, Item 16 (strength training). The beneficiary is primarily yourself.

chapters.title: Having Elderly Family Members at Home
chapters.intro: Scope of evaluation: money and personal freedom. When having elderly family members at home, most troubles do not stem from a shortage of money, but from failing to communicate clearly and sign the paperwork in advance. The four items concerning pressure ulcers in bedridden patients, cataract surgery, fractures from elderly people walking dogs, and seeking hospital evaluations for memory loss are evaluated based on mortality rates and are not compared with other items in this section.

entries.title: While the elderly person is of sound mind, designate a future guardian in writing
entries.cost: Executing one at a notary office costs a few hundred yuan. It can be decided with a single conversation with the elderly person. The hard part is broaching the subject: speaking face-to-face about the day when they will no longer be able to manage their own affairs.
entries.summary: While the elderly person is still clear-minded, spend a few hundred yuan to execute a written document at a notary office specifying who will serve as their guardian in the future. Without this document, once the elderly person can no longer make decisions independently, the statutory order takes effect: spouse first, followed by parents and children, then other close relatives. If family members dispute this matter, the guardian will be appointed by the neighborhood committee, village committee, civil affairs department, or court.
entries.benefit: The Civil Code provides that an adult of sound mind who can make their own decisions (legally termed "an adult with full capacity for civil conduct") may consult in advance to agree on who will serve as their future guardian. The counterpart of such an agreement can be a close relative, or any other individual or organization willing to serve as guardian. Once agreed upon, they must "determine their guardian in written form." In the future, when they can no longer make decisions or can only make partial decisions (legally termed "loss or partial loss of capacity for civil conduct"), this designated person will take charge. Without this document, guardianship follows the order specified in Article 28 of the Civil Code: spouse; parents and children; other close relatives; and then other willing individuals or organizations approved by the neighborhood committee, village committee, or civil affairs department. Article 31 of the Civil Code provides that where there is a dispute over who shall serve as guardian, the guardian shall be designated by the neighborhood committee, village committee, or civil affairs department; parties who disagree may apply to the court for designation, or they may apply directly to the court.
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (Articles 28, 31, and 33). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>
entries.notes: This document is called "guardianship by mandate" (appointed guardianship), meaning a person designated by oneself in advance. This person takes precedence over the statutory default guardianship order. It is especially necessary to handle this in advance if the elderly person lives alone, their children live in other localities, or family relationships are complicated. It is recommended to have it notarized at a notary office.

entries.title: Draft a will, and remember that a later will overrides an earlier one, while notarized wills no longer take precedence
entries.cost: Handwriting a will yourself costs nothing. Having it notarized by a notary office costs several hundred to over a thousand yuan. The hard part is broaching the subject: discussing post-mortem affairs with family members.
entries.summary: The law recognizes six forms of wills, each with mandatory procedural requirements that must be met. For a handwritten holographic will, the testator must personally write it by hand from beginning to end, sign it, and specify the year, month, and day. If multiple wills are made with conflicting contents, the last one made prevails. Starting in 2021, notarized wills no longer automatically take priority.
entries.benefit: The Civil Code recognizes six forms of wills: handwritten holographic wills, wills written on behalf of the testator, printed wills, audio-video recorded wills, oral wills, and notarized wills. Each form has its own mandatory procedural requirements (legally termed "formal requirements"). For a handwritten holographic will, Article 1134 of the Civil Code requires that it "shall be written by the testator in his own handwriting, signed by the testator, with the year, month, and day specified." If multiple wills are made and their contents conflict, the last one made shall prevail. Starting in 2021, notarized wills no longer automatically take priority.
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (Articles 1134 through 1142). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; Supreme People's Court (2020). Interpretation (I) on the Application of the Inheritance Part of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (Fa Shi [2020] No. 23, Article 24). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/282091.html>
entries.notes: For a handwritten holographic will, the testator must write the entire document by hand from beginning to end, sign it, and clearly write the year, month, and day. A printed will must have two or more witnesses. The testator and witnesses must sign each page and clearly write the year, month, and day. Heirs, individuals designated in the will to receive property, and persons with an interest in them cannot serve as witnesses. Interested parties specifically named in the judicial interpretation are creditors, debtors, and business partners of these individuals. Whether their close relatives, such as spouses and children, count as interested parties is not explicitly stated in either statutory provisions or judicial interpretations. The author recommends not using them as witnesses to avoid future disputes. Procedural defects invalidate the entire document, which is the most common point of failure. On whether the inheritance of small deposits and real estate after someone passes away requires notarization, see Section 25, Item 12 (do not default to notary services first when handling inheritance).

entries.title: Keep elderly individuals' funds in a separate account, and establish a two-person confirmation rule for large expenditures
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Discussing it once with family members and agreeing on an amount is all it takes. The difficult part is how to broach the topic without making the elderly person feel that you are guarding against them.
entries.summary: Those who scam the elderly often start by giving small gifts, expressing excessive care and warmth, and accumulating sufficient trust before defrauding them of large sums of money. Scammers also frequently urge, "Don't tell anyone." Agree on a rule in advance: for expenditures exceeding a certain amount, inform a designated person first. This way, family members will know before the money is paid, and the decision to pay is delayed.
entries.benefit: In 2022, the Supreme People's Procuratorate released typical cases of elderly-care fraud. It noted that such crimes first exploit small favors and feigned filial care to gain trust, followed by false advertising and promises of high returns to defraud victims of large sums of property. In one case, a company selling counterfeit collectibles sent employees to clean elderly people's homes, chat with them, and even form "godparent" bonds. When delivering goods, they sealed the items in black bags and warned the elderly victims not to open them, with the aim of preventing their families from finding out. The company collected over 1.92 million yuan, and the owner was sentenced to 7 years and 6 months for fraudulent fundraising. In 2023, the Beijing Municipal Local Financial Regulatory Bureau warned the elderly not to believe scammers when they say "don't tell anyone." When undecided, consult more with family members, children, and trusted neighbors or friends, and seek more opinions from family before investing. The U.S. Federal Trade Commission tracked the total fraud losses reported by adults aged 60 and older. It was approximately 600 million USD in 2020, rising to approximately 2.4 billion USD in 2024. The increase was primarily driven by cases with individual losses exceeding 100,000 USD. Agreeing in advance that "expenditures exceeding a certain amount must first be communicated to a designated person" ensures family members know about the matter before money is paid out and delays the decision.
entries.sources: Supreme People's Procuratorate (2022). SPP Releases Typical Cases of Combating and Rectifying Elderly-Care Fraud Crimes (Xu et al. Fraudulent Fundraising Case and Q&A with Journalists). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbt/202206/t20220617_560010.shtml>; Beijing Municipal Local Financial Regulatory Bureau (2023). Uncovering New Scams Targeting the Elderly, Raising Fraud Prevention Awareness, and Guarding the "Money Bag". <https://jrj.beijing.gov.cn/jrxcjy/jraq/ffffjzxkt/202311/t20231127_3310210.html>; Federal Trade Commission (2025). FTC Issues Annual Report to Congress on Agency's Actions to Protect Older Adults (Protecting Older Consumers, 2024-2025). <https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2025/12/ftc-issues-annual-report-congress-agencys-actions-protect-older-adults>
entries.notes: No study has compared how much less frequently families that establish this rule fall victim to fraud. A Grade B rating was assigned because the mechanics of the scams and the recommendation to "consult more with family" originate from procuratorates and financial regulatory authorities. The nature of the evidence is the same as in Item 6 (housing-for-pension schemes). When people become emotionally aroused, they are more easily persuaded; see Item 4 ("I need to go home and discuss this with my family"). For general fraud prevention rules, see Section 8 and Section 13. Do not frame this as "we're afraid you'll get scammed." Framing it as "consolidating and managing family bookkeeping together" makes it much easier for elderly family members to accept. Also, do not hand over all of an elderly person's money to their adult children for safekeeping, as that will spark another category of disputes.

entries.title: Prepare a ready-to-use excuse for elderly family members that they can say at any time: "I need to go home and discuss this with my family"
entries.cost: Costs no money. A single conversation with the elderly family member, taking only a few minutes, is sufficient.
entries.summary: Hard selling and fraud rely on high-pressure environments on the spot, aiming to get you to hand over money before you have time to think. Once a person's emotions are stirred, their desire to purchase items featured in exaggerated advertisements increases, and older adults show an even stronger impulse to buy than younger individuals. Agree in advance on a set phrase with the elderly relative: "I need to go home and discuss this with my family." They can utter this at any moment to give themselves an easy out on the spot, allowing them to calm down after returning home before deciding.
entries.benefit: Both high-pressure sales pitches and scams depend on putting pressure on you on the spot. The Federal Trade Commission's scam prevention guide states that scammers want you to act before you have time to think. During phone calls, they will tell you not to hang up to prevent you from verifying their claims. The solution provided by the guide is to talk to someone—a friend, family member, or neighbor—before doing anything; saying it out loud may reveal that it is a scam. A 2021 risk warning from the former China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (CBIRC) also advised elderly individuals to consult more with family before purchasing wealth management products. One experiment recruited 116 older adults aged 65 to 85 and 115 individuals aged 30 to 40. Researchers first used a win-or-lose game to induce high emotional arousal in some participants, and then showed them misleading, exaggerated advertisements. Participants who experienced genuine emotional arousal showed a stronger desire to buy the advertised items. Regardless of emotional arousal levels, older adults consistently showed a greater desire to buy than younger people. The authors recommend waiting until emotions settle before making financial spending decisions. Another experiment recruited individuals who had previously lost money to mail fraud, most of whom were older adults. Among those who received no forewarning, nearly half immediately agreed when receiving a simulated fraudulent sales call. Among those who were forewarned via phone calls two to four weeks in advance, the proportion agreeing immediately was significantly lower. Agreeing on the phrase "I need to go home and discuss this with my family" in advance gives elderly family members an exit strategy so they do not have to make decisions on the spot.
entries.sources: Federal Trade Commission (2023). How To Avoid a Scam. <https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-avoid-scam>; Consumer Protection Bureau of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (2021). Risk Warning on Guarding Against "Investment for Eldercare" and "Housing-for-Pension" Financial Scams (Issue 3 of 2021). <https://dfjrjgj.hunan.gov.cn/dfjrjgj/yhlj/202106/t20210608_19450856.html> (reprinted by the Hunan Provincial Local Financial Supervision and Administration Bureau); Kircanski K, Notthoff N, DeLiema M, et al. (2018). Emotional arousal may increase susceptibility to fraud in older and younger adults. Psychology and Aging, 33(2), 325-337. <https://doi.org/10.1037/pag0000228>; Scheibe S, Notthoff N, Menkin J, et al. (2014). Forewarning reduces fraud susceptibility in vulnerable consumers. Basic and Applied Social Psychology, 36(3), 272-279. <https://doi.org/10.1080/01973533.2014.903844>
entries.notes: The reason for assigning Grade B is that neither experiment tested this exact phrase itself. One tested the willingness to buy under high emotional arousal, while the other tested whether forewarning works; no study has compared how much less frequently elderly individuals who prepared this phrase are scammed. Use this in conjunction with Item 3 (keep the elderly person's money in a dedicated separate account). Take care of home anti-fall modifications while you're at it; see Section 1. This phrase is meant to provide an elderly family member with a face-saving exit so they do not have to confront anyone directly on the spot; it is not meant to be used to guard against them. When cornered by aggressive sales pitches, the hardest part is speaking up to refuse in front of a whole room of people—harder even than discerning truth from falsehood.

entries.title: Never touch any "eldercare investments" that demand money upfront: membership cards, purchasing beds, buying eldercare apartments, seasonal travel care, and senior product sales are all variants of the same illegal fundraising scheme
entries.cost: Costs no money. Reading the list of pretexts below to your elderly family members takes just a few minutes. Whenever they encounter them in the future, they should refuse outright: do not attend lectures, do not join tour visits, and do not leave a phone number. The difficulty lies in cases where an elderly relative has already attended multiple times and become familiar with the promoters, making them hard to persuade.
entries.summary: Eldercare schemes that require seniors to pay upfront while promising returns are all variations of the same scam. Common pretexts include purchasing membership cards, buying beds, purchasing eldercare apartments, seasonal travel care, and seminar marketing of products for seniors. By legal regulation, participants must bear any financial losses entirely on their own. One perpetrator collected 136 million yuan under the guise of reserving beds in eldercare apartments, defrauding over 2,100 victims.
entries.benefit: The Ministry of Civil Affairs listed five manifestations; recognizing the pretext is more reliable than judging the person. First, operating under the guise of an eldercare service institution: having no physical entity, renting a temporary venue, and falsely claiming to have signed cooperation agreements with legitimate eldercare institutions to trade off their reputation. Second, in the name of providing "eldercare services": selling "VIP cards," "membership cards," and "prepaid cards" to induce people to prepay "eldercare service fees," where the promised services significantly exceed their actual bed-supply capacity. Third, in the name of investing in "eldercare projects": common pretexts include buying equity shares in wellness and eldercare bases, selling fictitious eldercare apartments, long-term leasing of eldercare beds, and "time banking" mutual eldercare, under gimmicks like principal-return sales, sale-and-leaseback arrangements, and agreed buybacks. Fourth, in the name of selling "senior products": product buybacks, consignment sales, consumption rebates, free health checkups, complimentary gifts, seminar marketing, wellness lectures, and free expert clinics. Fifth, in the name of enjoying "seasonal travel care": low-cost or free tours, stored-value rebates, and points-based eldercare. The money cannot be recovered, as explicitly stated in administrative regulations. Article 25 of the Regulations on the Prevention and Handling of Illegal Fundraising stipulates that "losses incurred from participating in illegal fundraising shall be borne by the fundraising participants themselves"; any lost money must simply be absorbed by oneself. In cases officially published as warnings, Dai Mouping and others illegally raised 136 million yuan under the guise of reserving beds in eldercare apartments, affecting over 2,100 victims. Dai Mouping was sentenced to 15 years' imprisonment for fraudulent fundraising and fined 400,000 yuan. Cao Mouming fraudulently raised 13.207 billion yuan in the name of investing in the eldercare industry, involving over 110,000 individuals. Cao Mouming was sentenced to life imprisonment, deprived of political rights for life, and had all personal property confiscated. Seminar sales of health supplements are prosecuted as fraud crimes. Ni Mourong used complimentary banquets, free gifts, and dedicated vehicle pick-up services to pull seniors into attending lectures. Lecturers used "fabricated personas, fake cases, and artificially inflated bargain discounts" to fabricate anti-cancer and cancer-preventive benefits. Seniors were tricked into buying "dihydroquercetin" at dozens of times its cost price, totaling over 620,000 yuan in sales. Ni Mourong was sentenced to 10 years and 3 months' imprisonment and fined 120,000 yuan (National; the Regulations came into force on May 1, 2021).
entries.sources: Ministry of Civil Affairs (2023). Risk Warning on Illegal Fundraising in the Eldercare Services Sector. <https://www.gov.cn/lianbo/bumen/202306/content_6886556.htm> (published by The State Council of the People's Republic of China); Ministry of Civil Affairs and China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (2021). Risk Warning on Illegal Fundraising in the Eldercare Sector. <https://www.mca.gov.cn/n152/n164/c36171/content.html>; State Council (2021). Regulations on the Prevention and Handling of Illegal Fundraising (State Council Decree No. 737, Articles 2, 25, and 30). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-02/10/content_5586632.htm>; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2022). Typical Cases of Procuratorial Organs Cracking Down on and Rectifying Eldercare Fraud Crimes. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbt/202206/t20220617_560010.shtml>; Supreme People's Court (2025). Typical Cases of Punishing Fraud Crimes in Areas Affecting People's Livelihood in Accordance with the Law (Case 5: Ni Mourong Fraud Case). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/482861.html>
entries.notes: Do not judge based on "this place looks legitimate"; judge based on "whether they require you to pay upfront, and whether they promise returns." Eldercare institutions are fundamentally providers of services; as soon as their pitch mentions investment, returns, or capital recovery, do not believe it. The fact that seniors are invited to attend lectures, go on tours, or receive free clinic visits is not illegal in itself and is very difficult to prevent. What can be stopped is the step of handing over money, used in coordination with the two-person confirmation rule in Item 3. If money has already been paid, immediately call 110 or 96110 in accordance with Section 8, Item 2 to request payment suspension. Simultaneously report it to the local lead department responsible for handling illegal fundraising. Housing-for-pension is another track; see Item 6 (reverse mortgage eldercare insurance). For caps on deposits, membership fees, and designated receiving accounts at legitimate nursing homes, see Item 11 (deposits capped at a maximum of 12 months of bed fees). For cases where someone joins a budget tour and gets taken to shopping stores to buy goods, see Section 5, Item 50 (taken into shopping stores during group tours).

entries.title: Avoid all "housing-for-pension" schemes except for reverse mortgage eldercare insurance offered by insurance companies; never mortgage a home to purchase wealth management products
entries.cost: Costs no money. Never hand over the household property ownership certificate to anyone who comes to your door under the banner of "housing-for-pension." Mortgages, guarantees, loan agreements, and similar contracts should always be reviewed by adult children before signing. The difficulty is that door-to-door sales agents are often extremely enthusiastic and visit repeatedly, making it embarrassing for seniors to say no.
entries.summary: There is only one legitimate form of housing-for-pension: reverse mortgage eldercare insurance provided by insurance companies, which is still in a pilot stage. The "housing-for-pension" touted by scammers is completely unrelated to it; it tricks seniors into mortgaging their homes and using the borrowed funds to purchase wealth management products recommended by the scammers. Some victims did not even realize their homes had been mortgaged, ending up with their properties lost while remaining burdened with debts.
entries.benefit: The CBIRC Consumer Protection Bureau made the distinction between the genuine and the fraudulent crystal clear. There is only one legitimate form of housing-for-pension, known as "reverse mortgage eldercare insurance for the elderly." Elderly individuals who hold complete legal property ownership rights mortgage their real estate to an insurance company. The house remains theirs to live in, use, and collect rent from. Any sale or disposal requires the consent of the mortgagee (the insurance company). The senior receives pension payouts based on agreed terms until their death. This business remains in a pilot stage, with relatively few participants. The "housing-for-pension" touted by unlawful elements is "completely unrelated" to the state-piloted reverse mortgage eldercare insurance; it is "a tactic that exploits national policies to generate buzz and publicity for illegal fundraising activities." Its operation involves tricking elderly individuals into taking out property mortgages and using the borrowed funds to purchase recommended wealth management products, "which are often Ponzi schemes paying old investors with money from new ones." The original text describes the consequences: "Some participants did not even know their property had been mortgaged, ultimately losing their homes while still bearing loans." The advisory also provided a benchmark for evaluating returns. The exact wording states: "If a wealth management product promises a return rate exceeding 6%, a question mark must be raised; if it exceeds 8%, it is very dangerous; above 10%, one must be prepared to lose the entire principal; 'guaranteed principal with high yield' is financial fraud." The same advisory also demanded: "Treat the contract-signing stage with prudence, and do not sign blank contracts" (National, June 2021).
entries.sources: Consumer Protection Bureau of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (2021). Risk Warning on Guarding Against "Investment for Eldercare" and "Housing-for-Pension" Financial Scams (Issue 3 of 2021). <https://dfjrjgj.hunan.gov.cn/dfjrjgj/yhlj/202106/t20210608_19450856.html> (reprinted by the Hunan Provincial Local Financial Supervision and Administration Bureau); Ministry of Civil Affairs and China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (2021). Risk Warning on Illegal Fundraising in the Eldercare Sector (Fourth Manifestation: Illegal Fundraising Under the Pretext of Declaring "Housing-for-Pension"). <https://www.mca.gov.cn/n152/n164/c36171/content.html>
entries.notes: The Grade B rating was assigned because these statements come from regulatory risk warnings and empirical assessments, not research trial data. The three benchmark thresholds of 6%, 8%, and 10% are reference guidelines provided by regulators to consumers, not statutory legal standards. The CBIRC has been merged into the National Financial Regulatory Administration, and the original publication page is no longer accessible; the citation here points to a reprint page from a provincial financial regulatory bureau. Losing money on wealth management is secondary; once a home is mortgaged away, the senior is left owing a massive loan, resulting in losses far exceeding the principal. For general rules regarding contract signing and blank contracts, see Section 8, Item 17; for how to stop payments after being scammed, see Section 8, Item 2.

entries.title: If an elderly relative at home is bedridden long-term or severely incapacitated, apply for long-term care insurance at the healthcare security department where their insurance is registered; it is not issued exclusively to the elderly
entries.cost: Submit an application once to the healthcare security department of the insurance registration locality. Then undergo a disability level assessment. For those who pass on the initial assessment, the assessment fee is paid by the fund, requiring no out-of-pocket payment.
entries.summary: Long-term care insurance pays for care service fees and generally does not disburse cash directly. If a household member is severely incapacitated for more than six months, apply to the healthcare security department in the locality where their insurance is held. There is no deductible for care fees; coverage reimburses around 70% for those insured under urban employee policies and around 50% for those under urban and rural resident policies, while bed fees and meal fees are not reimbursed. The policy document sets no age threshold; young people who are severely incapacitated can also apply.
entries.benefit: Qualifying long-term care service expenses have no deductible. A deductible means you must pay a specified amount out of pocket before reimbursements start; here, no upfront out-of-pocket buffer is required. For individuals insured under policies for enterprise employees, the fund reimburses approximately 70%. For those insured under policies for non-employed urban and rural residents, it is approximately 50%. The maximum amount that can be reimbursed in a year (annual ceiling on fund payouts) does not exceed 50% of the previous year's per capita disposable income of urban and rural residents in the local pooling district. Eligible beneficiaries are individuals who have enrolled and paid premiums according to regulations, whose incapacity generally persists for more than 6 months, and who are assessed and confirmed following an application; the initial launch stage prioritizes coverage for severely incapacitated individuals. The document sets no age threshold: unemployed individuals under the age of 18 are enrolled alongside their parents, and those who meet the conditions receive benefits according to urban and rural resident standards. The fund primarily disburses payments directly to care institutions and caregiving personnel; in principle, it does not issue cash directly to incapacitated individuals. Non-care service costs, such as institutional bed fees and meal expenses, as well as medical expenses that should be paid by medical insurance, are not covered by the fund.
entries.sources: National Healthcare Security Administration and eight other departments (2026). Notice on Printing and Distributing the Implementation Plan for Accelerating the Establishment of the Long-Term Care Insurance System. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202603/content_7063915.htm>: Covered targets are "incapacitated persons who participate in insurance and pay contributions according to regulations, whose state of incapacity persists on a long-term basis (generally for 6 months or more), and who are recognized through assessment upon application"; "the initial stage of the system guarantees severely incapacitated persons"; "no deductible standard is set for entitlement to benefits. For eligible long-term care service expenses, where insurance is participated in according to the non-employed urban and rural resident insurance policy, the fund payment ratio is around 50%; where insurance is participated in according to the employee insurance policy, the fund payment ratio is around 70%, with retirees enjoying employee insurance treatment"; "the annual maximum payment ceiling from the fund for insured persons shall not exceed 50% of the per capita disposable income of urban and rural residents in the pooling region for the preceding year"; "except for special groups such as newborns, for circumstances where insurance was not initially participated in when the local long-term care insurance system was launched, as well as re-enrolling after an interruption of payments, a waiting period for benefit enjoyment shall be established... the fixed waiting period for benefit enjoyment shall in principle be set at 6 months"; "the fund shall not pay for non-care service expenses such as institutional bed fees and meal fees, as well as medical expenses that should be paid by basic medical insurance"; "in principle, cash shall not be issued directly to incapacitated persons"; see also General Office of the CPC Central Committee and General Office of the State Council, Opinions on Accelerating the Establishment of the Long-Term Care Insurance System. <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2026/issue_12666/202604/content_7065119.html>
entries.notes: Incapacity must "persist long-term (generally 6 months or more)"; being hospitalized for a few weeks does not yet meet the application criteria. For those who did not participate when the local system was launched and enrolled later, or who re-enrolled after an interruption in premium payments, there is a waiting period before enjoying benefits, which in principle is 6 months. Non-care expenses such as bed fees and meal costs are not paid by long-term care insurance. Medical expenses that ought to be covered by medical insurance are likewise not paid by long-term care insurance. Those who are already receiving work-related injury living care subsidies cannot receive overlapping payments. This funding and the nursing care subsidy under the "two subsidies for persons with disabilities" involve two separate procedures and two separate funds, which do not conflict; see Section 7, Item 8 (the two subsidies). Reimbursement ratios tilt preferentially toward receiving care at home or within the community, meaning one does not necessarily have to be admitted to an institution. This system is being rolled out in phases across regions, and disability assessment standards also vary. First call 12393 or the telephone number of the local healthcare security administrative agency in the insured locality to ask whether the local program has launched and how to schedule an assessment. If the assessment is not approved, do not give up; you can apply again if the state of incapacity worsens.

entries.title: If someone at home is bedridden long-term, treat pressure ulcers as enemy number one: use an alternating electric pressure mattress, turn them regularly, and inspect bony prominences every day
entries.cost: A home alternating electric pressure air mattress starts from a few hundred yuan. Turning a person over takes only a few minutes. The difficulty is that turning must be done every two to three hours around the clock, even through the night, which cannot be sustained by one person alone.
entries.summary: Elderly patients who have pressure ulcers before undergoing hip fracture surgery face an approximately 20% higher likelihood of dying within 30 days. Switching to an electric pressure mattress reduces new pressure ulcers by about 60%. In the ICU, relying on sensor reminders to ensure repositioning is performed on time reduces them by roughly 70%, whereas placing patients in a prone position actually leads to significantly more pressure ulcers. Inspect the sacrococcyx, heels, hips, shoulders, and back every day; if non-blanchable erythema (redness that does not fade when pressed) is found, contact a nurse or doctor that very day.
entries.benefit: In 19,520 older patients undergoing surgery for hip fractures (US NSQIP 2016–2019), those with pre-existing pressure ulcers prior to surgery had a higher 30-day mortality rate. After controlling for other factors, this association remained significant (OR 1.2, odds increased by 21%, P=0.004). These individuals were also more prone to other complications: deep vein thrombosis (OR 1.59), pneumonia (OR 1.39), and unplanned readmission (OR 1.43). The mean length of hospital stay was also 0.4 days longer. In 324 hospitalized older adults (mean age 86 years) followed for a median of 18 months, pressure ulcers independently predicted long-term mortality (HR 1.500, 95% CI 1.059 to 2.126, P=0.020). Independent prediction means that after controlling for other factors, it predicts the outcome on its own. Sixty-five randomized trials were analyzed together (network meta-analysis), comparing powered active airflow support surfaces against standard hospital mattresses (standard hospital bed support surfaces). Powered active airflow support surfaces refer to categories such as powered alternating-air mattresses. Those using them had a lower incidence of pressure ulcers (RR 0.42, 95% CI 0.29 to 0.63, moderate certainty). For powered hybrid airflow support surfaces, the RR was 0.22 (0.07 to 0.66). A Cochrane review of 11 trials with 4,462 participants (updated in 2026) found that when comparing repositioning every 2 hours versus every 4 hours, the difference was unclear (RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.79 to 1.39, very low certainty). Comparisons between other repositioning intervals were similarly highly uncertain. In a trial of 1,226 ICU patients, wearable sensors providing real-time prompts and visual alerts were used to strictly implement 2-hour repositioning, resulting in a lower incidence of pressure ulcers compared with standard care (RR 0.28, 95% CI 0.10 to 0.75, moderate certainty). In a trial of 116 patients, the group in the prone position (lying face down) had a higher incidence of pressure ulcers than the group in the supine position (lying on the back) (RR 4.55, 95% CI 2.31 to 8.98).
entries.sources: Porter SB, Pla R, Chow JH, et al. (2022). Preoperative Pressure Ulcers, Mortality, and Complications in Older Hip Fracture Surgery Patients. JAAOS Global Research & Reviews, 6(11). <https://doi.org/10.5435/JAAOSGlobal-D-22-00117>; Ottaviani S, Rondanina E, Longo E, et al. (2026). Impact of pressure ulcers and frailty on long-term mortality: a prospective cohort study of hospitalized older adults. European Geriatric Medicine, 17(2), 665-672. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s41999-025-01331-8>; Shi C, Dumville JC, Cullum N (2018). Support surfaces for pressure ulcer prevention: A network meta-analysis. PLoS ONE, 13(2), e0192707. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0192707>; Latimer SL, Chaboyer WP, Probst S, et al. (2026). Repositioning for pressure injury prevention in adults. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 6, CD009958. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD009958.pub4>
entries.notes: There are three reasons for assigning a grade of B. First, the two mortality studies only observed that "people with pressure ulcers fared worse later on," which does not equate to "preventing pressure ulcers can reduce mortality." Second, the findings from the randomized trials on repositioning intervals are very weak. Third, while the evidence for alternating-pressure air mattresses is somewhat firmer, the studies compared mattresses on hospital beds, and applying these findings to home mattresses constitutes extrapolation. Daily inspection of the sacrococcyx, heels, hips, and shoulders/back for "non-blanchable erythema (redness that does not fade under pressure)" is routine nursing practice without standalone literature. For care services reimbursable under long-term care insurance, see item 7 of this section. For sudden swelling in one leg managed as deep vein thrombosis, see Section 13, item 11. For prolonged bed rest due to falls or severe injuries, see Section 1, item 34.

entries.title: If an older adult's cataracts have already affected their ability to see the path while walking, go to ophthalmology for surgical evaluation; if both eyes are affected, do not delay the second eye for too long
entries.cost: First accompany the older adult to an ophthalmology clinic for an examination, letting the doctor determine whether surgery should be performed. The surgery is done one eye at a time; many hospitals perform it as day surgery, allowing patients to return home the same day. If both eyes have cataracts, the operations must be performed in two separate sessions. How much you pay out of pocket depends on which type of intraocular lens (artificial lens) is chosen to be implanted into the eye and how local health insurance reimburses it; clarify this before surgery.
entries.summary: When women over 70 undergo expedited cataract surgery for their first eye, the number of falls over one year decreases by about 34%, and fewer people experience fractures. However, the number of individuals who experienced a fall was not reduced. Whether the second eye is operated on showed no significant difference in terms of falls. Older adults who underwent surgery had an approximately 16% lower rate of hip fractures within one year.
entries.benefit: A randomized trial recruited 306 women aged 70 and older with cataracts. Half received surgery on the first eye within about 4 weeks, while the other half waited the routine 12 months. Over one year, those who underwent expedited surgery experienced about 34% fewer falls. The original value was a rate ratio of falls of 0.66, with a confidence interval of 95% CI 0.45 to 0.96. The proportion of individuals who fell at least once was 49% in the surgery group and 45% in the waiting group, showing no reduction. Those who fell more than twice accounted for 18% in the surgery group and 25% in the waiting group. Four people in the surgery group sustained fractures (3%) compared to 12 people in the waiting group (8%). A Cochrane review included this trial and concluded that first-eye surgery in women reduced the number of falls, whereas second-eye surgery did not. A randomized trial on second-eye surgery recruited 239 women aged 70 and older. The fall rate in the surgery group was 32% lower, but the difference could have been due to chance (fall rate ratio 0.68, 95% CI 0.39 to 1.19). In a 5% sample of US Medicare, there were 1,113,640 cataract patients aged 65 and older (2002 to 2009). This study was purely an observational follow-up without control grouping. Those who underwent surgery had approximately 16% lower odds of hip fracture within one year (OR 0.84, 95% CI 0.81 to 0.87). The absolute difference was 0.20 percentage points, or approximately 2 fewer cases per 1,000 individuals.
entries.sources: Harwood RH, Foss AJ, Osborn F, Gregson RM, Zaman A, Masud T (2005). Falls and health status in elderly women following first eye cataract surgery: a randomised controlled trial. British Journal of Ophthalmology, 89(1), 53-59. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bjo.2004.049478> ; Foss AJ, Harwood RH, Osborn F, Gregson RM, Zaman A, Masud T (2006). Falls and health status in elderly women following second eye cataract surgery: a randomised controlled trial. Age and Ageing, 35(1), 66-71. <https://doi.org/10.1093/ageing/afj005> ; Gillespie LD, Robertson MC, Gillespie WJ, et al. (2012). Interventions for preventing falls in older people living in the community. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 9, CD007146. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD007146.pub3> ; Tseng VL, Yu F, Lum F, Coleman AL (2012). Risk of fractures following cataract surgery in Medicare beneficiaries. JAMA, 308(5), 493-501. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2012.9014> ; Desapriya E, Subzwari S, Scime-Beltrano G, et al. (2010). Vision improvement and reduction in falls after expedited cataract surgery: systematic review and metaanalysis. Journal of Cataract and Refractive Surgery, 36(1), 13-19. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jcrs.2009.07.032> ; Meuleners LB, Lee AH, Ng JQ, Morlet N, Fraser ML (2012). First eye cataract surgery and hospitalization from injuries due to a fall: a population-based study. Journal of the American Geriatrics Society, 60(9), 1730-1733. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1532-5415.2012.04098.x> ; Meuleners LB, Fraser ML, Ng J, Morlet N (2014). The impact of first- and second-eye cataract surgery on injurious falls that require hospitalisation: a whole-population study. Age and Ageing, 43(3), 341-346. <https://doi.org/10.1093/ageing/aft177> ; Keay L, Ho KC, Rogers K, et al. (2022). The incidence of falls after first and second eye cataract surgery: a longitudinal cohort study. Medical Journal of Australia, 217(2), 94-99. <https://doi.org/10.5694/mja2.51611> ; National Health Commission (2022). "14th Five-Year" National Eye Health Plan (2021–2025). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-01/17/content_5668951.htm>
entries.notes: Controversy: When pooling the two randomized trials together, there was no significant reduction in the number of individuals who had fallen (OR 0.81, 95% CI 0.55 to 1.17). In whole-population hospitalization records from Western Australia, hospital admissions due to fall injuries actually increased by 27% in the year following first-eye surgery. During the interval between the two surgeries, such hospital admissions were 2.14 times higher than before surgery. Such before-and-after comparisons cannot separate the effect of surgery from the effect of aging. In another Australian longitudinal cohort study, the greatest reduction in the number of falls occurred after the second-eye surgery was completed. Therefore, if both eyes have cataracts, do not delay the second eye for too long. During the period between the two surgeries, be exceptionally cautious when walking and going up and down stairs. Cochrane also included a trial that helped older adults address vision issues, where the number of falls instead increased by about 57%. Surgery addresses whether one can see clearly; reducing falls also relies on Section 1, item 13 (balance and leg strength). For whether bones can withstand falls, see Section 1, item 39 (bone mineral density testing) and Section 1, item 40 (initiating medication once osteoporosis is diagnosed). The National Eye Health Plan clearly states that cataract sight-restoring surgery has been widely established at the county level, so it is not necessary to travel to hospitals in large cities. The beneficiaries are primarily your parents and grandparents.

entries.title: When older family members walk the dog, hold the leash in the palm rather than wrapping it around the hand, keep the leash short, and train the dog beforehand not to lunge forward while leashed
entries.cost: Holding the leash properly and shortening it cost nothing; it only takes accompanying the older adult on one walk and teaching them once. Training a dog not to pull or lunge forward takes time, which you can do yourself or hire a dog trainer for; hiring someone costs money, and prices vary widely across different areas. The difficulty lies in getting older adults who are accustomed to retractable leashes and used to wrapping the leash around their wrists to change their habits.
entries.summary: In the United States, fractures among individuals aged 65 and older while walking dogs numbered approximately 1,700 in 2004 and approximately 4,400 in 2017. Eighty percent were women, nearly thirty percent required hospitalization, and hip fractures were the most common single fracture site. Among patients with dog-leash-related hand injuries at one hand surgery clinic, about three-quarters were caused by the leash wrapping around the hand and the dog suddenly pulling. Therefore, hold the leash in the palm, keep it short, and train the dog not to lunge forward.
entries.benefit: US emergency department surveillance data estimated the nationwide number of fractures among individuals aged 65 and older while walking dogs on a leash. There were approximately 1,671 individuals in 2004 and approximately 4,396 individuals in 2017, an increase that was statistically significant. Among those with fractures, 78.6% were women, and 28.7% required hospitalization. By individual anatomic site, hip fractures were the most frequent, accounting for 17.3%. By broad category, upper extremity fractures were the most common, accounting for 52.1%. Another nationwide US emergency department dataset examined the years 2001 to 2018. Dog-leash-related injuries were estimated at approximately 360,000 cases (exact value 356,746). Of these, 193,483 cases were injuries from being pulled by a dog, and 136,767 cases were from being tripped or tangled in the leash. The injury rate per million population rose from 25.4 to 105.5. A hand surgery clinic treated 443 patients with dog-leash-related hand injuries over a 5-year period. About three-quarters were injuries sustained when the hand or fingers were entangled in the leash and the dog pulled (the abstract reports 337 patients, 75.9%). About one-fifth required surgery (96 patients, 21.6%). According to US CDC statistics, from 2001 to 2006, approximately 86,629 fall-related injuries annually were associated with cats and dogs. Of these, 88.0% were associated with dogs. Among dog-related falls, 26% occurred while walking a dog, and 21.2% were caused by being pushed or pulled down by a dog.
entries.sources: Pirruccio K, Yoon YM, Ahn J (2019). Fractures in Elderly Americans Associated With Walking Leashed Dogs. JAMA Surgery, 154(5), 458-459. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamasurg.2019.0061>；Forrester MB (2020). Dog leash-related injuries treated at emergency departments. American Journal of Emergency Medicine, 38(9), 1782-1786. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ajem.2020.05.082>；Plusch K, Givner D, Wiafe B, Lutsky K, Beredjiklian P (2026). Hand and Wrist Dog-Leash Injuries in the Outpatient Setting: A Review of 443 Cases. Hand, 21(4), 582-586. <https://doi.org/10.1177/15589447241299128>；CDC (2009). Nonfatal fall-related injuries associated with dogs and cats — United States, 2001-2006. MMWR, 58(11), 277-281. <https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/preview/mmwrhtml/mm5811a1.htm>；Rosa R, Buckley RE (2024). Leash-related injuries associated with dog walking: an understudied risk for dog owners? Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association, 262(7), 973-978. <https://doi.org/10.2460/javma.23.11.0608>
entries.notes: Holding the leash in the palm rather than wrapping it around the hand is the advice given by physicians at that hand surgery clinic. They explicitly noted that this protects the fingers and wrists, but cannot prevent a person from being pulled over when a dog lunges forward. They also recommended shortening the leash: with a short leash, the dog cannot build up speed, so the force of the pull is lighter; with a long leash, it is also easy to snag on objects and trip people. When a retractable leash is extended, it becomes a long leash. However, no studies have specifically compared whether retractable leashes or standard leashes lead to more falls; a 2024 review explicitly stated that there are no data regarding what type of leash was being used at the time of injury. Training the dog not to lunge forward while on a leash was recommended by both the US CDC and the authors of the fracture paper. The fracture paper also suggested that older adults who are considering getting a dog choose a smaller one. How much these practices can reduce falls has not been calculated by studies, so the magnitude of benefit is judged as small based on professional assessment. For whether bones can withstand falls, see Section 1, item 39 (bone mineral density testing) and Section 1, item 40 (initiating medication once osteoporosis is diagnosed). For routine balance training, see Section 1, item 13 (balance and leg strength). For whether walking a dog counts as exercise, see Section 2, item 44 (counting dog walking toward walking volume). The beneficiaries are primarily your parents and grandparents.

entries.title: When admitting an older adult to a nursing home, first check whether it has filed a record with the civil affairs department and sign a written agreement; deposits may cover at most 12 months of bed fees and must be deposited into a dedicated bank account
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Before signing the contract, call the local county-level civil affairs department to inquire, or ask the nursing home to present its record-filing receipt. Then verify the agreement, fee schedule, and receiving bank account against one another; half a day is sufficient. The difficulty lies in nursing homes where beds are tight, where family members feel awkward scrutinizing the contract.
entries.summary: Legitimate nursing homes must file a record with the civil affairs department and sign a written agreement with you. Deposits can be collected for at most 12 months of bed fees, and service fees can be collected in advance for at most 12 months. Deposits and membership fees must be deposited into a dedicated bank account opened by the facility at a bank. If they exceed the ceiling, ask you to transfer funds to a personal account, or only provide a receipt without an official invoice, do not pay yet.
entries.benefit: The Ministry of Civil Affairs' Administrative Measures for Elderly Care Institutions stipulate that an elderly care institution must file a record with the civil affairs department within 10 working days after admitting an elderly person. If the materials are complete, the civil affairs department issues a filing receipt. The elderly care institution must sign a service agreement with the elderly person or their agent, specifying the care level, fee schedule, refunds, and liability for breach of contract. For failure to sign an agreement, the civil affairs department orders rectification and issues a warning; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of up to 30,000 yuan is imposed. A 2024 document from seven departments, including the Ministry of Civil Affairs, set caps on advance fee collections. Elderly care service fees may be collected in advance for at most 12 months. The deposit cannot exceed 12 times the monthly bed fee for that elderly person. Deposits can only be used for refunds, advancing emergency medical expenses for the elderly person, offsetting overdue fees, and compensation. Publicly run and publicly built/privately run nursing homes must not collect membership fees. Nursing homes that are not yet built or are not yet able to admit elderly persons also must not collect membership fees. Deposits and membership fees must all be deposited into dedicated deposit accounts under third-party bank escrow; collecting payments via personal accounts is prohibited. Invoices must be issued upon receiving money; receipts must not be used as substitutes. If the agreement is terminated before the elderly person moves in, the nursing home must promptly refund the advance fees collected. If they have already moved in, after deducting the portion already consumed, in principle, the remainder should be refunded in a lump sum via the original payment channel. This document came into effect on October 1, 2024, and provinces may set stricter rules. The 2025 escrow guidelines require that after a nursing home submits a refund application, the escrow bank must refund the remainder in a lump sum via the original payment channel on the same day, or by the next day at the latest.
entries.sources: Ministry of Civil Affairs (2020). Model Contract Database (Model contract templates for elderly care institution services in various provinces, such as Gansu Province 2024 edition). <https://htsfwb.samr.gov.cn/View?id=8377c6f9-b7f8-4cb4-a218-0e5b65de5cce>
entries.notes: Each province may set shorter deposit caps and advance service fee collection time limits; check your province's regulations before signing. Agreements can be signed following the model service contract templates for elderly care institutions issued by provincial civil affairs and market regulation departments, which can be found in the State Administration for Market Regulation's model contract database. Filing is only handled after admitting the elderly person; newly opened nursing homes might still be processing it, so you can ask when they will complete the filing. If refund negotiations stall, the avenues provided by the documents are negotiation, mediation, complaint, arbitration, and litigation. File complaints with the civil affairs department responsible for supervision, which is free of charge. For lawsuits, the ordinary first-instance procedure is stipulated to conclude within 6 months, which may be extended, and attorney fees are borne by yourself. If principal repayment, interest, or investment returns are promised when collecting money, it is no longer a normal advance fee collection; see item 5 (investing in elder care). The beneficiaries are primarily your parents and grandparents. The advance fee caps are written according to documents as of October 2026.

entries.title: If only-child parents are hospitalized, check whether provincial regulations provide parental care leave for children; if so, submit a written application to your employer with hospitalization proof
entries.cost: Free. Searching your province's two regulations on the National Database of Laws and Regulations takes about a dozen minutes. Then submit a written application to your employer with the hospitalization proof. The difficulty lies in employers being reluctant to grant it, and workers fearing offending supervisors by asking for leave.
entries.summary: Some provinces have established nursing care leave for only children to care for hospitalized parents, with the number of days varying by province. Henan provides no less than 20 days per year, Fujian no more than 10 days, and Guangdong no more than 15 days if hospitalized. Henan specifies it counts as regular attendance; Fujian specifies wages and benefits remain unchanged. If the employer refuses to grant it or docks pay, Fujian and Guangdong specify that one can turn to the human resources and social security department.
entries.benefit: Provinces stipulate nursing care leave in different local regulations. The Henan Provincial Regulations on the Protection of the Rights and Interests of the Elderly stipulate that during the hospitalization of elderly parents holding the Certificate of Honor for Parents of an Only Child, the child's employer must grant nursing care leave. The leave shall accumulate to no less than 20 days per year, during which attendance is deemed regular. The Fujian Provincial Regulations on the Protection of the Rights and Interests of the Elderly stipulate that when only-child parents reach the age of 60 and are hospitalized for illness, the employing unit must grant the child nursing care time. The nursing care time shall accumulate to no more than 10 days per year, with wages and benefits remaining unchanged. If the employer fails to pay wages and benefits during the nursing care period, the human resources and social security department or relevant departments shall order payment within a time limit. The Guangdong Provincial Population and Family Planning Regulations govern provincial registered household couples who voluntarily had only one child during the years when the state advocated one child per couple. When they reach age 60, the employer grants the child 5 days of nursing care leave per year. If hospitalized for illness, it accumulates to no more than 15 days per year. If an employer fails to implement the leave stipulated in the regulations, the human resources and social security department at or above the county level shall order rectification. The legal liability chapter of the Henan regulation does not specify what to do if an employer refuses to grant nursing care leave.
entries.sources: Standing Committee of Henan Provincial People's Congress (2018). Henan Provincial Regulations on the Protection of the Rights and Interests of the Elderly (Article 29). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c90e5ba65c68cf70165d0eed8020053>; Fujian Provincial People's Congress (2017). Fujian Provincial Regulations on the Protection of the Rights and Interests of the Elderly (Articles 27, 70). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=4028abcc61277793016128072d0848f4>; Standing Committee of Guangdong Provincial People's Congress (2021). Guangdong Provincial Population and Family Planning Regulations (Ninth amendment in 2021, Article 36, Item 5; Article 45). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817fb1209d017fb5c92e623844>
entries.notes: How to check provincial regulations: search for "Province Name + Regulations on the Protection of the Rights and Interests of the Elderly" and "Province Name + Population and Family Planning Regulations" on the National Database of Laws and Regulations (flk.npc.gov.cn). Check both, and only look at the version marked "Effective". If the province has no provisions, search municipal regulations. Most provinces only grant this to only children; those with siblings are mostly not covered by the text. If the employer refuses the leave or deducts wages, first dial 12333 or complain to the Human Resources and Social Security Bureau's labor inspection division, which is free. To recover docked pay, you can also apply for labor arbitration, which is free, concludes within 45 days of acceptance, and can be extended by at most 15 days. Henan's text says "no less than" 20 days, whereas Fujian and Guangdong say "no more than"; in the latter two provinces, an employer granting fewer days is not considered a violation. A B grade is assigned because days and criteria are determined by each province. The beneficiaries are your parents, while the money accrues to yourself. The days for the three provinces are written according to regulations as of October 2026 and may be revised in the future.

entries.title: If an elderly person's memory is worsening and begins disrupting daily life, take them to a hospital's memory clinic or neurology department for an examination to first rule out modifiable causes such as depression, medications, or poor hearing/vision
entries.cost: Register for a memory clinic or neurology visit, and undergo cognitive testing, blood draws, and urinalysis, taking half a day to a day. Fees follow local pricing standards, and basic medical insurance reimburses per regulations. The difficulty lies in the elderly person refusing to admit they are confused and being unwilling to go.
entries.summary: Worsening memory does not necessarily mean senile confusion. First check for modifiable causes such as depression, improper medication use, or poor hearing and vision. However, very few can truly be cured; genuinely improved dementia cases account for less than one percent. Early screening has another use: while the elderly person can still make their own decisions, settle who will manage their finances and medical care in the future.
entries.benefit: The UK's NICE dementia guideline (NG97) requires that when dementia is suspected, first take a medical history from both the person and a family member who knows them well. A physical examination must also be conducted, along with blood and urine tests to rule out reversible causes, followed by cognitive testing. The guideline specifically identifies four categories to investigate first: delirium (fluctuating, sudden confusion), depression, sensory impairment (poor vision/hearing), and medications with high anticholinergic burden. If dementia is still suspected after ruling these out, refer to specialists such as memory clinics for a definitive diagnosis. A 2003 meta-analysis pooled 39 studies involving 5,620 people diagnosed with dementia. Alzheimer's disease accounted for 56.3%, and vascular dementia accounted for 20.3%. Causes with potential reversibility accounted for 9%, while those showing genuine improvement were only 0.6%: partial improvement was 0.29%, and full improvement was 0.31%. The same NICE guideline requires discussing advance planning with the patient and family as early as possible. Matters to discuss include authorizing others to manage health and finances on their behalf, as well as their wishes for future care. A 2024 action plan by 15 departments including the National Health Commission requires promoting initial cognitive screening for elderly people over 65 and encouraging hospitals to set up memory clinics.
entries.sources: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (2018). Dementia: assessment, management and support for people living with dementia and their carers (NG97, recommendations 1.1.12, 1.2.1, 1.2.2, 1.2.6). <https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng97/chapter/Recommendations>; Clarfield AM (2003). The decreasing prevalence of reversible dementias: an updated meta-analysis. Archives of Internal Medicine, 163(18), 2219-2229. <https://doi.org/10.1001/archinte.163.18.2219>; 15 departments including the National Health Commission (2024). National Action Plan for Addressing Dementia in the Elderly (2024–2030). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202501/content_6996231.htm>
entries.notes: The benefit is rated small because very few identified cases can truly be reversed, and no research proves that early screening extends life. A B grade is assigned because the diagnostic approach comes from guidelines, while the figures only describe the proportion of reversible cases. That meta-analysis included studies up to 2002; the current proportion may be even lower. If medications cause confusion, do not stop them on your own; take the medicine boxes and consult a doctor. Becoming sluggish and having an unsteady gait weeks after hitting the head is a different issue; see Section 13, Item 10 (cranial CT after hitting the head). For hearing aids in response to hearing loss, see Section 33, Item 17 (hearing aids). While still lucid, handle Item 1 (designating future guardians in writing) and Item 2 (wills). If they can no longer manage their own affairs, an application must be filed with the court for determination; see Section 33, Item 18 (applying to the court for determination). The beneficiaries are primarily your parents and grandparents.

chapters.title: Is Raising a Child Cost-Effective?
chapters.intro: This section tallies two ledgers: money and time. Just like calculating the marriage ledger in Section 10, this section only breaks down the ledger for you to see, without drawing conclusions for you. If you are already pregnant and need to handle things step-by-step according to procedures, see Section 27.

entries.title: First, factor in what you can claim: national childcare subsidy of 3,600 yuan per child per year, distributed until age 3; individual income tax special additional deduction of 2,000 yuan per child per month
entries.cost: Free. Apply for the subsidy where the child's household registration (hukou) is located; it takes just one trip to complete. Fill in the individual income tax deduction on the mobile "Individual Income Tax" App, or hand it over to your employer to fill in
entries.summary: For children under 3 years old, a childcare subsidy of 3,600 yuan can be collected each year, tax-free. For those born before 2025, it is calculated proportionally based on the remaining months. In addition, from the child's birth until the completion of full-time schooling, 2,000 yuan per month per child can be deducted from the parents' taxable income. If fully claimed by one party, those with a 3% tax bracket pay 720 yuan less per year, and those at 10% pay 2,400 yuan less.
entries.benefit: The scheme issued by the General Office of the CPC Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council stipulates: starting January 1, 2025, subsidies are provided for infants and young children under 3 years of age until they reach 3 years of age, with a standard of "3,600 yuan per child per year". For those born before January 1, 2025, and still under 3 years of age, it is calculated proportionally based on the number of eligible subsidy months. One of the child's parents or other guardians files the application. This subsidy is "exempt from individual income tax". When determining assistance such as the minimum living security (dibao), it is "not counted into household or individual income". 3,600 yuan is the "national basic standard", and "funds needed for the portion raised by local standards are borne independently by local public finance". The scheme also stipulates that "governments below the county level must not independently introduce childcare subsidy policies or standards"; if provincial or municipal governments introduce other childcare subsidy policies or raise standards, they must file for the record with the competent supervisory department at the next higher level. Regarding individual income tax, the State Council established the deduction for care of infants and children under 3 in 2022. In 2023, it raised this along with the deduction for children's education, both to 2,000 yuan per month per child starting January 1, 2023. The children's education deduction covers the period from when the child reaches age 3 until before primary school, as well as full-time academic education from primary school all the way through doctoral studies. Parents "may choose to have one party deduct 100% of the deduction standard, or choose to have both parties deduct 50% of the deduction standard separately", which cannot be changed within a single year once selected. Calculation example: one child yields a deduction of 2,000 yuan multiplied by 12 months, totaling 24,000 yuan per year. If deducted entirely by one party, a person in the 3% tax bracket pays 720 yuan less, and one in the 10% bracket pays 2,400 yuan less. If both split it equally, deducting 12,000 yuan each, the 3% bracket pays 360 yuan less and the 10% bracket pays 1,200 yuan less. Tax brackets are calculated based on annual taxable income: the portion not exceeding 36,000 yuan is 3%, and the portion exceeding 36,000 yuan up to 144,000 yuan is 10%.
entries.sources: General Office of the CPC Central Committee, General Office of the State Council (2025). Implementation Scheme for the Childcare Subsidy System. <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2025/issue_12206/202508/content_7035435.html>; State Council (2022). Notice of the State Council on Establishing a Special Additional Deduction for Care of Infants and Young Children under 3 Years Old for Individual Income Tax (Guo Fa [2022] No. 8, Articles 1, 2). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-03/28/content_5682013.htm>; State Council (2023).
