Notice of the State Council on Raising Relevant Special Additional Deduction Standards for Individual Income Tax (Guo Fa [2023] No. 13, Articles 1, 2, 5). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202308/content_6901207.htm>; State Council (2018). Interim Measures for Special Additional Deductions for Individual Income Tax (Guo Fa [2018] No. 41, Articles 5, 6). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2018-12/22/content_5351181.htm>; State Taxation Administration (2023). Announcement on Implementing and Enforcing the Policy of Raising Relevant Special Additional Deduction Standards for Individual Income Tax (State Taxation Administration Announcement 2023 No. 14, Article 3). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202309/content_6901454.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). Individual Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China (Article 6, Individual Income Tax Rate Table 1). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf724bd0609>
entries.notes: This is a nationally unified basic standard. The scheme permits provincial and municipal governments to raise standards or issue separate childcare subsidy policies, but governments below the county level cannot issue them on their own. Whether your locality has added to it and how to claim it depends on your province's implementation plan. The three-year total of 10,800 yuan is only a tiny portion of the expense of raising a child; do not treat it as the basis for deciding whether or not to have children. If the individual income tax deduction was not entered during regular payroll periods, it can still be claimed retroactively during the annual final settlement; see Section 5, Item 2 (individual income tax settlement). For individuals whose annual taxable income is already zero, the deduction will not reduce taxes. For those crossing brackets after the deduction, the tax savings will fall between the amounts calculated for the two brackets. When both parents pay tax, letting the parent in the higher tax bracket deduct the entire amount saves the family more money.

entries.title: Maternity leave is 98 days, and maternity allowances are paid by the maternity insurance fund based on the employer's average monthly employee wage from the previous year; paternity leave for men and parental leave for couples follow provincial regulations
entries.cost: Free. The employer handles the filing; you do not need to make trips yourself
entries.summary: Giving birth entitles you to at least 98 days of maternity leave, with additional days for dystocia (difficult labor) or multiple births, during which maternity allowances are paid by the maternity insurance fund. If the employer has not enrolled you in maternity insurance, it is paid directly by the employer itself. Male paternity leave and parental leave for both spouses follow provincial regulations. In Beijing, paternity leave is 15 days, and each parent gets 5 working days of parental leave per year before the child reaches age 3.
entries.benefit: The number of maternity leave days is stipulated by the State Council. "Female employees are entitled to 98 days of maternity leave, of which 15 days may be taken prior to delivery; in cases of dystocia, an additional 15 days of maternity leave are granted; for multiple births, an additional 15 days of maternity leave are granted for each additional infant born." Money received during maternity leave is called a maternity allowance. For those already enrolled in maternity insurance, it is "paid by the maternity insurance fund based on the standard of the employing unit's average monthly employee wage from the previous year." For those not enrolled, it is paid to you by the employing unit based on your wage standard prior to maternity leave. Male paternity leave and couples' parental leave are determined by each province's population and family planning regulations. Beijing: females receive an additional extended maternity leave of 60 days, and males receive 15 days of paternity leave. Before the child reaches 3 years of age, the couple "each enjoys five working days of parental leave per year", and wages may not be reduced during leave. Shanghai: females receive an additional maternity leave of 60 days, and male spouses receive 10 days of paternity leave. Before the child reaches 3 years of age, "both parties may enjoy five days of parental leave each per year", with wages paid as earned for normal attendance. Guangdong: females receive an incentive leave of 80 days, and males receive 15 days of paternity leave. For children under 3 years of age, parents each get 10 days of parental leave per year, with wages paid as usual during leave. Sichuan (2025 edition): females receive an extended maternity leave of 90 days, and males receive 30 days of nursing care leave. For children under 3 years of age, the couple each gets 10 working days of parental leave per year, during which attendance is deemed regular. In 2024, the General Office of the State Council required all regions to ensure that "maternity-related leaves, such as maternity leave, childbirth reward leave, paternity leave, and parental leave, are implemented fully in practice."
entries.sources: State Council (2012). Special Rules on the Labor Protection of Female Employees (State Council Decree No. 619, Articles 7 and 8). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2012-05/07/content_6584.htm>; Standing Committee of the Beijing Municipal People's Congress (2021). Beijing Municipal Regulations on Population and Family Planning (Amended on November 26, 2021, Article 19). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817d99878a017db82d98345523>; Standing Committee of the Shanghai Municipal People's Congress (2021). Shanghai Municipal Regulations on Population and Family Planning (Amended on November 25, 2021, Article 31). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817f3b9178017f4f90542e04f4>; Standing Committee of the Guangdong Provincial People's Congress (2021). Guangdong Provincial Regulations on Population and Family Planning (Amended on December 1, 2021, Article 30). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817fb1209d017fb5c92e623844>; Standing Committee of the Sichuan Provincial People's Congress (2025). Sichuan Provincial Regulations on Population and Family Planning (Promulgated on November 28, 2025, Article 24). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081819aedd63e019b2b65f9852f95>; General Office of the State Council (2024). Several Measures on Accelerating the Improvement of the Fertility Support Policy System to Promote the Construction of a Fertility-Friendly Society (Guobanfa [2024] No. 48). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202410/content_6983486.htm>
entries.notes: 98 days is the national minimum standard. The regulations of the four provinces/municipalities above all add another 60 to 90 days of childbirth reward leave, totaling 158 to 188 days. How much other provinces add requires checking your own province's regulations. Regarding who pays the wages during this period of reward leave, the regulations vary by province. To check the regulations in your province, go to the National Database of Laws and Regulations (flk.npc.gov.cn), search for "省名加人口与计划生育条例" [province name plus Population and Family Planning Regulations], and look for the version marked "有效" [effective]. Paternity leave is called nursing leave in some provinces; childcare leave is calculated based on working days in some places and calendar days in others. The number of days for the four provinces/municipalities above is written based on the regulations as of October 2026 and may be amended in the future.

entries.title: Know this rule: Wages must not be reduced, nor can you be dismissed, due to pregnancy, childbirth, or breastfeeding
entries.cost: Costs no money
entries.summary: It is illegal for an employer to cut your pay or fire you because you are pregnant, giving birth, or breastfeeding. If your child is under one year old, you are entitled to 1 hour of breastfeeding time each day, and the employer cannot schedule you for overtime or night shifts; violators face a fine of 1,000 to 5,000 yuan per person. For how to claim compensation, see Section 19.
entries.benefit: The State Council stipulates: "An employing unit shall not reduce the wages of, dismiss, or terminate the labor or employment contract with a female employee due to pregnancy, childbirth, or breastfeeding." During these three periods, the employer cannot cut your money, nor can they fire you or terminate your contract. For female employees breastfeeding infants under 1 year of age, they are entitled to 1 hour of breastfeeding time each day. The employer also must not arrange for you to work extended hours or assign night shifts. Violations such as overtime or night shifts during the breastfeeding period carry a fine of not less than 1,000 yuan and not more than 5,000 yuan per person. For wage reductions or dismissal, this regulation does not specify a fine; those unlawfully dismissed should go through labor arbitration to request reinstatement or compensation.
entries.sources: State Council (2012). Special Rules on the Labor Protection of Female Employees (State Council Decree No. 619, Articles 5, 9, and 13). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2012-05/07/content_6584.htm>
entries.notes: If you are indeed unlawfully dismissed, see Section 19 for the compensation claim pathway. The key to collecting evidence is written notifications of reassignment and salary reduction, as well as chat logs; keep both of these safe.

entries.title: Calculate the time ledger of raising children by "whose time is consumed", not by "how hard it feels"
entries.cost: Costs no money; what it costs is time. Before the child reaches age 3, basically the entire day is occupied. The hard part is that it is like this every single day; you cannot just grit your teeth for a few days to get through it.
entries.summary: Convert the daily hours of watching the child and the number of times being woken up at night into time. Then multiply this by the hourly wage of the person performing these tasks. The calculated figure is generally far greater than the cost of milk powder and diapers. Therefore, the division of labor should ideally be negotiated before having the child.
entries.benefit: Convert the daily time spent caring for the child and the number of times being woken up at night into hours. Then multiply by the hourly wage of the person doing these chores. The resulting number is usually far greater than the cost of milk powder and diapers. Although no one pays for tasks like caregiving, cooking, and getting up at night, factor them into the cost in this exact way. The calculation method is the same as the framework for calculating housework in Section 10. Agree on the division of labor first before deciding whether to have a child.
entries.sources: Author's experience, no direct literature; for methodology, see Section 10
entries.notes: The numbers do not need to be calculated with pinpoint precision. What is useful is for both partners to negotiate the division of labor against the same table before giving birth, so as to avoid arguing afterward. If your employer reassigns your post or cuts your pay upon returning to work after childbirth, see Section 19, Item 23 (Refusing post reassignment and pay reduction) on how to state your position.

entries.title: Calculate the financial ledger in three stages: ages 0 to 3, compulsory education, and post-compulsory education
entries.cost: There is no fixed amount for how much it costs; it varies enormously depending on the city and the caregiving approach. The hard part is settling down to calculate the three stages of accounts separately, rather than pulling a number out of thin air based on a gut feeling.
entries.summary: Money from age 0 to 3 is primarily spent on how the child is cared for: caring for them yourself, having grandparents care for them, or hiring someone. The stage from elementary school to junior high school is primarily spent on housing and extracurriculars. From then on, it is primarily spent on the educational advancement track. The spending patterns across the three stages are completely different; lumping them together will only produce a terrifying total.
entries.benefit: The major chunk for ages 0 to 3 is the mode of care: caring for the child yourself, having grandparents do it, or hiring help. The major chunk during compulsory education (elementary to junior high school) is housing and extracurricular expenses. After that, the major chunk is the educational advancement pathway. Where the money goes in these three stages is completely different; calculating them together will only yield a terrifying total.
entries.sources: Author's experience, no direct literature
entries.notes: First factor in the money you are certain to receive—such as childcare subsidies, maternity allowances, and medical insurance reimbursements—and then see how much of a gap remains. Do not make decisions based on circulating internet claims like "it takes hundreds of thousands to raise a child"; the methodology of such figures is unclear, and you have no idea what they included or what they left out.

entries.title: Keep separate ledgers for having a child for elders, for marriage, and for eldercare
entries.cost: Costs no money; what it costs is a serious conversation. The hard part is opening up and speaking frankly without talking around it.
entries.summary: Other people wishing for you to have children can be counted as one of your considerations. However, the time and money are billed to your own account. "Raising children to provide for old age" needs a separate calculation, because it gambles on another person's financial capacity and willingness twenty years from now. Write down the consequences of not having children as well, and compare both sides.
entries.benefit: The thinking is the same as in Section 10. Other people's expectations can be factored in as one of your considerations. But the costs must be recorded on your own ledger, not theirs. "Raising children to provide for old age" especially requires a separate calculation, because it assumes the financial capability and willingness of another human being twenty years down the line.
entries.sources: Author's experience, no direct literature; for similar analysis, see Section 10
entries.notes: Write down the "consequences of not having children" as well, and compare them side by side with the "consequences of having children". Only writing down one side of the ledger is not accounting.

entries.title: If planning to have children a few years later, first factor in the woman's age: the chances of natural conception and the success rate of IVF both decline significantly around age 40
entries.cost: Costs no money; what it costs is a serious conversation. The hard part is lining up childbearing alongside work and homebuying plans, rather than merely pushing it back.
entries.summary: The older the woman, the harder it is to conceive naturally; in one's early 40s, the monthly probability of conceiving is only about half that of one's early 30s. The proportion of miscarriages after conceiving also climbs upward, reaching about one-third between ages 40 and 44. Turning to IVF does not fully compensate either: at ages 43 and 44, only about 5% of embryo transfers result in a live birth.
entries.benefit: For natural pregnancy, look at a prospective follow-up study in the US that recruited women aged 30 to 44 who had no history of infertility and were just beginning to try to conceive. Compared with ages 30 and 31, the monthly probability of conceiving at ages 40 and 41 was about 53% lower (ratio 0.47, 95% CI 0.28–0.78), and at ages 42 to 44 it was about 59% lower (0.39, 0.16–0.93). At ages 38 and 39 it was about 30% lower (0.70, 0.48–1.01), with the confidence interval just touching "no difference". There was no difference between ages 32–33 and 30–31. For women who had never been pregnant before, the probability of conceiving was lower at every age. In a similar Danish study, the probability for women aged 35 to 40 was 0.77 of that for women aged 20 to 24. The impact of paternal age was much smaller, being 0.95 for men aged 35 to 39. For miscarriage, look at registry data from Norway on approximately 420,000 pregnancies between 2009 and 2013: the miscarriage rate was lowest at ages 25 to 29, at 9.8%. It was 10.8% at ages 30 to 34, 16.7% at ages 35 to 39, 32.2% at ages 40 to 44, and 53.6% for age 45 and above. For embryonic chromosomes, look at tests performed by a US reproductive center on 15,169 IVF embryos. Chromosomal abnormalities rose steadily with age after age 26. Among IVF patients aged 26 to 37, those whose cultured embryos all showed chromosomal abnormalities accounted for 2% to 6%, compared to 33% at age 42 and 53% at age 44. For IVF success rates, look at the preliminary 2022 statistics from the UK fertility regulator. For treatments using own eggs and fresh embryo transfers, the proportion of live births per embryo transferred was: 35% for ages 18 to 34, 26% for ages 35 to 37, 18% for ages 38 and 39, 10% for ages 40 to 42, and 5% for ages 43 and 44. Domestic regulations: The Ministry of Health's 2003 "Norms for Human Assisted Reproductive Technology" explicitly states that "it is prohibited to perform human assisted reproductive technology on couples and single women who do not comply with the national population and family planning laws and regulations". In 2024, the General Office of the State Council mandated localities to include appropriate assisted reproductive technology services within medical insurance coverage. In July 2025, the National Healthcare Security Administration stated that all 31 provinces and the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps had fully incorporated assisted reproductive technology into coverage, with over 1 million person-times enjoying benefits in 2024.
entries.sources: Steiner AZ, Jukic AM (2016). Impact of female age and nulligravidity on fecundity in an older reproductive age cohort. Fertility and Sterility 105(6):1584-1588. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fertnstert.2016.02.028>; Rothman KJ et al. (2013). Volitional determinants and age-related decline in fecundability: a general population prospective cohort study in Denmark. Fertility and Sterility 99(7):1958-1964. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fertnstert.2013.02.040>; Magnus MC et al. (2019). Role of maternal age and pregnancy history in risk of miscarriage: prospective register based study. BMJ 364:l869 (Table 1). <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.l869>; Franasiak JM et al. (2014). The nature of aneuploidy with increasing age of the female partner: a review of 15,169 consecutive trophectoderm biopsies evaluated with comprehensive chromosomal screening. Fertility and Sterility 101(3):656-663. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fertnstert.2013.11.004>; Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority (2024). Fertility treatment 2022: preliminary trends and figures. <https://www.hfea.gov.uk/about-us/publications/research-and-data/fertility-treatment-2022-preliminary-trends-and-figures/>; Ministry of Health (2003). Norms for Human Assisted Reproductive Technology (Annex to Weikejiaofa [2003] No. 176, Section III, Code of Conduct for Technical Personnel, Item 13). <https://www.nhc.gov.cn/wjw/gfxwj/200309/8da11b0f3edb49cbbe5dea1dc18794a9/files/1733388793099_97897.doc>; General Office of the State Council (2024). Several Measures on Accelerating the Improvement of the Fertility Support Policy System to Promote the Construction of a Fertility-Friendly Society (Guobanfa [2024] No. 48). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202410/content_6983486.htm>; State Council Information Office (2025). Press Conference of the State Council Information Office on the Childcare Subsidy System and Fertility Support Measures (Q&A with the Head of the Department of Healthcare Security of the National Healthcare Security Administration). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202507/content_7034595.htm>
entries.notes: This does not advocate who should have children early or late; it simply lays out the age factor to examine together with the financial ledger in Item 5 and the time ledger in Item 4. These are all averages from large cohorts of people and vary widely when applied to an individual; to find out your own situation, consult a hospital's reproductive medicine department. Single women cannot access assisted reproductive technology in formal domestic hospitals in China. Which assisted reproductive items are covered by medical insurance and how much is reimbursed vary by province; consult your local healthcare security administration. Once you decide to have a child, start reading from Section 27, Item 1 (Folic acid supplementation) for what to do next.

chapters.title: Employment, Resignation, and Work-Related Injuries
chapters.intro:
This section calculates money: how money is calculated, how to sign your name, and how deadlines are calculated. The first three items cover money you should receive while still in your position, the middle five items cover leaving a job, and the subsequent seven items cover occupational diseases and work-related injuries. Money for work-related injuries is an order of magnitude larger than severance for being laid off, and the statutory time limits are much stricter. The physical damage caused by occupational diseases simply cannot be replaced. At the end of the section, there are nine additional items. Among them, the first four discuss what to do when bullied at work, how to request a certificate of employment termination, how individual income tax on severance pay is calculated, and how social security accounts are transferred when relocating to work in another city. The middle three items discuss double wages for not signing a contract, employers failing to pay social insurance, and facing demands for liquidated damages upon leaving. The final two items address how to express your stance when an employer wants to reassign your post or cut your pay, and whom to turn to for the wages and compensation of labor dispatch workers.

Entries in this section are grouped by topic into the following blocks, with item numbers in parentheses.

**Contracts and Money While in Your Position**: Overtime pay (Item 1), annual leave (Item 2), probation periods (Item 3), double wages for failure to sign a written labor contract (Item 20), failure to pay or underpaying social insurance (Item 21), stating objections in writing if disagreeing with post reassignment or wage cuts (Item 23), equal pay for equal work for dispatched workers (Item 24), long-term workplace bullying (Item 16).

**Resignation and Layoffs**: Calculating N first when laid off (Item 4), failure to give 30 days' advance notice (Item 5), compensation for unlawful termination (Item 6), do not sign "voluntary resignation due to personal reasons" (Item 7), preserving evidence prior to leaving (Item 8), certificate of employment termination (Item 17), individual income tax on severance pay (Item 18), being asked for liquidated damages upon leaving (Item 22), transferring social security accounts to the new insured location (Item 19).

**Occupational Diseases and Work-Related Injuries**: Three occupational health examinations (Item 9), protective equipment must be provided by the employer (Item 10), applying for work-related injury determination (Item 11), calling 120 first upon sudden discomfort (Item 12), unpaid work-related injury insurance (Item 13), appraisal of labor capacity (Item 14), three payments for work-related death (Item 15).

entries.title: Overtime pay is calculated across three tiers at 1.5x, 2x, and 3x; if not paid, file a complaint with labor supervision, and overdue payments incur an extra 50% to 100%
entries.cost: Costs no money. In regular times, routinely save a copy of clock-in records, shift rosters, and overtime approval forms, and take screenshots of messages from leaders assigning tasks in work group chats. The hard part is remembering to save them every month.
entries.summary: Regular overtime is paid at 1.5 times wages, and rest day overtime where no compensatory time off is arranged is paid at 2 times. Working on statutory holidays such as New Year's Day, Spring Festival, Labor Day, and National Day is paid at 3 times, and the statutory provisions contain no option to substitute this with compensatory time off. If the company fails to pay, file a complaint with labor supervision. If they still do not pay after being ordered to pay within a specified time limit, the employer must pay an additional indemnity of 50% to 100% of the arrears.
entries.benefit: The statutory normal working hours are no more than 8 hours per day and an average of no more than 44 hours per week. Regular overtime generally must not exceed 1 hour per day. Where longer hours are required for special reasons, it must not exceed 3 hours per day, and the cumulative total must not exceed 36 hours in a month. Overtime pay is divided into three tiers. If you are arranged to work extended hours on regular working days, pay is not less than 150% of wages. If you are arranged to work on rest days and no compensatory time off can be arranged, not less than 200%. If you are arranged to work on statutory holidays, not less than 300%. For the statutory holiday tier, the statutory provisions contain no option to "substitute with compensatory time off". Where an employer arranges overtime but fails to pay overtime pay, the labor administrative department shall order it to pay within a specified time limit. If it fails to pay after the time limit, it shall be ordered to pay additional compensation to the employee of not less than 50% and not more than 100% of the payable amount on top of the arrears (nationwide). To check which days are statutory holidays, see Article 2 of the State Council's Measures on National Holidays: New Year's Day (1 day), Spring Festival (4 days), Qingming Festival (1 day), Labor Day (2 days), Dragon Boat Festival (1 day), Mid-Autumn Festival (1 day), and National Day (3 days). Article 7 of the holiday measures permits "unified holiday shifts and swaps", connecting these days with weekends into longer holidays.
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). Labor Law (Second Amendment of 2018, Articles 36, 41, 43, 44). <https://www.samr.gov.cn/zw/zfxxgk/fdzdgknr/bgt/art/2023/art_d9aa750028b14b99a776cb93726a360d.html> (Published by the State Administration for Market Regulation); Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Labor Contract Law (Article 85, Item 3). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm>; State Council (2024). Measures for National Holidays and Memorial Days (Revised by State Council Order No. 795, effective January 1, 2025, Articles 2 and 7). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2024/issue_11726/202411/content_6989774.html>
entries.notes: Rest days and statutory public holidays must be calculated separately. Across the entire year, statutory public holidays only include those specific statutory days for New Year's Day, Spring Festival, Labor Day, National Day, etc. In consecutive holiday stretches pieced together by swapping rest days, the days that are not the actual festival day listed in the holiday measures are calculated according to the rest day tier: if compensatory time off can be arranged, it may be arranged; if it cannot be compensated with time off, pay 200%. This is derived from Article 2 of the holiday measures and Article 44 of the Labor Law. Statements like "company policy requires overtime to be pre-approved" or "I stayed voluntarily" do not mean the company can get away with not paying, but they will make it harder for you to produce evidence, so keep records of assigned tasks and approval requests. If a company wants to implement special working hour arrangements like comprehensive calculation of working hours or non-standard working hours, it must first obtain approval from the labor administrative department—it is not up to the company to decide on its own. For the statute of limitations for labor dispute arbitration, see Section 8, Item 19.

entries.title: Annual leave is calculated at 5, 10, or 15 days based on cumulative work experience; untaken leave is converted to pay at 300% of daily wage
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Add up all the years you have worked across all employers; your social insurance contribution records serve as proof. The difficulty lies in managing not to sign when the company hands you a "voluntary waiver of annual leave" form.
entries.summary: If your cumulative work experience across all employers is at least 1 year but less than 10 years, you get 5 days of annual leave per year. Reaching 10 years gives 10 days, and reaching 20 years gives 15 days; it continues to accumulate even if you have changed jobs. If the employer cannot arrange it and you agree not to take it, those days are paid at 3 times your daily wage. Once you sign a "voluntary waiver of annual leave" form, only your regular wages remain.
entries.benefit: Having worked continuously for 12 months entitles you to annual leave. The number of days is determined by **cumulative** working time, adding up all the years worked across all employers. At least 1 year but less than 10 years gives 5 days; at least 10 years but less than 20 years gives 10 days; 20 years or more gives 15 days. National statutory public holidays and rest days are not counted toward annual leave days. If the employer genuinely cannot arrange the leave due to operational needs and obtains your consent not to take it, for those days that should have been taken but were not, it must "pay annual leave wage remuneration at 300% of the employee's daily wage income." This 300% already includes the single daily wage that should have been paid for working normally on that day, so what you actually receive extra is 200%. Daily wage = personal monthly wage ÷ 21.75. The monthly wage is calculated based on the wages of the 12 months prior to the payment of this sum, taking the monthly average after excluding overtime pay. For those who joined the employer in the current calendar year, it is converted proportionally based on the remaining calendar days at that employer. Upon resignation, it is prorated and settled based on how long you have worked in the current year; any leave already taken in excess will not be deducted back. If an employer neither arranges leave nor pays the remuneration, it will be ordered to rectify within a specified time limit. If it fails to rectify past the deadline, in addition to that annual leave wage remuneration, it must pay an additional compensation fee of the same amount (Nationwide, effective January 1, 2008)
entries.sources: State Council (2007). Regulations on Paid Annual Leave for Employees (State Council Order No. 514, Articles 2, 3, 4, 5, 7). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2008/content_859865.htm>; Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2008). Implementation Measures for Paid Annual Leave of Enterprise Employees (MOHRSS Order No. 1, Articles 3, 4, 5, 10, 11, 12, 15). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2009/content_1265995.htm>
entries.notes: Cumulative working time must be added up across employers; if you have changed jobs, do not calculate it solely based on seniority at your current employer. **Only when an employee "proposes in writing not to take leave due to personal reasons" may the employer pay only regular wages**, so do not sign the "voluntary waiver of annual leave" form. If you take personal leave totaling 20 days or more in a year and the employer does not deduct your salary, you will not be entitled to annual leave for that year. Nor are you entitled to it if sick leave exceeds the corresponding number of months: 2 months for work experience under 10 years, 3 months for 10 to 20 years, and 4 months for 20 years or more. Home visit leave, marriage or bereavement leave, maternity leave, and the period of suspension of work with pay for work-related injury are not counted into annual leave.

entries.title: Probation periods have statutory caps, wages must not fall below 80%, and probation can only be agreed upon once
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Spend a few minutes before signing to cross-check the contract term written against the length of the probation period.
entries.summary: For contracts signed for 3 months to 1 year, the probation period can be at most 1 month; for 1 to 3 years, at most 2 months; for more than 3 years, at most 6 months. The same company can only put you on probation once; moving you to another role after confirmation and doing it again is illegal. Probation wages cannot be lower than the lowest grade for the same position or 80% of the wage agreed upon in the contract, nor lower than the local minimum wage.
entries.benefit: For contracts signed for 3 months or more but less than 1 year, the probation period may not exceed 1 month. For contracts signed for 1 year or more but less than 3 years, it may not exceed 2 months. For contracts signed for 3 years or more, as well as open-ended contracts without a stated expiration date, it may not exceed 6 months. Contracts with a term based on the completion of a specific task, or contracts with a total duration of less than 3 months, are not permitted to set a probation period. "The same employer and the same employee may agree upon a probation period only once"—the same company can only test the same person once. If a contract only specifies a probation period, that probation period does not hold, and that duration constitutes the term of the labor contract. Probation wages "shall not be lower than the minimum wage rate for the same post in the employing entity or 80 percent of the wage agreed upon in the labor contract, and shall not be lower than the minimum wage standard of the place where the employing entity is located." If the probation period agreed upon exceeds the statutory length and the employee has actually worked it, the employer must pay an additional compensation fee. This is calculated for the period exceeding the statutory limit based on the monthly wage standard after the expiration of your probation period. If the employer wishes to terminate the contract during the probation period, it may only do so under the specific circumstances listed by law, and must state the reasons to the employee (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Labor Contract Law (Articles 19, 20, 21, 83). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm>
entries.notes: The three most common unlawful practices: First, signing a contract for only 1 year yet stipulating a 3-month probation period. Second, transferring posts after passing probation and setting another probation period. Third, "no social insurance during probation"; the obligation to pay social insurance begins on day one of starting work and has nothing to do with whether you are on probation; for employer obligations, see Section 12, Item 16. Being dismissed during probation does not mean receiving nothing at all; it depends on whether the reason provided by the employer falls under the grounds permitted by law for dismissal. In cases of unlawful termination, calculate at 2N according to Item 6.

entries.title: When laid off, first calculate N clearly: one month's salary for each full year, half a month for less than six months
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Calculate it once with a calculator, ten minutes.
entries.summary: The severance compensation a company must pay upon layoff is calculated like this: one month's salary for each full year worked; six months or more but less than one year counts as one year; less than six months gives half a month. Here, monthly salary is the average over the 12 months prior to leaving, and bonuses, allowances, and subsidies must all be included. If the salary exceeds 3 times the local average monthly wage of the previous year, it is capped at 3 times, and the length of service is calculated up to a maximum of 12 years.
entries.benefit: Statutory severance compensation under the Labor Contract Law is the money the employer must pay upon layoff, commonly referred to as N. The calculation method is: "payment of one month's salary for each full year worked... for periods of six months or more but less than one year, it is calculated as one year; for periods of less than six months, payment of half a month's salary shall be made to the employee." If the monthly salary exceeds three times the local average monthly wage of employees in the previous year, it is capped and calculated at three times, and work tenure is counted up to a maximum of twelve years
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (Effective January 1, 2008) (Article 47). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm>
entries.notes: Monthly salary refers to the average wage of the twelve months prior to the termination of the labor contract. Bonuses, allowances, and subsidies must all be counted, not just basic salary. This point is where companies are most likely to lower the figure. For whether this payment is subject to individual income tax, see Item 18 of this section (Individual Income Tax on Severance)

entries.title: If the company dismisses you citing medical inability, incompetence, or major changes in circumstances, and fails to give 30 days' advance notice, it must pay an extra month's salary
entries.cost: Costs nothing.
entries.summary: If a company dismisses you because you cannot perform work after an illness, are incompetent at the job, or because circumstances have changed drastically, it must give 30 days' advance written notice. If no notice is given, an additional month's salary must be paid on top of N; this is what is commonly called N+1. During negotiations, list this one month separately—do not let the company fold it into N.
entries.benefit: The Labor Contract Law stipulates that when an employer terminates a labor contract under this article, there are two approaches. One is to "notify the employee in writing 30 days in advance." The other is that "the labor contract may be terminated after paying the employee an extra month's wage." If they want you to leave immediately, they must pay an extra month's salary. This additional month is colloquially known as payment in lieu of notice and is an amount calculated separately on top of N. This one month is calculated based on your wage for the preceding month, whereas N is calculated based on your average wage over the 12 months prior to departure; the base figures for the two amounts are different
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (Effective January 1, 2008) (Articles 36, 39, 40, 41, 46, 47, 87). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm>; State Council (2008). Implementation Regulations of the Labor Contract Law (State Council Order No. 535) Article 20: "Where an employing entity chooses to terminate a labor contract by paying an extra month's wage to an employee pursuant to Article 40 of the Labor Contract Law, the extra wage paid shall be determined according to the wage standard of the employee for the preceding month." <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2008/content_1107604.htm>
entries.notes: This extra month appears only in the three scenarios under Article 40 of the Labor Contract Law: an employee who falls ill or sustains a non-work-related injury cannot engage in the original work or other work newly arranged after the medical treatment period expires; an employee who cannot perform the work remains unable to do so after training or adjustment of posts; or the objective circumstances under which the contract was concluded have undergone a major change and both parties fail to reach an agreement through consultation. No other scenario provides this extra month. Economic layoffs (Article 41) only require the company to explain the situation to the labor union or all employees 30 days in advance. Where the company proposes and both parties agree to terminate by mutual consent, what is paid is N. If you are dismissed for serious misconduct or similar faults, there is no severance. If the company terminates unlawfully, what is paid is 2N. For cases falling under those three scenarios of Article 40, calculate N and the 1 separately during negotiations, and do not let the company fold that extra month into N

entries.title: Where a company terminates unlawfully, compensation is twice the standard of economic severance
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Going through arbitration requires waiting several months. The difficulty lies in staying committed throughout these months without giving up halfway.
entries.summary: Where a company's termination constitutes an unlawful termination, compensation is doubled based on the standard for economic severance—this is commonly called 2N. Whether it is an unlawful termination depends on specific circumstances. First consult legal aid or a lawyer to get clarity, then decide whether to negotiate with the company or proceed to arbitration.
entries.benefit: The Labor Contract Law stipulates that where an employer revokes or terminates a labor contract in violation of the provisions of this Law, it "shall pay damages to the employee at twice the rate of the severance payment stipulated in Article 47 of this Law." The calculation method is to first compute one share according to that set of standards for economic severance, and then double it for you
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (Effective January 1, 2008) (Article 87). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm>
entries.notes: This is what is colloquially known as 2N. What counts as unlawful termination depends on the specific circumstances. Consult legal aid or a lawyer first before deciding whether to negotiate or go to arbitration; for the pathways, see Section 7

entries.title: Do not sign "voluntary resignation for personal reasons"—once signed, there is no N
entries.cost: Costs nothing. The difficulty lies in withstanding the pressure to sign on the spot.
entries.summary: Signing to acknowledge "voluntary resignation for personal reasons" typically causes both severance compensation and unemployment insurance benefits to fall through together. Proposing resignation yourself is fundamentally not among the scenarios for which severance is paid, except where the company has committed statutory faults like withholding wages or failing to pay social insurance. You do not have to sign on the same day; sleep on it and cool off before deciding.
entries.benefit: The Labor Contract Law restricts the scenarios where severance compensation should be paid to those categories explicitly listed in the law. An employee proposing to leave on their own initiative is not among them, unless it is due to statutory employer faults such as wage arrears or failure to pay social insurance. Once you sign "voluntary resignation," severance compensation and unemployment insurance benefits typically fall through together
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (Effective January 1, 2008) (Articles 38 and 46). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm>
entries.notes: A common company line is "sign first so we can process the exit procedure, and compensation will be given separately." If agreed, have it written directly into the agreement on the spot; if it is not written, do not sign. Not signing on that day carries zero legal consequences; cool off for a night before speaking again

entries.title: Before leaving, save your pay stubs, attendance records, labor contracts, social insurance records, and chat logs first
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Spend half an hour saving the materials properly. The difficulty lies in remembering to save them before leaving.
entries.summary: Disputes over dismissal or wage deductions must be proven by the employer, but overtime requires you to prove it first, and employers are only required to retain payroll records for two years. Once you hand back your computer and accounts, you can no longer obtain these materials. Holding pay stubs, attendance, social insurance records, and original chat logs gives you leverage when the employer refuses to acknowledge claims.
entries.benefit: Once you hand back your computer and accounts, you will never be able to retrieve these materials again. Labor disputes follow the principle of "the burden of proof lies on the claimant": for things you claim, you must produce evidence. Where evidence is in the hands of the employer, the employer must produce it; if it fails to do so, the employer bears the adverse consequences. During arbitration, if you cannot obtain materials in the employer's possession, the arbitration tribunal can order the employer to submit them within a specified time limit. For disputes involving expulsion, dismissal, termination of contract, reduction of wages, and calculation of working years, the burden of proof rests on the employer. Overtime pay is different: you must first prove that you actually worked overtime. Only when you can prove that overtime records are held by the employer and the employer refuses to produce them will the employer bear the adverse consequences. The employer is only obligated to preserve wage payment records for two years or more. When paying wages, the employer must also provide you with an individual wage voucher. Where no written contract was signed, payroll records, social insurance payment records, and employee ID badges can all be used to prove the existence of an employment relationship with the employer. Recruitment registration forms, attendance records, and testimony of other employees can also be used. Chat logs qualify as electronic data under the law and can serve as evidence. Submitting evidence requires presenting original copies; printouts made directly from the original records also qualify as original copies. The Shanghai Procuratorate handled a case: a worker seeking a decade's worth of minimum wage shortfalls was only recognized for the final two years prior to departure in both first and second instance courts. The court's rationale was that the employer is only required to preserve records for two years, and the worker bore the burden of proof for the preceding eight years. He had ten years of pay stubs and bank statements in hand, but the company refused to acknowledge the authenticity of the pay stubs. In August 2024, he applied for procuratorial supervision. Following a protest filed by the procuratorate, the employer paid 19,000 yuan in compensation pursuant to mediation. He had filed the lawsuit when the company laid off workers in 2021; by the time he applied for supervision, roughly three years had passed (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Law on Mediation and Arbitration of Labor Disputes (Articles 6 and 39). <https://rsj.ankang.gov.cn/Content-2150407.html> (Reprinted by Ankang Human Resources and Social Security Bureau); Supreme People's Court (2020). Interpretation (I) on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Labor Dispute Cases (Fa Shi [2020] No. 26, Articles 42 and 44). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/282121.html>; Supreme People's Court (2019). Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Procedures (Fa Shi [2019] No. 19, Articles 14 and 15). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/212721.html>; Ministry of Labor (1994). Interim Provisions on Wage Payment (Article 6), cited by Heilongjiang Provincial People's Government "Ask Policy for You". <https://www.hlj.gov.cn/hlj/c116413/202402/c00_31712524.shtml>; Ministry of Labor and Social Security (2005). Notice on Matters Concerning the Establishment of Labor Relations (Lao She Bu Fa [2005] No. 12), cited by Heilongjiang Provincial People's Government "Ask Policy for You". <https://hlj.gov.cn/hlj/c116413/202408/c00_31757488.shtml>; Guo Yonghui, Bian Wanru (2025). Who Should Bear the Burden of Proof for Wage Payment Conditions Beyond Two Years? Procuratorial Daily. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/llyj/202508/t20250806_703164.shtml> (Published on the Supreme People's Procuratorate website); For rights protection pathways, see Section 7
entries.notes: What you are saving are your own employment relationship materials. Do not casually take the company's source code, client lists, or technical documentation; for the risks of taking them, see Section 11. Do not just take screenshots of chat logs—keep the original records on your mobile phone without deleting them. It is best to save pay stubs and bank statements monthly; if you seek to settle old scores many years after leaving, the employer is no longer required to retain records from more than two years ago. That Shanghai case was overturned because of a procuratorial protest; most people do not reach that stage. When leaving, also ask the employer for a proof of employment termination; see Item 17 of this section (Proof of Termination)

entries.title: Before taking up a post involving dust, noise, or chemicals, check whether the contract states the hazards; three occupational health examinations are arranged and paid for by the employer
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Read through the "Occupational Disease Hazard Notification" section item by item when signing the contract. Request and keep a copy of the report for each health check for yourself. The difficulty lies in asking in person and obtaining the materials face-to-face.
entries.summary: When signing a contract, the employer must truthfully state in the contract what occupational disease hazards the post carries, protective measures, and entitlement benefits. If they conceal this from you, you have the right to refuse the work, and the employer cannot terminate you for doing so. Three occupational health examinations—pre-employment, on-the-job, and upon departure—must be arranged and paid for by the employer. Without completing an exit medical examination, the employer cannot terminate the contract with you.
entries.benefit: The Law on the Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases stipulates that when signing an employment contract, the employer must clearly explain four matters. These four are: what occupational disease hazards may arise from performing this work, what consequences may result, how to protect against them, and what benefits are provided. The original statutory text states: "truthfully inform the worker and specify them in the labor contract, and shall not conceal or deceive." If, after the contract is signed, you are transferred to perform hazardous work not disclosed in the contract, the employer must truthfully inform you anew and negotiate with you to amend the contract terms. If the employer fails to do so, "the worker has the right to refuse to engage in operations involving occupational disease hazards, and the employer shall not terminate the labor contract concluded with the worker on this ground." Physical examinations occur three times in total: pre-employment, during employment, and upon departure. "The expenses of occupational health examinations shall be borne by the employer"—the money is paid by the employer, and the results must be communicated to you in writing. For individuals who have not undergone a pre-employment physical examination, the employer shall not assign them to perform work involving exposure to occupational disease hazards. Individuals whose physical conditions are fundamentally unsuitable for such work (those with occupational contraindications) must also not be assigned to perform these contraindicated operations. If health damage related to this work is detected, the person must be transferred away from the original post and properly accommodated. **"An employer shall not rescind or terminate a labor contract concluded with a worker who has not undergone a pre-departure occupational health examination."** Upon departure, you "have the right to request a duplicate copy of your occupational health surveillance dossier, and the employer shall truthfully and gratuitously provide it, and affix a seal to the duplicate copy provided." The employer must faithfully provide you with a photocopy of this occupational health surveillance dossier free of charge and stamp the copy with an official seal (National)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). Law on the Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases (2018 Amendment, Articles 33, 35, and 36). <https://www.beijing.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengcefagui/qtwj/201711/t20171104_779851.html> (Reprinted by the People's Government of Beijing Municipality)
entries.notes: Asking three questions during an interview is enough to roughly gauge whether an enterprise is compliant: Are there occupational disease hazards in this position? Are they written into the contract? Who pays for the pre-employment physical examination? If they cannot answer or say "just start working first and we'll see," weigh the risks yourself. Pre-departure physical examinations are the most easily overlooked: without conducting a pre-departure physical examination, the employer cannot rescind or terminate the labor contract with you. This physical examination is also a key piece of evidence for diagnosing an occupational disease in the future; the same applies to the copy of the surveillance dossier—obtain it before leaving. The occupational disease itself is processed as a work-related injury; see Item 11 onward for benefits.

entries.title: Much of the damage caused by dust, noise, and toxic chemicals is irreversible (such as pneumoconiosis and noise-induced deafness): protective equipment must be provided by the employer, and work lacking protective measures can be refused
entries.cost: Costs no money. The difficulty lies in continuously wearing particulate respirators, earplugs, and protective goggles, as well as refusing unprotected work, at the cost of potentially being called "troublesome" by colleagues.
entries.summary: Pneumoconiosis, noise-induced deafness, and chemical eye burns are all statutory occupational diseases; once the lungs and hearing are damaged, they cannot be cured or reversed. You have the right to know what hazards exist in your position, and the right to require the employer to provide protective facilities and personal protective equipment. You may refuse to perform work that lacks protection. If the employer reduces your salary or dismisses you because of this, none of those actions are legally valid.
entries.benefit: Starting from August 1, 2025, statutory occupational diseases encompass 135 conditions across 12 broad categories, which include 4 open-ended catch-all clauses. Ranking as the first category is occupational pneumoconiosis. Within it are silicosis, coal worker's pneumoconiosis, graphite pneumoconiosis, carbon black pneumoconiosis, asbestosis, and talc pneumoconiosis. There are also cement pneumoconiosis, mica pneumoconiosis, potter's pneumoconiosis, aluminum pneumoconiosis, welder's pneumoconiosis, and founder's pneumoconiosis, plus one open-ended clause. Under occupational ear, nose, throat, and oral diseases, there are noise-induced deafness and blast deafness. Under occupational eye diseases, there are chemical ocular burns and electric ophthalmia. Among these, the damage from pneumoconiosis and noise-induced deafness is permanent. The US National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) states that silicosis is permanent lung damage that worsens progressively, with no currently known cure. A Lancet review states that even after a patient is no longer exposed to dust, lung function continues to deteriorate with disease progression. The US Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) states that hearing loss caused by noise is permanent and cannot be corrected by surgery or medication. The law grants four rights that can be invoked on the spot. First is to know what occupational disease hazards exist in the workplace, what consequences they will cause, and what protective measures should be adopted. Second is to demand that the employer provide compliant protective facilities and personal protective equipment, and improve working conditions. Third is to criticize, report, and lodge complaints against practices that violate laws and regulations on occupational disease prevention and control, as well as practices that endanger life and health. Fourth is to "refuse to follow commands given in violation of regulations and orders forcing the performance of operations without occupational disease protective measures"—you can refuse non-compliant commands and unprotected work. Furthermore, "Where an employer lowers the wages, welfare, or other benefits of a worker or rescinds or terminates the labor contract concluded with the worker because the worker lawfully exercises their legitimate rights, such acts shall be invalid." If they reduce your pay, slash your benefits, or dismiss you because you exercised these rights, these actions do not count legally (National)
entries.sources: National Health Commission, Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, National Disease Control and Prevention Administration, All-China Federation of Trade Unions (2024). Classification and Catalogue of Occupational Diseases (Effective August 1, 2025). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202412/content_6992843.htm>; for the scope of the 135 conditions in 12 broad categories in the new catalogue, see National Health Commission (2024). The New Catalogue Adjusts Occupational Diseases to 135 Conditions Across 12 Broad Categories. <https://www.gov.cn/lianbo/bumen/202412/content_6992838.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). Law on the Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases (Article 39). <https://www.beijing.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengcefagui/qtwj/201711/t20171104_779851.html> (Reprinted by the People's Government of Beijing Municipality); National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (2026). Silica Symptoms and Medical Monitoring: "permanent lung damage called silicosis. It is a progressive, debilitating, and sometimes fatal disease" "There is no known cure for silicosis". <https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/silica/symptoms/index.html>; Leung CC, Yu IT, Chen W (2012). Silicosis. Lancet, 379(9830), 2008-2018: "Impairment of lung function increases with disease progression, even after the patient is no longer exposed". <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(12)60235-9>; Occupational Safety and Health Administration. Occupational Noise Exposure: "permanent hearing loss that cannot be corrected through surgery or with medicine". <https://www.osha.gov/noise>
entries.notes: Identify masks correctly; particulate respirators must be worn in dusty positions—this is the author's experience. In noisy positions, if the employer does not issue earplugs, buy them yourself; they cost a few yuan a pair, and lost hearing cannot be recovered. "Work for two years, save enough money, and leave" does not hold up against pneumoconiosis. Silicosis continues to worsen even after exposure to dust has ceased. Therefore, pre-departure physical examinations are exceptionally critical (see Item 9: the three occupational health examinations are arranged and paid for by the employer). The new catalogue also adds two new categories. One is occupational musculoskeletal disorders, which contains carpal tunnel syndrome, limited to manufacturing workers who perform prolonged repetitive wrist movements or forceful physical labor. The other is occupational mental and behavioral disorders, which contains post-traumatic stress disorder. It is limited to emergency responders such as people's police officers, healthcare personnel, and firefighting/rescue personnel who participate in emergency response operations. For on-site management of chemical splashes on the body, see Section 13, Item 21. For how to treat post-traumatic stress disorder, see Section 29, Item 14 (trauma-focused psychotherapy).

entries.title: If injured at work or struck in an accident on the way to/from work, the very first step is to seek a work-related injury determination; if the employer does not file, file it yourself
entries.cost: Costs no money; requires a trip to the administrative department of social insurance. Bring three items of documentation: the work-related injury determination application form, proof of employment relationship, and a medical diagnosis certificate.
entries.summary: Injuries sustained at work due to job duties qualify as work-related injuries, as do injuries from traffic accidents on the way to or from work where you do not bear primary responsibility. However, without a work-related injury determination, medical expenses, wages paid as normal during recovery, and disability subsidies will all fall through. The employer should file within 30 days. If the employer does not file, you, your family members, or the trade union can file directly with the administrative department of social insurance within one year.
entries.benefit: Without obtaining a work-related injury determination, medical expenses, wages paid as normal during recovery (wages during the work-stop wage-retention period), and disability subsidies will all fall through. If the employer fails to file within 30 days, the work-related injury benefit expenses that should have been granted during this period must be paid out of the employer's own pocket
entries.sources: State Council (2010 Revision). Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance (State Council Decree No. 586), Article 14 lists seven circumstances that "shall be determined as a work-related injury", including "(6) Suffering injury in a traffic accident or urban rail transit, passenger ferry, or train accident on the way to or from work where the employee does not bear primary responsibility"; Article 17 states: "The employer shall, within 30 days from the date the accident injury occurred or from the date the occupational disease was diagnosed or appraised, submit an application for work-related injury determination to the social insurance administrative department of the pooling region" "Where the employer fails to submit an application for work-related injury determination in accordance with the preceding paragraph, the injured worker or their close relatives or trade union organization may, within 1 year from the date the accident injury occurred or from the date the occupational disease was diagnosed or appraised, directly submit an application for work-related injury determination to the social insurance administrative department of the pooling region where the employer is located" "Where the employer fails to submit the application for work-related injury determination within the time limit prescribed in the first paragraph of this Article, relevant expenses such as work-related injury benefits that comply with the provisions of this Regulation occurring during this period shall be borne by the employer"; Article 19 states: "Where the employee or their close relatives consider it a work-related injury, but the employer does not consider it a work-related injury, the employer shall bear the burden of proof"; Article 20 states: "A decision on work-related injury determination shall be made within 60 days from the date of accepting the application for work-related injury determination"; Article 55 states: regarding "dissatisfaction with a decision not to accept an application for work-related injury determination" or "dissatisfaction with the conclusion of a work-related injury determination", one "may apply for administrative reconsideration according to law, or initiate an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court according to law". <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1778064.htm>; Supreme People's Court (2014). Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Administrative Cases Involving Work-Related Injury Insurance (Fa Shi [2014] No. 9), Article 7: "Where the time limit for applying for work-related injury determination is exceeded due to reasons not attributable to the worker or their close relatives, the delayed time shall not be counted towards the application time limit for work-related injury determination", listing circumstances as "(1) Force majeure; (2) Restriction of personal freedom; (3) Reasons attributable to the employer; (4) Deficiencies in the registration system of the social insurance administrative department; (5) The parties apply for arbitration or initiate civil litigation regarding whether an employment relationship exists". <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/6775.html>
entries.notes: Take the 1-year deadline seriously; do not drag your feet. However, time lost due to reasons not of your own making does not count toward the 1 year. There are five such categories of reasons: force majeure, restriction of personal freedom, employer-related reasons, deficiencies in the registration system of the social insurance department, and the fifth is applying for arbitration or going to court to establish an employment relationship. Therefore, if the employer drags its feet and does not file, delaying past the deadline, still go apply and bring evidence of the employer's delay. If the social insurance department refuses to accept it, or if you disagree with the determination conclusion, you can apply for administrative reconsideration or sue directly. If the employer claims it does not count as a work-related injury, the employer bears the burden of proof. Still, you should preserve materials yourself: photos from the day of the incident, colleagues' contact information, medical records, and attendance records. Article 16 of the Regulation lists three non-qualifying circumstances: intentional crime, intoxication or drug abuse, and self-harm or suicide. Article 15 separately provides for injuries "deemed as work-related": sudden illness during working hours and at the work post leading to death, or resulting in death within 48 hours after emergency rescue efforts fail.

entries.title: Do not believe "holding out until you reach your workstation counts as a work-related injury": in a sudden medical emergency, call 120 first, do not rush to clock in
entries.cost: Costs no money.
entries.summary: Rushing to the company during a sudden medical emergency will not yield you extra money. Being deemed a work-related injury requires the person to fall ill during working hours and at the work post; falling ill en route without arriving at the post does not qualify in the first place. Conversely, if emergency resuscitation exceeds 48 hours, it also does not qualify. Trading those tens of minutes delayed just to satisfy technical criteria sacrifices your own survival rate.
entries.benefit: Being deemed a work-related injury requires that a person suddenly falls ill and dies "during working hours and at the work post", or dies after ineffective emergency rescue within 48 hours. Delaying medical care to scrape together these two conditions gambles away your own chance of survival, and the compensation sought in return might not even be obtained
entries.sources: Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance, Article 15, Paragraph 1, Item (1): "During working hours and at the work post, suddenly contracting an illness leading to death or resulting in death within 48 hours after ineffective emergency rescue" shall be deemed a work-related injury; Article 14, Item (6) only designates "suffering injury in a traffic accident or urban rail transit, passenger ferry, or train accident on the way to or from work where the employee does not bear primary responsibility" as a work-related injury; sudden illness en route is not included. <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1778064.htm>
entries.notes: Both conditions must be met simultaneously: during working hours, and at the work post. Falling ill en route before arriving at the post does not apply. If one falls ill while on duty and is subsequently sent home or to the hospital, and dies within 48 hours after ineffective emergency treatment, it may still apply. What matters is where the person was when the illness struck, not where they ultimately passed away. Short videos present this as "tough it out until you reach the company to get paid," which has the direction completely reversed. What can alter the outcome is whether you went to the hospital in those critical tens of minutes following the onset of illness. In addition, 48 hours is a hard line; if resuscitation efforts exceed 48 hours, it actually does not count.

entries.title: Even if the employer failed to pay work-related injury insurance for you, work-related injury benefits still apply, fully funded by the employer under identical standards
entries.cost: Costs no money. If the employer refuses to recognize it, you will have to pursue arbitration or even litigation, taking several months at minimum. The difficulty lies in having to follow through with the proceedings across these months.
entries.summary: Even if the employer did not pay work-related injury insurance for you, work-related injury benefits still exist. It simply shifts so that the employer pays in full according to the same items and standards, not a single cent less. Failing to enroll incurs additional penalties on the employer: ordered to pay back-dues, assessed a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day, and fined 1 to 3 times the unpaid amount if overdue. "The company didn't buy work injury insurance so it cannot compensate" is a falsehood.
entries.benefit: The Regulation clearly states: for an employer that has not paid work-related injury insurance for an employee, if the employee suffers a work-related injury, that employer must disburse the money according to the items and standards stipulated in the Regulation. Exactly which items should be paid and how much is given for each are completely identical to those for an insured worker, except that the employer pays out of pocket
entries.sources: Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance, Article 62, Paragraph 2: "Where an employee of an employer that ought to participate in work-related injury insurance pursuant to the provisions of this Regulation but failed to participate suffers a work-related injury, the employer shall pay the expenses in accordance with the work-related injury insurance benefit items and standards prescribed by this Regulation." Article 62, Paragraph 1: ordered to participate and make supplementary payments within a specified period, "a late-payment fine of 0.05% per day shall be levied from the date of default; if it still fails to pay within the time limit, a fine of not less than 1 time but not more than 3 times the amount of the overdue payment shall be imposed". <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1778064.htm>
entries.notes: "The company didn't buy work-related injury insurance for you, so it cannot compensate" is the most common lie in such situations. Non-participation means the employer faces heavier penalties; your benefits are not diminished.

entries.title: Undergo an appraisal of labor capability once your injury stabilizes; disability grades translate directly into money
entries.cost: Costs no money. Going through the labor capability appraisal procedure requires waiting for a period of time before and after.
entries.summary: Undergo a labor capability appraisal after your injury stabilizes; the assigned grade translates directly into money. The lump-sum disability subsidy is calculated based on your own wages: Grade 5 is 18 months, Grade 6 is 16 months, Grade 7 is 13 months, Grade 8 is 11 months, Grade 9 is 9 months, and Grade 10 is 7 months. Do not sign a "one-off full and final settlement" agreement before the appraisal results are released.
entries.benefit: The lump-sum disability subsidy is converted into several months of wages according to the disability grade and paid out in one lump sum. Grade 5 is 18 months, Grade 6 is 16 months, and Grade 7 is 13 months of the worker's own wage. Grade 8 is 11 months, Grade 9 is 9 months, and Grade 10 is 7 months of the worker's own wage
entries.sources: Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance, Article 21: "Where disability exists and labor capability is affected after the injury is relatively stable following medical treatment, an appraisal of labor capability shall be conducted"; Article 22: "Impairment of labor functioning is divided into ten disability grades, with Grade 1 being the most severe and Grade 10 being the least severe"; Article 36 covers benefits for Grades 5 and 6 (a lump-sum disability subsidy of 18/16 months of the worker's own wage, and a monthly disability allowance of 70%/60% of the worker's own wage); Article 37 covers benefits for Grades 7 to 10 (13/11/9/7 months of the worker's own wage). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1778064.htm>
entries.notes: For Grades 5 and 6, the employment relationship is retained, the person is still an employee of the employer, and they receive a monthly disability allowance. For individuals in Grades 7 to 10, when the contract expires or when they propose termination themselves, there are two additional sums of money. The lump-sum work-related injury medical subsidy is paid by the fund, and the lump-sum disability employment subsidy is paid by the employer; the amounts provided are determined by the province. Do not sign a "one-off full and final settlement" agreement before the appraisal results are issued. Equipping assistive devices such as prosthetic limbs or wheelchairs for work-related injuries requires prior confirmation by the Labor Capability Appraisal Committee; see Section 33, Item 7 (ask completely at the county-level disabled persons' federation).

entries.title: Distinguish the three sums of money for work-related death: funeral subsidy, pension for dependent relatives, and lump-sum work-related death subsidy
entries.cost: Costs no money; requires completing a set of procedural steps.
entries.summary: Death arising from work involves three sums of money; do not negotiate for only one of them. The funeral subsidy is 6 months of the local average monthly wage of employees in the preceding year. The pension for dependent relatives is disbursed monthly based on the deceased's own wage: 40% per month for a spouse, and 30% per month per person for other relatives. The lump-sum work-related death subsidy is 20 times the national per capita disposable income of urban residents in the preceding year—this single figure applies nationwide.
entries.benefit: Money for work-related death is divided into three sums. The first sum is the funeral subsidy, the amount of which is 6 months of the average monthly wage of employees in the preceding year in the region where insurance was maintained (pooling region). The second sum is the pension for dependent relatives, paid out monthly based on the deceased's own wage: 40% per month for a spouse, and 30% per month per person for other relatives. The third sum is the lump-sum work-related death subsidy, the amount of which is 20 times the national per capita disposable income of urban residents in the preceding year. There is only this one single figure nationwide, regardless of region. For a work-related death occurring in 2026, this sum is approximately 1.13 million CNY (exact figure: 1,130,040 yuan). The calculation is 56,502 yuan—the national per capita disposable income of urban residents in the preceding year—multiplied by 20.
entries.sources: Article 39 of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance: "(1) The funeral subsidy is 6 months of the average monthly wage of employees in the pool area in the previous year; (2) The pension for dependent relatives is paid at a certain proportion of the employee's own wage to relatives who were mainly dependent on the deceased employee's living sources during their lifetime and lack the capacity to work. The standards are: 40% per month for spouses, 30% per person per month for other relatives, with an additional 10% on top of the above standards per person per month for solitary elderly people or orphans... (3) The standard for the one-off work-related death subsidy is 20 times the per capita disposable income of urban residents nationwide in the previous year." <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1778064.htm>; National Bureau of Statistics (2026). Income and Consumption Expenditure of Residents in 2025. <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfbhjd/202601/t20260119_1962321.html>
entries.notes: The one-off work-related death subsidy is uniform nationwide, with the amount updated annually based on data released by the National Bureau of Statistics. When negotiating compensation, do not accept the claim that "local standards on our side are lower."

entries.title: If chronically bullied, insulted, or given a hard time at work, don't just tough it out: document it first to preserve evidence, then file a complaint, report to the police, or seek arbitration depending on the nature of the conduct
entries.cost: Costs no money. It takes time to document: dates, people present, exact words spoken by the other party, and keeping original files of chat screenshots and emails. Going through arbitration or lawsuits takes several months. Changing jobs carries the highest cost; whether to leave is up to you to calculate.
entries.summary: People bullied at work have about a 60% higher risk of later developing heart disease and stroke, and the more they are bullied, the higher the risk. People who are bullied have roughly double the odds of developing suicidal ideation a few years later compared to others. Enduring insults and mistreatment is not a minor matter that just passes if you put up with it.
entries.benefit: In terms of health, three cohorts from Sweden and Denmark combined, totaling 79,201 employed individuals aged 18 to 65. None had cardiovascular disease initially, with an average follow-up of 12.4 years. 9% of people reported being bullied at work in the past year. Those bullied had an approximately 59% higher risk of developing cardiovascular disease (coronary heart disease and cerebrovascular disease) (HR 1.59, 95% CI 1.28–1.98). For those who experienced workplace violence, it was about 25% higher (HR 1.25, 1.12–1.40). For both, the greater the exposure, the higher the risk. A nationally representative randomized follow-up survey in Norway of 1,846 employed individuals was assessed every two to three years for a total of three waves. People who were bullied had about twice the odds of later developing suicidal ideation compared to others (OR 2.05, 95% CI 1.08–3.89). Conversely, those who already had suicidal ideation were not more likely to be bullied later. Legally, China has no law specifically addressing "workplace bullying"; specific actions must be matched to corresponding provisions. If an employer insults, subjects to corporal punishment, beats, illegally searches, or detains a worker, it will be subject to administrative penalties, must pay compensation if harm is caused, and criminal liability will be pursued if a crime is constituted. If an employer uses violence or threats to force you to work, you may terminate the contract immediately without prior notice and still receive financial compensation.
