Employers must take measures to prevent and stop anyone from using powers of office or hierarchical relationships to commit sexual harassment. Victims may demand civil liability from the harasser. Labor arbitration cases are concluded within 45 days from the date of acceptance, extended by at most another 15 days for complicated cases.
entries.sources: Xu T et al. (2019). Workplace bullying and workplace violence as risk factors for cardiovascular disease: a multi-cohort study. European Heart Journal. <https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehy683>; Nielsen MB, Nielsen GH, Notelaers G, Einarsen S (2015). Workplace Bullying and Suicidal Ideation: A 3-Wave Longitudinal Norwegian Study. American Journal of Public Health. <https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2015.302855>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Labor Contract Law (Article 38, Paragraph 2, Article 46, Article 88). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm>; National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 1010). Full text reprinted by the Supreme People's Procuratorate <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2022 Revision). Law on the Protection of Women's Rights and Interests (Article 25). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808181841257210184281512de0eec>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Law on Mediation and Arbitration of Labor Disputes (Article 43). Full text reprinted by Ankang Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau <https://rsj.ankang.gov.cn/Content-2150407.html>
entries.notes: Reason for assigning grade B: The health figures come from longitudinal follow-up records rather than randomized grouped experiments, and "being bullied" was self-reported. There are four steps you can take first. Step one: start documenting from today; for audio recording, see Section 8, Item 41 (Audio Recording). Step two: report in writing through internal employer channels, preserving a record that you reported it. Step three: if beaten, detained, or publicly insulted, call the police. Step four: if forced out due to wage arrears or failure to pay social insurance, handle it according to Item 7 (Don't Sign Voluntary Resignation) and Item 8 (Preserve Evidence Before Leaving) of this section. For how financial compensation is calculated, see Item 4 of this section (Calculate N First When Laid Off). Simple cold-shouldering, exclusion, and being given a hard time mostly do not match a specific legal article; the available avenues are mainly internal complaints, internal transfers, and changing jobs. Arbitration takes at most 60 days from acceptance; first-instance trials in court must be concluded within 6 months according to regulations, which can be extended, with attorney fees paid out of pocket. If you can no longer hold out, first call 12356; see Section 1, Item 25 (12356). Resigning immediately whenever mistreated is not advocated; the cost of changing jobs is for you to calculate.

entries.title: When leaving a job, ask the employer for a proof of departure, specifying the contract term, termination date, post, and years of service
entries.cost: Costs no money. Ask in person before leaving, or send a written message asking for it, keeping a record of having asked. The difficulty lies in having to make this request when relations have turned sour. If the employer stalls and refuses to provide it, you must file a complaint or apply for arbitration, taking several dozen days to a few months from start to finish.
entries.summary: Whether you are dismissed, the contract expires, or you resign voluntarily, the employer must provide a proof of departure upon your leaving and transfer your personnel files and social insurance within 15 days. The certificate must state the contract term, termination date, job post, and how many years you worked at this employer. It is needed to handle unemployment registration. If the employer refuses to provide it, the labor department will order correction, and if this causes you losses, they must compensate.
entries.benefit: The Labor Contract Law stipulates that employers must issue proof when rescinding or terminating a labor contract. The statutory provision does not distinguish who initiated it; non-renewal upon contract expiration, your own resignation, and dismissal are all included. The employer must also handle the transfer procedures for personnel files and social insurance relations for you within 15 days. The implementation regulations specify that the certificate must state four items: the term of the labor contract, the date of rescission or termination, the job post, and the years of service with this employer. The Regulation on Unemployment Insurance stipulates that after becoming unemployed, an employee must take this certificate issued by the employer to promptly handle unemployment registration at the social insurance agency. Unemployment insurance benefits are calculated starting from the date of handling unemployment registration. Where an employer fails to issue written proof, the labor administrative department will order correction. If it causes you harm, the employer must compensate. The law separately stipulates that where a new employer hires a person whose contract with the original employer has not been rescinded, causing losses to the original employer, it shall bear joint and several liability for compensation. The proof of departure is the written evidence that you have already rescinded the contract with the original employer (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2012 Amendment). Labor Contract Law (Articles 50, 89, 91). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf74d7106b3>; State Council (2008). Implementation Regulations for the Labor Contract Law (State Council Decree No. 535, Article 24). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f3cbb3c016f40927caf049c>; State Council (1999). Regulation on Unemployment Insurance (State Council Decree No. 258, Article 16). <https://xzfg.moj.gov.cn/front/law/detail?LawID=517>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Law on Mediation and Arbitration of Labor Disputes (Articles 2, 27, 43, 53). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf64f28039d>; State Council (2004). Regulation on Labor Security Supervision (State Council Decree No. 423, Article 17). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2004/content_63042.htm>; State Council (2006). Measures for the Payment of Litigation Costs (State Council Decree No. 481, Articles 6, 13, 29). <https://www.gov.cn/ziliao/flfg/2006-12/29/content_483682.htm>
entries.notes: The statutory provisions do not tie issuing proof to the handover of work; what is paid only after completion of the handover is financial compensation. If the employer stalls and refuses to provide it, first send a written message to ask again. If they still refuse to provide it, call 12333 or go to the labor supervision division of the human resources and social security bureau to complain. Filing a complaint is free of charge; investigation is completed within 60 working days after filing, and complicated cases can be extended by another 30 working days. To seek compensation for losses from the employer, go through labor arbitration, which is also free of charge, with application required within 1 year. Arbitration cases are concluded within 45 days after acceptance, extended by at most another 15 days. You must provide evidence to prove your losses yourself, such as missing unemployment registration or being rejected by a new employer due to lacking proof. If dissatisfied with the arbitral award, proceed to court; first-instance regular procedures must be concluded within 6 months according to regulations, which can be extended. The acceptance fee charged by the court for labor dispute cases is 10 yuan per case; attorney fees are not included in litigation costs and must be paid out of pocket. Among the four items required by the regulations, there is no reason for departure. If the certificate states "voluntary resignation for personal reasons" when that is not the case, raise an objection on the spot; for reasons, see Item 7 of this section (Don't Sign Voluntary Resignation). For how to claim unemployment insurance benefits, see Section 7, Item 1 (Unemployment Insurance Benefits).

entries.title: Check individual income tax upon receiving severance compensation: up to 3 times the local average annual employee wage of the previous year is tax-free; the excess portion is calculated separately and not combined into the current year's wages
entries.cost: Costs no money. Look up the local average employee wage for the previous year, then spend a few minutes verifying how the employer deducted the tax. Declaration details for each item of income can be checked in the Individual Income Tax App.
entries.summary: For one-off compensation received due to the rescission of a labor contract, the portion within 3 times the local average annual employee wage of the previous year is not subject to individual income tax. The excess portion is taxed separately and not combined with that year's wages. If the employer bundled the entire amount into the current month's wages to deduct tax, first check with the employer to clarify, then call 12366 to consult the tax bureau.
entries.benefit: The Ministry of Finance and the State Taxation Administration have a document governing one-off compensation income received by individuals upon rescinding labor relations with employing units. This income includes economic compensation, living subsidies, and other subsidies. Among these, the portion within 3 times the local average employee wage of the previous year is exempt from individual income tax. The portion exceeding 3 times is not combined into the comprehensive income for the current year, but is calculated separately according to the comprehensive income tax rate schedule. On this schedule, the tax rate is 3% for the portion within 36,000 yuan annually, and 10% for the portion from 36,000 yuan to 144,000 yuan. It increases in tiers above that up to 45%. For example, if the local average annual employee wage of the previous year is 100,000 yuan, 3 times is 300,000 yuan. If you receive 360,000 yuan in compensation, tax is calculated only on the excess 60,000 yuan, which amounts to 3,480 yuan. If the entire 360,000 yuan were calculated according to this table, it would be 58,080 yuan. This rule has been implemented since January 1, 2019, with no expiration date specified (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Ministry of Finance, State Taxation Administration (2018). Notice on Issues Concerning the Convergence of Preferential Policies After the Amendment of the Individual Income Tax Law (Cai Shui [2018] No. 164, Article 5, Item (1), Article 8, Article 9). <https://fgk.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfgk/c102416/c5202364/content.html> (State Taxation Administration Policy and Regulation Database); Ministry of Finance, State Taxation Administration (2023). Announcement on Continuing the Implementation of the Individual Income Tax Policy for Annual One-Off Bonuses (Announcement No. 30 of 2023). <https://fgk.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfgk/c102416/c5211524/content.html> (State Taxation Administration Policy and Regulation Database); Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018 Amendment). Individual Income Tax Law (Articles 3, 9, Individual Income Tax Rate Table I). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf724bd0609>
entries.notes: In the same document, the item for annual one-off bonuses had an expiration date, which was later extended to December 31, 2027. The item for compensation upon rescinding labor relations has no expiration date specified and does not follow the bonus provision. The document specifically named only economic compensation, living subsidies, and other subsidies, without separately naming pay in lieu of notice and compensation for unlawful termination. If unsure whether these two items count, call 12366 to consult the local tax bureau. Which figure is used for the "local average employee wage of the previous year" is also subject to the local tax bureau. For how compensation itself is calculated, see Item 4 (Calculate N First When Laid Off), Item 5 (Without 30 Days' Prior Notice), and Item 6 (Compensation for Unlawful Termination) of this section. One-off subsidies received for early retirement or internal retirement have separate calculation methods and do not apply to this rule.

entries.title: When moving to work in another city, transfer pension and medical insurance relations to the new contribution location so payment years continue accumulating; do not surrender the insurance
entries.cost: Costs no money. After participating in insurance and paying contributions in the new location, the transfer application is submitted by your new employer or yourself, taking a trip to the counter or handled online. The pension part takes several dozen working days from start to finish, and medical insurance takes around 15 working days.
entries.summary: When changing cities for work, both pension and medical insurance relations can follow you, with previously contributed years continuing to add up. Before reaching the age to draw a pension, you cannot surrender the insurance to withdraw the money. If medical insurance is interrupted for more than 3 months, you may have to wait up to 6 months in the new location before being reimbursed, so do not leave too long a gap in between.
entries.benefit: The Social Insurance Law stipulates that for those employed in another locality (formally termed "cross-pooling areas"), pension relations transfer with the individual, and contribution years are calculated cumulatively. The same applies to employee medical insurance: the relations follow the person, and years are calculated cumulatively. Upon retirement, pensions are calculated by segments and paid centrally. Transferring pension relations across provinces is handled according to the interim measures for transfer and continuation forwarded by the General Office of the State Council. Before reaching the age to receive benefits, pension relations must not be terminated and insurance surrender must not be processed. The Social Insurance Law also specifies that individual accounts must not be withdrawn early. The money in the individual account is transferred entirely with principal and interest. The portion contributed by the employer is called the pooled fund, which is transferred at 12% of your actual wage base for contributions in each year after 1998. When claiming a pension, it is calculated based on your contribution wages in each year, contribution years, and the average wage in each year of the receiving location. The procedure is that after participating in insurance and contributing in the new location, the employer or you submit a written application to the new contribution location. The new contribution location reviews it within 15 working days, and the original contribution location completes the transfer-out within 15 working days of receiving the letter of consent to receive. After the new contribution location receives the relations and funds, it concludes the process within another 15 working days. According to the 2020 cross-provincial handling list, this matter was to achieve cross-provincial handling by the end of that year. You only need to apply to the receiving location and do not need to return to the transferring location to process it. For employee medical insurance, the original contribution location must first suspend coverage and insurance must already be joined in the new location before you can apply for a transfer. Applications can be made online via the National Medical Insurance Service Platform or at the counter. The original contribution location transfers out within 10 working days, the new contribution location transfers in within 5 working days, and the balance of the individual account is transferred over together. If the interruption before transfer is within 3 months, after supplementary contributions are made according to the regulations of the new location, no waiting period is set: reimbursement is available in the month of payment, and the gap period can also be reimbursed retroactively. If interrupted for more than 3 months, the waiting period is set according to local regulations, in principle not exceeding 6 months (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2010, 2018 Amendment). Social Insurance Law (Articles 14, 19, 32). <https://www.gov.cn/guoqing/2021-10/29/content_5647616.htm>; Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, Ministry of Finance (2009). Interim Measures for the Transfer and Continuation of Basic Pension Insurance Relations of Urban Enterprise Employees (forwarded by Guo Ban Fa [2009] No. 66, Articles 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2009-12/29/content_8104.htm>; General Office of the State Council (2020). Guiding Opinions on Accelerating the Promotion of "Cross-Provincial Handling" of Government Services (Guo Ban Fa [2020] No. 35, Annex Item 7). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-09/29/content_5548125.htm>; National Healthcare Security Administration Office, Ministry of Finance General Office (2021). Interim Measures for the Transfer and Continuation of Basic Medical Insurance Relations (Yi Bao Ban Fa [2021] No. 43, Articles 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-11/28/content_5653856.htm>; National Healthcare Security Administration (2021). Policy Interpretation of the Interim Measures for the Transfer and Continuation of Basic Medical Insurance Relations (National Medical Insurance Service Platform website fuwu.nhsa.gov.cn). <http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2021-11/28/content_5653855.htm>
entries.notes: If the inter-provincial destination is not the province where household registration (hukou) is located, and the male is age 50 or older or the female is age 40 or older, pension relations remain in the original contribution location. The new location only opens a temporary account, recording all contributions from the employer and the individual. The rules for where to claim the pension upon retirement are as follows: If relations are in the province of household registration, receive it in the household registration locality. If not in the household registration locality, but contributions have cumulatively reached 10 years in the locality where relations are held, receive it locally. If under 10 years in all localities, transfer back to the last locality where 10 years of contributions were completed to receive it. If under 10 years in every locality, aggregate to the household registration locality to receive it. Different receiving locations use different average wages to calculate pensions. How transfers are made across cities within the same province is determined by measures established by each province; inquire with the local social insurance agency. Those who are already receiving pensions do not transfer relations anymore. For how years are calculated after contribution interruptions and which qualifications require continuous contributions, see Section 7, Item 18 (Social Insurance Interruption). For paying social insurance on your own without joining an employer, see Section 31, Item 11 (Flexible Employment).

entries.title: If the employer has not signed a written labor contract with you after one full month of employment, you can claim double wages starting from the second month, for at most 11 months; if still unsigned after one full year, it is deemed that an open-ended contract has been signed
entries.cost: Costs no money. Retain evidence of working during normal times: salary bank flows, attendance records, work badges, and chat records in work groups. If the employer refuses to acknowledge it, you must apply for labor arbitration. Arbitration is free of charge, concluding within 45 days after acceptance, extended by at most 15 days. Those who disagree can still go to court; first-instance regular procedures must be concluded within 6 months according to regulations, which can be extended, with attorney fees paid out of pocket. The difficulty lies in having to withstand the pressure of demanding money while still working at this firm.
entries.summary: If the employer has not signed a written contract with you after one full month of working, an extra month's wage is given each month starting from the second month, for at most 11 additional months. If still unsigned after one full year, it is regarded as having already signed a contract with no expiration date. Sign when the employer hands the contract to you; those who intentionally stall and refuse to sign cannot obtain this money.
entries.benefit: The Labor Contract Law provides that establishing an employment relationship requires signing a written labor contract. If it is not signed on the day you start work, it must be signed within one month starting from the day you begin working. If more than one month but less than one year has elapsed since you began working and it has still not been signed, the employer must pay you double wage each month. The Implementation Regulations specify the start and end dates: calculated starting from the day after completing one full month of work until the day before the contract is belatedly signed. If you have worked for a full year and it has still not been signed, double wage is calculated up to the day before completing the full year, for a maximum of 11 months. Starting from the day of completing one full year, both parties are deemed to have entered into an open-ended labor contract, and the employer must belatedly sign one immediately. An open-ended contract is a contract with no agreed expiration date. The Supreme People's Court judicial interpretation effective September 2025 provides that double wage is calculated on a monthly basis, and periods of less than a month are calculated based on actual working days. If the employer can prove that the failure to sign was due to force majeure, or due to your own intentional conduct or gross negligence, it does not have to pay. Within the first month of work, if the employer notifies you in writing to sign and you refuse to sign, the employer may notify you in writing to terminate the employment relationship. In this case, the employer pays no economic compensation, paying only your wages for the days you actually worked. For the period that is already deemed an open-ended contract, if you demand double wage again, the court will not support it (National)

entries.notes: Regarding how soon you must claim that extra portion of wages, the Supreme People's Court has not established a nationwide standard. The 2023 Draft for Comments contained a statute of limitations rule, but it was not retained in the interpretation officially promulgated in 2025. Beijing's standard is that the extra portion is subject to a 1-year arbitration statute of limitations. It is calculated on a daily basis by counting back one year from the date you raise the claim. Calculation methods vary somewhat across localities, but the longer you delay, the fewer months you can recover. Therefore, apply for arbitration as soon as possible, whether while still employed or after leaving. For the general rules on the arbitration statute of limitations, see Section 8, Item 19 (Rights Protection Has a Time Limit). If the contract is belatedly signed and backdated to the first day of work, Beijing's standard is generally not to support double wage anymore, unless you can prove that the belated signing was not voluntary on your part. For this issue viewed from the employer's side, see Section 12, Item 16 (Signing a Written Contract Within the First Month of Employment).

entries.title: If your employer does not pay or underpays social insurance, file a complaint first to make it pay the arrears; if you want to resign and claim economic compensation because of this, state clearly in your resignation notice that it is because the employer failed to pay social insurance in accordance with the law
entries.cost: Costs no money. First check your own social insurance payment records, and save them by taking screenshots or printing them out. To demand back payments, call 12333 or go to the human resources and social security bureau's labor inspection to file a complaint. To claim economic compensation, go through labor arbitration, which is free of charge, with cases concluded within 45 days, extendable by at most 15 days. If dissatisfied, you can then go to court; under the rules, first-instance ordinary procedure must conclude trial within 6 months, which can be extended, with attorney fees paid out of pocket. The difficulty lies in needing to secure your next income first after resigning.
entries.summary: If your employer has not paid social insurance for you or has not paid enough, you can file a complaint to make it pay the arrears and additionally pay late fees. You can also notify the employer in writing to terminate the contract and claim economic compensation. The notice must clearly state that the reason is the employer's failure to pay social insurance in accordance with the law; if you write personal reasons, you will not receive it. Agreements stating that 'the employee voluntarily waives social insurance' do not count.
entries.benefit: The Social Insurance Law provides that employers must declare on their own and pay social insurance on time and in full. Except for statutory grounds such as force majeure, payments cannot be deferred, reduced, or exempted. If an employer infringes upon your social insurance rights and interests, you can request the social insurance administrative department or social insurance fee collection agency to handle the matter according to law. If an employer fails to pay on time and in full, the collection agency orders it to make up the shortfall within a specified time limit, and imposes a late fee of 0.05% per day starting from the date of arrears. If it still fails to pay after the deadline, it is fined 1 to 3 times the amount in arrears. Among the matters supervised by labor security inspection is whether employers participate in social insurance and pay social insurance premiums. Investigations are completed within 60 working days after case filing, and complex cases can be extended by another 30 working days. The Labor Contract Law provides that if an employer fails to pay social insurance for you according to law, you may terminate the labor contract, and the employer must pay economic compensation. If you give 30 days' advance notice and resign on your own, the employer does not have to pay economic compensation. Therefore, the notice must clearly state that the termination is because the employer failed to pay social insurance according to law. The Supreme People's Court judicial interpretation effective September 2025 explicitly states that agreements between the employer and you not to pay social insurance, or promises made by yourself that payment is not needed, are both void. If an employer fails to pay social insurance according to law, and you terminate the contract and claim economic compensation on these grounds, the court will support it according to law. If an employer fails to handle social insurance procedures for you, and the social insurance agency cannot process them retroactively, causing you to be unable to receive benefits, you can seek compensation for losses from the employer. This falls under labor disputes accepted by the courts (National)

entries.notes: To demand back payments, take the complaint route. The standard of the Beijing High People's Court and the arbitration commission is that simply demanding back payments does not count as a labor dispute, and you must go to the labor administrative department. Do not delay your complaint: if an unlawful act has not been discovered and no one has complained within 2 years, the labor security department will no longer investigate and handle it. Where payments have been continuously in arrears, the 2-year period is calculated starting from the date the non-payment stopped. The Supreme People's Court has not specified whether paying under a lower contribution base counts as 'failing to pay according to law' and whether you can claim economic compensation based on this. Beijing's standard lists only two situations: not establishing a social insurance account within one year prior to termination, or having incomplete insurance types. There is no nationwide unified standard for paying under a lower base, so ask your local arbitration commission first. If the employer previously converted social insurance funds into cash and paid it to you, and later paid the social insurance arrears, it can demand that you return that money. For work-related injuries occurring when work injury insurance was not paid, see Item 13 of this section (Failure to Pay Work Injury Insurance for You). For how years are calculated after payment interruptions, see Section 7, Item 18 (Interruption of Social Insurance Payments).

entries.title: When you resign and the company demands you pay liquidated damages, check which type it is first: liquidated damages can only be agreed upon for a service period with special training and non-compete restrictions; other terms are not permitted by law to stipulate liquidated damages
entries.cost: Costs no money. Pull out your labor contract, training agreement, and non-compete agreement and check them over, which takes a few minutes. If the company deducts wages to offset liquidated damages, go through labor arbitration to get it back. Arbitration is free of charge, with cases concluded within 45 days, extendable by at most 15 days. If dissatisfied, you can then go to court; under the rules, first-instance ordinary procedure must conclude trial within 6 months, which can be extended, with attorney fees paid out of pocket.
entries.summary: Where a contract states 'quitting early requires paying damages', the law allows this under only two circumstances: the company pays to send you for professional technical training, or non-compete restrictions. Where genuine special training exists, the damages paid cannot exceed the training expenses, and must also be proportionally converted based on the unserved portion of the service period.
entries.benefit: The Labor Contract Law provides that, except for the two situations of a service period for special training and non-compete restrictions, an employer shall not stipulate that an employee bear liquidated damages. The first situation is where the employer provides special training expenses and sends you for professional technical training, in which case it may agree with you on a service period. If you violate the service period by leaving early, you pay liquidated damages as agreed. Liquidated damages shall not exceed the training expenses provided by the employer. The amount the employer can actually demand shall not exceed the training expenses apportioned to the unserved portion of the service period. For example, if training expenses are 30,000 yuan, the service period is 3 years, and you leave after completing 2 full years, the employer can demand at most 10,000 yuan. Training expenses must have vouchers, including training fees, travel expenses during the training period, and other direct expenses incurred due to training. If you lawfully terminate the contract and leave due to employer faults such as failure to pay social insurance or wage arrears, it does not count as a breach of the service period, and the employer cannot demand liquidated damages. The second situation is non-compete restrictions; for the rules, see Section 11, Item 12 (Non-Compete Agreements). Additionally, contract clauses by which an employer exempts itself from statutory liabilities or excludes employees' rights are void (National)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2012 Amendment). Labor Contract Law (Articles 22, 23, 25, 26, 37, 90). <https://fgk.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfgk/c100009/c5193025/content.html> (Reprinted by the Policy and Regulation Database of the State Taxation Administration); State Council (2008). entries.notes: Not being able to demand liquidated damages does not mean you do not have to compensate a single cent upon leaving. If you leave without giving 30 days' advance written notice, or violate confidentiality or non-compete agreements, causing losses to the employer, you must compensate for the losses. As to how much the loss is, the employer must produce evidence. If the employer provided special perks such as hukou and agreed on a service period, and you leave early, the court may order you to compensate. The compensation amount depends on actual losses, the fault of both parties, and how long you have already worked. Beijing's standard is that if an employer agrees on liquidated damages on the grounds of helping obtain a hukou, liquidated damages will not be supported, but if you breach good faith and cause losses to the employer, you must still compensate. If you are terminated by the employer on grounds such as severe breach of discipline, severe dereliction of duty, or being held criminally liable, liquidated damages for the service period are still payable as usual. If the labor contract expires before the service period ends, the contract is extended until the service period ends, unless otherwise agreed by both parties. For how to recover deducted wages, see Section 7, Item 2 (When Owed Wages, Complain to Labor Inspection First). Rating the benefit as moderate is a matter of judgment: the amount of liquidated damages is stipulated in each individual contract, with no standardized number.

entries.title: If the employer wants to reassign your post or cut your pay, raise your objection in writing on the spot if you disagree; do not keep silent and work under the new arrangement for more than a month
entries.cost: Costs no money. After receiving notice of a post reassignment or pay cut, send a written message stating your disagreement and save a screenshot, which takes a few minutes. The difficulty lies in still working at this company and having to withstand the pressure of an open confrontation. If the employer dismisses you or deducts your money because of this, go through labor arbitration. Arbitration is free of charge, with cases concluded within 45 days after acceptance, extendable by at most 15 days. If dissatisfied, you can then go to court; under the rules, first-instance ordinary procedure must conclude trial within 6 months, which can be extended, with attorney fees paid out of pocket.
entries.summary: Changing a job post or changing wages constitutes modifying the contract, which requires mutual agreement through consultation between both parties, as well as being executed in writing. However, if you keep silent and work at the new post with the new wage for more than a month, courts generally will no longer rule the modification invalid simply because no written document was signed. If you disagree, say so in writing on the spot; both WeChat and email count.
entries.benefit: The Labor Contract Law provides that an employer and an employee may modify the content agreed upon in a labor contract only upon reaching an agreement through consultation. Modifications must be in written form. A judicial interpretation of the Supreme People's Court contains another rule. If both parties orally modify the contract upon mutual agreement, and actually perform according to the new content for more than one month, the modification is still valid. If you then claim the modification is invalid on the grounds that 'no written form was used', the court will not support it. The prerequisite is that the modified content is not unlawful and does not violate public order and good morals. The standard of the Beijing High People's Court and the Beijing Arbitration Commission is as follows. If the contract does not specify a post or specifies it unclearly, and the employer has legitimate reasons to reasonably reassign the post according to business operational needs, it is considered the employer's employment autonomy. Whether it is reasonable depends on four factors: whether it is necessary in terms of business operations, whether the purpose is legitimate, whether you are competent for the new post, and whether wages and benefits have deteriorated. If the contract explicitly specifies a post and does not stipulate how reassignments are handled, the employer's unilateral reassignment of the post constitutes a breach of contract, and the difference in wages must be paid retroactively with reference to the original post's wage. If the contract defines the work location in broad terms such as 'Nationwide' or 'Beijing', it is deemed an unclear agreement, and the actual location where you report for work shall prevail. The employer shall not change this location without legitimate reasons. If the employer fails to pay wages on time and in full, you may terminate the labor contract, and the employer must pay economic compensation (National; Beijing standards apply only in Beijing)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2012 Amendment). entries.notes: Reason for assigning Rating B: The rule that 'continuing to work without saying anything counts as agreement' is not directly stated in statutory provisions. It is deduced from Article 43 of the judicial interpretation and local judicial standards. There is no nationwide unified standard for 'reasonable post reassignment'; what is listed above is Beijing's standard. After raising an objection in writing, it is best to report to work as usual and expressly state your reservation of objections, because refusing to report to work may lead to the employer dismissing you for absenteeism. If the post reassignment is later found unreasonable, this dismissal constitutes unlawful termination, calculated according to Item 6 of this section (Compensation for Unlawful Termination). If found reasonable, you cannot receive this money. If the objective circumstances upon which the contract was entered into undergo major changes and no agreement on modification can be reached through consultation with you, the employer may terminate the contract. In this case, payment must be made according to Item 5 of this section (Failure to Give 30 Days' Advance Notice). For how to claim back the wages underpaid after a pay cut, see Section 7, Item 2 (When Owed Wages, Complain to Labor Inspection First). Rating the benefit as moderate is a matter of judgment: pay cut margins vary across companies, with no standardized number.

entries.title: If you are dispatched via labor dispatch to work at another company, your wages must be calculated under the same method as regular employees in similar positions, and if you suffer injury or damage at the employing unit where you work, both companies compensate jointly
entries.cost: Costs no money. Pull out your labor contract to see which company stamped it, which takes a few minutes. Then ask the dispatch company about the wages and social insurance written in the dispatch agreement; it has an obligation to tell you. If a dispute genuinely arises, go through labor arbitration, which is free of charge, with cases concluded within 45 days after acceptance, extendable by at most 15 days. If dissatisfied, you can then go to court; under the rules, first-instance ordinary procedure must conclude trial within 6 months, which can be extended, with attorney fees paid out of pocket.
entries.summary: Dispatched workers sign contracts with the dispatch company, but the unit where you work every day also has statutory obligations. Wages must be calculated under the same method as people in similar positions at that unit, and overtime pay and performance bonuses are also paid by it. If you suffer injury or damage at that unit, both companies compensate jointly, and you can demand it from either company. For months where you have no work after being returned, the dispatch company must still pay you according to the minimum wage.
entries.benefit: The Labor Contract Law stipulates that the labor dispatch company is your employer, which must sign a fixed-term contract of 2 years or more with you and pay wages on a monthly basis. During periods when you are not assigned to work, wages must be paid monthly at the local minimum wage. The dispatch company must inform you of the contents of the dispatch agreement and shall not deduct any wages paid to you by the entity where you actually work (legally termed the "accepting entity"). Neither entity may charge any fees to you. Dispatched workers have the right to equal pay for equal work as the employees of the accepting entity. The accepting entity must apply the same labor remuneration distribution method to positions of the same category. Where there are no positions of the same category, remuneration is determined with reference to the remuneration of identical or similar positions in the local area. The accepting entity must pay overtime pay and performance bonuses, provide benefits related to the position, and must not discriminate against dispatched workers. For continuous employment, normal wage adjustments must be made. Labor dispatch may only be used for temporary, auxiliary, or substitute positions; a temporary position refers to a position with a duration of no more than 6 months. The number of dispatched workers used by an accepting entity shall not exceed 10% of its total workforce. Where the accepting entity causes harm to a dispatched worker, the dispatch company and the accepting entity bear joint and several liability for compensation. Joint and several liability means you can seek full compensation from either one of them, or seek compensation from both. If a labor dispute arises between you and either party, both parties are joint parties to the arbitration. If you suffer a work-related injury at the accepting entity, the dispatch company shall apply for the work-related injury assessment and bear the work-related injury insurance liability, and the accepting entity must assist in the investigation. The accepting entity may return you only under several statutory circumstances. Where labor is used under the guise of contracting or outsourcing but is actually conducted in the manner of labor dispatch, it shall likewise be handled according to the provisions on labor dispatch (Nationwide, Interim Provisions effective March 1, 2014)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2012 Amendment). Labor Contract Law (Articles 58, 60, 62, 63, 66, 92). <https://fgk.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfgk/c100009/c5193025/content.html> (reprinted by the Policy and Regulation Database of the State Taxation Administration); Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2014).
