entries.notes: Equal pay for equal work compares whether the same distribution method is used for positions of the same category; it does not guarantee that everyone takes home the exact same penny. After being returned, if the dispatch company re-dispatches you under conditions reduced from the original contract and you do not agree, the dispatch company may not terminate the contract on these grounds. If the dispatch company rescinds or terminates the contract with you due to statutory circumstances, it must pay economic compensation; for the calculation method, see Item 4 of this section (Calculate N clearly before being laid off). If injured at the accepting entity, first have the dispatch company report the work-related injury. If it does not report, report it yourself; see Item 11 of this section (Undergo work-related injury assessment). For deducted or unpaid wages, see Section 7, Item 2 (File a complaint with labor inspection first when wages are owed). Rating the benefit as moderate is based on judgment: the gap in equal pay for equal work and the magnitude of harm vary from person to person, with no uniform figure.

chapters.title: How to Care for a Newborn
chapters.intro: Scope: Infant mortality and money. This section covers only matters that bear on whether a baby can survive or how much money you will spend, and only includes those with sufficiently large differences and hard evidence. How to soothe, how to carry, and other parenting details are not covered in this book. For things to handle before birth and on the day of hospital discharge, see Section 27.

entries.title: Have infants sleep on their backs, on a firm, flat surface, sharing a room but not a bed, with no soft items in the bed
entries.cost: Free. Changing to a firm mattress costs several hundred yuan. The difficulty lies in resisting advice from elders and sticking to this consistently
entries.summary: While a child is still an infant, have them lie face-up to sleep on a non-inclined, firm, flat surface; inclined cradles and infant seats cannot be used as beds. Adults and the child sleep in the same room, but not in the same bed. Do not place soft items such as pillows, quilts, crib bumpers, or plush toys in the bed. In the United States alone, about 3,500 infants die each year from sleep-related causes.
entries.benefit: About 3,500 infants in the United States die each year from sleep-related causes. These include sudden infant death syndrome, ill-defined deaths, and accidental suffocation in bed. The safe sleep environment recommended by the American Academy of Pediatrics is: "Supine positioning; use of a firm, noninclined sleep surface; room-sharing without bed-sharing; and avoidance of soft bedding and overheating." Several other things can also reduce risk: breastfeeding, keeping the child away from nicotine and alcohol, vaccinating on schedule, and using a pacifier
entries.sources: Moon RY, Carlin RF, Hand I, Task Force on Sudden Infant Death Syndrome and the Committee on Fetus and Newborn (2022). Sleep-Related Infant Deaths: Updated 2022 Recommendations for Reducing Infant Deaths in the Sleep Environment. Pediatrics, 150(1), e2022057990. <https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2022-057990>
entries.notes: "No soft items in the bed" means not placing pillows, quilts, crib bumpers, plush toys, or infant head-shaping pillows at all. Do not place nursing pillows that seem very safe either. Inclined cradles and infant seats must not be used as sleeping places. In this section, this item makes the biggest difference and requires resisting pressure from elders the most

entries.title: Administer the first dose of the hepatitis B vaccine within 24 hours after birth
entries.cost: Free. The hepatitis B vaccine belongs to the National Immunization Program and is inherently free. It is administered right at the hospital on the day the baby is born, requiring no extra trip
entries.summary: The child should receive the first dose of the hepatitis B vaccine within 24 hours of birth. Among individuals infected with hepatitis B during infancy and early childhood, about 95% develop chronic hepatitis. Among those infected only in adulthood, the vast majority can recover on their own, so the earlier this dose is administered, the more effective it is. If the mother is hepatitis B surface antigen-positive, the child must also receive hepatitis B immunoglobulin within 12 hours of birth.
entries.benefit: The World Health Organization states: "All infants should receive the hepatitis B vaccine as soon as possible after birth, ideally within 24 hours." The reason is that "infection in infancy and early childhood will lead to chronic hepatitis in about 95% of cases." The vast majority of infections acquired in adulthood can self-heal (recover without treatment). The WHO's original words are that "less than 5%" of infections acquired in adulthood develop into chronic hepatitis. The National Health Commission's specifications for blocking mother-to-child transmission require that for children born to mothers who are hepatitis B surface antigen-positive, "the first dose of hepatitis B vaccine should be administered as early as possible within 12 hours after birth, and 100 international units of hepatitis B immunoglobulin should be injected at the same time"
entries.sources: World Health Organization. Hepatitis B fact sheet. <https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/hepatitis-b>; General Office of the National Health Commission (2020). Work Specification for the Prevention of Mother-to-Child Transmission of HIV, Syphilis, and Hepatitis B (2020 Edition). <https://wjw.xinjiang.gov.cn/hfpc/zhgl6/202012/08b7de496f0b40e586d4b99d00cf79c4.shtml> (reprinted by the Health Commission of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region)
entries.notes: If the mother is hepatitis B surface antigen-positive, the child must also receive an injection of hepatitis B immunoglobulin at birth. This matter should be checked and clarified during prenatal checkups; do not wait until after delivery to ask. For screenings the mother herself needs to undergo, see Section 1

entries.title: Receive all required vaccines under the National Immunization Program, entirely free of charge; if doses are missed, only make up the uncompleted doses
entries.cost: Free. The law explicitly states that "vaccination units administering immunization program vaccines shall not charge any fees." Several trips to the vaccination clinic will be required according to monthly age. Keep the vaccination certificate safe; do not lose it
entries.summary: Vaccines in the National Immunization Program are completely free, and vaccination clinics cannot charge fees. Vaccination certificates are checked when children enter nursery, kindergarten, and school; missed doses are generally identified and caught up. If missed, only make up the doses not yet completed without restarting from the beginning, and vaccination can continue even if the manufacturer changes.
entries.benefit: When children enter child care facilities and schools, child care institutions and schools must inspect their vaccination certificates. If any child is found not to have been vaccinated with immunization program vaccines in accordance with regulations, they must report to the vaccination unit and cooperate in urging the guardian to catch up on vaccination. Therefore, missed vaccines are generally discovered when checking vaccination certificates upon enrollment in child care and school. The 2026 edition schedule is currently being implemented. The human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine has been incorporated into the National Immunization Program. The starting vaccination age for the DTP vaccine was changed from 3 months of age to 2 months of age. There are 5 doses in total, with 1 dose administered at 2 months, 4 months, 6 months, 18 months, and 6 years of age, respectively. Age-eligible children in Tibet, Qinghai, Xinjiang, and the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps also receive routine Japanese encephalitis vaccination starting in March 2026. Several vaccines can be administered on the same day: at the current stage, National Immunization Program vaccines can all be administered simultaneously according to immunization schedules or catch-up principles. Two or more injectable vaccines must be administered at different sites; "it is strictly prohibited to mix two or more vaccines into the same syringe for administration." If not administered on the same day, an interval of not less than 28 days must be maintained between two or more injectable live attenuated vaccines. No interval restrictions are imposed between inactivated vaccines, oral live attenuated vaccines, and other vaccines. The catch-up principle for persons under 18 years of age is to catch up as early as possible, where "it is only necessary to make up the uncompleted doses, without needing to restart the full schedule of vaccination"; switching manufacturers for the same vaccine allows continuing the series (Nationwide, 2026 Edition Schedule)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2019). Vaccine Administration Law (Articles 48, 49). <http://ynswsjkw.yn.gov.cn/html/2019/faguiguizhangxin_0731/6509.html> (reprinted by Yunnan Provincial Health Commission); National Disease Control and Prevention Administration, National Health Commission (2026). Q&A on the Interpretation of the "Children's Immunization Schedule and Instructions for National Immunization Program Vaccines (2026 Edition)". <https://www.ndcpa.gov.cn/jbkzzx/c100013/common/content/content_2073002930292035584.html>
entries.notes: The most common misunderstanding is "the child has poor constitution, don't vaccinate yet." The official position is: a so-called "allergic constitution," family members having allergic diseases, or a child's past allergies to foods or drugs are not reasons to withhold vaccination. For atopic dermatitis (eczema), urticaria, allergic rhinitis, and bronchial asthma, vaccination can proceed normally as long as the condition is stable. If currently taking anti-allergy medication or using inhaled corticosteroids, vaccination can also proceed. Neonatal physiological jaundice and breast milk jaundice can also be vaccinated normally. There are only two true contraindications: a history of severe acute allergic reaction after receiving the same vaccine previously, or severe allergy to a known component in the vaccine. Children with immunodeficiencies, as well as children currently undergoing chemotherapy or radiotherapy or using immunosuppressants, must be evaluated individually; explain the situation at the vaccination clinic before deciding. For the first dose of hepatitis B, see Item 2. Self-paid non-immunization program vaccines charge additional vaccine fees and vaccination service fees, which have nothing to do with the free status mentioned in this entry.

entries.title: Feed exclusively breast milk for the first 6 months without even giving water, introduce complementary foods starting at 6 months while continuing breastfeeding
entries.cost: Free, and also saves money on infant formula. What it consumes is time, as nursing takes up a significant amount every day. The difficulty lies in keeping up the feeding continuously without stopping during the first 6 months
entries.summary: Initiate feeding within the child's first hour of life. Feed exclusively breast milk for the first 6 months, without even giving water. Starting at 6 months of age, introduce complementary foods, which must include iron-rich animal foods daily, and continue breastfeeding until 2 years of age or beyond. If breast milk is insufficient or cannot be fed, use infant formula.
entries.benefit: The World Health Organization's recommendation is to "initiate breastfeeding within the first hour of birth." During the first 6 months, practice "exclusive breastfeeding, meaning no other food or liquid is provided, including water." Then "from 6 months of age, start adding safe and adequate complementary foods while continuing to breastfeed up to 2 years of age or beyond." The National Health Commission's service guidelines also advocate exclusive breastfeeding from 0 to 6 months of age. These guidelines also require that from 6 months of age onward, "daily complementary food must include iron-rich animal foods"
entries.sources: World Health Organization. Breastfeeding. <https://www.who.int/health-topics/breastfeeding>; General Office of the National Health Commission (2024). Service Guidelines for Nutritional and Feeding Assessment of Infants and Young Children (Trial) (Guo Wei Ban Fu You Han [2024] No. 452). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202502/content_7002872.htm>
entries.notes: If breast milk is insufficient or physical conditions do not allow breastfeeding, use formula milk; there is no need to feel guilty. Whether to feed breast milk or formula milk makes far less of a difference than the safe sleep item; this is the author's judgment. The frequency of complementary feeding follows the Health Commission's service guideline: 1 to 2 times daily for 6 to 8 months of age, and 2 to 3 times daily for 9 to 12 months of age. Daily complementary foods should be selected from seven food categories, no fewer than four categories. For whether to avoid peanuts when a child has severe eczema or egg allergy, see Item 12 of this section (Don't avoid peanuts). If the mother is vegetarian and wants to feed the child a vegetarian diet, see Item 14 of this section (Supplement vitamin B12 daily if eating vegetarian).

entries.title: Prepare powdered infant formula with water above 70 °C, cool before feeding, and discard leftovers
entries.cost: Free. Wait a few extra minutes each time for the milk to cool. The difficulty lies in waiting for the water temperature to drop before mixing even when the baby is crying with hunger
entries.summary: Powdered infant formula is not sterile and may harbor a bacterium that kills 40% to 80% of infected newborns. Pour hot water first and wait until it drops to about 73.8 °C before adding formula powder; in most cases, this reduces the bacterium to below one-hundred-thousandth of its original level. Hot water reduces vitamin C somewhat, but tested formulas still meet standards. Cool after preparing before feeding, and discard leftovers.
entries.benefit: Powdered infant formula is not sterile and may carry Cronobacter sakazakii. The case fatality rate following infection in newborns is reported to be 40% to 80%. Experimental studies show: pouring hot water into the bottle first and waiting until the water temperature drops to about 73.8 °C before adding formula powder keeps the milk liquid temperature above 70 °C in the vast majority of cases. This can reduce the bacterium by more than 5 log cycles, down to less than one-hundred-thousandth of the original level. The trade-off of hot water is in vitamin C. WHO and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations held an expert meeting in 2006. The data presented at the meeting showed: when preparing with boiling water, only vitamin C decreased significantly, by 5.6% to 65.6% across 4 infant formulas. Vitamin C is inherently over-fortified during formula manufacturing. Even for the type with the greatest reduction, there was still 9.0 mg per 100 kcal after preparation, higher than the lower limit of 8 mg in the Codex Alimentarius standard. The meeting saw only this single study, so it drew no definitive conclusions on the matter
entries.sources: Beary MA, Daly SE, Baker J, Snyder AB (2025). Assessing Hot Water Reconstitution Instructions and Labeling of Powdered Infant Formula to Ensure Cronobacter spp. Reduction. Journal of Food Protection, 88(9), 100571. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfp.2025.100571>；Sima WG, Legesse T, Girma S, et al. (2025). Emerging microbial risks: Cronobacter sakazakii in powdered infant formula for infants under six months of age in Ethiopia. BMC Microbiology, 26, 307. <https://doi.org/10.1186/s12866-025-04380-y>；World Health Organization & FAO (2007). Safe preparation, storage and handling of powdered infant formula: guidelines. <https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241595414>；Bundesinstitut für Risikobewertung (2022). Recommendations for the hygienic preparation of powdered infant formula. Updated BfR Opinion No. 009/2022. <https://doi.org/10.17590/20220510-104706>；Agostoni C, Axelsson I, Goulet O, et al. (2004). Preparation and handling of powdered infant formula: a commentary by the ESPGHAN Committee on Nutrition. Journal of Pediatric Gastroenterology and Nutrition, 39(4), 320-322. <https://doi.org/10.1097/00005176-200410000-00002>；Silano M, Paganin P, Davanzo R (2016). Time for the 70 °C water precautionary option in the home dilution of powdered infant formula. Italian Journal of Pediatrics, 42, 17. <https://doi.org/10.1186/s13052-016-0228-9>；Losio MN, Pavoni E, Finazzi G, et al. (2018). Preparation of Powdered Infant Formula: Could Product's Safety Be Improved? Journal of Pediatric Gastroenterology and Nutrition, 67(4), 543-546. <https://doi.org/10.1097/MPG.0000000000002100>
entries.notes: Controversy: The German Federal Institute for Risk Assessment (BfR) issued an opinion in 2022 stating that for full-term healthy infants, preparation with water at 20 to 50 °C is sufficient. It noted that what most manufacturers write on cans is also 40 to 50 °C. Its rationale is that 70 °C water cools very quickly when poured into a baby bottle, so the actual bacteria killed is not as high as calculated. Hot water also causes some nutrient loss, and feeding before it cools will scald the child. The European Society for Paediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition (ESPGHAN) in 2004 also did not favor preparation with boiling water, citing concerns about destroying vitamins and probiotics added to formula. The WHO and UN FAO still recommend above 70 °C. Preterm infants, infants with birth weights under 2500 grams, infants under 2 months of age, and immunocompromised infants are at the highest risk and should have formula prepared according to the 70 °C standard, or consult a doctor. For full-term healthy infants prepared according to the temperature on the can, this German opinion considered the infection risk extremely low. This 70 °C threshold comes from public health guidelines. Beary et al.'s original words are that "public health guidelines for caregivers of high-risk infants recommend reconstituting PIF with water heated to at least 70 °C (158 °F) to inactivate microorganisms." Do not use water that has sat in a thermal flask for a full day to prepare formula. Nor should prepared formula be left at room temperature waiting to be fed at the next meal

entries.title: Do not feed honey to infants under 1 year of age
entries.cost: Free
entries.summary: If a child is under 1 year old, do not feed honey. Honey water, honey mixed into complementary foods, and pastries containing honey all count. Honey may harbor bacteria that cause botulism. The intestinal flora in adults can suppress it, but infants cannot.
entries.benefit: The US CDC states "do not feed honey to children under 1 year of age" because "honey may contain bacteria that cause infant botulism." The intestinal microbiota of adults can suppress these spores (the dormant state of this bacterium), but infants cannot
entries.sources: US CDC. Preventing Botulism. <https://www.cdc.gov/botulism/prevention/index.html>
entries.notes: What cannot be fed includes honey water, complementary foods mixed with honey, and pastries containing honey

entries.title: The vitamin K injection at birth must be administered
entries.cost: 0 yuan to several tens of yuan. This expense is usually already included in the hospitalization cost for childbirth and does not require an additional payment
entries.summary: Newborns store very little vitamin K in their bodies, and lack of supplementation can cause bleeding; the late-onset type often presents as intracranial hemorrhage. In Tashkent, where this prophylaxis was not universally implemented, 478 out of every 100,000 newborns developed this bleeding. With prophylaxis, it is estimated that over 78% of cases can be eliminated. For births at home or in non-standard institutions, actively ask whether it was administered.
entries.benefit: Newborns have very little vitamin K stored in their bodies. Failure to supplement may lead to vitamin K deficiency bleeding; the late-onset form often manifests as intracranial hemorrhage (bleeding inside the brain). The Belgian consensus recommendation is "a single intramuscular injection of 1 or 2 mg of vitamin K at birth." In areas where prophylaxis is not systematically provided, the incidence of vitamin K deficiency bleeding is 478 cases per 100,000 people. This figure comes from 42,000 newborns in Tashkent. The authors estimate that prophylaxis can reduce the incidence by "greater than 78.5%"
entries.sources: Fiesack S, Smits A, Rayyan M, et al. (2021). Nutrients, 13(11), 4109. <https://doi.org/10.3390/nu13114109>；Tursunov D, Yoshida Y, Yrysov K, et al. (2018). Nagoya Journal of Medical Science, 80(1), 11. <https://doi.org/10.18999/nagjms.80.1.11>
entries.notes: When giving birth in regular hospitals in China, hospitals generally administer this shot routinely; this is the author's experience, as no unified national official regulation was found. Check the discharge summary before leaving the hospital, or ask. For births at home or in non-standard institutions, take the initiative to confirm. The injection mentioned here is intramuscular. That Belgian consensus refers to oral administration as a "somewhat inferior alternative," used only when parents refuse injection: 2 mg orally at birth, followed for breastfed infants by 1 to 2 mg weekly for 3 consecutive months

entries.title: For infants under 3 months of age, go directly to the hospital once body temperature reaches 38 °C, instead of observing at home
entries.cost: Registration fee plus examination costs several hundred yuan
entries.summary: If a child is under 3 months old, go directly to the hospital once the body temperature reaches 38 °C. Do not observe at home, and do not first give fever-reducing medication to wait and see. The American Academy of Pediatrics specifically formulated management pathways for febrile infants who appear well, so "looking in reasonably good spirits" cannot serve as a reason to wait at home. UK guidelines also classify children under 3 months of age with a fever reaching 38 °C as high risk for serious illness.
entries.benefit: The American Academy of Pediatrics developed dedicated guidelines for well-appearing, full-term infants aged 8 to 60 days. This guideline defines fever as "temperature ≥38.0 °C." It divides infants into three tiers—8 to 21 days, 22 to 28 days, and 29 to 60 days of age—giving a management pathway for each. Infants under 8 days of age are not within the scope of this guideline. The UK NICE fever guideline covers children under 5 years of age. It states that children under 3 months of age with a temperature of 38 °C or higher belong to the "high-risk group for serious illness"
entries.sources: Pantell RH, Roberts KB, Adams WG, et al. (2021). Evaluation and Management of Well-Appearing Febrile Infants 8 to 60 Days Old. Pediatrics, 148(2), e2021052228. <https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2021-052228>; NICE (2019, updated 2021). Fever in under 5s: assessment and initial management (NG143), 1.2.12. <https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng143/chapter/Recommendations>
entries.notes: For children in this age range, a serious bacterial infection may only present as fever. Therefore, appearing "in good spirits" cannot be used as a reason to observe at home. Nor should you give fever-reducing medication on your own first and then wait to see.

entries.title: No Matter How Tired or Angry You Are, Never Shake an Infant
entries.cost: Costs nothing. The difficulty lies in stopping yourself when you are extremely tired and furious.
entries.summary: Infants have large heads and weak necks. Forceful shaking can cause bleeding in their brain and eyes, which can be fatal or leave lifelong disabilities. Gentle swaying when soothing to sleep does not count; what is dangerous is uncontrollable, violent shaking. When you are on the verge of losing your temper, place the baby back in the crib and step away for a few minutes; letting them cry for a little while is safer than holding and shaking them.
entries.benefit: An infant's head makes up a large proportion of their body, and their neck muscles are weak. Violent shaking can cause intracranial hemorrhage and retinal hemorrhage (bleeding in the brain and eyes), which can be fatal or result in lifelong disability. Gentle swaying when soothing them to sleep does not count; what is dangerous is uncontrolled, violent shaking. In medicine, this type of injury caused by shaking or impact is called "abusive head trauma." It is the leading cause of death from head trauma in children under 2 years of age. In the United States from 1999 to 2014, it caused the deaths of nearly 2,250 children under 5 years old.
entries.sources: Spies EL, Klevens J (2016). Fatal Abusive Head Trauma Among Children Aged <5 Years — United States, 1999–2014. MMWR 65(20):505-509. <https://doi.org/10.15585/mmwr.mm6520a1>; Choudhary AK et al. (2018). Consensus statement on abusive head trauma in infants and young children. Pediatric Radiology 48(8):1048-1065. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00247-018-4149-1>
entries.notes: When you truly reach the point of losing control, first put the baby back into the crib and step away for a few minutes. Letting them cry for a little while is far safer than shaking them in your arms. People caring for a baby alone and those who are chronically sleep-deprived must remember this most of all. On how to manage your own emotions, see Section 3.

entries.title: Do Not Choose Diapers by Brand, Look at Three Things: Fit, Frequency of Changes, and Whether They Have Been Flagged in Random Inspections
entries.cost: Ranges from two to three hundred to over a thousand CNY per month, depending on which tier you use.
entries.summary: No official agency has ever ranked "which brand is best." There are only two things you can look up: product quality random inspection bulletins from the State Administration for Market Regulation, and regulatory authorities' investigations into specific incidents. Expensive does not equal safe; imported does not equal compliant. Buy a small pack first to test for a week, see if the baby gets diaper rash or red marks, and only stock up if it fits well.
entries.benefit: No official agency has ever published a ranking of "which brand is best," so this book does not provide brand recommendations. There are only two categories of verifiable information. One is product quality random inspection bulletins from the State Administration for Market Regulation. The other is regulatory authorities' investigations into specific incidents. After the "formamide issue in infant and toddler disposable diapers" drew public attention in June 2026, the State Administration for Market Regulation took the lead in establishing a joint investigation team to conduct an inspection.
entries.sources: State Administration for Market Regulation (2026-06-22). The State Administration for Market Regulation takes the lead in establishing a joint investigation team to investigate the "formamide issue in infant and toddler disposable diapers": "In response to media reports regarding the 'formamide issue in infant and toddler disposable diapers,' the State Administration for Market Regulation, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, the National Health Commission, and the National Disease Control and Prevention Administration attach great importance to the matter and have established a joint investigation team to investigate the relevant issues of formamide in infant and toddler disposable diapers and handle them in accordance with laws and regulations. Relevant details will be published in a timely manner." <https://www.samr.gov.cn/xw/zj/art/2026/art_78c0425db7604b27bd7a3f36ba319975.html>; Reprinted by the Chinese Government Network. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202606/content_7072931.htm>; NHS. Nappy rash (reviewed 2026-08-28). <https://www.nhs.uk/baby/caring-for-a-newborn/nappy-rash/>
entries.notes: When the joint investigation team was established, it only stated that "relevant details will be published in a timely manner." As of September 30, 2026, no conclusions from this investigation have been found on the official website of the State Administration for Market Regulation or in recent national supervisory spot-check bulletins. How to buy in practice: Expensive does not equal safe; imported does not equal compliant. Buy a small pack first to test for a week to see if the child gets diaper rash or red marks, and only stock up if it is suitable. These few sentences are the author's practical experience. The UK NHS notes that common causes of diaper rash are urine and feces staying in contact with the skin for too long, diaper changes not being frequent enough, and the diaper chafing the skin. Some diapers that do not absorb water or are not breathable can also cause it. The NHS also recommends that diapers should fit properly and not be fastened too tightly. For methods to check inspection bulletins, see Section 5.

entries.title: Consider Big-Ticket Items in the Order of "Borrow, Buy Secondhand, Buy New"; Do Not Buy Everything at Once
entries.cost: Requires no additional expenditure; the money saved is usually measured in thousands of CNY. The difficulty lies in resisting the urge to buy everything all at once.
entries.summary: Strollers, swaddles, and toys are used for a short time; borrow them first, buy secondhand if borrowing is not an option, and only buy new as a last resort. For secondhand car seats, make sure they have not been in a relatively severe crash, have not been recalled, and have all parts complete—if this cannot be confirmed, do not use them. In a Scottish study, routinely sleeping on a mattress used by another child was associated with approximately three times the risk of sudden infant death, though it is unclear whether the mattress caused it. Mattresses are best bought new.
entries.benefit: Strollers, cribs, swaddles, and toys have very short periods of use, and supply in the secondhand market far exceeds demand. Three safety boundaries must be maintained for secondhand items. The first is car seats. The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration recommends replacing and never reusing a car seat that has been in a moderate or severe crash. Only when all five conditions are met is it considered a minor crash, allowing the seat to continue being used. The five conditions are: the vehicle could be driven away, the vehicle door nearest the car seat was undamaged, no one in the vehicle was injured, the airbags did not deploy, and there is no visible damage to the car seat. Secondhand car seats must satisfy five confirmations before use. The five items are: it has not been in a moderate or severe crash, has labels with the manufacture date and model number, has not been recalled, has all parts complete, and still has the instruction manual. The manufacture date and model number are used to check for recalls and whether the seat is too old. The second is mattresses. A study in Scotland compared infants who died suddenly with healthy infants of the same age, retrospectively checking what mattress each had slept on. Routinely sleeping on a mattress previously used by another child was associated with a higher risk of sudden infant death syndrome (OR 3.07, approximately 3-fold, 95% CI 1.51–6.22). It was 4.78 when the mattress came from another home and 1.64 when it came from the child's own home, the latter showing no meaningful difference. The authors stated that current evidence is insufficient to determine whether the mattress itself caused it. The third is cribs. The United States implemented new mandatory crib standards on June 28, 2011, which secondhand cribs must also meet. Traditional drop-side crib styles were phased out. The US Consumer Product Safety Commission stated that old cribs would have to be dismantled and tested to destruction to know whether they comply, so no self-inspection checklist can be provided. From November 2007 to April 2010, 147 deaths related to standard full-size cribs were reported in the United States. Among them, 35 were due to structural failure of the crib, and 18 were related to malfunctions of drop-side rails. Loose screws caused at least 10 deaths. US law classifies inclined infant sleepers as banned products regardless of the year manufactured, written into regulatory rules in 2023 (US, UK).
entries.sources: The money-saving portion is the author's experience, without direct literature citations; US NHTSA. Car Seat Use After a Crash. <https://www.nhtsa.gov/car-seats-and-booster-seats/car-seat-use-after-crash>; US NHTSA. Used Car Seat Safety Checklist. <https://www.nhtsa.gov/car-seats-and-booster-seats/used-car-seat-safety-checklist>; Tappin D, Brooke H, Ecob R, Gibson A (2002). Used infant mattresses and sudden infant death syndrome in Scotland: case-control study. BMJ, 325(7371), 1007. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.325.7371.1007>; Blair P, Fleming P, Smith I (1997). Case-control study of sudden infant death syndrome in Scotland. Income level or bed sharing would confound any effect of previous use of mattress. BMJ, 315(7111), 812. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.315.7111.812a>; US Consumer Product Safety Commission (2010). Safety Standards for Full-Size Baby Cribs and Non-Full-Size Baby Cribs; Final Rule. Federal Register 2010-32178. <https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2010/12/28/2010-32178/safety-standards-for-full-size-baby-cribs-and-non-full-size-baby-cribs-final-rule>; US Consumer Product Safety Commission (2023). Ban of Inclined Sleepers for Infants. Federal Register 2023-17350. <https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2023/08/16/2023-17350/ban-of-inclined-sleepers-for-infants>; For impulsive spending, see Section 5.
entries.notes: The level of evidence remains C because the money-saving half lacks literature. Each of the three safety boundaries has its sources, but they are all from the US and the UK. No domestic official alerts specifically targeting secondhand cribs or secondhand car seats were found in China. Objections were raised regarding the mattress study: in 1997, scholars wrote in a letter that household income and bed-sharing could confound any effect of a secondhand mattress. For why car seats must be used when riding in a vehicle, see Section 1, Item 10 (Car Seats). For how infants should sleep and what to place in the crib, see Item 1 of this section (Sleeping on the Back). For postpartum care centers, early education classes, and infant swimming centers, this book neither recommends nor rejects them. However, they are all substantial expenses that you can choose to spend or not spend, and the 24-hour cooling-off period discussed in Section 5 applies to them.

entries.title: If Your Child Has Severe Eczema or Egg Allergy, Do Not Avoid Peanuts; Introduce Them Early Under a Doctor's Guidance, but Never Feed Whole Peanuts
entries.cost: A jar of peanut butter costs a few tens of CNY. Fed a few times a week, it is easy to do. Before introducing it, take the child to see a doctor for an evaluation.
entries.summary: Infants with severe eczema or egg allergy regularly consumed peanuts starting between 4 and 11 months of age. Among those who initially had no reaction on skin prick tests, only 1.9% of those who ate peanuts developed a peanut allergy by age 5, compared to 13.7% of those who completely avoided them. Among those who already had a slight skin test reaction, 10.6% of those who ate them developed an allergy compared to 35.3% who avoided them. Take the child to see a doctor before introducing them, and never feed whole peanuts, which can be aspirated into the airway.
entries.benefit: The UK LEAP randomized trial enrolled 640 infants with severe eczema, egg allergy, or both. They were 4 to 11 months old at enrollment. They were randomly divided into two groups: one regularly consumed peanut products, and the other avoided them completely, assessing peanut allergy rates at 60 months of age. Among the 530 participants with a negative peanut skin prick test at enrollment, 13.7% in the avoidance group developed an allergy versus 1.9% in the consumption group (P < 0.001). Among the 98 participants who already had a weakly positive skin test at enrollment, 35.3% in the avoidance group developed an allergy versus 10.6% in the consumption group (P = 0.004). There was no difference in serious adverse events between the two groups.
entries.sources: Du Toit G, Roberts G, Sayre PH, et al. (2015). Randomized trial of peanut consumption in infants at risk for peanut allergy. New England Journal of Medicine, 372(9), 803-813. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1414850>; General Office of the National Health Commission (2020). Core Information on Health Education for Infant and Toddler Feeding. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-08/01/content_5531915.htm>; Perkin MR et al. (2016). Randomized Trial of Introduction of Allergenic Foods in Breast-Fed Infants. New England Journal of Medicine, 374(18), 1733-1743. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1514210> (The EAT trial in general infants mentioned in the notes)
entries.notes: **The format must only be thinned peanut butter or peanut powder mixed into complementary food; never give whole peanuts.** The National Health Commission's core feeding information explicitly states: "Whole peanuts, tree nuts, jelly, and similar foods are easily aspirated into the trachea and cause choking, and infants and young children should avoid consuming them." For what to do if choking occurs, see Section 13, Item 43 (Infant Choking and Unable to Cry) for under 1 year old, and Section 13, Item 26 (Someone Choking and Unable to Speak) for over 1 year old. This applies only to high-risk children: those with severe eczema or who are already allergic to eggs. **An evaluation by a doctor must be conducted before introduction; do not try it at home on your own**: the LEAP trial performed a skin prick test on every child before enrollment. Children with a skin test wheal greater than 4 mm were excluded from the trial and were not allowed to eat peanuts. The evidence for general children is much weaker. In another trial of 1,162 general breastfed infants, analyzed by group allocation, food allergy occurred in 5.6% of the early introduction group and 7.1% of the standard group, a non-significant difference (P = 0.32); the difference was significant only among the subset of children who actually adhered to the regimen (2.4% vs. 7.3%). This method of calculation tends to exaggerate the effect, and the authors themselves stated that the analysis by assigned group failed to prove efficacy, though it also indicated that early introduction is safe. Official Chinese feeding documents currently have no stance on "whether allergenic foods should be introduced early or avoided," so this entry is written based on international trial evidence. Timing should also be noted: LEAP started at 4 months of age, whereas China recommends starting complementary foods at 6 completed months of age, see Item 4 of this section (Exclusive Breastfeeding for the First 6 Months). At what age and how to start for high-risk children should follow the doctor's instructions.

entries.title: Keep an Eye on Several Signals of Neonatal Jaundice: Jaundice Within 24 Hours of Birth, or Being Difficult to Wake and Not Feeding, Warrant Going to the Hospital the Same Day; Becoming Increasingly Jaundiced or Having Pale Stools Warrants Being Checked as Soon as Possible
entries.cost: Registration plus bilirubin testing costs within a few hundred CNY. If phototherapy is needed, it typically involves about two days under blue light in the hospital. The difficulty lies in making this trip even when the baby looks fine.
entries.summary: Over 80% of newborns will have some jaundice. Jaundice appearing within 24 hours of birth, or jaundice accompanied by unusual lethargy and difficulty waking, refusal to feed, or limp or stiff muscles, requires going to the hospital immediately. Becoming increasingly jaundiced after 24 hours, or having pale stools, also warrants being checked as soon as possible; pale stools may indicate biliary atresia. Excessively high bilirubin can damage the brain, leaving lifelong disability.
entries.benefit: The 2022 guidelines from the American Academy of Pediatrics state that "more than 80% of newborns will have some degree of jaundice." Excessively high bilirubin can cause acute bilirubin encephalopathy and kernicterus. The guidelines describe kernicterus as "a permanent, disabling neurologic disorder." Its manifestations include cerebral palsy characterized by involuntary writhing movements of the hands and feet, inability to look upward, enamel dysplasia in primary teeth, and hearing impairment. The guidelines list "jaundice appearing within 24 hours of birth" as a risk factor for developing severe jaundice. The UK National Health Service (NHS) gives parents guidance divided into two tiers. The first tier requires calling emergency services or going directly to the emergency department. This tier applies when the baby has jaundice and is also more lethargic than usual or difficult to wake, not feeding, limp or stiff, or having seizures. Jaundice appearing before the baby is 24 hours old also falls into this tier. The second tier requires booking an appointment with a doctor as soon as possible. This tier applies when the baby is older than 24 hours, the jaundice is not improving or is worsening, urine is dark yellow or brown, or stool is pale cream-colored. Globally, it was estimated that in 2010, approximately 480,000 newborns developed Rh hemolytic disease (caused by maternal-fetal blood group incompatibility) or extreme hyperbilirubinemia. Among these children, 24% died, and 13% developed kernicterus. Among the children who survived kernicterus, over 83% were left with one or more impairments. Pale stools may indicate biliary atresia, a condition for which performing the Kasai procedure within 60 days yields significantly better treatment outcomes. Starting in 2004, Taiwan printed infant stool color cards into every newborn's child health manual. The proportion of surgeries performed within 60 days rose from 60% in 2004 to 74.3% in 2005. In another population-wide study in Taiwan, following the rollout of the color card, mortality among children with biliary atresia dropped from 26.2% to 15.9%. This is a before-and-after comparison, not a randomized trial.

entries.notes: Phototherapy (blue light therapy) uses a special light to illuminate the baby's skin, transforming bilirubin into a form that is easier to excrete. Do not substitute it with sunbathing at home: the American Academy of Pediatrics states that sunbathing is difficult to do safely without causing sunburn, so it does not recommend it as a treatment. Also, do not feed water or glucose water to reduce jaundice; the guidelines explicitly advise against this as well. Visual inspection alone cannot accurately estimate how high the bilirubin level is. The UK's NICE guidelines clearly state not to rely solely on visual inspection, and to get it tested whenever in doubt. Babies born before 38 weeks, those whose older siblings received phototherapy, and those with insufficient breast milk intake are more likely to develop severe jaundice. Follow the National Basic Public Health Service Specification for follow-ups: medical personnel conduct a home visit within 1 week after discharge. At 28 to 30 days after birth, follow up at a community health service center or township health center. Jaundice must be evaluated during both visits. If the doctor scheduled a separate appointment at discharge for a bilirubin check, go at the scheduled time. For term infants with jaundice lasting more than 14 days, and preterm infants exceeding 21 days, NICE guidelines require checking conjugated bilirubin and checking whether the stool appears pale. Jaundice itself does not delay vaccination; see Item 3 of this section (Vaccines). For newborn screening, see Section 27, Item 13 (Heel Prick Screening).

entries.title: If on a vegetarian or vegan diet during pregnancy or breastfeeding, supplement vitamin B12 or consume fortified foods; complementary foods for the baby must include animal-source foods, and consult a doctor first if insisting on a strictly vegan diet
entries.cost: A bottle of vitamin B12 supplements costs a few tens of yuan, taken as one tablet daily. Adding eggs, meat, and fish to a baby's complementary foods does not cost much. The difficulty lies in changing one's mind when the entire family firmly believes that eating vegetarian is healthier
entries.summary: Vitamin B12 is found almost exclusively in meat, eggs, and dairy; strict vegans must rely on fortified foods or supplements. If a mother eats a strictly vegan diet without supplementing, her breastfed baby is prone to deficiency. Most problems appear in babies at 4 to 8 months of age: failure to thrive and developmental delays, and if prolonged, the resulting neurological damage may be irreversible. A baby's daily complementary foods must include animal-source foods.
entries.benefit: In 2003, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported two infants. Both were raised on breast milk by vegetarian mothers, both had vitamin B12 deficiency, and both experienced failure to thrive and developmental delays. The mother of the first child had eaten a strictly vegan diet for 7 years. When hospitalized at 15 months of age, the infant was diagnosed with severe anemia, and brain MRI showed global brain atrophy. After receiving B12 supplementation, the child improved, but by 32 months of age, speech and language remained delayed. The report noted that the most common cause of B12 deficiency in infants and young children is maternal dietary deficiency. In breastfed infants, it typically manifests at 4 to 8 months of age. With prolonged deficiency, some infants are left with irreversible neurological damage, the severity of which depends on how severe and how long the deficiency lasted. Without relying on fortification, the only reliable sources are animal-source foods: meat, dairy products, and eggs. Most natural B12 in plants cannot be utilized by the human body. Cereals, soy milk, and nutritional yeast with added B12 can serve as stable sources. The report urged individuals following vegetarian diets, especially pregnant and lactating women, to determine how much B12 is in the foods they consume or consult a nutrition professional. The 2016 position paper of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics stated: "Vegans need reliable sources of vitamin B-12, such as fortified foods or supplements." The 2017 position paper on complementary feeding by the European Society for Paediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Nutrition (ESPGHAN) stated that all infants should receive iron-rich complementary foods, including meat products and/or iron-fortified foods. Vegan diets should only be conducted under appropriate medical or dietetic supervision, and parents must understand the serious consequences of failing to follow advice regarding supplementation. The 2020 core feeding information from the National Health Commission requires no fewer than 4 types of complementary foods daily. These must include at least one animal-source food, one vegetable, and one grain or tuber food

entries.notes: Controversy: The 2016 position of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics is that appropriately planned vegetarian and vegan diets are appropriate for all stages of life, including pregnancy, lactation, infancy, and childhood. However, it likewise states that vegans must have reliable sources of B12, such as fortified foods or supplements. The disagreement between the two sides lies in whether a vegan diet can be fed to infants; there is no disagreement on the point that "B12 must be supplemented." Lacto-ovo vegetarian diets carry lower risk, but those who rarely consume eggs or dairy are equally prone to deficiency. The mother of the second child in the report had been a vegetarian for 20 years and rarely consumed meat, fish, or dairy products. Early symptoms of B12 deficiency are non-specific, and the US CDC noted that anemia indices are not suitable for screening. If a child grows slowly or lags behind in development, take the initiative during doctor visits to inform the physician that the household follows a vegetarian diet; what tests to perform is decided by the doctor. Do not refuse doctor-prescribed treatments out of belief in folk remedies; see Section 16, Item 4 (Do not stop formal treatment to try folk remedies). For how to introduce complementary foods, see Item 4 of this section (Introducing complementary foods starting at 6 months); for folic acid during pregnancy, see Section 27, Item 1 (Supplementing 0.4 mg of folic acid daily).

entries.title: Do not buy wheeled baby walkers when purchasing baby gear; if you want the baby to sit and play, replace them with stationary activity centers or playpens without wheels
entries.cost: Costs no money, and even saves the expense of an infant walker. Stationary activity centers and playpens without wheels must be purchased separately, or can be borrowed. The difficulty lies in being willing to discard them if elders have gifted one or if it has already been bought
entries.summary: Sitting in a baby walker, a child can propel forward over 0.9 meters in 1 second; in most injury cases, an adult is watching right nearby. From 1990 to 2014 in the US, approximately 230,000 emergency department visits among children were due to baby walkers, with 90% of injuries to the head and neck, mostly from tumbling down stairs along with the walker. Baby walkers also do not teach children how to walk.
entries.benefit: In the United States from 1990 to 2014, an estimated 230,000 emergency department visits (precise value: 230,676) were associated with infant walkers among children younger than 15 months. Among them, 90.6% sustained injuries to the head or neck, and 74.1% tumbled down stairs while seated in a walker. Those hospitalized after injury accounted for 4.5%, and among hospitalized children, 37.8% suffered skull fractures. The US implemented mandatory safety standards for infant walkers beginning in 2010. Over the subsequent 4 years, the average annual number of injuries dropped by 22.7% compared to the preceding 4 years. However, the authors stated that infant walkers remain a significant source of injury for children—and an entirely preventable one. The American Academy of Pediatrics' 2001 policy statement noted that 34 walker-related deaths were reported in the US between 1973 and 1998. Warning labels, public education, adult supervision, and stair gates have all proven inadequate to prevent such injuries. Because infant walkers offer no clear benefits, the Academy advocates for a ban on the manufacture and sale of wheeled infant walkers, recommending stationary activity centers without wheels as alternatives instead. The Academy's guidance for parents notes that most infant walker injuries occur while an adult is watching right nearby. Seated in a baby walker, a child can dash more than 3 feet (about 0.9 meters) in 1 second. As for whether walkers help children learn to walk, the Academy's position is that they do not, and may in fact delay it. The evidence that walking is delayed is not strong. In an Irish survey of 190 infants, children who used baby walkers achieved independent walking on average about 3 weeks later (61.12 weeks versus 58.14 weeks). The more they were used, the greater the delay. However, this was merely a one-time questionnaire survey without a grouped control. A small 2002 review identified two randomized controlled trials, neither of which showed a significant impact on the onset of walking. Pooling four studies together yielded a delay of 11 to 26 days, but the study qualities were all relatively low

entries.notes: Canada banned the sale, advertising, and importation of baby walkers starting April 7, 2004. Secondhand ones are also forbidden from being sold at flea markets and garage sales, and for those already in households, authorities recommend dismantling and discarding them. The current Canada Consumer Product Safety Act lists them under prohibited items; no person may manufacture, import, advertise, or sell them. No regulations banning their sale were found domestically in China; infant walkers are manufactured according to the current national standard GB 14749-2006. Standards regulate the product itself, but cannot prevent a child from dashing toward stairs. In the US, since 1997, walkers have had to either be wider than doorways or feature stair-stop braking mechanisms, yet the Academy still deems this insufficient. Seated inside, a child can reach higher, potentially pulling down a tablecloth to knock over hot coffee, grabbing pan handles on the stove, or falling into pools or bathtubs along with the walker. The Academy suggests three alternatives: stationary activity centers without wheels (with seats that rotate and bounce), playpens, and high chairs. When taking a child to daycare facilities or others' homes, also verify that baby walkers are not in use there. For the order of acquiring large gear, see Item 11 of this section (Consider big-ticket items in the order of "borrowing, buying secondhand, buying new").

entries.title: Feed 400 IU of vitamin D daily starting right after birth, especially ensuring not to miss it for breastfed infants; full-term infants generally do not need extra calcium supplementation within 6 months
entries.cost: A bottle of vitamin D drops costs a few tens of yuan, administered as one drop daily. The difficulty lies in remembering it every single day, feeding it at least until 1 year of age
entries.summary: Breast milk contains very little vitamin D, and infants should not have extensive sun exposure, so daily supplementation is necessary. Among unsupplemented children in rural Turkey, 3.8% developed rickets within one year, whereas none who received supplementation developed it. Administer the amount directed by the doctor. Normal full-term infants generally do not need additional calcium supplementation within 6 months of age.
entries.benefit: A 2020 Cochrane review states that vitamin D levels in breast milk are low, making exclusively breastfed infants prone to deficiency. The American Academy of Pediatrics states that children need sun protection when spending extended periods outdoors, so all infants should be supplemented with vitamin D. The National Health Commission's 2020 core feeding information notes: "Infants should, from birth and under a doctor's guidance, be supplemented with 400–800 international units of vitamin D daily." The same paragraph also states: "Normal full-term infants generally do not need calcium supplementation within the first 6 months of life." The 2016 Global Consensus on Rickets involved 11 international academic organizations. The consensus stated that 400 IU (10 micrograms) daily is sufficient to prevent rickets. All infants should receive supplementation from birth to 12 months, regardless of whether they are breastfed or formula-fed. This is a strong recommendation based on moderate-quality evidence. In a study conducted in a rural area of northeastern Turkey, none of the children supplemented daily with 400 IU developed rickets. Among unsupplemented children, new cases of rickets accounted for 3.8% over 12 months. The consensus also noted that worldwide, there are no reported cases of radiographically confirmed rickets in infants who regularly received 400 IU daily. In 1992, a randomized group study in four northern and southern Chinese cities evaluated daily supplementation of 100, 200, or 400 IU. By 6 months, no child in any of the three groups developed rickets. However, cord blood vitamin D levels in northern newborns were only about one-third of those in the south (12.5 vs. 35.0 nmol/L). The higher the supplementation dose, the higher the levels at 6 months; the authors recommended daily supplementation of 400 IU.

entries.notes: A rating of B was assigned because the figures for rickets prevention come from non-randomized comparisons. The 2020 Cochrane review pooled trials on infant supplementation. Supplementing with 400 IU daily reduced the proportion of vitamin D-deficient children by about 40% (RR 0.57). However, the trials were all small and could not determine whether rickets incidence decreased. The benefit was rated as moderate based on judgment, as data on the prevalence of rickets among domestic infants could not be found. Recommendations for formula-fed infants vary. The American Academy of Pediatrics states that if an infant consumes more than approximately 800 ml (27 oz) of vitamin D-fortified formula daily, additional supplementation is not necessary. The domestic core information states that all infants should receive supplementation, with specific details following a doctor's advice. Do not increase the dose on your own: in a Canadian trial, the group receiving 1,600 IU daily was stopped early because their blood vitamin D levels were excessively high. There were no differences in linear growth or bone measures across the 400 to 1,200 IU groups. Adults who are not vitamin D deficient should not supplement for longevity; see Section 6, Item 3 (People who are not vitamin D deficient).

entries.title: When bathing an infant, fill with cold water first then add hot water, test with the inner wrist or elbow before putting the baby in; adjust water heaters with settable outlet temperatures below 50 °C
entries.cost: Zero monetary cost. Takes an extra minute or two each bath to test the water temperature. If you want greater consistency, you can buy a bath thermometer. The challenge lies in remembering to test the water before putting the baby in, even when the baby is crying and the adult is in a rush.
entries.summary: Just 2 seconds of contact with 65 °C water will cause third-degree burns in most adults, and an infant's skin is even thinner. Fill the tub with cold water first and then mix in hot water, stir well, and test with the inside of your wrist or elbow before putting the child in; do not bathe under running faucets. In a US state, hospital admissions for pediatric scald injuries dropped by more than half after factory preset temperatures for water heaters were lowered to 49 °C.
entries.benefit: The US Consumer Product Safety Commission states that 2 seconds of contact with 150 °F (about 65 °C) water will cause third-degree burns in most adults. Contact with 140 °F (60 °C) water for 6 seconds, or 130 °F (about 54 °C) water for 30 seconds, will also result in scald injuries. Even at 120 °F (49 °C), soaking for 5 minutes can cause third-degree burns. A World Health Organization report notes that infants' and young children's skin is thinner than that of adults, meaning lower temperatures can cause burns, and the burns penetrate deeper. The American Academy of Pediatrics advises parents: test tub water with the inside of your wrist or elbow, and ensure it feels "warm, but not hot." "Never bathe your baby in running water," because as water moves through pipes, its temperature fluctuates, and a sudden shift can cause burns. In 1983, Washington State enacted legislation requiring new water heaters to have a factory preset of 49 °C. By 1988, the average household hot water temperature fell from 61 °C in 1977 to 50 °C. Pediatric hospitalizations due to tap water scalds fell from 5.5 cases per year in the 1970s to 2.4 per year. Burn surface area, skin graft requirements, mortality, and hospital stay durations also decreased. This is a before-and-after comparison, not a controlled trial. Australia mandates that bathroom hot water taps must not exceed 50 °C. In New South Wales from 1989 to 1996, the hospitalization rate for scalds among children aged 0–4 decreased by 13%. Severe scalds requiring more than 10 days of hospitalization fell by 30% in the two years following the second phase. In three domestic statistics on pediatric burn hospitalizations, scalds from hot liquids accounted for 87.6% to 90.6%, with children under age 3 making up the largest share.

entries.notes: A rating of B was assigned because figures come from before-and-after comparisons and medical record statistics, rather than randomized controlled trials. The benefit was rated as moderate based on judgment, as isolated figures for domestic bathwater scalds could not be found. Water heaters fall into two main types. For tankless instantaneous types like gas water heaters, set the output temperature directly below 50 °C. Storage-type electric water heaters are a different case: WHO guidelines on preventing Legionella recommend keeping water heater output at 60 °C and hot water at the faucet no lower than 50 °C. Legionella is a bacterium that causes pneumonia. The same guidelines state that Legionella prevention must not increase the risk of scalding children; a thermostatic mixing valve can be installed at the outlet. If you do not have one installed, rely on adding cold water first and then hot water, and testing before placing the child in. Never walk away while bathing a child. The American Academy of Pediatrics states that more than half of children who drown in bathtubs are under 1 year of age; see Section 1, Item 12 (Keep children in sight near water). Do not carry hot water or hot soup while holding a child: the WHO notes that in high-income countries, the most common scalds in infants under 1 year old are caused by hot beverages in cups. If scalded, flush with cool water first; see Section 13, Item 14 (Flush scalds with cool water).

chapters.title: Going Abroad, Travel, and Overseas Safety
chapters.intro: This section weighs money and personal freedom, and several items also bear on personal safety. Once abroad, you are governed by the host country's laws, not China's. There are clear boundaries to how far Chinese embassies and consulates can assist you.

entries.title: Check the Ministry of Foreign Affairs safety alerts once before departure, and avoid traveling to places marked "Do Not Travel"
entries.cost: Zero monetary cost. Open the China Consular Affairs website and browse through it; it takes only a few minutes to read.
entries.summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs categorizes overseas safety risks into four tiers, the highest of which is "Do Not Travel." Starting September 15, 2026, avoiding high-risk countries and regions has been written into administrative regulations. When you apply for travel documents and pass border inspection upon exit, personnel will also remind you, and when necessary, advise you against going. Browsing that page before departure takes just a few minutes.
entries.benefit: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs publicly issues overseas safety alerts based on risk levels. From low to high, these are roughly four tiers: "Stay Safe," "Enhance Safety Precautions," "Exercise Caution When Traveling," and "Do Not Travel." New regulations effective September 15, 2026, have incorporated individual obligations into administrative regulations. The original text states: "Chinese citizens shall pay attention to overseas safety alerts and tourism destination safety risk warnings, and avoid traveling to and staying in high-risk countries or regions." The new rules simultaneously require immigration management authorities (the departments that issue exit-entry documents and manage border inspection) to issue reminders to individuals intending to visit high-risk areas during document processing and exit border inspections. The original text of this clause states: "For Chinese citizens intending to travel to countries or regions where the risk level is at the highest tier or where incidents seriously endangering personal safety occur frequently and suddenly, they shall be dissuaded from traveling when necessary."

Regulations on Consular Protection and Assistance (State Council Decree No. 763). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891761.htm> (Articles 19 and 21); Department of Consular Affairs of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Safety Alerts. <https://cs.mfa.gov.cn/zggmzhw/lsbh/aqtx/>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). Tourism Law (2018 Amendment, Articles 58 and 62). <https://zwgk.mct.gov.cn/zfxxgkml/zcfg/fl/202105/t20210526_924763.html> (reprinted in the public government information disclosure by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism)
entries.notes: Alerts change with situational developments; this book does not transcribe the full list, so check that page yourself before traveling. As of September 7, 2026, the column still carries the following "Do Not Travel" category alerts: Eswatini (2026-08-25), Palestine (2023-10-10), and Sudan (2023-04-17). Four others are Afghanistan (2023-02-17), Syria (2023-01-04), Peru (2022-12-29), and Somalia (2022-11-24). In addition, there are dedicated alerts for northern Myanmar and certain provinces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Travel agencies also have a duty to inform. The Tourism Law stipulates that when signing a package tour contract, the travel agency must inform you of safety precautions as well as the destination's laws, customs, and religious taboos. Package tour contracts must be signed in writing. Before joining a tour group, you can ask them to write down the destination's risks in writing; this is the author's suggestion.

entries.title: Save 12308 and the local embassy or consulate's consular protection number in your phone, copy them onto a slip of paper for your wallet, and don't wait until something happens to search for them
entries.cost: Zero monetary cost. Saving two numbers and writing down a copy takes only a few minutes.
entries.summary: When an emergency occurs, call the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' global consular protection hotline first. Dial 12308 from within China, and dial +86-10-12308 from abroad. Since its launch, this hotline has answered over 3 million calls. Over the same period, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and overseas missions handled more than 500,000 consular protection cases.
entries.benefit: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs maintains a Global Emergency Call Center for Consular Protection and Services, staffed 24 hours a day. Dial 12308 from within China. Dial +86-10-12308 or +86-10-65612308 from abroad. From its launch in 2014 to the present, this hotline has handled a cumulative total of more than 3 million incoming calls. During the same period, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and overseas missions handled more than 500,000 cases of various consular protection matters.
entries.sources: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Chinese Embassy and Consulates in Myanmar (2023). Consular Alert on the Current Security Situation in Northern Myanmar. <https://cs.mfa.gov.cn/zggmzhw/lsbh/aqtx/202311/t20231109_11176682.shtml>; State Council Information Office (2023). State Council Policy Routine Briefing on Consular Protection and Assistance. <https://www.gov.cn/xinwen/2023zccfh/11/index.htm>
entries.notes: The local embassy or consulate also has its own consular protection telephone number, which is usually faster than the central hotline. Look it up by country on the China Consular Affairs website before departing, and save it in your phone alongside the central hotline numbers. If your phone is lost or out of battery, saved numbers become useless. Therefore, keep a handwritten copy in your wallet, or write down a copy for family members.

entries.title: Know what consular protection can and cannot do: they can visit, but cannot get you out of detention, and you still pay your own expenses
entries.cost: Zero monetary cost. Spend a few minutes reading and understanding this boundary.
entries.summary: If you are arrested abroad, what embassies and consulates can do is: verify the situation with local authorities, request fair and lawful handling according to law, visit you, and attend court hearings as an observer. They cannot overturn verdicts for you, nor can they take you out of detention. Any room and board, transportation, or medical expenses advanced by others will ultimately still be paid by you. Therefore, prepare adequate funds and insurance before going abroad, and do not treat "the state will bail me out if something happens" as a plan.
entries.benefit: When you are arrested, embassies and consulates can do several specific things: verify the situation with relevant authorities of the host country and request handling in accordance with the law and impartiality. The original text of the regulations states: "Conduct visits to or communicate with the Chinese citizen in accordance with the laws of the host country and international treaties concluded or acceded to by our country and the host country, ascertain their relevant needs, and request relevant authorities of the host country to grant humanitarian and fair treatment to the Chinese citizen." In plain language, the embassy or consulate will visit you, contact you, and ask what you need in accordance with local laws and bilateral treaties, and demand that the local authorities treat you according to humanitarian and fair standards. When court sessions are held, the embassy or consulate may attend as an observer and demand the protection of your litigation rights. If you are injured or caught in a disaster, it can urge the local government to provide emergency assistance and assist family members in handling follow-up matters. However, regarding expenses, the regulations are equally explicit: "Where Chinese citizens, legal persons, or unincorporated organizations receive room and board, transportation, medical care, and other supplies and services provided by third parties during the process of consular protection and assistance, they shall pay the expenses that ought to be borne by themselves." If someone else fronts the money for your room and board, transportation, or medical care, you are still the one who has to pay what is rightfully yours to bear.
entries.sources: State Council (2023). Regulations on Consular Protection and Assistance (State Council Decree No. 763). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891761.htm> (Articles 9, 10, 14, and 26)
entries.notes: Embassies and consulates will not pay fines on your behalf, will not cover your medical expenses, will not buy your plane tickets, and cannot alter the rulings of host-country courts. What they can provide you is information on local lawyers, translators, medical institutions, and funeral services, as well as help in contacting relatives and friends and locating relief channels. Therefore, prepare your funds and insurance yourself before traveling abroad; do not treat "the state will bail me out if something happens" as a plan.

entries.title: Buy an Insurance Policy That Includes Overseas Medical Care and Medical Evacuation; Do Not Just Buy Flight Delay Insurance
entries.cost: A short-term overseas travel insurance policy costs several tens to several hundreds of yuan.
entries.summary: Medical expenses abroad must come out of your own pocket. Domestic basic medical insurance covers virtually nothing abroad, and embassies and consulates do not front the money. What can truly bankrupt a family is not outpatient fees, but hospitalization following severe injuries and transporting the patient back to China—which requires a charter flight or medical escort. When purchasing travel insurance, focus primarily on two coverage limits: overseas medical expenses, and emergency medical evacuation and repatriation.
entries.benefit: Medical expenses abroad must be paid out of your own pocket. Domestic medical insurance basically offers no reimbursement overseas. Consular protection also does not advance these funds; see Section 3 (What Consular Protection Can and Cannot Do). The legal basis is Article 26 of the regulations. What can truly drag a family into financial ruin is not outpatient costs, but hospitalization and medical transfer following a severe injury. Transferring a patient from an overseas hospital back to China requires a dedicated chartered plane or medical escort, which ranks among the most expensive out-of-pocket expenses. According to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, emergency medical transport from a remote area to a high-quality hospital can cost over $100,000 if paid out-of-pocket. When shopping for insurance, prioritize two coverage limits: first, the coverage limit for overseas medical expenses; second, the coverage limit for emergency medical evacuation and repatriation, which covers the maximum payout for hospital transfers and returning the individual to China after an incident.
entries.sources: State Council (2023). Regulations on Consular Protection and Assistance (State Council Decree No. 763). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891761.htm> (Article 26); U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Travelers' Health: Travel Insurance: "Medical evacuation insurance covers emergency transportation from a remote area to a high-quality hospital, which could otherwise cost more than $100,000." <https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/page/insurance>; remainder based on author experience, no direct literature
entries.notes: $100,000 is stated as a lower limit, not an expense range. Since official or publicly available industry statistics on expense ranges could not be found, this book does not specify an exact range. Confirm three things before buying. First, whether the country you plan to visit is within the coverage scope. Second, whether high-risk activities such as scuba diving, skiing, and motorcycling are excluded. Third, whether claims settlement is handled directly between the insurer and the hospital, or whether you must front the cash and seek reimbursement upon return. You still need to buy it even when traveling to visa-exempt countries.

entries.title: "Overseas High-Salary Recruitment" Should Invariably Be Treated as Fraud; If Duped into Telecom Fraud, You May Face Exit Restrictions Upon Return
entries.cost: Free. The hard part is turning down an opportunity that appears exceptionally lucrative with your own hands.
entries.summary: Outrageously high monthly salaries, no educational or experience requirements, no formal contracts, instructions to assemble first in a border city, and having your passport held on your behalf. If you take this kind of work, neither your person nor your passport remains in your own hands. If you falsify documentation when leaving the country, border inspection authorities will intercept you and deny departure. Those who commit crimes abroad or endanger national security and interests may also be barred from exiting China for 6 months to 3 years upon return.
entries.benefit: The official characterization of such cases is very blunt. Recent years have seen instances where individuals "were deceived into exiting the country or fabricated justifications to unlawfully exit the country to engage in cross-border gambling, telecom and online fraud, and other illegal activities, severely endangering the safety of people's lives and property." This refers to being lured abroad or sneaking out under false pretenses to conduct gambling and telecom fraud there. New regulations tighten controls from both ends against this issue. On the exit side: "The grounds stated for applying for exit, entry, stay, or residence shall be genuine and lawful." For those who submit false materials or make misrepresentations, immigration management authorities have the power to refuse the issuance of travel documents and deny departure. On the return side: "Where a Chinese citizen engages in illegal or criminal activities abroad that endanger national security and interests, a decision may be made... to prohibit them from exiting China for a period of 6 months to 3 years starting from the date of their return." Those who are subjected to administrative detention for fraudulently obtaining travel documents or for unlawful exit/entry are likewise barred from leaving the country for 6 months to 3 years.
entries.sources: State Council (2026). Provisions on Exit and Entry Administration (State Council Decree No. 841). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202607/content_7077173.htm> (Articles 3 and 4); Ministry of Justice, Ministry of Public Security, and National Immigration Administration (2026). Press Conference on the State Council Provisions on Exit and Entry Administration. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202608/content_7077270.htm>
entries.notes: The identifying features are largely consistent: monthly salaries far exceeding peer positions, no education or experience requirements, no formal contracts, instructions to assemble in a border city first, and offers to handle visas and retain your passport. Specialized consular warnings have already been issued for northern Myanmar. If you actually go, your personal freedom and passport will not be in your own control; do not assume you can leave whenever you want.

entries.title: Overseas Cash Withdrawals Cannot Exceed 100,000 Yuan Per Year Calculated Across All Cards Under Your Name; When Carrying Cash Across the Border, the Limit Is 20,000 Yuan per Trip, and Foreign Currency Exceeding 5,000 USD Must Be Declared to Customs
entries.cost: Free. Estimate before departure how much cash you will need to withdraw on the trip, and rely on card swipes for the rest. The difficult part is breaking the habit and choosing card payments over cash withdrawals whenever possible. Those carrying large amounts of foreign currency cash out of the country must first visit a bank to obtain a permit, adding an extra errand.
entries.summary: Overseas cash withdrawals are capped at 100,000 CNY per calendar year aggregated across all bank cards under your name; exceeding this threshold results in a ban on withdrawals for both the current year and the following year. Card purchases remain unaffected. When carrying cash across the border, the limit is at most 20,000 CNY per trip, and foreign currency exceeding 5,000 USD must be declared in writing to Customs. Failure to declare can result in fines; concealing cash is classified as smuggling and will result in confiscation.
entries.benefit: The legal basis is the State Administration of Foreign Exchange Notice on Regulating Large-Amount Overseas Cash Withdrawal Transactions Using Bank Cards (Huifa [2017] No. 29, effective January 1, 2018). Article 1: "Where an individual holds a domestic bank card and withdraws cash overseas, the total amount withdrawn per calendar year across all bank cards (including supplementary cards) under the individual's name shall not exceed the equivalent of 100,000 CNY. Those who exceed the annual quota shall have their overseas cash withdrawal privileges on domestic bank cards suspended for the current year and the subsequent year." Paragraph 2 of the same article: "Individuals shall not evade or assist in evading overseas cash withdrawal management by borrowing other people's bank cards or lending their own bank cards." Article 2: SAFE sends the suspension list to card-issuing banks daily, and card-issuing banks shall suspend the listed individuals from using their bank cards to withdraw cash overseas no later than 17:00 Beijing Time that day.
