Article 3: Individuals placed on the suspension list may take their valid personal identity documents to a local SAFE branch or sub-branch to inspect their overseas cash withdrawal details. Article 4: The daily withdrawal cap per foreign currency card was adjusted from the equivalent of 1,000 USD to the equivalent of 10,000 CNY; RMB cards maintain a daily limit of no more than the equivalent of 10,000 CNY per card. Article 6: Card-issuing banks, domestic RMB card clearing institutions, and individuals who violate the provisions of this Notice shall be penalized pursuant to the relevant provisions of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Foreign Exchange Administration. A SAFE press briefing further clarified several points: The Notice does not affect card payments for purchases made by individuals overseas. Current account transactions related to overseas travel, business, and study—such as dining, accommodation, transportation, and shopping—can all be settled by swiping bank cards. These purchases also do not count toward the individual convenient foreign exchange purchase quota of 50,000 USD per year. The annual quota is tallied by SAFE by aggregating data from all card-issuing financial institutions; because real-time interception would slow down transaction response times, "SAFE employs delayed control measures" (no on-the-spot blockage). Additionally, statistics show that in 2016, 81% of domestic bank cards withdrew less than 30,000 CNY in cash overseas (nationwide). Carrying cash in and out of the country is governed by a separate set of rules. The reverse side of the new Customs Declaration Form implemented on April 1, 2025, states: "RMB carried by each person entering or exiting each time shall not exceed 20,000 yuan." When entering with foreign currency cash, "amounts exceeding the equivalent of 5,000 USD shall be declared in writing to Customs." When exiting the country carrying more than the equivalent of 5,000 USD up to 10,000 USD, one must first obtain a Foreign Exchange Carrying Permit from a bank and then declare it to Customs. For amounts exceeding 10,000 USD, the permit must be obtained from SAFE. SAFE's administrative measures specify that departing travelers "in principle may not carry foreign currency cash exceeding the equivalent of 10,000 USD out of the country." Customs supervisory measures on luggage and articles stipulate that carrying currency cash exceeding prescribed amounts into or out of the country must be declared in writing to Customs. If written declaration procedures have not been completed when Customs begins its inspection, it is deemed a failure to declare. For those who fail to declare but did not conceal or stash the cash, Customs will issue a warning and may impose a fine of up to 20% of the value of the items. Concealing, disguising, or falsely declaring constitutes smuggling, resulting in the confiscation of the cash and an optional additional fine equal to or less than the equivalent value.
entries.sources: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (2017). Notice on Regulating Large-Amount Overseas Cash Withdrawal Transactions Using Bank Cards (Huifa [2017] No. 29, Articles 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 7, effective January 1, 2018). <https://www.safe.gov.cn/safe/2017/1230/21873.html>; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (2017). Relevant Official of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange Answers Reporters' Questions on Regulating Large-Amount Overseas Cash Withdrawal Transactions Using Bank Cards. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2017-12/31/content_5251958.htm>; UnionPay International. Overseas ATM Cash Withdrawal. <https://m.unionpayintl.com/wap/cn/serviceCenter/cardUsingInstructions/805.shtml>; General Administration of Customs (2025). Announcement on Matters Concerning Declaration of Luggage and Articles of Inbound and Outbound Passengers (GAC Announcement No. 43 of 2025, Annexed Declaration Form, reverse side "Important Notice" Part II). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202504/content_7017195.htm>; General Administration of Customs (2025). Measures of the Customs of the People's Republic of China on the Supervision of Inbound and Outbound Luggage and Articles (GAC Decree No. 276, Articles 9, 10, and 11). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202502/content_7005697.htm>; State Administration of Foreign Exchange and General Administration of Customs (2003). Notice on Issuing the Interim Measures for the Administration of Carrying Foreign Currency Cash In and Out of the Country (Huifa [2003] No. 102, Articles 3, 5, and 7). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2004/content_63085.htm>; People's Bank of China (2004). People's Bank of China Announcement [2004] No. 18 (RMB entry and exit limit adjusted to 20,000 yuan, effective January 1, 2005). <https://www.pbc.gov.cn/tiaofasi/144941/3581332/3582861/2018072309595152720.pdf>; State Council (2022 Revision). Implementation Regulations on Customs Administrative Penalties (Articles 7, 9, and 19). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff80818180e0a61301811e43f41f1fa2>; U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Money and Other Monetary Instruments: "Federal law mandates that when entering or leaving the United States you must report amounts exceeding $10,000" "the $10,000 threshold applies to the total amount they are carrying or sending collectively, not per individual". <https://www.cbp.gov/travel/international-visitors/kbyg/money>
entries.notes: The quota is calculated on a calendar year basis and resets on January 1. What is suspended is only overseas cash withdrawals; swiping cards for purchases is not affected. If you genuinely need large amounts of cash overseas, purchase foreign exchange in advance in accordance with the Measures for the Administration of Personal Foreign Exchange, and then carry foreign currency cash abroad. If it exceeds 5,000 USD, remember to obtain the carrying permit in advance and take the red channel at Customs to declare it. Destination countries also have their own declaration thresholds; verify them once before departure. For example, U.S. Customs explicitly states that carrying over 10,000 USD into or out of the U.S. on a single trip must be declared, and family members traveling together are calculated based on the aggregate total. Cash regulations were verified against official websites as of October 14, 2026. The withdrawal process itself contains two pitfalls, as noted on UnionPay International's "Overseas ATM Cash Withdrawal" page. First, dual-logo cards cannot select the UnionPay routing on certain ATMs in some countries. Second, some overseas ATMs will display an additional surcharge on the screen; this fee is collected by the local acquiring institution and is "unrelated to UnionPay." The same page also notes: "Because credit card withdrawals incur cash advance interest, cardholders are advised to use UnionPay debit cards for overseas withdrawals." What to do if your card is lost, swallowed, or fraudulently used: see Section 14, Item 5 (If Your Card Is Fraudulently Used, First Report Loss and Freeze It, Then Report to the Police). Limits on cash withdrawals and carried cash are current as of October 2026; refer to the latest announcements from SAFE and Customs before departure.

entries.title: Photograph and Store Copies of Your Passport, Visa, and ID Card in the Cloud; If Lost, Report to the Police First Before Applying for a Travel Document
entries.cost: Free. Take a few photos before departure.
entries.summary: If you lose your passport, the embassy or consulate can issue a travel document for your return to China, but you must be able to prove who you are. Having photos of your bio-data page and visa page, along with your entry/exit records, will make reissuance much faster. You must also report the loss to local police first and obtain a police report receipt, as exit immigration inspections and insurance claims in many countries require this document. Mobile phones are frequently lost together with passports; do not store the photos only on your phone.
entries.benefit: If you lose your passport, Chinese embassies and consulates abroad can issue you a travel document for returning to China, but you must first prove your identity. Having clear photos of your passport bio-data page, visa pages, and entry/exit records makes a substantial difference in replacement processing speed. At the same time, you must first report the incident to the local police to obtain a police report receipt. Exit control checks and travel insurance claims in many countries require this paperwork. The entry point for contacting the embassy or consulate consists of the two consular protection telephone numbers saved in Item 2.
entries.sources: State Council (2023). Regulations on Consular Protection and Assistance (State Council Decree No. 763). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891761.htm> (Article 16); author experience, no direct literature
entries.notes: The storage method is to take the photos and place them in two different locations, such as keeping one copy in cloud storage and sending one copy to a family member. In addition, print a paper photocopy and store it separately from the original documents. Also photograph bank cards and prescriptions for regular medications. Mobile phones and passports are commonly lost together; storing them solely on your phone is equivalent to not storing them at all. Cloud storage logins that require SMS verification codes may become inaccessible once your phone is lost. Perform a trial login on another device before departing to confirm you can access the files without relying on that phone. Document photos are sensitive information, so choosing an encrypted storage method is safer. However, if you forget the password to an encrypted archive, no one can open it, which is why sending a copy to family members cannot be skipped.

entries.title: Before Driving Abroad, Confirm Whether the Destination Recognizes Chinese Driver's Licenses; Most "International Driving Permits" Sold Online Are Waste Paper
entries.cost: Free. Check the destination's regulations once before departure.
entries.summary: The "international driving permits" handled by third-party agents online do not hold valid legal standing in mainland China. That document is a translation document mutually recognized among contracting parties to the 1949 Geneva Convention, and mainland China is not among the 103 contracting parties. Therefore, no matter who issues it to you within China, it carries no legal validity. Whether you can drive with a Chinese driver's license depends on the destination's own regulations; do not drive without verifying clearly.
entries.benefit: The so-called "International Driving Permit" (IDP) is a translation document mutually recognized among contracting states to the 1949 Convention on Road Traffic. This convention was concluded in Geneva on September 19, 1949, and entered into force on March 26, 1952. It currently has 103 contracting parties (signatory countries and territories). Mainland China is not on this list. Therefore, China does not issue this type of international driving permit. Any agency acting as an "agent for international driving permits" within China produces no legal validity. Whether you can drive using a Chinese driver's license depends on the regulations of the destination country or region itself. Some recognize a Chinese driver's license alongside a notarized translation, some require exchanging it for a local driver's license, and some do not recognize it at all.
entries.sources: United Nations Treaty Collection. Convention on Road Traffic, Geneva, 19 September 1949 — status of treaties. <https://treaties.un.org/pages/ViewDetailsV.aspx?src=TREATY&mtdsg_no=XI-B-1&chapter=11&clang=_en>
entries.notes: If the driver's license used for driving is not recognized locally, insurance companies may deny coverage in the event of an accident—which is where the true cost lies. This statement is based on author experience; refer specifically to insurance policy terms and local laws. There are two ways to verify: check the "Notice for Chinese Citizens" for the destination country on the China Consular Service website, or ask the car rental company directly for written confirmation. Hong Kong, Macao, Taiwan, and certain countries have separate bilateral arrangements.

entries.title: When Hiring an Agency for Visas, Study Abroad, or Immigration, First Ask If It Has Filed with Immigration Authorities
entries.cost: Free. Simply ask an extra question about whether it has completed filing, and retain written documentation.
entries.summary: Starting September 15, 2026, agencies handling visas, study abroad, and immigration must file records with immigration management authorities. Soliciting clients with exaggerated promotions and providing or assisting in providing fraudulent documentation are strictly prohibited. When hearing claims such as "guaranteed pass," "guaranteed visa approval," or "we'll fabricate the materials for you," exercise caution.
entries.benefit: In 2018, access licensing for entry-exit intermediary agencies for private purposes was abolished (opening an agency no longer required obtaining official approvals first). Thereafter, the number of agencies grew rapidly, bringing about problems such as "an unclear baseline count of agencies, some agencies conducting business in violation of laws and regulations, and infringement upon the lawful rights and interests of entry and exit personnel"—authorities could not even count how many there were. Starting September 15, 2026, such intermediaries shifted to filing-based record-keeping management. An agency must file a record with the local immigration administration authority within 15 days from the date of its establishment. Those already operating prior to this must complete retroactive filing within 90 days from the effective date. Expressly prohibited behaviors include the following categories: First, "publishing false information, or soliciting clients through methods such as exaggerated advertising or misleading advertising." Second, "providing or assisting in providing false materials, assisting others in irregularly obtaining entry-exit documents or handling formalities such as visas, stay and residence permits, or passports." Third, "leaking, selling, or unlawfully providing... personal privacy or personal information." Fourth, "organizing or assisting others in engaging in cross-border illegal or criminal activities." Overseas enterprises and institutions may not provide such intermediary services within the territory of China.
entries.sources: State Council (2026). Provisions on Exit and Entry Administration (State Council Decree No. 841). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202607/content_7077173.htm> (Articles 7, 8, 10, 12, 13); United States Code, Title 8, §1182(a)(6)(C)(i) Misrepresentation. <https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/8/1182> (Reprinted by the Legal Information Institute, Cornell University)
entries.notes: Agencies that constantly toss around promises like "guaranteed pass," "guaranteed visa," or "we'll manufacture your materials for you" are doing things that are explicitly prohibited in the first place. Once uncovered, it is the applicants themselves who bear the consequences. If an unintentional mistake occurs while filling out a form yourself, it usually just results in a visa denial this time around, based on the author's experience. If fake materials are used and determined to constitute fraud and misrepresentation, the consequences are far more severe. Taking the United States as an example, immigration law stipulates that any alien who applies for a visa by fraud or willfully misrepresenting a material fact is "inadmissible." Non-profit policy consulting and information inquiries do not count as intermediary services.

entries.title: Do not issue invitation letters on behalf of strangers, and do not let others use your name to handle entry-exit formalities
entries.cost: Costs no money. The hard part is turning down a favor in person.
entries.summary: If you issue an invitation letter or application materials for someone else with untrue content, the party who issued them is penalized. Individuals face fines ranging from 5,000 to 10,000 yuan, along with the confiscation of any unlawful gains. Entities face fines ranging from 10,000 to 50,000 yuan, and the handling personnel are separately fined 5,000 to 10,000 yuan. Doing someone a favor ends up meaning paying this money out of your own pocket.
entries.benefit: The person issuing an invitation letter must be responsible for whether the content is authentic. The original text states: "Where an individual issues a false letter of invitation or other application materials for another person to apply for exit/entry or stay/residence, a fine of not less than 5,000 yuan but not more than 10,000 yuan shall be imposed by the immigration management authority; where there are illegal gains, the illegal gains shall be confiscated." Where an entity issues false materials, a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan shall be imposed. At the same time, the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible personnel (the managing supervisor and the handling personnel) shall be separately fined not less than 5,000 yuan but not more than 10,000 yuan.
entries.sources: State Council (2026). Provisions on Exit and Entry Administration (State Council Decree No. 841). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202607/content_7077173.htm> (Articles 3, 11)
entries.notes: This involves the same type of risk as Section 8, "Do not carry items for strangers": if materials are issued under your name, the consequences fall squarely on you. If public officials or military personnel attempt to irregularly obtain foreign citizenship or overseas residence status through intermediaries, the intermediaries are not only forbidden to handle it, but must also report it to supervisory organs.

entries.title: Before leaving the country, send your itinerary, accommodation, and travel companions to a family member, and agree on how often to check in
entries.cost: Costs no money. Send a single message before departure.
entries.summary: If someone goes missing overseas, family members can turn to embassies and consulates for help; the embassy or consulate will tell family members how to report the case to local police, and will press for updates after a case is opened. The prerequisite is that someone back in China knows where you are supposed to be and when you are supposed to be in touch. Sending your flight numbers, accommodation addresses, travel companions' phone numbers, and the agreed contact frequency to just one family member is enough.
entries.benefit: When a Chinese citizen's whereabouts abroad are unknown, relatives may request assistance from diplomatic missions stationed abroad. The original text of the regulations states that "diplomatic missions stationed abroad shall provide local police-reporting methods and other information for obtaining rescue and assistance." After the local police file a case, embassies and consulates will urge them to handle it promptly. Whether these assistance mechanisms can be initiated depends on whether someone in China knows where you were supposed to be and when you were supposed to check in.
entries.sources: State Council (2023). Regulations on Consular Protection and Assistance (State Council Decree No. 763). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891761.htm> (Article 13); Author's experience, no direct literature
entries.notes: Listing four items clearly is enough: flight numbers, accommodation addresses, names and phone numbers of travel companions, and the agreed contact frequency. If heading to places with poor cellular reception or poor public security, make sure to also state clearly: "Call the police if there is no news for this long." The cost of doing this is near zero, yet all the rescue and relief procedures mentioned above can only begin if a family member knows your itinerary in the first place.

entries.title: When bringing medications abroad, check the destination's regulations first: for cold and cough medications containing pseudoephedrine or codeine, sleeping pills, psychiatric drugs, and potent painkillers, keep original packaging, prescriptions or doctor's certificates, and carry only amounts for personal use
entries.cost: Costs no money. Checking the official destination website takes a few minutes before departure. If carrying controlled medications, you will also need to make an extra trip to the hospital for certificates and apply roughly two weeks in advance.
entries.summary: Cold medicines and cough medicines with pseudoephedrine exceeding 10% or codeine exceeding 1% are regulated in Japan as stimulant raw materials or narcotics, requiring prior approval applications. Bringing more than a one-month supply of sleeping pills into Japan also requires prior certificates, and Singapore requires advance application for medications with controlled ingredients. Keeping original packaging and doctor's certificates, and carrying only amounts for personal use, are necessary to avoid confiscation of medications, fines, or even criminal imprisonment.
entries.benefit: Japan regulates medications in several categories based on ingredients. Medications containing more than 10% pseudoephedrine are classified as "raw materials for stimulants." Those containing more than 1% codeine are classified as narcotics. These two categories require applying for permission from the Narcotics Control Department of the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare at least 14 days prior to entry. Medications must be carried on your person and cannot be mailed or carried by family members on your behalf. For psychiatric drugs such as diazepam and triazolam, carrying within a 1-month supply does not require an application. General medications also have quantitative limits: up to a 1-month supply for prescription drugs, and up to a 2-month supply for other medications. Exceeding these requires obtaining a "Certificate of Import Confirmation" (Yakkan Shoumei) beforehand. The original reminder from the Chinese Embassy in Japan states: unlawfully and irregularly carrying medicines and other items into Japan, "violators will face fines, detention, or even imprisonment, and contraband will be confiscated." Regulations from Singapore's Health Sciences Authority (HSA) state: for medications without controlled ingredients, you may bring up to a 3 months' supply. Carry a copy of the prescription or doctor's letter on your person. Medications must be kept in their original packaging bearing pharmacy labels. For medications containing controlled ingredients, apply for approval at least 2 weeks in advance. Quantities exceeding a 3 months' supply are strictly prohibited from entry, and medications in chewing gum form are also prohibited. Carrying medication on behalf of others is restricted strictly to prescription medication belonging to immediate family members. Non-compliant medications will be confiscated, and enforcement action may be taken. On China's end, the Customs Law requires that articles carried by individuals entering or exiting the territory "shall be limited to personal use and reasonable quantities." For narcotics and Category I psychotropic substances, up to the maximum dosage of a single prescription may be carried with a hospital diagnosis certificate and identity document. Customs releases them according to the principle of personal use and reasonable quantity.
entries.sources: Narcotics Control Department, Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, Japan. Application Guidance (Carrying medicines containing controlled substances into/out of Japan): "When you enter/leave Japan carrying your medicine containing controlled substances in Japan for your own medical use, you need to get a permission in advance." "You should apply at least 14 days prior to your travel." "you can't send your medicine to/from Japan and you can't also entrust carrying it to other people, such as your family." <https://www.ncd.mhlw.go.jp/en/application2.html>; Narcotics Control Department, Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, Japan (2024). Controlled Substances List (December 12, 2024 version): "Ephedrine, Pseudoephedrine (*Any substances containing 10% or less of ephedrine or pseudoephedrine are excluded.)" "Codeine … (*Any substances containing 1% or less of codeine or its salt are excluded.)" <https://www.ncd.mhlw.go.jp/dl_data/keitai/cotrolled_substances_list20241212%20.pdf>; Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, Japan. Information for those who are bringing medicines for personal use into Japan: "Poison, Deadly poison, Prescription drug : Up to 1 month supply" "Other Drugs, Quasi drugs : Up to 2 month supply". <https://www.mhlw.go.jp/stf/seisakunitsuite/bunya/kenkou_iryou/iyakuhin/kojinyunyu/topics/tp010401-1_00001.html>; Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, Japan. On Personal Import of Pharmaceuticals, etc.: "Personal import of medical psychotropics (diazepam, triazolam, etc.): If importing quantities exceeding a 1-month supply or injectables, an import confirmation certificate must be obtained in advance". <https://www.mhlw.go.jp/stf/seisakunitsuite/bunya/kenkou_iryou/iyakuhin/kojinyunyu/topics/tp010401-1.html>; Embassy of the People's Republic of China in Japan (2018). Please Do Not Carry Contraband When Traveling to Japan. <https://jp.china-embassy.gov.cn/jbwzlmnew/lszcnew/LSBHYXZ/LSBHLBZN/201811/t20181113_9475556.htm>; Health Sciences Authority, Singapore. Bringing in personal medications: "You may bring up to 3 months' supply if no approval is needed and the medication is not prohibited." "Please note that imports of quantities exceeding 3 months' supply are not allowed." "Failure to comply will result in your medication being confiscated or enforcement action may be taken." <https://www.hsa.gov.sg/travelling-with-medication-and-medical-devices/personal-medications/>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2021 Amendment). Customs Law (Article 46). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817ab22b8a017abd719e0f05c0>; State Council (2024 3rd Revision). Regulations on the Administration of Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (Article 44). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081819c230ff2019c2d0fcaed641d>
entries.notes: Regulations change, and countries differ; this book only describes how to look them up. Before departure, check the official website of the destination's health department or customs, or consular reminders from the local Chinese embassy. The aforementioned regulations for Japan and Singapore were verified against official websites as of October 14, 2026. To check whether a medicine contains these ingredients, check the ingredient list on the package insert; if unsure, ask the prescribing physician. It is best if the traveler carrying the medicine is the person taking it; Singapore only permits carrying prescription medication on behalf of immediate family members for their own use. This follows the same rationale as Section 8, Item 29 (Do not carry items for strangers). Take photos of prescriptions and medicine boxes to back them up; for storage methods, see Item 7 of this section (Save a copy of photos to the cloud).

entries.title: When returning to China from abroad, do not bring meat products (including vacuum-packed ham and jerky), cheese, fresh fruit, or seeds; if carrying animal or plant products, declare them via the red channel
entries.cost: Costs no money. Steer clear of these categories when buying local specialties abroad, and search through your luggage before returning home. If carrying items you are unsure about, take the red channel when going through customs and wait in line a bit longer.
entries.summary: When returning to China, meat cannot be brought regardless of whether it is raw or cooked, no matter how tightly ham, jerky, or sausage is packed. Cheese, butter, fresh eggs, fresh fruits, vegetables, and seeds are also on the prohibited list. Carrying them will result in return or destruction. Failing to declare animal and plant products you are carrying may also incur a fine, with an upper limit of 5,000 yuan.
entries.benefit: The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs and the General Administration of Customs published a prohibited carry-in list in 2021. It governs carry-on baggage, checked luggage, mailed items, express parcels, and cross-border e-commerce direct purchases. The categories most relevant to ordinary tourists are as follows: The first category is meat, specified in the original text as "(raw or cooked) meat (including viscera) and its products"; the list makes no exceptions based on packaging. The second category is dairy and eggs, including cream, butter, cheese, and condensed milk, as well as century eggs, salted eggs, and mayonnaise. The third category is "fresh fruits and vegetables" and fresh cut flowers. The fourth category is seeds, seedlings, and other plant materials capable of propagation. The fifth category is live animals, excluding cats and dogs. Bird's nest is also prohibited, except for commercially sterile canned bird's nest. Article 29 of the Law on the Entry and Exit Animal and Plant Quarantine clearly specifies that bringing items on the list into the territory "shall be returned or destroyed." Animal and plant products not on the list may be brought in, but must likewise be declared. Customs supervision measures for luggage and articles specify that those carrying animals, plants, and animal/plant products must make a written declaration to customs. If written declarations are not completed by the time customs begins inspection, it is deemed failure to declare. The original text of the measures also states: "Those who are unclear about customs regulations or do not know how to choose channels shall select the 'Red Channel.'" Penalties for failure to declare are found in Article 39 of the Quarantine Law, where "failure to apply for quarantine inspection" is punished by a fine. Article 59 of the Implementing Regulations for the Law on the Entry and Exit Animal and Plant Quarantine sets such fines at 5,000 yuan or less.
entries.sources: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, General Administration of Customs (2021). Announcement No. 470 of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs and the General Administration of Customs (Catalogue of Animals, Plants, and Their Products and Other Quarantine Objects Prohibited from Being Carried or Sent into the People's Republic of China). <https://www.moa.gov.cn/nybgb/2022/202202/202203/t20220324_6393815.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2009 Amendment). Law on the Entry and Exit Animal and Plant Quarantine (Articles 29, 30, 39). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf6ab3604e7>; State Council (1996). Regulations for the Implementation of the Law on the Entry and Exit Animal and Plant Quarantine (State Council Decree No. 206, Articles 41, 59). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f3cbb3c016f4086afae03c1>; General Administration of Customs (2025). Measures of the Customs of the People's Republic of China for the Supervision and Administration of Inbound and Outbound Luggage and Articles (General Administration of Customs Decree No. 276, Articles 9, 11, 12, 25, 27). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202502/content_7005697.htm>; General Administration of Customs (2025). Announcement on Matters Concerning the Declaration of Luggage and Articles of Inbound and Outbound Personnel (General Administration of Customs Announcement No. 43 of 2025, Articles 1, 3). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202504/content_7017195.htm>
entries.notes: The list was verified against the announcement on the official website of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs as of October 14, 2026. The two ministries stated that they will conduct "dynamic adjustments," so check again before departure. There are a few exceptions: dried and cooked aquatic products are not on the prohibited list—such as dried squid and dried shrimp—but must still be declared. Those that have undergone approval and possess official quarantine certificates from the exporting country are not restricted by the list. Cats and dogs are limited to one per person and must have official quarantine certificates and vaccination certificates from the exporting country. When going abroad, many destination countries likewise do not allow meat products to be brought into the territory. The lookup method is identical to Item 12 of this section (When bringing medications abroad, check destination regulations first): check the official website of the destination's customs or consular reminders from the Chinese embassy or consulate.

chapters.title: How to Relax: Entertainment Venues and Stress Relief
chapters.intro: The first half of the section discusses which expenditures in entertainment venues are money wasted and where safety exits are located, measured in terms of money and personal freedom. The second half discusses how to relieve stress, measured in terms of energy and all-cause mortality. Numbers from the two halves are not converted together. Items 11 and 12 at the end of the section cover how to stay safe while having fun: do not soak in hot springs or use saunas after drinking alcohol; wear helmets when skiing or cycling, measured in terms of mortality. Section 3 has already detailed which actions to take first when experiencing low mood; here, more concrete practices are provided.

entries.title: Check where the emergency exits are before entering a KTV, bar, or escape room; switch to another venue if they are locked or blocked
entries.cost: Costs no money. Look up for 10 seconds upon entering.
entries.summary: By regulation, evacuation passages and safety exits must remain unobstructed while entertainment venues are in business; blocking, locking, obstructing with objects, and concealing directional signs are prohibited. Internet cafes are likewise forbidden from blocking doors or locking windows. Failure to comply is illegal, and you can report it. If private rooms are underground, have only one exit, or have corridors cluttered with miscellaneous items, switch to another venue.
entries.benefit: This is a statutory obligation of operators. Failure to comply is illegal, and you can report it. Original text of the regulations: "During business hours, entertainment venues shall ensure that evacuation passages and safety exits remain unobstructed, and shall not block or lock evacuation passages and safety exits, nor set up barriers such as railings in evacuation passages and safety exits that impede evacuation." The regulations also require: "Prominent signs shall be installed in evacuation passages and safety exits, and directional signs shall not be obstructed or covered." Internet cafes are subject to the same rule, being required to "prohibit blocking or locking doors, windows, safe evacuation passages, and safety exits during business hours" and "prohibit open flames for lighting and smoking."
entries.sources: State Council (2006). Regulations on the Administration of Entertainment Venues (State Council Decree No. 458, Articles 20, 21). <http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_6297.htm>; State Council (2002). Regulations on the Administration of Business Places for Internet Access Services (State Council Decree No. 363, Article 21). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2002/content_61788.htm>
entries.notes: If any of the following apply, switch to another place: the private room is underground, there is only one exit, hallways are piled high with clutter, or the emergency exit indicator lights are not on. When fires break out in these types of venues, smoke is heavy, hallways are narrow, crowds are large, and most people have been drinking. The time left for you to escape is measured in seconds. According to the regulations, reporting phone numbers should be written on warning signs inside the venue.

entries.title: Ask for a price list before ordering; entertainment venues must clearly mark prices, and "play first, settle up later" is not acceptable
entries.cost: Costs no money. Open your mouth and ask for the list once. The difficulty lies in asking for prices in front of others—it feels a bit embarrassing.
entries.summary: According to regulations, entertainment venues selling services or goods must clearly mark prices and proactively show you the price list. So-called "sky-high priced drinks" often happen in situations where no price list was viewed and bills are settled based on verbal quotes after the fact. Upon entering the private room, first ask for the menu/price list to take photos, and after ordering ask for a confirmed checklist. If there is a dispute when paying the bill, call 12315 on the spot.
entries.benefit: Original text of the regulations: "Entertainment venues providing entertainment service items and selling goods shall clearly mark prices and present price lists to consumers; they shall not force or deceive consumers into accepting services or purchasing goods." Those violating pricing laws and regulations shall be punished by relevant departments in accordance with the law. Common scenarios of so-called "sky-high priced drinks" disputes involve failing to present price lists and settling bills based on verbal quotes after the fact. This sentence is the author's experience; no official statistics were found.
entries.sources: State Council (2006). Regulations on the Administration of Entertainment Venues (State Council Decree No. 458, Articles 29 and 53). <http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_6297.htm>
entries.notes: What to do: Upon entering a private room, first ask for a price list, either paper or digital, and take photos once received. After ordering, ask for a confirmed checklist. For "special blends" or "fruit platters" recommended by servers, without exception ask the price first before ordering. When there is a dispute upon settling the bill, call 12315 on the spot. Do not pay first and then seek rights protection later; once paid, it will be much harder for you to produce evidence.

entries.title: If someone hands you "stuff" at a venue, leave immediately; accommodating or providing is never just "helping a friend"
entries.cost: Costs no money. Stand up and walk out. The difficulty lies in having to leave the table in front of a whole room of people.
entries.summary: Entertainment venues are not permitted to traffic drugs, provide drugs, or harbor people using drugs inside. Violators must suspend business for rectification for 3 to 6 months, and serious cases will have licenses revoked. Letting someone "use a bit" in a private room you booked or in your residence may constitute the crime of accommodating others to take drugs. If someone takes out unidentified powders, pills, or vape pods and invites you to try, leave on the spot.
entries.benefit: The regulations explicitly prohibit entertainment venues from "trafficking or providing drugs, or organizing, coercing, instigating, luring, deceiving, or accommodating others into ingesting or injecting drugs." Employees are also not allowed to consume drugs, nor provide conditions for customers to engage in the aforementioned acts. For violators, public security organs will confiscate illegal income and illegal property, and order suspension of business for rectification for 3 to 6 months. Under serious circumstances, the entertainment business permit will be revoked. The regulations also require venues to hang warning signs prohibiting drugs, gambling, and prostitution in conspicuous locations in lobbies and private rooms/compartments, indicating reporting phone numbers. On the individual side: the Criminal Law stipulates that "whoever accommodates others to ingest or inject drugs shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years, criminal detention, or public surveillance, and shall also be fined." Judicial interpretations by the Supreme People's Court list circumstances constituting crimes, including accommodating multiple people at one time, accommodating multiple times within two years, accommodating minors, or accommodating for profit. For cases not amounting to a crime, detention of 10 to 15 days is imposed in accordance with the Public Security Administration Punishment Law, and a fine of up to 3,000 yuan may be concurrently imposed. Where circumstances are relatively minor, detention of not more than 5 days or a fine of up to 1,000 yuan shall be imposed. Personally ingesting or injecting drugs likewise results in detention of 10 to 15 days, and a fine of up to 3,000 yuan may be concurrently imposed.
entries.sources: State Council (2006). Regulations on the Administration of Entertainment Venues (State Council Decree No. 458, Articles 14, 30, and 42). <http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_6297.htm>; National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Article 354). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml>; Supreme People's Court (2016). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Drug Crime Cases (Fa Shi [2016] No. 8, Article 12). <https://www.sc.jcy.gov.cn/zlxx/sfjs/201606/t20160617_1809560.shtml> (reprinted by Sichuan Provincial People's Procuratorate); Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2025). Public Security Administration Punishment Law (2025 Revision, Articles 84 and 85). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml>
entries.notes: As long as someone pulls out unknown powders, tablets, or electronic vape cartridges and invites you to "try," leave on the spot; do not stay behind to watch the excitement. The risks you personally take on are heavier than those of the venue. Personally using drugs is in itself subject to public security administrative punishment. "Letting a friend use it here" in a private room you booked or in your own residence may constitute the crime of accommodating others to ingest drugs.

entries.title: Do not eat candy and snacks given by strangers, do not drink beverages that have left your sight, and do not accept vape pods handed to you by others
entries.cost: Costs no money. Never take anything handed over by others without exception. If your own glass leaves your sight, replace it with a new one.
entries.summary: Modern drugs do not look like drugs. "Head-rush" e-cigarettes laced with synthetic cannabinoids look similar to ordinary e-cigarettes, and some people specifically hand them out for trials in bars, KTVs, and hotels. Those who deceive others into consuming face detention of 10 to 15 days plus fines; those who ingest also face detention, while those deceived into ingesting can be given lighter penalties or exempted from punishment. If a beverage has left your sight, replace it with a new one.
entries.benefit: Modern drugs do not look like drugs. Synthetic cannabinoid substances have been placed under generic scheduled control since July 1, 2021; this entire broad class is controlled as drugs. Some people blend it into e-liquid to make "head-rush" e-cigarettes. In cases reported by the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the description by investigating personnel was: this e-liquid "can be turned into various colors and flavors by adding food coloring," and "is basically identical to ordinary e-cigarettes in appearance." Sellers gather friends and companions to promote it in bars, KTVs, and hotels, enticing others to consume it. According to reports, among the consumption cases handled locally that year, minor consumers accounted for nearly 40%. Etomidate has been listed in the Category II Psychotropic Drugs Catalogue since October 1, 2023. Deceiving people into consuming is in itself an offense. Those who entice, instigate, deceive, or coerce others into ingesting or injecting drugs are detained for 10 to 15 days and fined 1,000 to 5,000 yuan. Where it constitutes a crime, the sentence is up to 3 years; where circumstances are serious, 3 to 7 years; for coercion, 3 to 10 years; and penalties are heavier for targeting minors. Personally ingesting or injecting drugs is penalized with 10 to 15 days of detention and a possible fine of up to 3,000 yuan. Where circumstances are relatively minor, detention of up to 5 days or a fine of up to 1,000 yuan applies. For those who consume only because they were coerced or deceived, the same law specifies "lighter punishment, mitigated punishment, or exemption from punishment." One may also be simultaneously ordered not to enter entertainment venues for 6 months to 1 year. Those who become addicted are ordered to undergo community-based drug rehabilitation for 3 years. Refusing community-based rehabilitation, or consuming again during rehabilitation, leads to compulsory isolation for drug rehabilitation for 2 years, which can be extended for up to 1 additional year (nationwide, Public Security Administration Punishment Law effective January 2026).
entries.sources: Supreme People's Procuratorate (2021). Wujiang District, Suzhou, Jiangsu: Handling Prosecutors Uncover New Types of Drugs Cloaked in Trendy Guises. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/zdgz/202110/t20211011_531831.shtml>; National Medical Products Administration, Ministry of Public Security, National Health Commission (2023). Announcement on Adjusting the Catalogues of Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Drugs (2023 No. 120). <https://yjj.sh.gov.cn/qtgzwj/20230911/3b612c94e35b4b63abba314c972a2593.html> (reprinted by Shanghai Municipal Medical Products Administration; original page nmpa.gov.cn returned 412 on local machine); Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2025). Public Security Administration Punishment Law (2025 Revision, Articles 20, 84, and 85). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml>; National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Article 353). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Narcotics Control Law (Articles 33, 38, and 47). <http://www.gd.gov.cn/zwgk/wjk/zcfgk/content/post_2520706.html> (reprinted by People's Government of Guangdong Province)
entries.notes: The same applies not only to entertainment venues, but also outside school gates, at gatherings of friends, and on long-distance buses. Whether what is offered is candy, a beverage, or a vape pod, it is all the same. Being drugged is often followed by robbery, sexual assault, and extortion; this part lacks public official statistics and represents an experiential judgment. As long as a drink has left your sight, replacing it with a new cup is far less troublesome than pursuing accountability after the fact. For what to do when someone takes out unknown powders, tablets, or vape pods at a venue, see Item 3 of this section. For carrying items on behalf of others, see Section 8, Item 29.

entries.title: Avoid going to LARP/murder mystery games and escape rooms located in residential buildings or below basement level 2
entries.cost: Costs no money. Just ask which floor the address is on before booking.
entries.summary: A 2022 notice from five departments clearly stated that script entertainment venues must not be opened inside residential buildings, nor below basement level 1. Such sites are often dim with narrow passages; some are decorated with combustible materials, and evacuation passages are locked or blocked, making it difficult to flee during a fire. Check the address and floor on review pages before booking, and switch to another business if it is non-compliant.
entries.benefit: The 2022 specialized notice from five departments stated very specifically: "Script entertainment business premises shall not be established in residential buildings, below basement level 1 of buildings (excluding basement level 1), or other such locations." The notice also required venues to implement the requirements of the Work Safety Law and the Fire Protection Law, "regularly carrying out self-awareness, self-inspection, and self-rectification of fire risks, improving the capacity for organizing evacuation, escape, and initial fire fighting under emergency circumstances." The same notice also required scripts to provide age-appropriate warnings. Where scenes are unsuitable for minors, minors must not be allowed to enter. Except for statutory holidays, rest days, and winter/summer breaks, script entertainment activities must not be provided to minors. The fire rescue and cultural/tourism departments of Qingpu District, Shanghai inspected 13 such venues at the end of 2021. The briefing stated that such venues typically feature dim environments and narrow passageways, with problems such as decoration using combustible materials and evacuation passages being locked and occupied.
entries.sources: Ministry of Culture and Tourism, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, Ministry of Emergency Management, State Administration for Market Regulation (2022). Notice on Strengthening the Administration of Script Entertainment Business Premises. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-06/27/content_5698021.htm>; Qingpu District Bureau of Culture and Tourism, Shanghai (2022-01-10). Briefing on the Special Fire Safety Inspection of "Escape Room" Venues in Our District. <https://www.shqp.gov.cn/tv/wlzwgk/ml/yw/20220217/913272.html>
entries.notes: That Qingpu briefing also mentioned that some merchants design rooms to be intricate and confusing for atmosphere, and even conceal evacuation signage and emergency lights. Once an accident occurs, it is not easy for people to locate exits right away. Before booking, you can see the floor on the review page, and you can also tell whether it is a residential building. If it is non-compliant, directly switch to another establishment.

entries.title: When your mood drops to the point of depression, go for a walk or a run; the antidepressant effect size is directly proportional to intensity
entries.cost: Costs no money. Around half an hour each time. The hard part is that you least want to move when feeling down, so you have to push yourself.
entries.summary: When people with major depression exercise, brisk walking or jogging brings the most noticeable improvement. Next are yoga, strength training, and tai chi/qigong, with little difference among these several types. The higher the intensity dialed in, the better the effect; strength training and yoga are easiest to stick with. The quality of evidence in this area is on the lower side; what is certain is that moving is better than staying still, so pick the type you can stick with.
entries.benefit: This is the pooled result of 218 randomized controlled trials with two-arm allocations, involving 495 arms and 14,170 participants meeting clinical criteria for major depression. An algorithm compared various exercises against one another (Bayesian network meta-analysis). Comparisons were made against usual care and placebo tablets (active controls). Effect sizes are expressed as Hedges' g, where more negative numbers indicate greater symptom improvement. Brisk walking or jogging −0.62 (95% credible interval −0.80 to −0.45, meaning the true value roughly falls within this range). Yoga −0.55 (−0.73 to −0.36). Strength training −0.49 (−0.69 to −0.29). Mixed aerobic exercise −0.43 (−0.61 to −0.24). Tai chi or qigong −0.42 (−0.65 to −0.21). The original text states that "the effect of exercise was proportional to the intensity prescribed": the higher the intensity prescribed, the better the effect. Strength training and yoga had the best acceptability and were the easiest to adhere to.
entries.sources: Noetel M, Sanders T, Gallardo-Gómez D, et al. (2024). Effect of exercise for depression: systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials. BMJ, 384, e075847. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2023-075847>
entries.notes: Controversy. The authors themselves explicitly noted that among the 218 studies, only 1 was conducted cleanly enough not to be easily biased by study design. According to standard grading methods, brisk walking and jogging only count as "low" credibility, while the rest are "very low." In addition, exercise cannot be blinded from participants; when people know they are working out, they tend to feel better, and this expectation cannot be removed. The directional conclusion remains usable: moving is better than not moving, don't keep the intensity too low, and choose the type you can sustain. This is an expansion of Section 3's "When feeling down, get moving first," and cannot replace standardized treatment after diagnosis.

entries.title: When anxiety interferes with life, mindfulness-based stress reduction courses are non-inferior to common anti-anxiety medications
entries.cost: Signing up for a course costs a little money. The course lasts 8 weeks, with one class per week, plus daily home practice. The hard part is practicing every day for 8 consecutive weeks.
entries.summary: For people diagnosed with anxiety disorders taking an 8-week mindfulness-based stress reduction course, symptom improvement is virtually identical to taking the anti-anxiety drug escitalopram. Nearly 80% of those taking medication experienced adverse reactions, and some dropped out because of them. Around 15% of course participants experienced adverse reactions, and none dropped out. The course must be a standardized 8-week curriculum; random meditation apps do not count.
entries.benefit: This was a trial conducted at 3 urban academic medical centers in the United States to examine whether taking courses would be inferior to taking medication (a non-inferiority randomized controlled trial). 276 adults diagnosed with anxiety disorders were randomized 1:1 into two halves. One group attended an 8-week mindfulness-based stress reduction course. One group took escitalopram (flexible dosing of 10 to 20 mg). 208 people completed the entire process. At the conclusion, calculated by physician-rated anxiety severity scores (Clinical Global Impression of Severity scale), the mindfulness group dropped by 1.35 and the medication group dropped by 1.43. The difference between the two groups was −0.07 (95% CI −0.38 to 0.23, meaning the true gap roughly falls within this range; P=0.65, meaning this small difference is indistinguishable from no difference). The lower bound of this interval did not cross the predetermined line for "not considered worse" (non-inferiority margin −0.495). There was a substantial difference in side effects: 78.6% of the medication group had at least one study-related adverse event, with 10 people dropping out because of it. In the mindfulness group, it was 15.4%, with zero dropouts.
entries.sources: Hoge EA, Bui E, Mete M, Dutton MA, Baker AW, Simon NM (2023). Mindfulness-based stress reduction vs escitalopram for the treatment of adults with anxiety disorders: a randomized clinical trial. JAMA Psychiatry, 80(1), 13-21. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamapsychiatry.2022.3679>
entries.notes: The trial used a standardized 8-week mindfulness-based stress reduction course (MBSR); any random meditation app cannot be equated with it. It applies to individuals who have reached diagnostic criteria for anxiety disorders; you should still see a doctor when needed. If you have been putting off treatment due to concerns over medication side effects, there is another option with comparable evidentiary strength.

entries.title: To recover your calm on the spot, use 5 minutes of "cyclic sighing": two-stage inhalation, prolonged exhalation
entries.cost: Costs no money. 5 minutes a day.
entries.summary: Doing 5 minutes of breathing exercises daily for a month yields better improvements in mood and breathing slowdown than mindfulness meditation of the same duration. Among several breathing techniques, "cyclic sighing," which emphasizes prolonging exhalation, is the best. The method is to take an inhale through the nose, take another small supplemental inhale to fill the lungs completely, and then slowly exhale fully through the mouth. This is only a single trial with outcomes self-reported by participants, but it costs nothing.
entries.benefit: This was an at-home, randomized controlled trial comparing three types of daily 5-minute breathing exercises against mindfulness meditation of the same duration over 1 month. The three breathing techniques were: cyclic sighing (emphasizing prolonged exhalation), box breathing (equal duration of inhalation, breath retention, and exhalation), and cyclic hyperventilation with retention (long inhalation, short exhalation). When pooling individual session data together (mixed-effects models), breathing exercises all outperformed mindfulness meditation, especially cyclic sighing, which emphasizes exhalation. It was superior in both mood improvement (P<0.05, meaning this difference is unlikely to be pure coincidence) and reduction in respiratory rate (P<0.05).
entries.sources: Balban MY, Neri E, Kogon MM, et al. (2023). Brief structured respiration practices enhance mood and reduce physiological arousal. Cell Reports Medicine, 4(1), 100895. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xcrm.2022.100895>
entries.notes: The technique is to inhale through the nose, briefly take a small supplemental inhale to fill the lungs completely, and then slowly and deeply exhale all air through the mouth, repeating for 5 minutes. There is only this one trial, done at home, where outcomes were self-reported via questionnaires, and the participant count was not large. The effect is merely slightly better than meditation and cannot be considered a cure-all. However, it costs no money, takes only 5 minutes, can be done anytime and anywhere, and has high cost-effectiveness.

entries.title: Treat "meeting people regularly" as a health expense, rather than reaching out only when in a bad mood
entries.cost: Requires spending a bit of money, plus the time spent meeting up. The hard part is proactively asking people out even when in a good mood.
entries.summary: People who rarely interact with others in daily life have an approximately 30% higher risk of death over the same period. For those feeling lonely, it is about one-quarter higher; for those living alone, about 30% higher; and this is more pronounced in people under 65. These are all tracked observational findings; it may also be that people whose health is already poorer are more likely to live alone.
entries.benefit: This is the pooled result of 70 studies that recorded baseline conditions and tracked participants prospectively (meta-analysis), totaling 3.4 million participants with an average follow-up of 7 years. Social isolation, loneliness, and living alone were all associated with increased mortality. After controlling for confounding factors such as age and health status, the weighted average odds ratios were: social isolation 1.29, loneliness 1.26, and living alone 1.32. Converted, the probabilities of death during the same period were higher by about 30%, about one-quarter, and about 30%, respectively. The effect sizes of the three were similar, and they were larger in populations under 65 years old than in elderly populations.
entries.sources: Holt-Lunstad J, Smith TB, Baker M, Harris T, Stephenson D (2015). Loneliness and social isolation as risk factors for mortality: a meta-analytic review. Perspectives on Psychological Science, 10(2), 227-237. <https://doi.org/10.1177/1745691614568352>
entries.notes: Controversy. These are all associations observed by tracking cohorts, not randomized controlled trials; cause and effect cannot be disentangled. People whose health is inherently poor are more likely to live alone and socialize less. The authors view social relationships as a health factor on the same magnitude as smoking and obesity, but there are no randomized trials proving that "increasing social interaction reduces mortality." This item does not conflict with Section 3's "Cut back on interpersonal relationships that drain you": that one cuts ties that deplete you, whereas here the goal is to protect the few relationships that restore your energy.

entries.title: Factor surrounding green space into choosing a residence, but do not count on "visiting parks more" to prolong life
entries.cost: Costs no money. Just glance at the surrounding greenery while viewing apartments.
entries.summary: The better the greening within 500 meters around a residence, the lower the probability of death during the same period—calculated as roughly 4% lower for every 0.1 increase in vegetation index. What is measured is the greening surrounding the residence, not the number of times you visit parks. In areas with good greenery, residents are often wealthier and the air is better. Therefore, do not treat this as if going to parks will lengthen lifespan; simply factoring surrounding green spaces in when choosing a home is enough.
entries.benefit: This is the pooled result of 9 cohort studies that tracked populations over many years (a meta-analysis of cohort studies), involving 8.32 million people across 7 countries. It examined surrounding greenness within 500 meters of residences, measured by the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI, a figure converting ground vegetation coverage into a number). For every 0.1-unit increase in NDVI, the pooled hazard ratio for all-cause mortality was 0.96 (95% CI 0.94–0.97). The probability of dying during the study period was about 4% lower, with the true value largely falling between 3% lower and 6% lower. Seven of the 9 studies found lower mortality with higher greenness, and the difference did not appear to be coincidental. The other 2 studies found no association.
entries.sources: Rojas-Rueda D, Nieuwenhuijsen MJ, Gascon M, Perez-Leon D, Mudu P (2019). Green spaces and mortality: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies. The Lancet Planetary Health, 3(11), e469-e477. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S2542-5196(19)30215-3>
entries.notes: Controversial. Results varied widely across individual studies (I² = 95%; higher values mean studies align less with each other). Furthermore, it measured surrounding greenness around residences, not the frequency of your visits to parks. People living in greener areas are often wealthier, enjoy better air quality, and exercise more; it is impossible to separate which of these factors alongside greenness is driving the effect. Do not read this as "visiting parks can extend your life"; the actionable takeaway is to factor green space into your choice of residence, which carries zero financial cost. For NDVI values, bare land and concrete are close to 0, while dense vegetation is close to 1. Thus, "0.1" roughly corresponds to the difference between moving from a bare block to a street lined with rows of trees.

entries.title: Do not soak in hot springs or use saunas after drinking alcohol, nor take a hot bath after returning home
entries.cost: Free. If you have been drinking, reschedule your soak for another day, and just take a quick shower when you get home. The difficulty lies in hot springs and saunas often being the next stop after dinner; when the whole table is going, you have to speak up and decline.
entries.summary: In Finland, half of the people who died in saunas had consumed alcohol. In Tokyo, roughly one quarter of bath-related death victims who underwent autopsies had significant blood alcohol levels, and in one bathtub drowning record, alcohol intoxication was the most common contributing factor. Japanese authorities list "avoid bathing after drinking" as a key drowning prevention rule. If a companion has had too much to drink, do not let them go in to soak alone either.
entries.benefit: Finland examined sauna-related deaths case by case from 1990 to 2002 using police and forensic pathology reports. Such deaths occur at fewer than 2 per 100,000 people annually, with the original text stating that "overall, 50% of victims were under the influence of alcohol." The authors noted that alcohol risk is rising, and prevention focuses on reducing drinking and not leaving intoxicated individuals alone in a sauna. Tokyo medical examiners investigated 3,289 bath-related deaths from 2009 to 2011. Among the 550 cases autopsied, 140 had a blood alcohol concentration exceeding 0.5 mg/mL, accounting for about one quarter. Another autopsy record in Tokyo documented 77 bathtub drownings, where alcohol intoxication was the most frequent contributing factor (25 cases), followed by heart disease (22 cases). A December 2025 reminder from Japan's Consumer Affairs Agency noted that 7,776 people drowned in bathtubs in Japan in 2024, of whom 7,363 were aged 65 or older. Key safety tips noted: avoid bathing immediately after a meal, after consuming alcohol, or after taking medication. The Chinese Embassy in Japan warned that "it is inappropriate to bathe after drinking," because "bathing after drinking can easily trigger acute cardiovascular emergencies." Health education from the Shaanxi Provincial Health Commission noted that when soaking in hot springs after drinking, high water temperatures cause blood vessels to dilate, potentially leading to hypotension, hypoglycemia, or even syncope.
entries.sources: Kenttämies A, Karkola K (2008). Death in sauna. Journal of Forensic Sciences, 53(3), 724-729. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1556-4029.2008.00703.x>; Suzuki H, Hikiji W, Tanifuji T, Abe N, Fukunaga T (2015). Characteristics of sudden bath-related death investigated by medical examiners in Tokyo, Japan. Journal of Epidemiology, 25(2), 126-132. <https://doi.org/10.2188/jea.JE20140068>; Mishima S, Suzuki H, Fukunaga T, Nishitani Y (2018). Postmortem computed tomography findings in cases of bath-related death: applicability and limitation in forensic practice. Forensic Science International, 282, 195-203. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.forsciint.2017.11.030>; Consumer Affairs Agency (2025). Let's be careful of accidents involving the elderly during the New Year holidays!: "Avoid bathing immediately after meals, after drinking alcohol, or after taking medication." <https://www.caa.go.jp/policies/policy/consumer_safety/caution/caution_084/>; Embassy of the People's Republic of China in Japan (2015). Consular Reminder No. 17: "It is not advisable to bathe on an empty stomach, on a full stomach, or after drinking alcohol. Bathing after drinking easily triggers acute emergencies of the heart or vascular system." <https://jp.china-embassy.gov.cn/chn/jbwzlmnew/lszcnew/LSBHYXZ/LSBHLBZN/201503/t20150327_9475462.htm>; Shaanxi Provincial Health Commission (2021). Hot springs preserve health only when done right: "Never soak in hot springs after drinking alcohol or on an empty stomach; under the stimulation of high water temperatures, it easily causes peripheral vasodilation, resulting in hypotension, hypoglycemia, or even syncope." <https://sxwjw.shaanxi.gov.cn/ywgz/gbbj/202101/t20210111_2148844.html>
entries.notes: Rated B because these studies only examined deceased individuals. No one has calculated how many people who soak after drinking experience accidents, so it is impossible to state how many times higher the risk is. The benefit is rated "Moderate" based on judgment: while total deaths in saunas and bathtubs are inherently low, individuals who had consumed alcohol account for one quarter to one half of the deceased. Most bathtub drowning victims in Japan are elderly, but young people who have consumed alcohol face equal risks in saunas. For the routine benefits of bathing along with reminders on water temperature and duration, see Section 2, Item 36 (Take baths when feasible). For how to look after an intoxicated companion, see Section 13, Item 46 (When someone gets drunk).

entries.title: Wear a helmet when skiing, snowboarding, roller skating, or mountain biking
entries.cost: Buying one costs a few hundred yuan. Putting it on and fastening the buckle strap takes a few seconds each time.
entries.summary: Wearing a helmet when skiing or snowboarding reduces the likelihood of head injury during falls or collisions by about one third, and by about 60% in children under 13. Wearing a bicycle helmet reduces severe head injuries by about 70% and fatal head injuries by about two thirds. Wearing a helmet does not make neck injuries more likely.
entries.benefit: Figures for skiing and snowboarding come from a pooled analysis of 12 studies. Most studies compared individuals with head injuries against others to examine who was wearing a helmet (case-control). Among helmet wearers, the odds ratio (OR) for head injury was 0.65 (95% CI 0.55–0.79), a reduction of about 35%. In studies including children under 13, the OR was 0.41 (0.27–0.59), a reduction of about 59%. For neck injuries, the OR was 0.89 (0.72–1.09), showing no increase. Bicycle figures come from 40 studies covering over 64,000 individuals involved in crashes or falls. For head injuries, the OR was 0.49 (0.42–0.57), a reduction of about 51%. For severe head injuries, the OR was 0.31 (0.25–0.37), a reduction of about 69%. For fatal head injuries, the OR was 0.35 (0.14–0.88), a reduction of about 65%. For facial injuries, the OR was 0.67 (0.56–0.81), a reduction of about 33%. For neck injuries, the OR was 0.96 (0.74–1.25), showing no apparent association. The Beijing Municipal Bureau of Sports stated that following the 2017 revision of Beijing's local ski resort standards, wearing a helmet is required to access advanced slopes.
entries.sources: Russell K, Christie J, Hagel BE (2010). The effect of helmets on the risk of head and neck injuries among skiers and snowboarders: a meta-analysis. CMAJ, 182(4), 333-340. <https://doi.org/10.1503/cmaj.091080>; Olivier J, Creighton P (2017). Bicycle injuries and helmet use: a systematic review and meta-analysis. International Journal of Epidemiology, 46(1), 278-292. <https://doi.org/10.1093/ije/dyw153>; Beijing Municipal Bureau of Sports. Response to Proposal No. 1276 of the 4th Session of the 13th Beijing Municipal Committee of the CPPCC: "Explicitly requires skiers to wear helmets before they can enter advanced ski slope areas." <https://tyj.beijing.gov.cn/bjsports/zfxxgk_/1421305/jytablgz/11180211/index.html>
entries.notes: These numbers calculate the likelihood of head injury once a fall or collision occurs; wearing a helmet will not make you fall less often. No comparable pooled studies were found for roller skating and skateboarding, so the recommendation is extrapolated by analogy because the mechanisms of falling and hitting the head are similar. Helmets must fit properly, straps must be fastened tightly, and rented helmets should be tried on first. For wearing helmets while riding motorcycles and electric bicycles, see Section 1, Item 2 (Wear helmets).

chapters.title: Which Skills Are Cost-Effective to Learn
chapters.intro:
This section evaluates money and time, with Item 2 additionally factoring in mortality rates. The first six items address one question: whether you should continue your schooling. Item 1 first explains which options are ruled out by law, Item 2 calculates the relationship between education and life expectancy, and Item 3 examines where the national population stands in terms of educational attainment. Item 4 explains what financial aid is available if you cannot afford schooling, and Item 5 discusses alternatives if you did not test into a regular high school. Item 6 frames "schooling versus working" as a problem, providing a DIY calculation method. The following seven items address another question: once you decide to learn something, how to choose. In China, wage statistics broken down by occupation are difficult to verify individually from public official sources. Therefore, this section covers only matters with verifiable sources: how much wages roughly increase with each additional year of schooling (also called returns to education), how to verify whether a credential is legitimate, where training subsidies come from, and which skill dimensions make you less vulnerable to replacement. This book does not provide monthly wage figures for specific occupations. Items 14 through 19 address a third question: once you decide what to learn, how to study to save time. These six items calculate time without converting it into monetary value. Items 20 through 23 address a fourth question: if you are already engaged in professional technical work, where to apply for professional titles, how to take the exams, which pitfalls to avoid, and how much value obtaining a title brings. Items 24 and 25 address whether to pursue a master's or doctoral degree upon graduating with a bachelor's or master's degree. Because domestic income figures controlling for individual differences could not be found, British studies are cited.

Items in this section are grouped by topic as follows, with item numbers in parentheses:

**Whether to continue schooling**: Minors under 16 years of age cannot work (Item 1), whether education is useful when factoring into mortality (Item 2), nationwide educational attainment structure (Item 3), when unable to afford schooling, calculate according to policy first (Item 4), paths when missing regular high school admission (Item 5), calculating schooling versus working as a math problem (Item 6).

**How to choose what to learn**: Returns on an additional year of education (Item 7), checking the vocational qualification directory before testing for certificates (Item 8), pursuing training through government-subsidized channels (Item 9), choosing skills requiring hands-on work and on-site judgment (Item 10), checking whether skills have grade assessments (Item 11), checking local shortage occupation directories (Item 12), selecting short-cycle programs leading directly to employment (Item 13).

**How to study to save time**: Test yourself with closed books after studying (Item 14), spacing time over several days (Item 15), not treating highlighting as your primary study method (Item 16), mixing multiple problem types during practice (Item 17), not choosing study methods based on visual vs. auditory styles (Item 18), creating quiz questions to test yourself on memorization material (Item 19).

**Professional title evaluation**: Finding application channels for professional titles (Item 20), primary and intermediate accounting titles rely on unified national exams (Item 21), avoiding third-party agencies for title evaluation (Item 22), obtaining a title does not equal a salary raise (Item 23).

**Graduate and doctoral studies**: Whether to continue to a master's degree after graduating with a bachelor's (Item 24), whether to continue to a doctorate after graduating with a master's (Item 25).

entries.title: Under 16 years of age, "going to work" is not an option: hiring units are fined 5,000 yuan per month, and those willing to hire are illegal sweatshops
entries.cost: Free. Takes one minute to calculate your age.
entries.summary: Junior high school graduation usually occurs at ages 15 to 16, right on this boundary line. Under 16 years of age, apart from special recruitment by cultural, arts, or sports organizations, an employer hiring you violates the law and is subject to a fine of 5,000 yuan per month for every child laborer employed. Consequently, any employer willing to take you on is operating illegally. If an accident occurs, medical expenses and compensation can only be pursued against that employer.
entries.benefit: Article 11 of the Compulsory Education Law: "All children who have reached the age of six shall be sent to school by their parents or other statutory guardians to receive and complete compulsory education." Article 14: "Employing units are prohibited from recruiting school-age children and adolescents who should receive compulsory education." Article 58: Where, without justifiable reasons, school-age children or adolescents are not sent to school in accordance with this Law, the local township people's government or the administrative department of education of the county people's government shall "give criticism and education, and order rectification within a specified time limit." Article 2 of the Provisions on the Prohibition of Using Child Labor: State organs, social groups, enterprises, public institutions, private non-enterprise entities, or individual industrial and commercial households "shall not recruit minors under the age of 16." Article 6: "Punishment shall be imposed at a standard of a 5,000 yuan fine per month for each child laborer employed"; those failing to rectify within the deadline shall be fined 10,000 yuan per person per month. Article 7: Those introducing child labor into employment "shall be fined 5,000 yuan for each person introduced." Article 10: Where a child laborer suffers illness or injury, the employing unit "shall be responsible for sending them to a medical institution for treatment and bear all medical and living expenses during the treatment period," and provide a one-off compensation in cases of disability or death. Article 13 leaves only one exception: arts and sports organizations, with the consent of parents or other guardians, may recruit professional performers and athletes under 16 years of age (Nationwide).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). Compulsory Education Law (Second Amendment of 2018, Articles 11, 14, 58). <http://www.moe.gov.cn/jyb_sjzl/sjzl_zcfg/zcfg_jyfl/202110/t20211029_575949.html> (published by the Ministry of Education); State Council (2002). Provisions on the Prohibition of Using Child Labor (State Council Decree No. 364, Articles 2, 6, 7, 10, 13). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2002/content_61798.htm>
entries.notes: The beneficiary is yourself. Working after reaching 16 is lawful. If you want to learn a trade before working, you can review it against the dimensions in Item 10 of this section (Pick skills resistant to automation). Overtime pay, annual leave, and work injury benefits covered in Section 19 all presuppose an established labor relationship and evidence. If a child laborer is injured, according to Article 10 of the Provisions on the Prohibition of Using Child Labor, the employing unit must bear all medical and living expenses during the treatment period, and provide a one-off compensation in cases of disability or death.

entries.title: Factor whether "education is useful" into mortality calculations: each additional year of education reduces adult mortality risk by about 1.9%
entries.cost: Free. The cost is the time and effort spent pursuing those extra years of schooling; for the tuition portion, see Item 4 of this section (Secondary vocational tuition and grants). The difficulty lies in persisting all the way through without dropping out halfway.
entries.summary: For each additional year of schooling, adult mortality risk is about 1.9% lower on average. The effect is most pronounced for individuals aged 18 to 49, with each additional year lowering risk by about 2.9%, compared with only 0.8% lower for those over 70. People who can stay in school continuously often had better background circumstances to begin with, making it impossible to separate how much of this is the effect of education itself.
entries.benefit: Pooling and analyzing all identified previous studies together (systematic review and meta-analysis). The search period spanned January 1980 to May 2023, ultimately including 603 studies, 70 locations across 59 countries, and 10,355 observations. Education and adult mortality (all-cause mortality) exhibit a dose-response relationship (the more years of schooling, the greater the reduction).
