For each additional year of education, mortality risk decreased by an average of 1.9% (95% uncertainty interval 1.8–2.0, with the true value largely falling within this range). For individuals aged 18 to 49, each additional year decreased risk by 2.9% (2.8–3.0). For those aged 70 and older, the decrease was 0.8% (0.6–1.0). No differences were found between males and females. When broken down by national development levels (Socio-demographic Index), no differences were observed either.
entries.sources: IHME-CHAIN Collaborators (2024). Effects of education on adult mortality: a global systematic review and meta-analysis. The Lancet Public Health, 9(3), e155-e165. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S2468-2667(23)00306-7>
entries.notes: Controversial. The authors themselves reported publication bias (p < 0.0001), meaning studies with favorable results were more likely to be published. Results across individual studies also varied substantially. All included studies were longitudinal observational cohorts, not randomized controlled trials. Years of schooling are confounded with family background, region, and occupation. Observational studies cannot distinguish how much of this 1.9% stems from schooling itself versus "people who can stay in school continuously were in better circumstances to begin with." Nor can they separate reverse causality: individuals who suffered from illness or psychological issues in childhood are more prone to drop out of school and also more prone to die earlier, which can make the effect of schooling appear larger than it actually is. Thus, while it strongly illustrates that "more schooling and living longer move in the same direction," this does not equate to "going to school will lengthen your life by 1.9%." Magnitude of benefit is rated Minor: readers typically face whether to study for an additional three or four years, which at 1.9% per year adds up to under 10%, qualifying as Minor under the book's thresholds. The beneficiary is yourself.

entries.title: Before judging whether "degrees have devalued," first look at the national educational attainment structure: only 15,467 out of every 100,000 people have a college or university education (2020 census, sample projection for 2025 is about 19%)
entries.cost: Free. Just glance at the numbers below.
entries.summary: During the 2020 national census, about 15% of the nationwide population had attained a junior college education or above. Projections from the 2025 sample survey estimated this at about 19%, gaining a few percentage points over five years. In both instances, those with a junior high school education formed the largest demographic. People aged 15 and above had an average of only 9.91 years of schooling, barely past junior high school graduation. Therefore, in China, a junior high school education represents the most populous demographic bracket and can hardly be considered scarce.
entries.benefit: The standard reference time for the Seventh National Population Census was 00:00 on November 1, 2020. Among the national population, 218,360,767 people possessed a university (junior college and above) education level; 213,005,258 people possessed a senior high school (including secondary specialized school) level; 487,163,489 people possessed a junior high school level; and 349,658,828 people possessed a primary school level. Compared with the Sixth National Population Census in 2010, the number of people with a university education level per 100,000 people rose from 8,930 to 15,467; senior high school rose from 14,032 to 15,088; junior high school dropped from 38,788 to 34,507; and primary school dropped from 26,779 to 24,767. The average years of schooling for the population aged 15 and above increased from 9.08 years to 9.91 years. The illiteracy rate declined from 4.08% to 2.67%. The standard reference time for the 2025 National 1% Population Sample Survey was November 1, 2025, with a sample size of 20.52 million people. Extrapolated from the sample, the national population was 1,405.45 million people. Among them, university (junior college and above) accounted for 272.33 million people, senior high school (including secondary specialized school) accounted for 242.72 million people, junior high school accounted for 452.83 million people, and primary school accounted for 331.22 million people. The communique did not provide figures per 100,000 people. Calculated independently against the total population, university accounted for approximately 19.4%, and junior high school accounted for approximately 32.2%, remaining the most populous demographic bracket.
entries.sources: National Bureau of Statistics, Office of the Leading Group of the State Council for the Seventh National Population Census (2021). Communiqué of the Seventh National Population Census (No. 6) — Educational Attainment of the Population. <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/tjgb/rkpcgb/qgrkpcgb/202302/t20230206_1902006.html>; National Bureau of Statistics (2026). Main Data Communiqué of the 2025 National 1% Population Sample Survey. <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202605/t20260522_1963788.html>
entries.notes: These numbers only illustrate whether an academic credential is scarce among the general population. Whether schooling is cost-effective for a specific individual must be calculated on one's own using the method in item 6 of this section ("How to calculate schooling versus working"). It should also be noted: census figures count the entire national population, including the elderly and children; they do not represent the labor force, nor do they represent your peer age group. The communiqués do not break down figures by age. Seeing that the number of people with a university education level per 100,000 rose by more than 70% from 2010 to 2020, the proportion among young people is very likely higher than the national figure; this is an inference. Comparing national figures directly with your peers will therefore overestimate your own advantage. What it can show is this: across the entire national population, university-level education is still a minority. The 2025 figures are sample estimates, whereas the census is an exhaustive household-by-household count; the two statistical scopes differ. Hence, both sets of figures are juxtaposed rather than replacing the old figures with the new ones. The 19.4% and 32.2% figures are self-calculated based on the population numbers and total population in the communiqué. Beneficiary: oneself.

entries.title: If you think you "can't afford to study," calculate according to policies first: tuition at public secondary vocational schools is already waived for most rural and financially disadvantaged students, grants are 2,300 yuan, and student loans reach up to 20,000 yuan per year
entries.cost: Costs no money. Before school starts, visit the school's student financial aid management office once and submit application materials once.
entries.summary: In public secondary vocational schools, tuition is already waived for rural students, urban students enrolled in agriculture-related majors, and students from financially disadvantaged families. Starting in spring 2025, national grants for secondary vocational schools and regular high schools are 2,300 yuan per year. In college, national grants are 3,700 yuan per year, and student loans allow borrowing up to 20,000 yuan per year. When money is tight, calculate these options first before deciding whether to drop out and work.
entries.benefit: Secondary vocational tuition exemption has been policy since the fall semester of 2012. The original text states: "Tuition is waived for all rural (including county and town) students, urban students enrolled in agriculture-related majors, and students with financial difficulties among regular first-, second-, and third-year full-time students in public secondary vocational schools (excluding students in arts-related performance majors)." In 2024, student financial aid policies were adjusted. The National Grant for undergraduate and junior college students was raised from 3,300 yuan per student per year to 3,700 yuan. The National Encouragement Scholarship was raised from 5,000 yuan to 6,000 yuan. Both took effect from the fall semester of 2024 (the Encouragement Scholarship starting in 2024). National grants for both secondary vocational schools and regular high schools were raised from 2,000 yuan per student per year to 2,300 yuan, taking effect from the spring semester of 2025. National student loans were also adjusted starting from the fall semester of 2024. For undergraduate and junior college students, "the maximum loan application limit per person per year was increased from no more than 16,000 yuan to no more than 20,000 yuan." For postgraduate students, "increased from no more than 20,000 yuan to no more than 25,000 yuan." The interest rate is the Loan Prime Rate (LPR) of the corresponding tier for the same period minus 70 basis points (an additional 0.7 percentage points lower) (Nationwide).
entries.sources: Ministry of Finance, National Development and Reform Commission, Ministry of Education, Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2012). Opinions on Expanding the Scope of the Policy for Tuition Exemption in Secondary Vocational Education and Further Improving the National Financial Aid System (Cai Jiao [2012] No. 376). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2013/content_2332779.htm>; Relevant Department Heads of the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Education, and Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2024). Answering Reporters' Questions on Adjusting Student Financial Aid Policies. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202410/content_6983672.htm>; Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Education, People's Bank of China, National Financial Regulatory Administration (2024). Notice on Adjusting and Improving Relevant Policies for National Student Loans (Cai Jiao [2024] No. 188). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202411/content_6984812.htm>
entries.notes: Beneficiaries: oneself and children. Specific coverage criteria for tuition waivers and tier classifications for grants are determined by each province. Private schools subsidize according to local public standards for comparable majors, and the difference must still be paid out of pocket, so check local documents before enrollment. Student loans are loans, not grants, and must be repaid after graduation. However, they separate "unable to produce tuition right now" from "whether these years are cost-effective" into two distinct matters; do not take lacking funds as an immediate conclusion to stop studying. Section 7 covered training subsidies and temporary relief during periods of unemployment; if the household has genuinely lost income, apply for those items first.

entries.title: Failing to test into a regular high school does not mean the road is blocked: secondary vocational schools have integrated admissions and independent exams, and public institution recruitment for skilled posts can lower academic credential requirements
entries.cost: Costs no money. Check your provincial vocational education admissions platform once before filling out high school entrance examination preferences.
entries.summary: The 2022 Vocational Education Law explicitly states: vocational education holds equal status and importance alongside general education. Secondary vocational schools can coordinate integrated admissions with higher vocational colleges, and higher vocational colleges must reserve enrollment quotas or hold independent entrance examinations specifically to recruit secondary vocational graduates. Employers are also barred from creating hurdles to screen you out just because you graduated from a vocational school. Scoring too low for a regular high school means changing tracks, not being stuck forever with a junior high school education.
entries.benefit: Article 3 of the Vocational Education Law (effective May 1, 2022): "Vocational education is a type of education that holds equal status and importance alongside general education." Article 37: Secondary vocational schools "may, in accordance with relevant national regulations, implement integrated admissions and training with higher vocational school education in relevant majors." Higher vocational schools "may, in accordance with relevant national regulations, enroll students through assessment methods combining cultural literacy and vocational skills." Educational administrative departments at or above the provincial level must establish unified vocational education admissions platforms to compile and publish information on schools, major offerings, and admissions, and provide inquiry and application services. Article 53: "Students of vocational schools enjoy equal opportunities with students of regular schools at the same tier in advancing to higher education, employment, career development, and other areas." Higher vocational schools and regular higher education institutions offering vocational education "shall designate appropriate quotas in enrollment plans or adopt independent examination methods specifically to recruit vocational school graduates." "Employers shall not set conditions for application, recruitment, or hiring that hinder equal employment and fair competition for vocational school graduates." In public recruitment by public institutions (shiye danwei), for positions with vocational skill grade requirements, "academic credential requirements may be lowered appropriately" (Nationwide).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2022). Vocational Education Law (2022 Revision, Articles 3, 37, 53). <http://www.moe.gov.cn/jyb_sjzl/sjzl_zcfg/zcfg_jyfl/202204/t20220421_620064.html> (published by the Ministry of Education)
entries.notes: Beneficiaries: oneself and children. These are statutory channels, not guaranteed admission. Which majors offer integrated training, what proportion is reserved for independent admissions, and which subjects are tested on the vocational education college entrance examination are all decided by each province. Before submitting preferences, you must check your province's vocational education admissions platform and enrollment plan for the current year; do not extrapolate from other provinces' experiences. When picking a secondary vocational major, run it through the dimensions in item 10 of this section ("Picking automation-resistant skills"): majors that require physical presence and non-standard environments are much harder to displace. When selecting a school, check whether it is listed in your province's vocational education admissions plan for that year. Verify its issued certificates against the three steps in item 8 ("Checking whether a certificate is in the catalog"). Reject without exception any admissions marketing promising "guaranteed job placement" or "guaranteed pass."

entries.title: Framing "study or work" as a math problem: the three years of early wages earned by working first versus the annual income gap across decades gained by continuing to study
entries.cost: Costs no money. Sit down and calculate once, taking about half an hour.
entries.summary: Going straight to work lets you earn a few years of wages early, but you only collect that sum once. Continuing your education means earning more every single year down the line than if you hadn't, collecting that difference across thirty or forty years. Therefore, you must compare these two sums side-by-side. In urban China, each additional year of schooling yields an annual income roughly 4.0% to 10.2% higher, though this reflects pre-2001 data and only serves as a rough reference.
entries.benefit: This is an estimate for urban China from 1988 to 2001. How much higher income becomes with each additional year of education is called the rate of return to education. The original text states that it "rose substantially from 4.0% per year of education in 1988 to 10.2% in 2001." The increase occurred primarily after 1992. It reflects the fact that the extra earnings college-educated individuals make over those without college (the higher education wage premium) were expanding. This represents a usable domestic Chinese benchmark when converting "one additional year of schooling" into an annual income difference. For global averages, see item 7 of this section ("Global average returns per additional year of education").
entries.sources: Zhang J, Zhao Y, Park A, Song X (2005). Economic returns to schooling in urban China, 1988 to 2001. Journal of Comparative Economics, 33(4), 730-752. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jce.2005.05.008>
entries.notes: Before calculating, first deduct the tuition exemptions and grants mentioned in item 4 of this section ("Secondary vocational tuition and grants"), and also incorporate the mortality calculus from item 2 of this section ("One additional year of education and mortality"). The data runs up to 2001 and covers only urban areas, so it cannot be used directly as today's figure. The same applies to the 9% global average in item 7 of this section. What is provided here is the calculation method, not the answer: following this method, the conclusion will vary from person to person. For high-tuition tracks with mismatched majors and jobs and prolonged study durations, the math may genuinely show it is not cost-effective. However, that only proves that specific program is not cost-effective, not that education is useless. Several factors cannot fit into the formula, but are very real: statutory educational credential thresholds (see item 5 of this section on integrated admissions and independent exams for secondary vocational schools), resistance to automation (see item 10 on picking automation-resistant skills), and the flexibility to switch industries. Beneficiary: oneself.

entries.title: Remember the baseline first: for each additional year of education, the global average private return (the portion accruing to personal income) is approximately 9% per year
entries.cost: Costs no money. Memorize this figure and treat it as a yardstick to gauge various "learning something" schemes.
entries.summary: Based on worldwide averages, each additional year of schooling raises personal income by about 9% annually, with returns for women consistently higher than for men. This figure refers to formal schooling; it cannot be applied directly to signing up for a training course. Use it as a yardstick: if a course requires you to spend 30,000 yuan and six months, ask whether the income change it brings matches an extra year of schooling.
entries.benefit: A review spanning 1950 to 2014, covering 139 countries and 1,120 estimates, concluded: "The global average private rate of return for an additional year of schooling is 9% per year." Private return refers to the portion accruing to personal income: with each extra year of schooling, income is on average about 9% higher. Private returns to higher education are rising. Social returns to education (the portion accruing to society as a whole rather than the individual) remain high. The average returns to education for women are consistently higher than for men.
entries.sources: Psacharopoulos G, Patrinos HA (2018). Returns to investment in education: a decennial review of the global literature. Education Economics, 26(5), 445-458. <https://doi.org/10.1080/09645292.2018.1484426>; World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 8402. <https://doi.org/10.1596/1813-9450-8402>
entries.notes: This is a global average for "one additional year of schooling"; it cannot be equated to the return of "enrolling in a training course," nor is it a specific figure for China—it serves only as an order-of-magnitude benchmark. Its purpose is to provide a ruler for evaluating any training proposal. If a course asks you to spend 30,000 yuan and half a year of time, you should ask whether it can generate an income change equivalent to one year of formal education. Furthermore, keep in mind that global averages mask enormous differences across fields of study and countries.

entries.title: Before spending money to get certified, verify whether the certificate is in the National Vocational Qualification Catalog or on the list of evaluation institutions registered with the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security
entries.cost: Costs no money. Takes about ten-odd minutes to check once.
entries.summary: Some organizations operate illicit classes, charge arbitrary fees, and issue unregulated certificates under the guise of "new professions" and "skill levels," with some even impersonating authoritative institutions—practices specifically cracked down upon by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security. Before enrolling, follow three steps: check whether the occupation is in the National Vocational Qualification Catalog, whether the issuing body is an evaluation agency registered with human resources and social security departments, and whether the certificate number can be queried on the official platform. If it cannot be queried, do not sign up.
entries.benefit: The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security launched a nationwide enforcement campaign specifically addressing this issue. Malpractices singled out in the official document include: "some institutions and entities arbitrarily hold training, evaluation, and certification activities under the guise of new vocational qualifications, vocational skill levels, etc., charging arbitrary fees and indiscriminately issuing certificates; some institutions and entities engage in false or exaggerated publicity, and even organize training, evaluation, and certificate issuance in the name of counterfeit authoritative institutions." Enforcement actions include joint crackdowns with cyberspace administration, public security, market regulation, and other departments to "severely crack down on appraisal and certification activities by counterfeit appraisal agencies and evaluation agencies not registered with human resources and social security departments." Non-compliant promotional materials on websites and new media are shut down in accordance with the law. The document simultaneously mandates "guiding the public to understand certificate query channels and methods to judge certificate legitimacy, compliance, and credibility."
entries.sources: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2022). Notice on Carrying Out Special Rectification Work Against "Counterfeit Certificates" in Technical and Skilled Categories. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-03/18/content_5679641.htm>
entries.notes: Verify in this exact sequence. First, see whether the occupation is in the National Vocational Qualification Catalog; if not, it is not a national vocational qualification. Second, check whether the issuing body is an evaluation agency registered with human resources and social security authorities. Finally, visit the official vocational skills talent evaluation certificate query platform to check whether the certificate number can be found. If it cannot be found, do not sign up under any circumstances. Programs bearing labels like "International," "Senior/Advanced," or "Certified," or promising "guaranteed pass" or "income via credential renting/affiliation," carry the highest risk. For pay-to-play degree mill programs claiming "academic credential upgrading," see Section 31, item 10 ("Only recognize academic credentials verifiable on CHSI").

entries.title: Prioritize government-subsidized channels for training; do not jump straight into paying out-of-pocket for commercial classes
entries.cost: Costs no money, or qualifies for substantial fee reductions. The training itself takes time. The hard part is resisting the impulse to pay out-of-pocket for classes right away, and checking the subsidy catalog first.
entries.summary: From 2025 through the end of 2027, the state plans to deliver subsidized training to over 30 million person-times. Funding comes from multiple channels, including employment subsidy funds, unemployment insurance funds, and enterprise employee education funds. The more an occupation faces shortages and the higher its training costs, the higher the subsidy. Those currently employed should ask their employers first; others should review the local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau's subsidy catalog before deciding what to learn.
entries.benefit: The national scale is clear: from 2025 through the end of 2027, "conduct subsidized training for more than 30 million person-times, focusing on advanced high-tech industries, urgently needed sectors, and key employment target groups." Funding sources have been pooled into an integrated package: employment subsidy funds, unemployment insurance funds, industry development funds, East-West collaboration funds, enterprise employee education funds, and more. Subsidy levels are calibrated according to how critically needed and scarce the occupation (job type) is and its training costs, varying by job type. For enterprises, it is also required to "fully set aside and utilize employee education funds in accordance with regulations, ensuring that at least 60% is used for the education and training of frontline employees."
entries.sources: State Council Leading Group for Employment Promotion and Labor Protection (2025). Guiding Opinions on Carrying Out Large-Scale Vocational Skill Enhancement Training Actions. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202507/content_7032222.htm>
entries.notes: Specific claiming procedures and subsidy amounts are decided by each province. Entry points are the "Vocational Training Subsidy Catalog" on the local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau's official website and public practical training bases. Section 7 covered vocational training subsidies during periods of unemployment (claimable up to 3 times per person) and social insurance subsidies. Employed individuals should ask about their company's employee education funds first. Checking the subsidy catalog before choosing what to study saves vastly more money than picking a course first and hunting for subsidies afterward.

entries.title: When picking skills, prioritize "whether hands-on action and on-site judgment are required"; these types are the hardest to displace with automation
entries.cost: Costs no money. Filter the tasks you want to learn against this dimension before choosing.
entries.summary: According to US estimates, about 47% of jobs face a high risk of being taken over by computers, though subsequent task-based estimates yielded far lower percentages. There are three hurdles that machines struggle to overcome: manual dexterity, coming up with new ideas, and interpersonal interactions. Therefore, jobs requiring on-site presence, non-standard environments, and real-time judgment are much harder to displace, whereas routine roles focused primarily on processing information face the highest risk.
entries.benefit: Evaluating 702 occupations in the United States one by one regarding "how likely this work can be assigned to computers" (computerization probability assessment) revealed that about 47% of employment fell into the high-risk range. What determines the level of risk in the model are three hurdles that machines currently cannot clear, which the authors call "engineering bottlenecks." The first is perception and manipulation, including finger dexterity, manual dexterity, and operating within cramped work spaces and awkward body positions. The second is creative intelligence (the ability to generate novel ideas). The third is social intelligence (the ability to negotiate and interact with people). Consequently, tasks in non-standard environments requiring manual craftsmanship and on-the-spot judgment have consistently shown lower probabilities of substitution, which is not an accident of isolated occupations. Roles with fixed procedures and those centered on information processing carry the highest risk.
entries.sources: Frey CB, Osborne MA (2017). The future of employment: how susceptible are jobs to computerisation? Technological Forecasting and Social Change, 114, 254-280. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.techfore.2016.08.019>
entries.notes: Controversy: This study was an unpublished 2013 manuscript, and what it scored was "whether an entire occupation could be taken over by machines." Subsequent studies switched to breaking occupations down into specific tasks to estimate risk, yielding much lower proportions at high risk. Nor does it state in which year this would happen. When using it, do not fixate on the 47% figure; look at the three bottlenecks for machines that it identified. This is precisely why work like on-site installation, maintenance/inspection, and nursing care is more resistant to replacement than purely clerical work. Therefore, when "learning a skill," you should prioritize those that require going on-site and dealing with non-standard environments.

entries.title: Before learning a skill, first confirm whether it has a tier-based evaluation system and whether tiers translate into money
entries.cost: Costs no money. Looking it up once is enough.
entries.summary: The state is promoting the "New Eight-Tier Worker" system, requiring enterprises to link post wages with skill tiers, and allowing outstanding employees to be certified directly regardless of length of service or seniority. This is a policy direction; regional and enterprise-level variations are substantial. Only skills that possess national occupational standards and tier advancement pathways can realistically offer tier-based salary increases down the road; check whether these exist before learning.
entries.benefit: The state is currently promoting the "New Eight-Tier Worker" vocational skill grading system. Official documents explicitly require linking skill tiers to compensation, stating verbatim: "Strengthen a skills-oriented compensation distribution system... guide enterprises in implementing a distribution method that double-links post compensation to both post value and skill tier." Localities must "increase the intensity and batches of evaluation and employment for senior workers and above." Qualified enterprises may conduct vocational skill tier evaluations for their own employees. For outstanding employees, "conditions such as years of service, rank, and seniority may be waived, and corresponding vocational skill tiers may be directly recognized."
entries.sources: State Council Leading Group for Employment Promotion and Labor Protection (2025). Guiding Opinions on Carrying Out Large-Scale Vocational Skill Upgrading Training Actions. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202507/content_7032222.htm>; Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2021). Implementation Plan for the "Skills China Action". <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-07/06/content_5622619.htm>
entries.notes: This is a policy direction, not an already-realized wage figure; the degree of implementation varies widely across regions and enterprises. The actionable takeaway is: when choosing a skill, check whether it has corresponding national occupational standards and tier progression channels; only with an established channel can there be any talk of tier-based salary increases later on. For "skills" without tier certification and without industry entry barriers, after learning them you can only rely on finding odd jobs on your own.

entries.title: Don't mistake "online claims of high wages" for labor shortages; check local catalogs of occupations in short supply and subsidy catalogs
entries.cost: Costs no money. Check two local documents.
entries.summary: Which types of work local governments subsidize heavily for training is determined by urgency, shortage degree, and training costs; therefore, subsidy amounts reveal whether a locality actually lacks workers. Online claims like "how much a certain job pays per month" are mostly listed prices on recruitment platforms or self-reported personal anecdotes. Those you see are mostly people who made money, without factoring in working hours, commutes, occupational diseases, or peak versus off-peak seasons.
entries.benefit: The subsidy amount itself is the government's official pricing of "which types of work are experiencing labor shortages." Policy requires "improving a differentiated subsidy mechanism determined according to the degree of urgent need and shortage of the occupation (type of work), training costs, and other factors," based on which localities determine the scope of their local subsidized vocational skill training projects. Thus, the difference in subsidy amounts for the same type of work across different cities directly reflects the degree of local shortage.
entries.sources: State Council Leading Group for Employment Promotion and Labor Protection (2025). Guiding Opinions on Carrying Out Large-Scale Vocational Skill Upgrading Training Actions. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202507/content_7032222.htm>; National Bureau of Statistics (2026). Annual Average Wages of Employed Persons in Urban Units in 2025: "The annual average wage of employed persons in enterprises above designated size was 106,080 yuan; among them, middle-level and above management personnel were 210,016 yuan, professional and technical personnel were 155,491 yuan, clerical personnel and related personnel were 94,936 yuan, social production service and living service personnel were 79,857 yuan, and production, manufacturing, and related personnel were 80,739 yuan." <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202605/t20260515_1963707.html>; Employment and Training Technical Guidance Center of the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2023). Ranking of the 100 Occupations with the Greatest Labor Shortages Nationwide Where Recruitment Exceeded Job Seekers in the Fourth Quarter of 2022 (China Employment Web). <https://chinajob.mohrss.gov.cn/c/2023-01-30/367442.shtml>
entries.notes: Official wage data by occupation only breaks down into five broad job categories, without specific job types. The National Bureau of Statistics' 2025 figure indicates that the average annual wage in enterprises above designated size was approximately 106,000 yuan (exact value: 106,080 yuan). Middle management and above were approximately 210,000 yuan (exact value: 210,016 yuan), professional and technical personnel were approximately 155,000 yuan (exact value: 155,491 yuan), clerical personnel were 94,936 yuan, production and manufacturing personnel were 80,739 yuan, and social production and daily living service personnel were 79,857 yuan. The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security's "Ranking of the 100 Occupations with the Greatest Labor Shortages" can be looked up on China Employment Web; the latest release halted at the fourth quarter of 2022. This ranking is compiled from recruitment and job-seeking data across public employment service agencies in 102 cities nationwide. Online circulating figures about "how much a certain occupation makes per month" almost entirely stem from listed prices on recruitment platforms or personal self-reports. Those that reach your eyes are mostly the batch of people who made money, and none of them account for working hours, commuting, occupational illnesses, or peak and off-peak seasons. To see real demand, go to the local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau official website to check the subsidy catalog, then check the job demand rankings of public employment service institutions. Finally, visit actual construction sites, factories, and storefronts to ask employed workers.

entries.title: For the same money and time, prioritize short-cycle programs that allow immediate job entry
entries.cost: Requires paying tuition for short-term courses, which is not much money. It takes up a chunk of time. The hard part is stopping according to pre-agreed conditions when halfway through without seeing results.
entries.summary: Policies encourage "short, fast, and nimble" training that can lead to short-term employment, as well as micro-majors at vocational colleges. In picking a program, look at only one criterion: after completing it, is there a specific position you can submit a resume to. For programs that take six months or a year and still require "accumulating more experience" upon completion, the actual time spent far exceeds the sticker price. Before starting, write down your exit criteria: stop if you reach a certain point without finding work.
entries.benefit: Official policy wording aligns with this: supporting "private training institutions in carrying out market-oriented, high-quality vocational skill training programs and 'short, fast, and nimble' vocational skill training programs that can achieve short-term employment." At the same time, promoting vocational colleges to "focus on knowledge and skills urgently needed in the job market... offer micro-majors and vocational competence training courses."
entries.sources: State Council Leading Group for Employment Promotion and Labor Protection (2025). Guiding Opinions on Carrying Out Large-Scale Vocational Skill Upgrading Training Actions. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202507/content_7032222.htm>
entries.notes: The evaluation criterion boils down to just one: after completion, is there a specific post where you can submit a resume? For programs taking six months to a year that still require "gaining further experience" after graduation, the real cost far exceeds the sticker price. The exit criteria discussed in Section 4 apply equally: write down clearly before starting "at what point of not finding work will I stop."

entries.title: After studying, close the book and test yourself first; do not go back and reread
entries.cost: Costs no money, and total time does not need to increase. Convert the time originally spent on rereading into closing the book to write from memory or solve practice questions. The difficulty is that self-testing immediately exposes what you haven't retained, which feels more uncomfortable than rereading.
entries.summary: Compared with reading through a text again, closing the book and testing yourself yields better results. Adding quizzes in the classroom improves academic performance by a moderate magnitude. When ranking ten common study methods, self-testing ranks in the highest tier. After finishing a section, first write down key points from memory, then turn back to verify.
entries.benefit: A meta-analysis of 222 independent studies and 48,478 students: classroom quizzes improved student academic achievement with a moderate effect size (g = 0.499). The effect size was moderated by several conditions: what learning method the control group used, whether the quiz format aligned with the final exam, whether materials matched, and whether corrective feedback was provided. Other factors included how many times quizzes were repeated, where and when they were administered, the duration of the intervention, and what experimental design was used. Another comprehensive review evaluating ten common learning techniques one by one rated "practice testing" and "distributed practice" in the highest tier (high utility). The rationale was that they are effective across learners of different ages and ability levels, and have been validated across multiple assessment formats and authentic educational contexts.
entries.sources: Yang C, Luo L, Vadillo MA, Yu R, Shanks DR (2021). Testing (quizzing) boosts classroom learning: A systematic and meta-analytic review. Psychological Bulletin, 147(4), 399–435. <https://doi.org/10.1037/bul0000309>；Dunlosky J, Rawson KA, Marsh EJ, Nathan MJ, Willingham DT (2013). Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques: Promising Directions From Cognitive and Educational Psychology. Psychological Science in the Public Interest, 14(1), 4–58. <https://doi.org/10.1177/1529100612453266>
entries.notes: Self-testing is meant to force the retrieval of information from memory, not to assign grades. The procedure: after finishing a section, close the book, write down the key points from memory first, and then flip back to check. Those with corrective feedback work better, so after checking answers, clearly identify where you went wrong. The benefit magnitude is recorded as "large," judged according to the effect size and rating. These two sources of evidence measured academic test performance rather than hours saved, so they were not fitted against the time-saving threshold. Self-testing and item 15 (spreading the same time over multiple days) are the two highest-rated techniques in the same review; use them in tandem.

entries.title: Spread the same time across several days; do not learn it all in one sitting
entries.cost: Costs no money, and total time remains unchanged. All that changes is the scheduling: the same 3 hours split into 1 hour each across three days. The hard part is needing to start several days in advance, rather than putting it off until the final night.
entries.summary: Given the same amount of time, studying across several days yields better retention than studying in a single sitting. There is also a practical rule: however far into the future you need to retain the material, that is how long your review intervals should be stretched. The further away the test, the longer the interval, though studies do not provide a universal number of days.
entries.benefit: A meta-analysis synthesizing 184 articles, 317 experiments, and 839 evaluations of distributed practice effects. It compared two things: massed completion versus spaced learning across several sessions (the spacing effect), and short intervals versus long intervals (the lag effect). The conclusion was that the review interval and the retention interval ("how far into the future you need to retain it") jointly determine final test retention: the longer the retention interval, the longer the inter-study interval needed to achieve optimal retention. Another comprehensive review evaluating ten common learning techniques rated distributed practice in the highest tier (high utility).
entries.sources: Cepeda NJ, Pashler H, Vul E, Wixted JT, Rohrer D (2006). Distributed practice in verbal recall tasks: A review and quantitative synthesis. Psychological Bulletin, 132(3), 354–380. <https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.132.3.354>；Dunlosky J, Rawson KA, Marsh EJ, Nathan MJ, Willingham DT (2013). Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques. Psychological Science in the Public Interest, 14(1), 4–58. <https://doi.org/10.1177/1529100612453266>
entries.notes: It works best when layered with item 14 (closing the book to self-test): distribute the self-testing itself over several days. Materials in Cepeda's meta-analysis mostly consisted of word-list memorization and the like; no universal number of days was provided for optimal intervals with complex material. "The further away the test, the longer the interval" is the general rule given in the original paper, without a specific calendar schedule. The problem with cramming the night before an exam isn't that it doesn't work on the spot, but that it is forgotten rapidly.

entries.title: Don't treat highlighting, rereading, and summarizing as primary study techniques
entries.cost: Costs no money; in fact, it saves time. The difficulty is that these techniques are the most comfortable to perform and give the strongest feeling of "I am studying."
entries.summary: What students use most frequently are highlighting and rereading, yet in the ranking of ten common study methods, both fall in the lowest tier. Summarization, the keyword mnemonic, and imagery use for text also sit in the lowest tier. They are not completely useless, but the conditions under which they work are too narrow; swapping that same time into self-testing is more cost-effective.
entries.benefit: A comprehensive review evaluating ten common learning techniques assigned ratings based on "whether effects generalize across learning conditions, student characteristics, materials, and criterion tasks." Rated in the highest tier were practice testing and distributed practice. Rated in the moderate tier were elaborative interrogation, self-explanation, and interleaved practice. The five rated in the lowest tier were: summarization, highlighting (or underlining), the keyword mnemonic, imagery use for text learning, and rereading. The review explicitly stated: most students report using rereading and highlighting, but these two techniques do not consistently boost performance. The review concluded that they should be replaced with other techniques, such as substituting practice testing for rereading.
entries.sources: Dunlosky J, Rawson KA, Marsh EJ, Nathan MJ, Willingham DT (2013). Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques: Promising Directions From Cognitive and Educational Psychology. Psychological Science in the Public Interest, 14(1), 4–58. <https://doi.org/10.1177/1529100612453266>
entries.notes: Underlining is not forbidden. Underlining can be used to "mark out which points to self-test on in a moment"; the problem lies in treating underlining itself as studying. The review also made clear that being in the lowest tier does not equate to zero utility, only that the conditions under which they work are narrow and require more research. For replacement actions, see item 14 (close the book to self-test) and item 15 (spread the same time over multiple days).

entries.title: Mix several problem types together; don't do twenty of the same type in a row
entries.cost: Costs no money. Change doing practice workbooks in order of problem type to shuffling them. The difficulty is that mixed practice produces lower accuracy on the spot, feeling like regression.
entries.summary: Doing a long streak of the same type of problem goes smoothly on the spot. Shuffling several types of problems together yields better long-term results, of a moderate magnitude. However, this trick is picky about materials: visual materials like recognizing painters' styles are the most effective, math problems show a smaller effect, and memorizing vocabulary actually fares worse than blocked practice.
entries.benefit: A multilevel meta-analysis including 59 studies, 238 effect sizes, and 158 samples. The overall effect of interleaved practice relative to blocked practice was moderate (Hedges' g = 0.42). Broken down by material, painting classification was highest (g = 0.67), and other visual materials were also relatively good. The effect for mathematics tasks was smaller (g = 0.34). Overall effects for expository texts and gustatory materials were not significant. For vocabulary, blocked practice was actually better (g = −0.39). Regression analysis indicated: the more similar categories are to each other, the more dissimilar items within the same category are, and the more complex the materials, the greater the benefit of interleaving.
entries.sources: Brunmair M, Richter T (2019). Similarity matters: A meta-analysis of interleaved learning and its moderators. Psychological Bulletin, 145(11), 1029–1052. <https://doi.org/10.1037/bul0000209>
entries.notes: The review cited in item 16 (don't treat highlighting as a primary study method) rated interleaved practice in the moderate tier on the grounds that there was insufficient research at the time. Looking at the two together, content requiring "identifying which category this belongs to and which method to use" should be practiced in a mixed fashion, such as math problem types, medical cases, and legal article application. Content requiring rote memorization should be practiced in blocks, such as vocabulary words and noun definitions.

entries.title: Don't choose study methods based on "I'm a visual learner, they're an auditory learner"
entries.cost: Costs no money. It simply means no longer picking materials or courses according to this categorization, and no longer paying for learning style assessments.
entries.summary: Many people believe that everyone has their own learning style, such as visual or auditory, and that one only learns well when taught according to their style. Very few studies have rigorously tested this, almost none support it, and several have found the exact opposite. People certainly have preferences, but there is no evidence that receiving instruction matched to preferences leads to better learning; there is no need to spend money on style assessments.
entries.benefit: A commissioned review evaluating the evidence for learning styles pointed out: to prove that "teaching tailored to learning styles" is effective, one must first group students by style, then randomly assign students within each group to different instructional methods, and finally assess them using the same test. The criterion for efficacy is the emergence of a specific interaction: the instructional method most effective for one style is not the most effective for another style. The review's conclusion was: virtually no such interactions were found. Although the literature on learning styles is vast, studies employing adequate experimental designs are exceedingly rare, and the results of several of them directly contradicted the "meshing hypothesis." The authors accordingly concluded that current evidence is insufficient to justify incorporating learning style assessments into educational practice.
entries.sources: Pashler H, McDaniel M, Rohrer D, Bjork R (2008). Learning Styles: Concepts and Evidence. Psychological Science in the Public Interest, 9(3), 105–119. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1539-6053.2009.01038.x>
entries.notes: The review simultaneously explained that this does not mean every version of learning style theory has been tested and refuted; many have simply never been tested. What must be avoided are two things: spending money on style assessments, and selecting training classes based on styles. For criteria on choosing training, see item 9 (prioritize government-subsidized channels for training) and item 13 (prioritize short-cycle programs that lead directly to employment).

entries.title: Test yourself on memorized content according to how it will be used in the future; don't stop at rote recitation verbatim
entries.cost: Costs no money and takes no extra time. All that changes is the practice method: replace "reciting verbatim from start to finish" with "generating test questions for yourself based on how it will be used in the future." The hard part is having to clearly think through how these things will actually be used beforehand.
entries.summary: Closing the book to test yourself yields benefits that don't stop at the exact words memorized. Pooling 192 comparisons and over 10,000 individuals, it also works for questions with altered formats, application problems, and reasoning problems, with a small-to-moderate magnitude. However, effects are weakest in two scenarios: reversing cues and targets, and content that was only seen in the book but never tested.
entries.benefit: A meta-analysis synthesizing over 40 years of research, comprising 67 published and unpublished articles, 122 experiments, 192 transfer effect sizes, and a total of 10,382 participants. Compared to the "restudy without testing" control, learning brought about by practice testing indeed transferred to other contexts, with an effect size of d = 0.40 (95% CI 0.31 to 0.50). The situations showing the strongest transfer were: testing in an altered question format, testing application and reasoning problems, medical diagnostic problems, and testing with synonym cue words. The situations with the weakest transfer were: reversing stimulus and response, material seen during initial study but never tested, and worked-example problems. Three moderating factors strongly influenced whether positive transfer appeared: whether the response formats during practice and testing were aligned, whether retrieval practice included detailed feedback, and whether initial tests were answered correctly. The authors also adjusted for publication bias using two methods. The effect sizes of the moderators were minimally affected, but intercept estimates were substantially lowered: when none of the above conditions were met, positive transfer was often not observed.
entries.sources: Pan SC, Rickard TC (2018). Transfer of test-enhanced learning: meta-analytic review and synthesis. Psychological Bulletin, 144(7), 710-756. <https://doi.org/10.1037/bul0000151>
entries.notes: The colloquial word "memorize" conflates two distinct things: reviewing material again (rereading, highlighting), and closing the book to actively recall. The former was rated lowest in that review ranking ten study techniques; to see the ratings themselves, see item 16 (don't treat highlighting, rereading, and summarizing as primary study techniques). What should be done is the latter: closing the book to actively recall, detailed in item 14 (close the book to self-test), and spacing it across several days, see item 15 (spread across several days). The method is to first think through how it will be used in the future: will you need to select it on an exam sheet, or judge it on site? Then frame questions to test yourself according to that format. Testing in reverse is also worth doing, because in this meta-analysis transfer in the reversed direction was weakest, so both directions must be practiced.

entries.title: For professional title evaluation, first clarify your series and grade, then find application channels based on your employer's organizational nature
entries.cost: Costs no money. Check your province's application announcement for the current year once, which takes about half an hour.
entries.summary: Nationwide, professional titles are divided into 27 series, with each series categorized into junior, intermediate, and senior grades. Generally, one must apply tier by tier. Those working at an employer are reviewed and publicly displayed by the employer before being submitted upward. Those in private enterprises can apply via professional title application service points, human resources intermediary agencies, or industry associations. Freelancers apply for reviews organized by local human resources and social security departments.
entries.benefit: A total of 27 professional title series are established nationwide, such as economics, engineering, health, and publishing. Professional titles are divided into three levels: senior, intermediate, and junior. Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security Decree No. 40 applies to enterprises, public institutions, social organizations, individual economic organizations, and also freelancers. Applicants generally must apply step by step. Your employer must review the materials and conduct an internal public notice within the organization for no less than 5 working days. For private enterprise employees and freelancers, personnel agency institutions and similar bodies may review, publicly display, and recommend on your behalf. Localities must set up professional title application service acceptance points in science and technology parks, high-tech zones, and other areas, or accept applications through talent intermediary agencies, industry associations, chambers of commerce, and academic societies. Eligible freelancers participate in evaluations organized by local human resources and social security departments based on territorial jurisdiction. For materials that can be verified online, you shall not be required to provide separate proof. If application materials are incomplete, the reviewing party must inform you of all missing items at one time. Employees of private enterprises generally apply at the location of their labor relations. Those dispatched out of town for full continuous service of at least one year may apply at the location of dispatch. Retired personnel cannot apply. Staff of public institutions subject to disciplinary sanctions of demerit or above cannot apply during the sanction period (nationwide).
entries.sources: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security Order No. 40 (2019). Interim Provisions on the Administration of Professional Title Evaluation. <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2019/content_5437137.htm>: Article 2, Article 13, Article 14, Article 15, Article 16, Article 17, Article 18; General Office of the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2020). Circular on Further Improving Professional Title Work in Private Enterprises. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-03/03/content_5486340.htm>: "Establish professional title application receiving service stations in startup incubation bases, high-tech development zones, science and technology parks, and other places where professional and technical talents are concentrated, or accept professional title applications from professional and technical talents in private enterprises through social organizations such as talent intermediary service agencies, federations of industry and commerce, industry associations and chambers of commerce, and academic societies"; "Where professional and technical personnel of private enterprises are stationed to work in another locality for more than one consecutive year, they may apply for professional title evaluation in the stationed locality in accordance with relevant regulations"; Xinhua News Agency (2024). Professional Title Evaluation Enters Peak Season: How to Check Information? What Are the New Changes? <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202410/content_6978917.htm>: "Our country has established a total of 27 professional title series, including economics, engineering, health, and publishing"; "Eligible freelancers may apply to participate in the professional title evaluation organized by the local human resources and social security department based on the territorial principle"; General Office of the CPC Central Committee and General Office of the State Council (2016). Opinions on Deepening the Reform of the Professional Title System. <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2017/content_5163445.htm>: "Academic papers shall not be used as a restrictive condition for evaluating applied talents"; "No unified requirements shall be made for foreign language and computer application proficiency tests for professional titles"; "Eligible highly skilled personnel may participate in the evaluation of professional titles for professional and technical personnel in the engineering series"; "Civil servants shall not participate in the evaluation of professional titles for professional and technical personnel".
entries.notes: There is no unified nationwide checklist for what materials need to be prepared. Each series and each province issues an application notice each year, which specifies the checklist of materials, the application timeline, and the performance criteria. Therefore, the first step is to locate that year's notice on the official website of your provincial Department of Human Resources and Social Security. Academic papers are no longer universally mandatory: the 2016 reform opinions require that papers must not be treated as a hard threshold for applied talents, nor are there unified requirements for foreign language and computer proficiency examinations for professional titles. Skilled workers also have a pathway: eligible highly skilled talents can participate in professional title evaluations in the engineering series. Civil servants cannot participate in professional title evaluations.

entries.title: Junior and intermediate professional titles such as accounting are obtained through unified national examinations; check your academic credentials and years of work experience first before registering
entries.cost: Registration fees are paid according to each province's standards. Exam preparation will take several months of spare time.
entries.summary: For some series, junior and intermediate professional titles are obtained through examinations; passing the exam is sufficient, and no separate evaluation is conducted. Accounting is one such case: Assistant Accountant requires a high school diploma or above, while Accountant requires 4 full years of accounting work with a bachelor's degree, or 5 full years with an associate degree. Those who have already obtained certain occupational qualifications may also be directly recognized as holding the corresponding professional title.
entries.benefit: The 2016 reform opinions stipulate that for professions where junior and intermediate professional titles are subject to unified national examinations, corresponding evaluations or accreditations will no longer be conducted. In fields where professional titles and occupational qualifications are closely related, obtaining an occupational qualification allows one to be recognized as possessing the corresponding professional title, and it can also serve as a prerequisite for applying for the next higher level. Take accounting as an example. Assistant Accountant and Accountant are administered via unified national examinations. Senior Accountant combines examinations with evaluation, while Professor-level Senior Accountant generally uses evaluation only. Eligibility requirements are as follows. Assistant Accountant: high school graduate or above, including secondary specialized schools, vocational high schools, and technical schools. Accountant: doctoral degree; or master's degree with 1 full year of accounting work; or second bachelor's degree or completion of a postgraduate diploma program with 2 full years of work; or bachelor's degree with 4 full years of work; or associate degree with 5 full years of work. Those holding a professional master's or doctoral degree in accounting can be exempt from taking "Financial Management" when sitting for the Accountant exam (Nationwide)
entries.sources: General Office of the CPC Central Committee and General Office of the State Council (2016). Opinions on Deepening the Reform of the Professional Title System. <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2017/content_5163445.htm>: "When professional and technical personnel obtain an occupational qualification, they can be recognized as possessing the professional title of the corresponding series and tier, which may also serve as a prerequisite for applying for a professional title at the next higher level. For specialties where junior and intermediate professional titles are subject to unified national examinations, corresponding professional title evaluations or accreditations shall no longer be conducted."; Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and Ministry of Finance (2019). Guiding Opinions on Deepening the Reform of the Professional Title System for Accounting Personnel. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2019-09/27/content_5433803.htm>: "Assistant Accountants and Accountants shall implement the unified national accounting professional and technical qualification examination"; "Senior Accountants shall adopt a combination of examination and evaluation, while Professor-level Senior Accountants shall generally adopt the evaluation method"; "Civil servants who meet the requirements may take the accounting professional and technical qualification examination, but must not participate in the professional title evaluation for accounting personnel"; Ministry of Finance et al. (2024). Circular on Performing Relevant Work on Bridging Professional Degrees in Accounting with Accounting Professional and Technical Qualifications. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202405/content_6952602.htm>
entries.notes: To find out whether your series uses exams, evaluation, or a combination of exam and evaluation, consult the "Guiding Opinions on Deepening the Reform of the XX Professional Title System" for that specific series. These have been issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security along with respective industry governing authorities for each series, and can be retrieved from the State Council Policy Document Repository on Gov.cn. Registration deadlines and subjects for examinations are subject to that year's examination announcement. Civil servants can take the accounting examination, but cannot participate in accounting professional title evaluations.

entries.title: Do not hire agencies to evaluate on your behalf, do not buy ghostwritten papers, and do not falsify materials: once substantiated, titles are revoked and entered into integrity archives for 3 years
entries.cost: Costs 0 yuan. The hard part is resisting advertisements promising "guaranteed passes with payment."
entries.summary: Professional titles obtained through forged materials, ghostwritten papers, or plagiarized achievements will be revoked once verified. The dishonesty record lasts for 3 years and enters the national credit platform. If the letter of commitment signed during application contains falsehoods, one cannot apply again within 3 years. Human resources and social security authorities also specifically investigate and penalize false advertising, fake evaluations, and counterfeit certificates by intermediary agencies.
entries.benefit: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security Order No. 40 stipulates that if anyone obtains a professional title by submitting false materials, plagiarizing others' works and academic achievements, or using other improper means, the professional title shall be revoked. At the same time, this will be recorded in the professional title evaluation integrity archive database, integrated into the National Credit Information Sharing Platform, with a recording period of 3 years. The 2024 supervisory measures explicitly singled out several types of applicant violations: false commitments and falsified information, falsifying or ghostwriting academic papers, falsifying performance achievements, and pulling strings or soliciting favors. A personal commitment letter must be signed upon application; if commitments are untruthful, one may not apply for 3 years. Human resources and social security departments, in conjunction with public security, cyberspace administration, and market regulation authorities, crack down on intermediary agencies' fake websites, false advertising, contract traps, counterfeit evaluations, and forged certificates. Where circumstances are serious and suspected of constituting a crime, the case will be transferred to relevant authorities for processing (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security Order No. 40 (2019). Interim Provisions on the Administration of Professional Title Evaluation. <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2019/content_5437137.htm>: Article 39; Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2024). Interim Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Professional Title Evaluation. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202408/content_6969436.htm>: Article 5, Article 15, Article 17, Article 27; General Office of the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2022). Circular on Further Doing a Good Job in Professional Title Evaluation Work. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-12/24/content_5733407.htm>: "Evaluation results of professional title evaluation committees that have not completed filing will not be included in the National Professional Title Evaluation Information Query and Verification System"; Xinhua News Agency (2024). Professional Title Evaluation Enters Peak Season: How to Check Information? What Are the New Changes? <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202410/content_6978917.htm>: "Everyone can log in through various channels such as the www.12333.gov.cn website, the 12333 mobile client, the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security portal website, and the 'Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security' WeChat official account"; Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate (2019). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases Such as Organizing Cheating in Examinations (Fa Shi [2019] No. 13, Article 1). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/xwfbh/wsfbh/201909/t20190903_430901.shtml>: "Professional technical qualification examinations such as the National Unified Legal Professional Qualification Examination, the National Teacher Qualification Examination, the National Unified CPA Examination, and the Accounting Professional Technical Qualification Examination..."
entries.notes: There is a way to distinguish genuine from fake: professional titles obtained through formal evaluations can be found on the National Professional Title Evaluation Information Query Platform. Access points are the 12333 website, the 12333 mobile client, and the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security official website. Titles evaluated by committees that have not completed registration cannot be retrieved in this system. Therefore, any promises of "guaranteed pass," "no need to participate in person," or "usable even if not verifiable in the certificate system" can basically be judged as problematic. The beneficiary is primarily oneself; the magnitude of benefit is evaluated on the basis of "avoiding revocation of professional title and a 3-year dishonesty record." The accounting professional and technical qualification examination is included in the list of "national examinations stipulated by law" specified in judicial interpretations; hiring substitutes, selling answers, or organizing cheating in such examinations constitutes a crime. Simply buying answers and peeking at them yourself is not listed as a crime by statutory provisions, and is handled according to examination discipline regulations; see Section 9, Item 29 (do not hire substitutes).

entries.title: Obtaining a professional title does not equal a pay raise: first clarify whether your employer evaluates and appoints according to post ratios, or whether evaluation does not guarantee appointment
entries.cost: Costs 0 yuan. Asking your organization's HR department once is sufficient.
entries.summary: Professional titles serve as a basis for hiring, performance appraisal, and promotion, but obtaining a title and getting hired into a position are two different matters. Public institutions practicing post management generally evaluate within post ratios. Organizations that do not practice post management can separate evaluation from appointment; earning the title does not guarantee that the employer will grant the corresponding post or salary. After changing employers or locations, professional titles may need to be re-evaluated or reaffirmed.
entries.benefit: Article 2 of Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security Order No. 40: Evaluation results of professional titles are an important basis for hiring, evaluating, and promoting professional and technical personnel. The 2016 reform opinions stipulate that public institutions fully implementing post management shall generally carry out professional title evaluations within the structural ratios of positions. Organizations not implementing post management, as well as highly versatile series and emerging professions, may adopt a separation of evaluation and appointment. When professional and technical personnel move across regions or organizations, their professional titles shall be re-evaluated or reaffirmed according to administrative authority, unless otherwise provided by the state (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security Order No. 40 (2019). Interim Provisions on the Administration of Professional Title Evaluation. <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2019/content_5437137.htm>: Article 2, Article 29; General Office of the CPC Central Committee and General Office of the State Council (2016). Opinions on Deepening the Reform of the Professional Title System. <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2017/content_5163445.htm>: "For public institutions that have fully implemented post management and where the academic and technical levels of professional and technical talents are closely related to post responsibilities, professional title evaluations should generally be conducted within the post structural ratio. For organizations that do not implement post management, as well as professional title series and emerging occupations with strong general versatility that are widely distributed across various social organizations, the method of separating evaluation from appointment may be adopted."
entries.notes: The evidence grade is rated B because documents only describe how evaluation and appointment interface, without giving a uniform nationwide figure for "how much pay raises upon obtaining a title." What you can act on: in public institutions and state-owned enterprises, first ask the human resources department about post vacancies and appointment rules in your organization. In private enterprises, first ask the employer whether this credential is recognized and whether it comes with a raise.

entries.title: Should you continue on to a master's degree after finishing a bachelor's: first calculate tuition fees and the 2–3 years of forgone wages, then look at whether your specific major earns more; those already working can pursue a part-time master's, which holds the same legal validity as full-time
entries.cost: Costs 0 yuan. Checking the admissions brochure and tuition standards once, then calculating based on current job opportunities, takes about one to two hours.
entries.summary: Pursuing a master's requires paying tuition and losing two to three years of wages, the latter usually being the larger component. A British study, after controlling for differences in family background and undergraduate grades, found that by age 35, women with a master's earned only about 2% more, while men actually earned about 2% less, with significant variations across majors. Those already working can pursue a part-time master's degree; the certificate has the same validity as a full-time one, but does not receive the national stipend.
entries.benefit: First look at the costs. National opinions in 2013 stipulate that tuition for full-time academic master's degrees should, in principle, not exceed 8,000 yuan per student per year. Full-time professional master's degrees follow previous charging policies and are not restricted by this cap, often costing much more. Full-time graduate students within the state enrollment plan can receive national graduate stipends, which are not less than 6,000 yuan per year for master's students, with specific rates set locally. Next look at the returns. A 2020 study published by the UK Department for Education tracked individuals who completed bachelor's degrees between the mid-1990s and mid-2000s using national education and tax records. The study controlled for family background and undergraduate grade differences, observing earnings at age 35. The original text states: "we estimate returns of 2% (women) and -2% (men) for masters": women with a master's earned about 2% more than those with only a bachelor's, while men earned about 2% less. Variation across majors was substantial. Women with master's degrees in law, economics, and management earned roughly 20% more, while those in arts, English, and philosophy earned over 10% less. For men, master's returns in most majors were significantly negative, though law, economics, management, and engineering remained distinctly positive. Those already employed can sit for part-time master's examinations to study while working. A 2016 Ministry of Education circular stipulates that part-time and full-time students take the same exam and are educated to the same standards. Both diploma and degree certificates "enjoy equal legal status and the same validity," with the graduation certificate indicating the mode of study. National stipends are only granted to full-time graduate students within the enrollment plan, and part-time students are not eligible. In 2019, five government departments including the Ministry of Education issued a circular requiring that civil service recruitment as well as public institution and state-owned enterprise public hiring provide equal employment opportunities to graduate students with different modes of study. Such recruitment must not set application criteria unrelated to post requirements. The Ministry of Education's 2021 graduate employment notice stated explicitly that recruitment notices from Party and government organs, public institutions, and state-owned enterprises must not treat the study mode as a restrictive condition. The 2022 notice reiterated that no campus recruitment events of any type may impose such restrictions
entries.sources: Ministry of Finance, National Development and Reform Commission, Ministry of Education (2013). Opinions on Improving the Input Mechanism for Graduate Education (Cai Jiao [2013] No. 19). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2013/content_2404719.htm>: "In principle, at the present stage, tuition standards for full-time academic graduate students shall not exceed 8,000 yuan per student per year for master's students, and 10,000 yuan per student per year for doctoral students. Full-time professional degree graduate students and graduate students currently subject to fee policies implemented according to regulations shall temporarily follow the original fee policies"; "The funding standard for doctoral students shall not be less than 10,000 yuan per student per year, and for master's students not less than 6,000 yuan per student per year"; Britton J, Buscha F, Dickson M, van der Erve L, Vignoles A, Walker I, Waltmann B, Zhu Y (2020). The earnings returns to postgraduate degrees in the UK. Department for Education. <https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/5f609e478fa8f5106d1563cc/PG_LEO_report_FINAL.pdf>; General Office of the Ministry of Education (2016). Circular on Coordinating the Administration of Full-Time and Part-Time Graduate Students (Jiao Yan Ting [2016] No. 2). <http://www.moe.gov.cn/srcsite/A22/moe_826/201609/t20160914_281117.html>: "Issue corresponding graduation certificates indicating the mode of study in accordance with relevant national regulations"; "Full-time and part-time graduate students implement the same examination and enrollment policies and training standards, and their academic degree certificates have equal legal status and the same validity"; Cai Jiao [2013] No. 19 ibid.: "The coverage of the national graduate student grant covers all full-time graduate students within the national graduate admissions plan"; General Office of the Ministry of Education and four other departments (2019). Circular on Further Doing a Good Job in the Employment of Part-Time Graduate Students (Jiao Yan Ting Han [2019] No. 1). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-02/05/content_5490220.htm>: "Civil service recruitment at all levels, as well as open recruitment by public institutions and state-owned enterprises, shall formulate recruitment requirements reasonably according to job needs, provide equal employment opportunities for graduate students of different forms of education, and must not set application qualifications unrelated to job requirements"; Ministry of Education (2020). Circular on Doing a Good Job in the Employment and Entrepreneurship of Graduates of Ordinary Higher Education Institutions Nationwide in 2021 (Jiao Xue [2020] No. 5). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-12/01/content_5566303.htm>: "In recruitment announcements and practical operations, graduating institutions, overseas study experience, and learning modes (full-time and part-time) shall not be used as restrictive conditions"; Ministry of Education (2021).
