Circular on Doing a Good Job in the Employment and Entrepreneurship of Graduates of Ordinary Higher Education Institutions Nationwide in 2022 (Jiao Xue [2021] No. 5). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-11/21/content_5652326.htm>: "In all types of campus recruitment activities, no discriminatory terms that violate state regulations shall be established, and graduating institutions, learning modes (full-time and part-time), etc. shall not be used as restrictive conditions"; Ministry of Education (2024). Provisions on the Administration of National Postgraduate Admissions in 2025 (Jiao Xue [2024] No. 4) Article 77. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202410/content_6978684.htm>: "The admissions regulations shall publish, in accordance with relevant provisions, the application conditions, learning modes, length of schooling, tuition standards, reward and assistance measures, graduation employment, accommodation conditions, and training campuses for master's degree students in each specialty of the unit. In principle, part-time master's students recruited by admissions units shall be in-service directed employment personnel"
entries.notes: Disputes. Previous UK studies had consistently estimated positive returns for master's degrees; the authors of this study argue that their data is more granular and controlled more cleanly. The authors also concede that differences such as motivation and career preferences cannot be fully controlled for. The data only runs up to age 35 and uses individuals who graduated two to three decades ago; furthermore, no domestic figures controlling for personal differences in the same way have been found, so this can only serve as directional reference. The evidence grade is therefore set at B. The accounting method is the same as Item 6 of this section (studying versus working): offset the two to three years of forgone wages against the incremental higher earnings in each subsequent year. Some job recruitment announcements explicitly mandate a master's degree, such as colleges and universities, research institutes, and certain state-owned enterprises; in such cases, the degree threshold itself constitutes a return and must be calculated separately. The several documents on part-time degrees are ministerial departmental notices that do not specify penalty provisions or indicate to whom one can complain if violations occur. They govern how recruitment announcements are drafted, but cannot dictate who the employer ultimately chooses. Campus recruitment has explicit restrictions, but no explicit provisions were found governing study modes in private enterprises' social recruitment. The 2025 admissions management regulations specify that, in principle, part-time programs only enroll employed personnel who will return to their original employers upon graduation. Tuition, financial aid, and accommodation are determined by institutions and published in their admissions brochures. Regarding household registration (hukou) and personnel dossiers, national documents reviewed for this book contain no uniform rules; read the admissions brochure carefully and consult the school prior to applying.

entries.title: Should you continue on to a doctorate after finishing a master's: only pursue it if your target post explicitly requires a PhD, and factor in the psychological burden before enrolling
entries.cost: Costs 0 yuan. Check the educational requirements in the job announcements of your target organizations once, and have a chat with two or three current doctoral students.
entries.summary: In the same UK study, after controlling for differences in family background and undergraduate academic performance, at age 35, women with a PhD earned about 8% more than those with only an undergraduate degree, whereas men earned about 9% less. The psychological burden of pursuing a PhD is also heavy: across doctoral students in various countries, about one in four has noticeable depressive symptoms, and about one in six has noticeable anxiety symptoms. Therefore, first check whether your target jobs strictly require a PhD before deciding whether to pursue one.
entries.benefit: The 2020 UK Department for Education study cited in Item 24 of this section (Pursuing a Master's Degree) also calculated figures for doctorates. The original text states "8% (women) and -9% (men) for PhDs": after controlling for differences in family background and undergraduate performance, at age 35, women with a PhD earned about 8% more than those with only an undergraduate degree, while men earned about 9% less. The study also found that a doctorate reduced the likelihood of unemployment and of having an annual income below £30,000, but also reduced the likelihood of earning an annual income exceeding £40,000. Returns vary greatly across different disciplines; returns on a PhD in mathematics are particularly low, while a PhD in psychology is among the highest-yielding. For the psychological burden during doctoral study, see a 2021 meta-analysis. Across 16 studies and 23,469 doctoral students, a pooled total of approximately 24% (95% CI 18%–31%, confidence interval) had noticeable depressive symptoms. Across 9 studies and 15,626 doctoral students, about 17% (12%–23%) had noticeable anxiety symptoms. Differences between studies were substantial (I² around 98%). Domestic costs follow the 2013 Opinions: tuition fees for full-time academic doctoral degrees in principle do not exceed 10,000 yuan per year, and the national graduate financial assistance grant is not less than 10,000 yuan per year.
entries.sources: Britton J, Buscha F, Dickson M, van der Erve L, Vignoles A, Walker I, Waltmann B, Zhu Y (2020). The earnings returns to postgraduate degrees in the UK. Department for Education. <https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/5f609e478fa8f5106d1563cc/PG_LEO_report_FINAL.pdf>; Satinsky EN, Kimura T, Kiang MV, et al. (2021). Systematic review and meta-analysis of depression, anxiety, and suicidal ideation among Ph.D. students. Scientific Reports, 11, 14370. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-021-93687-7>; Liu H, Gao Y, Tuerxun N, Cabirou L (2026). More than Depression: Doctoral Students' Mental Health in China: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Behavioral Sciences, 16, 1355. <https://doi.org/10.3390/bs16081355>; Ministry of Finance, National Development and Reform Commission, Ministry of Education (2013). Opinions on Improving the Investment Mechanism for Postgraduate Education (Cai Jiao [2013] No. 19). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2013/content_2404719.htm>
entries.notes: Controversies: That set of depression and anxiety figures merely pools the proportions from surveys across various countries without comparing them to peers of the same age, and the scales used also differed. Therefore, it indicates that such symptoms are common among doctoral students, but cannot demonstrate that they are caused by pursuing a PhD. A synthesis of domestic Chinese studies found that the psychological symptoms of doctoral students and master's students differ little, but both are higher than national norms and youth norms. The limitations of the income figures are the same as in Item 24 of this section (Pursuing a Master's Degree), and they can only serve as directional references. Recruitment announcements for university faculty positions, research institutes, and certain R&D posts often clearly state that a PhD is required; if you want to take this path, first browse through the announcements of target institutions from recent years. If low mood persists for more than two weeks during your studies, first do the few things listed in Section 3, Item 18 (Things to Do First When Feeling Depressed). If you have suicidal thoughts, call 12356; see Section 1, Item 25 (Call 12356 When Depressed or Having Suicidal Thoughts).

chapters.title: Seeking Medical Care: How to Spend Less Money and Take Fewer Detours
chapters.intro:
Metric: Money and time. This section covers the path of seeking medical care itself: which hospital to go to first, how to be referred upward, and where you can spend less money. In addition, it covers how to queue in emergency departments, and what disability/medical appraisals to complete and certificates to obtain after severe injuries are treated. For what benefits you can claim, see Section 7. For how to manage chronic diseases over the long term, see Section 16. For what to do first at the scene of an acute medical emergency, see Section 13.

This section is primarily based on the "Several Measures on Accelerating the Construction of a Tiered Healthcare System" issued by the General Office of the State Council in April 2026. Tiered healthcare means determining which tier of hospital to visit first based on the severity of the illness. This document directly ties "going to primary care facilities" to "saving money." However, implementation progress varies across regions; the main text describes the rules at the national level. Specifically for your insurance pool area, the statements of your local healthcare security and health departments shall prevail. An insurance pool area is the locality where your medical insurance is registered, usually a municipality.

entries.title: See Community Clinics First for Common Diseases; When Referred Upward Tier-by-Tier Through Primary Care, the Inpatient Deductible Counts Continuously
entries.cost: Costs no money. Requires going to the community clinic first. The difficulty lies in resisting the urge to directly register for an expert appointment.
entries.summary: Go to the community clinic first, and then be referred by the community clinic to a large hospital for hospitalization; the portion paid out of pocket first can be counted continuously without having to pay it all over again. Specific calculation methods are determined locally; Sichuan only charges the difference between the deductibles of the two facilities. For patients transferred back from large hospitals to community clinics for continued inpatient stays, it is also not recalculated within the same disease episode.
entries.benefit: For insured patients who are referred upward tier-by-tier through primary-level medical and healthcare institutions, inpatient deductibles at higher-level hospitals can be calculated continuously. The deductible is the portion paid out of pocket first for each hospitalization before medical insurance begins reimbursement. The State Council General Office document did not specify how continuous calculation is computed in practice, leaving it to local authorities to determine. Sichuan's practice is to only make up the difference between the deductibles of the two hospitals: if the deductible at the county traditional Chinese medicine hospital is 600 yuan and the patient is transferred to the county people's hospital (deductible of 800 yuan), only an additional 200 yuan needs to be topped up. For hospitalized patients transferred downward from higher-level hospitals back to primary-level institutions, no separate deductible is set within the same disease cycle.
entries.sources: General Office of the State Council (2026). Several Measures on Accelerating the Construction of a Tiered Healthcare System. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202604/content_7065031.htm>: "For insured patients referred tier-by-tier through primary-level medical and healthcare institutions within the insurance pool area, the inpatient deductible at higher-level hospitals may be calculated continuously; for hospitalized patients transferred downward from higher-level hospitals to primary-level medical and healthcare institutions, no separate inpatient deductible shall be established within the same disease cycle."; Sichuan Provincial Healthcare Security Administration (2025). Reply Letter on the Handling of Proposal No. 14041026 of the Fourth Session of the 14th Provincial People's Congress. <https://ylbzj.sc.gov.cn/scsybj/nc010414/2025/3/19/fea6f0a5f8ba416abf7ed17541afdc7a.shtml>: "The deductible for Yilong County People's Hospital is 800 yuan, and the deductible for Yilong County Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine is 600 yuan. When transferring from Yilong County Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine to Yilong County People's Hospital, only the difference of 200 yuan needs to be topped up for the deductible."
entries.notes: Referral rules are formulated separately by each province, city, and medical consortium; consult your community clinic before going. For chronic diseases in a stable phase, do not go to large hospitals to get prescription refills anymore, because such general outpatient clinics at large hospitals will be phased down gradually. Community clinics can prescribe up to 12 weeks of medication at one time; see Section 16, Item 5 (Community Clinics Prescribing Up to 12 Weeks of Medication at Once).

entries.title: Within the Same Insurance Pool Area (Medical Insurance Registration Locality), Lower-Tier Facilities Offer Higher Reimbursement Rates, with Gaps Around 10 Percentage Points
entries.cost: Costs no money. The difficulty lies in resisting the urge to rush to large hospitals.
entries.summary: According to the requirements of the document, for the same inpatient bill, the lower the hospital's tier, the higher the reimbursement rate. Localities are required to establish tiered differentials, with a gap of around ten percentage points for each step upward. For example, on a 10,000-yuan inpatient bill, if reimbursement drops from 80% to 70%, your out-of-pocket payment increases from 2,000 yuan to 3,000 yuan. Newly added medical insurance funds are also tilted toward primary care.
entries.benefit: The document requires localities to establish differentials in inpatient reimbursement levels across different tiers of medical institutions, in principle maintaining a gap of around 10 percentage points from tier to tier. Based on this gap, for the exact same inpatient bill, for each tier higher you move up in hospital level, the extra out-of-pocket amount is roughly 10% of these reimbursable expenses. For example, on 10,000 yuan of reimbursable inpatient expenses, if the reimbursement rate drops from 80% to 70%, out-of-pocket payment increases from 2,000 yuan to 3,000 yuan. The extra 1,000 yuan paid out of pocket accounts for 10% of total expenses, but represents a 50% increase compared to what was originally paid out of pocket. Actual proportions vary across localities, and deductibles and reimbursement caps will also alter the difference; this is merely an illustrative calculation based on the document's 10 percentage points. Annual newly added medical insurance funds are also tilted toward primary-level institutions.
entries.sources: General Office of the State Council (2026). Several Measures on Accelerating the Construction of a Tiered Healthcare System. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202604/content_7065031.htm>: "Appropriately establish differentials in inpatient reimbursement levels for insured personnel across medical and health institutions of different tiers according to local conditions; in principle, inpatient reimbursement rates across medical and health institutions within the insurance pool area shall maintain a tier-by-tier gap of around 10 percentage points." "Where conditions permit, localities may discretionarily establish differentials in outpatient reimbursement levels for insured personnel across medical and health institutions of different tiers according to tiered diagnosis and treatment orientations."
entries.notes: For the same inpatient bill, the difference in out-of-pocket expenses between a primary care facility and a tertiary hospital could be several thousand yuan. For illnesses that can be handled at the primary level, do not rush upward; this does not mean every single illness must be treated at a community clinic.

entries.title: If You Need to Go to a Large Hospital, Go Through Primary Care Referrals or the Hospital's Referral Center; Do Not Use Scalpers
entries.cost: Costs no money. Requires completing one additional referral procedure.
entries.summary: Leading large hospitals within a medical consortium must reserve a portion of appointment slots and beds specifically for people referred from primary care facilities. Hospitals must also set up referral centers or designate a dedicated department specifically managing referrals, achieving full coverage by 2027. Being unable to book an appointment does not mean there is no way in; there is no need to turn to ticket scalpers.
entries.benefit: Lead hospitals of close-knit medical consortiums must reserve a certain proportion of appointment quotas and beds for primary-level institutions and promptly admit and treat patients referred from the primary level. A close-knit medical consortium is a group of institutions where several hospitals and community health institutions are bound together in collaboration. Therefore, being referred upward from the community clinic grants dedicated appointments and beds, avoiding the scramble with crowds fighting for appointments in the lobby. Medical institutions must establish referral centers or designate dedicated departments, achieving full coverage by 2027.
entries.sources: General Office of the State Council (2026). Several Measures on Accelerating the Construction of a Tiered Healthcare System. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202604/content_7065031.htm>: "Lead hospitals must reserve a certain proportion of appointment quotas and beds for primary-level medical and health institutions, and promptly admit and treat patients referred from the primary level." "Medical institutions shall strengthen unified management of referral services, establishing referral centers or designating dedicated departments to undertake patient referral service work, achieving full coverage by 2027."
entries.notes: Reserved appointment quotas are set aside specifically for referred patients; if you cannot secure a regular booking, you can use the referral channel. If you cannot find the referral center, call the hospital's customer service number to inquire.

entries.title: Inquire Locally Before Seeking Out-of-Province Cross-Regional Medical Care; Necessity In Principle Requires Evaluation by an Associate Chief Physician or Above
entries.cost: Costs no money. Ask one extra question before departing.
entries.summary: Whether it is necessary to go elsewhere for medical treatment is, in principle, evaluated by doctors with the title of associate chief physician or above at secondary or tertiary hospitals. Reimbursement rates for temporary travel to seek medical care differ from those at hospitals of the same tier in your insurance pool locality, depending on local regulations. Asking locally before departure is far better than discovering it cannot be reimbursed after you have already arrived elsewhere.
entries.benefit: The necessity of cross-pool-area and cross-provincial medical care is, in principle, evaluated by personnel with professional titles of associate chief physician and above at secondary and tertiary hospitals. Crossing pool areas means stepping outside your medical insurance registration locality. Whether going out of town is necessary in principle requires an assessment from a doctor of sufficient rank. Reimbursement levels for personnel temporarily traveling across provinces for medical care maintain a reasonable difference compared to institutions of the same tier in the insurance pool locality. For the same illness treated elsewhere, the money reimbursed will be a notch lower than at home.
entries.sources: General Office of the State Council (2026). Several Measures on Accelerating the Construction of a Tiered Healthcare System. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202604/content_7065031.htm>: "In principle, personnel with professional titles of associate chief physician and above at secondary and tertiary hospitals shall evaluate the necessity of patients seeking medical care across insurance pool areas and across provinces." "Further strengthen the direct settlement management and services for cross-regional medical care; reimbursement levels for personnel temporarily traveling across provinces for medical care shall maintain a reasonable difference from the reimbursement levels of medical institutions of the same tier in the insurance registration locality."
entries.notes: "Temporary travel for medical treatment" and "long-term residence in another locality" are two distinct filing categories with different reimbursement levels. For how to file and which categories of illnesses support direct settlement, see Section 16. Do not rush off to another city first before thinking about reimbursement issues.

entries.title: Keep Your Own Copy of Medical Records, Examination Reports, and Imaging After Every Medical Visit
entries.cost: Costs no money. Hospitals may charge a production cost fee according to regulations for copying, and fee standards must be made public. The difficulty lies in remembering to get copies after each visit.
entries.summary: Accessing and copying your own medical records is a right granted to you by law. Outpatient records, inpatient records, lab reports, imaging, surgery and anesthesia records, pathology materials, and billing statements can all be copied. Hospitals must designate dedicated departments or personnel to handle requests and may only charge production cost fees. Switching hospitals, getting a second opinion from another doctor, filing commercial insurance claims, or handling real disputes all rely on this pile of materials.
entries.benefit: Regulations explicitly list consulting and copying medical records as patient rights. The scope covers outpatient medical records, inpatient records, lab sheets, medical imaging data, surgery and anesthesia records, pathology data, medical expenses, and all other materials. Switching hospitals, finding a second doctor for a review, claiming commercial insurance, or handling real disputes all depend on these.
entries.sources: State Council (2018). Regulations on the Prevention and Handling of Medical Disputes (State Council Decree No. 701), Article 16: "Patients have the right to consult and duplicate their outpatient medical records, inpatient logs, temperature charts, doctor order sheets, laboratory test sheets (inspection reports), medical imaging examination materials, special examination consent forms, surgery consent forms, surgery and anesthesia records, pathology data, nursing records, medical expenses, and all other materials categorized as medical records under regulations of the State Council health administrative department." "Where a patient requests duplication of medical record materials, the medical institution shall provide duplication services and affix a certification stamp on the duplicated medical record materials... A production cost fee may be charged, and fee schedules shall be made public." "Where a patient dies, their close relatives may consult and duplicate medical record materials in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations." Article 15: "No entity or individual may tamper with, forge, conceal, destroy, or seize medical record materials." <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2018-08/31/content_5318057.htm>; National Health and Family Planning Commission, State Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine (2013). Provisions on the Administration of Medical Records in Medical Institutions (2013 Edition): Medical institutions "shall designate departments or dedicated (part-time) personnel responsible for accepting applications for duplicating medical record materials," and duplication shall be conducted in the presence of the applicant with a certification stamp affixed. <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2014/content_2600084.htm>
entries.notes: Copying is handled by departments designated by the hospital; there is no need to beg the physician. For the checklist of what to copy, read directly from Article 16 of the Regulations on the Prevention and Handling of Medical Disputes. First are outpatient medical records, inpatient logs, temperature charts, doctor order sheets, lab sheets, and imaging materials. Next are surgery and anesthesia records, pathology records, nursing records, and medical expense itemized bills. Once obtained, store them chronologically in a folder. The most critical items inside are discharge summaries, surgical records, pathology reports, and key imaging. For chronic diseases, record indicators from successive visits in the same notebook; see Section 16.

entries.title: If You Have Doubts About Diagnosis or Treatment, Request On-the-Spot Sealing of Medical Records: Both Parties Present, Inventory Drawn Up, Each Retains One Copy
entries.cost: Costs no money. Request the sealing from the hospital and wait for both medical staff and patient parties to be present to complete the formalities. The difficulty lies in uttering these words directly in front of the doctor.
entries.summary: If you have doubts about medical treatment, you can request that the medical records be sealed. Sealing requires both the medical and patient parties to be present, an inventory to be drawn up, signatures and seals affixed, and each party taking one copy. If the medical record is not yet finished, seal the completed portion first. If an issue is suspected with IV infusion, blood transfusion, injections, or medications, that bag of fluid, that medicine, and the infusion set must be sealed together.
entries.benefit: The regulations stipulate: "Where medical records need to be sealed or unsealed due to a medical dispute, it shall be conducted in the presence of both the medical institution and the patient." Sealed materials can be original documents or duplicates, retained and safeguarded by the medical institution. Where medical records are not yet complete and need to be sealed, the completed portion shall be sealed first, and the subsequent portion sealed after completion. The medical institution shall draw up a sealing inventory for the sealed medical records, signed or sealed by both parties, with each party retaining one copy. Where adverse consequences are suspected of being caused by infusions, blood transfusions, injections, medication, etc., both the medical and patient parties shall jointly seal and unseal the physical objects at the scene. Where testing is required, both parties shall jointly commission a qualified testing institution. Where both parties cannot jointly agree on a commission, it shall be designated by the health administrative department of the county-level people's government where the medical institution is located. Where adverse consequences are suspected of being caused by blood transfusion and blood needs to be sealed, the medical institution shall notify the blood station to dispatch personnel to be present. There is another strict constraint: "No entity or individual may tamper with, forge, conceal, destroy, or seize medical record materials." If the dispute has been resolved after sealing, or if no further resolution request has been raised after 3 full years, the medical institution may unseal the materials on its own (Nationwide, effective October 1, 2018).
entries.sources: State Council (2018). Regulations on the Prevention and Handling of Medical Disputes (State Council Decree No. 701, Articles 15, 24, 25). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2018-08/31/content_5318057.htm>
entries.notes: Sealing and copying are two separate matters. Copying is something that should be done routinely; see Item 5 (Keep Your Own Copy of Medical Records and Imaging). Sealing is meant to secure evidence when a dispute occurs, guarding against retroactive writing and alterations. If an issue is suspected with IV infusions, blood transfusions, or medication, in addition to the medical records, seal the bag of fluid, that medication, and the infusion set together—do not let anyone take them away and discard them. Medical institutions must prominently display channels, procedures, and contact methods for resolving medical disputes, and establish a unified complaint management department. If an issue arises, approach that department first; do not argue with the attending physician on duty.

entries.title: For Urgent and Severe Injuries or Illnesses, Head Straight for the Emergency Triage Desk; Do Not Line Up at the Registration Window
entries.cost: Costs no money. Take a few extra steps upon entering to locate the triage desk. State the single most life-threatening symptom in one sentence.
entries.summary: The emergency department does not operate on a first-come, first-served basis; patients are queued according to disease severity across four levels. The place where the tier is determined is the emergency triage desk at the entrance, not the registration window. Upon arrival, report the most dangerous symptom first: massive hemorrhage, severe breathlessness, loss of consciousness, chest pain resembling a heart attack, or unbearable pain.
entries.benefit: The National Health Commission's 2024 edition of emergency medicine quality control indicators stipulates that emergency pre-examination triage must "categorize patients into four levels according to the severity of their condition." "Level I represents critically ill patients who need immediate medical treatment." "Level II represents acutely severe patients, where assessment and treatment are often conducted simultaneously." "Level III represents urgent patients who need medical diagnosis and treatment within a short period of time." "Level IV represents non-urgent or sub-urgent patients, who receive medical treatment sequentially in the general clinic area." Pre-examination triage means that upon entering the emergency department, dedicated personnel first assess the severity of the condition to determine the order of care. Beijing's implementation standards provide the response requirements for each level. Level 1: "Immediately assess and treat, and arrange for the patient to enter the resuscitation room or trauma resuscitation bay." Level 2: "Immediately monitor vital signs, receive treatment within 10 minutes, and arrange for the patient to enter the trauma resuscitation bay." Level 3: "Receive prioritized diagnosis and treatment ahead of Level 4 patients, and arrange for the patient to wait in the general clinic area; if the waiting time exceeds 30 minutes, reassessment is required." Level 4: "Sequential care; unless the condition changes, the waiting time will be longer; if the waiting time exceeds 4 hours, reassessment may be conducted." In the Beijing standard, manual assessment criteria for Level 1 include "acute altered consciousness." Level 2 includes "active or severe hemorrhage," "severe respiratory distress," "chest pain resembling cardiac etiology," and "severe pain from all causes (scores 7–10)." Triage must "adhere to the principle of priority treatment for critically and severely ill patients," and a pre-examination triage area should be set up in a prominent position at the entrance of the emergency department (the four-level classification standard is national, while the response times follow Beijing standards).
entries.sources: General Office of the National Health Commission (2024). Notice on Issuing Medical Quality Control Indicators for 6 Specialties Including Emergency Medicine (2024 Edition) (Guo Wei Ban Yi Zheng Han [2024] No. 150), Annex 1, Indicator 4: "Emergency Tiered Triage Implementation Rate". <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202405/content_6951260.htm>; Beijing Municipal Health Commission (2019). Beijing Action Plan for Strengthening Emergency Pre-examination Triage and Classification and its Annex "Beijing Hospital Emergency Pre-examination Triage and Classification Standards (Trial)": "Adhere to the principle of priority treatment for critically and severely ill patients. In accordance with the severity of the patient's condition, follow the principle of prioritizing the more severe over the less severe, and rapidly changing conditions over relatively stable ones, rationally arranging the sequence of patient care." "Set up an emergency pre-examination triage area at a prominent location at the entrance of the emergency department." "Pre-hospital emergency medical doctors should conduct initial triage on patients according to relevant standards, and promptly notify the receiving hospital's emergency department to prepare for intake for Level 1 and 2 patients." <http://wjw.beijing.gov.cn/zwgk_20040/ylws/201912/t20191216_1242338.html>
entries.notes: The division into four levels is unified nationwide. How long each level waits before receiving care is determined independently by each province and municipality; this Beijing document is a version that can be verified word for word. Grading is based on symptoms and indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, and blood oxygen saturation; pain level is also one of the metrics, and pain scored at 7 to 10 can be classified as Level 2. The hard indicators for Level 1 include several specific criteria. First, heart rate greater than 180 beats/min or less than 40 beats/min. Second, systolic blood pressure below 70 mmHg (systolic pressure is the high pressure reading). Third, blood oxygen saturation below 80%. Fourth, shock, definite myocardial infarction, or acute altered consciousness. If you feel triage has graded you too low, provide supplementary details clarifying your most dangerous symptom. If your condition changes while waiting, immediately return to the triage desk for a reassessment. In truly critical situations, call 120 (see Section 13). Beijing's plan requires pre-hospital emergency medical doctors to conduct preliminary grading on patients according to the standards, and promptly notify the emergency department of the receiving hospital to prepare for intake for Levels 1 and 2.

entries.title: Even if you bring no money, no ID, and cannot explain who you are, the emergency department must still provide emergency treatment first
entries.cost: Free.
entries.summary: The state maintains an Emergency Disease Relief Fund specifically to cover emergency medical expenses for two types of people: those whose identities cannot be determined, and those who cannot afford to pay. Hospitals cannot refuse or delay emergency resuscitation, and emergency centers cannot refuse to dispatch an ambulance over money issues. Therefore, do not endure an emergency at home simply because you lack funds, and do not avoid calling an ambulance for fear of unpaid bills. This fund only covers emergency treatment; subsequent hospitalization is still handled through basic medical insurance and medical assistance.
entries.benefit: The targets of the emergency disease relief system are "patients within the territory of China who suffer from acute, severe, or critical injuries and illnesses, require emergency treatment, but have an unidentified identity or are unable to pay the corresponding expenses." The fund pays for two categories of expenses: "emergency medical expenses incurred by patients whose identities cannot be ascertained" and "unpaid emergency medical expenses owed by patients whose identities are clear but who are unable to pay." The document also explicitly states that "medical institutions of all levels and types and their staff must promptly and effectively treat acute, severe, and critically injured patients, and must not refuse, shirk, or delay treatment for any reason." Pre-hospital emergency care also has regulations: the nationwide pre-hospital medical emergency call number is "120." Emergency medical centers (stations) "must not refuse, shirk, or delay pre-hospital emergency medical services due to command and dispatch reasons," nor "refuse or delay pre-hospital emergency medical services due to fee issues." Patient transfers follow the "principle of proximity, urgency, meeting professional needs, and considering the patient's wishes" (Nationwide, effective from 2013).
entries.sources: General Office of the State Council (2013). Guiding Opinions on Establishing the Emergency Disease Relief System (Guo Ban Fa [2013] No. 15). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2013-03/01/content_6069.htm>; National Health and Family Planning Commission (2014). Administrative Measures for Pre-hospital Medical Emergencies (Commission Order No. 3, Articles 13, 22, 23, and 25). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2014/content_2580977.htm>
entries.notes: The fund only covers the portion designated as "emergency medical expenses," and care is delivered first, with medical institutions applying to the fund retroactively—it is not cash you collect at the window. Those with basic medical insurance proceed through medical insurance first as usual. Application processes and funding limits vary across provinces. In the transfer principles, "proximity and urgency" take precedence over "patient wishes," so the ambulance might not take you to your preferred hospital; in critical conditions, the nearest facility capable of handling the case takes precedence. If the out-of-pocket costs for subsequent treatment remain an excessive burden, proceed through medical assistance; see Section 7, Item 10 (Medical Assistance).

entries.title: Disability assessment must wait until medical treatment is concluded or clinical therapeutic outcomes have stabilized
entries.cost: The assessment fee ranges from several hundred to 2,000 yuan, generally advanced by the party making the application. You must wait until medical treatment is concluded or clinical outcomes are stable; how long to wait depends on the injury condition, as determined by doctors. The difficulty lies in resisting the urge to settle the grade quickly while the injury has not fully healed.
entries.summary: Compensation amounts depend primarily on which grade is assessed, and the grade depends on how much functional impairment remains after treatment is finished. The standard explicitly states that it must be performed after treatment is concluded or clinical therapeutic outcomes are stable. Going for an assessment before bones have properly knitted does not meet this requirement. Ordinary fractures that have healed and do not affect function generally do not qualify for a disability grade.
entries.benefit: The evaluation principle of the "Classification of Impairment and Disability for Human Injuries" is that it "should be based on the consequences or outcomes of injury treatment, objectively evaluating the degree of tissue/organ loss and/or functional impairment." The standard stipulates that the timing of assessment "should be conducted after the treatment of the primary injury and its definitely related complications is concluded or clinical therapeutic effects are stable." The standard "divides the degree of human injury disability into 10 grades, from Grade I (100% human disability rate) to Grade X (10% human disability rate), with each grade differing by 10% in disability rate." The criteria for determination are "the structural damage to human tissues and organs, functional impairment, and their degree of dependence on medical and nursing care, with appropriate consideration given to the impact on social interaction and psychological factors caused by the disability." Provisions in Grade X related to fractures include the following: First, "a compression fracture of one vertebral body (compression degree reaching 1/3) or a comminuted fracture." Second, "fractures at two or more sites of the pelvis or comminuted fractures, healed with deformity." Third, "functional loss of 25% or more in any one major joint of the limbs (excluding the ankle joint)." Disabilities of the same body part and nature must not be counted repeatedly. For disabilities across two or more sites, their grades should be stated separately (Nationwide, effective as of January 1, 2017).
entries.sources: Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of State Security, Ministry of Justice (2016). Announcement on the Promulgation of the "Classification of Impairment and Disability for Human Injuries" (Promulgated April 18, 2016, effective January 1, 2017), Standard Articles 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 5.10.6, and 6.2. <https://www.moj.gov.cn/pub/sfbgw/zwxxgk/fdzdgknr/fdzdgknrtzwj/201908/P020210316701681025917.pdf>
entries.notes: Three disability assessment systems are not interchangeable—do not confuse them. Assault injuries, traffic accidents, and other personal injuries go through the judicial appraisal system's "Classification of Impairment and Disability for Human Injuries," which is used to calculate disability compensation (see Section 9). Work-related injuries go through work ability assessment, which uses a different set of ten disability grades and governs work-related injury benefits (see Section 19). If you want to receive policy benefits for persons with disabilities, you must separately obtain a Person with Disability Certificate (see Item 10, Person with Disability Certificate). Assemble your medical records, surgical notes, and follow-up imaging before the assessment (see Item 5, Keep Your Own Copy of Medical Records and Imaging). The standard does not specify whether performing the assessment too early results in a grade that is too low or too high; this is derived from the principle of being "based on the consequences or outcomes of injury treatment": assessing too early evaluates your status at that moment, and functions that have not yet recovered may improve later, or they may deteriorate. When this injury is compounded with pre-existing conditions, the assessment opinion must also clarify what proportion of the disability outcome this injury accounts for. This entry directly impacts the compensation amount.

entries.title: If functional impairment remains after treatment, apply for a Person with Disability Certificate at the county-level disabled persons' federation where your household registration is located
entries.cost: The certificate itself carries no processing fee. In principle, assessment fees and photo costs are borne by yourself; those in hardship can apply for reductions or waivers. Bring your ID card, household register (hukou), and 3 two-inch white-background photos to your county-level disabled persons' federation. Once the assessment passes, it is publicized in the village (community) for 5 business days, and the disabled persons' federation completes review within 10 business days. The difficulty lies in making these multiple trips and waiting through this period.
entries.summary: The Person with Disability Certificate is the threshold for receiving disability policy benefits, not proof of injury severity. It is divided into seven categories: visual, hearing, speech, physical, intellectual, psychiatric, and multiple disabilities, each graded from Level 1 to 4. The procedure consists of application, acceptance, assessment at a designated institution, public announcement, review and approval, and certificate issuance; it is valid for ten years and renewed free of charge upon expiration. Those who dispute the assessment conclusion may apply for a reassessment.
entries.benefit: The Person with Disability Certificate "is the legal credential certifying persons with disabilities, their disability categories, and disability levels, and is an important basis for persons with disabilities to enjoy preferential policies from the national and local governments in accordance with the law." The assessment standard is the national standard "Classification and Grading of Disabilities" (GB/T 26341-2010). Certificate issuance adheres to voluntary application and territorial administration. Persons with disabilities across seven categories—visual, hearing, speech, physical, intellectual, psychiatric, and multiple—can apply, with disability grades ranging from Level 1 to Level 4. County-level disabled persons' federations are responsible for processing applications and issuing certificates, based on assessment conclusions drawn by provincially designated hospitals or professional institutions. Where the assessment conclusion meets the standard, it is publicized in the village (community) for five business days, and the county-level disabled persons' federation "completes review within ten business days." "No manufacturing cost fee is charged for processing the Person with Disability Certificate." Assessment and photo costs are "in principle borne by the applicant personally; where conditions permit, local public finance may provide subsidies, and for applicants with special difficulties, relevant departments should be coordinated to grant reductions or waivers." The certificate is valid for ten years and renewed free of charge upon expiration. If the disability category or grade changes, an application for reassessment may be filed. Those who dispute the assessment conclusion may apply for reassessment at the municipal-level disabled persons' federation within ten business days. If a dispute still remains, the provincial disability assessment expert committee renders the final determination (Nationwide, effective as of January 1, 2018).
entries.sources: China Disabled Persons' Federation, National Health and Family Planning Commission (2017). Measures for the Administration of the Person with Disability Certificate of the People's Republic of China (Promulgated May 27, 2017, effective January 1, 2018; Articles 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 17, 19, 22, and 25). <https://www.bdpf.org.cn/cms68/web1459/subject/n1/n1459/n1508/n1509/n1512/c68465/content.html>
entries.notes: Calculate the ledger before deciding whether to apply. The certificate itself does not directly disburse money. What it connects to are the Two Subsidies for Persons with Disabilities: persons with disabilities in households receiving the minimum subsistence guarantee (dibao) receive a living allowance, while those with Level 1 or 2 disabilities who require long-term care receive a nursing care allowance; see Section 7, Item 8 (The Two Subsidies). The certificate also connects to regional concessions for rehabilitation, assistive devices, tax breaks, employment, and public transportation. These standards vary substantially by province, so check the official website of your local disabled persons' federation first before deciding whether to make the trips. It is entirely separate from the judicial appraisal's disability grades and the work-related injury labor ability assessments, and none substitute for the others (see Item 9, Disability Assessment Must Wait Until Treatment Is Concluded). The certificate is strictly for personal use and must not be lent out. If your disability condition no longer meets the standard, it will be revoked, and you cannot reapply within one year after revocation. Multiple disabilities are graded according to the most severe individual category.

entries.title: To thank a doctor who saved your life, use thank-you letters, banners, and satisfaction reviews rather than red envelopes: the guidelines prohibit property, not gratitude
entries.cost: Free. Writing a thank-you letter or completing an evaluation on a satisfaction platform takes about ten to twenty minutes.
entries.summary: Slipping cash in advance will not buy priority: appointment slots, hospital beds, scarce medications, and surgical schedules are all prohibited from being exchanged for benefits. If you want to thank a doctor who saved your life after the fact, you may express gratitude, but do not send cigarettes, alcohol, or cash-filled red envelopes—accepting them constitutes a violation for the doctor. If you want to show thanks, you can thoughtfully complete a satisfaction evaluation, write an official thank-you letter naming the physician, or present an appreciation silk banner.
entries.benefit: The "Nine Rules for Honest and Upright Practice of Medical Institution Staff" (Guo Wei Yi Fa [2021] No. 41), Rule 7: "Maintain medical order and do not undermine fairness in seeking medical care. Uphold the principle of equality and jointly build a fair environment for medical treatment. Strictly prohibit using medical resources such as appointment slots, bed allocations, and scarce drugs and consumables, or clinical arrangements such as examinations and surgeries, to accept benefits or enrich oneself at the expense of the public." Rule 8: "Jointly build harmonious relations and do not accept 'red envelopes' from patients. Abide by medical ethics and strictly exercise self-discipline." The same rule also explicitly stipulates: "Strictly prohibit soliciting or accepting gifts, gift money, prepaid consumer cards, negotiable securities, equity, other financial products, and other property from patients and their relatives." Meals and entertainment paid for by patients are likewise restricted: "Strictly prohibit participating in banquets, travel, fitness, entertainment, or other activities arranged, organized, or paid for by them." The document also requires medical institutions to implement primary responsibility, conduct supervision, and "resolutely investigate and punish violations." Satisfaction evaluations have been incorporated into the performance appraisals of tertiary public hospitals. The legal basis is the "Opinions of the General Office of the State Council on Strengthening the Performance Appraisal Work of Tertiary Public Hospitals" (Guo Ban Fa [2019] No. 4). The document states: "The performance appraisal indicator system for tertiary public hospitals consists of indicators in 4 areas: healthcare quality, operational efficiency, sustainable development, and satisfaction evaluation." The document further specifies: "Hospital satisfaction consists of two parts: patient satisfaction and medical personnel satisfaction..." It goes on to state that hospitals should "measure patients' sense of gain and medical personnel's enthusiasm through outpatient, inpatient, and medical staff satisfaction evaluations." There is also a unified national platform for this evaluation: "The state establishes a public hospital satisfaction management system..." The timeline specifies: "Before the end of March 2019, all tertiary public hospitals nationwide shall be incorporated into the National Health Commission's satisfaction survey platform. All regions must utilize the National Health Commission's satisfaction survey platform and incorporate the survey results into the performance appraisals of tertiary public hospitals." Hospitals are also mandated to handle complaints. The basis is Article 2 of the "Measures for the Administration of Complaints in Medical Institutions" (National Health Commission Order No. 3, effective 2019). Complaint management refers to patients "putting forward opinions, suggestions, or complaint requests" regarding medical service behavior, medical management, medical quality, safety, and other aspects. Hospitals are responsible for investigation, handling, and feedback. "Medical institutions at or above the secondary level shall establish a doctor-patient relations office or designate a department (hereinafter collectively referred to as the complaint management department) to centrally undertake complaint management work." The duties of the complaint management department include "centrally accepting complaints, investigating and verifying complaint matters, putting forward handling opinions, and replying to patients in a timely manner." Medical institutions "shall encourage staff to take the initiative to collect patients' opinions and suggestions regarding medical services, medical quality, safety, and other aspects" (Nationwide).
entries.sources: National Health Commission, National Healthcare Security Administration, National Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine (2021). Notice on Issuing the Nine Rules for Honest and Upright Practice of Medical Institution Staff (Guo Wei Yi Fa [2021] No. 41). State Council Gazette <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2022/content_5678098.htm>; General Office of the State Council (2019). Opinions on Strengthening the Performance Appraisal Work of Tertiary Public Hospitals (Guo Ban Fa [2019] No. 4). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2019-01/30/content_5362266.htm>; National Health Commission (2019). Measures for the Administration of Complaints in Medical Institutions (Commission Order No. 3). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2019-10/08/content_5436976.htm>
entries.notes: The beneficiary is yourself, as well as the person who saved you. It is entirely human to want to say thank you after an all-night emergency resuscitation; you can show gratitude, but only the format needs to change. Red envelopes, cigarettes, and alcohol shift risk onto the other party, whereas thank-you letters, banners, and satisfaction evaluations are institutionalized, officially recognized methods. If you already offered something and the other party pushed it back, do not assume they found it too little or were putting on airs—that is what they are required to do by regulation. In addition, distinguish between two things: giving a red envelope to a doctor is governed by industry discipline and hospital management, whereas giving money or property to investigators or law enforcement officers constitutes the crime of bribery under the Criminal Law; the two are not of the same magnitude (for the latter, see Section 8, Item 40). Writing thank-you letters and presenting silk banners are widely accepted by hospitals, but claims that they "will enter personal and department records" are anecdotal rule-of-thumb knowledge, not specified by formal regulations. What has documentary basis is the rule that satisfaction survey results are incorporated into tertiary public hospital performance appraisals. If you have doubts about the diagnosis and treatment itself, demand on the spot that medical records be sealed (see Item 6 of this section, Sealing Medical Records) and retain copies of medical records and imaging (Item 5, Keep Your Own Copy of Medical Records and Imaging).

entries.title: Before getting dental implants, ask clearly what items are included in the package price, prioritize institutions committed to participating in price regulation, and do not trust low-price advertisements
entries.cost: Free. Check the list of institutions on the National Healthcare Security Administration's official WeChat public account before dental treatment, and clarify the price list in person, taking ten to twenty minutes.
entries.summary: Following centralized price reductions for dental implants in 2023, the overall cost of a single conventional dental implant dropped from an average of 15,000 yuan to between 6,000 and 7,000 yuan. In tertiary public hospitals, the service fee per tooth is in principle capped at 4,500 yuan, with the implant and dental crown calculated separately. Dental implants, dental prostheses, and orthodontics are not reimbursed by basic medical insurance, but therapeutic dental procedures are widely reimbursable nationwide.
entries.benefit: A January 2024 announcement by the National Healthcare Security Administration stated that the cost of a routine single dental implant consists of three parts. The first part is the medical service fee, which is charged as a comprehensive lump sum. The scope of this lump sum includes "consultation and examination fees throughout the entire implantation process, biochemical test and imaging examination fees, implant placement fees, crown placement fees, and scanning, design, and modeling fees, excluding tooth extraction, periodontal scaling, root canal treatment, bone grafting, and soft tissue grafting." "In principle, the medical service charge for a single routine dental implant at tertiary public hospitals across all regions shall not exceed 4,500 yuan"; according to a 2022 special governance notice, economically developed regions may relax this limit by at most 20%. The second part is the dental implant system, for which a national centralized procurement was conducted in January 2023, with "the winning bid price range between 548 yuan and 1,855 yuan, with an average price of over 900 yuan." The leading Sichuan Healthcare Security Administration announced that high-priced imported brands dropped from a median procurement price of 5,000 yuan to around 1,850 yuan, and the several brands with the highest usage volumes dropped from around 1,500 yuan to around 770 yuan. The third part is the dental crown, with "the price range between 100 yuan and 656 yuan, with an average price of over 300 yuan." A National Healthcare Security Administration press conference in the second half of 2023 stated that local governance measures were fully implemented nationwide by late April and early May, and "the overall cost of a dental implant dropped from an average of 15,000 yuan to around 6,000–7,000 yuan." Whether medical insurance covers it: A 1999 document by departments including the Ministry of Labor and Social Security listed "dentures" (false teeth) and "non-functional cosmetic and orthopedic surgeries" as not payable by basic medical insurance. When replying to a proposal from the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) in 2019, the National Healthcare Security Administration stated that "cosmetic diagnosis and treatment items (including restoration of missing teeth, orthodontics, etc.) are not included in the scope of payment by the medical insurance fund. However, for therapeutic dental diagnosis and treatment items, they are not excluded at the national level, and local authorities have generally included them in the scope of medical insurance payment" (National, as of October 2026).
entries.sources: National Healthcare Security Administration (2024). Announcement on Releasing Information Such as the "List of Medical Institutions Committed to Participating in Dental Implantation Price Governance" (January 12, 2024). <https://www.nhsa.gov.cn/art/2024/1/12/art_109_11954.html>; National Healthcare Security Administration (2022). Notice on Carrying Out Special Governance of Oral Implantation Medical Service Charges and Consumables Prices (Yibao Fa [2022] No. 27, Articles 4 and 6). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-09/08/content_5709065.htm>; National Healthcare Security Administration (2023). National Healthcare Security Administration Holds Regular Press Conference for the Second Half of 2023 (September 22, 2023). <https://www.nhsa.gov.cn/art/2023/9/22/art_14_11321.html>; Sichuan Healthcare Security Administration (2023). Proposed Winning Selection Results for Centralized Volume-Based Procurement of Oral Implant Systems (January 11, 2023). <https://ylbzj.sc.gov.cn/scsybj/nc020100/2023/1/11/ac5565c7e0454890be086a2bc41f9acd.shtml>; Ministry of Labor and Social Security et al. (1999). Notice on Issuing Opinions on the Administration of Diagnosis and Treatment Items, Scope of Medical Service Facilities, and Payment Standards for Urban Employee Basic Medical Insurance (Laoshebu Fa [1999] No. 22, Annex 1). <https://policy.mofcom.gov.cn/claw/clawContent.shtml?id=39317>; National Healthcare Security Administration (2019). Letter in Reply to Proposal No. 4043 of the Second Session of the 13th National Committee of the CPPCC. <https://www.nhsa.gov.cn/art/2019/12/3/art_26_2096.html>
entries.notes: The 4,500 yuan cap applies only to public hospitals. Private institutions set their own prices, but the special governance notice requires that they must not induce patients with false or misleading "subsidies" or "low prices." Low prices in advertisements often cover only the implant fixture itself. Items outside the lump sum—such as tooth extraction and bone grafting—are where markups occur. Therefore, before signing, obtain an itemized list clearly stating the price of every component. The list of institutions committed to participating in price governance is published by the National Healthcare Security Administration on its official WeChat public account. If you are missing one or two teeth, an implant is not strictly mandatory; fixed partial dentures (bridges) and removable partial dentures are also restorative options, and their prices have not changed along with these policies—ask your dentist which option suits you. Regarding whether an employee basic medical insurance personal account can pay for dental implants, there is no unified national policy—consult your local healthcare security department; for how personal accounts can be shared with family members, see Section 5, Item 13 (Family mutual assistance). For why you should see a dentist when a tooth is missing, see Section 2, Item 10 (Seeing a dentist when missing a tooth). The benefit magnitude is classified as Medium: the price drop is driven by policy, and what readers can save on their own through this step primarily comes from avoiding extra markups outside the lump sum and avoiding high-priced institutions, amounting to several thousand yuan per tooth.

entries.title: When a hospital says a national medical-insurance-negotiated drug is out of stock or not admitted to the hospital formulary, ask the doctor to write a prescription and purchase it at a medical insurance "dual-channel" designated retail pharmacy, where it is reimbursed according to regulations just the same
entries.cost: Free. You need to ask a doctor to issue a prescription, and then make a trip to a designated pharmacy. In some localities, you must first complete a medication eligibility verification.
entries.summary: When a hospital says a certain nationally negotiated drug is out of stock or not admitted to its formulary, that does not mean the drug cannot be reimbursed. If this drug is included in your province's "dual-channel" mechanism, have the doctor write a prescription as usual and take it to a "dual-channel" designated pharmacy to purchase it; the reimbursement policy is identical to buying it at a hospital. According to national documents, hospitals also cannot cite medical insurance global budget caps or drug revenue percentage quotas as excuses to stall and not stock the drug.
entries.benefit: Negotiated drugs are medications included in the medical insurance catalog after price negotiations between the National Healthcare Security Administration and pharmaceutical enterprises. The 2021 policy interpretation by the National Healthcare Security Administration stated that because the catalog is adjusted annually, the sequence has shifted to "entering medical insurance first, entering hospitals later," causing certain negotiated drugs to face "difficulties in hospital admission." To address this, the National Healthcare Security Administration and the National Health Commission issued Document Yibao Fa [2021] No. 28. The document states that the "dual channel" is a "mechanism to supply negotiated drugs through two channels—designated medical institutions and designated retail pharmacies—and synchronously incorporate them into medical insurance payment." For drugs included in the "dual channel," "a unified payment policy shall be implemented in designated medical institutions and designated retail pharmacies." Reimbursement rules for purchasing at a pharmacy are the same as purchasing at a hospital. Which drugs are included is, in principle, determined by provincial healthcare security departments. Which pharmacies are included must be "promptly and proactively disclosed to the public" by healthcare security departments. Prescriptions are transmitted to pharmacies via prescription circulation centers within the medical insurance system, requiring "ensuring the smooth circulation of electronic prescriptions." Document Yibao Han [2021] No. 182 in September of the same year required that for negotiated drugs that hospitals temporarily cannot dispense, they must "enhance drug accessibility through channels such as the 'dual channel.'" Reasonably used negotiated drugs are tracked separately and not counted toward hospitals' drug revenue percentage assessments. The document also explicitly states that "limiting factors such as medical insurance global budget caps, medical institution formulary quantity caps, and drug revenue percentage ratios shall not be used as grounds to affect the implementation of negotiated drugs." It also required at the time that by the end of November 2021, each prefecture-level city have at least 1 "dual-channel" retail pharmacy. The notice for the 2025 edition of the medical insurance drug catalog (Yibao Fa [2025] No. 33) reiterated this phrase: "shall not use... as grounds." The notice also stated that, in principle, a negotiated drug must not be removed from the "dual channel" simply because it transitions into a regular catalog drug. Designated pharmacies dispensing "dual-channel" drugs "must all route such prescriptions through the electronic prescription center." The new edition of the catalog is implemented starting January 1, 2026 (National, as of October 2026).
entries.sources: National Healthcare Security Administration, National Health Commission (2021). Guiding Opinions on Establishing and Improving the "Dual-Channel" Management Mechanism for National Medical-Insurance-Negotiated Drugs (Yibao Fa [2021] No. 28, Articles 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-05/10/content_5605595.htm>; National Healthcare Security Administration (2021). Policy Interpretation of the "Guiding Opinions on Establishing and Improving the 'Dual-Channel' Management Mechanism for National Medical-Insurance-Negotiated Drugs". <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2021-05/10/content_5605596.htm>; National Healthcare Security Administration, National Health Commission (2021). Notice on Adapting to the Normalization of National Medical Insurance Negotiations and Continuing to Do a Good Job in Implementing Negotiated Drugs (Yibao Han [2021] No. 182, Articles 2, 3, and 5). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-09/11/content_5636762.htm>; National Healthcare Security Administration, Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2025). Notice on Issuing the "Drugs Catalog for National Basic Medical Insurance, Maternity Insurance, and Work-Related Injury Insurance" and the "Commercial Health Insurance Innovative Drugs Catalog" (2025) (Yibao Fa [2025] No. 33, Part 1). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202512/content_7050533.htm>
entries.notes: The procedure consists of four steps. First, ask the doctor whether this drug is a "dual-channel" drug in your province and whether they can prescribe it; prescriptions generally flow through the electronic prescription system of medical insurance. Second, check which pharmacy carries it. Provincial healthcare security administrations publish lists of drugs and pharmacies, or you can call the local healthcare security department. The National Healthcare Security Service Platform App launched a directory query for institutions stocking negotiated drugs in 2021. Third, bring your medical insurance card or electronic medical insurance certificate to make the purchase. The pharmacy must verify that the person for whom the prescription was issued is the same person taking the medication. Fourth, clarify the reimbursement percentage, whether it counts as an outpatient chronic or severe/special disease, and whether it qualifies for separate payment, all of which are determined locally. Not every negotiated drug is included in the "dual channel"; those that are not can only be purchased at hospitals. Regarding whether direct settlement is supported when purchasing out of town, official documents only state "advance steadily"—inquire before traveling. For how to obtain certification for outpatient chronic and severe/special diseases and their cross-regional direct settlement, see Section 16, Item 2 (Certification of outpatient chronic and severe/special diseases). The benefit magnitude is classified as Large based on judgment: no national document was found giving the specific amount an individual patient can be reimbursed. However, the policy interpretation states that the focus for inclusion in the "dual channel" is on drugs with "high clinical value, urgent demand, and high costs." Calculated over a treatment course, the difference between out-of-pocket costs and reimbursement is estimated to be on the order of tens of thousands of yuan. The beneficiaries are primarily yourself and your family members.

entries.title: To refill prescriptions for chronic diseases diagnosed at a hospital with stable conditions, you can undergo an online follow-up consultation and obtain medication through that hospital's internet hospital; initial consultations for the condition cannot be conducted online
entries.cost: Free. You need to locate the entry portal for the hospital's internet hospital on your mobile phone and complete real-name authentication once. Consultation fees for online follow-ups at public hospitals are charged at general outpatient rates. Home delivery shipping fees for medications are paid out-of-pocket and are not reimbursed by medical insurance.
entries.summary: If a chronic disease has been definitively diagnosed at a hospital and the condition is stable, and you still need the same medications, you can schedule an online follow-up consultation with the original hospital, and medications can be shipped to your home. Where local medical insurance has incorporated this, you can settle payment directly using medical insurance. If it is the first time you are being seen for this condition, or if your condition changes, the doctor must require you to visit the hospital in person.
entries.benefit: What is saved is the time spent traveling back and forth to the hospital and waiting in line for registration each time. The "Administrative Measures for Internet Diagnosis and Treatment (Trial)" stipulate that online consultations are limited to follow-up visits for certain common and chronic diseases. The prerequisite is that you have already received a definitive diagnosis at a physical hospital, the physician possesses your medical record materials, and the follow-up consultation targets the same diagnosis. The measures explicitly specify that "internet diagnosis and treatment activities shall not be conducted for first-visit patients." If your condition changes and requires an in-person physical examination by a physician, the hospital must immediately terminate the online diagnosis and treatment and guide you to a physical hospital. Online prescriptions must have the physician's electronic signature, and after review by a pharmacist, a third party may be entrusted to deliver the medication to your home. Specially managed medications such as narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances cannot be prescribed online. When prescribing medications online for children under 6 years of age, a guardian and a physician of the relevant specialty must be present. For medical insurance reimbursement, refer to Document Yibao Fa [2020] No. 45 issued by the National Healthcare Security Administration in 2020. It states that for follow-up consultations and prescription issuance at designated "Internet+" hospitals within the local pooling region, consultation fees and medication costs may be paid in accordance with local medical insurance regulations. The portion borne by the individual may be paid using an urban employee basic medical insurance personal account in accordance with regulations. The cost of providing medication delivery services is not included in the scope of medical insurance payment. Local authorities may start with outpatient chronic and severe/special diseases and gradually expand the payment scope. Local medical insurance administrative agencies must disclose the directory of such designated hospitals to the public. Document Yibao Fa [2019] No. 47 stipulates that for internet follow-up consultations conducted by public medical institutions, regardless of the seniority rank of the medical personnel providing the service, fees are charged according to the price of general outpatient consultation items (National, as of October 2026).
entries.sources: National Health Commission, National Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine (2018). Notice on Issuing 3 Documents Including the Administrative Measures for Internet Diagnosis and Treatment (Trial) (Guoweiyifa [2018] No. 25; "Administrative Measures for Internet Diagnosis and Treatment (Trial)" Articles 2, 16, 18, and 19; "Administrative Measures for Internet Hospitals (Trial)" Articles 19 and 20). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2019/content_5358684.htm>: "Internet diagnosis and treatment activities shall not be conducted for first-visit patients."; National Healthcare Security Administration (2020). Guiding Opinions on Actively Promoting Medical Insurance Payment for "Internet+" Medical Services (Yibao Fa [2020] No. 45, Items (3), (4), and (5)). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-11/03/content_5556883.htm>: "Consultation fees and medication costs incurred when insured persons undergo follow-up consultations and have prescriptions issued at designated medical institutions for 'Internet+' medical services within their pooling region may be paid in accordance with the medical insurance regulations of the pooling region. Among these, expenses borne by the individual may be paid by the employee medical insurance personal account according to regulations. Fees for providing drug delivery services are not included in the scope of medical insurance payment."; National Healthcare Security Administration (2019). Guiding Opinions on Improving Pricing and Medical Insurance Payment Policies for "Internet+" Medical Services (Yibao Fa [2019] No. 47, Item "Refining Pricing Policies Based on the Characteristics of Various Services"). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2019-08/30/content_5456428.htm>: "When public medical institutions carry out internet follow-up consultations, services provided by medical personnel of different ranks shall all be charged at the price of general outpatient consultation items"
entries.notes: First, ask your attending physician whether this disease qualifies for online follow-up consultations, and then look for the internet hospital portal in the hospital's official WeChat public account or app. Make sure to identify the internet hospital operated directly by the hospital where you were diagnosed. Whether medical insurance settlement is supported is determined locally; consult the designated institution directory published by the local healthcare security department or call to inquire. For those insured in other localities, official documents only mention "exploring" direct cross-regional online settlement; clarify this before using the service. If your condition is stable and your community health service center carries your medication, you can obtain up to a 12-week supply at once at the community center; see Section 16, Item 5 (Obtaining up to 12 weeks of medication at once at a community health center). If the community clinic does not carry the medication, or if a specialist must supervise dosage adjustments, an online follow-up consultation is more suitable. The benefit magnitude is classified as Medium based on judgment: a monthly trip to a major hospital for medication takes roughly half a day, translating to about one hour per week. Beneficiaries are primarily yourself and your family members, with elderly individuals with limited mobility saving the most.

entries.title: Request an itemized bill during hospitalization to verify item by item, clarify non-reimbursable out-of-pocket items before consenting, and if discrepancies arise, first file a price complaint with the hospital, and if that fails, report it to the healthcare security department
entries.cost: Free. Request an itemized statement every few days during hospitalization; checking it takes ten to fifteen minutes. The hard part is overcoming embarrassment to ask the doctors and nurses.
entries.summary: During hospitalization, you can request an itemized billing statement that lists the unit price, quantity, and date for every medication and every examination. For medications and tests not covered by medical insurance, except in emergencies and resuscitation, the hospital must obtain prior consent from you or your family. If you discover duplicate charges or billing for services never performed, first call the hospital's price complaint hotline; if the hospital refuses to acknowledge it, report it to the healthcare security department.
entries.benefit: The "Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of the Use of Healthcare Security Funds" stipulate that designated hospitals must "truthfully issue billing receipts and related materials to insured personnel." Insured persons also have the right to demand that hospitals truthfully issue them. Hospitals must not perform excessive examinations, and must not engage in duplicate billing, charging above prescribed rates, or unbundling billing items. For medications and services outside the scope of medical insurance fund payment, except in emergencies and resuscitation, consent must be obtained from the insured person or their close relatives or guardians. For violations of these provisions, the healthcare security department will order corrections. If losses are caused to the healthcare security fund, it will order a refund and impose a fine of 1 to 2 times the amount of the loss. Using items not reimbursable by medical insurance without consent and refusing to correct the violation carries a fine of 10,000 to 50,000 yuan. The National Health Commission's 2019 "Provisions on the Internal Price Behavior Management of Medical Institutions" require hospitals to establish an itemized billing statement system, including electronic statements. When a patient needs it, the hospital must provide printing services. The itemized statement must clearly specify the name and code of items, drugs, and medical consumables, as well as the unit price, pricing unit, date of use, quantity, and amount. Services charged by disease type or DRG (Diagnosis-Related Group prospective bundled payment) are exempt from this requirement. Hospitals must publish price consultation and complaint telephone numbers in prominent locations, implement a first-contact responsibility system for complaints, and receiving staff must record the content and handling results. To report violations to the healthcare security department, use its publicly announced website, phone number, fax, or mailing address. Reports can be submitted anonymously; the personal information of real-name whistleblowers must be kept confidential. Where verified to be true, rewards will be granted to whistleblowers in accordance with national regulations (National, as of October 2026).
entries.sources: State Council (2021). Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of the Use of Healthcare Security Funds (State Council Decree No. 735, Articles 15, 17, 35, 38, and 39). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-02/19/content_5587668.htm>: "Except for special circumstances such as emergencies and resuscitation, the provision of pharmaceutical and medical services outside the payment scope of the healthcare security fund shall be subject to the consent of the insured person or their close relatives or guardians." "Insured persons have the right to require designated pharmaceutical and medical institutions to truthfully issue fee receipts and related materials."; National Health Commission, National Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine (2019).
