Notice on Issuing the Provisions on the Internal Price Behavior Management of Medical Institutions (Guowei Caiwu Fa [2019] No. 64, Articles 15, 16, and 18). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-01/02/content_5466052.htm>: "Medical institutions shall establish an itemized fee statement (including electronic statement) system, provide itemized lists of fees for medical services, pharmaceuticals, and medical consumables to patients in various forms (except for those charged by disease type or DRG), and provide printing services when patients need them."; National Healthcare Security Administration (2022). Interim Measures for Handling Reports on the Supervision and Administration of the Use of Healthcare Security Funds (National Healthcare Security Administration Decree No. 5, Articles 6, 7, 8, 16, 21, and 25). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2022/content_5687509.htm>
entries.notes: Reporting to the healthcare security department addresses the hospital's non-compliant use of medical insurance funds. What the regulations specify are orders to rectify, refunds to the healthcare security fund, and fines; they do not specify refunding the overcharged portion directly to you. To recover money you overpaid out of pocket, you primarily rely on the hospital itself correcting the charges; therefore, first approach the hospital's price complaint window, keeping all billing statements and communication records. Filing a lawsuit in court over a few hundred yuan—where the first-instance ordinary procedure is legally prescribed to conclude within 6 months and can be extended, while attorney fees are borne by yourself—is generally not cost-effective. A report must specify concrete clues: which item on the statement, on which date, and how many times it was billed. If you simply want to ask about reimbursement policies, call the medical insurance consultation line; that does not count as a report. For items you do not understand, first ask the nursing station or the inpatient billing office; they are not necessarily irregular charges. Non-reimbursable medications are not necessarily unnecessary; clarify how much they cost per day and whether reimbursable alternatives exist before signing. Upon discharge, request a comprehensive summary statement and store it together with your medical records; see Item 5 (Keeping your own copies of medical records and imaging). The benefit magnitude is classified as Medium based on judgment: no official figure was found for the amount an individual patient is overcharged; according to this book's thresholds, a few hundred to several thousand yuan counts as Medium. Beneficiaries are primarily yourself and your family members, and auditing bills on behalf of hospitalized elderly relatives is especially crucial.

chapters.title: What to do after someone passes away
chapters.intro:
Scope: Money. This section only covers how procedures are handled and how money is claimed, including what to do first right after a person passes away, and which fees have checklists available for cross-checking. It also covers which accounts have funds that can be retrieved, and what matters close relatives are legally entitled to handle directly. The first five items are arranged chronologically: the scene, the death certificate, the remains and cremation, what to do if there is a dispute over the cause of death, and household registration cancellation. Arrangements an elderly person should make while alive—such as voluntary guardianship, wills, and accounts—can be found in Section 17. The three compensation payments for work-related death can be found in Section 19.

The funeral and interment portion is based on the revised Regulations on Funeral and Interment Management, effective from March 30, 2026. How to calculate funeral subsidies and survivor pensions under basic pension insurance can be found in Item 9 (Housing provident fund balance, social security benefits).

entries.title: When someone passes away at home or outdoors, first distinguish between a normal death and an unnatural death: in cases of accident, unknown cause of death, or when discovered living alone, call the police immediately, and do not touch the remains or the scene
entries.cost: Free of charge. It just takes a phone call.
entries.summary: For those who die by accident, whose cause of death is unknown, or who lived alone and were only discovered after a long time without receiving hospital treatment, the death certificate is issued by public security authorities. If the scene has been disturbed, circumstances become impossible to clarify, and the certificate will be difficult to issue. Without this document, subsequent cremation, household registration cancellation, and insurance claims will all be stalled. If you cannot tell which situation applies, call 110 first; the police will still issue the certificate after concluding their investigation.
entries.benefit: Regulations on Household Registration, Article 8, Paragraph 2: "When a citizen dies due to an accidental incident or the cause of death is unknown, the head of household or the discoverer shall immediately report to the local public security police station or the township/town people's committee." This means: if an accident occurs, or it is unknown how the person died, the head of household and the person who discovered them must immediately report to the police station or the township/town government. Regulations on Funeral and Interment Management, Article 23: "Where a natural person dies a normal death, medical and healthcare institutions shall issue a death certificate in a timely manner. For deceased persons involving unnatural death cases (incidents) handled in accordance with the law by public security organs and who have not received treatment from medical and healthcare institutions, public security organs shall issue a death certificate." This means: for those who died of normal illness, the medical institution that treated them issues the death certificate. For those who did not receive hospital treatment and fall under the purview of public security handling, public security issues it. If the scene has been disturbed, it becomes impossible to clarify and difficult to issue. Subsequent cremation, household registration cancellation, and insurance claims all depend on this single document.
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (1958). Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Household Registration (Article 8). <http://www.gd.gov.cn/zwgk/wjk/zcfgk/content/mpost_2531969.html> (Published on the Guangdong Provincial People's Government Portal Website); State Council (2026). Regulations on Funeral and Interment Management (State Council Decree No. 824, effective March 30, 2026, Article 23). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202601/content_7054169.htm>
entries.notes: Passing away at home after a prolonged bedridden illness counts as a normal death. You can ask the institution that provided medical care during their lifetime to issue the certificate, or you can go to the community health service center or township health center covering their residential area. Regarding which treating entity issues the death certificate, see Item 2 (Death certificate). If you cannot distinguish which category applies, treat it as an unnatural death and call 110 first; after the police arrive and finish investigating, they can still issue the certificate. If you clean up the scene before calling the police, no one will be able to help you. Do not move the remains yourself, do not wash or change their clothes, and do not remove medicine bottles or notes.

entries.title: The death certificate is the key to everything that follows: issued by whoever provided medical treatment, or obtained from community healthcare institutions for normal death at home; issued within one day
entries.cost: Free of charge.
entries.summary: For deaths occurring in a hospital, obtain the death certificate from the medical facility responsible for the treatment. For normal deaths at home, obtain it from the community healthcare service institution or township health center covering the residential area. For normal deaths with clear causes of death, it is issued within one day. Household registration cancellation, cremation, withdrawing housing provident funds, claiming social security benefits, insurance claims, and handling inheritance all require it; make several photocopies as soon as you receive it.
entries.benefit: The "Specifications for Population Death Information Registration and Management (Trial)" states: For deaths occurring within medical and healthcare institutions, it shall be "issued by the medical and healthcare institution responsible for treatment"—if the person passed away in a hospital or health clinic, have the facility in charge of treatment issue it. For normal deaths at home or in other venues, it shall be "issued by the community healthcare service institution or township (subdistrict) health center within the jurisdiction"—have the community health service center or township/subdistrict health clinic covering the residential area issue it. For cases determined by public security and judicial organs to be unnatural deaths, they shall be processed by public security and judicial departments according to current regulations and procedures. The 2026 circular from five ministerial departments states: For the Death Certificate, "the paper version and the electronic license have equal legal validity," meaning the digital version works just as well as the paper version. For normal deaths where the cause of death is already clear, it must be issued within one day after the death occurs. If the certificate is lost, you may apply once to the original issuing institution for a reissuance. If the basic information contains errors, you may apply once for a reissuance based on supporting documentation.
entries.sources: General Office of the National Health and Family Planning Commission (2014). Specifications for Population Death Information Registration and Management (Trial) (Guo Wei Ban Gui Hua Fa [2014] No. 68, Article 9). <https://mzj.sz.gov.cn/szmz/pc/zwgk/jcxxgk/zcfg/byfw/content/post_2952215.html> (Forwarded by the Shenzhen Civil Affairs Bureau); National Health Commission, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of Civil Affairs, National Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine, National Disease Control and Prevention Administration (2026). Circular on Strengthening the Management of Resident Medical Death Certificate Information Registration and Electronic Licenses (Guo Wei Gui Hua Fa [2026] No. 5). <https://wjw.fujian.gov.cn/xxgk/fgwj/gjwj/202602/t20260228_7102810.htm> (Forwarded by the Fujian Provincial Health Commission)
entries.notes: Household registration cancellation, cremation, housing provident fund withdrawal, claiming social security benefits, insurance claims, and inheritance processing each require it. Once you receive it, first make several photocopies, and apply simultaneously for an electronic license if available. There is only one chance for reissuance, so do not lose the original. If there are errors in the name or citizen identification number, correct them on the spot, because if you only discover them when handling inheritance, you will have to make return trips to every single service window.

entries.title: Transport, storage, and cremation of remains can only be handled by funeral homes; hospital mortuaries do not provide funeral services, and storage generally does not exceed 3 days
entries.cost: Free of charge.
entries.summary: Transport, storage, preservation, body preparation, and cremation can only be carried out by funeral homes. Hospital mortuaries do not conduct funeral services, offering at most temporary placement of the remains. Storage at a funeral home generally does not exceed 3 days; to store for additional days, you must go through extension procedures. Cremation requires a death certificate and a cremation confirmation form; the cremation certificate provided after cremation will also be required for inheritance and insurance claims.
entries.benefit: Regulations on Funeral and Interment Management, Article 25: "Services for the transport, storage, preservation, body preparation, and cremation of remains shall be specifically provided by funeral homes." No other entities are permitted to handle these tasks. Article 24: "Mortuaries of medical and healthcare institutions shall not be contracted out, shall not carry out funeral services, and may provide convenient services for the temporary placement of remains." Hospital mortuaries can only be used for temporary placement and cannot organize funeral matters. Article 27: "Storage of remains in funeral homes generally shall not exceed 3 days; where extended storage is needed, the bereaved family or the party transferring the remains shall complete procedures for extended storage at the funeral home." If you need to store them for more days, go to the funeral home to apply for an extension. Article 28: "Funeral homes shall cremate remains against death certificates and cremation confirmation forms, and issue cremation certificates." Neither of the two materials can be missing, and after cremation is completed, a cremation certificate will be given to you. Article 29: "In areas where cremation is practiced, remains shall be cremated locally and at a nearby funeral home"—meaning you must find a nearby funeral home in the area where the person passed away to carry out the cremation.
entries.sources: State Council (2026). Regulations on Funeral and Interment Management (State Council Decree No. 824, effective March 30, 2026, Articles 8, 9, 24, 25, 27, 28, 29). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202601/content_7054169.htm>
entries.notes: "One-stop service" operators approaching you after a death in a hospital are mostly not funeral home staff. Transport itself falls under basic items with regulated pricing; see Item 6 (Checklist of basic items). Keep the cremation certificate safe, as it will be needed for inheritance, insurance, and transferring ashes. Whether a locality practices cremation or burial is determined by the provincial-level government. Funeral customs of ethnic minorities are protected under Article 9 of the Regulations. For cases where burial is carried out instead of required cremation, or where burials or graves are constructed outside cemeteries and ecological burial areas, the civil affairs department will order rectification within a prescribed time limit (restoring the site within a deadline).

entries.title: If there is a dispute over the cause of death, raise it and conduct an autopsy within 48 hours, while sealing the medical records
entries.cost: Free of charge. The difficult part is still remembering to raise it at that moment.
entries.summary: If you have questions about the cause of death, an autopsy must be conducted within 48 hours after the person passes away; this can be extended to 7 days if the hospital has freezing storage facilities. An autopsy requires signed consent from close relatives; if consent is refused or if time limits are delayed past the deadline, the responsibility for the inability to determine the cause of death falls on that party. When requesting an autopsy, simultaneously demand that medical records be sealed. Once the remains are cremated, an autopsy can never be performed again.
entries.benefit: The time limit for autopsies is written in Article 26 of the Regulations on the Prevention and Handling of Medical Disputes. The original text states: "When a patient dies and both the medical institution and the patient side dispute the cause of death, an autopsy shall be conducted within 48 hours after the patient's death; where conditions for freezing bodies are met, it may be extended to 7 days." Therefore, if you wish to determine the cause of death, an autopsy must be performed within 48 hours after the person passes away, with an extension up to 7 days at most if the hospital has refrigerated storage conditions. The same article also states: "The autopsy shall be subject to the consent and signature of the deceased's close relatives; refusal to sign shall be deemed as the deceased's close relatives disagreeing to conduct the autopsy." If family members do not sign, it is treated as a refusal. It also states: "Where refusal or delay of the autopsy exceeds the prescribed time limit and affects the determination of the cause of death, the party refusing or delaying shall bear the responsibility." Whoever disagrees or delays past the deadline will bear the responsibility if the cause of death cannot be determined later. Article 24: Sealing and unsealing medical record materials "shall be carried out in the presence of both the medical institution and the patient side." Both you and the hospital must be present when medical records are sealed and unsealed.
entries.sources: State Council (2018). Regulations on the Prevention and Handling of Medical Disputes (State Council Decree No. 701, Articles 24, 26). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/content/2018-08/31/content_5318057.htm>
entries.notes: Saying "I felt something was wrong back then" after this time limit has passed will cause liability to fall conversely on the delaying party. Once the remains are cremated, an autopsy is no longer possible, so this matter must be decided before contacting the funeral home. For details on how to seal medical records, see Section 24.

entries.title: There are statutory time limits for canceling a deceased person's household registration: before burial in cities, and within one month in rural areas
entries.cost: Free of charge. Bring the death certificate and household registration booklet (hukou bu) to make a trip to the police station.
entries.summary: In cities, household registration must be canceled before burial; in rural areas, within one month. Bring the death certificate and household registration booklet to the police station to complete the process. Procrastinating will cause inheritance transfers, benefit claims, and insurance cancellations to get stuck on household registration status checks.
entries.benefit: Regulations on Household Registration, Article 8, Paragraph 1: "When a citizen dies, the head of household, relatives, dependants, or neighbors shall declare death registration to the household registration organ and cancel household registration before burial in cities, or within one month in rural areas. If a citizen dies in a place of temporary residence, the household registration organ of the place of temporary residence shall notify the household registration organ of the place of permanent residence to cancel the household registration." This means: do it before burial in cities, and within one month in rural areas. The head of household, relatives, dependants, or neighbors can all go to the household registration organ (police station) to report the death and cancel the household registration. If the person passed away while staying temporarily elsewhere, the police station at the temporary residence will notify the police station at the registered permanent residence to cancel the household registration.
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (1958). Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Household Registration (Article 8). <http://www.gd.gov.cn/zwgk/wjk/zcfgk/content/mpost_2531969.html> (Published on the Guangdong Provincial People's Government Portal Website)
entries.notes: If the household registration remains active, procedures for inheritance transfers, claiming benefits, and canceling insurance will all be held up, as these service windows all verify household registration status. If pension payments continue to be disbursed, that constitutes fraudulent collection and must eventually be returned. When visiting the police station, ask concurrently: how to suspend social insurance and medical insurance benefits, and how to apply for funeral subsidies. Those funds can be found in Item 9 (Housing provident fund balance, social security benefits).

entries.title: Funeral services are divided into basic items and non-basic items; basic items have a checklist, and fees are formulated in accordance with the law
entries.cost: Free of charge. Spend a few minutes looking over the checklist before heading out.
entries.summary: Transport of remains, storage, farewell ceremonies, cremation, storage of ashes, and ecological burials are all included in the national checklist of basic items. Columbaria niche interments provided by public institutions are also included. Prices for these items are set according to regulations, and other services must also be listed on a checklist, with unauthorized fee items strictly prohibited. Before heading out, ask clearly which items count as basic items and what the local standards are before negotiating anything else.
entries.benefit: Transport of remains, storage of remains, farewell ceremonies for remains, cremation of remains, storage of ashes, and ecological burials are all included in the national checklist of basic items. Columbaria niche interments provided by government-run funeral service institutions are also included in the checklist. Pricing standards for these items are established in accordance with the law, and rates are set by regulation rather than determined arbitrarily by funeral homes themselves. The checklist for non-basic items is determined by civil affairs departments at or above the city divided into districts level (prefecture-level cities and above).
entries.sources: State Council (2026). Regulations on Funeral and Interment Management (State Council Decree No. 824, revised and adopted at the 72nd Executive Meeting of the State Council on November 14, 2025, "effective March 30, 2026"). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202601/content_7054169.htm> Article 5: "Funeral services are divided into basic items and non-basic items. Pricing policies shall be formulated by the development and reform department and the finance department of the State Council in conjunction with civil affairs and other departments of the State Council." "The State establishes a checklist of basic funeral service items, incorporating transport of remains, storage of remains, farewell ceremonies for remains, cremation of remains, storage of ashes, ecological burials, as well as columbaria niche interments provided by government-run funeral service institutions into the scope of the checklist"; Article 50: "Funeral services shall be subject to checklist-based management with dynamic adjustments; creating items or charging fees outside the checklist is prohibited."
entries.notes: Provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may add further items on the basis of the national checklist. First ask clearly which items belong to basic items and what the local pricing standards are before discussing the rest. Prices of basic items are determined in accordance with regulations; items outside basic items are optional, but must also be reviewed against the checklist and fee standards. By distinguishing between these two categories, you will have grounds to challenge any overcharged amounts. There is nothing wrong with wanting to arrange a decent funeral for your relative, and this guide does not urge you to cut corners; where money is spent is entirely up to you.

entries.title: When encountering mandatory tie-in sales, price markups beyond marked prices, or splitting a single item into multiple fees, document them to file a complaint
entries.cost: Free of charge. The difficult part is still being willing to be meticulous at that moment.
entries.summary: Price illegalities explicitly cited by the Regulations include: failing to post a price list, charging additional money beyond marked prices, bundling and forcing sales of funeral supplies, and compelling you to accept paid services from third parties. Splitting a single service into multiple chargeable items also counts as a disguised price increase. Request a price list on the spot, preserve fee receipts and chat logs, and it will still be in time to file a complaint afterward. For price oversight, contact market regulation authorities; for funeral service management, contact civil affairs.
entries.benefit: The Regulations enumerate five categories of illegal pricing behaviors; four of them are discussed below. Failing to display a price list or charging more money than the marked price constitutes failing to clearly mark prices or adding markups beyond the marked price. Refusing to perform a service unless a product is purchased constitutes tying sales or attaching unreasonable conditions to enforce sales. Forcing paid services from another provider upon you constitutes compelling or disguisedly compelling the acceptance of third-party paid services. Charging extra money under an altered name constitutes increasing fee standards in disguise. In addition, "disguisedly increasing fee standards by splitting items, expanding fee-charging scopes, or other forms" is strictly prohibited. Breaking down one service item into multiple sub-items to charge separately, or broadening the scope of fees charged, are all within the scope of prohibited conduct.
entries.sources: State Council (2026). Regulations on Funeral and Interment Management (State Council Decree No. 824, revised and adopted at the 72nd Executive Meeting of the State Council on November 14, 2025, "effective March 30, 2026"). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202601/content_7054169.htm> Article 42: "Funeral service institutions shall not establish fee-charging items without authorization in violation of relevant regulations, or disguisedly increase fee standards by splitting items, expanding the fee-charging scope, or other forms." Article 43 enumerates illegal pricing behaviors including: "(1) Failing to clearly mark prices according to regulations, or adding markups beyond marked prices or charging unlisted fees;" "(3) Compelling or disguisedly compelling the sale of funeral supplies or provision of funeral-related services and collecting fees by bundling, attaching unreasonable conditions, or unreasonable restrictions;" "(4) Compelling or disguisedly compelling bereaved families to accept paid services from third parties, or repeatedly charging fees using related service outlets;" Article 51 requires civil affairs departments to establish an information sharing and supervision mechanism with government service convenience hotlines, "and regarding funeral service issues reported by bereaved families, they shall promptly handle them in conjunction with relevant departments and notify the bereaved families of the handling results."
entries.notes: Investigating and handling pricing violations falls under the market regulation department, while funeral services themselves fall under the civil affairs department. Request a price list on the spot, keep fee vouchers and chat records intact, and you will still have ample time to file a complaint afterward.

entries.title: Intermediaries such as funeral agencies, funeral supplies purchasing agents, and event planning/emceeing must register with county-level civil affairs departments
entries.cost: Free of charge. Just ask whether they have filed a record.
entries.summary: Intermediaries such as funeral agencies, supply purchasing agents, event planning and emceeing, and information consulting must file records with the county-level civil affairs department. Those without records filed are not included in the civil affairs department's funeral service information system. Whether you can look this up yourself varies by location; the most reliable method is to call the county-level civil affairs department to inquire. Those who charge unauthorized fees via deceptive means or resell deceased persons' information will be penalized according to law.
entries.benefit: Intermediaries that have not filed records are not in the funeral service information system administered by civil affairs departments. Those that charge fees in violation of regulations through deceitful means, induce lavish spending, compel acceptance of services, or resell personal information of the deceased will be handled in accordance with the law. They will also be tagged in the system and disclosed to the public, where anyone can view them.
entries.sources: State Council (2026). Regulations on Funeral and Interment Management (State Council Decree No. 824, revised and adopted at the 72nd Executive Meeting of the State Council on November 14, 2025, "effective March 30, 2026"). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202601/content_7054169.htm> Article 41: "Except for funeral service institutions, organizations and individuals engaged in funeral-related service activities such as funeral agency services, supplies purchasing agency, planning and emceeing, and information consulting shall file records with the civil affairs department of the county-level people's government." "Those exhibiting behaviors that harm the rights and interests of bereaved families—such as irregularly collecting fees through deception, inducing extravagant ceremonies, compelling acceptance of services, and reselling information of the deceased—shall be dealt with in accordance with the law, flagged in the funeral service information system, and disclosed to the public."
entries.notes: Online memorial platforms are regulated in the same way. Article 45 of the Regulations prohibits them from inducing consumption and from unlawfully processing the deceased's personal information.

entries.title: Money scattered across various places must be claimed one by one: housing provident fund balances, social security benefits, and work-related injury compensation
entries.cost: Free of charge, but requires visiting multiple service windows. Prepare both the death certificate and proof of kinship before going.
entries.summary: The housing provident fund balance can be withdrawn by heirs; since it is not held in a standard bank account, it is easily overlooked. Remaining funds in the basic pension insurance personal account can also be inherited. For participants in enterprise employee basic pension insurance who die of illness, their families can additionally claim a funeral subsidy and a survivor pension ranging from 3 to 24 months. For work-related deaths, there are separately three compensation payments for work-related injury.
entries.benefit: The balance of the housing provident fund account (the money remaining in their provident fund account) can be withdrawn by heirs or legatees. A legatee refers to the person named in a will to whom property is bequeathed. In the event of a work-related death, there are three separate sums of money: funeral subsidy, dependent relatives' pension, and a lump-sum work-related death grant. The Social Insurance Law explicitly stipulates that the money remaining in an individual pension insurance account can be inherited. When a participant in employee basic pension insurance dies due to illness or non-work-related causes, family members can also receive a funeral subsidy and a pension, collectively known as survivor benefits. The standards for enterprise employees are calculated according to a nationally unified formula. The funeral subsidy is 2 times the province's previous year's monthly per capita disposable income of urban residents. The pension also takes this monthly per capita income as its base and is paid for 3 to 24 months depending on the contribution years. If contribution years are under 5 years, 3 months are paid; 5 to under 10 years, 6 months; 10 to under 15 years, 9 months; for 15 years or more, 1 additional month is added for each additional year, up to a maximum of 24 months. For those who have already retired, 1 month is deducted for each year pension was received, with a minimum of 9 months.
entries.sources: State Council (2026). Regulations on the Administration of Housing Provident Funds (amended by State Council Decree No. 844, effective September 20, 2026), last paragraph of Article 24. <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2026/issue_12946/202608/content_7079363.html>: "Where an employee dies or is declared dead, the employee's heir or legatee may withdraw the deposit balance in the employee's housing provident fund account; where there is neither an heir nor a legatee, the deposit balance in the employee's housing provident fund account shall be included in the appreciation revenue of the housing provident fund."; for the three benefits under Article 39 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, see Section 19. <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1778064.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018 Amendment). Social Insurance Law (Articles 14 and 17): "Where an individual dies, the balance in the individual account may be inherited" "Where an individual participating in basic pension insurance dies of illness or from non-work-related causes, their survivors may receive a funeral subsidy and a pension." <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f135f46016f210989b9179a> (National Database of Laws and Regulations); Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, Ministry of Finance (2021). Interim Measures for Survivor Benefits under Enterprise Employee Basic Pension Insurance (Ren She Bu Fa [2021] No. 18, effective September 1, 2021, Articles 4 and 5), the original document was not published online, text verified against the verbatim citation in Administrative Reconsideration Decision of the People's Government of Huadu District, Guangzhou Municipality (Hua Du Fu Xing Fu [2022] No. 226): "The standard for funeral subsidy is calculated as 2 times the monthly per capita disposable income of urban residents in the province ... for the previous year at the time of the insured person's death" "Where the contribution years are less than 5 years, the number of months paid is 3 months ... Where the contribution years are 30 years or more, it shall be calculated as 30 years, with the maximum number of months paid being 24 months." <https://www.huadu.gov.cn/xxgk/xzfy/content/post_8672730.html>; Fujian Provincial Department of Human Resources and Social Security. Frequently Asked Questions: "For each 1 year of basic pension received, 1 month is deducted, with the minimum number of months paid being 9 months" "Where cumulative contribution years are less than 5 years, the total standard of survivor benefits (including funeral subsidy and pension) shall not exceed the sum of their individual contributions." <http://rst.fujian.gov.cn/wz/cjwt/czzgly/202311/t20231113_6294929.htm>
entries.notes: The provident fund sum is most often forgotten because it is not in a bank account and does not automatically enter estate distribution. The money remaining in the individual pension insurance account and the survivor benefits are calculated separately and issued separately; you must go to the social security service counter at the insured location to process them together. Required materials vary by locality. If contributions were paid for less than 5 years, the total survivor benefits cannot exceed the money they paid themselves. This formula comes from the measures for enterprise employee pension insurance; ask at the service counter for survivor benefits under public institutions and government agencies or urban and rural residents' pension insurance. If funeral subsidies and pensions have been deposited into their bank account, see Item 12 (Withdrawing deposits directly at the bank) for how to withdraw them. For formal requirements regarding wills and inheritance, see Section 17. If you plan to renounce inheritance to evade debts, do not withdraw this money yet; see Item 11 (Written declaration of renunciation of inheritance).

entries.title: Close relatives may request to access, copy, correct, or delete a deceased person's accounts and personal information
entries.cost: Costs nothing. You only need to file a complaint or bring a lawsuit if the platform refuses to cooperate.
entries.summary: After a person passes away, close relatives may, for their own lawful and legitimate interests, request the platform to access, copy, correct, or delete the deceased person's personal information. If the platform refuses, it must state the reasons. You can also file a lawsuit in court. There is one exception: if the deceased made other arrangements during their lifetime, such as designating an account heir or leaving clear wishes, follow their arrangements.
entries.benefit: The law clearly stipulates: upon the death of a natural person, their close relatives may, for their own lawful and legitimate interests, exercise the rights to access, copy, correct, delete, etc., the relevant personal information of the deceased. Close relatives can request the platform to display their information for inspection, provide a copy, correct errors, or delete it. Article 50 requires platforms to establish convenient application acceptance and processing mechanisms: "where a request by an individual to exercise their rights is rejected, the reasons shall be stated." If the platform refuses, "the individual may file a lawsuit with a people's court in accordance with the law."
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2021). Personal Information Protection Law. NPC.gov.cn. <http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202108/t20210820_313088.html> Article 49: "Where a natural person dies, their close relatives may, for their own lawful and legitimate interests, exercise the rights to access, copy, correct, delete, etc., provided for in this Chapter concerning the relevant personal information of the deceased; except where the deceased made other arrangements prior to death."; Article 50: "Personal information handlers shall establish convenient mechanisms for accepting and processing applications by individuals to exercise their rights. Where a request by an individual to exercise their rights is rejected, the reasons shall be stated" "The individual may file a lawsuit with a people's court in accordance with the law"
entries.notes: The legal provision includes the clause "except where the deceased made other arrangements prior to death"; if the person designated an account heir during their lifetime or left explicit wishes, follow what they left behind. Therefore, while a person is lucid, it is worth writing down where accounts and passwords should go; see Section 17. Canceling an account and deleting personal information are two different things; see Section 14.

entries.title: When a relative passes away leaving debts, heirs are only required to repay them using the inherited estate; if you do not want to assume them, make a written declaration renouncing inheritance before estate distribution
entries.cost: Writing a written declaration costs nothing. The real cost is that estate assets such as houses and bank deposits are also renounced along with it. If you accept the inheritance, creditors may sue you; you must respond to the suit and be able to produce materials showing how much the estate is worth.
entries.summary: When a person passes away, the debts they owe do not disappear along with them. However, heirs such as children and spouses are only required to repay them with the portion of the estate they inherited, and do not have to pay out of their own pockets for any shortfall. If you do not want to touch these debts, write a written declaration renouncing inheritance before the estate is divided, which also means giving up the estate entirely. Staying silent is deemed acceptance of inheritance.
entries.benefit: Article 1161 of the Civil Code: "An heir shall pay the taxes and debts that the decedent should pay according to law to the extent of the actual value of the estate obtained. The portion exceeding the actual value of the estate may be paid by the heir voluntarily, which shall not be subject to this limitation." This means: for the taxes and debts they owed, you only need to repay them with the portion of the estate you inherited. You do not need to repay the excess portion, unless you are willing to do so voluntarily. Paragraph 2 of the same Article: "Where an heir renounces inheritance, they may bear no liability for the repayment of the taxes and debts that the decedent should pay according to law." Article 1159 of the Civil Code states that dividing an estate requires first paying off the taxes and debts owed by the deceased. Article 1124 of the Civil Code: to renounce inheritance, one must "make a declaration of renouncing inheritance in writing before the estate is disposed of; if no declaration is made, it shall be deemed as acceptance of inheritance." Article 33 of Interpretation (I) of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Inheritance Book of the Civil Code: deliver the written declaration to the estate administrator or other heirs. Article 35 of the same Interpretation: renouncing after the division of the estate is not renouncing the right of inheritance, but rather property already acquired. Article 1145 of the Civil Code: heirs may elect an estate administrator; if none is elected, they jointly serve as administrators. Article 1147 of the Civil Code: the estate administrator shall take inventory of the estate, compile an estate inventory list, and handle their creditor's rights and debts. In a case in Yuzhou, Henan, the borrower died of illness in March 2023, and the children did not renounce inheritance in writing. In May 2023, the court ordered the children to repay CNY 95,000 in principal and interest within the scope of the actual value of the inherited estate. The children claimed it was unclear how much the inherited company was worth, and the judgment could not be enforced. The children's accounts and vehicles were frozen and seized, and they were placed on the restricted high-spending list. It dragged on until February 2025 before a settlement was reached, paying CNY 90,000. In a Chongqing case, the borrower died of illness before paying off the principal and interest on a CNY 400,000 loan, and all heirs declared renunciation of inheritance. However, his spouse and daughter had already withdrawn the basic pension insurance funds and occupational annuity that counted as his estate. The procuratorial organ determined that the two had not expressly renounced, which was deemed acceptance of inheritance; in November 2025, the spouse settled with the creditor and paid in full. Such debts range from tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of yuan, and the benefit is therefore rated as large
entries.sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (Articles 1064, 1124, 1145, 1147, 1153, 1159, 1161). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5c500bf>; Supreme People's Court (2020). Interpretation (I) on the Application of the Inheritance Book of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (Fa Shi [2020] No. 23, Articles 32, 33, 35). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/282091.html>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2023 Amendment). Civil Procedure Law (Articles 152, 164). <https://fgw.sh.gov.cn/ys-syjf-zc-2.4.1-h5/20240408/073febdb2b04464390546232d4089f51.html> (reposted by Shanghai Municipal Development and Reform Commission); State Council (2006). Measures on the Payment of Litigation Costs (State Council Decree No. 481, Articles 6, 29). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_6929.htm>; Song Wentao (People's Procuratorate of Yuzhou City, Henan Province) (2025-05-23). Illuminating Life with the Civil Code, Guarding Beauty | When a Borrower Suddenly Passes Away, Debts Incurred Are Not "Accounts without a Head". Procuratorial Daily, published on Supreme People's Procuratorate website. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/zdgz/202505/t20250523_696425.shtml>; Chongqing Municipal People's Procuratorate (2026-05-23). [Cases Explaining the Civil Code] Deng Chuan: Inheriting an Estate Also Requires Repaying Debts to the Extent of the Estate Acquired. <http://www.cq.jcy.gov.cn/jcdt/202605/t20260523_7740396.shtml>
entries.notes: The beneficiaries are primarily yourself, your spouse, and your children. The spouse must be calculated separately. Debts signed jointly by both parties or borrowed for daily household expenses count as joint marital debts. In this case, the spouse is personally a debtor, and renouncing inheritance will not allow them to evade it. When dividing the estate, half of the joint marital property must first be allocated to the spouse; the remainder is the estate. If you intend to renounce, do not withdraw money from their accounts yet. The provident fund balance and individual pension insurance account balance mentioned in Item 9 of this Section (Provident fund balance, social security benefits) are funds that only heirs are entitled to withdraw. The Chongqing case occurred precisely because they withdrew the money and then claimed to renounce. If renouncing inheritance causes you to be unable to fulfill statutory obligations such as supporting parents or rearing children, the renunciation is invalid. When debt collectors come knocking, first ask for proof such as IOUs and contracts, and have the other party contact the estate administrator or file a lawsuit. For any portion exceeding the estate, do not sign repayment commitments, because the law also recognizes voluntary repayments you agree to make. If actually sued, ordinary first-instance procedure is required by rule to conclude within 6 months of case filing, which may be extended; summary procedure is 3 months. Attorney fees are not included in the litigation costs borne by the losing party, so hiring a lawyer must be paid out of your own pocket. Keep good records of the estate inventory list and materials showing how much the house and deposits are worth; during enforcement, these are relied on to calculate how much you should repay. For why repaying debt with death does not work, see Section 29, Item 13 (Don't use death as debt repayment).

entries.title: When handling inheritance after a family member passes away, do not default to notarization first: deposits under CNY 50,000 in a single bank can be withdrawn directly at the bank, and real estate can be handled by all heirs going together to the real estate registration agency
entries.cost: Costs nothing. You have to visit banks where there are deposits one by one. For real estate, all heirs must be gathered to arrive at the registration counter on the same day. If someone refuses to show up or someone disagrees on how to divide it, this path will not work, and the only options are notarization or litigation.
entries.summary: If the deceased's deposits in a single bank total no more than CNY 50,000, the spouse, children, or parents can withdraw them by bringing the necessary documents, without notarization. Real estate does not strictly require notarization either; all heirs going together to the real estate registration agency can get it handled. Notarization costs money; taking Fuzhou and Xiamen as examples, real estate is charged by area, with a single property generally capped at CNY 10,000.
entries.benefit: On the deposit side, Document No. 18 issued by the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission and the People's Bank of China in 2021 stipulated that notarization is no longer required for eligible small deposits. There are three conditions. First, the total account balance in the same bank does not exceed CNY 10,000, which banks may raise on their own up to CNY 50,000. Second, the applicant is a spouse, child, or parent, or an heir or legatee designated by a notarized will. Third, the withdrawal must be made all at once, and the account canceled after withdrawal. A spouse, child, or parent must submit four items: death certificate, kinship proof materials such as a household register (hukou), marriage certificate, or birth certificate, their own identification documents, and a handwritten signed commitment letter. Jin Gui [2024] No. 6 stipulated that starting June 1, 2024, the limit was uniformly raised to CNY 50,000. Small and medium rural banks could delay implementation until December 31, 2025. Gold accumulation products as well as government bonds and wealth management products sold through banks can also be withdrawn this way upon maturity or redemption, with the amounts counted toward the CNY 50,000 limit. Funeral subsidies and pensions deposited into the account are not counted toward the CNY 50,000 limit, and spouses, children, or parents can also withdraw them using this set of documents. On the real estate side, Article 14 of the Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the Interim Regulations on Real Estate Registration: when applying for registration of inheritance or legacy, "death certificates, a will or an agreement on real estate distribution among all statutory heirs, materials proving kinship with the decedent, etc., shall be submitted; notarized materials or effective legal documents may also be submitted." Notarization is merely one optional method. In 2016, the Ministry of Justice issued a document repealing the 1991 joint circular that required strengthening notarization in real estate registration. The Fuzhou Real Estate Registration and Transaction Center explained what to do without submitting notarized materials. All statutory heirs or legatees must go together to the registration agency to verify materials and sign a written statement of commitment (a written statement guaranteeing that the materials are true). For fees, look at Fujian's standards: for inheritance notarization not involving real estate, the portion within CNY 200,000 is charged at 0.8%, with a minimum of CNY 300. Real estate is charged by area: in Fuzhou and Xiamen, no more than CNY 70 per square meter, and in principle no more than CNY 10,000 per single property. Calculating by this standard, the notarization fee for a deposit of CNY 50,000 is CNY 400, and for a 90-square-meter apartment in Fuzhou it is at most CNY 6,300. What is saved is hundreds to thousands of yuan, and the benefit is rated as medium
entries.sources: General Office of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission, General Office of the People's Bank of China (2021). Notice on Simplifying Matters Related to the Withdrawal of Small Deposits of Deceased Depositors (Yin Bao Jian Ban Fa [2021] No. 18, Articles 1, 2, 4, 5, 12). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-02/04/content_5584887.htm>; National Financial Regulatory Administration, People's Bank of China (2024). Notice on Optimizing Relevant Requirements for the Withdrawal of Small Deposits of Deceased Depositors (Jin Gui [2024] No. 6, Articles 1, 2, 4, 5, 8). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202404/content_6947875.htm>; Ministry of Natural Resources (2024 Amendment). Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the Interim Regulations on Real Estate Registration (Article 14). <https://bdcdj.fuzhou.gov.cn/zwgk/fgwj/202406/t20240618_4844825.htm> (published by Fuzhou Real Estate Registration and Transaction Center); Ministry of Justice (2016). Notice on the Repeal of the "Joint Notice of the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of Construction on Strengthening Notarization in Real Estate Registration Management" (Si Fa Tong [2016] No. 63). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2017/content_5174534.htm>; Fuzhou Real Estate Registration and Transaction Center (2019). Real Estate Inheritance Registration Cannot Be Processed Directly with Only a Will. <https://bdcdj.fuzhou.gov.cn/jdhy/zcjd/201902/t20190203_2757732.htm>; Bureau of Justice of Jin'an District, Fuzhou City (2024). How Much Does It Cost to Notarize the Right of Inheritance? (citing Min Fa Gai Fu Jia [2021] No. 533). <https://www.fzja.gov.cn/xjwz/hdjl/hdzsk/sfj/gzgl/202309/t20230919_4676656.htm>
entries.notes: The CNY 50,000 limit is calculated separately for each bank; if there are CNY 40,000 across three banks each, all three can be withdrawn this way. Amounts exceeding CNY 50,000 are not covered by these two notices; before going, ask clearly what materials that specific bank requires. It also does not apply if the depositor or applicant is a compatriot from Hong Kong, Macao, or Taiwan, a foreign national, or someone residing abroad. Having only a notarized will also does not allow direct title transfer; all statutory heirs still need to appear in person to confirm. If you plan to renounce inheritance to evade debts, do not withdraw money yet; see Item 11 (Written declaration of renunciation of inheritance). When first-order statutory heirs withdraw money, they can also request account statements for the 6 months prior to death and after death. To check other personal information, see Item 10 (Accounts and personal information). If heirs have disagreements and cannot reach an agreement, they must litigate. Ordinary first-instance procedure is required by rule to conclude within 6 months, which may be extended; attorney fees are paid out of your own pocket. Notarization fee standards differ across provinces; refer to documents from local development and reform commissions and justice departments. The CNY 50,000 limit is current as of October 2026; refer to the latest notices from the National Financial Regulatory Administration and the People's Bank of China.

chapters.title: Building a Website or Platform: Qualifications, Filings, and Servers
chapters.intro: You want to build a website or an app. This section answers four questions: what kind of business it counts as legally, which license or permit you need to obtain, where to place servers, and who is responsible for the content users post and the money they collect on it. The framing criteria are personal freedom and money. If you are an employed technical worker, see Section 11 for the red lines. For how to register a company and file taxes, see Section 12; this section will not repeat them. For the comparison table of various licenses and the decision table for selecting servers, see [docs/Licenses Required to Build a Platform.md](../docs/做平台要办哪些证.md).

entries.title: Platforms should not collect payments themselves and then transfer them to sellers; let funds settle directly through a licensed payment institution
entries.cost: Costs nothing. It requires spending some time integrating a licensed payment institution's product. A licensed payment institution is a company that has obtained a payment license from the central bank. By using its profit-sharing or escrow transaction features, the buyer's money settles directly to the seller without entering the platform's own account
entries.summary: If a buyer's money enters your account first and you then transfer it to the seller, that means you are engaging in payment business. Operating this line of business requires approval from the People's Bank of China, as well as actually providing CNY 100 million in capital. Doing this without approval will get you shut down, your earnings confiscated, and fined; the business owner and handlers will be fined separately, and serious cases may even lead to criminal sentencing. There is only one safe approach: never let the money enter your account.
entries.benefit: Payment business as defined by regulations refers to "transferring monetary funds in accordance with electronic payment instructions submitted by payees or payers." Put simply, it means transferring money on behalf of others according to someone else's instructions. To engage in this business, one "shall obtain approval from the People's Bank of China and acquire a payment business permit." The registered capital must be at least 100 million yuan, and it must be paid-in monetary capital—this 100 million yuan must be real money transferred into the company's account. "Anyone who, without lawful approval, establishes a non-bank payment institution without authorization, or engages in or engages in payment business in disguised form, shall be banned by the People's Bank of China in accordance with the law, and the illegal gains shall be confiscated." Those who do this without approval will be shut down directly, and whatever money was earned will be confiscated. If the illegal gains are 500,000 yuan or more, an additional fine of 1 to 5 times the illegal gains will be imposed. If there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than 500,000 yuan, a fine of 500,000 to 2 million yuan will be imposed. The legal representative and directly responsible personnel will be fined an additional 100,000 to 500,000 yuan. The Criminal Law also classifies "illegally engaging in fund payment and settlement business" as illegal business operations. In serious circumstances, the sentence is fixed-term imprisonment of not more than 5 years; in particularly serious circumstances, the sentence is fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 5 years. What counts as "serious circumstances" has a threshold drawn in the judicial interpretation by the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate. That threshold is an illegal business operation amount of 5 million yuan or more, or illegal gains of 100,000 yuan or more (Nationwide, effective May 2024)
entries.sources: State Council (2023). Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Non-Bank Payment Institutions (State Council Decree No. 768, Articles 2, 6, 8, 27, 47). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2024/issue_11086/202401/content_6924970.html> ; People's Bank of China (2024). Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Non-Bank Payment Institutions (People's Bank of China Order [2024] No. 4, Article 68). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2024/issue_11546/202408/content_6970979.html> ; National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Article 225, Item 3). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml> ; Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate (2019). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Illegally Engaging in Fund Payment and Settlement Business and Illegally Trading Foreign Exchange (Articles 1, 3, 4). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbt/201901/t20190131_407161.shtml>
entries.notes: Designing the money flow so that funds do not enter your account is the only safe and prudent approach. In the market, this kind of collecting and paying on behalf of others is commonly called "secondary settlement" (erqing), but this term does not appear in official documents. The term used in the implementation rules is "engaging in payment business in disguised form," which means transferring money on behalf of others based on user instructions without approval. That interpretation from the Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate only lists three circumstances: cashing out by fabricating fictitious transactions, cashing out using entity accounts, and cashing out using checks. It does not explicitly single out platform collection and payment on behalf of others, so one cannot say that platform collection and payment on behalf of others "definitely constitutes a crime."

entries.title: Most websites that charge fees require a license; those selling their own goods without allowing third-party merchants to onboard do not; facilitating transactions requires another category of license; free websites only require ICP filing
entries.cost: Filing does not cost money. A Value-Added Telecommunications Business Operating License costs money; it governs "whether a website that charges users money can operate." To apply for this license, you must first have a company. For operations within a single province, the registered capital must be no less than 1 million yuan. For cross-provincial operations, it must be no less than 10 million yuan. The review period is 60 days, and the license is valid for 5 years
entries.summary: Websites that collect money from users mostly need to obtain a Value-Added Telecommunications Business Operating License first, and individuals cannot obtain this license. The Guangdong Communications Administration replied: those who only sell goods on their own website or App and do not allow third-party merchants to set up shop do not need to obtain it. Those who only operate WeChat or Alipay mini-programs or online storefronts also do not need to. Opening a site and collecting money without obtaining the required license will lead to confiscation of income plus fines, and in serious cases, site shutdown.
entries.benefit: The statutory text states: "The State implements a licensing system for commercial Internet information services; and implements a filing system for non-commercial Internet information services. Those who have not obtained a license or have not completed filing formalities shall not engage in Internet information services." Those collecting money must obtain a license first, and those not collecting money must file first; if you have neither, you cannot launch the site. What counts as commercial? Regulations define it as "service activities that provide information or webpage production and other services to online users for compensation via the Internet." In plain terms, it means collecting money from users. The category that facilitates transactions is called Online Data Processing and Transaction Processing services, abbreviated in the industry as EDI. Regulations define it as "the business of utilizing various data and transaction/affair processing application platforms connected to public communications networks or the Internet to provide users with online data processing and transaction/affair processing via public communications networks or the Internet." It also "includes transaction processing services, electronic data interchange services, and network/electronic equipment data processing services." This refers to websites processing data online on behalf of users, or facilitating and processing transactions between buyers and sellers. Operating without obtaining a license, or operating beyond the authorized business scope, will result in confiscation of illegal gains plus an additional fine of 3 to 5 times the illegal gains. Operating beyond scope means having a license, but conducting activities that exceed the scope written on the license. If there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than 50,000 yuan, a fine of 100,000 to 1 million yuan will be imposed. In serious circumstances, an order to shut down the website will be issued (Nationwide). Collecting money does not necessarily mean you must obtain a license. A Q&A released by the Guangdong Communications Administration in October 2025 stated that per Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) requirements, the following three scenarios do not require this license. First scenario: an enterprise "directly sells its own or other enterprises' goods or services in a self-operated manner" on its own website or App, and has no other entities or individuals onboarded to open shops. Second scenario: an enterprise only posts its own information on its own website or App, without providing a platform for others to publish information. Third scenario: an enterprise conducts business solely relying on mini-programs, official accounts, video channels, or online shops on platforms like WeChat and Alipay, "and has no other independently operated platform." Conversely, as long as you let others onboard to open shops or allow users to publish information on your platform, you are not covered by these three exceptions
entries.sources: Guangdong Communications Administration (2025). Frequently Asked Questions on Applying for Value-Added Telecommunications Business Operating Licenses (October 17, 2025, Item 1). <https://gdca.miit.gov.cn/bsfw/bszn/jyxk/tzgg/art/2025/art_6bcbfa4f041247868c0de08e765b33e9.html> ; State Council (2000). Measures for the Administration of Internet Information Services (State Council Decree No. 292, second revision on December 6, 2024, Articles 3, 4, 7, 19). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1860864.htm> ; State Council (2024). Decision on Amending and Repealing Certain Administrative Regulations (State Council Decree No. 797, Item 18). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2025/issue_11786/202501/content_6997034.html> ; State Council (2000). Telecommunications Regulations (second revision in 2016, Articles 7, 9, 13, 69). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2016/content_5139478.htm> ; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (2017). Measures for the Administration of Telecommunications Business Operating Licenses (MIIT Order No. 42, Articles 6, 9, 11, 14). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2017/content_5240090.htm>
entries.notes: Whether what you plan to do falls under the EDI category is something you must match against the definitions in the "Telecommunications Business Classification Catalog" yourself. There is not a single sentence from official sources stating outright that "e-commerce platforms with matchmaking and fund processing must obtain an EDI license." The MIIT administrative service guide merely says "apply for the corresponding telecommunications business operating license according to business boundaries." Therefore, whether you need to apply can only be judged by matching against the definition yourself. Another point: individuals cannot obtain this license; the applicant must be a legally established company. The three scenarios where self-operation does not require a license originate from the Guangdong Communications Administration's Q&A. The Q&A explicitly states this is per MIIT requirements, but identical public text has not been found in other provinces. If unsure, call your local communications administration first. This Q&A also reminds that there is no need to hire an intermediary to apply for the license; simply submit materials on the MIIT "Telecommunications Business Market Comprehensive Management Information System," and the government charges no fees

entries.title: Live streaming requires an Online Culture Operating License; that audiovisual program license is basically unobtainable for private companies
entries.cost: The Online Culture Operating License is colloquially called the "Wangwen license"; it governs "whether one can make money from online performances such as live streaming and gaming commentary." It is approved by provincial-level cultural administrative departments, with results issued within 20 days of acceptance, valid for 3 years, and renewed 30 days before expiration. The audiovisual program license governs "whether one can broadcast programs online," and it requires applicants to be wholly state-owned or state-controlled entities
entries.summary: Conducting live streaming or gaming commentary requires an Online Culture Operating License issued by the provincial cultural department, and the business scope must explicitly specify online performances. Results are issued within 20 days of acceptance, and the license is valid for 3 years. Streamed video archives must be retained by yourself for a full 60 days. Launching without obtaining a license will result in an order to cease, a warning, and a fine of up to 30,000 yuan; refusing to stop leads to blacklisting.
entries.benefit: Entities conducting online performances must obtain a license first. The statutory text states: "shall, in accordance with the 'Interim Provisions on the Administration of Internet Culture', apply to the provincial-level cultural administrative department to obtain an 'Online Culture Operating License', and the business scope of the license shall explicitly include online performances." Playing games for an audience to watch or providing commentary is also regulated under this framework; the regulatory text says "managed with reference to these Measures." For all online performance video materials, "the retention period shall not be less than 60 days," meaning you must personally keep streamed videos for a full 60 days. Those engaging in commercial Internet cultural activities without approval shall be ordered to cease, given a warning, and fined up to 30,000 yuan. Those who still do not stop after being ordered will be placed on the cultural market blacklist. Broadcasting programs online requires a different license: one "shall obtain an 'Information Network Dissemination of Audiovisual Programs License'." The applicant must "possess legal person status and be a wholly state-owned or state-controlled entity"; it must be a fully state-owned or state-holding entity, which is basically impossible for private companies to obtain. Conducting activities without this license results in a warning, an order to rectify, and an optional fine of up to 30,000 yuan. Under serious circumstances, penalties are imposed in accordance with regulations on the administration of radio and television (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Ministry of Culture (2016). Measures for the Administration of Online Performance Business Activities (Wenshifa [2016] No. 33, Articles 2, 4, 6, 13, 20). <https://zwgk.mct.gov.cn/zfxxgkml/scgl/202012/t20201206_918194.html> ; Ministry of Culture (2011). Interim Provisions on the Administration of Internet Culture (Ministry of Culture Order No. 51, revised by Ministry of Culture Order No. 57 in 2017, Articles 7, 8, 9, 16, 21, 28). <https://zwgk.mct.gov.cn/zfxxgkml/zcfg/bmgz/202012/t20201204_905340.html> ; State Administration of Radio, Film, and Television, Ministry of Information Industry (2007). Provisions on the Administration of Internet Audiovisual Program Services (Decree No. 56, revised in 2015, Articles 2, 7, 8, 24). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2022-08/23/content_5722664.htm> ; Cyberspace Administration of China and seven other departments (2021). Guiding Opinions on Strengthening the Standardized Administration of Online Live Streaming (Guoxinbanfawen [2021] No. 3, Item 9). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-02/10/content_5586472.htm>
entries.notes: Which license matches which business is stated most clearly in that seven-department document. Platforms that make money through live streaming require an Online Culture License plus an ICP filing—ICP filing being the registration procedure for websites with the MIIT. Those broadcasting programs online require an audiovisual license, or must complete registration. Those publishing news require an Internet News Information Service License. In addition, the "Interim Provisions on the Administration of Internet Culture" republished by the State Council website (www.gov.cn) in 2025 displayed the unrevised 2011 original text. Citations should take the current text from the Ministry of Culture and Tourism as authoritative

entries.title: Placing servers within mainland China requires filing; Apps and mini-programs also require filing before launch; access providers must themselves hold a value-added telecommunications license
entries.cost: Filing does not cost money. It is submitted alongside the server via the service provider, usually taking from several days to several weeks. Filing for Apps and mini-programs is submitted via service providers or app stores, and is completed within 20 working days once materials are complete. Checking once whether a service provider possesses qualifications takes only ten minutes
entries.summary: If servers are located within mainland China, filing must be done before launching the site; it does not cost money and generally takes several days to several weeks. Operating without filing results first in an order to rectify and a 10,000-yuan fine; refusing to rectify leads to site shutdown. Apps and mini-programs must also be filed in advance; app stores and mini-program platforms are forbidden from listing unfiled ones.
entries.benefit: The statutory text states: "Without filing, no one may engage in non-commercial Internet information services within the territory of the People's Republic of China." Websites that do not charge users money must also file first, as long as they are hosted within the territory. Those operating without filing shall be ordered to rectify within a specified period and fined 10,000 yuan. Those refusing to rectify will have their websites closed down. The service provider that helps connect your server to the Internet is also regulated: it "shall not provide Internet access services for organizations or individuals that have not completed filing to engage in non-commercial Internet information services." The same applies to service providers that collect money on your behalf. Regulations state that such service providers "shall not provide access, billing collection, or other services to entities or individuals that have not legally obtained an operating license or performed non-commercial Internet information service filing formalities." This means that for sites without a license and without a filing, compliant service providers are prohibited from taking them on. Furthermore, server room colocation and cloud hosting are termed Internet Data Center services in regulations, while broadband access is termed Internet Access Services. These two themselves require licenses, so the service provider must possess a license first. Those failing to display the filing number on the website homepage shall be ordered to rectify and fined 5,000 to 50,000 yuan. Apps and mini-programs must also be filed starting from September 2023. An MIIT notice states that App sponsors providing services in the mainland who "have not fulfilled filing formalities shall not engage in APP Internet information services." Distribution platforms include mini-program platforms. The notice requires app stores, mini-program platforms, and smartphone manufacturers "not to provide network access, distribution, pre-installation, or other services for APPs that have not fulfilled filing formalities." Once the provincial communications administration receives complete and accurate materials, "it shall grant filing within twenty working days." The filing number must be marked in a prominent position within the App. The Anti-Telecom and Online Fraud Law also explicitly provides that establishing an App "shall involve completing licensing or filing formalities with telecommunications competent departments in accordance with relevant state regulations" (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Ministry of Information Industry (2005). Measures for the Administration of Non-Commercial Internet Information Services Filing (MII Order No. 33, revised by MIIT Order No. 68 in 2024, Articles 5, 13, 18, 22). <https://www.miit.gov.cn/gyhxxhb/jgsj/cyzcyfgs/bmgz/xxtxl/art/2024/art_84a0cfa0ebd049bbbe751dca9a008e56.html> ; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (2017). Measures for the Administration of Telecommunications Business Operating Licenses (MIIT Order No. 42, Articles 20, 24). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2017/content_5240090.htm> ; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (2015). Telecommunications Business Classification Catalog (2015 Edition, B11, B14, B21, B25). <https://www.miit.gov.cn/zwgk/zcwj/wjfb/tg/art/2020/art_e98406cd89844f7e92ea1bcf3b5301e0.html> ; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (2023). Notice on Carrying Out the Filing Work for Mobile Internet Applications (MIIT Xin Guan [2023] No. 105, Part II Items 1, 7, 8, 9, Part III Item 2). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202308/content_6897341.htm> ; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2022). Anti-Telecom and Online Fraud Law (Article 23). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202209/t20220902_575631.shtml>
entries.notes: Check whether the service provider holds a license before negotiating prices. To check licenses, use the MIIT Telecommunications Business Market Comprehensive Management Information System tsm.miit.gov.cn, searching by the full company name or license number. To check website filings, use beian.miit.gov.cn. For an "unlicensed server room," if something goes wrong one day, you won't even know whom to file a complaint against. For websites that have already completed filing, App filing only requires supplementing the App's information without refilling the sponsor's identity details. Placing a website's servers outside the mainland can indeed bypass website filing, but Apps wishing to be listed on domestic Chinese app stores cannot bypass it. When users are in the mainland and money is in the mainland, not a single one of the obligations described in Items 5 through 10 of this section can be skipped, and an extra layer of cross-border data transfer costs is added

entries.title: If you allow users to sell things on your platform, the platform must verify and register them, submit information, and retain records for three years
entries.cost: Does not cost money. You need to verify seller qualifications in the backend and establish a registration archive. Submit tax-related information once every quarter, and retain transaction data for three years. The difficulty lies in the fact that it is ongoing work year-round, not something done just once
entries.summary: If you allow others to sell things on your platform, you must first verify the seller's identity, address, contact information, and administrative licenses, and then register and archive them. Once archived, re-verify at least once every six months. Who the sellers are must be reported to market regulation, and tax-related details must be reported to tax authorities quarterly; product and transaction records must be kept for three years. Missing any item leads first to an order to rectify; failing to rectify incurs a fine of 20,000 to 100,000 yuan.
entries.benefit: The law imposes a set of requirements on platforms. The statutory text states that they "shall require operators applying to enter the platform to sell goods or provide services to submit real information such as their identity, address, contact details, and administrative licenses, verify and register such information, establish registration archives, and regularly verify and update them." Before sellers enter the platform, they must submit their identity, address, contact details, and the administrative licenses they should hold. You must verify them once, register and establish an archive, and check back to re-verify at regular intervals thereafter. How long is "regularly"? Departmental rules specify it in more detail: "verify and update at least once every six months." You must also submit the identity information of platform operators to market regulation departments. Reports must also be submitted to taxation authorities; the statutory text states: "in accordance with the provisions of tax collection and administration laws and administrative regulations, submit the identity information of platform operators and tax-related information to taxation departments." Thus, who the sellers are must be reported to market regulation, and seller identities and tax situations must be reported to taxation authorities. For commodity and service information and transaction information, "the retention period shall be not less than three years from the date of completion of the transaction," meaning data must be kept for at least three years starting from the day a transaction is completed. Failure to fulfill any of the above items will result in an order to rectify within a specified time limit. Those failing to rectify within the time limit will be fined 20,000 to 100,000 yuan. In serious circumstances, an order to suspend business for rectification will be issued, along with an additional fine of 100,000 to 500,000 yuan.
