Tax-related information must be submitted "within the month following the end of each quarter," meaning it must be submitted in the month immediately following the conclusion of each quarter. Penalties for failing to report on time are the same (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). E-Commerce Law (Articles 10, 27, 28, 31, 80). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf8af050b81> ; State Administration for Market Regulation (2021). Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Online Transactions (SAMR Order No. 37, Articles 8, 24, 25, 31). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2021/content_5602020.htm> ; State Council (2025). Provisions on the Submission of Tax-Related Information by Internet Platform Enterprises (State Council Decree No. 810, Articles 2, 3, 4, 10). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2025/issue_12146/202507/content_7030983.html> ; State Taxation Administration (2025). Announcement on Matters Concerning the Submission of Tax-Related Information by Internet Platform Enterprises (STA Announcement [2025] No. 15). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202506/content_7029727.htm>
entries.notes: Sellers themselves must also go through market entity registration. The law lists several categories that do not require registration: "individuals selling self-produced agricultural and sideline products or household handicraft products, and individuals using their own skills to engage in convenience labor activities and sporadic, small-amount transaction activities that do not require a license according to law." "Sporadic, small-amount" has a specific figure: Article 8 of the Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Online Transactions sets it at an annual transaction volume of 100,000 yuan. The platform still has two more things to do: separately mark registered and unregistered sellers, and never delete consumer reviews.

entries.title: You must manage user-generated content: review mechanisms, reporting portals, immediately halt transmission and report upon discovering violations
entries.cost: Hiring human reviewers costs money; this is a platform's largest long-term expense. Audit trails must be maintained for the reporting portal and every action taken. The difficulty lies in requiring daily monitoring; a single day's lapse can lead to trouble.
entries.summary: The platform is responsible for managing what users post. Systems must be established for registration, post review, comment review, daily patrols, and incident handling. Place a reporting portal in a prominent spot on the page. Upon spotting illegal information, halt its transmission immediately, preserve records, and report to the competent authorities. Failure to do so can lead to fines ranging from 50,000 to 500,000 yuan, or even more in severe cases.
entries.benefit: Regulations state that platforms "shall fulfill the primary responsibility for information content management," meaning the platform itself is responsible for managing user-posted material. Specifically, it must "soundly establish systems for user registration, account management, information release review, follow-up comment review, page layout ecology management, real-time patrolling, emergency response, and handling of online rumors and black-market industry chain information." From registration, posting, and comments to routine patrols and emergency response, every step must have documented rules. Platforms "shall also set up a convenient complaint and reporting entrance in a prominent location"; the reporting button must be positioned where users can see and click it at a glance. Upon discovering illegal information, platforms "shall immediately take disposal measures according to law, preserve relevant records, and report to the competent authorities." The Cybersecurity Law is even more specific. Its exact wording is: "Upon discovering information whose publication or transmission is prohibited by laws or administrative regulations, transmission of that information shall be immediately halted, disposal measures such as removal taken to prevent information diffusion, relevant records preserved, and a report made to the relevant competent authorities." Failure to comply results in orders for rectification, warnings, public reprimand, and optional fines of 50,000 to 500,000 yuan. For refusal to rectify or under severe circumstances, fines range from 500,000 to 2,000,000 yuan. Platforms may also be ordered to suspend business for rectification, shut down websites or applications, or have permits or business licenses revoked. Directly responsible personnel face separate fines of 50,000 to 200,000 yuan (Nationwide).
entries.sources: Cyberspace Administration of China (2019). Provisions on the Ecological Governance of Online Information Content (CAC Order No. 5, Arts. 8, 9, 10, 16, 37). <http://www.cac.gov.cn/2019-12/20/c_1578375159509309.htm> ; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2025). Cybersecurity Law (2025 Amendment, effective Jan. 1, 2026, Arts. 49, 69). <https://www.cac.gov.cn/2025-12/29/c_1768735112911946.htm> ; State Council (2000). Measures for the Administration of Internet Information Services (Arts. 15, 16, 23). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1860864.htm>
entries.notes: You do not need to invent review rules yourself; just copy the official ones. Which nine categories of content are prohibited is clearly listed in Article 15 of the Measures for the Administration of Internet Information Services. Those doing livestreams have three additional obligations: "establish a livestreaming content review platform," be able to cut off an active livestream at any time (the statutory term for this is "real-time blocking"), and retain livestream content and logs for 60 days. Video materials for online performances must likewise be kept for no less than 60 days.

entries.title: Providing information publishing or instant messaging services requires demanding real identity information from users
entries.cost: Requires integrating a real-name verification gateway, which charges per verification. Design the product around "real-name behind the scenes, voluntary up front": store the real name in the backend while displaying a nickname on the page.
entries.summary: If your website allows posting or chatting, you must collect the user's real identity information when they set up the service. If they refuse to provide it, you cannot let them use the service. Livestream regulations require backend real-name storage while leaving frontend nicknames up to the user, with verification possible via mobile phone number. Failure to enforce real-name verification results first in an order to rectify; failure to rectify brings fines of 50,000 to 500,000 yuan, along with potential site shutdown.
entries.benefit: The exact wording of the law is: "When network operators handle network access or domain name registration services for users, process network access procedures for fixed-line or mobile phones, or provide users with information publishing, instant messaging, and other services, they shall require users to provide real identity information when signing agreements with users or confirming the provision of services. Where a user does not provide real identity information, the network operator shall not provide them with relevant services." If you fail to demand real-name verification, or if a user fails to provide real identity details and you let them use the service anyway, you will be ordered to rectify. Refusal to rectify or severe circumstances incur fines of 50,000 to 500,000 yuan. You may also be ordered to suspend relevant operations, suspend business for rectification, shut down websites or applications, or face revocation of permits or business licenses. Directly responsible personnel face separate fines of 10,000 to 100,000 yuan. Livestreaming services follow the principle of "real-name behind the scenes, voluntary up front," conducting "real identity information authentication based on mobile phone numbers and other methods." This means the platform backend stores the user's real name, the nickname displayed on the page is up to the user, and verification relies on methods such as mobile phone numbers. Requirements for livestream e-commerce are stricter, requiring "real identity information authentication based on identity documents, Unified Social Credit Codes, and other credentials." The Unified Social Credit Code is the registration number on a business license (Nationwide).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2025). Cybersecurity Law (2025 Amendment, effective Jan. 1, 2026, Arts. 26, 64; in the 2016 text, Arts. 24, 61). <https://www.cac.gov.cn/2025-12/29/c_1768735112911946.htm> ; Cyberspace Administration of China (2016). Provisions on the Administration of Internet Livestreaming Services (Arts. 12, 16). <https://www.cac.gov.cn/2016-11/04/c_1119847629.htm> ; Seven Departments including the CAC (2021). Measures for the Administration of Online Livestreaming Marketing (Trial) (CAC Issuance [2021] No. 5, Art. 8). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-04/23/content_5601682.htm>
entries.notes: The article numbers have shifted. The Cybersecurity Law was amended in 2025 and takes effect on January 1, 2026. The real-name verification article moved from Article 24 to Article 26, and penalty provisions moved from Article 61 to Article 64. The statutory text itself remains unchanged. If materials in your possession still cite the old article numbers, update them.

entries.title: Do not open livestream accounts for individuals under 16; manage tipping in tiers by age
entries.cost: Zero monetary cost. Add a check at registration and another at payment: first verify the age, then confirm parental or guardian consent.
entries.summary: Those under 16 years of age cannot register a broadcasting account on your platform. Those aged 16 and older must verify their identity and obtain the consent of parents or other guardians. Tipping is divided into three tiers: under 8 cannot tip; ages 8 to 16 require guardian consent; ages 16 and older require guardian consent or verified proof of income. If a child tips behind their guardian's back and the guardian demands a refund, courts will order it returned.
entries.benefit: The exact wording of the law is: "Online livestreaming service providers shall not provide online livestream broadcaster account registration services to minors under the age of sixteen; when providing online livestream broadcaster account registration services to minors who have reached the age of sixteen, they shall verify their identity information and obtain the consent of their parents or other guardians." The regulations also require "establishing a dynamic verification mechanism for the real identity information of online livestream broadcasters," meaning you must be capable of re-verifying a broadcaster's identity at any time. Additionally, platforms must "reasonably limit the single consumption amount and daily cumulative consumption amount of minors of different age groups when using their services," setting single-transaction and daily spending caps for minors based on age. Virtual tipping is currently divided into three tiers: "Tipping services shall not be provided to minors under eight years of age. Providing tipping services to minors aged eight to sixteen shall require the consent of their guardians. Providing tipping services to minors aged sixteen and older shall require the consent of their guardians or verification of their proof of income." Furthermore: where a person with limited capacity for civil conduct sends virtual tips without guardian consent and the guardian requests the money back, the court shall support it, and the funds can be recovered. A person with limited capacity for civil conduct refers to a minor who legally cannot yet make entirely independent decisions (Nationwide).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2020). Law on the Protection of Minors (Arts. 74, 76). <https://www.cac.gov.cn/2020-10/22/c_1604928959588622.htm> ; State Council (2023). Regulations on the Online Protection of Minors (State Council Order No. 766, Arts. 31, 44). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2023/issue_10806/202311/content_6913813.html> ; Secretariat of the Cyberspace Administration of China (2026). Notice on Strengthening the Standardized Management of Online Livestreaming Tipping (Item 7). <https://www.cac.gov.cn/2026-04/13/c_1777815804150225.htm> ; Supreme People's Court (2020). Guiding Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Lawful and Proper Trial of Civil Cases Involving the COVID-19 Epidemic (II) (Fa Fa [2020] No. 17, Art. 9). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/230181.html>
entries.notes: If a refund dispute actually arises, resolve it in the manner most favorable to the minor. The rules on this matter have changed over time. The 2022 Four-Department Opinions and the NRTA's 2020 Notice both stated that minors were categorically prohibited from tipping. The new April 2026 notice shifted to age-based tiers at 8 and 16 years old, yet it did not explicitly state that the previous two documents were repealed, nor did authorities clarify how the policies interface. Therefore, the statement "minors are categorically prohibited from tipping" is currently inaccurate.

entries.title: Handle infringement notices promptly; reinstate content if no follow-up occurs within 15 days of forwarding the non-infringement statement
entries.cost: Zero monetary cost. Establish a standard workflow: receive notice, forward to seller, receive seller's counter-statement, publicly announce the outcome. Archive every step.
entries.summary: If someone sends an infringement notice accompanied by preliminary evidence, you must promptly delete, block, or disconnect links to the material, while forwarding the notice to the seller. If you stall, you will share joint liability with the seller for any expanded losses. If the seller submits a counter-statement, forward it to the claimant and wait 15 days. If the claimant neither files an administrative complaint nor sues in court, restore the content.
entries.benefit: Rights holders "have the right to notify e-commerce platform operators to take necessary measures such as deletion, blocking, disconnecting links, and terminating transactions and services. The notice shall include preliminary evidence of infringement." A rights holder is the owner of rights such as trademarks, copyrights, or patents. Sending just a bare assertion does not count; preliminary evidence must be attached. Upon receiving a notice, the platform "shall promptly take necessary measures and forward the notice to the on-platform business operator; failure to take necessary measures promptly shall result in joint and several liability with the on-platform business operator for the expanded portion of the damages." If you stall and fail to handle it, you must compensate the additional damages alongside the seller. After the seller counters, if the platform "does not receive notice within fifteen days after the forwarded statement reaches the intellectual property rights holder that the rights holder has filed a complaint or lawsuit, it shall promptly terminate the measures taken." This means forwarding the seller's counter-statement to the rights holder and waiting 15 days. If the claimant neither lodges an administrative complaint nor brings a lawsuit, restore what was deleted or taken down. If a platform knows or should have known of an infringement but fails to act, it bears joint and several liability with the infringer. Intellectual property authorities may also order you to rectify within a specified time limit; failure to rectify brings fines of 50,000 to 500,000 yuan, or 500,000 to 2,000,000 yuan in severe cases. Conversely, "where a false notice is sent maliciously, causing losses to an on-platform business operator, double liability for compensation shall be borne" (Nationwide).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). E-Commerce Law (Arts. 42, 43, 44, 45, 84). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf8af050b81> ; National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Arts. 1195, 1196, 1197). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/233181.html>
entries.notes: If you are not an e-commerce platform but an ordinary website, follow the notice-and-takedown rules in the Civil Code. The distinction lies in how long you must wait after the counter-statement: the E-Commerce Law gives a definite 15 days, whereas the Civil Code specifies only a "reasonable period." Furthermore, publicly announcing received notices, seller counter-statements, and your disposition results is an explicit statutory requirement under Article 44 of the E-Commerce Law. If the platform itself organizes the uploading of pirated materials or knowingly allows infringements to persist unchecked, the "delete upon notice" safe harbor will not protect it. See Section 9, Item 24 (translating foreign comics, reposting movies and TV series).

entries.title: Do not casually transfer user information overseas; cross-border data transfers carry statutory conditions and headcount thresholds
entries.cost: Zero monetary cost. The simplest approach is keeping user data within the country. If overseas transmission is truly necessary, use standard contracts or certification.
entries.summary: Transferring domestic users' information to overseas machines is considered a cross-border data transfer, and the same applies if servers are located abroad. Generally, you must pass a CAC security assessment, obtain certification, or sign a standard contract. If the annual cumulative total is under 100,000 individuals and contains no sensitive information, all three requirements are waived. You must also disclose to users who receives it abroad and what it will be used for, and obtain their separate consent.
entries.benefit: Providing domestic users' information to foreign companies or storing it on overseas machines is legally termed providing personal information across borders, and "shall satisfy" one of four conditions: first, passing a security assessment organized by cyberspace authorities; second, obtaining personal information protection certification from a specialized institution; third, executing a contract with the overseas recipient in accordance with standard contracts formulated by cyberspace authorities; fourth, other conditions stipulated by laws or administrative regulations. At the same time, you must inform users of the following: the overseas recipient's name, contact details, processing purposes, processing methods, types of personal information, and procedures for exercising their statutory rights. Furthermore, you must "obtain the separate consent of the individual," asking the user specifically about this matter. Specific thresholds are tiered by cumulative headcounts. Ordinary enterprises are referred to in regulations as data processors other than critical information infrastructure operators. These enterprises have an exemption line, verbatim: "where personal information of fewer than 100,000 individuals (excluding sensitive personal information) has been provided overseas accumulatively since January 1 of the current year." If you stay below this threshold, declaring an assessment, entering standard contracts, and undergoing certification are all waived. For 100,000 or more but fewer than 1,000,000 individuals, a standard contract must be executed or certification passed. For 1,000,000 or more individuals, or where sensitive personal information reaches 10,000 or more individuals, a security assessment must be declared (Nationwide, starting March 2024).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2021). Personal Information Protection Law (Arts. 38, 39, 40). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202108/t20210820_527244.shtml> ; Cyberspace Administration of China (2024). Provisions on Promoting and Regulating Cross-Border Data Flows (CAC Order No. 16, Arts. 3, 4, 5, 7, 8). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2024/issue_11366/202405/content_6954192.html> ; Cyberspace Administration of China (2022). Measures for the Security Assessment of Outbound Data Transfers (CAC Order No. 11, Art. 4). <https://www.cac.gov.cn/2022-07/07/c_1658811536396503.htm>
entries.notes: Locating servers overseas does not mean "data has not left the country." If a user registers domestically and you transmit their information to machines abroad, that constitutes a cross-border transfer. One category does not need to go through security assessments, certification, or standard contracts: cross-border shopping, cross-border shipping, and booking flights or hotels, as these are genuinely necessary "for the conclusion or performance of a contract to which the individual is a contracting party." Also pay attention to how headcounts are tallied: it is calculated as "accumulated since January 1 of the current year," not counting back twelve months from today.

entries.title: When choosing a server, first evaluate downtime tolerance, then check for maintenance staff, and compare prices only at the end
entries.cost: Cloud hosts from mainstream cloud providers cost hundreds to thousands of yuan per month. VPS from small providers starts from dozens of yuan per month. A VPS is simply a small virtual server. Dedicated server colocation starts from several thousand yuan per year, and you must purchase the hardware yourself.
entries.summary: The difference between the three tiers is not the price, but what you have in hand when disaster strikes. Major providers offer ICP filing channels, published qualifications, incident announcements, contractual compensation clauses, and accessible support. Small providers are half the price, but when they oversell, pull an exit scam, or get blocked upstream, you will not even know whom to contact. For static sites without user data, a VPS costing dozens of yuan is sufficient.
entries.benefit: The difference between the three tiers is not the price, but what you have in hand when disaster strikes. Mainstream cloud vendors provide ICP filing channels, open qualifications, public incident notices, contractual compensation clauses, and reachable staff. Small providers can be half the price, but when they oversell, vanish, or get blocked by upstream providers, you have no avenue for grievance. Therefore, before negotiating prices, check the MIIT system to see if they hold a Value-Added Telecommunications Business Operating License. Dedicated server colocation is cost-effective only when two conditions are met simultaneously: bandwidth or hardware costs are substantially cheaper, and you have in-house personnel handling operations and maintenance. How to choose: for static sites with no user data, the cheapest VPS is plenty. For sites with user registration and transactions, choose cloud hosts capable of elastic scaling and snapshot backups, keeping backups in at least two separate locations.
entries.sources: Author's experience, no direct literature; for statutory requirements on provider qualifications and ICP filing, see Item 4 of this section; for 6-month log retention and Multi-Level Protection Scheme (MLPS) obligations, see Section 11, Item 16.
entries.notes: The above is empirical judgment, lacking literature-based evidence. The only thing you can truly verify is the provider's license. If you want to cut costs, save on configuration and bandwidth—do not skimp on credentials.

entries.title: If user information on your website or App leaks, take immediate remediation, notify users and competent authorities, and report to public security if under attack
entries.cost: Zero monetary cost. Draft an incident contingency response plan in advance: who makes final decisions, which loophole to plug first, and how user notices should be worded. The difficulty lies in the initial instinct to cover it up and keep users in the dark when disaster strikes.
entries.summary: If user information leaks or may leak, take immediate remedial action and notify the competent authorities and affected users. Covering it up and failing to report leads first to an order to rectify; failure to rectify brings fines up to 1,000,000 yuan, or up to 50,000,000 yuan in severe cases. If users suffer harm as a result and you cannot prove lack of fault, you must compensate them. Those who implement safeguards, handle incidents according to contingency plans, and report promptly may be granted leniency or exempted from liability depending on circumstances.
entries.benefit: The exact wording of the Personal Information Protection Law is: "Where personal information leakage, tampering, or loss has occurred or is likely to occur, personal information processors shall immediately take remedial measures and notify departments fulfilling personal information protection duties and individuals." The notification must state three things: what categories of information were leaked, the causes, and the potential harm; what remedial measures you have taken and what users themselves can do to mitigate the harm; and your contact information. If your remedial measures can genuinely avert harm, you may refrain from notifying users. However, if the competent authorities deem that harm may be caused, they have the power to require you to notify. The Regulations on Network Data Security Management state that notifications may be made by "telephone, SMS, instant messaging tools, email, public announcements, or other means." If leads suspecting criminal offences are discovered during handling, reports must be made to public security organs and state security organs. Failure to perform these obligations shall result in an order to make corrections, a warning, and confiscation of unlawful gains; non-compliant apps may be ordered to suspend or terminate services. For refusal to make corrections, a fine of up to 1 million yuan shall be imposed, and directly responsible persons shall be fined 10,000 to 100,000 yuan. Where circumstances are serious, a fine of up to 50 million yuan or up to 5% of the previous year's annual turnover shall be imposed, and persons in charge shall be fined 100,000 to 1 million yuan. In civil law, if a user suffers damage as a result, if you "cannot prove that you are not at fault, you shall bear tort liability such as compensation for damages." Large-scale leaks must also be reported within specified time limits. The Cyberspace Administration of China's measures stipulate that leaking personal information of 1 million or more people constitutes a "relatively large cybersecurity incident." For such incidents, general websites and apps must report to the provincial cyberspace administration department of their location, "no later than 4 hours at the latest," one channel being the 12387 hotline. A summary report must also be submitted within 30 days after handling concludes. Late reporting, omitted reporting, false reporting, or concealing reporting that leads to major harmful consequences shall be heavily punished. Conversely, for those who have taken reasonable and necessary protective measures, handled the incident according to emergency plans, and reported in a timely manner, "punishment may be mitigated or waived depending on the circumstances" (Nationwide, reporting measures effective from November 2025).
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2021). Personal Information Protection Law (Articles 57, 66, 69). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202108/t20210820_527244.shtml> ; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2025). Cybersecurity Law (Amended in 2025, coming into force on January 1, 2026, Articles 27, 44, 71; 2016 text Articles 25, 42). <https://www.cac.gov.cn/2025-12/29/c_1768735112911946.htm> ; State Council (2024). Regulations on Network Data Security Management (State Council Decree No. 790, Article 11). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2024/issue_11646/202410/content_6980863.html> ; Cyberspace Administration of China (2025). Measures for the Administration of Reporting National Cybersecurity Incidents (Articles 4, 8, 9, 10, 11, Annex "Guidelines for the Classification of Cybersecurity Incidents"). <https://www.cac.gov.cn/2025-09/15/c_1759583017717009.htm>
entries.notes: If a small website leaks data of a few hundred or a few thousand people, it must still take remedial measures and issue notifications according to the Personal Information Protection Law; it simply does not reach that 4-hour reporting threshold. When notifying users, make actionable steps concrete: which password to change, and watch out for calls impersonating customer service. Keep logs for at least 6 months so that when an incident occurs, you can trace clearly where the leak originated; see Section 11, Item 16 (retaining logs according to Multi-Level Protection Scheme requirements). For how users can protect themselves after their data has been leaked, see Section 14.

entries.title: For those selling auto-renewing memberships, prominently remind users both before activation and before each deduction, and make the cancellation entry point easy to find
entries.cost: Costs no money. State auto-renewal clearly on the activation page, send a separate reminder before each deduction, and place a button in the personal account center that can be canceled at any time. The difficulty is that a portion of users will casually cancel upon receiving the reminder.
entries.summary: When selling auto-renewing memberships, you must remind users in an eye-catching way before they activate and before each deduction. During the membership period, you must provide an entry point to cancel or modify at any time that is easy to find and click, and charging unreasonable additional fees is prohibited. Deducting money without giving a reminder can result in fines of 1 to 5 times the unlawful gains, or up to 300,000 yuan if there are no unlawful gains.
entries.benefit: The exact wording of the Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Online Transactions is that service providers adopting methods such as automatic renewal or automatic extension "shall, prior to consumers accepting services and prior to dates such as automatic extension and automatic renewal, draw consumers' attention in a prominent manner for consumers to choose autonomously." During the service period, they must also "provide consumers with prominent, simple options to cancel or alter at any time, and shall not charge unreasonable fees." The Regulations for the Implementation of the Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests carry the same reminder requirements. Failure to provide reminders will be penalized under the Implementation Regulations: an order to make corrections, potential warnings, confiscation of unlawful gains, and fines of 1 to 5 times the unlawful gains. Where there are no unlawful gains, fines of up to 300,000 yuan shall be imposed. Where circumstances are serious, an order to suspend business for rectification or revocation of the business license shall be imposed. Failure to provide a convenient cancellation entry point shall result in an order to make corrections within a time limit, and may incur a fine of up to 30,000 yuan (Nationwide).
entries.sources: State Administration for Market Regulation (2021, amended 2025). Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Online Transactions (SAMR Decree No. 37, Articles 18, 41). <https://www.samr.gov.cn/zw/zfxxgk/fdzdgknr/fgs/art/2025/art_4b47c79b8d994a42bba4835997688faa.html> ; State Council (2024). Regulations for the Implementation of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests (State Council Decree No. 778, Article 10, Paragraph 2, Article 50). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202403/content_6940159.htm>
entries.notes: The regulations do not specify exactly what "a prominent manner" looks like. The prudent practice is to send an individual reminder before each deduction and retain the transmission records so that you can produce evidence when complaints arise. For how to turn off auto-renewal from the user's perspective, see Section 5, Item 1 (turn off all auto-renewals).
