The practices used by licensed, legitimate institutions to mitigate risks are standard routines anyway: first map out the course of blood vessels beneath the injection site, and use blunt cannulas instead of sharp needles; inject small amounts while withdrawing the needle; and prepare hyaluronidase in advance. Every single step requires execution by a trained physician, which is also the reason not to turn to unlicensed, irregular channels. Before proceeding, verify everything first according to Item 2 of this section (checking institutional licenses and attending physicians).

entries.title: Do not purchase weight-loss drugs, slimming coffees, diet candies, or enzyme plums (plums claimed to be soaked in enzymes) that promise "rapid weight loss"
entries.cost: Costs no money. In fact, it saves the money spent on buying these products. The hard part is accepting that there is no such thing as "losing several jin in a week."
entries.summary: Such products are frequently found to be illicitly adulterated with sibutramine, an ingredient originally used as a weight-loss medication that was discontinued in China in 2010. Among overweight individuals aged 55 and older who had heart disease or diabetes and took it for over three years, nonfatal myocardial infarctions were about 30% higher, and strokes were about 36% higher. Additional weight loss was only 1.7 kilograms. By the time spot-check inspections detect it, you have already ingested it.
entries.benefit: The SCOUT trial enrolled 9,804 participants. All of them were aged 55 or older, overweight or obese, and had cardiovascular disease or type 2 diabetes. These individuals were randomized by lottery into medication and non-medication groups, with an average treatment duration of 3.4 years. The primary endpoint was a pre-specified count of adverse events: nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, resuscitation after cardiac arrest, and cardiovascular death. The incidence rates of these events were 11.4% vs 10.0%. HR was 1.16 (95% CI 1.03–1.31, P=0.02), meaning those taking the medication had an approximately 16% higher risk of experiencing adverse events. The true value falls roughly between 3% higher and 31% higher. Nonfatal myocardial infarction was 4.1% vs 3.2%, HR 1.28 (1.04–1.57), about 30% higher. Nonfatal stroke was 2.6% vs 1.9%, HR 1.36 (1.04–1.77), about 36% higher. Cardiovascular death and all-cause mortality did not increase; all-cause refers to all causes combined. Following randomization, the sibutramine group achieved an average of 1.7 kg more weight loss. Based on a safety evaluation, the former State Food and Drug Administration determined that "the risks of weight-loss treatment outweigh the benefits" and issued a circular in October 2010 halting the production, sale, and use of sibutramine formulations and active pharmaceutical ingredients. Both sibutramine and phenolphthalein are prohibited from being added to food, which includes health foods.
entries.sources: James WPT et al. (2010). Effect of sibutramine on cardiovascular outcomes in overweight and obese subjects. NEJM. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1003114>; Tianjin Municipal Administration for Market Regulation. Be vigilant against illegal addition of "sibutramine hydrochloride" and "phenolphthalein" in some foods. <https://scjg.tj.gov.cn/tjsscjdglwyh_52651/hdpt/cjwtyxfts/202007/t20200720_2972549.html>
entries.notes: SCOUT enrolled a high-risk population that already had heart disease or diabetes. This trial did not prove that healthy young people taking it would experience the exact same adverse events. However, precisely because it is impossible to distinguish who is at high risk, regulators simply withdrew it from the market altogether. Another ingredient frequently adulterated illicitly is phenolphthalein. Originally a laxative, excessive long-term consumption disrupts electrolyte balance in the body and induces cardiac arrhythmias. How to judge: legitimate weight-loss drugs are prescription drugs, and their approval numbers can be checked at pharmacies and hospitals. Products sold under the banner of "coffee," "candy," "plums," or "meal replacements" that also promise losing several jin in a week are by definition not supposed to produce drug effects; if they do produce drug effects, it indicates that substances have been added. The original text discontinuing sibutramine is Notice Guoshiyaojianban [2010] No. 432, published on the website of the National Medical Products Administration. What is cited here is the secondary webpage from the Tianjin market regulation department, where the two phrases "risks outweigh benefits" and "halting production, sale, and use in October 2010" can be verified verbatim.

entries.title: Do not use anabolic steroids ("muscle-building injections," "oral medications") to gain muscle
entries.cost: Costs no money, and additionally saves drug expenses. The hard part is accepting that muscle builds slowly.
entries.summary: Men testing positive for doping in gyms face a mortality risk 3 times higher than their peers of the same age, and they make more than double the number of hospital visits each year. Acne, gynecomastia, and erectile dysfunction affect at least one out of every ten users. In China, such drugs are prescription medications; channels selling them to you without a prescription are themselves breaking the law.
entries.benefit: In Denmark, researchers reviewed historical records, matching each user with age-matched controls. The users were 545 men who tested positive for androgenic anabolic steroids in gym doping controls between 2006-01-03 and 2018-03-01, matched with 5,450 controls. In addition, the findings were re-verified using 644 individuals who refused testing and 6,440 controls. Results: The mortality rate among users was 3 times that of controls, HR 3.0 (95% CI 1.3–7.0), with the true multiple falling roughly between 1.3 and 7. The median number of hospitalizations or clinic visits per year was 0.81 vs 0.36 (P<0.0001). Median means that half the people had more and half had fewer than this number. This P-value indicates that this difference is almost impossible to be mere coincidence. Acne (breakouts), gynecomastia, and erectile dysfunction each affected more than 10% of users—meaning at least one in every ten users was affected—all significantly higher than in controls (P<0.0001). The batch analyzed for re-verification showed consistent results. Article 7 of the Anti-Doping Regulations: The State exercises strict management over prohibited substances listed in the Doping Control Catalog; no entity or individual may illegally manufacture, sell, import, or export them. The same regulations specify that anabolic preparations and peptide hormones are managed as prescription drugs, meaning they can only be purchased with a doctor's prescription; anabolic preparations is the statutory term for this class of drugs in the regulations.
entries.sources: Horwitz H et al. (2019). Health consequences of androgenic anabolic steroid use. J Intern Med. <https://doi.org/10.1111/joim.12850>; State Council (2004). Anti-Doping Regulations (Decree of the State Council No. 398, Articles 7 and 9). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2004/content_63129.htm>
entries.notes: Controversy: This is a study that followed a cohort of people to observe outcomes, not a randomized controlled trial. Drug users themselves might also take more risks in other areas, so the 3-fold figure cannot be attributed entirely to the drugs. The true multiple could be as low as 1.3 or as high as 7.0, a very wide range. However, that "acne, gynecomastia, and erectile dysfunction each affect more than 10% of people" represents visible side effects, which are less susceptible to this type of bias. This class of drugs is written as "anabolic preparations" in regulations; whenever those four Chinese characters are seen, it refers to them. Regular protein powder and creatine do not fall within the scope of this item. The trouble is that products "claiming to build muscle exceptionally fast" may secretly contain adulterants. The method of evaluation is identical to the entry on weight-loss products (Item 4, do not buy weight-loss drugs promising rapid weight loss): legitimate medications are prescription drugs with verifiable approval numbers. Those sold under names like "muscle-building powder" or "nutritional supplements" that promise results in a few weeks have had substances added if they are truly effective.

entries.title: If taking weight-loss drugs or injecting weight-reduction shots such as semaglutide, obtain a prescription at a hospital, titrate doses, and follow up as scheduled by a doctor; do not purchase from online stores that dispatch shipments without a prescription, and do not receive injections at beauty salons
entries.cost: One registration fee, plus a round trip. Several tens of yuan, half a day of time. For those receiving weight-reduction injections, follow-up visits must also be made according to the doctor's appointment schedule. Medication costs are separate, and because weight will mostly rebound after discontinuing injections, this expense must be calculated based on long-term medication use.
entries.summary: Prescription drugs must be sold against prescriptions; online sales also require genuine prescriptions and real-name registration. For online shops that ship goods without consultations, and beauty salons providing home-visit injections, the drugs are mostly of unknown origin, with no one responsible for dosing or contraindications. One year after discontinuing weight-reduction injections, approximately two-thirds of the lost weight rebounds, so this must be accounted for as a long-term treatment.
entries.benefit: The Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Quality of Pharmaceutical Operation and Use stipulate that pharmaceutical retail enterprises must abide by the classification management system for prescription and non-prescription drugs. This system divides drugs into two categories: one must be purchased with a doctor's prescription, and the other can be purchased on one's own. Pharmacies must sell prescription drugs against prescriptions in accordance with regulations, retaining prescriptions for no less than five years. When pharmacists or other pharmaceutical technical personnel are absent from duty, signs should be hung to notify the public, and prescription drugs must not be sold without their review. Prescription drugs shall not be sold on open shelves, meaning they cannot be placed on shelves for customers to pick up themselves. Article 9 of the Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Online Pharmaceutical Sales stipulates that anyone selling prescription drugs to individuals via the internet shall ensure that prescription sources are authentic and reliable, and implement real-name management. Article 10 requires risk warning information to be prominently displayed under each pharmaceutical display page. Prior to passing prescription review, package inserts must not be displayed, and purchasing services must not be provided. If the prescription has not been reviewed, the page should not even provide a purchase button. Article 8 stipulates that drugs under special State administration shall not be sold over the internet. Such drugs include vaccines, blood products, narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances, toxic drugs for medical use, radioactive pharmaceuticals, and pharmaceutical precursor chemicals. The National Health Commission's Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Obesity (2024 Edition) clearly state that five drugs have been approved by the National Medical Products Administration in China for weight loss in adults with primary obesity. These five are orlistat, liraglutide, beinaglutide, semaglutide, and tirzepatide. The same guidelines consider a BMI of 24 to less than 28 as overweight, and 28 and above as obese. Medication is considered only when an individual is overweight and has related comorbidities such as hyperglycemia, hypertension, dyslipidemia, or fatty liver disease, or is already obese. The prerequisite is that lifestyle modifications have failed to reduce weight; medications are added on top of that baseline. The guidelines require a thorough evaluation of the medical condition and contraindications prior to drug use, along with regular follow-ups under the guidance of professional physicians during medication therapy. Semaglutide starts at 0.25 mg weekly, with a maintenance dose of 2.4 mg or 1.7 mg. Tirzepatide starts at 2.5 mg weekly, up to a maximum of 15 mg. For those whose weight reduction is less than 5%, the guidelines recommend discontinuing the drug. As for what happens after drug discontinuation, look at three trials. The STEP 1 extension study followed 327 participants; injecting semaglutide for 68 weeks resulted in an average weight loss of 17.3%. One year after discontinuation, weight rebounded by 11.6 percentage points, leaving a net weight loss of only 5.6%. The authors' conclusion was that two-thirds of the previously lost weight rebounded, with most cardiometabolic indicators also reverting to near baseline. STEP 4 randomized 803 participants who had already received injections for 20 weeks and lost an average of 10.6%. Those who continued injections lost another 7.9% of body weight over the subsequent 48 weeks, while those switched to placebo regained 6.9%. In SURMOUNT-4, 670 participants first received tirzepatide for 36 weeks, losing an average of 20.9% of body weight. Subsequently, those who continued injections lost another 5.5%, while those switched to placebo regained 14.0%. In July 2026, the Yinchuan Municipal Administration for Market Regulation issued a risk warning. The warning stated that trending "weight-loss shots" and "slimming pens" on the market are mostly repackaged, smuggled, or counterfeit drugs of unknown origin. Self-injecting after purchasing online or through personal procurement agents can easily trigger severe allergies, acute pancreatitis, organ damage, and wound infections. Injectable procedures and similar medical aesthetic treatments can only be performed in institutions qualified for medical aesthetic practices; administering injections at home or privately inside beauty salons is non-compliant, see Item 2 of this section (checking two things before getting injections, thread embedding, or surgery).
entries.sources: State Administration for Market Regulation (2023). Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Quality of Pharmaceutical Operation and Use (SAMR Decree No. 84). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2023/issue_10846/202311/content_6917322.html>; State Administration for Market Regulation (2022). Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Online Pharmaceutical Sales (SAMR Decree No. 58, Articles 8 to 10). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2022/content_5717002.htm>; General Office of the National Health Commission (2024). Notice on Issuing the Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Obesity (2024 Edition) (Annex Part 3 "10. Pharmacotherapy"). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202410/content_6981734.htm>; Wilding JPH et al. (2022). Weight regain and cardiometabolic effects after withdrawal of semaglutide: The STEP 1 trial extension. Diabetes Obes Metab. <https://doi.org/10.1111/dom.14725>; Rubino D et al. (2021). Effect of Continued Weekly Subcutaneous Semaglutide vs Placebo on Weight Loss Maintenance in Adults With Overweight or Obesity: The STEP 4 Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2021.3224>; Aronne LJ et al. (2024). Continued Treatment With Tirzepatide for Maintenance of Weight Reduction in Adults With Obesity: The SURMOUNT-4 Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2023.24945>; Yinchuan Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (2026). Market Regulation Department Risk Warning on Medical Aesthetics Consumption and "Miracle Weight-Loss Drugs". <https://scjg.yinchuan.gov.cn/zxdt/tzgg/202607/t20260703_5281032.html>
entries.notes: Statutory provisions can be verified verbatim, and figures on post-discontinuation rebound also come from randomized controlled trials. However, "how many fewer adverse events occur when using drugs under prescription compared to purchasing and using them on one's own" has not been quantitatively studied, which is why it is rated Grade B under "difficult to quantify." The STEP 1 extension study stopped not only the medication, but diet and exercise guidance was also discontinued simultaneously, and it only followed a subset of the participants from the original trial. The steroids and sex hormones discussed in Items 5 and 7 of this section also follow this exact same set of rules. When someone truly reaches the point where medication is needed for weight reduction, a doctor will first evaluate the body mass index, the presence of other comorbidities, and whether any contraindications exist before determining whether to take medication and which kind to use. This clinical judgment cannot be bought.

entries.title: Use sex hormone medications only under the premise of a physician's prescription and regular follow-up checks; do not purchase them online, and do not adjust doses on your own
entries.cost: Regular registration fees, plus blood test follow-ups. Several hundred yuan per year, taking up several half-days.
entries.summary: This does not discuss whether they should be used, but only how they should be used. Among transgender women using estrogen, those developing blood clots in blood vessels are significantly more numerous than peers of the same age, with approximately 4 excess cases per 1,000 individuals over two years, and approximately 17 excess cases over eight years. These types of risks must be monitored through regular follow-up checks; buying drugs online and adjusting doses yourself leaves no one to check them for you.
entries.benefit: Researchers tracked a cohort of individuals from the electronic medical records of the Kaiser Permanente healthcare system. Among them were 2,842 transgender women and 2,118 transgender men. Mean follow-up was 4.0 years and 3.6 years, respectively. Each person was matched by birth year, race/ethnicity, clinical site, and enrollment timing with approximately 10-fold cisgender controls, totaling 48,686 cisgender men and 48,775 cisgender women. Transgender women experienced more venous thromboembolism (blood clots forming in and blocking blood vessels) than controls. Compared with cisgender men, the rate was 4.1 cases per 1,000 individuals at 2 years (95% CI 1.6–6.7). At 8 years, it was 16.7 cases (6.4–27.5). Calculated out, there were 4.1 excess cases per 1,000 people over two years, and 16.7 excess cases over eight years. Compared with cisgender women, these two numbers were 3.4 (1.1–5.6) and 13.7 (4.1–22.7). Overall rates of ischemic stroke (strokes where blood vessels are blocked) and myocardial infarction were similar across groups. However, among transgender women who initiated hormone therapy only during the follow-up period, differences in venous thromboembolism and ischemic stroke were more pronounced. Evidence for transgender men was insufficient to draw conclusions. The authors concluded that "these results may indicate the need for long-term vigilance regarding the vascular side effects of estrogen in transgender hormone therapy."
entries.sources: Getahun D et al. (2018). Cross-sex Hormones and Acute Cardiovascular Events in Transgender Persons: A Cohort Study. Ann Intern Med. <https://doi.org/10.7326/M17-2785>; State Administration for Market Regulation (2022). Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Online Pharmaceutical Sales (SAMR Decree No. 58, Article 9). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2022/content_5717002.htm>
entries.notes: The researchers themselves explicitly noted the shortcoming of this study: they could not track how many people purchased medications on their own outside the hospital system. Therefore, the boundary of "whether one used medication" was inherently blurred. Conversely, this precisely demonstrates that medication use should be incorporated into formal follow-up care. This study only examined whether vascular incidents occurred; it does not answer whether hormone therapy should be used or what benefits it offers—that belongs to a different set of evidence. This applies equally to all contexts where sex hormones are used, including birth control pills, menopausal hormone therapy, and testosterone supplementation. For anyone who purchases drugs online, adjusts dosages based on online posts, and never checks blood clot, liver, and kidney indicators, the risks stem from the phase of "having no one monitor it," not from the reason for taking the medication. The formal pathway in China is to visit the endocrinology department or the corresponding specialist department in a legitimate medical institution for evaluation, prescription, and follow-up examinations.

entries.title: If "feeling ugly" has reached the point of repeatedly looking in the mirror and repeatedly wanting to change your appearance, undergo a body image assessment first before discussing surgery
entries.cost: Registering for an appointment in psychiatry or clinical psychology costs several tens of yuan. The hard part is making this trip before scheduling surgery.
entries.summary: Among people visiting plastic surgery clinics, about 15% have body dysmorphic disorder, which means magnifying flaws that others can barely see to the point where it affects daily life. Among dermatology patients, it is about 13%; in both groups, more than 70% are female. Register for an appointment first to see whether this applies to you before deciding whether to undergo surgery.
entries.benefit: Following rigorous methodology, 33 studies were gathered and pooled together. Among plastic surgery patients, the prevalence of body dysmorphic disorder (magnifying flaws that others can barely see to the extent that it affects daily life) was 15.04%, with individual studies ranging between 2.21% and 56.67%. In terms of headcounts, about 15 out of every 100 people seeking plastic surgery met the criteria, ranging from 2 to 57 across individual studies. The mean age of this group was 34.54 ± 12.41 years (the latter number being the margin of variation), and 74.38% were female. Among dermatology patients, it was 12.65%, ranging between 4.52% and 35.16% across studies, with a mean age of 27.79 ± 9.03 years, and 76.09% being female. The authors recommended that plastic surgeons and dermatologists proactively assess patients, identify high-risk individuals, and arrange multidisciplinary co-management. Another study surveyed 200 patients with body dysmorphic disorder; 71.0% had sought non-psychiatric treatments such as dermatology or plastic surgery, and 64.0% had received them. The author's conclusion was that such treatments "rarely improve" body dysmorphic disorder and appear to be ineffective for it.
entries.sources: Ribeiro RVE (2017). Prevalence of Body Dysmorphic Disorder in Plastic Surgery and Dermatology Patients: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis. Aesthetic Plast Surg. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00266-017-0869-0>；Crerand CE, Phillips KA, Menard W, Fay C (2005). Nonpsychiatric medical treatment of body dysmorphic disorder. Psychosomatics, 46(6), 549-555. <https://doi.org/10.1176/appi.psy.46.6.549>；NHS. Body dysmorphic disorder (BDD). <https://www.nhs.uk/mental-health/conditions/body-dysmorphia/>
entries.notes: The proportions measured across studies ranged widely from 2.21% all the way to 56.67%. The reason is that the questionnaires used and the populations surveyed differed. Therefore, one can only infer that "this proportion is not low and warrants an initial screening"; 15.04% cannot be taken as an exact figure, which is also why this is rated Grade B. Based on this proportion, the majority of people visiting plastic surgery clinics do not have body dysmorphic disorder. This entry targets the small subset of people whose condition is "repetitive, persistent, and already impacting work and social life"; undergoing surgery or skin treatments rarely helps them improve. Clues for identification listed by the UK NHS include: spending a lot of time comparing one's appearance with others, constantly looking in mirrors or completely avoiding mirrors, making great efforts to conceal a certain body part, and picking at the skin to make it "smooth." It affects work, social life, and interpersonal relationships.

entries.title: When undergoing orthodontic treatment, seek an in-person examination from a doctor certified in orthodontics and return for regular follow-up visits; do not buy aligners online to wear at home by yourself
entries.cost: Compared to purchasing online, it costs extra for registration and follow-up visits, requiring visits to the clinic at regular intervals. The difficulty lies in the fact that treatment courses often last one to two years, requiring persistent follow-up attendance.
entries.summary: Clear aligners are Class II medical devices in China, and package inserts require wearing them under the guidance of a doctor certified in orthodontics, along with regular follow-up visits. The US FDA states that it has never approved aligners sold directly to consumers without a prescription from a dentist. Without in-person examinations, risks include bite misalignment, unintended tooth movement, pain, and even tooth loss.
entries.benefit: The 2022 "Guidelines for Technical Review of Bracketless Orthodontic Appliances Registration" by the Center for Medical Device Evaluation of the National Medical Products Administration states that this type of aligner is "classified as Class II under administrative supervision." It mandates that the product manual clearly state that "wearing must be carried out under the guidance of a physician with professional orthodontic qualifications during the treatment process," as well as specifying "requirements for eating, tooth brushing, and regular follow-up visits." Regarding product names, it notes that "it is not recommended to include unsubstantiated, hypothetical conceptual names such as 'invisible'." The statement from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is: "The FDA has not authorized clear aligners that are sold directly to consumers without a prescription and supervision by a dentist or orthodontist", meaning that it has not approved a single clear aligner sold directly to individuals without a prescription and supervision by a dentist. The FDA also states: "In-person examination by a dentist or orthodontist can help lower the risks of uneven bite, unintended tooth movement, pain, and tooth loss", meaning in-person examinations by a dentist can reduce the risks of bite unevenness, tooth shifting, pain, and tooth loss. Regular in-person follow-up visits after beginning wear are necessary to confirm that teeth are moving safely according to plan. Both documents are regulatory documents and do not provide an incidence rate of complications.
entries.sources: Center for Medical Device Evaluation, National Medical Products Administration (2022). Guidelines for Technical Review of Bracketless Orthodontic Appliances Registration (2022 No. 41). <https://www.cmde.org.cn/flfg/zdyz/zdyzwbk/20230103095116100.html>; General Office of the National Health Commission et al. (2023). Notice on Further Promoting Dental Healthcare Services and Guarantee Management (Guo Wei Ban Yi Zheng Fa [2023] No. 11, Section V, Item (2)). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202309/content_6903786.htm>; U.S. Food and Drug Administration (2026). Clear Dental Aligners (Page updated September 9, 2026). <https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/dental-devices/clear-dental-aligners>
entries.notes: The magnitude of benefit is rated as small because no adverse event rate was found, and judgment can only rely on the severity of the consequences. Risk warnings from Chinese drug regulatory and health authorities regarding "buying aligners online to wear at home on one's own" could not be located; therefore, this entry relies primarily on registration requirements and FDA statements. Orthodontics is a medical practice. For teeth straightening of a medical aesthetic nature, the institution's license must include the corresponding specialty, and the operating doctor must be properly qualified. For how to verify, see Item 2 of this section (institutional licenses, attending physicians). In 2023, four departments including the National Health Commission issued a notice on oral healthcare. For those operating without a practice license or clinic filing certificate, or hiring non-health-technical personnel to practice dentistry, the notice requires that they "be severely punished in accordance with laws and regulations." Orthodontics is not covered by basic medical insurance; see Section 24, Item 12 (Ask clearly about the all-inclusive lump-sum price before dental implants).

entries.title: When buying blemish-fading and whitening creams, first check the "Guo Zhuang Te Zi" approval number on the packaging against the National Medical Products Administration website; do not use spot-fading creams sold by WeChat merchants or mixed by beauty salons
entries.cost: Costs no money; checking a registration number takes a few minutes. The hard part is not buying those specific products that acquaintances and WeChat merchants promote most aggressively.
entries.summary: Blemish-fading and whitening creams must be registered with the National Medical Products Administration and obtain a "Guo Zhuang Te Zi" registration number before they can be sold. Spot checks have uncovered blemish creams with mercury exceeding limits by thousands of times; although the packaging bore a Guo Zhuang Te Zi number, the labeled manufacturer had never produced that batch. Mercury absorbed into the body through facial skin can cause kidney damage; stopping use combined with medical treatment resolves most cases, but treatment takes several months to two years.
entries.benefit: Article 16 of the "Cosmetics Supervision and Administration Regulations" classifies freckle-removing and skin-whitening cosmetics as special cosmetics. Article 17 stipulates that special cosmetics can only be produced or imported after being registered with the drug regulatory department of the State Council. Article 36 requires that the registration certificate number for special cosmetics be marked on the label. Article 20 requires that registration information be disclosed to the public, so the number can be looked up on the National Medical Products Administration website. Article 62 of the "Measures for the Administration of Cosmetics Registration and Filing" specifies that domestic numbers use "Guo Zhuang Te Zi" plus the year and sequential number, while imported ones use "Guo Zhuang Te Jin Zi". Circular No. 14 of 2026 of the National Medical Products Administration announced two batches of spot-fading creams that were found to contain mercury at 4,938 mg/kg and 9,281 mg/kg, respectively. The limit listed in the appendix to the circular is no more than 1 mg/kg; these two batches exceeded it by thousands of times. They were purchased from two small cosmetic shops in Sichuan and Anhui, and the packaging was printed with Guo Zhuang Te Zi numbers. The labeled manufacturer filed an objection, and after review, the Guangdong Provincial Medical Products Administration determined that this enterprise had never manufactured this batch of goods. A review summarized 30 cases reported in academic journals where patients developed nephrotic syndrome—meaning massive amounts of protein leaking into the urine—after using mercury-containing skin-lightening creams. All 30 patients were Asian females, mostly aged 18 to 52. The duration from initial use to disease onset ranged from 1 to 60 months, with half within 5 months. Renal biopsies mostly showed minimal change disease (67%) or membranous nephropathy (23%), which are two types of glomerular disorders. Very few resolved spontaneously within a month and a half after cessation. Among the few documented cases, urine protein negative conversion took 1 to 9 months (median: 2 months) with mercury-chelating agents. All 3 cases without chelating agents took more than 12 months. A hospital in Beijing treated 288 patients with mercury poisoning between 2014 and 2019, of whom 84 (29.27%) were related to cosmetics. Cosmetics were the primary source of poisoning among women. Among the 18 followed-up nephrotic syndrome patients, 15 had their urine protein and albumin return to normal after an average of 22.67 months. The mercury exposure in these 18 individuals did not all originate from cosmetics.
entries.sources: State Council (2020). Cosmetics Supervision and Administration Regulations (State Council Decree No. 727, Articles 16, 17, 20, 36, 42, 60). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-06/29/content_5522593.htm>; State Administration for Market Regulation (2021). Measures for the Administration of Cosmetics Registration and Filing (SAMR Decree No. 35, Article 62). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-01/12/content_5579239.htm>; National Medical Products Administration (2026). Circular of the National Medical Products Administration on 25 Batches of Cosmetics Found to Contain Prohibited Raw Materials (2026 No. 14) and Appendix. <https://www.nmpa.gov.cn/xxgk/ggtg/hzhpggtg/hzhpchjgg/hzhpcjgjj/20260424173212101.html>; Chan TYK, Chan APL, Tang HL (2020). Nephrotic syndrome caused by exposures to skin-lightening cosmetic products containing inorganic mercury. Clin Toxicol. <https://doi.org/10.1080/15563650.2019.1639724>; Yawei S et al. (2021). Epidemiology, clinical presentation, treatment, and follow-up of chronic mercury poisoning in China: a retrospective analysis. BMC Pharmacol Toxicol. <https://doi.org/10.1186/s40360-021-00493-y>
entries.notes: The two batches mentioned above show that registration numbers can also be forged or misappropriated. Therefore, when checking a number, verify whether the retrieved product name, manufacturer, and packaging match, and it is best to buy from official brand stores or legitimate department stores. Article 42 of the Regulations stipulates that when beauty salons use cosmetics on clients, they must abide by the rules applicable to cosmetic operators. Article 60, Item 5 prohibits operators from formulating cosmetics without authorization; "salon-exclusive blemish-fading creams" custom-blended by beauty salons are themselves illegal. If you have already used blemish-fading creams of unknown origin for an extended period, stop using them immediately, and bring the product to the hospital to test urinary mercury and urinary protein. In that review, 6 individuals had normal blood mercury levels, while all 24 who were tested for urinary mercury were above the upper limit of normal. Because cases are reported individually on a case-by-case basis, it is impossible to calculate what percentage of people who use mercury-containing creams will suffer kidney damage, which is why this is rated Grade B. The magnitude of benefit is rated moderate based on consequences: most cases of nephrotic syndrome can be cured, but treatment requires several months to two years.

chapters.title: After Experiencing a Severe Blow
chapters.intro:
The death of a loved one, being diagnosed with a critical illness, unemployment, divorce. These life events share a common thread in research: what suffers is not just your mood, but also your body. The period of highest risk is concentrated in the first few weeks to the first year. This section does not discuss how to "move on"; it focuses solely on what matters must be monitored by someone during this timeframe, which decisions must be postponed, and when you should register for a hospital appointment. Most entries calculate mortality probabilities. The four entries discussing expenditures and entitlements calculate money. These four are: do not rush into spending money on grief counseling right away (Item 9), calling 12356 and registering for psychological outpatient clinics (Item 11), postponing major irreversible decisions (Item 12), and not treating death as a way to repay debts (Item 13). The two types of figures are not interchangeable. For those who have neither relatives nor friends to turn to, see Item 6 on how to put the phrase "find someone to keep an eye on you" into practice. For those experiencing persistent nightmares and flashbacks after personally undergoing car accidents, assaults, or disasters, see Item 14 (Trauma-focused psychotherapy).

For formalities, handling of the body, and claiming funds due at the time of a loved one's passing, see Section 25. For guardianship and wills during an elder's lifetime, see Section 17. For what can be claimed during unemployment, see Section 7. For exercise and light exposure during depressive moods, see Section 3 and Section 22. For calling 12356 first when having suicidal thoughts, see Section 1, Item 25; for the time scale of such thoughts, see Section 1, Item 32. For sequelae after being resuscitated, see Section 1, Item 33. None of these are repeated in this section.

entries.title: Do not stay alone during the first few days after a loved one passes away; those with heart disease, hypertension, or diabetes should take medications as usual, and call 120 if experiencing crushing chest pain
entries.cost: Costs no money. Do not stay alone during these few days, and take medications as usual.
entries.summary: On the first day following the death of a loved one, the probability of an acute myocardial infarction is 21.1 times that of normal times, decreasing day by day thereafter. Among individuals aged 60 to 89, the incidence of myocardial infarction or stroke roughly doubles within 30 days after the death of a spouse, dropping back after one month. People with pre-existing cardiovascular disease must not stop taking their medications during these days. Call 120 immediately if experiencing crushing chest pain, shortness of breath, or weakness in limbs on one side.
entries.benefit: In 1,985 acute myocardial infarction patients, self-matched comparisons were made using different time windows before and after disease onset in the same individual. Among them, 270 people (13.6%) had lost a significant person within 6 months prior to the onset, and 19 had experienced the loss within 1 day before the myocardial infarction. Within 24 hours of losing a significant person, the incidence rate of acute myocardial infarction increased by 21.1-fold (95% CI 13.1–34.1, with the true fold-increase roughly between 13 and 34). Thereafter, it declined day by day. In terms of absolute numbers: among individuals with a 10-year myocardial infarction risk of 5%, there is 1 additional case for every 1,394 newly bereaved individuals. Among those with a 20% risk, there is 1 additional case for every 320 individuals. Another UK study compared 30,447 bereaved individuals aged 60 to 89 with 83,588 matched controls. For those experiencing a myocardial infarction or stroke within 30 days post-bereavement, there were 50 individuals in the bereaved group (0.16%) versus 67 individuals in the control group (0.08%). The IRR was 2.20 (1.52–3.15), meaning the incident rate was approximately 2.2 times that of controls. Specifically, for myocardial infarction it was 2.14 (1.20–3.81), roughly 2.1 times; for stroke, it was 2.40 (1.22–4.71), roughly 2.4 times. The effect attenuated after 30 days. Two other categories of diseases were also tracked within 90 days. One was non-MI acute coronary syndrome (acute cardiac blood supply compromise that does not meet the criteria for myocardial infarction), with an IRR of 2.20 (1.12–4.29). The other was pulmonary embolism (blood clots lodging in pulmonary blood vessels), with an IRR of 2.37 (1.18–4.75). Regarding how to identify these diseases, the UK National Health Service (NHS) lists warning signs requiring an immediate emergency call. For myocardial infarction: chest pain that feels like being pressed or squeezed, which may radiate to the arms, neck, or jaw, along with shortness of breath. For stroke: one side of the face drooping, weakness or numbness in one arm or one side of the body, and slurred speech.
entries.sources: Mostofsky E, et al. (2012). Risk of acute myocardial infarction after the death of a significant person in one's life: the Determinants of Myocardial Infarction Onset Study. Circulation. <https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.111.061770>；Carey IM, et al. (2014). Increased risk of acute cardiovascular events after partner bereavement: a matched cohort study. JAMA Internal Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamainternmed.2013.14558>；NHS. Heart attack: symptoms. <https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/heart-attack/symptoms/>；NHS. Symptoms of a stroke. <https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/stroke/symptoms/>
entries.notes: Hand over the pill organizer to someone else to manage; do not rely on your own memory. Avoid long-distance driving during these days. Do not rely on drinking alcohol to endure it; the ledger on alcohol is detailed in Section 2. How to recognize myocardial infarction and stroke and how to call an ambulance are found in Section 13. Both studies were retrospective analyses of population data and cannot distinguish how many individuals were predisposed to developing the disease anyway. However, both point in the same direction and toward the same timeframe. For those who have no one to hand their pill organizer to and are bound to stay alone in the room during these days, see Item 6 of this section.

entries.title: During the week of receiving a critical illness diagnosis, do not go pick up the report alone, and postpone decisions other than medical treatment
entries.cost: Costs no money. Find someone to accompany you to pick up the report. Defer major decisions unrelated to medical treatment by a few days.
entries.summary: In the first week of receiving a cancer diagnosis, the probability of suicide is 12.6 times that of undiagnosed individuals, and the probability of dying from cardiovascular disease is 5.6 times. By the first year, suicide risk drops to 3.1 times, an effect more pronounced with harder-to-treat cancers. Therefore, bring someone along on the day you pick up the report, and do not stay alone at home. Leave matters like resigning from work or selling a house until your next outpatient visit.
entries.benefit: A Swedish national registry tracked over 6.07 million people (6,073,240 individuals) from 1991 to 2006. Compared with individuals not diagnosed with cancer, the relative risk of suicide in the first week following diagnosis was 12.6 (95% CI 8.6–17.8), approximately 12.6-fold. The true fold-increase falls roughly between 8.6 and 17.8. The incidence rate during this week was 2.50 per 1,000 person-years, meaning 2.5 cases per 1,000 people followed for one year. By the first year, it decreased to 3.1 (2.7–3.5, 0.60 per 1,000 person-years), roughly 3.1-fold. Cardiovascular mortality in the first week was 5.6 (5.2–5.9, 116.80 per 1,000 person-years), roughly 5.6-fold. In the first 4 weeks, it was 3.3 (3.1–3.4, 65.81 per 1,000 person-years). The elevated risks receded rapidly within the first year after diagnosis. The more difficult the cancer type is to treat and the lower the probability of survival, the more pronounced the increase. Self-matched comparisons of the same cohort across different time periods yielded consistent conclusions.
entries.sources: Fang F, et al. (2012). Suicide and cardiovascular death after a cancer diagnosis. New England Journal of Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1110307>
entries.notes: These are data for cancer patients. For other major diagnoses, there are no original texts of equivalent weight. The actual number of people affected is very small: the suicide rate in the first week was 2.50 per 1,000 person-years, meaning 2.5 cases per 1,000 people followed for one year. Writing this out is not intended to scare anyone, but to show that during "those first few days after finding out," someone needs to be by your side. For post-diagnosis long-term management, reimbursement, and follow-up examinations, see Section 16 and Section 24. For those who cannot find anyone to accompany them, see Item 6 of this section (replacing "that person" with neighbors and the community visiting list).

entries.title: After becoming unemployed, first establish a fixed daily routine, health insurance, and job-hunting rhythm; do not stay at home all day
entries.cost: Costs no money. First go register for unemployment and claim unemployment insurance benefits, then schedule job hunting into a fixed daily routine. The difficulty lies in getting up on time when no one is pressing you.
entries.summary: Unemployed individuals have about a 60% higher subsequent probability of death compared to employed individuals, an effect that is more pronounced in men and younger people, and highest in the first ten years. Subtracting the effects of smoking and drinking reduces the increase by about a quarter—this part you can control yourself. First go register for unemployment and claim unemployment insurance benefits.
entries.benefit: Pooled analysis of 42 studies, 235 mortality risk estimates, and over 20 million people. After adjusting for conditions such as age, the average all-cause mortality HR for unemployed individuals was 1.63, about 60% higher than for employed individuals. Higher in men than in women. The effect was pronounced in individuals in their early and mid-career stages, and smaller in late career. Risk was highest during the first 10 years of follow-up, declining thereafter. In the subset of studies that also accounted for health behaviors such as smoking and drinking, the average HR was 24% lower, meaning the calculated increase was reduced by about a quarter
entries.sources: Roelfs DJ, et al. (2011). Losing life and livelihood: a systematic review and meta-analysis of unemployment and all-cause mortality. Social Science & Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.socscimed.2011.01.005>
entries.notes: These are retrospective studies looking back at population data, which cannot determine the direction of causality. People with poorer health to begin with are also more likely to become unemployed. However, the finding that "after subtracting the influence of lifestyle habits, the effect is 24% lower" provides an actionable starting point. For what benefits can be claimed upon unemployment, where to claim them, and how to continue social insurance coverage, see Section 7. For how much severance pay you should receive upon dismissal and why not to sign a voluntary resignation, see Section 19.

entries.title: If a loved one died by suicide, accident, or homicide, do not expect to just tough it out; take the initiative to seek professional help
entries.cost: Calling 12356 costs no money. If you need to see a doctor, registering for a psychology/psychiatric outpatient clinic costs the same as a regular outpatient visit. The difficulty lies in opening your mouth to reach out to someone yourself.
entries.summary: People whose spouses died by suicide have about an 80% (men) and 70% (women) higher probability of being diagnosed with a psychiatric disorder within five years compared to the general population. Compared to those whose spouses died of other causes, it is also 70% to 100% higher. People bereaved in this way are more likely to feel alienated and ashamed. This is precisely the reason to proactively seek someone out; do not just wait for yourself to get better.
entries.benefit: Danish national registries followed 6.7 million adults from 1980 to 2014, totaling over 136 million person-years (the sum of follow-up years across all individuals). Compared to the general population, individuals widowed by spousal suicide had an IRR of 1.8 (95% CI 1.6–2.0) for a new psychiatric disorder diagnosis within 5 years in men, an increase of about 80%. In women, it was 1.7 (1.6–1.8), an increase of about 70%. Compared to individuals widowed by other causes of death, the IRR was 1.7 (1.5–1.9) for men and 2.0 (1.9–2.2) for women, an increase of 70% to 100%. In this group, suicide attempts, mortality, and the proportion requiring municipal support were also higher. Risks for physical conditions such as liver cirrhosis and sleep disorders were likewise elevated. Another 57 studies were summarized individually without pooling the numbers. Bereavement by suicide was associated with the following four outcomes: first, an increased risk of suicide in the partner; second, an increased risk of psychiatric hospitalization in parents following a child's suicide; third, an increased risk of suicide in mothers following an adult child's suicide; and fourth, an increased risk of depression in children following a parent's suicide. Compared to people bereaved by other violent deaths, those bereaved by suicide more frequently reported feeling alienated and ashamed
entries.sources: Erlangsen A, et al. (2017). Association Between Spousal Suicide and Mental, Physical, and Social Health Outcomes: A Longitudinal and Nationwide Register-Based Study. JAMA Psychiatry. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamapsychiatry.2017.0226>; Pitman A, et al. (2014). Effects of suicide bereavement on mental health and suicide risk. The Lancet Psychiatry. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S2215-0366(14)70224-X>; Kristensen P et al. (2012). Bereavement and mental health after sudden and violent losses: a review. Psychiatry. <https://doi.org/10.1521/psyc.2012.75.1.76> (the review mentioned in the notes)
entries.notes: Sudden, violent deaths refer to accidents, homicides, and disasters. Following these types of deaths, the rates of post-traumatic stress disorder, depression, and stuck grief are all higher than after death from disease. Recovery is also slower. For those who still experience nightmares, flashbacks, and avoidance behavior after one month, see Item 14 of this section (trauma-focused psychotherapy). For what to do when experiencing suicidal thoughts oneself, see Section 1, Item 25.

entries.title: In the first six months after spousal bereavement, designate a specific person to keep an eye on your meals, sleep, chronic disease medications, and follow-up visits
entries.cost: Costs no money. Find a specific person—children, siblings, or friends are all fine—and have them visit or call regularly. The difficulty lies in bringing yourself to entrust this matter to someone.
entries.summary: Within the first six months after spousal bereavement, the probability of death during the same period is about 40% higher than for non-bereaved individuals. After six months, it drops to about 15% higher. For men, it is about 23% higher, while for women the difference is small enough that it may just be chance. What should be done is to assign medications, meals, and follow-up checks to a specific person; do not expect to remember them yourself.
entries.benefit: Pooled analysis of 15 prospective studies (enrolling first, then following forward) comprising 2,263,888 individuals. For bereavement of less than 6 months, mortality RR was 1.41 (95% CI 1.26–1.57), meaning the concurrent probability of death was about 40% higher than for non-bereaved individuals. After 6 months it was 1.14 (1.10–1.18), dropping to about 15% higher. In men, RR was 1.23 (1.18–1.28), about 23% higher. In women, it was 1.04 (1.00–1.08, not statistically significant, meaning this small difference may just be chance). No significant difference was observed between those under 65 and those 65 or older. Another analysis pooled 123 publications, 1,377 risk estimates, and over 500 million people. After adjusting for differences in baseline conditions, the HR was 1.23 (1.19–1.28), an overall increase of about 23%. Men were still higher than women: men 1.27 (1.19–1.35), 27% higher; women 1.15 (1.08–1.22), 15% higher
entries.sources: Moon JR, et al. (2011). Widowhood and mortality: a meta-analysis. PLoS ONE. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0023465>；Shor E, et al. (2012). Widowhood and mortality: a meta-analysis and meta-regression. Demography. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s13524-012-0096-x>
entries.notes: These are retrospective studies looking back at population data, and confounding factors cannot be completely eliminated. Married couples already share similar lifestyles and health conditions to begin with. The finding that "the first six months are significantly higher than afterward" was calculated by the first pooled study using stratified time intervals since bereavement. The second study did not stratify by time since bereavement, but only by how long the studies followed participants. Studies following participants for only 6 months pooled an HR of 1.58 (1.32–1.88), while those following for 16 to 20 years were 1.22 (1.02–1.47). Based on this, the authors concluded that the risk is highest in the first few years after bereavement, but also noted that most studies did not start follow-up immediately at bereavement. Both studies point in the same direction, making it worthwhile to treat the first six months as a crucial window for care. Men have higher risks and are also less likely to ask for help. If there are bereaved elderly family members at home, sort out accounts, guardianship, and wills together according to Section 17. For those who cannot find such a person (living alone, shidu [having lost an only child], or whose children are also gone), entrust this to the community and your mobile phone; see Item 6 of this section.

entries.title: If you have neither family nor friends, replace "the person keeping an eye on you" with three things: a neighbor who can enter your home, the community visiting list, and emergency contacts in your phone
entries.cost: Costs no money. The difficulty lies in taking the initiative to speak up and telling your neighbors and neighborhood committee: "I live alone, and something just happened in my family."
entries.summary: When you have neither family nor friends, two things need to be looked after: ensuring someone discovers you if something goes wrong, and taking your medicine and eating meals on time. Taking medicine and eating meals rely on yourself: write checklists and set alarms; do not rely on memory. Ensuring someone discovers you relies on three things: leaving a spare key with a neighbor, going to the neighborhood committee to ask if you can be placed on the visiting and care list, and setting up emergency contacts on your phone without turning it off.
entries.benefit: 44,573 outpatients with risk factors for or a history of atherothrombosis (the kind of condition where plaques grow in blood vessels and are prone to blockage by blood clots). They were enrolled by physicians across multiple countries into the international REACH project for follow-up, recruited between December 2003 and December 2004 and followed for 4 years. Among them, 8,594 (19%) lived alone. Over 4 years, all-cause mortality was 14.1% for those living alone versus 11.1% for those cohabiting. Cardiovascular mortality was 8.6% versus 6.8%. Both log-rank P<0.01, indicating the differences are unlikely to be coincidental. The disparity varied across different age groups (interaction P=0.03). At ages 45 to 65, mortality for living alone versus cohabiting was 7.7% versus 5.7%. After adjusting for other conditions, the HR was 1.24 (95% CI 1.01–1.51), about 24% higher. At ages 66 to 80, it was 13.2% versus 12.3%, HR 1.12 (1.01–1.26), about 10% higher. For those over 80, it was 24.6% versus 28.4%, HR 0.92 (0.79–1.06), showing no increase instead. A 2022 policy opinion from ten ministries including the Ministry of Civil Affairs stipulates the implementation of visiting and care services. The target recipients are elderly people who live alone, are empty-nesters, left-behind, disabled, severely handicapped, or from family planning special families. The service methods are "regular home visits, telephone and video calls, and remote monitoring." Townships (subdistricts) conduct screenings and investigations with assistance from village (neighborhood) committees to grasp basic information and "willingness to receive visiting and care services," incorporating them into grassroots grid-based management (divided by zones and assigned to dedicated personnel for monitoring). By the end of 2025, "ensure the monthly visiting rate for elderly people with special difficulties reaches 100%," and "for disabled elderly people with special difficulties, conduct visiting and care no less than once a month." The document also advocates that households configure smart call systems, smart electricity and water meters, health monitoring products, and eldercare monitoring devices, "so that when abnormal monitoring occurs, timely warnings can be issued, and alert messages can be synchronized to emergency contacts." When service personnel discover emergency issues, they "shall immediately assist in dialing emergency call numbers"
entries.sources: Udell JA, et al. (2012). Living alone and cardiovascular risk in outpatients at risk of or with atherothrombosis. Archives of Internal Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1001/archinternmed.2012.2782>; Ten departments including the Ministry of Civil Affairs (2022). Guiding Opinions on Carrying Out Visiting and Care Services for Elderly People with Special Difficulties (Min Fa [2022] No. 73). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-10/13/content_5718017.htm>
entries.notes: How to specifically implement these three things. First, give a spare key or temporary door lock code to a neighbor or property management, and tell them, "I'm on my own these days." You do not need a close relationship; you only need someone to know you are inside the apartment. Second, go to the community neighborhood committee to explain that you live alone and ask if you can be placed on the visiting and care list. Among the elderly, those living alone, empty-nesters, and shidu individuals are explicitly defined service recipients; also ask whether there are smart call devices, smart water meters, or similar equipment installed for free locally. Third, set up emergency contacts and a medical emergency card on your phone; do not mute or turn it off during these days. There are two reasons for assigning a grade of B. First, the association between living alone and mortality comes from retrospective population studies. It cannot rule out the reverse explanation that "people with poorer baseline health and conditions are more likely to live alone," and the original paper itself states that this finding awaits confirmation. Second, that visiting and care policy document only covers the elderly. For those under 60, there is no corresponding dedicated institutional system. What can be counted on is a provision in another document, which requires grid workers and social workers to "promptly identify psychological crisis risks such as family misfortunes, unemployment, and dropping out of school" (see Item 11 of this section; call 12356 if you need someone to talk to). Why having "someone inside the room" is valuable can be seen in Section 13, Item 1 (chest compressions). Among out-of-hospital cardiac arrests, 79.2% occur at home. When someone nearby performs compressions, 16.1% survive to discharge, compared to only 3.9% when no one is present. Having nobody in the room puts you squarely in that lower bracket. Two other things you can handle along the way. Handling funeral arrangements inherently requires visiting multiple service counters: funeral homes, community health service institutions, public security bureaus, and housing provident fund offices (see Section 25). Scheduling this into a regular routine of going out once a day provides ready-made outing arrangements for these days. Hotlines can be called repeatedly, not just once (see Item 11 of this section; call 12356 if you need someone to talk to). "Living alone" itself is also a long-term risk factor. The odds ratio for mortality among those living alone is 1.32, about 30% higher; see Section 22, Item 9 (treating regular meetings with people as a health expense). However, this section only addresses the immediate few days; that long-term balance sheet is calculated separately.

entries.title: After a parent passes away, tell the child truthfully and let them participate in the farewell
entries.cost: Costs no money. The difficulty lies in having to explain things clearly to the child while you yourself are grieving.
entries.summary: Children who lose a father or mother before age 18 have about a 50% higher subsequent probability of death compared to children who have not experienced this. For parental death due to accidents or suicide, it is about 80% higher; for death due to illness, it is about 30% higher. The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends truthfully explaining what happened to the child and supporting the child in attending funerals and farewell ceremonies.
entries.benefit: Included the entire populations born in Denmark between 1968 and 2008 and Sweden between 1973 and 2006, along with 89.3% sampled from those born in Finland between 1987 and 2007. Over 7.3 million people in total. Among them, 189,094 lost a parent before age 18. This group of children had a 50% higher all-cause mortality rate compared to non-bereaved individuals (mortality rate ratio 1.50, 95% CI 1.43–1.58, i.e., approximately 1.5 times). For parental death due to unnatural causes such as accidents and suicide, it was 1.84 (1.71–2.00), about 80% higher. For natural causes such as disease, it was 1.33 (1.24–1.41), about 30% higher. The risk was highest when the child's cause of death fell into the same category as the parent's cause of death. A 2016 American Academy of Pediatrics clinical report for pediatricians directs that when talking with bereaved children, one should explain clearly what happened and what it means, correcting misinformation and misconceptions the child may have heard. The report also provided recommendations on how to support children in participating in funerals and other memorial ceremonies
entries.sources: Li J, et al. (2014). Mortality after parental death in childhood: a nationwide cohort study from three Nordic countries. PLoS Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pmed.1001679>；Schonfeld DJ, Demaria T, Committee on Psychosocial Aspects of Child and Family Health, Disaster Preparedness Advisory Council (2016). Supporting the Grieving Child and Family. Pediatrics, 138(3), e20162147. <https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2016-2147>
entries.notes: When speaking to the child, do not make up stories like "they went on a long journey"; guardianship and foster care arrangements must be put in writing. No original research or guidelines were found regarding whether to transfer schools or send the child to live elsewhere. The author's view is that fewer changes in the child's life are better. The rating of B is not because the numbers are soft. This is a follow-up study of the entire populations of three countries, and the numbers themselves qualify for grade A. The B rating is given because there is no direct trial evidence linking these numbers to specific practices like "how to talk to the child and whether they should attend farewell services." The authors also stated that data on parent-child relationships and children's lifestyles after bereavement are lacking. The elevated risk includes both innate constitutional factors and the long-term impact left by bereavement. For appointing guardians and arranging property, see Section 17. For child support payments and schooling, see Section 18.

entries.title: If grief remains unchanged after six months and life cannot go on, register for an appointment in psychiatry or clinical psychology
entries.cost: Registration fee plus treatment fee. Such therapies are conducted in courses; in trials, they averaged 16 sessions over 19 weeks. The difficulty lies in taking the step yourself to make the appointment.
entries.summary: Approximately one in ten bereaved adults gets stuck. Persistent yearning past six months to the point of being unable to eat, work, or care for children, feeling numb, and believing life is meaningless. This is not a matter of not being strong enough; it has diagnostic criteria and specialized treatments. Targeted therapy has an effective rate of 51%, compared to 28% for general psychotherapy, and it takes effect faster.
entries.benefit: Pooled analysis of 14 studies involving adults whose loved ones did not die from violence and who were not receiving psychiatric treatment themselves. The prevalence of prolonged grief disorder was 9.8% (95% CI 6.8–14.0), or about 10 out of every 100 bereaved adults. The proportion was higher with older age. Another study testing the accuracy of these diagnostic criteria recruited 291 bereaved individuals and conducted three interviews at 0–6, 6–12, and 12–24 months post-loss. The core manifestation of the diagnosis is intense yearning for the deceased. In addition, at least five of the following nine items must be present. The first five are emotional numbness, shock, feeling that life is meaningless, distrust of others, and distress over the loss. The remaining four are difficulty accepting the loss, identity confusion regarding who one is supposed to be, avoiding reality, and inability to move forward with life. These manifestations must occur daily or be severe enough to impair function. Furthermore, they must persist for at least 6 months after the loved one's death and continue to impair daily life. Another randomized trial of 95 people divided into two groups received 16 sessions of treatment over an average of 19 weeks. The response rate for complicated grief therapy was 51%. Standard interpersonal psychotherapy was 28% (P=0.02, difference unlikely to be coincidental). The former also had a faster onset. Number needed to treat was 4.3, meaning on average one additional person improves for every 4.3 individuals treated
entries.sources: Lundorff M, et al. (2017). Prevalence of prolonged grief disorder in adult bereavement: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Journal of Affective Disorders. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jad.2017.01.030>；Prigerson HG, et al. (2009). Prolonged grief disorder: Psychometric validation of criteria proposed for DSM-V and ICD-11. PLoS Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pmed.1000121>；Shear MK, et al. (2005). Treatment of complicated grief: a randomized controlled trial. JAMA. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.293.21.2601>
entries.notes: Do not get fixated on counting months yourself. The true criterion is whether it "impairs eating, sleeping, working, or caring for children"; if these match, go make an appointment. The clinical departments are called psychiatry, psychology, or clinical psychology, and are available in public psychiatric specialty hospitals. In different sources, this diagnosis is called complicated grief or prolonged grief disorder. Different criteria also vary on how long symptoms must persist, with some specifying 6 months and others 12 months. The 9.8% figure comes from 14 studies with considerable methodological differences, and the authors also caution that it may not generalize to other populations.

entries.title: Do not spend money on grief counseling right off the bat; first check whether your grief is genuinely stuck (the symptoms listed in Item 8)
entries.cost: Free; in fact, it saves a counseling fee.
entries.summary: Arranging psychological counseling for all bereaved individuals offers very minimal benefit, which disappears after a while, because most people would naturally recover on their own anyway. But for those who clearly struggle to adapt, therapy is just as effective as treating other psychological issues. Therefore, first check against Item 8 (go to psychiatry if grief is stuck); only spend this money if you match it.
entries.benefit: Calculated by pooling 61 controlled studies: universally providing psychological interventions to bereaved individuals yielded very small benefits immediately after treatment ended, and after some time had passed, no benefits could be seen. Interventions that only recruited bereaved individuals who "clearly struggled to adapt" were as effective as psychotherapy for other psychological issues. The reason studies without prior screening yielded poor results was that the non-intervention group naturally recovered over time on their own anyway. Another pooled analysis of 14 randomized controlled trials showed: treatment delivered to those who had already developed problems was significantly better than control both post-treatment and at follow-up visits, with effects continuing to widen over time. Universal preventive interventions for those who had not yet developed problems were ineffective. Additionally, a study followed 205 people from before spousal loss through 6 and 18 months post-loss. This study identified five trajectories: common grief, chronic grief, chronic depression, improvement during bereavement, and resilience (coping well). Among them, the resilience type was the most common, while the common grief type was relatively uncommon.
entries.sources: Currier JM, et al. (2008). The effectiveness of psychotherapeutic interventions for bereaved persons: a comprehensive quantitative review. Psychological Bulletin. <https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.134.5.648>; Wittouck C, et al. (2011). The prevention and treatment of complicated grief: a meta-analysis. Clinical Psychology Review. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cpr.2010.09.005>; Bonanno GA, et al. (2002). Resilience to loss and chronic grief: a prospective study from preloss to 18-months postloss. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. <https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.83.5.1150>; Stroebe M, et al. (2007). Health outcomes of bereavement. Lancet. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(07)61816-9> (the review cited in the notes)
entries.notes: What is stated here is "not everyone needs to do it," not "nobody should do it." High-risk bereavement, such as that described in Item 4 (loved one died by suicide, accident, or homicide), is precisely supported by evidence as needing it. Those who are already stuck, as in Item 8 (go to psychiatry if grief is stuck), are too. A Lancet review reached the same conclusion: grief is not an illness, and most people do not need professional intervention. Efforts should be directed toward high-risk individuals, as well as those who have already developed complicated grief, post-bereavement depression, and stress disorders.

entries.title: After separation or divorce, do not let health insurance lapse, and do not rely on alcohol to cope
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Renew your health insurance and stop drinking. The difficulty lies in the tendency to rely on alcohol to cope during this period.
entries.summary: People who are separated or divorced have a significantly higher probability of premature death than those who remain married, with the increase being greater for men and younger individuals. This is not necessarily caused by divorce itself; divorced individuals may inherently differ in health and income. There are two things you can control yourself: do not let your health insurance lapse, and do not rely on tobacco or alcohol to get by.
entries.benefit: Calculated by pooling 32 prospective cohort studies, covering over 6.5 million people, 160,000 deaths, over 755,000 divorces, across 11 countries: compared with those who remained married, separated or divorced adults had a significantly elevated risk of premature death. The increase was more pronounced in men and younger individuals than in women and older adults. The authors discussed four possible pathways: first, social selection—people with differing baseline health or conditions are more likely to end up divorced; second, resource disruption—interruption of income and social security; third, health behavior changes—worsening tobacco and alcohol use and sleep routines; fourth, chronic psychological stress (long-term strain).
entries.sources: Sbarra DA, et al. (2011). Divorce and Death: A Meta-Analysis and Research Agenda for Clinical, Social, and Health Psychology. Perspectives on Psychological Science. <https://doi.org/10.1177/1745691611414724>
entries.notes: The original text only stated "significantly elevated" and subgroup comparisons, without providing citable fold-increases, so specific figures are not given here. The magnitude of benefit is rated as Moderate based on "direction is known, but no applicable threshold decrease is available." For property, debts, and bride price upon divorce, see Section 8 and Section 10. For child custody and support arrangements, see Section 10, Item 23 (specify child support and visitation clearly in the divorce agreement).

entries.title: Call 12356 if you need someone to talk to, call 12355 for minors and adolescents, and register for an outpatient psychotherapy clinic if you need to see a doctor
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Both hotlines are free. Outpatient psychotherapy clinics are registered as standard outpatient visits.
entries.summary: If you want someone to talk to, call 12356—this is the National Psychological Assistance Hotline, and it is free. For minors and adolescents, there is also the 12355 Youth Comprehensive Service Platform. If you need to see a doctor, register for an outpatient clinic in psychiatry, psychology, or clinical psychology. When encountering major family changes, unemployment, or dropping out of school, community grid workers and social workers are already supposed to proactively identify these cases.
entries.benefit: The 2026 plan by 25 departments including the National Health Commission mandates improving the operating system of the 12356 psychological assistance hotline, ensuring stable operations and improving answer rates. It requires promoting the establishment of provincial-level 12356 IT platforms, strengthening coordination mechanisms with service hotlines such as 110, and enhancing and effectively utilizing the 12355 Youth Comprehensive Service Platform in linkage and collaboration with 12356. There are three targets for 2030: first, over 80% of administrative villages and urban communities must set up psychological counseling rooms or social work rooms to provide psychological services; second, public psychiatric specialty hospitals at all levels and at least one hospital in every county (district) must provide outpatient psychological services; third, every province must establish a provincial-level 12356 psychological assistance platform. Psychological crisis intervention and psychological assistance teams are composed of psychiatrists, psychotherapists, psychological counselors, licensed social workers, and volunteers. The plan also requires three types of personnel to maintain routine vigilance and detect issues early: grid workers (community staff responsible for designated grid zones), licensed social workers, and volunteers. They must promptly identify psychological crisis risks such as major family changes, unemployment, and dropping out of school (nationwide, issued March 2026).
entries.sources: National Health Commission and 25 other departments (2026). Notice on the Issuance of the Implementation Plan for Improving the Social Psychological Service System and Crisis Intervention Mechanism (Guowei Yizheng Fa [2026] No. 8). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202604/content_7065035.htm>
entries.notes: Rated B because the village and community counseling rooms and county-level psychological outpatient services are goals targeted for completion by 2030, and are not currently available everywhere. Meanwhile, 12356 and 12355 can be dialed right now. For the operating hours and daily service duration of 12356, see Section 1, Item 25. Psychological counseling and psychotherapy are not the same thing. Making diagnoses and prescribing medications must be done by a psychiatrist, and therapy must be conducted in accredited medical institutions. Commercial "healing" and "spiritual counseling" billed by the hour on the market are not part of this system.

entries.title: For the first three months after a major life change, postpone all irreversible major decisions without exception
entries.cost: Costs nothing; it merely delays decisions, though some opportunities might be missed as a result. The difficulty lies in feeling at the time that opportunities wait for no one.
entries.summary: During this period, your judgment regarding various "opportunities" is at its worst. In experiments, grieving individuals were willing to accept 10-odd to over 30 percent less money just to avoid waiting 3 months. For anything involving an amount exceeding one month's income or carrying high costs of regret, postpone it by three months without exception. Talk it through first with someone who has no financial interest in the matter; do not finalize it on the same day.
entries.benefit: Avoid making irreversible property dispositions during the period right after a blow when judgment is at its worst. Such matters include selling a home, resigning from a job, investing survivor pensions or compensation payouts in a lump sum, hastily remarrying, or acting as a guarantor for others. The monetary amount of such decisions is typically on the order of tens of thousands of yuan to an entire house, so the benefit is rated as Moderate. Official documents similarly categorize "major family changes, unemployment, and dropping out of school" as psychological crisis risks that communities should proactively screen for; a person's state during this period is inherently recognized as requiring external support. The U.S. National Institute on Aging (NIA) grief guide lists "trouble making decisions" as a common symptom of grief. It advises: if you have a choice, postpone major life decisions until you feel better; when you are grieving and may not be thinking clearly, it is best not to make major changes such as selling your home or quitting your job. One study conducted three experiments: researchers randomly assigned participants to enter a sad state and then had them choose between "getting money now" or "getting money in 3 months." Compared to emotionally calm individuals, sad individuals were willing to forgo 13% to 34% of the money just to avoid waiting 3 months. This was sadness induced in an experiment, not real bereavement. The U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) warned in 2023 of a scam where imposters pose as funeral homes and tell family members the funeral will be canceled unless extra money is paid immediately. Its primary piece of advice is to resist the pressure to "act immediately"; legitimate businesses will give you time to make decisions.
entries.sources: National Health Commission and 25 other departments (2026). Implementation Plan for Improving the Social Psychological Service System and Crisis Intervention Mechanism (Guowei Yizheng Fa [2026] No. 8). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202604/content_7065035.htm>; National Institute on Aging. Coping With Grief and Loss ("Postpone major decisions if possible" section, page updated 2026-01-26). <https://www.nia.nih.gov/health/grief-and-mourning/coping-grief-and-loss>; Lerner JS, Li Y, Weber EU (2013). The financial costs of sadness. Psychological Science, 24(1), 72-79. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797612450302>; Puig A, Federal Trade Commission (2023-06-15). Imposters prey on families preparing for the funeral of a loved one. <https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2023/06/imposters-prey-families-preparing-funeral-loved-one>
entries.notes: If there is no such disinterested person around you, call 12356 and talk it through once (see Item 11 of this section, call 12356 if you need someone to talk to).
