You can also write it down yourself and re-read it after three days. Rated B because "postponing" is directionally supported by official grief guidelines and a randomized experiment, but no study has directly compared the financial outcomes of bereaved individuals who postponed versus those who did not. The NIA also merely says "until you feel better," without giving a specific timeframe. "Three months" and "exceeding one month's income" are cutoffs set by the author. For common scams targeting the bereaved and elderly, see Section 17 (pension investment, reverse mortgages) and Section 6 (fortune telling). For pitfalls regarding loan guarantees and IOUs, see Section 8. Certain funds must be claimed proactively and are not subject to "postponing": housing provident fund balances, social security benefits, and the three work-related death benefits; see Section 25 and Section 19.

entries.title: Do not treat death as a way to clear debts: life insurance within two years does not pay out, work-related injury is not recognized, and debts are still deducted from the estate first
entries.cost: Costs nothing; it simply does the math clearly.
entries.summary: Life insurance contracts do not pay out for suicide within two years, refunding only what little can be refunded from the policy's cash value. Nor is it recognized as a work-related injury, meaning not a single cent of the three work-related death benefits will be paid. Debts owed are deducted first from the estate you leave behind, and your family only receives what remains. They must also bear the health costs described in Item 4 of this section (bereavement due to suicide or violent death).
entries.benefit: Article 44 of the Insurance Law governs contracts where death of the insured is the condition for payment of insurance proceeds. If the insured commits suicide within two years from the date the contract is formed or its validity is restored, the insurer shall not bear liability for paying insurance proceeds. Cases where the insured lacks civil capacity at the time of suicide—meaning those legally unable to be responsible for their own actions—are exempt from this rule. In such circumstances, the insurance company shall refund the cash value of the insurance policy in accordance with contractual agreements, meaning it only refunds the small amount refundable from the policy, rather than paying the insured sum. Life insurance coverage amounts are typically on the order of hundreds of thousands of yuan, so the benefit is rated as Large. Article 16, Item 3 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance stipulates: self-harm or suicide shall not be identified as a work-related injury or deemed as a work-related injury. Consequently, all three work-related death benefits under Article 39 fall through: first, funeral grants, paid at 6 months of the local average monthly wage of employees in the previous year; second, pensions for dependent relatives; third, a one-off work-related death grant, which is 20 times the previous year's national per capita disposable income of urban residents. Article 1159 of the Civil Code provides: dividing the estate shall clear the taxes and debts that the decedent ought to pay according to law, meaning taxes and debts must be paid out of the estate first, and only the remainder is distributed. Article 1161 provides: heirs shall clear debts limited to the actual value of the estate obtained, meaning they only pay using the inherited portion without paying out of pocket, and those who waive inheritance may be exempt from liability for clearance.
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2015 Amendment). Article 44 of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China. <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7c4060811>; State Council (2010 Revision). Articles 16 and 39 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance (State Council Decree No. 586). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1778064.htm>; National People's Congress (2020). Articles 1159 and 1161 of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China. <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5c500bf>
entries.notes: This calculates only the financial ledger. The other entries in this section and Section 1 are about preventing things from reaching this point. Article 44 of the Insurance Law only governs the first two years; it is cited here to state the statutory provision in full, not to provide a timeline. For the health toll on family members, see Item 4 of this section (spouses of suicide decedents have a 70% to 80% higher risk of newly developing psychiatric disorders within 5 years). For what to do when suicidal thoughts arise, see Section 1, Items 25 and 32; for sequelae after resuscitation, see Section 1, Item 33. For standards on the three work-related death benefits, see Section 19, Item 15. For how estates and debts are handled, see Section 25, Item 11 (heirs only repay using inherited estate assets). For funds that should be claimed, see Section 25, Item 9 (proactively claim housing provident fund and social security benefits one by one).

entries.title: After personally experiencing a car accident, assault, or disaster, do not count on a one-off debriefing immediately following the event; if nightmares, flashbacks, and constant hypervigilance remain severe after one month, go to psychiatry for trauma-focused psychotherapy
entries.cost: Registration fee plus therapy fees, typically 8 to 12 sessions. The difficulty lies in therapy requiring you to revisit the very experiences you are most terrified of remembering.
entries.summary: After a major ordeal, nightmares and being easily startled are very common in the first few weeks, and most people will naturally recover on their own. If they remain severe after a month, it may be post-traumatic stress disorder, for which trauma-focused psychotherapy is noticeably effective. Pulling someone in right after the event to recount what happened—this sort of one-off debriefing—cannot prevent this disorder. In one trial, those who received it were actually worse off three years later.
entries.benefit: The National Health Commission's Diagnostic and Treatment Guidelines for Mental Disorders (2020 Edition) states that an average of approximately 8% of people who experience psychological trauma will develop post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). The core manifestations fall into three categories. First, nightmares and flashbacks, where the scene of the traumatic event repeatedly intrudes. Second, avoiding topics, places, and people associated with the event. Third, persistent hyperarousal, being easily startled, and insomnia. A diagnosis is made only when symptoms persist for more than 1 month and severely impair family life, study, or work. The guidelines state in the section on acute stress disorder that most people return to normal through self-adjustment or acute crisis intervention. Regarding treatment efficacy, look at a 2020 pooled analysis covering 114 randomized controlled trials and 8,171 individuals. Trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy compared with waitlist or usual care showed an SMD of −1.32 (95% CI −1.57 to −1.08, credibility interval), with moderate-quality evidence. Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) was −1.23 (−1.69 to −0.76), with low-quality evidence. SMD and d are on the same scale; 0.8 or higher is considered large, and both therapies exceed this threshold. Standard supportive counseling compared with waitlist showed no significant difference (−0.43, −0.90 to 0.04). A 2013 Cochrane systematic review by the same group of authors included 70 trials and 4,761 individuals, showing a consistent direction. Trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy was −1.62 (−2.03 to −1.21), and EMDR was −1.17 (−2.04 to −0.30). However, the evidence quality assessed at that time was very low. The UK NICE 2018 guideline lays it out as follows: for adults with severe symptoms within one month of the event, provide individual trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy. For those diagnosed or with marked symptoms after one month, provide the same, typically conducting 8 to 12 sessions. For trauma not caused by war, if symptoms have not resolved after 3 months, also offer EMDR. For those with mild symptoms who do not meet the diagnostic threshold, observe during the first month and schedule a follow-up review within the month. The psychological therapies listed in the domestic Chinese guidelines are also these types: prolonged exposure, cognitive processing therapy, and EMDR. Regarding single-session debriefing conducted immediately after an incident, consider three sources of material. A 2002 Cochrane review pooling 11 trials found that a single individual debriefing session did not alleviate distress, nor did it prevent post-traumatic stress disorder. At 3 to 5 months, the OR was 1.22 (0.60–2.46), showing no difference. In one of the trials followed up to 1 year, those who underwent debriefing actually had a higher risk of developing the disorder: OR 2.88 (1.11–7.53), roughly 2.9 times. The authors concluded that compulsory debriefing for traumatized individuals should cease. Another trial recruited hospitalized patients after traffic accidents and randomly assigned them. After 3 years, the debriefed group had significantly worse psychiatric symptoms, travel anxiety, pain, physical problems, overall functioning, and financial difficulties. Among individuals who had severe flashbacks and avoidance at baseline, those who were debriefed still had symptoms after 3 years, while those who were not debriefed had recovered. The NICE guideline explicitly states not to offer psychologically-focused debriefing for the prevention or treatment of PTSD. The rationale is that neither individual nor group sessions demonstrated any benefit, and there were indications of worse outcomes than doing nothing.
entries.sources: Lewis C, et al. (2020). Psychological therapies for post-traumatic stress disorder in adults: systematic review and meta-analysis. European Journal of Psychotraumatology. <https://doi.org/10.1080/20008198.2020.1729633>; Bisson JI, et al. (2013). Psychological therapies for chronic post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in adults. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, CD003388. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD003388.pub4>; Rose S, et al. (2002). Psychological debriefing for preventing post traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, CD000560. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD000560>; Mayou RA, Ehlers A, Hobbs M (2000). Psychological debriefing for road traffic accident victims. Three-year follow-up of a randomised controlled trial. British Journal of Psychiatry. <https://doi.org/10.1192/bjp.176.6.589>; National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (2018). Post-traumatic stress disorder (NG116), recommendations 1.6.4, 1.6.5, 1.6.15–1.6.19. <https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng116/chapter/Recommendations>; General Office of the National Health Commission (2020). Notice on Issuing the Diagnostic and Treatment Guidelines for Mental Disorders (2020 Edition) (Guo Wei Ban Yi Han [2020] No. 945), Chapter 8: Trauma- and Stressor-Related Disorders. <https://www.nhc.gov.cn/yzygj/c100068/202012/b4305ace9e14440792eb76d29602c88a.shtml>
entries.notes: Single-session debriefing refers to bringing people together or meeting individually within a few days after an incident, asking them to recount the entire event and their feelings at that time from beginning to end. The domestic Chinese guidelines still list group debriefing in the table of psychological treatments for acute stress disorder, which diverges from NICE; this entry is written based on trial findings. If your workplace or school organizes such a session following an incident, you do not have to speak if you do not want to, and do not force others to speak either. During the first few weeks, prioritize ensuring physical safety, eating and sleeping properly, and having people around you. When registering at a psychiatry department, psychological department, or clinical psychology department, ask directly whether trauma-focused psychotherapy is available. The principle is the same as in item 9 of this section (Do not spend money on grief counseling right off the bat). Not everyone needs professional intervention; effort should be focused on individuals who remain stuck after one month. Those whose family members died from accidents or homicides often present with these symptoms as well; see item 4 of this section (Family member died from an accident or homicide). For what to do first after sexual assault, see section 13, item 42 (After being sexually assaulted). When emergency responders such as police officers, healthcare workers, and firefighters develop this condition due to work, it is already included in the occupational disease catalog. For details, see section 19, item 10 (Notes under the item on dust, noise, and chemical toxins).

chapters.title: School-Age Children
chapters.intro:
Section 20 covers the first year of a child's life after birth. Section 18 calculates how much money and time it takes to raise a child. The intervening span of over a decade—ages 3 to 18—is addressed in this section. The item on age-specific screen time management starts from age 0, because the official tiers are specifically 0–3 years, 3–6 years, and primary/secondary school, so splitting it up would make it less practical to use. This section answers only one question: when "don't compromise academic study" collides with "physical health," which things cannot wait. They cannot wait because these matters have time-sensitive windows; once missed, they cannot be made up. Whether academics ought to be so fiercely competitive is not discussed in this section; only the windows and numbers are provided.

The first eight items, item 12 (Cycloplegic refraction), item 13 (Pit and fissure sealing), items 15 through 19, and item 21 (Head injuries during sports) account for mortality and genuine, lasting physical and psychological harm. Among them, items 16 and 17 discuss how to manage children at home: no hitting or scolding, and attend parenting classes that teach actionable methods. Item 18 discusses not sending children to closed-management internet addiction boot camps. Item 19 discusses teaching children to recognize private body parts and to tell parents when touched. Item 9 (Do not buy "myopia cure" products) and item 20 (Riding a bicycle on the road before the legal age) calculate financial costs. Item 10 (Explicit regulations on sleep, homework, physical education, and academic rankings), item 11 (Suspending schooling while retaining student status), and item 14 (When children love playing video games) calculate time. For drowning, traffic safety, helmets, and HPV vaccines, see section 1. For infants and toddlers, see section 20. For child scams and in-game top-ups, see section 5. For legal red lines minors themselves must not cross, see section 9. For recognizing medical emergencies and calling an ambulance, see section 13. For children following the death of a parent, see section 29. None of these will be repeated in this section.

The entries in this section are divided by theme into the following blocks, with item numbers in parentheses:

**Medical Care That Cannot Wait**: Immediate hospital visits for sudden severe pain (Item 1), do not delay treatment to wait for exams to finish (Item 2), annual student physical examination report forms (Item 7).

**Eyes and Teeth**: Spending a full 2 hours outdoors (Item 4), age-based regulations on screen denial (Item 5), the deeper the degree of myopia (Item 6), do not buy "myopia cure" products (Item 9), cycloplegic refraction (Item 12), pit and fissure sealing (Item 13).

**School Affairs**: Reporting bullying to the school on the same day (Item 3), explicit regulations on sleep, homework, physical education, and rankings (Item 10), eligibility for leave of absence while retaining student status (Item 11).

**Psychology and Home Discipline**: Depression screening (Item 8), when children love playing video games (Item 14), when a child discloses same-sex attraction (Item 15), do not use physical discipline to manage children (Item 16), attending parenting classes (Item 17), do not send children to internet addiction boot camps (Item 18), recognizing private body parts (Item 19).

**On the Road and on the Sports Field**: Do not ride on roads under the legal age (Item 20), do not return to play on the same day after a head impact in sports (Item 21).

entries.title: If a child complains of sudden, progressively worsening severe pain, go to the hospital immediately; do not make them endure it until school lets out
entries.cost: Costs no money. Take half a day off work and take the child to the emergency department.
entries.summary: Some medical conditions are measured in hours. Sudden severe pain on one side of a boy's scrotum may be testicular torsion—meaning the blood vessel connected to the testicle has twisted, cutting off blood supply. If managed within 6 hours, the testicular salvage rate is 97.2%. If delayed to 19 to 24 hours, only 42.5% remain salvageable. This type of pain cannot wait until school dismisses, nor can it wait until exams are over.
entries.benefit: Following rigorous criteria, 30 sets of case reports covering 2,116 patients with testicular torsion were compiled and analyzed together. Among these, 1,283 cases were tabulated in 6-hour intervals. Calculated from pain onset, the testicular salvage rate was 97.2% at 0 to 6 hours; 79.3% at 7 to 12 hours; 61.3% at 13 to 18 hours; 42.5% at 19 to 24 hours; 24.4% at 25 to 48 hours; and 7.4% after 48 hours. Grouped into broader time windows, it was 90.4% within 12 hours, 54.0% at 13 to 24 hours, and 18.1% beyond 24 hours. The authors concluded that the salvageable window can be longer than the commonly cited 6 to 8 hours. Therefore, even if pain has persisted for a long time, medical intervention is still necessary; do not skip care assuming "it is too late anyway." In US pediatric inpatient data from the three years 2000, 2003, and 2006, 2,443 boys aged 1 month to under 18 years underwent surgery for testicular torsion. There are two peak ages of onset: one during the first year of life, and the other right at the onset of puberty.
entries.sources: Mellick LB, et al. (2019). A Systematic Review of Testicle Survival Time After a Torsion Event. Pediatric Emergency Care. <https://doi.org/10.1097/PEC.0000000000001287>；Zhao LC, Lautz TB, Meeks JJ, Maizels M. (2011). Pediatric testicular torsion epidemiology using a national database: incidence, risk of orchiectomy and possible measures toward improving the quality of care. Journal of Urology, 186(5), 2009-2013. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.juro.2011.07.024>
entries.notes: Tell boys in advance: if there is sudden severe pain down there, speak up immediately—there is no need to feel embarrassed. Testicular torsion is common in boys just entering puberty. In the author's experience, quite a few children feel too embarrassed to say anything and simply endure it silently. Other conditions similarly measured in hours include acute appendicitis (prolonged delays lead to perforation), diabetic ketoacidosis, and meningitis. This section did not verify item-by-item the exact "rate of deterioration per hour of delay" for these latter conditions. The author summarizes their shared warning signs as: sudden onset, continuous worsening, and completely unlike anything experienced before. For recognizing medical emergencies and calling an ambulance, see section 13.

entries.title: Do not postpone necessary treatments just to "wait until exams are over"; some windows track bone age, not examination schedules
entries.cost: Costs no money; the only decision is whether to do it earlier or later. Taking leave and follow-up visits require time, while treatment costs are separate. The difficult part is that bracing requires wearing the brace for at least 18 hours a day, which the child must endure continuously.
entries.summary: Scoliosis is a sideways curvature of the spine. A brace is a rigid shell vest worn on the torso to support the spine. When worn while bones are still growing, 75% of children do not progress to a 50-degree curve by the time skeletal growth finishes, compared with only 42% of those observed without bracing. The window for wearing it aligns with the completion of skeletal growth, not with the high school or college entrance exams; by the time exams finish, the opportunity may be lost.
entries.benefit: A multicenter trial enrolled 242 patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis who met the criteria for bracing. Among them, 116 were randomized, and 126 chose their own treatment track (bracing vs. observation). Success and failure criteria were predefined: curve progression to 50 degrees or greater was counted as treatment failure, while failing to reach this degree by the completion of skeletal growth was counted as treatment success. Children in the bracing group were instructed to wear the brace for at least 18 hours daily. Analysis was conducted on an intention-to-treat basis according to initial group assignment, regardless of whether they actually wore it enough. In the randomized cohort, the success rate was 75% in the bracing group versus 42% in the observation group (OR 4.11, 95% CI 1.85–9.16), meaning the odds of success were approximately 4 times that of observation alone. Combining the randomized and preference cohorts yielded 72% versus 48% (after adjusting for baseline differences between cohorts, OR 1.93, 1.08–3.46, still roughly 1.9 times). A higher number of daily brace-wear hours was associated with higher success rates (P < 0.001, making it highly unlikely to be a chance finding). The trial was terminated early because bracing proved clearly effective.
entries.sources: Weinstein SL, et al. (2013). Effects of bracing in adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis. New England Journal of Medicine. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1307337>
entries.notes: Scoliosis is used as an example here because it has randomized controlled trials and a well-defined time window. It also happens to be one of the key screening items in student health checks (see item 7). In the author's experience, conditions in the same category include strabismus, amblyopia, dental caries, and elective surgeries for conditions such as congenital heart disease. The later these are addressed, the worse the outcomes may be, or the higher the cost. This section has not verified each condition's specific window individually; consult a specialist for exact timings. If concerned about missing schoolwork, during compulsory education, students can take a suspension of study (leave of absence) for up to 1 year while retaining their student status; see item 11.

entries.title: If a child is bullied, report it to the school on the same day and demand a written resolution; directly call the police if it involves physical assault, extortion of money, or spreading rumors
entries.cost: Costs no money. Reach out to the homeroom teacher, as well as the school's student bullying prevention and governance committee. If calling the police, dial 110. The difficult part is withstanding well-meaning advice like "don't make a big deal out of this."
entries.summary: Children who are bullied by peers are approximately 2.2 times as likely to develop suicidal ideation compared with those who are not bullied, and roughly 2.6 times as likely to attempt suicide. Upon receiving a report, the school must investigate immediately; if bullying is confirmed, it must implement disciplinary punishment or sanctions. Serious cases cannot be concealed and must be reported to public security organs. Therefore, report on the same day, demand that the formal determination procedure be initiated, and leave a paper trail.
entries.benefit: Synthesizing 34 studies covering 284,375 children and adolescents, peer victimization was associated with suicidal ideation, OR 2.23 (95% CI 2.10–2.37), meaning the odds of developing ideation were approximately 2.2 times higher than among non-bullied peers. Another 9 studies with 70,102 individuals showed that being bullied was associated with suicide attempts, OR 2.55 (1.95–3.34), roughly 2.6 times. Results were consistent across gender, age, and varying study qualities. Cyberbullying showed an even stronger association with suicidal ideation than offline bullying. Article 21 of the Provisions on the Protection of Minors in Schools lists five categories of behaviors: beating, kicking, slapping, scratching/biting, shoving, and pulling/dragging; insulting, mocking, and assigning derogatory nicknames; snatching, extorting, demanding by force, or intentionally damaging property; malicious ostracism and isolation; and fabricating facts online to defame or disseminate rumors. This article also stipulates that when the party with an advantage in age, physical strength, or numbers deliberately or maliciously engages in these acts, causing personal injury, property loss, or psychological harm, it can be formally determined as bullying. Article 22 mandates that school faculty and staff who discover abnormal student emotions or physical injuries must promptly investigate and report them. Article 23 requires schools to investigate immediately upon receiving a report, submit the matter to the bullying governance committee for determination and handling, and notify parents to participate. When bullying is determined to have occurred, educational discipline or disciplinary sanctions must be imposed. Severe bullying behaviors that violate public security administration or are suspected of constituting crimes must not be concealed, and must be promptly reported to public security organs and education administrative departments (Nationwide, effective September 1, 2021).
entries.sources: van Geel M, et al. (2014). Relationship between peer victimization, cyberbullying, and suicide in children and adolescents: a meta-analysis. JAMA Pediatrics. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamapediatrics.2013.4143>; Ministry of Education (2021). Provisions on the Protection of Minors in Schools (Order of the Ministry of Education No. 50, Articles 21, 22, 23). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-06/02/content_5614946.htm>; Ministry of Education and eleven other departments (2017). Comprehensive Governance Plan for Strengthening the Prevention of Bullying among Primary and Secondary School Students (Jiao Du [2017] No. 10, III (1)). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2018/content_5294435.htm>
entries.notes: The signs singled out in Article 22 are obvious emotional abnormalities and physical injuries. If an unexplained injury appears on a child's body, or their mood suddenly seems wrong, ask first. This pooled analysis that combined multiple studies was merely a longitudinal record without controlled grouping, so it cannot prove that bullying alone causes suicide. However, the direction and magnitude of the risk are clear. The Comprehensive Plan for Strengthening the Governance of Bullying Among Primary and Secondary School Students additionally mandates strictly distinguishing between bullying and rough-and-tumble play among students. Therefore, schools are obligated to make formal determinations, rather than brushing things off with "children just fooling around."

entries.title: Having children spend a full 2 hours outdoors every day is currently the only myopia prevention measure supported by randomized trials among cost-free, non-pharmaceutical options
entries.cost: Costs nothing. However, time must be carved out every day, which mostly has to be squeezed from homework and online class time. The difficulty lies in having to achieve it every single day, not just doing it a few times.
entries.summary: Adding 40 minutes of outdoor class time per day for first graders in primary school reduced new cases of myopia after 3 years from about 40% to about 30%. The target given by the National Health Commission is no less than 2 hours outdoors during daytime each day, or a cumulative 14 hours per week. Overcast days count as well.
entries.benefit: First-grade students across 12 primary schools in Guangzhou were randomized by school cluster (952 students in intervention schools, 951 in control schools, mean age 6.6 years). The intervention consisted of adding one 40-minute outdoor activity class each school day and encouraging parents to take children outside more after school. Over 3 years, the cumulative incidence rate of new-onset myopia was 30.4% in the intervention group (259 cases among 853 eligible participants) versus 39.5% in the control group (287 cases among 726 participants). The difference between the two groups was -9.1 percentage points (95% CI -14.1 to -4.1, P<0.001), with the true difference roughly falling between 4 and 14 percentage points lower. Over 3 years, the increase in degree (change in spherical equivalent refraction) was -1.42 D versus -1.59 D, a difference of 0.17 D (P=0.04). The intervention group progressed slightly less. D (diopter) is the unit measuring prescription power. For axial length elongation (the front-to-back length of the eyeball), no difference between the two groups was detected (P=0.07). The Ten Core Knowledge Items on Prevention and Control of Myopia in Children and Adolescents requires that children and adolescents spend no less than 2 hours per day, or a cumulative 14 hours per week, in daytime outdoor activities. It notes that outdoor activities retain protective effects even on overcast days, and instructs to avoid periods of intense sunlight and high temperatures in the afternoon. Randomized trials also exist for pharmaceutical myopia prevention. In Hong Kong, 474 non-myopic children aged 4 to 9 were divided into three groups to use eye drops once nightly for two consecutive years. Among those using 0.05% atropine, the incidence of myopia over two years was 28.4%, compared to 53.0% for the placebo group. For 0.01% atropine, it was 45.9%, showing no detectable difference compared to placebo
entries.sources: He M, et al. (2015). Effect of Time Spent Outdoors at School on the Development of Myopia Among Children in China: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2015.10803>；Yam JC, Zhang XJ, Zhang Y, et al. (2023). Effect of Low-Concentration Atropine Eyedrops vs Placebo on Myopia Incidence in Children: The LAMP2 Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA, 329(6), 472-481. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2022.24162>；General Office of the National Health Commission (2023). Ten Core Knowledge Items on Prevention and Control of Myopia in Children and Adolescents (Guo Wei Ban Fu You Han [2023] No. 278). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6894284.htm>
entries.notes: This trial lasted only 3 years, and the participating children all started at age 6. A 9.1 percentage point difference in myopia incidence between the two groups can only keep a portion of people from becoming myopic; it cannot guarantee myopia prevention. The same Ten Core Knowledge Items document also provides several practices. Reading and writing should follow the "one foot, one fist, one inch" rule (eyes one foot from the book, chest one fist from the desk, fingers one inch from the pen tip). After 20 minutes of close-up visual work, look into the distance for at least 20 seconds. For primary and secondary school students using electronic screens for non-learning purposes, a single session should not exceed 15 minutes, and daily cumulative time should not exceed 1 hour. "Spending time outdoors" and "having physical education class" are not the same thing; standing outside during class breaks counts as well. The authors of the atropine eye drops trial noted that further trials are needed for confirmation, and long-term safety must be evaluated further. Whether to administer drops and what concentration to use should be discussed with an ophthalmologist. The author found no randomized trials for other cost-free, non-pharmaceutical methods.

entries.title: No screens for ages 0 to 3, minimize screens for ages 3 to 6, and no more than 1 hour per day for non-learning purposes among primary and secondary school students
entries.cost: Costs nothing. What is difficult is taking screens away from children's hands, and also for parents themselves to watch less in front of their children.
entries.summary: The National Health Commission requires providing no screens for ages 0 to 3, and avoiding contact as much as possible for ages 3 to 6. For primary and secondary school students, non-learning use should not exceed 15 minutes per session and 1 hour per day. The rationale is that prolonged close-up eye use causes myopia to develop earlier. The evidence linking screens to myopia is not as robust; what has genuinely proven effective in trials is 2 hours outdoors every day.
entries.benefit: Item 4 of the Ten Core Knowledge Items on Prevention and Control of Myopia in Children and Adolescents verbatim states: "Infants and toddlers aged 0–3 years should not use video screen electronic devices such as mobile phones, tablets, and computers; young children aged 3–6 years should avoid exposure to and use of video screen electronic devices such as mobile phones, tablets, and computers as much as possible; for primary and secondary school students, single-session duration of non-learning electronic screen use should not exceed 15 minutes, and daily cumulative duration should not exceed 1 hour." The same item explicitly notes: "Prolonged close-up use of electronic screen products easily depletes children's hyperopic reserve and is a major cause of early-onset and high-prevalence myopia among children and adolescents." The 2018 implementation plan issued by eight departments including the Ministry of Education set consistent requirements for parents, adding: "The younger the age, the shorter the continuous use time of electronic products should be." The research evidence is far weaker: a systematic review included 33 studies, with 11 entered into meta-analysis, covering subjects aged 3 months to 33 years. Looking only at smart mobile phones and tablets, the odds ratio for myopia was 1.26 (95% CI 1.00 to 1.60, I²=77%). Combining them with computers yielded 1.77 (1.28 to 2.45, I²=87%). The authors' conclusion only reached "may be associated," and made clear that not one of the 33 studies possessed a reliable measurement of screen time
entries.sources: General Office of the National Health Commission (2023). Ten Core Knowledge Items on Prevention and Control of Myopia in Children and Adolescents (Guo Wei Ban Fu You Han [2023] No. 278). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6894284.htm> ; Ministry of Education and seven other departments (2018). Implementation Plan for Comprehensive Prevention and Control of Myopia in Children and Adolescents (Jiao Ti Yi [2018] No. 3). <http://www.moe.gov.cn/srcsite/A17/moe_943/s3285/201808/t20180830_346672.html> ; Foreman J, Salim AT, Praveen A, et al. (2021). Association between digital smart device use and myopia: a systematic review and meta-analysis. The Lancet Digital Health, 3(12), e806-e818. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S2589-7500(21)00135-7> ; Madigan S, McArthur BA, Anhorn C, Eirich R, Christakis DA (2020). Associations between screen use and child language skills: a systematic review and meta-analysis. JAMA Pediatrics, 174(7), 665-675. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamapediatrics.2020.0327>
entries.notes: Rated B because what the authorities provide are age-tiered regulatory provisions, not figures measured from trials. The lower bound of the odds ratio given by the study sat right at 1.00, and the authors only dared to describe it as "may be associated." Therefore, treat it simply as an actionable house rule; do not treat it as "avoiding screens means you won't get myopia." What is truly backed by randomized trials is Item 4 (2 hours outdoors). Eyes must also be checked in the preschool years. The same document stipulates that regular refractive screenings should be conducted for ages 1–3, 4–6, and after age 7 to track how much hyperopic reserve remains. For screening methods, see Item 12 (cycloplegic refraction). The relationship between screens and children's language skills has also been meta-analyzed, pooling 42 studies and 18,905 individuals. Greater screen time was associated with poorer language skills (r=−0.14, 95% CI −0.18 to −0.10). However, co-viewing and watching programs with educational content were conversely positively correlated (r=0.16 and 0.13). This is correlation, not causation, and merely shows that substituting screen time for spending time talking with children is a bad trade-off.

entries.title: Treat myopia as lasting damage: the higher the degree, the more retinal detachment, macular degeneration, and glaucoma in the future
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Requires doing nothing in itself; the necessary actions are covered in Items 4 and 5 (2 hours outdoors, age-tiered screen management).
entries.summary: Myopia does not resolve on its own, and the degree cannot be rolled back. Nor is it simply a matter of "putting on a pair of glasses." Compared with non-myopic individuals, the likelihood of developing myopic macular degeneration is over a dozen times higher for mild myopia, and hundreds of times higher above 600 degrees. For retinal detachment, mild myopia is roughly 3 times higher, and above 600 degrees is roughly 13 times higher. Therefore, the deeper a child's myopia progresses, the greater the risks they must bear in the future.
entries.benefit: A systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized studies prior to June 2019, categorized into three tiers by refractive error: low (−0.5 to −3.00 D), moderate (−3.00 to −6.00 D), and high (≤−6.00 D, above 600 degrees). Compared to non-myopic individuals, the odds ratios for myopic macular degeneration were successively 13.57 (95% CI 6.18 to 29.79), 72.74 (33.18 to 159.48), and 845.08 (230.05 to 3104.34). For retinal detachment, they were successively 3.15 (1.92 to 5.17), 8.74 (7.28 to 10.50), and 12.62 (6.65 to 23.94). For posterior subcapsular cataract, they were successively 1.56 (1.32 to 1.84), 2.55 (1.98 to 3.28), and 4.55 (2.66 to 7.75). For open-angle glaucoma, low myopia was 1.59 (1.33 to 1.91), while moderate and high myopia combined was 2.92 (1.89 to 4.52). The odds ratios for developing visual impairment over age 60 across the three tiers were successively 1.71 (1.07 to 2.74), 5.54 (3.12 to 9.85), and 87.63 (34.50 to 222.58). The Ten Core Knowledge Items on Prevention and Control of Myopia in Children and Adolescents states congruently: an error above 600 degrees constitutes high myopia; the incidence of blinding eye diseases such as cataracts, open-angle glaucoma, myopic macular degeneration, retinal detachment, and myopic optic neuropathy is significantly higher in this population than in other groups, and "myopia is preventable and controllable, but irreversible"
entries.sources: Haarman AEG, Enthoven CA, Tideman JWL, Tedja MS, Verhoeven VJM, Klaver CCW (2020). The complications of myopia: a review and meta-analysis. Investigative Ophthalmology & Visual Science, 61(4), 49. <https://doi.org/10.1167/iovs.61.4.49> ; General Office of the National Health Commission (2023). Ten Core Knowledge Items on Prevention and Control of Myopia in Children and Adolescents (Guo Wei Ban Fu You Han [2023] No. 278). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6894284.htm>
entries.notes: All studies included in the pooling were observational, and the odds ratios are unusually large. The confidence interval for high myopia and macular degeneration ranges from 230 to 3104, indicating substantial heterogeneity among the underlying studies. The figures can only be interpreted as orders of magnitude, not as precise values. The visual impairment numbers in the benefits section were calculated on people over 60 years old. From this, the author infers that these consequences mostly do not manifest until middle-to-older age. Myopia is not solved merely by prescribing a pair of glasses; it is well worth the effort to delay and control it. For follow-up checkups after diagnosis, see Item 12 (cycloplegic refraction). Do not purchase products claiming to cure it; see Item 9 (curing myopia).

entries.title: Review the annual student physical examination report card yourself, and take abnormal findings to the hospital for evaluation within the year
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Physical examination fees during compulsory education are paid from school public operating funds; parents do not pay extra.
entries.summary: Primary and secondary schools organize a student physical examination once a year. The key items to look out for on the report card are overweight, obesity, malnutrition, abnormal spinal curvature, poor vision, and dental caries. Don't just glance at the height and weight and put the sheet away. If there are abnormalities in these items, take your child to a specialist within the year to have it evaluated thoroughly.
entries.benefit: The Administrative Measures for Student Health Examinations in Primary and Secondary Schools (2021 Edition) mandates that primary and secondary schools organize 1 health examination per year for enrolled students. Surgical examinations include the head, neck, chest, spine, limbs, skin, and lymph nodes. Ophthalmic examinations include external eye appearance, distance visual acuity, and diopters (degree of myopia or hyperopia). The individual report card issued must include the detected findings, an overall evaluation, and health guidance recommendations. Among these, overweight, obesity, malnutrition, abnormal spinal curvature, poor vision, and dental caries (tooth decay) must serve as focal points for guidance. Educational administration departments should establish records and conduct follow-up for students presenting with health problems (documenting them and tracking them thereafter). Health examination costs for students during the compulsory education stage are covered by school public operating funds, with parents paying nothing extra (nationwide, promulgated September 2021)
entries.sources: National Health Commission, Ministry of Education (2021). Administrative Measures for Student Health Examinations in Primary and Secondary Schools (2021 Edition) (Guo Wei Yi Fa [2021] No. 29). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-10/21/content_5644100.htm>
entries.notes: Rated B because this is a document specifying school requirements rather than an efficacy study. What it guarantees is "checking every year, checking these specific items, and following up on discovered abnormalities"; it does not guarantee that someone will manage it once detected. A physical examination is merely an initial screening, not a definitive diagnosis. Poor vision requires an ophthalmology visit for cycloplegic refraction (Item 12). Abnormal spinal curvature requires orthopedics or spine surgery (Item 2; do not delay treatment just to wait until after exams). Both steps require parents to take the child themselves.

entries.title: Conduct a depression screening for children aged 12 to 18; do not treat school psychological evaluations as a clinical diagnosis
entries.cost: 0 to several tens of yuan, completing a screening questionnaire at a community health center or outpatient clinic. Calling the 12355 and 12356 hotlines is free of charge.
entries.summary: US preventive guidelines recommend screening children aged 12 to 18 for major depression, whereas evidence is insufficient for ages 11 and under. In the United States, suicide is the second leading cause of death among children aged 10 to 19. Annual school psychological evaluations are merely broad surveys and cannot serve as diagnoses. If a child expresses distress themselves, register directly for psychiatric or clinical psychology care.
entries.benefit: The US Preventive Services Task Force issued a recommendation statement in 2022. It recommends screening adolescents aged 12 to 18 for major depressive disorder (B recommendation). A "B" rating indicates moderate certainty that the net benefit is moderate, making it worth doing. For screening children aged 11 and under for major depressive disorder, evidence is insufficient (I statement, meaning evidence is inadequate to make a recommendation). For dedicated screening of suicide risk in children and adolescents, evidence for both benefits and harms is insufficient (I statement). The document notes that suicide is the second leading cause of death among individuals aged 10 to 19. It also points out that major depression in children and adolescents is closely linked to many subsequent problems. These issues include recurrent depressive episodes in adulthood, other mental disorders, and elevated risks of suicidal ideation, suicide attempts, and suicide mortality. The Ten Measures to Further Strengthen Mental Health Work in Primary and Secondary Schools requires establishing a three-tier service system comprising homeroom teachers, full-time and part-time mental health teachers, and psychiatrists. Each student is to undergo psychological evaluations no more than once per academic year on average. The document also calls for advancing referral mechanisms for psychiatric medical care and post-recovery return-to-school mechanisms. It mandates leveraging the roles of the 12355 youth service desk and the 12356 psychological assistance hotline (nationwide, promulgated October 2025)
entries.sources: US Preventive Services Task Force (2022). Screening for Depression and Suicide Risk in Children and Adolescents: US Preventive Services Task Force Recommendation Statement. JAMA. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2022.16946>；General Office of the Ministry of Education (2025). Ten Measures to Further Strengthen Mental Health Work in Primary and Secondary Schools (Jiao Ji Ting [2025] No. 2). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202510/content_7045528.htm>
entries.notes: Rated B because the original text provides a rating of recommendation strength, not an effect size convertible into numbers. Furthermore, it is a US recommendation; there are no corresponding official domestic screening guidelines in China. A positive screening result merely indicates that further evaluation is required; it is not equivalent to a diagnosis. For actions to take when suicidal ideation is present, see Section 1, Item 25. For coping strategies at home, see Section 29.

entries.title: Do not purchase products and services claiming to "cure myopia" or "reduce prescription degrees"
entries.cost: Costs no money; on the contrary, it saves you this expense.
entries.summary: The State Administration for Market Regulation has explicitly stated that "under current medical technology conditions, myopia cannot be cured." Those promoting claims such as "recovery," "diopter reduction," "curing myopia," and "diopter restoration" are to be strictly investigated and dealt with. Exclude products immediately upon seeing such wording, with no need to compare prices further. Eye protection devices count as medical devices, and e-commerce platforms have a responsibility to verify whether sellers are qualified to sell them.
entries.benefit: A special rectification campaign notice from the General Office of the State Administration for Market Regulation (November 2021 to March 2022) made clear: "Under current medical technology conditions, myopia cannot be cured." The notice demanded that marketing activities for children and adolescent myopia prevention and control products using misleading expressions such as "rehabilitation," "recovery," "diopter reduction," "myopia cure," "myopia nemesis," and "diopter restoration" be investigated and handled strictly in accordance with the law. The notice required intensified crackdowns targeting acts of deceiving consumers through marketing propaganda that falsely appropriates the name of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) or makes false pretexts using TCM theories and techniques. The notice also required severe crackdowns on two types of false and illegal advertisements: those using the names or images of patients to compare effects before and after treatment, and those making reassuring commitments regarding the safety and efficacy of treatment. The notice required e-commerce platforms to strictly fulfill their responsibility for reviewing business qualifications for medical devices such as eye protection devices and related special commodities (verifying whether sellers are qualified to sell them) (National)
entries.sources: General Office of the State Administration for Market Regulation (2021). Notice on Launching a Special Rectification Campaign Against Illegal and Non-Compliant Commercial Marketing and Promotion of Children and Adolescent Myopia Prevention and Control Products. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-11/12/content_5650400.htm>
entries.notes: A grade of B is given because this is based on the regulatory authority's enforcement determination criteria rather than results measured from controlled product trials. However, regarding the statement that "myopia cannot be cured," the health authorities and regulatory authorities are in agreement: the *Ten Core Knowledge Points for Children and Adolescent Myopia Prevention and Control* states that "myopia is preventable and controllable, but irreversible." The two interventions that genuinely have evidence are in Item 4 (outdoors) and Item 12 (standardized optometric exams, glasses fitting, and follow-ups). For anti-blue light glasses, see Section 6.

entries.title: Sleep, homework, physical education, and rankings all have explicit regulations; if the school fails to meet them, you can raise the issue
entries.cost: Costs no money. Knowing the provisions is enough, and reporting them to the school or local education administrative department when necessary. The difficulty lies in having to speak up.
entries.summary: Documents specify that primary school students should sleep 10 hours a day, middle school students 9 hours, and high school students 8 hours. Primary school morning classes generally begin no earlier than 8:20, and secondary schools no earlier than 8:00. In 2025, it was further stipulated that daily physical activities must not be less than 2 hours, and ranking students by test scores is prohibited. If a child chronically doesn't get enough sleep, check against these rules first rather than immediately blaming the child for dawdling.
entries.benefit: The *Notice on Further Strengthening the Management of Sleep for Primary and Secondary School Students* stipulates: primary school students should sleep 10 hours a day, junior high school students 9 hours, and senior high school students 8 hours. Morning class time for primary schools is generally no earlier than 8:20, and for secondary schools generally no earlier than 8:00. Schools may not require students to arrive early at school to participate in unified educational and teaching activities. Bedtime for primary school students is generally no later than 21:20, for junior high school students no later than 22:00, and for senior high school students no later than 23:00. Off-campus training institutions must conclude tutoring no later than 20:30, and online live-streamed tutoring must conclude no later than 21:00. Gaming services may not be provided to minors daily from 22:00 to 8:00 the following day (National, issued March 2021). The *Ten Measures for Further Strengthening Mental Health Work for Primary and Secondary School Students* includes several other provisions: comprehensively promote a daily comprehensive physical activity time of no less than 2 hours for primary and secondary school students, and encourage the implementation of "15-minute class breaks." It also stipulates that ranking students based on test scores is prohibited, strictly forbids assigning mechanical, repetitive, and punitive homework, and encourages setting one "homework-free day" each week (National, issued October 2025)
entries.sources: General Office of the Ministry of Education (2021). Notice on Further Strengthening the Management of Sleep for Primary and Secondary School Students (Jiao Ji Ting Han [2021] No. 11). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-04/02/content_5597443.htm>; General Office of the Ministry of Education (2025). Ten Measures for Further Strengthening Mental Health Work for Primary and Secondary School Students (Jiao Ji Ting [2025] No. 2). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202510/content_7045528.htm>
entries.notes: Both of these are documents issued by the competent authorities. How well they are implemented varies greatly across localities and schools, which is why this item is graded B. Their utility is in letting you know what things schools were supposed to do in the first place, giving you grounds to stand on when negotiating. For adults' sleep accounting, see Sections 2 and 3.

entries.title: If a child can no longer hold up, they can take a leave of absence; the school must preserve their student status, for up to 1 year
entries.cost: Costs no money. The parents or other legal guardians submit an application to the school. The difficulty lies in first accepting that the child will pause for a period of time.
entries.summary: Taking a leave of absence has a formal system. Parents or other guardians submit an application, which is confirmed by the school and reported to higher authorities for approval. Each leave lasts up to 1 year; if further leave is needed upon expiration, reapply. During the leave of absence, the school must preserve the child's student status, and they return to continue their schooling upon resumption. Specific measures are determined by each province; inquire with the school's academic affairs office or the local education bureau.
entries.benefit: Article 16 of the *Measures for the Management of Primary and Secondary School Student Status* stipulates how to handle leaves of absence. A student's leave of absence is applied for by parents or other legal guardians. After confirmation by the school, it is reported to the superior student status management department for approval. Upon resumption of studies, the school should process relevant procedures promptly. The duration of a single application for a leave of absence shall not exceed 1 year; if it is genuinely necessary to continue the leave upon expiration, a new application should be processed. During the student's leave of absence, the school should preserve their student status (keeping the student's identity and spot reserved). Specific measures for leave of absence and resumption of studies are formulated by provincial-level education administrative departments (National, issued January 2025). The *Ten Measures for Further Strengthening Mental Health Work for Primary and Secondary School Students* requires promoting the construction of mechanisms for referral and medical treatment of mental illnesses and resumption of studies after recovery, and guiding schools in formulating contingency plans for managing campus psychological crises
entries.sources: Ministry of Education (2025). Measures for the Management of Primary and Secondary School Student Status (Jiao Ji [2025] No. 1, Article 16). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202502/content_7002620.htm>; General Office of the Ministry of Education (2025). Ten Measures for Further Strengthening Mental Health Work for Primary and Secondary School Students (Jiao Ji Ting [2025] No. 2). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202510/content_7045528.htm>; Ministry of Education (2021). Provisions on the School Protection of Minors (Ministry of Education Order No. 50, Article 12). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-06/02/content_5614946.htm>
entries.notes: In the author's experience, clarify three things before processing it: what medical certificates need to be issued, how the student status is recorded in the system during the leave of absence, and whether resuming studies means returning to the original grade or repeating a grade lower. A grade of B is given because the conditions required for a leave of absence, what materials to submit, and how resumption of studies connects are all decided by provincial education departments themselves; the national level only establishes a framework. Article 12 of the *Provisions on the School Protection of Minors* also requires compulsory education schools to improve reporting and filing systems for students who drop out, take leaves of absence, or take long-term leave. Therefore, a leave of absence is something schools have handled before, not a special exception made only for you.

entries.title: If poor vision is detected, go to a hospital for cycloplegic refraction, and then follow up according to the intervals prescribed by the doctor
entries.cost: Several tens to several hundreds of yuan in examination and eyewear fitting fees. After pupil dilation, the child will experience photophobia and blurred near vision, taking half a day to one or two days to recover.
entries.summary: Cycloplegic refraction involves first instilling a type of eyedrop to relax the muscle responsible for focusing inside the eye before testing the prescription. This is performed in a hospital and is the most accurate method for diagnosing myopia. The National Health Commission explicitly states that these eyedrops cause no damage to healthy eyes, and vision returns to normal after discontinuing the medication. Do not treat a single computerized refraction at an optical shop as a diagnosis, nor refrain from getting glasses for a child out of "fear that their prescription will increase."
entries.benefit: The *Ten Core Knowledge Points for Children and Adolescent Myopia Prevention and Control* explains what cycloplegic refraction entails. A cycloplegic agent is applied first, followed by refraction. A cycloplegic agent is an eyedrop that relaxes the muscle in the eye responsible for focusing. Cycloplegic refraction is a medical refraction performed in a hospital and serves as the "gold standard" (the most accurate method) for diagnosing myopia. Cycloplegic drugs do not cause damage to healthy eyes; after administration, photophobia and blurred near vision may appear in the short term, returning to normal once the drug is stopped. Once myopia is diagnosed, timely and scientific interventions should be undertaken, correcting it through wearing glasses or other methods. Wearing appropriate glasses can effectively correct blurred vision and slow myopia progression. For those whose vision is normal with glasses, preschool and primary school children should be rechecked once every 3 to 6 months, and junior and senior high school students once every 6 to 12 months, deciding whether to replace glasses based on specific circumstances. Children aged 1 to 3, 4 to 6, and after age 7 should regularly undergo refractive screening (checking refractive status) to monitor hyperopia reserve (National, issued July 2023)
entries.sources: General Office of the National Health Commission (2023). Ten Core Knowledge Points for Children and Adolescent Myopia Prevention and Control (Guo Wei Ban Fu You Han [2023] No. 278). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6894284.htm>
entries.notes: A grade of B is given because this represents the practices provided in an official science communication document rather than original research with specific numerical figures. High myopia can lead to conditions such as retinal detachment, so follow-ups are not just for replacing glasses. "Poor vision" identified during student physical exams is merely a preliminary screening result; it still requires taking the child to a hospital for a comprehensive ophthalmic examination, see Item 7.

entries.title: Apply pit and fissure sealants after permanent molars erupt
entries.cost: Several tens to one or two hundred yuan per tooth. No anesthesia, no drilling/enamel grinding needed, taking a few minutes each time. Many localities offer free programs for age-eligible children.
entries.summary: Pit and fissure sealing seals the grooves on the chewing surface of molars with resin so that food debris cannot become trapped. Two years after completion, the chance of developing dental caries is approximately one-eighth of that without sealing. If 16% of tooth surfaces would decay without sealing, only about 5% do with sealing. It remains effective after four years.
entries.benefit: In a Cochrane review systematically gathering and pooling 38 trials involving 7,924 children aged 5 to 16, resin-based sealants were compared with no sealant. For the first permanent molars of children aged 5 to 10, caries development at 24 months post-treatment had an OR of 0.12 (95% CI 0.08–0.19), making the chance of developing cavities approximately one-eighth of that without sealant. This finding came from 7 trials, with 1,548 randomly assigned and 1,322 ultimately evaluated, with moderate quality of evidence. If 16% of tooth surfaces in the control group developed caries within 24 months, it was 5.2% (3.13%–7.37%) after sealing. When the control group was at 40%, it was 6.25% (3.84%–9.63%). When the control group was at 70%, it was 19% (12.3%–27.2%). At 48 to 54 months post-treatment, the OR was 0.21 (0.16–0.28), still approximately one-fifth of no sealant. The authors concluded that resin sealants resulted in 11% to 51% less caries at 24 months compared to no sealant. In 4 trials that reported adverse events, no adverse events occurred. Evidence was insufficient regarding which material is superior among other sealant classes like glass ionomer
entries.sources: Ahovuo-Saloranta A, et al. (2017). Pit and fissure sealants for preventing dental decay in permanent teeth. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD001830.pub5>
entries.notes: The first permanent molar (the big tooth that will not be replaced again) generally emerges around age 6, and the second around age 12. Sealing should be done right after the tooth erupts and before it decays; once it is already decayed, filling is the only option. Many regions include pit and fissure sealing for age-eligible children as a free program; ask the local CDC or community health service center. This section found no national documents that could be verified verbatim, so coverage scope and age brackets are omitted. Dental caries is also a key item targeted for guidance in student physical examinations, see Item 7.

entries.title: If a child loves playing video games, first check whether sleep, homework, and outdoor activities have been crowded out, rather than focusing solely on how long they played
entries.cost: Costs no money. Take note once a week of what time the child goes to sleep, whether homework has been handed in, and whether they have gone outdoors for activities.
entries.summary: Those who genuinely qualify for "gaming disorder" account for roughly two to three per hundred people. Setting questionnaire thresholds low and exclusively screening adolescents will inflate the proportion. Looking at real logs from gaming companies, there is virtually no discernible effect of playing more or less on well-being. Minors are restricted by regulation to playing only between 8:00 PM and 9:00 PM on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays, and statutory holidays.
entries.benefit: A meta-analysis aggregated 53 studies across 17 countries, comprising 226,247 individuals. The prevalence of gaming disorder was 3.05% (95% CI 2.38–3.91, this is the credible interval). Counting only studies with stricter sampling, it was 1.96%. Results varied widely across studies, with 77% of the variance stemming from which questionnaire was used. Having adolescent samples, low cutoff scores, and small sample sizes all inflated the proportion. Another study obtained data from 7 gaming companies, linking the actual gameplay duration of 38,935 players over six weeks with their self-reported well-being. Evidence that time spent playing impacts well-being was almost nonexistent. The National Press and Publication Administration stipulates that gaming enterprises may only provide 1 hour of services to minors from 20:00 to 21:00 daily on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays, and statutory holidays (National / International, from 2021 onwards)
entries.sources: Stevens MW, Dorstyn D, Delfabbro PH, King DL. (2021). Global prevalence of gaming disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Australian and New Zealand Journal of Psychiatry, 55(6), 553–568. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0004867420962851>; Vuorre M, Johannes N, Magnusson K, Przybylski AK. (2022). Time spent playing video games is unlikely to impact well-being. Royal Society Open Science, 9(7), 220411. <https://doi.org/10.1098/rsos.220411>; National Press and Publication Administration (2021). Notice on Further Strict Management to Effectively Prevent Minors from Becoming Addicted to Online Games (Guo Xin Chu Fa [2021] No. 14). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-09/01/content_5634661.htm>
entries.notes: A grade of B is given because prevalence varies too much depending on the questionnaire, and the well-being study only followed subjects for six weeks. In the author's judgment, the most common cost of gaming is crowding out sleep and outdoor time; no research figures were found for this point. For explicit sleep requirements, see Item 10 of this section (sleep, homework, physical education). For outdoor activity, see Item 4 of this section (2 hours outdoors daily); for screen time, see Item 5 of this section (no more than 1 hour daily for non-learning purposes). For top-ups and refunds, see Section 5, Item 9 (children using mobile phones for top-ups and tipping). If academic performance, sleep, and family relationships all break down together and persuasion fails to stop it, take the child to psychiatry or child psychology at that point. Do not send them to closed-management internet addiction boot camps; see Item 18 of this section (internet addiction schools). The beneficiary is the child.

entries.title: If a child says they like the same sex, don't scold them, don't kick them out of the house, and don't send them for "conversion": family attitude is linked to whether they attempt suicide
entries.cost: Costs no money. The difficulty lies in parents needing to first process their own emotions and not say harsh words in the moment.
entries.summary: Among domestic secondary school students, children who are attracted to the same sex or both sexes attempted suicide roughly 3 to 5.5 times as often as others within a year. Foreign studies found that children who were strongly rejected by their families during adolescence were far more likely to have attempted suicide later. Those sent by their parents for "conversion" were also far more likely to have attempted suicide.
entries.benefit: A domestic survey covered 506 secondary schools across 7 provinces, totaling 150,822 students from Grade 7 through Grade 12. Among those who attempted suicide in the past year, for boys, those attracted only to the opposite sex were 2.2%, only to the same sex were 6.9%, and to both sexes were 12.2%. Corresponding rates for girls were 3.1%, 8.9%, and 10.9%. Calculated, this is about 3 to 5.5 times that of peers attracted only to the opposite sex. The researchers controlled for factors including age, academic pressure, family finances, and bullying. After adjusting, the ORs for the two groups of boys were 3.13 (95% CI 2.28–4.28) and 3.83 (2.85–5.14), about two to three times higher. A meta-analysis pooling 35 studies calculated an OR of 3.50 (2.98–4.12) for suicide attempts among sexual minority adolescents. A US study interviewed 224 gay and bisexual young adults aged 21 to 25, asking them to recall family reactions during adolescence. Compared with peers whose families showed virtually no rejection, those with high levels of family rejection had an OR of 8.4 for suicide attempts. In another study, when parents themselves attempted to change their child's sexual orientation, the OR for the child attempting suicide was 3.08 (1.39–6.83). When parents additionally sent their child to therapists or religious leaders, it was 5.07 (2.38–10.79) (China / Multiple countries / United States)
entries.sources: Huang Y, Li P, Guo L, et al. (2018). Sexual minority status and suicidal behaviour among Chinese adolescents: a nationally representative cross-sectional study. BMJ Open, 8(8), e020969. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2017-020969>; di Giacomo E, Krausz M, Colmegna F, Aspesi F, Clerici M. (2018). Estimating the Risk of Attempted Suicide Among Sexual Minority Youths: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. JAMA Pediatrics, 172(12), 1145–1152. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jamapediatrics.2018.2731>; Ryan C, Huebner D, Diaz RM, Sanchez J. (2009). Family rejection as a predictor of negative health outcomes in white and Latino lesbian, gay, and bisexual young adults. Pediatrics, 123(1), 346–352. <https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2007-3524>; Ryan C, Toomey RB, Diaz RM, Russell ST. (2020). Parent-Initiated Sexual Orientation Change Efforts With LGBT Adolescents: Implications for Young Adult Mental Health and Adjustment. Journal of Homosexuality, 67(2), 159–173. <https://doi.org/10.1080/00918369.2018.1538407>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2024 Amendment). Law on the Protection of Minors (Article 17). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081818f197cf001905e567af635a0>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2015). Anti-Domestic Violence Law (Article 2). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7f9d60889>
entries.notes: A grade of B is assigned because these are all one-off surveys, and the degree of family rejection relies on adult recall; they can only demonstrate an association, not prove causality. Parents do not need to accept it immediately, but first and foremost, do not do things that harm the child. Legally, parents must not mistreat or abandon their children, nor may they commit domestic violence against them. Habitual verbal abuse and intimidation also qualify as domestic violence. If the child's mood is low or they say they do not want to live anymore, call 12356 first; see Section 1, Item 25 (Call 12356 When Having Suicidal Thoughts). You can also go to a psychiatry department in accordance with Item 8 of this section (Get a Depression Screening Done Once Between Ages 12 and 18). For why you should never touch "conversion," see Section 6, Item 28 (Do Not Undergo Sexual Orientation Conversion). The beneficiary is the child, and also yourself.

entries.title: When Disciplining Children, Do Not Hit Them, Yell at Them, or Call Them Stupid: Children Who Are Frequently Beaten and Scolded Have More Behavioral and Emotional Problems
entries.cost: Free of charge. The difficulty lies in stopping your hands and mouth the moment your temper flares, and switching to a disciplinary approach that does not involve hitting or scolding. For what approach to switch to, see Item 17 of this section (Parenting Classes That Teach Specific Techniques).
entries.summary: Children who are frequently hit exhibit more aggression and mental health issues, become more alienated from their parents, and suffer heavier beatings more often. The evidence is inconclusive on whether hitting can make a child comply on the spot. Children who are frequently yelled at and called stupid at age 13 experience more trouble-making and depression later on, which cannot be offset no matter how affectionate parents are in everyday life.
entries.benefit: Look at hitting first. A meta-analysis only counted the specific act of "open-handed spanking on the buttocks or extremities." It synthesized 75 studies with 111 effect sizes, covering a total of 160,927 children. Out of 17 outcomes, 13 were significantly associated with being hit, and all were in an adverse direction. d represents effect size, where 0.2 is considered small and 0.5 is moderate. Childhood aggression was d = 0.37 (95% CI 0.13–0.61, confidence interval). Externalizing problems were 0.41, referring to behaviors like hitting others and breaking rules. Internalizing problems were 0.24, referring to issues like anxiety and depression. Mental health problems were 0.53, poor parent-child relationship was 0.51, low self-esteem was 0.15, and poor cognitive ability was 0.17. Being subjected to physical abuse by parents was 0.64. Adult antisocial behavior was 0.36, and adult mental health problems were 0.24. Combined across the 111 effect sizes, d = 0.33 (0.29–0.38). Whether the child complies on the spot had no significant association with being hit or not (d = 0.14, −0.19–0.47), an outcome with only 5 effect sizes. Another review looked solely at longitudinal prospective studies, totaling 69 studies. Physical punishment consistently predicted more subsequent behavioral problems in children, with no observed association with any long-term positive outcomes. Among them, 7 studies examined the frequency of hitting, and 5 found that the more frequent the hitting, the more severe the problems. Now look at yelling and scolding. A study in the United States followed 976 two-parent families. When children were 13 years old, if parents frequently shouted, cursed, or called them stupid or lazy, the children's trouble-making behaviors and depressive symptoms both increased between ages 13 and 14. Whether parents were usually affectionate or not could not offset this association. The reverse was also true: children who caused more trouble at age 13 were scolded more subsequently. Legally, parents must not commit domestic violence against their children. Article 2 of the Anti-Domestic Violence Law lists forms of domestic violence: beating, binding, mutilating, restricting personal freedom, as well as habitual verbal abuse and intimidation. Article 12 of the law requires guardians to conduct family education in a civilized manner. Where parents infringe upon a child's rights and interests, neighborhood committees and village committees must admonish and stop them, and report serious cases to the public security organs. If discovered by public security organs, people's procuratorates, or courts, parents must be reprimanded, and may be ordered to undergo family education guidance (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Gershoff ET, Grogan-Kaylor A. (2016). Spanking and child outcomes: Old controversies and new meta-analyses. Journal of Family Psychology, 30(4), 453–469. <https://doi.org/10.1037/fam0000191>; Heilmann A, Mehay A, Watt RG, et al. (2021). Physical punishment and child outcomes: a narrative review of prospective studies. Lancet, 398(10297), 355–364. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(21)00582-1>; Wang MT, Kenny S. (2014). Longitudinal links between fathers' and mothers' harsh verbal discipline and adolescents' conduct problems and depressive symptoms. Child Development, 85(3), 908–923. <https://doi.org/10.1111/cdev.12143>; Ferguson CJ. (2013). Spanking, corporal punishment and negative long-term outcomes: a meta-analytic review of longitudinal studies. Clinical Psychology Review, 33(1), 196–208. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cpr.2012.11.002>; Larzelere RE, Kuhn BR. (2005). Comparing child outcomes of physical punishment and alternative disciplinary tactics: a meta-analysis. Clinical Child and Family Psychology Review, 8(1), 1–37. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10567-005-2340-z>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2015). Anti-Domestic Violence Law (Articles 2 and 12). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7f9d60889>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2024 Amendment). Law on the Protection of Minors (Articles 11, 17, and 118). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081818f197cf001905e567af635a0>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2021). Family Education Promotion Law (Articles 23 and 53). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817cac3b2d017cac5a6c6f0109>
entries.notes: Controversies. Almost all of these studies are merely tracking observations without randomized controlled designs, so they cannot prove causality. In the spanking meta-analysis, 72% of the studies only looked at whether two events co-occurred, or relied on retrospective recall. Another meta-analysis included only prospective longitudinal studies. After controlling for children's baseline behaviors, the association between spanking and externalizing problems shrank to only 0.07, and for internalizing problems to only 0.10. The authors of that paper considered the effect to be very small. Another meta-analysis found that "conditional spanking" was more effective in reducing noncompliance and antisocial behavior than 10 out of 13 alternative disciplinary tactics. It also found that when hitting was overly severe or used as the primary method, it was worse than alternative disciplinary tactics. Therefore, what the counterarguments can demonstrate is: a small amount of conditional hitting is not necessarily worse than other disciplinary tactics. When hitting is severe or hitting and scolding are frequent, both sides agree it is worse. The statutory provisions do not explicitly state that hitting someone once or shouting a single phrase occasionally constitutes domestic violence; what they single out are beatings, habitual verbal abuse, and intimidation. The primary beneficiary is the child. If someone else in the family hits the child, see Section 8, Item 43 (Personal Safety Protection Orders) for reporting to the police and applying for a protection order. When seeing other families chronically hitting their children, anyone has the right to dissuade them, or report it to public security, civil affairs, and education departments. For matters occurring in a stranger's home, calling 110 or notifying the neighborhood committee is sufficient; do not show up at their door to break up the fight yourself.

entries.title: If Your Child Is Difficult to Manage and You Cannot Help Hitting and Scolding Them, Attend a Term of Parenting Classes That Teach Specific Techniques
entries.cost: Parenting schools operated by schools and kindergartens, as well as online parenting schools run by provincial-level or higher governments, are stipulated by law to be of a public welfare nature. The evidence-based type of classes meets once a week or every other week, each session lasting one to two hours, ranging from four to twenty-four weeks. You need to practice at home accordingly. The difficulty lies in persisting through to completion and practicing every day.
entries.summary: For children who were inherently difficult to manage, after parents attended classes teaching specific disciplinary techniques, children's hitting and rule-breaking behaviors decreased, and parents' moods improved. Parents' hitting and scolding of children also declined, which was most evident immediately upon class completion; the effect was still present one to two years later, though substantially smaller. Shanghai has also trialed such classes, and they were effective.
entries.benefit: A Cochrane review pooled 13 trials, of which 10 were randomized, covering 1,078 parents. The children were 3 to 12 years old and all had behavioral problems. The included courses met weekly or biweekly, lasting one to two hours per session, for at least three sessions. Shorter programs ran consecutively for 4 weeks, while longer ones ran consecutively for 24 weeks. For parents who took the classes, their children's behavioral problems decreased. Parent-reported ratings showed an SMD of −0.53 (95% CI −0.72 to −0.34, confidence interval), and independent assessments by others showed −0.44 (−0.77 to −0.11).
