SMD and d use the same benchmark scale, where 0.5 is considered moderate. Parents' mental health improved, at −0.36 (−0.52 to −0.20). Negative or harsh disciplinary tactics decreased, with parent-reported ratings of −0.77 (−0.96 to −0.59) and other-reported ratings of −0.42 (−0.67 to −0.16). The authors noted that these were short-term effects. Another meta-analysis screened 346 randomized trials, 60 of which measured behaviors such as hitting and scolding children, spanning 22 countries. Hitting and scolding decreased immediately upon class completion, d = −0.46 (−0.59 to −0.33). At 1 to 6 months post-intervention, it was −0.24 (−0.37 to −0.11). At 7 to 24 months, it was −0.18 (−0.34 to −0.02), diminishing further over time. Most of these figures were self-reported by parents. Trials have also been conducted domestically. In Shanghai, 81 parents were randomly allocated, with a portion attending Triple P group courses. After completing the course, the children's adjustment problems, as well as the parents' disciplinary methods and emotional states, were better than those of parents on the waitlist, with effects still persisting 6 months later. In a rural kindergarten, 191 caregiving adults participated, with a portion undertaking self-directed online courses plus two group discussions. Two weeks after completion, their reported child-maltreating behaviors were approximately 33% lower than those who were only given reading materials (IRR 0.67). Three months later, children's behavioral problems had also decreased (d = −0.40). The Family Education Promotion Law requires parents to conscientiously study family education knowledge. Primary and secondary schools and kindergartens may establish parenting schools to regularly organize public-welfare family education guidance. Neighborhood committees and village committees may establish community parenting schools. Governments at or above the provincial level must establish public-welfare online parenting schools and service hotlines. Family education guidance institutions must not organize for-profit training (Nationwide, implemented as of January 1, 2022)
entries.sources: Furlong M, McGilloway S, Bywater T, Hutchings J, Smith SM, Donnelly M. (2012). Behavioural and cognitive-behavioural group-based parenting programmes for early-onset conduct problems in children aged 3 to 12 years. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (2), CD008225. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD008225.pub2>; Backhaus S, Leijten P, Jochim J, Melendez-Torres GJ, Gardner F. (2023). Effects over time of parenting interventions to reduce physical and emotional violence against children: a systematic review and meta-analysis. eClinicalMedicine, 60, 102003. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eclinm.2023.102003>; Guo M, Morawska A, Sanders MR. (2016). A Randomized Controlled Trial of Group Triple P With Chinese Parents in Mainland China. Behavior Modification, 40(6), 825–851. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0145445516644221>; Wang W, Zhang H. (2026). A self-directed parenting program to reduce the risk of child maltreatment in rural China: A cluster randomized controlled trial. Child Abuse & Neglect, 173, 107937. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chiabu.2026.107937>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2021). Family Education Promotion Law (Articles 18, 25, 31, 38, and 40). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817cac3b2d017cac5a6c6f0109>
entries.notes: An A grade is awarded because the figures are pooled from Cochrane reviews and multiple randomized controlled trials. The courses evaluated in the trials share several common features: instructors teach concrete techniques—such as playing with the child, praising, rewarding, and disciplining; parents practice and role-play during class, and are assigned homework to complete at home. Courses that merely distribute informational materials or hold open discussions were excluded, so this evidence does not apply to attending a one-off lecture. The content and teaching approaches of non-profit community parenting schools across China vary by region, and they may not necessarily belong to this category. When choosing a course, check whether it runs for multiple consecutive weeks and requires you to practice specific techniques. Among the trials included in the two meta-analyses, common course names included Triple P and Incredible Years. This book does not endorse specific commercial institutions or paid products. The effect of reducing scolding and physical punishment diminishes after one to two years, meaning practice must continue even after the course ends. The beneficiaries are both the child and yourself. If the child already has severe emotional problems, take them to a psychiatric or child psychology clinic; see Item 8 of this section (Depression screening).

entries.title: Do not send children to closed-management "internet addiction treatment schools" or "special training camps": the law prohibits using methods that harm physical and mental health to treat internet addiction, and children have already died in custody
entries.cost: Costs nothing, and even saves on tuition fees. The difficulty lies in parents resisting the urge to hand the child over to outsiders for "closed-off discipline" when the child acts out most severely.
entries.summary: The law explicitly prohibits using methods that harm a minor's physical or mental health to treat internet addiction. A special training school in Hefei handcuffed a newly admitted boy in a solitary confinement room, and he died approximately 44 hours later. Yuzhang Academy in Nanchang placed students in solitary confinement, resulting in criminal convictions for four individuals; the court dismissed the parents' claims demanding tuition refunds.
entries.benefit: Article 68 of the Law on the Protection of Minors stipulates that no organization or individual may intervene in a minor's internet addiction in ways that infringe upon their physical and mental health. Court judgments exist for both of the following cases. The first occurred in Hefei, Anhui. In August 2017, the parents of an 18-year-old boy signed an agreement with a special training school to send him for internet addiction treatment. School personnel forcibly took him away, locked him in a solitary confinement room, and handcuffed both of his hands to window bars. They restricted his access to food, water, and rest, and beat him. Approximately 44 hours later, the boy died. The forensic evaluation concluded that high temperature, restrained posture, lack of food and water, and physical trauma caused water-electrolyte imbalance resulting in death. On October 31, 2018, the Hefei Intermediate People's Court rendered its first-instance judgment. The person in charge of the school was convicted of intentional injury and unlawful detention, receiving a 16-year sentence. Four instructors received sentences ranging from 1 year to 8 years and 6 months. On December 28, 2018, the Anhui Provincial Higher People's Court upheld the original judgment in the second instance. The second-instance ruling stated that the school had not obtained approval from relevant government departments, and none of the defendants held teaching qualifications. The second case occurred in Nanchang, Jiangxi. Yuzhang Academy was founded in 2013 and deregistered and closed in November 2017. During its operation, the school placed some students in a "trouble relief room" for solitary confinement under dedicated guard, locking them up for three to ten days at a time. On April 28, 2023, the Anyuan District People's Court of Pingxiang City announced the first-instance retrial verdict, finding five defendants guilty of unlawful detention. Four were sentenced to imprisonment, reported by Xinhua News Agency in verbatim terms as "fixed-term imprisonment ranging from two years and ten months to eleven months." These four individuals were also prohibited from engaging in education-related professions for a specified period, while one was exempted from criminal punishment. The parents demanded compensation for tuition fees and round-trip travel expenses, but the court did not support their claims (National / Anhui / Jiangxi)

entries.notes: A C grade is assigned because there are only individual cases and no casualty statistics for these types of schools. The Hefei case relies solely on media reports quoting the first-instance judgment and second-instance ruling, as the original text of the court judgment could not be found on official court websites. The Yuzhang Academy case is based on Xinhua News Agency's report of the court's sentencing. If a child enjoys playing video games, first assess according to Item 14 of this section (Children loving video games) whether sleep, homework, and outdoor activities are being crowded out. If academic performance, sleep, and family relationships all break down together and counseling cannot stop the behavior, take the child to a psychiatric or child psychology clinic for professional medical diagnosis and treatment. If the child has already been sent to such a facility, bring them back. If the child reports being confined or beaten, call the police. The beneficiary is the child.

entries.title: Teach children to recognize private body parts and to tell parents if touched or asked to keep a secret; believe the child first without scolding if they tell, and take them to report to the police and seek medical care
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Bring it up casually during daily bathing or changing clothes, and check in again periodically. The difficulty lies in parents feeling embarrassed to name body parts, as well as holding back anger and not scolding the child if they actually disclose something.
entries.summary: Children who took child sexual abuse prevention courses showed significantly more self-protective actions during stranger-lure role-playing drills. The acquired knowledge was retained after six months, without making the children more fearful. Whether it genuinely reduces actual victimizations has not yet been measured. Because acquaintances account for a high proportion of child sexual abuse perpetrators, children must be taught which parts cannot be touched by others, and to report home if touched or asked to keep a secret.
entries.benefit: A 2015 Cochrane review synthesized 24 trials of school-based child sexual abuse prevention programs, covering a total of 5,802 students aged 5 to 18 years. Most of these programs taught several core concepts: safety rules, bodily autonomy, and which body parts are private. They also taught children to distinguish which types of touch are inappropriate, which secrets must not be kept, and whom to tell. Many courses also emphasized that if something happens, it is never the child's fault. Looking first at whether children can protect themselves: researchers had actors pose as strangers to lure children across 2 trials with 102 participants. Children who took the courses had an OR of 5.71 (95% CI 1.98–16.51) for executing protective actions, representing roughly 5.7 times the odds of untrained peers. Converted according to the original text, about 390 per 1,000 untrained children executed protective actions, compared to about 795 per 1,000 trained children. Next, looking at knowledge: across 18 trials with 4,657 participants, questionnaire scores showed an SMD of 0.61 (0.45–0.78), where 0.5 is considered moderate. After six months, it remained at 0.69 (0.51–0.87). Three studies with 795 participants examined potential harms; children's anxiety and fear neither increased nor decreased (SMD −0.08, −0.22 to 0.07). Three studies with 1,788 participants examined whether children would disclose abuse. Disclosing prior sexual abuse had an OR of 3.56 (1.13–11.24), increasing from about 4 per 1,000 to about 14 per 1,000. However, children within the same class and school share similarities; after adjusting for this clustering, the difference was no longer statistically discernible (OR 3.04, 0.75–12.33). The quality of evidence for all outcomes was moderate. The authors noted that long-term follow-up is necessary to determine whether these programs truly reduce sexual abuse. In 2018, six United Nations agencies, including UNESCO, published sexuality education guidance. It recommends teaching children the names of all body parts, including genital organs, starting at ages 5 to 8. It also recommends teaching children to understand which parts of the body are private. When someone touches them or makes them uncomfortable, they should say "no," move away, and tell a trusted adult. The guidance states clearly that sexual abuse is never the victimized child's fault, even when committed by acquaintances, trusted individuals, or family members. A child sexual abuse prevention manual from People's Daily provided a memorable rule of thumb: parts covered by a vest and shorts may not be viewed or touched by others. Article 16 of the Law on the Protection of Minors requires parents to conduct safety education for children to enhance their awareness and ability for self-protection. Article 40 requires schools and kindergartens to conduct age-appropriate sex education. When schools and kindergartens discover sexual assault or sexual harassment, they must not conceal it and must promptly report to public security and education authorities. In 2020, nine departments including the Supreme People's Procuratorate established a mandatory reporting system. Mandated reporters include personnel from schools, kindergartens, hospitals, childcare institutions, neighborhood committees, village committees, and hotels. When discovering that a minor has suffered or is suspected of having suffered harm in the course of their work, they must immediately report to public security organs. Situations requiring reporting include: suspected abnormal injuries to genital organs or private body parts, or a female under the age of 14 suspected of being sexually abused, pregnant, or having undergone an abortion. Reporter information must be kept confidential. Reporters bear no legal liability for disputes arising from making reports. In 2025, procuratorial organs prosecuted 42,873 individuals for sexual assault against minors, including rape and molestation of children, a 5.5% decrease from the previous year. This accounted for 58.9% of all prosecutions for crimes infringing upon minors. Among cases involving crimes against minors prosecuted that year, leads in 3,852 cases originated from mandatory reporting, accounting for 7.1%. A 2025 opinion issued by 16 departments, including the Supreme People's Court, noted that acquaintances account for a relatively high proportion of perpetrators in such cases. Some young children lack awareness of prevention, and guardians are negligent in paying attention, leaving children unaware that they have been sexually assaulted (National / Multi-country)

entries.notes: A B grade is given because the figures all derive from school-based curricula measuring knowledge and simulation actions rather than actual reductions in abuse incidence. No standalone trials exist for parents teaching at home. The benefit is rated small because only these surrogate endpoints exist without figures demonstrating the exact percentage reduction in actual assault. The teaching method should follow the points outlined above: use the proper anatomical names of body parts, and explain which areas are private. Then instruct the child that anyone telling them to keep a secret or forbidding them from telling their parents must be reported at home, and that telling will not lead to getting scolded. If the child discloses, believe them first; do not interrogate whether it is made up, and do not scold them. The law requires teachers and doctors to report upon mere "suspicion," so parents need not wait for certainty. Reassure the child that it is not their fault, then dial 110. Do not bathe the child or wash their clothes before a forensic medical examination; see Item 42 of Section 13 (After sexual assault). Follow this regardless of who the perpetrator is; report relatives and teachers to the police as well. For the legal consequences if the other party is under 14 years old, see Item 18 of Section 9 (The other party is under 14 years old). If a friend's child tells you, inform their parents and call the police together. For incidents involving unfamiliar children, dial 110 and leave it to the police; do not confront the other party yourself. The law explicitly provides that anyone has the right to report violations to public security organs. The beneficiary is the child.

entries.title: Do not let children under 12 years of age ride bicycles on roads, or children under 16 ride electric bicycles on roads: parents pay compensation if someone is hit, and may bear partial liability even if the child is hit
entries.cost: Costs nothing, but requires switching school commute methods: parental pickup and drop-off, taking public transit, or walking. The difficulty lies in children throwing tantrums when their classmates are all riding.
entries.summary: One must be at least 12 years of age to ride a bicycle on roads, and at least 16 to ride an electric bicycle. A 14-year-old child scanned their mother's code to ride a shared electric bike and struck someone, causing Grade 10 disability; the court ordered the parents to pay approximately 187,000 yuan in compensation. When underage children are struck themselves, even if the other party is found fully liable, some courts still rule that the child's side bears part of the loss.
entries.benefit: Article 72 of the Regulations on the Implementation of the Road Traffic Safety Law stipulates that on roads, "one must be at least 12 years of age to drive bicycles and tricycles." The same article also stipulates that "one must be at least 16 years of age to drive electric bicycles and motorized wheelchairs for the disabled." Violations are punishable by a warning or a fine of 5 to 50 yuan under Article 89 of the Road Traffic Safety Law, and the vehicle may be impounded if the fine is refused. The fine is modest; what matters is the financial liability after an accident. Article 1188 of the Civil Code stipulates that when a minor causes harm to another person, the guardian shall bear tort liability. If the minor has property of their own, compensation is paid first from their property; any shortfall is covered by the guardian. The Lianjiang County Court in Fujian heard such a case. In May 2022, a child who had just turned 14 used their mother's account to scan a QR code and rent a shared electric bicycle. He collided with an electric bicycle rider, causing Grade 10 disability to the victim; traffic police determined the child bore full liability. The rental company and insurance company argued that the user agreement required riders to be 16 years or older, meaning the child was not an authorized rider, and thus denied coverage. The court ordered the child's parents to pay approximately 187,000 yuan in compensation (exact amount: 187,017.83 yuan). Children also lose out when struck themselves. A Beijing judge wrote about a case: a 10-year-old child riding a bicycle after school was hit by an electric bicycle, sustaining Grade 10 disability; traffic police determined the other party bore full liability. Article 1173 of the Civil Code provides that if the victim is at fault regarding the occurrence of the harm, the tortfeasor's liability may be mitigated. Based on this, the court determined that the child rode on the road under 12 years of age and the guardian failed to stop it, ruling that the child's side bear a portion of the loss. Injuries are also more severe. A trauma center in Israel admitted 337 children with traffic injuries between 2014 and 2016. Among those injured while riding electric bicycles, traumatic brain injury accounted for 13%, compared to 3% among those riding conventional bicycles. After adjusting for other factors, the odds of sustaining more severe injuries were approximately 2.6 times higher than for conventional bicycle riders (OR 2.56, 95% CI 1.1–5.88) (National / Fujian / Beijing / Israel)

entries.notes: A B grade is assigned because both statutory provisions and two court precedents were verified, but the injury severity statistics come from only a single overseas hospital, with no age-stratified casualty statistics found domestically in China. The Lianjiang case was sourced from a legal education column reprint by the Bureau of Justice; the original court judgment text was not retrieved. The benefit is rated large based on applying monetary criteria to the 187,000 yuan compensation in that case, but not every accident incurs compensation that high. Shared electric bicycle user agreements also require riders to be 16 or older; do not let children scan codes using your account. Once reaching the eligible age, a helmet must still be worn; see Item 2 of Section 1 (Wear a helmet and fasten it) and Item 12 of Section 22 (Wear a helmet when mountain biking). The beneficiary is primarily the child, while the ones paying the compensation are the parents themselves.

entries.title: If a child hits their head during sports and later experiences headache, dizziness, or confusion, keep them off the field for the rest of the day; seek immediate emergency care if they vomit repeatedly, become increasingly drowsy, or have worsening headache
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Have the child leave the field, with no further practice or competition that day. The difficulty lies in situations where the game is intense, the child insists they are "fine," and both coaches and parents want them to stay in the game.
entries.summary: Children who continued playing after a concussion took an average of 44 days to recover, compared to about 22 days for those removed immediately. If anything feels off after a head impact, do not return to play that day, and only resume once cleared by a physician. Repeated vomiting, progressive drowsiness or difficulty waking up, worsening headaches, slurred speech, and seizures are all red flags requiring immediate emergency care.
entries.benefit: A concussion is a temporary disturbance of brain function following a blow to the head, and it usually cannot be seen on imaging scans. An American study tracked 69 athletes who sustained sports-related concussions, with an average age of about 15. The 35 athletes who were removed from play immediately took an average of 22.0 days to recover. The 34 athletes who continued playing while symptomatic took an average of 44.4 days (P=0.003, unlikely to be due to chance). For those who continued playing, the odds of recovery dragging on beyond 21 days were 8.80 times higher than for those who were removed immediately. The 2022 Amsterdam International Consensus Statement on Concussion in Sport stated that anyone displaying loss of consciousness, convulsions, unsteadiness, confusion, behavioral changes, or amnesia must be removed from play immediately. These individuals should not return to competition or practice on the same day. The sole exception is if an experienced healthcare professional conducts an immediate evaluation on-site and confirms that it was not caused by a concussion. The U.S. CDC guidelines for parents and coaches put it even more directly: remove from play immediately upon any suspected symptoms, keep them out for the rest of the day, and wait until a healthcare provider clears them to return. It also states not to judge severity on your own; only healthcare providers can perform the evaluation. It lists red-flag signs that warrant immediate emergency department care: seizures or convulsions, inability to recognize people or places, repeated nausea or vomiting, unusual behavior, increasing confusion or irritability, as well as progressive drowsiness or inability to awaken after passing out, slurred speech, weakness or numbness in arms or legs, headache that worsens and does not ease, and unequal pupil sizes or double vision (United States / Multi-country)
entries.sources: Elbin RJ, Sufrinko A, Schatz P, et al. (2016). Removal From Play After Concussion and Recovery Time. Pediatrics, 138(3), e20160910. <https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2016-0910>；Patricios JS, Schneider KJ, Dvorak J, et al. (2023). Consensus statement on concussion in sport: the 6th International Conference on Concussion in Sport-Amsterdam, October 2022. British Journal of Sports Medicine, 57(11), 695-711. <https://doi.org/10.1136/bjsports-2023-106898>；CDC (2025). Signs and Symptoms of Concussion. HEADS UP. <https://www.cdc.gov/heads-up/signs-symptoms/index.html>；CDC. How to Respond. HEADS UP. <https://www.cdc.gov/heads-up/response/index.html>
entries.notes: A grade of B is assigned because the two groups—those who continued playing and those who were removed immediately—were not randomized, and the sample size was small. The benefit is rated as large because it is modeled on cutting the recovery duration approximately in half. The consensus also states that screen time should be minimized during the first two days, light activities like walking are permitted, and activity can be gradually increased after 24 to 48 hours according to tolerance. However, sports carrying risks of collision or falling must wait until a healthcare provider grants clearance. For wearing helmets while cycling or skiing, see Section 22, Item 12 (Wearing a helmet when riding a mountain bike). For situations where elderly individuals develop problems weeks after bumping their heads, see Section 13, Item 10 (Elderly person bumped their head). The beneficiary is children.

chapters.title: Which Paths Lie Ahead After Age Eighteen
chapters.intro:
This section tallies money and time, and the entry on refusal of military service also bears on personal freedom. This is a path map, not an instruction manual for any single path. This section first lays out the statutory thresholds of each path side by side, and then breaks down line by line the practical details that are only useful once known: what can be obtained from military service, what entryways into the public sector exist besides civil service examinations, which two majors directly lead to established public-sector staffing (bianzhi) when filling out college entrance examination preferences, whether educational credentials can still be made up later, what kinds of companies to look for if one wishes to work abroad as a laborer, what to do about social insurance if one does not enter an employer institution, and whether money is available to borrow where the state subsidizes part of the interest if you lack startup capital.

The paths one can take after turning eighteen go far beyond those covered in this section. Included here are only those paths that possess public documents at the national level and whose thresholds and benefits can be cross-checked line by line. Entering state-owned enterprises, entering factories, working as seafarers, doing freelance work, or continuing on to high school and university are also paths one can take. However, because they lack unified public documents for verification, this book does not set forth their conditions based on mere impression.

Which path you choose is your own business. This section provides only two things: which documents contain the thresholds, and which deadlines and qualifications will expire and become void once you embark upon them. For how to calculate the equation between schooling versus working and how to select skills, see Section 23. For overtime pay, work-related injuries, and severance pay after joining an employer, see Section 19. For capital and exit costs when opening a shop or running a company, see Section 12. For studying abroad, see Section 32. For security and protections after becoming unemployed, see Section 7. None of these will be repeated here.

entries.title: Check the thresholds first: Age and education requirements for most of the twelve paths are strictly codified in writing
entries.cost: No monetary cost. Spend ten minutes checking through them to see whether you meet the requirements.
entries.summary: The thresholds for most of these twelve paths are clearly written in official documents. General employment requires reaching 16 years of age; military conscription applies to males who have reached 18 years of age, which can be extended to 24 years of age for college graduates. Civil service examinations generally require ages 18 to 35 and an associate degree (dazhuan) or higher. Higher Education Self-Study Examinations (Zikao) have no age or education restrictions, but full-time students currently enrolled in schools cannot register; registering as an individual industrial and commercial household (getihu) requires only 'the capacity to operate'.
entries.benefit: For military service, see the Military Service Law: 'Male citizens who have reached eighteen years of age shall be conscripted for active service; those not conscripted in that year may still be conscripted for active service before reaching twenty-two years of age. Conscription age for graduates of regular institutions of higher learning may be relaxed up to twenty-four years of age, and conscription age for postgraduates may be relaxed up to twenty-six years of age.' For civil service examinations, see Article 18 of the Provisions on Civil Service Recruitment. Application requirements include 'aged 18 and above, 35 and below' and 'possessing an educational level of college associate degree or higher.' These two criteria may be appropriately adjusted subject to approval by civil service authorities at or above the provincial level. Article 19 of these Provisions lists five categories of persons who shall not apply, such as those who have been subjected to criminal punishment for committing crimes, those who have been dismissed from public employment, and those listed as targets of joint disciplinary action for untrustworthiness. For firefighters, see the Measures for Recruitment and Employment of Firefighters in the National Comprehensive Fire and Rescue Team. Article 5 specifies 'aged 18 and above, 22 and below' and 'possessing an educational level of high school or higher.' Article 6 specifies 'for persons with a college associate degree or higher, and discharged soldiers from the People's Liberation Army and the People's Armed Police Force... the age limit may be relaxed up to 24 years of age.' For civilian personnel in the military, see Article 9 of the Regulations on Civilian Personnel of the Chinese People's Liberation Army, whose basic qualifications include 'having reached 18 years of age.' Article 19 of these Regulations stipulates that the maximum age for initial recruitment and hiring for lower-grade positions is 35 years of age. Lower-grade positions refer to entry-level posts. For public institutions (shiye danwei), see Article 8 of the Regulations on Personnel Management of Public Institutions: 'Newly hired personnel of public institutions shall be recruited openly from society.' For individual industrial and commercial households (getihu), see the Regulations on Promoting the Development of Individual Industrial and Commercial Households: 'Citizens with the capacity to operate... who register as individual industrial and commercial households in accordance with the law shall be subject to these Regulations.' For self-study examinations, see the Interim Regulations on Higher Education Self-Study Examinations. Article 3 states: 'Citizens of the People's Republic of China, regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, race, and prior educational attainment, may participate in Higher Education Self-Study Examinations in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations.' Article 20 states: 'Enrolled students of full-time schools of all levels and categories may not apply.' For government-funded normal university students, see Article 2 of the Implementation Measures for the Articulated Undergraduate-to-Postgraduate Tuition-Free Education for Normal Students of Normal Universities Directly Under the Ministry of Education. Recruitment is conducted only at six normal universities directly under the Ministry: Beijing Normal University, East China Normal University, Northeast Normal University, Central China Normal University, Shaanxi Normal University, and Southwest University. The undergraduate and postgraduate stages are integrally designed with phased evaluations, allowing students to transition directly into graduate studies upon completing undergraduate education. Tuition and accommodation fees during the schooling period are borne by the central treasury, and a living allowance subsidy is additionally provided. Article 5 of these Measures specifies that 'recruitment of tuition-free normal students shall implement early-batch admission,' meaning admission takes place before standard admission batches. For targeted medical students, see the Circular on Doing a Good Job in Employment Placement and Contract Performance Management for Rural Order-Oriented Free Medical Students. It states: 'After admission and prior to receiving the admission notice, an agreement must be signed with the training institution, the county-level health administrative department at the location of targeted employment... and the human resources and social security department.' For working abroad as a laborer, see the Regulations on the Administration of Overseas Labor Cooperation. Article 5 states: engaging in overseas labor cooperation shall require approval from the commerce administrative department to obtain operational qualifications. Article 7, Paragraph 4 states: 'Those that have not obtained an overseas labor cooperation operation qualification certificate in accordance with the law and completed registration shall not engage in overseas labor cooperation.' A company organizing individuals to work abroad without this qualification certificate is illegal in itself. Article 8, Paragraph 2 states: 'No entity or individual may organize labor personnel to work abroad under the pretext of business, tourism, study abroad, or other guises.' Platform gig work and flexible employment have no statutory education thresholds; the basis for self-enrolled social insurance and occupational injury protection can be found in Items 11 and 12 of this section. For general wage labor, see the Compulsory Education Law: 'Employers are prohibited from recruiting children and adolescents of school age who should receive compulsory education.' Article 2 of the Provisions on the Prohibition of Child Labor specifies that persons under 16 years of age shall not be employed; for penalties, see Section 23, Item 1 (Under 16 years of age).

entries.notes: There are also several paths where thresholds are not strictly fixed. The regulations for public institutions only require open recruitment; specific age and education requirements depend on each recruitment announcement. Platform gig work has no statutory education threshold. Age and education requirements for civil service examinations can be adjusted with approval from supervisory departments at or above the provincial level. After meeting the entry thresholds, one must still clear hurdles such as political eligibility, physical examination, and political vetting. These stages have no publicly released scoring rubrics and cannot be looked up in codified clauses. For admission entryways into secondary vocational schools, technical schools, and integrated vocational educational programs, see Section 23, Item 5; for financial aid when families cannot afford schooling, see Section 23, Item 4. The fact that individual businesses (getihu) do not screen for educational credentials does not mean running a shop is easy. For capital requirements, personal guarantees, and shutdown and exit costs, see Section 12. A personal guarantee means that if the business cannot repay, you must repay the debts yourself. For whether startup loans can be obtained where the state subsidizes part of the interest, see Item 16 of this section. The two paths of government-funded normal students and targeted medical students are locked in on the day you fill out college entrance examination preferences; their costs and commitments are detailed in Item 13. The threshold for working abroad as a laborer lies not within you, but in whether the company holds proper qualifications; how to verify them is shown in Item 14. This section does not make comparisons regarding which path is more cost-effective.

entries.title: Military service registration must be completed before October 31 of the year you turn eighteen; active duty for compulsory soldiers is two years
entries.cost: No monetary cost. Registration is filled out online once and takes just a few minutes. If you actually enlist, the cost is two years of full-time commitment, during which you cannot do other things simultaneously.
entries.summary: Military service registration is a statutory obligation, not an application to enlist; registering does not mean you have to go. Male citizens who turn 18 in that year must complete online registration before October 31. For those who fail to register, the county government will order correction within a prescribed time limit; if still not corrected, you will be compelled to fulfill military service obligations and fined. If you actually enlist, active duty for compulsory soldiers is two years.
entries.benefit: For registration, see the Provisions on Military Service Registration Work. It states: 'The military service organs of the people's governments of counties, autonomous counties, cities not divided into districts, and municipal districts shall organize male citizens within their administrative areas who reach 18 years of age on or before December 31 of that year to carry out initial military service registration before October 31 each year.' The same provisions also state: 'Initial military service registration shall be conducted primarily via online registration, completed independently by citizens through the military service registration web platform.' For what happens if one fails to register, see Article 57, Paragraph 1 of the Military Service Law. This paragraph governs those who 'refuse or evade military service registration.' The penalty is: 'the county-level people's government shall order correction within a prescribed time limit; if not corrected within the time limit, the county-level people's government shall compel the fulfillment of military service obligations and impose a fine.' The target group for initial military service registration specified in Article 15 of the Military Service Law is 'male citizens who reach eighteen years of age on or before December thirty-first each year.' Article 20, Paragraph 2 states that 'according to military needs, female citizens may be conscripted for active service in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph.' Article 15 of the Provisions on Military Service Registration Work states that 'according to military needs... eligible female citizens may be organized to perform reserve service registration.' The Military Service Law also states that 'the term of active service for compulsory soldiers is two years.' 'According to military needs and personal voluntariness, citizens who have reached seventeen years of age but have not reached eighteen years of age may be conscripted for active service.' For non-commissioned officers (sergeants), 'those who have served on active duty for twelve years or meet other conditions prescribed by the state shall be arranged with jobs by the local people's government at or above the county level in the place of resettlement.' For sergeants, 'those who have served on active duty for thirty years, or have reached fifty-five years of age, or meet other conditions prescribed by the state, shall be resettled through retirement.' Job arrangement means the government assigns you a job, and retirement resettlement means handling discharge under retirement status. The Regulations on Conscription Work state: 'priority shall be guaranteed for the conscription of graduates of regular institutions of higher learning and recruits with special requirements for political or physical conditions or professional skills.' These regulations also state: 'conscripts who are full-time enrolled students or graduating students of regular institutions of higher learning may enlist at the place of their household registration prior to enrollment or at the location of their school' (National)
entries.sources: General Office of the State Council, General Office of the Central Military Commission (2025). Provisions on Military Service Registration Work (Guo Ban Fa [2025] No. 41). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202512/content_7051363.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2021). Military Service Law (2021 Revision, Articles 15, 20, 25, 26, 54, and 57). <http://www.mod.gov.cn/regulatory/2021-08/20/content_4892491.htm> (published by the Ministry of National Defense); State Council, Central Military Commission (2023). Regulations on Conscription Work (State Council, Central Military Commission Order No. 759, Article 5). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2023/content_5753313.htm>
entries.notes: Registration and enlistment are two separate matters, with a huge difference in cost. The series of punitive measures barring exit from the country for two years penalizes only those who renege after enlisting; see Item 3 (Refusal of military service). The target of initial military service registration written in law includes only males; females are conscripted based on military needs and may also undergo reserve registration based on military needs. The conditions for enlisted soldiers taking military academy examinations or high-performing soldiers being promoted to officers (tigan) are written in internal military regulations and cannot be looked up externally. The Military Service Law states only two sentences: active-duty officers are selected and recruited from persons including 'active-duty soldiers with outstanding performance,' and military academies recruiting cadets are not subject to conscription age restrictions. Specific cutoff scores and quotas are not provided in this book.

entries.title: Refusing military service after being conscripted bars you from leaving the country or advancing/resuming studies for two years, and disqualifies you from civil service and state-owned enterprises
entries.cost: No monetary cost. The cost is that before signing up, you must think through completely whether you want to go.
entries.summary: If you sign up and then refuse to serve, and still fail to correct after being ordered to do so, a chain of consequences follows. You cannot be hired as a civil servant, nor can you be employed by state-owned enterprises or public institutions. For two years, you are barred from leaving the country and from advancing to higher education or resuming studies, and you will be placed on the list of entities subject to joint disciplinary action for serious untrustworthiness in fulfilling national defense obligations. Therefore, 'signing up first and backing out if it doesn't work out' is a very costly notion.
entries.benefit: Article 57, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Military Service Law covers situations where 'a conscripted citizen refuses or evades conscription for active service.' The penalty is likewise that 'the county-level people's government shall order correction within a prescribed time limit; if not corrected within the time limit, the county-level people's government shall compel the fulfillment of military service obligations and impose a fine.' Paragraph 2 of the same article states: 'Whoever commits the act specified in Item 2 of the preceding paragraph and refuses to correct shall not be employed as a civil servant or personnel managed with reference to the Civil Servant Law of the People's Republic of China, shall not be recruited or hired as personnel of state-owned enterprises or public institutions, shall not be permitted to leave the country or advance to higher education or resume schooling within two years, and shall be included in the list of entities subject to joint disciplinary action for serious untrustworthiness in fulfilling national defense obligations for the implementation of joint disciplinary sanctions.' Joint disciplinary action means multiple government departments coordinate using the same list to collectively enforce the above restrictions. Article 58 applies the same set of sanctions to personnel who have already enlisted. If military personnel refuse to perform their duties or flee their unit for the purpose of evading military service, the consequences depend on the outcome of disposition. Those removed from the military rolls, stripped of military status, or held criminally liable in accordance with the law shall be punished in accordance with Article 57, Paragraph 2. Among them, those removed from the rolls shall additionally be fined (National, effective October 1, 2021)
entries.sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2021). Military Service Law (2021 Revision, Articles 57 and 58). <http://www.mod.gov.cn/regulatory/2021-08/20/content_4892491.htm> (published by the Ministry of National Defense)
entries.notes: What is calculated here is personal freedom and employment qualifications, not money. This series of disciplinary measures punishes only two kinds of people. One is 'conscripted citizens who refuse or evade conscription for active service.' The other is those who, after enlisting, are removed from the rolls, stripped of military status, or investigated for criminal liability. Merely failing to complete military service registration is not included; for military service registration, see Item 2. The prerequisite for punishment is 'refusal to correct,' which is determined and penalized by the county-level people's government. The fine amount is determined locally and is not stated in this book. Whether to go is up to you to decide, but the decision must be finalized before applying.

entries.title: The two most tangible benefits of college students enlisting: Tuition compensation of up to 20,000 yuan per year, retention of academic status for two years after discharge, and dedicated programs for master's degree entrance exams
entries.cost: No monetary cost. After discharge, submit application materials according to university requirements, which entails one or two administrative trips.
entries.summary: When enrolled college students, fresh graduates, and newly admitted students enlist in the military, the state covers tuition fees for the years of study. The maximum subsidy is 20,000 yuan per year for undergraduate and associate-degree students, and up to 25,000 yuan for graduate students; if tuition is already lower, only the actual amount paid is compensated. Academic enrollment status is preserved during service, and studies can be resumed within two years after discharge. For master's degree entrance examinations, there is also a dedicated special admission quota exclusively recruiting discharged college-student soldiers.
entries.benefit: A 2024 notice from four government departments, including the Ministry of Finance, states that college students who enlist in military service receive three types of treatment: tuition compensation, compensatory repayment of national student loans used for tuition, and tuition waivers. Compensatory repayment means that the state pays off this student loan on your behalf. The standards for these three benefits "are correspondingly adjusted to a maximum of no more than 20,000 yuan per person per year for undergraduate and junior college students, and a maximum of no more than 25,000 yuan per person per year for graduate students." The new standards take effect starting from the autumn semester of 2024. As for exactly how much compensation is provided, look at this sentence: "Implemented according to whichever is higher between the tuition fees actually paid by the student or the national student loan received (including principal and interest accrued before full repayment)." A subsequent sentence further states that "amounts exceeding the standard will not be compensated, repaid on the student's behalf, or waived." Therefore, for the money received each year, first take the higher of the actual tuition and the student loan, and then compare it with the ceiling, taking the smaller amount. If the tuition is 5,000 yuan per year, 5,000 yuan will be compensated. The number of years compensated is calculated based on the number of years spent studying, not the number of years of military service. The 2019 Administrative Measures for Student Financial Aid Funds state: "The prescribed schooling period completed prior to enlistment serves as the duration for tuition compensation or compensatory repayment of national student loans; the remaining prescribed schooling period continued and completed after retirement and resumption of studies serves as the duration for tuition waivers." For fresh graduating students who enlist, the tuition for the entire standard schooling duration is compensated. Regarding academic student status, see the Veterans Protection Law. It states: "Active-duty military personnel who were admitted to ordinary higher education institutions or were studying in ordinary higher education institutions prior to enlistment shall have their admission qualifications or student enrollment status retained during active duty, and shall be permitted to enroll or resume studies within two years after discharge; they may transfer to other majors within their school in accordance with relevant state regulations." The law also states: "Higher education institutions may recruit and examine veterans through methods such as separate quotas and independent admissions in accordance with unified state arrangements." For master's degree examinations, see the 2026 notice from the General Office of the Ministry of Education. This program is called the "Retired College Student Soldiers Program." The notice states: "Issued separately and designated for dedicated use within the total quota of the national master's degree graduate student admissions plan, and must not be adjusted into general plans or other special programs. Admissions units shall independently determine... preliminary examination score requirements (generally not higher than the preliminary examination score requirements for regular plan candidates in the corresponding disciplines and majors of the institution)... Under equal conditions, candidates with longer lengths of active service shall be prioritized for admission." The meaning of being separately allocated and for dedicated use is that these spots are set aside independently and can only be used to admit retired college student soldiers. In 2026, this program is undertaken by 532 ordinary higher education institutions (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Education, People's Bank of China, and National Financial Regulatory Administration (2024). Notice on Adjusting and Improving Relevant Policies on National Student Loans (Cai Jiao [2024] No. 188). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202411/content_6984812.htm>; Ministry of Finance and four other departments (2019). Administrative Measures for Student Financial Aid Funds (Cai Ke Jiao [2019] No. 19, Article 5; enlistment financial aid duration: "The prescribed schooling period completed prior to enlistment serves as the duration for tuition compensation or compensatory repayment of national student loans; the remaining prescribed schooling period continued and completed after retirement and resumption of studies serves as the duration for tuition waivers", for graduates "the duration of tuition compensation or compensatory repayment of national student loans is calculated respectively according to the corresponding standard schooling duration stipulated by the state"). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2019/content_5421553.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2020). Veterans Protection Law (Articles 34 and 35). <http://www.mod.gov.cn/gfbw/fgwx/flfg/16048597.html> (Published by the Ministry of National Defense); General Office of the Ministry of Education (2025). Notice on Doing a Good Job in the Admissions Work of the 2026 Special Master's Degree Graduate Student Admissions Program for Retired College Student Soldiers (Jiao Xue Ting [2025] No. 8). <http://www.moe.gov.cn/srcsite/A15/moe_778/s3261/202512/t20251211_1423174.html>; Ministry of Veterans Affairs (2022). 23 Policies on Education and Training for Retired Soldiers: "Starting from 2022 admissions, vocational (junior college) graduates and current students (including newly admitted college students) who enlist in the army and complete their vocational (junior college) studies after discharge may apply for junior-college-to-bachelor upgrade programs exempt from academic subject examinations" (based on Jiao Xue Ting [2021] No. 8). <https://www.mva.gov.cn/sy/xx/bnxx/202201/t20220107_55052.html>; Ministry of Education (2026). Administrative Provisions on the National Master's Degree Graduate Student Admissions Work in 2027 (Jiao Xue [2026] No. 2, Articles 22, 24, and 25), published on the China Graduate Admissions Information Web. <https://yz.chsi.com.cn/kyzx/jybzc/202609/20260924/2293971511.html>; Ministry of Education (2024). Administrative Provisions on the National Master's Degree Graduate Student Admissions Work in 2025 (Jiao Xue [2024] No. 4, Article 22). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202410/content_6978684.htm>
entries.notes: There are two other pathways. First is exemption from academic subject exams for junior-college-to-bachelor upgrades: junior college students who enlist and complete their junior college studies after discharge can apply for an exam-exempt junior-college-to-bachelor upgrade, with schools testing vocational skills and admitting candidates on a competitive basis. This rule has been implemented starting with 2022 admissions; for specific measures, consult your province's notice for that year. Second is 10 bonus points on the master's preliminary examination: retired college student soldiers who take the graduate entrance examination within 3 years after discharge receive an extra 10 points added to their total preliminary examination score. If applying through the special program, you will not receive bonus points; the two cannot be enjoyed together. Those who have won a Second-Class Merit Citation or above may apply for admission to graduate school exempt from the preliminary examination. The list of schools participating in the special program changes annually; in 2025, there were 523 institutions. The tuition standard has been adjusted twice: in 2019 it was 8,000/12,000, in the autumn of 2023 it was changed to 16,000/20,000, and in the autumn of 2024 it was changed to 20,000/25,000. The Ministry of Veterans Affairs' 2022 summary still cites the earliest version, so do not copy that blindly.

entries.title: Only six circumstances qualify for government-arranged jobs after discharge; those independently seeking employment must register within 30 days
entries.cost: Free. Bring your discharge certificate and make a trip to the veterans affairs department at your resettlement destination.
entries.summary: "Guaranteed job assignments for military service" has long ceased to be the general rule. Currently, only six circumstances qualify for government-arranged employment; the vast majority of compulsory servicemembers discharged after two years of service do not fall within these six categories. The category where the government does not arrange employment is called independent employment, which carries a strict deadline: you must report for registration within 30 days after discharge from active service. Exceeding 30 days without a legitimate reason is considered a forfeiture of your resettlement benefits.
entries.benefit: Article 25 of the Regulations on the Resettlement of Veterans lists six circumstances in which the people's government of the resettlement destination arranges employment. The original text reads: "(1) Sergeants who have served on active duty for a full 12 years; (2) Individuals who were awarded medals or honorary titles during active service; (3) Individuals who were awarded a Third-Class Battle Merit, a Second-Class Merit Citation, or higher during active service; (4) Individuals who received a First-Class Commendation during active service; (5) Individuals disabled in battle who have been evaluated with a disability rating from Level 5 to Level 8; (6) Children of martyrs." The regulations also state: "The people's government of the resettlement destination shall complete the task of arranging employment for retired sergeants and compulsory servicemembers within 6 months of receiving them." Employer units "shall, in accordance with regulations, sign a medium- to long-term employment contract or labor contract of no less than 3 years with them. Among them, enterprises that accept retired sergeants with a military length of service of more than 10 years shall sign an open-ended labor contract with them." An open-ended contract means no expiration date is written on the contract. During the waiting period for job arrangement, "a living subsidy shall be issued on a monthly basis in accordance with the local monthly minimum wage standard." If one is not arranged for placement in accordance with regulations due to reasons not attributable to oneself, "living expenses shall be issued monthly at a standard of no less than 80% of the average wage of personnel with equivalent conditions in the unit until the post is assumed." Circumstances ineligible for resettlement via government-arranged employment include expulsion from the Communist Party of China and having received criminal penalties. For the deadline regarding independent employment, see Article 51: "Retired sergeants and compulsory servicemembers seeking independent employment shall, within 30 days from the date of approval of discharge from active service, report to the competent department of veterans affairs of the people's government at the resettlement destination. Those who fail to report at the designated time for more than 30 days without justifiable reasons shall be deemed to have forfeited resettlement entitlements." (Nationwide, effective September 1, 2024)
entries.sources: State Council and Central Military Commission (2024). Regulations on the Resettlement of Veterans (Order No. 787 of the State Council and the Central Military Commission, promulgated on July 29, 2024, effective September 1, 2024; Articles 25, 31, 32, 35, 51, and 75). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2024/issue_11526/202408/content_6969192.html>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2020). Veterans Protection Law (Articles 13, 14, and 15). <http://www.mod.gov.cn/gfbw/fgwx/flfg/16048597.html> (Published by the Ministry of National Defense)
entries.notes: On the same day this regulation took effect, the 2011 Regulations on the Resettlement of Retired Soldiers (Order No. 608 of the State Council and the Central Military Commission) was repealed. Numerous online guides still cite the old regulations, but the wording of the conditions has already changed; the old version read "awarded a Second-Class Merit Citation or above in peacetime, or awarded a Third-Class Merit Citation or above in wartime." The 30-day deadline applies only to the independent employment category; other resettlement categories report "in accordance with the prescribed time." Upon reporting, a veteran preferential treatment card will be issued, from which follow-up discharge severance pay, employment and entrepreneurship support, and educational subsidies are connected.

entries.title: Three financial accounts after discharge: lump-sum discharge severance pay, military service counted as working years, and 20,000 yuan annual tax deductions for self-employment
entries.cost: Free. Upon discharge, the military transfers out your social insurance relations and funds. You then handle the continuation procedures at the social security agency (the social insurance handling service window) at your resettlement destination.
entries.summary: There are three financial accounts after discharge. The first is the lump-sum discharge severance pay for independent employment, issued based on the years of active service, with increased amounts for those who earned merit citations. The second is military service counted as working years, where contribution years are calculated cumulatively with those before enlistment and after discharge. The third is taxation: those who open a shop and start a business can reduce their taxes by up to an annual cap of 20,000 yuan within 3 years, with the cap eligible to float upward by up to 20%.
entries.benefit: For the first account, see the Regulations on the Resettlement of Veterans. It states: "Lump-sum discharge severance pay shall be issued to retired sergeants and compulsory servicemembers who pursue independent employment based on their length of active service." Who pays the money: "Specifically allocated through the central fiscal budget; specific standards shall be determined by the competent department of veterans affairs under the State Council and the Political Work Department of the Central Military Commission jointly with the finance department under the State Council... and adjusted in a timely manner." Additional payment ratios are divided into five tiers. An increase of 25% for receiving medals or honorary titles, and 20% for First-Class Battle Merits or First-Class Commendations. An increase of 15% for Second-Class Battle Merits, First-Class Merit Citations, or Second-Class Commendations. An increase of 10% for Third-Class Battle Merits or Second-Class Merit Citations, and 5% for Fourth-Class Battle Merits or Third-Class Merit Citations. The regulations also state: "Veterans who are not promptly employed may apply for unemployment insurance benefits with the human resources and social security department at the place of household registration in accordance with law; the length of active service shall be deemed as the period of insured contribution payment, with the exception of veterans resettled through retirement or care-taking arrangements." Deemed contribution payment years means that even though you did not pay money during these years, they are counted as if paid. For the second account, see the Veterans Protection Law: "The length of active service of veterans shall be calculated as working years, and shall be cumulatively calculated with the working years at the current unit after discharge." Working years refers to the number of years one has participated in work; the years of active service and the years after discharge are added continuously. The law also states that the length of active service and the pension, medical, and unemployment insurance payment years before enlistment and after discharge shall be "combined and calculated according to law," and "the active duty experience of retired sergeants and compulsory servicemembers shall be deemed as grassroots work experience." The Military Personnel Insurance Law states: "The length of active service of military personnel shall be deemed as the payment years of urban employee basic medical insurance, and shall be combined and calculated with the payment years of participating in urban employee basic medical insurance before enlistment and after discharge from active duty." For the third account, see Announcement No. 14 of 2023 by the Ministry of Finance, the State Taxation Administration, and the Ministry of Veterans Affairs. The announcement addresses circumstances where independently employed retired soldiers engage in individual businesses: "Within 3 years (36 months, the same below), the value-added tax, urban maintenance and construction tax, educational surcharge, local educational surcharge, and individual income tax actually payable for the current year shall be deducted sequentially subject to a limit of 20,000 yuan per household per year. The ceiling standard may float upward by up to 20%." Deduction means reducing down sequentially from these types of taxes payable in the current year until the limit is reached; it is not money paid out directly to you. For enterprise recruitment, "the fixed quota standard is 6,000 yuan per person per year, which may float upward by up to 50%." The implementation period is from January 1, 2023 to December 31, 2027. Those whose 3-year period has not expired upon conclusion may continue to enjoy the benefit until the period ends (Nationwide)
entries.sources: State Council and Central Military Commission (2024). Regulations on the Resettlement of Veterans (Order No. 787 of the State Council and the Central Military Commission, Articles 21, 22, 74, 81, and 85). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2024/issue_11526/202408/content_6969192.html>; Ministry of Veterans Affairs (2020). Ten Questions Concerning Lump-Sum Discharge Severance Pay (reprinted from China Veterans, 2020 Issue 10): "Basic standard. For each full year of active duty served by a soldier, 4,500 yuan shall be issued" "The severance pay standard shall be adjusted in a timely manner". <https://www.mva.gov.cn/sy/zzxc/202011/t20201113_43153.html>; Department of Veterans Affairs of Guizhou Province (2024). Additional Lump-Sum Discharge Severance Pay, Important Changes!: "The standard currently implemented is: for each full year of active duty served by a soldier, 4,500 yuan is issued". <http://tyjrswt.guizhou.gov.cn/zfxxgk/fdzdgknr/zdlyxx_5621158/tyaz_5621161/202408/t20240809_85367194.html>; People's Government of Muping District, Yantai City (2025). The reply cites the Notice of Yantai Municipal Bureau of Veterans Affairs and Yantai Municipal Bureau of Finance on Adjusting the Standards of One-Time Economic Subsidies for Independently Employed Retired Soldiers: "For those discharged from active service in 2024, a subsidy of 6,000 yuan per year of service shall be granted". <https://www.muping.gov.cn/art/2025/11/10/art_105032_2960250.html>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2020). Veterans Protection Law (Articles 42, 44, and 50). <http://www.mod.gov.cn/gfbw/fgwx/flfg/16048597.html> (Published by the Ministry of National Defense); Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2012). Military Personnel Insurance Law (Articles 16 and 23). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf73e160645> (National Database of Laws and Regulations); Ministry of Finance, State Taxation Administration, and Ministry of Veterans Affairs (2023). Announcement on Further Supporting the Tax Policies Related to the Entrepreneurship and Employment of Independently Employed Retired Soldiers (Announcement No. 14 of 2023). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202308/content_6896456.htm>
entries.notes: The regulations only state that the specific amount shall be determined separately by the competent departments. The official figure that can be verified is "issued at 4,500 yuan for each full year of active service" in an article published on the official website of the Ministry of Veterans Affairs in 2020; the same article also states "adjusted in a timely manner." The additional payment percentages in that article no longer match the current regulations, and the regulations should prevail. An article published by the Department of Veterans Affairs of Guizhou Province in August 2024 still states under the new regulations that "the standard currently implemented is: for each full year of active service served by a soldier, 4,500 yuan is issued." The 4,500 yuan is the standard cited in this provincial article. No formal document has been found for the current nationwide standard; refer to the statement of the local veterans affairs department at the time of discharge. Furthermore, do not confuse this with local "lump-sum economic subsidies." That is a separate payment determined and issued locally by various areas; for instance, Yantai provided a subsidy of 6,000 yuan for each year of service for those discharged in 2024. Most new numbers found in online guides have no sources, and some simply conflate these two payments. During the service period of compulsory servicemembers, their families can also separately collect a family preferential treatment allowance. The Military Service Law only states that "standards are formulated by local people's governments, with fixed subsidies provided by central finance"; for the specific amount, ask the county-level people's government that approved your enlistment. The tax entry refers to the maximum amount of tax you can pay less each year, not cash distributed into your hands. If the business does not take off, you cannot fully utilize the quota, so the overall benefit scale of the entry is rated only as "Medium." The Regulations on the Promotion of Employment and Entrepreneurship for Veterans, effective August 1, 2026, adds another provision: skilled personnel occupational qualification certificates obtained during active service remain valid nationwide after discharge.

entries.title: Entering the public sector involves more than regular civil service exams: completing two years in grassroots service projects unlocks annual 10% targeted recruitment plans
entries.cost: Free. The trade-off is serving at the township grassroots level for two years. Over these two years, you receive fiscal subsidies rather than market wages; the difficulty lies in enduring these two years.
entries.summary: Taking the regular civil service examination is not the only way to enter the public sector. Completing two years in grassroots service projects such as "Three Supports and One Help" with a qualified evaluation enables you to register for targeted recruitment plans open exclusively to such personnel. Each province must allocate around 10% of its civil service examination recruitment plan each year to recruit these individuals. If taking the master's entrance examination within three years, 10 bonus points are also added to your preliminary exam score. The trade-off is that you receive fiscal living subsidies during these two years.
entries.benefit: The notice for the Fourth Round of the "Three Supports and One Help" Plan states that "the service period is two years." It also states: "Each province (autonomous region, municipality directly under the Central Government) shall designate around 10% of its civil service examination recruitment plans each year for targeted recruitment of grassroots service project personnel such as the 'Three Supports and One Help' plan. When public institutions at the county and township grassroots levels in various provinces (autonomous regions, municipalities directly under the Central Government) conduct open recruitment, they shall, based on local realities, set aside a certain number or proportion of positions to conduct special recruitment for personnel who have completed their 'Three Supports and One Help' service period and passed the evaluation... Upon employment, probationary periods may no longer be stipulated." The meaning of targeted recruitment and special recruitment is that these spots are competed for only among people who have completed grassroots service projects; others cannot register. The same notice also states: "'Three Supports and One Help' personnel who have completed their service period and passed evaluation, when participating in the National Master's Degree Graduate Student Admissions Examination within three years, shall have 10 points added to their total preliminary examination score, and shall be prioritized for admission under equal conditions... Vocational (junior college) graduates who have completed their service period and passed evaluation may be enrolled in adult higher education junior-college-to-bachelor upgrade programs exempt from examinations." Exam-exempt enrollment means attending the junior-college-to-bachelor upgrade directly without taking another examination. The notice further states: "Personnel without prior work experience before participating in the 'Three Supports and One Help' plan who have completed their service period and passed evaluation may, within two years, equally enjoy relevant policies for fresh graduates in participating in examinations and recruitment for party and government organs, enterprises, and public institutions, independent entrepreneurship, household registration, further education, etc. The service years of 'Three Supports and One Help' personnel at the grassroots level shall be calculated as working years, and their time of starting work shall be calculated from the date they reported to the grassroots unit." The central fiscal subsidy standards are 30,000 yuan per person per year in western regions, 24,000 yuan in central regions, and 12,000 yuan in eastern regions. Opinions from the General Office of the CPC Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council state: "Personnel who had no prior work experience before participating in grassroots service projects may, within 2 years after completing their service period and passing evaluation, equally enjoy policies applicable to fresh college graduates in participating in examinations and recruitment for organs and public institutions, employment absorption by various enterprises, independent entrepreneurship, household registration, further education, etc." The opinions also state: "Civil service recruitment for organs at or above the provincial level, with the exception of special positions, shall in accordance with relevant regulations be conducted entirely from among personnel who possess more than 2 years of grassroots work experience." Another route is the Western Volunteer Service Program. It is "jointly organized and implemented by the Central Committee of the Communist Youth League, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Finance, and the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security." It recruits graduating college students or current graduate students "to engage in voluntary service at the grassroots level in the western region for a period of 1 to 3 years" (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee, Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, et al. (ten departments) (2021). Notice on Implementing the Fourth Round of the "Three Supports and One Assistance" Plan for College Graduates (Ren She Bu Fa [2021] No. 32, Articles 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, and 13). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-06/04/content_5615404.htm>; General Office of the CPC Central Committee, General Office of the State Council (2017). Opinions on Further Guiding and Encouraging College Graduates to Work at the Grassroots Level (Articles 5, 16, and 18). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2017/content_5171278.htm>; National Project Management Office of the College Graduate Volunteer Service Western Program (2026). Recruitment Agreement for the 2026–2027 College Graduate Volunteer Service Western Program. <http://xibu.youth.cn/tzgg/202604/t20260423_16623558.htm>
entries.notes: The fourth round of the "Three Supports and One Assistance" plan governs 2021 through 2025. This search did not locate fifth-round documents or the 2026 annual notice; check the recruitment announcement for the current year before applying. In 2025, central fiscal funds supported the recruitment of 34,430 individuals. The original text of the implementation plan for the Western Program cannot be found online; the policy section on its official website fails to load content. Its preferential policies upon completion follow the document issued by the General Offices of the CPC Central Committee and the State Council that governs all grassroots service projects. During these two years, you receive fiscal subsidies rather than market wages; this cost must be weighed together with the targeted examination and recruitment opportunities available two years later. For how fresh graduate status is recognized and what to check before signing an employment agreement, see Item 17 of this section ("Fresh Graduates").

entries.title: Special post teachers who complete their three-year service term, pass evaluations, and are willing to stay should be promptly granted permanent establishment (bianzhi)
entries.cost: Costs no money. The trade-off is teaching in rural compulsory education schools for three years, and you must pass the teacher qualification certificate examination before entering. The difficult part is staying the course for these three years.
entries.summary: The Special Post Plan is one of the few pathways explicitly specifying "absorption into permanent establishment upon term completion." The requirements are a bachelor's degree or higher, primarily in teacher education majors, age not exceeding 30 years old, and possession of the corresponding teacher qualification certificate. The service period is three years, during which compensation and benefits under equal conditions are the same as those of established teachers in local public schools. For those who pass evaluations upon completing the three-year term and wish to stay, policy documents mandate prompt inclusion into permanent establishment.
entries.benefit: The recruitment conditions stated in the 2024 Special Post Plan notice are: "Requiring a bachelor's degree or higher, primarily in teacher education majors, with primary school stages allowed to appropriately recruit graduates from normal junior colleges." "Age not exceeding 30 years old." Candidates must also possess corresponding teacher qualification certificates. The notice further states: "Under equal conditions, priority admission will be given to volunteers who participated in the 'College Graduate Volunteer Service Western Program' and have teaching experience, as well as normal college graduates who participated in student-teaching internships for more than half a year." "Support and encourage qualified military veterans to teach in primary and secondary schools; age restrictions may be relaxed accordingly for veterans by comprehensively considering factors such as years of active service." Regarding compensation and establishment inclusion, note these provisions: "Starting from January 1, 2024, salary subsidy standards for special post teachers are increased; central fiscal funding... increases from 35,200 yuan per person per year to 38,800 yuan in the central region, and from 38,200 yuan to 41,800 yuan in the western region." "Under equal conditions, enjoy the same treatment as established teachers in local public schools regarding salary and compensation, professional title evaluation and appointment, honors and awards selection, annual performance evaluation, and other aspects." "Ensure that special post teachers who complete the three-year service term, pass evaluations, and are willing to remain in service are promptly placed on permanent establishment and assigned working posts, properly handle the transfer of relevant personnel and wage relationships, calculate years of service and teaching seniority consecutively, and no longer impose a probationary period" (Nationwide).
entries.sources: General Office of the Ministry of Education, General Office of the Ministry of Finance (2024). Notice on Doing a Good Job in Implementing the 2024 Special Teacher Post Plan for Rural Compulsory Education Stage Schools (Jiao Shi Ting [2024] No. 1). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202405/content_6950803.htm>
