entries.notes: The benefit magnitude is rated "Large" because entering permanent establishment upon term completion is equivalent to securing long-term established employment, valued well over 10,000 yuan. The latest notice that could be retrieved is the 2024 annual notice; those for 2025 and 2026 have not entered the policy database. Specific posts, subsidy standards, and age requirements are subject to the current year's notice and provincial implementation plans. The central government sets the broad framework, while detailed rules are determined by provinces. Teacher qualification certificates must be obtained beforehand and cannot be supplemented after starting employment.

entries.title: Firefighters and military civilian personnel are two other avenues of open recruitment, with lower thresholds than the civil service examination
entries.cost: Costs no money. Going from application to hiring involves medical examinations, political background checks, physical fitness tests, psychological assessments, and interviews, taking several months from start to finish. The challenge lies in surviving this series of elimination stages one by one.
entries.summary: Neither of these two paths strictly imposes the "associate degree or higher" requirement. Firefighters recruit individuals aged 18 to 22 with a high school education or higher, with the age limit relaxed to 24 for those with an associate degree or higher and discharged soldiers. Military civilian personnel only require reaching 18 years of age, with the maximum age for initial recruitment into entry-level posts set at 35. The shared cost is elimination through political background checks and medical examinations.
entries.benefit: For firefighters, consult the *Measures for the Recruitment of Firefighters in the National Comprehensive Fire and Rescue Teams*. Basic requirements in Article 5 include "aged 18 and above, 22 and below" and "possessing an educational level of high school or above." Article 6: "For personnel with a college associate degree or higher, discharged soldiers from the People's Liberation Army and the People's Armed Police, and government full-time firefighters and government full-time forest firefighters with more than 2 years of practical firefighting and rescue experience, the age limit may be relaxed to 24 years old; for special professional talents urgently needed for firefighting and rescue work, the age may be further relaxed upon approval by the Ministry of Emergency Management, in principle not exceeding 28 years old." Article 7: "Firefighters are openly recruited from society, primarily from permanent residents within the provincial administrative region, and may also be recruited from other provinces as needed." The recruitment procedure outlined in Article 9 includes "publicity and mobilization, organizing registration, qualification review, physical examination, political assessment, physical fitness and job suitability tests, psychological assessment and interview, public notification, and hiring." For military civilian personnel, consult Article 18 of the *Regulations on Military Civilian Personnel of the Chinese People's Liberation Army*: "The military implements a recruitment and employment system for civilian personnel that combines open examinations, direct talent introduction, and targeted special recruitments." These are three avenues: recruiting personnel through open examinations, directly introducing established talent, and conducting targeted recruitments for specific groups. Article 9 of the regulations lists basic conditions including "having reached 18 years of age," "meeting the political criteria for military recruitment and employment of civilian personnel," and "possessing the educational level, professional competence, and work capability required by the post." Article 19 specifies that the maximum age for initial recruitment and appointment to lower-tier posts is 35 years old. The regulations also stipulate that "civilian personnel positions shall give priority recruitment and employment to qualified military veterans" (Nationwide).
entries.sources: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, Ministry of Emergency Management (2021). Measures for the Recruitment of Firefighters in the National Comprehensive Fire and Rescue Teams (Ren She Bu Fa [2021] No. 58, Articles 5, 6, 7, and 9). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-08/27/content_5633684.htm>; State Council, Central Military Commission (2022). Regulations on Military Civilian Personnel of the Chinese People's Liberation Army (Second Revision, Decree of the State Council and the Central Military Commission No. 757, effective January 1, 2023; Articles 9, 18, 19, and 20). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808181857bca5e01859ee5a6c06d62> (National Database of Laws and Regulations)
entries.notes: The *Regulations on Promoting Employment and Entrepreneurship for Veterans*, effective August 1, 2026, additionally stipulates two points. First, firefighter recruitments must allocate a certain quota specifically for discharged non-commissioned officers and conscripts. Second, when recruiting police auxiliary personnel (auxiliary police), priority should be given to veterans under equal conditions. Quotas, posts, and specific conditions for these two paths are subject to the current year's announcements; this book only documents the fixed, permanent criteria defined in regulatory measures. Firefighting is a disciplined service role; fully think through the occupational risks before joining.

entries.title: Academic credentials are not a one-shot deal: self-taught examination has no age or prior education limits, adult college entrance exams and open universities can both make up deficits; only degrees verified on CHSI count, and do not enroll in degree-upgrading programs claiming "no exams needed and guaranteed pass"
entries.cost: Registration fees and textbook costs run several hundred yuan per year. The trade-off is long-term self-study or attending classes during spare time; non-full-time (studying while working) top-up programs from associate to bachelor's degree take at least two and a half years, and the difficulty lies in persevering over the long haul.
entries.summary: Missing out on education at age eighteen is followed by three formal avenues: self-taught higher education examinations (Zikao), adult college entrance examinations (Chengkao), and open universities. Self-taught examination does not limit age or prior educational background, but enrolled full-time students cannot register. Graduation certificates only count if they can be queried on CHSI (China Higher Education Student Information and Career Center), and schools cannot alter them once recorded. Do not pay money to anyone claiming "no studying needed" or "no exams needed and guaranteed pass."
entries.benefit: For self-taught examinations, see the *Interim Regulations on Higher Education Self-Taught Examination*. Article 3: "Citizens of the People's Republic of China, regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, race, and prior educational attainment, may take higher education self-taught examinations in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations." Article 20: "Enrolled students of full-time schools of all levels and types shall not register for the examination." Article 25 outlines three conditions for obtaining a graduation certificate: passing all courses, completing graduation theses or practical tasks, and passing moral and ideological evaluations. Meeting all of these qualifies one for a graduation certificate. This article also states, "Those who obtain an associate (foundation) or bachelor's graduation certificate shall have their educational credentials recognized by the state." Article 32 outlines wage treatment for graduation certificate holders: "Upon hiring, non-employed personnel receive the same treatment as comparable graduates of regular institutions of higher education." Article 21 of the *Higher Education Law*: "The state implements a higher education self-taught examination system; those who pass examinations shall be issued corresponding academic credential certificates or other academic certificates." For adult college entrance examinations, see the *2025 National Regulations on Adult Higher Education Admissions*. Target applicants are "practitioners and other members of society other than enrolled students in various types of higher and secondary schools recognized by the state." "Candidates applying for high school to bachelor's degree or high school to associate degree programs should be graduates of senior secondary education schools or possess equivalent academic ability. Candidates applying for top-up programs from associate to bachelor's degree must be individuals who have obtained... an associate graduation certificate, a bachelor's completion certificate, or higher credentials." "The shortest study duration for full-time off-job study is: four years for high school to bachelor's, two years for high school to associate degree and associate to bachelor's; the shortest study duration for non-full-time study is: five years for high school to bachelor's, two and a half years for high school to associate degree and associate to bachelor's." Full-time off-job means leaving work to study full-time on campus; non-full-time means studying while remaining employed without leaving work. For open universities, see the Ministry of Education's *Opinions on Running Open Universities Well*. It states: "Open universities implement open registration admission; students who finish coursework and earn corresponding credits may obtain course certificates; those who accumulate required credits and satisfy relevant requirements may obtain corresponding academic degree and non-degree certificates; those meeting degree-awarding criteria shall be awarded corresponding degrees" (Nationwide). To verify degree authenticity, see the Ministry of Education's *Measures for the Electronic Registration of Student Status and Academic Credentials in Institutions of Higher Education*. Article 2 specifies that self-taught examination graduation certificates must also undergo electronic registration. Article 5: CHSI "is the sole website for querying electronic registration information of student status and academic credentials in institutions of higher education." Article 19: After academic credentials are registered and made available for online inquiry, "schools may not alter certificate contents or registration information." For advertising compliance boundaries in student recruitment, see the 2021 notice issued by five departments including the Ministry of Education. Advertisements for continuing academic education "must not contain false or irregular content such as 'no study required' or 'no classes needed'." Nor may they "contain explicit or implied promissory guarantees of educational outcomes such as 'fast certificate acquisition,' 'exam exemption and guaranteed pass,' or 'full refund if failed'." Institutions like specialty institutes and research/training institutes cannot issue academic degrees, and advertisements must not conflate them with colleges and universities that have degree-granting authority.
entries.sources: State Council (1988, revised 2014). Interim Regulations on Higher Education Self-Taught Examination (Articles 3, 20, 25, and 32). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f3cbb3c016f415d64e5236d> (National Database of Laws and Regulations); Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). Higher Education Law (Article 21). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f135f46016f20df64ec16c5> (National Database of Laws and Regulations); General Office of the Ministry of Education (2025). Notice on Doing a Good Job in the 2025 National Adult Higher Education Admissions Work (Jiao Xue Ting [2025] No. 6) and its attachment "2025 National Regulations on Adult Higher Education Admissions". <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202509/content_7040877.htm>; Ministry of Education (2016). Opinions on Running Open Universities Well (Jiao Zhi Cheng [2016] No. 2). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2016/content_5067956.htm>; Ministry of Education (2007). Notice on Further Strengthening the Admissions Management Work of Various Higher Education Institutions (Jiao Fa [2007] No. 13): "The regular associate-to-bachelor degree enrollment plan shall be arranged at a proportion not exceeding 5% of the graduating class of regular vocational college (associate degree) graduates of that year." <http://www.moe.gov.cn/s78/A03/s7050/201006/t20100607_88782.html>; Ministry of Education (2014). Notice on Issuing the "Measures for the Electronic Registration of Student Status and Academic Credentials in Institutions of Higher Education" (Jiao Xue [2014] No. 11, Articles 2, 5, and 19). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2015/content_2806021.htm>; General Office of the Ministry of Education et al. (five departments) (2021). Notice on Strengthening the Administration of Advertisement Publishing for Higher Academic Continuing Education (Jiao Zhi Cheng Ting Han [2021] No. 21). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-10/14/content_5642410.htm>; Central People's Government of the People's Republic of China (2020). Expanding Master's Degree Enrollment by 189,000 and Associate-to-Bachelor's Enrollment by 322,000 This Year—Employment Support for Graduates Takes Effect; Vice Minister of Education Weng Tiehui: "Expand the scale of regular associate-to-bachelor degree programs, striving for a year-on-year increase of 322,000 students." <http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2020-02/29/content_5484774.htm>; Fujian Provincial Education Examination Authority (2026). Quoting upon forwarding: "Notice of the Department of Higher Education Student Affairs of the Ministry of Education on Doing a Good Job in the 2026 Regular Higher Education Associate-to-Bachelor Degree Examination and Enrollment Work (Jiao Xue Si Han [2025] No. 53)". <https://www.eeafj.cn/gkzsb/20260310/14437.html>
entries.notes: There is also a regular associate-to-bachelor (Zhuanshengben) track designed for graduating full-time associate degree students. The publicly available national-level document is the 2007 Ministry of Education notice, stating that the associate-to-bachelor plan does not exceed 5% of that year's graduating associate class. Starting in 2020, the Ministry of Education expanded the scale of this program, targeting a year-on-year increase of 322,000 students that year. Whether the 5% cap remains enforced today cannot be confirmed from explicit public texts. Specific annual arrangements are issued via letters from the Department of Higher Education Student Affairs of the Ministry of Education, such as Jiao Xue Si Han [2025] No. 53 for 2026. This letter is not made public externally, and its reference number can only be seen through forwarding notices issued by various provinces. Target applicant criteria are set by each province independently and almost exclusively admit graduating full-time associate students from their own province; hence, these conditions are not detailed in the main text. Starting in the fall of 2025, continuing higher academic education will no longer use the terms "correspondence" (hanshou) or "spare-time" (yeyu), unifying them under "non-full-time" (feituochan). Continuing higher academic education refers to the category of academic credentials supplemented later by adults; be wary of promotional materials still using obsolete terminology. Catching up on credentials and "which skills are cost-effective to learn" are two different matters; the latter is covered in Section 23. Paid "fast certificate issuance" schemes and knockoff certificates are discussed in Section 23, Item 8.

entries.title: Not joining an established employer constitutes flexible employment: you must enroll in pension and healthcare yourself at your place of employment; household registration (hukou) restrictions have been lifted
entries.cost: You must pay the full amount for pension and medical insurance yourself, amounting to over 1,000 yuan per month based on the local contribution base. The contribution base is simply a baseline figure used to calculate premiums. This is the recurring expense most easily overlooked in flexible employment; the challenge is paying it on time every single month.
entries.summary: Not working for an established employer does not mean social security is non-existent; it simply means no one is paying the employer's half for you. Official documents require all localities to lift hukou restrictions on flexible workers participating in social security at their place of employment, with select megacities permitted to phase this in gradually. Do not misinterpret "freelance freedom" as an excuse to ignore social security. If contributions are interrupted, your retirement pension and medical insurance reimbursements will both be calculated according to contribution break rules.
entries.benefit: For insurance participation, see the *Guiding Opinions on Safeguarding the Labor and Social Security Rights and Interests of Workers in New Forms of Employment*. It states: "All localities shall lift household registration restrictions on flexibly employed persons participating in basic pension and basic medical insurance at their place of employment; where individual megacities face difficulties in achieving this in a single step, they should actively create conditions to phase it in gradually based on local realities. Flexibly employed workers who have not participated in basic pension and basic medical insurance for urban employees shall be organized to participate in basic pension and basic medical insurance for urban and rural residents in accordance with regulations, ensuring full coverage. Urge enterprises to participate in social insurance according to law. Enterprises shall guide and support workers in new forms of employment who do not fully meet the conditions for establishing a labor relationship to participate in corresponding social insurance based on their own circumstances." The same document categorizes employment into three types: "Where conditions for establishing a labor relationship are met, enterprises shall enter into labor contracts with workers according to law. Where conditions for establishing a labor relationship are not fully met but the enterprise exercises labor management over the worker... guide enterprises to conclude written agreements with workers... Where individuals independently carry out business activities or engage in freelance occupations relying on platforms, the rights and obligations of both parties shall be governed by civil law" (Nationwide, effective from 2021).
entries.sources: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security et al. (eight departments) (2021). Guiding Opinions on Safeguarding the Labor and Social Security Rights and Interests of Workers in New Forms of Employment (Ren She Bu Fa [2021] No. 56, Articles 2 and 8). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-07/23/content_5626761.htm>; General Office of the State Council (2020). Opinions on Supporting Multi-channel Flexible Employment (Guo Ban Fa [2020] No. 27). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-07/31/content_5531613.htm>
entries.notes: The original text reads "lift" hukou restrictions while retaining leeway for megacities, rather than "nationwide complete cancellation." To what extent restrictions have been lifted must be verified with the specific city where you intend to participate. The benefit magnitude is rated "Large" because missing contributions jeopardizes pension and medical coverage itself, which is worth far more than 10,000 yuan. However, the cost is also very real: paying the full contribution out of pocket exceeds 1,000 yuan per month. For how to make up missed social security payments and how contribution years accrue, see Section 7, Item 18 (Social Security Contribution Breaks). For how to transfer pension and medical insurance relations after switching cities, see Section 19, Item 19 (Transferring Pension and Medical Insurance Relations to a New Place of Coverage). For which bracket to select when paying employee pension insurance on your own and how many years you must draw benefits to break even, see Section 5, Item 46 (Paying Urban Employee Pension Insurance on Your Own). Additionally, individuals selling agricultural/sideline products or daily necessities at government-designated locations and times, or utilizing their own craft skills to perform convenience-service tasks that do not legally require licensing, do not need to obtain a business license. This provision is documented in Guo Ban Fa [2020] No. 27.

entries.title: For food delivery, ride-hailing, and intra-city freight, platforms pay occupational injury protection fees on a per-order basis, requiring no contribution from you
entries.cost: Costs no money; this fee is paid entirely by the platform. What you need to do is verify whether the platform you take orders from is included in the pilot program. There are two methods: look for "Occupational Injury Protection" on the app's protection or rights page, or call your provincial human resources and social security bureau to inquire whether this platform has been filed.
entries.summary: For individuals engaged in food delivery, ride-hailing, and intra-city freight, platforms must pay occupational injury protection fees for you on a per-order basis; you do not pay a single cent yourself, and every accepted order is covered. This remains a pilot program, so check whether your province and platform fall within its scope before accepting orders. Those who have already established a formal labor relationship with a platform follow standard work-related injury insurance, not this system.
entries.benefit: For this protection, refer to the Measures for Occupational Injury Protection for Persons in New Forms of Employment (Trial). Article 2 states: "Platform enterprises shall participate in occupational injury protection for persons in new forms of employment in accordance with the provisions of these Measures... and pay occupational injury protection fees for persons in new forms of employment who register and take orders through the platform, provide labor such as ride-hailing/travel, instant delivery, and intra-city freight in the name of the platform enterprise, and obtain remuneration or income, realizing mandatory coverage for every single order and mandatory coverage for every single person. For laborers to whom the provisions of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance apply, enterprises shall participate in work-related injury insurance for them in accordance with the law, and these Measures shall not apply." Article 9 states: "During the trial period, the travel/ride-hailing industry shall implement the rate at 0.01 yuan per order; the instant delivery industry shall implement the rates at 0.07 yuan and 0.25 yuan per order; the intra-city freight industry shall implement the rate at 0.18 yuan per order." For how the pilot program expands outward, look at this passage: "Starting from July 1, 2025, on the basis of the 7 provinces and 7 platform enterprises that piloted earlier... 10 provinces including Tianjin, Hebei, Liaoning, Zhejiang, Anhui, Fujian, Shandong, Hubei, Guangxi, and Ningxia shall be added... In 2026, promote the implementation of the occupational injury protection pilot program in 31 provinces nationwide and the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps; comprehensively incorporate platform enterprises in the three industries of travel/ride-hailing, instant delivery, and intra-city freight into the scope of the occupational injury protection pilot program" (Pilot, expanding scope year by year)
entries.sources: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and eight other departments (2025). Notice on Expanding the Pilot Program of Occupational Injury Protection for Persons in New Forms of Employment (Ren She Bu Fa [2025] No. 24) and Annex Measures for Occupational Injury Protection for Persons in New Forms of Employment (Trial), Articles 2 and 9. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202507/content_7031656.htm>
entries.notes: This is still a pilot program, not yet a formal nationwide system. Before accepting orders, confirm whether your province and platform fall within the scope; if not, your only remaining layer is to purchase commercial insurance yourself. Another document, Guiding Opinions on Safeguarding the Labor and Social Security Rights and Interests of Workers in New Forms of Employment, also puts forward several requirements. Remuneration paid by platforms to people working normally must not be lower than the local minimum wage, must be paid on time and in full, and must not be deducted or delayed without cause. Reasonable remuneration must also be paid for statutory holidays. The document number of this document is Ren She Bu Fa [2021] No. 56; the flexible employment item also cites it, see Item 11. If an incident occurs, first proceed according to this system; do not first settle privately with the station. For the medical insurance and pension parts, you still need to enroll yourself; for flexible employment insurance enrollment, see Item 11.

entries.title: Two paths to basically lock in public establishment status on the day of filling out Gaokao preferences: tuition-free normal students and targeted medical students, at the cost of 6 years of contractual fulfillment
entries.cost: You do not need to pay tuition or accommodation fees, and you can also receive a living allowance. The cost is that you cannot freely choose your career for 6 years after graduation; breaching the contract requires refunding money, paying liquidated damages, and being entered into credit records. The difficulty lies in being unable to change locations during these 6 years.
entries.summary: Both of these paths involve the state paying for you in advance, and after graduation, you go to designated locations to work for 6 years according to the agreement. Tuition-free normal students are only recruited at six normal universities directly affiliated with the Ministry of Education, through early batch admission. Targeted medical students must sign a tripartite agreement before receiving the admission letter. Breaching the contract requires refunding money, paying liquidated damages, and entering credit records. Think carefully about whether you can accept these 6 years before filling out your preferences.
entries.benefit: For tuition-free normal students, see Implementation Measures for Undergraduate-Master's Articulated Tuition-Free Education of Normal Students at Normal Universities Directly Affiliated with the Ministry of Education (2024, the 2018 Measures were repealed simultaneously). Article 2: The central treasury shall bear the tuition and accommodation fees of students during their schooling period and provide living allowances. Article 3: Key focus is on training for prefectures (cities, prefectures, leagues) and below, outside provincial capital cities in central and western regions. It also states that "students shall not be targeted to teach in the main urban areas of municipalities directly under the central government, cities under separate state planning, or provincial capital cities (except for the five autonomous regions, land border provinces, Hainan Province, Guizhou Province, and Qinghai Province)." Article 9: After graduation, students generally return to primary and secondary schools in the targeted prefecture (city, prefecture, league) of their province of origin to teach, "promising to engage in primary and secondary school education work for more than 6 years." Those working in urban schools "should teach and serve in rural compulsory education schools for at least 1 year." Article 13: Those who fail to fulfill the agreement or have an insufficient period of fulfillment shall bear liability according to the agreement. One consequence is that "the breach of contract shall be included in credit records and shared in a timely manner with the National Credit Information Sharing Platform, and materials related to the breach of contract shall be included in the individual's personnel dossier." Another sentence states: "Before completing the fulfillment task, they shall not teach outside the targeted prefecture (city, prefecture, league), and shall not be recruited (hired) as other public officials. Relevant credit shall be restored immediately after completing the fulfillment task." Before the service period stipulated in the agreement is fully served, one cannot apply for other public office positions; only when it is fully served will credit records be restored. Article 6: Those who are found unsuitable for teaching after inspection upon admission shall refund the tuition-free education fees already enjoyed within 1 year of enrollment and be transferred to non-normal majors. Article 14: Those who fail to obtain the Master of Education degree certificate, graduation certificate, and teacher qualification certificate within the prescribed years of study shall be handled as breach of contract, refunding fees and paying liquidated damages. Article 21: Localities shall resolve the public establishment quota required for tuition-free normal students to teach in primary and secondary schools within their existing total institutional establishment quota. Article 12 states that prefectures and cities shall organize special recruitments by hiring schools for tuition-free normal students, "effectively securing teaching schools and positions for every graduating tuition-free normal student through two-way selection and other methods." For rural order-based targeted tuition-free medical students, see another notice. After admission and before obtaining the admission letter, they must sign an agreement with the training school and the county-level health and human resources and social security departments of the targeted employment location. In the agreement, they must "promise to serve in targeted rural primary healthcare institutions for 6 years after graduation." Fulfilling the contract means going to the designated location to complete the full term according to the agreement. Regarding the establishment quota, the notice states that provincial health departments "should actively seek the support of local institutional establishment departments, and within the total local establishment quota, properly resolve the employment placement issue of targeted medical graduates in accordance with prescribed procedures." For those reporting to central and western regions, the county shall organize special recruitment to "handle official hiring procedures as formal staff of public institutions." After reporting for employment to fulfill the contract, they must participate in 3 years of standardized residency training in general practice, abbreviated as Guipei. Guipei is the stage after graduation where one continues to hone skills in a hospital according to unified standards. During the training period, the original personnel and wage relations remain unchanged. Records of breach of contract are entered into the individual's personnel dossier and serve as a credibility evaluation basis for open recruitment (hiring) by administrative and public institutions such as medical and healthcare institutions, standardized residency training admission, and postgraduate student admissions. Those who commit malicious breaches of contract will be publicized nationwide through the "Credit China" website and subjected to joint disciplinary actions for dishonesty. The training years of breach of contract do not count toward the service period. For those who fail to refund fees and liquidated damages according to the agreement, the county-level health administrative department shall recover them through legal channels (Nationwide)
entries.sources: General Office of the State Council (2024). Notice on Forwarding the Implementation Measures for Undergraduate-Master's Articulated Tuition-Free Education of Normal Students at Normal Universities Directly Affiliated with the Ministry of Education by the Ministry of Education and Other Departments (Guo Ban Fa [2024] No. 27, Articles 2, 3, 6, 9, 12, 13, 14, 21). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202406/content_6957261.htm>; National Health Commission, State Commission Office of Public Sectors Reform, National Development and Reform Commission, Ministry of Education, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, National Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine (2019). Notice on Accomplishing the Work of Employment Placement and Contract Fulfillment Management for Rural Order-Based Targeted Tuition-Free Medical Students. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2019-11/13/content_5451684.htm>
entries.notes: The 2024 measures changed tuition-free normal students to "undergraduate-master's articulation" (continuing straight into a Master of Education after undergraduate studies). The old 2018 measures have been repealed; the claim still circulating online that "one directly starts teaching upon undergraduate graduation" is obsolete. Those who already signed agreements before the measures were issued follow the original agreements. "Having an establishment quota" does not mean "you don't have to care once you get in": establishments must be freed up from within the existing total quota, and specific positions are specially recruited by hiring schools organized by prefectures and cities, where you and the school select each other mutually. Regarding the establishment quota for targeted medical students, the document only says to strive for it and properly resolve it; practices vary across provinces, so check your province's documents before filling out preferences. If targeted medical students want to leave when their service period expires, that is permitted; the document specifies that "upon expiration of the service period, consent should be given to those choosing employment independently." For those who have already breached the contract, there is also a way to remove the breach record. The price is to serve fully for at least another 6 years under the original agreement, or transferred to other rural primary-level institutions within the province; fees and liquidated damages already paid will not be refunded. Medical students also have to factor in the 3 years of residency training, making the overall cycle longer than for normal students. Each province also has its own tuition-free normal student and targeted medical student programs, with conditions set by the province; check that year's provincial admissions documents before filling out preferences.

entries.title: If you want to go abroad to work, first check whether the company has the business qualification for foreign labor service cooperation: it must not collect a deposit from you
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Spend ten or twenty minutes verifying company qualifications before departure, and then finish reading both contracts.
entries.summary: When it comes to going abroad to work, the law does not regulate you; it regulates the company that organizes you to go out. Only enterprises that have obtained the Foreign Labor Service Cooperation Business Qualification Certificate and completed registration can do this. Hearing "first get a tourist visa to go over and then convert it to a work visa" indicates in itself that the other party is breaking the law. The company also must not collect a deposit from you under any name or require you to provide property as collateral.
entries.benefit: Regulations on the Management of Foreign Labor Service Cooperation, Article 5: Engaging in foreign labor service cooperation shall obtain business qualifications upon approval by the provincial or divided-district municipal commercial administrative department. This business qualification is that Foreign Labor Service Cooperation Business Qualification Certificate; without it, one cannot organize people to go abroad to work. Article 7: The list of business qualification certificates shall be reported to the State Council's commercial administrative department and notified to Chinese embassies and consulates abroad. This article also states that "anyone who has not lawfully obtained a Foreign Labor Service Cooperation Business Qualification Certificate and completed registration shall not engage in foreign labor service cooperation." Article 8: "No unit or individual may organize labor service personnel to work abroad under the names of business, tourism, study abroad, etc." Article 9: An enterprise shall, within 5 working days from the date of registration, deposit a "foreign labor service cooperation risk disposal reserve fund of not less than 3 million RMB yuan" in a designated bank, and the list of deposits shall be publicized to society. Article 10: The reserve fund is used to pay for refundable service fees, labor remuneration, and legally compensated losses that the enterprise refuses to bear or is unable to bear. It is also used for "expenses required for labor personnel to return to the country or receive emergency assistance due to the occurrence of emergencies." Article 11: Labor personnel must not be organized to go abroad to engage in work related to gambling or pornographic activities. Article 12: Those for whom training has not been arranged must not be organized to go abroad. Article 13: Personal accidental injury insurance during the period of working abroad must be purchased for labor personnel. Articles 21 and 23: Written contracts must be signed separately with foreign employers and with labor personnel; those without contracts signed must not be organized to go abroad. Article 25: "Labor personnel shall not be charged a deposit under any name, nor shall labor personnel be required to provide property guarantees." Article 26: File with the commercial administrative department within 10 working days from the date of contract conclusion. Article 29: If the actual rights and interests of labor personnel are inconsistent with the contract, the enterprise shall assist in claiming compensation; if due compensation is not obtained, they have the right to require the enterprise to bear compensation liability. Article 31: If the security situation of the relevant country or region makes it difficult to guarantee personal safety, the enterprise must not organize labor personnel to go there. Article 37: The commercial administrative department establishes an adverse credit record and announcement system. Penalties are in the following articles. Article 39: Those lacking qualifications to engage in foreign labor service cooperation shall be investigated, dealt with, and banned; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be pursued. Article 40: Those organizing departures under the names of business, tourism, or study abroad, lending qualifications, or organizing engagement in gambling or pornography-related work shall have their business qualification certificates revoked. Article 43: Those organizing departures without signing contracts, or by concealing information or providing false information, shall be fined between 100,000 yuan and 200,000 yuan. The primary responsible person shall also be fined between 20,000 yuan and 50,000 yuan (Nationwide)
entries.sources: State Council (2012). Regulations on the Management of Foreign Labor Service Cooperation (State Council Decree No. 620, Articles 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 21, 23, 25, 26, 29, 31, 37, 39, 40, and 43). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2012-06/11/content_1091.htm>
entries.notes: The compliant process is as follows: the company first signs a written labor service cooperation contract with the foreign employer, and then signs a written service contract or labor contract with you. The contract must clearly state the job content, term, remuneration, working hours, rest and vacation, social security, and personal safety risks. Within 10 working days after signing, the company must file it with the commercial administrative department. The company must also arrange for you to receive training on skills, safety precautions, foreign languages, and local laws and customs, and purchase personal accidental injury insurance for you for the period of working overseas. Companies that do not let you read the contract, ask for a deposit, or urge you to leave first and supplement formalities later are the exact kind of companies to avoid. For overseas high-salary recruitment scams and telecom fraud compounds, see Section 21, Item 5; safety alerts to check before departure and 12308 are in Section 21, not repeated here. The regulations do not set educational or age thresholds for people going out to work; the thresholds lie in the company's qualifications, and also in whether the country where the work takes place grants permission. The company can only sign contracts with enterprises or institutions approved by that country, not with foreign individuals. The reserve fund is mobilized by the competent department when the company defaults; you cannot withdraw it yourself. Therefore, if something really happens, you must still first complain to the commercial administrative department; Article 20 gives you this right to complain. When sending more than 100 people to the same country or region, accompanying management personnel must be arranged and reported to embassies and consulates for filing. Projects with fewer people lack this layer of protection, making it all the more important to retain contracts and bank transfer records yourself.

entries.title: Working remotely from home for an overseas company counts as domestic income under tax law: file IIT yourself, and receive remittances under "employee remuneration"
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Conduct the annual final settlement once a year, from March 1 to June 30 of the following year. When foreign exchange settlement exceeds the annual total quota, you also need to prepare an employment contract and proof of income. The difficulty is that you must remember to declare this tax yourself.
entries.summary: Whether this money counts as domestic or overseas depends on where you perform the work, not where the money is transferred from. Working remotely for an overseas company while in China counts as domestic income, and individual income tax must be paid domestically. If the overseas company has no establishment in China, no one will withhold it on your behalf; you must declare this tax yourself. Remitting the money in takes the "employee remuneration" route.
entries.benefit: Whether this money counts as domestic income depends on Article 3 of the Regulations for the Implementation of the Individual Income Tax Law (State Council Decree No. 707, effective January 1, 2019). It states: "Unless otherwise prescribed by the finance and tax competent departments of the State Council, the following income, regardless of whether the place of payment is within the territory of China, shall be income derived from within the territory of China: (1) Income obtained from providing labor services within the territory of China due to holding office, employment, performance of agreements, etc." Article 6 of the same regulations defines two tax categories. One is wages and salaries: "Income from wages and salaries refers to wages, salaries, bonuses, year-end salary increases, labor dividends, allowances, subsidies, and other income related to holding office or employment obtained by an individual due to holding office or employment." The other is remuneration for personal services: "Income from remuneration for personal services refers to income obtained by an individual engaged in labor services, including income obtained from engaging in design, decoration, installation, drafting, testing, examination, medical care, law, accounting, consulting, lecturing, translation, proofreading, calligraphy and painting, carving, film and television, sound recording, video recording, shows, performances, advertising, exhibitions, technical services, referral services, brokerage services, agency services, and other labor services." Article 6 of the Individual Income Tax Law specifies how to calculate taxable income: "The taxable income amount of a resident individual's comprehensive income shall be the balance of the income amount in each tax year after deducting expenses of 60,000 yuan as well as special deductions, special additional deductions, and other deductions determined in accordance with the law." The same article also states that "the income amount for remuneration for personal services, author's remuneration, and royalties shall be the balance after deducting 20% of expenses from the income." The deduction of 20% only lists these three categories; wages and salaries are not included. Therefore, wages and salaries are calculated into the income amount at full value, and the taxes calculated for the two tax categories differ. Article 9: "Individual income tax takes the person who obtained the income as the taxpayer and the unit or individual paying the income as the withholding agent." Article 10: "Under any of the following circumstances, a taxpayer shall handle tax declarations in accordance with the law: ... (2) Obtaining taxable income without a withholding agent; ... (4) Obtaining overseas income." Article 11: "Resident individuals obtaining comprehensive income shall calculate individual income tax on an annual basis... Where final settlement is required, it shall be handled between March 1 and June 30 of the year following the year in which the income was obtained." For receiving remittances, see the Measures for the Administration of Individual Foreign Exchange (People's Bank of China Decree [2006] No. 3, effective February 1, 2007). Article 9: "Annual total quota management is implemented for individual foreign exchange settlement and domestic individual foreign exchange purchases. Within the annual total quota, it shall be handled at banks on the strength of the individual's valid identity documents; for amounts exceeding the annual total quota, under current account items, it shall be handled at banks on the strength of the individual's valid identity documents and certifying materials showing the transaction amount, etc." Article 7: "Banks and individuals handling individual foreign exchange business shall comply with the relevant provisions of these Measures, and must not evade limit supervision through splitting or other methods, nor use false commercial documents or vouchers to evade authenticity management." Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the Measures for the Administration of Individual Foreign Exchange (Hui Fa [2007] No. 1), Article 2: "Annual total quota management is implemented for individual foreign exchange settlement and domestic individual foreign exchange purchases. The annual total quotas are respectively the equivalent of 50,000 US dollars per person per year." Article 10: "Where non-business foreign exchange settlement under current account items of domestic individuals exceeds the annual total quota, it shall be handled at banks on the strength of the individual's valid identity documents and the following certifying materials: ... (7) Employee remuneration: employment contract and income certificate" (Nationwide)
entries.sources: State Council (2018). Regulations for the Implementation of the Individual Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China (State Council Decree No. 707, Articles 3 and 6). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2018-12/22/content_5351177.htm>; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). Individual Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China (Seventh Amendment in 2018, Articles 6, 9, 10, and 11). <http://www.npc.gov.cn/zgrdw/npc/xinwen/2018-09/05/content_2060671.htm>; State Taxation Administration Policy and Regulation Database. Individual Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China (Article 6). <https://fgk.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfgk/c100009/c5193028/content.html>; People's Bank of China (2006). Measures for the Administration of Individual Foreign Exchange (People's Bank of China Decree [2006] No. 3, Articles 7 and 9). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_786257.htm>; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (2007). Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the Measures for the Administration of Individual Foreign Exchange (Hui Fa [2007] No. 1, Articles 2 and 10). <https://www.safe.gov.cn/safe/2007/0105/22509.html>
entries.notes: Which tax category applies depends on the relationship between you and the other party. If you signed an employment contract and your work is directed and arranged by the other party, it counts as wages and salaries. If you take on work independently on a project basis and deliver deliverables, it counts as remuneration for personal labor services. The taxes calculated under these two categories differ, so clarify which category you fall under before filing. When funds are remitted inward, for amounts within the equivalent of USD 50,000 per year, foreign exchange settlement can be handled directly at the bank using your Resident Identity Card; for the portion exceeding this amount, you must submit your employment contract and proof of income to the bank. Do not use multiple individuals to split transactions to bypass the quota. The above applies to scenarios where an individual remains in Mainland China without traveling abroad. Actually traveling abroad to work for an overseas employer is an entirely different matter; see Section 31, Item 14 (If planning to work abroad, first verify whether the company holds qualification for foreign labor cooperation operations). The following four matters are temporarily omitted from this book. All four may involve actual costs, but at present no verifiable word-for-word legal bases can be identified: First, whether value-added tax (VAT) must be paid on this income and whether invoices need to be issued on your behalf (daikai fapiao). Second, whether engaging in this long-term requires obtaining a business license or registering as an individually owned business (getihu). Third, whether you can assert rights against an overseas employer under the Labor Law, such as annual leave, overtime pay, and severance compensation upon termination. Fourth, cross-border data transfer and confidentiality.

entries.title: Starting on Your Own Without Joining an Employer? Check Entrepreneurship Guaranteed Loans for Initial Capital: Up to CNY 300,000 for Individuals, with Fiscal Subsidies Covering Half the Interest
entries.cost: Consultations are free. First, make one trip to the human resources and social security department for eligibility verification, and then complete procedures once each at the guarantee institution and the handling bank (the lending bank). The difficulty lies in the fact that borrowed money must ultimately be repaid.
entries.summary: If you belong to key priority groups such as college graduates, retired military personnel, or registered unemployed persons, check this fiscally subsidized loan first when borrowing start-up funds. Individuals can borrow up to CNY 300,000 for a maximum term of 3 years, with the government treasury paying half of the interest on your behalf. When applying, neither you nor your spouse may have any other loans under your names, excluding mortgages, auto loans, student loans, and consumer loans under CNY 50,000.
entries.benefit: The eligibility criteria for individual applicants are stipulated in Article 6 of the Administrative Measures for Special Funds for Inclusive Financial Development (Caijin [2023] No. 75). The first condition is belonging to key employment groups. The document lists registered unemployed persons in urban areas, persons with employment difficulties (including persons with disabilities), retired military personnel, and released prisoners upon completion of sentence. It also includes college graduates (including university student village officials and overseas returnee students), as well as employees and unemployed workers affected by capacity-reduction enterprises. It further includes returning migrant workers starting businesses, online merchants, individuals lifted out of poverty, and rural self-employed farmers, among others. The second condition is having no other outstanding loans under your name: 'Except for student loans, micro-credit for populations lifted out of poverty, housing loans, automobile purchase loans, and small consumer loans under CNY 50,000 (including credit card spending), the applicant and their spouse must have no other loans at the time of submitting the entrepreneurship guaranteed loan application.' Article 9: 'For qualifying entrepreneurship guaranteed loans, the finance department will grant a fiscal interest discount of 50% of the loan's actual interest rate. In principle, the finance department will not grant interest discounts on entrepreneurship guaranteed loans that are extended or overdue.' An interest discount means the government treasury pays half of the interest on your behalf. An extension refers to extending the term upon maturity, and overdue means failing to repay after the due date; the government treasury will no longer pay for you in either case. Article 10: In principle, counter-guarantees are eliminated for entrepreneurship guaranteed loans applied for by individuals under CNY 100,000, eliminating the need to find an additional third-party guarantor or pledge property to the guarantee agency. Article 11: For individual entrepreneurship guaranteed loans included in the scope of incentive and subsidy support, 'the quota shall not exceed CNY 300,000, and the loan term shall not exceed 3 years.' For partnership entrepreneurship, this may be appropriately increased, up to a maximum not exceeding 110% of the sum of the individual quota caps. The interest rate caps for loans supported by incentives and subsidies are divided into three tiers: LPR+50 bps in the eastern region, LPR+150 bps in the central and western regions, and LPR+250 bps in regions lifted out of poverty. LPR is the Loan Prime Rate of the banking market, and bps is the unit of measurement for interest rates; the more is added, the higher the interest. Those with 'active repayment, strong capacity to drive employment, and good entrepreneurial projects' may continue to apply upon loan maturity, with cumulative applications not exceeding 3 times. Article 8: Applicants first submit an eligibility verification application to the local human resources and social security department, and then submit applications to the guarantee institution and the handling bank. Article 12: Subject to approval by provincial people's governments, localities may expand the scope of support, raise quotas, and increase interest discount ratios (Nationwide)
entries.sources: Ministry of Finance (2023). Notice on Issuing the Administrative Measures for Special Funds for Inclusive Financial Development (Caijin [2023] No. 75, Articles 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, and 12). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202309/content_6903691.htm>
entries.notes: The government treasury paying half of the interest does not change the fact that 'borrowed money must be repaid.' This book's stance in Section 12, Item 1 remains unchanged: when starting a business, only risk money you can afford to lose, do not deplete family reserves, do not sign personal guarantees for corporate loans, and spouses should never co-sign. If you have already decided to borrow, this type of policy loan sits in the lowest interest rate bracket; stay away from consumer loans and private lending. Quotas and eligibility scopes can be adjusted upward by each province; the actual approved amount is subject to the official word of the local human resources and social security department for that current year. The 2020 notice issued during the pandemic regarding 'up to CNY 200,000 for individuals' was a temporary document; rely on the current measures now. For choosing between registering as an individually owned business (getihu) or establishing a company, permits, tax filing, and exiting a business, see Section 12. For training subsidies, social insurance subsidies, and job internships during periods of unemployment, see Section 7, Item 13 (Vocational training subsidies).

entries.title: Still Planning to Take the Civil Service Exam Within Two Years of Graduation? Check How the Exam Announcement Defines 'Recent Graduates' Before Signing a Job Contract or Transferring Your Dossier: The National Exam Requires Your Dossier and Hukou to Remain at School or a Talent Service Agency
entries.cost: Free. Spend half an hour before signing with an employer to locate and read through the announcements for the specific examinations you intend to take. The difficulty is that standards vary across regions and must be checked on an exam-by-exam basis.
entries.summary: Many positions in the National Civil Service Examination primarily recruit recent graduates. Those who have not secured an employment unit within two years of graduation and whose personnel dossiers and household registration (hukou) remain at their school or a talent service agency are also counted as recent graduates. Provincial regulations differ; in Fujian, having signed a contract and paid social insurance still counts. Therefore, check the announcement for your targeted exam before signing a job contract or transferring your dossier.
entries.benefit: The 2027 National Civil Service Examination recruitment announcement states that for central authorities, 'direct subordinate agencies at and below the municipal (prefectural) level primarily recruit recent college graduates.' Question 3 of the exam application guide for the same year specifically addresses whether previous graduates count as recent graduates. The original text reads: 'Graduates of regular higher education institutions recruited under the unified national admission plan who have not secured an employment unit upon leaving school or during the career selection period (stipulated by the state as two years), and whose household registration (hukou), personnel dossier, and Party/Youth League organizational relationship are still retained at their graduating school, or at graduate employment administrative departments (graduate employment guidance service centers) at various levels, talent exchange service agencies at various levels, or public employment service agencies at various levels, may be treated as recent college graduates.' The career selection period refers to those two years after graduation spent looking for work. Therefore, the National Civil Service Examination requires satisfying two conditions simultaneously: having not secured an employment unit during the two years, and not having your dossier, hukou, and organizational relationship transferred to an employer. Provincial exams are determined by each province independently. A 2023 notice from Fujian states: 'Signing employment agreements, labor contracts, paying social insurance, etc., by recent graduates in the current year shall not affect their recognition as recent graduates; graduates from the previous year with work experience and social insurance payment records may apply for recent graduate positions.' This provision governs Fujian's civil service, public institutions (shiye danwei), state-owned enterprises (SOEs), and central SOE branches located in Fujian. A 2025 notice from Chongqing treats the two categories of exams separately. For the Chongqing civil service exam, it repeats the exact phrasing from the National Exam quoted above. For Chongqing public institutions and SOEs, as long as the applicant has not been recruited into an established budgeted position (bianzhi) within two years, 'the signing of employment contracts (agreements), work experience, social insurance contributions, etc., shall not affect their eligibility to apply' (Nationwide, separate provincial rules apply)
entries.sources: National Civil Service Bureau (2026). Announcement for the Examination and Recruitment of Civil Servants by Central Authorities and Their Directly Subordinate Agencies for the 2027 Year, and the Application Guide for the Same Year (Questions 3, 11, 21, and 48), reposted on the Tongren Municipal People's Government Website. <https://www.trs.gov.cn/xwzx/tzgg/zkxx/202610/t20261013_90984626.html>; National Civil Service Bureau (2025). Application Guide for the Examination and Recruitment of Civil Servants by Central Authorities and Their Directly Subordinate Agencies for the 2026 Year (Question 3 containing identical text), reposted on the Beijing Municipal People's Government Website. <https://www.beijing.gov.cn/fuwu/bmfw/sy/jrts/202510/t20251014_4222424.html>; Organization Department of the CPC Fujian Provincial Committee and Three Other Departments (2023). Notice on Policies Related to the Employment of Recent College Graduates (Min Ren She Wen [2023] No. 84, Article 1). <https://rst.fujian.gov.cn/zw/zfxxgk/zfxxgkml/zyywgz/zynljs/202307/t20230706_6201113.htm>; Organization Department of the CPC Chongqing Municipal Committee and Three Other Departments (2025). Notice on Matters Related to the Employment of College Graduates (Trial) (Yu Ren She Gui [2025] No. 5, Articles 1, 2, and 3). <https://rlsbj.cq.gov.cn/zwgk_182/zfxxgkml/zcwj_145360/jfxzgfxwj/202504/t20250418_14533212.html>; Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee (2019). Regulations on Civil Service Employment (Article 4). <https://www.12371.cn/2020/01/08/ARTI1578447606460158.shtml> (Published on Dangjian Web / Communist Party Member Network)
entries.notes: The National Civil Service Exam guide does not explicitly state whether signing a labor contract and paying social insurance counts as 'having secured an employment unit.' When in doubt, call the inquiry telephone number of the recruiting agency listed in the recruitment prospectus; Question 21 of the guide instructs applicants to contact the recruiting agency directly. It is commonly said online that 'once social insurance has been paid, you are no longer considered a recent graduate'—this is the administrative interpretation for certain exams, not a unified national rule. The two documents cited above for Fujian and Chongqing are merely illustrative examples; provincial policies may change each year, so defer to the announcement for the year you intend to take the exam. Those participating in grassroots service programs such as 'Three Supports and One Help' (San Zhi Yi Fu) can also apply for recent graduate positions within two years of completing their term of service; see Section 31, Item 7 (Grassroots service programs). The same application guide also explicitly clarifies that this exam does not designate study preparation books, nor does it conduct or commission any institution or individual to conduct exam preparation classes. Article 4 of the Regulations on Civil Service Employment explicitly states that civil service recruitment adopts the method of 'open examinations, strict evaluation, equal competition, and selection based on merit.' Therefore, if anyone demands money and promises 'internal quotas' or 'guaranteed bianzhi placement,' treat it as a scam and report it to the police; see Section 8, Item 3 (Hard rules against fraud). The policy interpretation for the National Civil Service Exam is written based on the 2027 announcement current as of October 2026; for future years, consult that year's announcement as well.

chapters.title: Studying Abroad: Visa Status, Working Part-Time, Insurance, and Domestic Credential Authentication
chapters.intro:
This chapter calculates the balance sheet of finances and personal liberty; it does not discuss whether one should study abroad, nor does it compare the merits of different schools. Failing to understand the following four matters will result in suffering losses: how to keep visa status unbroken, where the upper limits on work hours lie, which insurance policies and fees are mandatory, and whether the degree will be recognized after returning to China.

Covering four countries—the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Australia—with figures listed country by country. Sources are drawn from official web pages of immigration authorities of each respective country and the Ministry of Education of China. **Study abroad policies across countries change frequently, even more frequently than Chinese regulations. The cutoff date for all figures in this chapter is September 2026. Before departing and before each visa renewal, check every link in the sources column yourself.**

For how to contact embassies and consulates if something goes wrong abroad, what the 12308 consular hotline covers, and how to purchase overseas medical and evacuation/repatriation insurance, see Section 21. For the cost-benefit trade-off between studying and working, see Section 23. For account theft, see Section 14; for telecommunications fraud, see Section 8. None of these will be repeated here.

entries.title: Before Paying Tuition, First Check Whether the Institution Is on CSCSE's Recognized Institutions List
entries.cost: Free. Enter the institution's name once into CSCSE's 'Recognized Institutions Query' tool; the check takes just a few minutes
entries.summary: If you need to use this academic credential for further education, employment, or examinations upon returning to China, you can apply for credential authentication with the Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (CSCSE) of the Ministry of Education. It publishes a list of institutions whose credentials have passed authentication over the past five years. Being on the list does not guarantee approval, and not being on the list does not necessarily mean an application will not be accepted. Check once before paying tuition; if an institution is not on the list, inquire further.
entries.benefit: Article 1 of the Administrative Measures for the Authentication of Foreign and Overseas Academic Credentials and Degrees issued by the Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (CSCSE) of the Ministry of Education explicitly states that authentication is conducted to 'meet the needs of applicants for further education, employment, examinations, etc.' Article 2 explicitly states that authentication is performed 'based on the applicant's voluntary application.' CSCSE provides a query portal for recognized institutions where searches are conducted by institution name. Its User Notice explicitly states that the list comprises foreign credential-granting institutions involved in applications that have passed authentication within the past five years, which is 'solely for the reference of study-abroad personnel and does not serve as any guarantee or basis for passing authentication.' The notice also clarifies that the scope of acceptance 'is not limited to the institutions displayed in this query function,' that each application is evaluated on an individual basis, and that whether an institution is lawful and holds degree-granting qualification is only one of the considerations. The list is updated once per year. In the 2025 update, 270 institutions that had not produced an authentication certificate within the past 5 years were removed. In addition, the Jiaoyu Shewai Jianguan Xinxiwang (Information Platform for Foreign Regulatory Education of the Ministry of Education) publishes supervisory and regulatory information on Sino-foreign cooperative education and overseas education operations
entries.sources: Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (CSCSE) of the Ministry of Education. Query of Recognized Institutions (including User Notice). <http://yxcx.cscse.edu.cn/>; Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (CSCSE) of the Ministry of Education (2023). Administrative Measures for the Authentication of Foreign and Overseas Academic Credentials and Degrees (Articles 1 and 2). <http://zwfw.cscse.edu.cn/zwfw/lxfwzxwsfwdt2020/xlxwrz32/409891/rzbf/2026042823373762003/index.html>; Information Platform for Foreign Regulatory Education of the Ministry of Education (Jiaoyu Shewai Jianguan Xinxiwang). <https://jsj.moe.gov.cn/>
entries.notes: Verbal claims by agencies that an institution is 'recognized by the Ministry of Education' do not count; rely strictly on the results you find online yourself. The list is subject to change; an institution on the list at the time of matriculation may not necessarily still be on it upon graduation, so recheck once every year during your studies. Sino-foreign cooperative education programs operate under a separate accreditation and registration system. Students admitted after 2008 can verify their registration serial numbers on the Information Platform for Foreign Regulatory Education using their name and Resident Identity Card number.

entries.title: Keep an Eye on the US F-1 Rule Lawsuit: 'Maximum Four Years, Depart Within 30 Days After Completion' Was Scheduled to Take Effect on September 15, 2026, but Was Stayed by a Court the Day Before; Currently Still 'Duration of Status'
entries.cost: Free. Copy the program end date from your Form I-20 into your calendar, setting an advance reminder 90 days prior. The Form I-20 is the certificate of eligibility for nonimmigrant student status issued by your school. Additionally, check notices from your school's International Student Office once each semester to see if there are new developments in this litigation
entries.summary: The United States originally planned to change the F-1 visa admission to a maximum of four years with a requirement to depart within 30 days of completion. One day before it took effect, a federal court stayed it. Therefore, the old rule remains in effect for now: admission lasts as long as your studies do (Duration of Status), with a 60-day grace period to depart after completion. A stay is not a vacatur; the government can appeal, and rules may change again at any time.
entries.benefit: On July 17, 2026, the Department of Homeland Security published a rule scheduled to take effect on September 15, 2026. Under this rule, F-1 students would no longer be admitted for 'Duration of Status' (D/S), but for a fixed time period of up to four years, requiring a separate application for an extension of stay upon expiration. After completion of studies or practical training, only 30 days would be granted to prepare for departure. On September 14, 2026, Judge Saylor of the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts postponed the effective date of this rule pursuant to Section 705 of the Administrative Procedure Act. The stay applies nationwide and covers the entire rule. The court did not vacate the rule; the motion for vacatur was denied without prejudice to renewal. The case continues to be heard. Pursuant to this court order, individuals on F, J, and I visas continue to be admitted under 'Duration of Status' (D/S), the 60-day departure grace period remains intact, and no separate extension of stay application is required
entries.sources: DHS (2026). Establishing a Fixed Time Period of Admission and an Extension of Stay Procedure for Nonimmigrant Academic Students, Exchange Visitors (Published 2026-07-17, originally scheduled to take effect 2026-09-15). <https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/17/2026-14439/establishing-a-fixed-time-period-of-admission-and-an-extension-of-stay-procedure-for-nonimmigrant>; Presidents' Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration v. U.S. Department of Homeland Security, No. 1:26-cv-13799-FDS (D. Mass. Sept. 14, 2026), court docket. <https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/74661796/presidents-alliance-on-higher-education-and-immigration-v-united-states/>; Yale Office of International Students & Scholars (2026-09-14). Important Update: Court Action on the D/S Rule. <https://oiss.yale.edu/news/important-update-court-action-on-the-ds-rule>; AILA (2026). One Day Before Taking Effect, Federal Court Postpones the F, J, and I Fixed Admission Period Rule. <https://www.aila.org/blog/think-immigration-one-day-before-taking-effect-federal-court-postpones-the-f-j-and-i-fixed-admission-period-rule>; 8 CFR 214.2(f). <https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-8/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-214/section-214.2>
entries.notes: This entry is current as of September 25, 2026. The government can appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit, and the Department of Homeland Security can also reissue the rule after revisions. Therefore, those planning to study for multiple years should not assume the old rule will remain permanent. The court scheduled a status conference for October 2, 2026, to hear progress updates from both parties; check your school's notices again after that date. If the new rule takes effect in the future, extensions will require a separate application before the authorized period expires and will not renew automatically. Under the old rule, for those who discontinue their studies early, the departure timeline is different from those who complete their studies; consult your school's International Student Office first. The J visa is included in the same rule, but its details differ from the F-1; check according to your specific visa classification.

entries.title: Working While Studying Abroad: Check the Maximum Work Hour Limits for the US, Canada, UK, and Australia First; Terms, Vacations, and Job Types Must Be Counted Separately
entries.cost: Free. Track your working hours yourself on a weekly basis. The challenge is that employers may claim 'no one checks if you work a few extra hours'—never trust this statement
entries.summary: Working hours must be verified by country, job type, and academic term. In the US, on-campus employment is limited to a maximum of 20 hours per week during the term; in the UK, eligible degree courses allow 20 or 10 hours per week. In Canada, off-campus work during term time is capped at 24 hours per week; in Australia, it is capped at 48 hours per fortnight while courses are in session. Vacations, internships, and cross-border remote work are governed by separate rules and cannot be treated under a single uniform cap.
entries.benefit: For F-1 students in the United States, on-campus employment must not exceed 20 hours per week during the school term. Off-campus part-time work approved under regulatory item (f)(9) is likewise limited to a maximum of 20 hours per week during the school term. Eligible vacation periods allow full-time work. Curricular Practical Training (CPT) and other practical training are implemented separately according to their specific training category and authorized scope; the aforementioned caps cannot be applied blanketly to all off-campus work. For UK student visas, working hours also depend on whether the institution and course comply with regulations. Those sponsored by a higher education institution with a track record of compliance studying full-time at degree level or above may work 20 hours per week during term time. For courses below degree level sponsored by such institutions, the limit is 10 hours per week. Eligible short-term exchange programmes at overseas higher education institutions also permit 20 hours per week during term time. Other courses, including part-time courses, do not permit work. Self-employment (working for oneself) is generally prohibited, as is working as a professional sportsperson or entertainer. The basis for this is the student section of the UK Immigration Rules, Appendix Student ST26.1, ST26.5, and ST26.8. In Canada, eligible students may work off campus for up to 24 hours per week during regular academic terms, with the hours from multiple off-campus jobs calculated cumulatively. The basis is Section 186(v) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR). During scheduled regular breaks by the school, full-time work is permitted if eligible. Working remotely for an employer located outside Canada does not count toward this 24-hour cap, though one must still comply with study permit conditions. For eligibility during the final academic term and transition periods between programmes, see Section 4 (Full-time Status, Leaves of Absence, and Transfers). On an Australian student visa, working hours are limited to a maximum of 48 hours per fortnight while the course is in session. Masters by research students, doctoral students, and their family members are not subject to this restriction.
entries.sources: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(9)、(10). <https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-8/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-214/section-214.2>；UK Home Office. Immigration Rules Appendix Student（ST26.1、ST26.5、ST26.8）. <https://www.gov.uk/guidance/immigration-rules/immigration-rules-appendix-student>；IRCC. Work off campus as an international student. <https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/work-off-campus.html>；IRCC. Can I continue to work during scheduled school breaks? <https://www.ircc.canada.ca/english/helpcentre/answer.asp?qnum=499>；Australian Government Department of Home Affairs. Student visa (subclass 500). <https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing/student-500>
entries.notes: The employment conditions in this entry were reviewed on October 21, 2026. Off-campus work in the US requires obtaining the corresponding authorization in advance according to the category. For those requiring an application to USCIS for authorization, work cannot commence while Form I-765 is still pending review. Curricular Practical Training (CPT), on the other hand, is authorized by the school's designated school official and endorsed on Form I-20; not all off-campus work requires submitting Form I-765. In Canada, older permits may state 20 hours per week, but as long as conditions are met, one may actually work up to 24 hours, governed by current regulations. A regular break refers to a scheduled break arranged by the school, not taking a break from classes on one's own initiative. In the UK, the scope of restrictions on self-employment includes taking freelance gigs, running an online store, and freelance work. Specific exceptions during visa switching periods should be verified against official UK rules.

entries.title: Before reducing study load to part-time, taking a leave of absence, withdrawing, or transferring, verify work eligibility and exceptions first
entries.cost: Free. Before suspending classes, taking a leave of absence, or switching schools, consult your school's international student office first to clarify your immigration status.
entries.summary: Whether you can work while studying abroad must be checked against the country you are in and your academic enrollment status. In Canada, during an approved leave of absence or when transferring schools without actively studying, you cannot work off campus under your study permit. However, if taking a reduced course load in your final term, or during the gap bridging a completed programme to a new one, you can still work if eligible. An unexpired visa does not replace verifying eligibility.
entries.benefit: When working under the authorization attached to a Canadian study permit, you may not work off campus during an approved leave of absence. You may also not work off campus during a school transfer if you are not actively studying, and must wait until resuming studies. However, there is an exception for the final academic term: if enrolled part-time solely because a full course load is not required to complete the programme, and you maintained full-time status previously, you may still work off campus. All other work conditions must also be fully met.
