During the gap period between completing a previous programme and starting a new one, there is another set of conditions permitting full-time work, which must all be satisfied simultaneously: you were already eligible for off-campus work during your previous studies; you hold a valid study permit or applied for an extension before it expired; you have received written confirmation of programme completion from your original institution, as well as an acceptance letter for a new full-time programme at a Designated Learning Institution (abbreviated as DLI); and the new programme must start within 150 calendar days of receiving the confirmation of completion for the old programme. This differs from suspending studies to transfer before graduating; you cannot start working solely on the basis of \"having a new offer of admission.\" In the United States, on-campus work eligibility requires an F-1 student to have an \"Active\" status in SEVIS. SEVIS is the US student status record system, where \"Active\" indicates valid enrollment. Students must also maintain the academic course load required to maintain status; before reducing your course load, have the school verify whether you qualify for an exception. In the UK, work authorization is granted according to the institution and course type; part-time courses do not permit work.
entries.sources: IRCC. Work off campus as an international student. <https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/work-off-campus.html>；U.S. Department of Homeland Security, Study in the States. Working in the United States. <https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/students/work/working-in-the-united-states>；U.S. ICE SEVP, SEVIS Help Hub. Terminate a Student. <https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/sevis-help-hub/student-records/completions-and-terminations/terminate-a-student>；UK Home Office. Immigration Rules Appendix Student（ST26.1）. <https://www.gov.uk/guidance/immigration-rules/immigration-rules-appendix-student>
entries.notes: If academic pressure is heavy and you want to reduce your course load, ask clearly first: at what point does it no longer count as full-time? Troubles arise on this point even earlier than with working. In the United States, if a school terminates a SEVIS record due to a status violation, there is no grace period: you must either apply for reinstatement of status or depart the country immediately. Those with an approved authorized early withdrawal have a 15-day departure grace period. Rules in the other three countries differ; consult the respective country's immigration department website. Do not wait until the school sends a formal letter before taking action.

entries.title: United States: New address must be reported within 10 days of moving
entries.cost: Free. Submitting an address change online takes ten minutes.
entries.summary: If you change residences in the United States, the law requires notifying immigration authorities within 10 days. Failing to report is not a minor matter. First, it is illegal in itself; second, you may miss mail sent to you by the immigration agency.
entries.benefit: US federal immigration regulations under 8 CFR 265.1 mandate that aliens required to be registered by law must report any change of address within 10 days of such change. It must be reported to USCIS (U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services) through its prescribed procedures, reporting both the fact that the address changed and the new address.
entries.sources: 8 CFR 265.1. <https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-8/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-265/section-265.1>；USCIS. AR-11, Alien's Change of Address Card. <https://www.uscis.gov/ar-11>；UK Government. Report a change of circumstances if you have a visa or expired BRP. <https://www.gov.uk/change-circumstances-visa-brp>；Australian Government Department of Home Affairs. See your visa conditions（Student visa subclass 500）. <https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/already-have-a-visa/check-visa-details-and-conditions/see-your-visa-conditions?product=500>
entries.notes: After reporting to USCIS, your SEVIS record at the school (your international student status file) must be updated separately. In the UK, holders of a visa or biometric residence permit must report changes in circumstances, and changes of address are updated in one's UKVI account. Australian student visas carry Condition 8533, titled \"Notify provider of address.\" No identical regulation was found for Canada in this review. Timeframes and methods vary by country; follow the instructions on the immigration department webpage of the country where you reside.

entries.title: Before departure and during studies, check the Ministry of Education's study abroad safety alerts
entries.cost: Free. Check once before departure, and once each term thereafter.
entries.summary: The Ministry of Education issues specific alerts for certain countries or regions where public safety or policy conditions have recently turned unfavorable for Chinese international students. These are publicly released official risk advisories, accessible in black and white, and far more reliable than claims made by education agents. Checking costs nothing.
entries.benefit: The Ministry of Education publishes study abroad alerts through the Jiaoyu Shewai Jianguan Xinxi Wang (Information Platform for Foreign-Related Education Supervision). In 2025, a total of 4 alerts were issued. Alert No. 1 cautioned that higher education bills passed by relevant US states contained negative provisions concerning China (2025-04-09). Alerts No. 2 and No. 3 advised twice on the frequent occurrence of cases targeting Chinese citizens in the Philippines and an unfavorable study-abroad environment (2025-07-18, 2025-08-30). Alert No. 4 warned of unfavorable public security conditions and an unfavorable study-abroad environment in Japan, advising cautious planning for studying in Japan (2025-11-16).
entries.sources: Ministry of Education Foreign-Related Education Supervision Information Platform. Early Warning Information. <https://jsj.moe.gov.cn/>; Ministry of Education Issues Study Abroad Alert No. 4 of 2025. <https://jsj.moe.gov.cn/n2/2/2/2060.shtml>; No. 1. <https://jsj.moe.gov.cn/n2/2/2/2001.shtml>
entries.notes: An alert is not a ban, nor does it mean you cannot go; it provides an official basis for weighing local risks. Alert lists change with circumstances and will not be maintained with ongoing updates in this section; refer to the current webpage of the site. For personal safety abroad and consular protection, see Section 21.

entries.title: Australia: OSHC must cover the entire stay without gaps; failure to present insurance upon landing may result in refusal of entry
entries.cost: Several thousand to over ten thousand Chinese yuan. Purchased as a lump sum based on visa length, covering as many years as you will study.
entries.summary: Australia makes Overseas Student Health Cover a visa condition, not an optional purchase. Insurance must cover the entire period of stay. When renewing a visa or switching policies, there must be no gap in between. If you cannot provide proof of insurance upon entry, you may be refused entry on the spot. Family members accompanying the student must also hold this insurance.
entries.benefit: The Australian Department of Home Affairs requires student visa applicants and their dependants to purchase Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC), which must be maintained continuously for the entire duration of their stay in Australia without gaps. Insurance must be provided by an approved Australian health insurance provider, unless qualifying for an exemption from purchase. There must be no gap between a new insurance policy and insurance from a previous visa. Failure to show proof of maintained insurance upon entry may result in refusal of entry. For those entering Australia earlier than their course start date, the insurance start date must be listed as the actual day of arrival in Australia.
entries.sources: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs. Student visa (subclass 500). <https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing/student-500>
entries.notes: If arranged through the school, verify the insurance company's name, policy start and end dates, and policy number, as these must be filled in on the visa application. Purchasing too short a duration will cause issues during visa extension; it is preferable to buy coverage lasting past graduation with some extra buffer.

entries.title: United Kingdom: Alongside the visa fee is an annual Immigration Health Surcharge of £776 per year for students, payable in full at the time of application
entries.cost: Visa fee £558. Immigration Health Surcharge £776 per year. Both are paid in full as a lump sum at application.
entries.summary: The money you must pay to go to the UK is not limited to the visa fee. You must also prepay the Immigration Health Surcharge based on the number of visa years, which grants access to the UK's National Health Service. A two-year visa means paying £1,552 all at once. Combined with the visa fee, this sum must be paid in full prior to departure, so do not leave it out of your budget.
entries.benefit: The UK student visa fee is £558. Applying from outside the UK, extending in-country, or switching all incur this same amount. Additionally, there is the Immigration Health Surcharge, which must be paid to access the UK's National Health Service, prepaid at the time of application according to the number of visa years. For the student and their dependants, it is £776 per year, meaning a 2-year visa costs £1,552. For other application categories, it is £1,035 per year. Visas lasting more than 6 months but less than 1 year are charged at the full annual rate.
entries.sources: UK Government. Student visa. <https://www.gov.uk/student-visa>；UK Government. Pay for UK healthcare as part of your immigration application. <https://www.gov.uk/healthcare-immigration-application>
entries.notes: Fee amounts and exchange rates fluctuate; calculate using the current figures on the two pages cited in the sources. Those studying degree-level courses who are 18 or older can generally stay for a maximum of 5 years; below degree level, it is 2 years. Estimate the required surcharge based on this duration.

entries.title: Allow time for verification before returning to China: CSCSE credential evaluation takes 10 to 20 working days
entries.cost: Online application, online payment. Preparing materials plus review, calculated in working days, takes around one month in total.
entries.summary: To use foreign academic qualifications in China, you must first complete academic credential evaluation. The review alone takes 10 to 20 working days, not counting the time required to prepare documentation. Autumn campus recruitment, civil service exam registrations, and hukou household registration all have hard deadlines; do not wait until you urgently need it to start the process.
entries.benefit: Evaluation of overseas academic credentials and degrees is handled via the online service portal of the Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (CSCSE), Ministry of Education. The process consists of four steps: register and complete real-name verification, submit application and materials online, pay fees online, and wait for evaluation and review. The published processing timeframe for evaluation is 10 to 20 working days. Working days exclude weekends and statutory holidays; this period covers the time used by CSCSE for evaluation.
entries.sources: Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (Ministry of Education). Online Service Hall · Academic Credential and Degree Evaluation. <http://zwfw.cscse.edu.cn/>
entries.notes: The required materials include: diploma/degree certificate, passport or travel permit, residence permit or visa endorsement, passport-style photo, and letter of authorization. Border entry and exit records during your overseas study period are retrieved directly by the system, so do not misplace the visa pages from your time abroad. CSCSE's website also publishes announcements stating which verification certificates have been revoked and which schools have had evaluation applications suspended. Check prior to applying whether your school is affected.

entries.title: Search your school name in CSCSE announcements before applying: institutions under \"enhanced review\" require at least 60 working days for evaluation
entries.cost: Free. Before applying for enrollment, search your school name in CSCSE notices and announcements.
entries.summary: CSCSE names certain overseas institutions to subject their degree evaluations to separate enhanced scrutiny, and also suspends processing evaluation applications for select schools. Searching the institution's name prior to enrolling is far easier than filing appeals afterwards.
entries.benefit: The Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (CSCSE), Ministry of Education, has continuously issued announcements placing academic credential evaluations of certain overseas institutions under enhanced evaluation review (adding an extra review stage specifically for diplomas from these schools). The latest issue is No. 9 (2025-10-28), naming 4 institutions. During the enhanced review period, credential evaluation applications for these schools \"in principle require no less than 60 working days from the date of application submission (inclusive).\" The basis is Article 28 of the \"Measures for the Evaluation of Overseas Academic Credentials and Degrees\": in situations such as anomalous evaluation data or receiving leads reporting issues, CSCSE may initiate enhanced review, requiring applicants, institutions, and others to assist in providing materials, while extending the evaluation timeframe. In May 2025, CSCSE also issued a notice of \"re-enhanced evaluation review\" for 3 institutions. CSCSE has also issued announcements suspending the acceptance of evaluation applications for certain overseas institutions. The August 2025 anti-fraud warning explicitly states: \"Any claims by organizations or individuals promising 'guaranteed certification,' 'internal expedited channels,' 'pandemic back-registration,' or 'expedited evaluation' constitute false advertising.\"
entries.sources: Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (Ministry of Education). Announcement on Enhanced Evaluation Review for Academic Credentials and Degrees of Certain Overseas Institutions (IX) (2025-10-28). <https://www.cscse.edu.cn/cscse/sy/tzgg/2025102809225023345/index.html>; Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (Ministry of Education) (2025-08-29). Important Notice on Guarding Against Fraud Exploiting Overseas Credential Evaluation. <https://www.cscse.edu.cn/cscse/sy/tzgg/2025082913242989351/index.html>; Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (Ministry of Education) (2023). Measures for the Evaluation of Overseas Academic Credentials and Degrees (Article 28). <http://zwfw.cscse.edu.cn/zwfw/lxfwzxwsfwdt2020/xlxwrz32/409891/rzbf/2026042823373762003/index.html>; Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (Ministry of Education). Notices and Announcements. <https://www.cscse.edu.cn/cscse/sy/tzgg/index.html>
entries.notes: \"Enhanced review\" means an additional check is conducted and the processing period is extended; it does not mean evaluation is definitely impossible. Any promises of \"guaranteed certification\" or \"expedited through internal channels\" are false advertising according to CSCSE warnings. Hiring cross-border ghostwriters for theses or having others attend online classes on your behalf will, if discovered, result not only in the qualification being revoked, but may also jeopardize visa records.

entries.title: United States: When on post-completion OPT, track your days of unemployment—they cannot exceed 90 days cumulatively, and cannot exceed 150 days in total with a STEM extension
entries.cost: Free. Record the start and end dates of every period without employment. Once employed, immediately report employer information to the school. The difficulty lies in days ticking upward day by day when job hunting does not go smoothly.
entries.summary: OPT is authorization granted by the US to F-1 students for post-graduation practical training employment; during this time, your status is sustained by holding employment. If days without work accumulate past 90 days, your status may be terminated. For those who obtain a STEM extension, the total combined unemployment across the entire period cannot exceed 150 days. Having no employer registered in the school's system also counts as being unemployed.
entries.benefit: US federal immigration regulations under 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(E) stipulate that during post-completion OPT, legal status is contingent on employment. Cumulative days of unemployment must not exceed 90 days. For those granted a 24-month STEM extension, total unemployment during the entire OPT period must not exceed 150 days, counting the period prior to the extension. Official guidance from the Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP) states: if there is no employer information in the SEVIS record, it is counted as unemployed. Upon reaching a cumulative 90 days, SEVP officials may manually terminate the student's status. SEVIS is the United States' international student status record system. Application filing timing, per the USCIS webpage: applications may be submitted starting 90 days prior to graduation, and at the latest 60 days post-graduation. After the school enters the recommendation into SEVIS, the application must be filed within 30 days.
entries.sources: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(E), (f)(11)(i)(B). <https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-8/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-214/section-214.2>; U.S. ICE SEVP, SEVIS Help Hub. F-1 Optional Practical Training (OPT). <https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/sevis-help-hub/student-records/fm-student-employment/f-1-optional-practical-training-opt>; USCIS. Optional Practical Training (OPT) for F-1 Students. <https://www.uscis.gov/working-in-the-united-states/students-and-exchange-visitors/optional-practical-training-opt-for-f-1-students>; DHS (2026). Optional Practical Training Fees (Proposed Rule, Published 2026-10-08). <https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/08/2026-20660/optional-practical-training-fees>
entries.notes: This entry is current as of October 14, 2026. OPT rules are currently shifting, with two matters to watch. First, the new rule currently enjoined as mentioned in Section 2 (Lawsuits over the New F-1 Rules) shortened the \"apply within 60 days post-graduation\" window to 30 days. The eCFR website currently displays the text of the new rule, so the safest approach is to submit your application prior to graduation. Second, the Department of Homeland Security proposed fees for OPT on October 8, 2026: $70,000 for the initial OPT, and $30,000 for each subsequent OPT. This remains merely a proposed rule with public comments open through November 9, 2026, and has not taken effect. If planning to remain and work in the US after finishing studies, factor this potential cost into calculations before paying tuition, and verify again prior to submitting an application.

entries.title: Canada: Obtain a Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL/TAL) through your school before applying for a study permit; those pursuing master's or doctoral degrees at public universities are exempt starting in 2026
entries.cost: No additional cost; simply apply through the school that accepted you. In most cases, you must first accept the offer of admission and pay partial or full tuition before the school will process it for you.
entries.summary: To study in Canada, most applicants must submit a Provincial Attestation Letter alongside their study permit application, proving they have secured an allocated study permit spot in that province. This letter cannot be retroactively submitted. If applying again after a study permit is approved or refused, or when transferring schools, a new letter must be obtained. Those pursuing master's or doctoral degrees at public universities are exempt.
entries.benefit: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) states that attestation letters are issued by the province or territory where you intend to study. It proves you have been allocated one of their study permit spots. Most study permit applications must include it, and it must be submitted together with the application; it cannot be provided retroactively later. Kindergarten through Grade 12 students are exempt. Starting January 1, 2026, students pursuing master's or doctoral degree programmes at public institutions are also exempt. Those studying in Quebec must instead submit a Québec Acceptance Certificate (CAQ) issued by Quebec. Tuition-exempt exchange students, those extending their study permit for the same study level at the same institution, and several other special circumstances are also exempt. Those who are exempt must attach proof of qualifying for the exemption when applying. An attestation letter is generally valid only for the calendar year in which it was issued; letters issued in 2026 are valid until December 31, 2026. It only needs to be valid at the time the study permit application is submitted; expiring by the time school starts does not matter. If reapplying after a study permit has been approved or refused, a new attestation letter must be obtained. Starting January 22, 2025, transferring schools also requires obtaining a new one.
entries.sources: IRCC. Provincial attestation letter or territorial attestation letter (page modified 2026-09-02). <https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents/provincial-attestation-letter.html>; IRCC. Study permit: Get the right documents (page modified 2026-10-06). <https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents.html>
entries.notes: This entry is current as of October 14, 2026. Canada resets its international student quotas annually, and the exemption list has changed several times; check the pages in the sources column once again before applying. Before paying tuition in exchange for an attestation letter, ask the school clearly first: if the study permit is rejected, how much tuition can be refunded? For the upper limit on working hours while studying in Canada, see item 3 (working hours).

chapters.title: How to Live After a Disability
chapters.intro:
This section covers the days after a disability has already occurred. How to prevent disabling conditions is covered in Section 1 and Section 13, and will not be repeated here.

Four accounting metrics are calculated separately and are not converted into one another. Entries on acute conditions and complications are measured by mortality rates. Entries on subsidies, entitlements, and lawsuits are measured in money. Entries on schooling and administrative procedures are measured in time. Entries on psychiatric hospitalization, legal capacity, and guardianship are measured in personal freedom.

The fact sheet Disability published by the World Health Organization in March 2023 gave three figures. Approximately 1.3 billion people worldwide experience significant disability, accounting for 16% of the world's population, or roughly one in every six people. Some people with disabilities die up to 20 years earlier than people without disabilities. People with disabilities face twice the risk of developing depression, asthma, diabetes, stroke, obesity, or poor oral health. The fact sheet stated clearly that these health inequities arise from the unfair conditions faced by persons with disabilities: discrimination, poverty, exclusion from education and employment, as well as barriers within the healthcare system itself. Therefore, the entries in this section are half about the body, and half about administrative procedures and rights.

Five matters already covered elsewhere are only cross-referenced here and not repeated. How to apply for a disability certificate and how the seven categories and grades 1 through 4 are assessed, see Section 24, Item 10 (Disability certificate). How long to wait before undergoing disability assessment, see Section 24, Item 9 (Disability assessment). How to receive the two disability subsidies, see Section 7, Item 8 (Two subsidies). How work-related injury capacity appraisals and disability grades translate into money, see Section 19, Item 14 (Work capacity assessment). How to apply for long-term care insurance for severe disability, see Section 17, Item 7 (Long-term care insurance). That entry is written in the "Elderly at Home" section, but that benefit has no age threshold; young people can receive it just the same.

The beneficiaries of most entries in this section are yourself and your family members, belonging to the highest two tiers. Instances involving others are noted separately in the remarks.

The entries in this section are divided by theme into the following blocks, with item numbers in parentheses.

**Body and Rehabilitation**: Sudden severe headache following spinal cord injury (Item 1), changing wheelchair cushions to pressure-relieving models (Item 5), not buying therapies that claim to cure paralysis (Item 6), undergoing rehabilitation at legitimate institutions (Item 16), getting fitted with hearing aids for hearing loss (Item 17), avoiding long-term indwelling urinary catheters after spinal cord injury (Item 21).

**Benefits and Subsidies**: Asking the disabled persons' federation all at once about entitlements (Item 7), applying for rehabilitation assistance for children with disabilities (Item 8), applying for home modification subsidies for ramps, handrails, and bathrooms (Item 9), individual income tax reductions (Item 11).

**Job Hunting and Rights Protection**: Proactively disclosing certificate holding when seeking employment (Item 10), suing when rejected from hiring due to disability (Item 20).

**Schooling and Travel**: Taking guide dogs into public places (Item 12), applying for reasonable accommodations for the Gaokao (Item 13), schools being prohibited from rejecting children with disabilities (Item 14), obtaining a driver's license even after bilateral lower limb loss (Item 15).

**Psychology and Caregivers**: Suicide risk during the first ten years post-disability (Item 2), caregivers taking proper care of their own bodies (Item 4).

**Mental Disorders and Guardianship**: Voluntary principle for psychiatric hospitalization (Item 3), applying to the court for determination of legal capacity (Item 18), determining guardians according to statutory order (Item 19).

entries.title: Sudden severe headache and sweating after a spinal cord injury: first help the person sit upright and loosen clothing, while calling 120
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Three actions, completed in tens of seconds.
entries.summary: For people with spinal cord injuries, a segment of the body's alarm wiring is cut off. If the bladder is distended or clothing is constricting, the person may feel nothing, yet blood pressure can surge violently upward. The signal is a sudden severe headache and sweating. At this time, first help the person sit upright, loosen tight clothing, check for urinary retention, and call 120 at the same time.
entries.benefit: This type of episode is called autonomic dysreflexia. A systematic review searched four databases—Medline, CINAHL, EMBASE, and PsycINFO—including 31 studies, 6 of which were randomized controlled trials. The review stated that the non-pharmacological management at the time of an episode consists of three steps: positioning the patient upright, loosening tight clothing, and removing the triggering stimulus. The basis for these three steps is clinical consensus and physiological data, belonging to Level 5 evidence. The main text of the review stated that this type of episode is most commonly seen in injuries at the T6 level and above, with the most common triggers being stimulation of the bladder or bowel. Stimuli below the level of injury trigger massive sympathetic discharge, causing blood pressure to rise acutely, while sensation below the level of injury is partially or completely lost. Symptoms include severe headache and profuse sweating above the level of injury, or there may be no symptoms at all. Failure to manage it may lead to intracranial hemorrhage, epileptic seizures, and even death. No study has specifically measured the effect of sitting up during an episode, but when people with spinal cord injuries change from lying flat to sitting up or tilting, resting blood pressure decreases significantly. Antihypertensive medications are used only when blood pressure remains persistently elevated, among which prazosin has Level 1 evidence, while nifedipine and prostaglandin E2 have Level 2 evidence. The review also stated that preventive strategies for episodes mainly target the two common categories of triggers—the genitourinary system and surgical operations—with most supported only by Level 4 and Level 5 evidence
entries.sources: Krassioukov A, Warburton DE, Teasell R, Eng JJ; Spinal Cord Injury Rehabilitation Evidence Research Team (2009). A systematic review of the management of autonomic dysreflexia after spinal cord injury. Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation, 90(4):682-695. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apmr.2008.10.017>
entries.notes: Assigned Grade B because there are no randomized controlled trials behind those three on-site actions, only consensus and physiological reasoning. The review itself noted that most of these interventions are supported only by uncontrolled studies. The medication section is a matter for doctors; do not administer antihypertensive medications on your own at home. Letting the person lie flat causes blood pressure to rise even higher, so help them sit upright. Family members and caregivers must also know these three steps. Do not treat it as a common headache and try to tough it out.

entries.title: The first ten years following disabling spinal cord injury represent a high-risk period for suicide; do not dismiss it as something solved merely by "looking on the bright side"
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Make one phone call, or register for an appointment once.
entries.summary: Long-term follow-up at two spinal cord injury centers in the UK found that the suicide rate among this cohort was five times that of the general population. Over 90% of suicides occurred within the first ten years post-injury. For those whose initial cause of injury was itself suicide, the risk was notably higher still.
entries.benefit: The study tracked 2,304 patients with traumatic spinal cord injury newly admitted between 1991 and 2010 who survived their first year post-injury and had neurological deficits at discharge, following them through the end of 2014. Among them, the injury cause in 63 cases (2.7%) was itself an attempted suicide. By the end of follow-up, 533 people had died, of whom 4.2% died by suicide, with 91% of suicides occurring in the first ten years after injury. The age-standardized suicide mortality rate was 62.5 cases per 100,000 person-years (95% CI 36.4–88.6, confidence interval), which was five times the general population suicide rate in England and Wales in 2014 (12.2 cases per 100,000 persons). For the subpopulation whose injuries resulted from attempted suicide, compared with other injury causes, the odds ratio for mortality was 4.32 (P<0.001), and the odds ratio for suicide was 9.46 (P<0.001)
entries.sources: Savic G, DeVivo MJ, Frankel HL, Jamous MA, Soni BM, Charlifue S (2018). Suicide and traumatic spinal cord injury - a cohort study. Spinal Cord, 56(1):2-6. <https://doi.org/10.1038/sc.2017.98>
entries.notes: This study looked only at spinal cord injuries; applying it to other disabling causes like blindness, amputation, or burns constitutes extrapolation. What it demonstrates is the time window: the risk does not pass simply upon discharge; it must be monitored for ten years. If you need someone to talk to, call 12356; see Section 29, Item 11 (12356). Do not stockpile sleeping pills and pesticides at home; see Section 1, Item 25 (Suicidal ideation). If grief and emotional distress remain stuck in place after six months, register for an appointment in psychiatry or clinical psychology; see Section 29, Item 8 (Grief lasting over half a year).

entries.title: Psychiatric hospitalization follows the voluntary principle; only two circumstances permit admission without the individual's consent
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Commit the two circumstances to memory so you can state them when needed.
entries.summary: A statement from family members or an employer cannot keep a person hospitalized in a psychiatric facility. The law recognizes only two circumstances, and a diagnosis of severe mental disorder must be established first: having harmed oneself or presenting such a danger, or having endangered the safety of others or presenting such a danger. The first circumstance requires guardian consent for admission. For the second, if there is an objection, a rediagnosis may be requested within three days, after which an independent appraisal may still be commissioned.
entries.benefit: Article 30 of the Mental Health Law explicitly states that "inpatient treatment for mental disorders shall implement the voluntary principle." Inpatient treatment shall be implemented only when diagnostic conclusions and condition assessments indicate that the patient is a patient with a severe mental disorder, and one of the following circumstances exists. The first is "having engaged in self-harming behavior, or presenting a danger of self-harm." The second is "having engaged in behavior endangering the safety of others, or presenting a danger of endangering the safety of others." Article 31: For cases falling under the first circumstance, the medical institution may implement inpatient treatment only with the consent of the guardian; if the guardian does not consent, it shall not be implemented. Article 32: If the individual or the guardian objects under the second circumstance, they may request a rediagnosis, which shall be filed within three days from the date of receiving the diagnostic conclusion, to be performed by two practicing psychiatrists other than the initial diagnosing physicians; if they still object to the rediagnosis conclusion, they may independently commission an appraisal institution that has obtained professional qualifications according to law to perform a medical appraisal of the mental disorder. Article 35: Where the rediagnosis conclusion or appraisal report indicates that the patient cannot be confirmed as a patient with a severe mental disorder, or that the patient does not need inpatient treatment, the medical institution shall not implement inpatient treatment on them. Article 78: Whoever deliberately sends a person who does not have a mental disorder into a medical institution for treatment as a patient with a mental disorder shall bear liability for compensation in accordance with the law (Nationwide, effective May 1, 2013, amended 2018)
entries.sources: Mental Health Law of the People's Republic of China (Amended 2018, Articles 30, 31, 32, 35, and 78). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7448a066d>
entries.notes: Conversely, it is not the case that nobody can be brought in for medical attention. Article 28 stipulates that where a suspected person with a mental disorder has engaged in behavior harming themselves or endangering the safety of others, or presents such danger, their close relatives, employer, or local public security organ shall immediately take measures to stop it and send them to a medical institution for diagnosis of mental disorders. Upon receiving the person brought in, the medical institution shall not refuse to make a diagnosis. Thus, "bringing in for diagnosis" and "retaining for inpatient hospitalization" are two separate thresholds: the former is low, while the latter is high. Article 75 lists the liabilities of medical institutions: those who implement restraint and seclusion in violation of regulations, or diagnose non-psychiatric patients as patients with mental disorders, will face administrative sanctions up to the revocation of their practicing licenses. For what to do when someone around you has violent impulses, see Section 8.

entries.title: The person providing long-term care to a family member with a disability needs someone monitoring their own physical health
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Delegate part of the caregiving tasks and go get a physical examination for yourself.
entries.summary: A caregiver collapsing from exhaustion is not being melodramatic. A US study tracked more than 800 older adults over four years. Those who cared for a disabled spouse while reporting mental strain had an approximately 60% higher risk of death compared with non-caregivers. Those who provided care but did not feel strained showed no such increase. Therefore, what needs monitoring is not caregiving itself, but that prolonged state of tension.
entries.benefit: The study was a prospective population-based cohort conducted across four US communities from 1993 to 1998, with an average follow-up of 4.5 years. It included 392 caregivers and 427 non-caregivers, aged 66 to 96 years, all living with their spouses. Within four years, 103 individuals (12.6%) died. After adjusting for sociodemographic factors, preexisting illness, and subclinical cardiovascular disease, those who provided care while reporting mental or emotional strain had a 63% higher mortality risk than non-caregiving controls (RR 1.63, 95% CI 1.00–2.65, confidence interval). Neither individuals who provided care but did not report strain (RR 1.08, 95% CI 0.61–1.90) nor those with a disabled spouse who did not provide care themselves (RR 1.37, 95% CI 0.73–2.58) showed increased adjusted mortality rates
entries.sources: Schulz R, Beach SR (1999). Caregiving as a risk factor for mortality: the Caregiver Health Effects Study. JAMA, 282(23):2215-2219. <https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.282.23.2215>
entries.notes: Controversy: The lower bound of this study's confidence interval sat right at 1.00; the possibility of "no difference" was not entirely ruled out. The population consisted of older American adults living with spouses, and the care recipients were disabled elderly spouses; applying this to individuals caring for young disabled family members constitutes extrapolation. What it demonstrates is the direction: the subgroup experiencing strain has higher risk. Share and delegate caregiving duties whenever possible; inquire with the local disabled persons' federation and civil affairs bureau regarding respite care and day care services. Caregivers must not stop medications for their own chronic diseases; see Section 16, Item 1 (Take medications in full according to medical advice). The beneficiary is yourself.

entries.title: For long-term wheelchair users, switch the seat cushion to a pressure-relieving type, and inspect the ischium and coccyx daily
entries.cost: A pressure-relieving seat cushion costs several hundred to over a thousand yuan. Daily inspection takes one minute.
entries.summary: Older nursing home residents using pressure-relieving seat cushions had significantly fewer pressure ulcers at the ischium than those using conventional segmented foam cushions, though no difference was seen when including the coccyx. Everyone in the trial was first fitted with a properly sized wheelchair, so the wheelchair itself must also be fitted to the individual's measurements rather than simply buying a generic model.
entries.benefit: This randomized clinical trial was conducted across 12 nursing homes, enrolling 232 residents aged 65 and older between 2004 and 2008 who used wheelchairs for at least 6 hours daily and had a Braden score of 18 or lower. All participants were first fitted with a properly fitting wheelchair, and then randomly allocated into two groups. One group used skin protection cushions (air, viscous fluid plus foam, or gel plus foam), and the other group used 7.6 cm thick segmented foam cushions. Follow-up lasted 6 months or until a pressure ulcer developed. For pressure ulcers at the ischial tuberosities, there were 8 cases (6.7%) in the segmented foam group and 1 case (0.9%) in the skin protection cushion group, P=0.04. When combining pressure ulcers at the ischium and sacrococcyx, there were 21 cases (17.6%) in the segmented foam group and 12 cases (10.6%) in the skin protection cushion group, P=0.14, showing no statistically significant difference
entries.sources: Brienza D, Kelsey S, Karg P, et al. (2010). A randomized clinical trial on preventing pressure ulcers with wheelchair seat cushions. Journal of the American Geriatrics Society, 58(12):2308-2314. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1532-5415.2010.03168.x>
entries.notes: There are two reasons for assigning Grade B. First, the sample size was only 232 people; the P-value of 0.04 for the primary endpoint barely crossed the significance threshold, and the secondary endpoint showed no difference. Second, the cohort consisted of advanced-age nursing home residents; applying this to younger wheelchair users constitutes extrapolation. Everyone in the trial was first fitted with a properly sized wheelchair, so "proper fit" and "cushion" work together—do not merely swap the cushion. For pressure ulcer prevention in long-term bedridden individuals, including air mattresses and scheduled repositioning, see Section 17, Item 8 (Pressure ulcers). For how to apply for configuration subsidies for basic assistive devices, see Item 7 of this section (Inquire comprehensively at the county-level disabled persons' federation).

entries.title: Do not purchase therapies and devices that claim to "cure paralysis, blindness, or deafness"
entries.cost: Costs nothing; it saves money. The difficulty lies in family members clinging to hope and refusing to be dissuaded.
entries.summary: The Advertising Law leaves no room for ambiguity. Advertisements for medical services, pharmaceuticals, and medical devices are not permitted to guarantee efficacy, state cure rates or effective rates, or use endorsers for recommendation or verification. Therefore, claims like "standing up in three courses of treatment" or "see how many people have recovered" are themselves illegal advertisements, without needing to analyze their claimed mechanisms. Items that are not medical devices are not even permitted to mention disease treatment.
entries.benefit: Article 16 of the Advertising Law stipulates that advertisements for medical treatment, pharmaceuticals, and medical devices shall not contain the following contents: "(1) Assertions or guarantees regarding efficacy and safety; (2) Statements of cure rates or effective rates; (3) Comparisons with the efficacy and safety of other pharmaceuticals or medical devices, or with other medical institutions; (4) Use of advertising endorsers for recommendation or certification." Article 17 stipulates that, with the exception of advertisements for medical treatment, pharmaceuticals, and medical devices, "any other advertisement is prohibited from involving disease treatment functions, and shall not use medical terminology or terminology likely to confuse the promoted goods with pharmaceuticals or medical devices." Article 4 stipulates that advertisements shall not contain false or misleading content, and shall not deceive or mislead consumers; advertisers shall be responsible for the authenticity of advertising content (Nationwide, amended 2021)
entries.sources: Advertising Law of the People's Republic of China (Amended 2021, Articles 4, 16, and 17). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817ab231eb017abd6bd860052d>
entries.notes: There is only one method of judgment: see whether it dares to make absolute claims. Rehabilitation departments in legitimate hospitals will not promise you that you can stand up in a few courses of treatment. When encountering this type of marketing, report it to 12315 or the local market supervision department. The pitch patterns for health supplements follow the exact same playbook; see Section 6, Item 10 (Health supplements). If you have already made a purchase and want a refund, proceed according to the methods for online shopping and prepaid consumption; see Section 5, Item 29 (Rely on platform rules for online shopping). The beneficiaries are yourself and your family.

entries.title: Once the disability certificate is issued, visit the county-level disabled persons' federation to inquire comprehensively about everything you can apply for at once
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Make one trip to the county-level disabled persons' federation and spend one morning asking questions. You will need to visit more than one department afterward.
entries.summary: The disability certificate itself does not disburse money; it is a key. What follows behind it are several independent benefits, each of which must be applied for on your own initiative; none will be delivered to your door automatically. When visiting the disabled persons' federation for the first time, asking through the list item by item saves far more trouble than making multiple trips back and forth.
entries.benefit: There are at least six entitlements linked to holding the certificate, each with its own legal basis. Living subsidies for persons with disabilities in financial hardship and nursing care subsidies for persons with severe disabilities are covered in Section 7, Item 8 (Two Subsidies). Rehabilitation assistance for children with disabilities is covered in Item 8 of this section (Rehabilitation Assistance). Subsidies for the provision of basic assistive devices are based on Article 26 of the Regulations on Disability Prevention and Rehabilitation of Persons with Disabilities. Subsidies for home accessibility modifications are covered in Item 9 of this section (Ramp, Handrail, and Bathroom Modifications). Proportional employment and employment services are covered in Item 10 of this section (Proactively Disclose Certificate). Individual income tax reductions are covered in Item 11 of this section (Individual Income Tax Reduction). Article 26 of the Regulations on Disability Prevention and Rehabilitation of Persons with Disabilities also specifies that the state provides basic rehabilitation services to urban and rural persons with disabilities in poverty and persons with severe disabilities by implementing key rehabilitation projects, and "provides subsidies for the provision of basic assistive devices in accordance with relevant state provisions." Article 20 stipulates that relevant departments of people's governments at or above the county level and Disabled Persons' Federations shall utilize community resources to establish rehabilitation venues or purchase services, conducting community rehabilitation work such as rehabilitation guidance, daily living ability training, rehabilitation care, assistive device provision, information consulting, and referrals (nationwide, effective July 1, 2017). Article 21 of the same regulations stipulates that providing rehabilitation services requires first conducting a needs assessment, and then determining an individualized plan based on the assessment results. The State Council's 2016 document states that "localities where conditions permit may provide subsidies for the provision of basic rehabilitation assistive devices to urban and rural persons with disabilities in poverty and persons with severe disabilities." The three-year action plan issued by the Ministry of Civil Affairs and other departments in 2026 specifies the need to "standardize and strengthen the subsidy system for basic assistive device adaptation services for persons with disabilities." Those disabled due to work-related injuries follow a different path. The Administrative Measures for the Provision of Assistive Devices in Work-Related Injury Insurance govern prosthetic limbs, orthotics, artificial eyes, dentures, wheelchairs, and the like. It stipulates that confirmation by a labor capacity assessment committee is required prior to provision. The costs of fitting, maintenance, and training are paid by the work-related injury insurance fund in accordance with regulations. If one procures devices independently without prior confirmation, or procures them at non-contracted institutions, the administrative agency will not pay.
entries.sources: State Council (2017). Regulations on Disability Prevention and Rehabilitation of Persons with Disabilities (Articles 20, 21, 26). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2017-02/27/content_5171308.htm>; State Council (2016). Several Opinions on Accelerating the Development of the Rehabilitation Assistive Device Industry (Guo Fa [2016] No. 60). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2016-10/27/content_5125001.htm>; Ministry of Civil Affairs et al. (2026). Three-Year Action Plan for Expanding Capacity and Improving Quality in the Rehabilitation Assistive Device Industry (2026–2028) (Min Han [2026] No. 48). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202607/content_7075249.htm>; Decree No. 27 of the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, Ministry of Civil Affairs, and National Health and Family Planning Commission (2016). Administrative Measures for the Provision of Assistive Devices in Work-Related Injury Insurance (Articles 2, 15, 24). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2016/content_5074060.htm>
entries.notes: The procedure for obtaining the certificate itself can be found in Section 24, Item 10 (Disability Certificate). For items like wheelchairs, prosthetic limbs, and hearing aids, inquire clearly about the assessment and provision procedures required for subsidies before buying. The work-related injury track explicitly stipulates confirmation before provision; devices procured independently beforehand will not be reimbursed. Work-related injury identification and labor capacity assessment are covered in Section 19, Item 14 (Labor Capacity Assessment). For assistive device subsidies, the State Council document states that "localities where conditions permit may" provide them, so whether they exist and how much is provided are determined locally. The following points are based on author experience: when inquiring, write down the name of each program, return home, and look up the original documents by name on the official websites of the local Disabled Persons' Federation and the local government; do not rely solely on verbal statements made at service counters. Do not expect to get the full picture all at once; go back and ask again after a year, as policies change.

entries.title: If a child is under 7 years old and has a disability or autism, apply to the county-level Disabled Persons' Federation for rehabilitation assistance
entries.cost: Free. Submit an application once to the county-level Disabled Persons' Federation, then choose a facility from the designated institutions.
entries.summary: The state has established a rehabilitation assistance system for children with disabilities and children with autism aged 0 to 6, covering surgeries, assistive devices, and rehabilitation training. The assistance targets prioritize families facing economic hardship; areas with adequate local fiscal capacity may expand the age range and ease family financial conditions. By regulation, the assistance covers children up to age 6; do not delay until it is time to start school. Institutions must be chosen from the Disabled Persons' Federation's designated list.
entries.benefit: The State Council Opinions on Establishing a Rehabilitation Assistance System for Children with Disabilities specifies that the targets of assistance are eligible children aged 0–6 with visual, hearing, speech, physical, intellectual, and other disabilities, as well as children with autism. This includes children with disabilities from families receiving urban and rural minimum living allowances or registered impoverished households, children with disabilities sheltered and raised by child welfare institutions, disabled orphans, children with disabilities included within the scope of support for extremely poor persons, and children with disabilities from other economically disadvantaged families. The specific determination measures for other economically disadvantaged families are formulated by local people's governments at or above the county level. The document also specifies that "regions where conditions permit may expand the age range for rehabilitation assistance for children with disabilities, and may also ease the restrictions on the family economic conditions of assistance recipients." Funding guarantee standards are determined by local people's governments at or above the county level on a categorized basis according to local financial capacity, the number of guaranteed recipients, disability categories, and other factors, with a dynamic adjustment mechanism established. Applications are submitted to the county-level Disabled Persons' Federation at the place of the child's household registration (or where the residence permit is issued). For approved applications, guardians independently select a designated rehabilitation institution. Designated rehabilitation institutions are "selected and determined in accordance with the principles of openness and merit-based selection" by local Disabled Persons' Federations at or above the county level in conjunction with health, education, civil affairs, and other departments. Expenses incurred at designated institutions are directly settled between public finance departments and the institutions. "For expenses incurred from receiving rehabilitation services at non-designated rehabilitation institutions with the review and consent of county-level Disabled Persons' Federation organizations, settlement measures shall be specified by the county-level Disabled Persons' Federation organizations in consultation with public finance departments at the same level." The document required provincial-level people's governments to roll out local systems and supporting policies before the end of September 2018. The superior legal authority is Article 26 of the Regulations on Disability Prevention and Rehabilitation of Persons with Disabilities: the state establishes a rehabilitation assistance system for children with disabilities, "gradually achieving free provision of services such as surgeries, assistive device fittings, and rehabilitation training for children aged 0–6 with visual, hearing, speech, physical, intellectual, and other disabilities, as well as children with autism" (nationwide, starting in 2018)
entries.sources: State Council (2018). Opinions on Establishing a Rehabilitation Assistance System for Children with Disabilities (Guo Fa [2018] No. 20). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2018-07/10/content_5305296.htm>; State Council (2017). Regulations on Disability Prevention and Rehabilitation of Persons with Disabilities (Article 26). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2017-02/27/content_5171308.htm>
entries.notes: Assistance programs and standards are set by local governments at or above the county level; check the provincial rehabilitation assistance measures for children with disabilities on the local Disabled Persons' Federation official website first. Designated institutions are selected by the Disabled Persons' Federation in conjunction with relevant departments; request the list from the Disabled Persons' Federation. The document requires the Disabled Persons' Federation to work with relevant departments to strengthen supervision over the admission and exit of designated rehabilitation institutions, establish regular inspection and comprehensive assessment mechanisms, and establish a blacklist system. If you want to use an institution outside the list, you must first obtain the review and approval of the county-level Disabled Persons' Federation; how the funds are settled is determined locally. If you go independently without prior consent, there is no provision in the document for reimbursement. The beneficiary is your child, categorized under Tier 2. Institutions promising "guaranteed cures" should be handled according to Item 6 of this section (Can Cure Paralysis).

entries.title: You can apply to governments at or above the county level for subsidies for home ramp, handrail, and bathroom modifications
entries.cost: Applying is free. The modification itself is mostly subsidized, though you may still need to cover a portion yourself. Requires trips to the Disabled Persons' Federation and subdistrict offices.
entries.summary: The Barrier-Free Environment Creation Law includes a provision: people's governments at or above the county level shall support and guide home accessibility modifications. Appropriate subsidies shall be granted to eligible households of persons with disabilities and elderly individuals. The subsidy amounts and which items are modified are decided locally; inquire at the local Disabled Persons' Federation first.
entries.benefit: Article 19 of the Barrier-Free Environment Creation Law: "People's governments at or above the county level shall support and guide home accessibility modifications. Appropriate subsidies shall be granted to eligible households of persons with disabilities and elderly individuals." Article 18 stipulates that for existing residential buildings, residential areas, public buildings, public places, transportation facilities, urban and rural roads, etc., that do not meet construction standards for accessibility facilities, people's governments at or above the county level shall formulate targeted accessibility modification plans based on actual conditions and organize their implementation. Article 22: "The state supports the installation of elevators or other barrier-free facilities in existing multi-story residential buildings in old urban communities to provide convenience for persons with disabilities and the elderly." The same article stipulates that people's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments shall "give play to the role of primary-level community organizations" to promote the installation of elevators in existing multi-story residential buildings. Article 62 provides that any organization or individual has the right to submit opinions and suggestions to relevant competent government departments on strengthening and improving barrier-free environment creation, and to file complaints and reports against violations of this Law; upon receiving complaints and reports, competent departments "shall handle them in a timely manner and provide responses." Article 63 stipulates that for acts violating the provisions of this Law that harm the public interest of society, people's procuratorates may issue procuratorial suggestions or initiate public interest litigation (nationwide, effective September 1, 2023)
entries.sources: Barrier-Free Environment Creation Law of the People's Republic of China (Articles 18, 19, 22, 62, 63). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff80818188d7430b0189018493370940>
entries.notes: This is rated B because the law only states that "appropriate subsidies shall be granted," leaving how much is subsidized and who qualifies entirely to local authorities, with no nationwide unified figure. First search for "home accessibility modifications for severely disabled persons in financial hardship" on the local Disabled Persons' Federation official website. Installing elevators in residential communities is a different path; Article 22 requires the government and relevant departments to promote it through primary-level community organizations, so inquire first with the subdistrict office and community committee. If barrier-free facilities in public places fall below standard, file a complaint with the competent department pursuant to Article 62; it must give you a response.

entries.title: When looking for work, proactively mention that you hold a disability certificate; hiring you offsets fees for enterprises
entries.cost: Free. Just one extra sentence during an interview. The hard part is bringing it up.
entries.summary: The proportion of disabled employees hired by an employer must not be lower than 1.5% of its total on-duty workforce, with exact ratios set by each province. If an employer fails to meet this, it must pay an employment security fund based on the shortfall in heads, with each head calculated using the employer's average annual employee wage from the previous year. Through the end of 2027, this is discounted to 50% or 90%, and enterprises with 30 or fewer employees are exempt. Therefore, hiring you saves real money; state clearly during interviews that you hold a certificate.
entries.benefit: Article 8 of the Regulations on Employment of Persons with Disabilities: "The proportion of disabled persons employed by an employer shall not be lower than 1.5% of the total number of on-duty employees of that employer. The specific proportion shall be prescribed by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government according to the actual circumstances of their respective regions." Article 9: Those failing to reach the proportion prescribed by the local provincial-level people's government shall pay the employment security fund for persons with disabilities. Article 8 of the Administrative Measures for the Collection, Use, and Management of the Employment Security Fund for Persons with Disabilities provides the formula: "Annual amount of security fund payable = (Number of on-duty employees of the employer in the preceding year × Proportion of employed persons with disabilities prescribed by the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where the employer is located - Actual number of persons with disabilities employed by the employer in the preceding year) × Average annual wage of on-duty employees of the employer in the preceding year." Article 16: Within 3 years from the date of business registration, small and micro enterprises with 20 or fewer on-duty employees (inclusive) that fail to reach the prescribed proportion of employed disabled persons are exempt from the security fund. Article 7: Only when an employer recruits a person with a disability as a staff member on the formal establishment, or signs a labor contract of 1 year or more with a person with a disability within working age, pays an actual wage not lower than the local minimum wage standard, and pays social insurance premiums in full, "may this be counted toward the number of disabled persons employed by the employer." Employing 1 person holding a Grade 1 or Grade 2 disability certificate is counted as employing 2 persons. Ministry of Finance Announcement [2023] No. 8 further stipulates that from January 1, 2023, to December 31, 2027, if the employment proportion reaches 1% but has not reached the provincially mandated ratio, payment shall be made at 50% of the amount due; if below 1%, payment shall be made at 90%; "enterprises with 30 or fewer on-duty employees (inclusive) continue to be exempt from the employment security fund for persons with disabilities." Article 36 of the Law on the Protection of Persons with Disabilities stipulates that the state grants tax preferences in accordance with the law to employers that meet or exceed the prescribed proportion in employing persons with disabilities or that arrange centralized employment for persons with disabilities (nationwide, Regulations on Employment of Persons with Disabilities effective May 1, 2007)
entries.sources: State Council (2007). Regulations on Employment of Persons with Disabilities (Articles 8, 9). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_6646.htm>; Ministry of Finance, State Taxation Administration, China Disabled Persons' Federation (2015). Administrative Measures for the Collection, Use, and Management of the Employment Security Fund for Persons with Disabilities (Cai Shui [2015] No. 72, Articles 6, 7, 8, 16). <http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2015-09/15/content_5650063.htm>; Ministry of Finance (2023). Announcement on Continuing the Implementation of Preferential Policies for the Employment Security Fund for Persons with Disabilities (Ministry of Finance Announcement 2023 No. 8). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2023-03/28/content_5748750.htm>; Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Persons with Disabilities (Article 36). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f135f46016f1d134c88132b>
entries.notes: Enterprises with 30 or fewer on-duty employees are exempt from paying the security fund through the end of 2027; for them, this reason does not hold, so do not count on it. The relief policies for the security fund have been continuously adjusted over the years; how calculations are handled after 2027 will depend on the Ministry of Finance's announcements at that time. In addition, proportional employment requires genuine employment: signing a contract of 1 year or longer, paying wages not lower than the minimum wage, and paying social insurance in full are prerequisites for being counted toward the employed headcount. For the identification of persons with employment difficulties and social insurance subsidies, see Section 7, Item 12 (Persons with Employment Difficulties). For vocational training subsidies, see Section 7, Item 13 (Vocational Training Subsidies). The beneficiary is yourself.

entries.title: Individual income tax for persons with disabilities can be reduced; call the provincial tax bureau to ask how much
entries.cost: Free. Check a box during filing, or submit record-filing materials once.
entries.summary: The Individual Income Tax Law states that income of persons with disabilities may receive an individual income tax reduction. However, how much and for how long are left by law to provincial-level governments to decide, so policies vary by province. The method is to call the 12366 tax service hotline to inquire with your provincial tax bureau, or look for tax reduction and exemption items in the Individual Income Tax App.
entries.benefit: Article 5 of the Individual Income Tax Law: "Under any of the following circumstances, individual income tax may be reduced; the specific magnitude and duration shall be prescribed by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and reported to the standing committees of the people's congresses at the same level for the record: (1) Income of persons with disabilities, solitary elderly individuals, and family members of martyrs; (2) Those suffering significant losses due to natural disasters." Article 36 of the Law on the Protection of Persons with Disabilities additionally stipulates that the state grants tax preferences in accordance with the law to persons with disabilities engaged in individual businesses, and exempts them from administrative and institutional fees (nationwide, Individual Income Tax Law effective January 1, 2019)
entries.sources: Individual Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China (amended in 2018, Article 5). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf724bd0609>; Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Persons with Disabilities (Article 36). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f135f46016f1d134c88132b>
entries.notes: Rating the magnitude of benefit as "small" is based on judgment, because the law itself does not provide a figure, and how much is reduced is determined by each province. Handling it once allows long-term use, so it is worth the effort. For how much is reduced specifically in your province, refer to the regulations of the provincial government and announcements from your provincial tax bureau; comparison tables circulated online may be outdated. For those running their own small shops, administrative and institutional fees are exempted under Article 36 of the Law on the Protection of Persons with Disabilities; proactively bring this up when applying for your business license.

entries.title: Guide dogs may be brought into public places and public transportation; blind persons ride urban public transit for free
entries.cost: Free. If stopped, you must speak up and cite legal articles, which may involve a brief standoff.
entries.summary: The law specifies that public places and public transportation must provide convenience to persons with disabilities accompanied by guide dogs, hearing dogs, and service dogs. Blind persons ride urban buses, subways, and ferries for free with valid identification, and persons with disabilities may carry essential personal assistive devices for free. If stopped, cite these two provisions; if that fails, file a complaint.
entries.benefit: Article 46 of the Barrier-Free Environment Creation Law: "Entities operating and managing public places, transportation facilities, and public transportation vehicles shall provide convenience to persons with disabilities carrying service dogs such as guide dogs, hearing dogs, and assistance dogs." Paragraph 2 of the same article provides that persons with disabilities entering or exiting public places and riding public transportation with service dogs "shall abide by relevant state regulations, equip service dogs with distinct identification gear, and take necessary protective measures." Article 68 stipulates that where departments and entities charged with public service duties fail to provide barrier-free social services in accordance with the law, the people's government at the corresponding level or superior competent department shall order them to make corrections within a specified time limit; if corrections are not made within the time limit, sanctions shall be imposed in accordance with the law on the directly responsible persons in charge and other directly liable personnel. Article 35 stipulates that government service convenience hotlines and emergency call systems such as police alarms, fire emergencies, traffic accidents, and medical emergencies shall gradually possess barrier-free functions such as voice, large print, Braille, and one-touch calling. Article 62 stipulates that any organization or individual has the right to file complaints and reports against violations of this Law, and the competent department shall handle them in a timely manner and provide responses. Article 50 of the Law on the Protection of Persons with Disabilities: "Blind persons riding urban public buses, trolleybuses, subways, ferries, and other public transportation vehicles with valid certificates shall be free of charge. Mailings of reading materials for the blind shall be delivered free of charge." The same article also provides that people's governments at or above the county level shall grant conveniences and preferential treatment to persons with disabilities riding public transportation, and persons with disabilities may carry essential personal assistive devices free of charge (nationwide, Barrier-Free Environment Creation Law effective September 1, 2023)
entries.sources: Barrier-Free Environment Creation Law of the People's Republic of China (Articles 35, 46, 62, 68). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff80818188d7430b0189018493370940>; Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Persons with Disabilities (Article 50). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f135f46016f1d134c88132b>
entries.notes: The law says "provide convenience" and does not specify fines; Article 68 only governs ordering corrections and disciplining responsible personnel, so during an on-site standoff, the other party might not back down immediately. Keeping a screenshot of the legal articles on your phone works better than reciting article numbers—this is based on author experience. If it cannot be resolved on the spot, file a complaint pursuant to Article 62; the competent department is required to respond. The law also requires equipping service dogs with clear identification gear and proper protections, so prepare these before going out. Before taking trains or planes, call customer service beforehand to clarify requirements for service dogs. As for which type of "valid certificate" is recognized for free transit, check clearly with the local Disabled Persons' Federation.

entries.title: Persons with disabilities taking the Gaokao can apply for reasonable accommodations; test time is extended by half when using Braille papers
entries.cost: Free. Requires submitting a written application within the timeline prescribed by the province, as well as an in-person on-site verification.
entries.summary: Candidates with disabilities taking the Gaokao (National College Entrance Examination) can apply for Braille test papers, large-print test papers, exemption from the foreign language listening test, separate testing rooms, bringing hearing aids and wheelchairs into the venue, as well as extended test time. These are not granted automatically; you must submit a written application within the timeframe prescribed by your province, accompanied by a second-generation or newer disability certificate. If dissatisfied with the result, you can apply to the provincial education department for a review.
entries.benefit: Article 5 of the *Provisions on the Administration of Reasonable Accommodations for Persons with Disabilities Participating in the National Unified Examination for Admissions to General Higher Education Institutions* lists twelve reasonable accommodations. These include providing candidates with visual disabilities with current Braille test papers, large-print test papers, or standard test papers; exempting candidates with hearing disabilities from foreign language listening comprehension tests; permitting candidates with visual disabilities to bring assistive devices such as Braille styluses, Braille writing slates, non-storage Braille typewriters, non-storage electronic vision enhancers, white canes, and optical magnifiers; permitting candidates with hearing disabilities to wear hearing aids and cochlear implants; permitting candidates with physical mobility impairments to use wheelchairs and walkers, and allowing those with special needs to bring their own specialized desks and chairs. The extent of time extensions is specified in Item 6 of Article 5: "For candidates with visual disabilities who use Braille test papers, the testing time shall be extended by 50% based on the prescribed total testing duration for that subject; for candidates with visual disabilities who use large-print test papers or standard test papers, and candidates with severe writing difficulties—such as candidates whose upper limbs cannot write normally or who lack upper limbs due to cerebral palsy or other conditions—the testing time shall be extended by 30% based on the prescribed total testing duration for that subject." In addition, accommodations include priority entry into test centers and examination rooms, individual standardized examination rooms, and the provision of guiding assistants and sign language interpreters. Article 7 specifies the application procedure: Candidates must submit a formal written application in accordance with the time, place, and manner prescribed by the provincial educational examination authority, and provide their own second-generation or higher Disability Certificate; an expert panel conducts on-site verification and comprehensive evaluation, and the provincial educational examination authority issues a *Notice of Determination*. Article 8 provides that if a candidate disputes the *Notice of Determination*, they may submit a written application for administrative review to the provincial administrative department of education. Article 9 specifies that for those exempted from foreign language listening comprehension, the foreign language subject score is calculated as "written test score × total points for the foreign language subject / total points for the written test portion". Article 18 provides that where persons with disabilities participate in other national educational examinations and require reasonable accommodations, implementation may refer to these Provisions (Nationwide, promulgated and implemented on April 7, 2017).
entries.sources: Ministry of Education, China Disabled Persons' Federation (2017). Provisions on the Administration of Reasonable Accommodations for Persons with Disabilities Participating in the National Unified Examination for Admissions to General Higher Education Institutions (Jiao Xue [2017] No. 4, Articles 5, 7, 8, 9, 18). <http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2017-04/12/content_5650060.htm>
entries.notes: Application deadlines are set by each province and are specified in that year's Gaokao registration procedures; once missed, there is no second chance. Therefore, check the official website of the provincial educational examination authority during the first semester of the third year of senior high school to confirm the dates. Article 18 also provides that other national educational examinations, such as postgraduate entrance exams and adult higher education entrance exams, may also refer to these provisions to apply. The provision stating that schools may not reject disabled students during schooling stages is discussed in Item 14 of this section (Schools May Not Reject Students). The beneficiary is yourself or your child.

entries.title: When Children with Disabilities Apply for Enrollment, Schools May Not Reject Them; for Those Unable to Attend School, the Education Bureau Arranges Home-Delivered Teaching
entries.cost: Free. Requires submitting an application and may require undergoing an evaluation. When a school makes excuses to shirk responsibility, you must escalate to the education bureau.
entries.summary: Kindergartens and all categories of schools may not reject eligible children with disabilities who apply for admission; regular vocational schools are also subject to this rule. For children who require dedicated care and cannot attend school in person, the county education bureau will arrange home-delivered instruction or distance education, and they will still be granted formal student status (xueji). Admission and school transfers are evaluated and recommended first by the education bureau's expert committee, rather than being determined solely by a school's unilateral say.
entries.benefit: Article 7 of the *Regulations on Education for Persons with Disabilities*: "Preschool education institutions, schools of all levels and categories, and other educational institutions shall provide education for persons with disabilities in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations and relevant national laws and regulations; they shall not reject the admission of persons with disabilities who meet the conditions prescribed by laws and regulations." Article 29: "Regular vocational schools shall not refuse to admit persons with disabilities who meet the admission standards prescribed by the state, and regular vocational training institutions shall actively recruit persons with disabilities for enrollment." The regulations also provide that for school-age children and adolescents with disabilities who require dedicated care and cannot attend school in person, the administrative department of education under the county-level people's government shall make overall arrangements to implement compulsory education through methods such as providing home-delivered teaching or distance education, and incorporate them into student status management.
