Article 20 provides that the administrative department of education under the county-level people's government shall, in concert with the administrative department of health, the civil affairs department, and the Disabled Persons' Federation, establish an Expert Committee on Education for Persons with Disabilities composed of experts in education, psychology, rehabilitation, social work, and other fields, which evaluates their physical condition, capacity to receive education, and adaptability to school study and life, and offers recommendations on admission and transfer; evaluation results are the child's private information, and relevant units and personnel have a duty of confidentiality. Article 23 provides that for disabled students attending classes in regular schools (inclusive education), the curriculum plans, curriculum standards, and teaching materials of regular compulsory education may be applied, but learning requirements for them may possess moderate flexibility. Article 52 provides that where persons with disabilities participate in national educational examinations and require necessary support conditions and reasonable accommodations, they may submit an application (Nationwide, implemented since May 1, 2017).
entries.sources: State Council (2017). Regulations on Education for Persons with Disabilities (Articles 7, 20, 23, 29, 52). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2017-02/23/content_5170264.htm>
entries.notes: A school orally claiming "we don't have the accommodations here" does not count. Demand that they provide a written response, and take that written response to the county-level education bureau. The evaluation is conducted by an expert committee commissioned by the education bureau. The clause in Article 23 stating that "learning requirements may possess moderate flexibility" is very useful; it can be cited when encountering a school using academic performance as an excuse to pressure a student to withdraw. For how to preserve evidence when a child is bullied at school and what mandatory procedures schools must follow, see Item 3 of Section 30 (Campus Bullying). For reasonable accommodations in the Gaokao, see Item 13 of this section (Reasonable Accommodations). The beneficiary is your child.

entries.title: You Can Still Take the Driver's License Test Even If You Have Lost Your Right Lower Limb or Both Lower Limbs; the Permitted Vehicle Type Is Designated as C5
entries.cost: Tuition is comparable to regular driver's licenses, running several thousand yuan in most places. The vehicle must be modified for manual hand controls. A physical examination is required once every three years.
entries.summary: Individuals who have lost or cannot move their right lower limb or both lower limbs, but are able to sit upright independently and meet upper limb requirements, can take the driving test for a specialized disability automatic transmission passenger car license, coded C5. Those missing one palm while the other hand meets criteria may also apply. Individuals with monocular visual impairments or hearing impairments each have vehicle types they are eligible to drive. Physical examinations must be performed at designated specialized hospitals recognized by the province.
entries.benefit: Annex 1 of the *Provisions on the Application for and Use of Motor Vehicle Driving Licenses* specifies physical conditions in great detail. Item 8: "Where the right lower limb or both lower limbs are missing or have lost motor function but the individual is able to sit upright independently, and the upper limbs comply with the provisions of Item 5 of this paragraph, an application may be submitted for a motor vehicle driving license for the permitted driving vehicle type of specialized small automatic passenger cars for persons with disabilities. Where one palm is missing, the thumb of the other hand is intact, at least two other fingers are intact, upper limb and finger motor functions are normal, and the lower limbs comply with the provisions of Item 6 of this paragraph, an application may be submitted for a motor vehicle driving license for the permitted driving vehicle type of specialized small automatic passenger cars for persons with disabilities." Item 6: Where only the left lower limb is missing or has lost motor function, but the right lower limb is normal, an application may be submitted for the permitted vehicle type of small automatic cars. The vision category: "Where there is monocular visual impairment, the naked-eye vision or corrected vision of the better eye reaches 5.0 or above on the logarithmic visual acuity chart, and the horizontal field of vision reaches 150 degrees," an application may be submitted for the permitted vehicle types of small cars, small automatic cars, low-speed goods vehicles, three-wheeled motor vehicles, and specialized small automatic passenger cars for persons with disabilities. The hearing category: Those with hearing impairment who can distinguish the direction of sound sources while wearing hearing aids may apply for the permitted vehicle types of small cars and small automatic cars, and must wear hearing aids when driving. Article 85 provides that when handling business related to driving licenses for specialized small automatic passenger cars for persons with disabilities, the submitted certification of physical condition shall be issued by a specialized medical institution recognized by the provincial administrative department of health. Holders of this permitted vehicle type must undergo a physical examination once every three years and submit a certification of physical condition within 30 days after the scoring cycle ends. Article 78 provides that when driving, a dedicated disability motor vehicle sign shall be displayed on the vehicle body according to regulations. Article 79, Paragraph 1, Item 9 provides that for those holding the permitted driving type of specialized small automatic passenger cars for persons with disabilities, "who fail to submit a certification of physical condition within one year following the conclusion of three scoring cycles," the vehicle administration office shall cancel the driving license (Nationwide, amended by Ministry of Public Security Order No. 172, effective January 1, 2025). Article 23, Paragraph 1, Item 5 of the *Provisions on the Registration of Motor Vehicles* provides that where auxiliary driving control devices for persons with physical disabilities are installed, removed, or replaced on small or miniature automatic passenger cars, the motor vehicle owner shall apply for modification recordation with the vehicle administration office at the place of registration within 30 days of the modification. Article 24 provides that when processing, identity certification, the vehicle travel license, the motor vehicle safety technical inspection qualification certificate, and the installation qualification certificate of the auxiliary driving control device must be submitted, and the motor vehicle must be presented for inspection (Ministry of Public Security Order No. 164).
entries.sources: Ministry of Public Security Order No. 172. Provisions on the Application for and Use of Motor Vehicle Driving Licenses (Articles 78, 79, 85, Annex 1). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2025/issue_11866/202502/content_7004031.html>; Ministry of Public Security Order No. 164. Provisions on the Registration of Motor Vehicles (Articles 23, 24). <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2022/content_5682413.htm>; Road Traffic Safety Law of the People's Republic of China (2021 Revision, Articles 58, 119). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817ab231eb017abd617ef70519>
entries.notes: Another route with a much lower threshold is motorized wheelchairs for persons with disabilities. Article 119 of the *Road Traffic Safety Law* classifies motorized wheelchairs for persons with disabilities whose design speed, unladen mass, and exterior dimensions conform to national standards as non-motor vehicles, meaning no driver's license is required; Article 58 provides that when motorized wheelchairs for persons with disabilities travel in non-motor vehicle lanes, the maximum speed shall not exceed 15 kilometers per hour. For C5 vehicles, auxiliary driving control devices for persons with physical disabilities must be installed, an installation qualification certificate must be obtained after installation, and modification recordation must be completed at the vehicle administration office within 30 days. Failure to submit a certification of physical condition within one year after the conclusion of three scoring cycles will lead to the cancellation of the driving license.

entries.title: Perform Rehabilitation in Regular Institutions with a Rehabilitation Medicine Department; Follow the Therapist's Guidance on Intensity, as More Intense Is Not Always Better (Evidence from Stroke)
entries.cost: Inpatient rehabilitation costs several hundred yuan per day; the out-of-pocket portion varies by location. Time is measured in months. Daily practice is required, which is very tedious.
entries.summary: After a stroke, admission to an organized stroke unit with coordinated care results in more patients still alive and living at home after one year. However, do not increase the intensity on your own: exercising earlier, more frequently, and with greater volume within 24 hours post-stroke actually led to worse outcomes at three months. How much to train and when to train should follow the guidance of the rehabilitation department and therapists.
entries.benefit: A Cochrane systematic review included 29 trials and 5,902 participants, comparing organized inpatient stroke unit care with other models of care. The review described stroke units as multidisciplinary teams utilizing standard protocols to manage common post-stroke issues, providing coordinated multidisciplinary care. At final follow-up (median 1 year), the odds ratio for adverse outcomes (death, dependency, or requiring institutional care) was 0.77 (95% CI 0.69–0.87, credible interval), the odds ratio for death was 0.76 (95% CI 0.66–0.88), and the odds ratio for death or dependency was 0.75 (95% CI 0.66–0.85), with moderate-quality evidence. Converted to absolute numbers, for every 100 individuals receiving stroke unit care, 2 more survive, 6 more live at home, and 6 more achieve independent daily living. On the other hand, the AVERT trial randomized 2,104 patients across 56 acute stroke units in 5 countries, comparing "usual care" with "usual care plus very early high-intensity mobilization." At three months, 480 patients (46%) in the very early mobilization group achieved a favorable outcome (modified Rankin Scale score 0–2), compared with 525 patients (50%) in the usual care group, yielding an adjusted odds ratio of 0.73 (95% CI 0.59–0.90, P=0.004). Deaths were 88 versus 72, showing no statistically significant difference (odds ratio 1.34, 95% CI 0.93–1.93, P=0.113).
entries.sources: Langhorne P, Ramachandra S; Stroke Unit Trialists' Collaboration (2020). Organised inpatient (stroke unit) care for stroke: network meta-analysis. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 4:CD000197. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD000197.pub4>；AVERT Trial Collaboration group (2015). Efficacy and safety of very early mobilisation within 24 h of stroke onset (AVERT): a randomised controlled trial. Lancet, 386(9988):46-55. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(15)60690-0>
entries.notes: Controversy: Both pieces of evidence originate from stroke; extrapolating them to other causes of disability such as spinal cord injury, amputation, or burns constitutes an external extrapolation. The AVERT trial demonstrates that "earlier and more aggressive is better" does not hold true; it does not mean "early mobilization is useless." In that trial, the vast majority of patients in both groups mobilized out of bed within 24 hours; the difference lay in frequency and total dose. When choosing an institution, check whether it has a Department of Rehabilitation Medicine and dedicated full-time physical therapists and occupational therapists, rather than merely relying on the word "rehabilitation" on the signage. This principle is inferred from the stroke unit's reliance on multidisciplinary team care. For how to transfer between grassroots facilities and tertiary hospitals and how deductibles are calculated, see Item 1 of Section 24 (Stepwise Referrals). For community rehabilitation and assistive device provisioning, see Item 7 of this section (Inquire Comprehensively at the County Disabled Persons' Federation).

entries.title: Get Fitted with a Hearing Aid When Hearing Declines; the Reason to Fit It Is to Hear, Not to Prevent Dementia
entries.cost: Hearing aids cost several thousand to tens of thousands of yuan, mostly out-of-pocket. They require professional fitting and several rounds of adjustment.
entries.summary: The claim that "wearing hearing aids prevents dementia" is currently unsupported by solid evidence. A three-year trial involving nearly 1,000 participants found no difference overall. A difference was observed only in the subset of individuals who were already at higher baseline risk of cognitive decline. Therefore, the reason to get a hearing aid is for immediate benefits—hearing clearly right now, being able to converse with people, and hearing traffic when crossing the street—not for your brain decades later.
entries.benefit: The ACHIEVE trial was conducted in 4 communities in the United States, enrolling 977 individuals aged 70 to 84 with untreated hearing loss and no substantial cognitive impairment. Participants were randomized into two groups: one received a hearing intervention (hearing counseling and hearing aid fitting), and the other received a health education control, with follow-ups every 6 months. The primary endpoint was the 3-year change in global cognitive score. In the primary analysis pooling the two source populations, there was no significant difference between the two groups: −0.200 (95% CI −0.256 to −0.144) in the hearing intervention group versus −0.202 (95% CI −0.258 to −0.145) in the control group, with a difference of 0.002 (95% CI −0.077 to 0.081), P=0.96. A prespecified sensitivity analysis showed that the intervention effect differed between the two source populations (interaction P=0.010). Participants originating from the long-term observational cardiovascular health study were older, had more risk factors for cognitive decline, and had lower baseline cognitive scores. In this subgroup of 238 individuals, the hearing intervention group experienced 48% less 3-year cognitive decline (difference 0.191, 95% CI 0.022–0.360, P=0.027). Among the other 739 newly recruited healthy volunteers, there was no significant difference between the two groups (difference −0.061, 95% CI −0.151 to 0.028, P=0.18). The investigators concluded that hearing intervention may reduce 3-year cognitive change in populations at higher risk of cognitive decline, but not in populations at lower risk. The trial reported no study-related serious adverse events.
entries.sources: Lin FR, Pike JR, Albert MS, et al.; ACHIEVE Collaborative Research Group (2023). Hearing intervention versus health education control to reduce cognitive decline in older adults with hearing loss in the USA (ACHIEVE): a multicentre, randomised controlled trial. Lancet, 402(10404):786-797. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(23)01406-X>
entries.notes: Controversy: The claim that "hearing aids reduce cognitive decline by nearly half" comes from the figures in a subgroup of 238 individuals in this trial, which was not its primary outcome; the primary outcome was that there was no difference between the two groups. "Fitting hearing aids" and "preventing dementia" should be viewed separately: the former should be done, while the latter should not be used as the justification. Candidates with hearing disabilities taking the Gaokao may be exempted from foreign language listening tests; see Item 13 of this section (Reasonable Accommodations). Drivers with hearing impairments must wear hearing aids when driving; see Item 15 of this section (C5).

entries.title: Claiming That an Adult "Cannot Manage Their Own Affairs" Requires Applying to a Court for Determination; Family Members' Word Alone Does Not Count
entries.cost: Applying to a court does not incur case acceptance court fees. If an appraisal/expert evaluation is required, appraisal fees are charged separately and are generally paid by the applicant. The law requires proceedings to conclude within 30 days, though undergoing appraisals will prolong the duration.
entries.summary: Whether an adult has "no capacity for civil conduct" or "limited capacity for civil conduct" can only be determined by a court. Family members, work units, and neighborhood committees cannot decide this on their own. An application must be submitted to the court by an interested party or relevant organization. Conversely, if their mental capacity or psychiatric health recovers, an application may also be filed to recognize the restoration of their capacity for conduct. This procedure serves as a restriction as well as a protection.
entries.benefit: Article 21 of the *Civil Code*: "An adult who is unable to recognize their own conduct is a person without capacity for civil conduct, and their statutory agent shall represent them in performing civil legal acts." Article 22: "An adult who is unable to fully recognize their own conduct is a person with limited capacity for civil conduct, and the performance of civil legal acts by them shall be represented by their statutory agent or subject to the consent or ratification of their statutory agent; however, they may independently perform civil legal acts that purely yield benefits or civil legal acts that are commensurate with their intelligence and mental health condition." Article 24: "For an adult who is unable to recognize or fully recognize their own conduct, their interested parties or relevant organizations may apply to the people's court to have that adult recognized as a person without capacity for civil conduct or a person with limited capacity for civil conduct." The same article also provides that after such recognition, upon application by the individual, an interested party, or a relevant organization, the people's court may, in accordance with the condition of recovery of their intelligence and mental health, recognize them as having restored limited capacity for civil conduct or full capacity for civil conduct. Relevant organizations include: residents' committees, villagers' committees, schools, medical institutions, women's federations, disabled persons' federations, legally established organizations for the elderly, civil affairs departments, etc. Article 23 provides that the guardian of a person without capacity for civil conduct or a person with limited capacity for civil conduct is their statutory agent (Nationwide, implemented since January 1, 2021). The procedural rules are set out in the Special Procedures chapter of the *Civil Procedure Law*. Article 198: The application is filed with the basic-level people's court where the citizen resides, and "the application shall state the facts and grounds regarding that citizen's absence of capacity for civil conduct or limited capacity for civil conduct." Article 199: "After accepting the application, the people's court shall, when necessary, arrange an expert evaluation of the citizen requested to be determined as lacking capacity for civil conduct or having limited capacity for civil conduct." Article 187: Cases handled under special procedures "shall be concluded within thirty days from the date of case filing or within thirty days following the expiration of the public notice period"; extensions required under special circumstances must be approved by the president of the court. Article 8 of the *Measures for the Payment of Litigation Costs*: For cases tried according to the special procedures prescribed in the Civil Procedure Law, no case acceptance fee shall be paid. Article 12: For expenses incurred during litigation such as appraisal fees, the people's court shall determine that the parties pay them directly to the relevant institutions based on the principle of "whoever makes the claim bears the burden".
entries.sources: Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (Articles 21, 22, 23, 24, 171). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5c500bf>; Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Amendment, Articles 187, 198, 199). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081818a21dc13018b425303b7086d>; State Council Decree No. 481. Measures on the Payment of Litigation Costs (Articles 8, 12). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_6929.htm>
entries.notes: The application follows the special procedure of the court, with a statutory trial time limit of 30 days, which is shorter than ordinary civil cases, but conducting an appraisal takes additional time. The application must clearly state the facts and grounds, and hospital diagnostic certificates are generally attached—this is the author's experience. When necessary, the court shall conduct an appraisal; appraisal fees follow the rule of "whoever makes the claim bears the cost" and are generally paid by the applicant. If you sign for someone or dispose of their property without going through this procedure and without being their statutory agent, according to Article 171 of the Civil Code, it has no effect on them without ratification; even if a house has been sold, it may have to be returned. This is deduced by the author from legal provisions. One more point to keep in mind: limited capacity for civil conduct does not mean being unable to do anything at all. Acts commensurate with their intelligence and mental state, as well as acts purely for their benefit, can be done by themselves; do not handle everything on their behalf across the board. For how guardians are determined, see Item 19 of this section (Guardians).

entries.title: Adult guardians are determined in statutory order; if the ward injures someone else, the guardian pays compensation
entries.cost: Costs no money. When disputes arise, they must be resolved through the neighborhood committee, villagers' committee, civil affairs department, or the court.
entries.summary: After an adult loses capacity for civil conduct, guardians are designated in order: spouse, parents and children, other close relatives, and finally other individuals or organizations approved by neighborhood committees and other relevant bodies. When disputes arise, designation is made by the neighborhood committee, villagers' committee, or civil affairs department; if unsatisfied, seek resolution from the court. While lucid, one can designate a future guardian in writing. If the ward injures someone else, compensation is first paid from their own funds, and any shortfall is covered by the guardian.
entries.benefit: Article 28 of the Civil Code: For an adult with no capacity for civil conduct or with limited capacity for civil conduct, the following persons who are capable of acting as guardians shall serve as guardians in the following order: "(1) spouse; (2) parents, children; (3) other close relatives; (4) other individuals or organizations willing to serve as guardians, provided that consent is obtained from the residents' committee, villagers' committee, or civil affairs department at the domicile of the ward." Article 31: Where there is a dispute over the determination of a guardian, the residents' committee, villagers' committee, or civil affairs department at the domicile of the ward shall make the designation; anyone dissatisfied with the designation may apply to the people's court for designation, or may apply directly to the people's court. When making the designation, "the true intention of the ward shall be respected, and the principle of what is in the best interests of the ward shall be followed." If the rights and interests of the ward are left unprotected prior to designation, the residents' committee, villagers' committee, relevant organizations prescribed by law, or civil affairs department shall serve as temporary guardians. Article 33: "An adult with full capacity for civil conduct may, through prior consultation with close relatives or other individuals or organizations willing to serve as guardians, determine their own guardian in written form." Article 1188: "Where a person with no capacity for civil conduct or with limited capacity for civil conduct causes damage to others, the guardian shall bear tort liability. If the guardian has fulfilled guardian duties, their tort liability may be mitigated." If the person has property, compensation expenses shall be paid from their own property; any shortfall shall be compensated by the guardian. Article 1189: Where a guardian entrusts guardian duties to another person, the guardian shall still bear tort liability; if the entrustee is at fault, the entrustee shall bear corresponding liability (National, effective January 1, 2021)
entries.sources: Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (Articles 28, 31, 33, 1188, 1189). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5c500bf>
entries.notes: Article 33 refers to voluntary guardianship (guardianship by mandate). Selecting the person in written form while still lucid can eliminate more than half of subsequent disputes; for specific details on how to write it, see Section 17, Item 1 (Voluntary Guardianship). Be careful regarding the compensation part: handing a person over to a care facility or relatives for care still leaves the liability on the guardian; the entrustee bears corresponding liability only when they are at fault themselves. Therefore, buying guardian liability insurance for the ward is meaningful. Article 78 of the Mental Health Law also stipulates that where a guardian abandons a patient or fails to perform guardianship duties, causing damage, they shall bear liability for compensation in accordance with the law.

entries.title: If refused hiring, denied conversion to regular status, or paid less due to disability, you can sue, but calculate process costs first
entries.cost: Attorney fees range from several thousand to tens of thousands of yuan, paid out of pocket. First-instance ordinary procedure is required to be completed within 6 months, which can be extended. Evidence must be preserved by yourself.
entries.summary: The law prohibits discrimination against persons with disabilities in recruitment, conversion to regular employment, promotion, professional title evaluation, remuneration, and social insurance. You can file a complaint with the competent authorities or sue in court. However, even if you win the lawsuit, the opposing party will not pay your attorney fees. Therefore, file a complaint first, apply for legal aid at the same time, and only then consider going to court.
entries.benefit: Article 3 of the Law on the Protection of Disabled Persons: "Discrimination on the basis of disability is prohibited. Insulting or infringing upon persons with disabilities is prohibited." Article 38: "No discrimination against disabled persons shall be practiced in the recruitment, conversion to regular employment, promotion, professional title evaluation, labor remuneration, living welfare, rest and vacation, social insurance, and other aspects of workers." The same article also provides that the employing units of disabled workers shall provide appropriate working conditions and labor protection according to the characteristics of disabled workers, and renovate workplaces, work equipment, and living facilities based on actual needs. Article 64: "Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, discrimination is practiced against disabled persons in the recruitment of workers and other aspects, the competent department concerned shall order correction; disabled workers may file a lawsuit in the people's court in accordance with the law." Article 4 of the Regulations on the Employment of Disabled Persons: "Discrimination against disabled persons in employment is prohibited." Article 13: Employing units shall not discriminate against disabled workers in promotion, salary grade advancement, professional title evaluation, remuneration, social insurance, living welfare, and other aspects. Article 42 of the Legal Aid Law provides that where an applicant possesses materials proving that they belong to "specific groups such as minors, the elderly, and disabled persons who have no fixed source of living," verification of their financial difficulty status shall be waived. Article 45 provides that when providing legal aid services to the elderly and disabled persons, legal aid institutions shall provide accessible facilities, equipment, and services based on actual circumstances (National)
entries.sources: Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Disabled Persons (Articles 3, 38, 64). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f135f46016f1d134c88132b>; State Council (2007). Regulations on the Employment of Disabled Persons (Articles 4, 13). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_6646.htm>; Legal Aid Law of the People's Republic of China (Articles 42, 45). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817b6472a3017b6577820f0061>
entries.notes: Process costs must be calculated first. First-instance ordinary procedure is required to be completed within 6 months, which can be extended; summary procedure takes 3 months. Attorney fees are not among the litigation costs listed in Article 6 of the Measures on the Payment of Litigation Costs, and the "burden on the losing party" in Article 29 does not include attorney fees. Therefore, take two low-cost routes first: lodge a complaint with human resources and social security departments or the disabled persons' federation, so the competent department can order correction; at the same time, apply for legal aid, as Article 42 waives the financial difficulty verification for persons with disabilities. Gathering evidence is the most difficult hurdle. When rejected during interviews, the other party rarely leaves written reasons; if you can record audio or preserve chat records, do so. For those already employed, pursue arbitration as a labor dispute; for evidence retention and time limits, see Section 19, Item 8 (Retaining Evidence Before Resignation). The beneficiary is yourself.

entries.title: If unable to urinate after a spinal cord injury, decide the urination method together with a doctor; do not leave a catheter in place long-term without supervision, and undergo lifelong regular kidney and bladder checks
entries.cost: Self-timed catheterization must be done four to six times a day, taking several minutes each time, and catheters must be continuously purchased. Follow-up examinations occur every one to two years, requiring visits to urology or rehabilitation departments. The difficulty lies in doing it every single day without interruption for decades.
entries.summary: If you cannot urinate after a spinal cord injury, you must rely on methods such as catheterization to empty the bladder. In British data spanning seventy years, over ten percent of deaths were related to the genitourinary system. Among people with long-term indwelling catheters, the complication rate is about twice as high as that of scheduled self-catheterization. Regardless of the method used, kidneys and bladders require lifelong regular examinations.
entries.benefit: Two British spinal cord injury centers examined 5,483 patients with traumatic spinal cord injuries. They were injured between 1943 and 2010, all survived the first year after injury, and were followed up until the end of 2014. A total of 2,322 died, of whom 2,170 had reliable causes of death. The leading causes of death were respiratory diseases 29.3%, circulatory diseases 26.7%, neoplasms 13.9%, and genitourinary diseases 11.5%. After adjusting for age differences, the genitourinary mortality rate was higher than that of the general population; although it has been declining over the years, it remains elevated. Another US study reviewed medical records of 316 patients with traumatic spinal cord injuries, with an average follow-up of 18.3 years post-injury, grouped by bladder management method. The proportions of people experiencing complications were 53.5% in the long-term transurethral indwelling catheter group, 27.2% in the clean intermittent catheterization group, 32.4% in the spontaneous voiding group, and 44.4% in the suprapubic cystostomy group. Complications included infections, stones, urethral injury, and imaging abnormalities. This was only a retrospective review of medical records, not a randomized trial. The European Association of Urology 2026 guidelines state that transurethral indwelling catheters carry many complications and high urinary tract infection risks, and should be avoided whenever possible. The same applies to suprapubic cystostomy, only to a lesser degree. The guidelines also specify that long-term follow-up must be conducted lifelong to check for risks of upper urinary tract damage and renal failure. The follow-up interval in most cases does not exceed one to two years. High-risk individuals undergo ultrasound approximately every six months, with annual physical examinations and urinalysis. Section 3.4.2.e of the guidelines states that both intermittent catheterization and indwelling catheters are standard practice for individuals who cannot empty the bladder, recommending shared decision-making between the physician and the individual. Among people with spinal cord injuries, quality-of-life scores for intermittent catheterization were worse than those for indwelling catheters, especially for those experiencing more than 4 urinary tract infections a year. In an observational study, 42.1% of people using intermittent catheterization discontinued it within 12 months, mainly due to inconvenience, leakage, and increased infections. The guidelines state that silicone catheters are preferable because they are less prone to encrustation, and latex allergies are frequent among patients with neurological diseases. Section 3.5.1 lists the most common signs of urinary tract infection in such patients: fever, new or worsening incontinence, increased spasticity, fatigue, cloudy urine with worsened odor, renal or bladder pain, and autonomic dysreflexia
entries.sources: Savic G, DeVivo MJ, Frankel HL, Jamous MA, Soni BM, Charlifue S (2017). Causes of death after traumatic spinal cord injury - a 70-year British study. Spinal Cord, 55(10):891-897. <https://doi.org/10.1038/sc.2017.64>; Weld KJ, Dmochowski RR (2000). Effect of bladder management on urological complications in spinal cord injured patients. Journal of Urology, 163(3):768-772. <https://doi.org/10.1016/s0022-5347(05)67800-7>; European Association of Urology (2026). EAU Guidelines on Neuro-Urology (Sections 3.3.8, 3.4.2.e, 3.5.1, 3.7). <https://uroweb.org/guidelines/neuro-urology/chapter/the-guideline>
entries.notes: Controversy: The same guideline lists both intermittent catheterization and indwelling catheters as standard practices, requiring doctors and patients to decide together. Among people with spinal cord injuries, quality-of-life scores for intermittent catheterization were actually worse, especially noticeable in those with more than 4 urinary tract infections a year. Over 40% of people using intermittent catheterization stopped using it within one year. Therefore, for those with impaired hand function or no family members to help, an indwelling catheter can be a reasonable choice; this is deduced by the author from the above points. For those using indwelling catheters, the guideline recommends using silicone tubes. Do not make decisions entirely on your own, and do not leave a catheter inserted for years without follow-up checks. New-onset leakage, cloudy and foul-smelling urine, worsened spasticity, and fever may indicate a urinary tract infection and should be examined. Allowing the bladder to become overly full can trigger autonomic dysreflexia; see Item 1 of this section (Sudden Severe Headache). The original text of domestic neurogenic bladder guidelines could not be retrieved and is not cited. The beneficiary is yourself.

chapters.title: Avoid Mishaps with Household Over-the-Counter Medications
chapters.intro:
Fever reducers, pain relievers, cold medicines, stomach medicines, and antidiarrheals can often be bought on your own at pharmacies. Being able to buy them without a prescription does not mean you can take them however you like. This section does not discuss which medicine to take for each illness; it only highlights a few actions where a single step can prevent severe consequences.

Entries in this section are all categorized under mortality metrics. Most focus on severe outcomes such as liver failure, gastrointestinal bleeding, and neonatal renal failure, while a few examine headaches and reaction times while driving. Benefits are mostly framed as "avoiding one severe accident"; research cannot provide figures on "what percentage risk is reduced by doing this." Therefore, benefit magnitudes are judged based on the severity of consequences, with the basis explained in the notes of each entry.

For matters already covered elsewhere, only directions are provided here. For what to do first if medications or cleaning products are accidentally ingested, see Section 13, Item 20 (Accidental Ingestion). For completing medication courses for chronic diseases as prescribed, see Section 16, Item 1 (Take Medications for the Full Duration as Prescribed). For prescription verification when buying prescription drugs online, see Section 28, Item 6 (Get Prescriptions at the Hospital for Weight-Loss Drugs).

Beneficiaries of the entries in this section are yourself and your family, belonging to the top two tiers.

entries.title: Before taking two cold medicines or painkillers simultaneously, check the ingredient list first; acetaminophen can only come from one, and go to the hospital that day even if feeling no discomfort after an overdose
entries.cost: Costs no money. Taking a glance at the ingredient list of each medicine box takes one or two minutes.
entries.summary: Many cold medications contain acetaminophen; taking two boxes together means taking a double dose, and overdosing harms the liver. In the United States, nearly 30% of patients with acute liver failure caused by it died before receiving a liver transplant. Domestic package inserts recommend a maximum of 2 grams per day, and the US further warns against drinking more than 3 alcoholic beverages daily while taking the medication. If an overdose occurs, go to the hospital immediately even without discomfort; the earlier the antidote is administered, the better.
entries.benefit: Twenty-two hospitals in the United States continuously registered 662 cases of acute liver failure over 6 years. Among them, 275 cases (42%) were caused by acetaminophen, with a median ingested dose of 24 grams. Among these 275 people, 131 (48%) took an overdose accidentally, not intentionally. Among those who overdosed accidentally, 38% simultaneously took two or more medications containing this ingredient. Among these 275 people, 27% died before receiving a liver transplant, and 8% underwent liver transplantation. In 2020, the National Medical Products Administration required over-the-counter package inserts to state: excessive use will cause severe liver damage, and it is recommended that the maximum daily amount not exceed 2 grams. Package inserts must also state to avoid combined use with drugs containing acetaminophen or other antipyretic analgesics as much as possible. US regulations require the first item of warnings for such over-the-counter drugs to clearly state three liver damage scenarios: exceeding the maximum daily dose, taking with other drugs containing acetaminophen, and having 3 or more alcoholic drinks daily while using this product. The same announcement from the NMPA also required extended-release package inserts to specify: in case of accidental overdose by adults or children, seek medical attention immediately, regardless of whether there is discomfort. The antidote is called N-acetylcysteine; its package insert states it should be administered as early as possible, with satisfactory efficacy within 12 hours and poorer efficacy beyond 24 hours. A US multicenter study from 1976 to 1985 tracked 2,540 overdose patients treated with this antidote. Among patients deemed likely to develop liver damage based on plasma drug concentrations, 6.1% developed liver injury when medication was initiated within 10 hours. When initiated between 10 and 24 hours, 26.4% developed liver injury. When initiated within 8 hours after overdose, it exerted a protective effect regardless of how high plasma drug concentrations were.
entries.sources: Larson AM, Polson J, Fontana RJ, et al.; Acute Liver Failure Study Group (2005). Acetaminophen-induced acute liver failure: results of a United States multicenter, prospective study. Hepatology, 42(6):1364-1372. <https://doi.org/10.1002/hep.20948>; Announcement of the National Medical Products Administration on Revising the Package Inserts for Acetaminophen Immediate-Release and Extended-Release Formulations (No. 15 of 2020) and Annex 1 "Revision Requirements for Prescription Drug Package Inserts of Acetaminophen Immediate-Release Formulations", Annex 2 "Revision Requirements for Over-the-Counter Drug Package Inserts of Acetaminophen Immediate-Release Formulations", Annex 3 "Revision Requirements for Package Inserts of Acetaminophen Extended-Release Formulations" (reposted by Hunan Provincial Medical Products Administration). <http://mpa.hunan.gov.cn/mpa/xxgk/tzgg/wjtz/202003/t20200311_11809335.html>; 21 CFR 201.326(a)(1)(iii)(A) Liver warning. <https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-201/subpart-G/section-201.326>; Smilkstein MJ, Knapp GL, Kulig KW, Rumack BH (1988). Efficacy of oral N-acetylcysteine in the treatment of acetaminophen overdose: analysis of the national multicenter study (1976 to 1985). New England Journal of Medicine, 319(24):1557-1562. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJM198812153192401>; MedlinePlus. Acetaminophen (In case of emergency/overdose). <https://medlineplus.gov/druginfo/meds/a681004.html>
entries.notes: Acetaminophen is also called paracetamol. If the generic name of a compound cold medication contains the characters for 'an-fen' (referring to paracetamol/acetaminophen)—such as paracetamol and pseudoephedrine, or paracetamol, caffeine, and chlorpheniramine—it contains this ingredient. If you are unsure, bring all the medicine boxes to show the pharmacist at the drugstore. Rated B because the American figures come from a case registry without a control group, making it impossible to calculate how many adverse events can be prevented by checking the ingredients list. The benefit is rated 'Large' based on consequences: nearly 30% of acute liver failure cases directly result in death. The figure showing that earlier administration of the antidote is better comes from a non-randomized multicenter observational study, compared only against historical cases.

entries.title: Do not use aspirin, nimesulide, or metamizole (analgin) for children's fevers; do not give cold medications containing metamizole to minors; measure liquid fever medications using the measuring device provided in the package
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Just check the generic name and ingredients list when buying fever medication.
entries.summary: Aspirin is linked to Reye's syndrome, a condition that damages the brain and liver, causing death in approximately 30% of affected children. Nimesulide is contraindicated in children under 12, and metamizole is contraindicated under 18. Measure liquid fever medications with the measuring tool included in the medicine box; household spoons vary widely in size. Drops and oral solutions may differ in concentration—differing by threefold in a US example—so do not feed the same milliliter dose if switching dosage forms.
entries.benefit: Reye's syndrome can cause encephalopathy and fatty liver degeneration, typically occurring after influenza or chickenpox. In nationwide US surveillance from 1981 through 1997, 1,207 cases were reported in individuals under 18 years of age. Salicylate, an ingredient in medications such as aspirin, was detectable in the blood of 82% of affected children. The overall case fatality rate was 31%. Warnings regarding salicylate medications began being issued in 1980. That year saw 555 reported cases, the peak, and from 1987 onward, no more than 36 cases were reported per year. In 2011, the State Food and Drug Administration mandated that oral nimesulide preparations are contraindicated in children under 12 years of age. In 2020, the National Medical Products Administration mandated that metamizole tablets are contraindicated in children and adolescents under 18 years of age. Metamizole-containing Compound Artemisinin and Metamizole Tablets, Zhongganling Tablets, and Zhongganling Capsules are likewise contraindicated under 18 years of age. For measuring medication, consider the US figures: in 2011, the US FDA clarified that infant acetaminophen drops contained 80 mg per 0.8 mL, while oral liquid for older children contained 160 mg per 5 mL. Based on these two numbers, for the same 1 mL volume, the medication dose in the drops is about 3 times that of the oral liquid. The US FDA stated that having both concentrations coexist easily causes confusion, leading to accidental overdoses in children, and measuring devices from different products must never be mixed. A Greek study measured 71 teaspoons and 49 tablespoons across 25 households, finding that when filled with water, capacities ranged from 2.5 mL to 7.3 mL. In a US emergency department study, 42.5% of parents whose dose units were teaspoons or tablespoons made dosing errors, compared to 27.6% of parents who used only milliliters—adjusted OR 2.3, 95% CI 1.2–4.4 (the odds of dosing error were more than double).
entries.sources: Belay ED, Bresee JS, Holman RC, Khan AS, Shahriari A, Schonberger LB (1999). Reye's syndrome in the United States from 1981 through 1997. New England Journal of Medicine, 340(18):1377-1382. <https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJM199905063401801>; Notice on Strengthening the Administration of the Use of Oral Formulations of Nimesulide (Guo Shi Yao Jian An [2011] No. 209). <https://www.nmpa.gov.cn/xxgk/fgwj/gzwj/gzwjyp/20110515145101552.html>; National Medical Products Administration Announcement on Revising Package Inserts for Metamizole-Related Varieties (2020 No. 34) and Attachments 1 to 3. <https://www.nmpa.gov.cn/directory/web/nmpa/xxgk/ggtg/ypggtg/ypshmshxdgg/20200317171201660.html>; U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Questions and Answers – Important change in concentration for over-the-counter (OTC) liquid acetaminophen marketed for infants. <https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/questions-and-answers-important-change-concentration-over-counter-otc-liquid-acetaminophen-marketed>; Falagas ME, Vouloumanou EK, Plessa E, Peppas G, Rafailidis PI (2010). Inaccuracies in dosing drugs with teaspoons and tablespoons. International Journal of Clinical Practice, 64(9):1185-1189. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1742-1241.2010.02402.x>; Yin HS, Dreyer BP, Ugboaja DC, et al. (2014). Unit of measurement used and parent medication dosing errors. Pediatrics, 134(2):e354-e361. <https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2014-0395>
entries.notes: Metamizole is not a first-choice medication for adults either. The package insert specifies that it can cause agranulocytosis, aplastic anemia, and anaphylactic shock, and should only be used short-term when the condition is acute and severe and no other effective medications are available. Zhongganling sounds like an ordinary cold medication, but it contains metamizole. Ask a pediatrician or pharmacist about which fever medication a child should use and what dosage to give based on body weight. If a child under 3 months old develops a fever, go directly to the hospital; see Section 20, Item 8 (go directly to the hospital at 38 °C). Rated B because the figures for Reye's syndrome come from surveillance reports, and the decrease in cases followed the issuance of warnings chronologically rather than in a controlled trial. Benefit rated 'Large' because after the warnings, cases dropped from 555 per year to under 36.

entries.title: People aged 60 and older, those with a history of stomach bleeding, or those taking anticoagulants or corticosteroids should consult a doctor before taking painkillers like ibuprofen
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Just ask a doctor or pharmacist once.
entries.summary: Painkillers like ibuprofen, naproxen, and aspirin can damage the stomach. In high-dose trials, the risk of stomach bleeding and perforation in people taking ibuprofen was about 4 times that of non-users. The risk is even higher for older adults, people who have had stomach bleeding, people concurrently taking anticoagulants or corticosteroids, and those who drink more than 3 alcoholic drinks a day.
entries.benefit: These medications are called nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs); common examples include ibuprofen, naproxen, and diclofenac. A meta-analysis pooled 280 randomized trials of NSAIDs versus placebo, encompassing a total of 124,513 people. Compared with placebo, the risk of upper gastrointestinal perforation, obstruction, or bleeding was: ibuprofen RR 3.97 (95% CI 2.22–7.10, roughly 4-fold), naproxen 4.22 (2.71–6.56), and diclofenac 1.89 (1.16–3.09). All of these drugs roughly doubled the risk of heart failure. US regulations require over-the-counter NSAIDs to display a stomach bleeding warning. The warning lists six categories of people at higher risk: aged 60 and older, having a history of stomach ulcers or bleeding, taking anticoagulants or corticosteroids, taking other NSAIDs at the same time, drinking 3 or more alcoholic drinks every day while using the drug, or taking more or for a longer time than directed by the insert.
entries.sources: Coxib and traditional NSAID Trialists' (CNT) Collaboration; Bhala N, Emberson J, Merhi A, et al. (2013). Vascular and upper gastrointestinal effects of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs: meta-analyses of individual participant data from randomised trials. Lancet, 382(9894):769-779. <https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(13)60900-9>；21 CFR 201.326(a)(2)(iii)(A) Stomach bleeding warning. <https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-201/subpart-G/section-201.326>
entries.notes: The paper's conclusions pertain to high-dose regimens. For the risk of taking them occasionally for one or two days at label doses, this paper did not provide separate figures. Many compound cold medications also contain these ingredients; taking them along with painkillers results in duplication, so check the ingredients list first. If a doctor has prescribed long-term low-dose aspirin to prevent blood clots, do not discontinue it on your own, and do not add another painkiller on your own. For how to use these drugs for dysmenorrhea and when to get evaluated in gynecology, see Section 3, Item 25 (take painkillers like ibuprofen for dysmenorrhea).

entries.title: If children under 2 years old catch a cold, do not give them compound cold medications and cough suppressants on your own
entries.cost: Costs nothing, and even saves money on medication.
entries.summary: The National Medical Products Administration required warnings to be added to 14 pediatric compound cold medications. The warning states that it is not recommended for parents to administer them to children under 2 on their own; they should be used under the guidance of a physician or pharmacist. In trials conducted in children, neither cough medicines nor antiallergy drugs were more effective than placebo.
entries.benefit: National Medical Products Administration Announcement No. 57 of 2021 revised the package inserts for 14 varieties, including Paracetamol, Pseudoephedrine and Dextromethorphan Oral Solution, Pediatric Paracetamol, Artificial Cow-bezoar and Chlorpheniramine Maleate Granules, and Pediatric Paracetamol and Amantadine Hydrochloride Granules. The newly added boxed warning states: 'It is not recommended for parents or guardians to administer this product to infants and young children under 2 years of age on their own; it should be used under the guidance of a physician or pharmacist.' The precautions added: 'Must be used strictly in accordance with the usage and dosage specified in the package insert to avoid overdose.' They also added: 'Concomitant use of cold medications containing identical or similar active ingredients should be avoided.' A Cochrane systematic review included 29 randomized controlled trials, 10 of which were conducted in children. In the pediatric trials, none of the following classes of drugs performed better than placebo: cough suppressants, antihistamines (antiallergic ingredients), antihistamines combined with decongestants (nasal-unblocking ingredients), and cough suppressants combined with bronchodilators. Twenty-one studies reported adverse effects, with more adverse reactions observed in formulations containing antihistamines and dextromethorphan.
entries.sources: National Medical Products Administration Announcement on Revising the Drug Package Inserts of 14 Varieties Including Paracetamol, Pseudoephedrine and Dextromethorphan Oral Solution (2021 No. 57) and Attachments. <https://www.nmpa.gov.cn/directory/web/nmpa/xxgk/ggtg/ypggtg/ypshmshxdgg/20210423105404141.html>; Smith SM, Schroeder K, Fahey T (2014). Over-the-counter (OTC) medications for acute cough in children and adults in community settings. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (11):CD001831. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD001831.pub5>
entries.notes: Many of these 14 medications have 'an-fen' in their names and contain acetaminophen/paracetamol; taking them alongside fever medications results in duplication; see Section Item 1 (acetaminophen). In that review, one trial found that honey was better than placebo, but honey cannot be fed to infants under 1 year old; see Section 20, Item 6 (honey). Rated B because the review had few trials for each drug class, and the authors did not pool the numbers. Benefit rated 'Moderate' based on the assessment that these drugs offer no proven benefits to young children, while the risks are mainly overdose and ingredient duplication.

entries.title: After 20 weeks of pregnancy, do not take painkillers like ibuprofen on your own
entries.cost: Costs nothing.
entries.summary: Taking medications like ibuprofen after 20 weeks of pregnancy may damage the fetus's kidneys and reduce amniotic fluid. Among such reports received in the US, there have been cases of neonatal death. Doctor-prescribed low-dose aspirin is not included in this.
entries.benefit: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued a safety alert in October 2020. Using NSAIDs around 20 weeks or later in pregnancy may cause fetal kidney problems leading to low amniotic fluid (oligohydramnios). The warning covers both prescription and over-the-counter drugs, including aspirin, ibuprofen, naproxen, diclofenac, and celecoxib. The FDA searched adverse event reports through July 2017 and identified 35 cases of oligohydramnios or neonatal renal insufficiency, all of which were serious outcomes. Among them, 5 resulted in neonatal death, all accompanied by neonatal renal failure. In the medical literature, most cases of oligohydramnios resolved within 72 hours to 6 days after discontinuing the drug. The FDA recommends that pregnant women avoid these medications after 20 weeks unless specifically advised by a physician. Low-dose aspirin at 81 mg, when prescribed by a doctor for specific conditions during pregnancy, is not subject to this restriction. When pain relief or fever reduction is needed, the FDA mentioned that other drugs such as acetaminophen may be used; consult a pharmacist or doctor first.
entries.sources: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (2020-10-15). FDA recommends avoiding use of NSAIDs in pregnancy at 20 weeks or later because they can result in low amniotic fluid. Drug Safety Communication. <https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/fda-recommends-avoiding-use-nsaids-pregnancy-20-weeks-or-later-because-they-can-result-low-amniotic>
entries.notes: The FDA cautions that many over-the-counter medicines for colds, flu, and sleeplessness also contain these ingredients, so check the ingredients list. US over-the-counter labels originally only warned against use during the last 3 months of pregnancy; this change moved the threshold earlier to around 20 weeks. For using low-dose aspirin to prevent preeclampsia, see Section 27, Item 5 (low-dose aspirin). Rated B because the numbers come from adverse event reports, and it is unknown how many people took the medication without complications. Benefit rated 'Moderate' based on the assessment: the outcome is severe, but occurs rarely.

entries.title: If buying omeprazole over-the-counter for acid reflux and heartburn, take it for at most 7 days; go directly to the hospital for difficulty swallowing, hematemesis, or black stools
entries.cost: Costs nothing. Take it for the number of days specified in the package insert.
entries.summary: Omeprazole enteric-coated tablets became available without a prescription starting in 2022, but the package insert specifies taking it on your own for no more than 7 days, and not taking it again within two months. Do not take it on your own if experiencing difficult or painful swallowing, vomiting blood, bloody stools, or black stools, as these may be signals of serious conditions. This medication can also mask the symptoms of gastric cancer and delay diagnosis.
entries.benefit: National Medical Products Administration Announcement No. 68 of 2022 converted omeprazole enteric-coated tablets from prescription to over-the-counter status and released a template package insert. The indications listed in the template are 'short-term relief of heartburn and acid reflux symptoms caused by hyperacidity.' The precautions state: do not use for more than 7 days; if symptoms do not resolve, consult a physician or pharmacist. Do not take again within two months; if symptoms recur, seek medical attention immediately. Do not use when experiencing difficulty or pain swallowing, vomiting blood, bloody stools, or black stools, as these may be signs of a serious condition. When alarm symptoms such as significant weight loss, recurrent vomiting, difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, or black stools occur, malignancy must be ruled out first, because treatment may mask symptoms and delay diagnosis. Individuals aged 55 and older who develop new symptoms or changes in symptoms should consult a physician. Those taking clopidogrel should avoid taking omeprazole concurrently. The reason can be found in the US prescribing information for clopidogrel (Plavix): omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, the enzyme that metabolizes clopidogrel in the body. The insert states: 'omeprazole was shown to reduce significantly the antiplatelet activity of Plavix when given concomitantly or 12 hours apart.' Whether taken together or 12 hours apart, clopidogrel's anti-thrombotic effect is significantly weakened. The uses listed in this prescribing information are acute coronary syndrome, recent myocardial infarction, recent stroke, and established peripheral arterial disease.
entries.sources: National Medical Products Administration Announcement on the Conversion of Omeprazole Enteric-Coated Tablets from Prescription to Over-the-Counter Status (2022 No. 68) and Attachment 2 'Template Package Insert for Over-the-Counter Drugs'. <https://www.nmpa.gov.cn/yaopin/ypggtg/20220826171517123.html>; Sanofi-Aventis U.S. (2025). PLAVIX (clopidogrel) tablets, US prescribing information, sections 1, 5 and 7 (DailyMed). <https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=de8b0b67-eb25-4684-83b5-7ad785314227>
entries.notes: Clopidogrel is an antithrombotic drug, commonly used by people who have suffered a myocardial infarction or stroke. Omeprazole weakens its effect, so those taking it should consult a doctor first. Rated B because these are instructions from package inserts, and no studies have calculated how many adverse events following them avoids. Benefit rated 'Moderate' based on the assessment: it prevents delays in diagnosing stomach bleeding or gastric cancer, though most cases of acid reflux and heartburn are not severe.

entries.title: Do not ask a doctor for antibiotics for a common cold
entries.cost: Costs nothing, and even saves medication money.
entries.summary: Taking antibiotics for a cold does not help you recover any faster than not taking them. When adults take them, the risk of side effects is more than double that of non-users. For purulent nasal discharge lasting less than 10 days, taking antibiotics also offers no definitive benefit.
entries.benefit: A Cochrane systematic review pooled 6 randomized trials involving 1,147 individuals. Comparing antibiotics to placebo for the common cold, there was no significant difference in the proportion of participants who were not cured or had persistent symptoms (RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.60–1.14, difference not significant). The risk of adverse events was 1.8 times that of the placebo group (95% CI 1.01–3.21). Among these, it was 2.62 times in adults (1.32–5.18), with no increase in children (0.91, 0.51–1.63). For acute purulent rhinitis with purulent nasal discharge lasting less than 10 days, taking antibiotics also offered no clear benefit (RR 0.73, 0.47–1.13), while adverse events increased (RR 1.46, 1.10–1.94, about 46% higher). The authors concluded: routine use of antibiotics is not recommended for either condition.
entries.sources: Kenealy T, Arroll B (2025). Antibiotics for the common cold and acute purulent rhinitis. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 11:CD000247. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD000247.pub4>
entries.notes: This edition was re-published in 2025, and the abstract states that literature searches were conducted up to 2013. In China, antibiotics are prescription-only drugs that pharmacies sell only with a prescription; do not take leftover antibiotics at home on your own either. Benefit rated 'Moderate' based on the assessment: it prevents adverse reactions, not death. Do not request IV infusions for a cold either; see Section 6, Item 35 (demanding IV infusions for colds and fevers).

entries.title: Drink oral rehydration salts to rehydrate first when experiencing diarrhea; do not give antidiarrheal medications to children under 5
entries.cost: A box of oral rehydration salts costs a few to a dozen or so yuan; keep a box at home.
entries.summary: The most crucial step in treating diarrhea is rehydration, not stopping diarrhea. Reconstitute oral rehydration salts with water according to package directions and drink it; do not substitute fruit juice beverages, as excess sweetness actually dehydrates the body further. Do not give antidiarrheal medications like loperamide to children under 5; severe cases can cause bowel obstruction and may be fatal.
entries.benefit: The World Health Organization's diarrhea treatment manual states that 'antidiarrheal' and antiemetic medicines have no practical benefit for acute or persistent diarrhea in children. They neither prevent dehydration nor improve nutrition. The original phrasing in the Chinese edition of the manual states: 'Some drugs have dangerous and sometimes fatal side-effects. These drugs must never be given to children under 5 years of age.' Drugs like loperamide that slow bowel motility can cause severe paralytic ileus, which can be fatal, and may also prolong infection. The manual also states that overly sugary drinks such as soft drinks and commercial fruit juices draw water from the body into the gut, causing hypernatremic dehydration. The WHO manual recommends a reduced osmolarity formulation with a total osmolarity of 245 mOsm/L. Compared with the older formulation, it reduced unscheduled intravenous fluid infusions by 33%. A Cochrane review pooling 8 trials found similar results (OR 0.59, 95% CI 0.45–0.79, roughly a 40% reduction).
entries.sources: World Health Organization (2005). The treatment of diarrhoea: a manual for physicians and other senior health workers, 4th revision. <https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/43209> (Chinese edition: The Treatment of Diarrhoea: A manual for physicians and other senior health workers, Section 2.6, downloadable from the same page); Hahn S, Kim S, Garner P (2002). Reduced osmolarity oral rehydration solution for treating dehydration caused by acute diarrhoea in children. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (1):CD002847. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD002847>
entries.notes: When purchasing, check the osmolarity on the package insert and choose a low-osmolarity formulation. The manual clearly states that blood in a child's stool is mostly due to bacterial dysentery; see a doctor to get antibiotics, and do not rely solely on rehydrating at home. The benefit is rated "Moderate" based on judgment: the available numbers compare two types of rehydration salts, not drinking versus not drinking.

entries.title: Do not take painkillers for more than 15 days a month, and combination painkillers for no more than 10 days; otherwise, the headache may be caused by the medication itself
entries.cost: Free. You need to keep track of the number of days you take medication, and resist the urge to take it casually.
entries.summary: Taking painkillers every day whenever frequent headaches strike may make the pain worse the more you take. The International Classification of Headache Disorders calls this medication-overuse headache. Experiencing headaches on 15 or more days a month, and taking regular painkillers on 15 or more days or combination painkillers on 10 or more days, continuously for more than 3 months, meets the diagnostic criteria. Most people improve after stopping the overused medication.
entries.benefit: The International Headache Society's The International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition provides the diagnostic criteria: a person with a preexisting headache disorder who has headaches on 15 or more days per month, while regularly overusing acute headache medication for more than 3 months. For non-opioid analgesics such as acetaminophen, aspirin, and ibuprofen, the threshold for overuse is 15 or more days per month. For combination analgesics, the threshold is 10 or more days per month. Combination analgesics refer to medications combining two or more classes with pain-relieving effects, or containing adjuvant ingredients such as caffeine—for example, acetaminophen plus codeine. If several non-opioid analgesics are taken alternately, the days are counted together. The classification notes clearly state that epidemiological evidence from multiple countries shows that among people who have headaches on 15 or more days per month, more than half fall into this type of headache. Most patients improve after discontinuing the overused medication, and preventive headache treatments also become more effective.
entries.sources: Headache Classification Committee of the International Headache Society (2018). The International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition. Cephalalgia, 38(1):1-211. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0333102417738202>; ICHD-3 online edition 8.2 Medication-overuse headache (including 8.2.3, 8.2.5). <https://ichd-3.org/8-headache-attributed-to-a-substance-or-its-withdrawal/8-2-medication-overuse-headache-moh/>
entries.notes: Painkiller tablets with "ka" (caffeine) in their drug name generally contain added caffeine and count as combination medications with a 10-day limit. If the number of headache days in a month is increasing, visit a neurology department instead of relying solely on taking more pills. The evidence is rated B because the classification criteria provide diagnostic thresholds, not controlled trials. The benefit is rated "Moderate" based on judgment: what it buys back is fewer headache days, without involving mortality.

entries.title: Regularly clear out expired medicines and unused leftover medicines, throw them along with their packaging into hazardous waste bins, and do not keep them at home
entries.cost: Free. Go through your medicine cabinet once a year, taking ten to twenty minutes.
entries.summary: In the United States, nearly half of the medications accidentally ingested by children without adult supervision are prescription tablets. Among accidentally ingested prescription medications, about 30% belong to grandparents. Clearing out unused medications means one fewer thing that children can rummage through. Throw cleared-out medicines along with their packaging into hazardous waste bins, or hand them over to pharmacies that collect old medicines.
entries.benefit: US emergency department surveillance data estimates that from 2004 to 2013, children under 6 years old who accidentally ingested medications without adult supervision accounted for approximately 640,000 emergency department visits (estimated 640,161 visits). In 2013 alone, there were approximately 59,000 visits (59,092 visits). From 2010 to 2013, the most common type was oral prescription tablets, accounting for 45.9%. Among prescription medications, the most common were opioid analgesics (13.8%) and benzodiazepine sedatives/hypnotics (12.7%). In 2017, five US poison control centers surveyed parents who called seeking help. Among children who accidentally ingested prescription medications, 30.7% took their grandparents' medications. More than half (51.5%) of the prescription medications had already been removed from their original packaging by adults before the children got hold of them. In China, the National Catalogue of Hazardous Wastes (2025 Edition) classifies waste pharmaceuticals and their packaging generated in household daily life as hazardous waste within municipal solid waste. Shanghai's waste sorting guidelines classify waste pharmaceuticals as hazardous waste. The guidelines state that waste pharmaceuticals include expired medicines, medicine capsules, tablets, and inner packaging of medicines, and that "discarded medicines should preferably be disposed of together with their packaging." Shanghai also mandates that expired and discarded household medicines collected by pharmacies be assigned temporary transfer points established by district market supervision departments. The US FDA states that the best way to dispose of expired and unused medicines is to take them to a take-back site.
entries.sources: Lovegrove MC, Weidle NJ, Budnitz DS (2015). Trends in Emergency Department Visits for Unsupervised Pediatric Medication Exposures, 2004-2013. Pediatrics, 136(4):e821-e829. <https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2015-2092>; Agarwal M, Lovegrove MC, Geller RJ, et al. (2020). Circumstances Involved in Unsupervised Solid Dose Medication Exposures among Young Children. Journal of Pediatrics, 219:188-195.e6. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jpeds.2019.12.027>; Ministry of Ecology and Environment, et al. (2024). National Catalogue of Hazardous Wastes (2025 Edition), Appendix "List of Exempted Management for Hazardous Wastes", Item 1. <https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2025/issue_11906/202503/content_7011162.html>; Shanghai Municipal Bureau of Landscaping and City Appearance (2024). Guidelines for the Sorting and Disposal of Domestic Waste in Shanghai (2024 Edition) (Hu Lv Rong [2024] No. 278). <https://www.shanghai.gov.cn/gwk/search/content/40b9feaa-53db-472f-8a6b-2c3cf0465def>; Shanghai Municipal Bureau of Landscaping and City Appearance, Shanghai Environmental Protection Bureau, Shanghai Food and Drug Administration (2018). Notice on Standardizing the Whole-Process Management of Hazardous Waste from Domestic Waste Sorting. <https://www.shanghai.gov.cn/nw12344/20200813/0001-12344_57440.html>; U.S. Food and Drug Administration (2025). Where and How to Dispose of Unused Medicines. <https://www.fda.gov/consumers/consumer-updates/where-and-how-dispose-unused-medicines>
entries.notes: Waste sorting directories vary somewhat across regions; follow the directory posted at your residential community's garbage station. Shanghai classifies traditional Chinese medicine dregs as wet waste (food waste), not hazardous waste. Keep retained medications in their original boxes; do not pour them into pill organizers or other bottles, and place them out of reach of children—see Section 13, Item 20 (Accidental Ingestion). Also, do not take leftover antibiotics at home on your own—see Section 34, Item 7 (Antibiotics). In the US, when take-back sites are unavailable, people are advised to mix medicines with coffee grounds or cat litter, seal them in a bag, and toss them into regular trash, while a few potent painkillers are permitted to be flushed down the toilet. This is the US approach; in China, follow local sorting and disposal rules. The evidence is rated B because those US figures are merely registry data, and no studies have quantified how many accidental ingestions can be prevented by cleaning out medicine cabinets. The benefit is rated "Small": the available figures are emergency room visit counts rather than deaths, and the effect size of the act of clearing out cannot be calculated.

entries.title: Do not drink alcohol during and within 7 days after stopping antimicrobial drugs such as cephalosporins and metronidazole, and avoid alcohol-containing medicines like Huoxiang Zhengqi water and cough syrup
entries.cost: Free. Refrain from drinking alcohol for a little over a week, and check the ingredients for ethanol before taking other medications.
entries.summary: When certain cephalosporins, metronidazole, and similar drugs encounter alcohol, they can cause facial flushing, sweating, and heart palpitations; severe cases involve breathing difficulties and dropping blood pressure. It is not just liquor and beer—alcohol-containing medications like Huoxiang Zhengqi water and cough syrup can also trigger it. Avoid them entirely during medication and for 7 days after stopping.
entries.benefit: This is known as a disulfiram-like reaction. A 2023 popular science article on safe medication by the Fujian Medical Products Administration stated that drinking alcohol before or after taking certain cephalosporin medications can trigger this reaction. The article noted that this "can seriously damage health and even cause life-threatening danger." Symptoms include facial flushing, sweating, palpitations, and even dyspnea, blood pressure drop, and anaphylactic shock. According to the Clinical Medication Guidelines of the Pharmacopoeia of the People's Republic of China, the drugs listed in the article include cefazolin, ceftriaxone, cefoperazone, metronidazole, tinidazole, furazolidone, and others. The article clearly states that "drinking alcohol and consuming alcohol-containing medicines, foods, etc. are prohibited within 7 days after medication," with examples such as liquor-filled chocolates and Huoxiang Zhengqi water. The reason is that the enzyme inhibited by the drug often takes 4 to 5 days to recover. A hospital in Guangzhou summarized 82 cases over 2 years. 57 cases (69.51%) were caused by cephalosporins, and 10 cases (12.20%) by nitroimidazoles (such as metronidazole and tinidazole). Alcohol came from alcoholic beverages in 40 cases (48.78%) and from ethanol-containing medications in 31 cases (37.80%). Oral medications included Huoxiang Zhengqi water, cough syrup, Motherwort liquid extract, etc. Among the 82 cases, 68 were mild, 9 were moderate, and 5 were severe; all resolved within 1 to 3 hours, with no deaths. The US package insert for metronidazole requires avoiding alcohol and propylene glycol-containing products during treatment and for at least 3 days after discontinuation.
entries.sources: Fujian Medical Products Administration (Fujian Drug Science Popularization and Regulatory Data Center) (2023). 2023 "National Safe Medication Month" original science popularization tip: Why you cannot drink alcohol when taking cephalosporins. <https://yjj.scjgj.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/kpzl/qgaqyyy/202312/t20231215_6334595.htm>; Fang Caifu, Tu Xing, Liu Tao, Huang Hongbing, Qiu Meng, Liang Weiting (2015). Analysis of 82 cases of disulfiram-like reactions in our hospital. China Pharmacy, 26(29):4089-4091. <https://doi.org/10.6039/j.issn.1001-0408.2015.29.19>; Pfizer (2026). FLAGYL 375 (metronidazole) capsules, prescribing information: Contraindications, Interaction with Alcohol. DailyMed. <https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=a2883ca1-5a9a-4259-9d80-46ab67274384>
entries.notes: Not every cephalosporin causes this, but ordinary people cannot tell the difference; following this rule regardless of which one you take is the easiest approach. When a doctor prescribes cephalosporins or metronidazole, proactively mention whether you have had any alcohol in recent days. That popular science article recommends avoiding alcohol for 3 days before taking medication as well, while acknowledging that there is currently no authoritative consensus on this specific interval. If facial flushing or palpitations occur, immediately stop all alcohol-containing substances. The article says mild cases can resolve on their own, while severe cases require emergency medical attention. Also do not drink alcohol while taking acetaminophen—see Section 34, Item 1 (Acetaminophen). The evidence is rated B because the evidence consists of case series and package inserts, without controls. The benefit is rated "Small": all 82 cases resolved within hours, there were no deaths, and only 5 cases were severe. For how to look after someone who is intoxicated, see Section 13, Item 46 (When Someone Is Intoxicated).

entries.title: After taking cold medicines or allergy medicines containing chlorpheniramine (piriton) or diphenhydramine, do not drive, work at heights, or operate machinery during the medication period
entries.cost: Free. Check the ingredient list when buying medicines. For the days you take the medication, switch to taking public transit or taxis, or ask a doctor or pharmacist to switch to a non-drowsy alternative.
entries.summary: Many combination cold medicines contain anti-allergy ingredients such as chlorpheniramine and diphenhydramine, which cause drowsiness when taken. The National Medical Products Administration warns not to drive, work at heights, or operate machinery while taking such medications. In a driving simulator, people who took diphenhydramine drove worse than those who drank alcohol. Feeling that you are not sleepy does not mean your driving is unimpaired.
entries.benefit: A 2010 Adverse Drug Reaction Information Bulletin from the State Food and Drug Administration stated that Vitamin C Yinqiao Tablets contain chlorpheniramine maleate, also known as piriton. Its adverse reactions mainly include drowsiness, weakness, somnolence, and dry mouth. The bulletin advised doctors and pharmacies to remind patients: during medication, do not drive aircraft, motor vehicles, or boats, and do not engage in high-altitude work, mechanical operations, or operating precision instruments. A 2020 public medication advisory from the National Medical Products Administration stated that combination cold medicines often contain anti-allergy ingredients like chlorpheniramine and diphenhydramine, which cause drowsiness.
